geometry_source: vertical excitations computed on the C2v MP2 geometry because MP2 reproduces the experimental structure better than CASSCF; CASSCF-geometry values given in the SI. Gas-phase electron diffraction gives an average nitro torsional angle of 13.3 +/- 1.4 degrees, which is not directly comparable with the static equilibrium value because of the nitro torsional vibration and the very low rotation barrier
method: MS-CASPT2//CASSCF; MC-PDFT as an economical alternative; CAM-B3LYP/def2-TZVPP frequencies for the vibrational corrections to the vertical energies
active_space_orbital_description: the union of the two fragment spaces: 13 electrons in 10 orbitals for the NO2 moiety, and 7 electrons in 7 orbitals for the phenyl fragment (its 6-electron/6-orbital pi system plus the singly occupied sigma orbital involved in the C-N bond). This covers inter- and intra-fragment transitions as well as C-N bond breaking. The C-C sigma orbitals of the ring are not included
active_space_protocol: (20,17) selected fragment-wise: NO2 requires (13,10), and any other choice of its active orbitals causes symmetry breaking of the radical wavefunction; phenyl requires (7,7), namely the (6,6) pi system plus the singly occupied sigma orbital of the C-N bond. Smaller active spaces were also tested to check active-space dependence
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged per symmetry species (SAn-CASSCF notation); five singlet valence states fall in the 4.0-6.0 eV range
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1 1A1. MS-CASPT2 vertical excitation energies (eV) with oscillator strengths: 1 1A2 3.83 (f < 1e-5, [n sigma]1[pi*(NO2)]1, 68 percent); 1 1B2 4.30 (f = 1.01e-4, [sigma1(NO2)]1[pi*(NO2)]1, 66 percent); 1 1B1 4.72 (f = 4.83e-3, mixed [pi2(bz)]1[pi*(NO2)]1 45 percent); 2 1A1 5.11 (f = 0.294, [pi3(bz)]1[pi*(NO2)]1, 72 percent); 2 1B1 5.81 (f = 3.97e-2, [n pi]1[pi*(NO2)]1, 47 percent); 2 1A2 7.00; 2 1B2 7.02 (f = 1.13e-5); 3 1B1 7.04 (f = 8.03e-2); 3 1A2 7.36; 3 1B2 7.51 (f = 3.59e-4); 3 1A1 7.60 (f = 1.06e-2). Triplets: 1 3A1 4.03, 2 3A1 4.75, 3 3A1 6.88 eV. Experimental gas-phase absorption maxima at 350 and 280 nm (weak) and 240 and 193 nm (strong). Ground-state dissociation to phenyl plus NO2: experimental delta_r H(0 K) = 307.2 kJ/mol, reproduced well by the calculation
Other: Explicitly framed as a test of how far the active space can be reduced. The key negative result is that reducing the active space gives erroneous results specifically in the dissociation region, because orbital rotations change the composition of the active space along the C-N dissociation coordinate; the authors flag this as a serious drawback for automated active-space selection procedures and for CASSCF-like methods that automatically shrink or grow the active space. Reference CASSCF weights were at least 0.70 for every singlet and triplet state. The one band the calculation gets wrong in intensity is the shortest-wavelength one, which involves the benzene ring breathing vibration, because the ring C-C sigma orbitals were left out of the active space. Vibrational corrections were made from zero-point energies of ground and excited states, with the gradient and rotational/translational modes projected out of the excited-state Hessian; these are not 0-0 transitions. MS-CASPT2 used a 0.1 imaginary shift and the standard IPEA value of 0.25.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet carbene. Relative energies (kcal/mol) at (10,8)CASPT2/6-31G*//(10,8)CASSCF/6-31G*, energies relative to -266.32458 Ha and enthalpies to -266.24648 Ha: carbenadioxolane 0.0 (0.0); concerted fragmentation transition structure 6.2 (activation enthalpy at 298 K 4.0); singlet diradical 3b 29.2 (25.2, with two imaginary frequencies excluded from the thermal correction). The concerted and stepwise pathways therefore differ by 23.0 kcal/mol at CASPT2, only 0.4 kcal/mol less than the (U)B3LYP difference. For contrast, B3LYP/6-31G* gives an activation enthalpy of 8.4 kcal/mol, MP2/6-31G** 6.3, and zero-point-corrected RHF 30.4 kcal/mol with the 4-31G basis and 41.2 kcal/mol with 6-31G*
Other: The point of the study is that the 1981 RHF result attributing a 30.4 kcal/mol barrier to this fragmentation was an artefact of missing electron correlation rather than of the small basis set, since enlarging the RHF basis makes the barrier worse (41.2 kcal/mol). CASSCF and CASPT2 were used specifically because UB3LYP singlet-diradical wavefunctions are badly spin-contaminated: the UB3LYP <S^2> for singlet 3b was 1.01, an even mixture of singlet and triplet. Both the CASSCF and B3LYP vibrational analyses give the singlet diradical two imaginary frequencies corresponding to out-of-plane motions of the terminal methylene hydrogens, so it is not even a local minimum, and relaxing along them leads to conformer 3a which fragments to ethylene plus CO2 without a barrier

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 4F free-ion term, split by the square-pyramidal ligand field. Ligand field analysis: the 3d7 4F term splits in an octahedral field into 4T1g, 4T2g and 4A2g; lowering to C4v splits 4T1g into 4E and 4A2; the real symmetry of complex 1 splits the 4E term into two terms separated by only 244 cm-1, with a third term at 1616 cm-1. Spin-orbit coupling on these three lowest ligand-field terms produces six Kramers doublets spanning 0-2048 cm-1. From the magnetic fit, the ground to first excited Kramers doublet gap is 145 cm-1. Ligand-field parameters from the magnetic data fit: alpha = 2.16, delta-ax = -1503 cm-1, delta-rh = -270 cm-1, lambda = -105 cm-1; from the ab initio calculation, delta-ax = -1508 cm-1, delta-rh = -164 cm-1, alpha-lambda = -223 cm-1; refitting the magnetic data with alpha-lambda, delta-ax and delta-rh fixed at the ab initio values gives alpha = 1.86 and lambda = -120 cm-1, reduced from the Co(II) free-ion value of -180 cm-1 by the covalency of the donor-acceptor bond

The calculated d-orbital splitting for the real complex closely resembles that of an idealized [CoBr5]3- square pyramid (ordering dxy, then dyz and dxz, then dz2, then dx2-y2) except that the dxz/dyz degeneracy is lifted by the lower real symmetry. method: fully variational incremental CASSCF (iCASSCF) for geometry optimization and the reaction path, with iCAS-CI(n=3) single-point energies on the optimized orbitals; ROHF reference

compound_name: Coelenterazine (CTZ) dioxetanone, the reactive bioluminescent intermediate, in the NanoLuc luciferase protein (also computed in the gas phase and in PCM for comparison)
geometry_source: QM/MM optimized in this work. The protein-solvent system was equilibrated for 10 ns of classical AMOEBA MD, the CTZ+O2 coordinates were then manually replaced by the dioxetanone, and only a 932-atom relaxed region around the chromophore was optimized (rest frozen at the snapshot); QM region 177 atoms, comprising the chromophore plus hydrogen-bonding side chains. Reactant and product were also optimized separately in the gas phase and in PCM (eps = 78.4). Reaction path by interpolation between the optimized reactant and product for each environment
method: SA-CASSCF with polarizable QM/MM embedding in the AMOEBA force field (SA-CASSCF/AMOEBA), dynamically weighted with S0 as reference state and a 3 eV bandwidth in the PCM and QM/MM calculations; minimum-energy conical intersection searches on top
software: TeraChem for the QM part coupled to OpenMM for the MM part
active_space_orbital_description: chosen to contain enough active orbitals to describe the O-O bond dissociation of the dioxetanone ring; the low-lying states it produces are n->sigma* and sigma->sigma* local excitations in the O-O bond region
active_space_protocol: (8,9) sized around the breaking O-O bond; state-averaging over four singlets and two triplets, with dynamic weights referenced to S0 using a 3 eV bandwidth. A separate, much smaller SA(2)-CASSCF(4,3)/3-21G space was used only on an HBDI-valine model to parametrize the force field and to compare link-atom schemes
nroots_per_mult: 4 singlets and 2 triplets in the state-average
Other: State characters from attach-detach density analysis at image 20 of the gas-phase path: S1, S2 and S3 are all local 1(n,sigma*) excitations in the O-O region; T1 is 3(n,sigma*) and T2 is 3(sigma,sigma*). Environment changes the picture qualitatively. In the gas phase and in PCM the S1-S0 gap closes as the O-O bond dissociates and the MECI geometry closely resembles the product; in QM/MM the S1-S0 gap no longer approaches zero along the path, S2 and S3 rise well above their gas-phase positions (they acquire core-region excitation character), and reaching the MECI requires rotating the O-C-O group by almost 90 degrees out of the dioxetanone ring plane. The MECI topology also differs: peaked in PCM, sloped in QM/MM. Protonation: unconstrained QM/MM optimization always ends with HPh protonated and D139 deprotonated; forcing the deprotonated state requires O-H distance constraints and costs 15.6 kcal/mol. The proton-transfer energy computed with AMOEBA embedding is less sensitive to QM-region size than with a fixed-charge (AMBER-FB15 / SPC-Fw / GAFF) model.
reference_short: A Polarizable QM/MM Model That Combines the State-Averaged CASSCF and AMOEBA Force Field for Photoreactions in Proteins, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2024)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Metal-free organic (metal_center = none). geometry_source: optimized at B3LYP/6-31G(d) with Gaussian 16 (stated for the BODIPY dye, which was newly added here; the remaining structures come from the benchmark set of the paper's Ref. 52)
method: CD-GIAO-CASSCF: isotropic NMR nuclear magnetic shieldings from coupled-perturbed CASSCF (CP-CASSCF) with gauge-including atomic orbitals and Cholesky-decomposed two-electron integrals (CD threshold 1e-5)
software: CFOUR (MINT, SCF, CASSCF and CP-CASSCF modules); Gaussian 16 for the B3LYP geometries
active_space_protocol: active spaces taken from the established benchmark set of the paper's Ref. 52. The CASSCF starting orbitals are unrestricted natural orbitals (UNOs): the RHF wave function is checked for instabilities, every broken-symmetry UHF solution is optimized, and the natural orbitals of the averaged density matrix are used. The authors advocate this as a black-box active-space selection procedure that simultaneously diagnoses whether a multireference treatment is warranted at all; its cost is that computing the symmetry-broken UHF solutions can rival the CASSCF itself

This molecule replaced nothing except that the BODIPY dye was substituted for chlorophyll from the original set, since chlorophyll needs out-of-core handling of the Cholesky vectors which is not yet implemented.
reference_short: Computation of NMR shieldings at the CASSCF level using gauge-including atomic orbitals and Cholesky decomposition, J. Chem. Phys. (2022)

compound_name: Manganese atom (Mn) in an intense near-infrared laser field
geometry_source: single atom or atomic ion - no molecular geometry
method: time-dependent CASSCF (TD-CASSCF) and time-dependent occupation-restricted multiple active space (TD-ORMAS), full-dimensional all-electron real-time propagation under an intense laser field, with MCTDHF as the fully active reference
active_space_orbital_description: 15 spatial orbitals spanning the 3s, 3p, 3d and 4s shells plus correlating/virtual orbitals; the 1s and 2s2p shells are frozen in the baseline setting
active_space_protocol: Orbital space is partitioned into time-independent frozen-core orbitals, time-dependent doubly occupied dynamical-core orbitals, and active orbitals. 15 spatial orbitals in total, which is the minimum needed to get the correct spin multiplicities; treating all 15 as active is the MCTDHF limit, and TD-CASSCF results with 2p frozen overlap it perfectly, confirming convergence at this orbital count. The frozen/active boundary was then scanned deliberately as a diagnostic: freezing up to 3s barely changes the spectrum, but freezing 3p makes the resonant harmonic vanish, which is how the 3p electrons were identified as responsible. TD-ORMAS runs use 24 orbitals, subdividing the active set into Active1 and Active2 with at most two-electron excitations from Active1 to Active2 and at most two electrons in Active2.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 6S5/2, configuration [Ar]4s2 3d5. Strong single-photon excitation line at about 50 eV, reproducing the known 3p-3d giant resonance
Other: Experimental ionization potential 7.43 eV; barrier-suppression intensity 1.2e13 W/cm2. TD-CASSCF uses 52 determinants, TD-ORMAS 86510. HHG spectra computed for a 770 nm, 3e14 W/cm2, four-cycle sin^2 pulse show a resonant harmonic slightly above 50 eV, strongly enhanced over its neighbours and in excellent agreement with the experimental value of about 50 eV. Repeating at 1333 nm and 1e14 W/cm2 (same ponderomotive energy) leaves the peak at 50 eV, so its position is set by atomic structure rather than laser parameters. Freezing 3p removes the peak entirely, establishing the 3p-3d resonance as its origin. Even starting from neutral Mn the spectrum extends to the cutoff expected for Mn2+.

compound_name: Azomethane (CH3-N=N-CH3), cis-to-trans photoisomerization, both outside and inside an optical cavity
geometry_source: cis and trans ground-state minima optimized at B3LYP/6-31G* (Gaussian 16) with frequency analysis confirming they are stationary points; the S1/S0 conical intersection optimized at SA-2-CAS(6,4)/6-31G* using Yarkony's method in Molpro 2015. The reaction path is a rigid linear interpolation in internal coordinates from the CI geometry out to each isomer, 60 geometries total, not further optimized. B3LYP frequencies also drive the Wigner sampling of initial conditions
method: SA-2-CASSCF for adiabatic energies, gradients, permanent and transition dipoles and nonadiabatic couplings, feeding on-the-fly trajectory surface hopping; a machine-learning model is trained on the molecular dipoles and their derivatives to make the ab initio molecular cavity QED (Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian) simulation affordable
software: Gaussian 16 for the DFT geometries and frequencies; Molpro 2015 for the CASSCF and conical-intersection optimization
active_space_protocol: SA-2-CAS(6,4): six electrons in four orbitals, state-averaged over two states, adopted from previous studies of this molecule rather than re-derived. The same space is used for the energies, gradients, dipoles, nonadiabatic couplings and the conical-intersection optimization
electronic_structure_description: The trans isomer lies about 0.5 eV below the cis isomer in the ground state
Other: Outside the cavity: dynamics is started from the cis isomer on Franck-Condon excitation (chosen because its ground-to-excited transition dipole is larger than the trans isomer's). There is no barrier on the excited-state surface between the cis minimum and the conical intersection, so nearly half the trajectories hop down within about 50 fs and essentially all are on the ground state by about 330 fs; the CNNC dihedral passes through +/-90 degrees at the intersection and the trans population rises to nearly 1 by about 70 fs. Inside the cavity (cavity frequency 2.72 eV, loss rate 4 meV, field polarized along Y): increasing the light-matter coupling from 0.005 to 0.05 a.u. slows the population transfer, raises the |g,1> photonic state population and hence the intracavity photon number, and significantly suppresses the trans population - i.e. the cis-to-trans isomerization is inhibited by strong coupling, because the reduced polaritonic nonadiabatic coupling keeps more trajectories on the upper state after they leave the Franck-Condon region. The authors caution that the Ebbesen photoisomerization experiments are in the collective coupling regime, unlike this single-molecule simulation.

method: CASSCF(6,6) and MRCISD+Q as the multireference references, compared against variational and lattice-regularized diffusion quantum Monte Carlo built on a Jastrow antisymmetrized geminal power wave function (VMC/JAGP and LRDMC/JAGP); QD-NEVPT2/CAS(6,6) results from the literature also used for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF and MRCISD+Q references; cc-pVTZ and VTZ-ANO in the QMC and DFT comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: the pi valence space of the conjugated pentadieniminium chain
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* is treated by the authors as the standard compromise for this system - adequate for the reaction paths but the specific thing they test, since the CI position and the relative stability of TSCT and TSDIR are exactly where it is expected to be least reliable. The paper separately shows that a Jastrow AGP wave function is formally comparable to a CAS(2,n) space, and analyses the transition from a (2,2) to a (2,n) active space
Other: The central quantitative result is the location of the S1/S0 conical intersection along the BLA coordinate. CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* places the CI between TSCT and TSDIR and gives a peaked intersection; VMC/JAGP instead pushes it out to about 0.075 A, beyond TSDIR, and LRDMC/JAGP to about 0.06 A, closer to MRCISD+Q. Most other correlated approaches put it at 0.03-0.04 A, the exception being QD-NEVPT2/CAS(6,6) which extrapolates to 0.05 A. The QMC intersection is sloped and intermediate rather than peaked. Before the crossing (smaller BLA) the ground state is a closed-shell charge-transfer pi^2 configuration; after it, a covalent diradical pi-pi* configuration. Charge-transfer character of the cis isomer ground state: 0.313 at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G*, 0.355 at MRCISD+Q/6-31G*, 0.375 at PBE/cc-pVTZ (which also gives a dipole of 3.784 D; PBE/VTZ-ANO with an ECP gives 3.758 D). In the diradical portion of the BLA path the triplet lies above the pi^2 singlet by about 10-12 kcal/mol at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G*, and the triplet stays above the singlet below BLA of 0.055 A (VMC) or 0.05 A (LRDMC).
reference_short: Quantum Monte Carlo Treatment of the Charge Transfer and Diradical Electronic Character in a Retinal Chromophore Minimal Model, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2015)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Metal-free organic cation (metal_center = none). Recorded because it is a direct, quantitative test of where CASSCF(6,6) fails on a much-used benchmark chromophore: the active space is adequate for the reaction paths but places the conical intersection roughly half as far along the BLA coordinate as the QMC treatments do. Charge transfer in the QMC framework is measured as the electronic density in the allyl region beyond the plane bisecting the C2=C3 bond, validated against Mulliken charges, since Mulliken charges are unavailable in QMC.

method: tailored distinguishable cluster singles and doubles (TDCSD) and tailored CCSD (TCCSD), with the active-space amplitudes taken from FCIQMC or deterministic FCI; benchmarked against internally contracted MRCI+Q (optionally F12-corrected) and high-order coupled cluster

active_space_orbital_description: the (10,8) full valence space - two sigma, two pi, two sigma* and two pi* built from the 2s and 2p orbitals of both atoms - enlarged by 8 further virtual orbitals which are 3s and 3p at short distance and acquire 3d character as the bond stretches

Active spaces in this paper are defined in two competing ways and compared head to head: from CASSCF natural orbitals, or from the most-active DCSD natural orbitals. The paper's conclusion is that DCSD natural orbitals give accuracy quite comparable to CASSCF-defined spaces depending on system and size, which matters because they are far cheaper to obtain. The CI amplitudes inside the active space come from FCIQMC (or deterministic FCI where feasible), which is what makes the large spaces reachable.
Other: With the (10,8) valence space the TDCSD curve tracks MRCI+Q much better than TCCSD does, especially at stretched geometries; it coincides with plain DCSD out to 3.4 bohr and then stays with the reference while DCSD degrades. method: quantum CASSCF: the active-space eigenvalue is obtained by VQE (UCCSD ansatz from a Hartree-Fock initial state, or a hardware-efficient ansatz) on a Jordan-Wigner-encoded qubit Hamiltonian, while the inactive-space energy is treated by Hartree-Fock; benchmarked against a classical FCI driver
software: VeloxChem and MultiPsi for the integrals and Hartree-Fock orbitals; IBM Qiskit for the Jordan-Wigner encoding and the VQE; noisy simulations on the IBMQ QASM Simulator with the IBMQ Santiago v1.3.14 coupling map and noise model, 1000 shots
basis_set: STO-3G, 6-31G, cc-pVDZ and ANO-L-VDZP compared; a CASSCF(2,2) was used for the noisy hardware-efficient-ansatz study
active_space_orbital_description: HOMO-2, HOMO-1, LUMO and LUMO+1. The HOMO is deliberately excluded: it is the oxygen lone pair and does not correlate significantly with any other valence orbital
active_space_protocol: the active space is fixed at 4 molecular orbitals (8 qubits) while the basis set is enlarged from STO-3G through ANO-L-VDZP, in order to separate what the basis set buys from what the quantum calculation buys. Orbital selection is by role rather than by energy order - the oxygen lone pair HOMO is skipped because it carries no useful correlation. Central finding of the paper, applicable to any CASSCF orbital optimization run on noisy hardware: canonical orbitals converge and noncanonical orbitals de-converge. For water with the HEA-VQE driver under IBMQ Santiago noise, canonical orbitals give a minimum average energy of -76.047720 Ha with average standard deviation 0.068468 and average 95 percent confidence 0.030007 Ha, versus noncanonical -75.990149 Ha with 0.146013 and 0.063992 - against a noiseless converged -76.063804 Ha and FCI -76.068513 Ha. The same trend, though weaker, holds for stretched CO. Choosing canonical orbitals is therefore itself a form of error mitigation.
Other: Qubit count scales with the full basis, not the active space, for the unrestricted problem: STO-3G 7 contracted basis functions / 14 qubits, 6-31G 13 / 26, cc-pVDZ 24 / 48 - which is precisely the motivation for using an active space. With CAS(4,4) the UCCSD-VQE energy differs from the FCI driver by only 7.8e-6 Ha. Noisy-simulation numbers for the CASSCF(2,2) case are given in the active_space_protocol field.
reference_short: de Gracia Trivino, Delcey and Wendin, Complete Active Space Methods for NISQ Devices: The Importance of Canonical Orbital Optimization for Accuracy and Noise Resilience, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 19, 2863 (2023)

compound_name: Cyclopropanone, photodissociation to carbon monoxide and ethylene (Norrish-type CO release) plus a polymerization channel
geometry_source: initial conditions from ground-state molecular dynamics sampling at constant excitation energy, mimicking continuous-wave excitation in resonance with the laser; 100 geometries sampled across the spectrum. The cheaper (2,4) active space was used for this ground-state sampling stage
method: a controlled comparison of eight electronic structure methods - SA-CASSCF, SS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, XMS-CASPT2, MRCI, FOMO-CASCI, MR-CISD/OM3 and SI-SA-REKS - crossed against several nonadiabatic algorithms (Landau-Zener surface hopping, fewest-switches surface hopping, AIMSWISS), to separate the influence of electronic structure from that of the coupled electron-nuclear algorithm
software: BAGEL for the CASPT2 simulations; other packages per method
basis_set: 6-31G* for most calculations; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 runs in BAGEL where 6-31G* is unavailable; a pseudominimal basis by default for MR-CISD/OM3
active_space_orbital_description: two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO) and two sigma*(CC)
active_space_protocol: (8,7) - two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO), two sigma*(CC) - used for every method except SI-SA-REKS. The choice was triangulated three ways rather than assumed: previous studies of this molecule, automated selection with the AutoCAS code, and the authors' own benchmarking of potential energy surfaces and absorption spectra. Two reduced spaces appear for practical reasons: (2,4) for the cheaper ground-state sampling, and (2,2) containing only n(O) and pi*(CO) for SI-SA-REKS, which has no other space implemented. All CASPT2 calculations used a 0.5 a.u. level shift, tested to be insensitive across a wide range. Only S0 and S1 were treated, equally weighted in the SA-CASSCF state-averaging
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, equally weighted)
Other: The paper's central result is that the electronic structure method matters far more than the nonadiabatic algorithm. Excited-state lifetimes across the ab initio family span nearly a factor of two: XMS-CASPT2 39 fs, MS-CASPT2 54 fs, FOMO-CASCI 58 fs, SA-CASSCF 68 fs - a spread the authors call surprising given that the underlying potential energy surfaces differ negligibly. Semiempirical MR-CISD/OM3 is fastest at 36 fs (within XMS-CASPT2 error bars); SI-SA-REKS is an outlier at 90 fs whose population transfer stops abruptly at 140 fs. CO release quantum yields: all ab initio methods agree within error bars and sit close to the experimental 0.73 (intensity-weighted average); MR-CISD/OM3 overestimates at 0.89; SI-SA-REKS fails outright at 0.20 (the authors could not reproduce the 0.44 +/- 0.11 previously published for that method). All ab initio methods find the polymerization channel at least once while the DFT and semiempirical ones never do. By contrast the coupled electron-nuclear algorithms give identical quantum yields within statistical error and consistent population transfer, with FSSH and LZSH essentially equivalent - so when conical intersections are well defined the cheaper LZSH is sufficient.
reference_short: Janos and Slavicek, What Controls the Quality of Photodynamical Simulations? Electronic Structure Versus Nonadiabatic Algorithm, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2023)

geometry_source: initial geometries and velocities sampled from the Wigner distribution without temperature broadening using SHARC tools; 100 trajectories propagated for 150 fs with a 0.5 fs time step
method: trajectory surface hopping (fewest switches, energy-based decoherence correction with a 0.1 Hartree decay factor) with XMS-CASPT2 using analytical nonadiabatic coupling vectors as the reference, compared against XMS-CASPT2 with local diabatization, MS-CASPT2, CASSCF, CC2, ADC(2), CIS, and TD-/TDA-DFT (PBE, PBE0, CAM-B3LYP)
software: SHARC for the dynamics; BAGEL for the reference XMS-CASPT2 (NACV and local diabatization); OpenMolcas for XMS-CASPT2 (lLD), MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF with the RI approximation and analytical Cholesky decomposition; Turbomole 7.3 for CC2 and ADC(2); Gaussian 16, Turbomole and ORCA 5.0.3 for the CIS and DFT variants
active_space_orbital_description: the pi and pi* orbitals plus the two nitrogen lone pairs
active_space_protocol: (6,4): pi, pi* and the two nitrogen lone pairs, used identically for XMS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF so the methods are compared on equal footing. The reference XMS-CASPT2 used no level shift and had IPEA deactivated. Note the independent convergence on this same (6,4) space for azomethane in 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00917 and 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c00137, though those papers do not all spell out the orbital composition
Other: Reference XMS-CASPT2 dynamics resolves four time regimes: (I) about 30 fs during which all molecules stay cis on S1; (II) crossing of a first conical intersection region up to about 60 fs, giving 20-25 percent nonadiabatic S1-to-S0 decay and complete cis-to-trans isomerization; (III) a roughly 40 fs plateau with most molecules trans; (IV) a second strong-coupling region with further decay, during which some molecules return to cis. The 90 degree conical intersection is reached after about 40 fs and the 270 degree one from about 120 fs. The end of regime II appears at about 60 fs regardless of electronic structure method. Method verdict: multireference methods are the preferred choice. CC2, TD-PBE, TDA-PBE, TD-PBE0 and TD-CAM-B3LYP are too unstable near electronic degeneracies to give trustworthy statistics. ADC(2) with local diabatization, TDA-PBE0 and TDA-CAM-B3LYP reproduce the timescale (despite up to 40 percent of trajectories crashing) but predict almost total decay through the first crossing and so badly describe the 'rotator' trajectories. CIS additionally fails to reproduce the population plateau. The authors' most transferable caution: which methods would succeed could hardly be predicted from a static analysis of the potential energy surfaces, so the usual practice of validating an electronic structure method on static energetics before running dynamics may not be sufficient.

compound_name: PSB3 (penta-2,4-dieniminium cation), the minimal retinal chromophore model
geometry_source: S1 potential energy scans built by constraining the torsional coordinate; quantum-classical trajectories from sampled initial conditions
method: quantum-classical (surface hopping) trajectories driven by CASSCF, XMS-CASPT2, RMS-CASPT2 and the REKS-family SSR(2,2) and SSR(3,2) methods (BHHLYP functional), compared on identical footing
software: OpenMolcas for the CASPT2-level QM calculations and OpenMolcas/Tinker for QM/MM; the OpenMolcas-GAMESS-US/Tinker interface for the REKS calculations
active_space_orbital_description: all pi and pi* orbitals of the conjugated polyenic chain
active_space_protocol: Active spaces are set by the conjugated chain: all pi and pi* orbitals of the polyenic backbone. That gives CAS(6,6) for PSB3 and its methylated derivatives, CAS(8,8) for PSB4, and CAS(12,12) for the full retinal chromophore in the rhodopsin QM/MM model. A deliberate CAS(2,2) - HOMO and LUMO, pi and pi* only - was run alongside CAS(8,8) in XMS-CASPT2 scans of PSB4 specifically to isolate what the small active space of the REKS/SSR methods costs. The answer is directly useful: XMS-CASPT2(2,2) energy profiles resemble the REKS ones much more closely than XMS-CASPT2(8,8) does, especially along the C4=C5 coordinate, so the REKS discrepancies are substantially an active-space-size effect rather than purely a functional effect. Follow-up tests showed that increasing exact exchange (BHHLYP 50 percent, PBE-2X 54 percent, HFLYP 100 percent) brings SSR much closer to XMS-CASPT2(8,8), and that HF-REKS, which has no dynamic correlation, agrees better with CASSCF(2,2) than with any CASPT2 variant.

method: SA-CASSCF for geometry optimization and conical-intersection searches, with MRCI (with and without Davidson correction), MS-CASPT2 (0.2 level shift) and EOM-CCSD single points for the vertical excitation energies; natural population analysis and Wiberg bond indices for the electronic structure characterization

active_space_protocol: A worked example of choosing an active space under a cost ceiling, with the reasoning spelled out. The chemically correct space is (20,16): eight pi plus two nO lone-pair orbitals on uracil, and six pi orbitals on benzene. That space generates 14 158 144 CSFs and 64 128 064 determinants and is affordable only for single points, not for geometry optimization or conical-intersection searches. Dropping the highest unoccupied orbital gives (20,15), 2 186 184 CSFs and 9 018 009 determinants, which the authors identify as the best compromise for vertical excitation energies - explicitly better than the alternative of transplanting the previously used reduced spaces for the separate fragments, (12,9) for uracil plus (6,6) for benzene, which would give (18,15). All geometry optimizations were then done at (20,14), the largest space they could afford for optimization, and MRCI and MS-CASPT2 single points were computed on top of it. 5BU has 106 electrons in 53 doubly occupied orbitals; during MCSCF optimization the lowest 43 orbitals were closed but still fully optimized, and for the correlated single points those same 43 were frozen.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S1 and S2)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0. Vertical excitation energies in eV, S1 (n-pi*) then S2 (pi-pi*), in the printed order of Table 2: SA-CASSCF(20,14) 4.85 / 7.92; SA-CASSCF(18,14) 4.94 / 5.34; SA-CASSCF(20,15) 5.02 / 7.02; SA-CASSCF(18,15) 4.94 / 5.21; SA-CASSCF(20,16) 4.94 (f = 0.003) / 7.10 (f = 0.571); MS-CASPT2(20,13) 5.02 / 6.83; MS-CASPT2(20,14) 4.93 / 6.28; MRCI(20,14) 5.08 / 7.12; MRCI+D(20,14) 5.11 / 6.90; EOM-CCSD 5.13 / 5.44; LT-DF-LCC2 4.94 / 5.07
Other: The active space controls S2 far more than S1. Removing two active electrons at fixed orbital count collapses S2 from 7.92 to 5.34 eV at (20,14) versus (18,14), and from 7.02 to 5.21 eV at (20,15) versus (18,15), while S1 moves by only 0.01-0.09 eV. Enlarging the virtual space from (20,15) to (20,16) shifts S2 only from 7.03 to 7.10 eV and leaves S1 unchanged, so the virtual orbitals matter much less than the occupied ones. Dynamic correlation then brings the CASSCF values of 6.93 and 8.48 eV down to 5.83 and 6.93 eV at MS-CASPT2. Because the saturated methylene bridge blocks pi communication between the two rings, the 5BU excited states track the isolated fragments closely: the first two excited states at 5.13 and 5.44 eV match isolated uracil (5.17 eV) and isolated benzene (5.30 eV), and the third and fourth lie at 5.78 and 6.55 eV. active_space_protocol: A four-space progression that is itself the key result. CAS(8,11): five Fe 3d orbitals, five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals and one sigma(Fe-N) bond. CAS(12,15): adds the four Gouterman pi frontier orbitals, shown to be crucial for stabilizing the triplet over the quintet. CAS(14,18): NOT an extension of (12,15) - instead it adds four Fe 4s4p orbitals and the remaining three sigma(Fe-N) bonds on top of (8,11), deliberately omitting the Gouterman pi orbitals. CAS(32,34): the largest, containing the entire pi system together with the CAS(14,18) orbitals. CAS(32,34) is too large for conventional CASSCF, so Stochastic-CASSCF optimized its orbitals. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. Large spaces (over 30 electrons in 30+ orbitals) are built from DCSD natural orbitals whose occupations deviate strongly from 0 and 2, with the explicit requirement that both spin states get a similar space - if an orbital type matters for one spin state it is included for both, so the states are balanced. FCIQMC then supplies the CI vectors inside these large spaces to tailor the distinguishable-cluster/coupled-cluster amplitudes.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 3Eg (triplet), stabilized over 5A1g (quintet). Quintet-triplet spin gap dE = E(Q) - E(T), a few kcal/mol with the triplet below the quintet. At CAS(32,34): tailored TDCSD-F12a and TCCSD(T)-F12a both give 5.8 kcal/mol; recent Stochastic-MRCISD on the same CAS(32,34) (correlating 96 electrons in 159 orbitals) gives 6.8 kcal/mol; CCSD(T)-embedded CAS(32,34)+dF12 gives 5.7 and DCSD-embedded 3.6 kcal/mol. Largest doubles amplitude in CAS(32,34): 0.242 (LS/triplet) and 0.221 (HS/quintet) - much more multiconfigurational than the octahedral complexes.
Other: The clearest active-space lesson in the paper: the entire porphyrin pi system must be in the space to stabilize the triplet ground state. Smaller CASs erroneously predict a quintet ground state; only once the full pi system is included (via the Gouterman orbitals and ultimately CAS(32,34)) does the correct triplet-below-quintet ordering emerge, already at the Stochastic-CASSCF level, and tailoring plus F12 enlarges the gap further. compound_name: He...He van der Waals dimer ground state (with He...H2 excited-state and hydrogen-bonded dimers as further tests)
geometry_source: interaction energy curves versus interatomic distance; van der Waals minimum near 5.6 bohr
method: supermolecular CASSCF interaction energies analyzed for their dispersion content, with a derived closed-form CAS dispersion energy (Edisp_CAS) from CAS transition density matrices; benchmarked against SAPT dispersion at the FCI level and an exact reference potential
basis_set: aug-cc-pV5Z for the interaction curves; aug-cc-pVTZ for the long-range C6 analysis
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(4,4) for the dimer, dissociating to a product of CAS(2,2) monomers; larger dimer spaces up to CAS(4,28) also tested
active_space_protocol: A quantitative warning about active-space size and intermolecular dispersion. CASSCF itself recovers a PORTION of the dispersion energy, and that portion GROWS with active-space size, so naively adding a dispersion correction to a supermolecular CASSCF interaction energy double-counts intermonomer correlation by an amount that increases with the space. For He...He: CAS(4,4)+dispersion deviates from the benchmark by only 6.6% at the vdW minimum, but CAS(4,28)+dispersion OVERestimates by 72% and shifts the minimum from 5.6 to 5.3 bohr. The paper's fix (CAS+DispCAS, subtracting the dispersion already in the CASSCF energy) keeps errors under 2% at any active-space size. The complementary limitation: even CAS(4,18) recovers only about 50% of the He...He C6 coefficient (0.735 vs the reference 1.461 a.u.) and no higher Cn, because only p orbitals are in the active space. He...H2 excited-state dimers used CAS(2,5)/CAS(2,4) for the 1Sigma_u+ state and CAS(2,2) on He with CAS(2,10) on H2 for the 1Pi_u state.
Other: The study also decomposes interaction energies of hydrogen-bonded dimers (H2O...H2O, HCN...HCN and others). The overarching message for anyone choosing a CASSCF active space for intermolecular interactions: enlarging the active space captures more dispersion inside the CASSCF energy, so dispersion corrections must be made active-space-consistent or they will double-count - a counterintuitive direction, since bigger is not automatically safer here.
reference_short: How Much Dispersion Energy Is Included in the Multiconfigurational Interaction Energy? J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2020)

compound_name: O(1D) + N2O(X 1Sigma+) reaction system — ground 1A' potential energy surface giving NO+NO and N2+O2(a 1Dg)
point_group: Cs (1A' ground PES; N2O itself linear, NNO = 180.0 deg)
geometry_source: optimized in this work at CASSCF (no analytical CASPT2 gradients in MOLCAS 4.1, so CASSCF geometries were made as good as possible); stationary points first located with (14,12) then reoptimized at CASSCF(18,14); transition-state geometries additionally refined at the CASPT2 level to give approximate CASPT2 structures
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF geometries with point-wise CASPT2 single points; transition state theory used for the kinetics
basis_set: Pople Cartesian Gaussian basis sets, chiefly 6-311G(2d) (100 basis functions for the system); 6-311+G(2d) also used for some stationary points
active_space_orbital_description: (14,12)B = all atomic 2p-derived molecular orbitals; (14,12)A = the same but with one 2p-derived MO replaced by one N-2s-derived MO; (18,14)A/B add 4 electrons in two further 2s(N and O)-derived MOs to (14,12)A or B respectively. CI expansion ~85 000 CSFs for (14,12) and ~500 000 CSFs for (18,14) in 1A' symmetry
active_space_protocol: Active orbitals chosen by a natural-orbital-occupation-number (NOON) criterion — keep as active the MOs with NOONs between 0.02 and 1.98 in the state-averaged first-order density matrix, which is argued to give the lowest energy for a fixed CI expansion size. Applied strictly, this criterion gives a DIFFERENT space per reactive channel — (14,12) for the NO+NO channel and (12,10) for the N2+O2 channel — hence inconsistent at, e.g., reactants; the authors instead adopt a homogeneous space over the whole PES even where NOONs fall outside those limits, accepting spaces that are not strictly homogeneous, and aiming at the lowest-energy ground-PES stationary points (NOONs maximally different from 0.0/2.0). Full valence is not feasible for this system, so trial and error plus comparison with experiment was needed. Sequence: (14,12)B all 2p-derived MOs; (14,12)A swaps one for an N 2s MO — needed because nitrogen is a limiting case for which orbitals to make active; (18,14)A/B add two 2s(N,O) MOs (+4 electrons). (18,14)A partitions as O(2,2)+N2O(16,12), i.e. the full valence space of the N2O fragment is correlated. At CASSCF, space A is clearly favoured for (14,12) and the A/B differences shrink for (18,14); once point-wise CASPT2 is applied all four spaces give similar results. B-type spaces were always used in products and describe some regions better
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A' (lowest singlet PES of the O(1D)+N2O system). Reaction energies, paper's kcal/mol at CASSCF with point-wise CASPT2 in parentheses [eV converted from the CASPT2 values], across the four active spaces: O(1D)+N2O -> NO+NO — (14,12)A -76.1 (-79.7) [-3.456]; (14,12)B -93.1 (-82.4) [-3.573]; (18,14)A -78.3 (-80.5) [-3.491]; (18,14)B -80.0 (-81.0) [-3.513]; experiment -80.4 [-3.486]. O(1D)+N2O -> N2+O2(a 1Dg) — (14,12)A -100.8 (-103.8) [-4.501]; (14,12)B -117.8 (-106.4) [-4.614]; (18,14)A -101.3 (-103.6) [-4.492]; (18,14)B -103.0 (-104.0) [-4.510]; experiment -100.9 [-4.375]
Other: The active-space choice is itself a main result: exoergicities and the N2O geometry vary strongly between the A and B spaces at CASSCF(14,12) (the NO+NO exoergicity swings from -76.1 to -93.1 kcal/mol), the spread narrows at (18,14), and CASPT2 washes out the difference almost entirely — evidence that dynamic correlation compensates an imperfect reference. N2O geometries (RNN / RNO / NNO angle, A and deg) for (14,12)A/(14,12)B and, in parentheses, (18,14)A/(18,14)B: 1.1323/1.1146 (1.1343/1.1339) [expt 1.1273]; 1.1901/1.1949 (1.1931/1.1919) [expt 1.1851]; 180.0 throughout. The 1Dg state of O is five-fold degenerate and resolves in the Cs subgroup into three A' and two A'' components; several 1A' and 1A'' PESs correlate reactants with both product channels. Stationary points reported at CASPT2//CASSCF(18,14)/6-311G(2d) except TS A3 (CASPT2//CASSCF(14,12)/6-311G(2d)); compared with BD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ and earlier CASPT2(10,10)/6-311+G(2d)//CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G(d) work. CASSCF(18,14) is computationally very expensive, so some out-of-plane properties were not computed at that level. TST rate constants based on the CASPT2 structures agree well with experiment

Other: Central methodological result: the near degeneracy in the long range of the same-symmetry states 2 3Sigma_u+ and A 3Sigma_u+ can produce unphysical mixing of these states in a CASSCF calculation; the authors derive the correct asymptotic behaviour dictated by the quadrupole-quadrupole interaction and show how to recover it. Vibrational energies G(v) and rotational constants B(v) reproduce all experimentally known levels of A 3Sigma_u+ to a few tenths of a percent, the largest errors being for the highest vibrational levels just below dissociation. R-dependent spin-orbit couplings between the eight ungerade states are reported

compound_name: Nb3N2 cluster and its cation Nb3N2+ (niobium trimer dinitride)
ligand_set: 2 N atoms bound to a Nb3 triangle (bridging/triply bridging geometries discussed)
point_group: C2v (all calculations performed in C2v; note the arbitrary sigma_v/sigma_v' assignment means B1/B2 labels were swapped to make MOLPRO and GAUSSIAN output consistent)
geometry_source: full geometry optimizations of each electronic state up to the octet, performed in this work in C2v at both B3LYP/srsc (GAUSSIAN03) and CASSCF (MOLPRO-2006) levels
method: CASSCF (Werner-Meyer-Knowles) with single-point MRCI and MRCI+Q (Davidson correction), compared against B3LYP DFT
software: MOLPRO-2006 for CASSCF/MRCI; GAUSSIAN03 for DFT
basis_set: Nb: Stuttgart (srsc) basis with quasirelativistic ECP replacing the first 28 electrons; N: cc-pVDZ. For basis-set tests on the ground states, Dunning bases cc-pVDZ to aug-cc-pVTZ on N with a (10s9p8d2f1g)/[5s5p4d2f1g] basis on Nb
relativistic_treatment: quasirelativistic effective core potential on Nb (first 28 electrons replaced)
active_space_orbital_description: final active space is the 3a1, 2a2, 2b1 and 3b2 orbitals (10 orbitals) lying above the closed 9a1/2a2/5b1/5b2 set, holding 11 electrons (10 for the cation). Nb 4s/4p and N 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are always doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: Explicit reduction from a full valence space: the full valence active space of Nb3N2/Nb3N2+ is 40 orbitals in C2v (16a1, 5a2, 13b1, 6b2), which gives an intractable number of CSFs. First reduction — the Nb 4s and 4p and N 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are frozen closed (doubly occupied). The remaining 26 orbitals were still too large, so preliminary CASSCF calculations with a large active space were run and used as a screen: orbitals doubly occupied in ALL configurations were made closed, and high-energy orbitals not occupied in ANY configuration were removed. The resulting space closes the lowest 9a1, 2a2, 5b1, 5b2 and makes active the next 3a1, 2a2, 2b1, 3b2 — 11 electrons (10 for the cation) in 10 orbitals, totalling 7000 CSFs. No excitations were allowed from the closed orbitals but they were allowed to relax. In the MRCI, all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients >= 0.05 were used as references, giving up to 125 million configurations
multiplicities_studied: 1,2,3,4 — neutral: doublets and quartets at MRCI (geometries optimized for all states up to the octet, 2S+1 = 8); cation: singlets and triplets at MRCI (up to septet optimized)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2B2 for neutral Nb3N2 (1A1 for Nb3N2+). The MRCI leading configuration of each ground state agrees with DFT but accounts for only up to 70% of the total wave function. Excited states of neutral Nb3N2 (eV above ground state): B3LYP puts three states (2A1, 4B2, 4B1) 0.64-0.94; CASSCF puts the first three (2A1, 4B2, 2A2) at 1.0 <= dE <= 1.2; at MRCI and MRCI+Q the 2A1 and 2A2 states rise sharply and only 4B2 remains below 2 eV, so 4B2 is the true first excited state. The 4B2 leading configuration is obtained from the 2B2 ground configuration by exciting an electron from 11a1 into 12a1 and is only 54% of the MRCI wave function. The Nb3N2+ ground 1A1 state is highly multireference with three major configurations. Adiabatic ionization potential (2B2 -> 1A1, removing the unpaired 7b2 electron): experiment 5.44315 eV (ZEKE origin at 43901.7 cm-1, their Ref. 10); this work B3LYP 5.67; MRCI 4.55 and MRCI+Q 4.80 with the smallest basis, MRCI 4.51 with cc-pVTZ on Nb (MRCI+Q unchanged to 3 s.f.); increasing the N basis quality did not affect the IPs
Other: Central finding: transition energies between the neutral and cationic manifolds are predicted POORLY by MRCI relative to the computationally cheap DFT — the MRCI/MRCI+Q adiabatic IPs sit ~0.6-0.9 eV below the very precisely measured ZEKE value while B3LYP is within ~0.23 eV. Adding unlinked quadruple excitations (Davidson) raises the IP by 0.25 eV but not enough. Literature DFT comparisons for the IP: BP86 (ADF) and LSDA (DEMON) both 5.60 eV; B3P86 (GAUSSIAN94) 6.37 eV, ~1 eV too high, consistent with that functional's known 0.3-1.0 eV overestimation. CASSCF and DFT geometries are in general agreement. At CASSCF, the 8A2, 4B1 and 2B1 states are the only ones with triply bridging geometries. A CASSCF-vs-MRCI discrepancy of 2.75 versus 4.75 eV is noted for one state. Geometric, frequency and energetic data for all species are in the supplementary material

The Nb 4s and 4p and C 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are frozen closed; preliminary CASSCF calculations with a large active space then identified which further orbitals to close (doubly occupied in all configurations) or discard (unoccupied in all configurations), leaving the lowest 9a1, 2a2, 5b1, 5b2 closed and the next 4a1, 1a2, 2b1, 3b2 active — 9 electrons (8 for the cation) in 10 orbitals, 7000 CSFs. No excitations from the closed orbitals, but they were allowed to relax; MRCI references are all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients >= 0.05
multiplicities_studied: 1,2,3,4 — neutral: doublets and quartets at MRCI (all states up to the octet optimized); cation: singlets and triplets at MRCI (up to septet)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2B2 (B3LYP/srsc global minimum, a triply bridging structure). Unlike Nb3N2, Nb3C2 has low-energy doubly AND triply bound structures. At B3LYP the ground-state assignment is ambiguous — four states lie within 0.55 eV, two of them transition states; the two lowest excited states are 3B1 at 0.40 eV and 1B1 at 0.51 eV, both triply bridging. At CASSCF and MRCI+Q the assignment is unambiguous: the next lowest states are 3B2 at 0.62 eV and 1B2 at 0.63 eV, both doubly bridging, and the lowest triply bridging states are 5A1 at 1.51 eV and 3B1 at 1.59 eV (CASSCF). A triply bridging 2A1 search located a transition state with one short and two long Nb-Nb bonds, separated from the 2B2 state by only 1e-5 hartree, indicating Jahn-Teller components of a distorted D3h structure. Ionization potentials (eV, srsc on Nb / cc-pVDZ on C) vs experiment 5.04 (their Ref. 11): MRCI (TB) 2A1 -> 1A1 4.56, MRCI+Q 4.69; MRCI (DB) 2A1 -> 3A2 4.55, MRCI+Q 5.07; B3LYP (TB) 2B2 -> 1A1 5.13; B3LYP (DB) 2B2 -> 1A1 5.93 and 2B2 -> 3A2 5.75
Other: Main chemical conclusion for this cluster: a higher-energy isomer of Nb3C2 may have an electronic transition in the same spectral vicinity as the lowest-energy isomer, which matters for interpreting the observed spectrum (the Nb3C2 spectrum has much richer vibronic structure than Nb3N2). The DB/TB isomer barrier lies between 0.05 and 0.10 eV. As for Nb3N2, DFT electronic configurations agree universally with the MRCI leading configurations, but those leading configurations contribute no more than 70% of the total wave function. One MRCI+Q IP agreeing with experiment is described by the authors as 'fortuitously close'

Earlier studies used an active space of the Br 4p and I 5p shells only — (10 electrons, 6 orbitals) — or that plus the Br 4d shell — (10,11); the authors note those give good agreement with experiment but argue the iodine 5d orbitals deserve inclusion, giving more symmetric active spaces. Authors' caveat: a balanced description at the dissociation limit would require non-truncated p and d shells in the CAS; because the target here is vertical transitions at and around the ground-state equilibrium geometry, the CAS was optimised for that region instead

Other: Excited-state properties of atmospheric mercury compounds were essentially unknown before this work, in contrast to the interhalogens; the motivation is characterising photolysis channels for HgBr2 and related species (HgBr, HgBrOH, HgBrOBr, HgCl2, HgBrNO2). The present MS-CASPT2 VEEs sit systematically ~0.5-0.8 eV above the older POL(1) CI values and agree much better with the measured band positions (5.39/5.54 and 6.26/6.36 eV). Experiment does not settle the gas-phase R(HgBr): 2.41 A (Akishin and Spiridonov, used by Wadt) versus 2.374 A (Hargittai review, best estimate from thermal averages). Prior CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVXZ-PP work by Balabanov and Peterson on HgCl2, HgBr2 and HgBrCl explored basis set, SOC, scalar-relativistic and core-valence correlation effects and confirmed linear structures for all the covalent mercury halides

compound_name: Series of six Fe(II) thermal spin-crossover complexes with mono-, bi- and tridentate ligands: [Fe(mtz)6]2+ and [Fe(iso)6]2+ (monodentate); Fe(phen)2(NCS)2, [Fe(pic)3]2+ and [Fe(bpy)3]2+ (bidentate); [Fe(terpy)2]2+ (tridentate)
ligand_set: mtz = 1-methyltetrazole and iso = isoxazole (monodentate, FeN6); phen = 1,10-phenanthroline with 2 NCS-; pic = 2-picolylamine; bpy = 2,2'-bipyridine; terpy = 2,2':6',2''-terpyridine — all giving an FeN6 first coordination sphere
geometry_source: DFT-optimized geometries (B3LYP taken as reference, PBE0 also tested) for the LS and HS states; one-dimensional CASPT2 potential energy surfaces built by interpolating between the HS- and LS-optimized geometries along the reaction coordinate
method: CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0.25 a.u., standard zeroth-order Hamiltonian; larger IPEA also compared) on CASSCF references, combined with DFT (B3LYP, PBE0) for geometries, normal modes and zero-point/vibrational entropy contributions
basis_set: relativistic ANO-type atomic natural orbital basis sets: (7s,6p,5d,4f,3g,2h) for Fe; (4s,3p,1d) for the N atoms bonded to Fe; (3s,2p) for the remaining N, O and C; (4s,3p) for S; (2s) for H
relativistic_treatment: atomic natural orbital basis sets specifically designed to include relativistic effects
active_space_orbital_description: ten electrons in 12 orbitals: the five Fe 3d orbitals, two eg-like sigma-bonding ligand orbitals, and a second set of diffuse Fe 3d orbitals (double shell) to account for the large 3d-shell electron correlation
active_space_protocol: (10,12) used for both the LS and HS CASSCF wave functions of every complex — five Fe 3d + two eg-like sigma-bonding ligand orbitals + a second diffuse Fe 3d shell. The composition is chosen to describe both the Fe d-states and ligand-to-metal charge transfer effects, with the double shell included specifically for 3d radial correlation; the same space was used in the authors' previous studies. CASPT2 then correlates all electrons except the deep core (1s2 for N and C; 1s2,2s2,2p6 for Fe and S). The authors note in closing that the size of the active space is the limiting problem for larger SCO systems and that a restricted active space (RAS) reference would be the way to go beyond this complete-active-space approach
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: low-spin singlet (1A1g, Fe(II) d6) with the high-spin quintet as the thermally accessible excited state. HS-LS electronic energy differences (cm-1) by method — PBE0 / B3LYP / CASPT2 / experiment: [Fe(mtz)6]2+ -3333 / -1822 / 1051 / 120; [Fe(iso)6]2+ -3942 / -2336 / 1062 / n.a.; Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 -4089 / -2551 / 1362 / 719; [Fe(pic)3]2+ -3864 / -2157 / 1320 / 744; [Fe(bpy)3]2+ -726 / 830 / 5807 / ~6000; [Fe(terpy)2]2+ -785 / 713 / 7919 / n.a. Both DFT functionals give the WRONG SIGN (negative, i.e. HS below LS) for most complexes, whereas CASPT2 gives the right order for all of them
Other: Thermodynamics and transition temperatures. Computed Delta_S_HL(T1/2) (J K-1 mol-1), Delta_H_HL (cm-1), experimental Delta_H_HL, computed T1/2 (K) and experimental T1/2: [Fe(mtz)6]2+ 29 / 69 / 120 / 28 / 78 (and 63); [Fe(iso)6]2+ 35 / 149 / - / 41 / 91 (site A); Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 55 / 568 / 719 / 136 / 176; [Fe(pic)3]2+ 51 / 349 / 744 / 82 / 114-121; [Fe(bpy)3]2+ 84 / 5138 / ~6000 / 727 / >450; [Fe(terpy)2]2+ 93 / 7097 / - / 911 / -. The recommended recipe is: compute the HS-LS energy difference with CASPT2 and add DFT vibrational corrections. Zero-point energy corrections (cm-1): -913 for [Fe(iso)6]2+, -794 for Fe(phen)2(NCS)2, -971 for [Fe(pic)3]2+, -669 for [Fe(bpy)3]2+, -822 for [Fe(terpy)2]2+; these vary only ~100 cm-1 with functional or basis set, and the largest contribution comes from the lowest vibrational modes since high-frequency ligand modes are similar in HS and LS. A low-frequency entropy approximation Delta_S_vib = pR ln(nu_LS/nu_HS) using modes below 600 cm-1 gives astonishing agreement for Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 (49 lowest modes: 36.7 J K-1 mol-1 vibrational, 50.1 total vs 49 experimental) and [Fe(pic)3]2+ (36 modes: 59.0 vs 59.5 experimental), but the authors judge this accidental because it fails badly for the other systems and the nu_LS/nu_HS ratio depends strongly on how many modes are included. B3LYP geometries were chosen over the slightly better PBE0 ones because the interpolated CASPT2 optimal Fe-N distance is practically identical for both, frequencies are nearly identical, and B3LYP energetics are slightly better; results are quantitatively very similar with PBE0 throughout. The approach is described by the authors as not quantitative enough for accurate T1/2 but able to reasonably estimate the transition temperature
reference_short: Rudavskyi, Sousa, de Graaf, Havenith, Broer, J. Chem. Phys. 140, 184318 (2014)

compound_name: SH and SD radicals (mercapto radical and its deuterated isotopologue) — ultraviolet photodissociation from vibrationally excited X 2Pi levels via the A 2Sigma+ repulsive wall
geometry_source: ab initio potential energy curves computed as a function of internuclear distance; the 1 2Sigma- and 2 2Pi potentials are adapted from their Ref. 17
method: CASSCF followed by MRSDCI (multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction) including the Davidson correction; electronic transition dipole moments and photodissociation cross sections computed from these
active_space_orbital_description: active space consists of three sigma orbitals, one pi_x orbital and one pi_y orbital (five orbitals); the three lowest sigma orbitals and the first pi_x and pi_y orbitals were kept doubly occupied. The paper does not state the number of active electrons
active_space_protocol: single active space throughout, no build-up: molecular orbitals from a CASSCF in which the three lowest sigma orbitals and the first pi_x and pi_y orbitals are kept doubly occupied, with three sigma, one pi_x and one pi_y orbital active; MRSDCI with the Davidson correction on top
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 2Pi. The paper reports potential energy curves, A 2Sigma+ <- X 2Pi and 2Delta <- X 2Pi electronic transition dipole moments and photodissociation cross sections rather than tabulated excitation energies, so no state energies in eV are recorded here. Photodissociation of SH (X 2Pi, v'' = 2-7) and SD (X 2Pi, v'' = 3-7) was studied at 288 and 291 nm
Other: Both experiment (velocity map imaging of the S(1D2) product angular and speed distributions) and the CASSCF-MRSDCI/aug-cc-pV5Z cross sections show that SH/SD photodissociation from X 2Pi (v'' <= 7) proceeds via the repulsive wall of the A 2Sigma+ state. The S(1D2) angular distributions indicate the dissociation approaches the sudden recoil limit of the A 2Sigma+ state, yielding strongly polarized fragments. Figure 1 illustrates the mechanism for SD (X 2Pi, v''=3) at 288 nm, showing the ab initio potentials, the A 2Sigma+ <- X 2Pi transition dipole moment mu_x (e*a0), the bound X 2Pi (v''=3) wave function and the continuum A 2Sigma+ wave function
reference_short: Janssen, Wu, Radenovic, van Roij, Garcia, Parker, J. Chem. Phys. 126, 094304 (2007)

compound_name: linear SiC3H- anion (and the neutral l-SiC3H radical) — silicon-carbon chain of astrochemical interest
point_group: C-infinity-v (linear; states labelled 1Sigma+, 1Pi, 1Delta, 1Sigma-, 3Sigma+, 3Pi, 3Delta, 3Sigma- for the anion and 2Pi, 2Sigma+, 2Delta, 2Sigma-, 4Sigma+, 4Delta, 4Sigma-, 4Pi for the neutral)
geometry_source: optimized in this work; CASSCF was also used to search for isomers because static correlation can matter for low-stability carbon-chain isomers
method: CASSCF and CASSCF/MRCI (internally contracted multireference CI) for vertical excitation energies and dipole moments; RCCSD(T) and RCCSD(T)-F12 for ground-state properties, with an RCCSD(T)-F12 anharmonic force field via second-order perturbation theory (FIT-ESPEC code)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF and MRCI vertical excitation energies and electric properties; aug-cc-pV5Z also used
active_space_orbital_description: all the pi-valence electrons were correlated; the core orbitals and the sigma-valence orbitals were considered doubly occupied in all configurations and were optimized. For the electric-property CASSCF calculations on the SiCnH series with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 carbon atoms, respectively 8, 10, 12, 14 and 19 orbitals were kept doubly occupied in all configurations and optimized during the CASSCF procedure. The paper does not state the active space as an explicit (nel,norb) pair
active_space_protocol: single pi-valence active space, no build-up sequence: all pi-valence electrons active, with core and sigma-valence orbitals doubly occupied but variationally optimized. The number of doubly-occupied (inactive) orbitals is specified per chain length rather than the active space itself — 8, 10, 12, 14 and 19 for SiCnH with n = 1-5 carbons. CASSCF was preferred over RCCSD(T) for the one-electron properties because coupled-cluster wave functions do not satisfy the Hellmann-Feynman theorem in the usual sense, and because for carbon chains with high densities of electronic states near the ground state, expectation values from multiconfigurational methods are 'safer' than monoreferential ones (first observed for C4H)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1Sigma+ for l-SiC3H- (X 2Pi for the neutral l-SiC3H). Vertical excitation energies (eV) with aug-cc-pVTZ, CASSCF then MRCI. Anion l-SiC3H-: 1Sigma+ 0.0 / 0.0 (E = -493.205588 a.u. at CASSCF, -403.597248 a.u. at MRCI as printed); 1Pi 3.03 / 3.09; 1Delta 4.11 / 3.29; 1Sigma- 3.47 / 3.22; 3Sigma+ 2.57 / 2.48; 3Pi 2.65 / 3.10; 3Delta 2.98 / 2.66; 3Sigma- 3.43 / 2.85. Neutral l-SiC3H: X 2Pi 0.0 / 0.0 (E = -403.139215 / -403.509450 a.u.); 2Sigma+ 2.45 / 2.01; 2Delta 5.99 / 5.66; 2Sigma- 5.42 / 5.43; 4Sigma+ 3.82 / 3.43; 4Delta 4.78 / 3.82; 4Sigma- 5.34 / 4.19; 4Pi 2.77 / 2.21. Dominant configurations are given for every state, e.g. the anion ground state is (11sigma)2(2pi)4(3pi)4 and the neutral ground state (11sigma)2(2pi)4(3pi)3
Other: Astrochemical detection motivation: electron affinities and dipole moments of linear CnSi and SiCnH chains are computed to assess detection probability and anion formation viability. Anions with singlet electronic ground states (SiCH-, SiC3H-, SiC5H-) display significant electron affinities, but their dipole moments — which grow with molecular size — are lower for singlets than for triplets; SiCnH- anions show unexpectedly large dipoles when the electronic ground state is a triplet. Species covered in the comparison are the neutrals SiC (X 3Pi), SiC2 (X 1A1), SiC3 (X 3Sigma-), SiC4 (X 1Sigma+), SiC5 (X 3Sigma-), SiCH (X 2Pi), SiC2H, SiC3H, SiC4H and their anions; almost all are linear except SiC2. An electron affinity of 2.70 eV is obtained with RCCSD(T)-F12A. For l-SiC3H- and l-SiC3D- the absence of previous studies prevents rigorous accuracy conclusions
reference_short: Theoretical characterization of the SiC3H- anion, J. Chem. Phys. 133, 184107 (2010)

compound_name: Br2 (bromine molecule) — nonadiabatic transitions among the lower Omega = 1u states and photodissociation
geometry_source: potential energy surface scan performed in this work at CASSCF/aug-cc-pVTZ, giving adiabatic potential curves
method: CASSCF with the time-independent Schrodinger equation for nonadiabatic transitions; time-dependent quantum dynamical method (program of Balint-Kurti et al. 1993) for the photodissociation cross sections
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF potential energy scan; a standard 6-31+G(d,p) basis also used in the CASSCF procedure
active_space_orbital_description: 10 electrons distributed over 8 molecular orbitals: {Br-Br*, x(Br), x*(Br), y(Br), y*(Br), 2 n(Br), Br-Br} — i.e. the Br-Br sigma bonding/antibonding pair, the x and y bonding/antibonding pairs and two bromine lone-pair orbitals
active_space_protocol: (10,8) used throughout, with the orbital composition itemized explicitly; no build-up sequence is described
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1Sigma_g+. Spectroscopic constants, this work vs experiment (Huber and Herzberg 1979; Coxon 1973) — Re (A), De (kJ/mol), omega_e (cm-1), omega_e x_e (cm-1): X 1Sigma_g+ 2.304 / 188.53 / 320.7 / 1.24, experiment 2.280 / 190.17 / 325.3 / 1.08; A 3Pi_1u 2.758 / 22.57 / 144.8 / 2.85, experiment 2.690 / 24.77 / 153 / 2.7; B 3Pi_0+u 2.760 / 43.51 / 163.1 / 1.91, experiment 2.677 / 44.96 / 167.6 / 1.64. Agreement is described by the authors as reasonable
Other: Main result: from configuration analysis of the CASSCF wave functions, the nonadiabatic transition between the two 1u states is a NONCROSSING type, while that between a 1u state and B 3Pi_0+u is a CROSSING type. State correlations: A 3Pi_1u (1u) and 1Pi_u (1u) correlate to the ground-state Br+Br limit, whereas B 3Pi_0+u (0u+) correlates to the Br+Br* limit; a further repulsive 1u state correlating to Br+Br* is implicated in the proposed explanation for the non-limiting beta values observed for the Br+Br* product recoil velocity distributions (Cooper et al. 1998). Absorption cross sections for the ground and lower excited states in the photodissociation of Br2 are presented, along with numerical estimates of nonadiabatic transition probabilities, and the five highest occupied and five lowest unoccupied orbitals of Br2. TD-DFT excitation energies, main excitations and oscillator strengths are tabulated separately for comparison
reference_short: Abdel-Hafiez, Atteya, Medhat, Int. J. Phys. Sci. 5(7), 978-983 (2010)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand by aimdb; identified via OpenAlex title match (no DOI printed in the PDF text). compound_name: CH3I-O2 van der Waals complex — charge-transfer (CT) state relevant to cluster-enhanced X-O2 photochemistry (X = CH3I, C3H6, C6H12, Xe)
point_group: Cs (the CT state considered is of A'' symmetry, chosen so it is accessible by an allowed electric dipole transition from the ground state)
geometry_source: isomers of the complex located in this work; the isomer with the shortest I-to-O2-centre distance (Rm = 3.57 A) was selected for the vertical gap. The CT complex structure was then optimized at CASSCF(10,6), giving theta = 191.8 deg, phi = 60.7 deg, Rm = 2.63 A
method: CASSCF(10,6) for the CT state properties and geometry optimization, with a CASSCF(10,6)-MP2 single point on the optimized CT structure
basis_set: same basis sets as used for the structure and binding energy of the complex ground state (not itemized in the extracted text)
active_space_orbital_description: two doubly occupied nonbonding n_p orbitals of the iodine atom, two singly occupied antibonding pi orbitals of molecular oxygen, and a pair of doubly occupied bonding pi orbitals of molecular oxygen
active_space_protocol: (10,6) used for the CT state throughout, with the composition chosen to span the donor and acceptor manifolds of the charge-transfer transition — iodine lone pairs as the donor, and the O2 bonding and antibonding pi pairs as the acceptor. No build-up sequence is described
electronic_structure_description: Vertical energy gap between the ground state and the A'' charge-transfer state of the CH3I-O2 complex at its equilibrium geometry: Delta_E_vert = 5.81 eV (CASSCF(10,6)). After optimizing the CT state geometry at CASSCF(10,6), a CASSCF(10,6)-MP2 single point places that configuration 3.43 eV above the ground state of the complex

In all isomers the CH3I subunit points almost perpendicular to the O-O bond. The paper combines these CASSCF calculations for the ground and CT states of the complex with literature potential energy surface data

compound_name: HXeC2H (H-Xe-C(triple)C-H, xenon-inserted acetylene) and the parent acetylene HC2H — excited states underlying the linear and nonlinear optical (L&NLO) properties
geometry_source: excited states computed at the MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ optimized ground-state geometries; equilibrium structure of H-Xe-C(triple)C-H reported at MP2 and CCSD(T) levels (e.g. MP2/aug-cc-pVDZ R(CC) 1.249, R(CH) 1.078, R(XeC) 2.350, R(HXe) 1.750 A)
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 for the excited states (standard zeroth-order Hamiltonian, imaginary level shift 0.2 a.u. to avoid intruder states); transition dipole moments at CASSCF, excitation energies at CASPT2. Complete active space valence bond (CASVB) used for the bonding analysis; MP2 and CCSD(T) for the L&NLO properties themselves
software: MOLCAS 6.0 for CASSCF/CASPT2; VB2000 for CASVB; GAUSSIAN 98 and DALTON also used
basis_set: relativistic ANO-RCC type basis sets contracted to Xe [7s6p4d2f1g] / C [4s3p2d1f] / H [3s2p1d] for the CASSCF/CASPT2; aug-cc-pVnZ (n = 2-5) series for the property calculations, with a small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Xe in some MP2 work
relativistic_treatment: relativistic ANO-RCC basis sets for the CASSCF/CASPT2; small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Xe in the MP2 property calculations
active_space_orbital_description: 3 sigma, 2 pi, 3 sigma* and 2 pi* valence orbitals plus four Rydberg orbitals (one s and three p)
active_space_protocol: Different active spaces were tested to assure the reliability of the results; the final calculations use CASSCF(10,14) comprising 3 sigma, 2 pi, 3 sigma*, 2 pi* valence orbitals plus four Rydberg orbitals (one s, three p). The Rydberg orbitals matter here because the lowest excited state of HXeC2H involves a sigma(Xe-H)* antibonding orbital with diffuse Rydberg-like s character. Separately, CASSCF calculations on the ground states of all studied molecules confirmed that a single electronic configuration dominates the wave function by at least 87%, justifying the single-reference MP2/CCSD(T) treatment of the L&NLO properties
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet, dominated by a single configuration (>= 87% in all studied molecules). Key CASPT2 excitation energies for HXeC2H at the ground-state geometry: lowest singlet excited state of pi-sigma* type at 5.32 eV, involving the sigma(Xe-H)* antibonding orbital with diffuse Rydberg-like s character; second singlet excited state of sigma-sigma* character at 6.45 eV. By contrast, in acetylene the low-lying pi-sigma* state (sigma mainly the antibonding CC orbital) is expected above 9.0 eV. Acetylene excitation energies compare favourably with other experimental and theoretical values
Other: Interpretation via a sum-over-states (SOS) perturbative approach connecting excited-state structure to the L&NLO properties. Two striking effects of Xe insertion: (1) it produces much longer/weaker sigma bonds and therefore much lower-energy sigma,sigma*-involving excited states (9.0+ eV in HC2H down to 5.32 eV in HXeC2H); (2) the low-lying valence pi-pi* states are NOT strongly perturbed by Xe insertion and therefore cannot be responsible for the change in NLO property values. The derivatives of interest were synthesized in a Xe matrix, so the local-field (LF) effect of the Xe environment on the properties of HXeC2H was also computed and found significant for some properties. Bonding analysed with CASVB, whose nonorthogonal VB orbitals allow maximum localization without loss of accuracy relative to CASSCF. Effect of Xe core electrons tested by correlating 18 versus 26 electrons explicitly, giving practically the same properties. compound_name: O2-O2 van der Waals complex — triplet states of O2(X 3Sigma_g-) with O2(X 3Sigma_g-, a 1Delta_g, b 1Sigma_g+); collision-induced absorption
point_group: benchmarks at high-symmetry geometries (H-shaped: theta_A = theta_B = pi/2, phi = 0); full surfaces computed at general low-symmetry geometries
geometry_source: global potential energy and dipole moment surfaces computed as functions of the intermolecular separation R and the three angles; the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 corresponds to the minimum of the triplet O2(X)-O2(X) potential
method: explicitly correlated multireference configuration interaction with Davidson size-consistency correction (F12-MRCI+Q) for the potentials; dipole surfaces at both MRCI and CASSCF; F12-CASPT2 also used for benchmarks. Potentials and dipole surfaces transformed to a diabatic basis with a multiple-property-based diabatization algorithm
basis_set: augmented correlation-consistent aug-cc-pVnZ (n = D, T, Q) with the corresponding standardized auxiliary basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: three nested spaces: sCAS = four electrons in the four pi* orbitals; mCAS = 12 electrons in the pi shell; lCAS = 16 electrons in the p shell. The orbital counts for mCAS and lCAS are not given numerically
active_space_protocol: Three explicitly defined choices, used as a convergence ladder: (1) sCAS — four electrons in the four pi* orbitals, the MINIMAL active space that gives a zeroth-order description of all states of interest, i.e. all states arising from the (pi)4(pi*)2 configuration of the O2 monomers; (2) mCAS — 12 electrons in the pi shell, which additionally captures the static correlation of the pi electrons, important for O2 because of the well-known Hartree-Fock instability associated with artificial breaking of inversion symmetry; (3) lCAS — 16 electrons in the p shell. lCAS is prohibitively expensive at low-symmetry geometries, so the full potential energy and dipole moment surfaces could NOT be computed with it; mCAS is the production space for the surfaces, with lCAS used only for benchmarks at high-symmetry geometries. Benchmarking shows the interaction energy converges reasonably smoothly, albeit slowly, with active space and basis set, so accurate energies are obtainable from affordable MRCI; the transition dipole moment behaves quite differently and depends strongly on the level of theory. Prior systematic work (their Ref. 18) comparing MRCI, CASPT2 and ACPF against CCSD(T) for the high-spin quintet suggests treating MRCI and CASPT2 as upper and lower limits to the potential respectively, with CASPT2 the more reliable; MRCI is nevertheless used here because it gives straightforward access to the transition properties needed for the dipole surface and the diabatization
multiplicities_studied: 3 (seven triplet states of the dimer); monomer states X 3Sigma_g-, a 1Delta_g, b 1Sigma_g+
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet O2(X 3Sigma_g-)-O2(X 3Sigma_g-). Seven triplet states of the dimer are treated. The monomer transitions underlying the collision-induced bands are X 3Sigma_g- -> a 1Delta_g at 7883 cm-1 and X 3Sigma_g- -> b 1Sigma_g+ at 13 122 cm-1. Interaction energies for the seven triplet states are tabulated at the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 using F12-MRCI+Q with all three active spaces and with mCAS F12-CASPT2, but the individual values are not reproduced here
Other: For the triplet ground state of the complex the potential energy surface agrees reasonably with previous calculations, while global EXCITED state potentials are reported here for the first time. Central caveat: the transition dipole moment surfaces depend strongly on the level of theory at which they are computed, as confirmed by the high-symmetry benchmarks, so the authors conclude that ab initio calculations of collision-induced absorption spectra cannot become quantitatively predictive until more accurate transition dipoles are available. The paper also derives the angular expansion of the surfaces and the symmetry constraints on the expansion coefficients, gives working equations for obtaining them by numerical integration over angles, and presents an interpolation scheme with exponential extrapolation to short and large separations for the R dependence

compound_name: furan (C4H4O) — photoionization from the ground and excited electronic states, at planar and bent geometries
point_group: C2v for the ground-state (planar) geometry; a bent geometry is also treated
geometry_source: ground-state (planar, C2v) geometry and a bent geometry; the same active space was selected for both
method: CASSCF with NEVPT2 (partially contracted, PC(2) level) corrections for residual dynamical correlation, used to build Dyson orbitals; TDDFT and ADC(2) also used for comparison; continuum dipole matrix elements from a B-spline static-exchange DFT scattering treatment
software: MOLPRO for the HF, CASSCF and NEVPT2 calculations (plus in-house modules); Turbomole for TDDFT and ADC(2)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ (polarization and diffuse functions) for O, C and H; Dyson orbitals projected onto a B-spline basis
active_space_orbital_description: six valence electrons distributed among nine orbitals: one a1, four b1, one b2 and three a2 — comprising 3 occupied (1b1-2b1, 1a2) and 6 virtual (1a1, 3b1-4b1, 7b2, 2a2-3a2)
active_space_protocol: (6,9) used throughout, itemized by irrep (one a1, four b1, one b2, three a2; 3 occupied + 6 virtual), and deliberately kept IDENTICAL for the bent geometry so that planar and bent results are directly comparable. No build-up sequence. Both excitation and ionization energies are then corrected for residual dynamical correlation via partially contracted PC(2)-NEVPT2. For the Dyson orbitals, the overlap between CASSCF wave functions separately optimized for the neutral molecule and for the ion is evaluated, with the N-electron wave function expanded in minors
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet in C2v. The valence-shell molecular orbital sequence of ground-state furan is (4a1)2(5a1)2(3b2)2(4b2)2(6a1)2(7a1)2(1b1)2... The paper's quantitative outputs are photoionization cross sections and asymmetry parameters computed from Dyson orbitals rather than a table of vertical excitation energies, so no eV state energies are transcribed here. Ionization energies calculated with the NEVPT2 approach are described as in excellent agreement (with experiment/previous work)
Other: Methodological point: Dyson orbitals are computed at three levels — TDDFT, ADC(2) and CASSCF — and then projected onto a B-spline basis, which decouples the Dyson orbital calculation from that of the continuum dipole matrix elements and lets different electronic structure methods be used interchangeably. The B-spline static-exchange DFT scattering procedure gives a quantitative description of dynamical photoionization observables and generally agrees excellently with experiment. Photoionization from excited electronic states, as well as from the ground state, is treated — relevant to time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
