compound_name: NO + O2 scattering system — multistate electronic quenching of NO A 2Sigma+ by O2, nonadiabatic pathways
point_group: C1 used for the potential energy surfaces in general orientations (unless specified otherwise); Jacobi coordinates used throughout
geometry_source: potential energy surfaces computed in this work over Jacobi coordinates; asymptotic state ordering evaluated at R = 15 A with fixed monomer bond lengths (O2 1.0634 A)
method: state-averaged CASSCF (SA(20)-CASSCF) for the potential energy surfaces, chosen because it models nonadiabatic effects and multiconfigurational character accurately; XMS-CASPT2 with IPEA level shift 0.25 for dynamic correlation; a spline/switched (SW-)CASSCF variant also used
basis_set: t-aug-cc-pVTZ for the SA-CASSCF(19,13) surfaces; t-aug-cc-pVDZ for the XMS-CASPT2(11,9) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: NO and O2 2sigma*, 3sigma, pi_x, pi_y, pi*_x, pi*_y orbitals plus the NO 4sigma orbital, giving CAS(19,13). The reduced space contains only the pi and pi* orbitals together with the NO 4sigma orbital, giving (11,9)
active_space_protocol: (19,13) — NO and O2 2sigma*, 3sigma, pi_x, pi_y, pi*_x, pi*_y plus NO 4sigma — used for the CASSCF potential energy surfaces, with a schematic of the orbital energetic ordering at asymptotic separation given in the paper. (11,9) — only the pi and pi* orbitals plus NO 4sigma — used for the XMS-CASPT2 calculations purely because the full space is too expensive at the CASPT2 level. The number of states is coupled to the active-space choice: because the O2 a 1Delta_g and b 1Sigma_g+ states lie BELOW the NO A 2Sigma+ state, the NO X 2Pi degeneracy couples with the O2 X, a and b states, producing eight doublet and two quartet surfaces below NO A 2Sigma+ + O2 X 3Sigma_g-. The active-space/number-of-states combination was therefore fixed for the spin-doublet states first, giving a minimum of 9 spin-doublet states required, and the production runs used a 20-state average. An IPEA level shift of 0.25 was applied to compensate the usual CASPT2 bias
multiplicities_studied: 2,4 — 2 and 4 (eight doublet and two quartet surfaces below the entrance channel)
nroots_per_mult: SA(20)-CASSCF (20-state average); minimum of 9 spin-doublet states required by the state-ordering analysis
electronic_structure_description: Asymptotic state ordering (R = 15 A, fixed bond lengths), energies in eV, SW-CASSCF then XMS-CASPT2, labelled by NO state / O2 state: A 2Sigma+ / b 1Sigma_g+ 5.569 (CASSCF); X 2Pi / A 3Sigma_u 5.267 / 6.670; X 2Pi / A' 3Delta_u 5.128 / 6.522; A 2Sigma+ / a 1Delta_g 5.095 / 5.582; X 2Pi / c 1Sigma_u- 4.978 / 6.313. Computed with SA(20)-CASSCF(19,13)/t-aug-cc-pVTZ and XMS-CASPT2(11,9)/t-aug-cc-pVDZ
Other: The paper examines how dynamic correlation affects the accessibility and relaxation of the quenching event — comparing SW-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 shows dynamic correlation raises the X 2Pi-based channels by roughly 1.3-1.4 eV while affecting the A 2Sigma+/a 1Delta_g channel much less (5.095 -> 5.582 eV), i.e. it substantially reorders the quenching channels. O2 c 1Sigma_u- was suggested by Few et al. (their Ref. 9) as a potential quenching product, which is why the state selection was built around the spin-doublet manifold. Triply augmented Dunning basis sets were chosen as optimized for modelling electronic correlation

compound_name: Model phenylalanine protein chains: NAPA B (N-acetylphenylalaninylamide), Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A, and Ac-Gln-Phe-NH2 C — singlet pipi* and npi* excited states
geometry_source: conformers of the model peptide chains (the NAPA B conformer corresponds to a specific folded structure, see their Fig. 1 and Ref. 6)
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 with RASSCF, GASSCF and ORMAS (occupation-restricted multiple active space) as determinant-reduction alternatives beyond the CASSCF limit; RASPT2 and Q+DDCI (difference-dedicated CI) for dynamic correlation; benchmarked against CC2
software: MOLCAS for RASSCF/GASSCF (with DoLo orbital localization and Cholesky decomposition, threshold 1e-8 a.u.); GAMESS for ORMAS (with Pipek-Mezey localization)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ throughout; cc-pVTZ also tested for NAPA B (CASSCF/CASPT2, Q+DDCI and CC2) but the effects were weak at very high computational cost, so cc-pVDZ was retained for the other systems
active_space_orbital_description: all the pi and pi* orbitals of the phenyl and of the carbonyl groups, plus the nitrogen and oxygen lone pairs (the highest in energy, i.e. the pure-p lone pair). This is what is required to describe the low-lying local excitations: pi -> pi* centred on the phenyl group and n -> pi*(CO) centred on the peptide bonds
active_space_protocol: Active space built from the states that must be described — all phenyl and carbonyl pi/pi* orbitals plus the pure-p N and O lone pairs — and it then scales with the number of peptide bonds: CAS(18,14) for NAPA B (4 008 004 determinants), CAS(24,18) for Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A with one more peptide bond (344 622 096 determinants, 'cumbersome but still tractable'), and CAS(30,22) for Ac-Gln-Phe-NH2 C with two more (29 085 255 936 determinants, UNFEASIBLE). Beyond the CASSCF limit three determinant-reduction strategies are benchmarked: (i) RASSCF with subspaces (18,n,n; 9,0,5), (24,n,n; 12,0,6) and (30,n,n; 15,0,7) for the three systems — note RAS2 is empty, all orbitals sit in RAS1/RAS3 — giving for n = 3/4/5 respectively 36 916 (0.9%) / 243 376 (6.1%) / 905 128 (22.6%) determinants for NAPA B, 158 669 (0.05%) / 1 787 219 (0.5%) / 11 577 923 (3.4%) for Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A, and 510 546 (0.002%) / 8 812 371 (0.03%) / 89 200 497 (0.3%) for Ac-Gln-Phe-NH2 C; (ii) GASSCF/ORMAS partitioning into (6,6)/(6,4) blocks — (6,6)/(6,4)/(6,4) for NAPA B (220 192 det, 5.5%), with one extra (6,4) block per additional peptide bond, giving 5 510 848 (1.6%) and 140 843 008 (0.5%) for the larger two. Percentages are relative to the full CASSCF determinant count. Orbital localization (DoLo or Pipek-Mezey) is required because orbitals must be assigned to distinct subspaces. In RASSCF the orbitals with notably varying occupation numbers must be placed in RAS2
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet. The low-lying excited states are local excitations: singlet pi -> pi* centred on the phenyl group and singlet n -> pi*(CO) centred on the peptide bonds (n being N or O pure-p lone pairs). Vertical excitation energies for Ac-Gly-Phe-NH2 A around 5.6-6.1 eV are tabulated across the different optimized-MO sets (RASSCF with n = 3, 4, 5; GASSCF MOs; CASSCF MOs) at the RASPT2, CASPT2 and Q+DDCI levels — e.g. CAS(12,8)-based values of 5.72, 5.61, 5.76, 5.67, 5.68 eV for one state across the five MO sets, and rows at 5.82/5.82/5.84/5.83/5.82 and 6.05/6.02/6.05/6.03/6.02 eV, with CAS1/CAS2 entries at 5.89/5.77/5.92/5.85/5.83 eV. The paper's conclusion is that these alternative schemes reproduce both the nature and the excitation energies of the singlet pipi* and npi* states without loss of accuracy relative to full CASSCF
Other: The point of the paper is active-space scaling: it quantifies how far the determinant count can be cut (to 0.002%-23% of full CASSCF) while preserving excited-state accuracy, which is exactly the regime where CASSCF becomes unaffordable for biomolecular chromophores. CC2 is assessed as an alternative for such large systems. Dynamic electron correlation is noted to be a local effect, motivating the localized-orbital subspace partitioning. compound_name: TTF+ — tetrathiafulvalene monoradical cation, UV/Vis absorption spectrum
point_group: D2h (states labelled 1 2B1u, 2 2B1u, 2 2B2u, 4 2B2u, 5 2B2u, 8 2B1u; singly occupied active b3u orbital)
geometry_source: optimized with PBE0 (structure provided in the supplementary material; their Ref. 71)
method: MC-RPA (multiconfigurational random phase approximation, i.e. CASSCF linear response) compared with SA-CASSCF and SS-NEVPT2; AO-driven integral-direct implementation with natural transition orbitals for analysis
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(13,10) includes all pi orbitals and electrons (13 860 CSFs), well suited to describe the delocalization of the unpaired electron in the pi system; the singly occupied active orbital is of b3u symmetry. The augmented CAS(21,14) additionally contains four nonbonding orbitals at the sulfur atoms
active_space_protocol: CAS(13,10) — all pi orbitals and electrons, 13 860 CSFs — used for all multireference calculations. Its sufficiency was TESTED by running an augmented SA-CASSCF with CAS(21,14) that adds the four sulfur nonbonding orbitals, which could in principle give n -> pi* excitations: that test showed the low-energy n -> pi* excitations are all dipole-forbidden, so CAS(13,10) suffices to describe every characteristic electronic transition of TTF+. A second reason for excluding the sulfur nonbonding orbitals is convergence trouble in the SS-CASSCF energy minimization preceding MC-RPA; consistently, in the ground-state SS-CASSCF the four largest natural occupation numbers are nearly 2.0 because those orbitals take no part in the delocalization of the electron hole. In the SA-CASSCF the MOs were optimized for an average of the 30 lowest states
nroots_per_mult: 30 (SA-CASSCF orbitals averaged over the 30 lowest states)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: doublet radical cation with a singly occupied b3u orbital. The experimental spectrum (recorded in acetonitrile, their Ref. 77) shows three shouldered peaks between 2.0 and 4.0 eV. All three multireference treatments (MC-RPA, SA-CASSCF, NEVPT2) reproduce three characteristic peaks — 1 2B1u, 2 2B1u and 2 2B2u — falling near that window, allowing a tentative assignment; the singly occupied b3u orbital acts as electron donor or acceptor in all three low-energy transitions. For these three transitions both MC-RPA and NEVPT2 give excitation energies much LOWER than SA-CASSCF, as they do for the 5 2B2u NEVPT2 transition corresponding to the 4 2B2u MC-RPA one. The 8 2B1u SA-CASSCF transition is lowered by 1.39 eV (MC-RPA) and 1.99 eV (NEVPT2). In general MC-RPA and NEVPT2 lie below SA-CASSCF because of orbital relaxation and dynamic correlation respectively, and both agree better with experiment
Other: Method caveats stated by the authors: neither MC-RPA nor NEVPT2 is optimal for describing many excited states and their spectral properties — MC-RPA misses a large fraction of the dynamic correlation not captured by the CSFs in the active space, while NEVPT2 describes orbital relaxation only in a limited sense through redundancies. The experiment/theory comparison is only a rough estimate because TTF+ was measured in acetonitrile, a polar solvent that stabilizes the positive charge, while the calculations are in vacuum. The largest COSX grid was needed to avoid trailing convergence issues associated with the large high-angular-momentum diffuse basis

compound_name: Octahedrally coordinated Ni(II) complex with triazole ligands (231 atoms) — absorption and ECD spectra
geometry_source: structure from Schweinfurth et al. (their Ref. 71)
method: CASSCF linear response (MC-RPA) in an efficient AO-driven implementation, used to simulate absorption and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) spectra of a 231-atom complex
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(2,2) containing the Ni dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals, in accordance with the ligand-field picture for octahedral Ni(II) d8 complexes — i.e. the two eg-derived orbitals holding the two unpaired electrons. The larger CAS(8,5) contains all five d orbitals and eight d electrons
active_space_protocol: The paper deliberately uses a SMALLER space than previous work on this complex: a CAS(2,2) with a single CSF comprising the Ni dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals, following the ligand-field picture for octahedral Ni(II) d8, i.e. a restricted open-shell high-spin wave function. The full d-shell alternative, CAS(8,5) with all d orbitals and electrons, was tried for the triplet ground state but gave three d orbitals (dxy, dyz, dxz) with natural occupation numbers of exactly 2.0 and converged slowly — those orbitals are doubly occupied and contribute no static correlation in this ligand field. For that reason the CASSCF response calculations are shown only for the CAS(2,2) restricted open-shell high-spin wave function. This is a useful negative result: for an octahedral d8 ion the t2g set is inert and enlarging the CAS to the full d shell buys nothing but convergence trouble
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet — the energetically lowest spin state of this Ni(II) complex, as established by the CASSCF and NEVPT2 calculations of Schweinfurth et al. (Ref. 71) and Guo et al. (Ref. 17). Absorption and ECD spectra are simulated with CASSCF linear response; individual excitation energies are presented graphically rather than tabulated in the extracted text, so no eV values are recorded here
Other: This calculation is the paper's demonstration that the AO-driven CASSCF linear response implementation scales to genuinely large open-shell systems — 231 atoms with a def2-TZVPP basis — which is the practical claim of the method. Reported alongside the TTF+ benchmark (companion row -a)

compound_name: s-trans-1,3-butadiene — excited-state potential energy curves along the terminal twist coordinate
geometry_source: scan along a terminal twist coordinate with all other bonds and angles frozen at their S2 planar minimum values
method: SA-CASSCF compared with dynamically weighted CASSCF using a new dynamical-weight-with-spline (DWS) scheme; analytical gradients for DWS-CASSCF derived for the first time, enabling energy-conserving excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: 4 electrons in 4 orbitals (the butadiene pi system)
active_space_protocol: (4,4) held fixed; the paper's subject is the STATE-AVERAGING scheme rather than the orbital space. SA-4-CASSCF/6-31G* (four states in the average) exhibits energy discontinuities in ALL states at the point where S3 — which is included in the state averaging — crosses S4, which is not. This is the general pathology: discontinuities appear in SA-CASSCF potential energy surfaces whenever a state left out of the average crosses one that is included, and they break energy conservation in excited-state dynamics. The remedy demonstrated here is dynamical weighting with a spline, DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF, which mimics SA-CASSCF while smoothly removing the discontinuities due to unweighted state crossings. Practical guidance: when choosing how many states to state-average, the risk is not only the orbital active space but which states are omitted from the average along the coordinate of interest
nroots_per_mult: 4 for SA-4-CASSCF; DWS3-(4,6eV)-CASSCF uses a dynamical weight with an energy width parameter of 6 eV
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet (S0). States S0-S4 are followed along the terminal twist coordinate; the discontinuity arises at the S3/S4 intersection, with S3 included in and S4 excluded from the state averaging, and is visible even in S2. Absolute state energies are presented graphically rather than tabulated in the extracted text, so no eV values are recorded here
Other: Method contribution: a new dynamical weight with spline (DWS) scheme that reproduces SA-CASSCF behaviour while removing energy discontinuities from unweighted state crossings, plus the first derivation of analytical gradients for DWS-CASSCF and other dynamically weighted schemes. This enables energy-conserving excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics in cases where SA-CASSCF fails. Butadiene's terminal twist coordinate is used as the demonstration because SA-CASSCF discontinuities there are severe

active_space_orbital_description: all distributions of the 10 valence electrons among the 10 corresponding bonding, antibonding and nonbonding orbitals: sigma(SiH1), sigma(SiH2), sigma(SiN), pi(SiN), sigma(pN), 2pN, sigma*(SiH1), sigma*(SiH2), sigma*(SiN), pi*(SiN) — 7400 CSFs of 3A2 spin and spatial symmetry
active_space_protocol: (10,10) chosen as the full valence set of Si-H and Si-N bonding/antibonding orbitals plus the two nitrogen lone-pair-type orbitals, because the ion has two valence holes (one in the terminal in-plane 2p nitrogen orbital and one in the 2p pi orbital on nitrogen) so nondynamic correlation was expected to be essential; CSFs restricted to 3A2 symmetry
multiplicities_studied: 1,3 — 3 (ground state); singlet and triplet excited states surveyed for the electronic spectrum
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 3A2 in C2v — an open-shell triplet lying below the closed-shell singlet, with silicon retaining sp2 hybridization rather than pyramidalizing. ROHF occupancy (1a1)2(2a1)2(3a1)2(1b2)2(4a1)2(5a1)2(6a1)2(2b2)2(2b1)1(7a1)2(3b2)1. The leading CSF carries only about 67% weight in the CASSCF wave function (versus more than 90% for the SiNH2+ isomer), with the next two at 5.2% and 3.2%; these three account for only 76% of the wave function, the rest spread over many tiny contributions. The small reference weight is what makes single-reference MPn treatments unreliable here. Geometry: r(SiN) 1.794 A, r(SiH) 1.485 A, angle SiNH 118.60 deg at CASSCF/6-311++G** (vs 1.785 / 1.464 / 118.37 at CCSD(T)). The Si-N bond is longer than in SiN (1.572 A), HNSi (1.551 A) or SiNH2+ (1.66 A) because the pi(SiN) bond is much weaker. H2SiN+ lies about 115 kcal/mol above the absolute minimum of the (H,H,Si,N)+ surface, the X 1A1 state of SiNH2+; ROHF puts this gap 40 kcal/mol lower, a difference entirely attributable to nondynamic correlation (85 kcal/mol recovered for SiNH2+ on going ROHF -> CASSCF versus only 46 kcal/mol for H2SiN+). Valence-virtual dynamic correlation, defined as CASSCF minus SOCI, is 90 kcal/mol (82 kcal/mol in SiNH2+). Dipole moment 3.40 D (CASSCF), 4.03 D (FOCI), 3.8 +/- 0.2 D (SOCI). Scaled CASSCF rotational constants recommended for the main isotopomer: A0 149.811, B0 15.405, C0 13.969 GHz. Scaled CASSCF vibrational frequencies (cm-1, relative intensity): SiH2 wagging 542 (19.3%), SiH2 out-of-plane 411 (9.1%), SiN stretch 719 (3.0%), SiH2 bending 955 (38.9%), symmetric SiH2 stretch 2315 (11.4%), antisymmetric SiH2 stretch 2330 (18.4%). Predicted intense bands near 550, 950 and 2300 cm-1. Electronic spectrum: within 10 eV, 12 symmetry-allowed states, none with oscillator strength above 7.3e-2; only two significant features, near 6.4 and 8.1 eV.
reference_short: Interstellar silicon-nitrogen chemistry. III. The spectral signatures of the H2SiN+ molecular ion, J. Chem. Phys. 104, 1979 (1996)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free main-group species, so metal_center is 'none' and the metal columns are left empty. The paper's central methodological point is that the single-reference MPn and CCSD(T) infrared spectra are qualitatively wrong for this ion: at CASSCF the out-of-plane SiH2 deformation drops from about 600 to 411 cm-1 and loses a factor of four in intensity, because of the sigma(SiH2) / in-plane 2pN interaction that the single-reference methods miss. FOCI involved 599,768 CSFs; the SOCI was truncated. Frequencies quoted here are the scaled values (CASSCF scaling factor 0.941 for the frequency table, derived from comparisons with experimental spectra of the related HNSi, HSiN, HSiNH2 and HNSiH2 species). The isomer SiNH2+ is used as a comparison throughout but its own active space is not restated in this paper, so it gets no row of its own.

compound_name: S4 2+ tetrasulfur dication (square-planar D4h form; CASSCF applied to the transition state for its formation from two S2+)
point_group: D4h for the square-planar minimum; the reaction path was traced in both C2v and D2h symmetry
geometry_source: eleven isomers fully optimized at RHF with 3-21G* and 6-31G* (overall symmetry the only constraint); MP2/6-31G* optimizations on the four most stable isomers; the minimum energy path for dissociation into two S2+ traced using the distance between the midpoints of the S-S bonds as reaction coordinate. The CASSCF work covers only the region around the first transition state.
method: CASSCF (as implemented in GAUSSIAN 90) for the transition-state region; RHF and MP2 for geometries and energetics
basis_set: 3-21G* for the CASSCF calculations (restricted for lack of computer time); 3-21G* and 6-31G* for RHF, 6-31G* for MP2
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons in two orbitals: the 7b1u and 2b1g orbitals in D2h symmetry, correlating the two configurations ...(7b1u)2(2b1g)0 and ...(7b1u)0(2b1g)2
active_space_protocol: (2,2) minimal space chosen specifically to convert the crossing of two SCF configurations into an avoided crossing, so the potential maximum at the transition state is rounded off rather than a sharp cusp; the authors state only partial mixing of the two configurations could be achieved
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet; the square-planar D4h structure is the most stable of the eleven isomers considered at RHF/6-31G*, followed by the trans-planar C2h structure. Square S4 2+ is 105.9 kcal/mol less stable than two separated S2+. First transition state TS1, from the crossing of the two SCF configurations, lies 43.4 (3-21G*) / 48.0 (6-31G*) kcal/mol above square S4 2+ on the C2v path and 46.6 / 51.3 kcal/mol on the D2h path. CASSCF/3-21G* lowers these to 36.0 kcal/mol (C2v) and 39.0 kcal/mol (D2h), and shifts the transition state from R = 2.33 A to R = 2.37-2.38 A. MP2/6-31G* brings the barrier down to about 33 kcal/mol. A second, very shallow transition state TS2 occurs at large separation: R(midpoint-midpoint) 6.1 A in C2v, 27.6 / 26.4 kcal/mol above the pi* complex, and R = 5.25 A in D2h, 28.2 / 25.4 kcal/mol above it. Calculated vibrational frequencies for the square structure compare well with experiment.
reference_short: On the structure of S4 2+ and its formation from 2 S2+. Ab initio SCF and CASSCF studies, Can. J. Chem. 72, 298 (1994)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free main-group species, so metal_center is 'none'. The CASSCF role in this paper is deliberately narrow: a (2,2) two-configuration treatment used only near the transition state, on a 3-21G* basis, to replace an artificial SCF configuration crossing with a proper avoided crossing. The authors themselves state that much higher correlation treatments (extensive MCSCF or multireference CI) would be needed to establish the most stable structure of the intermediate and a reliable activation barrier, so the CASSCF numbers here are a lower bound on the barrier rather than a converged result. The PDF is an OCR of a scanned page in which the S4 2+ formula frequently renders as 's?' or 'sq2+'; only unambiguous numbers were transcribed.

compound_name: hexaquoferrous cation [Fe(H2O)6]2+ — high-spin 5T2g and low-spin 1A1g states
point_group: Oh idealized; the 5T2g high-spin state Jahn-Teller distorts to pseudo-D4h (two axial Fe-O bonds shorter than the four equatorial, with the O-Fe-O axis inclined 1.7 deg from perpendicular and two equatorial waters rotated about 11.4 deg out of plane); the 1A1g low-spin state was optimized in D3d neglecting hydrogens
geometry_source: automatic structure optimization and frequency calculations (to confirm minima) at the CASSCF level; CASPT2 was single-point only
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 with two active spaces, plus SORCI (spectroscopy-oriented configuration interaction) as an independent check; compared against a wide range of DFT functionals
software: MOLCAS for CASSCF/CASPT2 and the restricted Hartree-Fock reference; ORCA for SORCI; GAUSSIAN and ADF for the DFT and SCF comparisons
basis_set: 6-31G* and 6-31G** quality for the MOLCAS CASSCF/CASPT2 work (basis D = 6-31G* on Fe and O, 6-31G** on H); ANO-S additionally used for the free Fe2+ atomic calculations; SORCI used Wachters (8s6p4d2f) on Fe with added f functions, Ahlrichs TZVP on O and Ahlrichs TZV on H
active_space_orbital_description: CAS2 = [12,10]: the five 3d orbitals plus a second d shell, formed by adding to the [6,5] space the lowest three and highest two of the surrounding orbitals (i.e. beyond just the HOMO and LUMO), so that all of the 3d density that mixes with p-type orbitals on the ligand oxygens is included. CAS1 = [6,5]: the six d electrons distributed among the five 3d orbitals.
active_space_protocol: [6,5] six d electrons in the five 3d orbitals; [12,10] adds a second d shell — the '3d double-shell effect' — by including the lowest three and highest two orbitals around the HOMO/LUMO, to capture the large radial correlation from 3d-3d interaction and all the 3d density mixed into ligand-oxygen p orbitals. The lowest 30 orbitals were frozen in the molecular CASPT2.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 5T2g, (t2g)4(eg)2, with the low-spin 1A1g (t2g)6(eg)0 state the excited spin state. LS-HS energy differences (cm-1), direct and after shifting the dissociation asymptote to the experimental atomic Fe2+ 5D -> 1I splitting: CASSCF(6,5)/D 23125; CASSCF(12,10)/D 21180 direct, 17892 shifted; CASPT2(6,5)/D 21610; CASPT2(12,10)/D 16185 direct, 12347 shifted; SORCI 13360 (no shift needed). Literature reference values quoted for comparison: SCF 27500, CASSCF 23200, CI 17100 direct / 13700 shifted. Best estimate of the true HS-LS energy difference: 12000-13000 cm-1. The SORCI route gives a 1A1g vertical excitation of 12553 cm-1 at the singlet-optimized geometry, plus 807 cm-1 of quintet geometric relaxation, for an unshifted adiabatic 13300 cm-1. Geometries: CASSCF(12,10) high-spin 5T2g equatorial Fe-O 2.194 A, axial Fe-O 2.171 A; low-spin 1A1g Fe-O 2.077 A with O-Fe-O 90.0 deg. Experimental Fe-O distances for Fe(II) salts range about 2.07-2.15 A. Atomic Fe2+ 5D -> 1I excitation energies used for the shift: experiment 29897.3 cm-1 (3.70 eV); CASSCF(6,10)/6-31G* 33185, CASSCF(6,10)/ANO-S 32850, CASPT2(6,10)/6-31G* 33735, CASPT2(6,10)/ANO-S 32130 cm-1.
reference_short: Comparison of density functionals for energy and structural differences between the high- (5T2g) and low- (1A1g) spin states of the hexaquoferrous cation [Fe(H2O)6]2+, J. Chem. Phys. 120, 9473 (2004)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). The paper's ab initio numbers are the reference against which the DFT functionals are judged, so the CASSCF/CASPT2 results are the primary content here rather than a side calculation. The authors conclude their own CASPT2 LS-HS gap is significantly overestimated because of basis-set limitations: the atomic Fe2+ 5D -> 1I asymptote comes out about 3000 cm-1 too high, and they apply an empirical shift built from that atomic error. SORCI needs no such shift. The separate atomic Fe2+ calculations used a (6,10) active space rather than the molecular (12,10); that atomic active space is recorded in this row's electronic_structure_description rather than the active-space columns, which describe the molecular calculation.

compound_name: H2NO aminoxyl (nitroxide) radical — ground state and the sigma -> pi* and n -> pi* excited states
point_group: Cs for the pyramidal form (C2v in the planar limit); the out-of-plane angle alpha is the coordinate of interest
geometry_source: MCSCF/CASSCF geometry optimization; then multireference FOCI optimization; then SOCI scans of the inversion coordinate with NO, NH and HNH held fixed while alpha was varied
method: CASSCF (full valence) and internal-set-partitioned MCSCF, followed by multireference first-order CI (FOCI) and second-order CI (SOCI); Full Valence CI (FVCI) over the internal sets
software: Alchemy II (IBM version, on IBM 3090 and IBM RISC 6000)
basis_set: DZP plus diffuse functions (34 a' and 16 a'' molecular orbitals in Cs)
active_space_orbital_description: the full valence space of H2NO — the NH bonding and antibonding pair, the sigma(NO) and sigma*(NO), the oxygen sp lone pair, the pi and pi* of the NO group and the oxygen p lone pair — with only the O 1s and N 1s as core. Wavefunction [13] correlates all 13 valence electrons in this single internal set, giving 6986 CSFs.
active_space_protocol: a sequence of internal-set partitions was tested before the full space: [5] the pi system plus the pO lone pair (5 electrons) with everything else core — rejected because the resulting MCSCF orbitals could not be used further, the sigma-pi separation surviving only under the imposed C2v symmetry; [4,9] separating the NH fragment (4 electrons) from the NO fragment (9 electrons); [2,2,9] splitting the NH set further into two subsets; and finally [13], all 13 valence electrons in one complete active space, i.e. CASSCF. The authors' conclusion is that the aminoxyl group is an irreducible 9-electron entity: any partitioning of that {9 electrons in 6 orbitals} space gives a non-stable wavefunction and potentially qualitatively wrong potential surfaces, and the oxygen sp lone pair must be in the active space alongside the pO orbital for hybridization reasons.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: doublet, unpaired electron in a pi* orbital. Planar (C2v) configuration (1a1)2(2a1)2(3a1)2(4a1)2(1b2)2(5a1)2(1b1)2(2b2)2(2b1)1, becoming (1a')2(2a')2(3a')2(4a')2(1a'')2(5a')2(6a')2(2a'')2(7a')1 in the pyramidal Cs form; in localized terms 1sO2 1sN2 NH(+)2 NH(-)2 NO2 spO2 n2 piO2 pi*1. Two excited states studied, sigma -> pi* and n -> pi*, matching the two absorptions seen experimentally for stable aminoxyls (an intense band and a weak one). Geometries: FOCI optimization gives NO 1.288 A, NH 1.033 A, HNH 115.2 deg, alpha 24.6 deg — only slightly changed from the CASSCF optimization, but with alpha reduced into agreement with earlier RHF+CI work. The SOCI treatment with wavefunction [2,2,9] gives NO 1.309 A, NH 1.012 A, HNH 121.3 deg, alpha 0 deg: the minimum is planar. Correlation increases pi delocalization of the NO bond and flattens the molecule. For the n -> pi* state the SOCI optimization gives an NO length of 1.642 A, the authors concluding that correlation matters a great deal for this state's NO bond. CSF counts: 6986 for the CASSCF/FVCI, 11156 for the FOCI, 193318 for the SOCI (and 666260 for the 12e-/1e- internal-external partition). Ground-state dipole moments computed at FVCI and FOCI agree well with the experimental values for aminoxyl radicals II and III (3.12 and 3.14 D); the SOCI value is slightly larger.

Full-valence CASSCF shows pronounced multireference character, the two dominant CSFs carrying 70% and 13%; the authors note the second CSF is the one that could support two sigma bonds. For the isoelectronic species, CN+ shows distinct minima in its lowest four spin states, whereas BN's 7Sigma_u+ state is dissociative — so the authors assign latent quadruple bonding to C2 and CN+ but not BN. electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 6H15/2 for Dy(III), 4f9. The magnetic anisotropy axis lies along the axial O-Dy-O bond, perpendicular to the ground-state beta electron density, minimizing electrostatic repulsion. Ground and first-excited Kramers doublets are strongly axial (gx = gy ~ 0.0), and the angle between the ground and first-excited anisotropy axes is under 6 degrees, so relaxation proceeds via higher excited states. Significant thermally-activated QTM at the second excited state sets the relaxation path |-15/2> -> |-13/2> -> |-1/2> -> |+1/2> -> |+13/2> -> |15/2>. Axial crystal-field parameters (k = 2, 4, 6; q = 0) exceed the non-axial ones, confirming substantial axiality in all three. For complex 1 (Cl): gz = 19.857 in the ground Kramers doublet; the eight ground Kramers doublets from 6H15/2 span up to 902.0 K; Ucal = 606.3 K. This is the smallest barrier of the series, attributed to the smaller, strongly hydrogen-bonded chloride and the correspondingly smaller axial B2-0 crystal-field parameter.

electronic_structure_description: Three unpaired electrons. Unlike the mono-nitrene and carbene complexes, here the quartet is slightly more stable than the broken-symmetry doublet: dG(298K) = -1.4 kcal/mol. The small gap and the very similar geometries of the two spin states suggest a significant Boltzmann population of the broken-symmetry doublet. Both states correspond to two nitrene radicals (N1 and N2) bearing alpha-spin unpaired electrons plus an unpaired electron on the porphyrin ligand — alpha-spin in the quartet, beta-spin in the broken-symmetry doublet. In the doublet, the two most stable alpha-spin SOMOs are Npy(1) at 63.5% and the second nitrene-based orbital. This species is the paper's clearest case that a multireference, multideterminant wavefunction is genuinely required: DFT cannot properly describe the broken-symmetry doublet arising from three unpaired electrons.

MRMP2(8,10)/def2-TZVP//CASSCF(8,10)/def2-SVP puts TS2 only 0.24 kcal/mol below TS1, and the IRCs show a flat surface around both transition structures and around the NEB highest-energy image, all three highest-energy points having nearly identical energies. geometry_source: minima, conical intersections, minimum-energy paths and intersystem crossings optimized at CASSCF; conical intersections not found along MEPs computed at CASSCF with a degeneracy restriction via restricted Lagrange multipliers (no nonadiabatic coupling elements); linear interpolation in internal coordinates where MEPs were not possible. method: CASPT2//CASSCF protocol: CASSCF geometries with CASPT2 single points for dynamical correlation; imaginary shift 0.2 au to avoid intruder states, no IPEA shift (for consistency with earlier studies); spin-orbit couplings from atomic mean field integrals (AMFI); solvent by PCM

active_space_orbital_description: the full pi system (12 electrons in 10 orbitals) plus three n orbitals, giving 18 electrons in 13 orbitals for the vertical and adiabatic energies
active_space_protocol: Explicit three-tier reduction. Including all pi (12 electrons, 10 orbitals) and all n (8 electrons, 4 orbitals) character would give CAS(20,14), which the authors state is not feasible, so a systematic study was run to find the smallest space retaining the relevant orbitals. (18,13) = full pi system plus three n orbitals, used for the vertical and adiabatic energies and for the CASPT2 single points. (16,12) = nine pi orbitals plus three n orbitals, obtained from (18,13) by moving the pi orbital localized on the NH2 group into the inactive space on energy and occupation-number criteria, as done in earlier adenine studies; used for geometry optimizations of minima and conical intersections. (12,10) = pi only, used for the minimum-energy paths on the 1(pi pi)* surfaces.
electronic_structure_description: Photophysics of 8-azaadenine analysed with the CASPT2//CASSCF protocol, compared throughout with adenine. Singlet and triplet manifolds are mapped via minima, conical intersections and intersystem crossings, with AMFI spin-orbit couplings quantifying the singlet-to-triplet channels. Dynamical correlation for every optimized structure comes from single-point CASPT2(18,13) - 18 electrons in three n plus ten pi/pi* orbitals.

method: CASSCF/NEVPT2 for the exchange couplings, alongside broken-symmetry DFT; parameters fitted to a Heisenberg Hamiltonian
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,15) on a (Mn(III), S = 2)3 subunit — 12 electrons (three Mn(III) d4 centres) in 15 orbitals

The full (Mn(III), S = 2)3 trimer is then treated with CAS(12,15) to test whether the pairwise couplings are transferable, computing the lowest energy level for each total spin S = 0 to S = 6 and fitting exchange parameters directly to those computed energies.
multiplicities_studied: total spin S = 0 through S = 6 for the Mn3 subunit

The CAS(12,15) trimer calculation gives the lowest spin level for every S from 0 to 6, from which couplings are extracted by direct fit, allowing the transferability of the Mn2+Ga pairwise couplings to be checked. Fitting the experimental susceptibility while excluding data above 50 K gives an improved J = -3.7 cm-1 for the coupling between the (Mn(III), S = 2)3 units.

active_space_protocol: A four-step expansion driven by disagreement with experiment. CAS(5e,5o), the usual d-orbital-only space, put the lowest quartet ligand-field term at 9396 cm-1 - far from the magnetic data - and gave a too-small axial ZFS D = 2.06-2.1 cm-1. Adding a pi-type ligand-based orbital gave CAS(7e,6o); adding the diffuse 4d metal orbitals gave CAS(7e,11o); finally a sigma-type ligand-based orbital was found essential, giving CAS(9e,12o). The quartet-sextet ligand-field gap falls 9396 -> 4679 (CAS(7e,11o)) -> 2749 cm-1 (CAS(9e,12o)) and D rises 2.06 -> 7.85 cm-1, the latter close to the experimental value. The authors state explicitly that the dominant changes came from the pi- and sigma-type ligand-based orbitals and that this 'points out the importance of balancing the active space'.
multiplicities_studied: 2,4,6 — 6, 4 and 2 (sextet, quartet and doublet ligand-field terms)

Temperature dependence at the largest space: the quartet-sextet gap decreases with the temperature at which the crystal structure was measured, and D rises from 7.85 cm-1 (100 K structure) to 10.08 cm-1 (295 K structure). Experimentally, out-of-phase susceptibility appears at 1.9 K above 100 Hz but without clear maxima, so the paper stops short of claiming SMM behaviour.

ligand_set: per uranium: one eta6- and one eta4-bound anthracenide (C14H10)2-, with bridging methoxide linking the two uranium centres
geometry_source: model system optimized at RI-PBE-D3/def2-TZVP (def-TZVP for U) in Turbomole, in the triplet, quintet and septet spin states, all confirmed as minima by harmonic vibrational analysis; multireference calculations are single points on these

active_space_orbital_description: Final reduced space (8e,12o). The ideal space would hold all molecular orbitals that are linear combinations of the uranium 5f orbitals plus the U-arenide bonding and antibonding orbitals. 1* has 14 5f orbitals in total but crystal-field effects leave most unoccupied, so only 8 were needed: (4e,8o). Inspection of those orbitals identified 10 further pi-bonding/antibonding pairs, beyond CASSCF's reach.
active_space_protocol: Staged reduction. (4e,14o): all 14 uranium 5f orbitals with their 4 electrons - at CASPT2 this leaves the singlet, triplet and quintet within 0.3 kcal/mol, so no single spin state can be assigned. (4e,8o): reduced after finding that only 8 of the 14 5f orbitals need be included, the rest being unoccupied through crystal-field effects. RASSCF/RASPT2 (2e,2h,2e; 10o,8o,10o) in the notation of Sauri et al.: 10 pi-bonding orbitals in RAS1, the 8 5f orbitals in RAS2, 10 pi-antibonding orbitals in RAS3, with excitations restricted so more orbitals can be carried than CASSCF permits. RAS1 occupations come out at 1.96 or higher and RAS3 at 0.04 or less, i.e. effectively doubly occupied and empty, which justifies a final reduction to (8e,12o) that reproduces the RASSCF results.
multiplicities_studied: 1,3,5,7 — 1, 3, 5 and 7 (singlet through septet examined; triplet, quintet and septet optimized)
electronic_structure_description: At CASPT2 with the 5f-only (4e,14o) space the singlet, triplet and quintet lie within 0.3 kcal/mol, so the paper explicitly declines to assign a single spin ground state and expects the true ground state to be a spin-orbit coupled mixture of those spin-free states. DFT shows covalent U-arenide interaction, which is what motivated the RASSCF treatment; the eta4-anthracenide is better described as bidentate, bonding through pi at the bridgehead carbons with negligible contribution from the remaining central-ring carbons. Relative charge on the eta4-C14H10 ligands exceeds that on the eta6-arenides. Optimized U-C distances (triplet, averaged): U-C(eta6) 2.746 / 2.723 A, U-C(eta4) 2.659 / 2.639 A, U-O 2.331 A, against experimental 2.713, 2.658 and 2.328 A.

electronic_structure_description: Substantial multireference character. Best described as an S = 1 Co(III) centre antiferromagnetically coupled to an S = 1/2 TAML-centred radical, giving a net doublet, with configuration (dxy)2.00 (dz2)2.00 (dxz+Lpi)1.38 (dyz)1.07 (Lpi-dxz)0.64 - in agreement with Collins' early interpretation. The paper's contribution is the correction step: for each MD snapshot the molecular-orbital overlap matrix against a reference-geometry wavefunction (e.g. the vacuum equilibrium geometry with the desired active space) is computed, and where the optimized active space has drifted, orbital pairs are swapped and a second CASSCF optimization is run using the previous wavefunction as the initial guess. compound_name: lutein (xanthophyll carotenoid, ten conjugated C=C double bonds) - excited states along the bond-length-alternation coordinate
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed along the bond-length-alternation (BLA) coordinate
method: CASSCF and DMRG-based large-active-space calculations for the four lowest singlet states
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(20,20), the chemically complete pi space: 20 pi-type molecular orbitals occupied by 20 electrons, corresponding to the ten conjugated C=C double bonds. This choice was independently confirmed by the authors' automatic UNO-based active-space selection procedure, making it both chemically motivated and unbiased. Four asymmetric alternatives were also studied, each with six more virtual orbitals than electrons: CAS(8,14), CAS(10,16), CAS(12,18) and CAS(14,20).
active_space_protocol: The paper's central result is a documented failure of the chemically complete space. CAS(20,20) - the full pi valence space, confirmed by automatic UNO selection - is adequate for the GROUND state but gives an unbalanced description of the excited-state manifold: the bright state is artificially shifted to high energy and the expected sequence of state crossings along the BLA coordinate is lost. Four deliberately asymmetric spaces were therefore tested, each carrying six more virtual orbitals than electrons - CAS(8,14), CAS(10,16), CAS(12,18), CAS(14,20) - the rationale being prior insight into the expected excitation patterns plus a qualitative orbital analysis.
nroots_per_mult: four lowest singlet states
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy curves for the four lowest singlet states of lutein along the bond-length-alternation coordinate. The bright state evolves along BLA through a series of crossings, but only with a suitably unbalanced active space: with the chemically complete CAS(20,20) the bright state is placed artificially high in energy and the crossing sequence is wrong. This makes the paper a direct counterexample to the assumption that the full valence pi space is the safe choice for excited states of long polyenes.
reference_short: Can CASSCF model the excited states of xanthophyll lutein? A Density Matrix Renormalization Group journey (ChemRxiv preprint, 2026)
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Metal-free organic carotenoid. Not peer reviewed (ChemRxiv).

ligand_set: two bridging oxo ligands and one bridging acetate, with terminal ligands completing each Mn coordination sphere
geometry_source: experimentally characterized complex; the paper works from its crystallographically known structure
method: DMRG-CASCI and spin-state-averaged DMRG-CASSCF, with DMRG-NEVPT2 for dynamic correlation; broken-symmetry DFT computed for comparison

nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over all spin states involved
electronic_structure_description: Heisenberg exchange coupling constant J. Experiment gives J = -90.0 cm-1 (antiferromagnetic). compound_name: copper corrole, Cu(C) - the unsubstituted parent, saddled C2 structure
metal_ox_state: III or II - the non-innocence question the paper addresses
ligand_set: corrole macrocycle (trianionic if Cu is III, dianionic radical if Cu is II)
point_group: C2 for the saddled minima (planar C2v structures also studied)

electronic_structure_description: Relative energies of the competing Cu(III) closed-shell and Cu(II) corrole pi-cation-radical states. CASPT2 on state-specific CAS(12in13) orbitals gives relative energies of -4.0, 0.0, 9.3, 3.1, 0.0 and 11.1 kcal/mol across the states considered; RASPT2 on state-specific RAS(36in34) orbitals gives -3.4, 0.0, 3.8, 0.0 and 7.4 kcal/mol. The experimental reference structure has R(Cu-N) = 1.893 A and a saddling angle of 7.33 degrees. The hybrid functionals PBE0 and B3LYP give a qualitatively different picture from the multireference treatment.
Other: Methodological conclusion: an active space containing only the four HOMO-LUMO pi orbitals is too small to balance the Cu(III) state against the various Cu(II) pi-cation-radical states, or those states among themselves; extending into the corrole pi shell is worth the cost. compound_name: monophenylsulfonium cation, PhSH2+ (MPS) - C-S bond dissociation
geometry_source: equilibrium geometry optimized with MP2 and with the M06-L functional in cc-pVDZ; MP2 and DFT-M06L give identical bond angles and lengths for this species
method: localized active space SCF (LASSCF) and CASSCF references, both with pair-density functional theory on top (LAS-PDFT and CAS-PDFT); DFT with several functionals for comparison
software: PySCF with the mrh extension for the multireference work, except that OpenMolcas was used for the CASSCF calculations on monophenylsulfonium; Gaussian 16 A01 for the DFT
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for all multireference calculations (cc-pVTZ testing on monophenylsulfonium showed no appreciable change in dissociation energies); def2-TZVP for the DFT
active_space_orbital_description: LASSCF partitions the active space into fragment subspaces rather than using one monolithic space; the scans use eight orbitals split as ((2,2),(6,6),(4,4)) in one ordering and ((2,2),(4,4),(6,6)) in another, so the recorded total is the sum over fragments
active_space_protocol: LASSCF with fragment subspaces ((2,2),(6,6),(4,4)) and the alternative ordering ((2,2),(4,4),(6,6)); CASSCF references computed for comparison, with LAS-PDFT and CAS-PDFT on top
multiplicities_studied: 1,3 — singlet and triplet (homolytic cleavage gives a radical pair)
electronic_structure_description: C-S bond dissociation of MPS. The calculations indicate a heterolytic cleavage pathway for this cation. LASSCF reproduces the CASSCF bond dissociation energies at substantially lower cost, which is the methodological claim. Triphenylsulfonium salts are the practical motivation - they are photoacid generators used in semiconductor lithography, where light-induced C-S photolysis of Ph3S+ produces the reactive intermediates that trigger acid-catalyzed chemistry.
Other: One of three phenylsulfonium cations compared: monophenyl dissociates heterolytically while di- and triphenyl dissociate homolytically.
reference_short: Wang, Agarawal, Hermes, Motta, Rice, Jones, Gagliardi, Distinguishing homolytic versus heterolytic bond dissociation of phenylsulfonium cations with localized active space methods
notes: Hand-supplied PDF, batch 4 (automated OA fetch had previously failed). Metal-free organic cation. This is the first chemical application of LASSCF. The motivating problem is recorded because it bears directly on active-space selection: even when a CASSCF active space is affordable, it often fails to change consistently from reactant to product, producing discontinuities in the potential energy surface; LASSCF partitions the space into fragment subspaces to avoid that. reference_doi and year taken verbatim from papers_index.csv.

electronic_structure_description: The paper is a documented failure case for a minimal active space. The barrier separating the closed-shell alternating and non-alternating minima of small C4n rings passes through an open-shell transition state. CASSCF(2,2) over the HOMO/LUMO pair overestimates the barrier substantially, and adding second-order perturbation theory then cancels it entirely, placing the non-alternating geometry well below the alternating one. A simple zwitterionic picture is supported by DFT, TDDFT and UV-vis, but CASSCF reveals a more intricate situation. ligand_set: two cyclopentadienyl ligands and a kappa2-bound di-tert-butylcarbodiimide (heterocumulene) unit
geometry_source: DFT geometry optimisation at M06-L/6-311G(d,p), selected because it matched the experimentally measured X-ray structure very closely
method: CASSCF, with QT-AIM and ELF topological analysis performed on the CASSCF wavefunction; DFT (M06-L), NBO and solid-state CP-MAS 13C NMR alongside
active_space_orbital_description: all the valence and bonding orbitals for the Ti-N-C-N atoms. The HOMO is primarily the carbon 2py orbital with a smaller titanium 3dz2 contribution in an apparent sigma interaction; the LUMO is the corresponding sigma* combination with a nodal plane between titanium and carbon.
active_space_protocol: CAS[14,14] chosen to span all valence and bonding orbitals of the Ti-N-C-N core
electronic_structure_description: Natural orbital occupations from the CASSCF wavefunction: HOMO 1.68, LUMO 0.33 (beta = 0.312). Mayer bond order analysis on the CASSCF natural orbitals gives a Ti-C bond order of 0.19, showing that the Ti-carbene-bonded resonance form is an important but minor contributor. Occupations below about 0.4 correspond to Ti(IV), so the complex is better described as Ti(IV) than Ti(III). Overall description: a free carbene with partial Ti-Cbeta bonding arising from Ti-N pi-bonding mixing with N-C-N sigma-bonding of the bent N-C-N framework.
reference_short: Beaumier, Gordon et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc.
notes: Active space written CAS[14,14] with square brackets rather than parentheses. Used here not for energetics but to settle a bonding question - which of three limiting resonance structures describes the Ti-C interaction - via natural-orbital occupations and Mayer bond orders.

method: embedded correlated wavefunction (ECW) theory coupled to density functional embedding theory (DFET): emb-CASSCF, emb-CASPT2, emb-NEVPT2, and adaptive sampling configuration interaction emb-ASCI-PT2 and emb-ASCI-SCF-PT2
active_space_orbital_description: the H-H sigma and sigma* orbitals plus six occupied and six unoccupied Cu 4s-derived MOs on the Cu12 cluster
active_space_protocol: systematic escalation: (14,14) with the H-H sigma/sigma* and six occupied and six unoccupied Cu 4s-derived MOs; then (38,38) adding 12 occupied and 12 unoccupied Cu 3d-derived MOs on the Cu12 cluster; then (62,62) adding a further 12 occupied and 12 unoccupied Cu 3d-derived MOs. The (38,38) space was used in emb-ASCI-SCF-PT2 to test the importance of self-consistent orbital optimisation.
electronic_structure_description: Benchmark of adaptive sampling CI against emb-CASSCF/CASPT2/NEVPT2 for a surface reaction. With the same (12,12) active space, emb-ASCI-PT2 reproduces emb-CASSCF(12,12) reference energies to 0.001 eV using 100,000 determinants; the point of the study is that ASCI lifts the factorial-scaling limit on active space size that constrains CASSCF.
reference_short: Zhao, Zhang, Martirez, Carter
notes: Embedded cluster model of a periodic metal surface rather than a discrete molecule; included because the chemical system (H2 on Cu(111)) is specific and the active-space escalation from (14,14) to (62,62) is unusually well documented. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty: the Cu atoms are metallic surface atoms, not a coordination centre with a defined oxidation state.

compound_name: CH4 dissociation on the Cu(111) surface, modelled as a CH4 + Cu10 embedded cluster
geometry_source: Cu10 cluster carved out of a four-layer Cu(111) periodic slab model (21 x 21), embedded via the DFET embedding potential Vemb
method: embedded correlated wavefunction (ECW) theory coupled to density functional embedding theory (DFET): emb-CASSCF, emb-CASPT2, emb-NEVPT2, and adaptive sampling configuration interaction emb-ASCI-PT2 and emb-ASCI-SCF-PT2
active_space_orbital_description: the orbitals involved in the C-H bond breaking plus Cu-derived MOs on the Cu10 cluster; the largest space adds 10 occupied and 10 unoccupied Cu 3d-derived MOs
active_space_protocol: active space for CH4 dissociation ranges from (12,12) up to (58,58), the latter adding 10 occupied and 10 unoccupied Cu 3d-derived MOs to the Cu10 cluster space; emb-CASSCF(12,12) energies serve as the reference against which the ASCI variants are benchmarked
electronic_structure_description: Second benchmark reaction. Demonstrates that adaptive sampling CI can reach active spaces far beyond what CASSCF can afford, up to (58,58) here, while remaining embedded in a DFT description of the extended surface.
reference_short: Zhao, Zhang, Martirez, Carter
notes: See the companion H2 desorption row from the same paper. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty for the same reason.

compound_name: Mn(III) site of a series of one-dimensional Mn(III) chain coordination polymers assembled by salicylic-based Schiff base ligands (compounds 1-8)
ligand_set: salicylic-based Schiff base ligands forming 1D chains; a single molecule was cut out of the chain of each compound for the calculation
geometry_source: X-ray crystal structures (determined for compounds 2-4 and 8; 1 and 7 reported earlier); a single molecule cut from the chain
method: state-averaged CASSCF for the spin-orbit coupling contribution to D and E; the spin-spin contribution computed with the coupled-perturbed scheme
basis_set: TZVP for Mn and all coordinated atoms, SVP for all remaining atoms
active_space_orbital_description: four electrons in the five Mn(III) 3d orbitals (d4)
active_space_protocol: four electrons in 5 orbitals, with 5 quintet and the lowest 35 triplet states taken into account
nroots_per_mult: 5 quintet and the lowest 35 triplet states
electronic_structure_description: High-spin Mn(III) d4 chains. Both the spin-orbit coupling contribution and the spin-spin contribution to the zero-field-splitting parameters D and E were computed, the latter via the coupled-perturbed scheme in ORCA.
reference_short: Stetsiuk, Plyuta, Avarvari, Goreshnik, Kokozay, Petrusenko, Ozarowski
notes: Notable for computing the spin-spin contribution to the zfs explicitly rather than assuming spin-orbit coupling accounts for all of it, hence ss_included = yes. The eight compounds share the same computational treatment and Mn(III) d4 active space, so they are condensed into one row.

point_group: Cs (molecule in the yz plane, z the C2 symmetry axis)
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimisations of the excited states; solvent effects for water treated with a sequential Monte Carlo / quantum mechanics approach
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2 (multiconfigurational second-order perturbation theory)

ligand_set: two tridentate Schiff-base catecholate ligands in their mononegative (Cat-N-BQ-) or dinegative (Cat-N-SQ2-) radical forms
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2
basis_set: atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis sets derived from primitive sets (17s12p9d4f) for iron, nickel and cobalt
active_space_orbital_description: the five Fe 3d orbitals plus two ligand orbitals; six electrons in seven MOs, chosen so the space is flexible enough to allow either five or six electrons (Fe(III) or Fe(II)) to localise on the iron and either one of the ligand orbitals to be occupied
active_space_protocol: CAS[6,7]SCF: six electrons in seven MOs, deliberately sized so that the metal oxidation state is not imposed but determined variationally - the space accommodates both the Fe(III) and Fe(II) distributions. The two lowest septet (S = 3) solutions were converged first, because that multiplicity forces single occupation of all active MOs, one of which is a ligand orbital.
nroots_per_mult: the two lowest septet (S = 3) states converged first, then used as the starting point
electronic_structure_description: Coexistence of two thermally induced intramolecular electron transfer (IET) processes. metal_ox_state is deliberately left EMPTY: the whole point of the calculation is that the iron centre can display either five or six d electrons (Fe(III) or Fe(II)) depending on the valence tautomer, and the active space was constructed not to prejudge this.
reference_short: Evangelio et al., Chem. Eur. J.
notes: Active space written CAS[6,7] with square brackets. Part of a series [M(Cat-N-BQ)(Cat-N-SQ)]/[M(Cat-N-BQ)2] with M = Co (2), Fe (3), Ni (4); only the iron member has its active space stated explicitly, so only that row is recorded. method: CASSCF/CASPT2, used to benchmark and spin-purify broken-symmetry DFT energies
software: MOLCAS 7.0 (CASSCF/CASPT2); MN-GFM, a locally modified Gaussian 03 (DFT)
active_space_orbital_description: the five 3d orbitals on Cu plus two orbitals of the initial O2 moiety that are involved in the bond rearrangements
active_space_protocol: the typical active space for all ligand systems included the 3d orbitals on Cu and two orbitals of the initial O2 moiety involved in the bond rearrangements; a Cholesky decomposition threshold of 1e-6 was used for all CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations. For the O2 reference calculation a full-valence active space was used.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet-triplet splittings for O2 of 14.9, 29.1 and 24.0 kcal/mol from broken-symmetry protocols 1-3 with a full-valence CASSCF/CASPT2 reference. Broken-symmetry DFT for the singlet gives a Kohn-Sham determinant with <S2> = 1, so CASSCF/CASPT2 was used to spin-purify and to test the DFT description of the C-H activation mechanism.
reference_short: Huber et al., Chem. Eur. J.
notes: active_space_nel left EMPTY: the paper describes the active space by its orbital content (Cu 3d plus two O2 orbitals, hence 7 orbitals) but never states the number of active electrons. Recorded as partial for that reason. The paper explicitly remarks that applying CASSCF/CASPT2 is not straightforward here because of uncertainties in active space construction and size limitations.

compound_name: the anionic chromophore of reversibly switchable fluorescent proteins (RSFPs), in QM/MM models of Dronpa and Padron and a set of Dronpa mutants
geometry_source: QM/MM: initial structure optimised at HF/3-21G/MM, then CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*/MM optimisation; conical intersections located with the CI optimisation method in Molcas
method: CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*/MM geometry optimisation with CASPT2(12,11)/6-31G*/MM single points; 3-root state averaging
software: MOLCAS 7.8 with the MOLCAS/Tinker interface for QM/MM
active_space_orbital_description: all pi orbitals of the chromophore with natural occupancies not close to 0 or 2
active_space_protocol: a single-point CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*/MM calculation was performed specifically to define and verify the correct active space orbitals, which were taken to be all pi orbitals with occupancies not close to 0 or 2; conical-intersection optimisations used the same CASSCF(12,11) level with CASPT2 single points at the optimised structures
nroots_per_mult: 3-root state average; CASPT2 single-root single-point calculations performed on the 3-root SA reference
electronic_structure_description: Systematic study of the excited states along the photoisomerisation path of reversibly switchable fluorescent proteins. Absorption and emission energies reproduce the experimental trends and signs even where absolute values are a few kcal/mol blue-shifted; the analysis addresses how a limited set of beta-barrel and alpha-helix amino-acid replacements shift the absorption maximum by as much as 40 nm while the chromophore itself is unchanged.
reference_short: Smyrnova, Marin, Olivucci, Ceulemans
notes: A clear statement of active-space selection by natural occupation number: the space is defined as the pi orbitals whose occupancies are not close to 0 or 2, verified by a dedicated single-point calculation before the production runs. The compound is the protein-embedded chromophore; the protein environment enters through the MM region.

geometry_source: DFT geometries (M06-2X, B3LYP, wB97X) from Gaussian 09
method: CASSCF and CASPT2, with DMRG for the larger active spaces; DFT-based unrestricted broken-symmetry as a cross-check
basis_set: two different basis sets compared for the CASSCF(12,12)/CASPT2(12,12) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: the pi space of the dimerising system; the maximum pi space for the reactant complex comprises the full set of pi orbitals and pi electrons of the two monomer units
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(12,12) and CASPT2(12,12) for the reactants, transition states and intermediates of the dimerisation step, with a larger (20,18) space accessible through DMRG; DMRG is expected to and does decrease the triplet-singlet gap relative to the smaller CAS
electronic_structure_description: Diradical character of the p-quinodimethane monomers and of the intermediate dimers along the Gilch polymerisation route. Complete-active-space methods were used precisely because DFT cannot describe the diradical character; specific substituents alter the monomer electronic structure and thereby the polymerisation mechanism.
reference_short: Nikolic, Wouters, Romanova et al.
notes: Records the (12,12) CAS used for the reported CASSCF/CASPT2 energies; a larger (20,18) space was reached with DMRG and is noted in the protocol. ground_state_mult left empty because the singlet-triplet ordering is itself the quantity under investigation and varies with substituent.

method: CASPT2//CASSCF

reference_short: Giussani, Merchan et al.
notes: A case where the active space needed no justification beyond the chromophore itself: the entire pi system is active.

ligand_set: two pentamethylcyclopentadienyl (Cp*) ligands and the 4,5-diazafluorene N-donor ligand
method: CASSCF with a perturbative PT2 correction; state-specific calculations
active_space_orbital_description: 4 active orbitals - two ytterbium 4f orbitals and the two lowest ligand pi* orbitals - holding 4 active electrons
active_space_protocol: a CAS of 4 active orbitals (2f and the 2 lowest pi*) with 4 active electrons was shown to give results similar to a larger CAS of 8 active orbitals (6f and 2 pi*) with 12 active electrons, so the smaller (4,4) space was used. nroots_per_mult: state-specific calculations
electronic_structure_description: Two open-shell singlets are calculated to lie BELOW the triplet state, and the observed temperature-dependent magnetism results from a Boltzmann equilibrium between those two open-shell singlet configurations - consistent with the low effective magnetic moment measured. metal_ox_state left empty: the multiconfigurational ground state is an intermediate-valence mixture rather than a single integer oxidation state, which is the point of the study.
reference_short: Nocton, Booth, Maron, Andersen
notes: Explicit documented equivalence test between a small and a large active space - (4,4) versus (12,8) - with the smaller one adopted after being shown to give similar results. That kind of stated justification is exactly what active_space_protocol is for.

reference_short: Piquemal and Pilme

compound_name: ozone, O3, ground-state global potential energy surface for the O2 + O -> 3O dissociation
geometry_source: global ab initio PES constructed pointwise
method: RASSCF followed by CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: 12 active electrons in nine active orbitals, consisting of only the 2p orbitals of all three oxygen atoms
active_space_protocol: different combinations of active electrons and orbitals were tested on a small portion of the PES near the transition region - 12e/9o, 12e/7o, 12e/12o, 18e/15o and 18e/12o - and the 12-electron, nine-orbital space consisting of only the O 2p orbitals was found to be reasonably accurate and computationally inexpensive, so it was adopted for the global surface
electronic_structure_description: Global ground-state O3 surface used for quasi-classical trajectory dissociation cross-sections. In total 27 electronic states would need to be considered for the O3 system in the absence of spin-orbit interaction, and the conical intersection between the two lowest PESs increases the importance of non-adiabatic effects; the present work uses the single ground-state surface.
reference_short: Mankodi, Bhandarkar et al., J. Chem. Phys. 2017
notes: Explicit five-way active-space size test (12e/9o, 12e/7o, 12e/12o, 18e/15o, 18e/12o) with the chosen space justified on a stated accuracy-versus-cost tradeoff - unusually complete provenance for a PES paper. The companion N2 + N system is a diatomic-plus-atom collision and is not recorded separately.

compound_name: free-base porphin (FBP), the parent free-base porphyrin
geometry_source: geometry optimisations with Gaussian 98
method: CASSCF with CASPT2; compared against CIS, RPA, ZINDO, TDDFT and SAC-CI
software: MOLPRO for the multiconfiguration tasks; Gaussian 98 for geometries, CIS, RPA and ZINDO
basis_set: excitation energies computed with basis sets ranging from STO-3G to 6-31+G
active_space_orbital_description: the Gouterman four-orbital model: HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1 in the 5b1u, 2au, 4b2g and 4b3g irreducible representations of D2h, holding 4 active electrons
active_space_protocol: a hierarchy of active spaces was tested, starting from Gouterman's four-orbital model (model A), enlarged by four virtual MOs 21ag, 18b2u, 18b3u and 15b1g (model B), and further extended by two occupied (4b1u, 3b3g) and two unoccupied (6b1u, 3au) orbitals (model C). The paper concludes that even the lowest-energy transitions are insufficiently described in the CAS formalism and that a much larger active space, or more inactive orbitals in the correlation treatment, would be needed for sufficient accuracy.
electronic_structure_description: Electron excitation spectra of porphins. CASPT2 was performed for FBP in the smaller active space (model G), with an additional 6 electrons correlated in the PT2 treatment; correlating more electrons was computationally unfeasible.
reference_short: Estimation of electron spectra transitions in porphins, Int. J. Mol. Sci. 2004
notes: Only the Gouterman four-orbital model (4 electrons, 4 orbitals) is recorded numerically; the enlarged models B and C are described in the protocol but their bracketed labels in the extracted text are ambiguous as to which number is electrons and which is orbitals, so they are not converted to numeric fields. A rare paper reporting that its own CAS approach was INADEQUATE, which is useful negative evidence.

compound_name: thorocene, ThCOT2 (bis(eta8-cyclooctatetraenyl)th), an actinocene sandwich complex
ligand_set: two eta8-cyclooctatetraenyl (COT) dianion rings in a sandwich arrangement
geometry_source: An-to-ring-centroid distance optimised against CASPT2 energies, with the COT ligand geometry held fixed
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 for the geometry optimisation and RASSI for state interaction; QTAIM topological analysis of the resulting densities
active_space_orbital_description: 16 orbitals: the highest occupied COT pi orbitals of au, b1u, ag and b1g symmetry; the seven actinide f orbitals of au (f-delta), b1u (f-sigma, f-delta), b2u (f-pi, f-phi) and b3u (f-pi, f-phi) symmetry; and five d orbitals of ag (d-sigma, d-delta), b1g (d-delta), b2g (d-pi) and b3g (d-pi) symmetry
active_space_protocol: a single 16-orbital active space is held FIXED across the whole Th-to-Cm series - COT pi donors plus the actinide 7f and 6d manifolds - with only the electron count changing, from 8 for Th to 14 for Cm. Written by the authors as CASSCF(n,16). The An-to-COT-centroid distance was optimised against CASPT2 energies with the COT ligand geometry held fixed.
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state electron density of thorocene, ThCOT2 computed at CASSCF and analysed topologically (QTAIM) to quantify the covalent contribution of f-orbital participation to An-COT bonding across the series. The multiconfigurational character of these complexes is assessed explicitly.
reference_short: Kerridge, f-orbital covalency in the actinocenes
notes: A seven-member isostructural series sharing one 16-orbital active space, so the (n,16) family maps directly onto the actinide 5f occupation. Because dynamic correlation enters via CASPT2 and spin-orbit via RASSI, the authors note it was not possible to generate total electron densities amenable to QTAIM from those steps, so the topological analysis is performed on the CASSCF densities. This compound is also studied in other papers already in this database under different DOIs; those are independent studies, not duplicates. d/f electron count 5f0 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the Th(4) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

compound_name: thymine-thymine (6-4) adduct formation in DNA - the stacked thymine dinucleotide and its photoproduct

reference_short: Giussani, Conti et al.
notes: A rare explicit statement of active-space reduction driven by CONVERGENCE FAILURE rather than by cost or accuracy: the (4,4) space exists because (8,6) would not converge at that particular minimum. Worth keeping as evidence that active-space choice is sometimes forced.

electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies to the excited electronic states of the C6N isomers, of astrochemical relevance as possible interstellar species; all isomers can be intermediates of relevant chemical processes.
reference_short: Mogren Al-Mogren and Senent

method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with a level shift of 0.50 a.u.
active_space_orbital_description: built from the valence-based space of 6 electrons in 5 d-type MOs for Co(III), extended by a second set of d-type metal-centred virtual orbitals carrying an extra radial node (the 3d' double shell), plus the sigma-type ligand orbitals that are essentially empty in the low-spin S=0 configuration but become occupied in the high-spin S=2 one
active_space_protocol: a 10-electron / 12-orbital active space is stated to be REQUIRED for the electronic description of a d6 ion in a CASPT2 approach. The construction is described stepwise: start from the valence-based space (6 electrons in 5 d-type MOs for Co(III)), add the traditional second set of d-type virtuals with an extra radial node (3d'), and include the antibonding cobalt 3d orbitals that are empty in LS but occupied in HS. Written by the authors as CAS[10,12].
electronic_structure_description: Vacancy-induced deformation and its effect on the low-spin (S=0) / high-spin (S=2) balance at the cobalt site, as a function of the number and positions of Rb ions. The work proposes a vacancy-induced scenario for the Fe-to-Co electron transfer that underlies the photomagnetism of this Prussian blue analogue.
reference_short: Krah, Suaud et al., Eur. J. Inorg. Chem.
notes: One of the clearest stepwise active-space constructions in this database: valence d shell, plus the 3d' double shell, plus the ligand-field orbitals whose occupation changes between spin states - each addition justified by what the LS/HS comparison requires. Embedded cluster model of a solid, recorded on the same basis as the other embedded-cluster rows.

active_space_protocol: the MOs were obtained from CASSCF calculations state-averaged over the lowest 8, 11 and 14 electronic states for the O1s-1, C1s-1 and S2p-1 CVV states respectively; for the VVVV states the averaging covered 18000 singlet and 18000 triplet states. electronic_structure_description: Theoretical support for the interpretation of Auger spectra following double core hole creation: each single photon may eject four electrons, two from the primary double-core-hole process and two fast electrons from secondary Auger transitions.
reference_short: Auger spectra of OCS, Chemical Physics
notes: Numeric active-space fields left EMPTY: the space is specified as full valence without printed counts. Recorded chiefly for the root counts, which are the largest in this database by a wide margin - 18000 singlets and 18000 triplets for the VVVV manifold, against a typical few tens elsewhere.

compound_name: C2F4 (tetrafluoroethylene), rupture of the carbon-carbon double bond
geometry_source: dissociation path scanned along the C-C coordinate
method: CASSCF(8,8) and CASSCF(8,8)+NEVPT2; compared against CCSD, CCSD(T) and DFT (M06-L, M06-2X)
active_space_orbital_description: the eight orbitals of the C-C bonding manifold selected automatically
active_space_protocol: the (8,8) active space was selected using a MODIFIED AVAS (atomic valence active space) technique: core orbitals are excluded from the projecting step, and the threshold is split between the occupied and virtual spaces. An automated, projection-based orbital selection rather than a hand-picked space.
electronic_structure_description: Dative versus electron-sharing description of the carbon-carbon interaction in C2F4. The dissociation path is followed with multiple methods to test whether the C=C bond is better described as two dative bonds between CF2 fragments or as a classical electron-sharing double bond; only in the CCSD/CCSD(T) calculations were the core electrons frozen.
reference_short: Andrada, Casals-Sainz, Martin Pendas, Frenking
notes: One of very few papers in this database that names an AUTOMATED active-space selection scheme (AVAS) rather than describing a hand-chosen orbital set, and it documents its modifications to that scheme - excluding core orbitals from the projection and splitting the occupied/virtual threshold.

compound_name: pentalene, a pseudoaromatic bicyclic hydrocarbon - S0 and S1 potential energy surfaces
geometry_source: CASSCF optimisations; MMVB used to explore the surfaces more broadly
method: CASSCF; MMVB, a hybrid force-field / parametrised valence bond method designed to simulate CASSCF for ground and covalent excited states
basis_set: 4-31G, stated to be sufficient for the purpose
active_space_orbital_description: all eight pi molecular orbitals of pentalene, holding the eight pi electrons; the CASSCF wavefunction describes all possible occupations within that space
active_space_protocol: the full pi valence space - eight electrons in eight pi molecular orbitals. The MMVB companion method represents these same CASSCF active orbitals in a valence-bond space via a parametrised Heisenberg Hamiltonian, with an MM2 force field describing the inert sigma framework.
electronic_structure_description: S0 and S1 surfaces of pentalene. CASSCF bond lengths are reproduced by MMVB to within 0.01 A. At the D2h transition structure two of the CASSCF orbitals are singly occupied, giving a B1g open-shell singlet state, as predicted by Craig; the S0 barrier is about 8 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Bearpark, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 1996
notes: Historical interest: an explicit attempt to build a cheap surrogate (MMVB) that reproduces a specific CASSCF active space, with the agreement quantified. The active space is the full pi valence set, requiring no selection decision.

compound_name: Cp'2Th(bipy), a bipyridyl thorium metallocene (Cp' = substituted cyclopentadienyl, bipy = 2,2'-bipyridine)
ligand_set: two substituted cyclopentadienyl ligands and a 2,2'-bipyridine, the latter reduced to its dianion
geometry_source: DFT geometries at B3PW91 with Gaussian 09
method: CASSCF to determine the nature of the two lowest singlet states and the lowest triplet; DFT (B3PW91) for structures and energetics
active_space_orbital_description: a space spanning the thorium 5f and 6d orbitals together with the bipyridine pi* orbitals, sufficient to distinguish f0d0pi*2, f0d1pi*1 and related configurations; no counts are printed
active_space_protocol: CASSCF was used specifically because the precise nature of the electronic ground state cannot be ascertained at the DFT level, which tends to favour the closed-shell configuration - the multireference calculation is introduced to settle a question DFT is known to bias.
nroots_per_mult: the two lowest singlet states and the lowest triplet state were determined
electronic_structure_description: Answers the title question - is this a low-valent thorium complex? - in the negative: Cp'2Th(bipy) has a Th(IV)(bipy2-) ground state with an f0d0(pi*)2 closed-shell singlet configuration (S = 0). An open-shell singlet with f0d1(pi*)1 configuration, nearly degenerate with its triplet congener, lies only 9.2 kcal/mol higher and can be thermally populated, which explains the observed temperature-independent paramagnetism. The bipyridine-thorium interaction differs significantly between the two spin states.
reference_short: Ren, Lukens, Zi, Walter et al.
notes: Numeric active-space fields left EMPTY: the paper reports the CASSCF electronic configurations and their relative energies but never states the size of the active space. Recorded because the finding - a formally low-valent actinide that is actually Th(IV) with a reduced ligand - is exactly the sort of oxidation-state ambiguity a multiconfigurational treatment exists to resolve.

compound_name: NHC-stabilised dicationic B2P2 ring [4]2+ (from addition of a diphosphane to a boron-boron triple bond), butterfly and planar isomers
geometry_source: X-ray structure analyses combined with DFT optimisations
method: CASSCF followed by NEVPT2; DFT for structures and relative energies
active_space_orbital_description: a space spanning the B2P2 ring frontier orbitals, sufficient to describe the diradicaloid character; no counts are printed

electronic_structure_description: X-ray analysis with DFT and CASSCF/NEVPT2 shows the NHC-stabilised dicationic B2P2 rings adopt closed-shell butterfly-like structures. For the planar isomer planar-[4]2+, which lies only about 3 kcal/mol above the butterfly form at the DFT level, CASSCF/NEVPT2 predicts a LUMO occupation of 0.41 electrons - substantial diradicaloid character - together with a small singlet-triplet gap. Cationisation shortens the B-B bond and destroys planarity.
reference_short: Bruckner et al., Angew. Chem. (German)
notes: Numeric active-space fields left EMPTY: the article is in German and the computational section gives no (nel,norb) pair in the extracted text. The LUMO natural occupation of 0.41 electrons is the quantitative diradicaloid measure and is quoted verbatim.

notes: Active space built by explicit ligand-orbital / metal-correlating-orbital PAIRING: six ligand 2p orbitals each matched to a U-centred 5f/6d/7s combination of the same symmetry. The per-symmetry partition is given for both charge states, and the U(V) space is derived from the U(VI) one by a stated orbital swap - unusually complete provenance for a 2001-era paper. d/f electron count 5f0 added 2026-08-05: arithmetic from the U(6) oxidation state recorded in this row, not a value stated by the paper.

compound_name: cyanoacetylene (HC3N), photodissociation in its lowest singlet and triplet excited states
