software: MOLCAS 6.2; Gaussian 03 for some crossing-point optimisations
active_space_orbital_description: all the valence orbitals except the lowest sigma orbitals - thirteen orbitals holding fourteen electrons
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(14,13) comprising all valence orbitals except the low-lying sigma set, used for the optimisations and the CASPT2 single points; a REDUCED CASSCF(8,8) was used specifically for optimising the crossing points, where the full space was not affordable
electronic_structure_description: Photodissociation channels of cyanoacetylene, relevant to the haze chemistry of Titan. In the T1 state the dissociation products are H(2S) + CCCN(X 2Sigma+) and HCC(X 2Sigma) + CN(X 2Sigma+); at CASPT2(14,13)//CASSCF(14,13)+ZPE the barriers for adiabatic dissociation of the C4-H5 and C2-C3 bonds are 6.11 and 6.94 eV in S1, and 5.71 and 6.39 eV in T1.
reference_short: Luo, Du, Duan et al.
notes: Another small-space-for-hard-geometries case: the full (14,13) is used for optimisations and energies, but conical-intersection/crossing-point searches fall back to (8,8).

geometry_source: geometry optimisations under different symmetry constraints at CASSCF(8,8) and at several DFT functionals (BMK, M06-2X, BHandHLYP, wB97XD)
method: CASSCF(8,8); DFT with several functionals for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: an (8,8) space over the frontier pi system of the carbon ring
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(8,8) applied under different symmetry constraints as a check on the DFT geometries
electronic_structure_description: Electronic structure, aromaticity and surface coupling of cyclo[18]carbon. Attempts to optimise the CUMULENIC geometry - at CASSCF(8,8) and at every functional tested - always yielded a saddle point with one or more imaginary frequencies (1900i cm-1 at CASSCF(8,8)), indicating the cumulenic form is not a minimum; CASSCF(8,8) gives alternating bond lengths of 1.199 and 1.356 A.
reference_short: Baryshnikov, Valiev, Kuklin et al.
notes: A case where CASSCF and DFT AGREE on a negative result - the cumulenic structure is a saddle point at every level tested, with a very large imaginary frequency at CASSCF(8,8).

compound_name: NO2, nitrogen dioxide - bent and cyclic forms
geometry_source: geometry optimisations at six levels of theory, guided by HF/3-21G scans
method: CASSCF at two active-space sizes; HF and MBPT(2), MBPT(3), MBPT(4) for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: an (8,8) valence space; a smaller CAS(4,6) was also used
active_space_protocol: two active spaces compared directly on the same question: CAS(4,6) and CAS(8,8), both with the 6-31+G(d) basis. The relative energies of the bent and cyclic forms shift substantially between them - the barrier from the linear form is 86.56 kcal/mol at CAS(4,6) but 76.85 kcal/mol at CAS(8,8) - so the space size materially changes the answer.
electronic_structure_description: Can NO2 exist in bent or cyclic forms? Stationary points located at 180 degrees (linear), around 86 degrees (bent) and around 42-47 degrees (cyclic). At CAS(8,8) the bent form lies 76.85 kcal/mol above and the cyclic form higher still; the corresponding CAS(4,6) values are 86.56 kcal/mol and 175.13 kcal/mol, and the HF values differ again (108.33 and 209.37 kcal/mol).
reference_short: Fuzery, Burcl, Torday, Csaszar et al.
notes: Useful as a direct demonstration that active-space size changes a chemical conclusion: the bent-form barrier moves by nearly 10 kcal/mol between CAS(4,6) and CAS(8,8) on the same geometry and basis.

method: CASSCF, used as a check on the basis-set and method dependence of the computed molecular properties
basis_set: ANO-S basis used for the check; HF orbital energies obtained with 6-31G** for the active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: twelve orbitals selected around the frontier region; HOMO-3 through HOMO-5 lie within 0.41 eV of one another and were therefore included together rather than split
active_space_protocol: the active space was selected by STUDYING HF ORBITAL ENERGIES of neutral EDO-TTF with the 6-31G** basis: because HOMO-3 to HOMO-5 are close in energy (within 0.41 eV), they were kept together in the space rather than truncated between them - an explicit energy-gap criterion for where to cut the space.
electronic_structure_description: Ab initio molecular properties of the isolated EDO-TTF donor compared with those in the (EDO-TTF)2PF6 charge-transfer crystal, which undergoes a well-known photoinduced phase transition.
reference_short: Linker, van Loosdrecht et al.
notes: A rare explicit statement of the CRITERION used to choose where to truncate an active space: near-degeneracy of HF orbital energies, with a stated 0.41 eV window keeping HOMO-3 to HOMO-5 together.

active_space_protocol: (12,12) minimal space, the largest reachable by conventional emb-NEVPT2 — CO 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi, 2pi* plus the Pd 4d orbitals along the bond axis (z2, xz, yz); (16,16) add the nonbonding Pd 4d(x2-y2) and 4d(xy) and their correlating orbitals; (18,18) add a pair of Ag 5s orbitals to (16,16); (20,18) instead add the CO 3sigma and 4sigma to (16,16); (22,20) all CO 3sigma/4sigma/5sigma/6sigma/1pi/2pi*, all Pd 4d and a pair of Ag 5s — the largest sensible space, beyond which only more Ag 5s orbitals would enter
electronic_structure_description: CO adsorption free energy (eV) versus active space. (12,12): -1.38 (AVDZ), -2.00 (AVTZ), -2.26 (CBS) — strongly overbound. (16,16): -0.12 (CBS). (18,18): largely unchanged from (16,16). (20,18): -0.63 (CBS). (22,20): -0.90 (CBS). PW-DFT+D3 reference: -1.05 eV. emb-CASSCF (10e,10o) natural orbitals show the Pd is d10 in the SAA with all five 4d orbitals at equivalent fractional occupation and little hybridization with the Ag host 5s
Other: Pd adsorbs CO the most weakly of the four dopants studied. The minimal (12,12) space overbinds because the Pd 4d orbitals split on CO adsorption and the nonbonding d orbitals carry less static correlation, so the space preferentially stabilizes the adsorbed state. Adding Ag 5s orbitals has a smaller effect than adding the Pd d orbitals, reflecting poor dopant-host mixing
reference_short: Hutchison, Wei & Carter, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 22, 2313-2323 (2026)
notes: d_electron_count d10 is the paper's own assignment from the DFT PDOS and the emb-CASSCF (10e,10o) natural orbital occupations, not arithmetic from an oxidation state — the paper never states an oxidation state, so metal_ox_state is empty. active_space_nel/norb record the largest space, (22e,20o); the full (12,12)->(22,20) series is in active_space_protocol. point_group, SOC and spin-spin flags, and multiplicities are not stated for this dopant and are left empty. DMRG bond dimension M = 2000 for the initial DMRGSCF, with M = 500/750/900 restarts extrapolated for the NEVPT2 energies.

compound_name: CO adsorbed on a Rh-doped Ag(100) single-atom alloy (embedded Rh1Ag12 cluster)
metal_center: Rh (single-atom dopant in an Ag(100) host)
ligand_set: CO adsorbate on the dopant; Ag12 host cluster (8 surface-layer + 4 subsurface Ag)

method: density functional embedding theory / embedded correlated wavefunction (DFET/ECW) with embedded DMRGSCF and embedded DMRG strongly contracted NEVPT2 (emb-DMRG-sc-NEVPT2); emb-CASSCF/emb-NEVPT2 used for the minimal active spaces
software: PySCF v2.9.0 (locally modified) interfaced to Block2; VASP v6.4.3 for the periodic PW-DFT (PBE + D3(BJ)) slab geometries; EmbeddingIntegralGenerator for the embedding potential integrals
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ (C, O, Ni); aug-cc-pVDZ-PP / aug-cc-pVTZ-PP for Rh, Pd, Ag, Pt; density fitting with def2-TZVPP-jkfit (AVDZ) and def2-QZVPP-jkfit (AVTZ); CBS extrapolation a + b X^-3 (Helgaker)
relativistic_treatment: fully relativistic effective core potentials: ECP28MDF on Rh, Pd and Ag
active_space_orbital_description: CO 3sigma, 4sigma, 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi and 2pi*; all five Rh 4d orbitals; and a pair of Ag 5s orbitals representing the Fermi-level states
active_space_protocol: (13,13) minimal space for the odd-electron d9 Rh — CO 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi, 2pi*, the Rh 4d orbitals along the bond axis (z2, xz, yz) and the singly occupied Rh 4d(xy), leaving the 4d(x2-y2) pair out; (15,15) add the 4d(x2-y2) electron pair; (17,17) add a pair of Ag 5s orbitals; (19,17) all Rh 4d plus CO 3sigma, 4sigma, 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi, 2pi*; (21,19) add a pair of Ag 5s orbitals to (19,17)
electronic_structure_description: CO adsorption free energy (eV) versus active space. (13,13): -1.97 (AVDZ), -2.20 (CBS). (15,15): -2.02 (AVDZ), -2.17 (CBS). (17,17): identical to (15,15) with AVDZ. (19,17): -2.21 (AVDZ), -2.38 (CBS) — the most negative. (21,19): -2.19 (AVDZ), -2.29 (CBS). PW-DFT+D3 reference: -2.17 eV
Other: Rh adsorbs CO the most strongly of the four dopants. The adsorption free energy depends much less on active space size than for Pd, because the minimal space is already forced to contain most of the Rh 4d shell (including the singly occupied 4d(xy) that couples to the Ag 5s states at the Fermi level), giving a more balanced treatment of the adsorbed and desorbed states. The AVTZ point for (17,17) is missing because no natural-orbital set consistent with the AVDZ one could be obtained for adsorbed CO
reference_short: Hutchison, Wei & Carter, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 22, 2313-2323 (2026)
notes: d9 is the paper's own statement ('the d9 nature of Rh'), not arithmetic from an oxidation state; no oxidation state is given, so metal_ox_state is empty. active_space_nel/norb record the largest space, (21e,19o); the full series is in active_space_protocol. Rh used a four-layer slab (the others five) so the slab would have an even electron count. point_group, SOC/spin-spin flags and multiplicities are not stated and are left empty.

active_space_orbital_description: CO 3sigma, 4sigma, 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi and 2pi*; all Pt 5d (and 6d) orbitals; and a pair of Ag 5s orbitals
active_space_protocol: (12,12) minimal space containing all Pt 5d/6d orbitals and a pair of Ag 5s orbitals; for desorbed CO the lowest-energy (12,12) replaces Pt 5d(z2) by Pt 5d(x2-y2), so the paper distinguishes (12,12) — lowest-energy space for each state — from (12,12)* — the same active orbitals kept for adsorbed and desorbed CO; (16,16) all Pt 5d plus CO 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi, 2pi*; (18,18) add a pair of Ag 5s orbitals; (20,18) add the CO 3sigma, 4sigma pair instead; (22,20) all CO 3sigma-2pi*, all Pt 5d and a pair of Ag 5s
electronic_structure_description: CO adsorption free energy (eV) versus active space. (12,12) (lowest-energy space for each state): +0.46 (AVDZ), +0.35 (AVTZ), +0.30 (CBS). (12,12)* (orbitals held consistent): -1.53 (AVDZ), -1.63 (AVTZ), -1.66 (CBS). (16,16): +0.87 (AVDZ), -1.19 (AVTZ). (18,18): +1.15 (AVDZ), -1.25 (AVTZ). (20,18): +0.42 (AVDZ), -1.60 (AVTZ). (22,20): +0.66 (AVDZ), -1.67 (AVTZ). Natural-orbital occupations for desorbed CO in the minimal space (AVDZ): Pt 5d(xz) 1.97, 5d(yz) 1.97, 5d(x2-y2) 1.96; keeping 5d(z2) instead gives 1.99 for 5d(xz), 5d(yz), 5d(z2) but a wavefunction ~2.0 eV higher at emb-DMRG-NEVPT2
Other: The AVTZ (22e,20o) value agrees with the CBS (12,12)* value, which the authors take as confirming (12,12)* — consistent active orbitals across the reaction coordinate — as the correct minimal-space choice. The large AVDZ/AVTZ discrepancy traces to the multireference character of the Pt 5d/6d orbitals for desorbed CO: with AVDZ all Pt 5d occupations fall to 1.98 or below, with AVTZ they stay at 1.99. ECW predicts CO binds more strongly on Pt than on Ni, the opposite of the DFT ordering
reference_short: Hutchison, Wei & Carter, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 22, 2313-2323 (2026)
notes: d10 is the paper's own assignment from the DFT PDOS (Ni-, Pd- and Pt-doped systems suggested d10 dopants), not arithmetic from an oxidation state; no oxidation state is stated so metal_ox_state is empty. No CBS value is reported for the large Pt active spaces, so the AVDZ/AVTZ pairs are given as stated. active_space_nel/norb record the largest space, (22e,20o). point_group, SOC/spin-spin flags and multiplicities are not stated and are left empty.

compound_name: CO adsorbed on a Ni-doped Ag(100) single-atom alloy (embedded Ni1Ag12 cluster)
metal_center: Ni (single-atom dopant in an Ag(100) host)
ligand_set: CO adsorbate on the dopant; Ag12 host cluster (8 surface-layer + 4 subsurface Ag)
geometry_source: periodic PW-DFT (PBE-D3(BJ), VASP, 660 eV cutoff) optimized 5x5 Ag(100) slab, five layers (four for Rh), one dopant substituting a surface-layer Ag, bottom two layers frozen at bulk positions; a 13-atom cluster (dopant + 8 surface Ag + 4 subsurface Ag) carved out for embedding; CO placed at its slab-optimized position by the static surface approximation
method: density functional embedding theory / embedded correlated wavefunction (DFET/ECW) with embedded DMRGSCF and embedded DMRG strongly contracted NEVPT2 (emb-DMRG-sc-NEVPT2); emb-CASSCF/emb-NEVPT2 used for the minimal active spaces
software: PySCF v2.9.0 (locally modified) interfaced to Block2; VASP v6.4.3 for the periodic PW-DFT (PBE + D3(BJ)) slab geometries; EmbeddingIntegralGenerator for the embedding potential integrals
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ (C, O, Ni); aug-cc-pVDZ-PP / aug-cc-pVTZ-PP for Rh, Pd, Ag, Pt; density fitting with def2-TZVPP-jkfit (AVDZ) and def2-QZVPP-jkfit (AVTZ); CBS extrapolation a + b X^-3 (Helgaker)
relativistic_treatment: Ni, C and O all-electron (aug-cc-pVDZ/aug-cc-pVTZ); fully relativistic ECP28MDF on the Ag host atoms
active_space_orbital_description: CO 3sigma, 4sigma, 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi and 2pi*; all five Ni 3d orbitals (and the Ni 4s for the desorbed state); and a pair of Ag 5s orbitals
active_space_protocol: (12,12) minimal space — CO 5sigma, 6sigma, 1pi, 2pi* plus Ni 3d(xz), 3d(yz), 3d(z2) for adsorbed CO, and Ni 3d(xz), 3d(z2), 3d(xy) and 4s for desorbed CO; (16,16) all Ni 3d orbitals for adsorbed CO; (20,18) add the CO 3sigma, 4sigma pair; (22,20) additionally a pair of Ag 5s orbitals, capturing Ag 5s / Ni 3d,4s coupling
electronic_structure_description: Ground state of the CO-adsorbed cluster is a singlet; with CO desorbed the Ni is a triplet at the emb-DMRGSCF level, stabilized relative to the open-shell singlet with 3d(xy) and 4s each singly occupied. On CO adsorption 3d(xy) becomes doubly occupied and the singlet becomes favorable. CO adsorption free energy (eV) versus active space: (12,12) -1.48 (AVDZ and CBS); (16,16) -1.34 (AVDZ), -1.24 (CBS); (20,18) -1.52 (AVDZ), -1.39 (CBS); (22,20) -1.42 (AVDZ), -1.57 (CBS). PW-DFT+D3 reference: -1.63 eV. In the (16,16) space all Ni 3d orbitals have fractional occupations below 1.98
Other: Of the four dopants the Ni adsorption free energy is the least sensitive to active space size. A GTO rather than PW basis was used for the emb-DFT term for Ni, because enforcing the desorbed-state triplet on the embedded cluster with a PW basis spuriously magnetizes the Ag host
reference_short: Hutchison, Wei & Carter, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 22, 2313-2323 (2026)
notes: d10 is the paper's own PDOS-based assignment for the Ni dopant, not arithmetic from an oxidation state, which is never stated (metal_ox_state left empty). multiplicities_studied '1,3' is numeric 2S+1 for the singlet adsorbed and triplet desorbed states the paper explicitly identifies; ground_state_mult 1 refers to the CO-adsorbed cluster. active_space_nel/norb record the largest space, (22e,20o). SOC and spin-spin flags and point group are not stated and are left empty.

geometry_source: gas-phase geometries optimized at XMS-CASPT2(4e,5o) with FIC analytical gradients for S0 and T0 (and S1 for the bare corrole); no symmetry imposed; minima confirmed by harmonic vibrational analysis
method: XMS-CASPT2 with fully internally contracted (FIC) analytical gradients for geometry optimization (SA2-CASSCF reference, SS-SR contraction, no IPEA shift); single-point CASSCF(14e,15o)/CASPT2 and RASPT2 for the electronic structure
software: BAGEL (XMS-CASPT2 geometries and PES); RASPT2 single points on ANO-RCC
basis_set: cc-pVTZ on Cu and N, cc-pVDZ on C and H, density fitting with def2-TZVPP JKFIT (geometries); ANO-RCC for the RASPT2 single-point energies
active_space_orbital_description: the four Gouterman corrole pi orbitals (pi_1a2, pi_1b1 occupied; pi_2a2, pi_2b2 empty), the five Cu 3d orbitals, the correlating Cu 4d orbitals, and a Cu-ligand sigma-bonding orbital
active_space_protocol: (4,5) minimal space for geometry optimization — the four Gouterman corrole pi orbitals plus the Cu d(x2-y2), whose occupation is what decides the Cu oxidation-state assignment; (14,15) for the electronic structure — the four Gouterman orbitals, all five Cu 3d, the five correlating Cu 4d and a Cu-ligand sigma-bonding orbital; RAS (28e,2h,2e; 12o,5o,8o) — RAS1 = 11 corrole pi + Cu-ligand sigma, RAS2 = the (4,5) space, RAS3 = the remaining 8 corrole pi, max 2 holes in RAS1 and 2 particles in RAS3; largest RAS (36e,2h,2e; 16o,5o,13o) adds the four lowest Cu 3d to RAS1 and the five 4d to RAS3 (RASPT2 was run on the former, not the latter)
electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 is a multiconfigurational singlet with three dominant electron configurations, at a saddled geometry; T0 is planar and lies above it. Energy differences (kcal/mol): XMS-CASPT2(4e,5o) dE(S0-T0) 2.1, dH 2.1, dG 1.3; RASPT2(28e,2h,2e; 12o,5o,8o)/ANO-RCC dE 2.8, dH 2.8, dG 1.2. Between the two singlets, dE(S0-S1) 7.3, dH 7.5, dG 6.6. At the planar T0 geometry S0 and T0 become degenerate. Along the LIIC between the S0 and T0 minima the S0 multiconfigurational character falls off as the saddling angle decreases, while T0 stays single-reference. DFT dE(S0-T0) for comparison: PBE0-D3 -4.6, M06 -2.4, B3LYP-D3 -2.3, TPSSh-D3 3.0, M06-L 5.4, TPSS-D3 8.3, BLYP-D3 8.5, PBE-D3 9.6
Other: Saddling arises from electron transfer from a corrole pi orbital into the Cu d(x2-y2). Only TPSSh-D3 (10% HF exchange) approaches the XMS-CASPT2 energetics, and even then its singlet is the closed-shell state rather than the correct multiconfigurational one; increasing HF exchange favours the triplet. XMS-CASPT2 overestimates saddling while all the DFT functionals underestimate it. The XMS-CASPT2 dE(S0-T0) computed on TPSSh geometries differs by only 0.1 kcal/mol from that on the XMS-CASPT2 structure
reference_short: Molecular Geometry and Electronic Structure of Copper Corroles
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count deliberately left empty: the paper's whole point is that the S0 ground state is a multiconfigurational singlet intermediate between the Cu(III) d8 closed-shell and Cu(II) corrole-radical descriptions, and it does not commit to a single oxidation state for it. nroots_per_mult = 2 from the stated state-averaging over two states (SA2-CASSCF / SA2-RASSCF) for both the singlet and the triplet. active_space_nel/norb hold the (14e,15o) CAS used for the electronic structure; the (4,5) optimization space and both RAS spaces are in active_space_protocol. Real level shift 0.2 a.u. No SOC or spin-spin treatment is mentioned, so those flags are left empty. point_group empty: calculations were run without imposing symmetry, though the geometries are described as saddled (C2-like) and planar (C2v-like).

basis_set: cc-pVTZ on Cu and N, cc-pVDZ on C and H, density fitting with def2-TZVPP JKFIT (geometries); ANO-RCC for the RASPT2 single-point energies
active_space_orbital_description: the four Gouterman corrole pi orbitals, the five Cu 3d orbitals, the correlating Cu 4d orbitals, and a Cu-ligand sigma-bonding orbital

compound_name: dimethyltetroxide (MeO4Me) and the MeO2 + MeO2 -> MeO4Me -> MeO + MeO + O2 reaction system
geometry_source: wB97X-D3/aug-cc-pVTZ and M06-2X-D3Zero/aug-cc-pVTZ optimized structures (ORCA 5.0.3) for the coupled-cluster benchmarks; multireference geometries optimized at CASSCF(22e,14o) and CASPT2(22e,14o); frequency calculations confirm minima
method: CASSCF and fully internally contracted CASPT2 / CASPT2-IPEA (0.20 au) and FIC-NEVPT2, plus MRCISD+Q; benchmarked against CCSD(T)/CBS, W2X and W3X-L
software: ORCA 5.0.3 (DFT, CASSCF, CASPT2, NEVPT2, CC/CBS); Molpro (W2X components, restricted CC); MRCC (CCSDT and CCSDT(Q) corrections for W3X-L)
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the recommended multireference results; cc-pVDZ/cc-pVTZ/cc-pVQZ with CBS(2/3) and CBS(3/4) extrapolation for coupled cluster; aug-cc-pVTZ for the DFT geometries
active_space_orbital_description: all oxygen valence orbitals except the two C-O sigma bonding orbitals (and their antibonding partners)
active_space_protocol: (6,6) the three sigma and sigma* orbitals of the MeO-O-O-OMe chain — the smallest space that can qualitatively describe both tetroxide formation from two peroxyl radicals and decomposition to O2 plus two alkoxyl radicals; (10,8) adds two lone-pair/pi orbitals localized on the inner O-O oxygens, corresponding to the occupied pi orbitals of the O2 product; (22,14) all oxygen valence orbitals except the C-O sigma/sigma* — adopted after attempts to add only the individual inactive orbitals causing orbital rotations failed to give a stable active space
electronic_structure_description: Relative electronic energies (kcal/mol) with respect to the MeO4Me minimum. Two 30 A separated MeO2 radicals: CASSCF/cc-pVTZ 21.08 (6,6) / 2.99 (10,8) / 7.29 (22,14); CASPT2//CASSCF 18.10 / 8.39 / 11.61; CASPT2-IPEA//CASSCF 21.75 / 12.12 / 14.97; CASPT2/cc-pVTZ 13.83 / 9.36 / 11.63; CASPT2-IPEA//CASPT2 17.77 / 12.98 / 14.99 — against W3X-L 14.42 and CCSD(T)/CBS 15.05. Two 30 A separated MeO radicals plus O2: CASSCF 26.98 / -12.21 / -5.73; CASPT2//CASSCF -5.46 / 12.00 / 16.73; CASPT2-IPEA//CASSCF 3.18 / 17.80 / 22.56; CASPT2/cc-pVTZ -11.06 / 13.25 / 16.93; CASPT2-IPEA//CASPT2 -0.24 / 19.13 / 22.88 — against W3X-L 22.87 and CCSD(T)/CBS 23.01. CC//wB97X-D3/aug-cc-pVTZ benchmark (Table 1, CC/cc-pVTZ): MeO2 + MeO2 14.56, MeO4Me 0.00, MeO...MeO 16.75, MeO...O2 19.55, MeO + MeO + 3O2 20.48
Other: CASPT2-IPEA is the only multireference method tested that reproduces the coupled-cluster energetics; plain CASPT2, NEVPT2 and MRCISD+Q do not. The 5.5 kcal/mol W2X/W3X-L disagreement on the MeO...O2 complex indicates substantial multireference character there. CASPT2(22e,14o)-IPEA/cc-pVTZ finds no saddle points on the minimum energy path for either formation or decomposition; 2D relaxed scans indicate both MeO...O bonds break simultaneously. Formation of MeO4Me is exothermic and its decomposition endothermic; CASSCF alone wrongly predicts exothermic decomposition. Diffuse functions matter little; at least a triple-zeta basis is required
reference_short: Multireference and Coupled-Cluster Study of Dimethyltetroxide, J. Phys. Chem. A 128, 1825 (2024)
notes: Metal-free organic system: metal_center = none, metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty. One condensed row for the whole MeO2 + MeO2 -> MeO4Me -> MeO + MeO + O2 reaction, since every stationary point is treated with the same active-space series and the energies are reported relative to MeO4Me. active_space_nel/norb hold the recommended (22e,14o); the (6,6) and (10,8) spaces are in active_space_protocol. multiplicities_studied '1,3' (numeric 2S+1) covers the closed-shell tetroxide and the triplet O2 / triplet radical-pair channel that the reaction connects; the paper does not tabulate a per-multiplicity state count, so nroots_per_mult is empty. The (10,8) numbers carry substantial uncertainty from orbital rotations, per the paper's own footnote. No relativistic, SOC or spin-spin treatment is mentioned (W2X does include an all-electron scalar-relativistic CCSD(T) approximation, but that is a coupled-cluster composite, not the multireference result), so those flags are left empty.

point_group: Oh and D3h minima compared (DFT/MRCI run in C2v)
geometry_source: Oh and D3d/D3h structures taken from previous studies (Refs 9 and 12)
method: DFT/MRCI (individually selecting multireference CI on a KS-BHLYP reference with DFT-corrected diagonal Hamiltonian matrix elements)
software: TURBOMOLE (initial KS-BHLYP calculations) plus the DFT/MRCI code; Gaussian09 for the TD-DFT comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: initial reference configurations generated by promoting up to two electrons within an active space of ten electrons in ten orbitals; configurations then discarded by an energy-based selection criterion with a 1.0 hartree threshold
active_space_protocol: (10,10) reference space, single choice applied uniformly across the whole benchmark set; up to two electrons promoted within it to build the initial reference configurations, followed by energy-based configuration selection (threshold 1.0 hartree). Standard DFT/MRCI parameters for singlet and triplet states
electronic_structure_description: DFT/MRCI relative energy of the D3h minimum with respect to the Oh minimum: 22.0 kcal/mol. Literature comparisons in the same table: CASPT2(10,10) 49.0 (Ref 12), RASPT2(42,4,0;16,10,0) 17.8 and RASPT2(42,6,6;21,0,5) 16.5 kcal/mol (Ref 9), the last two taken as the best theoretical estimates

electronic_structure_description: Excited-state lifetimes from surface-hopping dynamics (t1 latency, t2 decay, tau total, fs): gas phase 49 / 79 / 128; n-hexane 56 / 58 / 114; water 51 / 64 / 115. Central C-C=C-C torsion at first hop: 108 +/- 25 deg (gas), 110 +/- 24 (n-hexane), 111 +/- 16 (water); bond-length alternation at hopping -0.016, -0.002, -0.024 A. Average time per trajectory near the crossing seam: 30 fs (gas), 32 fs (n-hexane), 16 fs (water). geometry_source: ground-state geometry optimized at MP2/SVP in C2v symmetry; excited-state structures and the minimum on the crossing seam optimized at the multireference level
method: SA-3-CASSCF(10,9) orbitals with MR-CIS and MR-CISD (size-extensivity corrected); ADC(2) used separately to assess the pi-sigma* state; solvent by the conductor-like screening model

active_space_protocol: SA-3-CASSCF(10,9) with equal weights over the three lowest singlets provides the orbitals. On those orbitals three reference spaces were tested: MR-CIS(10,9), MR-CIS(8,7) and MR-CISD(6,5); the 11 carbon and nitrogen 1s orbitals were frozen in every CI calculation. Orbital occupation schemes for the reference wavefunctions are tabulated in SI Table S1
nroots_per_mult: 3 singlets in the SA-3 state-averaging
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies (eV) at the MP2/SVP C2v ground-state geometry, oscillator strengths in parentheses, for basis sets DZ / +P/DZ / TZ / +P/TZ. SA3-CASSCF(10,9): 1B2 (LE) 4.626 (0.008) / - / 4.632 / -; 1A1 (CT) 5.969 (0.667) / - / 5.929 / -. MRCIS(10,9): 1B2 4.621 (0.026) / 4.516 / 4.598 / 4.468; 1A1 4.984 (0.670) / 4.662 / 4.936 / 4.601. MRCIS(8,7): 1B2 4.705 (0.025) / 4.325 / 4.768 / 4.433; 1A1 5.269 (0.688) / 4.902 / 5.113 / 4.738. MRCISD(8,7): 1B2 5.054 / 4.438 / 5.061 / 4.470; 1A1 5.606 / 4.917 / 5.599 / 4.941. MRCISD(6,5): 1B2 5.361 / 4.525 / 5.382 / 4.617; 1A1 5.736 / 5.100 / 5.727 / 5.124. Experimental gas-phase values quoted: S1 0-0 (LE) 3.995, S1 (LE) 4.130, S2 (CT) 4.569 eV. Literature comparisons: CASPT2/ANO 4.05 (LE) and 4.41 (CT); CASPT2 on CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G(d) geometry 4.297 and 4.610; CC2/TZVPP 4.41 and 4.77. The S2 (CT) state is stabilized along the dimethylamino twisting coordinate and crosses S1 at about 50 degrees at the minimum on the crossing seam
Other: Main absorption goes to S2, whose charge-transfer character is somewhat larger than S1's. The twisting angle is not part of the intersection (branching) space, so the seam stays accessible over a wide range of twist angles - consistent with nonadiabatic dynamics showing S2 to S1 decay in 8.5 fs at essentially planar geometries. Polar solvent has little effect on the position of the conical intersection. Under Cs restriction, ADC(2) finds CCN bending strongly stabilizing and strongly charge-transferring, but that structure is not a minimum and reverts to the LE structure once symmetry is released. The authors conclude the dual fluorescence arises from the twisted internal charge-transfer state alongside the LE state, and consider a nanosecond-stable structure of the kind previously proposed unlikely

method: variational multiconfigurational pair-density functional theory with complex translation, MC-ctPDFT and range-separated MC-sr-ctPDFT (orbitals relaxed under the influence of the functional, not post-SCF); CASPT2 computed in this work as the multireference reference
software: MultiPsi (MC-ctPDFT / MC-sr-ctPDFT, using VeloxChem for core functions); ORCA 6.0.0 (CASPT2, RI for the MCSCF integrals); Gaussian (PBE0/def2-TZVP geometry optimizations)
active_space_orbital_description: one sigma orbital mainly localized around the apical carbon atom plus three pi orbitals associated with the defect (SI)
active_space_protocol: CAS(4,4) incorporating one sigma orbital and three pi orbitals of the defect
electronic_structure_description: In the planar configuration the triplet is the ground state, in accordance with Hund's rule, with an exchange coupling J = 200 meV, qualitatively agreeing with previous DFT and CASPT2 studies. J changes sign when the apical carbon is displaced h_C = 0.3 A out of the plane, at which point the singlet becomes preferred - also in accordance with previous findings
Other: The sign change on out-of-plane displacement has previously been attributed to reduced correlation between the sigma and pi electrons and to their changed overlap. This is the only system in the study whose active space mixes sigma and pi character
reference_short: Magnetic Coupling in Non-Kekule Diradical Hydrocarbons via Multiconfigurational Pair-Density Functional Theory (2025)
notes: Metal-free carbon system: metal_center = none, other metal columns deliberately empty. J is reported as a function of the out-of-plane displacement h_C of the apical defect carbon; the 200 meV value is the planar configuration. Energies in meV.

geometry_source: optimized thioformaldehyde structure; initial conditions for dynamics sampled from a Wigner distribution
method: multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory (MC-PDFT) energies and analytic gradients on a state-averaged CASSCF reference, driving fewest-switches trajectory surface hopping with energy-based decoherence (FS-TSH-EDC)
software: SHARC molecular dynamics package for the trajectory propagation
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian, chosen for consistency with the earlier MS-CASPT2 study; the literature benchmark values used ANO-RCC-VQZP
active_space_orbital_description: state-averaged singlet orbitals of the (12,10) active space at the optimized thioformaldehyde geometry (shown in the paper's Figure 1); the smaller (10,6) space is shown in SI Figure S1
active_space_protocol: (10,6) the space used in the earlier MS-CASPT2 and SA-CASSCF dynamics studies; (12,10) the larger space, which MS-CASPT2 dynamics could not afford - MC-PDFT dynamics were run with both
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in eV (S1 / T1 / T2 / T2-S1 gap). This work: MC-PDFT(12,10) 2.34 / 2.04 / 3.47 / 1.13; SA-CASSCF(12,10) 2.40 / 2.16 / 3.31 / 0.91; MC-PDFT(10,6) 2.35 / 2.03 / 3.58 / 1.23; SA-CASSCF(10,6) 2.31 / 2.02 / 3.08 / 0.77. Literature values used as the benchmark: MRCISD+P(12,10) 2.19 / 1.91 / 3.42 / 1.23 and MS-CASPT2(12,10) 2.25 / 2.00 / 3.45 / 1.20, averaged to a benchmark of 2.22 / 1.96 / 3.44 / 1.22; MS-CASPT2(10,6) 2.14 / 1.84 / 3.31 / 1.17. RMSD from benchmark (dE / ddE, eV): MC-PDFT(12,10) 0.09 / 0.06; SA-CASSCF(12,10) 0.17 / 0.26; MC-PDFT(10,6) 0.12 / 0.05; SA-CASSCF(10,6) 0.22 / 0.36
Other: The T2-S1 gap governs the intersystem crossing dynamics. SA-CASSCF(10,6) underestimates it by 0.45 eV, which the authors judge makes dynamics at that level unreliable; the two MC-PDFT gaps deviate from the benchmark by only 0.01 and 0.09 eV. In the dynamics, MC-PDFT(10,6) agrees with previous MS-CASPT2(10,6) simulations, and MC-PDFT(12,10) reduces S1 to T2 population transfer by a factor of about 7.5 relative to the (10,6) result. Population oscillations trace to the C-S bond length modulating the S1-T2 spin-orbit coupling. MC-PDFT allowed excited-state dynamics with the larger active space that MS-CASPT2 could not afford; SOC detail: yes - spin-orbit couplings between S1 and the T2 manifold are computed and drive the intersystem crossing
reference_short: Calio, Truhlar & Gagliardi, first implementation of nonadiabatic molecular dynamics by MC-PDFT (2022)
notes: Metal-free organic compound: metal_center = none, other metal columns deliberately empty. active_space_nel/norb hold the larger (12,10) space; both spaces are in active_space_protocol and both sets of results are recorded. MRCISD+P and MS-CASPT2 values are clearly attributed to the earlier study (Ref 30) and are recorded only as the benchmark the authors compare against. correlation_correction is left to derive from the method string; the MC-PDFT on-top functional is not a perturbative correction in the CASPT2/NEVPT2 sense. Full-database schema audit (GPT-5.6, 2026-08-11): normalized verbose SOC/SS flags to yes/no and retained the original wording in Other.

geometry_source: ground- and excited-state geometries optimized with analytic MC-PDFT nuclear gradients
method: state-averaged MC-PDFT with analytic nuclear gradients using meta and hybrid meta on-top functionals (tPBE, tPBE0, MC23), and linearized PDFT (L-PDFT), on SA-CASSCF references; SA-CASSCF given for comparison
software: not named in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: 4 electrons in 4 orbitals, state-averaged over 2 states, SA(2)
active_space_protocol: SA(2)-(4,4) throughout for this molecule
nroots_per_mult: 2 (SA(2) state averaging)
electronic_structure_description: 1 1Ag -> 2 1Ag excitation energies in eV (vertical / adiabatic, no vibrational zero-point energy). This work: SA(2)-tPBE(4,4) 6.91 / 5.77; SA(2)-tPBE0(4,4) 6.82 / 5.68; SA(2)-MC23(4,4) 6.91 / 5.78; L(2)-tPBE(4,4) 6.92 / 5.78; SA(2)-CASSCF(4,4) 6.56 / 5.42. Literature comparisons: SA(2)-CASPT2(4,4)/aug-cc-pVTZ 6.68 / 5.68; MS(2)-CASPT2(4,4)/6-31G** 6.69 (experimental geometry); CCSD/6-31G** 7.69; CC3/aug-cc-pVTZ 6.67; theoretical best estimates 6.39 (Watson and Chan) and 6.50 (Loos et al., extrapolated CBS-FCI). Optimized internal coordinates for the 1 1Ag state at SA(2)-tPBE(4,4)/jul-cc-pVTZ: r(C=C) 1.336 A, r(C-C) 1.459 A, theta(CCC) 124.1 deg; for 2 1Ag: 1.497, 1.398, 124.1
Other: L-tPBE and tPBE differ by only 0.01 eV for the vertical excitation, showing that state interaction between 1 1Ag and 2 1Ag is unimportant here and that multistate L-PDFT does not degrade single-state MC-PDFT accuracy when the coupled states interact weakly. tPBE0 is the best PDFT functional for the vertical excitation and gives an adiabatic excitation energy identical to CASPT2. MC23 performs almost identically to tPBE for both
reference_short: Hennefarth, Kim, Jangid, Wardzala, Hermes, Truhlar & Gagliardi, MC-PDFT nuclear gradients and L-PDFT energies (2025)
notes: Metal-free organic compound: metal_center = none, other metal columns deliberately empty. The CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, CC3, CCSD and FCI/TBE values in the same tables are literature comparisons, clearly attributed in the paper's own footnotes, not this work's results - this work's multireference results are the SA-CASSCF and MC-PDFT/L-PDFT numbers. Geometries were optimized with the analytic MC-PDFT gradients that are the point of the paper. The LiH test case used to validate analytic against numerical gradients is a bare diatomic and is excluded by the standing scope convention.

geometry_source: B3LYP-D3(BJ) optimized structures (Turbomole v7.4); symmetry-constrained optimizations that turned out to be transition states were reoptimized without symmetry so all ground-state structures are true minima
method: DMRG-CASSCF with DMRG-CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0.25 au, imaginary shift 0.1 au), semicore correlation added by UB3LYP-CCSD(T) in a spin-unrestricted CASPT2/CC scheme; localized-orbital (R)CASCI for the valence-bond analysis; B3LYP and B3LYP* for comparison
software: OpenMolcas interfaced with the CheMPS2 DMRG library; Turbomole v7.4 (B3LYP-D3(BJ) geometry optimizations); ORCA v4.2 (UB3LYP-CCSD(T) semicore correction)
basis_set: ANO-RCC contracted to [7s6p5d3f2g1h] for the metals, [4s3p2d1f] for C, N and O, [5s4p2d1f] for Cl and [3s1p] for H; Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals at 1e-6 au; def2-TZVP (metals) / def2-SVP (ligands) for the geometry optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: five Fe(3d) orbitals, a maximum of five Fe(4d) correlating orbitals, one sigma(Fe-N) orbital, and all corrole pi orbitals except the eight localized on the corrole beta-carbons
active_space_protocol: CAS(24,25) or CAS(24,26) depending on whether the problematic Fe(4d) orbital is retained. General construction rule stated by the authors: all metal nd orbitals, all correlating (n+1)d orbitals for the double-shell effect, and all ligand orbitals able to interact with the metal nd orbitals. Where a state has an empty metal nd orbital the corresponding (n+1)d orbital rotates out and was removed, which is why several complexes carry two active-space sizes. A separate set of minimal localized-orbital (R)CASCI spaces was used for the valence-bond analysis: CAS(4,4) Fe[Cor]Cl, CAS(5,5) Mn[Cor]Cl, CAS(6,5) Fe[Cor]Ph, CAS(7,6) Mn[Cor]Ph, CAS(6,6) Fe[Cor](NO), CAS(6,6) Ru[Cor](NO), CAS(3,3) Mo[Cor]Cl2, each built from the singly occupied metal d orbitals, one corrole pi orbital and the axial-ligand orbitals that mix strongly with the metal d orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Second most noninnocent of the seven complexes. The ferromagnetically coupled Fe(III)-Cor(2-) radical state lies about 10 kcal/mol above the antiferromagnetically coupled ground state at DMRG-CASPT2, but it is not the first excited state: that lies only 4.4 kcal/mol up and is a high-spin (locally S = 5/2) Fe(III) centre antiferromagnetically coupled to a corrole A' radical
Other: Roos et al. previously studied this molecule at CASPT2/ANO-RCC-TZVP with CAS(14,13) and CAS(14,14). Their relative energies are systematically higher than the DMRG-CASPT2/CC values here, from about 1 kcal/mol for the 5A''-3A'' gap up to 19 kcal/mol for the 1A''-3A'' gap, which the authors attribute to those active spaces being too small. The two small spaces also disagree with each other - the 3A'-3A'' gap is 18.6 kcal/mol with CAS(14,13) but 26.1 kcal/mol with CAS(14,14) - leading the authors to conclude that as many macrocycle pi orbitals as possible must be active to compare noninnocent states
reference_short: Phung, Muchammad, Yanai & Ghosh, JACS Au (2021)
notes: DMRG bond dimension m = 4000 in all calculations; the Fe[Cor](NO) triplet-singlet splitting is stated to converge to within 0.1 kcal/mol already at m = 2000. Core and semicore electrons frozen in CASPT2 (through 3s/3p for Mn and Fe, 4s/4p for Ru and Mo), with the semicore contribution added separately by UB3LYP-CCSD(T) and found to be about 1 kcal/mol in every complex. metal_ox_state is deliberately left empty for the noninnocent cases: quantifying how far the oxidation state is ill-defined is the paper's entire subject, so assigning one would contradict the source. Energies are in kcal/mol as reported.

Where a state has an empty metal nd orbital the corresponding (n+1)d orbital rotates out and was removed, which is why several complexes carry two active-space sizes. electronic_structure_description: Essentially innocent - corrole radical character close to zero, grouped with the two phenyl complexes at the innocent end of the series

reference_short: Phung, Muchammad, Yanai & Ghosh, JACS Au (2021)

compound_name: Cu2(formate)4 copper paddle-wheel cluster with adsorbed CO2 (model of the open metal site in HKUST-1)
ligand_set: 4x bridging formate (paddle-wheel); CO2 adsorbed at the open axial metal site
geometry_source: M06-L/cc-pVDZ optimized cluster models; CO2-Cu distance fixed at 2.4 A for both the linear and tilted conformations
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 (imaginary shift 0.1 au, default IPEA shift 0.25 au); ROS-MP2, which the authors note is equivalent to (2,2) CASPT2; M06-L and M06 DFT for comparison
basis_set: ANO-RCC relativistic atomic natural orbital sets in three sizes - BS1 double-zeta plus polarization, BS2 triple-zeta plus polarization on Cu, O and C with double-zeta plus polarization on H, and a larger BS3; Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals at a 1e-4 threshold. DFT/ROS-MP2 used cc-pVDZ, aug-cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVTZ
active_space_orbital_description: the larger space explored is 10 electrons in 10 orbitals; the minimal (2,2) space contains the two electrons and two orbitals of the Cu-Cu interaction, for which CASSCF is equivalent to restricted open-shell HF and CASPT2 to ROS-MP2
active_space_protocol: (2,2) minimal space capturing the Cu-Cu interaction - equivalent to ROS-HF at CASSCF level and to ROS-MP2 at CASPT2 level; (10,10) the larger space tested. Both singlet and triplet lowest spin states were explored, and calculations were run without symmetry
electronic_structure_description: The singlet is the ground state in every case, lying 3 kJ/mol below the triplet - in good agreement with the experimental MOF-11 values of 3.4 kJ/mol (water-bound) and 5.3 kJ/mol (anhydrous). CASPT2 interaction energies between Cu2(formate)4 and CO2 for the singlet ground state, in kJ/mol, counterpoise-corrected with uncorrected values in parentheses, for BS1 / BS2 / BS3: linear (2,2) -15.0 (-43.2) / -18.7 (-33.5) / -20.2 (-31.7); linear (10,10) -14.8 (-46.6) / -18.6 (-36.8) / -20.1 (-35.0); tilted (2,2) -17.7 (-49.3) / -23.5 (-40.0) / -25.8 (-39.6); tilted (10,10) -15.8 (-51.1) / -21.8 (-41.7) / -23.9 (-41.1)
Other: The dicopper singlet ground state is genuinely multiconfigurational and needs a multiconfigurational treatment; the monocopper system is single-configurational and adequately described by MP2, as is the triplet state of the Cu2 system. Enlarging the active space from (2,2) to (10,10) changes the interaction energy by only about 1-2 kJ/mol, which is what justifies the authors' use of the much cheaper ROS-MP2 to parametrize a new UFF pairwise potential. Conventional DFT, even with dispersion corrections, severely underestimates the Cu paddle-wheel/CO2 interaction; the reparametrized force field reproduces the experimental CO2 adsorption isotherms of HKUST-1 and is transferable to other copper paddle-wheel MOFs
reference_short: Origin of the Strong Interaction between Polar Molecules and Copper(II) Paddle-Wheels in Metal Organic Frameworks (2017)

Frozen orbitals in ROS-MP2 were 1s for C and O and 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p for Cu. Energies in kJ/mol as reported.

metal_ox_state: II in the reactant, III in the product
ligand_set: 2x iodido + 4x tetrahydrofuran (explicit first solvation shell); acetone as the electron acceptor
geometry_source: PBE0-D3(BJ) optimized gas-phase structures; ACE-SmII I2 optimized with ECP52MWB-II and ACE(radical)-SmIII I2 with ECP51MWB-SV
method: all-electron CASSCF and CASPT2 including scalar relativistic effects; PBE0-D3(BJ) and a small-core Stuttgart-Dresden ECP benchmarked against them
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: all-electron basis with scalar relativistic treatment for the CASPT2; ECP52MWB-II and ECP51MWB-SV small-core pseudopotentials for the DFT geometries
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic effects included in the all-electron CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: the seven Sm 4f orbitals plus the ligand orbital of interest, extended by five further correlating orbitals expected to represent the Sm 5d shell (higher angular momentum functions mix in during orbital optimization)
active_space_protocol: (6,8) initial space - the seven 4f orbitals plus the ligand orbital of interest with the appropriate electron count; (6,13) adds five correlating orbitals expected to be the 5d shell. The larger space changed the triplet-quintet spin-splitting energies appreciably, so only (6,13) results are reported
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase single-electron-transfer energy dE = E(ACE-radical-SmIII I2(THF)4) - E(ACE-SmII I2(THF)4), in kJ/mol: CASSCF(6,13) 51.94; CASPT2(6,13) 48.94. The transfer is therefore endothermic and the equilibrium lies on the acetone side, not the ketyl-radical side. The perturbative correction is only 3.00 kJ/mol, which the authors read as CASSCF(6,13) already accounting well for dynamic correlation. DFT comparisons (kJ/mol): TPSS-D3 12.76; PBE-D3 28.91; TPSSH-D3 27.28; PBE0-D3 53.19; B3LYP-D3 55.40; BHLYP-D3 38.42; B3PW91-D3 69.66; B3PW91 40.02
Other: Lewis structures routinely imply a ketyl radical forms when SmI2 binds a carbonyl; these calculations say the equilibrium sits on the unreduced acetone side. PBE0-D3(BJ) with a small-core ECP reproduces the CASPT2 energy closely (53.19 vs 48.94 kJ/mol) while non-hybrid PBE and TPSS are far too low. The calculations also confirm the experimentally observed increase in the SmI2 reduction potential on adding HMPA, which replaces THF in the first solvation shell; SOC detail: no - spin-orbit coupling is explicitly stated to be excluded, along with thermal corrections and the second solvation shell
reference_short: Samarium Diiodide Acting on Acetone - Modeling Single Electron Transfer (2022)
notes: The reaction couple is recorded as one row because the two structures are the reactant and product of a single electron-transfer step whose energy difference is the reported quantity. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count carry both sides of the transfer, as the paper defines them. The septet is the spin state of the reported CASPT2(6,13) energy; triplet-quintet splittings are mentioned as the reason for preferring the larger active space but their values are not given in the main text. soc_included = 'no' is the paper's own explicit statement, not an assumption. method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with the standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au; TPSS, TPSSh, B3LYP and M06-L DFT for comparison

active_space_protocol: CAS(12,12) for [CuO2]+; the orbital selection for each species is described in the paper's Results section, and the active orbitals with their occupation numbers are shown in its Figure 3
electronic_structure_description: Singlet-triplet splitting dE(ts) = E(t) - E(s) in kJ/mol, CASPT2 with ANO basis (Dunning basis in parentheses): +2.4 (+2.1) - the singlet lies 2 kJ/mol below the triplet, i.e. the two are essentially degenerate. DFT/def2-TZVPP by contrast puts the triplet lowest: TPSS -16.0, TPSSh -15.5, B3LYP -19.0, M06-L -30.9. Both spin states are primarily Cu(II)-superoxide, differing only in spin coupling. Other: This species is expected to be the precursor to the other two intermediates. Going from the truncated model 1 to the larger model 2 decreases the stability of the triplet by 3-6 kJ/mol for B3LYP and TPSS. All valence electrons plus the Cu 3s3p semicore were correlated in CASPT2. Energies are in kJ/mol as reported, with the sign convention dE(ts) = E(triplet) - E(singlet), so a positive value means the singlet is lower. Values in parentheses are the Dunning-basis results. Structures are LPMO active-site models, so the row describes the model complex rather than an isolable compound.

method: state-averaged CASSCF with single-state CASPT2 (IPEA 0.25 au, imaginary shift 0.30 au), MC-PDFT with the tPBE functional and hybrid MC-PDFT with tPBE0 (25% CASSCF energy + 75% tPBE); ZFS from spin-orbit coupling via RASSI and SINGLE_ANISO

active_space_protocol: Active spaces were built up progressively from the smallest: (2,5) the metal nd shell alone - nd(z2) and nd(x2-y2) (the 'e' pair under pseudo-tetrahedral symmetry) plus nd(xy), nd(xz), nd(yz); (2,10) adds the correlating (n+1)d shell; (8,8) instead adds three metal-ligand t2 molecular orbitals to (2,5); (10,15) adds both the correlating d shell and the metal s bonding (sigma) and antibonding (sigma*) orbitals. For the first-row ions with 3d^m configurations the analogous series is (m,5), (m,10), (m+6,8) and (m+6,13). Active-space dependence of the results is minor, so the largest and most balanced space is the one reported; relative energies for all spaces are in ESI Tables S44-S70.
nroots_per_mult: 7 triplets and 9 singlets state-averaged

compound_name: QMspin carbene chemical space - approximately 8,000 diverse carbene scaffolds derived from QM9 (H, C, N, O, F)
geometry_source: carbene scaffolds combinatorially derived from the QM9 chemical space, optimized separately in the singlet and triplet states; spin gaps reported both vertically at each spin state's geometry (dE(s-t)//t and dE(s-t)//s) and adiabatically
method: state-averaged CASSCF over the two spin states with a (2e,2o) active space, followed by explicitly correlated MRCISD+Q-F12 (Davidson-corrected)
active_space_orbital_description: the two electrons in the two non-bonding orbitals of the divalent carbene carbon, denoted r and s; natural orbitals of the one-particle state-averaged density matrix in this space reproduce the chemical picture of the carbene lone pair and empty p orbital
active_space_protocol: (2,2) throughout - CASSCF state-averaged over the singlet and triplet, with the two non-bonding carbene orbitals active, then MRCISD+Q-F12 on that reference. The minimal space is deliberate: it is what allows the singlet's resonance stabilization to be measured directly as the mixing of two closed-shell configurations
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over the two spin states (one singlet, one triplet)
electronic_structure_description: A hard upper limit on the singlet-triplet gap emerges at about 30 kcal/mol across every carbene class in this chemical space, which the authors attribute to strong electron correlation. Within many individual classes the spin-gap ranges are much larger: over 100 kcal/mol vertically and over 60 kcal/mol adiabatically. The singlet ground state is described by two closed-shell configurations with coefficients cR and cS on the non-bonding orbitals r and s; their mixing is quantified by an entanglement angle theta = arctan(|cS|/|cR|) with cR >= cS, ranging from 0 degrees (weak resonance stabilization) to 45 degrees (maximum stabilization, two equally weighted configurations). The triplet-state bond angle at the carbene centre distributes around 130 degrees
Other: Carbene classes group into (a) sigma-electron-withdrawing, pi-electron-donating alpha-substituents such as oxo- and amino-carbenes, which strongly stabilize the singlet; (b) aliphatic and aromatic alpha-substituents such as vinyl-, alkynyl-, alkyl- and aryl-carbenes, which stabilize the triplet or give a near-zero gap; and (c) moderately sigma- and pi-withdrawing substituents such as cyano- and carbonyl-carbenes, where carbonyl-carbenes show strong conformational effects. For almost 90% of the initial candidates the divalent carbon was confirmed to have two well-localized non-bonding orbitals, i.e. to be a genuine carbene
reference_short: Schwilk, Tahchieva & von Lilienfeld, Large yet bounded: spin gap ranges in carbenes
notes: Metal-free organic compounds: metal_center = none, metal_ox_state / d_electron_count / ligand_set deliberately empty. This is ONE condensed row for a chemical-space study of about 8,000 carbenes and roughly 13,000 MRCI calculations, not one row per compound - the same treatment given to other benchmark-set papers in this database. Per-compound spin gaps live in the QMspin dataset released with the paper and are not transcribed here. The row is admissible under the bulk-table policy because both tests pass: the DOI genuinely sources the calculations (this paper performed them) and the active space is explicitly stated, unlike the Excited_states_energy.csv table that was rejected. compound_name, formula and point_group describe the space rather than a single molecule, by necessity.

geometry_source: ground-state geometry taken from earlier work, optimized at CASSCF(12,10)/6-311G*; excited-state minima and conical intersections optimized at MS-CASPT2
method: MS-CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0, imaginary level shift 0.2 au) as the reference level; SA-CASSCF, MRCIS, ADC(2) and TD-DFT assessed as cheaper alternatives
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VDZP for MS-CASPT2; cc-pVDZ-DK for SA-CASSCF and MRCIS; def2-TZVP for ADC(2); TZP for TD-DFT
active_space_orbital_description: nine pi/pi* orbitals, three lone-pair orbitals (nO1, nO2, nBr) and the sigma/sigma* pair of the C-Br bond
active_space_protocol: MS-CASPT2(20,14) is the production space - 9 pi/pi*, 3 lone pairs and the C-Br sigma/sigma* pair. Cheaper alternatives tested on the same geometry used SA-CASSCF(14,11)/cc-pVDZ-DK and an MRCIS(10,8) reference space. Either 9 singlet or 8 triplet states were included, a relatively large number needed to stabilize the active space

electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in eV (oscillator strength, character) at MS-CASPT2(20,14): S1 4.60 (0.30, pi4->pi1*); S2 4.92 (0.00, nO1->pi1*); S3 5.47 (0.00, pi4->sigma*CBr); S4 6.01 (0.03, pi3->pi1*); S5 6.23 (0.00, nO2->pi2*); S6 6.55 (0.00, nBr->sigma*CBr); S7 6.61 (0.00, nBr->pi1*); S8 7.08 (0.00, piBr->pi1*); T1 3.51 (pi4->pi1*). Experimental values for comparison: 4.66, 6.12, 7.20 eV for the observed singlets and 3.35 eV for T1. SA-CASSCF(14,11) by contrast puts S1 at 5.02 eV and MRCIS at 5.09 eV, both with zero oscillator strength and nO1->pi1* character - i.e. they misorder the bright state
Other: Three deactivation pathways follow from the three lowest excited states - the bright 1(pipi*), the dark 1(nO pi*) and a dissociative 1(pi sigma*). A barrierless path on 1(pipi*) reaches a conical intersection with S0; a second conical intersection interconverts 1(pipi*) into 1(nO), from which intersystem crossing to 3(pipi*) can occur; and above a barrier of at least 0.2 eV the molecule can cross from 1(pipi*) to 1(pi sigma*CBr), giving homolytic C-Br dissociation. MS-CASPT2 identifies relaxation to S0 as the most probable gas-phase pathway. The paper's purpose is partly to test whether cheaper methods could drive excited-state dynamics for this system

RS2C perturbation corrections lower the state energies but do not change the ordering. DFT-MRCI instead places B1u as S1, and since DFT-MRCI agrees with both ADC(2) and TDDFT, the authors conclude B1u is likely the true S1. 1B2u and 1B3g are characterised as primarily pi-pi* excitations, consistent with Amatatsu

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 7F0. geometry_source: optimized at RI-MP2/def2-TZVP in D3 symmetry with TURBOMOLE 6.5

compound_name: stoichiometric Li2O2 surface cluster with the departing O2 moiety (Li-air battery cathode during charging)

The authors' earlier MRCI work on the single vacancy found a complex set of closely spaced states driving geometry relaxation with carbon-carbon bond formation, and showed the state manifold to be significantly more complicated than previously anticipated, with avoided crossings between states

software: OpenMolcas and QCMaquis (DMRG, M = 1000 renormalized states); Gaussian 16 for the geometries; the authors' EDGA program for configuration selection
basis_set: ANO-L-VTZP on C, ANO-S-MB on H
active_space_orbital_description: all valence pi electrons and orbitals of the n-acene: ((4n+2)e, (4n+2)o)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1Ag; the triplet studied is 3B2u. S0-T1 gaps computed for n = 2-9 and reported only in Fig. 3 (no table): theory differs from experiment by around 0.07 eV for n = 2-5, and for n = 6-9 lies about 0.1 eV above the pp-RPA/B3LYP results of Yang et al. The gap shrinks monotonically with ring number and the ground state stays singlet throughout.
Other: Dynamic correlation is necessary: DMRG-CASCI with M = 1000 alone overestimates the S-T gaps, and only the ec-MRCISD+Q correction brings them near experiment. Experimental values track the adiabatic gaps more closely than the vertical ones.
reference_short: Luo, Ma, Wang, Ma, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2018)
notes: Mined from the arXiv OA text. The homologous acene series is condensed into one row (the active space is a formula in n, not a fixed number), following the treatment of the earlier polyacene-series row. active_space_nel/norb hold the symbolic (4n+2) because the paper states the space that way. S-T gap values appear only in a figure, so no numbers are transcribed. Two other systems in this paper: Cr2 (bare diatomic, excluded by the standing convention; (12e,12o) CASSCF start then (12e,42o) DMRG-CASCI, X2C/ANO-RCC-VQZP) and the Eu-BTBP(NO3)3 complex, recorded as row -b.

compound_name: O2-O2 van der Waals dimer - interaction of two rigid ground-state O2(3Sigma-g) monomers
geometry_source: rigid-rotor intermolecular grid: monomers held at re = 2.28 bohr, 1170 points computed for each spin state over the intermolecular coordinates (H/rectangular D2h, X, T-shape and skewed geometries all sampled)
method: CASSCF-based internally contracted MRCI+Q and CASPT2 for the interaction energies, counterpoise-corrected, with the asymptotic size-consistency residual at R = 70 bohr subtracted; combined with RCCSD(T) into the composite CC-MRCI and CC-PT2 surfaces
basis_set: 5s4p3d2f atomic natural orbital basis plus a (3s3p2d1f) bond-function set placed at the midpoint of the complex
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in eight active molecular orbitals correlating with the O2 pi shells
electronic_structure_description: The three spin states of the O2(3Sigma-g) + O2(3Sigma-g) system, S = 0, 1 and 2 (multiplicities 1, 3, 5), each on its own global surface. CC-PT2 and CC-MRCI give very similar singlet and triplet curves, CC-PT2 being slightly more attractive: well-depth differences of about 0.5 meV (4%) for the singlet and 0.3 meV (3%) for the triplet. Against the empirical Perugia potential the largest discrepancy is for the singlet, whose Perugia well is about 1.8 meV deeper than CC-PT2, with best agreement for the quintet. The triplet surface has its absolute minimum at the rectangular H geometry near R = 6 bohr; the quintet has a global minimum at the X geometry and a local minimum at a planar skewed structure.
Other: The size-consistency error is about an order of magnitude smaller for CASPT2 (about 50 meV before subtraction) than for MRCI. Davidson's correction was added to the MRCI energies. Triplet-singlet splittings are dominated by the (000), (448), (202), (224) and (6410) spherical-harmonic components, the (448) relevance tracing to the nodal character of the singly occupied pi_g monomer orbitals.
reference_short: Bartolomei et al., J. Chem. Phys. 133, 124311 (2010)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Four-atom van der Waals dimer, so in scope despite being built from two diatomics. ground_state_mult left empty: the three spin states are near-degenerate interaction surfaces and the paper reports splittings rather than naming a ground state for the complex. compound_name: formyl radical HCO and the H...CO transition state of the H + CO addition reaction
geometry_source: structures optimized at each correlated level (MP2, RCCSD, RCCSD(T), MRCI, MRCI+Q) with cc-pVXZ, X = D, T, Q; surfaces fit with SURVIB (26 points for the H...CO TS and HCO) and VIBROTN (9 points for CO)
method: internally contracted MRCI and Davidson-corrected MRCI+Q on a complete-active-space reference, compared against MP2, RCCSD and RCCSD(T); complete-basis-set limits extrapolated

active_space_orbital_description: complete active space of the valence electrons with the oxygen 2s orbital kept closed, giving 1204 configuration state functions
electronic_structure_description: Energetics of H + CO -> HCO rather than an excited-state manifold. The measured barrier is 2.0 +/- 0.4 kcal/mol, about 2 kcal/mol below the best computed value; the 0 K bond energies from measured enthalpies, 14.3 and 13.9 kcal/mol, agree well with MRCI+Q and RCCSD(T).

notes: Mined from the OA text. geometry_source: roughly 67 000 MRCI/cc-pVTZ energies fitted to a global surface; stationary-point configurations optimized at the MRCI level
method: multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) with the Davidson correction for quadruple excitations, used uniformly over the whole surface rather than stitching CCSD(T) and MRCI regions together
active_space_orbital_description: eight electrons in eight active orbitals (stated only as the size; the orbitals are not enumerated)
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state global surface rather than a state manifold. MRCI barrier heights differ from the earlier CCSD(T) values by roughly 1% or less; MRCI underestimates the H2CO dissociation energies relative to CCSD(T). Quasi-classical trajectories were run at a total energy of 36 233 cm-1 (103 kcal/mol) above the global minimum.

notes: Mined from the OA text. The whole surface uses one (8e,8o) MRCI+Q treatment, which is why a single row covers the isomers and dissociation channels rather than one row per stationary point. compound_name: NaFH reactive system (1A' ground state) for Na(3S) + HF(v,j) -> NaF + H, covering the van der Waals well and the late saddle point
point_group: Cs (all calculations performed within Cs symmetry)
geometry_source: 37 000 ab initio points spanning the interaction region and both the Na + HF and NaF + H asymptotes, fitted by three-dimensional cubic spline interpolation
method: internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (icMRCI+Q) on state-averaged CASSCF reference configuration state functions, the average taken with equal weights over the 1 2A' and 2 2A' states; about 2.0e6 contracted (6.6e7 uncontracted) configurations
active_space_orbital_description: seven electrons in eight valence orbitals: the 3s and 3p orbitals of Na, the 2p orbitals of F and the 1s orbital of H; inner orbitals constrained doubly occupied but fully optimized
electronic_structure_description: Ground doublet surface, with the CASSCF reference state-averaged over 1 2A' and 2 2A'. Energetics on the new surface: endoergicity dE = D0(HF) - D0(NaF) = 1.02 eV, against an experimental estimate of 0.87-0.93 eV; van der Waals well depth -0.082 eV relative to the Na(3S) + HF asymptote (the earlier TTCPP-B surface gives -0.074 eV); barrier height 1.002 eV relative to the same asymptote, well below TTCPP-B (1.270 eV) and the semiempirical surface (1.266 eV) and close to Lagana's corrected value (0.811 eV). The saddle point is later and less bent than on TTCPP-B, with theta(NaFH) near Lagana's 75 degrees.
Other: Equilibrium geometries and dissociation energies of the separated HF and NaF diatomics agree closely with experiment. The surface is smooth from asymptotic to interaction regions and so flat near the saddle point that the barrier is inconspicuous, matching earlier MRCI and MBPT(2) observations. Quantum wave-packet dynamics on the new surface improve agreement with measured rates for HF(v = 2), consistent with the earlier surface having overestimated the barrier.
reference_short: Yan, Tan, Lin, Shi et al., RSC Adv. (2023)
notes: Mined from the OA text (PMC). compound_name: N,N'-dimethylpiperazine radical cation (DMP+), mixed-valent charge-localized versus charge-delocalized structures, and the 3s-Rydberg state of neutral DMP
geometry_source: pre-generated pathway interpolating between the delocalized (D) and localized (L) structures; energies reported relative to the delocalized minimum
method: CASSCF and MRCI+Q using the CW-contracted CISD routine with Davidson size-consistency correction, run both state-specific and state-averaged (two lowest doublet states, equal weights); additional RASSCF calculations restricting holes in the doubly occupied and electrons in the virtual part of the active space to two and four respectively; non-orthogonal CI over three UHF solutions as a quasidiabatic basis for comparison
software: MOLPRO 2022.2 for all CASSCF-based work; Q-Chem 5.0 for the NOCI; TURBOMOLE, ORCA and CP2K for the supporting calculations
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ (aug-cc-pVDZ/C auxiliary sets for the density-fitted steps)
active_space_orbital_description: 11 electrons in 12 orbitals, taken identically to the earlier study: the two nitrogen lone pairs, their respective double-shell orbitals, the two C-C bonding orbitals and the two N-Me bonding orbitals together with the corresponding antibonding orbitals
active_space_protocol: (11,12) as in the earlier work; a RASSCF variant restricting the hole and electron counts to two and four, then a larger (19,20) space adding the bonding and antibonding orbitals of all sigma C-N bonds
electronic_structure_description: Two lowest doublet states of DMP+ along the delocalized-to-localized pathway, energies in eV relative to the delocalized minimum (curves in Fig. 1, not tabulated in the text). The apparent barrier separating localized and delocalized minima reported in earlier MRCI work is shown to be an artifact of unphysical curve crossings of the state-specific reference wave functions: state-averaged MRCI removes the discontinuity, leaving no barrier and hence no localized minimum for the bare cation. In the observed 3s-type Rydberg state of neutral DMP, by contrast, the Rydberg electron binds more strongly to a localized positive charge distribution and does produce a localized minimum, matching the experimental increase of about 0.11 eV in the Rydberg electron binding energy from the delocalized to the localized structure.
Other: CASSCF Mulliken spin densities at the hole-bearing nitrogen, taken from the first-order density matrix of the doublet ground state, track the localization along the path and are reported alongside the energies. Per-state electronic energies are in Supplementary Data 3.
reference_short: Reimann et al., Nat. Commun. 15, 293 (2024)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Metal-free organic radical cation, so metal_center is 'none'. active_space_nel/norb hold the primary (11,12) space used for the reported CASSCF and MRCI+Q curves; the RASSCF-only (19,20) variant is recorded in the protocol rather than the numeric columns. Energies live in Fig. 1 and Supplementary Data 3, so no per-point numbers are transcribed - only the 0.11 eV experimental binding-energy shift stated in the text.

geometry_source: global grid in Jacobi coordinates covering the H + Li2 and Li + LiH arrangements, fitted to a diabatic surface

active_space_orbital_description: of the 7 electrons in the system, 4 sit in 2 closed-shell orbitals (2 A' + 0 A''), leaving 3 electrons in the valence space across 13 active orbitals (10 A' + 3 A''); 319 external orbitals (192 A' + 127 A''). The MCSCF function comprises 570 determinants and 1014 intermediate states; in the MRCI step the 2 closed orbitals become core, giving 705 202 contracted configurations (420 internal, 28 548 single-external, 676 234 double-external)
electronic_structure_description: Three lowest adiabatic states of Li2H mapped globally, with the lowest two transformed to a diabatic representation - the first accurate diabatic surface for nonadiabatic H + Li2 dynamics. The reaction is exothermic with relatively deep wells along the reaction path, and the conical intersection geometry lies near the bottom of the potential well.
Other: Earlier surfaces the authors compare against: Siegbahn and Schaefer (SCF + full CI, 1975), Kim and Herschbach (well depth 3.812 eV), Maniero et al. (full CI, 394 points, 6-311G(2df,2pd), giving a barrierless exothermic H + Li2(X1Sigma-g+) -> Li + LiH(X1Sigma+) releasing 1.474 eV), Skomorowski et al. (CCSD(T), conical intersection reported), Song et al. (CASSCF/MRCI, 3726 points) and Yuan et al. (CASSCF/MRCI-F12, 29 842 points, cc-pVTZ).
reference_short: Yin, Gao, Cao, Li, Wang et al., RSC Adv. (2020)
notes: Mined from the OA text (PMC). Triatomic, so in scope. The active-space numbers are the paper's own decomposition - 7 total electrons, 4 in two closed-shell orbitals, 3 active across 13 orbitals - transcribed rather than re-derived. Multiplicity fields left empty: the paper labels the surfaces by adiabatic state index and Cs symmetry rather than by spin multiplicity. Well depths and reaction energies quoted are those the paper attributes to earlier surfaces; its own numbers are presented as figures.

compound_name: HAsO (and its deuterated isotopologue DAsO) - X1A' and A1A'' states behind the single-vibronic-level emission spectra
geometry_source: geometries optimized separately for each state at CASSCF/NEVPT2, RSPT2-F12 and MRCI-F12 (and CCSD(T*)-F12b for the closed-shell X1A'); potential energy functions then built from 334 and 320 CASSCF/MRCI-F12/CVQZ-F12 energies for X1A' and A1A'' over the ranges 1.2-2.8 A in r(HAs), 67-157 and 55-145 degrees in theta(HAsO), and 1.4-2.5 / 1.5-2.6 A in r(AsO)
method: CASSCF with a full valence active space followed by MRCI-F12, RSPT2-F12 and NEVPT2; CCSD(T*)-F12a/b for the closed-shell ground state. Some MRCI-F12 calculations correlate the As 3d10 core (core,4,1) on top of the frozen-core CASSCF full-valence orbitals, with the geminal Slater exponent raised from 1.0 to 1.5 as recommended for core-valence F12 work
basis_set: F12-designed basis sets (see the paper's Table 1); for NEVPT2, aug-cc-pVQZ on O and H with the ECP10MDF effective core potential and aug-cc-pVQZ-PP on As. For the core-correlated MRCI-F12, uncontracted tight 4d (12.0, 4.0, 1.3333333, 0.444444), 2f (14.0, 6.0) and 2g (9.6, 2.4) functions were added on As, giving 278 contracted functions for HAsO (denoted CVQZ-F12)
relativistic_treatment: ECP10MDF effective core potential on arsenic (accounting for As 1s2 2p2 2p6)
active_space_orbital_description: full valence active space at the CASSCF level (stated as 'full valence', with no (nel,norb) pair given). Sizes of the resulting MRCI-F12 expansions: 1 516 432 contracted / 138 334 504 uncontracted configurations with the default frozen core, rising to 15 388 677 / 3 175 152 080 with the As 3d10 electrons active
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X1A'; the emitting state is A1A'', an open-shell singlet for which single-reference methods such as B3LYP and CCSD(T) are inadequate. MRCI-F12 gives a T0 (adiabatic transition energy with zero-point correction) in good agreement with the experimental value and markedly better than the other multireference methods tried here or earlier computed values; T0 values of 11731 and 14225 cm-1 (1.454 and 1.764 eV) are quoted from the earlier level of theory being improved upon.
Other: Anharmonic vibrational wavefunctions from the fitted potential energy functions gave Franck-Condon factors including anharmonicity and Duschinsky rotation, which reproduce the vibrational structure of the observed single-vibronic-level emission spectra of both HAsO and DAsO but suggest a loss of intensity in part of the spectrum.
reference_short: Simulation of the single-vibronic-level emission spectra of HAsO and DAsO (2016)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic, in scope. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the paper specifies the space only as 'full valence' and never writes an (n,m) pair, so nothing is derived. The 11731 and 14225 cm-1 T0 values in the text belong to the earlier calculations the paper improves on; the paper's own MRCI-F12 T0 is described as agreeing with experiment but the number sits in a table that is not reliably readable in the extracted text. DAsO is the deuterated isotopologue of the same species and shares this row.

compound_name: HOF / FOH system (hypofluorous acid and its isomers) - global potential energy surfaces for the F(2P) + OH reaction
geometry_source: global surfaces from 8069 ab initio geometries covering the reaction channels, minima and transition states; stationary-point geometries and energies also computed with AVTZ, AVQZ, AV5Z and extrapolated to the complete basis set limit
method: state-averaged CASSCF (SA-CASSCF) references followed by internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (icMRCI+Q); the state average covers 6 states of 1A', 5 of 1A'', 5 of 3A' and 5 of 3A''
basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ (AVnZ) with n = T, Q, 5 and CBS extrapolation
active_space_orbital_description: the active space is formed by the molecular orbitals deriving from the valence atomic orbitals (a full-valence space, stated in prose without an (n,m) pair)
active_space_protocol: the number of state-averaged states had to be optimized: including only the states correlating with reactants and products left CI energies unstable in regions with avoided crossings against highly excited states, so states from other asymptotes were added, settling on 6 1A' + 5 1A'' + 5 3A' + 5 3A''
electronic_structure_description: Singlet and triplet A' and A'' surfaces for F(2P) + OH, computed globally so that reaction channels, minima and transition states are described on the same footing. The deep minimum corresponds to the bent HOF structure. Energy differences between the AVTZ, AVQZ and AV5Z results are of the order of 0.01 eV.
Other: Doctoral thesis (in Spanish) that also treats the related F + H2O system and compares against earlier semiempirical three-centre surfaces; an earlier branching ratio HF(v'=0):HF(v'=1) = 0.86:0.14 for F + OH is quoted from the literature. Experimental reference data cited include the HOF and DOF fundamental vibrational frequencies (3578.5, 1354.8, 889.0 cm-1 for HOF; 2643.5, 1003.9, 891.1 cm-1 for DOF).
reference_short: Superficies de energia potencial MRCI y dinamica de las reacciones quimicas F(2P) + OH (doctoral thesis, 2005)
notes: Mined from the OA text; the document is a Spanish-language doctoral thesis, so quoted phrasing is translated. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the space is described only as the molecular orbitals arising from the valence atomic orbitals, with no (n,m) pair anywhere. ground_state_mult left empty - the work maps reactive surfaces of both spin manifolds rather than assigning a ground term. electronic_structure_description: The three lowest adiabatic states of the N(2D) + H2 insertion system, mapped globally in Jacobi coordinates and fitted to accurate surfaces for scattering work.

notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic, in scope; the H2 fragment is an asymptote only. active_space_nel left empty on purpose: the paper states 9 electrons in total with one closed orbital, which would make 7 active electrons by subtraction, but it never writes the active electron count itself, so nothing is derived - the verbatim decomposition is kept in the orbital description. geometry_source: geometry optimized at CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ; the multireference scan follows dissociation of one He-He bond from that structure
method: MRCI+Q (multireference configuration interaction with the Davidson correction) on full CASSCF wave functions for the dissociation scan, alongside CCSD(T) optimizations, AQCC benchmarking and spin-coupled generalized valence bond (SCGVB) bonding analysis
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ for the MRCI+Q and SCGVB scans and the CCSD(T) optimizations; aug-cc-pVQZ for the AQCC benchmark
active_space_orbital_description: full CASSCF wave functions (the paper says 'full CASSCF' without writing an (n,m) pair); the complementary SCGVB analysis uses four one-electron full-valence orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell dication. The MRCI+Q scan of one He-He bond dissociation reveals a metastable profile with an energy barrier of 16.1 kcal/mol, which the authors associate with lifetimes on the order of hundreds of seconds. MRCI+Q and SCGVB give similar dissociation profiles, relative to the CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ optimized structure.
Other: Found in an exploratory screen of 270 doubly charged closed-shell triatomic molecules; the authors state a triatomic helium dication had never previously been established. Interference energy analysis decomposes the bonding into quasi-classical, interference (covalent) and inter-bond exchange contributions, all referenced to a 4.0 A separation.
reference_short: Chemical Aristocracy: He3 dication and analogous noble-gas-exclusive species (2024)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic, in scope. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the paper specifies the reference only as 'full CASSCF' with no (n,m) pair. Multiplicity fields empty - the species is treated as a closed-shell dication with no state manifold reported. Analogous heavier noble-gas species are predicted in the same paper but their multireference treatment is not separately specified, so only He3(2+) gets a row.

compound_name: linear [n]-acene series, n = 2-9 (naphthalene through nonacene) - La and doubly excited (DE) states
geometry_source: UB3LYP-optimized geometries (the same functional used for the natural-orbital occupation analysis)

software: ORCA 5.0.1 (CASSCF and NEVPT2, RI-JK approximation); the DFT/MRCI software for the DFT/MRCI comparison

active_space_orbital_description: pi active spaces ranging from 8 electrons in 8 pi orbitals (8,8) up to 14 electrons in 14 orbitals (14,14), the size chosen per system (further detail in the Supplementary Materials)

Other: Di- and poly-radical character quantified by the yi descriptors from spin-projected natural-orbital occupation numbers computed at UHF and UB3LYP levels, with i = 0 the diradical and i = 1 the tetraradical measure; the paper's question is how that radical character shifts the DE state relative to La.
