compound_name: LiCaF triatomic - ground-state surface for the Li + CaF -> Ca + LiF reaction under cold conditions
geometry_source: about 11 000 geometries lying below 4.5 eV relative to the global minimum, fitted analytically with a many-body expansion in the three internuclear distances
method: state-averaged CASSCF over the 1 1A', 1 3A' and 1 1A'' states followed by internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q); coupled-channel quantum reactive scattering in hyperspherical coordinates on the fitted surface
basis_set: aug-cc-pVQZ on Li and F; cc-pwCVQZ-PP on Ca, whose core electrons are described by a pseudopotential
active_space_orbital_description: full valence space: 10 active electrons in 9 active orbitals, comprising the 2s and 2s2p orbitals of Li and F and the 4s4p orbitals of Ca; the Li and F 1s orbitals and the Ca 3s3p orbitals are closed in the CASSCF and cored in the MRCI
electronic_structure_description: Ground singlet surface of the reactive system, with the CASSCF state-averaged over 1 1A', 1 3A' and 1 1A''. The reaction populates several low-lying vibrational levels and many rotational levels of the LiF product.
Other: Quantum scattering on the fitted surface shows the reaction is inefficient in the 1-100 mK regime, so cold Li atoms can sympathetically cool CaF rather than destroy it. An exothermicity of about -4440 cm-1 is quoted from the literature for the analogous process.
reference_short: da Silva et al., The Li + CaF -> Ca + LiF chemical reaction under cold conditions (2023)
notes: Mined from the OA text (accepted manuscript). Triatomic reactive system, so in scope; CaF and LiF appear only as asymptotic diatomics and get no rows. ground_state_mult left empty - the surface is the ground state of the reactive system and the paper does not assign a ground term.

compound_name: LiH2+ reactive system - singlet and triplet surfaces for H + LiH+ collisions (H/H+ transfer and abstraction channels)
geometry_source: grids in Jacobi coordinates over the r and R vectors spanning the reactive arrangements
method: CASSCF references (equal weights within each state symmetry) followed by internally contracted, explicitly correlated MRCI-F12; quasi-classical trajectory cross sections computed on the fitted surfaces
basis_set: cc-pVQZ-F12; no basis-set superposition correction applied, the F12 treatment being taken as effectively at the basis-set limit
active_space_orbital_description: all four electrons in 16 active orbitals (10 a' and 6 a''), used for the six states considered
electronic_structure_description: Six states treated: 1,2 1A', 1 1A'', 1,2 3A' and 1 3A''. Sizes of the resulting ic-MRCI-F12 expansions, contracted (uncontracted): about 0.81e6 (1.3e6) for 1,2 1A'; 0.37e6 (1.3e6) for 1 1A''; 0.80e6 (2.0e6) for 1,2 3A'; 0.42e6 (1.9e6) for 1 3A''.
Other: The chemically most important channels examined are H or H+ transfer/abstraction plus atom exchange; at least one channel is reported to proceed without energy barriers.
reference_short: Potential energy surfaces for singlet and triplet states of the LiH2+ system, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 25, 28052 (2023)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic cation, in scope; LiH+ is an asymptote only. ground_state_mult left empty - the paper maps both spin manifolds as reactive surfaces without assigning a ground term. Barrier and stationary-point values sit in Table 3, whose columns are not reliably readable in the extracted text, so no numbers are transcribed from it.

compound_name: N3+ triatomic radical cation - photodissociation to N2 + N+
geometry_source: Jacobi grid (R, r, theta) with r(N1-N2) in [1.55, 4.00] a0, R (N3 to the N1N2 centre of mass) in [1.5, 10.0] a0 and theta from a 7-point Legendre quadrature over 0-180 degrees; a 2d surface at r(NN) = 2.25 a0 was also built for the 2 3A'' state. Energies referenced to the N2 + N+ asymptote
method: MRCISD+Q (multireference CI with singles, doubles and the Davidson correction) on state-averaged CASSCF reference wave functions, the average taken over 8 states - the two lowest of each of 3A'' (ground), 1A', 1A'' and 3A' symmetry
active_space_orbital_description: full valence active space (stated in prose; no (n,m) pair given)
electronic_structure_description: Ground state is of 3A'' symmetry. Eight states enter the state averaging: the two lowest of 3A'', 1A', 1A'' and 3A' each. The photodissociation products are N2 + N+, which set the zero of energy.
reference_short: Patra, San Vicente Veliz, Koner et al., Photodissociation dynamics of N3+ (2022)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic cation, in scope. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the active space is described only as 'the full valence space', with no (n,m) pair anywhere in the text.

compound_name: F-H-Br collinear system - potential energy surfaces for the F + HBr / FH + Br reactive arrangement in linear geometry
point_group: C2v labels used for the linear arrangement (A1, B1, B2, A2 irreducible representations)
geometry_source: surfaces scanned in the collinear (linear) geometry; the figure showing the six SA-MCSCF states is at fixed R2 = 3.30 a0
method: dynamically weighted state-averaged MCSCF (SA-MCSCF, decay coefficient beta^-1 = 2.78 eV) over six states - the two lowest of each of 2A1, 2B1 and 2B2, charge-transfer states included because the transition-state region demands them - followed by explicitly correlated MRCI-F12 for the three lowest states 1 2A1, 1 2B1 and 1 2B2
active_space_orbital_description: 8 active orbitals (4 A1, 2 B1, 2 B2, 0 A2), with one valence orbital of A1 symmetry closed to excitation to keep the orbital ordering consistent in Molpro and avoid discontinuities in the surfaces
electronic_structure_description: Six doublet states enter the state averaging; the MRCI-F12 treatment is restricted to the three lowest, 1 2A1, 1 2B1 and 1 2B2, of which 1 2B1 and 1 2B2 are degenerate everywhere. States 1 2A1 and 1 2B1 cross, while the same-symmetry pair 1 2B1 and 2 2B1 shows an avoided crossing; these conical intersection seams make the surfaces non-smooth.
Other: The authors note the accuracy limit is the size of the active space rather than basis-set convergence: reaching 0.1 kcal/mol would require adding the F 3s and 3p orbitals, which in turn forces all Br 4d orbitals into the space and makes the calculation impractical.
reference_short: Ab initio calculations of F-H-Br system with linear geometry, Current Chemistry Letters 5, 1-6 (2016)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Triatomic reactive system, in scope. active_space_nel left empty: the paper gives only the orbital count and symmetry breakdown, never the active electron count. Bond-length and energy tables are not transcribed - the extracted text does not render them reliably.

compound_name: nitrosyl chloride ClNO - 1 and 2 1A' surfaces for photodissociation of the B band
point_group: Cs (states of A' or A'' symmetry)
geometry_source: 2464 ab initio points on a grid with r(ClN) every 0.25 bohr from 2.75 to 6.0 bohr then every 0.5 bohr to 10.0 bohr, and bond angle theta every 10 degrees from 20 to 170 degrees; fitted with 3D cubic splines
method: CASSCF state-averaged over the first three 1A' states, followed by MRCI (singles and doubles) with the Davidson correction using relaxed reference functions; all generated configuration state functions retained. MCTDH wavepacket dynamics run on the fitted surfaces
software: MOLPRO 2010 for the electronic structure; the Heidelberg MCTDH package for the dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: full valence active space, with the N and O 1s and the Cl 1s, 2s and 2p orbitals kept doubly occupied but not frozen; for r(ClN) beyond 6.0 bohr the occupation of the orbital corresponding to Cl 3s had to be restricted to two to prevent erroneous orbital reordering
electronic_structure_description: Ignoring spin-orbit coupling there are 12 states correlating to the ground-state fragments; surfaces were built for the 1 and 2 1A' states. The 2 1A' state (the B band) absorbs between 280 and 400 nm (3-4.5 eV) with a peak at 335 nm (3.72 eV).
Other: Vibrational and rotational distributions of the NO fragment computed on the 2 1A' surface and compared with 3D-imaging measurements; earlier experiments at 355 nm gave bell-shaped NO(v = 0) rotational distributions peaking near j = 46 or 43.
reference_short: Photodissociation of ClNO in the 2 1A' state, ChemPhysChem (2013)
notes: Mined from the OA text (PMC). Triatomic, in scope; NO appears only as a photofragment. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the space is specified as 'full valence' with the listed core orbitals doubly occupied, but no (n,m) pair is given. The Dunning basis is named without its cardinal number in the extracted text, so it is recorded as stated.

compound_name: borirane and its isomerization products - 2-bora-propa-1,3-diyl (A), vinylborane (B) and methyl methylideneborane (E)
geometry_source: stationary points optimized at the correlated levels used; the structure of 2-bora-prop-1,3-diyl (A) was also optimized at CASPT2/cc-pVTZ with analytic gradients, with harmonic frequencies from finite differences of those gradients
method: internally contracted multiconfiguration-reference configuration interaction with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q) on CASSCF references, alongside CCSD(T) (RHF-RCCSD(T) with partial spin projection for open-shell species) and CASPT2 for compound A
basis_set: correlation-consistent sets up to quadruple-zeta quality; cc-pVTZ for the CASPT2 optimization of A
active_space_orbital_description: the default reference is CASSCF(2,2) - two electrons in the HOMO and LUMO. For 2-bora-prop-1,3-diyl (compound A) a larger space of two electrons in the three pi orbitals, CASSCF(2,3), was used, and the same (2,3) space was used for its CASPT2 treatment
active_space_protocol: (2,2) HOMO/LUMO reference for most species; (2,3) with the three pi orbitals for the 2-bora-prop-1,3-diyl biradical A
electronic_structure_description: Borirane is isoelectronic with the cyclopropyl cation but resists electrocyclic ring opening. Formation of the ring-opened 2-bora-propa-1,3-diyl A is endothermic by roughly 15 kcal/mol, and A collapses back to borirane almost without barrier (0.2 kcal/mol). The vinylborane isomer B is more stable than borirane, with a formation barrier of 36-38 kcal/mol. Methyl methylideneborane E is only slightly less stable than B but reachable only over barriers of at least 60 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Krasowska, Bettinger, Computational study of the isomerization reactions of borirane (2018)
notes: Mined from the OA text. Metal-free organic/organoboron system, so metal_center is 'none'. active_space_nel/norb record the (2,3) space used for the biradical A and its CASPT2 treatment, with the more common (2,2) HOMO/LUMO reference kept in the protocol and orbital description. Isomers condensed into one row since they are one interconverting C2H5B system studied with the same protocol. Multiplicity fields left empty - the text discusses biradical character but does not label the states by multiplicity in the extracted passages.

compound_name: 18-electron triatomic sulfur-nitrogen anions N2S-, NSO- and NS2- (isomers SNS-, NSS-, etc.), with the isoelectronic SO2, S2O, O3 and S3 included for comparison
geometry_source: all stationary points optimized at MRCI-SD/def2-QZVP, with numerical MRCI-SD Hessians used to confirm minima and transition states
method: full valence CASSCF to generate starting orbitals, followed by MRCI-SD for geometries, energies, Hessians and absorption properties; PBE0/PBE1PBE density functional calculations run in parallel for comparison; electron density analysed with Molden2AIM and AIMAll on the MRCI-SD natural orbitals
active_space_orbital_description: full valence complete active space (stated as such; no (n,m) pair given)
electronic_structure_description: Most of the investigated 18-electron triatomics are well described by a single-configuration wave function; the exceptions are the SSS (6a) and OOO (7a) isomers, which show some diradical character. Computed MRCI-SD/def2-QZVP absorption maxima are 342 nm for SNS- (2a) and 327 nm for NSS- (2b), against PBE0/def2-QZVP values in acetonitrile of 353 and 333 nm. These support formation of SNS- on electrochemical or chemical reduction of SSNS-, which had been inferred from bands at 375 nm in acetonitrile and 390 nm in liquid ammonia. SNS- is less stable than NSS-.
Other: Optimized geometries for OSO (4a), OSS (5b) and OOO (7a) agree with experimental data. Bonding is qualitatively similar across the series, with the quantitative differences traced to bond polarization by electron-density analysis.
reference_short: Computational investigations of 18-electron triatomic sulfur-nitrogen anions (2018)
notes: Mined from the OA text (self-archived version). Triatomics throughout, so in scope. One row for the isomer series since a single full-valence protocol covers all of them. active_space_nel/norb left empty: the space is stated only as 'full valence complete active space' with no (n,m) pair, and it necessarily differs between the members.

compound_name: decapentane (linear polyene) - active-space scaling benchmark for approximate fourth-order NEVPT
method: approximate fourth-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT4), compared against NEVPT2, NEVPT3, a single MRCEPA(0) iteration and MRCCSD; the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion truncated after the quadratic commutator, with no dropped terms and no RDM approximations
active_space_orbital_description: pi active spaces of the polyene, scanned from CAS(2,2) up to CAS(10,10) to map cost scaling; the largest, CAS(10,10), is the reference point for the timing comparisons
active_space_protocol: CAS(2,2), then progressively larger spaces up to CAS(10,10), used to trace the scaling of NEVPT4 against NEVPT2, NEVPT3 and MRCEPA(0)

metal_ox_state: II and III across the series (Fe(III)-NTA for the spin-state study)
ligand_set: nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA), an industrially relevant chelating agent

method: DMRG-CASSCF with DMRG-NEVPT2 and MC-PDFT (translated functionals)
active_space_orbital_description: For Mn(II)-NTA and Fe(III)-NTA the largest 'SOE union 3d4d' spaces comprise 11 electrons in 16 orbitals. The largest active space in the whole study is 49 electrons in 36 orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Several families of active space are compared: singly-occupied-plus-empty (SOE) spaces, SOE extended by the 3d and 4d shells (SOE union 3d4d), and larger spaces reaching 49 electrons in 36 orbitals. DMRG-NEVPT2 used a maximum bond dimension of 1000, reduced to 600 for the largest (49,36) spaces. The reported outcome is that adding the 4d shell to the SOE space gave NO improvement over the SOE spaces themselves - a documented case where enlargement does not help.
multiplicities_studied: spin states of the Fe(III)-NTA complex across the accessible manifold
electronic_structure_description: Assessment of electronic-structure methods against two industrially motivated properties of the chelating agent NTA: its selectivity across six different first-row transition-metal ions, and the spin-state energetics of its Fe(III) complex. Active spaces compared are the singly-occupied-plus-empty (SOE) family, SOE extended by the 3d and 4d shells, and spaces up to 49 electrons in 36 orbitals. The reported result is that the 3d4d extension gives NO improvement over the plain SOE spaces - a documented case where enlarging the active space does not help. DMRG-NEVPT2 used a maximum bond dimension of 1000, reduced to 600 for the largest (49,36) spaces.
reference_short: Chelate Complexes of 3d Transition Metal Ions—A Challenge for Electronic-Structure Methods?

method: N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) on a CASSCF reference, used for full geometry optimization; energies also at CCSD(T)/CBS(T-Q)
software: ORCA 5.0.1 (TD-DFT in Gaussian 16; NBO 6 for the NBO analysis)

electronic_structure_description: Singlet ground state with the triplet 17.9 kcal/mol higher (CCSD(T)/CBS(T-Q)). The Z isomer is preferred over E by 12.6 kcal/mol, and the inversion transition state is essentially isoenergetic with the E carbene, so E would be unobservable in matrix isolation. Z isomer: H-C-N carbene angle 125 deg, C-N 1.23 A (between the C=N double-bond value of 1.27 A and the C-N triple-bond limit of 1.14 A), against 106 deg and 1.31 A in the parent aminomethylene; C-N stretch blue-shifted by more than 300 cm-1. Dipole moments at NEVPT2: 3.36 D (Z) versus 5.29 D (E). The sigma* N-I orbital is the LUMO; NBO gives 372 kcal/mol for donation of the carbene lone pair into sigma*(N-I). CASSCF/def2-TZVPP natural occupation numbers of the sigma and sigma* N-X orbitals are fractional, showing partial multireference character; T1 diagnostic only slightly above 0.02.
reference_short: Medvedko, Bhagat, Wagner, sigma-Resonance Stabilization of Aminomethylene by N-Halogenation, J. Comput. Chem.
notes: The (6e,5o) space is stated but its orbital composition is not, so active_space_orbital_description is left empty; the paper does identify sigma and sigma*(N-X) among the active orbitals through their fractional occupations. The ring-opening and ring-puckering conical intersections both have degenerate S0/S1, the opening CI with pi sigma* character and the puckering CI retaining pi pi*. Chlorine substitution lowers the S1 energy at the FC point, widening the S1-S2 gap, and pushes the relaxation time well above 100 fs - substantially slower than furan, which is favourable for the temporal resolution of ultrafast electron diffraction.

Comparison methods: DMRG-CASPT2(12e,28o) 1.610 eV / 1.681 A / 480 cm-1; MR-AQCC(12e,12o) 1.355 eV / 1.685 A / 459 cm-1; FP-AFQMC 1.63(5) eV. electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in vacuum at DMRG-SC-NEVPT2: 1 1Bu 3.86 eV, 2 1Ag 4.66 eV, against an experimental 1Bu value of 3.69 eV from fluorescence extrapolated to n_solv = 1, and literature DMRG/PPP (3.52, 3.91, 3.751, 3.57 eV) and SAC-CI results. compound_name: geometry-optimization test set: acrolein, benzene, benzyne (singlet and triplet), PSB3 (penta-2,4-dieniminium cation, rhodopsin chromophore model), pHBI (para-hydroxybenzylideneimidazolin-5-one anion, GFP chromophore model) and porphine; plus LiF and 1,2,4-pyrazine as gradient-accuracy tests
geometry_source: ground-state geometries optimized with the new SC-NEVPT2 and PC-NEVPT2 analytical gradients; CASSCF and single-state CASPT2 geometries optimized for comparison (real level shift 0.2 Eh in CASPT2). Cartesian coordinates in the Supporting Information
method: single-state analytical gradients for strongly contracted (SC) and partially contracted (PC) NEVPT2, with density fitting and a Z-vector/Lagrangian formulation requiring reduced density matrix derivatives up to fourth order
software: in-house NEVPT2 analytical-gradient program interfaced with BAGEL
basis_set: cc-pVTZ with the corresponding JKFIT density-fitting basis throughout (cc-pVDZ for the porphine CASPT2 comparison; SVP for the analytical-vs-numerical gradient tests)
active_space_protocol: one active space per molecule: acrolein (6,5); benzene (6,6); benzyne (2,2); PSB3 (6,6); pHBI (4,3); porphine (4,4); LiF (4,6); 1,2,4-pyrazine (6,6)
electronic_structure_description: RMS distances (A) from the PC-NEVPT2 geometry to the SC-NEVPT2 / CASSCF / CASPT2 geometries, cc-pVTZ: acrolein 0.005 / 0.027 / 0.006; benzene (SC did not converge) / 0.005 / 0.002; PSB3 0.004 / 0.033 / 0.007; pHBI 0.001 / 0.045 / 0.009; porphine (SC did not converge) / 0.028 / 0.032 (the porphine CASPT2 used cc-pVDZ; with matched cc-pVDZ the PC-NEVPT2/CASPT2 RMS difference is 0.001 A). NEVPT2 geometries are 2 to 5 times closer to CASPT2 than to CASSCF. Benzyne singlet-triplet splitting including geometry relaxation: 3.36 kcal/mol, 0.30 kcal/mol smaller than the previously reported unrelaxed value. RMS errors between analytical and numerical gradients (SVP), SC-NEVPT2 / PC-NEVPT2: LiF 2.39e-6 / 3.01e-6; acrolein 3.44e-6 / 3.36e-6; 1,2,4-pyrazine 1.28e-6 / 1.29e-6; benzene 1.69e-3 / 7.96e-7; distorted benzene 1.00e-5 / 7.89e-7 a.u. Timings for one PC-NEVPT2 gradient step on 36 cores: acrolein 5.63 s (176 basis functions), benzyne 13.1 s (236), benzene 20.6 s (264), PSB3 30.76 s (292), pHBI 77.96 s (518), porphine 467 s (916).
reference_short: Park, Analytical Gradient Theory for Strongly Contracted (SC) and Partially Contracted (PC) N-Electron Valence State Perturbation Theory (NEVPT2)
notes: Method paper condensed into one row over its test set; the per-molecule spaces are in active_space_protocol so nel/norb are left empty. The central finding is that SC-NEVPT2 analytical gradients are numerically unstable because the SC-NEVPT2 energy is not invariant to rotations among inactive orbitals: they fail exactly where inactive orbitals are degenerate by symmetry (benzene, porphine) and recover when the symmetry is broken (1,2,4-pyrazine, distorted benzene). PC-NEVPT2 is invariant and converged in every case.

compound_name: polyene C32H34 (PE-32) and the polyethylene glycol biradical .O-C32H64-O. (PEG-32)
point_group: C1 enforced (point-group symmetry not exploitable by the implementation)
geometry_source: linear extended chains (used to display pseudo-density matrix sparsity)
method: Laplace-transformed partially contracted NEVPT2 (PC-NEVPT2) formulated in the atomic and active molecular orbital basis, with a minimax numerical quadrature; Koopmans matrices from DMRG n-particle reduced density matrices
software: MOLCAS for the zeroth-order CASSCF orbitals; QCMaquis for the DMRG n-RDMs through the relmrpt2 module (a locally modified DMRG-NEVPT2 module); the Laplace-transformed AO/active-MO PC-NEVPT2 pilot implementation is integrated into the Kramers-restricted two-component AO-MP2 code of a development version of DIRAC; InteRest for the two-electron integrals
basis_set: SVP, with the 1s orbitals of C and O frozen
active_space_orbital_description: PE-32: eight active valence MOs delocalized over the whole conjugated pi system. PEG-32: the 10 electrons and six 2p orbitals of the two terminal O atoms, localized at the chain ends, with natural occupation numbers (2.00, 2.00, 2.00, 2.00, 1.00, 1.00)
electronic_structure_description: Used to show that the active pseudo-density matrices P[-1] and P[+1] are far sparser than the core and virtual pseudo-densities. For PE-32 the two active pseudo-densities are very similar, peaking along the diagonal of the C-C blocks, and no s-type basis function contributes to the pi active orbitals by symmetry. For PEG-32 the active pseudo-densities are localized on the O atoms, and P[-1] has far more significant elements than P[+1], as expected from the natural occupations - only basis functions with sizable coefficients in the two singly occupied active MOs matter for P[+1]. Together with the R^-6 decay of the [0], [-1] and [+1] energy terms this is the argument for a reduced- or linearly scaling AO-basis implementation.
reference_short: Helmich-Paris & Knecht, Laplace-transformed multi-reference second-order perturbation theories in the atomic and active molecular orbital basis
notes: No energies are reported for these two systems; they serve as sparsity demonstrations. Two molecules condensed into one row, spaces in active_space_protocol.

electronic_structure_description: Benchmark system chosen so that deterministic FCI results are still available for comparison. The distribution of the normalised importance measure chi_ij = Ci* Cj / |<Psi|Psi>| for sampled determinant pairs spans six orders of magnitude, mostly concentrated between 1e-8 and 1e-3, with most contributions of order 1e-6; this is what makes sparse importance sampling of the 4-RDM viable. Stochastic promotion ramps were run with chi_min at 1e-9, 1e-8 and 1e-7 and chi_max at each order of magnitude from 1e-9 to 1e-3, giving a significant speedup with no significant loss of NEVPT2 accuracy relative to the deterministic result even at this relatively small active space.

The 1A1g singlet is preferentially stabilised over the 5A1g quintet by the NEVPT2 treatment of external-space correlation. The authors decline to call this quantitative, citing basis-set incompleteness and the neglect of even scalar relativistic effects. Context: CASPT2 studies often find an incorrect quintet ground state, attributed to a poor PT2 description of semi-core correlation, while experiment and higher-accuracy methods point to a triplet. The active space for each spin state was optimized independently, with the FCIQMC dynamic sampling the 2-RDM for a two-step orbital optimization. The stochastic promotion scheme cut the higher-body accumulation time by about 80% (5.1 hours per seed).

NEVPT2 energy errors converge to well below chemical accuracy with 100k to 1M walkers. The separate N2 pi-space experiment adds a controlled Gaussian aberration to the exact CAS eigenfunction and shows that CASPT2 error grows sharply with the noise (and with the internal-contraction-facility overlap threshold, 1e-5 to 1e-8) whereas NEVPT2 and CASCI are far more stable - the reason the paper focuses on FCIQMC-NEVPT2.

DMRG-SC-NEVPT2: 3B1 3.4, 3.4, 3.1, 2.6, 1.9; 1A1 32.8, 33.1, 33.8, 32.8, 31.8. DMRG-PC-NEVPT2: 3B1 6.5, -34.1, 4.1, -1.3, 0.5; 1A1 -6.0, 3.3, 31.8, 28.7, 31.0. SC-NEVPT2 agrees with CCSD(T) in the same basis to within 1.3 kcal/mol and varies with m by less than 1 kcal/mol; the Cholesky decomposition changes the gaps by less than 0.1 kcal/mol (quintet-triplet) and about 0.3 kcal/mol (quintet-singlet). electronic_structure_description: A {CoNO}8 complex in the Enemark-Feltham notation. Natural orbital occupations from DMRG-SCF: the lowest singlet S0 most closely matches (3dxz)2(3dyz)2(3dz2)2(3dxy)2(3dx2-y2)0(pi*NO,y)0(pi*NO,x)0, i.e. a d8 Co coupled to NO+, though the 3dz2 and pi*NO,y occupations carry significant admixture of neutral NO with d7 Co. T2 is characterized as d7 Co with neutral NO. T1 has 3dyz and pi*NO,y occupations near 1.5 and 0.5, exactly between d7 and d8 Co and between neutral and cationic NO (T2 occupations quoted in the figure: 1.95, 1.97, 1.00, 1.98, 0.04, 1.03, 0.10). compound_name: N2, dissociation curve (4-RDM approximation test case)
geometry_source: N-N distance scanned from about 1.0 to 2.4 A
method: QRDM-NEVPT2, a hybrid quantum-classical strongly contracted NEVPT2 in which the CASCI step is replaced by VQE on a quantum computer and the n-particle reduced density matrices (up to n = 4) measured on the device are fed directly into the classical SC-NEVPT2 machinery
software: InQuanto, with TKET via pytket for circuit compilation and measurement reduction; Qulacs statevector simulator; Saitow's Fortran implementation of the Kutzelnigg cumulant expansion
electronic_structure_description: CAS(10,8)-SC-NEVPT2/cc-pVDZ dissociation curve benchmarked against FCI/cc-pVDZ. The exact 4-RDM is sparse - only about 5% of its elements are non-zero anywhere along the curve. The plain CU(4) cumulant approximation fails; the CU(4)-RDM-filtered variant, which replaces the significantly non-zero CU(4) elements by exact ones, unexpectedly made things far worse, with SC-NEVPT2 errors up to 2.5 Ha. The successful variant, CU(4)-PDM-screened, gives a smooth dissociation curve with only modest deviation from exact NEVPT2 at large separation, its binding-energy error running between about 0.0015 and 0.0040 Ha across the curve. The paper's conclusion is that cumulant approximations to the 4-RDM should be used with great caution in NEVPT2 and are expected to fail for highly multireference systems such as stretched N2 or Cr2.
reference_short: Krompiec & Munoz Ramo, Strongly Contracted N-Electron Valence State Perturbation Theory Using Reduced Density Matrices from a Quantum Computer
notes: Method benchmark, classical simulation of the quantum workflow. ACTIVE SPACE IS HARDWARE-LIMITED: this is a quantum-algorithm study in which the active-space eigenvalue is obtained by VQE on a quantum processor or its simulator, so the size of the space is set by the qubit budget (n active orbitals -> 2n qubits) rather than by the chemistry of the system. Do NOT read nel/norb here as a chemically motivated recommendation for this molecule.
