ligand_set: three histidine imidazole nitrogens per copper, plus the bridging O2 unit (free O2, superoxide or peroxide depending on the point along the path)
geometry_source: QM[M06-2X]/MM optimized structures in a 50 A cubic water box with Na+ and Cl- ions; relaxed two-dimensional scans in d(O-O) (1.19, 1.35, 1.47 A) and d(Cu-Cu) (4.8, 4.3, 4.0, 3.6 A for binding; 3.60, 3.25, 2.80 A for isomerization), with d(Cu-O) optimized and also sampled at fixed 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 A
method: NEVPT2 on a CASSCF reference inside a QM/MM embedding (QM[NEVPT2]/MM), compared against broken-symmetry DFT at M06-2X (QM[M06-2X]/MM) and against plain CASSCF
software: ASH interfaced with Gromacs and ORCA; Multiwfn for the Hirshfeld population analysis of the active molecular orbitals
basis_set: def2-TZVP on all atoms of the QM region
active_space_orbital_description: all of the O2 molecular orbitals (sigma_s, sigma_s*, sigma_pz, pi_px, pi_py, pi_px*, pi_py*, sigma_p*) plus two Cu d_xz orbitals
active_space_protocol: (6,4) expanded up to (16,12); the larger space was validated by reproducing the ground-state singlet-triplet splitting of oxyHc (-2J = 690 cm-1, consistent with the experimental diamagnetism -2J > 600 cm-1) and was then used for every subsequent QM[NEVPT2]/MM calculation
electronic_structure_description: Oxygen binding: NEVPT2 gives an O2 binding energy of about -2.3 kcal/mol, far closer to the experimental binding enthalpy of -6.0 kcal/mol than DFT's -11.9 kcal/mol, and a lower barrier than either DFT or CASSCF. The first electron transfer has a barrier of 18.7 kcal/mol at NEVPT2 versus 23.4 kcal/mol at DFT, and occurs earlier along the coordinate (a superoxide already at d(Cu-Cu) = 4.3 A) so that a stable singlet superoxide intermediate forms before the triplet-singlet intersystem crossing - a species seen spectroscopically but found only by the multireference method. The ISC preserves atom connectivity and the second electron transfer needs only about 2 kcal/mol, giving the peroxo-Cu2O2 butterfly core of oxyHc. The elongated-superoxide pathway (barrier 1.7 kcal/mol) is preferred over the concerted one (3.2 kcal/mol), i.e. O-O elongation precedes structural reorganization. Peroxo-to-bis-mu-oxo isomerization: NEVPT2 barrier 32.9 kcal/mol, against 57.8 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 110.0 kcal/mol at M06-2X; the peroxo form remains the more stable minimum inside the protein. At the bis-mu-oxo minimum the wave function is 63% peroxide (Cu2+)2(O2 2-) and only 4% oxide (Cu3+)2(O2-)2, so the Cu(III) configurations contribute only marginally and the bis-mu-oxo isomer is best described as a mixed-valence state. deoxyHc without O2 is a closed-shell singlet from two d10 Cu(I) centres; deoxyHc-O2 is a triplet.
reference_short: Fasulo, Teran, Pavone, Munoz-Garcia, Revisiting Oxygen Transport Features of Hemocyanin with NEVPT2 Level QM/MM Calculations, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 21, 2108-2117
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty on purpose: the copper oxidation state changes along the reaction coordinate (Cu(I) in deoxyHc, mixed valence in the superoxide intermediates, formally Cu(II) in the peroxo form) and the paper's own point is that the bis-mu-oxo isomer is a mixed-valence state rather than Cu(III). Entropy is excluded from the reported energetics because the experimental entropy contribution is small (about 3 cal/K/mol); water molecules near the active site were deliberately neglected.

compound_name: six octahedral Fe(II) complexes [Fe(H2O)6]2+, [Fe(NH3)6]2+, [Fe(NCH)6]2+, [Fe(PH3)6]2+, [Fe(CO)6]2+ and [Fe(CNH)6]2+: high-spin/low-spin adiabatic energy differences
ligand_set: six identical monodentate ligands spanning the spectrochemical series: H2O, NH3, NCH, PH3, CO and CNH
point_group: no symmetry constraints imposed in the calculation
geometry_source: TPSSh-optimized geometries taken from earlier work of the same group and used for all methods (DFT, CCSD(T) and CASPT2)
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference, with no IPEA shift, corrected for Fe 3s3p semicore correlation by a CCSD(T) calculation (the CASPT2/CC scheme of Pierloot and co-workers); used as the reference against which Hubbard U density-corrected DFT is benchmarked
software: BAGEL for the XMS-CASPT2; ORCA for the CCSD(T) semicore correction and the molecular DFT; Quantum ESPRESSO for the DFT+U and DFT+U+V
basis_set: cc-pVTZ-DK, cc-pVQZ-DK and cc-pV5Z-DK with a three-point extrapolation of CASSCF and CASPT2 energies separately to the CBS limit; cc-pV5Z-JKFIT density fitting; aug-cc-pwCVTZ-DK on Fe and cc-pVDZ on the ligand atoms for the CCSD(T) semicore correction
active_space_orbital_description: the Fe(II) 3d electrons and orbitals, the two ligand-eg molecular orbitals and the Fe 4d double shell, with their corresponding electrons
active_space_protocol: (10,12) for five of the six complexes; for [Fe(H2O)6]2+ a (10,12) space could not be converged with both ligand-eg orbitals retained in the low-spin state (the Fe 3s orbital consistently rotated in), so the CBS extrapolation used (6,10) instead - a substitution the paper justifies by literature CASPT2 values of -2.14 eV with (6e,10o) versus -2.15 eV with (10e,12o)
electronic_structure_description: Reference high-spin minus low-spin adiabatic energy differences dE(H-L) in eV, in the column order H2O, NH3, NCH, PH3, CO, CNH. CASPT2/CC: -1.83, -0.64, -0.16, 2.54, 2.02, 2.87. Plain CASPT2 (without the semicore CCSD(T) correction): -1.99, -0.85, -0.27, 2.31, 1.78, 2.66 - i.e. the correction shifts every complex by about +0.2 eV, reducing the overstabilization of the high-spin state. Literature comparisons quoted in the same table: CCSD(T) -1.45, -0.66, -0.19, 1.51, 1.25, -0.09; DLPNO-CCSD(T1) -1.44, -0.49, -0.38; DMC -1.78, -1.23, -1.17, 0.59. Against the CASPT2/CC reference the best density functionals are PBE[U] (MAE 0.44 eV overall, 0.30 weak-field, 0.57 strong-field), TPSSh (0.49) and M06-L (0.51), while Hartree-Fock density-corrected PBE[HF] gives 1.22 eV and M06-2X 2.41 eV.
reference_short: Mariano, Vlaisavljevich, Poloni, Improved Spin-State Energy Differences of Fe(II) molecular and crystalline complexes via the Hubbard U-corrected Density
notes: The multireference content of this paper is the CASPT2/CC reference set; the seven crystalline and molecular spin-crossover compounds treated later are PBE[U] only and get no row. d_electron_count 3d6 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(II) oxidation state. CAVEAT on the per-ligand mapping: the reported values are copied in the printed column order (H2O, NH3, NCH, PH3, CO, CNH), which makes the CASPT2/CC series non-monotonic across PH3/CO where every DFT row is monotonic; this may be a column-extraction artefact of the PDF rather than the paper's intent, so treat the PH3 and CO entries with care.

compound_name: pyridine N-oxide and its twelve ortho-, meta- and para-monosubstituted derivatives (R = CH3, Cl, NO2, OH)
geometry_source: optimized ground- and excited-state stationary points and conical intersections along the S1 rearrangement path
method: CASSCF with NEVPT2 corrections
active_space_orbital_description: the pi orbitals of the pyridine ring, the N-O bonding orbital, and a pair of oxygen non-bonding orbitals
electronic_structure_description: S0 -> S1 vertical excitations at NEVPT2(10,8)/cc-pVDZ, wavelength / energy / oscillator strength: parent NOx 304 nm / 4.08 eV / 0.01; m-CH3 285 / 4.35 / 0.02; o-CH3 290 / 4.27 / 0.01; p-CH3 296 / 4.19 / 0.01; m-Cl 301 / 4.11 / 0.01; o-Cl 301 / 4.12 / 0.03; p-Cl 318 / 3.90 / 0.01; m-NO2 327 / 3.79 / 0.03; o-NO2 296 / 4.19 / 0.03; p-NO2 290 / 4.27 / 0.02; m-OH 286 / 4.33 / 0.03; o-OH 278 / 4.46 / 0.04; p-OH 324 / 3.82 / 0.04. Experimentally the S0 -> S1 band lies at 270-330 nm for substituted N-oxides; for the parent the experimental values are 315 nm and f = 0.016 against the calculated 304 nm and 0.01. The vertical transition transfers charge density from the N-oxide group to the aromatic ring. Deactivation of S1 proceeds through conical intersections to oxaziridine-like intermediates; conversion of the oxaziridine (P) to the 1,2-oxazepine (P2) has a barrier of about 4.2 kcal/mol in both benzene and ethanol, lower in ethanol than in benzene throughout, with electron-donating CH3 and OH substituents (especially ortho and meta) and electron-withdrawing NO2 lowering the barrier while Cl raises it, particularly in benzene.
reference_short: Guerra, Rodriguez et al., Photochemical Rearrangements of Pyridine N-Oxides: Pathways to Oxaziridine Derivatives, Molecules 2025, 30, 4776
notes: Thirteen closely related molecules sharing one active space and one basis set, condensed into a single row per the project convention; the full per-derivative excitation table is in the electronic structure description. The paper's own methods text contains an internal slip - it writes both 'ten electrons distributed in eight orbitals' and 'ten active orbitals and eight reference orbitals (10,8)' - but the (10,8) label and the orbital list (ring pi, N-O sigma, two O lone pairs) are consistent with 10 electrons in 8 orbitals, which is what is recorded here.

geometry_source: optimized ground-state, S1(npi*) and T1(pipi*) minima and S1/S0 conical intersections; 13 surface-hopping trajectories started from S1, ten of which ran to the 2 ps final time
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2) for vertical excitations, critical-point energies and surface-hopping trajectory dynamics including non-adiabatic and spin-orbit coupling
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the vertical excitation energies; cc-pVDZ for the critical points and the trajectory dynamics
active_space_protocol: XMS-CASPT2(6,5)/cc-pVTZ for the vertical excitation energies of S1, S2, T1 and T2; XMS-CASPT2(8,7)/cc-pVDZ for the critical-point energies and the surface-hopping dynamics, the smaller basis leaving the energetic order of the states unchanged at the critical points
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitations (calculated, experimental in parentheses): S1(npi*) 3.73 eV / 333 nm (3.76 eV, 335 nm), transition dipole 0.0695 D; S2(pipi*) 5.74 eV / 216 nm (5.54 eV, 224 nm), transition dipole 4.53 D. S1 is almost dark. Along the relaxation path the T2(pipi*) state crosses S1(npi*) with a spin-orbit coupling of 37.96 cm-1, large enough for efficient intersystem crossing; T2 then passes the T1T2 conical intersection diabatically to become T1(pipi*), which is long-lived because its spin-orbit coupling to S0 is only 5.73 cm-1 and the gap is 1.06 eV. In the trajectories no ground-state repopulation through either S1S0 conical intersection was seen: S1 decayed entirely to the triplets with a time constant of about 750 fs (exponential fit 746 fs), consistent with the near-unity triplet quantum yield measured experimentally. Eleven net hops from S1 to T2 and eleven from T2 to T1, all at nearly planar geometries near the S1 minimum, with the wave function changing from 1(npi*) to 3(pipi*); T1 then relaxes to its twisted (pipi*) minimum by torsion about the HC=CH dihedral.
reference_short: Schwinger, Sagredo et al. (de Vivie-Riedle and co-workers), Activation of 2-Cyclohexenone by BF3 Coordination: Mechanistic Insights from Theory and Experiment, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 10155-10163
notes: The free enone, the reference against which the Lewis-acid complex is compared. Two active spaces are used for different purposes; nel/norb record the (6,5) space of the vertical excitations and both are given in active_space_protocol. software is left empty: the program used for the XMS-CASPT2 and the surface hopping is described only in the SI computational-methods section, which was not retrievable.

compound_name: the 2-cyclohexenone-BF3 Lewis acid complex (2), and its conformer 2'
geometry_source: optimized ground state, S1(pipi*) and S1(npi*) minima, T1(npi*) and T1(pipi*) minima, S2/S1 and two S1/S0 conical intersections; surface-hopping trajectories at cc-pVDZ without triplets or spin-orbit coupling because of cost
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2) for vertical excitations, critical-point energies and surface-hopping trajectory dynamics including non-adiabatic and spin-orbit coupling
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the vertical excitation energies; cc-pVDZ for the critical points and the trajectory dynamics
active_space_protocol: XMS-CASPT2(6,5)/cc-pVTZ for the vertical excitations; XMS-CASPT2(8,7)/cc-pVDZ for critical points and dynamics
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitations for conformers 2 / 2' (experimental in parentheses): S1(npi*) 4.87 / 4.87 eV, 255 / 255 nm (4.66 eV, 266 nm), transition dipoles 0.126 / 0.594 D; S2(pipi*) 5.08 / 5.15 eV, 244 / 241 nm (4.96 eV, 250 nm), transition dipoles 4.93 / 5.06 D. The two conformers - BF3 oriented toward or away from the C=C double bond, boron in the plane of the conjugated pi system - have nearly identical energies and spectra. Complexation stabilizes all the frontier pi, n and pi* orbitals relative to the free enone, most strongly the oxygen lone pair that forms the sigma bond to BF3, which is what produces the large red shift and brings S1 and S2 close together so both become optically addressable. The Franck-Condon geometry sits near an S2/S1 conical intersection that acts as a branching point: keeping pipi* character the system reaches a twisted S1S0 conical intersection, keeping npi* character it reaches the S1(npi*) minimum with BF3 rotated out of plane and the O-B bond elongated, from which heterolytic dissociation of the complex is possible in the gas phase and a second, ring-opened S1S0 conical intersection is reached. Unlike the free enone, then, internal conversion competes with intersystem crossing. Spin-orbit coupling between the crossing T2(pipi*) and S1 states is around 25 cm-1. T1 again has a local npi* and a global pipi* minimum joined by the T1T2 conical intersection.
reference_short: Schwinger, Sagredo et al. (de Vivie-Riedle and co-workers), Activation of 2-Cyclohexenone by BF3 Coordination: Mechanistic Insights from Theory and Experiment, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 10155-10163
notes: Second compound from the same paper. Boron is main-group, so metal_center is none. software left empty for the same reason as the enone row.

compound_name: 3-penten-2-one oxide, a five-carbon unsaturated Criegee intermediate (eight conformers)
geometry_source: conformer geometries optimized at B2PLYP-D3/VTZ with relative energies at CCSD(T)-F12/VTZ-F12 including anharmonic zero-point corrections; the eight optimized conformers are shown in ESI Fig. S9
method: CASPT2 for vertical excitation energies and oscillator strengths
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies and oscillator strengths for the first pi* <- pi transition of the eight conformers, given as relative conformer energy (kcal/mol), VEE (eV / nm), f: tEE 0.00, 3.42 / 362, 0.15; cEE 1.65, 3.25 / 380, 0.14; cZE 1.98, 3.24 / 382, 0.07; tZE 2.15, 2.73 / 453, 0.12; cEZ 2.84, 3.20 / 387, 0.11; tEZ 4.07, 3.48 / 356, 0.12; tZZ 6.26, 2.96 / 419, 0.09; cZZ 7.67, 3.34 / 371, 0.07. The lowest-energy tEE conformer's computed 362 nm matches the broad, unstructured experimental absorption peaking near 375 nm, and the spread of higher-energy conformers covers the observed 325-460 nm range, indicating they contribute to the band. OH radicals are detected from unimolecular decay of the energized Criegee intermediate.
reference_short: A five-carbon unsaturated Criegee intermediate: synthesis, spectroscopic identification, and theoretical study of 3-penten-2-one oxide, Chem. Sci. 2023
notes: Eight conformers of one species sharing a single active space and basis, condensed into one row with the full per-conformer table. The composition of the (12,10) space is not described in the main text, and the program used for the CASPT2 is not named there either (computational details are in the ESI, which was not retrievable), so active_space_orbital_description and software are left empty.

geometry_source: adiabatic singlet potential energy surfaces computed on a grid to parametrize a vibronic coupling model Hamiltonian, expanded to seventh order in the diabatic potentials and covering all twenty-one vibrational modes
method: CASPT2 for the adiabatic singlet surfaces, diabatized into a five-state vibronic coupling model Hamiltonian and propagated with multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (MCTDH) quantum dynamics
software: Molpro 2015 for the ab initio surfaces
active_space_orbital_description: all the pi orbitals plus the C-S sigma orbitals; earlier work showed the C-S sigma orbitals must be included to describe the dynamics correctly (the active space of Schnappinger et al.)
nroots_per_mult: 5 singlet states in the vibronic model
electronic_structure_description: The first absorption band is built from two closely spaced valence states, 1A1 (pi2 -> pi1*) and 1B2 (pi1 -> pi1*), S1 having A1 and S2 B2 symmetry; in C2v these two are coupled by modes of B2 symmetry. The MCTDH spectrum computed from the five-state, twenty-one-mode model reproduces the measured spectrum of Holland et al. (PCCP 2014, 16, 21629) very well and lets the previously unassigned vibrational features be assigned; the band origin is the peak at 5.16 eV with hot bands below it. Following photoexcitation thiophene undergoes both ring-opening and ring-puckering motions.
reference_short: Parkes & Worth, The 'Simple' Photochemistry of Thiophene
notes: The multireference content is the CASPT2 surface generation; the spectrum itself comes from MCTDH propagation on the fitted diabatic model. Only the ordering and symmetry of the states, not a table of vertical excitation energies, is given in the main text.

compound_name: N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) and its four protonated isomers E-NNOH+, Z-NNOH+, NNHO+ and the N-nitrosoammonium ion NHNO+ [(CH3)2NH-NO]+
geometry_source: CASPT2-optimized geometries; conical intersections optimized with the algorithm implemented in MOLCAS; solvated geometries optimized with PCM (methanol)
method: multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) on state-averaged CASSCF references, with IPEA shift fixed at 0.25 and an imaginary shift of 0.1
active_space_protocol: SA2-CASSCF(16,13) reference for neutral NDMA; SA2-CASSCF(16,14) for the four protonated species
nroots_per_mult: 2 (SA2-CASSCF)
electronic_structure_description: MS-CASPT2 vertical excitations as isolated molecules, state / dE eV (nm) / oscillator strength (length) / leading configuration. NDMA: 1A'' 3.52 (352) / 3.61e-3 / (sigma_NO)(pi*_NO) 86%; 2A' 5.73 (216) / 2.18e-1 / (pi_NN)(pi*_NO) 82%; 2A'' 7.75 (160) / 9.54e-3. E-NNOH+: 1A'' 5.59 (222) / 8.85e-3; 2A' 6.60 (188) / 2.41e-1; 2A'' 9.29 (134). Z-NNOH+: 1A'' 5.93 (209) / 1.82e-2; 2A' 6.55 (189) / 2.49e-1; 2A'' 8.29 (150). NNHO+: 1A'' 4.16 (298) / 2.37e-4; 2A' 5.71 (217) / 2.75e-1; 2A'' 9.21 (135). NHNO+: 1A'' 2.74 (453) / 6.31e-4 / (sigma_NN)(pi*_NO) 84%; 2A' 6.43 (193) / 4.62e-1; 2A'' 8.19 (151). With PCM (methanol) at PCM-optimized geometries the values shift only slightly, e.g. NHNO+ 1A'' 2.72 eV (456 nm). Only NHNO+, the N-nitrosoammonium ion protonated at the amine nitrogen, absorbs in the visible at 453 nm, and its S1 is dissociative, yielding the aminium radical cation and NO directly. Thermodynamics relative to E-NNOH+ (kcal/mol, gas phase): NHNO+ dU(0) 9.2, dH 9.8, dG 7.8; Z-NNOH+ 11.1 / 11.1 / 11.1; NNH+O 13.0 / 13.1 / 12.7. The Z-NNOH+ <-> NHNO+ equilibrium has a 60 kcal/mol barrier through TS1, and a conical intersection sits directly on the Z/E tautomerization path, hindering it by diabatic trapping - so NHNO+ formation is controlled dynamically rather than thermodynamically or kinetically.
reference_short: Soto, Pelaez, Algarra, CASPT2 study of the electronic structure and photochemistry of protonated N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA-H+) at 453 nm, J. Chem. Phys. 2023, 158, 204301
notes: Five closely related species from one paper sharing the basis set and, for the four cations, the same (16,14) space, condensed into one row; the neutral used (16,13) and that difference is recorded in active_space_protocol, with nel/norb holding the (16,14) space of the protonated species that the paper is about. The orbital composition of the space is given only through the configuration labels (sigma_NN, sigma_NC, sigma_NO, pi_NO, pi*_NO, 2sp_N, n_piN), so active_space_orbital_description is left empty.

compound_name: N-nitrosopiperidine and its protonated isomers N(H+)NO, Z-NNO(H)+ and E-NNO(H)+
geometry_source: CASPT2-optimized minima, a transition state TS0 and an S1/S0 conical intersection along the paths connecting N(H+)NO with E- and Z-NNO(H)+; PCM-optimized geometries for the solvated values
method: multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) on state-averaged CASSCF references, alongside MP2 and DFT
active_space_protocol: reference wave function 1: SA2-CASSCF(16,14)/ANO-RCC; reference wave function 2: SA2-CASSCF(16,13)/ANO-RCC, used for different isomers
nroots_per_mult: 2 (SA2-CASSCF)
electronic_structure_description: The site of protonation depends on the solvent: at the oxygen in protic solvents, at the amine nitrogen in aprotic solvents, so the only cationic species formed in aprotic media is R2N(H+)-NO. The first excited state has the same character in every isomer, a (sigma_NN / n_pi) -> (pi*_NO) excitation. Only the N-protonated species absorbs in the visible and its S1 dissociates directly into the aminium radical cation and nitric oxide, which is the photochemistry Patil and co-workers exploit synthetically. Three minima (N(H+)NO, Z-NNO(H)+, E-NNO(H)+) and three critical points including TS0 and an S1/S0 conical intersection were located; the relative Gibbs free energies rule out thermodynamic control, so which protonated isomer forms is dynamically determined. Solvent-corrected values (PCM) are reported in square brackets alongside the gas-phase ones.
reference_short: Soto, Identification of the Photoreactive Species of Protonated N-Nitrosopiperidine in Acid Medium: A CASPT2 and DFT Study, J. Phys. Chem. A 2023, 127, 9781-9786
notes: Companion study to the same author's NDMA paper, with the same method and basis. The per-isomer excitation energies live in a table whose numeric body did not survive text extraction cleanly, so only the state characters and qualitative findings are recorded rather than guessed numbers. software is left empty: the main text names no program (MOLCAS is used in the companion paper but is not stated here). nel/norb record reference wave function 1; the alternative (16,13) reference is in active_space_protocol.

point_group: C2v labels used throughout (retained under torsion about the C=C axis); the planar ground state is D2h-like
geometry_source: ground-state geometry optimized at MP2/aug-cc-pVDZ in Gaussian 09 (r(CC) 1.335 A vs 1.315 experimental, r(CF) 1.337 vs 1.323, r(CH) 1.087 vs 1.078, FCF 109.6 vs 109.1 deg, HCH 121.5 vs 121.8, CCF 125.2 vs 125.5, HCC 119.3 vs 119.1); normal modes from the same geometry, with the torsional mode replaced by the full torsion angle in the model Hamiltonian
method: multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) on a state-averaged CASSCF reference, used to parametrize a vibronic coupling model Hamiltonian (VCHam in the Quantics suite) for quantum dynamics on 12 nuclear degrees of freedom and 7 electronic states, with coupling terms up to sixth order in the torsion
software: MOLCAS for the MS-CASPT2; Gaussian 09 for the MP2 geometry; Quantics (VCHam) for the model Hamiltonian and dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: the pi and pi* orbitals plus the Rydberg orbitals 3s, 3px, 3py and 3pz
active_space_protocol: SA(11)-MS-CAS(2,6)PT2: the state average runs over eleven roots so as to cover every single and double excitation available within the chosen active space, even though only the lowest seven states enter the dynamics
nroots_per_mult: 11 (state-averaged over eleven roots; seven states used in the dynamics)
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitations (eV) at the Franck-Condon geometry and at 90 degrees of torsion, with experimental values where available, using Mulliken's ethylene labels (N for the closed-shell pi2, V for pipi*, Z for pi*2): N 0.00 (A1) and 3.30 at 90 deg; V 7.45 (exp 7.49, A1) and 3.47; pi-3s 7.07 (exp 7.06, B2) and 7.91; pi-3px 8.10 (A2) and 9.03; pi-3py 8.20 (B1) and 9.26; pi-3pz 8.93 (exp 8.97, A1) and 10.03; Z 13.77 (A1) and 9.27. The paper's earlier MS-CASPT2 work established that several Rydberg states must be included to describe the non-adiabatic dynamics correctly starting from the bright valence state, which is why they are in the active space here.
reference_short: Gomez, Singer, Gonzalez, Worth, Do we need delocalised wavefunctions for the excited state dynamics of 1,1-difluoroethylene?
notes: The tiny (2,6) electron count is genuine: only the two pi electrons are active, distributed over the pi, pi* and four Rydberg orbitals. The eleven-root state average, not the active space, is what makes the calculation balanced.

compound_name: uridine in aqueous solution (RNA nucleoside), excited-state relaxation
geometry_source: QM/MM setup generated from classical molecular dynamics of solvated uridine following the group's published protocol; surface-hopping trajectories with a 0.5 fs time step
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2) on a state-averaged CASSCF reference, driving QM/MM surface-hopping dynamics with the Tully-Hammes-Schiffer scheme and decoherence corrections; IPEA shift 0.0, imaginary shift 0.2; time-derivative couplings from the RASSI module
software: COBRAMM interfacing OpenMolcas (and Gaussian 16 for the TD-DFT comparison) with Amber for the MM region
active_space_orbital_description: eight valence pi/pi* orbitals plus two oxygen lone pairs, i.e. all frontier valence pi orbitals and the carbonyl lone pairs
nroots_per_mult: 9 (state-averaged CASSCF over nine states)
electronic_structure_description: The topology of the potential energy surfaces governing photoinduced relaxation is similar at TD-DFT and CASPT2: constraining the dynamics to the pipi* state gives similar energy fluctuations and relaxation lifetimes in both. The anomalously long TD-DFT excited-state lifetime is traced to npi* trapping, because TD-DFT in a QM/MM scheme with electrostatic embedding underestimates the pipi* energy and so inverts the pipi*/npi* ordering. CASPT2 with a valence-only pi active space is itself subject to a known error from dynamical sigma-pi polarization in ionic pipi* states: the paper cites a 0.25 eV blue shift (4.95 to 5.20 eV) on going from a (10,8) active space to a (0,0|10,8|2,12) RAS expanded with twelve extra-valence orbitals in RAS3 with up to double excitations. Full-pi active spaces small enough for dynamics are therefore prone to errors in relative state energies, which is the paper's central caveat.
reference_short: Jaiswal, Taddei, Nascimento, Garavelli, Conti, Nenov, Reconciling TD-DFT and CASPT2 electronic structure methods for describing the photophysics of DNA, Photochem. Photobiol. 2024, 100, 443-452
notes: The (10,8) and RAS (0,0|10,8|2,12) spaces quoted in the electronic structure description are literature values the paper cites for the gas-phase nucleobase, not calculations run here; the calculations of this work use the (14,10) space recorded in nel/norb. TD-DFT comparison used CAM-B3LYP/6-311G(d,p).

compound_name: sinapic acid (SA), trans and cis isomers
geometry_source: ground- and excited-state geometries optimized with a PCM solvent model in ethyl acetate, methanol and water; conical intersections located by RASSCF
method: RASSCF for locating conical intersection geometries and multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) for the photoisomerization potential energy surfaces, with a PCM solvent model; DFT and TD-DFT for the antioxidant descriptors
active_space_orbital_description: the pi and pi* orbitals of the conjugated system
active_space_protocol: RAS partitioning into RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 for the conical-intersection optimizations; (2,3) active space
nroots_per_mult: 4 (state-averaged over four electronic states to avoid root flipping during optimization)
electronic_structure_description: Photoisomerization between trans and cis forms was followed on MS-CASPT2/def2-TZVP surfaces with conical intersections located by RASSCF. In the ground state the cis isomers of both compounds have the higher antioxidant activity; in the S1 state the ranking is solvent-dependent, trans-sinapic acid performing better in ethyl acetate and water while cis-sinapic acid is more effective in methanol. Natural population analysis charges increase on photoexcitation for all four species, so photoexcitation itself enhances the antioxidant properties.
reference_short: Wang et al., The Effect of Photoisomerization on the Antioxidant Properties of Sinapic Acid and Methyl Sinapate in Different Solvents: A DFT/TD-DFT Study, Antioxidants 2025, 14, 633
notes: Two closely related compounds from one paper, one row each because they use different active spaces. The spaces are unusually small - (2,3) for sinapic acid and (4,4) for methyl sinapate - which the paper justifies as capturing the critical pi/pi* orbitals of the conjugated system; the orbital pictures are in the SI. Most of the antioxidant analysis (bond dissociation enthalpies, ionization potentials, NPA charges) is DFT/TD-DFT rather than multireference.

compound_name: methyl sinapate (MS), trans and cis isomers
geometry_source: ground- and excited-state geometries optimized with a PCM solvent model in ethyl acetate, methanol and water; conical intersections located by RASSCF
method: RASSCF for locating conical intersection geometries and multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) for the photoisomerization potential energy surfaces, with a PCM solvent model; DFT and TD-DFT for the antioxidant descriptors
active_space_orbital_description: the pi and pi* orbitals of the conjugated system
active_space_protocol: RAS partitioning into RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 for the conical-intersection optimizations; (4,4) active space
nroots_per_mult: 4 (state-averaged over four electronic states to avoid root flipping during optimization)
electronic_structure_description: Photoisomerization between trans and cis forms was followed on MS-CASPT2/def2-TZVP surfaces with conical intersections located by RASSCF. In the ground state the cis isomers of both compounds have the higher antioxidant activity; in the S1 state the ranking is solvent-dependent, trans-sinapic acid performing better in ethyl acetate and water while cis-sinapic acid is more effective in methanol. Natural population analysis charges increase on photoexcitation for all four species, so photoexcitation itself enhances the antioxidant properties.
reference_short: Wang et al., The Effect of Photoisomerization on the Antioxidant Properties of Sinapic Acid and Methyl Sinapate in Different Solvents: A DFT/TD-DFT Study, Antioxidants 2025, 14, 633
notes: Two closely related compounds from one paper, one row each because they use different active spaces. The spaces are unusually small - (2,3) for sinapic acid and (4,4) for methyl sinapate - which the paper justifies as capturing the critical pi/pi* orbitals of the conjugated system; the orbital pictures are in the SI. Most of the antioxidant analysis (bond dissociation enthalpies, ionization potentials, NPA charges) is DFT/TD-DFT rather than multireference.

compound_name: solvated adenine-uracil monophosphate dinucleotide (ApU), stacked conformer
formula: ApU dinucleotide plus a Na+ counterion and explicit water
geometry_source: two groups of structures taken from a 1 ns ground-state molecular dynamics run (the lowest-energy conformation and one with a low charge-transfer energy at 600 ps), reoptimized at the ONIOM(CASSCF/6-31+G*:AMBER) level; excited-state minima and conical intersections optimized at the same level, with only ApU, the Na+ ion and the 84 closest solvent molecules allowed to relax
method: ONIOM QM/MM with a CASSCF QM region, corrected by state-specific CASPT2 including the MM point charges (denoted CASPT2:AMBER); link-atom scheme with electronic embedding and charge equilibration; two-dimensional UV spectra from SA-80-CASSCF(8,8)/SS-CASPT2 energies and CASSCF transition dipoles through a sum-over-states nonlinear response
software: Gaussian for the ONIOM(CASSCF:AMBER) optimizations, Molcas for the CASPT2 energies, and a development version of Spectron 2.7 for the 2D-UV spectra
basis_set: 6-31+G* for the ONIOM(CASSCF:AMBER) optimizations; ANO-S for the CASPT2 energies and the spectra
active_space_orbital_description: six orbitals from each base, chosen so that the two bases are treated on an equal footing across all structures
active_space_protocol: (8,8), four orbitals on each base, for the excited-state minimum optimizations; for the conical intersection optimizations all pi orbitals of whichever base carries the excitation, (12,10) for adenine and (10,8) for uracil, which gives a better CASSCF correlation energy and avoids large degeneracy-lifting on adding CASPT2 (residual CASPT2 gaps at the intersections about 0.25 eV); (12,12) for the CASPT2 potential energies; SA-80-CASSCF(8,8) with SS-CASPT2 for the 2D-UV spectra
nroots_per_mult: 80 in the state average used for the spectra (SA-80-CASSCF)
electronic_structure_description: Relative CASPT2:AMBER energies (eV) of the critical points, referred to the FC-1 (group 1) and FC-2 (group 2) ground states, with vertical emission energies in parentheses and barriers to the intersections in square brackets. Vertical excitation spectrum, group 1 / group 2: 1Lb 4.70 / 4.92; 1La 4.88 / 5.07; uracil S(U) 5.42, 5.49 / 5.39; charge transfer 6.01 / 5.77. Minima: (A*pU-1Lb)min 4.56 (4.51) / 4.46 (4.40); (ApU*)min 5.42 (3.69) / 4.70 (3.77); (A+pU-)min 3.02 (2.51) / 4.19 (2.14); the doubly excited (ApU)*min 6.35 (4.46) in group 1 only. Conical intersections: (A*pU-1La/gs)CI-exo 4.30 [0.75] / 3.96 [0.59]; (A*pU-1La/gs)CI-endo 4.14 [0.68] / 4.45 [0.79]; (ApU*/gs)CI-exo 4.30 [0.17] / 3.82 [0.33]; (ApU*/gs)CI-endo 4.78 [0.24] / 3.89 [0.23]; (A+pU-/gs)CI 2.37 [<0.1] in group 1. The adenine 1La state decays barrierlessly to a conical intersection, while the 1Lb and uracil S(U) states have minima separated from their intersections by sizeable barriers (uracil-centred 0.17 and 0.23 eV, adenine-centred 0.68 and 0.59 eV). Depending on the backbone conformation the charge-transfer state either undergoes inter-base hydrogen transfer and decays through a conical intersection, or gives a long-lived minimum stabilized by a hydrogen bond between the ribose rings; (A+pU-)min-1 is stabilized by a 1.82 A hydrogen bond between the uracil O8 carbonyl and an adenine amino hydrogen. The 1Lb, S(U) and CT states may all contribute to the experimental 18 and 240 ps lifetimes. A recommended 2D-UV probe window of 25000-38000 cm-1 gives decongested, distinguishable fingerprints for each species.
reference_short: Li, Giussani, Segarra-Marti, Nenov, Rivalta, Voityuk, Mukamel, Roca-Sanjuan, Garavelli et al., Multiple Decay Mechanisms and 2D-UV Spectroscopic Fingerprints of Singlet Excited Solvated Adenine-Uracil Monophosphate, Chem. Eur. J. 2016, 22, 7497-7507
notes: Four different active spaces are used for four different purposes; nel/norb record the (12,12) space of the CASPT2 potential energies, which is the level the reported table is computed at, and the rest are in active_space_protocol. FC-1 is favoured by about 2.5 eV at CASPT2:AMBER, but the paper cautions this comes from potential-energy minimization rather than dynamics and is not representative of relative stability in solution.

compound_name: tetraoxoferrate(VI) ion FeO4(2-), as a bare cluster model for Fe(VI) doped into K2CrO4 and K2SO4 and in alkaline solution
ligand_set: four oxide ligands in a tetrahedron
point_group: Td (calculations run under C2v symmetry restrictions, with residual degeneracy splittings better than 200 cm-1)
geometry_source: bare cluster at the fixed experimental Fe-O distance of 1.66 A taken from the perfect K2FeO4 crystal structure; no geometry optimization and no embedding potentials
method: restricted active space self-consistent field (RASSCF)
basis_set: all-electron Wachters (14s11p5d) on Fe augmented with one diffuse d and a (3f) polarization function, contracted (62111111/4211111/3111/3); oxygens described by a 1s ab initio core model potential with a (5s5p) valence basis augmented by one diffuse p function for the anion, contracted (41/411)
active_space_orbital_description: the cluster molecular orbitals of main Fe(3d) character form a complete active space; on top of that, all single, double, triple and quadruple excitations from the twelve molecular orbitals of main O(2p) character into the Fe(3d) orbitals are allowed, i.e. up to four holes in the O4(2p) space. The resulting expansions contain 50000 to 100000 configuration state functions.
active_space_protocol: RAS: Fe(3d)-character orbitals as the complete active space (RAS2), with the twelve O(2p)-character orbitals allowed up to four holes (RAS1), so that single through quadruple ligand-to-metal excitations are included
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 3A2. The d2 (e2) ligand-field configuration carries less than 0.5% weight in the RASSCF wave function, and the ligand-to-metal 2p->3d single excitations only about 7%; the wave functions are dominated by high-order ligand-to-metal excitations, showing a strong inward delocalization of electron density away from the closed-shell oxide ligands driven by the unstable formal Fe(VI) charge, and an O(2p)/Fe(3d) near degeneracy. Vertical transitions fall into five increasingly dense and intense sets: (1) 1E alone; (2) 1A1 alone; (3) 3T2 and 3T1 superimposed, the 3T1 at 12100 cm-1 with f = 0.46e-3 accounting for most of the intensity of the band observed at 12670 cm-1 in solution; (4) a superposition of singlets, triplets (both spanning 16700-22400 cm-1) and quintets, the quintets starting about 1500 cm-1 lower, containing three spin- and dipole-allowed excitations to 3T1 states; (5) the beginning of a further set of singlets, triplets and quintets. The two narrow low-intensity bands agree remarkably with the spin- and dipole-forbidden 3A2 -> 1E, 1A1 transitions. The presence of quintet states in the 10000-25000 cm-1 region is unexpected from d2 ligand-field theory and forces completely new assignments of the broad intense bands. In the K2CrO4 and K2SO4 hosts the site symmetry is essentially Td with a small Cs distortion, which splits 3A2 into 3A'' and 3T2 into two 3A' plus one 3A''.
reference_short: Al-Abdalla, Seijo, Barandiaran, A new interpretation of the bonding and spectroscopy of the tetraoxoferrate(VI) FeO4(2-) ion, J. Chem. Phys. 1998, 109, 6396-6405
notes: active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY deliberately: the paper defines the space by its orbital content and excitation-level restrictions (Fe 3d as CAS, up to four holes in twelve O 2p orbitals) and never states an (nel,norb) pair. d_electron_count 3d2 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(VI) oxidation state, and the paper itself repeatedly refers to the d2 configuration - though its central finding is that this ligand-field label describes the wave function very poorly. The paper states its own limitations explicitly: no embedding potentials for the host crystals and no dynamic correlation.

compound_name: Pr3+/Pr4+ activator in cubic Lu2O3 (embedded PrO6(9-) and PrO6(8-) clusters), with Ti, Zr or Hf codopants, for intervalence and metal-to-metal charge transfer electron traps
formula: PrO6(9-) / PrO6(8-) clusters in c-Lu2O3; codopant clusters MO6 (M = Ti, Zr, Hf)
ligand_set: the six oxide ions of the immediate coordination shell of the dopant cation in a Lu3+ site of cubic Lu2O3; the rest of the lattice is represented by embedding potentials
point_group: C2 and C3i, the two crystallographically distinct Lu3+ sites of cubic Lu2O3
geometry_source: cluster geometries interpolated from solid-state DFT calculations of structures with the activator at each oxidation state of interest, so ionic-radius mismatch and nearby defects are modelled explicitly; embedded in a 12 A layer of ab initio model potentials (AIMPs) representing the unperturbed c-Lu2O3 lattice, surrounded by point charges out to about 77 A optimized with Lattgen to minimize electric multipoles of orders 2, 3 and 4 at the cluster atoms
method: state-averaged RASSCF followed by RASPT2 and RASSI-SO (restricted active space state interaction with spin-orbit coupling); CCSD(T) on single-root RASSCF references for the closed-shell codopant ground-state curves
software: OpenMolcas (SEWARD for the Douglas-Kroll-Hess integrals, Lattgen for the point-charge optimization)
active_space_orbital_description: RAS2 consists of the molecular orbitals of predominant Pr 4f, 6s and 5d character. Pr3+ (PrO6(9-)) puts two electrons in this space, Pr4+ (PrO6(8-)) one electron. All possible roots were included, i.e. the number of state-averaged roots equals the number of configuration state functions; for Pr3+ both singlets and triplets were considered.
active_space_protocol: single-orbital RASSCF (effectively SCF) plus CCSD(T) for the Ti4+/Zr4+/Hf4+ and M3+ codopant ground-state potential curves; state-averaged RASSCF/RASPT2/RASSI-SO with the Pr 4f/6s/5d RAS2 space for the Pr centres. IPEA shift zero; imaginary shift 0.3 for Pr, needed to get smooth Pr3+ RASPT2 curves. Frozen core: O 1s; Hf and Pr 1-4s, 2-4p, 3d, 4d; Ti 1-2s, 2p; Zr 1-3s, 2-3p, 3d. Zeroth-order reference weights in the RASPT2 step were typically 0.64-0.67.
electronic_structure_description: RASSI-SO energy levels for Pr3+ in both the C2 and C3i sites are compared with NIST free-ion levels and with experimental Lu2O3:Pr3+ levels. Pr3+ is less stable in the C3i site than in C2, so if one Pr had to be tetravalent it would be the C3i one. Thermal (TB) and vertical/optical (OB) barriers for Pr-Pr electron transfer, same site symmetry, forward and reverse in eV: 3H4(C3i)->3H4(C3i) 0.52 / 2.08; 1G4 0.55 / 2.18; 1D2 0.49 / 1.97; 1I 0.49 / 1.96. The excited-acceptor IVCT [3H4 Pr3+, Pr'4+] -> [Pr4+, 1D2 Pr'3+] has an activation barrier of 2.0-2.2 eV when both ions sit in sites of the same symmetry, which explains the 2 eV electron trap measured in Lu2O3:Pr. Transitions with the same Pr3+ excited state on both sides have small thermalization barriers of 0.3-0.5 eV, so the electron hops from site to site easily - part of why efficient thermoluminescence needs low dopant concentrations. For the Hf codopant, [Hf(C2), Pr(C3i)] gives trap depths of 2.0-2.5 eV for the 1D2 level, against experimental values near 1.36-1.44 eV, consistent with diabatic surface intersections giving upper-limit estimates; Zr behaves the same way. Excitation of Pr(C2) to 1D2 gives a 1.91 eV barrier to hole transfer, while excitation to 3P gives a moderate 1.33 eV barrier, so some Pr3+(C3i) can form at room temperature. IVCT absorption at 219 nm (5.66 eV) or shorter leads to a Pr3+(C3i) whose relaxation barriers back to 3P and 1D2 Pr(C2) are only 0.032 and 0.006 eV, so it emits from C2 Pr3+ anyway. Calculated Pr3+ f-d transitions in Lu2O3 begin near 300 nm, which makes the experimental band in that region hard to assign unambiguously to f-d rather than IVCT.
reference_short: Shyichuk & Krosnicki, Electron Trap Depths in Cubic Lutetium Oxide Doped with Pr and Ti, Zr or Hf - From Ab Initio Multiconfigurational Calculations, J. Phys. Chem. A 2023, 127, 4583-4595
notes: SOLID-STATE SYSTEM: a lanthanide activator and a codopant substituting Lu3+ sites in a cubic Lu2O3 host lattice, modelled as embedded MO6 clusters inside ab initio model potentials plus an optimized point-charge field - not a gas-phase molecular complex. active_space_norb is left EMPTY: the paper specifies RAS2 only by orbital character (Pr 4f, 6s, 5d) and never states an orbital count, and counting them would be inference. active_space_nel = 2 is the stated Pr3+ electron count; Pr4+ has one active electron. d_electron_count 4f2 follows from the stated Pr(III) assignment (Pr is a 4f lanthanide). The Ti, Zr and Hf codopant curves are CCSD(T) on an effectively single-determinant reference and carry no real active space, so they get no separate row.

compound_name: Cl-(Por+.)Fe(IV)=O, the chloride-ligated iron(IV)-oxo porphyrin pi-cation radical (Compound I model), reactant of the olefin epoxidation
ligand_set: porphyrin pi-cation radical, an axial oxo and an axial chloride
geometry_source: DFT optimization at LC-BLYP with cc-pVTZ on Fe, O, Cl and N and cc-pVDZ on C and H
method: CASPT2, spin-orbit CASPT2 (SO-CASPT2) and SAC-CI on DFT-optimized geometries
software: MOLCAS 7.8 for the CASPT2 and SO-CASPT2; Gaussian 09 (slightly modified for file access) for the SAC-CI
basis_set: cc-pVTZ on Fe, O, Cl and N and cc-pVDZ on C and H for the geometry; the CASPT2 basis is not separately stated
active_space_orbital_description: five Fe 3d-derived orbitals (d_pi_xz*, d_pi_yz*, d_sigma_z2*, d_sigma_x2-y2*, d_delta_xy) plus four porphyrin pi and pi* orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies of the low-lying states (eV), UB3LYP / CASPT2 / SAC-CI: quartet-1 0.00 / 1.05 / 0.46; quartet-2 - / 0.00 / -; quartet-3 - / 0.61 / 0.00; doublet-1 0.006 / - / 1.38; doublet-2 - / 0.01 / 1.38; doublet-3 - / - / 0.83; sextet-1 0.64 / 0.03 / 4.72; sextet-2 - / 3.78 / 2.66. Configurations: quartet-1 (dxy)2(pixz*)1(piyz*)1(a2u)1; quartet-2 [(dxy)1(sigma_x2-y2*)1(alphabeta-betaalpha)](pixz*)1(piyz*)1(a2u)1; quartet-3 (dxy)2(pixz*)1(piyz*)1(a1u)1; doublet-2 (dxy)2(a2u)1[(pixz*)1(piyz*)1 singlet-coupled]; sextet-1 (dxy)1(pixz*)1(piyz*)1(a2u)1(sigma_x2-y2*)1. All three methods agree on a quartet ground state, matching experiment, but assign different configurations: UB3LYP gives quartet-1 and SAC-CI quartet-3 (both with (dxy)2(pixz*)1(piyz*)1 on Fe but differing in the symmetry of the porphyrin pi-radical orbital), while CASPT2 gives quartet-2, which has a singlet-coupled (dxy)1(sigma_x2-y2*)1 pair and four singly occupied 3d orbitals. Flipping that pair to triplet coupling gives sextet-1, nearly degenerate at 0.03 eV. Because the quartet and doublet states lie so close, spin-orbit interaction matters: SO-CASPT2 produces a new (quartet-2)+(doublet-2) ground state and reproduces the experimental absorption peaks well.
reference_short: Ukaji, Abe, Hada, Fujii, High-Spin Fe(IV)-Oxo Porphyrin Complexes in Epoxidation Reaction of Olefin: A CASPT2 Study, J. Comput. Chem. Jpn. 2014, 13, 167-168
notes: active_space_nel is left EMPTY: the paper specifies the active space only as nine orbitals (five Fe 3d plus four porphyrin pi/pi*) and never states an electron count. d_electron_count 3d4 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(IV) assignment. Japanese-language short communication. SAC-CI used smaller bases (cc-pVTZ on Fe,O,N,Cl; 6-31G on C; STO-6G on H) to save time.

compound_name: Cl(Por)Fe(III), the chloroiron(III) porphyrin product of the epoxidation
ligand_set: porphyrin dianion and an axial chloride
geometry_source: DFT optimization at LC-BLYP with cc-pVTZ on Fe, O, Cl and N and cc-pVDZ on C and H
method: CASPT2, spin-orbit CASPT2 (SO-CASPT2) and SAC-CI on DFT-optimized geometries
software: MOLCAS 7.8 for the CASPT2 and SO-CASPT2; Gaussian 09 (slightly modified for file access) for the SAC-CI
basis_set: cc-pVTZ on Fe, O, Cl and N and cc-pVDZ on C and H for the geometry; the CASPT2 basis is not separately stated
active_space_orbital_description: five Fe 3d-derived orbitals (d_pi_xz*, d_pi_yz*, d_sigma_z2*, d_sigma_x2-y2*, d_delta_xy) plus four porphyrin pi and pi* orbitals
electronic_structure_description: All three methods give a sextet ground state, reproducing experiment. The gaps between multiplicities differ sharply between methods: SAC-CI puts the quartet only 0.003 eV above the sextet, whereas CASPT2 places it 1.61 eV higher - much larger than either of the other two methods.
reference_short: Ukaji, Abe, Hada, Fujii, High-Spin Fe(IV)-Oxo Porphyrin Complexes in Epoxidation Reaction of Olefin: A CASPT2 Study, J. Comput. Chem. Jpn. 2014, 13, 167-168
notes: Product side of the same reaction. active_space_nel left empty for the same reason as the reactant row. d_electron_count 3d5 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(III) assignment. SAC-CI basis for the product: 6-31G* on Fe and O, 6-31G on N, Cl and C, STO-6G on H.

ligand_set: six cyanide ligands, octahedral; aqueous solution treated with PCM
point_group: no symmetry imposed in the RASSCF calculations (the complex is octahedral)
geometry_source: geometry optimized at BLYP with LANL2DZ on Fe and 6-311+G(d) on C and N in Gaussian 09
method: restricted active space SCF (RASSCF) with RASPT2 for dynamic correlation (imaginary level shift 0.4 Hartree) and RASSI-SO for spin-orbit coupling in the L-edge spectra, computing X-ray absorption and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering spectra
basis_set: relativistic ANO-RCC-VTZ on Fe, C and N
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic Douglas-Kroll-Hess; spin-orbit coupling by state interaction (RASSI-SO) including directly interacting singlet and triplet states
active_space_orbital_description: for the Fe L-edge: three Fe 2p, two sigma-bonding sigma(eg), three 3d(t2g), two sigma-antibonding sigma*(eg), and three pi*(CN) + Fe d(t2g) orbitals. One hole allowed in the 2p orbitals; two holes in sigma(eg) and 3d(t2g); two particles in sigma*(eg) and pi*(CN)+d(t2g).
active_space_protocol: orbitals first optimized in a state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest fifteen valence singlet states, after which all occupied MOs except the active ones were frozen. For the nitrogen K-edge the space instead uses six N 1s orbitals in place of the three Fe 2p, complemented by twelve MOs of mainly bonding pi(CN) character to capture relaxation from them during the RIXS process, with single excitations from N 1s, pi(CN) and sigma(eg) and double excitations from 3d(t2g).
nroots_per_mult: lowest fifteen valence singlet states in the orbital-optimization state average
electronic_structure_description: Orbital compositions from RASSCF versus ground-state DFT: d character in the sigma(eg) MOs 33% (similar in both methods, quantifying sigma donation); d contribution to 3d(t2g) 99% (RASSCF) vs 77% (DFT); to pi*(CN)(t2g) 55% vs 16%; to sigma*(eg) 35% vs 57%. Orbital coefficients change substantially once relaxation on core-hole formation is included, the largest change being in the ligand pi* orbitals, whose d character it decreases. In the Fe L-edge XAS the 2p -> sigma*(eg) and 2p -> pi*(CN)+d(t2g) transitions have almost equal intensity, whereas in Fe(CO)5 the second is much more intense - so relative to iron pentacarbonyl, aqueous ferrocyanide shows stronger sigma donation and weaker pi back-donation. Ligand-to-metal charge transfer bands at the Fe L-edge and metal-to-ligand bands at the N K-edge are observed directly and give the orbital mixing.
reference_short: Engel, Bokarev, Suljoti, Garcia-Diez, Lange, Atak, Golnak, Kothe, Dantz, Kuhn, Aziz, Chemical Bonding in Aqueous Ferrocyanide: Experimental and Theoretical X-ray Spectroscopic Study
notes: d_electron_count 3d6 is arithmetic from the iron(II) oxidation state stated in the compound's name (potassium hexacyanoferrate(II)). nel/norb record the Fe L-edge space; the N K-edge space is different and is described in active_space_protocol. The comparison Fe(CO)5 numbers come from the group's earlier study, not from this work, and Fe(CO)5 was computed without solvent.

compound_name: [Fe(CN)5(NO)]2- nitroprusside anion, N-bound (eta1-N, 'standard'), O-bound (eta1-O, 'reverse') and side-on (eta2-NO, 'flat') linkage isomers
ligand_set: five cyanide ligands and one nitrosyl, bound through N, through O, or side-on
point_group: Cs constraint used for the DFT ground-state optimizations; the Gaussian transition-state search was run without symmetry
geometry_source: ADF-optimized structures: B3LYP with triple-zeta basis sets on all atoms, ZORA scalar relativistic corrections and COSMO methanol (eps = 32.7), with ground-state minima confirmed by all-real frequencies; separate Gaussian 09 B3LYP/6-31+G**(C,N,O)/SDD(Fe,Ru,Os) scans with PCM methanol to locate the transition states
method: multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) on a RASSCF reference, with PCM methanol solvent corrections; DFT and TD-DFT for the structures, energy profiles and absorption spectra
software: MOLCAS 8.2 for the RASSCF/MS-CASPT2; ADF and Gaussian 09 for the DFT
relativistic_treatment: ANO-RCC relativistic basis sets for the multireference step; ZORA in the DFT optimizations
electronic_structure_description: At MS-CASPT2 the S0 state of the standard N-bound isomer is again the global minimum of the three isomers, confirming the DFT ordering: the flat (side-on) isomer lies 1.62 eV and the reverse (O-bound) isomer 1.50 eV above it, with the reverse now slightly favoured over the flat. Conformational isomerism is unlikely on the S0 surface: the barriers for NO interconversion exceed 2 eV because the NO ligand almost decoordinates along the path. The osmium analogue shows a near-degeneracy of two excited states, and its isomerism, like the ruthenium one, should proceed adiabatically along the S0 surface.
reference_short: Daniel, Gourlaouen, Structural and Optical Properties of Metal-Nitrosyl Complexes, Molecules 2019, 24, 3638
notes: Only the iron complex received the RASSCF/MS-CASPT2 treatment; the ruthenium and osmium members of the [M(CN)5(NO)]2- series were studied at the DFT/TD-DFT level only, so they get no rows. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty: NO is a non-innocent ligand and the paper assigns no oxidation state to the metal. The composition of the (10,10) space is not described.

compound_name: non-heme iron(IV)-oxo-chloride complex reacting with cycloalkenes (epoxidation versus hydroxylation)
ligand_set: a tetradentate N4 chelate ligand, an oxo group and a chloride
geometry_source: B3LYP-D3 optimized geometries (6-31G* for optimization, 6-311++G** single points plus ZPE and thermal/entropic corrections); SMD solvation applied by repeating the whole process from the gas-phase geometries
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with the CASPT2 energies placed on the diagonal of the two-component Hamiltonian matrix; Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals with a 1e-6 au threshold and a level shift of 5 au in the CASSCF
basis_set: ANO-RCC contracted to [6s5p3d2f1g] for Fe, [4s3p2d] for the ligating O and N, [3s2p] for C, [4s3p] for Cl and [2s] for H
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH2) one-electron spinless Hamiltonian, for spin-free relativistic effects
active_space_orbital_description: the five Fe 3d orbitals, the three oxo 2p orbitals, and one sigma orbital based on the chelate ligand
electronic_structure_description: DFT and CASPT2 agree that all the reactions proceed on the quintet potential energy surface. The gas-phase iron(IV)-oxo-chloride complex prefers epoxidation, unlike condensed-phase iron(IV)-oxo complexes where hydrogen atom transfer usually dominates; the DFT transition-state energies for the epoxidation and hydroxylation pathways account for the observed chemoselectivity, and the SMD implicit solvation model predicts a relative increase in the hydroxylation channel.
reference_short: Terencio, Andris, Gamba, Srnec, Costas, Roithova, Chemoselectivity in the Oxidation of Cycloalkenes with a Non-Heme Iron(IV)-Oxo-Chloride Complex: Epoxidation vs. Hydroxylation Selectivity, J. Am. Soc. Mass Spectrom. 2019
notes: The multireference content is a CASPT2 check on the spin state of the reacting surface; the reaction energetics themselves are DFT. d_electron_count 3d4 is arithmetic from the stated iron(IV) assignment. Some optimized structures retain a small imaginary frequency corresponding to relative rotation of the iron complex and the cycloalkane substrate, which the authors flag in their coordinate files.

point_group: C2v (highest Abelian subgroup used); Lz^2 expectation values checked so both degenerate components of each Lambda state are accounted for
geometry_source: R/UCCSD(T) ground-state geometries; SO-CASPT2/aQ-PP potential curves from seven single points at r - re = -0.3, -0.2, -0.1, 0.0, +0.1, +0.3, +0.5 bohr around the CCSD(T)/awQ-DK equilibrium bond length
method: state-averaged CASSCF for the spin-free Lambda-S states followed by CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0.28), with spin-orbit coupling to give the Omega states (SO-CASPT2); CCSD(T) and the Feller-Peterson-Dixon composite scheme for the thermochemistry
basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ (n = D, T, Q) on C and cc-pVnZ-PP on U with a 60-electron small-core effective core potential optimized in multiconfigurational Dirac-Hartree-Fock calculations (denoted an-PP); the CCSD(T) reference geometries used DKH3 with aug-cc-pVnZ-DK on C and cc-pwCVnZ-DK3 on U
relativistic_treatment: 60-electron small-core relativistic ECP on U for the multireference work; third-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH3) for the coupled-cluster part
active_space_orbital_description: nine orbitals of dominant carbon 2pz and uranium 5f/7s character (4 a1, 2 b1, 2 b2, 1 a2 in C2v); the same orbital set is used for all three charge states, with the electron count changing

Test calculations adding the U 5s-6d and C 2s orbitals showed little effect on the low-lying states. Earlier work on UC used (10,16); this choice follows the (3,8) space used for UN.

Earlier CASPT2-SO work found a quintet ground state with Omega = 3, re 1.863 A, we 945 cm-1, and the measured fundamental vibration is 871.7 cm-1 in Ne and 827.8 cm-1 in Ar. T1 diagnostics for the ground states of all three species run 0.03 to 0.05.

electronic_structure_description: At both CASSCF and CASPT2 the ground state is a singlet, with three 5f atomic orbitals per U atom contributing to the actinide-actinide bond: one sigma and two pi orbitals give a formal triple bond with an effective bond order of 2.52. The triplet lies very close in energy with configuration sigma1 pix2 piy2 phi1 and the same EBO of 2.52. CASPT2 places the open-shell quintet and septet 30 kcal/mol above the singlet, contradicting earlier DFT claims that the U-U bond inside C60 is an artifact of cage compression. PBE0/TZP relative energies (kcal/mol), U-U and average U-C distances (A) and U2 spin density: orientation O1 - singlet 8.7, 2.388, 2.54, 0.000; triplet 14.6, 2.422, 2.51, 2.122; quintet 5.0, 2.453, 2.51, 4.285; septet 24.3, 2.442, 2.46, 4.498. Orientation O2 (one U tilted off the C3 axis) - singlet 0.0, 2.359, 2.44, 0.000; triplet 1.0, 2.374, 2.46, 2.142; quintet 10.2, 2.394, 2.47, 4.182; septet 17.3, 2.544, 2.45, 5.850. Six valence electrons transfer from U2 to the fullerene, leaving U(3+) ions with 5f3 configurations.

electronic_structure_description: For the short U-U distance the results closely match U2@C60: a singlet ground state with a sigma2 pix2 piy2 configuration and a formal triple U-U bond of effective bond order 2.57, with CASSCF orbitals resembling the DFT ones. For the long U-U arrangement different electronic configurations appear, with the six valence electrons of the two U atoms distributed differently, and the short-U-U orientation is destabilized by about 20 kcal/mol relative to it, so the triple bond is weakened - consistent with recent results on the naked U2 dimer. The U2 arrangement with d(U-U) = 2.406 A in U2@Ih(7)-C80 lies about 7 kcal/mol above the long one. Both arrangements are present in the larger fullerenes C78 and C80, while inside C60 the U ions keep metal-metal bond lengths below 2.5 A with effective bond orders near 2.5.
reference_short: Moreno-Vicente, Rosello, Chen, Echegoyen, Dunk, Rodriguez-Fortea, de Graaf, Poblet, Are U-U Bonds Inside Fullerenes Really Unwilling Bonds?, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2023, 145, 6710-6718
notes: Two conformations of the same endofullerene condensed into one row; their different active spaces are in active_space_protocol and nel/norb record the larger (6,13) space used for the long-U-U conformation. Same oxidation-state assignment as the C60 row.

geometry_source: B3LYP-D3 optimized structures with a quasi-relativistic small-core 4f-in-valence pseudopotential on La ([14s13p10d8f6g]/[10s8p5d4f3g] valence basis) and cc-pVTZ on N
method: CASSCF reference followed by CASPT2 for the dynamic correlation, used to confirm the DFT electronic structures; Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals
basis_set: all-electron ANO-RCC of triple-zeta valence plus polarization quality: 24s21p15d5f3g2h/[8s7p5d2f1g] for La and 14s9p4d3f2g/[4s3p2d1f] for N
active_space_protocol: active spaces constructed from state-averaged test calculations using 5 roots and the observed orbital occupations, balanced against cost for the larger structures: 7/10 for La(N2) and 11/12 for La(N2)2 and La(N2)6. Frozen core: N 1s and La up to 3d.
nroots_per_mult: 5 roots in the state-averaged test calculations used to choose the space
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2 confirms the B3LYP electronic structures: the dominant configuration in the CAS carries more than 85% weight for the quartet states and more than 70% for the doublets, with minor contributions of only a few percent, so these systems are reasonably described by DFT for structure and bonding. The doublet-quartet energy differences are mostly very small and the paper warns they should be treated with caution. End-on coordination is more stable than side-on in general, and the first coordination sphere holds eight N2 ligands end-on but only six side-on.
reference_short: Kovacs, Coordination of N2 ligands to lanthanum: the complexes La(N2)1-8, Struct. Chem. 2018, 29, 1825-1837
notes: Only selected members of the La(N2)x, x = 1-8 series received CASPT2 treatment; the rest are DFT only. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty - the paper reports natural charges and orbital occupations rather than a formal oxidation state, and La here is not in a well-defined ionic state. The orbital composition of the active spaces is not described.

geometry_source: geometries and harmonic frequencies from CCSD(T)/awn-DK, correlating the H 1s and Th 6s, 6p, 6d, 7s valence electrons plus the Th 5s, 5p, 5d core
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with spin-orbit coupling by the state-interacting method (SO-CASPT2); CCSD(T)/CBS and the Feller-Peterson-Dixon composite scheme for the thermochemistry
basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ on H and cc-pwCVnZ-DK3 on Th (denoted awn-DK), n = D and T
relativistic_treatment: third-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH3) for the coupled-cluster work; spin-orbit matrix elements built from the Th pseudopotential spin-orbit operator at the CASSCF level
active_space_orbital_description: eight orbitals dominated by the Th 7s, 6d and selected 7p; all lower orbitals constrained doubly occupied. The choice of eight follows the group's earlier ThH work and others' ThX (X = halogen) studies, and rests on the anionic character of the ligands.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(2/8) for ThH2 (a Th(II) centre, low-lying singlets and triplets from the 5f1 6d1 and 6d2 atomic ion configurations) and CASSCF(3/8) for ThH2- (a Th(I) centre, doublets and quartets from 6d1 7s2), on the same effective eight orbitals. Frozen core in the CASPT2: all Th orbitals through 5d (6s6p5f7s valence). IPEA shift 0.28.
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic electron affinity 0.82 eV and vertical detachment energy 0.84 eV at the Feller-Peterson-Dixon level, against an experimental VDE of 0.871 eV. The spin-orbit correction to the electron affinity is significant for ThH2 and falls off sharply for the larger hydrides. The observed ThH2- photoelectron spectrum has many transitions, all predicted at the SO-CASPT2 level. Bond dissociation energy ThH2 -> ThH + H is 75.0 kcal/mol before corrections and 67.1 kcal/mol after; heat of formation 117.7 kcal/mol at 0 K and 116.7 at 298 K. NBO shows a significant Th+H- ionic contribution with very little 5f participation, the Th valence being dominated by 7s and 6d - except in ThH2-, where there is a significant additional contribution.
reference_short: Vasiliu, Marshall, Zhu, Bowen, Dixon, Molecular Properties of Thorium Hydrides: Electron Affinities and Thermochemistry
notes: Neutral and anion condensed into one row; their spaces differ only in electron count and both are in active_space_protocol, with nel recording the neutral. d_electron_count left empty: Th(II) here is 5f1 6d1 / 6d2, not a clean single-shell d or f count.

compound_name: ThH3, ThH4, ThH5 and their anions
geometry_source: geometries and harmonic frequencies from CCSD(T)/awn-DK, correlating the H 1s and Th 6s, 6p, 6d, 7s valence electrons plus the Th 5s, 5p, 5d core
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with spin-orbit coupling by the state-interacting method (SO-CASPT2); CCSD(T)/CBS and the Feller-Peterson-Dixon composite scheme for the thermochemistry
basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ on H and cc-pwCVnZ-DK3 on Th (denoted awn-DK), n = D and T
relativistic_treatment: third-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH3) for the coupled-cluster work; spin-orbit matrix elements built from the Th pseudopotential spin-orbit operator at the CASSCF level
active_space_orbital_description: eight orbitals dominated by the Th 7s, 6d and selected 7p; all lower orbitals constrained doubly occupied. The choice of eight follows the group's earlier ThH work and others' ThX (X = halogen) studies, and rests on the anionic character of the ligands.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF in the same effective eight orbitals: ThH3 is a Th(III) centre with a single valence electron giving doublet states; ThH3- gives Th(II) again, so singlets and triplets from two electrons in eight orbitals. Same frozen core and IPEA shift as ThH2.
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic electron affinities 0.88, 0.51 and 2.36 eV and vertical detachment energies 0.88, 0.81 and 4.38 eV for x = 3, 4 and 5, against experimental VDEs of 0.88 eV for x = 3 and 4.09 eV for x = 5. Bond dissociation energies rise from 67 to 75 kcal/mol going from x = 2 to x = 4 (ThH3 -> ThH2 + H 72.7 raw / 69.4 corrected; ThH4 -> ThH3 + H 79.5 / 74.6), while ThH5 is much lower at 36.5 / 30.7 kcal/mol because it is really a complex of H2 with ThH3. Heats of formation: ThH3 100.0 (0 K) / 98.4 (298 K), ThH4 77.1 / 74.5, ThH5 98.0 / 94.9 kcal/mol. Hydride affinities for x = 2 to 4 are remarkably uniform at 67-71 kcal/mol and essentially independent of the number of hydrogens; the spin-orbit correction matters for ThH2 but is 1 kcal/mol or less thereafter.
reference_short: Vasiliu, Marshall, Zhu, Bowen, Dixon, Molecular Properties of Thorium Hydrides: Electron Affinities and Thermochemistry
notes: Three hydrides condensed into one row, all sharing the eight-orbital space; nel records the single valence electron of the Th(III) ThH3 case, with the rest in active_space_protocol. d_electron_count left empty for the same reason as the ThH2 row.

point_group: C2v (active orbitals labelled 5 a1, 3 b1, 3 b2, 2 a2)
geometry_source: CCSD(T) potential energy functions from seven single points at r - re = -0.3, -0.2, -0.1, 0.0, +0.1, +0.3, +0.5 bohr around the approximate equilibrium bond length
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with spin-orbit coupling by the state-interacting approach; CCSD(T)/CBS and the Feller-Peterson-Dixon scheme for the thermochemistry
basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ on H and cc-pwCVnZ-DK3 on U (denoted as/awn-DK)
active_space_orbital_description: thirteen orbitals of predominantly U 5f, 6d and 7s character (5 a1, 3 b1, 3 b2, 2 a2); the lower-energy U 5s, 5p, 5d, 6s, 6p and H 1s orbitals are constrained doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: An initial (5,12) space (4 a1, 3 b1, 3 b2, 2 a2), following Cao et al., failed to describe the states of UH-, so the 6d(z2) orbital was added, giving the final (5,13) for UH and (6,13) for UH-. The Lambda-S states of both species were state-averaged to give a common set of molecular orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 4I(9/2). Spectroscopic parameters Te, re, we, wexe and Be and potential energy curves are reported for the low-lying Omega states. Adiabatic electron affinity 0.457 eV, in excellent agreement with the experimental 0.462 +/- 0.013 eV; lowest vertical detachment energy 0.495 eV; adiabatic ionization energy 6.092 eV. Bond dissociation energies 223.2 kJ/mol for UH, 194.5 for UH- and 235.5 for UH+ - the UH value about 20% below that of ThH. NBO analysis shows a significant U+H- ionic component in the bond. For U+H- the coupling gives low-lying quartets and sextets; for U0H- it gives a manifold from septets down to singlets, but singlets and triplets lie very high so only quintets and septets were computed.
reference_short: de Melo, Vasiliu, Marshall, Zhu, Tufekci, Ciborowski, Blankenhorn, Bowen, Dixon, Experimental and Computational Description of the Interaction of H and H- with U
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty: the paper describes the bonding through NBO ionic character and U 5f/6d/7s occupations rather than a formal oxidation state.
