compound_name: [CuOCu]2+ mono-oxygen-bridged dicopper active site in Cu-CHA zeolite, and its reaction with methane (homolytic versus heterolytic C-H activation)
formula: [CuOCu]2+ in an 89-atom (small) or 145-atom (large) cluster cut from chabazite, plus CH4
ligand_set: the bridging oxygen of the [CuOCu]2+ core and the framework oxygens of the eight-membered ring of chabazite connecting two cages; methane as substrate
geometry_source: geometries and thermodynamic functions from B3LYP-D3(BJ) on both the 89-atom small model and the 145-atom large model along the entire reaction path; the DMRG/CASPT2 energies are single points on those geometries, with the B3LYP-D3(BJ) thermodynamic corrections added to give enthalpies. Thermodynamics also recomputed at 473.15 K
method: CASPT2 on a DMRG reference with the cu(4) cumulant approximation to the four-particle density matrix (DMRG/cu(4)-CASPT2), using the spin-adapted DMRG algorithm; compared against DFT with 97-98 exchange-correlation functionals
software: OpenMolcas interfaced with CheMPS2 for the DMRG/CASPT2; Turbomole 7.4 and ORCA 5.0.3 (with Libxc) for the DFT
basis_set: relativistic ANO-RCC with extensive contractions - Cu [7s6p5d3f2g1h]; C and O [4s3p2d1f]; H [3s2p1d]; Al and Si [5s4p2d1f] - with smaller sets on the terminal SiHn groups (basis III); Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals at a 1e-6 au threshold
active_space_orbital_description: the copper (3d, 4d) and oxygen (2s, 2p, 3s, 3p) shells of the [CuOCu]2+ cluster - covering the covalent Cu-O-Cu bonds and the Cu 3d and O 2s/2p double-shell effects - plus the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the reactive C-H bond of methane; chosen by the standard rules for transition metals in a ligand coordination environment
electronic_structure_description: Homolytic C-H dissociation proceeds most favourably through a triplet (S = 1) transition state TS1r, while the heterolytic H-abstraction transition state TS1n has a singlet (S = 0) ground state. DMRG/cu(4)-CASPT2 comes down clearly on the heterolytic route: activation enthalpy 12.3 kcal/mol against 21.1 kcal/mol for homolytic C-H dissociation. The DFT answer is strongly functional-dependent - B3LYP, almost the only functional used in previous cluster-model studies, prefers homolytic abstraction, whereas many other functionals, hybrid meta-GGAs in particular, agree with DMRG/cu(4)-CASPT2 on heterolytic activation. This reopens the debate on the general validity of the radical rebound mechanism for methane hydroxylation by [CuOCu]2+ in copper zeolites.
reference_short: Phung, Yanai, Plessers, Sels, Schoonheydt, Pierloot, Homolytic versus Heterolytic Methane Hydroxylation in Copper Zeolites
notes: SOLID-STATE SYSTEM: the [CuOCu]2+ core sits in the eight-membered ring of the chabazite framework and is modelled as an 89- or 145-atom cluster carved from the zeolite with terminal SiHn caps, not as an isolated molecular complex. d_electron_count 3d9 is arithmetic from the Cu(II) assignment the paper states for the active core. The DMRG/CASPT2 set was run only on the small model.

compound_name: FeO(OH)2 monomer, a model for the [FeO]2+ (hydro)oxide group, and its hydrogen-abstraction reaction with methane
formula: FeO(OH)2 (plus CH4 along the reaction path)
ligand_set: a terminal ferryl oxygen and two hydroxide ligands; methane as substrate at the transition state
geometry_source: B3LYP-optimized geometries used for all CASSCF/CASPT2 single points, at the 5A1 and 5B2 stationary structures (designated A and B) and along the reaction path: reactants R and R', transition state TS and product P (the DFT labels MI, MI', MII, MIII)
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with an imaginary shift of 0.2 to remove intruder states, used to verify broken-symmetry DFT results
basis_set: Stuttgart-Dresden-Bonn effective core potential on Fe; cc-pVDZ on all other atoms
relativistic_treatment: Stuttgart-Dresden-Bonn effective core potential on Fe
active_space_orbital_description: the five iron d orbitals, the three 2p orbitals of the ferryl oxygen, and the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-H bond of methane
electronic_structure_description: The CASSCF quintet ground state of the monomer without methane has the same ferryl electron configuration B3LYP predicts, its natural orbitals matching the paired orbitals of the B3LYP 5A1 solution. The CASSCF first excited state at that same geometry instead has a distinct oxyl structure, shown by negative Mulliken spin density on the terminal oxygen. Mulliken spin densities (Fe1, O1, O2, O3): A structure ground state 3.72, 0.16, 0.05, 0.05; A first excited state 4.05, -0.20, 0.07, 0.07; B structure ground state 4.28, -0.44, 0.08, 0.08; B first excited state 4.31, -0.48, 0.08, 0.08. The negative spin density on O1 correlates with increased positive spin density on Fe, so the excitation carries charge transfer from O1 to Fe, and the ground-to-excited change is close to the polarization density estimated for the H-abstraction transition state. The beta-spin occupied pi_y*(O) orbital lies in the molecular plane and is the key orbital for abstracting hydrogen from methane at the transition state. Another oxyl-type state of 5B1 symmetry lies 25 kcal/mol above the ferryl ground state and does not participate in the methane reaction. The whole picture depends strongly on whether the bridging ligand is -O- or -OH- in the iron hydroxides.
reference_short: Kovalskii, Shubin, Chen, Ovchinnikov, Ruzankin, Hasegawa, Zilberberg, Parmon, Hidden radical reactivity of the [FeO]2+ group of the (hydro)oxide species in the H-abstraction from methane: a DFT and CASPT2 study
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty deliberately: the paper's whole subject is that the ground state of [FeO]2+ is contested between oxyl Fe(III)-O and ferryl Fe(IV)=O, and it declines to settle on one assignment. The CASSCF axis convention differs from the DFT one - the paper notes that the DFT 5B2 state corresponds to 5B1 in CASSCF because the molecular plane was taken as xz. Tetramer Fe4O5(OH)3 models discussed elsewhere in the paper are DFT only.

compound_name: family of quasi-isotropic Mn(II) and Mn2(II) Schiff-base complexes 1-5 with Ni(II)-containing ligands, zero-field splitting of the sextet ground state
formula: e.g. [{NiL1Mn(H2O)2(MeOH)}{NiL1}2](ClO4)2 (1) and [Mn{NiL1}2](ClO4)2 (2); complexes 4 and 5 have Ni(mu-O)2Mn(mu-O)2Ni and Mn2Ni2 cores
ligand_set: o-vanillin-derived Schiff base ligands L1-L3 binding Ni(II) in the inner N2O2 cavity and Mn(II) in the external oxygen-donor cavity, with water and methanol completing the Mn coordination; the square-planar Ni(II) sites are diamagnetic
geometry_source: experimental X-ray crystal geometries used directly, without optimization
method: CASSCF followed by NEVPT2, with the zero-field-splitting tensor D extracted including the spin-orbit coupling correction
active_space_orbital_description: five electrons in the five active 3d molecular orbitals of Mn(II)
electronic_structure_description: Zero-field splitting of the sextet ground state, relative energies in cm-1 with the splitting parameters and calculated g values, for complexes 1* (the simplified Mn(mu-O)2Ni moiety), 1, 4 (two independent molecules) and 5: S0/S1 0.00 for all; S2/S3 0.27, 0.33, 0.21/0.11, 0.18; S4/S5 0.54, 0.61, 0.32/0.16, 0.41. D = 0.077, -0.090, -0.053/-0.056, -0.080 cm-1; E/D = 0.332, 0.265, 0.101/0.036, 0.277; g values all essentially isotropic near 2.0021 (g_iso 2.00206, 2.00206, 2.00209, 2.00206). Experimental EPR gives D = 0.080 cm-1 with E/D = 0.20 (or -0.084 with E/D 0.20) for complex 1, and D = 0.205 cm-1 with E/D = 0.036 (or -0.207 with E/D 0.035) for complex 4. The computed values for 4 are slightly underestimated but comparable, and complex 5 closely reproduces both the experimental D and the rhombicity. The sextet is the only possible electronic ground state and carries full weight; the quartets lie above 20000-25000 cm-1 before spin-orbit coupling and contribute negligibly, so the zero-field splitting produces three nearly degenerate levels. This is the first polynuclear Mn(II) complex with an S = 5 ground state to show slow relaxation of the magnetization.
reference_short: Pilichos, Font-Bardia, Aullon, Mayans, Escuer, Family of Quasi-Isotropic MnII and Mn2II Complexes Exhibiting Slow Relaxation of the Magnetization, Inorg. Chem. 2024, 63, 20415-20426
notes: Five closely related complexes sharing one active space, basis and program, condensed into a single row with the full per-complex ZFS table. d_electron_count 3d5 is arithmetic from the stated Mn(II) assignment and matches the high-spin d5 configuration the paper invokes throughout. The magnetic fitting of the chi-M-T data is experimental, not multireference: the paper argues that the decay for 1 and 2 comes from weak intermolecular interactions (zJ' about 0.015 cm-1) rather than from D near 1 cm-1, which would be unrealistic for Mn(II) in an O-donor environment.

geometry_source: potential energy curves computed as a function of internuclear distance; experimental bond energies from threshold photodissociation of FeCr+ in a cryogenic quadrupole ion trap
method: NEVPT2 on state-averaged CASSCF wave functions, with spin-orbit coupling added by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory; unrestricted CCSD(T) and CAM-B3LYP alongside
basis_set: DKH-def2-SVP for the CASSCF/NEVPT2 (DKH-def2-TZVP for the coupled-cluster work), with segmented all-electron relativistically contracted (SARC) Coulomb fitting basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: the five 3d orbitals and the 4s orbital of each of Fe and Cr
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(13,12) with equal state averaging over the ten doublet, quartet, sextet, octet and dectet potential energy curves correlating with the Cr+(6S, 3d5) + Fe(5D, 3d6 4s2) and Cr(7S, 3d5 4s1) + Fe+(6D, 3d6 4s1) asymptotes
electronic_structure_description: Both CCSD(T) and SOC+NEVPT2 give a 2Sigma+ ground state for FeCr+. Assigning it confidently is hard because six different spin-orbit states are predicted within 400 cm-1 of the ground state - an earlier DFT study at BPW91/6-311+G* had proposed 2Delta instead. Experimental threshold photodissociation gives D(Fe-Cr+) = 1.655 +/- 0.006 eV and D(Fe+-Cr) = 2.791 +/- 0.006 eV. The measured D(Fe-Cr+) is 10-20% larger than the computed values: CAM-B3LYP 1.48 eV, NEVPT2 1.40 eV and CCSD(T) 1.35 eV. States built on an s-sigma bonding configuration give shallower wells and longer bonds than those with a s-sigma^2 configuration. The paper emphasises that an abrupt rise in photodissociation yield at threshold requires a dense manifold of states.
reference_short: Marlton, Liu, Bieske, Bond dissociation energy of FeCr+ determined through threshold photodissociation in a cryogenic ion trap, J. Chem. Phys. 2024, 160, 034301
notes: A heteronuclear metal dimer cation, so metal_center lists both metals. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty: the paper describes the system through its atomic dissociation asymptotes (Cr+ 3d5 / Fe 3d6 4s2 and Cr 3d5 4s1 / Fe+ 3d6 4s1) rather than assigning formal oxidation states to the bound molecule. The measured bond energy exceeding every computed value by 10-20% is the paper's own headline discrepancy.

compound_name: Fe-pz, the spin-crossover Fe(II)-pyrazolylborate complex [Fe(H2B(pz)2)2(bipy)]-type, isolated molecule and deposited on Au(111)
ligand_set: two bidentate dihydrobis(pyrazolyl)borate ligands and a bipyridine-type chelate giving an FeN6 core
geometry_source: low-temperature and high-temperature X-ray bulk structures used for the LS and HS states respectively; rPBE-optimized geometries also used for comparison (mean Fe-N deviations from X-ray of 0.05 A for LS and 0.08 A for HS)
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 (imaginary level shift 0.20 au, IPEA scanned from 0.25 to 0.5 au) and, separately, state-specific CASSCF followed by NEVPT2 in both strongly and partially contracted schemes; ab initio ligand field theory (AILFT) for the ligand-field strength; periodic DFT for the surface
software: MOLCAS 8.0 for the CASSCF/CASPT2; ORCA for the NEVPT2 and AILFT; VASP for the periodic DFT
basis_set: ANO-RCC with contractions [5s4p3d2f1g] for Fe, [4s3p1d] for N, [3s3p1d] for C and B, and [2s] for H
active_space_orbital_description: the five Fe 3d orbitals, a second 3d shell to capture the dynamical correlation of the 3d electrons, and two eg-like occupied N ligand orbitals that introduce the ligand-to-metal charge transfer from sigma donation of the N ligands
electronic_structure_description: HS-LS energy difference for the isolated molecule (kJ/mol), on the X-ray geometries: CASPT2 12.1 at IPEA 0.25, 22.1 at 0.4 and 28.3 at 0.5 au - an almost linear dependence on the IPEA shift; NEVPT2 9.7 (partially contracted) and 20.3 (strongly contracted); rPBE 54.1 on the X-ray geometry but 10.0 once both spin states are optimized, 1.3 with zero-point correction, 52.7 with D3 and 44.0 with D3 plus ZPC. The experimental transition enthalpy for the bulk is 10.2 kJ/mol, and the wave-function estimates bracket it; the calculations neglect the intermolecular interactions present in the crystal. Periodic rPBE gives 29.5 kJ/mol for the molecular crystal, 18.2 for the isolated molecule in a periodic cell and 25.1 for the molecule on the Au(111) surface, while PBE (76.3) and SCAN (74.8) badly overestimate and dispersion corrections (PBE+D2 118.4, PBE+D3 95.1, rPBE+D3 65.5) strongly over-favour the low-spin state. For the LIESST photoconversion, NEVPT2 excited states were computed along a model reaction path as a function of the average Fe-N distance, tracking the five lowest singlets, triplets and quintets: blue light (405 nm) promotes a transition to an excited singlet that reaches the HS state through an intersystem crossing with the excited quintet, a pathway that bypasses the intermediate triplets and reproduces both the 405 nm activation and the roughly 600 nm reverse HS-to-LS transition. Deposited on Au(111), laser irradiation at 4.4 K converts up to 69% of molecules to HS.
reference_short: Montenegro-Pohlhammer, Sanchez-de-Armas, Calzado, The deposition of the spin crossover Fe(II)-pyrazolylborate complex on Au(111) surface at molecular level, Chem. Eur. J. 2020
notes: system_class is molecule, not solid-state: the multireference calculations are all on the isolated molecule (gas phase, MOLCAS/ORCA); the surface enters only through periodic DFT+U and rPBE calculations, which are not multireference. d_electron_count 3d6 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(II) assignment. The IPEA scan is deliberate - the paper notes there is no consensus on the right IPEA value for spin-crossover energetics, with literature values from 0.25 to 0.7 au, so it reports upper and lower limits rather than a single number.

compound_name: Fe(III)-Tiron complexes [Fe(Tiron)3]9-, [Fe(Tiron)2(H2O)2]5- and [Fe(Tiron)(H2O)4]-, and the [Fe(H2O)6]3+ aqua ion (Tiron = 4,5-dihydroxy-1,3-benzenedisulfonate)
ligand_set: one to three bidentate catecholate Tiron ligands, with the remaining coordination sites occupied by water
geometry_source: DFT-optimized structures; the calculated [Fe(Tiron)3]9- geometry has Fe-O bond lengths of 2.01-2.09 A averaging 2.05 A, against the X-ray values of 1.950 and 2.109 A (average 2.03 A) and an EXAFS solution value of 2.04 A
method: strongly contracted NEVPT2 (SC-NEVPT2) on state-averaged CASSCF wave functions, used to compute zero-field splitting parameters; the spin-orbit mean-field SOMF(1X) treatment, RI-JK approximation, and SMD bulk water solvation
basis_set: def2-TZVPP with the def2/JK auxiliary basis
active_space_orbital_description: five electrons in the five metal-based Fe 3d orbitals, CAS(5,5)
active_space_protocol: state-averaged CASSCF over one sextet, 24 quartet and 75 doublet roots
nroots_per_mult: 1 sextet; 24 quartets; 75 doublets
electronic_structure_description: Zero-field splitting parameters from NEVPT2 on CASSCF wave functions, for [Fe(Tiron)3]9-, [Fe(Tiron)2(H2O)2]5-, [Fe(Tiron)(H2O)4]- and [Fe(H2O)6]3+ respectively: D = -0.074, -0.220, 0.319 and 0.015 cm-1, with E/D = 0.101, 0.144, 0.094 and 0.008. D is negative for the tris and bis complexes, meaning two of the three Kramers doublets of the S = 5/2 ground state lie above the centre of gravity, and positive for the mono complex and the aqua ion. Accompanying DFT values in the same table: Fe-O(water) distances 2.157, 2.101 and 2.031 A; Fe-O(Tiron) 2.049, 2.004 and 1.981 A; 17O hyperfine coupling constants A_O/hbar of -71.0, -74.8 and -99.3 x 10^6 rad/s. The zero-field splitting lifts the degeneracy of the S = 5/2 magnetic sublevels into three Kramers doublets even at zero field and contributes significantly to electron relaxation; together with the NMRD analysis the calculations show that electronic relaxation depends strongly on the symmetry of the Fe3+ coordination environment.
reference_short: Nucera, Carniato, Baranyai, Platas-Iglesias, Botta, Characterization of the Fe(III)-Tiron System in Solution through an Integrated Approach Combining NMR Relaxometric, Thermodynamic, Kinetic, and Computational Data, Inorg. Chem. 2023, 62, 4272-4283
notes: Four complexes sharing one active space, basis and protocol, condensed into a single row with the full ZFS table. d_electron_count 3d5 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(III) oxidation state and matches the S = 5/2 ground state used throughout. Everything else in the paper - relaxivity, water exchange rates, stability constants, transchelation kinetics - is experimental or DFT, not multireference.

compound_name: ab initio ligand field theory test set: homoleptic octahedral 3d3 Cr(III) complexes with F-, Cl-, Br-, I-, CN- and NH3; 4d3 [MoCl6]3- and [TcF6]2-; 5d3 IrF6 and [ReX6]2- (X = F, Cl, Br); tetrahedral divalent chloride complexes of Ti through Ni; the chelates Cr(acac)3 and Mn(acac)3; and the high-valent [FeO4]2- and [MnO4]3-
metal_center: Cr, Mo, Tc, Ir, Re, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni
ligand_set: halides, cyanide, ammonia, oxide, and acetylacetonate chelates, in octahedral and tetrahedral geometries
geometry_source: DFT geometry optimizations at BP86-D3BJ with grid5 integration and C-PCM at infinite permittivity, to approximate environment effects
method: ab initio ligand field theory (AILFT) parametrized against effective Hamiltonians from three multireference treatments: strongly contracted NEVPT2, the second-order dynamic correlation dressed complete active space method DCD-CAS(2), and Hermitian quasi-degenerate NEVPT2 (HQD-NEVPT2), both of the latter being multistate perturbation theories that let the CASCI coefficients mix and relax under dynamic correlation
software: a development version of ORCA (the DCD-CAS(2) and HQD-NEVPT2 effective Hamiltonians were newly implemented for this work)
basis_set: DKH-def2-TZVP for elements lighter than Kr including the 3d metals, Sapporo-DK-TZP for elements lighter than Xe including the 4d metals, and SARC-DKH-TZVP for everything heavier; auxiliary bases from AutoAux
active_space_orbital_description: the five metal d orbitals; the electron count N is whatever the dn configuration of the particular complex provides, so the space is written CASSCF(N,5)
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(N,5) averaged over all possible roots of all multiplicities, unless otherwise stated; the strongly contracted version of (HQD-)NEVPT2 was used throughout. The LFT model has 15 one-electron ligand-field parameters for a dn configuration (28 for fn) plus the Racah A, B, C parameters
electronic_structure_description: The two multistate methods give AILFT fits with smaller root-mean-square deviations between the ab initio and ligand-field energies than NEVPT2 does. Because NEVPT2 modifies only the diagonal energies while leaving the CASCI coefficients untouched, its rmsd against the LFT model is often an order of magnitude larger, which can partly absorb its accuracy gain over plain CASCI. Comparison of AILFT excitation energies with experiment shows better agreement at the multistate level for some systems, precisely because of the smaller rmsds, though not for all. The earlier observation on [CrF6]3- - that DCD-CAS(2) is a better starting point for AILFT parametrization than NEVPT2 - is confirmed as a general trend. Complexes with a single electron or single hole in the dn manifold were deliberately excluded, since electron-electron repulsion plays no role there and the LFT model parametrizes them exactly.
reference_short: Lang, Atanasov, Neese, Improvement of Ab Initio Ligand Field Theory by Means of Multistate Perturbation Theory, J. Phys. Chem. A 2020, 124, 1025-1037
notes: A method paper condensed into one row over its whole test set. active_space_nel is left EMPTY on purpose: the space is defined as CASSCF(N,5) where N is the dn count of each complex and no single electron number applies. metal_center lists every metal in the set. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty for the same reason - the set deliberately spans different dn occupations, from 3d2 [FeO4]2- and [MnO4]3- at oxidation states +VI and +V up through the tetrahedral divalent chlorides of Ti to Ni.

compound_name: cytochrome P450 catalytic-cycle model compounds: the water-bound resting state, the pentacoordinate 'empty' state, a pyridine-inhibitor-bound active site, and Compound I (Cpd I)
formula: iron porphyrin models with a cysteine-derived thiolate axial ligand; Cpd I additionally carries an atomic oxygen
ligand_set: porphyrin macrocycle with an axial thiolate from cysteine; the fourth model adds a pyridine inhibitor, the resting state a water molecule, and Cpd I an oxo group
geometry_source: truncated active-site model systems of the CYP catalytic cycle; the truncation is justified by Lonsdale et al.'s finding that Cpd I electronic structures are very similar across human CYP isoforms
method: density matrix renormalization group with an n-electron valence state perturbation theory correction (DMRG+NEVPT2), alongside CCSD(T); quantum resource estimation for phase estimation via qubitized quantum walks with three tensor factorizations, compiled to the surface code
active_space_orbital_description: orbitals of the high-spin restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock state localized by the Pipek-Mezey scheme, starting from the five singly occupied orbitals of the high-spin reference
active_space_protocol: a hierarchy of eight nested active spaces (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, X), each a superset of the previous and all with roughly the same filling fraction, built by adding occupied and virtual localized orbitals to the five singly occupied high-spin orbitals. The same hierarchy was constructed for each of the four compounds. The per-space orbital and electron counts are tabulated only in SI Appendix section 8, Table 3, and are not given in the main text. The strategy deliberately aims at a balanced hierarchy for cost and convergence analysis rather than the most efficient space of a given size.
electronic_structure_description: For Compound I in the G active space - the largest DMRG calculation yet performed on any Cpd I model - the doublet lies below the quartet by only 0.02 kcal/mol, so both would be populated at room temperature, while the sextet is 42.7 kcal/mol above the two low-spin states. This is qualitatively consistent with most previous work. The three singly occupied natural orbitals of the doublet are two Fe-O orbitals of pi_xz* and pi_yz* character plus a sulfur nonbonding orbital, the latter mixed with one of the Fe-O orbitals. Cpd I is a polyradical neutral species whose nearly degenerate doublet and quartet ordering remains debated, and it is called a 'chameleon species' because its spin nature shifts with subtle structural changes in the protein. CCSD(T) is accurate within the active space for every compound with a high-spin electron configuration. Both classical and quantum resource estimates indicate that simulating CYP models at scales large enough to balance dynamic and multiconfigurational correlation is a candidate quantum-advantage problem.
reference_short: Goings et al., Reliably assessing the electronic structure of cytochrome P450 on today's classical computers and tomorrow's quantum computers, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 2022
notes: Four model compounds sharing one hierarchy of active spaces, condensed into a single row. active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY: the main text describes the hierarchy only qualitatively and puts every orbital and electron count in SI Appendix Table 3, which was not retrievable. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty as well - the paper treats Cpd I as a polyradical species whose formal iron oxidation state is not the useful description. software is left empty: no program name for the DMRG or NEVPT2 appears in the main text.

compound_name: [Fe(terpy)2]2+ (terpy = 2,2':6',2''-terpyridine), low-spin to high-spin transition and metal-centred excited states
ligand_set: two tridentate 2,2':6',2''-terpyridine ligands giving an FeN6 core
point_group: C2 symmetry constraint in the CASSCF/CASPT2, with the Fe-N(axial) bond as the symmetry axis (D2d used in the DFT work)
geometry_source: non-relaxed two-dimensional potential energy scan along the Fe-N(axial) bond length and the phi(NNN) bending angle, on structural parameters optimized for the 5E state, because CASPT2 geometry optimization of this system is too demanding; DFT geometries from BP86 and other functionals for comparison
method: CASSCF and state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with an IPEA shift of 0.25 au in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian and a 0.2 au level shift to exclude intruder states (verified stable against lower level shifts)
software: MOLCAS 7.6 (ORCA and ADF for the DFT and TD-DFT comparisons)
basis_set: ANO-RCC with contractions (7s6p5d4f3g2h) for Fe, (4s3p1d) for N, (3s2p) for C and (2s) for H
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian for scalar relativistic effects
active_space_orbital_description: following Pierloot's strategy: the two eg orbitals of bonding Fe-N character, the three Fe 3d(t2g) orbitals, the two eg* orbitals of antibonding Fe-N character, and an additional set of five Fe 4d orbitals needed to describe the dynamical correlation of the 3d electrons
active_space_protocol: (10,12) throughout. The Fe 3p orbital along the Fe-N(axial) bond had to be kept frozen in the CASSCF to preserve the character of the active orbitals across the whole Fe-N range. Deep core electrons (Fe 1s2...2p6; C and N 1s2) were excluded from the CASPT2 correlation treatment. For the singlet ground state the eg* orbitals are unoccupied in the dominant t2g6 eg0 determinant, so their correlating orbitals did not reliably stay in the active space; a state-averaged CASSCF over the four lowest singlet roots (two lowest for triplets) fixed this, and a quasi-state-specific singlet energy was generated at one geometry by weighting the ground state 10:1:1 against two excited states.
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2 high-spin/low-spin splitting energy dE(HL) for [Fe(terpy)2]2+ is 5888 cm-1, determined from the minima of the two-dimensional potential energy surface, with the lower-lying component of the high-spin state taken and the Jahn-Teller effect accounted for at the DFT level. Density functionals scatter enormously around this: BP86 11335, TPSS 11503, RPBE 7701, TPSSh 6297, OPBE 6422, OLYP 4637, B3LYP 755 and B3LYP* 3447 cm-1 (ORCA/TZVP), so the pure GGA and meta-GGA functionals strongly overstabilize the low-spin state while B3LYP erroneously favours the high spin state; reducing the Hartree-Fock exchange from 20% to 15% in B3LYP* brings it into reasonable agreement with CASPT2. Two-dimensional CASPT2 surfaces were computed for the lowest singlet, triplet and quintet states along the Fe-N(axial) length and the phi(NNN) angle; the spin transition requires a bending mode of the terpyridine rings, the in-plane rotation of the two side pyridines relative to the middle one.
reference_short: Papai, Theoretical Characterization of Electronic States of Iron Complexes, PhD thesis, Wigner Research Centre for Physics / Eotvos Lorand University
notes: PhD thesis. The CASPT2 values it quotes for the other two complexes in the series - [Fe(tz)6]2+ 220 cm-1 and [Fe(bipy)3]2+ 4617 cm-1 - are explicitly footnoted to the author's own earlier publications (refs 18 and 19), not computed in the thesis, so they are not recorded as data here; only [Fe(terpy)2]2+ is the thesis's own CASPT2 result. The Mossbauer chapter of the thesis is DFT only. d_electron_count 3d6 is arithmetic from the stated Fe(II) oxidation state.

ligand_set: two axial oxo (actinyl) oxygens and five equatorial water molecules
geometry_source: NEVPT2-optimized geometries of the actinyl pentahydrates [AnO2(H2O)5]q+; classical molecular dynamics snapshots on a B3LYP-based hydrated-ion force field supply the Debye-Waller factors and the configurational average
method: NEVPT2 on state-averaged CASSCF references, with the perturbative step done by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory; used to check how static and dynamic electron correlation change the actinyl geometry and hence the simulated EXAFS
basis_set: ma-def2-TZVP on O, def2-SVP on H, and SD(60,MWB)//DEF-TZVP on the actinoids
relativistic_treatment: SD(60,MWB) small-core relativistic pseudopotential on the actinide
active_space_orbital_description: the set of atomic-like actinide f orbitals plus the molecular orbitals formed by combining the actinide f orbitals with the oxo (O_yl) p orbitals
active_space_protocol: state average over the degenerate ground states only, excluding excited states, because the ground states are degenerate
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(7,10) reference. NEVPT2 changes the actinyl aqua-ion geometry by less than about 0.07 A relative to B3LYP, but that is enough to matter: computing the EXAFS spectrum from the NEVPT2-optimized pentahydrate structure while taking the Debye-Waller factors from the B3LYP molecular dynamics gives better agreement with experiment than the pure B3LYP force field does. Except uranyl, every actinyl studied is open-shell. The k = 6-8 A-1 region of the EXAFS remains hard to reproduce theoretically.
reference_short: Combining EXAFS and Computer Simulations to Refine the Structural Description of Actinyls in Water, Molecules 2020, 25, 5250
notes: Neptunium(VI); in the actinyl motif the actinoid is in oxidation state V or VI and bonds covalently to two oxo oxygens in a linear unit, with five equatorial waters. d_electron_count is left empty: the active space is built from 5f and O 2p orbitals and the paper assigns no explicit fn count.

notes: Neptunium(V) actinyl. Same reasoning as the Np(VI) row for the empty d/f count.

compound_name: 9H-adenine, photodynamics in vacuo and in water
geometry_source: XMS-CASPT2-optimized planar S0 minimum, C2-puckered S1 minimum, and C2- and C6-puckered minimum-energy conical intersections; gas-phase initial conditions from a Wigner distribution over the normal modes; for the QM/MM runs, 300 TIP3P waters added with packmol under a 13.01 A spherical boundary, equilibrated 1 ps with adenine frozen, re-seeded from the Wigner distribution, equilibrated a further 10 ps and then 200 fs of MP2 QM/MM, all at 300 K with OPLS all-atom Lennard-Jones parameters
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2) with analytical nuclear gradients and derivative couplings, driving on-the-fly fewest-switches surface-hopping dynamics; QM/MM for the solvated cases
software: BAGEL (gradients generated by the SMITH3 automatic code generator, parallelized with MPI remote memory access), interfaced to Newton-X for the surface hopping and Tinker for the classical molecular mechanics
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the corresponding density-fitting basis
active_space_orbital_description: two pi, two pi* and one n orbital; the active space was taken from a previous MRCIS study
active_space_protocol: (6,5) with five states included in the XMS-CASPT2 to handle the strong state mixing near the conical intersections; two states (S0 and S1) propagated in the surface hopping
nroots_per_mult: 5 states in the XMS-CASPT2; 2 states in the FSSH propagation
electronic_structure_description: Twenty trajectories each in the gas phase and in aqueous solution (40 total), all started from S1, integrated to 1 ps with a 0.5 fs nuclear time step and Granucci-Persico decoherence correction. Conical intersections are stabilized by solvation, becoming thermally reachable.
reference_short: Park & Shiozaki, On-the-fly CASPT2 Surface Hopping Dynamics
notes: Method-demonstration application. The (6,5) space is inherited from an earlier MRCIS study rather than optimized here.

compound_name: pHBI, the anionic green fluorescent protein model chromophore (para-hydroxybenzylideneimidazolin-5-one), in water
geometry_source: same initial-condition protocol as adenine; 21 atoms, 231 basis functions in the QM region
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2) with analytical nuclear gradients and derivative couplings, driving on-the-fly fewest-switches surface-hopping dynamics; QM/MM for the solvated cases
software: BAGEL (gradients generated by the SMITH3 automatic code generator, parallelized with MPI remote memory access), interfaced to Newton-X for the surface hopping and Tinker for the classical molecular mechanics
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the corresponding density-fitting basis
active_space_orbital_description: valence pi and pi* orbitals; the larger spaces used for the timing study, (6e,5o), (8e,7o), (10e,9o) and (12e,11o), consist of the same valence pi/pi* manifold
active_space_protocol: (4,3) with three-state averaging for the production dynamics, chosen because previous single-point CASPT2 studies showed it describes the neutral and charge-transfer states associated with chromophore twisting in a balanced way; (4,3) through (12,11) used for gradient timings
nroots_per_mult: 3 states averaged
electronic_structure_description: Within 1 ps, 70% of the trajectories decayed to the ground state; the experimental fluorescence decay constants are 0.21 ps (51%) and 1.1 ps (49%). Nonadiabatic S1 to S0 decay follows twisting of the bridge, consistent with earlier CASSCF and fitted-surface studies. Recomputing the XMS-CASPT2 energies along the same trajectories without solvation shows that solvation stabilizes the conical intersections: the minimum-energy conical intersections for the I and P channels lie 0.46 and 0.72 eV below the S1 Franck-Condon energy in water, and the S1-S0 gaps at twisted geometries are about 1.0 eV smaller in water than in the gas phase, so both channels become accessible. One XMS-CASPT2 nuclear gradient with CAS(4e,3o)/cc-pVDZ takes under 2 minutes on 256 CPU cores; in the dynamics, two gradients and one derivative coupling per time step took about 10 minutes, with trajectory propagation cost negligible beside the electronic structure.
reference_short: Park & Shiozaki, On-the-fly CASPT2 Surface Hopping Dynamics
notes: Method-demonstration application; the timing study sweeps the active space from (4,3) to (12,11) on this same chromophore.

compound_name: ethylene, minimum-energy conical intersections (with stilbene and the anionic GFP model chromophore pHBDI as larger test cases)
geometry_source: minimum-energy conical intersection geometries optimized with XMS-CASPT2
method: analytical derivative couplings for multistate CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2), with the SS-SR contraction scheme and a vertical shift of 0.2 Eh; conical intersections located by the gradient projection method
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ for the ethylene benchmark; cc-pVDZ with its JKFIT density-fitting basis for the larger molecules
active_space_orbital_description: the pi and pi* orbitals of the C=C bond
active_space_protocol: CAS(2e,2o) for the ethylene benchmark; a CAS(12e,11o) SA-CASSCF comparison was also run to test whether the artifact persists with a larger space
electronic_structure_description: Energies of the ground and excited states of ethylene at the S0 minimum and at the minimum-energy conical intersections, relative to the S0 minimum (eV), XMS-CASPT2 versus unc-MRCI+Q from the literature. S0 geometry: S0 0.00, S1 7.70, S2 13.04 (unc-MRCI+Q 0.00, 7.79). Py: 4.42, 4.42, 9.05 (4.40, 4.46, 9.24). Et: 4.63, 4.63, 5.79 (4.56, 4.56, 5.59). C3v-Et: 4.71, 4.71, 5.78 (4.69, 4.69, 5.59). Hm: 5.06, 5.06, 8.25 (5.15, 5.20, 8.48). To: 2.99, 5.43, 5.43 (2.92, 5.30, 5.42). The S0/S1 P-twisted conical intersection that SA-CASSCF predicts is an artifact: on the XMS-CASPT2 surface that MECI lies about 10 kcal/mol above the Franck-Condon point. SA-CASSCF stays qualitatively wrong even at CAS(12e,11o), where the MECIs come out 0.91 and 0.30 eV below the Franck-Condon point - and that itself differs qualitatively from an earlier CAS(12e,11o) result with two-state averaging, which shows the choice of states to average matters as much as the choice of active space.
reference_short: Park & Shiozaki, Analytical derivative coupling for multistate CASPT2 theory
notes: Method paper. nel/norb record the ethylene benchmark space; the SA-CASSCF comparison at (12,11) is in active_space_protocol. Stilbene and pHBDI are used to demonstrate that the method scales to large molecules, with geometries optimized at XMS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ, but no state energies for them appear in the main text.

ligand_set: a beta-diketiminate-type N,N'-diiminato chelate and a side-on bound dioxygen
geometry_source: geometries optimized with the analytical CASPT2 gradients reported in this work
method: analytical nuclear gradients for fully internally contracted CASPT2 (FIC-CASPT2), with the CASSCF and Z-vector equations solved using density fitting
software: BAGEL (gradients generated by the SMITH3 automatic code generator)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ for orbitals with def2-QZVPP/JKFIT auxiliary functions
active_space_orbital_description: an in-plane copper d orbital and eight valence orbitals of dioxygen, following earlier work
electronic_structure_description: Optimized Cu-O and O-O bond lengths (A) for the singlet ground state: CASSCF 1.886 / 1.386; CASPT2 1.820 / 1.399; partially contracted WK-CASPT2 in MOLPRO 1.820 / 1.400, and 1.820 / 1.400 without density fitting. Neither the degree of internal contraction nor the density fitting changes the geometry appreciably, which is the point of the comparison.
notes: Method-demonstration application. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty: the Cu-O2 bonding in this complex is exactly what the calculation is probing and the paper assigns no formal oxidation state.

compound_name: porphin (free-base porphyrin, C20H14N4), vertical and adiabatic ionization potentials
geometry_source: geometries optimized with the analytical CASPT2 gradients reported in this work
method: analytical nuclear gradients for fully internally contracted CASPT2, with geometries optimized at CASPT2
software: BAGEL (gradients generated by the SMITH3 automatic code generator)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the corresponding JKFIT density-fitting basis (def2-SVP for the PBE comparison)
active_space_orbital_description: the four frontier orbitals of Gouterman's four-orbital model
active_space_protocol: (4,4) for the neutral and (3,4) for the radical cation; 55 correlated inactive and 323 virtual orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Ionization potentials (eV), vertical / adiabatic / difference, with <S^2> of the radical cation at the neutral geometry: PBE 6.70 / 6.68 / 0.02, <S^2> 0.77; MP2 8.51 (cation geometry could not be optimized because of instability), <S^2> 1.47; CASPT2 6.84 / 6.65 / 0.18, <S^2> 0.75; CASPT2/PBE 6.83 / 6.85 / -0.02, <S^2> 0.75. Experimental vertical IP 6.9 eV. One optimization step took about 30 minutes on the hardware used.
notes: Second demonstration system in the same paper; the (4,4) neutral and (3,4) cation spaces are both recorded, with nel/norb holding the neutral.

compound_name: benzophenone, S0 and S1 geometries and adiabatic excitation energy
geometry_source: geometries optimized with the analytical CASPT2 gradients reported in this work
method: analytical nuclear energy gradients for (extended) multi-state fully internally contracted CASPT2, with vertical shifts; the SS-SR contraction scheme and a vertical shift of 0.2
software: BAGEL (gradients generated by the SMITH3 automatic code generator)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the corresponding JKFIT basis (def2-TZVP for the PBE0 comparison)
active_space_orbital_description: the non-bonding oxygen lone pair orbital n0 and several pi orbitals; the first excitation is n0 to the C=O pi*
active_space_protocol: (8,7) with the first three singlet states included in the XMS-CASPT2; SA-CASSCF(8,7) with the same basis and state averaging (Cholesky decomposition) run for comparison in MOLCAS, and PBE0 in Turbomole
electronic_structure_description: Selected geometric parameters for the optimized S0 / S1 states, CASPT2 / CASSCF / PBE0: C2-O 1.23-1.35 / 1.21-1.37 / 1.21-1.30 A; C1-C2 1.50-1.44 / 1.51-1.44 / 1.49-1.44; C2-C3 1.50-1.45 / 1.53-1.44 / 1.49-1.44; C1-C2-C3 angle 119-129 / 120 deg. The system was chosen partly because Pierloot et al. had reported that MS-CASPT2 overestimates the coupling between these states; in these calculations the coupling between CASPT2 states was found to be small. Where eigenvalues of the SA-CASSCF Hessian approach zero the active space is ill-defined - nearly empty or nearly doubly occupied active orbitals leave the state-averaged reference energy almost invariant - and the corresponding nearly redundant Z-vector elements can be set to zero.
notes: Method-demonstration application for the multistate gradient extension.

compound_name: timing and accuracy benchmark set for CASPT2 gradients with imaginary shift: p-HBDI- (deprotonated 4-hydroxybenzylidene-1,2-dimethylimidazolinone, the anionic GFP model chromophore), adenine, and iron(II) porphyrin (FeP)
formula: p-HBDI- (27 atoms, 114 electrons); adenine (15 atoms, 70 electrons); FeP (37 atoms, 186 electrons)
ligand_set: for FeP, a porphyrin macrocycle; the other two systems are metal-free
method: analytical nuclear gradient and derivative coupling theory for CASPT2 with an imaginary shift, derived by the Lagrangian approach as an extension of the real-shift algorithm; geometry optimizations at XMS-CASPT2 with both real and imaginary shifts for comparison
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the corresponding density-fitting basis for adenine and p-HBDI- (165 and 279 basis functions, 815 and 1373 auxiliary); SVP with its fitting basis for FeP (427 basis functions, 2288 auxiliary)
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian for the FeP calculations (scalar relativistic)
active_space_orbital_description: for FeP, the five metal 3d orbitals plus the four Gouterman orbitals of the porphyrin - a minimal active space for metal porphyrin-ligand binding
active_space_protocol: p-HBDI- (4,3) with 3 states; adenine a minimal (4,4) with 5 states; FeP (10,9) with 5 states, optimized for the low-spin singlet
electronic_structure_description: Vertical and adiabatic S1 excitation energies of p-HBDI- and the energy differences between the conical intersections and the Franck-Condon point were computed across a range of real and imaginary shift values. Excitation energies rise with increasing shift because less correlation is recovered, but the imaginary-shift results are markedly less sensitive to the shift value than the real-shift ones. Wall times per geometry optimization step, real shift versus imaginary shift (seconds, 256 CPU cores): adenine 84 vs 87; p-HBDI- 257 vs 260; FeP 2947 vs 3387. So for small active spaces the extra cost of the imaginary shift is marginal, while for the larger (10e,9o) FeP space it is about 15%, traceable to evaluating the correlated density-like quantities specific to the imaginary-shift terms (297 s becoming 729 s, of which 383 s is the shift-specific part).
reference_short: Park, Al-Saadon, Strand, Shiozaki, Imaginary shift in CASPT2 nuclear gradient and derivative coupling theory
notes: Three benchmark systems sharing one paper, condensed into a single row; nel/norb record the FeP (10,9) space, the largest and the only one with a described orbital composition, and the other two spaces are in active_space_protocol. metal_center, oxidation state and d count describe FeP only - the other two systems are organic. d_electron_count 3d6 follows from the stated iron(II) assignment.

compound_name: solvated polyene gradient benchmark: butadiene and hexatriene, each surrounded by an increasing number of methanol molecules
formula: C4H6 and C6H8 with explicit CH3OH solvent shells
geometry_source: butadiene and hexatriene surrounded by an increasing number of explicit methanol molecules; coordinates in the supplementary material
method: reduced-scaling analytical CASPT2 ground-state gradients built on the supporting subspace method, with tensor hyper-contraction for the MP2 electron repulsion integrals and GPU evaluation of the THC tensors and their gradients
software: TeraChem (currently supporting atom-centred spd Gaussian basis sets and spdf auxiliary sets)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with cc-pVDZ-RI auxiliary basis sets and THC grids optimized for cc-pVDZ
active_space_orbital_description: the conjugated pi valence space of the polyene
active_space_protocol: CASPT2(4,4) for solvated butadiene and CASPT2(6,6) for solvated hexatriene, the same test systems used in the companion energy paper. No frozen-core approximation - all molecular orbitals enter the perturbation - and a level shift of 0.3 hartree throughout.
electronic_structure_description: Timing benchmark rather than a spectroscopic study. Wall times for single-point gradient calculations run almost exactly parallel to the corresponding energy calculations across the solvent series, so the gradients inherit the same reduced scaling as the energies. Speedups of about 5.2x were observed on eight GPUs. Because the MP2-gradient step scales differently from the rest of the calculation, its cost is broken out separately.
reference_short: Song, Schmidt et al., Reduced scaling formulation of CASPT2 analytical gradients using the supporting subspace method, J. Chem. Phys. 2021, 154, 014103
notes: Two molecules with different spaces condensed into one row; nel/norb left empty and both spaces recorded in active_space_protocol. All timings on one Intel Xeon E5-2637 core plus one GeForce GTX 1080Ti GPU.

compound_name: benzene, potential energy curves from the Franck-Condon point to the S0/S1 minimum-energy conical intersection
geometry_source: geometries from SA-CASSCF optimizations with interpolation between endpoints where curves are reported
method: supporting subspace factorization of XMS-CASPT2, recast in a spin-free formulation so that multiple spin states can be treated; the factorization is analytically exact
software: TeraChem (conventional XMS-CASPT2 in BAGEL used as the reference)
active_space_orbital_description: the conjugated pi valence space
active_space_protocol: The paper states the spaces inconsistently: the body text says two singlets and three triplets were computed with active space (6e,6o) and three doublets and three quartets (for ionized benzene) with (5e,6o), while the caption of the corresponding figure gives XMS-CASPT2(4e,4o)/6-31G* and XMS-CASPT2(3e,4o)/6-31G* for exactly the same sets of states.
electronic_structure_description: Supporting-subspace XMS-CASPT2 reproduces conventional XMS-CASPT2 (BAGEL) along the whole FC-to-MECI path to within a maximum absolute-energy difference of 0.0177 eV (0.408 kcal/mol), confirming that the factorization is analytically exact. Endpoint geometries were optimized with SA-CASSCF and intermediate structures generated by interpolation in internal coordinates. Two singlet and three triplet states were computed for neutral benzene and three doublet and three quartet states for the ionized species.
reference_short: Song, New physical insights into the supporting subspace factorization of XMS-CASPT2 and generalization to multiple spin states via spin-free formulation, J. Chem. Phys. 2024, 160, 124106
notes: CAVEAT: active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY because the paper contradicts itself - the body text gives (6e,6o)/(5e,6o) and the figure caption (4e,4o)/(3e,4o) for the same states of the same molecule. Both are recorded in active_space_protocol; neither is asserted here. The (6e,6o) pi space would be the canonical choice for benzene, but that is inference, not the paper's statement.

compound_name: solvated polyene performance benchmark: butadiene and hexatriene with increasing numbers of methanol molecules
formula: C4H6 and C6H8 with explicit CH3OH
geometry_source: geometries from SA-CASSCF optimizations with interpolation between endpoints where curves are reported
method: supporting subspace factorization of XMS-CASPT2, recast in a spin-free formulation so that multiple spin states can be treated; the factorization is analytically exact
software: TeraChem (conventional XMS-CASPT2 in BAGEL used as the reference)
active_space_orbital_description: the conjugated pi valence space of the polyene
active_space_protocol: hexatriene (6e,6o) for singlet states and (5e,6o) for doublet states; butadiene (4e,4o) for singlets and (3e,4o) for doublets
electronic_structure_description: Performance benchmark of the spin-free supporting-subspace CASPT2, with timings broken into the dressed MP2 energy and the remainder and fitted to power laws. A direct comparison of the original spin-orbital formulation against the new spin-free one uses the same solvated butadienes.
reference_short: Song, New physical insights into the supporting subspace factorization of XMS-CASPT2 and generalization to multiple spin states via spin-free formulation, J. Chem. Phys. 2024, 160, 124106
notes: Timing/scaling benchmark; two molecules with different spaces condensed into one row, spaces in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: photoinduced electron transfer between 10-methylphenothiazine (donor D) and a nitroxide-linked acceptor (A-R)
geometry_source: geometries from SA-CASSCF optimizations with interpolation between endpoints where curves are reported
method: supporting subspace factorization of XMS-CASPT2, recast in a spin-free formulation so that multiple spin states can be treated; the factorization is analytically exact
software: TeraChem (conventional XMS-CASPT2 in BAGEL used as the reference)
active_space_orbital_description: the frontier orbitals of the donor-acceptor pair
active_space_protocol: (4e,3o); the implementation at the time supported only small active spaces, up to six active electrons
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy curves for four doublet states and two quartet states along an interpolation path connecting the SA-CASSCF-optimized D2/D3 and D0/D1 minimum-energy conical intersections, with energies relative to the D0 energy of the first structure. D1 and D2 are almost degenerate and both have [D+, A-R-] charge-transfer character; state characters were assigned by attachment-detachment analysis. This is the first test of the method on a system of this type. The paper states its own limitation plainly: the (4e,3o) space is not sufficient to capture the static correlation of these long conjugated systems, the curves may change qualitatively with a larger space, and the calculations should be revisited once large active spaces are supported.
reference_short: Song, New physical insights into the supporting subspace factorization of XMS-CASPT2 and generalization to multiple spin states via spin-free formulation, J. Chem. Phys. 2024, 160, 124106
notes: The paper's self-declared limitation on active space size is recorded verbatim in the electronic structure description because it bears directly on how much weight these curves carry.

compound_name: C2, N2 and O2: ground and valence excited states (35 electronic states) by the multireference correlation-consistent composite approach MR-ccCA
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed over a range of bond lengths; spectroscopic constants derived from them and compared with best-known experimental values
method: MR-ccCA, a multireference analogue of the correlation-consistent composite approach built on CASPT2, with additive corrections including basis-set, core-valence, scalar-relativistic and TQ-excitation terms; NEVPT2, MRMP2 and second-order generalized Van Vleck perturbation theory tested as alternatives to CASPT2 within the composite, and nR-MRCISD(TQ) and MRCISD[TQ] used for the triple/quadruple corrections
software: MOLPRO for the CASPT2 and NEVPT2; GAMESS for the MRMP2
basis_set: correlation-consistent basis sets with extrapolation to the complete basis set limit, in the composite scheme
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic corrections included as an additive term (found to have minimal effect on the derived spectroscopic quantities)
active_space_orbital_description: the complete valence active space of each diatomic; MRCISD[TQ] additionally uses an augmented set of active orbitals with total occupancy up to two in the RASSCF orbital optimization and four in the subsequent MRCI
active_space_protocol: complete valence active space throughout; the paper gives no (nel,norb) pair for any of the three molecules
electronic_structure_description: 35 electronic states across the three diatomics. MR-ccCA-P predicts spectroscopic constants with overall mean absolute deviations from experiment of 0.0006 A for the equilibrium bond length, 7.0 cm-1 for the harmonic frequency and 143 cm-1 for term values, comparable to much more costly MRCI-based methods. For C2 specifically, MR-ccCA-P with the g4 Hamiltonian gives MADs of 0.0007 A, 3.5 cm-1 and 0.7 kcal/mol for re, we and De, with the Te of the B 1Delta_g and B' 1Sigma_g+ states deviating from experiment by -278 and -122 cm-1. Where TQ corrections from nR-MRCISD(TQ) are included, MADs drop to 0.0002 A, 0.7 cm-1 and 37 cm-1 for re, we and Te, and dissociation energies land within -0.4 to 0.7 kcal/mol, so those curves can serve as benchmarks in their own right. Scalar relativistic corrections barely matter. The limits are honest: because the active space is restricted to valence orbitals, the N2 b 1Pi_u and b' 1Sigma_u+ states are excluded from the statistics for strong mixing with nearby Rydberg states, and the C' 3Pi_u minimum sits on the same curve as C 3Pi_u near an avoided crossing so it is not studied. Larger deviations in the dissociation energies of N2 and O2 excited states are attributed to size-consistency error, since the atomic energy sum rather than a supermolecule energy was used as the dissociation reference. CASPT2-based MR-ccCA is the recommended variant.
reference_short: Jiang & Wilson, Multireference composite approaches for the accurate study of ground and excited electronic states: C2, N2, and O2, J. Chem. Phys. 2011, 134, 034101
notes: Three diatomics condensed into one row. active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY: the paper specifies the space only as the complete valence active space of each molecule and never states an (nel,norb) pair, and deriving one per molecule would be inference.

compound_name: benchmark set of small and medium-sized organic molecules from the QUEST database (three to six non-hydrogen atoms), vertical excitation energies at CASPT3 versus CASPT2
geometry_source: geometries and theoretical best estimates for the vertical excitation energies taken from the QUEST database (available at the QUESTDB website)
method: single-state CASPT2 and CASPT3, in the frozen-core approximation, using the RS2 and RS3 schemes
active_space_orbital_description: active spaces are chosen per system and per transition, described exhaustively for each symmetry representation in the supplementary material rather than in the main text
active_space_protocol: one active space per system and transition, given per symmetry representation in the supplementary material. For the challenging transitions the active space was steadily enlarged to check convergence of the excitation energy. Relative to the group's earlier CASPT2 benchmark, the active spaces of acrolein, pyrimidine and pyridazine were slightly reduced to make the CASPT3 calculations technically achievable.
electronic_structure_description: Context from the authors' preceding study: an exhaustive benchmark of CASPT2 and NEVPT2 over 280 excited states of diverse character (singlet, triplet, valence, Rydberg, n->pi*, pi->pi* and double excitations) in 35 small and medium organic molecules with aug-cc-pVTZ, whose conclusion was that CASPT2 with an IPEA shift and partially contracted NEVPT2 both give fairly reliable vertical transition energies with slight overestimation. The present work extends that comparison to third order. The IPEA shift, though it can improve agreement with experiment, is noted as not systematically justified and significantly basis-set dependent.
reference_short: Boggio-Pasqua, Jacquemin, Loos, Benchmarking CASPT3 Vertical Excitation Energies
notes: QUEST-ADJACENT: this benchmark takes its geometries and reference values from the QUEST database, so it should be treated like a QUEST-series paper at the export boundary into claude-casscf, where QUEST is a held-out benchmark (see the repository CLAUDE.md and the QUEST-leak memory). Condensed into one row: active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY because the spaces vary per molecule, per transition and per symmetry representation and live entirely in the supplementary material, which was not retrievable.

method: renormalized internally contracted multireference coupled cluster with singles and doubles (RIC-MRCCSD) in a spin-free formulation, needing no reduced density matrices or cumulants beyond three-body; compared against NEVPT2, approximate fourth-order NEVPT4(SD), multireference CEPA(0) and Koehn's IC-MRCCSD
software: ORCA (Evangelista's Wick&d equation generator combined with ORCA's native AGE code generator)
basis_set: def2-TZVP with the frozen-core approximation (def2-SVP for the size-consistency tests)
active_space_orbital_description: the conjugated pi system spanning the two benzene rings and the two bridging carbon atoms
electronic_structure_description: Parallel runtimes in seconds for a single coupled-cluster iteration, RHF-CCSD / UHF-CCSD / RIC-MRCCSD: 1 process 3590 / 18228 / 8580; 2 processes 2054 / 10240 / 5353; 4 processes 1224 / 6319 / 3711; 8 processes 838 / 4430 / 2145. Each RIC-MRCCSD iteration is less than 3.5 times slower than RHF-CCSD despite containing far more contractions, and its cost sits between RHF-CCSD and UHF-CCSD even at this CAS(14,14). Size-consistency errors for both CASSCF and RIC-MRCCSD are within 1e-9 Eh, computed with def2-SVP and tight convergence (1e-12 and 1e-9 for the CASSCF energy and gradient, 1e-9 for the RIC-MRCCSD residuals).
reference_short: Szenes, Kayal, Sivalingam, Feldmann, Neese, Reiher, Efficient Implementation of the Spin-Free Renormalized Internally-Contracted Multireference Coupled Cluster Theory, J. Phys. Chem. A 2026, 130, 1417-1432
notes: Timing and size-consistency benchmark for the method.

method: renormalized internally contracted multireference coupled cluster with singles and doubles (RIC-MRCCSD) in a spin-free formulation, needing no reduced density matrices or cumulants beyond three-body; compared against NEVPT2, approximate fourth-order NEVPT4(SD), multireference CEPA(0) and Koehn's IC-MRCCSD
software: ORCA (Evangelista's Wick&d equation generator combined with ORCA's native AGE code generator)
electronic_structure_description: Large-scale demonstration: the ground state of a vitamin B12 model with a CAS(12,12) active space and 809 orbitals, showing the method scales to systems of this size.
reference_short: Szenes, Kayal, Sivalingam, Feldmann, Neese, Reiher, Efficient Implementation of the Spin-Free Renormalized Internally-Contracted Multireference Coupled Cluster Theory, J. Phys. Chem. A 2026, 130, 1417-1432
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty: the paper reports only that this is a vitamin B12 model and gives no oxidation-state assignment. The basis set for this calculation is not stated in the main text.

compound_name: benchmark set of 14 doubly and triply charged transition-metal ions, state-averaged excitation energies
formula: 14 TM ions in 2+ and 3+ charge states
method: renormalized internally contracted multireference coupled cluster with singles and doubles (RIC-MRCCSD) in a spin-free formulation, needing no reduced density matrices or cumulants beyond three-body; compared against NEVPT2, approximate fourth-order NEVPT4(SD), multireference CEPA(0) and Koehn's IC-MRCCSD
software: ORCA (Evangelista's Wick&d equation generator combined with ORCA's native AGE code generator)
active_space_orbital_description: two active space sizes were compared: the 3d orbitals alone, and 3d plus 4d (the double-shell)
electronic_structure_description: Errors in excitation energies relative to experiment, shown as violin plots against other multireference methods. Increasing the flow parameter s consistently reduces both the MAD and the spread, as expected since larger s recovers more dynamic correlation - at the cost of numerical robustness, with s = 0.5 Eh^-2 failing to converge. At the largest convergent value, s = 0.4 Eh^-2, RIC-MRCCSD accuracy with the 3d-only space lies between NEVPT2 and NEVPT4. Adding the 4d orbitals reduces the error further, with RIC-MRCCSD then even beating IC-MRCC on MAD - but the authors qualify this: the double-shell effect is traditionally invoked to compensate for missing dynamic correlation and should ideally not be needed by a high-accuracy multireference method, and indeed most standard MR methods barely change when the space is expanded.
reference_short: Szenes, Kayal, Sivalingam, Feldmann, Neese, Reiher, Efficient Implementation of the Spin-Free Renormalized Internally-Contracted Multireference Coupled Cluster Theory, J. Phys. Chem. A 2026, 130, 1417-1432
notes: Free atomic ions, in scope under the no-exclusions-by-system-class rule. active_space_nel/norb are left empty: the paper describes the two spaces only as '3d' and '3d + 4d' and states no electron or orbital counts, which vary across the fourteen ions anyway.

compound_name: EA/IP-MR-ADC(2)-X benchmark set: HF, F2, CO, N2, H2O, CS, H2CO and C2H4 at equilibrium and stretched geometries, plus the carbon dimer C2 and twisted ethylene t-C2H4
formula: HF; F2; CO; N2; H2O; CS; H2CO; C2H4; C2; t-C2H4
geometry_source: equilibrium geometries taken from the literature; stretched geometries obtained by doubling the bond length for the diatomics and the O-H, C-O and C-C distances for H2O, H2CO and C2H4 respectively; C2 fixed at a C-C distance of 1.2425 A; the twisted ethylene geometry taken from the literature and reproduced in the Supporting Information
method: extended second-order multireference algebraic diagrammatic construction theory for charged excitations, EA- and IP-MR-ADC(2)-X, with a small approximation to the second-order effective-Hamiltonian amplitudes giving O(M^5) scaling in the basis size; benchmarked against strongly contracted NEVPT2, EOM-CCSD, single-reference ADC(2) and ADC(3), with semi-stochastic heat-bath CI extrapolated to the full CI limit as the reference
software: Dice for the SHCI reference calculations
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ throughout, except that cc-pVDZ was used on the hydrogen atoms of H2CO, C2H4 and t-C2H4
active_space_orbital_description: frontier molecular orbitals; the notation (ne,mo) means m frontier orbitals and n active electrons
active_space_protocol: All multireference calculations in the main benchmark used 10 active orbitals. For electron affinities, n = 6 active electrons for every molecule except HF, where n = 4. For ionization potentials, n = 8, 14, 10, 10, 8, 10, 12 and 10 for HF, F2, CO, N2, H2O, CS, H2CO and C2H4 respectively. C2 used (6e,10o) and twisted ethylene (8e,12o). Ten ionized or electron-attached CASCI states were included in the model space, with truncation parameters eta_s = 1e-6 and eta_d = 1e-10 to remove redundant excitations. The 1s orbitals were frozen in the SHCI calculations for H2CO, C2H4 and t-C2H4; all electrons were correlated elsewhere.
electronic_structure_description: EA- and IP-MR-ADC(2)-X reach accuracy comparable to strongly contracted NEVPT2 while scaling more favourably with active space size and giving direct access to transition properties. Sample vertical attachment energies (eV) with spectroscopic factors, MR-ADC(2)-X / EOM-CCSD / sc-NEVPT2 / SHCI reference: HF 4-sigma -0.82 (P 0.99) / -0.83 / -0.88 / -0.81; HF 5-sigma -4.87 (P 0.98) / -4.93 / -4.97 / -4.88. Single-reference ADC(2) and ADC(3) give -0.84 and -0.82 for the HF 4-sigma state. The approximation to the second-order amplitudes costs about 0.04 eV mean absolute error in the EA-MR-ADC transition energies and 0.01 eV for IP-MR-ADC, with corresponding spectroscopic-factor errors of about 0.0008 and 0.0003; the larger EA errors reflect greater sensitivity to orbital relaxation and differential correlation. The algorithm for the first-order amplitude equations in MR-ADC and partially contracted NEVPT2 avoids the four-particle reduced density matrices entirely, without approximation or imaginary-time propagation.
reference_short: Chatterjee & Sokolov, Extended Second-Order Multireference Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theory for Charged Excitations
notes: Ten systems condensed into one row. active_space_norb records the 10 orbitals common to the main benchmark; active_space_nel is left EMPTY because the electron count is set per molecule and per process (4 or 6 for electron affinities, 8 to 14 for ionization potentials), with the full list in active_space_protocol. C2 and t-C2H4 use different spaces again, also recorded there.

compound_name: CBS[H] basis-set-incompleteness benchmark: the helium atom, and a set of representative molecules including N2, O2 and F2 (absolute energies at equilibrium, relative energies and dissociation energies)
formula: He; N2; O2; F2 among others
geometry_source: equilibrium geometries for the absolute energies; dissociation curves for the dissociation-energy errors
method: CBS[H], a basis-set-incompleteness correction that dresses the electronic Hamiltonian with an effective short-range electron-electron interaction, based on a local mapping between the Coulomb operator projected onto a finite basis and a long-range error-function interaction with a local range-separation parameter; unlike the earlier correction of Giner et al. it uses no short-range correlation density functionals. Applied on top of complete active space wave functions with correlation energies from the linearized adiabatic connection (AC0) and from NEVPT2, and compared against the DBBSC correction
basis_set: cc-pVXZ, X = D through 6, with two-point extrapolation from cc-pV5Z and cc-pV6Z as the benchmark; cc-pVXZ-F12 sets also tested
active_space_orbital_description: for helium, CAS(2,5)SCF and CAS(2,14)SCF reference wave functions were both used, alongside Hartree-Fock, to check that the correction is independent of the reference
active_space_protocol: helium: HF, CAS(2,5)SCF and CAS(2,14)SCF references. The active spaces for the molecular test set are not stated in the main text.
electronic_structure_description: Basis-set-incompleteness corrections to the helium correlation energy (mHa), CBS[H] / DBBSC / exact, against the exact energy of -2.903724 Ha. With a CAS(2,5)SCF reference: DZ -8.3 / -9.5; TZ -3.7 / -3.7; QZ -1.8 / -1.6; 5Z -1.0 / -0.9; 6Z -0.6 / -0.5, exact -3.5, -1.3, -0.6, -0.3 for TZ through 6Z. With CAS(2,14)SCF: DZ -16.1; TZ -3.3 / -3.6; QZ -1.5 / -1.8; 5Z -0.8 / -1.0; 6Z -0.6 / -0.5. With HF: DZ -9.0 / -12.3; TZ -3.9 / -5.1; QZ -1.9 / -2.3; 5Z -1.1 / -1.3; 6Z -0.7 / -0.8. From cc-pVTZ onward the CASSCF-based CBS[H] correction agrees with the exact value to within 0.2 mHa and stays sub-millihartree (at most 0.5 mHa) for larger bases; both corrections are nearly independent of the reference CASSCF wave function, as they should be, while HF-based errors exceed 0.5 mHa. The poor cc-pVDZ performance is attributed to projecting the short-range interaction operator onto the Hilbert space spanned by that basis. For the molecular set, CBS[H]-corrected AC0 and NEVPT2 correlation energies in a basis of cardinal number X (from X = 3) approach the uncorrected values in the (X+1) basis, so triple-zeta corrected results match uncorrected quintuple-zeta ones. CBS[H] works equally well for AC0 and NEVPT2. In cc-pVTZ the DBBSC-corrected relative energies stay within 1.5 mHa for every molecule while N2 is a clear CBS[H] outlier; conversely for O2 and F2, AC0-CBS[H] reaches 0.5 mHa at triple-zeta where DBBSC exceeds 1 mHa. In cc-pVDZ-F12 the CBS[H] relative-energy errors are smaller on average than in standard cc-pVDZ, and NEVPT2-CBS[H] there approaches uncorrected NEVPT2 in cc-pVTZ-F12.
reference_short: Hapka, Tucholska, Modrzejewski, Golub, Veis, Pernal, Correcting Basis Set Incompleteness in Wave Function Correlation Energy by Dressing Electronic Hamiltonian with an Effective Short-Range Interaction, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2025, 16, 6489-6499
notes: Method paper condensed into one row. nel/norb record the CAS(2,5)SCF helium reference, the only space given numerically in the main text; the CAS(2,14)SCF alternative is in active_space_protocol and the molecular test-set spaces are not stated there at all. software is left empty - no program is named in the main text.

compound_name: indole, first two singlet excited states 1Lb (covalent) and 1La (ionic)
geometry_source: Franck-Condon geometry plus optimized 1Lb and 1La minima on the S1 and S2 surfaces
method: restricted active space self-consistent field (RASSCF) by a new implicitly parallel, integral-block driven algorithm that finds whole blocks of CI-vector contributions through algebraic propagation rules instead of testing the index space, with a RAS model space; CASSCF for comparison
software: a RASSCF program developed as part of this work
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF reference calculations; 3-21G for the preliminary RAS active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: the pi system of indole for the CASSCF(10,9) reference; the RAS spaces are written RAS(N, MI+MII+MIII)[MxHole, MxElec] with N electrons distributed over MI RAS1, MII RAS2 and MIII RAS3 orbitals
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(10,9) as the reference. The first RAS test doubles the pi space by adding the nine 3p orbitals of A'' symmetry to the nine 2p ones: ten of these go into RAS3 and the three nearly doubly occupied CASSCF orbitals into RAS1, leaving a CAS(4,5) reference in RAS2 - written N = 10, MI = 3, MII = 5, MIII = 10, run at both MxHole = MxElec = 1 and 2. The second test augments that orbital space with ten sigma and sigma* orbitals for the ten CC and CN sigma bonds, giving RAS1 = 13, RAS2 = 5, RAS3 = 20 with N = 30 and excitations limited to one particle each way. The corresponding CASSCF(10,18) doubled-pi calculation is stated to be outside the scope of practical computation, which is the point of the RAS treatment.
electronic_structure_description: Indole's 1Lb (covalent) and 1La (ionic) states are separated by about 0.4 eV experimentally. CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G* overestimates the gap at 1.20 eV, chiefly by overestimating the ionic 1La state, and gets the surface qualitatively wrong - the 1La minimum lands on S2. CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G* energies versus CASPT2/ANO from Serrano and Roos and experiment (relative energies, eV): Franck-Condon S2 (1La) 6.20 vertical vs 4.73 and 4.77; FC S1 (1Lb) 5.00 vs 4.43 and 4.37; 1Lb minimum on S1 4.65 (0-0) vs 4.35 and 4.37; 1La minimum on S1 4.66 (0-0) at CASPT2 vs 4.54 experimental; S2 5.83 (0-0) at CASSCF. Preliminary RAS calculations in the 3-21G basis recover the gap progressively: N = 10 with 3/5/10 orbitals and MxHole = MxElec = 1 gives 0.90 eV; the same space at MxHole = MxElec = 2 gives 1.09 eV; and the sigma-augmented N = 30 space with 13/5/20 orbitals at 1/1 gives 0.78 eV.
reference_short: Klene, Robb, Blancafort, Frisch, A new efficient approach to the direct restricted active space self-consistent field method, J. Chem. Phys. 2003, 119, 713-728
notes: Method paper whose chemical application is indole. nel/norb record the CASSCF(10,9) reference; all three RAS partitions are in active_space_protocol, since a RAS space cannot be reduced to a single (nel,norb) pair. The CASPT2/ANO numbers are from Serrano and Roos, cited for comparison, not computed here.

compound_name: set of organic molecules, valence singlet and triplet excitation energies from RAS(h,p) with second-order perturbative corrections
geometry_source: not stated in the main text read
method: restricted active space configuration interaction in the hole and particle approximation, RAS(h,p) - the full CI within RAS2 plus all configurations with one hole in RAS1 and one electron in RAS3 - corrected at second order by Epstein-Nesbet (EN) and Davidson-Kapuy (DK) partitionings, with and without an energy level shift; benchmarked against NEVPT2 and literature reference data
basis_set: several basis sets compared; the DK correction is shown to depend weakly on basis set
active_space_orbital_description: RAS1, RAS2 and RAS3 subspaces in the hole-and-particle truncation; per-molecule spaces are not given in the main text
electronic_structure_description: RAS(h,p) lacks effective dynamic correlation and systematically overestimates singlet excitation energies by about 0.8 eV, with much smaller errors for triplets. Epstein-Nesbet perturbation gives only marginal improvement and increases the statistical scatter; Davidson-Kapuy gives a more consistent correction but tends to overcompensate, and adding an energy level shift to the DK partition removes that bias. Decomposing the correction shows that the dominant contribution comes from terms resembling a state-specific orbital relaxation through singles, while the more expensive 1h2p and 2h2p terms matter little - which the authors read as a route to cheaper targeted perturbative schemes. Because the DK-based corrections depend only weakly on the basis set, a composite strategy works: large-basis RAS(h,p) energies combined with small-basis DK-plus-shift corrections give significant savings at minimal accuracy cost.
reference_short: Perumal Marisami & Casanova, Assessing Second-Order Perturbative Corrections to Restricted Active Space CI for Valence Excitations in Organic Molecules, J. Phys. Chem. A 2025, 129, 11736-11748
notes: Benchmark paper condensed into one row. active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY: RAS(h,p) spaces are defined by the RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 partition rather than a single (nel,norb) pair, and the per-molecule partitions are not stated in the main text. software and geometry_source are likewise not named there.

compound_name: acrolein, gas-phase absorption cross section of the n->pi* band
geometry_source: ensemble of 100 structures sampled uniformly every 20 ps from equilibrated classical molecular dynamics (Amber, GAFF force constants, B3LYP/6-311G(2d,p) equilibrium parameters and Mulliken point charges, SHAKE on C-H bonds); vertical excitations also computed at B3LYP/6-31G and B3LYP/6-311G(2d,p) equilibrium geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by state-specific CASPT2, with an imaginary shift of 0.2 au against intruder states; vertical excitation energies and oscillator strengths converted into absorption cross sections sigma(lambda) and molar extinction coefficients epsilon(lambda) over nuclear ensembles from molecular dynamics
basis_set: ANO-L-VTZP, contracted C, N, O [4s3p2d1f] / H [3s2p1d]
active_space_orbital_description: the valence pi and pi* orbitals plus the carbonyl oxygen lone pair (n)
active_space_protocol: CAS(6,5) with a state average over eight roots; IPEA shift 0.25 au, chosen for consistency with the group's earlier acrolein work
electronic_structure_description: The lowest excited state is the carbonyl n -> pi* transition. Vertical excitation energy 3.66 eV (339 nm) at CASPT2/ANO-L-VTZP//B3LYP/6-31G and 3.52 eV (352 nm) at CASPT2/ANO-L-VTZP//B3LYP/6-311G(2d,p). The oscillator strength is negligible at planar geometries, so the band intensity comes entirely from the nuclear ensemble - which is the point of computing sigma(lambda) over sampled structures rather than from a single geometry.
reference_short: Multiconfigurational Quantum Chemistry Determinations of Absorption Cross Sections in the Gas Phase and Molar Extinction Coefficients in Condensed Phases, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021
notes: IPEA 0.25 au here versus 0.0 for the uracil adduct in the same paper; both choices are stated as matching the authors' respective earlier studies. software left empty - no program is named in the main text for the CASSCF/CASPT2 step.

compound_name: U6OH-radical, the OH adduct of uracil at the C6 position, molar extinction coefficient in water
geometry_source: nuclear ensembles from two-nanosecond NPT classical molecular dynamics in Amber14 at 300 K and 1 bar with periodic boundaries, a 2 fs step, Berendsen thermostat and barostat, SHAKE on C-H bonds and the TIP3P water model; the solvent enters the quantum calculation as the same field of point charges used in the MD
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by state-specific CASPT2, with an imaginary shift of 0.2 au against intruder states; vertical excitation energies and oscillator strengths converted into absorption cross sections sigma(lambda) and molar extinction coefficients epsilon(lambda) over nuclear ensembles from molecular dynamics
basis_set: ANO-S-VDZP, contracted C, N, O [3s2p1d] / H [2s1p]
active_space_orbital_description: all the pi bonding and pi* antibonding orbitals plus the oxygen and nitrogen lone-pair orbitals of the C=O, =N- and -OH groups
active_space_protocol: CAS(15,10) with a state average over ten roots; IPEA shift 0.0 au, for consistency with the group's earlier U6OH work
electronic_structure_description: Condensed-phase molar extinction coefficients epsilon(lambda) computed for the radical in water from the sampled ensemble, with the solvent represented by the MD point-charge field around a CASSCF/CASPT2 chromophore.
reference_short: Multiconfigurational Quantum Chemistry Determinations of Absorption Cross Sections in the Gas Phase and Molar Extinction Coefficients in Condensed Phases, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021
notes: Open-shell OH-adduct radical (the paper writes it U6OH-dot). ground_state_mult is left EMPTY: the paper does not state the spin multiplicity anywhere in the text read, and inheriting the closed-shell value of the paper's other system would be wrong for a radical. software left empty as well - no program is named for the CASSCF/CASPT2 step.

compound_name: benzene interacting with water clusters (H2O)n, n = 5, 6, 12, 14, 48 and 49, cut from two hexagonal-ice configurations
geometry_source: two series of geometries, GeoIEI and GeoIED, extracted from two benzene-hexagonal-ice configurations giving maximum and minimum ionization energies respectively
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by MS-CASPT2, with a level shift tuned per system and the standard IPEA shift; oscillator strengths from restricted active space state interaction (RASSI); TD-DFT with CAM-B3LYP benchmarked against these results
basis_set: ANO-L, contracted C, N, O (14s9p4d3f) -> [3s2p1d] and H (8s4p3d) -> [2s1p], augmented with system-specific diffuse functions from the Kaufmann series with Genano-derived coefficients, placed at the average position of the two centres of charge of the cations from the two highest benzene pi orbitals (called 'Gen.' in the tables)
