active_space_orbital_description: all the pi orbitals of benzene plus one s, three p and five d Rydberg orbitals; the same active space was used for every system. Including the water oxygen lone pairs was not feasible, so the n(O) -> Rydberg states could not be described.
active_space_protocol: state-averaged orbitals optimized over 42 singlet states to reach all the targeted states; the 34 lowest states carried through to MS-CASPT2. The level shift was chosen per system to stabilize the excitation energies and keep the reference weight of the excited states within 3% of the ground state: 0.3 for bare benzene and 0.4 for every other system.
nroots_per_mult: 42 in the state-averaged CASSCF; 34 at MS-CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: Vertical electronic spectra of benzene in water clusters, computed at MS-CASPT2 for the smallest systems as reference data for benchmarking TD-DFT. Rydberg states are interleaved with valence states in benzene, which is why the diffuse functions had to be defined per system; with them, all states of isolated benzene are better described, the Rydberg states considerably so. Despite some discrepancies, TD-DFT and MS-CASPT2 give similar trends in the positions and intensities of the bands. The standard IPEA shift was used because MS-CASPT2 underestimates the excitation energies without it.
reference_short: Ben Amor, Michoulier, Simon et al., Electronic excited states of benzene in interaction with water clusters: influence of structure and size
notes: active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY: the space is specified by orbital content only - all benzene pi orbitals plus one s, three p and five d Rydberg orbitals - with no counts stated, and summing them would be inference. The inability to include the water oxygen lone pairs is a stated limitation, not an oversight: it means the n(O) -> Rydberg states are simply absent from these spectra.

compound_name: trans-[RuCl(NO)(py)4]2+ ruthenium nitrosyl complex, NO photodissociation from the ground state and the MS1 and MS2 metastable linkage isomers
ligand_set: four pyridine ligands, one chloride and one nitrosyl (bound N-down in GS, O-down in MS1, side-on eta2 in MS2)
point_group: the relaxed pentacoordinated complex has C2 symmetry, the Jahn-Teller-broken form of the C4 doubly degenerate E state
geometry_source: relaxed scans along the Ru-N distance from 3GS and 3MS2 and along the Ru-O distance from 3MS1, computed at CAM-B3LYP/def2-TZVP with a small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Ru; CAM-B3LYP was chosen over B3LYP-D3, which suffers artificial charge transfer between the dissociating fragments and gives wrong asymptotic spin densities
method: CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference for the singlet ground state and lowest triplet excited states along the photodissociation paths
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VDZP and ANO-RCC-VTZP for the multireference step; def2-TZVP with a small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Ru for the DFT geometries
relativistic_treatment: small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Ru in the DFT scans; ANO-RCC relativistic basis sets in the CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: the three occupied Ru 4d valence orbitals correlating with t2g (the eg d_z2 and d_x2-y2 orbitals are not involved in NO dissociation and were left out), plus two pi/pi* pairs and the sigma/sigma* pair of NO
electronic_structure_description: Photodissociation from 3GS: CAM-B3LYP and CASPT2 agree well, with dissociation energies of 0.91 and 0.96 eV and smooth curves indicating weak state coupling. From 3MS2 and 3MS1 the two methods diverge substantially - CAM-B3LYP gives 0.08 and 0.41 eV where CASPT2 gives 0.25 and 0.67 eV. The 3MS2 path is complex, with many crossings among the lowest triplets and a local well on T1 at a Ru-N distance near 2.8 A produced by a T1/T2 crossing (also visible at B3LYP-D3 and CAM-B3LYP). The overall picture is a sequential two-step photon absorption photorelease mechanism coupled to partial photoisomerization to the side-on MS2 intermediate, consistent with earlier DFT work.
reference_short: CASPT2 Potential Energy Curves for NO Dissociation in a Ruthenium Nitrosyl Complex, Molecules 2020, 25, 2613
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty: NO is non-innocent here and the paper describes the system through orbital occupations along the dissociation coordinate rather than assigning a formal Ru oxidation state.

compound_name: ClSO sulfinyl radical, A-band absorption spectrum and the 1 2A'/2 2A' conical intersection
geometry_source: equilibrium geometries and relative energies from exploring the lowest three potential energy surfaces; radicals generated experimentally by pulsed-laser photolysis with transient absorption recorded from 300 to 580 nm in a flow reactor
method: extended dynamically weighted CASPT2 (XDW-CASPT2) on a CASSCF reference, alongside coupled-cluster (EOM-EE) calculations and a molecular-orbital analysis
active_space_orbital_description: a seven-electrons-in-five-orbitals CASSCF reference; the active orbitals at the ground-state equilibrium geometry are drawn in the paper's Figure 5, with out-of-plane orbitals distinguished
electronic_structure_description: A sloped-type conical intersection between the 1 2A' and 2 2A' states was located. Observed transient spectra were assigned by comparison with the ab initio results, and an MO analysis clarifies the role of the Cl atom and the sulfinyl electronic structure. The EOM-EE/ano-pVTZ calculation failed to converge for the upper state, which is part of why the multireference treatment was needed. By analogy with HSO, whose SOMO <- SOMO-1 chemiluminescence has been detected in the visible, ClSO might fluoresce after A-band excitation.
reference_short: Chao, Jones, Okumura et al., A-Band Absorption Spectrum of the ClSO Radical: Electronic Structure of the Sulfinyl Group, J. Phys. Chem. A
notes: Open-shell doublet radical. The (7,5) space is stated in prose as 'a seven-electrons in five-orbitals CASSCF reference' - a spelled/digit mixed form.

compound_name: 6-thioguanine (6TG), ultrafast excited-state decay in phosphate-buffered saline
geometry_source: three single points P1, P2 and P3 along the minimum energy path relaxing the S2(pipi*) state from the Franck-Condon region, at CASSCF(14,12)/ANO-L; coordinates in the supporting information
method: multi-state CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference, MS-CASPT2//CASSCF(14,12), supporting sub-20 fs UV transient absorption spectroscopy
electronic_structure_description: Energies and oscillator strengths of 6TG in vacuum at MS-CASPT2//CASSCF(14,12)/ANO-L. The three points along the S2(pipi*) relaxation path have close adiabatic energies, indicating a planar S2(pipi*) pseudo-minimum whose calculated emission wavelength matches the 398 nm Gaussian in the measured photoluminescence (the second Gaussian is at 454 nm). The calculations show S2 stays planar before reaching the conical intersection with S1, which acts as the doorway to the triplet manifold. Combined with the experiment - an 81 fs stimulated-emission signature for the S2 wave packet after 340 nm excitation and 522 fs to the triplet manifold - this establishes S2(pipi*) -> S1(npi*) -> T1(pipi*) as the major decay pathway and gives experimental evidence for the intermediate dark singlet.
reference_short: Ultrafast Excited-State Decay Mechanisms of 6-Thioguanine Followed by Sub-20 fs UV Transient Absorption Spectroscopy, Molecules 2022, 27, 1200
notes: software left empty - no program is named anywhere in the main text for the CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 step, and the paper's computational details are minimal. The composition of the (14,12) space is not described.

compound_name: molecular switch undergoing photoinduced forward and backward pedalo-type motion
geometry_source: QM/MM setup with three layers, the QM high layer treated by CASPT2
method: CASPT2 (and RASPT2) in a three-layer QM/MM scheme, with the QM high layer carrying the dynamical correlation needed to place the excited states correctly
electronic_structure_description: The QM high layer is described by CASPT2(18e,12o)/6-31G*, chosen to include the dynamical correlation whose energy components determine the relative excited-state energies; relative state energies are tabulated in the supporting information.
reference_short: Conti, Buma, Garavelli et al., Photoinduced Forward and Backward Pedalo-Type Motion of a Molecular Switch
notes: Text extracted from a UvA-DARE repository deposit whose body is largely truncated; only the QM/MM setup and the CASPT2(18e,12o)/6-31G* level survived extraction, so compound formula, software and the detailed photochemistry are not recorded. The active space is stated explicitly and is the reason this is extracted rather than discarded.

geometry_source: potential energy curves computed along the internuclear coordinate; millimeter-wave spectroscopy provides the experimental comparison
method: CASSCF reference states augmented by second-order perturbation theory (CASPT2); a second approach also used for comparison
basis_set: quadruple-zeta atomic natural orbital ANO-L-VQZP on both Mg and Cl
active_space_orbital_description: an augmented full-valence CAS containing all 9 valence electrons plus one additional a1 orbital, giving 9 orbitals in total, the extra orbital included to describe molecular dissociation cleanly
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy curves and spectroscopic constants for the electronic manifold of MgCl, focused on the (3) 2Sigma+ and (4) 2Sigma+ states, computed to interpret millimeter-wave spectra.
reference_short: Herman, Ravi et al., Probing the Electronic Manifold of MgCl with Millimeter-Wave Spectroscopy and Theory: (3) 2Sigma+ and (4) 2Sigma+ States, J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 9893-9903
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty - Mg is main-group and the paper assigns no oxidation state. The extra a1 orbital beyond the full valence set is the paper's own device for a clean dissociation limit.

compound_name: MgC4H radicals, low-lying isomers of astrophysical interest
geometry_source: isomer geometries optimized with DFT (wB97XD/6-311G++(2d,2p) among others); CASPT2 single points on the low-lying isomers
method: CASPT2, applied because some low-lying isomers show multireference character flagged by high T1 diagnostics; ELF and atoms-in-molecules analyses for the bonding
software: ORCA (Gaussian for the DFT; Multiwfn for the wavefunction analysis)
active_space_orbital_description: the entire pi-electron system plus all valence and unpaired electrons of the Mg atom
electronic_structure_description: Spectroscopic parameters for the MgC4H isomers computed at CASPT2 with the (11,11) space and cc-pVTZ. For isomer 1, detected in IRC+10216, the calculated rotational constant differs from the experimental B0 of 1381.512 MHz by about 0.78%. The first seven low-lying isomers have doublet ground electronic states.
reference_short: Roy, Satpati, Sinjari, Anoop, Thimmakondu, Ghosal, Energetic and Spectroscopic Properties of Astrophysically Relevant MgC4H Radicals Using High-Level Ab Initio Calculations, J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 1466-1476
notes: Main-group metal, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty. CASPT2 was applied selectively to the isomers whose T1 diagnostic flagged multireference character; the bulk of the isomer survey is DFT and coupled cluster.

compound_name: singlet oxygen reactions: common reaction motifs of O2 with organic substrates, benchmarked against spin-restricted descriptions
geometry_source: minimum energy reaction paths; xyz geometries of the stationary points computed with DFT are provided in the supporting information
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2) with a real shift of 0.2 au, on state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest two singlet states, with a single triplet computed separately; M11 and wB97X-D3 reaction pathways for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the reaction path calculations; def2-TZVPP and def2-QZVPP also used
active_space_orbital_description: chosen per reaction; the full details of active space selection for each reaction are given only in the Supporting Information
active_space_protocol: state-averaged CASSCF over the two lowest singlet states for the singlet calculations, with the triplet treated as a separate single-state calculation; per-reaction spaces in the SI
electronic_structure_description: Benchmarks of spin-restricted descriptions of singlet oxygen reactivity against XMS-CASPT2 along the common reaction motifs of singlet oxygen, with the aim of obtaining not only thermodynamic parameters but also an electronic-structure description of the bulk molecular species free of spin contamination. The lowest triplet and two lowest singlet states of O2 differ in the occupation of the degenerate pi* orbitals.
reference_short: Winslow, Hazelby, Robinson, Spin-Restricted Descriptions of Singlet Oxygen Reactions from XMS-CASPT2 Benchmarks, J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 4128-4137
notes: active_space_nel and active_space_norb left EMPTY: the paper states explicitly that active space selection is documented per reaction in the Supporting Information and gives no space in the main text.

compound_name: group 13 dimetallenes REER (E = Al, Ga, In, Tl; R = H, Me, tBu, Ph), metal-metal bonding and singlet diradical character
formula: REER, E = Al, Ga, In, Tl
geometry_source: optimizations and frequencies at DFT; AIM and ELF analyses on B3LYP/cc-pVTZ densities
method: CASSCF and CASPT2, alongside HF, MP2, CCSD(T), B3LYP and M06-2X
active_space_orbital_description: the frontier molecular orbitals of the trans-bent dimetallenes, illustrated in the paper for R = H; the paper notes theoretical ambiguities in assigning an active space for the monomeric units
electronic_structure_description: The metal-metal interaction in group 13 dimetallenes stems almost exclusively from static and dynamic electron correlation. Both dialuminenes and digallenes have an important singlet diradical component in their wave functions, distinguishing them from the heavier congeners. BSSE is expected to be minimal at HF and DFT levels provided polarized triple-zeta basis sets are used.
reference_short: Moilanen et al., Nature of Bonding in Group 13 Dimetallenes: a Delicate Balance between Singlet Diradical Character and Donor-Acceptor Interaction
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count left empty: these are main-group dimetallenes and the paper analyses the bonding through diradical character and donor-acceptor interaction rather than oxidation states. active_space_nel/norb left EMPTY - the space is shown only as a frontier-orbital figure, with the paper itself noting ambiguity in assigning an active space for the monomer units.

compound_name: AlH+ cation, X 2Sigma+ and A 2Pi states, hyperfine structure for optical pumping to a pure quantum state
geometry_source: calculations at the equilibrium geometry, R = 1.6018 A
method: restricted active space self-consistent field (RASSCF)
basis_set: pcJ-1, chosen because the pcJ-n family is optimized for indirect nuclear spin-spin coupling constants and has tight functions suited to the electron density near the nucleus
active_space_orbital_description: 5 inactive orbitals in RAS1, a full-valence five-orbital RAS2 space, and single and double excitations from RAS2 into a RAS3 space comprising the 30 remaining orbitals; the resulting wave functions contain 2439 determinants for X 2Sigma+ and 1947 for A 2Pi
electronic_structure_description: Hyperfine parameters for the X 2Sigma+ and A 2Pi states of AlH+, computed at the equilibrium geometry to support a protocol for optically pumping the ion into a single pure quantum state.
reference_short: Huang, Kain, Odom, de Oliveira-Filho, Protocol for Optically Pumping AlH+ to a Pure Quantum State
notes: RAS calculation: the RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 partition (5 inactive / 5 full-valence / 30 remaining with singles and doubles) does not reduce to a single (nel,norb) pair, so nel/norb are left empty and the whole partition is in the orbital description. Main-group metal, so no oxidation state or d count.

geometry_source: ground state optimized at MP2/cc-pVDZ in the gas phase; all excited-state minima and transition states (S1 min, T1 min, S1 TS) and the S2/S1, S1/S0 and T2/T1 minimum-energy conical intersections optimized at XMS-CASPT2/CASSCF(10,8)/cc-pVDZ, each validated by a frequency calculation at the same level
method: XMS-CASPT2 on a state-averaged CASSCF reference, supporting sub-20 fs time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
active_space_orbital_description: active orbitals shown in the paper's Figures S5-S6
active_space_protocol: (10,8) with five electronic states in the singlet state-averaging and two in the triplet state-averaging
nroots_per_mult: 5 singlets; 2 triplets
electronic_structure_description: Excited-state decay of enolic acetylacetone mapped through the S1 minimum, T1 minimum, an S1 transition state, and the S2/S1, S1/S0 and T2/T1 minimum-energy conical intersections, with minimum-energy paths between the key geometries, interpreted against sub-20 fs time-resolved photoelectron spectra.
reference_short: Severino, Aleotti et al., Mapping Excited-State Decay Mechanisms in Acetylacetone by Sub-20 fs Time-Resolved Photoelectron Spectroscopy
notes: The (10,8) space is given with its state-averaging scheme in the main text; the orbital pictures are in the SI.

compound_name: cyclobutanone, n->(3s) Rydberg excited photochemistry and ultrafast electron-diffraction spectra
geometry_source: geometries at the MP2/6-31++G* level, the diffuse functions being needed to describe excitation into Rydberg orbitals
method: XMS-CASPT2 on state-averaged CASSCF wave functions, with an imaginary shift of 0.2 and zero IPEA shift; spin-orbit coupling added a posteriori through a one-electron effective Hamiltonian in the atomic mean field approximation
basis_set: 6-31++G* for geometries; 6-31G* augmented with 1s1p1d and 8s8p8d Rydberg sets, and aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ, for the excited states
active_space_orbital_description: orbitals shown in the paper's Figure S1
active_space_protocol: a reduced |8,8| active space was used for this work, validated against the |12,12| space employed in previous studies as a benchmark; the lowest three singlets and three triplets were obtained in two separate state-averaged CASSCF calculations
nroots_per_mult: 3 singlets; 3 triplets
electronic_structure_description: Ultrafast photochemistry of cyclobutanone after n->(3s) Rydberg excitation, with simulated electron-diffraction spectra, resolved at the multireference perturbative level. Context from the literature: an MS-CASPT2 analysis of the npi* reactive surface gives a 6.7 kcal/mol (0.29 eV) ring-opening barrier, and ab initio multiple spawning dynamics on the npi* state give 176 fs for alpha C-C cleavage and 484 fs for internal conversion to the ground state; other work attributes the fast timescales to high ring strain and a 29 kJ/mol (0.3 eV) transition state.
reference_short: Jaiswal, Montorsi, Aleotti, Segatta, Keefer, Mukamel et al., Ultrafast photochemistry and electron-diffraction spectra in n->(3s) Rydberg excited cyclobutanone resolved at the multireference perturbative level
notes: nel/norb record the |8,8| space actually used; the |12,12| benchmark space from earlier work is in active_space_protocol. The barrier and timescale figures in the electronic structure description are from the cited literature, not computed here.

compound_name: two hydroxyl radicals in amorphous solid water clusters, the OH + OH route to interstellar hydrogen peroxide
geometry_source: clusters of 20-30 water molecules containing two hydroxyl radicals, with under 10% of the training set being pure water clusters; rigid scans along the inter-radical distance
method: state-averaged CASPT2 over the four lowest singlet states, used together with PBE(D3BJ)/def2-SVP to generate reference energies and forces for a machine-learned interatomic potential driving molecular dynamics
basis_set: 6-31+G(d,p) for the CASPT2; def2-SVP for the PBE part
active_space_orbital_description: six electrons and one virtual orbital; the (6,4) space proved the best compromise, since smaller or slightly larger spaces produced discontinuities in the rigid potential scans along the inter-radical distance
active_space_protocol: SA4-CASPT2(6,4)/6-31+G(d,p) averaging the four lowest singlet states. In the training set both OH radicals were treated by CASPT2 while the water molecules were described at the PBE level
electronic_structure_description: The inter-radical distance is the key coordinate; the (6,4) active space was selected precisely because alternatives gave discontinuous potential energy scans along it. The resulting CASPT2/PBE reference data train a machine-learned potential used to compare diffusive and non-diffusive routes to hydrogen peroxide formation on amorphous solid water.
reference_short: Postulka, Slavicek, Kastner, Molpeceres, Diffusive vs. non-diffusive paths to interstellar hydrogen peroxide: a machine learning-based molecular dynamics study, Astron. Astrophys. 2025
notes: system_class is molecule rather than solid-state: the water is an explicit finite cluster model of an amorphous ice surface treated at the PBE level, with only the two OH radicals in the CASPT2 region. The active-space description quotes the paper's own wording, 'constituting from 6 electrons and one virtual orbital', alongside the (6,4) label it uses throughout.

compound_name: reference database of ground- and excited-state geometries for small molecules: formaldehyde and its homologues (thioformaldehyde, selenoformaldehyde), acetylene, ketene, thioketene, diazomethane and related compounds
geometry_source: ground- and excited-state geometries optimized at CASPT2 and at coupled-cluster levels (CC2, CCSD, CCSDR(3), CC3), with the CC gradients obtained by numerical differentiation of total energies; the nature of each stationary point checked by frequency analysis
method: CASPT2 with the standard 0.25 au IPEA shift correcting the active orbital energies, alongside CC2, CCSD, CCSDR(3) and CC3; Cholesky decomposition with a 1e-4 threshold used to speed up the CASPT2, verified against non-Cholesky formaldehyde geometries
software: OpenMolcas 8.3 (Dalton, Turbomole and Gaussian for the coupled-cluster work)
basis_set: ANO-L with VQZP contraction under the frozen-core model for the first estimates, then aug-cc-pVTZ with no frozen orbitals so the results are directly comparable to the coupled-cluster ones; cc-pVQZ used for a CCSDR(3) check
active_space_orbital_description: one active space per molecule; the CASPT2 levels reported in the geometry tables include (10e,10o), (12e,10o) and (12e,15o) for different compounds
active_space_protocol: per-molecule active spaces, quoted in the individual geometry tables rather than as a single scheme: examples include CASPT2(10e,10o)/aug-cc-pVTZ, CASPT2(12e,10o)/aug-cc-pVTZ and CASPT2(12e,15o)/aug-cc-pVTZ
electronic_structure_description: Sample geometry comparisons at aug-cc-pVTZ, CASPT2 against coupled cluster, MR-AQCC and experiment. For one compound with a (10e,10o) space: CASPT2 gives 1.370 / 1.092 A and 122.2 deg for the ground state and 1.342 / 1.094 A and 132.4 deg for the excited state, essentially matching CC3 (1.371 / 1.090 / 122.2 and 1.342 / 1.093 / 132.9), MR-AQCC extrapolated (1.369 / 1.091 / 123.2 and 1.339 / 1.093 / 132.9) and Mk-MRCCSD, while CCSD alone gives shorter bonds (1.352 / 1.086 / 124.1). For a (12e,10o) case CASPT2 gives 1.326 / 1.090 A, 118.1 deg and a puckering angle of 38.2 deg, against CC3 1.326 / 1.089 / 118.3 / 36.8 and experiment 1.323 / 1.098 / 118.4 / 34. For a (12e,15o) case CASPT2 gives 1.711 and 1.845 A against experimental 1.682 and 1.856 A. Deviations between methods are most marked for the polarized CO and CN bonds and for the puckering angle in the formaldehyde homologues. Ketene, thioketene and diazomethane are C2v in the ground state but their C2v excited-state structures are unstable (CCSD imaginary frequencies of 761i, 338i and 579i cm-1), the minima being bent Cs structures close to a conical intersection back to the ground state, which is why these molecules photodissociate efficiently and experimental excited-state structural data barely exist.
reference_short: Budzak, Scalmani, Jacquemin, Accurate Excited-State Geometries: A CASPT2 and Coupled-Cluster Reference Database for Small Molecules, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2017
notes: Benchmark database condensed into one row. active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY because the space differs per molecule; the three CASPT2 spaces that appear in the geometry tables are recorded in active_space_protocol. The row deliberately does not name which molecule carries which space: the extracted text interleaves several tables and the compound labels did not survive extraction reliably enough to assign them.

compound_name: Fe(II) spin-crossover complexes including [Fe(tacn)2]2+, [Fe(bpy)3]2+ and [Fe(pic)3]2+; and meso-triphenyl copper corroles
ligand_set: triazacyclononane, bipyridine and picolinate chelates on the iron complexes; a meso-triphenylcorrole macrocycle on the copper complexes
geometry_source: geometries optimized with CASPT2 analytical gradients developed in the project; linear interpolation of internal coordinates between saddled and planar geometries for the corroles; partial Hessian vibrational analysis used to cut the cost of frequencies in large molecules
method: CASPT2 with analytical nuclear gradients, and XMS-CASPT2 for the electronic structure; compared against plane-wave DFT with a Hubbard-U correction
basis_set: cc-pVTZ on the metal and first coordination sphere, cc-pVDZ on the remaining atoms for the larger complexes
active_space_protocol: the project's recommendation is a (10e,12o) active space with cc-pVTZ on the metal and first coordination sphere, which converges to minimum structures more efficiently than truncated spaces; even a minimal (6e,5o) space already yields good Fe-ligand bond distances, and for the corroles a minimal space sufficed for structural characterization while larger spaces were needed for the electronic structure
electronic_structure_description: For Fe(II) spin-crossover complexes, DFT and CASPT2 geometries agree well overall, with the largest differences for the smaller complexes carrying strong-field ligands in the low-spin state. For the copper corroles, XMS-CASPT2 identifies the ground state as a multiconfigurational singlet (S0) with three dominant configurations at the lowest-energy saddled geometry, while the planar geometry corresponds to a triplet (T0) about 5 kcal/mol above S0. Across three families - spin-crossover complexes, metallocorroles and metal-metal-bonded species - CASPT2 gives good molecular geometries. The recurring theme is that static and dynamic correlation must be recovered in a balanced way to get quantitative results.
reference_short: Vlaisavljevich, Controlling Molecular Structure and Spin with Multiconfigurational Quantum Chemistry, DOE Final Technical Report DE-SC0019463
notes: DOE final technical report summarising a multi-year project, so it reports across several published studies rather than one calculation. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty because the row spans both Fe(II) and copper corrole systems. nel/norb record the project's recommended (10e,12o); the minimal (6e,5o) alternative is in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: DLPNO-NEVPT2-F12 benchmark: low-lying excited states of organic molecules, a [(C4SH3)-CnH2n-(C4SH3)]2+ scaling series, and cluster models of rhodopsin
geometry_source: not stated in the text read
method: linear-scaling explicitly correlated N-electron valence state perturbation theory, NEVPT2-F12, made near-linear-scaling by the domain-based local pair natural orbital (DLPNO) approximation
basis_set: double-zeta through cc-pVQZ; def2-SVP for parts of the work
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(10,10) references for the scaling series; the rhodopsin cluster models use an active space of 12 pi electrons in 12 pi orbitals
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(10,10) for the [(C4SH3)-CnH2n-(C4SH3)]2+ scaling series; a 12-pi-electron, 12-pi-orbital space for the rhodopsin cluster models, in systems exceeding 3300 basis functions
electronic_structure_description: For low-lying excited states of organic molecules, DLPNO-NEVPT2-F12 reproduces the exact NEVPT2-F12 excitation energies, giving the same absolute and relative energies as the conventional method. Strikingly, DLPNO-NEVPT2-F12 in a double-zeta basis already delivers absolute and relative energies more accurate than plain NEVPT2 in a quadruple-zeta basis. The crossover where DLPNO-NEVPT2-F12 becomes cheaper than canonical NEVPT2-F12 occurs at a system size of only about 10 atoms. The method reaches systems with more than 3300 basis functions.
reference_short: SparseMaps VI: Linear-scaling explicitly correlated N-electron valence state perturbation theory, J. Chem. Phys.
notes: Method paper; nel/norb record the CASSCF(10,10) of the scaling series, with the rhodopsin (12,12) pi space in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: 1,3-cyclohexadiene (CHD), ultrafast ring-opening from the 1B spectroscopic state to the photochemical product
point_group: C2 symmetry imposed in the geometry optimization; the electronic structure calculations were performed without symmetry
geometry_source: geometry optimization under a C2 constraint; the 1 1B minimum energy path used for the ionization calculations
method: CASSCF followed by multi-state multi-reference CASPT2 (MS-MR-CASPT2), interpreting time-resolved photoelectron spectra
active_space_orbital_description: four orbitals with six electrons for the neutral species
active_space_protocol: CAS(6,4) for the neutral; the cation states along the 1 1B minimum energy path were obtained from an SA2-CAS(5,4)-SCF wave function at MS-MR-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ
electronic_structure_description: Time-resolved photoelectron spectra of cyclohexadiene, with electron binding energy resolved along the reaction, are interpreted against MS-MR-CASPT2 energies for the neutral (CAS(6,4)) and the cation (SA2-CAS(5,4)) computed on the same 1 1B minimum energy path, giving a spectral observation of the complete reaction path from the spectroscopic 1B state to the photoproduct.
reference_short: Pemberton, Zhang et al., From the (1B) Spectroscopic State to the Photochemical Product of the Ultrafast Ring-Opening of 1,3-Cyclohexadiene: A Spectral Observation of the Complete Reaction Path
notes: Two spaces for two charge states, both recorded; nel/norb hold the neutral CAS(6,4).

compound_name: linear conjugated chromophores: a bridged polyene model (BP) and an extended model (ExBP), photoselectivity
formula: BP and ExBP conjugated polyene models
geometry_source: XMS-CASPT2 optimized geometries; vertical excitation energies computed on those geometries
method: XMS-CASPT2 on three-state-averaged (SA3) CASSCF reference wave functions
software: BAGEL (COLUMBUS, Dalton and Turbomole also used)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ with the cc-pVDZ-JKFIT density fitting basis
active_space_orbital_description: ten electrons in ten active pi orbitals for the BP model; twelve electrons in twelve active pi orbitals for the extended ExBP model
active_space_protocol: SA3-CASSCF(10,10) for BP and SA3-CASSCF(12,12) for ExBP, with vertical excitation energies of three excited states computed at XMS-CASPT2 on the XMS-CASPT2 geometries
electronic_structure_description: Photoselectivity of linear conjugated chromophores studied at the XMS-CASPT2 level, with vertical excitation energies for three excited states of each model computed on XMS-CASPT2 geometries; the extended model tests how the conclusions carry over as the conjugation lengthens.
reference_short: Sen & Deupi, Study of Photoselectivity in Linear Conjugated Chromophores Using the XMS-CASPT2 Method, ACS Phys. Chem. Au 2024, 4, 736-749
notes: Two models with different spaces; nel/norb hold the BP (10,10) and the ExBP (12,12) is in active_space_protocol. The paper writes the spaces in the reversed (orbitals, electrons) order as '(10o,10e)' and '(12o,12e)' but spells them out unambiguously as 'ten electrons in ten active pi-orbitals' and '12 electrons in 12 active pi-orbitals', so the symmetric pairs carry no ambiguity here.

compound_name: singlet pyridinylidenes with N-substituents X = I, Br, Cl, OCF3, OMe, NMe2, F, Me, and their transition states for H2 activation
formula: C5H4N-X carbene ring (X = I, Br, Cl, OCF3, OMe, NMe2, F, Me) plus H2
ligand_set: a nitrogen substituent X of varying bond strength on the pyridinylidene ring
geometry_source: all relevant stationary points optimized with DFT at B3LYP-D3/def2-TZVPP; intrinsic reaction coordinates followed from every transition state
method: NEVPT2 single-point energies on a CASSCF reference, without the frozen-core approximation, for all hydrogenation transition states; DLPNO-CCSD(T)/def2-QZVPP with TightPNO settings for the remaining single-point energies
basis_set: def2-TZVPP for the NEVPT2-(12,11) single points and the B3LYP-D3 optimizations; def2-QZVPP for the DLPNO-CCSD(T) energies
active_space_orbital_description: the sigma lone pair and the pi orbitals of the carbene in the ring, the bonding sigma and antibonding sigma* orbitals of the nitrogen substituent, and the bonding sigma and antibonding sigma* orbitals of dihydrogen
active_space_protocol: a single CASSCF-(12,11) space used for every hydrogenation transition state, chosen so that the carbene, the N-X bond and the incoming H2 are all described; singlet-triplet gaps and N-X bond dissociation energies were taken from DLPNO-CCSD(T) instead, which the authors argue removes the need to extend the active space for those quantities
electronic_structure_description: The nitrogen substituent controls which frontier configuration the singlet carbene adopts and hence which hydrogenation pathway it takes. I, Br, Cl and OCF3 give a sigma2 sigma*0 configuration and favour the sigma*-approach; OMe, NMe2 and Me give sigma2 pi0 and lower barriers for the pi-approach. Fluorine is the exception: it adopts sigma2 pi0 yet still prefers the sigma* pathway. In 1-I the carbene bond angle exceeds 120 degrees, letting the carbene sigma orbital mix strongly with the N-I sigma*, which shows up as pronounced deviation from integer occupation numbers in the CASSCF treatment. T1 diagnostics for the sigma/sigma* carbenes are elevated but only slightly above the 0.02 threshold.
reference_short: Schuster, Bhagat & Wagner, Competing Modes of Hydrogen Activation in Singlet Pyridinylidenes: pi-Approach vs sigma*-Approach Reaction Pathways, J. Phys. Chem. A (Michael A. Duncan Festschrift)
notes: The multireference treatment is NEVPT2-(12,11)/def2-TZVPP on the transition states; DFT supplies the geometries and DLPNO-CCSD(T) the remaining energetics. One row for the whole substituent series because a single active space is used throughout.

compound_name: sodium monoxide NaO, close-lying X2Pi and A2Sigma+ states (ExoMol line list XLIII)
point_group: C2v subgroup used in the calculation (the molecule is C-infinity-v)
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed on a grid of internuclear distances R = 1.0-50 A and represented analytically by an Extended-Morse-Oscillator form
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by internally contracted multireference configuration interaction MR-CISD with the Davidson correction; spin-orbit and L-uncoupling non-adiabatic matrix elements computed and used in a deperturbation model, with a full counterpoise correction applied state by state and the residual size-consistency error removed at R = 20 A
basis_set: aug-cc-pVQZ all-electron on both Na and O
active_space_orbital_description: 7 a1, 3 b1 and 3 b2 orbitals in C2v; the lowest two a1 orbitals were kept doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: the same active space of 7a1 + 3b1 + 3b2 orbitals was used for both the SA-CASSCF and the MR-CISD step, with the lowest two a1 orbitals doubly occupied; the state averaging took the lowest doublet (1-3)Pi, (1)Sigma+, (1)Sigma- and (1)Delta states with equal weights
nroots_per_mult: 6 doublets state-averaged: (1-3)Pi, (1)Sigma+, (1)Sigma-, (1)Delta
electronic_structure_description: NaO has an A2Sigma+ excited state lying only about 2000 cm-1 (Te) above the X2Pi ground state, so the two are strongly mixed and a deperturbation treatment is needed. The line list gives rovibronic term values, allowed electric dipole transitions, Einstein coefficients and partition functions from a variational solution of the coupled-channel Schroedinger equations in Duo, built on the MRCI potential curves, spin-orbit and L-uncoupling matrix elements and permanent/transition dipole moments.
reference_short: Mitev, Taylor, Tennyson et al., ExoMol molecular line lists XLIII: rovibronic transitions of the close-lying X2Pi and A2Sigma+ states of NaO, MNRAS
notes: active_space_nel is left EMPTY: the paper specifies the active space by orbital symmetry counts only (7a1, 3b1, 3b2) and never states how many electrons are correlated in it, so the electron count would have to be inferred.

compound_name: carbon monoxide cation CO+, opacity of the X2Sigma+, A2Pi and B2Sigma+ states
point_group: C2v subgroup used in MOLPRO (the ion is C-infinity-v)
geometry_source: ab initio points computed over internuclear distances of 0.8-6 A; the potential curves were additionally refined against experimental data with a Modified-Morse (MMorse) function
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by multireference configuration interaction with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q); vibrational levels and spectroscopic constants from LEVEL
active_space_orbital_description: the outermost eight molecular orbitals, comprising 4 A1, 2 B1 and 2 B2 in C2v; they hold the three electrons of C+ in its 2s2p orbitals and the six electrons of O in its 2s2p orbitals, i.e. nine electrons in eight orbitals
active_space_protocol: a single CAS of nine electrons in the outermost eight orbitals (4 A1, 2 B1, 2 B2) used for all three electronic states, with the CASSCF orbitals taken into MRCI+Q
nroots_per_mult: 3 doublets: X2Sigma+, A2Pi, B2Sigma+
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy curves and electric dipole transition moments for the X2Sigma+, A2Pi and B2Sigma+ states of CO+ at MRCI+Q/aug-cc-pV6Z. The MMorse potentials refined against experiment agree closely with the computed curves, and the spectroscopic constants and vibrational levels match other theory and experiment. Combining the MMorse potentials with the ab initio transition dipole moments gives the opacity at 100 atm over 298-15000 K: above 5000 K line broadening blurs the boundaries between band systems, and above 10000 K this mixing dominates, which the authors present as the microscopic mechanism of high-temperature spectral degradation.
reference_short: An Siyaolitu, Wang, Xiao, Liu, Zhang & Yan, Opacities of the X2Sigma+, A2Pi and B2Sigma+ states of CO+, Acta Phys. Sin. 74, 123101 (2025)
notes: Chinese-language paper (Acta Physica Sinica); the active space is stated in the text as the eight outermost MOs (4A1, 2B1, 2B2) holding nine electrons.

compound_name: HOx fragments of the OH + HO2 -> O2 + H2O reaction: H2, O2, OH, HO2, H2O, O3 and the HOx supermolecule
formula: H2; O2; OH; HO2; H2O; O3; HOx (OH+HO2)
point_group: D2h subgroup for H2 and O2, C2v for OH, H2O and O3, Cs for HO2, C1 for the HOx complex
geometry_source: fragment ground-state geometries optimized at CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ; excited-state geometries and total energies then optimized at the MRCI/aug-cc-pVTZ level
method: internally contracted single- and double-excitation MRCI (ic-MRCISD) on a quadratically convergent MCSCF reference; single-reference CCSD(T) used first to optimize fragment geometries and to identify the active space
active_space_orbital_description: a full valence active space - all valence orbitals and all valence electrons - for every fragment
active_space_protocol: full valence space per fragment, quoted by the paper in reversed (n orbitals, m electrons) order: H2 (2o,2e); O2 (12o,8e); OH (5o,7e); HO2 (9o,13e); H2O (6o,8e); O3 (12o,18e); and the HOx complex (12o,16e)
electronic_structure_description: A multi-electronic-state model of OH + HO2 -> O2 + H2O built from extensive MRCI calculations, aimed at two experimental puzzles: an unusually deep, narrow well in the Arrhenius curve near 1100 K and a slightly negative temperature dependence between 200 and 500 K. Every fragment's ground state is dominated by a single configuration (reference coefficients 0.990-0.999, and 0.900 for the HOx complex), with the valence orbitals occupied and no inner-shell hole. State-to-state processes are classified by relative energy as primary (below 1.5 eV), secondary (1.5-4.5 eV), thirdhand (4.5-10 eV) or least (above 10 eV). The MRCI results are intended as the basis for a multi-dimensional quantum-dynamics potential energy surface.
reference_short: Zhang, Yu & Meng, A Multi-Electronic-State Model to Interpret the Apparent Anomalous Arrhenius Curve of OH + HO2 -> O2 + H2O
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active space is full-valence and therefore different for each of the seven fragments; every per-fragment pair is listed in active_space_protocol. Note that the paper writes its spaces as (no,me) = (n orbitals, m electrons), the reverse of the usual order, and says so explicitly in the Table I caption.

compound_name: lithium chloride anion LiCl-, spectroscopic and transition properties and laser-cooling feasibility
point_group: C2v subgroup used in MOLPRO (the anion is C-infinity-v)
geometry_source: potential energy curves scanned over internuclear distance; spectroscopic constants obtained by solving the radial Schroedinger equation with LEVEL 8.0
method: restricted Hartree-Fock, then CASSCF to generate the multireference wave function, then MRCI with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q); spin-orbit coupling included at the MRCI+Q level through the Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian
basis_set: def2-AQZVPP-JKFIT all-electron on Li; AWCVQZ-DK all-electron on Cl
active_space_orbital_description: eight molecular orbitals distributed (4, 2, 2, 0) over the C2v irreducible representations (a1, b1, b2, a2), spanning the Li 2s2p and Cl 3s3p shells
active_space_protocol: CAS(9,8) with orbitals (4,2,2,0) in C2v; Li 1s and Cl 2s2p are treated as closed shells kept doubly occupied in the CASSCF and all remaining electrons frozen, while in the MRCI+Q step the Li 1s and Cl 2s2p shells are correlated to capture core-valence effects, giving 17 electrons in the correlation treatment
nroots_per_mult: 5 Lambda-S states (X2Sigma+, A2Pi, B2Sigma+, 3 2Sigma+, 2 2Pi) and 7 Omega states
electronic_structure_description: All five computed Lambda-S states of LiCl- are bound. The X2Sigma+ ground state correlates with Li(2Sg) + Cl-(1Sg); A2Pi and B2Sigma+ with the second limit Li(2Pu) + Cl-(1Sg); 3 2Sigma+ and 2 2Pi with the third, Li-(1Sg) + Cl(2Pu). The ground-state equilibrium bond length is 2.1352 A, and the computed electron affinity of LiCl is 0.4392 eV, 0.153 eV below the experimental value of Miller et al. Franck-Condon factors, Einstein coefficients and spontaneous radiative lifetimes for the A2Pi - X2Sigma+ transition are reported and used to assess building a quasi-cycling transition for laser cooling of the anion.
reference_short: Guo, Tan, Yuan, Zhang & Wan, Spectroscopic and transition properties of the LiCl- anion, Acta Phys. Sin. 71, 043101 (2022)
notes: Chinese-language paper (Acta Physica Sinica).

compound_name: cysteine-model / flavin fragments of the phototropin LOV-domain photocycle: an educt model with an HSCH3 fragment and an intermediate model with an SCH3 fragment
formula: HSCH3 and SCH3 cysteine models with the flavin chromophore
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of the neutral fragments were used for the separated arrangements and the ground-state geometry for the adduct; the single-point singlet and triplet calculations were then run without further geometry optimization
method: CASSCF(n,n) with n = 2, 4, 8 for the singlet ground state S0 and the lowest triplet T1; compared against B3LYP/UB3LYP (with wave-function stability checks) and against DFT-MRCI; Mulliken charges and spin densities computed from the CI expansion coefficients
basis_set: not stated for the CASSCF step in the text read; the accompanying DFT work used 6-31G* and the DFT-MRCI used SV(P)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(n,n) with equal numbers of active electrons and active orbitals, n = 2, 4 and 8
active_space_protocol: three nested CASSCF(n,n) spaces with n = 2, 4 and 8, applied to both the singlet ground state and the lowest triplet of both the educt and the intermediate model, to test how the computed charge and spin distribution converges with active space size
electronic_structure_description: In the singlet ground state S0, RB3LYP gives stable wave functions for the educt model and the adduct form, but for the intermediate form only a symmetry-broken UB3LYP solution is stable: it puts a spin density of -0.829 on the SCH3 fragment with <S2> = 0.8144 instead of zero. All three CASSCF(n,n) treatments and DFT-MRCI instead give a clean closed-shell singlet with essentially zero spin density (charges of about -0.008 on the fragment), so the ionic character of the intermediate is much smaller in the multideterminant treatments than UB3LYP suggests. In the lowest triplet T1 the picture is consistent across methods: <S2> is exactly 2 in all three CASSCF spaces and the spin density on the SCH3 fragment of the intermediate is about +0.998, i.e. one unpaired electron localized on the cysteine model.
reference_short: Quantenchemische und molekulardynamische Untersuchungen zum Reaktionsmechanismus von Phototropin, Dissertation, Universitaet Regensburg
notes: German-language doctoral thesis. nel/norb are left EMPTY because the CASSCF spaces are a deliberate series - (2,2), (4,4) and (8,8) - used side by side rather than one chosen space; all three are recorded in active_space_protocol. The basis set for the CASSCF step is not stated in the text read, so it is described rather than asserted.

compound_name: gas-phase bimolecular collisions of halocarbon dications CX2+ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) with noble gas atoms He, Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe: charge-transfer potential energy curves
formula: CF2+ + He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe; CCl2+ + Ar/Kr/Xe; CBr2+ + Ar/Kr/Xe; CI2+ + Ar/Kr/Xe
point_group: C2v (the Abelian subgroup Molpro requires for a collinear collision; Sigma+ -> A1, Sigma- -> A2, Pi -> B1+B2, Delta -> A1+A2)
geometry_source: potential energy curves scanned along the collinear collision coordinate; fragment reference data from CCSD(T) and MP4 calculations
method: state-averaged CASSCF (SA-CASSCF) followed by multireference configuration interaction with the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q); the resulting curves feed Landau-Zener charge-transfer cross sections through the LZRATE program
software: Molpro 2010 (LZRATE for the Landau-Zener cross sections)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVnZ (n = T, Q, 5) of Dunning and Woon for the light atoms; aug-cc-pVnZ-PP (n = T, Q) of Peterson for Kr, Xe and I
relativistic_treatment: relativistic pseudopotentials ECP10MDF (Kr, replacing the 1s-2p core of 10 electrons) and ECP28MDF (Xe and I, replacing the 1s-3d core of 28 electrons), optimized in Dirac-Hartree-Fock calculations
active_space_orbital_description: active spaces quoted as C2v orbital partitions (a1, b1, b2, a2), built from the carbon 2s2p valence orbitals, the halogen valence np orbitals and the noble-gas outermost np (or He 1s) orbitals, sometimes with extra symmetry orbitals added
active_space_protocol: one space chosen per collision system, all quoted as (a1,b1,b2,a2) partitions: CF2+ + He (4,3,3,0), including C 2s2p, F 2p, He 1s and two extra orbitals; CF2+ + Ne (5,3,3,0) with 15 active electrons, adding the Ne 2p orbitals; CF2+ + Ar (5,3,3,0) with C and F 2s2p plus Ar 3p; CF2+ + Xe (3,3,3,0) with C 2p1, F 2p4 and Xe 5p6, the C and F 2s2 and Xe 5s2 kept closed; CCl2+ + Ar (4,3,3,0) with C 2s2p plus Cl 3p and Ar 3p; CCl2+ + Kr (4,3,3,0) with C 2s2p, Cl 3s3p and Kr 4p, the Kr 4s electrons kept out; CCl2+ + Xe (4,3,3,0), thirteen electrons in ten orbitals, with C 2s2p, Cl 3p and Xe 5p; CBr2+ + Ar (4,3,3,0) with C 2s2p, Br 4p and Ar 3p; CBr2+ + Kr (5,3,3,0) with C 2s2p and Br/Kr 4p plus one extra symmetry orbital; CBr2+ + Xe (4,4,4,0) with C 2p, Br 4p and Xe 5p plus three extra a1/b1/b2 orbitals, restricted to doublet states only; CI2+ + Ar (4,3,3,0) with C 2s2p, Ar 3p and I 5p; CI2+ + Kr (4,3,3,0); and CI2+ + Xe (4,3,3,0) with C 2s2p and I/Xe 5p
electronic_structure_description: For each CX2+ + noble-gas pair the Lambda-S electronic states correlating with the asymptotic fragments were determined in C2v, and MRCI potential energy curves were built for these collisional systems for the first time in the literature. Quality was judged by the agreement between the computed and experimental fragment separation energies at the dissociation limits, which is excellent, and by requiring continuous curves and no more than a 10 percent deviation from literature dissociation-channel energy differences. The curves give the crossing radius and coupling needed for Landau-Zener charge-transfer cross sections. For CBr2+ + Xe the B1/B2 (Pi) and A2 (Sigma-, Delta) curves could not be constructed reliably, so that system was restricted to doublet states.
reference_short: Belinassi, Reacoes bimoleculares em fase gasosa entre dications de halocarbonos CX2+ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) e atomos e moleculas pequenas, tese, Universidade de Sao Paulo
notes: Portuguese-language doctoral thesis (corrected version). nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active space is chosen separately for each of the thirteen collision systems and is specified as a C2v orbital partition rather than an (n,m) pair; only two systems state an electron count explicitly (15 electrons for CF2+ + Ne, 13 electrons in 10 orbitals for CCl2+ + Xe). Every partition is listed in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: one-dimensional model atoms - helium, beryllium and carbon - used to test the TD-RASSCF method for laser-driven many-electron dynamics
formula: 1D model He (Z = Ne = 2), Be (Z = Ne = 4) and C (Z = Ne = 6)
geometry_source: not applicable: these are one-dimensional model atoms defined by a soft-Coulomb one-body potential V(x) = -Z/sqrt(x^2+1) and a soft-Coulomb electron-electron repulsion v(x1,x2) = 1/sqrt((x1-x2)^2+1); ground states obtained by imaginary-time relaxation
method: time-dependent restricted-active-space self-consistent-field (TD-RASSCF) theory formulated from the time-dependent variational principle, in the -S, -D, -SD and -SDT truncations, compared against MCTDHF, TDHF and TDCIS
software: not stated in the text read
basis_set: a discrete variable representation: the box [-25, 25] discretized by NDVR = 256 quadrature points associated with Fourier basis functions, with the P- and Q-space orbital equations regularized by a constant epsilon = 1e-10
active_space_orbital_description: the single-particle Hilbert space is split into the inactive-core space P0, the two active spaces P1 and P2, and the virtual Q space, holding M0, M1 and M2 spatial orbitals; orbital excitations from P1 into P2 are allowed subject to the RAS truncation
active_space_protocol: a RAS partition (M0, M1, M2) with M = M0 + M1 + M2. For the ground-state benchmarks the partition is (0, Ne/2, M-2) with M swept over 3, 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20; MCTDHF corresponds to (0, M, 0) and TDHF is recovered at M = 2. Limiting cases in the same formalism: TD-CASSCF is M2 = 0 with M0 + M1 = M, and MCTDHF is M0 = M2 = 0 with M1 = M. A worked six-electron illustration uses (M0, M1, M2) = (1, 2, 5) for TD-RASSCF-SD, and Fig. 1 illustrates (1, 3, 4).
electronic_structure_description: For the 1D beryllium atom the Hartree-Fock ground-state energy is -6.739450 a.u.; TD-RASSCF-S converges to -6.773288, -D to -6.784534, -SD to -6.784698 and -SDT to -6.785075, against the MCTDHF value -6.785078, but at far lower configuration counts (73, 1603 and 1675 configurations at M = 20 for -S, -D and -SD versus 36100 for MCTDHF). TD-RASSCF-S converges once M2 >= M1. A state-resolved analysis of the high-order harmonic generation spectrum of the 1D beryllium atom shows that only single-orbital excitations matter below the cutoff, while single- and double-orbital excitations are essential beyond it - exactly where the single-active-electron approximation and TDCIS break down.
reference_short: Miyagi & Madsen, Time-dependent restricted-active-space self-consistent-field theory for laser-driven many-electron dynamics II: extended formulation and numerical analysis, Phys. Rev. A
notes: These are ONE-DIMENSIONAL MODEL ATOMS with soft-Coulomb interactions, not three-dimensional atoms, and the orbitals live on a DVR grid rather than in an AO basis - the row must not be read as real atomic structure data. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the method is RAS, not CAS, and the partition (M0, M1, M2) is swept systematically rather than fixed, so it does not reduce to a single (n,m) pair.

compound_name: dimethyl disulfide (DMDS), sulfur K-edge X-ray absorption
geometry_source: geometries optimized at MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ with very tight convergence criteria in Gaussian09; vibrational frequencies confirm true minima
method: restricted active space self-consistent field (RASSCF) with no symmetry imposed for the sulfur-1s X-ray absorption transitions, improved by multi-state RASPT2 (MS-RASPT2); single-state CASPT2 for the ground-state energy with an IPEA shift of 0.25 Hartree and an imaginary shift of 0.3 Hartree; transition dipole moments from the RASSI module
active_space_orbital_description: 14 electrons distributed over 12 orbitals, split into RAS2, which holds all orbitals without occupational constraints, and RAS3, which holds the two sulfur 1s core electrons with at most single occupancy
active_space_protocol: RAS with two subspaces: RAS2 unconstrained, and RAS3 restricted to at most one electron so that configurations with a doubly filled sulfur-1s core orbital are suppressed; this grouping keeps irrelevant low-energy configurations out of the core-excitation calculation. All computed transition energies were shifted by -11.30 eV so that the lowest calculated DMDS transitions match the experimental DMDS spectrum.
electronic_structure_description: The static sulfur K-edge absorption spectrum of DMDS in cyclohexane shows two major transitions at 2471.6 and 2473.1 eV plus weaker features. DMDS is the reference species against which the whole calculated series is energy-calibrated. Earlier resonance Raman work at 267 nm and excited-singlet potential energy surfaces (Rinker et al.) had concluded that excitation into the lowest singlet excited state favours C-S cleavage because of a barrier to S-S dissociation, while the second excited singlet reverses that preference; the C-S bond (235 kJ/mol, 2.4 eV) is weaker than the S-S bond (280 kJ/mol, 2.9 eV).
reference_short: Ochmann, Hussain, von Ahnen et al., UV-photochemistry of the disulfide bond: evolution of early photoproducts from picosecond X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the sulfur K-edge
notes: ground_state_mult is left EMPTY: the paper never states the spin multiplicity of any computed species. The RAS partition is unusual in that the paper calls the core-hole-restricted subspace RAS3 rather than RAS1; recorded as written.

compound_name: methylperthiyl radical, a photoproduct of dimethyl disulfide, sulfur K-edge X-ray absorption
geometry_source: geometries optimized at MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ with very tight convergence criteria in Gaussian09; vibrational frequencies confirm true minima
method: restricted active space self-consistent field (RASSCF) with no symmetry imposed for the sulfur-1s X-ray absorption transitions, improved by multi-state RASPT2 (MS-RASPT2); single-state CASPT2 for the ground-state energy with an IPEA shift of 0.25 Hartree and an imaginary shift of 0.3 Hartree; transition dipole moments from the RASSI module
active_space_orbital_description: the same active space as dimethyl disulfide: 14 electrons distributed over 12 orbitals, split into an unconstrained RAS2 and a RAS3 holding the two sulfur 1s core electrons with at most single occupancy
active_space_protocol: RAS with two subspaces: RAS2 unconstrained, RAS3 restricted to at most one electron to suppress doubly filled sulfur-1s configurations; transition energies shifted by -11.30 eV to align the DMDS reference with experiment
electronic_structure_description: One of the early photoproducts tracked by picosecond sulfur K-edge X-ray absorption after UV excitation of the disulfide bond; its simulated sulfur-1s transitions use the same 14-electron, 12-orbital RAS space as the parent DMDS.
reference_short: Ochmann, Hussain, von Ahnen et al., UV-photochemistry of the disulfide bond: evolution of early photoproducts from picosecond X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the sulfur K-edge
notes: ground_state_mult is left EMPTY: this is an open-shell radical and the paper never states its multiplicity - the value must not be inherited from the closed-shell parent DMDS.

compound_name: methylthiyl radical, a photoproduct of dimethyl disulfide, sulfur K-edge X-ray absorption
geometry_source: geometries optimized at MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ with very tight convergence criteria in Gaussian09; vibrational frequencies confirm true minima
method: restricted active space self-consistent field (RASSCF) with no symmetry imposed for the sulfur-1s X-ray absorption transitions, improved by multi-state RASPT2 (MS-RASPT2); single-state CASPT2 for the ground-state energy with an IPEA shift of 0.25 Hartree and an imaginary shift of 0.3 Hartree; transition dipole moments from the RASSI module
active_space_orbital_description: a reduced space of 11 electrons in 11 orbitals, again split into an unconstrained RAS2 and a RAS3 holding the sulfur 1s core with at most single occupancy
active_space_protocol: RAS with two subspaces as for the other species, but reduced to 11 electrons in 11 orbitals for this smaller radical; transition energies shifted by -11.30 eV to align the DMDS reference with experiment
electronic_structure_description: The other early photoproduct of UV-excited dimethyl disulfide followed by picosecond sulfur K-edge X-ray absorption; its smaller size allowed the active space to be cut to 11 electrons in 11 orbitals.
reference_short: Ochmann, Hussain, von Ahnen et al., UV-photochemistry of the disulfide bond: evolution of early photoproducts from picosecond X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the sulfur K-edge
notes: ground_state_mult is left EMPTY: this is an open-shell radical and the paper never states its multiplicity.

compound_name: bacteriochlorophyll a monomers of the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of Rhodoblastus acidophilus: site energies and transition dipole moments
ligand_set: the bacteriochlorin macrocycle with its acetyl substituent; the C2-C3 torsion regulates how much of the C3-O4 double bond pi system joins the macrocycle conjugation
geometry_source: crystal structure of the LH2 complex from Rhodoblastus acidophilus (formerly Rhodopseudomonas acidophila), with hydrogen positions preoptimized at the PM6 level in Gaussian09
method: state-averaged RASSCF followed by multi-state RASPT2 (MS-RASPT2), the RAS analogue of MS-CASPT2; a single-point CC2 calculation in TURBOMOLE with cc-pVDZ was used alongside
software: MOLCAS 7.8, using developer-version features that split each MS-RASPT2 job across two CPUs (Gaussian09 for PM6, TURBOMOLE for CC2)
basis_set: ANO-RCC of double-zeta quality, with the ANO-RCC library and the frozen-core approximation; 1s orbitals of all non-hydrogen atoms plus the Mg 2s and 2p orbitals frozen in all RASSCF and MS-RASPT2 steps
active_space_orbital_description: 26 active electrons in 25 pi and pi* orbitals, partitioned into 11 RAS1, 4 RAS2 and 10 RAS3 orbitals
active_space_protocol: the final active space, called AS10, is a RAS space of 26 electrons in 25 pi/pi* orbitals divided as RAS1 = 11, RAS2 = 4, RAS3 = 10, with up to 3 holes in RAS1 and 3 excitations into RAS3; the full selection procedure is given in the Supporting Information. The 4 RAS2 orbitals are what make the excitation energies reliable and are reminiscent of the classical four-orbital model. Each MS-RASPT2 state with AS10 and 300 virtual orbitals took about three weeks on one processor.
electronic_structure_description: MS-RASPT2/RASSCF site energies and transition dipole moments were computed for every bacteriochlorophyll unit in LH2. The excitation energies vary from monomer to monomer, and the variation is governed by two structural handles: the curvature of the macrocycle ring and the dihedral angle of the acetyl moiety. Increasing the curvature raises the ground-state energy. The LH2 BChl units are almost planar in their macrocycle portion apart from the acetyl group. The resulting numbers are offered as benchmark parameters that remove free variables from the fitting of ultrafast spectroscopy of LH2 antenna systems.
reference_short: Anda, Hansen et al., Multireference excitation energies for bacteriochlorophylls A within light harvesting system 2, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2016, 12, 1305-1313
notes: RAS rather than CAS, but the paper states the total explicitly as 26 active electrons in 25 active orbitals, so nel/norb carry that total and the RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 partition with its 3 holes and 3 excitations is in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: one-dimensional model atoms - helium, beryllium and carbon - used to introduce the TD-RASSCF-S method for many-electron dynamics
formula: 1D model He, Be and C atoms
geometry_source: not applicable: one-dimensional model atoms with a soft-Coulomb nuclear potential and soft-Coulomb electron-electron repulsion, driven by an intense laser field
method: time-dependent restricted-active-space self-consistent-field singles (TD-RASSCF-S) method, compared against TDCIS, TDHF and MCTDHF
software: not stated in the text read
basis_set: a grid/DVR representation rather than an atomic orbital basis
active_space_orbital_description: the orbital space is partitioned as (M0, M1, M2) - inactive core P0, and the two active spaces P1 and P2 - with only single orbital excitations from P1 into P2 retained in the -S truncation
active_space_protocol: RAS partitions of the form (M0, M1, M2); the beryllium electron-density snapshots use TD-RASSCF-S with M = 4 and partition (0, 2, 2), benchmarked against MCTDHF with M = 20. For helium, beryllium and carbon the reference MCTDHF calculations used M = 8 and larger.
electronic_structure_description: Snapshots of the electron density rho(x,t) in the 1D beryllium atom at t = 0, T/2 and T, computed with TDCIS, TD-RASSCF-S (M = 4, partition (0,2,2)) and MCTDHF (M = 20), show where the singles-only description holds and where it fails. High-order harmonic spectra are obtained from the Fourier transform of the dipole acceleration.
reference_short: Miyagi & Madsen, Time-dependent restricted-active-space self-consistent-field singles method for many-electron dynamics, Phys. Rev. A
notes: Companion paper to the extended TD-RASSCF formulation (arXiv:1405.5380). These are ONE-DIMENSIONAL MODEL ATOMS with soft-Coulomb interactions on a grid, not three-dimensional atoms in an AO basis - the row must not be read as real atomic structure data. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the method is RAS with a swept (M0, M1, M2) partition, which does not reduce to a single (n,m) pair.

compound_name: uranyl in three environments: bare [UO2]2+, [UO2Cl4]2- and Cs2UO2Cl4 - oxygen K-edge XANES, covalency and environmental effects
ligand_set: two axial oxo ligands in every model; four equatorial chlorides in [UO2Cl4]2-; in the Cs2UO2Cl4 model the eight caesium counterions are represented by dummy atoms carrying fractional +1/4 au point charges to keep the system neutral
geometry_source: bond lengths and point-charge positions relative to uranium taken from the XRD structure of Cs2UO2Cl4, with minimal adjustments to retain overall D2h symmetry
method: RASSCF for the ground state and the core-excited states, with the core hole enforced by the RAS constraints; covalency quantified from the resulting wave functions
basis_set: all-electron relativistic ANO-RCC of TZVP quality: U (9s8p6d4f2g) with the higher angular momentum h functions removed to permit the subsequent analysis, O (4s3p2d1f), Cl (5s4p2d1f)
active_space_orbital_description: RAS1 holds the two linear combinations of the oxygen 1s orbitals (1s-sigma_g and 1s-sigma_u); RAS2 holds the six bonding orbitals (2 x pi_g, 2 x pi_u, sigma_g, sigma_u); RAS3 holds six antibonding orbitals plus the four empty non-bonding 5f orbitals (2 x 5f-delta and 2 x 5f-phi), ten in all
active_space_protocol: two schemes in the RASSCF(n,l,m;i,j,k) notation of Sauri et al.: RASSCF(16,1,1;2,6,10), called RAS(S), and RASSCF(16,1,2;2,6,10), called RAS(SD). Both enforce a single core hole across RAS1 and differ in whether one or two electrons may occupy RAS3. In RAS(S) the only electrons reaching RAS3 come directly from the oxygen 1s orbitals; in RAS(SD) they can also come from the RAS2 bonding orbitals. Truncating the CI expansion this way controls how much electron correlation is captured and keeps the cost manageable.
electronic_structure_description: All core-excited states accommodate at least one electron in RAS3 arriving directly from the oxygen 1s orbitals in RAS1, and in the RAS(SD) scheme additionally from the RAS2 bonding orbitals. In every O K-edge simulation, peak 1 is assigned to two intense transitions into the orbitals that are vacant in the ground state but populated on core excitation. Comparing the bare uranyl dication with the tetrachloride and with the full Cs2UO2Cl4 model isolates how the equatorial ligands and the crystalline environment change both the spectrum and the measured covalency.
reference_short: Stanistreet-Welsh & Kerridge, Quantifying Covalency and Environmental Effects in RASSCF-Simulated O K-Edge XANES of Uranyl, Inorg. Chem. 2024, 63, 15115-15126
notes: One row for all three environment models because they share one active space definition, stated once for the uranyl unit. norb = 18 is the sum the paper itself gives as the RAS partition 2 + 6 + 10; nel = 16 is stated directly in the RASSCF(16,...) label. d_electron_count is left empty: U(VI) uranyl is formally 5f0 6d0 and the paper describes the bonding in terms of the oxo sigma/pi manifold rather than a d count.

compound_name: perylene bisimide dyes: ultrafast nonlinear spectroscopy simulated and compared with experiment
geometry_source: geometries and numerical frequencies computed at the same level of theory as the electronic structure
method: RASSCF followed by RASPT2, in a state-averaged 10-root protocol, used to feed simulations of linear and nonlinear (transient absorption / 2D electronic) spectra
basis_set: ANO-L-VDZP for the RASSCF/RASPT2 computations (6-311G** used elsewhere in the work)
active_space_orbital_description: 20 electrons in 20 orbitals for both compounds, arranged in a RAS protocol allowing up to quadruple excitations
active_space_protocol: SA-10-RASSCF(20,4,4;10,0,10): 20 active electrons, up to 4 holes in RAS1 and up to 4 electrons in RAS3, with 10 RAS1 orbitals, 0 RAS2 orbitals and 10 RAS3 orbitals, averaged over 10 states; the same 20-electron, 20-orbital space was used for both compounds
electronic_structure_description: In silico ultrafast nonlinear spectroscopy of perylene bisimide dyes computed at the RASSCF/RASPT2 level and compared directly against measured spectra; the RAS protocol with up to quadruple excitations out of a 20-electron, 20-orbital space is what makes the doubly excited character accessible to the simulation.
reference_short: In Silico Ultrafast Nonlinear Spectroscopy Meets Experiments: The Case of Perylene Bisimide Dyes, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2021
notes: RAS with an empty RAS2 (0 orbitals), so the whole space is the 10 + 10 RAS1/RAS3 split; nel/norb carry the total the paper states as 20 electrons in 20 orbitals.

geometry_source: on-the-fly potential energy surfaces built by Shepard interpolation of RASSCF energies rotated into a diabatic picture during direct-dynamics propagation; cuts computed along the O-H stretch and the C-O stretch + bend modes
method: RASSCF potential energy surfaces computed on the fly for direct-dynamics variational multiconfigurational Gaussian (DD-vMCG) quantum dynamics; nuclear gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors taken at the CASSCF level because RASSCF analytical derivatives are unavailable; benchmarked against EOM-CCSD, CASSCF(12,12) and CASPT2(12,12)
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 12 orbitals in total, including the sigma and sigma* orbitals of both the C-O and O-H bonds and the Rydberg 3s and 3px orbitals that are the LUMO and LUMO+1
active_space_protocol: RASSCF(12,2+8+2)[1,1] in the notation RASSCF(n, mI+mII+mIII)[h,e]: 12 active electrons, 2 RAS1 orbitals with at most 1 hole, 8 RAS2 orbitals in which all configurations are generated, and 2 RAS3 orbitals with at most 1 electron. For the gradients and nonadiabatic couplings the space is reduced to the CASSCF level, namely the 8 RAS2 orbitals with 8 active electrons. Reference calculations used CASSCF(12,12) and CASPT2(12,12).
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies of the lowest states of methanol: S1 is the 2py(O) -> 3s Rydberg transition at 6.70 eV (EOM-CCSD), 6.32 eV (CASSCF), 6.80 eV (CASPT2) and 6.33 eV (RASSCF), against 6.76 eV experimentally; S2 is 2py(O) -> 3px Rydberg at 7.90, 7.49, 7.95 and 7.51 eV against 7.73 eV experimentally; S3 is sigma(OH) -> 3s Rydberg at 8.73 eV (EOM-CCSD). RASSCF(12,2+8+2)[1,1] proved remarkably stable along cuts through the potential energy surface in the two key modes, which is why it was chosen for the direct dynamics. Simulations at several initial excitation energies probe how the O-H versus C-O branching ratio depends on the electronic state prepared; trajectories ran until the wave-function norm squared fell to zero (full dissociation) or 100 fs.
reference_short: Cigrang & Worth, Modeling Photodissociation: Quantum Dynamics Simulations of Methanol, J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 7546-7557 (Massimo Olivucci Festschrift)
notes: nel/norb carry the total the paper states, 12 electrons in 12 orbitals; the RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 split 2+8+2 with [1,1] hole/electron limits and the reduced CASSCF(8,8) used for gradients are both in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: atomic beryllium, double-ionization dynamics in intense light fields (TD-RASSCF with space partition)
geometry_source: not applicable: a single atom in a radial box of rmax = 200 a.u., driven by linearly polarized light fields; the ground state obtained by imaginary-time relaxation
method: time-dependent restricted-active-space self-consistent-field with space partition (TD-RASSCF-SP), which splits the radial coordinate into an inner region treated with strong correlation and an outer region for the escaping photoelectrons; equations of motion derived both from an FEDVR-based formalism with additional time-independent orbitals and from a more general Bloch-operator (R-matrix-like) formalism, the former being the practical one
software: not stated in the text read
basis_set: finite-element discrete variable representation (FEDVR): NDVR = 10 per finite element, total radius rmax = 200, with N_fe(inner) + N_fe(outer) = 202 elements in the TD-RASSCF-SP calculations and N_fe = 200 in the reference calculations; orbital equations regularized with a constant 1e-10
active_space_orbital_description: the orbital space is partitioned in space rather than only in occupation: M-hat orbitals confined to the inner region and M-check orbitals for the outer region, with the excitation level Gamma limiting how many electrons may be in the outer region
active_space_protocol: TD-RASSCF-SP(M-hat, M-check; Gamma; r-Sigma) - the ground-state and dynamics illustrations use M-hat = 6, M-check = 3, Gamma = 2 and the partition radius r-Sigma = 30 a.u. M-hat must be large to capture the strong many-electron correlation near the nucleus, while M-check can be much smaller because the correlation between the two outgoing photoelectrons is weaker.
electronic_structure_description: Orbitals and one- and two-dimensional radial electron densities of ground-state beryllium computed with TD-RASSCF-SP(M-hat = 6, M-check = 3; Gamma = 2; r-Sigma = 30) join smoothly across the partition radius r = 30 even though each orbital individually looks independent of the others; the formalism guarantees the continuity. The method is then applied to double ionization in intense fields, where the two-dimensional radial density resolves the correlated emission of the two photoelectrons, at much lower cost than fully correlated multiconfigurational approaches.
reference_short: Miyagi & Madsen, Time-dependent restricted-active-space self-consistent-field theory with space partition, Phys. Rev. A 95, 023415 (2017)
notes: Third paper of the TD-RASSCF series, and unlike the earlier two this one treats a REAL three-dimensional beryllium atom on an FEDVR radial grid rather than a 1D model atom. active_space_norb is left EMPTY: the space is partitioned spatially into M-hat inner and M-check outer orbitals with an excitation limit Gamma, which does not reduce to a single orbital count; nel = 4 is the full electron count of the atom, all of which are active.

compound_name: 6-selenoguanine (6SeGua), photophysics of the selenium-substituted guanine nucleobase, compared with 6-thioguanine (6tGua) and natural guanine
geometry_source: minima and intersection structures optimized directly at the MS-CASPT2 level; linear interpolation in internal coordinates (LIIC) paths connecting them
method: multistate complete active space second-order perturbation theory (MS-CASPT2) for optimizations and single-point refinements, with IPEA set to zero and an imaginary shift of 0.2; two-electron integrals handled by Cholesky decomposition with on-the-fly unbiased auxiliary basis sets; spin-orbit couplings from the atomic mean-field approximation
basis_set: cc-pVDZ (optimizations) and cc-pVTZ (energy refinements) on C, N and H; aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ respectively on selenium; the spin-orbit calculations use the single-point basis
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 10 orbitals: 7 pi and pi* orbitals, 2 sigma and sigma* orbitals, and 1 n orbital of the selenium atom
active_space_protocol: a single 12-electron, 10-orbital space for all MS-CASPT2 calculations; three and five roots are used in the optimizations and single-point refinements, with equal weights. IPEA is set to zero because the tests reproduce the experimental S2 vertical excitation better that way (3.39 eV computed vs 3.47 eV experimental).
nroots_per_mult: 3 and 5, depending on the calculation
electronic_structure_description: Two excited-state relaxation paths leave the bright S2(1pipi*) state: S2(1pipi*) -> S1(1npi*) -> T1(3pipi*), and S2(1pipi*) -> S1(1npi*) -> T2(3npi*) -> T1(3pipi*). The very different measured T1 decay rates to S0 - 1.7 ns for 6SeGua against 1420 ns for 6tGua - are attributed primarily to the much larger T1/S0 spin-orbit coupling in the selenium compound rather than to the barriers, which are similar (0.11 eV in 6SeGua vs 0.16 eV in 6tGua). The S0 state of 6SeGua has pronounced multireference character with a significant open-shell configuration, which explains its longer C7-C11 bond compared with natural guanine and 6tGua.
reference_short: Fang, Peng, Fang, Fang & Cui, MS-CASPT2 Studies on the Photophysics of Selenium-Substituted Guanine Nucleobase, ACS Omega 2019
notes: 6tGua and natural guanine appear only as comparison values from experiment and earlier work, so they get no rows of their own.

compound_name: all-trans polyenes C2nH2n+2 (n = 4-12): longitudinal static second hyperpolarizability
geometry_source: geometries optimized at B3LYP/cc-pVDZ
method: internally contracted CASPT2 with the density matrix renormalization group as active space solver (DMRG-CASPT2), following Kurashige and Yanai; the 4-RDM contraction with the generalized Fock matrix is obtained from 3-RDMs of excited matrix product states, avoiding explicit 4-RDM construction; DMRG-SCF supplies the reference and RHF/MP2 are the single-reference comparison
active_space_orbital_description: (2n, 2n) active spaces - the full pi system of each polyene, 2n electrons in 2n orbitals for C2nH2n+2
active_space_protocol: one (2n,2n) space per chain length, so (8,8) for n = 4 through (24,24) for n = 12; the active spaces are fully converged, and the 3-RDM wall time scales as L^6.02 with L = 2n at a reduced virtual DMRG bond dimension D = 1000
electronic_structure_description: For the longitudinal static second hyperpolarizability of all-trans polyenes, DMRG-SCF and DMRG-CASPT2 give substantially lower values, and a substantially weaker growth with chain length, than RHF and MP2 respectively - the single-reference methods overestimate both the magnitude and the scaling. The work demonstrates that internally contracted CASPT2 can be run on active spaces well beyond conventional CASSCF by taking the required 4-RDM contraction from 3-RDMs of excited matrix product states.
reference_short: Wouters, Van Speybroeck & Van Neck, DMRG-CASPT2 study of the longitudinal static second hyperpolarizability of all-trans polyenes, J. Chem. Phys.
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active space is (2n,2n) and therefore different for each of the nine chain lengths studied; the rule is recorded in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: FCI benchmark set for the IPEA dilemma: first-row hydrides HLi, HBe, HB, HC, HN, HO, HF, the homodiatomics Li2, B2, C2, N2, and the triatomics H2O and CH2
formula: LiH; BeH; BH; CH; NH; OH; HF; Li2; B2; C2; N2; H2O; CH2
point_group: D2h for the homodiatomics, C2v for the first-row hydrides, full C2v for H2O and CH2
geometry_source: equilibrium distances of the diatomics from the NIST database; triatomic geometries from previous FCI studies; all geometries tabulated in Table S3 of the ESI
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2, run twice - once with the standard unshifted zeroth-order Hamiltonian (NOIPEA) and once with the IPEA-shifted Hamiltonian at the recommended eps = 0.25 a.u. - and compared against full CI
software: MOLCAS 8.0.15-05-24 for CASSCF/CASPT2; MOLPRO 2012.1 for the FCI reference
basis_set: 6-31G and 6-311G, the largest affordable for the FCI reference
active_space_orbital_description: all valence orbitals and electrons: the hydrogen 1s shell together with the 2s and 2p shells of every first-row atom
active_space_protocol: a full valence active space for every molecule, so the size varies from system to system; the frozen-core approximation was used for the homodiatomics and for H2O and CH2, matching the FCI treatment. Restricted Hartree-Fock starting orbitals for closed-shell ground states and unrestricted for open-shell ones, chosen to match the FCI starting orbitals. State-averaged CASSCF with equal weights plus MS-CASPT2 wherever several states of the same symmetry were computed.
electronic_structure_description: 137 electronic states of 13 di- and triatomic molecules were computed at CASSCF, CASPT2 and FCI. The CASPT2 total energies are very close to FCI even though CASPT2 is not variational, so the method reproduces FCI almost quantitatively for this set - which makes it a clean test bed for what the IPEA shift actually does, free of the vibronic and intermolecular effects that contaminate comparisons against experiment.
reference_short: Zobel, Nogueira & Gonzalez, The IPEA dilemma in CASPT2, Chem. Sci. 2017
