notes: First of two data sets in this paper; the second, the Thiel benchmark set, is row -b. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the space is full valence and so differs for every molecule.

compound_name: Thiel benchmark set of organic molecules: ground and excited states recomputed with and without the IPEA shift
formula: the organic molecules of the Thiel benchmark set
geometry_source: the same MP2/6-31G*-optimized geometries as the original Thiel-set publication
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with both the NOIPEA and the IPEA-shifted (eps = 0.25 a.u.) zeroth-order Hamiltonians, including the MS-CASPT2 variant and level shifts where the original work used them
basis_set: TZVP, as in the original publication
active_space_orbital_description: the same active spaces as the original Thiel-set publication; not restated in this paper
active_space_protocol: all CASSCF/CASPT2 parameters were taken over unchanged from the original Thiel-set study - the active spaces, the number of states per irreducible representation, the level shift for some molecules, and the use of the multi-state variant - so that only the IPEA shift differs between the two sets of results
electronic_structure_description: A literature survey of 356 excited states of 53 organic molecules computed with CASPT2 before the IPEA shift was introduced gives a mean signed error against experiment of only -0.02 eV; restricting to states where both experiment and theory are gas phase (295 states) leaves -0.03 eV. The authors' own IPEA-shifted MS-CASPT2 calculations reproduce nearly all the excitation energies of the original Thiel-set study, and the discussion is then based exclusively on their own consistent numbers. The expectation from the shift's own rationale - that closed-shell ground states with singly excited states should be underestimated by 0.13-0.26 eV - is not borne out by the survey.
reference_short: Zobel, Nogueira & Gonzalez, The IPEA dilemma in CASPT2, Chem. Sci. 2017
notes: Second data set of the same paper; the di-/triatomic FCI benchmark is row -a. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active spaces are inherited from the original Thiel-set publication and are not restated here, so they differ per molecule and cannot be read off this paper.

compound_name: ethene, used as the RASSCF demonstration example in a methods exposition on RASSCF, RASSI and CASPT2 for small molecules of astrophysical interest
geometry_source: not stated in the text read
method: RASSCF compared against a series of CASSCF calculations of growing active space, judged by the number of CSFs, the total energy, the expectation value of the sum of r^2 and the CPU time
basis_set: ANO-type atomic natural orbital basis (the text discusses ANO general contractions but does not name the specific set for this demonstration)
active_space_orbital_description: a RAS partition written RAS(5,2,22) - 5 RAS1, 2 RAS2 and 22 RAS3 orbitals, 29 active orbitals in all
active_space_protocol: the demonstration contrasts a sequence of CAS spaces of growing pi-orbital count against a single RAS(5,2,22) calculation with 29 active orbitals: the CAS sequence generates 28848, 92406, 268800 and 716523 CSFs for energies of -77.8993, -77.9239, -77.9341 and -77.9433 a.u., while the RAS calculation needs only 4704 CSFs and gives -78.0484 a.u. in 68 s of CPU. The exposition warns that the much lower RAS total energy is a dangerous quality measure here, and points to the expectation value of the sum of r^2 (22.8, 23.4, 23.0, 21.9 and 20.8 a.u. respectively) as the diagnostic that matters, because the orbitals of the ionic state come out too diffuse unless enough dynamic correlation is included.
electronic_structure_description: The illustrated state is the highly ionic V state of ethene, dominated by two valence-bond structures each with a positive and a negative methylene ion - a prototype case where the CASSCF orbitals come out too diffuse without dynamic correlation, and where the number of CSFs grows explosively in an ill-advised attempt to fix that by enlarging the CAS. The chapter notes that with twelve active electrons the practical CASSCF limit is around twelve or thirteen active orbitals, giving 226512 and 736164 singlet CSFs.
reference_short: Malmqvist, The RASSCF, RASSI, and CASPT2 Methods Used on Small Molecules of Astrophysical Interest
notes: Largely a methods exposition rather than a research paper; the one calculation it presents in full is the ethene RASSCF demonstration of Table 1, which is recorded here. active_space_nel is left EMPTY: the OCR of the CAS labels in Table 1 is mangled (they read as 'CAS (10<r,27r)' for what must be CAS(10 sigma, 2 pi) and so on), and the RAS row gives only the orbital partition, so no electron count can be read reliably. norb = 29 is stated in words as 'a RASSCF calculation with 29 active orbitals' and matches the 5 + 2 + 22 partition.

compound_name: lithium fluoride LiF, the covalent-ionic avoided crossing at long bond length
point_group: C2v subgroup used in MOLPRO (the molecule is C-infinity-v)
geometry_source: potential energy curves scanned along the bond length out past the avoided crossing near 5.3 A
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2): Granovsky's extended multireference quasi-degenerate perturbation theory combined with internally contracted MS-CASPT2, with analytical nuclear gradients; the first-order wave function is expanded in the union of the internally contracted basis functions of all reference functions, making the theory invariant to unitary rotations among them
active_space_orbital_description: six electrons in three a1, two b2 and two b1 orbitals, with the frozen-core approximation
active_space_protocol: a single space of six electrons in seven orbitals (3 a1 + 2 b2 + 2 b1) with frozen core, used for MS-CASPT2, XMS-CASPT2 and the MRCI comparison alike
electronic_structure_description: The covalent-ionic avoided crossing of LiF at long range is a notorious test for quasi-degenerate perturbation theories. The MS-CASPT2 curve carries an artificial hump of about 3 mEh around 5.3 A; the XMS-CASPT2 curves have no such hump and run almost parallel to the MRCI curves (computed without the Davidson correction) throughout the long-range region. The improvement of XMS-CASPT2 over MS-CASPT2 is unambiguous here.
reference_short: Shiozaki, Gyorffy, Celani & Werner, Communication: Extended multi-state complete active space second-order perturbation theory - energy and nuclear gradients, J. Chem. Phys. 135, 081106 (2011)
notes: One of two demonstration systems in this communication; pyrrole is row -b.

compound_name: pyrrole, low-lying Rydberg excited states in 1B1 and 1A2 symmetry
geometry_source: computational details follow the authors' earlier state-specific CASPT2 study of pyrrole; vertical and adiabatic excitation energies computed
method: extended multi-state CASPT2 (XMS-CASPT2): Granovsky's extended multireference quasi-degenerate perturbation theory combined with internally contracted MS-CASPT2, with analytical nuclear gradients; the first-order wave function is expanded in the union of the internally contracted basis functions of all reference functions, making the theory invariant to unitary rotations among them
basis_set: Dunning aug-cc-pVTZ, without d functions on hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: only pi electrons are active; the active orbitals are 10-11 a1, 1-3 b1, 7 b2 and 1-2 a2, eight orbitals in all
active_space_protocol: a pi-only active space of the orbitals 10-11a1, 1-3b1, 7b2 and 1-2a2; the CASSCF state averaging covers 1 1A1 and 1-2 1B1 among others
nroots_per_mult: the lowest two states in each of the 1B1 and 1A2 symmetries
electronic_structure_description: The first and second Rydberg excited states of 1B1 symmetry mix strongly, which is exactly what a quasi-degenerate treatment has to handle. Vertical excitation energies (eV): 1 1B1 (2b1 -> 3s) 5.91 CASPT2, 5.77 MS-CASPT2, 5.87 XMS-CASPT2, against 5.83 MRCI+Q and 5.85 CC3; 2 1B1 (1a2 -> 3py) 5.99 / 6.07 / 5.98 against 5.95 and 6.00; 1 1A2 (1a2 -> 3s) 5.21 / 5.19 / 5.20 against 5.08 and 5.10; 2 1A2 (1a2 -> 3pz) 6.00 / 6.00 / 5.99 against 5.86 and 5.86. Adiabatic excitation energies from MS- and XMS-CASPT2 are 5.72/5.73, 5.99/5.94, 4.96/4.97 and 5.84/5.83 eV. XMS-CASPT2 tracks the accurate references more evenly than MS-CASPT2, whose 1 1B1 value is visibly pulled down by the state mixing.
reference_short: Shiozaki, Gyorffy, Celani & Werner, Communication: Extended multi-state complete active space second-order perturbation theory - energy and nuclear gradients, J. Chem. Phys. 135, 081106 (2011)
notes: active_space_nel is left EMPTY: the paper specifies the pi-only space by listing the active orbitals by symmetry label and never states how many electrons occupy them.

compound_name: stacked nucleobase dimers of B-DNA: exciton delocalization, charge transfer and electronic coupling for singlet excitation energy transfer
formula: stacked dimers XY of cytosine, thymine, adenine and guanine
geometry_source: idealized regular B-DNA intra-strand stacking geometries with 3.38 A between the ring planes, built with the SCHNArP program; coordinates in the supplementary material
method: MS-CASPT2 with an imaginary shift of 0.1 a.u. and an IPEA shift of 0.25 a.u.; exciton localization and charge-transfer measures taken from the perturbationally modified CAS-CI (PM-CASCI) transition density matrix; diabatic energies and couplings fitted to the adiabatic MS-CASPT2 data by least squares
software: not stated in the text read (SCHNArP was used only to build the geometries)
basis_set: ANO-S, with the 3s2p1d contraction on C, N and O and 2s1p on H
active_space_orbital_description: a reduced pi space: the full pi count is 8 orbitals for cytosine and thymine, 10 for adenine and 11 for guanine, which would need 16-22 orbitals for a dimer; the pyrimidine fragments are cut from 8 to 4 orbitals and the purine fragments from 10 and 11 to 6
active_space_protocol: the fragment truncation gives (8,8) for a dimer of two pyrimidines, (12,12) for a dimer of two purines and (10,10) for a mixed pyrimidine-purine pair. CASSCF was state-averaged over 4 states for the monomers and 8 states for the dimers.
nroots_per_mult: 4 for the monomers, 8 for the dimers
electronic_structure_description: MS-CASPT2 adiabatic energies together with the fragment-localized and charge-transfer weights of each state are used as reference data from which diabatic energies and electronic couplings for singlet excitation energy transfer between stacked bases are extracted. Where the two-state model is inadequate - when the sum of the fragment weights departs appreciably from one - the treatment is extended to three states, and the coupling is taken as the geometric mean of the values obtained from the two states. The truncated active spaces are shown to reproduce the lowest excited-state energy well.
reference_short: Blancafort & Voityuk, Exciton delocalization, charge transfer, and electronic coupling for singlet excitation energy transfer between stacked nucleobases in DNA: an MS-CASPT2 study, J. Chem. Phys. 2014
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the space depends on which two bases are stacked - (8,8), (10,10) or (12,12) - and all three are recorded in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: donor-acceptor Stenhouse adduct (DASA) photoswitch, absorption properties
geometry_source: ground state optimized in vacuum at B3LYP/6-31+G(d); for the solvent study the ground state was reoptimized at the same level in each solvent
method: CASPT2 and strongly contracted NEVPT2 on a CASSCF reference, benchmarked against TD-DFT with a range of functionals; solvent treated implicitly with the polarizable continuum model (PCM) in methanol, acetonitrile and toluene; charge-transfer character analysed by Mulliken population analysis at TD-DFT, CASSCF and CASPT2 levels and by NBO analysis at TD-DFT
software: MOLCAS and ORCA (Gaussian and Dalton also used in the work)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 and NEVPT2 calculations; 6-31+G(d) for the B3LYP geometries
active_space_orbital_description: 14 electrons in 13 orbitals, the same space for both the CASPT2 and the strongly contracted NEVPT2 treatment
active_space_protocol: a single 14-electron, 13-orbital active space used for CASPT2/cc-pVDZ and SC-NEVPT2/cc-pVDZ alike, with the details given in the supporting material
electronic_structure_description: The vertical absorption of a DASA photoswitch is computed at TD-DFT, CASPT2 and NEVPT2 and compared. TD-DFT results proved almost insensitive to the choice of functional, so B3LYP/cc-pVDZ was carried forward for the comparison against the multiconfigurational methods. Because the charge-transfer character of the transition is what controls the absorption, it is quantified separately at each level. DASA derivatives can be excited with red or even infrared light, which is what makes them attractive for biological use, and unlike diarylethenes they give a large change in end-to-end distance on switching.
reference_short: Level of Theory and Solvent Effects on DASA Absorption Properties Prediction: Comparing TD-DFT, CASPT2 and NEVPT2, Materials 2017, 10, 1025

compound_name: bithiophene (2T), the two lowest 1Bu excited states and their assignment to the observed absorption spectrum
geometry_source: trans-planar C2h ground-state equilibrium geometries optimized at the CASPT2 level with the valence 0550 active space, separately for each basis set used
method: single-state and multi-state CASPT2 on state-averaged CASSCF references, with an IPEA shift of 0.25 eV and an imaginary shift of 0.1 hartree; compared against other quantum chemical methods
software: MOLCAS 7.4 (MOLPRO and TURBOMOLE also used for comparison)
active_space_orbital_description: the natural valence space is ten valence pi orbitals - five bg and five au - holding 12 active electrons, denoted 0550 for the orbital counts in the irreducible representations ag, bg, au, bu
active_space_protocol: a systematic series of spaces in the (ag, bg, au, bu) notation. The natural valence space is 0550, identical to the one Rubio et al. used. Because low-lying pi-pi* energies in five-membered heterocycles are known to be sensitive to extra virtual pi orbitals, it was extended to 0570, 0660 and 0770, and a further set of auxiliary spaces 0560, 0580, 0650, 0670, 0680, 0750, 0760 and 0780 was investigated to understand the dependence. Control calculations took the state-averaged 0560/aug-cc-pVDZ orbitals into CASPT2 with the 6th au orbital deleted, or shifted into the virtual space and frozen, at both CAS-CI and CAS-SCF reference levels; the effects of orbital optimization proved marginal and the results very close to the 0560 ones.
electronic_structure_description: Rubio et al. had reported two Bu states of similar energy (3.88 and 4.15 eV) plus a third much higher at 5.53 eV, raising the question whether the near-degeneracy is real or an artifact of the single-state CASPT2 / pi-only valence space / double-zeta basis combination. The 1 1Bu and 2 1Bu CASSCF wave functions are strikingly alike: the leading configuration is HOMO -> LUMO (43 percent in 1 1Bu, 36 percent in 2 1Bu) with sizable HOMO-2 -> LUMO (20, 19 percent) and HOMO -> LUMO+2 (7, 9 percent) contributions. The CASSCF energies of both transitions depend only weakly on the active space or basis, while the CASPT2 energies do not. The paper's resolution is that the two 1Bu states are unusually strongly coupled by dynamical correlation, which separates them by 0.89 eV with oscillator strengths of 0.29 and 0.13; the 6th au orbital works mainly by giving the CASSCF orbitals extra variational flexibility rather than by entering the wave function directly.
reference_short: Andrzejak & Witek, The elusive excited states of bithiophene: a CASPT2 detective story, Theor. Chem. Acc. 2011, 129, 161-172
notes: nel/norb carry the natural valence 0550 space, 12 electrons in 10 pi orbitals, which the paper states explicitly; the whole family of extended and auxiliary spaces is in active_space_protocol. The spaces are written as orbital counts per irreducible representation (ag, bg, au, bu), so 0570 means 5 bg and 7 au orbitals, not an (n,m) pair.

compound_name: pyrazole-fused quinone photoclick reaction: light-induced tetrazole-quinone 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition (compound 3i, referred to as PFQ)
geometry_source: excited-state structures and minimum energy paths optimized with SA-CASSCF; the paths along the C-N and N-N bond cleavage coordinates obtained by constrained relax-scan optimization; Cartesian coordinates of all optimized structures in the ESI
method: SA-CASSCF for structures and minimum energy paths, refined by MS-CASPT2 single points; DFT used alongside; two-electron integrals via Cholesky decomposition with unbiased auxiliary basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: 12 pi and 2 sigma electrons in an active space of 6 pi, 1 sigma and 3 pi* orbitals; for the MS-CASPT2 step an additional sigma* orbital is added
active_space_protocol: SA-CASSCF with two roots of equal weight in a space of 14 electrons (12 pi + 2 sigma) in 10 orbitals (6 pi + 1 sigma + 3 pi*); the MS-CASPT2 calculations add one sigma* orbital, giving 11 orbitals. All CASSCF active orbitals are shown in the ESI.
electronic_structure_description: The microscopic mechanism of the light-induced tetrazole-quinone 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition, including nitrogen extrusion along the C-N and N-N cleavage coordinates and the subsequent decay pathways. The CASSCF potential energy surfaces are overall similar to the MS-CASPT2 refined ones and the computed absorption spectrum agrees with experiment, which the authors take as confirmation that the strategy is sound.
reference_short: Yang He et al., Microscopic mechanism of light-induced tetrazole-quinone 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition: a MS-CASPT2 theoretical investigation, RSC Adv. 2022
notes: nel = 14 is the sum the paper itself states as 12 pi plus 2 sigma electrons; norb = 10 is its 6 pi + 1 sigma + 3 pi* orbital list for the CASSCF step. The extra sigma* orbital used at MS-CASPT2 (11 orbitals) is recorded in active_space_protocol rather than in norb.

compound_name: lithium fluoride LiF, ionic-covalent avoided crossing along dissociation
point_group: C2v symmetry imposed in the calculation
geometry_source: potential energy curves computed for internuclear distances from 2.4 to 14 a0 in steps of 0.2 a0
method: extended dynamically weighted CASPT2 (XDW-CASPT2), a new zeroth-order Hamiltonian partitioning that interpolates between state-specific and state-averaged Fock operators through a dynamical weighting parameter zeta; compared throughout against SA-CASSCF, single-state CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2
software: a development branch of OpenMolcas, version v18.09-617-g5a96a25e
basis_set: cc-pVTZ on lithium and aug-cc-pVTZ on fluorine
active_space_orbital_description: six electrons in 2 a1, 2 b1 and 2 b2 orbitals; the remaining 3 occupied a1 orbitals were relaxed during the optimization
active_space_protocol: SA-CASSCF over the three lowest singlet states with equal weights, in C2v symmetry, with six electrons in six orbitals (2 a1 + 2 b1 + 2 b2)
electronic_structure_description: The two lowest 1Sigma+ states of LiF switch rapidly between ionic and covalent character on dissociation. SA-CASSCF puts the avoided crossing at a much shorter distance than FCI because it misses dynamical correlation; adding that correlation state-specifically through single-state CASPT2 produces an artificial double crossing of the curves. The pathology is even clearer when three 1Sigma+ states are treated rather than the usual two. XMS-CASPT2 shows no unphysical behaviour regardless of the number of states, but pays for it with reduced accuracy in the relative energies at equilibrium - which is exactly the trade-off XDW-CASPT2 is designed to remove. In the zeta -> infinity limit the weights become unit vectors and the densities purely state-specific, giving curves that overlap the MS-CASPT2 ones but without the artifacts near the SA-CASSCF degeneracies; the wiggles seen at intermediate zeta are traced to the rapid variation of the weights themselves.
reference_short: Battaglia & Lindh, Extended Dynamically Weighted CASPT2: The Best of Two Worlds, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 1555-1567
notes: First of three test cases; the allene conical intersection is row -b and the Thiel-set vertical excitations row -c. Note the OpenMolcas CASPT2 implementation uses the SS-SR internally contracted basis, so invariance is never fully preserved, not even for XMS-CASPT2.

compound_name: allene, minimum energy conical intersection between the 1 1A' and 2 1A' states
point_group: Cs at the distorted MECI geometry
geometry_source: two-dimensional non-relaxed scans around the CASSCF MECI point, varying the C-C-C bend angle and the C-C-C-H torsion in steps of 0.25 degrees over -10 to +10 degrees
method: extended dynamically weighted CASPT2 (XDW-CASPT2), a new zeroth-order Hamiltonian partitioning that interpolates between state-specific and state-averaged Fock operators through a dynamical weighting parameter zeta; compared throughout against SA-CASSCF, single-state CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2
software: a development branch of OpenMolcas, version v18.09-617-g5a96a25e
basis_set: as in the authors' earlier study of this MECI; fully specified in the Supporting Information
active_space_orbital_description: 4 electrons in 3 orbitals of a' symmetry and 1 orbital of a'' symmetry
active_space_protocol: SA-CASSCF with 4 electrons in 3 a' plus 1 a'' orbitals, which amounts to a complete active space of just 12 totally symmetric configuration state functions - small enough that the potential energy surface can be followed as a function of the number of averaged states all the way to the complete active space limit
electronic_structure_description: At the MECI the 1 1A' and 2 1A' states are quasidegenerate, so only the space they jointly span is well defined. Projecting the zeroth-order Hamiltonian onto the individual model states gives a perturbation theory that is not invariant to unitary transformations among them, and that failure shows up as unphysical behaviour at conical intersections and near avoided crossings. Allene's MECI is the harder test of this than LiF, and it is where the invariance built into XDW-CASPT2 matters.
reference_short: Battaglia & Lindh, Extended Dynamically Weighted CASPT2: The Best of Two Worlds, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 1555-1567
notes: Second of three test cases in this paper; LiF is row -a and the Thiel set row -c.

compound_name: Thiel benchmark set of small to medium organic compounds: vertical energy gap between the ground state and the first excited singlet
formula: the organic molecules of Thiel's benchmark set, minus ethene and cyclopropene
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of Thiel's benchmark set
method: extended dynamically weighted CASPT2 (XDW-CASPT2), a new zeroth-order Hamiltonian partitioning that interpolates between state-specific and state-averaged Fock operators through a dynamical weighting parameter zeta; compared throughout against SA-CASSCF, single-state CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2
software: a development branch of OpenMolcas, version v18.09-617-g5a96a25e
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of Thiel's benchmark set, which differ from molecule to molecule and are not restated here
active_space_protocol: the molecules were taken from Thiel's benchmark set, excluding ethene and cyclopropene because no singlet excited state was considered for those two; the first singlet vertical energy gap was computed with XDW-CASPT2 and compared with MS-CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: When the ground state and the first excited state are separated by more than zeta^(-1/2), the dynamical weighting leaves the two density matrices essentially unmixed and state-specific, the rotated reference states stay close to the originals, and XDW-CASPT2 should reproduce MS-CASPT2 accuracy - which is what this benchmark confirms. The same argument extends to model spaces larger than two provided all the states stay well separated; the difficult regime is many model states packed into a narrow energy window and interacting strongly at zeroth order, where the rotated states are linear combinations of the originals and the physical content of the Fock operator becomes hard to read off the weights.
reference_short: Battaglia & Lindh, Extended Dynamically Weighted CASPT2: The Best of Two Worlds, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 1555-1567
notes: Third of three test cases in this paper. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active spaces are inherited from Thiel's benchmark set and are not restated, so they differ per molecule and cannot be read off this paper.

compound_name: benchmark of 265 excited states of small and medium organic molecules (acetaldehyde, cyclopropenone, cyclopropene, the carbon trimer C3, streptocyanine-C1 and many others): CASPT2 and NEVPT2 vertical transition energies
formula: small and medium organic molecules plus the linear carbon trimer C3
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of the benchmark sets from which the theoretical best estimates are taken
method: SA-CASSCF references followed by CASPT2 with and without the IPEA shift, and by strongly contracted and partially contracted NEVPT2; all compared against theoretical best estimates (TBEs) of near-FCI quality
software: MOLPRO for CASPT2, ORCA for NEVPT2
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ (TZVP and 6-31+G(d) appear for particular geometries)
active_space_orbital_description: one active space chosen per excited state, sized to capture the static correlation of that particular electronic excitation at the ground-state geometry
active_space_protocol: the active space is selected separately for each excited state, on the principle of describing mainly the static correlation associated with that excitation at the ground-state geometry; the authors note explicitly that a larger space could be defined for any of the states and would give a more accurate transition energy, and that studying excited states away from equilibrium, near conical intersections, would require adapting the orbital choice
electronic_structure_description: Over 265 excited states, taking the TBEs as reference: SA-CASSCF gives MSE 0.13, MAE 0.48, RMSE 0.60 eV with a spread up to 2.14 eV; CASPT2 with the IPEA shift gives MAE 0.11 eV; CASPT2 without it MAE 0.27 eV with a systematic underestimation (MSE -0.26 eV); SC-NEVPT2 MAE 0.15 eV and PC-NEVPT2 MAE 0.13 eV. ADC(2), CC2 and CCSD reach comparable average deviations but with a somewhat larger spread for the first two, and CC3 remains clearly more accurate than any of the multiconfigurational methods. Individual cases: for the carbon trimer, which has two genuinely doubly excited low-lying states with FCI-quality references, NEVPT2 lands extremely close to FCI while CASPT2 without IPEA underestimates badly; for cyclopropene the nearly degenerate sigma -> pi* (B1) and pi -> pi* (B2) transitions are ordered correctly by CASPT2(IPEA) and NEVPT2, matching CCSDT, but swapped by CASPT2(NOIPEA).
reference_short: Sarkar, Loos, Boggio-Pasqua & Jacquemin, Assessing the Performances of CASPT2 and NEVPT2 for Vertical Excitation Energies
notes: QUEST-ADJACENT - the theoretical best estimates and the single-reference comparison data are taken straight from the QUEST database, so this row carries the same held-out-benchmark contamination risk as the QUEST series itself and must be dropped on export to casscf-agent. nel/norb are left EMPTY: a different active space is chosen for each of the 265 excited states.

compound_name: benzene with the full pi active space, the CASPT2 geometry optimization example of the BAGEL program package
geometry_source: CASPT2 geometry optimization; BAGEL optimizes in non-redundant or redundant internal coordinates and can locate equilibrium structures, transition states and conical intersections
method: CASPT2 geometry optimization with analytical nuclear gradients, using a real shift of 0.2 and a frozen core; the CASPT2 gradient and derivative-coupling code is generated by the SMITH3 automatic code generator; every algorithm in the package uses density fitting
software: BAGEL (with an interface to NECI for FCI-QMC-based CASSCF with very large active spaces)
basis_set: not stated for this example; the Hartree-Fock timing benchmark elsewhere in the paper uses cc-pVTZ with the matching JKFIT auxiliary basis
active_space_orbital_description: the full pi active space of benzene: 6 active orbitals (nact = 6, orbitals 17, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 30) above 18 closed orbitals
active_space_protocol: the sample JSON input specifies nact = 6 and nclosed = 18 with the active orbital list [17, 20, 21, 22, 23, 30], described in the caption as benzene with the full pi active space
electronic_structure_description: A program description rather than a chemical study. BAGEL's distinguishing features are analytical CASPT2 nuclear energy gradients and derivative couplings, relativistic multireference wave functions based on the Dirac equation, and parallelization over both threads and MPI. CASSCF can be driven by external FCI solvers through loose coupling, with active Hamiltonians and reduced density matrices passed between packages - the NECI interface enables FCI-QMC-based CASSCF with very large active spaces and is extensible to DMRG. As a performance illustration, a Hartree-Fock SCF on eight benzene molecules in cc-pVTZ (2112 basis functions, 5232 auxiliary functions, 336 electrons) converges in 11 iterations in about two minutes.
reference_short: Shiozaki, BAGEL: Brilliantly Advanced General Electronic-structure Library
notes: Program-description paper; the only active space it states is the one in the sample CASPT2 input of Figure 1. active_space_nel is left EMPTY: the input specifies orbital counts (nact, nclosed) and an orbital list but no electron count, and 'full pi active space' would have to be converted to six electrons by inference.

compound_name: benzene adsorbed on a Cu13 cluster model of the Cu(110) copper surface
ligand_set: a physisorbed benzene molecule above a 13-atom copper cluster
geometry_source: cluster geometry cut from the Cu(110) surface; the adsorbed benzene takes a shape akin to the quinonoid form of the lowest excited triplet state of gas-phase benzene; DFT periodic-slab calculations of the same systems used for comparison
method: CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference, alongside MP2 on Hartree-Fock references and periodic-slab and cluster DFT
software: MOLCAS (GAUSSIAN used for the other methods)
basis_set: Stuttgart ECP10MWB with its 1s+2s+2p effective core potential on Cu, with 6-31+G* on C and H
relativistic_treatment: ECP10MWB effective core potential on copper
active_space_orbital_description: all 13 Cu 4s electrons distributed through all 13 Cu 4s orbitals; the chosen orbitals were 5 a1, 2 a2, 3 b1 and 3 b2, with 41 a1, 28 a2, 34 b1 and 35 b2 doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: the space was chosen to hold the 13 Cu 4s electrons in the 13 Cu 4s orbitals, but orbital rotations distorted this picture during optimization, mixing in benzene occupied and virtual orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Benzene physisorbs weakly on Cu(111), Ag(111), Au(111) and Cu(110) at low coverage. The potential energy surfaces are extremely flat, supporting structures that differ dramatically in geometry but only trivially in energy. The bonding is purely dispersive with minimal covalent character, which is why DFT binding energies fall dramatically short of experiment - dispersion is reproduced poorly by the functionals used. The CASPT2 calculations show that there is no binding at all at the Hartree-Fock level and that the intermolecular correlation (dispersive) energy is of the right size to account for the measured binding energies. DFT calculations on both the periodic Cu(110) surface and the cluster indicate that Cu13 is an adequate model of the surface.
reference_short: Bilic, Reimers & Hush, The adsorption of benzene on copper, silver, and gold surfaces
notes: SOLID-STATE: this row is a Cu13 cluster model of the Cu(110) surface with an adsorbed molecule, not a gas-phase molecular complex. ground_state_mult is left empty although the 13-electron space implies an open shell; the paper does not state the multiplicity. The (111) surfaces are treated only by periodic DFT, so they get no row.

compound_name: chloroiron corrole complex, spin states and iron oxidation number
ligand_set: a corrole macrocycle carrying a radical, plus one axial chloride
geometry_source: as in the earlier CD-CASPT2 study of this complex
method: frozen natural orbital CASPT2 (FNO-CASPT2): the virtual space is truncated by keeping only the natural orbitals with the largest occupations, with an MP2-type correction for the discarded ones; combined with the Cholesky decomposition (CD) of the two-electron integrals, and with local exchange screening using localized Cholesky molecular orbitals to speed up the CASSCF exchange Fock matrices
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VTZP on Fe, N and Cl, ANO-RCC-VDZP on C and H, 534 contracted functions in total; CD threshold 1e-4
active_space_orbital_description: 14 electrons in 14 orbitals; the composition is discussed in the earlier reference work rather than here
active_space_protocol: a single 14-electron, 14-orbital space, with the lowest state computed in each symmetry of Cs and in each spin state; FNO-CASPT2 run at 40, 60, 80 and 100 percent (full CD-CASPT2) virtual-space truncation
electronic_structure_description: The complex is a high-spin Fe(III) ion coupled antiferromagnetically to a radical corrole ring, and the point of the original study was to assign that spin state and oxidation number. It is a hard case for the FNO approximation because the states involved are of different natures with open shells delocalized over the whole molecule. Keeping only 40 percent of the virtual space gives an rms error of 0.29 eV in the excitation energies; this falls to 0.13 eV at 60 percent and 0.04 eV at 80 percent. The lesson drawn is that for transition metal systems, where large AO basis sets are needed anyway, truncating the virtual space is a more reliable economy than simply dropping to a smaller AO basis - the apparent accuracy of the latter is described as a fortuitous coincidence.
reference_short: Aquilante, Todorova, Gagliardi, Pedersen & Roos, Systematic truncation of the virtual space in multiconfigurational perturbation theory, J. Chem. Phys. 131, 034113 (2009)
notes: One of three demonstration systems in this method paper; the LaOn/glycine-dipeptide pair is row -b.

compound_name: the two organic and lanthanide demonstrations of FNO-CASPT2: spectroscopic constants of LaOn and LaOn+ (n = 1, 2), and the vertical electronic spectrum of the glycine dipeptide
formula: LaO; LaO2; LaO+; LaO2+; glycine dipeptide
geometry_source: the same geometries as the earlier CASSCF/CASPT2 study of the La + O and La + O2 chemionization mechanisms; the glycine dipeptide taken at Phi = 180 degrees, Psi = -180 degrees, the system of Serrano and Fulscher's polypeptide series
method: frozen natural orbital CASPT2 (FNO-CASPT2): the virtual space is truncated by keeping only the natural orbitals with the largest occupations, with an MP2-type correction for the discarded ones; combined with the Cholesky decomposition (CD) of the two-electron integrals, and with local exchange screening using localized Cholesky molecular orbitals to speed up the CASSCF exchange Fock matrices
basis_set: ANO-RCC of quintuple-zeta quality for the LaOn species, with the CD threshold set to 1e-8 so that CD-CASPT2 reproduces the reference numbers almost exactly; ANO-L at double-, triple- and quadruple-zeta contraction for the glycine dipeptide
active_space_orbital_description: the same active spaces as the reference studies; for the glycine dipeptide the active space extends over the entire molecule, which is why localized-orbital approaches cannot simplify the CASPT2 equations here
active_space_protocol: active spaces, basis sets and geometries were taken over unchanged from the earlier studies so that only the FNO error is being measured; no point group symmetry was used for the glycine dipeptide, and its CASSCF wave functions are state-averaged so that all states share one orbital set - which also means the MP2-type FNO correction cancels out of the relative energies
electronic_structure_description: For LaO geometry reproduction, raising the truncation level to 70 percent already converges Re to 1.856 A and omega_e to 807 cm-1, so geometries need fewer virtual natural orbitals than energy differences do. For the glycine dipeptide the vertical excitation energies at quadruple-zeta quality move from 5.85 to 5.75 eV (W(1)), 7.01 to 6.73 eV (NV1(1)) and 8.37 to 8.15 eV (CT2) as the truncation goes from 40 percent to the full CD-CASPT2 value, with the 80 percent numbers already essentially converged.
reference_short: Aquilante, Todorova, Gagliardi, Pedersen & Roos, Systematic truncation of the virtual space in multiconfigurational perturbation theory, J. Chem. Phys. 131, 034113 (2009)
notes: Second row of this method paper; the chloroiron corrole is row -a. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the spaces are inherited unchanged from the reference studies and are never restated here.

compound_name: 2-thiouracil (2TU), intersystem crossing pathways in a noncanonical nucleobase
geometry_source: on-the-fly dynamics; initial conditions sampled from a computed absorption spectrum; energies, numerical gradients and couplings all computed on the fly
method: MS-CASPT2 surface-hopping molecular dynamics including singlet and triplet states, run in a local development version of the SHARC (Surface Hopping including ARbitrary Couplings) suite; static single-state and multi-state CASPT2 calculations used as a consistency check
software: SHARC (local development version); the electronic structure back end is not named in the main text
active_space_orbital_description: a 12-electron, 9-orbital space; the orbitals themselves are shown in Figure S1 of the Supporting Information
active_space_protocol: MS-CASPT2(12,9)/cc-pVDZ for every on-the-fly energy, numerical gradient and coupling in the dynamics - described by the authors as the largest MS-CASPT2 setup used in excited-state dynamics at the time. The good agreement between single-state and multi-state static CASPT2 for 2TU is taken as evidence that the usual multistate artifacts are absent here.
electronic_structure_description: Nonadiabatic dynamics show that intersystem crossing in 2-thiouracil is very efficient, and the computed ISC time scales agree well with experiment. Cheaper methods normally used for excited-state dynamics, CASSCF or TD-DFT, give a qualitatively wrong potential energy landscape here, which is why the expensive MS-CASPT2 surfaces were needed. 2TU appears to be a rare exception to the rule that solvation strongly affects nucleobase dynamics: in uracil the reported ISC yields swing from a few percent in water to about 50 percent in aprotic nonpolar solvents, and SHARC on CASSCF potentials gives 67 percent for gas-phase uracil.
reference_short: Mai, Marquetand & Gonzalez et al., Intersystem Crossing Pathways in the Noncanonical Nucleobase 2-Thiouracil: A Time-Dependent Picture, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2016
notes: The active orbitals are only shown in the SI, but the (12,9) size is stated in the main text as part of the method label MS-CASPT2(12,9)/cc-pVDZ.

compound_name: hydrogen peroxide, six-dimensional analytical ground-state potential energy surface up to chemically significant energies
geometry_source: a six-dimensional grid of ab initio points covering the full internal coordinate space up to dissociation, fitted to an analytical form
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with all electrons correlated in the perturbation step; multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction (MRSDCI) computed as a benchmark for the lowest X 1A state as a function of the O-O distance
basis_set: a large atomic natural orbital basis with multiple polarization functions, 120 basis functions, contraction scheme given in the paper's Table I; cc-pVTZ also appears in the work
active_space_orbital_description: 10 correlated electrons in 8 active orbitals, giving 1176 configuration state functions; the lowest four orbitals were kept doubly occupied in the CASSCF
active_space_protocol: the space was chosen to capture the states correlating with both dissociation channels, OH(X 2Pi) + OH(X 2Pi) and OOH(X 2A'') + H(2S); the lowest four orbitals stay doubly occupied, and the zeroth-order CASSCF wave functions are corrected by second-order perturbation theory including all electrons
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2 recovers a large fraction of the correlation energy at much lower cost than other multireference methods, which is what makes a full six-dimensional surface affordable. The known danger is that perturbation theory can give erroneous energies for near-degenerate states when the active space is too small, and that risk is greatest along the coordinate leading to two hydroxyl radicals - which is exactly where the MRSDCI benchmark for the lowest X 1A state as a function of O-O distance was computed to check the method.
reference_short: Kuhn, Rizzo, Luckhaus, Quack et al., A new six-dimensional analytical potential up to chemically significant energies for the electronic ground state of hydrogen peroxide, J. Chem. Phys. 1999

compound_name: the methanol + OH reaction, hydrogen abstraction channel R2 (transition state TS2) and its reactants and products
geometry_source: structures optimized at the M08-HX/MG3S level; CASPT2 single points computed on those geometries
method: CASPT2 with the correlated participating orbitals (CPO) scheme, in its moderate (mod-CPO) variant, used to benchmark the barrier height of the multireference channel; CCSD(T)-F12a used for the single-reference channel R1; T1 and M diagnostics computed for every species to decide which treatment each channel needs
software: not stated in the text read
basis_set: MG3S for the CASPT2 calculations; jun-cc-pVTZ for the CCSD(T)-F12a benchmarks
active_space_orbital_description: the largest space examined, (11,11): the bond orbitals that break or form during the hydrogen transfer together with their electrons, plus four p orbitals geminal to those bonds and, for each of them, a correlating orbital in approximately the same region of space
active_space_protocol: active spaces are selected by the correlated participating orbitals (CPO) scheme, which includes the orbitals carrying the static correlation relevant to the reaction; the moderate CPO variant adds a correlating orbital for each geminal p orbital. Several active spaces were tested (Table S4 of the Supporting Information); the (11,11) mod-CPO space was adopted as the benchmark because it reproduces the experimentally based reaction energy.
electronic_structure_description: The T1 diagnostic identifies TS2 as the one genuinely multireference stationary point, with T1 = 0.055, and the M diagnostic agrees; everything else is well described by single-reference CCSD(T)-F12a. CASPT2(11,11)/MG3S//M08-HX/MG3S gives a classical energy of reaction of -12.45 kcal/mol against the experimentally based -12.4 +/- 0.8, and a classical forward barrier height of 3.06 kcal/mol with a reverse barrier of 15.51 kcal/mol. For comparison, CCSD(T)-F12a/jun-cc-pVTZ gives 3.98 and 16.30 kcal/mol and the density functionals tested land between 1.9 and 2.6 kcal/mol for the forward barrier. The CASPT2 numbers are the paper's best estimates for R2 and are what the rate constants over 30-2000 K are built on.
reference_short: Gao, Zheng, Fernandez-Ramos, Truhlar & Xu, Kinetics of the Methanol Reaction with OH at Interstellar, Atmospheric, and Combustion Temperatures, J. Am. Chem. Soc.
notes: Only channel R2 receives a multireference treatment; R1 is benchmarked with single-reference CCSD(T)-F12a, so it gets no row. ground_state_mult = 2 records that the reacting system is an open-shell doublet (methanol plus the OH radical).

compound_name: plutonyl dication PuO2(2+), geometry, electronic structure, f-f spectrum and vibrational frequencies
geometry_source: geometries optimized at the DFT level in Gaussian with the ultrafine integration grid to make the vibrational frequencies reliable; potential curves scanned along the Pu-O and Pu-N distances at the multiconfigurational level
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with the variational iterative difference-dedicated configuration interaction (IDDCI) method for comparison; spin-orbit coupling from the two-step uncontracted spin-orbit CI code EPCISO, in which all single excitations from the CAS(2,4) reference that are coupled by spin-orbit interaction are included, and an effective Hamiltonian on the spin-orbit model space carries the CASPT2 or IDDCI spin-free energies
software: MOLCAS 5.0 for CASSCF/CASPT2; CASDI for the IDDCI step; EPCISO for spin-orbit; Gaussian for the DFT
basis_set: Stuttgart relativistic small-core ECP on Pu treating 34 valence electrons (5s2 5p6 5d10 5f5 6s2 6p6 6d1 7s2) with the matching segmented basis contracted [11s11p9d8f]/[9s8p6d5f]; Toulouse ECPs on O and N with double-zeta plus polarization plus diffuse basis sets, or equivalently Stuttgart ECPs with double-zeta plus one d polarization function (exponents 0.73 for O, 0.8 for N); two g functions with exponents 1.1308 and 0.4524 added in all the multiconfigurational calculations
relativistic_treatment: shape-consistent relativistic effective core potentials on all atoms; spin-orbit coupling treated separately and a posteriori by EPCISO
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons in the two f-phi and two f-delta valence orbitals of plutonium (written in the paper as the two fu and two du valence orbitals), denoted CAS(2,4)
active_space_protocol: CAS(2,4) throughout, following Ismail et al. and Maron et al.; because the neutral isoelectronic UO2 has a triplet ground state involving the f-phi and sigma_g (7s-like) orbitals, a few tests were also run with a slightly larger CAS
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is the Omega = 4 component of 3Hg at all Pu-O distances, in agreement with Hay et al. and Maron et al. Two unpaired f electrons occupy the nonbonding f-delta and f-phi orbitals of Pu, and the LS coupling rules put Omega = 4 below Omega = 5 below Omega = 6; the curves are quasiparallel and the low-lying states track one another. The twelve lowest f-f transitions are reported. Spin-orbit effects barely touch the ground-state geometry or the vibrational frequencies, but they completely rearrange the distribution of electronically excited states - which is the paper's central point: an unambiguous assignment of the ground state and the electronic spectrum requires multireference methods including spin-orbit coupling, while single-reference DFT gives a reasonable account only of the ground-state properties.
reference_short: Clavaguera-Sarrio, Vallet, Maynau & Marsden, Can density functional methods be used for open-shell actinide molecules? Comparison with multiconfigurational spin-orbit studies, J. Chem. Phys. 121, 5312 (2004)
notes: d_electron_count is left EMPTY: the two active electrons are 5f, not d, and the paper describes the configuration purely in terms of the f-delta and f-phi orbitals. The states carry orbital angular momentum as high as six, which is why the paper tabulates the configurations explicitly.

compound_name: plutonium dinitride PuN2, the isoelectronic analogue of plutonyl
geometry_source: geometries optimized at the DFT level in Gaussian with the ultrafine integration grid to make the vibrational frequencies reliable; potential curves scanned along the Pu-O and Pu-N distances at the multiconfigurational level
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with the variational iterative difference-dedicated configuration interaction (IDDCI) method for comparison; spin-orbit coupling from the two-step uncontracted spin-orbit CI code EPCISO, in which all single excitations from the CAS(2,4) reference that are coupled by spin-orbit interaction are included, and an effective Hamiltonian on the spin-orbit model space carries the CASPT2 or IDDCI spin-free energies
software: MOLCAS 5.0 for CASSCF/CASPT2; CASDI for the IDDCI step; EPCISO for spin-orbit; Gaussian for the DFT
basis_set: Stuttgart relativistic small-core ECP on Pu treating 34 valence electrons (5s2 5p6 5d10 5f5 6s2 6p6 6d1 7s2) with the matching segmented basis contracted [11s11p9d8f]/[9s8p6d5f]; Toulouse ECPs on O and N with double-zeta plus polarization plus diffuse basis sets, or equivalently Stuttgart ECPs with double-zeta plus one d polarization function (exponents 0.73 for O, 0.8 for N); two g functions with exponents 1.1308 and 0.4524 added in all the multiconfigurational calculations
relativistic_treatment: shape-consistent relativistic effective core potentials on all atoms; spin-orbit coupling treated separately and a posteriori by EPCISO
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons in the two f-phi and two f-delta valence orbitals of plutonium (written in the paper as the two fu and two du valence orbitals), denoted CAS(2,4)
active_space_protocol: CAS(2,4) throughout, following Ismail et al. and Maron et al.; because the neutral isoelectronic UO2 has a triplet ground state involving the f-phi and sigma_g (7s-like) orbitals, a few tests were also run with a slightly larger CAS
electronic_structure_description: PuN2 is isoelectronic with PuO2(2+) and behaves the same way: its ground state is also the Omega = 4 component of 3Hg, which contradicts the earlier assignment of Archibong and Ray (J. Mol. Struct: THEOCHEM 530, 165 (2000)). As for the dication, spin-orbit effects are small on the ground-state geometry and frequencies but completely change the ordering and spacing of the excited states, and the twelve lowest f-f transitions are reported.
reference_short: Clavaguera-Sarrio, Vallet, Maynau & Marsden, Can density functional methods be used for open-shell actinide molecules? Comparison with multiconfigurational spin-orbit studies, J. Chem. Phys. 121, 5312 (2004)
notes: Companion system to PuO2(2+) (row -a), sharing the same CAS(2,4) and computational protocol. d_electron_count is left EMPTY for the same reason: the active electrons are 5f.

compound_name: carbon monosulfide CS, photoionization cross sections and asymmetry parameters from MS-CASPT2 Dyson orbitals
geometry_source: experimental ground-state equilibrium bond length, re = 1.535 A
method: multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) for the ionization energies and Dyson orbitals, with neutral and ionized states computed separately and the Dyson orbitals obtained in the RASSI state-interaction formalism over biorthonormal orbital sets; the Dyson orbitals are then coupled to an electronic continuum described by a multicentric B-spline LCAO basis at the DFT and TD-DFT levels; ionization energies also computed with EOM-CCSD for comparison
software: OpenMolcas (with a new Dyson-orbital implementation exploiting the full Abelian point group and corrected normalization); Q-Chem for EOM-CCSD; ADF for the ground-state densities feeding the continuum
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ on all atoms for the MS-CASPT2 work; DZP with the LB94 functional in ADF for the ground-state density, plus a one-centre expansion to Lmax = 20 with Rmax = 25 a.u. and step 0.125 for the B-spline continuum
active_space_orbital_description: the valence 5-7 sigma and 1 pi orbitals, plus 3 sigma and 2 pi virtual orbitals; 10 electrons in 12 orbitals
active_space_protocol: the same size for both molecules, called CAS-10/12: 10 electrons in 12 orbitals, built from the valence sigma and pi orbitals plus 3 sigma and 2 pi virtual orbitals in each case
electronic_structure_description: CS was chosen precisely because its smallness hides strong correlation effects, which show up in the photoionization observables. Of the isoelectronic diatomic series CS, CSe, CO, SiO and BF - all with 10 valence electrons in three sigma and one pi orbital - CS shows the strongest effects, and the paper anticipates them to be larger still in SiS. Earlier studies of this series were limited to DFT continua and CASSCF Dyson orbitals; here the Dyson orbitals come from MS-CASPT2 and the continuum from B-spline DFT and TD-DFT. The cross section is reported as dsigma/dk = (sigma/4pi)(1 + beta P2(cos theta)) for randomly oriented molecules with linearly polarized light in the dipole approximation.
reference_short: Tenorio, Ponzi, Coriani & Decleva, Photoionization Observables from Multi-Reference Dyson Orbitals Coupled to B-Spline DFT and TD-DFT Continuum, Molecules 2022, 27, 1203
notes: One of two prototype diatomics; SiS is row -b. The '10 electrons in three sigma and one pi orbitals' phrase in the introduction describes the isoelectronic valence shell of the series, not this paper's active space - the active space is the larger CAS-10/12, which adds 3 sigma and 2 pi virtuals.

compound_name: silicon monosulfide SiS, photoionization cross sections and asymmetry parameters from MS-CASPT2 Dyson orbitals
geometry_source: experimental ground-state equilibrium bond length, re = 1.929 A
method: multi-state CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) for the ionization energies and Dyson orbitals, with neutral and ionized states computed separately and the Dyson orbitals obtained in the RASSI state-interaction formalism over biorthonormal orbital sets; the Dyson orbitals are then coupled to an electronic continuum described by a multicentric B-spline LCAO basis at the DFT and TD-DFT levels; ionization energies also computed with EOM-CCSD for comparison
software: OpenMolcas (with a new Dyson-orbital implementation exploiting the full Abelian point group and corrected normalization); Q-Chem for EOM-CCSD; ADF for the ground-state densities feeding the continuum
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ on all atoms for the MS-CASPT2 work; DZP with the LB94 functional in ADF for the ground-state density, plus a one-centre expansion to Lmax = 20 with Rmax = 25 a.u. and step 0.125 for the B-spline continuum
active_space_orbital_description: the valence 7-9 sigma and 3 pi orbitals, complemented by 3 sigma and 2 pi virtual orbitals; 10 electrons in 12 orbitals
active_space_protocol: the same size for both molecules, called CAS-10/12: 10 electrons in 12 orbitals, built from the valence sigma and pi orbitals plus 3 sigma and 2 pi virtual orbitals in each case
electronic_structure_description: SiS is the third-row partner of CS, and correlation effects on its photoionization are expected to be even stronger. Because TD-DFT has a substantial effect on the photoionization properties of third-row atoms, the series was reinvestigated here with the improved Dyson-orbital treatment rather than the CASSCF Dyson orbitals of the earlier work. The comparison of CS with SiS shows that correlation effects vary appreciably even across an isoelectronic series.
reference_short: Tenorio, Ponzi, Coriani & Decleva, Photoionization Observables from Multi-Reference Dyson Orbitals Coupled to B-Spline DFT and TD-DFT Continuum, Molecules 2022, 27, 1203
notes: Second of two prototype diatomics; CS is row -a, and both use the same CAS-10/12 space.

compound_name: benzene, model Hamiltonian for its complex photochemistry (part II)
geometry_source: cuts of the potential energy surface computed along the normal modes from the ground-state equilibrium geometry, used to parametrize a diabatic vibronic-coupling model Hamiltonian
method: CASPT2 on a CASSCF zeroth-order wave function, used to fit a diabatic potential operator matrix for quantum dynamics; this work refines an earlier CASSCF-based model of the same states
basis_set: the MOLPRO-specific Roos (3s2p1d/2s) basis, an atomic natural orbital basis truncated to 6-31G* size
active_space_orbital_description: the six benzene pi orbitals with six electrons, CAS(6,6)
active_space_protocol: CAS(6,6) for the cuts along the vibrational modes; a larger (6,10) space was tested following earlier work and proved slightly more accurate at the equilibrium geometry but harder to use away from it
electronic_structure_description: The channel-three decay of benzene, debated since Callomon et al. first reported it, is now generally attributed to a conical intersection to a dark state becoming accessible at that energy, as shown by CASSCF and MRCI paths to the intersection. Photochemically, benzene rearranges substantially on irradiation: fulvene, benzvalene and Dewar benzene are all detected, with yields depending on the excitation wavelength - excitation of the A state at 254 nm gives quantum yields of 0.01 : 0.01 : 0.00 respectively. Prefulvene, the precursor of the rearrangement, is reached directly, but entering those photochemical channels is thought to require exciting a very specific combination of normal modes, which is what the model Hamiltonian is built to describe.
reference_short: Penfold & Worth, A model Hamiltonian to simulate the complex photochemistry of benzene II, J. Chem. Phys. 131, 064303 (2009)
notes: nel/norb carry the CAS(6,6) actually used for the surface cuts; the tested (6,10) alternative is in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: radical-radical reactions HCO + CH3 and HCO + NH2 in the presence of one and two water molecules, as models for interstellar icy grain surfaces
formula: HCO + CH3 and HCO + NH2 with 1 or 2 H2O
ligand_set: one or two water molecules (W1, W2) modelling the ice surface; the wider study also uses amorphous solid water clusters of 18 and 33 water molecules at the DFT level
geometry_source: all benchmark single points computed on B3LYP-D3 optimized geometries
method: CASPT2 single-point energies used as the multireference reference against which the B3LYP and BHLYP barrier heights are calibrated, with the CASSCF(2,2) orbitals as the initial guess; CCSD(T) single points used as the reference for the interaction energies
software: MOLCAS / OpenMolcas for the CASPT2 (Gaussian for the DFT)
basis_set: Dunning cc-pVTZ for the CASPT2; aug-cc-pVTZ for the CCSD(T); Pople 6-311++G(2df,2pd) for the DFT calibration
active_space_orbital_description: a two-electron, two-orbital space, the minimal description of the two radical electrons pairing up
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(2,2) supplies the starting orbitals for the CASPT2/cc-pVTZ single points on the B3LYP-D3 geometries; the CASPT2 numbers then serve as the multireference benchmark for the DFT energy barriers of the two radical-radical reactions with one and two water molecules
electronic_structure_description: If the HCO + CH3 and HCO + NH2 reactions occur on icy grains at all, they have two major competing channels: formation of the interstellar complex organic molecules CH3CHO and NH2CHO, and the alternative direct hydrogen abstraction. The point of the CASPT2 benchmark is that these are radical-radical encounters, so the DFT barriers cannot be trusted without a multireference check. The ice mantle is mimicked at several levels - 1, 2, 18 and 33 water molecules, with different reaction sites - but only the small W1 and W2 clusters are within reach of CASPT2.
reference_short: Enrique-Romero, Rimola, Ceccarelli, Ugliengo, Balucani & Skouteris, Reactivity of HCO with CH3 and NH2 on Water Ice Surfaces: A Comprehensive Accurate Quantum Chemistry Study
notes: system_class is 'molecule', not 'solid-state': the CASPT2 calculations are on gas-phase clusters of the two radicals with only one or two water molecules. The larger amorphous solid water clusters of 18 and 33 waters that model the actual grain surface are treated by DFT only.

compound_name: 2-thiouracil (2TU), ultrafast photophysics of a singly thionated uracil
geometry_source: excited-state geometries and relaxation paths computed on the fly with the Molcas-COBRAMM interface
method: CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference, run through the COBRAMM interface to Molcas for the excited-state dynamics, combined with femtosecond transient absorption experiments and global analysis of the measured spectra
software: Molcas 8 through its interface with COBRAMM
basis_set: ANO-L with contractions 5s4p2d1f on sulfur and 4s3p2d1f on carbon, oxygen and nitrogen
active_space_orbital_description: the sulfur lone pairs together with the valence pi orbitals, 12 electrons in 9 orbitals
active_space_protocol: the active space is built from the sulfur lone pairs and the valence pi orbitals, giving (12,9) for the singly thionated 2TU; the full orbital listings are in Tables S1 and S2 of the Supporting Information
electronic_structure_description: Thionation of uracil switches on efficient intersystem crossing, and this work pins down the mechanism by combining femtosecond transient absorption with CASPT2 excited-state calculations for the singly and doubly thionated species side by side, so that the effect of the second sulfur can be isolated.
reference_short: Teles-Ferreira, Conti, Borrego-Varillas, Nenov, Van Stokkum et al., A Unified Experimental/Theoretical Description of the Ultrafast Photophysics of Single and Double Thionated Uracils
notes: Companion row -b covers the doubly thionated 2,4-dithiouracil, which needs a larger space.

compound_name: 2,4-dithiouracil (24TU), ultrafast photophysics of a doubly thionated uracil
geometry_source: excited-state geometries and relaxation paths computed on the fly with the Molcas-COBRAMM interface
method: CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference, run through the COBRAMM interface to Molcas for the excited-state dynamics, combined with femtosecond transient absorption experiments and global analysis of the measured spectra
software: Molcas 8 through its interface with COBRAMM
basis_set: ANO-L with contractions 5s4p2d1f on sulfur and 4s3p2d1f on carbon, oxygen and nitrogen
active_space_orbital_description: the lone pairs of both sulfur atoms together with the valence pi orbitals, 14 electrons in 10 orbitals
active_space_protocol: the same construction principle as for 2TU - sulfur lone pairs plus valence pi orbitals - which grows to (14,10) once a second sulfur is present; orbital listings in Tables S1 and S2 of the Supporting Information
electronic_structure_description: The doubly thionated uracil is treated with the same protocol as 2TU so that the two can be compared directly; the larger active space follows from the extra sulfur lone pair rather than from a change of method.
reference_short: Teles-Ferreira, Conti, Borrego-Varillas, Nenov, Van Stokkum et al., A Unified Experimental/Theoretical Description of the Ultrafast Photophysics of Single and Double Thionated Uracils
notes: Companion row -a covers the singly thionated 2TU.

compound_name: the N(4S) + NO(X 2Pi) reaction: analytical fits of the ground (3A'') and first excited (3A') triplet potential energy surfaces, covering the N-abstraction and O-abstraction channels and the reverse reaction
geometry_source: grids of ab initio points computed over both surfaces, extending the grid of the earlier paper I, then fitted to a many-body expansion V = V(2)_NN' + V(2)_N'O + V(2)_NO + V(3)_NN'O
method: CASSCF including the lowest root in Cs symmetry for each of the two triplet surfaces, with dynamical correlation added by CASPT2 in the G2 variant; the fitted surfaces then feed variational transition-state theory calculations of thermal rate constants
active_space_orbital_description: ten electrons in nine orbitals, CAS(10,9)
active_space_protocol: a single CAS(10,9) with cc-pVTZ for every point on both surfaces, with the lowest root in Cs taken for each of 3A'' and 3A'; paper I had established that this level is accurate enough while staying cheap enough to compute the large grids both reaction channels require
nroots_per_mult: the lowest root in each Cs irreducible representation, 3A'' and 3A'
electronic_structure_description: Two new analytical surfaces are fitted, the ground 3A'' and the first excited 3A', spanning both the N-abstraction and the O-abstraction channel of N(4S) + NO(X 2Pi) as well as the reverse reaction. Beyond the kinetics, the surfaces are aimed at the reverse reaction under the non-equilibrium conditions of atmospheric re-entry vehicles.
reference_short: Gamallo, Gonzalez & Sayos, Ab initio derived analytical fits of the two lowest triplet potential energy surfaces and theoretical rate constants for the N(4S) + NO(X 2Pi) system, J. Chem. Phys. 119, 2545 (2003)

compound_name: scandium dimer Sc2, ground state and low-lying excited states
geometry_source: preliminary geometry optimizations and harmonic frequencies at B3LYP; the DMC calculations run at those optimized geometries
method: CASPT2 and CCSD(T) for the scandium atom's ground and low-lying excited states and for the two lowest states of the dimer; fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo with a Slater-Jastrow trial wave function built on CASSCF orbitals; B3LYP and UHF for comparison
software: GAMESS-US for the CASSCF/CASPT2; GAUSSIAN 03 for B3LYP, UHF and CCSD(T)
basis_set: TZVP+G(3df,2p): a Schaefer triple-zeta basis plus one diffuse s, two Wachters p sets, one diffuse pure-angular-momentum d optimized by Hay, and three uncontracted pure f sets with both tight and diffuse exponents, following Raghavachari and Trucks
active_space_orbital_description: six electrons in twelve molecular orbitals; the space initially considered held the same six electrons in eighteen orbitals, but the highest six were found to contribute negligibly and were dropped
active_space_protocol: the active space was first drawn as six electrons in 18 molecular orbitals (shown in the paper's Figure 1) and then trimmed to six electrons in 12 orbitals once the top six proved negligible; the same CASSCF orbitals also define the nodal surface of the fixed-node DMC trial wave function
electronic_structure_description: The 3Sigma_u and 5Sigma_u states of Sc2 come out close in energy by every method, but they order differently: DFT puts 5Sigma_u lowest by 0.08 eV, while DMC and CASPT2 both put 3Sigma_u lower, by 0.17 and 0.16 eV respectively. The computed frequencies and dissociation energies of both states agree with the available experiments, so the paper concludes the true ground state is 3Sigma_u - overturning the 5Sigma_u assignment (configuration 1sigma_g^2 1sigma_u^1 1pi_u^2 2sigma_g^1) that local spin density calculations and Walch et al.'s CASSCF/CI(SD) work had made to look settled. Getting the dissociation energy right requires reproducing the scandium atom's 2D -> 4F transition energy of 1.44 eV, since the ground state dissociates to excited atoms.
reference_short: Matxain, Rezabal, Lopez, Ugalde & Gagliardi, Quantum Monte Carlo study of the ground state and low-lying excited states of the scandium dimer, J. Chem. Phys. 128, 194315 (2008)
notes: nel/norb carry the final (6,12) space actually used; the initial (6,18) and the reason for trimming it are in active_space_protocol. ground_state_mult is left EMPTY on purpose: the whole point of the paper is that the ground-state multiplicity was disputed, and while it concludes 3Sigma_u, multiplicities_studied records both candidates.

compound_name: CUO, the uranium carbide oxide molecule: spin-orbit coupling and electron correlation in the assignment of its ground state
ligand_set: one carbide and one oxo ligand on a linear C-U-O axis
geometry_source: geometries optimized at the ZORA/DFT level with a gradient convergence of 1e-4 and integration accuracy 1e-10; full optimization at the correlated level was not affordable, so ECP-CASPT2 or DKH-CASPT2 structures from Roos, Widmark and Gagliardi were also considered. Because the singlet and triplet C-U bond lengths differ by about 0.10 A, adiabatic rather than vertical energy differences are essential: DC-CCSD(T) gives 15.1 kJ/mol on the singlet geometry but 40.6 kJ/mol with two separate geometries
method: four-component Dirac-Coulomb CCSD(T) as the primary method, with the spin-free (SFDC) transformed Hamiltonian used to separate spin-orbit from other relativistic effects; Fock-space multireference CCSD (MR-CCSD) run as a cross-check, computing three electron affinities of CUO+ from its 2Sigma+ ground state; DFT with several functionals for comparison
basis_set: fully uncontracted basis sets: cc-pVTZ exponents on carbon and oxygen, and either de Jong's 26s21p17d12f or Faegri's 33s29p21d15f3g1h on uranium; TZ2P in the ZORA/DFT geometry optimizations, with the C and O 1s cores and all U orbitals up to 5d frozen there
relativistic_treatment: full four-component Dirac-Coulomb Hamiltonian, with only the (LL|LL) and (SS|LL) two-electron integrals kept for efficiency - neglecting (SS|SS) costs only 0.4 percent in the energy gap; ZORA for the DFT geometries
active_space_orbital_description: for the Fock-space MR-CCSD the active virtual spinors are sigma_1/2 and phi_5/2; the correlated-electron space is chosen separately and ranges from 12 through 22 to 34 electrons
active_space_protocol: three nested choices of correlated electrons: the minimal one takes the six uranium electrons in the 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals plus the C and O 2s/2p valence, 12 electrons in all; adding the uranium subvalence 6p and the C and O 2s brings it to 22; and including core-valence correlation with the 5d and 6s electrons gives the largest space used, 34 electrons. The virtual space was truncated by deleting virtuals above 10 a.u. orbital energy. The MR-CCSD step instead defines a Fock-space model space through the active virtual spinors sigma_1/2 and phi_5/2, giving the electron affinities of CUO+ that correspond to the 1Sigma0+, 3Phi2 and 3Phi3 states.
electronic_structure_description: The paper's DC-CCSD(T) result puts the 1Sigma0+ ground state 58.2 kJ/mol below the first excited 3Phi2 state, contradicting both the earlier DFT work of Bursten (which omitted spin-orbit coupling entirely) and the CASPT2 calculations of Roos, Widmark and Gagliardi, which found the triplet lowest even before spin-orbit and about 50 kJ/mol below the singlet with it. The MR-CCSD cross-check confirms the single-reference trend at 34.3 kJ/mol. Under spin-orbit coupling the 3Phi state splits into three Omega components, of which 3Phi2 and 3Phi4 are single determinants. The singlet ground state supports reading the measured frequency shifts of CUO in various noble gas matrices as real chemical interaction between uranium and the heavier noble gases.
reference_short: Infante & Visscher, The importance of spin-orbit coupling and electron correlation in the rationalization of the ground state of the CUO molecule, J. Chem. Phys. 2004
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY and the CASPT2 numbers here are Roos/Widmark/Gagliardi's, not this paper's. What is this paper's own multireference content is a Fock-space MR-CCSD whose model space is defined by two active virtual spinors, not by an (n,m) CAS - and the authors themselves caution that 'one cannot speak of true multireference CC as symmetry prohibits mixing of the three excited states'. The 12/22/34-electron figures are correlated-electron counts for the coupled cluster, not CASSCF active spaces, and must not be read as such.

compound_name: test set for multi-state pair-density functional theory: LiF, LiH, HNCO, methylamine CH3NH2, phenol C6H5OH, O + O2 and O3 in their 3A' states, and a mixed-valence spiro cation
formula: LiF; LiH; HNCO; CH3NH2; C6H5OH; O + O2 (3A'); O3 (3A'); spiro cation
point_group: C1 for LiF, HNCO, CH3NH2 and phenol; C2v for LiH and the spiro cation; Cs for O + O2 and O3
geometry_source: potential energy curves scanned along one or two internal coordinates per system: r(LiF) 1.0-9.0 A; r(LiH) 1.0-12.0 A; r(NC) 1.25-3.00 A with tau(HNCO) 180-130 degrees; r(NH) 0.8-3.6 A with the H-C-N-H torsion at 0, 90, 95 or 100 degrees; r(OH) 0.5-3.0 A with the C-C-O-H torsion at 1 or 10 degrees; r(O1O3) 1.0-2.5 A; and the O-O-O angle from 60 to 180 degrees
method: extended multi-state pair-density functional theory (XMS-PDFT) and variational multi-state PDFT (VMS-PDFT), including the Fourier-based FMS-PDFT approximation, all built on a state-averaged CASSCF model space of the N lowest states; compared against MC-PDFT and XMS-CASPT2, the latter with an IPEA shift of 0.25 a.u.; FMS-PDFT was also implemented on top of DMRG
software: OpenMolcas v18.11 (tag 17-g792ff65), modified for FMS-PDFT/DMRG, with the QCMaquis DMRG suite
basis_set: jun-cc-pVQZ for LiF; aug-cc-pVQZ for LiH; cc-pVDZ for HNCO; 6-31++G(d,p) for CH3NH2; jul-cc-pVDZ for phenol; cc-pVTZ for O + O2 and O3; 6-31G(d) for the spiro cation
active_space_orbital_description: the active orbitals are specified per system by identity rather than by count: LiF, 8 electrons in the F 2pz and Li 2s; LiH, 2 electrons in the Li 2s, 2pz, 3s and 3pz plus the H 1s; HNCO, 16 electrons in the full valence shell (C, N, O 2s and 2p plus H 1s); CH3NH2, 6 electrons in 2 sigma, 1 sigma*, and the N 2pz, 3s and 3pz; phenol, 12 electrons in 3 pi, 3 pi*, sigma_OH, sigma*_OH, sigma_CO, sigma*_CO and the O pz; O + O2 and O3, 12 electrons in nine 2p orbitals; the spiro cation, 11 electrons in the space of the authors' earlier reference 17
active_space_protocol: one space per system with the active electron count and the identity of each active MO given in the paper's Table 1; state averaging over 2 states for LiF, HNCO, CH3NH2 and the spiro cation, 4 for LiH, 2 or 3 for phenol, and 6 for O + O2 and O3. The DMRG test on phenol reuses the same active space as the conventional FMS-PDFT calculation, with bond dimension M = 500. The PDFT on-top functional is translated PBE (tPBE). For the HNCO region r(NC) = 2.0-2.5 A at tau = 150 degrees the Fourier three-point fit fails and VMS-PDFT was run with a numerical maximization instead.
nroots_per_mult: 2 to 6 depending on the system
electronic_structure_description: LiF's avoided crossing between the ground and first excited state is the classic test: at equilibrium the ground state is ionic, the (2pz,F)2(2s,Li)0 configuration, of A1 symmetry in C2v. XMS-PDFT and VMS-PDFT succeed on every case in the set except the mixed-valence spiro cation. Since both are cheaper than XMS-CASPT2, they open well-correlated calculations on systems where the perturbation theory is unaffordable. Separately, the FMS-PDFT/DMRG and conventional-solver energies agree to within 0.04 meV; the motivation for the DMRG route is to reach much larger active spaces, the authors having previously run state-specific MC-PDFT/DMRG with 30 electrons in 30 orbitals and 34 electrons in 35 orbitals.
reference_short: Bao, Zhou, Varga, Kanchanakungwankul, Gagliardi & Truhlar, Multi-state pair-density functional theory, Faraday Discuss. 2020
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the paper gives an active electron count and a list of active orbital identities for each of eight systems but no single (n,m) pair, and the spiro cation's orbitals are only cross-referenced to an earlier paper. All eight per-system specifications are recorded in active_space_orbital_description.

compound_name: charge-transfer excitations in a dipeptide, a beta-dipeptide, a tripeptide, and the organic donor-acceptor molecules PP and DMABN
geometry_source: not stated in the text read
method: time-dependent range-separated density functional theory in which the long-range part is treated by MP2 or by a multiconfigurational self-consistent field wave function, with a spin-independent short-range exchange-correlation functional of Goll et al. based on PBE; DDCI2 and CASPT2 values used for comparison
basis_set: Dunning cc-pVTZ for all the molecules of Figure 1 (6-31G* and 6-31+G* also appear in the work)
active_space_orbital_description: a small CAS per system: (4,4) for the dipeptide and the beta-dipeptide, (6,6) for the tripeptide, and (8,8) for both organic molecules PP and DMABN
active_space_protocol: CAS(4,4) for the dipeptide and beta-dipeptide, CAS(6,6) for the tripeptide, CAS(8,8) for PP and DMABN, all with cc-pVTZ and the range-separation parameter mu = 0.4. Comparison values quoted in the tables come from DDCI2 on an underlying CAS(12,12) and from CASPT2(12,12).
electronic_structure_description: Charge-transfer excitation energies are the target, because they are where conventional TDDFT fails. For one of the systems the S0 -> S1 excitation comes out at 2.29 eV (oscillator strength 1.597) and S0 -> S2 at 3.63 eV (0.522) with this approach, against reference values of 2.27 and 3.07 eV. For the same S0 -> S1 excitation, CASPT2(12,12) from the literature gives 2.32 eV, a regular CAS(6,6) in this work gives 3.63 eV, and B3LYP gives 2.48 eV - an illustration of how sensitive the answer is to the size of the space.
reference_short: Assessment of charge-transfer excitations with time-dependent, range-separated density functional theory based on long-range MP2 and multiconfigurational self-consistent field wave functions, J. Chem. Phys. 2013
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the space varies with the system - (4,4), (6,6) or (8,8) - and all three are recorded in active_space_protocol. The CAS(12,12) and CASPT2(12,12) numbers in the comparison tables are taken from the literature, not computed here.

compound_name: tryptophan, environment-driven coherent population transfer in its ultrafast photophysics
geometry_source: ground-state geometry at the MP2 level; excited-state geometries optimized at the SS-CASPT2 level
method: single-state CASPT2 (SS-CASPT2) for the excited-state geometry optimizations and the excited-state energetics, with the Cholesky decomposition used to speed up the atomic integrals; combined with femtosecond transient absorption experiments
active_space_orbital_description: 10 electrons in nine orbitals, written by the paper in RAS notation as (0|10,9|0), comprising all of the valence pi orbitals
active_space_protocol: a single (0|10,9|0) space - no RAS1 or RAS3 orbitals, so effectively a CAS(10,9) - covering all the valence pi orbitals, used for both the excited-state optimizations and the subsequent CASPT2 energies
electronic_structure_description: The ultrafast photophysics of tryptophan is governed by coherent population transfer between the close-lying excited states, and the paper's point is that the surrounding environment is what drives it - so the same chromophore behaves differently depending on its solvation.
reference_short: Jaiswal, Kabacinski, Nogly et al., Environment-Driven Coherent Population Transfer Governs the Ultrafast Photophysics of Tryptophan, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2022
notes: The (0|10,9|0) notation is RAS-style with empty RAS1 and RAS3, i.e. a plain CAS(10,9); recorded as such.

compound_name: eleven fourth-row transition metal diatomics with singlet or doublet ground states - CuCl, CuF, CuH, ScF, ScH, ScO, ScS, TiN, ZnH, ZnO and ZnS - reference vertical excitation energies
formula: CuCl; CuF; CuH; ScF; ScH; ScO; ScS; TiN; ZnH; ZnO; ZnS
geometry_source: ground-state geometries optimized in the frozen-core approximation at CC3/aug-cc-pVTZ for the singlets and UCCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ for the doublets, with large frozen cores systematically chosen; optimized bond lengths tabulated alongside experimental values
method: state-averaged CASSCF references followed by CASPT2 in the RS2 contraction scheme with the default IPEA shift of 0.25 Eh and a systematic level shift of 0.3 Eh against intruder states, plus partially contracted NEVPT2 and NOIPEA CASPT2 variants; benchmarked against high-order coupled cluster (CC3, CCSDT, CC4, CCSDTQ) and, in some cases, selected-CI FCI estimates from CIPSI
software: molpro for CASPT2; cfour and gaussian16 for the geometries; cfour, psi4 and mrcc for the coupled-cluster work; quantum package for the CIPSI calculations
basis_set: two diffuse-containing Dunning sets throughout, aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ
relativistic_treatment: none: relativistic effects are deliberately not included, since the comparisons are theory against theory
