active_space_orbital_description: chosen per molecule from the metal d orbitals and the orbitals involved in the ligand interaction; the paper discusses the principle but does not tabulate the sizes in the text read
active_space_protocol: a state-averaged CASSCF including the ground state and at least the excited states of interest, with additional states added in some cases to cure convergence and root-flipping problems; the CASPT2 step then uses RS2 contraction with IPEA 0.25 Eh and a 0.3 Eh level shift. The paper notes explicitly that for transition metal compounds the space typically involves the metal d orbitals plus the ligand-interaction orbitals, and that sizing it is a delicate balance.
electronic_structure_description: Theoretical best estimates of the vertical transition energies are established for these eleven diatomics from the coupled-cluster hierarchy and CIPSI, then used to score the multiconfigurational methods. Against the safe TBEs, CC3 reaches a mean absolute error of 0.02 eV with a slightly negatively skewed error distribution (MSE -0.02 eV); the CASPT2 (with and without IPEA) and the SC- and PC-NEVPT2 error distributions are reported alongside. The set is offered as an enrichment of the QUEST database, which had contained no transition metal compounds.
reference_short: Jacquemin, Boggio-Pasqua & Loos, Reference Vertical Excitation Energies for Transition Metal Compounds
notes: QUEST-SERIES paper (an explicit extension of the QUEST database to transition metal compounds), so this row must be dropped when exporting to casscf-agent's literature.csv. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active space is chosen per molecule and the sizes are not given in the text read - they are presumably in the supporting information.

compound_name: [Fe(NCH)6]2+, a model for light-induced excited spin-state trapping (LIESST) in [Fe(ptz)6](BF4)2: low-spin to high-spin photoswitching
ligand_set: six HCN ligands coordinating through nitrogen, a minimal model of the six 1-propyltetrazole ligands of the real complex
geometry_source: nuclear motion sampled from full-dimensional trajectory surface hopping simulations; the three dominant Fe-N stretching modes nu13, nu14 and nu15 selected for the reduced-dimensional quantum dynamics, with CASSCF/CASPT2 scans along the most important coordinates
method: spin-vibronic quantum dynamics on CASSCF/CASPT2 potentials with spin-orbit couplings computed as a function of nuclear geometry; the Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian with a one-electron effective mean-field spin-orbit Hamiltonian and spin-orbit state interaction (SO-SI); CASPT2 with a 0.2 a.u. imaginary shift and a 0.25 a.u. IPEA shift
basis_set: ANO-RCC with contractions 7s6p5d4f3g2h on Fe, 4s3p2d1f on N, 4s3p1d on C and 2s1p on H
active_space_orbital_description: 14 electrons in 12 orbitals: the five Fe 3d and five Fe 4d orbitals, two sigma(Fe-N) bonding orbitals, and a correlating pair of Fe 3s/4s orbitals
active_space_protocol: a single 14e,12o space with the double-shell 3d/4d pair, the two Fe-N sigma bonding orbitals and the 3s/4s correlating pair; CASPT2 on top with imaginary shift 0.2 a.u. and IPEA 0.25 a.u.
nroots_per_mult: 37 spin-vibronic states in the dynamics: 1 singlet ground state, 3 for 1T1g, 9 for 3T1g, 9 for 3T2g and 15 for 5T2g
electronic_structure_description: The LIESST mechanism converts the 1A1g low-spin ground state to the 5T2g high-spin state through the triplet manifold, and the simulation follows that cascade explicitly: the electronic state index runs 1 (ground state), 2-4 (1T1g), 5-13 (3T1g), 14-22 (3T2g) and 23-37 (5T2g). Full-dimensional quantum dynamics is out of reach for this complex, so the three dominant modes are picked from the trajectory surface hopping normal-mode activity - all three are Fe-N stretches - and the spin-orbit couplings are analysed as functions of those coordinates, in absolute value because the real or imaginary part (or both) cancels. [Fe(ptz)6](BF4)2 is the complex on which LIESST was first observed, which is why this model was chosen.
reference_short: Papai, Toward Simulation of Fe(II) Low-Spin to High-Spin Photoswitching by Synergistic Spin-Vibronic Dynamics, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2022, 18, 1329

compound_name: extended benchmark set of doubly excited states in small and medium organic molecules (QUEST double excitations, improved and extended)
formula: small and medium organic molecules of the QUEST doubles set
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of the QUEST benchmark protocol
method: CASSCF references followed by CASPT2 and CASPT3, both with and without the IPEA shift (default 0.25 Eh) and with a 0.3 a.u. level shift, plus partially contracted and strongly contracted NEVPT2; the Fock operator in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian is systematically built from the state-specific density. Benchmarked against selected-CI (CIPSI) and the high-order coupled cluster hierarchy EOM-CC3, EOM-CCSDT, EOM-CC4 and EOM-CCSDTQ, with the %T1 diagnostic from CC3/AVTZ used to classify a state as singly or doubly excited
software: molpro for the multiconfigurational calculations (dalton also used)
basis_set: 6-31+G*, aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ, with cc-pV5Z appearing for some systems
active_space_orbital_description: a separate active space per system, per symmetry representation and per transition; the full description is given in the Supporting Information
active_space_protocol: active spaces are chosen individually for each system, each symmetry representation and each transition, following the protocol of the authors' earlier work; the SI carries the complete listing. The paper stresses that careful selection is what makes doubly excited states reachable at manageable cost, and that 0.1-0.2 eV accuracy is achievable with appropriate spaces. Whether the 3s Rydberg orbital is included in the space materially changes the answer: leave it out and a single genuine double excitation appears, put it in and the doubly excited configuration mixes with the Rydberg one.
electronic_structure_description: For one of the difficult cases the two computed states at 7.979(40) and 8.170(41) eV from CIPSI agree well with the reference 7.979 and 8.185 eV. Both states carry important singly and doubly excited configurations, combined in phase for the lower state and out of phase for the upper one; the mixing is weak at CASSCF and becomes pronounced only after the perturbative correction. Enlarging the basis from 6-31+G* to aug-cc-pVDZ or aug-cc-pVTZ stabilizes the (n -> 3s) Rydberg configuration relative to the (n,n -> pi*,pi*) one and suppresses the strong mixing - 6-31+G* is simply too compact to model it. Downgrading to CC4 or CCSDT also unmixes the two configurations, giving one genuine double and one Rydberg single; oddly the mixing returns at CC3, but for the wrong reason.
reference_short: Loos, Boggio-Pasqua, Jacquemin et al., Reference Energies for Double Excitations: Improvement and Extension
notes: QUEST-SERIES paper (the doubles subset of the QUEST database, extending 10.1021/acs.jctc.8b01205 which is already on the export-filter list), so this row must be dropped when exporting to casscf-agent's literature.csv. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the space differs per system, per symmetry and per transition, and the listing lives in the SI.

compound_name: the phenyl + propargyl radical-radical reaction and its diradical intermediates on the molecular-weight-growth pathway
geometry_source: geometries, frequencies and zero-point energies from CASSCF(12e,12o) for the diradical species; B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) elsewhere
method: a composite triplet-singlet gap treatment applied wherever the T1 diagnostic exceeded 0.02 and indicated diradical character: CASPT2(12e,12o)/cc-pVTZ combined with CCSD(T)-F12/cc-pVTZ-F12, on CASSCF(12e,12o) geometries; single-reference CCSD(T)-F12 elsewhere
software: not stated in the text read
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the CASPT2 and cc-pVTZ-F12 for the CCSD(T)-F12 component; 6-311G(d,p) for the B3LYP geometries
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 12 orbitals, the pi electron system of the reacting species
active_space_protocol: the (12e,12o) space is invoked selectively - only where the T1 diagnostic is above 0.02 and the wave function has diradical character does the composite CASPT2(12e,12o)/cc-pVTZ + CCSD(T)-F12/cc-pVTZ-F12 triplet-singlet gap method replace the single-reference treatment, with CASSCF(12e,12o) supplying the geometries, frequencies and zero-point energies for those species
electronic_structure_description: Phenyl plus propargyl is a radical-radical step in molecular weight growth toward polycyclic aromatics, and its intermediates include diradicals that single-reference coupled cluster cannot describe. The T1 diagnostic is used as the trigger for switching to the multireference composite scheme, so the (12,12) space is applied exactly where the wave function needs it.
reference_short: Selby, Goulay, Soorkia, Ray, Jasper, Klippenstein, Morozov, Mebel et al., Radical-Radical Reactions in Molecular Weight Growth: The Phenyl + Propargyl Reaction

compound_name: lambda-DFVB(U) test set: the diatomics H2, F2, HF, N2, O2, S2 and SiO, plus SiH4, C3H4 and C2H2O2, the AE6 atomization set, atomic excitation energies, and nucleophilic substitution reaction barriers
formula: H2; F2; HF; N2; O2; S2; SiO; SiH4; C3H4; C2H2O2; AE6 molecules
geometry_source: potential energy curves scanned from the equilibrium geometry to the dissociation limit for each diatomic; accurate reference curves for H2, F2, HF and N2 taken from the literature and for O2 from a separate source
method: lambda-DFVB(U), a hybrid density functional valence bond method that uses the unpaired electron density to scale the correlation functional, with spin densities built from the unpaired density to address the symmetry dilemma; benchmarked against VBSCF, lambda-DFVB(IS), KS-DFT and CASPT2
software: OpenMolcas v19.11 for the CASPT2, with an imaginary shift of 0.2 hartree and the default IPEA shift of 0.25 hartree; XMVB for the VBSCF and lambda-DFVB(U); Gaussian 16 for the KS-DFT
active_space_orbital_description: the space is defined by chemical role rather than by a fixed count: for the diatomics and SiH4, the atomic orbitals and electrons that take part in bonding; for C3H4 and C2H2O2, all bonding electrons and orbitals except those of the C-H bonds; for atomic excitation energies, all valence electrons and orbitals; for the reactions, the orbitals and electrons describing the bond being formed or broken
active_space_protocol: one space per system chosen by the rules above, with the full VB structure set in that space using overlap-enhanced orbitals; the size of the active space and the number of VB structures for every tested system are tabulated in the supplementary material. The same spaces underlie the CASPT2 comparison calculations.
electronic_structure_description: Mean absolute errors along the potential energy curves between equilibrium and dissociation (kcal/mol): VBSCF gives 5.2, 7.0, 13.6, 14.8 and 19.5 for H2, F2, HF, N2 and O2; lambda-DFVB(IS) gives 1.3, 1.3, 4.1, 9.2 and 6.3; lambda-DFVB(U) gives 3.6, 0.7, 2.2, 2.7 and 4.1; and CASPT2 gives 1.6, 0.9, 3.3, 6.6 and 2.7 - so the new method is competitive with CASPT2 curve by curve. On the AE6 atomization set VBSCF's 14.9 kcal/mol MAE reflects its missing dynamic correlation, which lambda-DFVB(U) recovers to the tune of about 10 kcal/mol. For reaction barriers, where transition states have high multireference character and need static and dynamic correlation in balance, CASPT2 is best at 1.4 kcal/mol MAE, VBSCF worst at 10.6, and lambda-DFVB(U) reaches 2.7 - at roughly the cost of VBSCF, since the Hartree-exchange-correlation energy needs only the 1-particle density.
reference_short: Zheng, Gan, Zhou, Su et al., lambda-DFVB(U): A hybrid density functional valence bond method based on unpaired electron density, J. Chem. Phys. 156, 204103 (2022)
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active space is specified per system by chemical role (bonding orbitals, valence shell, or the bond being made or broken) and the actual sizes are tabulated only in the supplementary material.

compound_name: 2,3-diamino-1,4-benzoquinone (DAPBQ), a captodatively stabilized biradicaloid tested as a singlet fission chromophore
geometry_source: ground and excited state geometries optimized at CASPT2/ANO-L-VTZP, run numerically because CASPT2 analytical gradients are unavailable in MOLCAS 8.0; two possible crystal structures of DAPBQ computed at the DFT level, with the most favourable molecular pair identified for the dynamics
method: state-specific CASSCF references with CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0.25 a.u.) and, at the CASPT2 geometries, partially and strongly contracted NEVPT2; all orbitals except the 1s cores correlated in the perturbation step. The excited-state dynamics of a DAPBQ dimer embedded in the crystal was then run by semiempirical QM/MM trajectory surface hopping
software: MOLCAS 8.0 for CASSCF/CASPT2; MOLPRO 2015.1 for NEVPT2
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 12 orbitals, split 8 and 4; the S0 natural orbitals closely resemble the active orbitals of 2,3-dichloro-1,4-benzoquinone from the benchmark calculations and do not differ qualitatively from those of S1 and T1
active_space_protocol: a state-specific CASSCF with 12 electrons in 12 orbitals (8 and 4) for the CASPT2 and NEVPT2 work; the semiempirical dynamics instead uses a 6-electron, 4-orbital space, whose vertical and adiabatic S1 and T1 energies for the monomer agree well with the CASPT2 results (other semiempirical Hamiltonians and space choices were less accurate)
electronic_structure_description: The CASPT2 excitation energies say the first adiabatic energy condition for singlet fission is not met, contradicting the earlier conclusion of Wen et al., who used a smaller basis (ANO-S-VDZP) and a smaller active space (12 electrons in 10 orbitals). This work's S1 energies - 2.44 eV vertical and 1.68 eV adiabatic - are markedly below the 2.63 and 2.23 eV reported there, and the gap survives even allowing a 0.3 eV systematic error in the adiabatic value. The first singlet and triplet excited states of DAPBQ are mainly single excitations. The subsequent QM/MM surface hopping simulation of the crystal dimer confirms the verdict: crystalline DAPBQ does not undergo singlet fission.
reference_short: Accomasso, Granucci, Havenith & Persico, Testing new chromophores for singlet fission: a computational protocol applied to 2,3-diamino-1,4-benzoquinone, Chem. Phys. 2018
notes: nel/norb carry the (12,12) space of the ab initio CASPT2/NEVPT2 work; the smaller (6,4) space of the semiempirical dynamics and the (12,10) of the contradicted earlier study are both in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: indigo and its isomers epindolidione and indirubin: excited-state intramolecular proton transfer and nonradiative deactivation
formula: C16H10N2O2 (indigo, epindolidione and indirubin are isomers)
geometry_source: S1 geometries optimized with TDDFT (CAM-B3LYP); the S1/S0 conical intersections optimized with CASSCF; single-proton-transfer paths on S1 scanned with TDDFT/CAM-B3LYP by taking the difference of the N-H and O-H distances as the reaction coordinate and optimizing the remaining degrees of freedom on S1
method: MS-CASPT2 energies on CASSCF-optimized conical intersection structures, with TDDFT/CAM-B3LYP for the S1 surface and the proton-transfer profiles
software: Molpro 2015.1 for CASSCF and MS-CASPT2; GAMESS for the TDDFT
active_space_orbital_description: a minimal (2,2) space, used for both the CASSCF and the MS-CASPT2 calculations
active_space_protocol: a (2,2) active space throughout the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 work, sufficient because the multireference character being described is the single bond that changes on proton transfer at the S1/S0 crossing
electronic_structure_description: Both TDDFT and MS-CASPT2 agree that indigo and indirubin have a lower barrier to excited-state intramolecular proton transfer, NH to CO, than epindolidione does. The energy of the S1/S0 conical intersection relative to the post-transfer minimum is highest for epindolidione. Together these say nonradiative deactivation is more efficient in indigo and indirubin - which matches the experimental picture that epindolidione's fluorescence quantum yield is far larger than indigo's, while indirubin's is very small.
reference_short: Sakiyama & Bannno, Theoretical Study on the Pathway of Nonradiative Deactivation in Indigo and Its Isomers, J. Comput. Chem. Jpn. 17 (2018)
notes: Japanese-language short paper; the PDF text extracts as mojibake in places, but the method sentence giving the (2,2) space, the Sapporo-DZP-2012 basis and the Molpro 2015.1 / GAMESS split is legible.

compound_name: molecular organic crystals of benzene, naphthalene and triazine (plus the benzene dimer): excited states under point-charge embedding schemes
formula: benzene; benzene dimer; naphthalene; triazine, embedded in their molecular crystals
geometry_source: molecules and dimers taken from the molecular crystal structures, with the crystal environment represented by embedding point charges from several different schemes
method: state-averaged CASSCF excited states in a point-charge embedded environment, testing how the choice of embedding charges changes the excitation energies; the paper notes that the spectra of these crystals are only reproduced accurately once the excited states are computed with CASSCF
basis_set: Dunning cc-pVDZ through aug-cc-pVQZ and Pople 6-31G through 6-311++G** sets appear across the study
active_space_orbital_description: the pi valence electrons in each case: CAS(6,6) for benzene, CAS(12,12) for the benzene dimer, CAS(10,10) for naphthalene and CAS(12,9) for triazine
active_space_protocol: one pi-valence space per system - (6,6), (12,12), (10,10) and (12,9) for benzene, the benzene dimer, naphthalene and triazine respectively - with state-averaged CASSCF used for benzene, the benzene dimer and naphthalene
electronic_structure_description: The question is how much of the excited-state energy in a molecular organic crystal is captured by embedding the chromophore in point charges, and which scheme of charges to use. Because these are pi-pi* excitations in stacked aromatics, a multiconfigurational treatment is needed - single-reference methods do not reproduce the measured spectra - so CASSCF in the embedded environment is the reference against which the embedding schemes are scored.
reference_short: Sidat, Ingham, Rivera, Misquitta & Crespo-Otero, Performance of point charge embedding schemes for excited states in molecular organic crystals, J. Chem. Phys. 2023
notes: SOLID-STATE: these are chromophores embedded in molecular organic crystals with point-charge environments, not isolated gas-phase molecules. nel/norb are left EMPTY because the space differs per system; all four are in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: triplet energy transfer beyond the Dexter limit: the iridium photosensitizers Ir(ppy)3 and Ir[dFppy]2(dtbbpy)(PF6), the acceptors 4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-2-styryl-1,3,2-dioxaborolane and 3-phenylbenzo[d]isothiazole-1,1-dioxide, and their encounter complexes
ligand_set: tris(2-phenylpyridine) on one photosensitizer; two difluorophenylpyridines plus a di-tert-butylbipyridine with hexafluorophosphate on the other
geometry_source: stationary points optimized at single-reference (PBE0-D3BJ) levels with PCM in dichloromethane; same-multiplicity conical intersections located with the Constraints keyword of OpenMolcas together with state-averaged CASSCF, and different-multiplicity crossings first found with sobMECP then refined with SA-CASSCF; intrinsic reaction coordinates connect the stationary points into a minimum energy pathway
method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2), interpreted within the Marcus electron transfer framework and combined with ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy and electrochemistry; Cholesky decomposition with dynamically generated unbiased auxiliary basis sets used for the integrals
software: OpenMolcas / Molcas for the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2; Gaussian for the DFT optimizations
basis_set: mixed BS-1 for the optimizations: Stuttgart ECP60MWB with its (8s7p6d2f1g)/[6s5p3d2f1g] basis on iridium and all-electron 6-31G(d) on C, H, F, B, O, S and N; single points use the same ECP on Ir with the larger 6-311+G(d,p) on the non-metal elements
relativistic_treatment: Stuttgart ECP60MWB effective core potential on iridium
active_space_orbital_description: the size and composition of the active space were fixed by a configuration-selection and orbital-localization strategy so that the active orbitals are the ones directly involved in the triplet energy transfer; the testing and selection process is documented in the Supporting Information
active_space_protocol: active spaces chosen per system (the two isolated substrates, the two photosensitizers, and their encounter complexes) by the authors' own configuration-selection plus orbital-localization procedure, benchmarked for a balance of cost and accuracy; state-averaged optimization throughout, on geometries from single-reference optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Persistent inconsistencies in photosensitized [2+2] cycloadditions motivate looking past the Dexter picture of triplet-triplet energy transfer. MS-CASPT2 plus transient absorption uncover two previously unrecognized pathways: a charge-transfer trap mechanism, and a CT-mediated sequential TTEnT in which separate electron- and hole-transfer steps bridge the donor and acceptor triplets. The two acceptors were chosen for their contrasting redox potentials, electronic structure and steric profiles, so that steric, electronic and energetic contributions to the transfer efficiency can be separated.
reference_short: Liu, Shi, Jie, Liu, Wang, Qiao, Feng, Fang, Su & Chen, A Charge Transfer Mediated Sequential Triplet Energy Transfer Model Beyond the Dexter Limit in Organic Photocatalysis, JACS Au 2025, 5, 5481-5492
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the paper describes its active-space selection procedure in the main text but puts the resulting sizes only in the Supporting Information. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty because the row spans two iridium complexes and two purely organic acceptors.

compound_name: benzonitrile anion, CN- formation in electron collisions with benzonitrile
geometry_source: structures optimized in Gaussian 16
method: CASPT2 for the anionic species, on top of a CASSCF reference, with all core orbitals frozen
software: OpenMolcas for the CASPT2; Gaussian 16 for the optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: 9 electrons in 15 orbitals, with all core orbitals kept frozen
active_space_protocol: a single 9-electron, 15-orbital space for the anion species, all core orbitals frozen, with ANO-S
electronic_structure_description: Dissociative electron attachment to benzonitrile produces CN-, and the mechanism is revisited here against the measured ion yield as a function of electron energy. The CASPT2 treatment is applied to the anionic states because the transient negative ion is where a single-reference description fails.
reference_short: Revisiting CN- Formation Mechanisms in Electron Collisions with Benzonitrile, ChemPhysChem 2025
notes: ground_state_mult is left EMPTY: the row covers the anionic species formed on electron attachment, and the paper does not state the multiplicity explicitly; multiplicities_studied records the doublet character of the transient anion.

compound_name: Thiel's benchmark set of 28 closed-shell organic molecules: 223 vertical excitation energies evaluated with fourth-order NEVPT
formula: the 28 closed-shell organic molecules of the Thiel benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the original Thiel benchmark study
method: approximate fourth-order N-electron valence perturbation theory, NEVPT4(SD): the fully internally contracted fourth-order NEVPT with the excitation space restricted to the first-order interacting space of internally contracted singles and doubles from the CASSCF reference, with the fourth-order renormalization terms dropped to keep size consistency in the absence of quadruples; compared against lower-order NEVPT variants, published CASPT2 results, and CC3 reference data
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of the earlier NEVPT study of Schapiro et al. on this benchmark set, chosen per molecule and not restated here
active_space_protocol: the protocol follows Schapiro et al., with state-averaged CASSCF used whenever several roots of the same symmetry are needed; although ORCA can state-average across different spatial and spin symmetries, the calculations were deliberately run separately per symmetry to allow direct comparison with the original work. Two protocols for the vertical energies: for excitations within the ground-state irreducible representation the ground-state energy comes from the state-averaged calculation, and a different route is used otherwise.
electronic_structure_description: Across 223 vertical excitation energies spanning pi -> pi*, n -> pi* and sigma -> pi* transitions in 28 molecules, NEVPT4(SD) systematically outperforms both the lower-order NEVPT variants and previously reported CASPT2 results, for singlets and triplets alike. The residual error is structured rather than random: n -> pi* transitions are overestimated by about 0.1 eV while pi -> pi* transitions are underestimated by about 0.04 eV. That shift persists at every NEVPT order but shrinks as the order increases.
reference_short: Kempfer, Sivalingam & Neese, Evaluation of Approximate Fourth-Order N-Electron Valence Perturbation Theory (NEVPT4(SD)) for the Excited States of Organic Molecules, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 21, 12185
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active spaces are inherited per molecule from Schapiro et al.'s earlier NEVPT study of the same benchmark set and are not restated in this paper.

compound_name: Schreiber (Thiel) benchmark set of organic molecules: correlated oscillator strengths and triplet excitation energies from adiabatic connection approaches on CAS wave functions
formula: the organic molecules of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
method: adiabatic connection (AC) correlation energy methods AC0 and AC0D built on extended random phase approximation (ERPA) with complete active space reference wave functions, plus a new perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrix for the oscillator strengths; benchmarked against CASPT2, LR-CC2, LR-CCSD, CCSD and FCI values
basis_set: the basis sets of the Schreiber et al. benchmark protocol (TZVP)
active_space_orbital_description: complete active spaces per molecule as in the benchmark protocol; the methods are designed so that cost grows more slowly with the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 or NEVPT2 do
active_space_protocol: state-averaged CASSCF reference states from the ground state up to the target state I are required for an AC0D excitation energy; because AC0 and AC0D depend only on reduced density matrices up to second order, they scale far better in the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 and NEVPT2, whose cost confines them in practice to roughly 20 active electrons
electronic_structure_description: Oscillator strengths computed from the perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrices, together with AC0 and AC0D excitation energies, match CASPT2 accuracy at lower cost, and the corrected transition dipole moments come essentially free because every intermediate is already available from the AC0 energy calculation. For triplet excitations on the Schreiber set, the deexcitation correction in AC0D genuinely improves on AC0, especially for the lowest excited states, where the accuracy becomes comparable to LR-CC2 and LR-CCSD - with the difference that AC0 and AC0D remain multireference methods. The perturbation-corrected transition density matrices also beat the uncorrected ERPA ones against CCSD and FCI in matching basis sets.
reference_short: Drwal, Pernal & Pastorczak, Multireference Correlated Oscillator Strengths from Adiabatic Connection Approaches Based on Extended Random Phase Approximation, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20, 3659-3668
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active spaces come from the Schreiber et al. benchmark protocol and differ per molecule; they are not restated here.

compound_name: four-membered heterocyclic peroxide (1,2-dioxetane-type), nonadiabatic dissociation dynamics from a transition state
geometry_source: the O-O transition state in S0 and the C-C transition states in T1 and S1 optimized with SA-CASSCF/6-31G and MS-CASPT2/ANO-RCC-VDZP respectively; trajectories launched from the transition state with a generalized initial velocity sampling scheme
method: state-averaged CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 for the stationary points, then trajectory surface hopping nonadiabatic molecular dynamics with an energy-based decoherence correction, run in SHARC 2.1 coupled to calibrated SA-CASSCF/6-31G with scaled spin-orbit couplings; velocity-Verlet integration at 0.5 fs, with the momentum after a hop adjusted along the projected nonadiabatic coupling to conserve nuclear angular momentum
software: OpenMolcas 21.06 for the electronic structure; SHARC 2.1 for the dynamics
basis_set: 6-31G for the SA-CASSCF optimizations and the dynamics; ANO-RCC-VDZP for the MS-CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 10 orbitals: four sigma and four sigma* orbitals of the four-membered ring, plus the two oxygen lone-pair occupied orbitals perpendicular to the ring
active_space_protocol: a single 12-electron, 10-orbital space for all the stationary-point optimizations; the dynamics uses calibrated SA-CASSCF/6-31G with scaled spin-orbit couplings. An earlier simulation of the same system used a much smaller SA8-CASSCF(8e,6o)/STO-3G+6-31G* treatment.
electronic_structure_description: The dissociation runs mainly through the S0 <-> T1 and T2 <-> T1 crossings, and the paper shows how the initial velocity sampling at the transition state controls the outcome: with more extra positive initial velocity the quantum yields shift, the dissociation half-time and the average number of surface hops per trajectory fall, and the S0 <-> T1 and T2 <-> T1 transitions become less frequent. The number of active states also affects the yields and dissociation times. Including all the different total initial kinetic energies together with extra positive initial velocities brings the simulated triplet excitation yield into close agreement with the measured value of 0.20; the corresponding singlet quantum yields are 0.127, 0.172 and 0.182, against 0.101 from the earlier SA8-CASSCF(8e,6o) simulation.
reference_short: Zhou, Shu, Michaels, Yang & Prezhdo, Generalized Velocity Sampling at a Transition State and Nonadiabatic Dynamics of Four-Membered Heterocyclic Peroxides, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2025, 16, 3473-3482

compound_name: Fe-MOF-74 cluster model, bare metal site (singlet)
ligand_set: the carboxylate/phenolate coordination sphere of the MOF-74 framework around an open Fe site
geometry_source: a small cluster model of Fe-MOF-74 previously used to represent the reaction center, chosen small enough that full wave-function energies remain computable for comparison
method: CASPT2 embedded in DFT (M06 functional) through the Huzinaga level-shift projection operator scheme; initial CCSD(T) calculations on the model showed that a multireference treatment was necessary for the adsorption interaction
basis_set: cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ, aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ across the study
active_space_orbital_description: 6 electrons in 5 orbitals, the Fe 3d manifold
active_space_protocol: the CAS is deliberately limited to the Fe 3d orbitals because the adsorption is localized on the metal; the wave-function subsystem carries a +2 charge matching the iron oxidation state, with -2 on the DFT region to keep the whole system neutral
electronic_structure_description: The embedding reproduces the full-system CASPT2 result with only the metal centre in the wave-function subsystem, which is the point of the method: multireference energies for a system far too large to treat entirely at that level. The convergence behaviour matches the other test systems, and the case reinforces the authors' rule of thumb for how to charge the subsystems.
reference_short: Robust, Accurate, and Efficient: Quantum Embedding Using the Huzinaga Level-Shift Projection Operator
notes: SOLID-STATE: a cluster model of the Fe-MOF-74 metal-organic framework, not a gas-phase molecule. Companion row -b is the same model with H2 bound.

compound_name: Fe-MOF-74 cluster model with molecular hydrogen bound at the open metal site
ligand_set: the MOF-74 coordination sphere plus an adsorbed H2 molecule at the open Fe site
geometry_source: a small cluster model of Fe-MOF-74 previously used to represent the reaction center, chosen small enough that full wave-function energies remain computable for comparison
method: CASPT2 embedded in DFT (M06 functional) through the Huzinaga level-shift projection operator scheme; initial CCSD(T) calculations on the model showed that a multireference treatment was necessary for the adsorption interaction
basis_set: cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ, aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ across the study
active_space_orbital_description: 8 electrons in 7 orbitals: the Fe 3d orbitals together with the bound hydrogen 1s orbitals
active_space_protocol: the space grows from (6,5) to (8,7) on binding H2, adding the hydrogen 1s orbitals to the Fe 3d manifold; the same +2 / -2 subsystem charging is used
electronic_structure_description: The hydrogen adsorption energy on Fe-MOF-74 needs a multireference wave function - CCSD(T) on the model already signalled that - and the embedded CASPT2 delivers it at a fraction of the cost, agreeing closely with full-system CASPT2 when only the metal and the adsorbed hydrogen sit in the wave-function region.
reference_short: Robust, Accurate, and Efficient: Quantum Embedding Using the Huzinaga Level-Shift Projection Operator
notes: SOLID-STATE: a cluster model of the Fe-MOF-74 metal-organic framework with an adsorbate. Companion row -a is the bare model.

compound_name: NbSi5- anion cluster, electronic states behind the photoelectron spectrum
geometry_source: geometries and vibrational frequencies of the electronic states optimized with DFT; CASSCF/CASPT2 single points on those structures
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, used to assign the features of the anion photoelectron spectrum; DFT and CCSD(T) for the structures and ground-state properties
basis_set: ANO-RCC with contraction 8s7p5d3f2g1h for Nb and 6s5p3d2f1g for Si
active_space_orbital_description: 15 orbitals drawn from a pool of 21 valence orbitals, comprising the Nb 4d and 5s orbitals and the Si 3p orbitals
active_space_protocol: 16 electrons in the 15-orbital space for the anion; the same 15 orbitals, selected from 21 valence orbitals (Nb 4d and 5s, Si 3p), serve both charge states
electronic_structure_description: The anion's ground state is the 1A1 state of a tetragonal bipyramidal isomer of C4v symmetry. The adiabatic and vertical detachment energies from this state to the neutral ground state are 2.72 and 2.74 eV. The CASSCF/CASPT2 excited states are what allow every feature of the measured anion photoelectron spectrum to be assigned - something DFT and CCSD(T), which had already fixed the structures, could not do.
reference_short: Tran Van Tan et al., Quantum chemical study of NbSi5(-/0) clusters, Dong Thap University Journal of Science 14 (5) (2025) 75-87
notes: Vietnamese/English bilingual paper. Companion row -b is the neutral cluster, which shares the 15-orbital space with one electron fewer.

geometry_source: geometries and vibrational frequencies of the electronic states optimized with DFT; CASSCF/CASPT2 single points on those structures
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, used to assign the features of the anion photoelectron spectrum; DFT and CCSD(T) for the structures and ground-state properties
basis_set: ANO-RCC with contraction 8s7p5d3f2g1h for Nb and 6s5p3d2f1g for Si
active_space_orbital_description: 15 orbitals drawn from a pool of 21 valence orbitals, comprising the Nb 4d and 5s orbitals and the Si 3p orbitals
active_space_protocol: 15 electrons in the same 15-orbital space used for the anion, drawn from 21 valence orbitals (Nb 4d and 5s, Si 3p)
electronic_structure_description: The neutral cluster's ground state is the 2B1 state of the same C4v tetragonal bipyramidal isomer; it is the final state of the detachment transitions whose ADE and VDE are 2.72 and 2.74 eV.
reference_short: Tran Van Tan et al., Quantum chemical study of NbSi5(-/0) clusters, Dong Thap University Journal of Science 14 (5) (2025) 75-87
notes: Vietnamese/English bilingual paper. Companion row -a is the anion.

compound_name: the simplest Criegee intermediate H2COO and its unimolecular decomposition network: cyc-H2CO2 (dioxirane), the OCH2O diradical, formic acid, and the product channels CO2 + H2, H2O + CO and HCO + OH
geometry_source: a reactive machine-learned potential energy surface covering the whole reaction network, trained on energies and forces for an earlier 5162-geometry set for the H2COO / cyc-H2CO2 transition extended with the OCH2O diradical, formic acid, all the product channels and every connecting transition state
method: CASPT2 on a CASSCF reference for all the electronic structure data underlying the machine-learned surface, followed by end-to-end photodissociation dynamics on that surface
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ (aug-cc-pV5Z, cc-pV6Z, cc-pVDZ and def2-TZVP also appear in the work)
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 11 orbitals
active_space_protocol: a single 12-electron, 11-orbital CASSCF space with CASPT2/aug-cc-pVTZ on top, used for every point of the reaction network so that the machine-learned surface is trained on one consistent level of theory
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies on the network (kcal/mol, relative to H2COO at 0): TS1 at 21.43, TS3 at 1.40, cyc-H2CO2 at -24.97, the OCH2O diradical at -16.95, TS2 at 35.44, formic acid at -116.36, HCO + OH at -7.02, CO2 + H2 at -114.27, H2O + CO at -109.97, with TS4 through TS7 at -18.05, -16.21, -43.66 and -40.59. Two further columns of the table give the corresponding values at the other levels compared, which agree to within about a kcal/mol on most stationary points. The OCH2O intermediate is a diradical, which is why the whole network has to be built at a multireference level rather than patched together from single-reference points.

compound_name: model keto-carotenoids COn with n conjugated double bonds (up to 13), and canthaxanthin in the orange carotenoid protein

method: DMRG-SCF with an NEVPT2 perturbative correction as the multireference route, compared against CC3 and EOM-CC3, time-dependent DFT and semiempirical CI (SECI); DMRG is used precisely because plain CAS-SCF cannot carry the natural active space of the longer chains

active_space_orbital_description: the 'natural active space' of each COn, defined by its n double bonds: n occupied and n virtual pi orbitals plus the two occupied nonbonding lone-pair orbitals - so 2n+2 orbitals for chain length n
active_space_protocol: the space grows with the chain: n occupied pi, n virtual pi and the two lone pairs for a COn with n double bonds. electronic_structure_description: The dark Ag- state has strong doubly excited character, so conventional TD-DFT overshoots its transition energy, while the bright Bu+ state is captured reasonably well by TD-DFT. The practical conclusion is that semiempirical CI is the right accuracy-cost compromise for real xanthophylls in their protein environment, demonstrated on canthaxanthin in the orange carotenoid protein.

formula: conjugated organic molecules of the QUEST#3 set
geometry_source: the QUEST protocol geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF references followed by NEVPT2, run as a consistency check on the coupled-cluster and selected-CI theoretical best estimates; the reference values themselves come from selected CI with tens of millions of determinants and from CC3/aug-cc-pVQZ, with basis-set corrections applied by the usual difference scheme
software: MOLPRO, CFOUR, DALTON, GAUSSIAN, ORCA and Q-CHEM across the study
basis_set: diffuse-containing Dunning sets, principally aug-cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVQZ; 6-31+G(d) for some smaller comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: active spaces carefully chosen and tailored to each desired transition; the definition for each system, and the number of states in the state-averaged calculation, are given in the Supporting Information
active_space_protocol: every state-averaged calculation includes at least the ground state together with the excited state of interest, with the per-system space and the number of averaged states specified in the SI. The authors are explicit that multiconfigurational results depend strongly on the space, and that their aim is to establish the typical error to expect from reasonable, chemically meaningful choices rather than from a maximal space.
electronic_structure_description: More than 200 aug-cc-pVQZ reference transition energies are defined and then used to score CIS(D), ADC(2), CC2, STEOM-CCSD, EOM-CCSD, CCSDR(3), CCSDT-3, CC3 and NEVPT2. For states dominated by single excitations the high-order coupled cluster methods are excellent - CC3 reaches a mean absolute error of 0.11 eV and CCSDT 0.06 eV - and surprisingly outperform the second-order multireference schemes CASPT2 and NEVPT2. The picture inverts for states with dominant double-excitation character: for the low-lying (n,n) -> (pi*,pi*) transition of nitrosomethane, at only 2 percent single-excitation character, single-reference methods without quadruples reach MAEs of 0.86 and 0.42 eV. The NEVPT2 cross-check matters most for states of intermediate %T1. The set's acknowledged biases are that it covers only conjugated organic molecules of 4 to 6 non-hydrogen atoms.
reference_short: Loos, Scemama, Jacquemin et al., A Mountaineering Strategy to Excited States: Highly Accurate Energies and Benchmarks for Medium-Sized Molecules (QUEST#3)

PC-NEVPT2 is preferred over SC-NEVPT2 on theoretical grounds - more perturbers and greater flexibility - and was run systematically for QUEST#3.

The accuracy of CASPT2 and NEVPT2 turns out to be the hardest to predict of any method in the set, because it depends on both the system and the chosen active space; the pattern that does emerge is that they are more accurate for transitions with a very small percentage of single-excitation character (error usually below 0.1 eV) than for the single-excitation-dominated ones, where the error approaches 0.1-0.2 eV. compound_name: Ce(3+) substituting at the La(3+) site of La2CaB10O19, the (CeLaO10)17- embedded cluster
ligand_set: ten oxygen ligands in the first coordination shell, embedded in ab initio model potentials and lattice point charges
geometry_source: Structures from PBE0-optimized supercell geometries of the doped crystal. Cerium-centred embedded clusters were constructed with their surroundings represented by ab initio model potentials and by 92584 to 91993 point charges at lattice sites, generated by the method of Lepetit so as to reproduce the same electrostatic potentials as the Ewald method. The undoped host lattice was first optimized with DFT-PBE0, giving lattice parameters a 11.050 (experimental 11.043) A, b 6.572 (6.563), c 9.108 (9.129) and beta 91.575 (91.470) degrees, with deviations no larger than 0.25 percent.
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with spin-orbit coupling, on embedded clusters within an ab initio model potential and point-charge environment; DFT-PBE0 for the periodic structure
basis_set: Relativistic effective core potential with a [Kr] core and a (14s10p10d8f3g)/[6s5p6d4f1g] Gaussian valence basis for cerium; a [He] core effective core potential with a (5s6p1d)/[2s4p1d] valence basis for oxygen; both augmented by auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets for a proper description of the inner core region; an extra (9s)/[1s] set on the boron atoms closest to the embedded clusters to improve orthogonality with the embedding environment
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potentials on Ce and O, with auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets; spin-orbit coupling included in the CASSCF/CASPT2 treatment
active_space_orbital_description: A [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space, adopted because of the many electrons involved in the CASSCF calculations. The bonding and the static and dynamic correlation effects of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and the O(2-) 2s and 2p electrons are accounted for at the CASPT2 stage.
active_space_protocol: The space is limited to the cerium 4f, 5d and 6s manifolds, chosen explicitly because of the number of electrons involved. Everything outside it that matters -- the Ce 5s and 5p semicore, the 4f and 5d correlation, and the oxygen 2s and 2p electrons -- is recovered perturbatively at the CASPT2 level rather than variationally. No symmetry is imposed (C1 point group), so the 4f and 5d levels are labelled 4f1 to 4f7 and 5d1 to 5d5 in order of increasing energy.
nroots_per_mult: Seven 4f levels and five 5d levels per cluster
electronic_structure_description: For all clusters the calculated 4f1 levels fall into two groups, 4f1 to 4f3 and 4f4 to 4f7, linked to the 2F5/2 and 2F7/2 multiplet terms of Ce(3+), split by 2359 to 2564 cm-1 through the spin-orbit interaction. The lowest 4f to 5d transition energy of Ce(3+) in a host lattice is lower by 12240 +/- 750 cm-1 than the lowest 4f2 to 4f1 5d1 transition of the corresponding Pr(3+) system. The redshift of the lowest 4f to 5d transition of Ce(3+) at the Ca(2+) site is explained quantitatively through the relation that the transition energy equals the difference between the ground 4f level and the 5d centroid minus the crystal field splitting of the lowest 5d level relative to that centroid. An observed band at about 36765 cm-1, labelled band J, is assigned mainly to the 4f to 5d transition of the cerium at the lanthanum site, with a deviation of 143 cm-1 between calculation and experiment. Another band is assigned to a transition of this same centre with a deviation of 1547 cm-1. The lowest 4f to 5d transition of cerium at the calcium site is redshifted relative to that at the lanthanum site.
Other: The active space is stated as a compromise forced by electron count: because of the many electrons involved in the CASSCF calculations, a [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space was adopted rather than anything larger. What that space omits is then handled explicitly rather than ignored -- the bonding and the static and dynamic correlation effects of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons together with the O(2-) 2s and 2p electrons are taken into account through the CASPT2 step, so the correlation of the semicore and ligand electrons enters perturbatively while only the 4f, 5d and 6s manifolds are variationally correlated. No symmetry at all is used, C1 point group, so the seven 4f and five 5d levels are simply labelled in order of increasing energy rather than by irreducible representation. Two basis-set decisions support the space rather than the correlation treatment: auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets were added to both cerium and oxygen for a proper description of the inner core region in the spin-orbit calculations, and an extra (9s)/[1s] set was placed on the boron atoms closest to the embedded clusters purely to improve orthogonality between cluster orbitals and their embedding environment. The internal consistency check comes from the two crystallographically distinct calcium sites: their 4f and 5d levels agree to 36 and 226 cm-1 on average, small enough that the two clusters are treated as one thereafter, which shows the space responds to the ligand field rather than to incidental geometric detail.
reference_short: Ning, Wang, Wang, Liu et al., J. Phys. Chem. C 2013, 117, 12444
notes: This is the isovalent substitution site, cerium replacing lanthanum with matching charge, and it gives the best agreement with experiment of the assignments made, 143 cm-1 on the band J assignment.

Cerium-centred embedded clusters were constructed with their surroundings represented by ab initio model potentials and by 92584 to 91993 point charges at lattice sites, generated by the method of Lepetit so as to reproduce the same electrostatic potentials as the Ewald method. The undoped host lattice was first optimized with DFT-PBE0, giving lattice parameters a 11.050 (experimental 11.043) A, b 6.572 (6.563), c 9.108 (9.129) and beta 91.575 (91.470) degrees, with deviations no larger than 0.25 percent.
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with spin-orbit coupling, on embedded clusters within an ab initio model potential and point-charge environment; DFT-PBE0 for the periodic structure
basis_set: Relativistic effective core potential with a [Kr] core and a (14s10p10d8f3g)/[6s5p6d4f1g] Gaussian valence basis for cerium; a [He] core effective core potential with a (5s6p1d)/[2s4p1d] valence basis for oxygen; both augmented by auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets for a proper description of the inner core region; an extra (9s)/[1s] set on the boron atoms closest to the embedded clusters to improve orthogonality with the embedding environment
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potentials on Ce and O, with auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets; spin-orbit coupling included in the CASSCF/CASPT2 treatment
active_space_orbital_description: A [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space, adopted because of the many electrons involved in the CASSCF calculations. The bonding and the static and dynamic correlation effects of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and the O(2-) 2s and 2p electrons are accounted for at the CASPT2 stage.
active_space_protocol: The space is limited to the cerium 4f, 5d and 6s manifolds, chosen explicitly because of the number of electrons involved. Everything outside it that matters -- the Ce 5s and 5p semicore, the 4f and 5d correlation, and the oxygen 2s and 2p electrons -- is recovered perturbatively at the CASPT2 level rather than variationally. No symmetry is imposed (C1 point group), so the 4f and 5d levels are labelled 4f1 to 4f7 and 5d1 to 5d5 in order of increasing energy.
nroots_per_mult: Seven 4f levels and five 5d levels per cluster
electronic_structure_description: For all clusters the calculated 4f1 levels fall into two groups, 4f1 to 4f3 and 4f4 to 4f7, linked to the 2F5/2 and 2F7/2 multiplet terms of Ce(3+), split by 2359 to 2564 cm-1 through the spin-orbit interaction. The lowest 4f to 5d transition energy of Ce(3+) in a host lattice is lower by 12240 +/- 750 cm-1 than the lowest 4f2 to 4f1 5d1 transition of the corresponding Pr(3+) system. The redshift of the lowest 4f to 5d transition of Ce(3+) at the Ca(2+) site is explained quantitatively through the relation that the transition energy equals the difference between the ground 4f level and the 5d centroid minus the crystal field splitting of the lowest 5d level relative to that centroid. This cluster differs from the first calcium-site cluster only in the slight details of its local geometry, and its 4f and 5d levels agree with those of the first to within average absolute deviations of 36 cm-1 and 226 cm-1 respectively. On that basis the two calcium-site clusters are referred to as a single Ce-at-calcium centre without distinction in the subsequent discussion.
Other: The active space is stated as a compromise forced by electron count: because of the many electrons involved in the CASSCF calculations, a [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space was adopted rather than anything larger. What that space omits is then handled explicitly rather than ignored -- the bonding and the static and dynamic correlation effects of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons together with the O(2-) 2s and 2p electrons are taken into account through the CASPT2 step, so the correlation of the semicore and ligand electrons enters perturbatively while only the 4f, 5d and 6s manifolds are variationally correlated. No symmetry at all is used, C1 point group, so the seven 4f and five 5d levels are simply labelled in order of increasing energy rather than by irreducible representation. Two basis-set decisions support the space rather than the correlation treatment: auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets were added to both cerium and oxygen for a proper description of the inner core region in the spin-orbit calculations, and an extra (9s)/[1s] set was placed on the boron atoms closest to the embedded clusters purely to improve orthogonality between cluster orbitals and their embedding environment. The internal consistency check comes from the two crystallographically distinct calcium sites: their 4f and 5d levels agree to 36 and 226 cm-1 on average, small enough that the two clusters are treated as one thereafter, which shows the space responds to the ligand field rather than to incidental geometric detail.
reference_short: Ning, Wang, Wang, Liu et al., J. Phys. Chem. C 2013, 117, 12444
notes: The near-equality of the two calcium-site clusters serves as an internal check that the computed level splittings reflect the ligand field rather than incidental structural detail.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF reference, accounting for the bonding and the static and dynamic correlation of the Ce 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and the O 2s and 2p electrons

geometry_source: Embedded clusters with surroundings simulated by 723 to 748 embedding ab initio model potentials and 73773 to 73779 point charges at lattice sites, generated with Lepetit's method. Samples of composition Sr(1-2x)Ce(x)Na(x)Al2O4 with x from 0.001 to 0.02 were characterized by XRD at room temperature against the JCPDS 74-0794 standard pattern and by XANES.
method: Embedded-cluster CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with spin-orbit coupling, to obtain the Ce(3+) 4f and 5d energy levels
basis_set: Relativistic effective core potential ([Kr] core) with a (14s10p10d8f3g)/[6s5p6d4f1g] Gaussian valence basis set for cerium; [He] core effective core potential with a (5s6p1d)/[2s4p1d] valence basis set for oxygen and aluminum; extra (11s8p)/[1s1p] basis added to the eight Al atoms closest to the embedded clusters to improve orthogonality of the cluster orbitals with the embedding environments
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potentials on the cerium and ligand atoms; spin-orbit coupling included in the casscf/caspt2 treatment
active_space_orbital_description: A [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space: the single 4f electron of Ce(3+) distributed over the thirteen molecular orbitals of mainly 4f, 5d and 6s character on the cerium ion.
active_space_protocol: A minimal [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space is adopted for the CASSCF step because of the number of electrons in the embedded cluster. Correlation of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons together with the ligand valence electrons is recovered only at the CASPT2 stage, and spin-orbit coupling only at the subsequent state-interaction stage, so neither enters the reference wave function. The identical space is applied to every crystallographically distinct dopant site so that the computed differences in 4f and 5d levels reflect the ligand field alone.
nroots_per_mult: Thirteen states, one per 4f/5d/6s-character orbital, state-averaged
Other: The active space is the same minimal [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space used across this family of Ce(3+)-doped host studies, holding the single 4f electron in the thirteen orbitals of mainly 4f, 5d and 6s character on the cerium ion. It is adopted because the number of electrons in the embedded cluster makes anything larger impractical, and everything it omits is recovered at a later stage rather than variationally: the dynamic correlation of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and of the ligand valence electrons enters only through the CASPT2 step, and spin-orbit coupling only through the state-interaction step afterwards. So the semicore and ligand correlation that shapes the crystal-field splitting is never in the reference wave function. Two basis-set choices exist to support that space rather than the correlation treatment: auxiliary spin-orbit basis sets are added for a proper description of the inner core region in the spin-orbit calculations, and extra diffuse sets are placed on the framework atoms nearest the cluster purely to improve orthogonality between cluster orbitals and the surrounding embedding potentials -- a numerical safeguard against the cluster orbitals leaking into the environment. Because the whole point of these calculations is to distinguish crystallographically distinct dopant sites whose 4f and 5d levels differ by only hundreds of wavenumbers, the fixed space applied identically to every site is what makes the site comparison meaningful; any per-site tuning would confound the ligand-field difference being measured.
reference_short: Shi, Qi, Ning, Pan, Zhou, Zhou, Huang & Liang, J. Phys. Chem. C 2015, 119, 19326
notes: The study combines experiment and theory to establish the site preference of Ce(3+) among the two inequivalent Sr sites, with sodium co-doping for charge compensation.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 considering the dynamic correlation effects of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons and the O(2-) 2s and 2p electrons

Correlation of the Ce(3+) 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons together with the ligand valence electrons is recovered only at the CASPT2 stage, and spin-orbit coupling only at the subsequent state-interaction stage, so neither enters the reference wave function. Other: The active space is the same minimal [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space used across this family of Ce(3+)-doped host studies, holding the single 4f electron in the thirteen orbitals of mainly 4f, 5d and 6s character on the cerium ion. compound_name: NH3 molecular and dissociative adsorption on the Si(100)-2x1 surface, Si9H12 cluster model
geometry_source: An embedded Si9H12 cluster used to model localized bonding on the surface, as in previous work. Structures of adsorbed NH3 on the embedded cluster and of the reactants NH3 gas plus the bare cluster were located with the quasi-Newton method, and the transition state for dissociative adsorption with the DIIS-Ridge method, both using CASSCF energies and gradients. Structures were considered converged when the gradient components of all movable atoms (all non-siligen atoms) fell below 1e-3 au. Calculations were performed within Cs symmetry; to verify this was not a restriction, geometry optimizations and the start of the saddle point search were first carried out with no symmetry constraints, and in all cases the structures evolved into Cs-symmetric ones exactly matching the symmetry-constrained results. Symmetry was then imposed for speed, which matters because the CAS is large.
method: CASSCF energies and gradients for geometry optimization and transition state search, with multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction (MRSDCI) single points for the final energetics
software: HONDO for all CASSCF energy and gradient calculations
basis_set: Dunning/Huzinaga valence double-zeta basis sets for Si, the hydrogen adsorbates and the siligens
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals, with the composition changing along the reaction path. For the desorbed and molecularly adsorbed structures the active orbitals are the two surface Si dangling bonds, the correlated N lone pair described by two orbitals, and the three N-H bonds with their respective antibonding orbitals. For the dissociatively adsorbed structure the space instead contains the Si-N and Si-H bonding and antibonding orbitals, the two remaining N-H bonding and antibonding orbitals, and the correlated N lone pair described by two orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A ten-orbital, ten-electron complete active space was found to be necessary to describe the reaction path for dissociative adsorption adequately. Its size is held fixed while its contents change with the chemistry: the three N-H bonding and antibonding pairs and the two surface dangling bonds of the reactant side are replaced, on the product side, by Si-N and Si-H bonding and antibonding pairs plus the two surviving N-H pairs, with the doubly described N lone pair carried through both. The MRSDCI reference space was then built from all configuration state functions in that CAS with coefficients at or above 0.01, giving final CI expansions of up to about 6.5 million configuration state functions.
electronic_structure_description: Dissociation of NH3 on the surface proceeds in two stages: gaseous NH3 first adsorbs molecularly, then dissociates to NH2(a) + H(a). The dissociation step is activated with a barrier of 15 kcal/mol. The exothermicity for molecularly adsorbed NH3 converting to dissociated NH2(a) + H(a) is 43 kcal/mol, and the overall exothermicity from gaseous NH3 plus a bare Si surface is 75 kcal/mol. Because the intermediate barrier lies 17 kcal/mol below the energy of the reactants, this highly exothermic reaction has no overall barrier to dissociative chemisorption; only if 17 kcal/mol of translational energy were required would a barrier be seen. Metastable molecularly adsorbed NH3 is strongly bound with respect to desorption at 32 kcal/mol, with a lower barrier of 15 kcal/mol to dissociate an N-H bond, which explains the observed behaviour at low temperatures (120 K), consistent with a barrierless, highly exothermic reaction. A large barrier of about 75 kcal/mol is noted elsewhere in the discussion. Based on error analysis on related systems, MRSDCI barriers are expected to be 2 to 5 kcal/mol too high and MRSDCI exothermicities about 2 kcal/mol too low, described as an acceptable level of accuracy for surface science models.
Other: The ten-orbital space is held at constant size while its contents are swapped wholesale between the two ends of the reaction coordinate: on the reactant side it holds the two surface silicon dangling bonds plus all three N-H bonding and antibonding pairs, and on the product side those are replaced by the Si-N and Si-H bonding and antibonding pairs together with the two N-H pairs that survive, with the nitrogen lone pair described by two orbitals throughout. That substitution is what allows a single space to span molecular adsorption, N-H cleavage and Si-N and Si-H bond formation on one surface. The paper states directly that a ten-orbital, ten-electron CAS was found to be necessary to describe the dissociative adsorption path adequately, so the size is a determined requirement rather than a convenient choice, and it notes that the resulting CASSCF energy and gradient calculations are computationally intensive enough that imposing Cs symmetry mattered for feasibility -- symmetry that was first shown to be an outcome rather than an assumption, since unconstrained optimizations evolved to Cs structures matching the constrained ones exactly. The MRSDCI built on this space selects references by a coefficient threshold of 0.01, reaching about 6.5 million configuration state functions, and the authors quote expected residual errors from analysis of related systems rather than claiming convergence: barriers 2 to 5 kcal/mol too high and exothermicities about 2 kcal/mol too low.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: singlet ground state with a thermally populated triplet. CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* natural-orbital-population analysis gives 35% diradical character. Experimental singlet-triplet gap 2J = -1730 +/- 100 cm^-1 by solid-state EPR and -1500 +/- 50 cm^-1 by magnetic susceptibility. MPW1PW91/6-31G* field scan gives a 1948 cm^-1 zero-field gap, 1980 cm^-1 at 0.18 V Angstrom^-1, a drop to 341 cm^-1 at 0.21 V Angstrom^-1, then 1118 cm^-1 at 0.64 V Angstrom^-1 for the field along the dimer long axis.
Other: X-ray structure: trans-cofacial centrosymmetric 7pi*-7pi* dimer with intradimer S(delta+)...N(delta-) contacts of about 3.20-3.26 Angstrom; dimers form chains through terminal C=N(delta-)...S(delta+) contacts of 3.023(3) and 3.167(2) Angstrom. At 230 K the EPR triplet has |D| = 0.0278(5) cm^-1 and |E| = 0.0047(5) cm^-1. Magnetic fit: g = 2.02(5), rho = 0.90(3)%, TIP = 1.25(4)e-3 emu mol^-1; magnetic moment 1.8 muB per dimer at 300 K. The radical melts near 330-332 K to an approximately fully dissociated paramagnetic liquid and shows an about 30 K thermal-hysteresis loop plus dark-green-to-brown-orange thermochromism; inferred in situ dimerization energy is about -10 kJ mol^-1.
reference_short: Shuvaev et al., Dalton Trans. (2008), 4029-4037
notes: Comprehensive GPT-5.6 read of all 9 article pages and all 3 ESI pages. geometry_source: Z/E ground-state equilibrium structures optimized with B3LYP; CASSCF/6-31G* minima, transition states, and minimum-energy S1/S0 conical intersections with frequency checks; relaxed SA-CASSCF/6-31G scans and CASSCF/CASPT2-corrected conical-intersection seams. method: SS/SA-CASSCF; SS/MS-CASPT2; RASSI transition moments; B3LYP ground-state geometry; conical-intersection and seam optimization
basis_set: 6-31G* for CASSCF stationary structures; 6-31G for relaxed two-dimensional CASSCF scans
active_space_orbital_description: For the (10e,9o) reference, pi orbitals on all first neighbors of the central C=C bond plus one bonding/antibonding pair from each benzene ring; the oxygen lone pair can replace the sulfur 3pz orbital or be included adaptively near n-pi*/intersection regions, and C1-H1 sigma/sigma* orbitals are included for CoInEt. The (14e,13o) space adds a further bonding/antibonding pair from each benzene ring.
active_space_protocol: (10e,9o) CASSCF excited-state optimizations and SA-2 relaxed scans, with individually adapted orbital content for different conical intersections; (10e,9o) oxygen-lone-pair reference contracted to 42 configuration-state functions near CoInAc to suppress single/double n-to-pi* excitations; (8e,8o) special lower E-to-Z scan excluding both sulfur and oxygen lone pairs; (14e,13o) enlarge by an additional bonding/antibonding pair per benzene ring for SS/MS-CASPT2 single points and seam corrections.
nroots_per_mult: SA-2/MS-2 for the S0/S1 surfaces and conical intersections; SS calculations at the Franck-Condon structures resolve S0, S1, and S2
electronic_structure_description: At SS-CASSCF(14,13), the dark n-pi* state lies below the bright pi-pi* state: Z 3.75/4.67 eV and E 3.57/4.39 eV. SS-CASPT2 reverses them to S1(pi-pi*)/S2(n-pi*): Z 3.48/3.72 eV and E 3.27/3.60 eV, versus experimental bright-band maxima 2.92 and 2.76 eV. At MS-2-CASPT2(14,13), accessible S1/S0 crossing structures include CoInS (0.49 eV residual gap), CoInAc (0.03 eV), and CoInCHD (0.48 eV); local seam reoptimization reduces gaps below 0.1 eV. CoInAc can yield either isomer, CoInS returns Z, and CoInCHD is an E-side photostabilizing channel.
Other: CASPT2 used an IPEA-modified zeroth-order Hamiltonian with IPEA shift 0.25 au and real denominator shift 0.30 au. RASSI supplied transition dipoles. The Z-to-E experiment gives 2.0 +/- 0.8 ps, 10 +/- 1 ps, and 650 +/- 200 ps components; E-to-Z gives 260 +/- 80 fs, 1.2 +/- 0.4 ps, and 13 +/- 6 ps. Reported photochemical yields are 0.230 +/- 0.035 (Z-to-E) and 0.053 +/- 0.016 (E-to-Z), with fluorescence yield 0.0003. The calculated mechanism attributes selectivity to heteroatom-controlled charge separation/recombination across an accessible CoInS-CoInAc seam and a rapid E-side CoInCHD loss channel.

basis_set: Small-core ECP basis: Re (Z=15.0 valence) (8s7p6d)/[6s5p3d]; C and N (Z=4.0/5.0) (4s4p)/[2s2p]; O (4s5p)/[2s3p]; H bases as for Mn
relativistic_treatment: small-core relativistic effective core potential (Andrae et al.); spin-orbit coupling omitted
active_space_orbital_description: The paper states that eight electrons—the metal nd electrons plus the two electrons in the M-R bond—are correlated in 10 orbitals comprising nd orbitals and their nd' correlating orbitals, σM-R and σ*M-R, and the lowest DAB-localized π* orbital
active_space_protocol: CASSCF averaged over five low-lying states of each symmetry and spin to generate common orbitals; for each state, monoreference CCI followed by MR-CCI using every configuration with coefficient >0.08 as a reference (4–12 references), with all single/double excitations to allowed virtuals; 250,000–1,000,000 configurations contracted to at most a few thousand
nroots_per_mult: five low-lying states of each symmetry and spin in the state-averaged CASSCF
electronic_structure_description: Singlet 1A' ground configuration (σRe-H)^2(5dx2-y2)^2(5dyz)^2(5dxz)^2. CASSCF/MR-CCI vertical transitions (cm-1): mixed 3MLCT/SBLCT a3A' 12600 (5dxz+σRe-H→π*, 0.71; σRe-H−5dxz→π*, 0.64); 3MLCT b3A' 13710 (5dx2-y2→π*, 0.90); 1MLCT b1A' 15250 (0.91, f=0.0003); 1MLCT/SBLCT c1A' 21720 (0.68/0.44, f=0.32); 3SBLCT/MLCT c3A' 27650 (0.69/0.59); 1SBLCT/MLCT d1A' 31340 (0.64/0.59, f=0.12).
Other: Triplet values are explicitly called 'pseudotriplet' energies because SOC was not included; appreciable splitting is expected and the authors call for CCI-level SOC. Relative to Mn-H, relativistic d-shell destabilization and π*DAB–Re 6pz stabilization lower the states and produce strong MLCT/SBLCT mixing; the 21720 cm-1 state is associated with the intense ~20000 cm-1 band of related Re complexes.

geometry_source: Computational model from the bent anion in the crystal structure of [PhCH2N(CH3)3]2[Fe2OCl6]: Fe-O-Fe 144.6 degrees and symmetric Fe-O 1.761 A; the complete Cartesian coordinates are printed in SI p. 6.
method: spin-adapted state-specific DMRG-CASSCF; conventional CASSCF and internally contracted MRCI/MRCI+Q comparisons
software: parallel DMRG code of Kurashige and Yanai; MOLPRO 2012.1 for conventional CASSCF/MRCI
basis_set: ANO-RCC with DKH2; BS0-BS5 contraction series. Principal BS3: Fe [6s,5p,3d,2f,1g], O [4s,3p,2d,1f], Cl [5s,4p,2d] (310 functions); SI Table S1 also gives unnamed 352/376-function and BS4/BS5 tests through Fe [9s,8p,6d,5f,4g,2h], O [7s,6p,4d,3f,2g], Cl [7s,6p,4d,3f,2g] (900 functions).
active_space_orbital_description: Largest space: all ten Fe 3d magnetic orbitals and their Fe 4d double shell plus bridging O 2p occupied orbitals and O 3p double shell. Tested spaces were (10,10) Fe 3d; (16,13) Fe 3d+O 2p; (16,16) Fe 3d+O 2p/O 3p; (10,20) Fe 3d/4d; and (16,26) Fe 3d/4d+O 2p/3p. SI Figure S1 identifies the ordered localized orbitals 75-100; Figure S2 provides every (16,26) and (16,13) singlet natural orbital and occupation.
active_space_protocol: High-spin B3LYP natural orbitals (S=5) were Pipek-Mezey localized; orbitals were ordered atom-wise and with valence/double-shell partners alternating. DMRG bond dimensions M=64-1000 were explicitly tested and the (16,26) singlet/triplet energies were linearly extrapolated against discarded weight to M=infinity. All orbitals were state-specific. Conventional MRCI correlated all valence and metal 3s/3p semi-core closed orbitals and applied the relaxed-reference Davidson +Q correction.
nroots_per_mult: one lowest state for each total spin S=0-5
electronic_structure_description: Antiferromagnetic singlet ground state. BS3 J values (cm-1): CAS(10,10) -39.7; CAS(16,13) -58.6; MRCI(10,10) -61.3; MRCI(16,13) -96.3; MRCI+Q(10,10) -75.6; MRCI+Q(16,13) -115.3; DMRG(16,16)[1000] -57.7; DMRG(10,20)[256] -49.0; extrapolated DMRG(16,26) -117.4, versus experiment -117. active_space_orbital_description: Four pi electrons in three dye pi orbitals analogous to the allyl-anion pi system: Boys-localized orbitals on the left ring, methine bridge, and right ring; pseudocanonical orbitals analogous to the highest bonding, nonbonding, and lowest antibonding allyl orbitals.
active_space_protocol: UHF charge-natural orbitals of the doubly cationic radical supplied the initial guess; three roots had equal weights. Production (4,3); (8,7) add one occupied and one virtual local-ring orbital per ring; (12,11) repeat that increment; (16,15) repeat to the full pi space. The MP2/SA-CASSCF/MS-MRPT2 (4,3) suite was repeated with MIDI!. MS-MRPT2 correlated 32 orbitals with a 0.1-au level shift.
nroots_per_mult: three equal-weight state-averaged roots; spin multiplicity is not explicitly stated

method: CASSCF(11,9) potential-energy surfaces followed by multireference contracted configuration interaction with all single and double excitations (CCI), natural-orbital transformation of the CASSCF active orbitals, and a modified Davidson correction (CCI+Q); extended- and restricted-reference CCI variants, basis-set comparisons, and diatomic/supermolecule calculations
basis_set: Common segmented [5s3p] contraction of van Duijneveldt 11s6p primitives on N and O. Surface CCI used [5s3p2d], with N d exponents 1.62 and 0.49 and O d exponents 2.27 and 0.68; selected calculations used [5s3p2d1f], with three d primitives contracted (21) and a two-term fitted f set. active_space_orbital_description: Six a' orbitals (7a'-12a') plus three a'' orbitals (1a''-3a'') with seven a' and four a'' electrons. active_space_protocol: Source-explicit CAS(11,9) spanning the valence orbitals required to correlate both N+O2 and NO+O limits. The extended CCI reference contains 28 CASSCF natural-orbital configurations (the first 27 selected at the saddle and the last at the N+O2 asymptote), all with CASSCF coefficient magnitude >0.05, producing about three million uncontracted configurations and permitting both NO and OO dissociation. A smaller roughly one-million-configuration CCI omitted electrons in 12a'; it is valid near reactants and the saddle but not when both bonds are simultaneously long. For the 4A' surface, the reference subset was additionally restricted to configurations with at least three open shells.
nroots_per_mult: one state for each of 2A' and 4A'
electronic_structure_description: The 2A' CASSCF surface has two saddle points and a shallow asymmetric NOO minimum; the extended CCI treatment removes that shallow minimum and yields one entrance-channel saddle. The 4A' surface has a higher barrier. State correlation is discussed without spin-orbit coupling, and the surfaces connect open-shell N+O2 and NO+O asymptotes rather than a single isolated-molecule ground state.

electronic_structure_description: formic acid + hydroxyl radical acidic-H abstraction TS1 (PCET): TS1 is a five-member-ring C1 doublet transition structure for acidic-H abstraction by proton-coupled electron transfer. The OH lone pair points at the acidic proton while the OH unpaired electron interacts with the carbonyl oxygen. CASSCF wavefunction analysis supports electron transfer from the carbonyl-oxygen lone pair to OH coupled to proton transfer from HCOOH to OH. QCISD spin populations are O1=0.603 and carbonyl O3=0.386; both C-O distances are about 1.258 A at the QCISD geometry, consistent with pi redistribution. TS1 is well characterized by B3LYP, MP2, CASSCF, and QCISD. | formic acid + hydroxyl radical acidic-H abstraction TS2 (conventional H abstraction): TS2 is a planar six-member-ring Cs doublet transition structure for conventional acidic-hydrogen radical abstraction: concerted O5-H6 breaking and H6-O1 formation. CASSCF wavefunction analysis and QCISD spin populations (O1=0.532, O5=0.428) support sharing of the unpaired electron between donor and acceptor oxygens. At the QCISD geometry the transferred H is closer to OH, r(O1-H6)=1.117 A versus r(O5-H6)=1.219 A, and a secondary H2...O3 hydrogen bond is 2.071 A. | formic acid + hydroxyl radical double-proton-transfer TS3: TS3 is a symmetric six-member-ring C2v doublet transition structure for simultaneous double proton transfer: acidic H transfers from formic acid to OH while the OH hydrogen transfers to the carbonyl oxygen, producing no net chemical reaction. Its 2B1 symmetry keeps the unpaired electron in an out-of-plane orbital mainly localized on the hydroxyl-radical oxygen, so the unpaired electron does not participate in the proton transfers. Both C-O distances are equal (about 1.264 A at the non-CASSCF comparison geometry), reflecting pi redistribution.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: cyclopropylidene 1-S is 1A1; the lowest triplet 1-T is 3B1. At MR-CISD/TZ2P//UB3LYP/TZP with four reference CSFs, the singlet-triplet separation is 11.1 kcal mol-1 (singlet lower); correcting by the source's computed methylene error gives 8.9 kcal mol-1. CCSD(T)/TZ2P gives 14.9 kcal mol-1. The ring-opening TS is predominantly single-reference (leading CISD coefficient about 0.94; T1 diagnostic below 0.02), so the authors caution that dynamic rather than nondynamic correlation controls its quantitative barrier.
Other: At CASSCF(4,4)/TZP geometries, total energies/ZPVEs are 1-S -115.84102 Eh/35.7 kcal mol-1 (0 imaginary modes), allene 2-S -115.95299 Eh/35.4, and ring-opening TS 3 -115.82212 Eh/35.2 (1 imaginary mode). B3LYP, CISD, and CCSD(T) instead locate asymmetric C1 TSs; the source concludes CASSCF lacks decisive dynamic correlation and predicts the wrong TS symmetry despite a similar corrected barrier.

A 300 nm photon initiates the 1(sigma sigma*) state of the disulfide, which decays via CI(S_sigmasigma/S0) with S-S bond fission generating cysteinyl radicals.

electronic_structure_description: High-spin d4 Mn(III) system. Experimental zero-field splitting D = -4.52 cm-1 with E/D = 0.05. The spin-spin contribution is -1.65 cm-1 at the CASSCF(4,5) level in the mean-field approximation. Of the spin-orbit contribution, 38% (-1.38 cm-1) comes from the quintets and 62% (-2.28 cm-1) from the triplets. The method predicts a SOC contribution to D of -4.68 cm-1. Spin-allowed ligand-field transitions 5Eg -> 5A1g, 5B2g, 5Eg are analysed.
Other: Spin-flip (triplet) excitations dominate the ZFS: 62% of the SOC contribution to D (-2.28 cm-1) comes from the S=1 roots versus 38% (-1.38 cm-1) from the quintets, so a quintet-only treatment fails. Direct spin-spin coupling contributes a further -1.65 cm-1 at CASSCF(4,5) and cannot simply be added to the SOC D-tensor because the two tensors have different orientations.
reference_short: Neese, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2006, 128, 10213
notes: Case study of zero-field splitting in a transition metal complex, establishing the importance of direct spin-spin coupling and spin-flip (triplet) excitations. Active space stated verbatim as CAS(4,5) = four electrons in the five Mn 3d-based MOs. Mn(III) / high-spin d4 is stated explicitly by the paper. Both spin-orbit and spin-spin couplings are treated, hence soc_included and ss_included are both yes.

method: CASSCF

active_space_protocol: six valence pi orbitals give a consistent space for the planar 1A1/2A1/1B1 valence states; extended for nonplanar geometries by testing several combinations of sigma orbitals and adopting the two sigma orbitals enframing the pi blocks in each symmetry species, subject to a practical limit of about 12 active orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1 1A1. States studied: 1 1A1, 2 1A1 and 1 1B1, all valence states. The covalent 2 1A1 state is dominated by the doubly excited (pi1)2(pi2)2(pi3)0(pi4)2 CSF but requires many further valence excitations; the singly excited (pi1)2(pi2)2(pi3)1(pi4)1 CSF is a good zeroth-order approximation to the 1 1B1 wave function. Out-of-plane (a2 and b2) harmonic frequencies of all three states are reported and compared with experiment for the ground state.

Four sigma orbitals are added to the six valence pi orbitals specifically because pi/sigma mixing switches on at nonplanar geometries, where a pi-only space would be unbalanced.
