geometry_source: two-dimensional potential energy surface scan as a function of the C-Br and C-Cl bond lengths
method: SA-CASSCF; SS-CASPT2; MS-CASPT2
basis_set: ANO-L contracted basis sets: C (14s9p4d)/[4s3p2d], H (8s4p)/[3s2p], Cl (17s12p5d)/[5s4p2d]; Br described by the relativistic AIMP core potential (9s8p4d)/[3s4p2d] with effective atomic number Z=7.0. electronic_structure_description: Lowest singlet states a 1A', b 1A', c 1A'. The photochemistry is controlled by a nonadiabatic crossing between the A and B absorption bands, attributed to the near-degenerate b 1A' and c 1A' states, which form a near-degeneracy line of almost equidistant C-Br and C-Cl bonds; a crossing point on that line is identified as a conical intersection in the reduced two-dimensional space. The c 1A' global minimum lies at 5.27 eV, where the b-c gap is about 0.19 eV; two further local minima on c 1A' lie at 5.97 eV (d(C-Br)=1.89, d(C-Cl)=2.99 A) and 5.93 eV (d(C-Br)=3.32, d(C-Cl)=1.65 A). At large separations the two lowest states become degenerate to within millielectronvolts.
Other: The located position of the conical intersection depends on the level of theory: CASSCF, SS-CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 are compared directly, and the nonorthogonality problem of perturbative approaches is discussed. The geometrical phase effect was checked with the MS-CASPT2 wave function to confirm a genuine CI rather than an avoided crossing. 11 A' roots are required so no low-lying state is missing after the CASPT2 reordering.
reference_short: Rozgonyi & Gonzalez, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 10251
notes: Comparison of conical intersection positions located at CASSCF, SS-CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 levels. geometry_source: geometry optimization at the UB3LYP/6-31+G(d) level; interaction energies corrected for basis set superposition error by the counterpoise method
method: CASSCF; MCQDPT on the CASSCF(2,2) reference (B3LYP used for geometries and comparison)
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals, the space spanned by the overlap of the SOMOs of the two [TTF]+ monomers, chosen so that both the closed-shell singlet (CSS) and open-shell singlet (OSS) states arising from the interaction of the two doublet radical cations can be properly described. The paper does not label the two orbitals further.
electronic_structure_description: MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) indicates the electronic ground state of the [TTF]2(2+) dimer is a closed-shell singlet with a non-negligible contribution from the open-shell singlet, as observed experimentally; this ground state is not well reproduced by B3LYP or by CASSCF(2,2) alone. For the [TTF]2(ClO4)2 aggregate at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), interaction energies are -147.3 kcal/mol (closed-shell singlet), -147.2 kcal/mol (open-shell singlet) and -134.4 kcal/mol (triplet), so the closed-shell singlet is the ground state with the open-shell singlet only 0.1 kcal/mol higher. Dimer stability is attributed to [TTF]+...anion- attractions outweighing the [TTF]+...[TTF]+ and anion-...anion- repulsions.
Other: MCQDPT on the CASSCF(2,2) reference is required to get the diamagnetic closed-shell singlet ground state with its non-negligible open-shell singlet contribution; neither B3LYP nor CASSCF(2,2) alone reproduces it. The same failure of B3LYP had been seen for [TCNE]2(2-).
reference_short: Capdevila-Cortada, Novoa et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 484

The quoted interaction energies are B3LYP values, labelled as such.

method: CASSCF; CASPT2; MR-CISD (all single and double excitations from a selected set of MCSCF reference configurations)
basis_set: DZP: C,N (9s5p1d)/[4s2p1d], H (4s1p)/[2s1p], polarization exponents ad(C)=0.75, ad(N)=0.8, ap(H)=0.75. TZ2P: C,N (10s6p2d)/[5s3p2d], H (5s2p1d)/[3s2p1d]. Pure (five-component) d functions throughout.
active_space_orbital_description: Written by the paper in 'n-in-m' notation: all possible singlet-spin configurations distributing n active electrons among m active molecular orbitals. The 4-in-4 space was used for the rotational transition state and for trans-1,2-dimethyldiazene and the semilinear transition state; a 6-in-6 space adds two further orbitals and two further electrons. The paper does not identify which orbitals occupy either space.
active_space_protocol: 4-in-4 CASSCF for geometry optimization of the rotational transition state and of trans-1,2-dimethyldiazene and the semilinear transition state; 6-in-6 CASSCF as an extended check (two additional orbitals and two additional electrons); MR-CISD using 6-in-6 CASSCF orbitals
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state potential energy surface, with isomerization and decomposition in competition. Isomerization by rotation about the N=N bond is symmetry-forbidden, so several configurations become near-degenerate along the path, which is why the CASSCF description is needed. The rotational transition state has a C-N-N-C torsional angle of about 89.9 degrees and the N-N bond order falls from 1.646 to 1.524. Reoptimization at 4-in-4 CASSCF does not change the transition state parameters significantly. The semilinear transition state is slightly distorted from Cs, with a C-N-N-C torsion of 9.5 degrees at a bond angle of 178.6 degrees. Transition structure VI has C1 symmetry and gives a symmetry-broken wave function unless symmetry is explicitly enforced; the same behaviour persists with the 6-in-6 space. MR-CI calculations include about 370000 configurations per reference configuration in the DZP basis.
Other: Enlarging 4-in-4 to 6-in-6 (two more orbitals, two more electrons) does not remove the symmetry breaking of transition structure VI, which persists unless symmetry is explicitly enforced - so the artefact is not a small-active-space effect.
reference_short: Vrabel et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 1997, 101, 5805
notes: Ground-state PES study of dimethyldiazene isomerization and decomposition. The paper uses 'n-in-m' notation and instantiates it as 4-in-4, 6-in-6 and (for the 1,1 isomer) 2-in-2; active_space_nel/norb record the 4-in-4 space that the geometry optimizations use, with the 6-in-6 variant in active_space_protocol. Orbital composition of the spaces is never stated.

method: CASSCF; CASPT2; MR-CISD (all single and double excitations from a selected set of MCSCF reference configurations)
basis_set: DZP: C,N (9s5p1d)/[4s2p1d], H (4s1p)/[2s1p], polarization exponents ad(C)=0.75, ad(N)=0.8, ap(H)=0.75. TZ2P: C,N (10s6p2d)/[5s3p2d], H (5s2p1d)/[3s2p1d]. Pure (five-component) d functions throughout.
active_space_orbital_description: 2-in-2 space in the paper's 'n-in-m' notation; the orbitals composing it are not identified.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A1. The 2-in-2 CASSCF/DZP calculations place the 3A2 triplet state 52.1 kJ/mol above the 1A1 singlet ground state, so this species has a singlet ground state in contrast to alkyl, aryl and cyano nitrenes, which have triplet ground states. reference_short: Vrabel et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 1997, 101, 5805
notes: Separate row for the 1,1 isomer, which the paper treats with its own 2-in-2 CASSCF/DZP space to obtain the singlet-triplet gap. Orbital composition not stated.

point_group: C2v for the symmetric ICT structure; distorted towards Cs by pyramidalization of the phenyl carbon bearing the dimethylamino group
geometry_source: CASSCF(12e/11o)/SVP optimized structures for the CASSCF results; CC2/TZVPP structures used for the coupled-cluster single points
method: CASSCF (used to test for multireference effects alongside CC2, CCSD and CCSDR(3))
software: DALTON (release 1.2) for the CASSCF and coupled-cluster calculations; TURBOMOLE for the RI-CC2 gradients
active_space_orbital_description: Three active spaces were tested, given in the paper's table footnotes as (6e/5o), (10e/9o) and (12e/11o); the orbitals composing them are not identified. The largest, (12e/11o), was also used for geometry optimization.
active_space_protocol: (6e,5o); (10e,9o); (12e,11o) - the stabilization energy of the pyramidalized form increases with the size of the active space
electronic_structure_description: Prototype molecule for dual fluorescence, with the anomalous emission attributed to an intramolecular charge-transfer (ICT) state. CASSCF/SVP energy differences associated with pyramidalization: -0.027 eV with the (6e/5o) space, -0.031 eV with (10e/9o) and -0.057 eV with (12e/11o); all tested active spaces make the pyramidalized form energetically more favourable, with the stabilization increasing with active space size. For comparison at the same SVP basis: CC2 4.283, CCSD 4.497, CCSDR(3) 4.322 eV. At CC2/TZVPP the ICT state lies 0.014 eV above the LE state before pyramidalization, and 0.08 eV below after it.
Other: Stabilization of the pyramidalized ICT structure increases monotonically with active space size: -0.027 eV at (6e/5o), -0.031 at (10e/9o), -0.057 at (12e/11o). All spaces agree on the sign, so the qualitative conclusion is space-independent while the magnitude is not.
reference_short: Kohn & Hattig, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2004, 126, 7399
notes: Primarily a CC2 study; the CASSCF calculations are the paper's own multireference check on the ICT-state structure, which is why this row exists. The row records the largest space, (12e/11o), which is also the one used for geometry optimization; the smaller two are in active_space_protocol.

basis_set: def2-TZVPP (Fe), def2-TZVP (N), def2-SVP (H), def2-TZVP(-f) (C), with corresponding auxiliary sets

electronic_structure_description: High-spin d6 Fe(II) in a trigonal ligand field, orbitally degenerate, studied as a single-molecule magnet. A 5E model subspace is constructed from the 10 lowest spin-orbit CI eigenvectors of the 160-microstate manifold.

Nontruncated complexes are stated to be essential - truncated models capture only a fraction of the observed differences in magnetic properties.

notes: One of a family of four trigonal pyramidal Fe(II) pyrrolide SMMs differing only in the peripheral tpa substituent; one row per complex, all sharing the CAS(6,5) metal-d active space stated in the Computational Details and confirmed by the paper's own 'CAS(6,5) wavefunction' phrasing. method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (IPEA shift 0.25 au)
active_space_orbital_description: A CAS of 15 orbitals (11 a' and 4 a'') holding 19 valence electrons, selected via an MRDCI wave function correlating all valence electrons. The resulting CASSCF wave function is a linear combination of 6246240 doublet spin-adapted configuration state functions.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 2A''. CASSCF(19,15)/aug-cc-pVTZ gives a central O-O bond length of 1.674 A and a classical dissociation energy De = 1.1 kcal/mol, with dissociation proceeding through a transition structure with a 1.5 kcal/mol barrier. CASPT2(19,15) gives a central O-O bond of 1.682 A (experiment 1.688 A) and De = 5.8 kcal/mol; with the zero-point correction from CASSCF(19,15) harmonic frequencies this becomes D0 = 3.0 kcal/mol, in excellent agreement with the experimental D0 = 2.9 +/- 0.1 kcal/mol of Le Picard et al. At the CASPT2 level no energetic barrier beyond the endoergicity of the reaction was found.
Other: Dynamic correlation is decisive for this radical: CASSCF(19,15) gives De = 1.1 kcal/mol with a 1.5 kcal/mol dissociation barrier, whereas CASPT2 on the same space gives De = 5.8 kcal/mol and no barrier beyond the reaction endoergicity. The CASPT2 D0 (3.0) matches experiment (2.9 +/- 0.1); the CASSCF value does not. Active space chosen via an MRDCI wave function correlating all valence electrons.
reference_short: Anglada, Olivella & Sole, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2010, 6, 2743
notes: Dissociation of the ground-state trans-HOOO radical. The (19,15) space and its a'/a'' symmetry breakdown are stated explicitly, as is the CSF count. The same CASSCF wave function had been used previously with a 6-311+G(2df,2p) basis in the authors' earlier study of the long O-O bond; this row records the aug-cc-pVTZ results of the present paper. Dissociation-product fragments HO and O2 are separate rows.

method: CASSCF (spin-spin dipolar and spin-orbit coupling from the one- and two-electron terms of the Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian); ROHF, CIS, CISD and CISDTQ also used for the spin-spin elements

active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals. The BKKM orbital localization is used to rotate the two singly occupied orbitals of the triplet open shell into the most localized pair; natural orbital analysis was based on triplet MOs. The paper notes the (6,6) ceiling was imposed by the memory available at the time, and that 8 electrons in 8 orbitals could be treated subsequently.
electronic_structure_description: 1,1-biradical. The zero-field-splitting parameters D' and E' of the T1 state of CH2 are dominated by spin-spin dipolar coupling. The CI expansion size ranges from 1 (ROHF) to 461916. Axis convention: x out-of-plane, y the two-fold axis, z parallel to the H-H line, which interchanges y and z relative to the usual labelling for these molecules.
Other: Both T1 zero-field-splitting parameters D' and E' of CH2 are dominated by spin-spin dipolar coupling rather than spin-orbit coupling - the opposite balance to SiH2. The (6,6) ceiling was a stated memory limitation of the time, not a chemical judgement, so the space size should not be read as a recommendation.
reference_short: Havlas & Michl, J. Phys. Chem. A 1998, 102, 5298

geometry_source: CASSCF/3-21G* geometry optimizations for all species, with one test case reoptimized at CASSCF/6-31G*; all 3N-6 internal coordinates relaxed apart from stated symmetry constraints; analytical CASSCF/3-21G* frequencies characterize every stationary point; IRC following at CASSCF(4,4)/3-21G*
method: CASSCF; MR-CI (size-consistency corrected by the Davidson, Siegbahn and Pople schemes); CASSCF(4,4)+MP2
active_space_orbital_description: The four electrons and four orbitals constituting the supermolecular pi system of the noninteracting fragments silene and ethylene. The paper states this choice secures a correct description of dissociation into the two interacting units and gives a sufficiently flexible description of the diradical nature of the intermediates.
electronic_structure_description: Multistep path from ethylene plus silene to silacyclobutane. Transition state 5 has one imaginary a' frequency at 997 cm-1 at CASSCF(4,4)/3-21G*, shifting to 1754 cm-1 when reoptimized at CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* with an almost identical structure. The imaginary normal mode corresponds to a concerted ring closure, and IRC following confirms a path toward a planar silacyclobutane ring (structure 7), itself a transition state of C2v symmetry. Energies are reported relative to a supermolecule of ethylene and silene separated by 20 A. Zero-point corrections come from unscaled CASSCF/3-21G* frequencies using the same active space.
Other: Space chosen as the supermolecular pi system of the separated fragments precisely so that dissociation into silene plus ethylene is described correctly and the diradical character of the intermediates stays flexible; MR-CI size-consistency errors were corrected three ways (Davidson, Siegbahn, Pople) and cross-checked against CASSCF(4,4)+MP2.
reference_short: Schaad & Skancke, J. Phys. Chem. A 1997, 101, 7408
notes: Condensed to one row for the ethylene + silene reaction system per the one-row-per-compound rule; the paper's tables span several stationary points and intermediates of the same C3H8Si surface. The (4,4) active space and its composition (the supermolecular pi system of the two fragments) are stated explicitly, together with the reasoning behind the choice. Si is main-group so metal_center is none.

geometry_source: CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* geometry optimizations using redundant internal coordinates, with analytical frequency calculations confirming the nature of each stationary point and providing zero-point corrections
method: CASSCF
active_space_orbital_description: For the 3(pipi*) and ground-state surfaces: six electrons in six orbitals, namely the six pi orbitals of the reactants. The orbitals change along the reaction - two pi orbitals become the sigma and sigma* of the first bond formed in the biradical intermediate, and two more become the sigma and sigma* of the second bond in the cyclobutane product. For the 3(npi*) surface the space is also six electrons in six orbitals but includes the n orbital on the acrolein oxygen in place of the carbonyl pi orbital.
active_space_protocol: (6,6) six reactant pi orbitals for the 3(pipi*) and ground-state surfaces; (6,6) with the acrolein oxygen n orbital replacing the carbonyl pi orbital for the 3(npi*) surface; (8,7) containing both the n and pi orbitals for reoptimization where possible, otherwise (8,7) single points with state-averaged orbitals weighted equally between the two states; 1(npi*) treated by (8,7) single points at the 3(npi*) geometries because optimizations would not converge
electronic_structure_description: Ground- and excited-state surfaces for the [2+2] photocycloaddition of alpha,beta-enones to alkenes, mapped for s-trans-acrolein plus ethylene. Addition proceeds via attack at the beta-carbon of acrolein to give a biradical intermediate and then the cyclobutane product. Two 1(npi*)/3(npi*)/3(pipi*) crossing regions exist, the first in acrolein itself. The 1(npi*) surface has a very similar topology to the 3(npi*) surface. Relative energies with and without ZPE are tabulated at the CAS(6,6)/6-31G* level.
Other: Active space is surface-dependent by design: six reactant pi orbitals for the 3(pipi*) and ground states, the same size but with the acrolein oxygen n orbital replacing a carbonyl pi for 3(npi*), and (8,7) containing both n and pi where the two must be described together. Dynamic correlation is neglected deliberately because the paper's arguments concern biradical regions, where CASSCF over-stabilizes biradicaloids relative to zwitterionic structures.
reference_short: Wilsey, Gonzalez, Robb & Houk, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2000, 122, 5866
notes: Condensed to one row for the acrolein + ethylene reaction system per the one-row-per-compound rule; the paper's tables span many stationary points on several coupled surfaces. Three distinct active spaces are used depending on the surface, all stated explicitly with their orbital composition: active_space_nel/norb hold the (6,6) space used for the geometry optimizations, and the (npi*) variant and the (8,7) space are recorded in active_space_protocol. The paper states dynamic correlation is neglected deliberately because its arguments concern the biradical regions.

point_group: Cs for the symmetrical spiro saddle point; C1 for the unsymmetrical spiro transition structure
geometry_source: CAS(12,12)/6-31G(d) and CAS(8,8) optimized transition structures; DFT, CCSD(T) and BD(T)/BD(TQ) single points at these and at CCSD(T)/6-31G* geometries
method: CASSCF; CASSCF+MP2; multireference RS perturbation theory (RSPT2); compared with B3LYP, CCSD, CCSD(T), BD(T), BD(TQ)
software: Gaussian 98 (revision A.7); GAMESS (CASSCF and multireference RS perturbation theory); ACES II
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF optimizations, with 6-31+G(d,p) and 6-311+G(d,p) used for larger spaces and single points
active_space_orbital_description: The paper states that in its experience CASSCF is not reliable for these very electron-rich systems unless the active space comprises essentially a full valence shell calculation, to ensure balanced correlation of all the oxygen lone pairs; the (12,12) space is chosen on that basis. The most active molecular orbitals, from HOMO-3 to LUMO+3, are tabulated for both the Cs second-order saddle point and the C1 transition structure at CAS(12,12)/6-31G(d).
active_space_protocol: (8,8)/6-31G(d) and (8,8)/6-311+G(d,p); (10,10)/6-31G(d); (12,12)/6-31G(d) - the paper's conclusion is that the space must approach a full valence shell for balanced correlation of the oxygen lone pairs
electronic_structure_description: Activation barriers for epoxidation of ethylene with dioxirane, comparing unsymmetrical (C1) and symmetrical (Cs) spiro approaches (kcal/mol, Table 1). CAS(8,8)/6-31G(d)+MP2: 15.41 (C1) vs 17.51 (Cs), difference 2.10. CAS(10,10)/6-31G(d)+MP2: 14.69 vs 20.07, difference 5.38. BD(T)/6-311+G(d,p)//CAS(12,12)/6-31G(d) gives a Cs-vs-C1 difference of 0.60, and BD(TQ) at the same geometries 1.37; BD(T)/6-311+G(d,p)//CAS(8,8)/6-311+G(d,p) gives -0.29. For comparison B3LYP/6-31G(d) gives 12.94 vs 12.95 and CCSD(T)/6-31G* 15.56 vs 16.98. The potential energy surface for the approach of dioxirane to the C=C is described as very soft.
Other: Central methodological claim: for these very electron-rich systems CASSCF is unreliable unless the space approaches a full valence shell, so that all oxygen lone pairs are correlated in a balanced way. The Cs-vs-C1 preference is space-sensitive - 2.10 kcal/mol at CAS(8,8)+MP2 but 5.38 at CAS(10,10)+MP2 - and the surface for dioxirane approaching the C=C is very soft.
reference_short: Dmitrenko & Bach, J. Phys. Chem. A 2004, 108, 6886
notes: Methodological reassessment comparing symmetrical (Cs) versus unsymmetrical (C1) spiro transition structures for oxygen atom transfer. Several active spaces are used, all stated: (8,8), (10,10) and (12,12); active_space_nel/norb record the (12,12) space used for the reported optimized transition structures, with the others in active_space_protocol. Barriers copied from Table 1 as printed. The paper also treats dimethyldioxirane (DMDO) but does not state a separate CASSCF active space for it, so no DMDO row is created.

geometry_source: excited-state optimized geometries compared across methodologies (AM1/CISD, HF/CIS, CASSCF, DFT/CI); the CASSCF wave function is specified without symmetry restrictions so it is valid over the whole potential energy surface independently of the input geometry
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (block-diagonal Fock-matrix approximation, CASPT2D); CASSI for transition properties
active_space_orbital_description: 12 active electrons in 12 active orbitals: all benzene and nitrile pi and pi* orbitals, the amino nitrogen n orbital, and one antibonding methyl orbital whose inclusion is stated to stabilize the calculations significantly. All 11 core orbitals are frozen and the remaining 22 valence orbitals are kept inactive.
electronic_structure_description: Comparative study of the dual fluorescence of DMABN, focused on the significance of excited-state optimized geometries. The first excited state has 1Lb character and the second 1La character. Geometries of the twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) state differ between methodologies. A barrier from 1Lb to the 1TICT state is obtained only with AM1/CISD geometries; AM1/CISD, HF/CIS and CASSCF all predict a strongly endothermic reaction. Reference weights of the CASSCF wave function within the CASPT2 solution are reported as a check on the validity of the perturbational treatment.
Other: Adding one antibonding methyl orbital to the benzene/nitrile pi,pi* plus amino-n space is stated to stabilize the calculations significantly. A barrier from 1Lb to the 1TICT state appears only with AM1/CISD geometries; CASSCF, AM1/CISD and HF/CIS all predict a strongly endothermic reaction, so the conclusion depends on which optimized excited-state geometry is used.
reference_short: Parusel et al., Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. / J. Phys. Chem. A 2002 (see reference_doi)
notes: Second DMABN paper in this batch, independent of 10.1021/ja0490572 and with a different active space: (12,12) here, with its full orbital composition stated, versus the (12e/11o) SVP space of the Kohn & Hattig study. The orbital partitioning (11 frozen core, 22 inactive valence) is stated explicitly. CASPT2 energies use the block-diagonal Fock approximation (CASPT2D) by the paper's own statement.

geometry_source: geometries from DFT with the B-P86 functional and a cc-pVTZ basis set; CASSCF energies computed on top of a Hartree-Fock reference
method: CASSCF
basis_set: cc-pVDZ, with the p functions on hydrogen omitted following Kawashima et al. for the parent anthracene, having been shown to be unimportant for optical transitions
active_space_orbital_description: A maximum of 13 active orbitals in each case: the 8 occupied valence orbitals plus the 5 most relevant virtual orbitals of the pi system, taken from the preceding Hartree-Fock step. Both the active space wave function coefficients and the wave functions themselves were optimized in the CAS step.
electronic_structure_description: Dual fluorescence of 2-methoxyanthracene derivatives, with ground-state and first-excited-state energies obtained from CASSCF to give optical transition energies, and rotation potential curves computed as a function of the substituent torsion angle. The paper cautions that its own active space is at the limit of what can be handled, and that the inevitable selection of active orbitals together with the size of the numerical iterations may make the computed rotation barriers artifacts to a large extent; a torsion minimum near 20 degrees is found in both ground and excited states.
Other: Authors' own caveat: the active space is at the limit of what can be handled, and the selection of active orbitals plus the size of the numerical iterations may make the computed rotation barriers largely artifacts. Treat the barrier heights as unreliable while the state ordering is qualitatively supported.
reference_short: Albrecht, Bohne, Granzhan, Ihmels et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 1036
notes: Series paper covering anthracene (1b), 2-chloroanthracene (1c), 2-methoxyanthracene (1d), 2-methoxy-6-methylanthracene (1e) and further derivatives 1f-1h; the paper does not tie its CASSCF active space to one specific member, so this row records the shared computational treatment rather than splitting per derivative. active_space_norb=13 is stated ('a maximum of 13 active orbitals'); active_space_nel=16 is the arithmetic consequence of the 8 occupied valence orbitals being doubly occupied and is not itself printed. The paper's own warning that the computed rotation barriers may be artifacts is recorded in electronic_structure_description and should be read before using those numbers.

compound_name: bicyclo[3.1.0]hex-3-en-2-one (8), rearranging to the ketonic tautomer of phenol (11)
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G(d) optimized stationary points on the S0 and T1 potential energy surfaces; CASPT2 single points at those geometries
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (CASPT2-g1 with the full Hartree-Fock matrix in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian)
software: Gaussian 98 (revision A.9) for the CASSCF calculations; MOLCAS 5 for the CASPT2
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for geometry optimizations; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 single points, given as [9s4p1d/3s2p1d] for C and O and [4s1p/2s1p] for H, with all valence electrons correlated
active_space_orbital_description: For the internal cyclopropane C-C bond cleavage on S0 and T1: six electrons in six orbitals, namely the four orbitals of the two pi systems (pi and pi* on the carbonyl and on the ethylene fragment) plus the sigma and sigma* pair of the C-C bond being broken; the six active electrons are four pi electrons and two sigma electrons.
active_space_protocol: (6,5) for the lower excited states of 8: the four pi/pi* orbitals of the carbonyl and ethylene fragments plus the oxygen lone pair n, holding four pi and two n electrons; (6,6) for the cyclopropane C-C cleavage on S0/T1, replacing the n lone pair with the sigma/sigma* of the breaking C-C bond; (8,8) for the 1,2-hydrogen shift transition structure of intermediate 10, adding the sigma/sigma* pair of the migrating C-H bond. Single-point (8,8) calculations were run for intermediates 10 and 11 at the (6,6) geometries so energies are comparable.
electronic_structure_description: Thermal and photochemical rearrangement of bicyclo[3.1.0]hex-3-en-2-one to the ketonic tautomer of phenol, followed on the S0 and T1 surfaces. The sequence proceeds by internal cyclopropane C-C bond cleavage to intermediate 10 and then a 1,2-hydrogen shift to 11.
Other: Textbook case of an active space grown to follow the reaction coordinate rather than fixed once: (6,5) with the oxygen lone pair for the vertical excited states, (6,6) swapping that lone pair for the sigma/sigma* of the C-C bond actually breaking, then (8,8) adding the sigma/sigma* of the migrating C-H for the hydrogen-shift transition state. Energies were made comparable by re-running (8,8) single points at the (6,6) geometries. CASPT2-g1 with the full Hartree-Fock matrix was used deliberately in place of standard CASPT2-0, which is known to underestimate open-shell states relative to closed-shell ones - directly relevant here since the comparison is between excited and ground states.
reference_short: Bertran, Sole et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2002, 124, 15375
notes: Condensed to one row for the rearrangement system per the one-row-per-compound rule; the paper's surfaces span reactant 8, intermediate 10 and product 11 on both S0 and T1. Three active spaces are stated with full orbital composition and are recorded in active_space_protocol; active_space_nel/norb hold the (6,6) space used for the C-C cleavage geometry optimizations.

method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (CASPT2-g1 with the full Hartree-Fock matrix in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian)
basis_set: 6-311+G(3df,2p) for both the CASSCF geometry optimizations and the CASPT2 single points, with all valence electrons correlated
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in ten molecular orbitals for several stationary points along the reaction; the space is built from the fragment orbitals of the two radicals (CO and OO sigma/sigma* and OO pi/pi* sets) as required to describe the coupled system.
active_space_protocol: Per-species spaces set from MRDCI natural orbital occupancies: (7,6) CH3O2*; (5,4) HO2*; (12,10) for several stationary points of the complex/transition structures; (4,4) CH3OOH; (8,6) O2
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase CH3O2* + HO2* -> CH3O2H + O2 reaction. A hydrogen-bonded complex CX-S is formed; inspection of the CASSCF(12,10) natural orbitals for CX-S shows two a'' orbitals with occupancies 1.022 and 1.017, the positive and negative combinations of the pi-type orbitals carrying the unpaired electron of each isolated radical. CX-S is therefore a hydrogen-bonded species in which the two unpaired electrons are not used for bonding but couple to an overall open-shell singlet of A' symmetry. Stabilization energy 4.9 kcal/mol at 0 K after correction.
Other: Active spaces were not fixed a priori: each species' space was set from the fractional occupancies of natural orbitals of an MRDCI wave function correlating all valence electrons, giving a different (nel,norb) per stationary point - (4,4) for CH3OOH up to (12,10) for several stationary points. CASPT2-g1 with the full Hartree-Fock matrix was chosen over standard CASPT2-0, which underestimates open-shell relative to closed-shell states - essential here because the reaction couples open-shell radicals to a closed-shell product.
reference_short: Anglada, Olivella & Sole, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 6073
notes: Condensed row for the reaction system; the isolated radicals and products carry their own rows because the paper assigns each its own separately determined active space. The open-shell-singlet character of the hydrogen-bonded complex is the paper's central computational evidence and is diagnosed directly from CASSCF natural orbital occupancies.

ligand_set: two trans oxo ligands (O) and four PH3
point_group: D4h idealised, with orbitals labelled in D2h
method: CASSCF; full CI within the CASSCF orbital space for excited states of the same space and spin symmetry; RHF for comparison
basis_set: effective core potentials of Stevens et al.; (5s5p4d) valence basis for Mo, contracted to double-zeta quality; (2s2p) double-zeta sets for the main-group atoms, with a d polarization function added for O and other ligand atoms
relativistic_treatment: effective core potentials, which the paper notes incorporate relativistic effects for elements with Z > 36
active_space_orbital_description: 14 electrons in 11 active orbitals: the metal-chalcogen bonding orbitals (5ag, 2b2g, 2b3g), the metal nonbonding orbital (6ag), the chalcogen lone pair orbitals (3b1u, 4b2u, 4b3u), the metal-chalcogen pi* orbitals (3b2g, 3b3g), and the metal-chalcogen and Mo-P sigma* orbitals (dz2 and dx2-y2). The same orbital space was used for the excited-state CASSCF calculations.
active_space_protocol: (14,11) for all four complexes; additionally (16,14) for Mo(S)2(PH3)4, obtained by adding the occupied 3b1g Mo-P bonding orbital and two empty orbitals of ag and b1u symmetry to the (14,11) set
electronic_structure_description: d2 Mo(IV) complex in an octahedral field distorted by axial compression. The eg (dx2-y2, dz2) set remains Mo-P and Mo-Q sigma antibonding and is not strongly split, while the t2g set splits substantially into a nonbonding b2g (dxy) orbital and a pi-antibonding eg (dxz, dyz) pair through pi interaction with the chalcogen. The HOMO is the metal nonbonding orbital and the LUMO the metal-chalcogen pi* (3b2g/3b3g). The oxo complex differs from the heavier chalcogenides in which transitions lie lowest. The 3b2g and 3b3g pi* orbitals are almost degenerate, so the calculated 1B2g and 1B3g energies are very close.
Other: Active space built from a chemically explicit orbital list rather than a d-only set: the metal-chalcogen bonding and pi* orbitals and the chalcogen lone pairs are all included, which is what allows the lone-pair-to-pi* assignment for the heavier chalcogenides to emerge. The (14,11) space was used for this complex; the sulfido analogue was additionally recomputed with a larger (16,14) space as a convergence check. Excited states of the same space and spin symmetry as the lowest were obtained by full CI within the same orbital space optimized for the CASSCF lowest state, so state ordering within a symmetry is not biased by separate orbital optimizations.
reference_short: Wei, Lin & Hall, Inorg. Chem. (trans-Mo(Q)2(PH3)4 electronic structure and spectra)
notes: One of four trans-Mo(Q)2(PH3)4 chalcogenido complexes (Q = O, S, Se, Te) sharing the same (14,11) active space, whose full orbital composition is stated explicitly; one row per chalcogen since the transition assignment changes down the group. Mo(IV) and the d2 configuration are stated by the paper; d_electron_count carries the 4d shell prefix per policy. Relativistic effects enter through the ECPs, which the paper states cover elements with Z > 36 - relevant for the Se and Te members.

The eg (dx2-y2, dz2) set remains Mo-P and Mo-Q sigma antibonding and is not strongly split, while the t2g set splits substantially into a nonbonding b2g (dxy) orbital and a pi-antibonding eg (dxz, dyz) pair through pi interaction with the chalcogen. point_group: C2h, Ci and C2 examined for the s-trans form; C2 for the gauche form
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G(d) optimized geometries, with vibrational frequencies from analytical derivatives
method: CASSCF; multiconfigurational linear response for transition properties (compared with UHF, UBLYP and UB3LYP)
active_space_orbital_description: Three electrons correlated in four pi orbitals - two au and two bg orbitals in C2h symmetry.
electronic_structure_description: Radical cation of 2,5-dimethyl-2,4-hexadiene, characterized by resonance Raman spectroscopy and assigned with the aid of the calculations. Spin contamination in the unrestricted references is minor (<S2> of 0.7531 for UBLYP and 0.7593 for UB3LYP against 0.75 exact).
Other: Open-shell space is deliberately asymmetric: three electrons in four pi orbitals for the cation versus four in four for the neutral, i.e. the orbital set is held fixed across the ionization while the electron count changes, so cation and neutral frequencies are compared on a common orbital footing. The CASSCF result is one of four methods (UHF, UBLYP, UB3LYP, CASSCF) cross-compared against the experimental resonance Raman spectrum, and the small <S2> values indicate the unrestricted single-reference treatments were not badly spin-contaminated for this system.
reference_short: Balakrishnan et al., J. Phys. Chem. A (resonance Raman of the 2,5-dimethyl-2,4-hexadiene radical cation)
notes: Resonance Raman study with supporting calculations. Active space (3 electrons, 4 pi orbitals with au/bg symmetry breakdown) stated explicitly for the radical cation; the neutral parent carries its own row with (4,4).

point_group: s-trans form and gauche form (C2) examined
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G(d) optimized geometries, with vibrational frequencies from analytical derivatives
method: CASSCF; multiconfigurational linear response for transition properties (compared with UHF, UBLYP and UB3LYP)
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in four pi orbitals; the same four-orbital pi set used for the radical cation, with one more electron.
electronic_structure_description: Neutral parent diene, computed alongside the radical cation so that geometry and frequency changes on ionization can be assigned.
Other: Same four pi orbitals as the radical cation row but with four electrons rather than three, so that the neutral and the cation are described with a consistent orbital space across the ionization; this is what makes the computed frequency shifts on ionization meaningful rather than an artifact of differing spaces.

notes: Neutral parent of the radical cation studied in the same paper; separate row because the electron count in the shared four-orbital pi space differs.

geometry_source: geometry optimizations in the 6-31G(d) basis (DFT/B3LYP and CASSCF), with the ground state of C151 reoptimized in that basis; 6-311G(d,p) geometries provided in the Supporting Information
method: CASSCF (state-averaged); CASPT2 in both single-state and multi-state variants; compared with TDDFT, CIS and ZINDO
software: MOLCAS 5.2 (CASSCF and CASPT2); Gaussian 98 (revision A.11.3) for geometry optimizations and DFT
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the geometry optimizations, with 6-31+G(d) and 6-311G(d,p) also used in the study; six Cartesian d functions in the 6-31G(d) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: A 10-electron, 10-orbital reference space. The paper's notation is 'CASSCF n-state x/y', meaning a CASSCF averaging the n lowest electronic states and distributing x electrons among y orbitals; single-state and multi-state CASPT2 built on these are denoted CASPT2 n-state x/y and MCASPT2 n-state x/y. The individual orbitals are not enumerated.
electronic_structure_description: Electronic excitation energies to several low-lying singlet states, plus ground- and excited-state dipole moments, computed across TDDFT, CASSCF, CASPT2/MCASPT2, CIS and ZINDO. TDDFT is reported to give excellent S1 <- S0 excitation energies.
Other: The active space size here is set by intruder states, not by the chemistry: reference spaces smaller than 10 electrons in 10 orbitals produce intruder-state problems in single-state CASPT2, with the squared reference coefficient dropping below 0.1 for one state while the other two sat near 0.6. The excitation energies from those smaller spaces were not in fact very different (especially at multi-state CASPT2), but the authors judged them less reliable and declined to report them. Multi-state CASPT2 is required at these larger reference spaces because of near-degeneracy in the second-order energies. Anyone reading (10,10) as a chemical recommendation for this chromophore would be misreading it.
reference_short: Cave, Castner et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2002 (ground and excited states of Coumarin 151 and Coumarin 120)
notes: Coumarin laser dye studied alongside Coumarin 120 in the same paper; one row each since the two required different active spaces. Space size stated explicitly; orbital composition never enumerated.

geometry_source: geometry optimizations in the 6-31G(d) basis (DFT/B3LYP and CASSCF), with the ground state of C151 reoptimized in that basis; 6-311G(d,p) geometries provided in the Supporting Information
method: CASSCF (state-averaged); CASPT2 in both single-state and multi-state variants; compared with TDDFT, CIS and ZINDO
software: MOLCAS 5.2 (CASSCF and CASPT2); Gaussian 98 (revision A.11.3) for geometry optimizations and DFT
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the geometry optimizations, with 6-31+G(d) and 6-311G(d,p) also used in the study; six Cartesian d functions in the 6-31G(d) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: A 14-electron, 10-orbital reference space, in the paper's 'CASSCF n-state x/y' notation (n lowest states averaged, x electrons among y orbitals). The individual orbitals are not enumerated.
electronic_structure_description: Electronic excitation energies to several low-lying singlet states, plus ground- and excited-state dipole moments, computed across TDDFT, CASSCF, CASPT2/MCASPT2, CIS and ZINDO.
Other: Intruder-state effects were described as 'similar, but in fact more extreme' than for Coumarin 151, and the 14-electron 10-orbital space was chosen specifically to avoid them. Note the contrast with the C151 row: same number of active orbitals but four more active electrons, driven entirely by intruder-state avoidance rather than by a difference in the chromophore's valence structure. Multi-state CASPT2 is needed at this reference space size because of near-degeneracy in the second-order energies.
reference_short: Cave, Castner et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2002 (ground and excited states of Coumarin 151 and Coumarin 120)
notes: Coumarin laser dye studied alongside Coumarin 151 in the same paper; separate row because it required a different (14,10) space where C151 used (10,10). Space size stated explicitly; orbital composition never enumerated.

compound_name: pyridylnitrene / carbene-nitrene rearrangement system (species 19, open-shell singlet and triplet)
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G* optimizations with single-point CASPT2; B3LYP/6-31G* and B3LYP/6-311G** used for the closed-shell species and IR spectra
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 single points (B3LYP with the Cramer-Ziegler sum method used for comparison on open-shell singlets)
software: MOLCAS version 7.2 (CASSCF and CASPT2); Gaussian 03 revision E.01 (DFT)
active_space_orbital_description: An 8-electron, 8-orbital active space; for species 19 this is three pi orbitals, three pi* orbitals, and the two p atomic orbitals on the nitrene nitrogen. Details of the correlated orbitals are given in the Supporting Information.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet nitrenes have an open-shell electronic structure, which is why CASSCF/CASPT2 rather than DFT is required for the 18 -> 19 reaction path. The T0-S1 gap (3A'' - 1A'') in 19 is computed as 18.6 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 19.7 at CASPT2, against 16.2 kcal/mol from B3LYP/6-31G* with the Cramer-Ziegler correction. For comparison, the literature triplet/open-shell-singlet gap in phenylnitrene is about 15 kcal/mol (18 assumed in earlier work). The overall carbene-nitrene rearrangement 10 (1A') -> 19 (1A'') would be exothermic by about 39-48 kcal/mol.
Other: CASSCF/CASPT2 is used selectively rather than throughout: the paper runs B3LYP for closed-shell species and IR spectra and switches to an (8,8) multireference treatment only for the open-shell singlet nitrene species, because singlet nitrenes are open-shell and a single-reference description fails there. The space is composed to match that physics - three pi, three pi*, plus the two p AOs on the nitrene nitrogen, i.e. the ring pi system together with the orbitals carrying the nitrene's two non-bonding electrons. The authors report the CASSCF reference weights staying stable at 77-80%, a stated check that the reference remains dominant and the CASPT2 is not being run on a poor zeroth order.
reference_short: Kvaskoff, Bednarek, Wentrup et al., J. Org. Chem. 2010, 75, 1600
notes: Matrix-isolation and computational study of carbene-nitrene rearrangements; the multireference component covers the open-shell singlet and triplet states of the nitrene species 19, which is what this row records. The (8,8) space size and its composition for 19 are stated in the main text, with fuller orbital detail deferred to the Supporting Information, which was not retrieved. Condensed to one row for the rearrangement system rather than splitting the many DFT-only species, none of which carry an active space.

point_group: C2v for the stable S0 and S1 structures
geometry_source: state-specific (10,9)CASSCF optimized S0 geometry, with global potential energy surfaces scanned at the same level; the S2/S1 conical intersection located with Gaussian 98
method: CASSCF (state-specific); MRMP2 (second-order multireference Moller-Plesset)
software: GAMESS, except for the determination of the S2/S1 conical intersection which used Gaussian 98
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta (DZ) augmented by polarization functions on carbon (alpha_d = 0.75)
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in nine orbitals: the highest four occupied pi orbitals and the lowest four unoccupied pi* orbitals, plus the fifth (lowest) occupied pi orbital added deliberately so the space stays consistent across conformations.
active_space_protocol: (8,8) - highest four occupied pi and lowest four pi* - shown by preliminary CI to describe the low-lying excited states at any single conformation; extended to (10,9) by adding the fifth occupied pi orbital for scanning the global potential energy surfaces
electronic_structure_description: Ground and low-lying excited singlet states of phenylacetylene. Preliminary CI shows the low-lying excited states are well described by configuration state functions from the highest four pi to the lowest four pi* orbitals. The S1 state has B2 symmetry under C2v and is assigned as the local excitation; excitation energies, oscillator strengths and main CSFs are tabulated at MRMP2 and other levels. An S2/S1 conical intersection is located.
Other: Clear example of an active space enlarged for surface continuity rather than for accuracy at a point. Preliminary CI established that (8,8) - the highest four occupied pi and lowest four pi* - suffices to describe the low-lying states at every conformation sampled. But which orbitals occupy that top set changes with conformation: the fifth (lowest) occupied pi orbital that lies outside the space at one geometry slips into it at another, and the paper states that a conformation-dependent active space leads to unphysical discontinuity of the potential energy surfaces. The fifth occupied pi was therefore added, giving (10,9) for the global surface scans. Anyone choosing a space for a single-point excitation energy on this system could use (8,8); anyone scanning a surface should not.
reference_short: Amatatsu & Hasebe, J. Phys. Chem. A (ab initio study on phenylacetylene in S1 and S2)
notes: Both active spaces are stated explicitly with their orbital composition and the reasoning for moving between them. active_space_nel/norb record the (10,9) space actually used for the reported surfaces and geometry optimization; the (8,8) space that suffices at a fixed conformation is recorded in active_space_protocol and Other.

geometry_source: CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G potential energy surfaces scanned as a function of R(C-C), with minimum structures optimized under C2 symmetry
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (10,10) single points to check dynamical correlation
basis_set: 6-31G, with additional single points in 6-31G* to check basis set dependence
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten pi orbitals.
active_space_protocol: (10,10) for both isomers - ten pi orbitals in the open-ring form, two sigma plus eight pi in the closed-ring form; (14,14) single points adding four more sigma electrons and the sigma orbitals of the C-S bonds, to check the dynamical correlation effect; (10,10)/6-31G* and CASPT2(10,10) single points as further checks
electronic_structure_description: Ground (1A) and two lower excited (2A and 1B) states, with potential energy surfaces computed as a function of the reacting R(C-C) distance and minimum structures located under C2 symmetry. CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G energies are quoted relative to -1178.22197 au (1A closed form) and CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G* relative to -1178.42459 au.
Other: The (10,10) space is held at the same size across the photochromic reaction but deliberately not at the same composition: ten pi orbitals in this open-ring form, versus two sigma plus eight pi in the closed-ring form, because the sigma bond formed on cyclization must be in the space on the closed side. Keeping the count fixed while letting the orbital character follow the reaction is what makes the two isomers' surfaces comparable along R(C-C). Convergence was checked three separate ways - (14,14) adding the C-S sigma electrons and orbitals, 6-31G* for basis dependence, and CASPT2(10,10) for dynamical correlation.
reference_short: Asano, Murakami, Kobayashi et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2003 (photochromic cycloreversion of dithienylethenes)
notes: Open-ring isomer of the photochromic dithienylethene; separate row from the closed-ring isomer because the ten active orbitals have different character in the two forms even though the (nel,norb) label is identical.

geometry_source: CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G potential energy surfaces scanned as a function of R(C-C), with minimum structures optimized under C2 symmetry
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (10,10) single points to check dynamical correlation
basis_set: 6-31G, with additional single points in 6-31G* to check basis set dependence
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals, which for the closed-ring isomer correspond to 2 sigma and 8 pi orbitals rather than the ten pi orbitals used for the open-ring form.
active_space_protocol: (10,10) for both isomers - ten pi orbitals in the open-ring form, two sigma plus eight pi in the closed-ring form; (14,14) single points adding four more sigma electrons and the sigma orbitals of the C-S bonds, to check the dynamical correlation effect; (10,10)/6-31G* and CASPT2(10,10) single points as further checks
electronic_structure_description: Ground (1A) and two lower excited (2A and 1B) states along the cycloreversion coordinate R(C-C), with the role of the conical intersection in the photochromic cycloreversion as the paper's focus. CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G energies are quoted relative to -1178.22197 au (1A closed form) and CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G* relative to -1178.42459 au.
Other: Same (10,10) count as the open-ring isomer but a different orbital set - 2 sigma and 8 pi here versus 10 pi there - so that the sigma bond broken during cycloreversion is inside the active space on this side of the reaction. This is the point a consumer would miss from the (10,10) label alone: the space must be re-composed, not merely re-sized, when following a ring-opening coordinate. Checked against (14,14) with the C-S sigma orbitals added, 6-31G*, and CASPT2(10,10).
reference_short: Asano, Murakami, Kobayashi et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2003 (photochromic cycloreversion of dithienylethenes)
notes: Closed-ring isomer of the photochromic dithienylethene; separate row from the open-ring isomer because the ten active orbitals have different character in the two forms even though the (nel,norb) label is identical.

compound_name: benzopyran (model for benzospiropyran photochromic ring opening)
geometry_source: critical points optimized at CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G with single points at 6-31G*; selected geometries (the conical intersection and others) reoptimized at 6-31G* because of their sensitivity; relaxation pathways computed at 6-31G*
method: CASSCF
basis_set: 6-31G for the optimizations, 6-31G* for single points and for reoptimizing sensitive geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals for benzopyran. A smaller pyran model is used for the S0 relaxation pathways, and an 'augmented' aminopyran model adds the nitrogen lone pair to the pyran active space as a check.
active_space_protocol: (12,11) for benzopyran; a reduced pyran model for modelling the S0 relaxation pathways; aminopyran with the nitrogen lone pair added to the pyran active space, used solely to test whether excluding nitrogen changes the conical intersection
electronic_structure_description: Conical intersection mechanism for photochemical C-O ring opening in benzospiropyran compounds. The excitation energy in benzopyran is about 107 kcal/mol at CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*. A Franck-Condon force analysis, an S1 minimum, a transition state and the conical intersection geometry are all located and characterized.
Other: Model reduction is validated rather than assumed, and the active space is the instrument for doing it. The real chromophore contains nitrogen, which the benzopyran and pyran models omit; the authors anticipated the objection that N-to-breaking-C-O conjugation could stabilize a zwitterionic state and change the character of the conical intersection, so they reoptimized the CI for aminopyran with the nitrogen lone pair added to the pyran active space. The CI in that augmented model came out very close to the pyran one, which is what justifies excluding nitrogen. The authors also state explicitly that accurate energetics (barriers, excitation energies) are NOT the aim - the work targets surface topology and reaction-coordinate structures - so the quoted energies should not be read as benchmark values.
reference_short: Celani, Bernardi, Olivucci, Robb et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1997
notes: Row records the benzopyran model at its stated (12,11) space; the smaller pyran and augmented aminopyran models are recorded in active_space_protocol because the paper does not state separate (nel,norb) values for them. The authors' own caveat that energetics are out of scope is carried in Other so the 107 kcal/mol figure is not mistaken for a converged excitation energy.

geometry_source: critical points optimized at SA-CASSCF(3,4)/3-21G* with energetics recalculated at SA-CASSCF(3,4)/6-31G*; the dynamics themselves run on SA-CASSCF(3,4)/STO-3G surfaces
method: SA-CASSCF (state-averaged over two states with equal weights); nonadiabatic dynamics by trajectory surface hopping and Ehrenfest algorithms implemented at the CASSCF level
software: the authors' CASSCF dynamics code (trajectory surface hopping and Ehrenfest)
basis_set: STO-3G for the dynamics, calibrated against 3-21G* optimizations with 6-31G* single-point energetics
active_space_orbital_description: Three electrons in an active space of four pi orbitals. State-averaged orbitals over two states with equal weights.
electronic_structure_description: Intramolecular electron transfer in the bis(methylene)adamantyl radical cation, presented as a case study of diabatic trapping. The D2 transition structure carries a small D1/D0 energy gap: 0.47 kcal/mol at the calibrated 6-31G* level, reduced to 0.23 kcal/mol with the STO-3G basis actually used for the dynamics.
Other: State-averaging here is not for spectroscopy but to keep the surface usable: averaging over two states with equal weights is stated to avoid discontinuities arising from symmetry breaking, without which the dynamics could not be propagated. The basis set is openly a resource compromise - STO-3G was forced by having to solve the SA-CP-MCSCF equations with 78 degrees of freedom at every trajectory time step - and the authors quantify the resulting bias rather than hiding it: the D1/D0 gap at the D2 transition structure shrinks from 0.47 to 0.23 kcal/mol on going to STO-3G, so the dynamics overestimate the tendency to hop surfaces. The small (3,4) space should be read as the minimum that supports on-the-fly dynamics, not as a converged description of this radical cation.
reference_short: Blancafort, Bernardi, Olivucci, Robb et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005
notes: Nonadiabatic dynamics study of intramolecular electron transfer. Active space (3 electrons, 4 pi orbitals) and the two-state equal-weight averaging are stated explicitly. The row records the dynamics level; the calibration levels (3-21G* optimization, 6-31G* energetics) use the same active space and are noted in basis_set and Other. The authors' quantified caveat about the STO-3G gap is carried in Other so the hopping probabilities are not taken at face value.

geometry_source: geometry locations and vibrational analysis mainly at CAS(14,12)/cc-pvdz; key points relocated at the CAS(8,6)+1+2/cc-pvdz level for comparison
method: CASSCF; internally contracted MR-CI including all single and double excitations relative to the CAS(8,6) reference, denoted CAS+1+2
software: MOLPRO (CAS and CAS+1+2); POLYRATE 8.2 (rate constants by conventional transition state theory)
active_space_orbital_description: The larger reference is a nearly full valence CAS - full valence except for the 2s orbitals of the oxygen atoms - consisting of 14 active electrons in 12 active orbitals. For the MR-CI a reduced eight-electron, six-orbital reference, CAS(8,6), is used.
active_space_protocol: (14,12) nearly full valence (excluding the O 2s orbitals) for geometry optimization and vibrational analysis; reduced to (8,6) as the MR-CI reference because MR-CI was not feasible on the larger reference; CAS(8,6)+1+2 then used to relocate key geometries and to compute the reported rate constants
electronic_structure_description: Reaction of triplet methylene with triplet dioxygen. On the singlet surface a transition state is located with a barrier of 1.65 kcal/mol, in good agreement with the experimental estimate of 1.0-1.5 kcal/mol; rearrangement and metathesis of the singlet intermediates are also examined. On the triplet surface, formation of CH2OO has a barrier of 5.79 kcal/mol and the triplet CH2OO can decompose to CH2O + O(3P) with a barrier of 2.92 kcal/mol. Total reaction rates at the CAS(8,6)+1+2/cc-pVDZ level fit k(T) = 4.27e-18 T^2.245 exp(-185/T) to within 5% over 295-2600 K.
Other: The two active spaces exist for a purely practical reason and the tradeoff is stated outright: the nearly-full-valence (14,12) reference is what the geometries and frequencies are built on, but MR-CI on that reference was not feasible, so the reference was cut to (8,6) for the CAS+1+2 work - and it is the smaller-reference CAS+1+2 numbers, not the larger CASSCF ones, that carry the reported rate constants. method: CASSCF; CASPT2; CASSI (CAS state interaction) for dipole transition moments
software: MOLCAS-3, with some calculations in Gaussian 94

active_space_orbital_description: Six active electrons in ten pi orbitals. The strongly correlating orbitals of fulvene are its six valence pi orbitals (four of b1 and two of a2 symmetry), of which the three lowest (pi1-pi3) are doubly occupied in the ground-state SCF wave function; this minimal (6,6) space was enlarged by four further orbitals (two b1 and two a2) because of intruder states, giving six pi electrons distributed among ten pi orbitals.

Other: Space selection stated as an explicit principle and then overridden by a practical problem. The stated criterion is to include all strongly correlating orbitals, those with occupation numbers appreciably different from 2 or 0, so that all static correlation and near-degeneracy sits in the CASSCF reference and no large terms appear in the perturbation expansion. geometry_source: full ground-state geometry optimizations with all degrees of freedom relaxed, at MP2 and/or CASSCF with 6-31G*, both in vacuo and in methanol via the ASEP/MD sequential QM/MM method
method: CASSCF for transition energies; CASPT2 for dynamic correlation; geometries at MP2 and/or CASSCF (denoted CASSCF//MP2, CASSCF//CASSCF, CASPT2//MP2, CASPT2//CASSCF)
active_space_orbital_description: The complete active pi space of the model: ten electrons in ten pi orbitals, corresponding to its five-double-bond skeleton.
electronic_structure_description: Minimal model of the rhodopsin chromophore, reproducing the 11-cis double bond, the iminium residue and the unsaturated chain but omitting the beta-ionone ring. Planar. Electronic absorption compared in the gas phase and in methanol, with the solvent shift and the nature of the absorbing states as the targets.
Other: Active space is defined by a rule rather than a number: the complete active pi space of whichever model is being treated, which is why it grows from (10e,10o) to (12e,12o) as a sixth double bond is added. The size therefore tracks the model's conjugation length and is not a tunable parameter here. Two caveats the paper raises bear on using these numbers: CASSCF geometries are known to overestimate bond length alternation, which significantly influences vertical excitation energies, and the torsion of the beta-ionone ring relative to the chain is very sensitive to the level of calculation - a larger torsion deconjugates the sixth double bond and raises the transition energy (a 0.3 eV hypsochromic shift was reported elsewhere on forcing that torsion to 90 degrees).

geometry_source: geometry and vibrational frequencies of the CeF4 ground state determined with the 4sigma/4sigma* CASSCF wave function, alongside RHF and ROHF
method: CASSCF (RHF, ROHF and MP2 also used)
software: not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Stevens RECP on cerium explicitly treating the 5s, 5p and 4f electrons, with a [4sp,2d,2f] contraction; all-electron 6-31G* on the halogens, with larger (11s,6p)/[5s,3p] for F and (13s,10p)/[6s,5p] Dunning triple-zeta for Cl, each augmented with two d polarization functions (TZ2P)
relativistic_treatment: relativistic effective core potential (Stevens et al.) on Ce
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons associated with the four Ce-X sigma bonds distributed among those bonding orbitals and the four sigma* antibonding orbitals, denoted 4sigma/4sigma* by the paper. A second, separate space denoted sigma2pi/sigma*2pi* holds the six electrons of one sigma and two pi orbitals of a single Ce-X bond together with the corresponding one sigma* and two pi* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: 4sigma/4sigma* (eight electrons, eight orbitals) used for the geometry and vibrational frequencies of the CeX4 ground state; sigma2pi/sigma*2pi* (six electrons, six orbitals localized on one Ce-X bond) used to investigate cleavage of that Ce-X bond
electronic_structure_description: At RHF, MP2 and CASSCF levels CeF4 possesses a stable tetrahedral (Td) structure. The paper contrasts the reduction of CeCl4 to CeCl3 with the CeF4 case to explain their different stabilities. The related open-shell CeX3 trihalides have a (4f z3)1 ground configuration, in which the singly occupied 4f orbital lies perpendicular to the molecular plane, minimizing electrostatic repulsion with the ligands.
Other: Two purpose-built active spaces rather than one general one, each matched to the property being computed: the delocalized 4sigma/4sigma* space over all four Ce-X bonds for the equilibrium geometry and vibrational frequencies, and a bond-localized sigma2pi/sigma*2pi* space on a single Ce-X linkage for the dissociation. Neither includes the 4f shell, which the RECP treats explicitly but which is formally empty in Ce(IV) - the 4f occupancy is instead the central issue for the open-shell CeX3 trihalides in the same paper, which are handled at RHF/ROHF/MP2 and carry no CASSCF space. The paper also warns that the relative stability of planar versus pyramidal CeCl3 depends strongly on both basis set and correlation treatment.
reference_short: Lanza & Fragala, J. Phys. Chem. A 1998, 102, 7990
notes: Ce(IV) tetrahalide, formally 4f0, treated with CASSCF; the trihalides CeX3 in the same paper are open-shell 4f1 systems handled at RHF/ROHF/MP2 with no stated active space, so they get no rows. Both CASSCF spaces are stated with their orbital composition; active_space_nel/norb hold the 4sigma/4sigma* space used for geometry and frequencies. d_electron_count is written 4f0 with its shell per policy, following from the stated Ce(IV) oxidation state. The program package is not named in the extracted text, so software is recorded as not stated.

point_group: Cs for the reference geometries; C1 geometries arise along the methyl internal rotation coordinate
geometry_source: CASSCF-optimized geometries; methyl internal rotation barriers computed in the X and B states
method: CASSCF; multireference singles and doubles CI (CAS+1+2), both uncontracted and internally contracted, with multireference Davidson corrections for higher-order excitations
active_space_orbital_description: Four active orbitals holding five electrons: the singly occupied radical orbital (3a''), the CO pi and pi* orbitals (2a'' and 4a''), and the oxygen lone-pair a' orbital with its two electrons. The smaller three-orbital reference is the radical orbital plus the CO pi and pi* alone.
active_space_protocol: (3,3) reference of the singly occupied radical orbital (3a'') plus the CO pi and pi* (2a'', 4a''), workable for the B state only at Cs geometries; enlarged to (5,4) by adding the oxygen lone-pair a' orbital and its two electrons so that C1 geometries can be treated
electronic_structure_description: Barrier to methyl internal rotation of the 1-methylvinoxy radical in the X (2A'') and B (2A'') states. Vibrational frequencies are reported unscaled with an estimated accuracy of 25 cm-1.
Other: The active space is enlarged for a symmetry reason, not an accuracy one. The compact (3,3) reference - radical orbital plus CO pi/pi* - is stated to be workable for the B state only at Cs geometries; along the methyl rotation coordinate the molecule drops to C1, where the oxygen lone-pair a' orbital must be brought into the space, giving (5,4). Since the whole point of the paper is a torsional barrier, the geometries that matter are exactly the ones the smaller space cannot handle. A consumer picking (3,3) from a Cs single-point description would fail on the rotation coordinate.
reference_short: Yamaguchi et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2000 (methyl internal rotation of 1-methylvinoxy radical)
notes: Both reference spaces are stated with their orbital composition and the symmetry condition distinguishing them. active_space_nel/norb hold the (5,4) space, which is the one that covers the C1 geometries along the rotation coordinate the paper is about; the (3,3) space is in active_space_protocol. Comparison values at CASSCF(3,3)/6-31G** and (3,3)-CAS+1+2 are quoted in the paper's tables from ref 25.

geometry_source: geometries optimized to within 1e-4 Eh/a0; torsional scans performed at the SA2-CAS(12,11)/6-31G(d) level
method: SA2-CASSCF (state-averaged over two states); SA2-MRMP2 for dynamic correlation; compared with RI-CC2, B3LYP, PBE0 and long-range-corrected LC-BLYP
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF and MRMP2; def-TZVP and def2-TZVP for the DFT and RI-CC2 comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals, state-averaged over two states (SA2). The paper does not enumerate which orbitals compose the space.
electronic_structure_description: 4-N,N-dimethylamino-substituted benzylidene malononitrile. Undergoes S1 -> S0 internal conversion; the paper examines nonradiative deactivation via a twisting coordinate, using a two-state model. Experimental reference values for JDMN are quoted as 25.9 +/- 0.5 and 6.7 +/- 0.1 with a ratio of 0.68 +/- 0.2 in the paper's table.
Other: Cautionary case for taking CASSCF vertical energies at face value. At SA2-CAS(12,11)/6-31G(d) the computed excitation energy comes out around 37.1 (in the paper's units) against an experimental 25.9 +/- 0.5 and RI-CC2 values near 25.6-27.3, i.e. the CASSCF number is far off; adding dynamic correlation via SA2-MRMP2(12,11) brings it to about 31.1, still high. The paper's use of the method is therefore for surface topology - the SA2-CASSCF torsional scan behaves qualitatively differently from the RI-CC2 surface - rather than for energetics. Anyone citing the (12,11) space should note it was state-averaged over two states specifically to describe the S1/S0 twisting coordinate, and that its vertical energies are not competitive with coupled cluster here.
reference_short: Swalina & Maroncelli, J. Phys. Chem. C 2010 (nonradiative deactivation in benzylidene malononitriles)
notes: One of two benzylidene malononitriles compared in the paper; one row each. The SA2-CAS(12,11) space is stated but its orbital composition is not, so active_space_orbital_description records that rather than assuming a pi space. The CASSCF vertical energies disagree markedly with experiment and coupled cluster, which is recorded in Other.

Four conformers exist, two for the Z form, distinguished by the relative arrangement of the cyclohexene C=C and the N=N double bonds. Note the separate treatment of the two error sources: the space handles static correlation, while vertical excitation energies in the Franck-Condon region are improved by multistate-CASPT2 with better bases (6-31+G* diffuse, or ANO-L), not by enlarging the space. An imaginary shift of 0.2 was applied to all state-averaged CASPT2 computations, the usual signal that intruder states were a concern.

electronic_structure_description: Minimum-energy form of semibullvalene in its degenerate Cope rearrangement. Selected CASSCF(6,6) bond lengths are reported as 1.489, 1.487, 1.340, 1.550 and 2.405 A. A minimal CAS(2,2) would describe the singlet diradical D, and two electrons in two orbitals likewise describe each one-electron excitation from D to form the zwitterionic Z state; the (14,13) space is the fuller alternative to that minimal picture.
active_space_protocol: CAS(2,2) identified as the minimal description of the singlet diradical D and of the one-electron D-to-Z excitations; CAS(14,13) over the full pi system adopted instead, and run two-state state-averaged with equal weights rather than single-state
electronic_structure_description: Twisted pi-system electro-optic chromophore whose gas-phase ground-state electronic configuration is diradicaloid (D), with a zwitterionic (Z) state accessible by one-electron excitation. State ordering changes entirely in a polarizing environment, so the computed first hyperpolarizability beta can be orders of magnitude larger in certain dielectric media than in the gas phase. Response properties are followed as a function of the interphenyl torsional angle.
Other: Two separate honesty markers from the authors, both bearing on how these numbers should be used. First, the switch from single-state to two-state state-averaged CASSCF was made because SS-CASSCF is computationally arduous for spaces this large and because the D and Z states must be treated even-handedly - equal weights, not a preference. Second, the 6-31G** basis is openly inadequate for response properties: the authors state large diffuse sets such as aug-cc-pVTZ are what accuracy requires, but were blocked by integral storage and by linear dependencies that prevented consistent convergence across the torsional scan. They therefore say outright that alpha and beta must be read semiquantitatively, for how sign, magnitude and local maxima vary with torsion, not as quantitative predictions. The active space is not the limiting approximation here - the basis is.
reference_short: Kang, Ratner, Marks et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2008, 112, 44
notes: Model D/Z tictoid chromophore rather than a specific named compound; the paper studies it as a generic twisted pi-system donor-acceptor motif and references experimental TMC-series chromophores for comparison without computing them at this level. Active space stated explicitly and attributed to Isborn et al. Condensed to one row since the paper scans one model system over a torsional coordinate rather than treating distinct compounds.

geometry_source: cc-pV(Q+d)Z CCSD(T) optimized geometries; the CASSCF wave functions were constructed at nine such stationary-point geometries
method: CASSCF (full valence, for interpretation); RHF for zeroth-order descriptions; CCSD, CCSD(T) and CCSDT with focal point analysis for the energetics
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: correlation-consistent cc-pVXZ for C and H and cc-pV(X+d)Z for Si, X = D, T, Q, with complete-basis-set extrapolation via focal point analysis; CASSCF constructed at cc-pV(Q+d)Z CCSD(T) geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space, 14 electrons in 14 molecular orbitals. In the correlated single-reference work the 11 lowest core orbitals (Si 1s, 2s, 2p-like and C 1s-like) are frozen.
electronic_structure_description: Isomers of disilacyclopropenylidene. Two unusual hydrogen-bridged isomers are established: 1S with a Si...H...Si bridge and 4S with an agostic CH...Si interaction. Complete-basis-set limit energies for the six lowest-lying singlet minima are obtained from extensive focal point analyses.
Other: Division of labour worth noting: the full-valence (14,14) CASSCF is used only to interpret geometries and physical properties at a correlated level, while the actual energetics - relative isomer energies and CBS limits - come from CCSD(T)/CCSDT focal point analysis, not from CASSCF. Being full valence, the space is fixed by the molecule rather than chosen, and the same space is applied uniformly at all nine stationary-point geometries so that comparisons between isomers are made on identical footing. A consumer should not treat this (14,14) as a tuned recommendation; it is the complete valence space for a four-heavy-atom system, and the multireference character it reveals is diagnostic rather than the source of the reported energies.
reference_short: Wu, Hao, Yamaguchi, Schaefer et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2010 (unusual isomers of disilacyclopropenylidene)
notes: Condensed to one row for the Si2CH2 isomer manifold: the paper applies one full-valence (14,14) CASSCF uniformly across nine stationary-point geometries and does not assign distinct active spaces to individual isomers, so splitting per isomer would duplicate a single stated space. geometry_source: conical intersection geometries optimized by the method of Bearpark et al. as implemented in MOLPRO; all other calculations in MOLCAS 7.0
method: SA-CASSCF, state-averaged over the ground state S0 and the first excited state S1
software: MOLPRO (conical intersection optimization); MOLCAS 7.0 (all other calculations)
active_space_orbital_description: Both a 2-electron/2-orbital and a 6-electron/6-orbital space were used, the smallest corresponding to the HOMO and LUMO assigned as pi and pi* type molecular orbitals. State averaging is over S0 and S1.
active_space_protocol: SA-CASSCF(2,2), HOMO/LUMO pi and pi* only; SA-CASSCF(6,6); compared against SA-CASSCF(14,12) from earlier work (ref 8)
electronic_structure_description: Photoisomerization of stilbene through conical intersections between S0 and S1, presented as landscapes of four-enantiomer conical intersections. Stilbene has 26 atoms and 72 internal coordinates, of which 58 relate to the two phenyl groups and the remaining 14 to the central unit. Four dihedral angles D1-D4 describe the main internal motions. Energies are reported relative to trans-S0.
Other: An explicit downward convergence test, which is the useful content here: the authors compared their SA-CASSCF(6,6) results against SA-CASSCF(14,12) from earlier work and concluded that (6,6) 'works well and can be good enough' for the intended purpose - on-the-fly nonadiabatic photoisomerization dynamics, where cost per step dominates. They also ran (2,2) with only the HOMO/LUMO pi and pi* pair. So the recommendation is task-conditional: (6,6) is endorsed as adequate for dynamics on the conical intersection landscape, not as converged for energetics, and the authors say plainly their aim was to demonstrate the four-enantiomer conical intersection concept rather than to refine numbers. The 6-31G basis without polarization is consistent with that scope.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2014, 118, 9021 (landscapes of four-enantiomer conical intersections for stilbene photoisomerization)
notes: Condensed to one row for stilbene; the paper maps several conical intersection structures of the same molecule rather than distinct compounds. active_space_nel/norb record the (6,6) space the authors endorse for future dynamics, with the (2,2) space and the (14,12) comparison from ref 8 in active_space_protocol. geometry_source: ground-state equilibrium geometries optimized at PBE0/(aug)-cc-pVDZ
method: SA-CASSCF; multistate multireference perturbation theory (aug-MCQDPT2) on a reference space of fifteen CASCI states
software: PC GAMESS (a version of the GAMESS(US) quantum chemistry program)
basis_set: (aug)-cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF and MCQDPT2; PBE0/(aug)-cc-pVDZ for the ground-state geometry optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: Sixteen electrons in fourteen orbitals. The active orbitals are not chosen by inspection: natural orbitals from preliminary CIS, MP2 and MCSCF(18/16) singles-and-doubles calculations are used as starting orbitals, and the 14 natural orbitals with the highest occupancy among the vacant set and the lowest occupancy among the occupied set are promoted to active. A smaller 14-electron, 12-orbital space is selected by the same rule.
active_space_protocol: MCSCF(18/16) with single and double excitations used as the preliminary calculation; natural orbital occupancies then used to select the reduced SA-CASSCF spaces (16/14) and (14/12); fifteen CASCI states form the reference space for the multistate perturbation theory
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over two states
electronic_structure_description: Photoabsorption of the anionic form of the MYG chromophore, a model of the asFP595 fluorescent protein chromophore. Vertical excitation energies estimated with aug-MCQDPT2 following state-averaged CASSCF over two states.
Other: Orbital selection is automated from occupation numbers rather than chosen chemically: a larger MCSCF(18/16) reference is run first, and the natural orbitals with occupancies furthest from 0 and 2 are promoted into the reduced (16/14) or (14/12) active space. That makes the space reproducible but also means the reported (nel,norb) is the product of a truncation rule, not a valence argument. Note too that the number of state-averaged roots is form-dependent - two for the anionic form, four for the neutral, six for the trans zwitterion and seven for the cis zwitterion - so the SA weighting differs between protonation states of the same chromophore, and comparisons across forms carry that caveat.
reference_short: Bravaya, Bochenkova et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 8804
notes: One of several protonation and isomeric forms of the asFP595 (MYG) chromophore treated in the same paper - anionic, neutral, and trans and cis zwitterionic - each with its own number of state-averaged roots; one row per form. Both reduced active spaces (16/14 and 14/12) are stated, with active_space_nel/norb holding the larger; orbital images are deferred to the Supporting Information, which was not retrieved.
