ligand_set: tris(pyrazolyl)borate (Tp; Tp* = hydrotris(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)borate in the parent complex 1) and one nitrosyl (NO)
geometry_source: UKS-B3LYP and UKS-OLYP optimized coordinates; CASSCF and multireference calculations run as single points on the OLYP-optimized geometry of 1
method: SA-CASSCF as the zeroth-order wave function; individually selecting MR-DDCI3 and SORCI multireference CI on top of it; broken-symmetry DFT (B3LYP, OLYP) for comparison
basis_set: def2 all-electron Gaussian basis sets of Ahlrichs type: def2-SVP and def2-TZVP, with def2-TZVPP augmented with diffuse functions where noted; def2 fitting bases used in the RI-J treatment
active_space_orbital_description: Five electrons in five orbitals, CASSCF(5,5). State-averaged over two roots corresponding to the ground states within the doublet and quartet spin manifolds, or over three roots when the sextet ground state is included as well.
active_space_protocol: SA-CASSCF(5,5) over two roots (doublet and quartet ground states) for one set of multireference calculations, and over three roots (doublet, quartet and sextet ground states) for the other; MR-DDCI3 and SORCI built on these references with an individual selection threshold Tsel = 1e-8 Eh
nroots_per_mult: two roots (doublet and quartet ground states) or three roots (adding the sextet ground state), depending on the calculation
electronic_structure_description: Spin-state energy gaps of the cobalt mononitrosyl. CASSCF(5,5) gives dE(quartet - doublet) = 7645.8 cm-1 and dE(sextet - doublet) = 15314.3 cm-1. MR-DDCI3 gives 9994.8 cm-1 (two-root) and 9770.1 / 24978.0 cm-1 (three-root); SORCI gives 10743.2 cm-1 (two-root) and 10522.6 / 26136.1 cm-1 (three-root). Broken-symmetry DFT BS(3,2) values range from 6743-9440 cm-1 (B3LYP) and 9122-12771 cm-1 (OLYP) for the quartet-doublet gap. Mulliken spin densities are compared between BS-DFT and CASSCF descriptions.
Other: The whole point of the multireference treatment is that the Co-NO bonding is extremely weak, implying significant multireference character, so the physical oxidation state of the metal is genuinely ambiguous - assignments in the literature span Co(0) to Co(IV) with multiple spin states for both metal and ligand. A minimal (5,5) metal-d space is used, but note the results are strongly method-dependent even at fixed space: the quartet-doublet gap moves from 7646 cm-1 at bare CASSCF(5,5) to ~9800-10700 cm-1 once MR-DDCI3 or SORCI dynamic correlation is added, and the sextet-doublet gap from 15314 to ~25000-26100 cm-1. Dynamic correlation, not active space size, is the dominant correction here. Also note the number of state-averaged roots changes the answer, so the two-root and three-root variants are not interchangeable.
reference_short: Ye, Neese, Lehnert et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2011, 133, 18785
notes: Condensed to one row for the cobalt mononitrosyl: the paper computes Tp*Co(NO) (1) at DFT level and the truncated TpCo(NO) (1') at CASSCF/multireference level, but treats them as the same chemical system with the methyls removed for tractability. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are deliberately left EMPTY: the paper's central finding is that the oxidation state of the cobalt is ambiguous, with literature assignments spanning Co(0) to Co(IV), so recording any single value would misrepresent the source.

geometry_source: B3P86 optimized geometries and harmonic vibrational frequencies; CASSCF(14,13)/cc-pVDZ geometric parameters also reported for ground and excited states
method: CASSCF; CASPT2; transition properties from the RASSI module; TD-B3P86 for comparison
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for CASSCF/CASPT2; 6-31G(d,p) for TD-B3P86; B3P86 geometries and harmonic frequencies
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in thirteen orbitals: the pi orbitals on the twelve carbon atoms together with the out-of-plane lone pair on the oxygen atom. The out-of-plane chlorine lone pairs are deliberately excluded, and the paper notes care was needed to keep them out of the space.
active_space_protocol: (14,13) pi orbitals on the twelve carbons plus the out-of-plane oxygen lone pair - the space adopted; (14,14) adding correlation of a further oxygen lone pair - tested and rejected, gained nothing and created very serious intruder problems in the subsequent CASPT2; (12,12), the smallest possible space - also tested and rejected for the same intruder problems
electronic_structure_description: Valence excited states of dibenzofuran (DF) - the parent compound, used as the model system. Minimum structures, harmonic vibrational frequencies and electronic spectra computed; CASPT2 on CASSCF(14,13) references, with TD-B3P86 for comparison. Rydberg states of 3px, 3dxz and 3dxy character may appear near 6 eV and mix with the valence pi-pi* manifold.
Other: An unusually explicit record of active spaces tried and rejected, and for a reason that runs against intuition: enlarging (14,13) to (14,14) to correlate a further oxygen lone pair 'gained nothing' and created very serious intruder-state problems in the CASPT2 step, and the smallest (12,12) space failed the same way. So both a larger and a smaller space were worse than the chosen one - the failure is non-monotonic in space size. The other actionable detail is a negative one for the chlorinated members: the out-of-plane chlorine lone pairs are superfluous and had to be actively kept out of the active space, which is the kind of orbital that would otherwise drift in during orbital rotation. Some Rydberg transitions (3px, 3dxz, 3dxy type) may appear around 6 eV and mix with the valence pi-pi* states; resolving that mixing would need diffuse basis functions and a further-expanded space, which this work did not attempt.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2007 (structure, vibrational frequencies and electronic spectra of dibenzofuran and chlorinated derivatives)
notes: One of three dibenzofuran congeners treated with the same (14,13) active space; one row each since the chlorination pattern is the variable under study. The space is defined by the carbon pi system plus the out-of-plane oxygen lone pair and deliberately excludes the chlorine lone pairs, so it is identical in composition across all three congeners.

geometry_source: CAS(8,7)/6-311G(d) geometry optimizations in Cartesian coordinates; conical intersections optimized in the (f-2)-dimensional intersection space by the method of Bearpark et al.; every stationary point characterized by analytic CASSCF harmonic frequencies
method: CASSCF; multireference Moller-Plesset (MP2-CAS) for dynamic correlation, using the same active space
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals: the five p-pi orbitals plus the sigma(C-N) and sigma*(C-N) orbitals; all other orbitals inactive.
electronic_structure_description: Photochemical transposition (isomerization) reactions of 2-cyanopyrrole - the parent system, which photoisomerizes to the 3-cyano isomer under UV light. Minima, transition states and conical intersection minima are located on the singlet surface; bond order analysis is carried out on the CAS(8,7) wave function. Relative energies quoted in the paper are at the MP2-CAS(8,7)/6-311G(d) level on CAS(8,7)/6-311G(d) geometries.
Other: The space is assembled to match the bond that must break: the five ring p-pi orbitals plus specifically the sigma and sigma* of the C-N bond involved in the transposition, rather than a pi-only space. Two scoping decisions follow from the experiment rather than from theory - the authors note that experimentalists found no indication of triplet participation in cyanopyrrole photochemistry, so triplet states are excluded from the study entirely and only the singlet manifold is treated. active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals: the seven conjugated pi/pi* orbitals plus the in-plane nonbonding orbital on the carbene carbon.
electronic_structure_description: Phenylcarbene, which has a triplet ground state. Starting point of the rearrangement to 1,2,4,6-cycloheptatetraene.
Other: An (8,8) space was imposed on every species specifically to keep the active space size consistent across the whole singlet surface, so relative energies are not contaminated by a changing description. What that consistency costs is spelled out for the bicyclic intermediate: with six pi orbitals chosen easily, the seventh and eighth had to be a sigma/sigma* pair, and there were two candidate C-C bonds of essentially equal length (1.50 A at RHF/6-31G*), making the choice 'somewhat arbitrary'. The authors then tested the consequence directly with a (6,6) pi-only calculation: it gave a somewhat shorter external C-C bond, but relative energies agreed with the (8,8) result to within 0.1 kcal/mol. method: state-specific CASSCF
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta (DZ) augmented by polarization functions on carbon (alpha_d = 0.75)
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals: the five occupied pi orbitals and the lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: S2-S1 internal conversion in phenylacetylene, analysed along reaction coordinates. Paths followed: from the S0 equilibrium geometry on S2 to the most stable S2 geometry (S2-bent); from the S2/S1 conical intersection back to S2-bent; and from that intersection to the globally stable S1 geometry. Additional paths from C-beta-H-beta out-of-plane bent geometries examine how initial bending motion affects the dynamics. Experimentally the S2-S1 internal conversion is very fast (relaxation time constant 54 fs) whereas S1-S0 is much slower (9.4 and 63 ps).
Other: Deliberate enlargement over the same authors' earlier phenylacetylene work, and stated as such: this study adopts a larger (10,10) space - five occupied pi plus the five lowest pi* - and reoptimizes several important conformations state-specifically precisely to check how much the size of the active space affects the geometries. That makes it the companion convergence test to the earlier (10,9) treatment of the same molecule, where the ninth orbital had been added only to keep the surface continuous across conformations. Same DZ+d(C) basis is retained throughout so the space is the only variable. State-specific rather than state-averaged orbitals are used here.
reference_short: Amatatsu, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 4479
notes: Follow-up to the same author's earlier phenylacetylene study (10.1021/jp0355253, mined separately in this database at (10,9)); this paper enlarges the space to (10,10) specifically to test the sensitivity of geometries to active space size. Condensed to one row since the paper maps reaction paths of a single molecule rather than distinct compounds.

software: ARGOS; a multireference CI program originally developed by Siegbahn; QMPRO for the quantum dynamics simulation
basis_set: metal (15,11,6) contracted to [9,6,3]; first-row atoms (10,6) contracted to [4,2]; hydrogen (6,1) contracted to [3,1]
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons correlated in ten active orbitals: the two orbitals involved in the hydrogen bonding (sigma_g, sigma_u) and their antibonding counterparts (sigma_g*, sigma_u*), together with the 3d orbitals and the d orbitals that correlate them.
multiplicities_studied: singlet and quintet (the CASSCF reference is a quintet)

electronic_structure_description: Photodissociation dynamics of the dihydride complex. The excited states of interest are 3d -> sigma_g*, 3d -> sigma_u*, and sigma_u -> sigma_g*. The CASSCF calculations were carried out for the lowest 5A2 high-spin state with main configuration (sigma_g)2(sigma_u)2(3dxz)2(3dyz)1(3dx2-y2)1(sigma_g*)1(sigma_u*)1. Excitation energies to the lowest excited states contributing to the absorption spectrum were computed and compared with CASSCF/CASPT2 values from a companion study.
Other: A single high-spin CASSCF wave function is used as the common reference for every excited state, rather than optimizing orbitals per state. The 5A2 quintet was chosen specifically because its half-open configuration assures a balanced description of the different excited states - a deliberate compromise that avoids biasing any one state through its own orbital optimization. The authors validated this shortcut against a companion CASSCF/CASPT2 study with state-specific wave functions and ANO bases, and concluded that CCI on top of one judiciously chosen CASSCF reference gives reasonable excitation energies - with the explicit caveat that this holds only as long as the reference is well chosen. The space itself is assembled around the dissociating bonds: the H-H sigma_g/sigma_u pair with their antibonding partners, plus the 3d set and its correlating d shell.

compound_name: PSB3, penta-2,4-dieniminium cation (minimal retinal chromophore model)
geometry_source: TS_CT and TS_DIR transition states optimized at equal-weight two-root SA-CASSCF/6-31G*; a bond-length-alternation path built by linear interpolation/extrapolation between them giving 14 structures; two further paths (MEP_CT and MEP_DIR) from IRC calculations at the CASSCF level with a 0.01 A.amu^(1/2) step size
method: SA-CASSCF as the reference, with dynamic correlation added variationally (MRCISD) and perturbatively (CASPT2, NEVPT2 and others)
active_space_orbital_description: The six pi orbitals of PSB3 occupied with six electrons (6-in-6), i.e. the complete pi valence space of the conjugated chain.
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state potential energy surface of the penta-2,4-dieniminium cation, a minimal model reproducing several features of the retinal chromophore. Two transition states, TS_CT (charge transfer) and TS_DIR (diradical), share the same isomerizing bond but have opposite bond-length-alternation patterns, and both connect the cis-PSB3 and trans-PSB3 minima. The BLA coordinate is defined as the difference between the average length of the formal double bonds (N=C1, C2=C3, C4=C5) and the formal single bonds (C1-C2, C3-C4).
Other: This is a study designed specifically to isolate the effect of dynamic correlation at fixed active space: the (6,6) complete pi space and 6-31G* basis are held constant while the missing dynamic correlation is added variationally with MRCISD and perturbatively with CASPT2, NEVPT2 and related schemes, so any disagreement between methods is attributable to the correlation treatment rather than to the reference. The two transition states are deliberately chosen as the probe because they carry opposite bond-length-alternation patterns on the same isomerizing bond - a charge-transfer versus a diradical character contrast that dynamic correlation is known to reweight. For a consumer, the useful reading is that a complete-pi (6,6) space on this chromophore does not by itself settle the relative energies; the correlation treatment on top of it is what moves them.

notes: Benchmark study of correlation methods on a fixed CASSCF reference; condensed to one row since the paper maps paths of a single model chromophore rather than distinct compounds. Active space stated explicitly as the complete six-orbital pi space. Related to but distinct from the graded retinal model series mined from 10.1021/jp800244h, which uses larger (10,10) and (12,12) pi spaces on longer chains.

electronic_structure_description: Potential energy surface of the BCP system. The most stable isomer is linear singlet BCP. The B-C and C-P bond dissociation energies in BCP at 0 K are 111.7 and 128.9 kcal/mol respectively at the CASPT2/ANO-L level. Vibrational frequencies of the triplet linear isomers were computed at CASSCF(12,12) to investigate the Renner-Teller effect.

method: CASSCF; CiLC analysis (CI / localized molecular orbital / CASSCF), in which CASSCF orbitals are Boys-localized and a determinant-level full CI is run in that localized basis
active_space_orbital_description: Six active orbitals corresponding to three pi and three pi* orbitals of the six-membered ring, holding the six pi electrons; all configurations within the active space are generated.
electronic_structure_description: Aromaticity of benzene (C6H6) as a six-membered ring with six pi electrons, assessed by the gap between the weights of singlet-coupling and polarization terms in the CiLC wave function. Rings of second-row elements (B, C, N) are found more aromatic than the corresponding third-row rings (Si, Al, P). Kekule cyclotriene reference structures were built using double and single bond distances taken from the equilibrium and twisted-pi diatomic compounds respectively.
Other: The active space here is not chosen for energetic accuracy but as the substrate for a bonding analysis: the CASSCF orbitals are Boys-localized into atomic-like p-pi orbitals and a determinant-level full CI is run in that localized basis, so the weights of singlet-coupling versus polarization configurations become readable as an aromaticity criterion. Because the (6,6) pi space is identical in composition for every ring in the series - C6H6, Si6H6, B6, Al6, N6 and P6 - the comparison across second-row and third-row elements is made at strictly constant active space, which is what licenses the paper's conclusion that second-row rings (B, C, N) are more aromatic than their third-row counterparts (Si, Al, P). The authors also verify that the CI total energy corresponds well to the CASSCF energy, confirming the localized-basis CI reproduces the parent wave function.

notes: One of six six-membered rings compared under an identical (6,6) pi active space in the same paper; one row each since the ring composition is the variable under study. The space is the analysis substrate for the CiLC aromaticity criterion rather than a convergence choice.

compound_name: N(2D) + CH4 reaction system (entrance-channel saddle point)
geometry_source: the entrance-channel saddle point optimized at CASSCF(5,5)/cc-pVTZ (and at CASSCF(5,5)/6-311G** for comparison); other stationary points fully optimized at MP2(full)/cc-pVTZ with harmonic frequencies and zero-point energies at the same level; IRC calculations at the CASSCF level with the smaller 6-311G** basis to save time
method: CASSCF; PMP4(full,SDTQ) single points with spin projection for the final energy diagram
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF geometry optimizations and the PMP4 energies; 6-311G** for the CASSCF IRC calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Five orbitals holding five electrons: the three nitrogen 2p orbitals plus the C-H sigma and sigma* orbitals of the breaking C-H bond in methane.
electronic_structure_description: Doublet potential energy surface for the N(2D) + CH4 reaction. The barrier height is reported as differing between basis sets - roughly 3.5 kcal/mol at CASSCF(5,5)/6-311G** versus the cc-pVTZ value. Spin-orbit interactions were not taken into account.
Other: CASSCF was reached for by necessity rather than by preference, and the paper says why: a single-reference Hartree-Fock wave function was found not to be a good approximation for the entrance-channel saddle point because it suffers considerable spin contamination. The (5,5) space is then assembled to match exactly that problem - the three nitrogen 2p orbitals carrying the 2D atomic state, plus the sigma/sigma* of the one C-H bond being broken. Note the mixed-level construction: only the saddle point is CASSCF-optimized, the remaining stationary points come from MP2(full), and the final energetics from spin-projected PMP4, so the (5,5) label describes one point on the surface rather than the whole reaction path. The IRC was run in a deliberately smaller 6-311G** basis to save time, and the barrier is basis-sensitive between the two.

notes: Condensed to one row for the N(2D) + CH4 reaction system; the CASSCF treatment applies specifically to the entrance-channel saddle point, with the rest of the surface at MP2/PMP4 and therefore carrying no active space. Space size and full orbital composition are stated explicitly.

active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen orbitals populated by ten electrons, abbreviated (10i13) by the paper. Alongside the metal 4d (Mo) or 5d (W) orbitals, each of four symmetry-distinct active spaces includes four linear combinations of the occupied ligand 1pi orbitals and four linear combinations of the unoccupied 2pi* ligand orbitals transforming according to that irreducible representation. A reduced (2i5) space of the five metal d orbitals holding the two d electrons was used for the spin-orbit calculations.
active_space_protocol: (10i13) per irreducible representation - metal d plus four occupied ligand 1pi and four unoccupied 2pi* combinations of that irrep, with each electronic state expanded in the active space of its own symmetry; reduced to (2i5), the five metal d orbitals only, for all relevant ligand-field states so that spin-orbit coupling could be computed
electronic_structure_description: Dodecahedral isomer of the octacyanometalate. The crystal field lifts the degeneracy of the metal d shell, with the pattern depending on both the ligand cluster geometry and the specific ligand-metal interaction. In the dodecahedral isomer the ground state places the two metal electrons in the x2-y2 orbital; in the square antiprismatic isomer they occupy the z2 orbital. The lowest excited states of both isomers are calculated to be ligand-field states. Spin-orbit coupling improves agreement with experiment, especially for tungsten, where large singlet-triplet mixings are calculated for the square antiprismatic isomer. The paper concludes a dynamic equilibrium between the two isomers exists in solution.
Other: Two structurally interesting choices. First, the active space is symmetry-partitioned rather than global: four different (10i13) spaces are built, one per irreducible representation, each containing the ligand pi and pi* combinations transforming as that irrep, and every electronic state is expanded in the space of its own symmetry - including its ground state, so excitation energies within a symmetry are computed consistently. Second, the space had to be CUT for the spin-orbit step: because of how spin-orbit coupling is implemented in MOLCAS, all states entering such a calculation must share one active space, so the ligand-field states were recomputed in a reduced (2i5) metal-d-only space. The spin-orbit results that improve agreement with experiment - notably the large singlet-triplet mixings in the square antiprismatic tungsten isomer - therefore rest on the smaller space, not the (10i13) one.
reference_short: Hendrickx, Chibotaru, Ceulemans et al., Inorg. Chem. 2004 (electronic spectra of [Mo(CN)8]4- and [W(CN)8]4-)
notes: One of four isomer/metal combinations treated in the same paper; one row each since ground-state d-orbital occupation and the spin-orbit behaviour differ between them. metal_ox_state=IV and the d2 count follow from the paper's own description of two metal d electrons in a tetraanionic octacyanide; d_electron_count carries the shell prefix per policy. The basis set is not fully specified in the extracted text.

geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations, minimum-energy paths, and conical intersection and singlet-triplet crossing searches, with CASPT2 single points at the optimized geometries
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 (final results reported as CASPT2(14,10)//CASSCF); spin-orbit coupling terms and transition dipole moments also computed
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons distributed in ten orbitals for the final CASPT2 results. The paper states that other active spaces were employed during the optimization procedures but does not enumerate the individual orbitals here, referring to previous papers and the Supporting Information for technical detail.
active_space_protocol: (14,10) for the final CASPT2//CASSCF results; other, unspecified active spaces used during the geometry optimization, minimum-energy path and crossing-search stages, following a strategy the authors report as previously successful
electronic_structure_description: Intrinsic population of the lowest triplet state of thymine. Minimum-energy paths, conical intersections and singlet-triplet crossings are located to trace how the triplet becomes populated, with spin-orbit coupling terms and transition dipole moments computed along the way.
Other: A deliberately two-tier strategy: smaller, unspecified active spaces are used for the expensive geometry work - optimizations, minimum-energy paths, conical intersection and singlet-triplet crossing searches - and the final energetics are then computed at CASPT2 with a larger (14,10) space at those geometries. The authors present this as an established recipe from their earlier work rather than a convergence argument. The practical consequence for a consumer is that (14,10) describes the reported energies only; the structures those energies sit on were obtained with something smaller that the paper does not specify here, deferring to prior publications and the Supporting Information.
reference_short: Serrano-Perez, Serrano-Andres, Merchan et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2008 (intrinsic population of the lowest triplet state of thymine)
notes: Condensed to one row for thymine; the paper maps paths and crossings of a single molecule rather than distinct compounds. The final (14,10) space is stated explicitly, but the smaller spaces used during optimization are not enumerated in the main text, so active_space_orbital_description records that rather than inferring a composition.

geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations; potential energy surfaces and trajectory dynamics computed at CAS(8,6)/STO-3G
method: CASSCF; CASDI (CASSCF plus all possible mono- and bi-excitations) for correlated energies; on-the-fly trajectory dynamics
basis_set: 6-31G(d) and STO-3G for the CAS(8,6) surfaces, with only CAS(8,6)/STO-3G used for the trajectory dynamics; 6-31G(d) used in the acetone calibration
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in six orbitals: the CAS(4,3) chromophore space - CO pi, pi* and the oxygen lone pair n - doubled for the two carbonyl chromophores of the diketone. The larger alternative was CAS(12,10), obtained by doubling a CAS(6,5) chromophore space that additionally includes a CO sigma/sigma* pair.
active_space_protocol: Calibrated on acetone as the isolated chromophore: CAS(4,3) = CO pi, pi* plus oxygen lone pair n, the minimum for n -> pi*; CAS(6,5) adds a CO sigma/sigma* pair to allow the >0.1 A CO bond lengthening of the n -> pi* state. Doubling for the two chromophores of the diketone gives CAS(8,6) or CAS(12,10) respectively; CAS(8,6) was adopted, with dynamics at CAS(8,6)/STO-3G.
electronic_structure_description: Rigidly linked bichromophoric diketone with two carbonyl groups in twisted cyclopentane rings of opposite chirality. Intramolecular electronic energy transfer is fast, with k(IEET) >= 1e10 s-1 - about 1000 times more efficient than in the tricyclic analogue. Potential energy surfaces for the S0 and S1 (n -> pi*) states are mapped and intramolecular electronic energy transfer dynamics simulated.
Other: Model-system calibration done properly and reported: rather than guessing a space for the diketones, the authors first ran a CASSCF study on acetone - the chromophore common to both systems - to find the smallest space that reproduces geometries and excitation energies adequately. The n -> pi* excitation needs at minimum the CO pi and pi* plus the oxygen lone pair n, i.e. CAS(4,3); but because the n -> pi* excited state lengthens the CO bond by more than 0.1 A, a sigma/sigma* pair was added to let that bond relax in the wave function, giving CAS(6,5). The explicit reason for minimising was that whatever space is chosen must be DOUBLED for the two-chromophore diketones, turning CAS(4,3) into CAS(8,6) and CAS(6,5) into CAS(12,10). CAS(8,6) was adopted in practice, and the trajectory dynamics ran at CAS(8,6)/STO-3G - so the dynamics rest on the smaller of the two candidate spaces and a minimal basis, a cost compromise the paper is explicit about.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 4358 (potential energy surfaces and dynamics of rigidly linked bichromophoric molecules)
notes: One of two rigidly linked bichromophoric diketones compared in the same paper; one row each since the energy-transfer rates differ by roughly three orders of magnitude. Both share the CAS(8,6) space obtained by doubling the acetone-calibrated chromophore space.

geometry_source: bond orders computed as a function of the H-H internuclear distance R
method: CASSCF; correlated first-order densities analysed through generalized Wiberg and Cioslowski covalent bond orders, localization indices and related quantities; MP2 and HF used for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals - the sigma and sigma* of the dissociating H-H bond.
electronic_structure_description: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen, used as the simplest test case. Bond order profiles as a function of internuclear distance R are compared across the generalized Wiberg definition, the Cioslowski covalent bond order, the localization index and a related quantity. Numerical values and the shapes of the bond order versus bond length curves differ considerably between definitions, but the inflection point of the Wiberg profile coincides with the sharp drop in the analogous localization-based dependence.
Other: The active space here is instrumental, not energetic: CASSCF supplies correlated first-order densities from which several competing bond-order definitions are computed, and the paper's question is how much the interpretation of electron reorganization depends on which definition is used. The spaces are therefore the minimum needed to make the density correlated in the bonds being broken and formed - (2,2) for the single H-H bond of dissociating H2, (4,4) for the two-bond reorganization of the cyclobutene ring opening. The paper also separates two effects that are usually conflated, with its x/y notation: the method used to compute the bond-order profile versus the method used to generate the IRC it is computed along, so a CASSCF/CASSCF profile and an MP2/MP2 profile can be compared without confounding the two choices.
reference_short: Ponec et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2003, 107, 2100
notes: One of the reactions analysed in a study of how bond-order definitions affect the picture of electron reorganization; one row per reacting system since each carries its own active space and basis. The CASSCF here provides correlated densities for the bond-order analysis rather than reaction energetics.

ligand_set: two bridging oxalate-linked Cu(II) centres with six ammine ligands, an aminic-type ligand replaced by NH3 in the model
geometry_source: crystallographically established geometry of the parent compound, with the aminic ligand replaced by NH3 in the model
method: CASSCF as the minimal reference; DDCI-type difference-dedicated configuration interaction on top; excitation-energy dedicated molecular orbitals (EEDMO) proposed as an alternative to enlarging the CASSCF active space
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: not specified in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Minimal CAS of two electrons in two orbitals, the magnetic orbitals being the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of Cu dz2-type orbitals. Extended CASSCF spaces such as 10 electrons in 10 orbitals were used in prior work as an alternative route to the bridging-ligand orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Oxalato-bridged dicopper(II) complex whose geometry is crystallographically established and whose magnetic coupling is measured at -9.27 meV. Dedicated-MO CI gives -10.58 meV; earlier work with bridging-ligand MOs from extended CASSCF gave -9.47 meV. Both agree well with the DDCI benchmark, the dedicated-MO route using a CI about 4% the size.
Other: This paper is an explicit argument AGAINST enlarging the active space. Its dedicated molecular orbitals are eigenvectors of density-matrix blocks tailored to a specific energy difference, and are offered as a substitute for CASSCF active-space enlargement and as a criterion for truncating the CI space. The comparison the authors draw is the useful number here: a magnetic coupling of -10.58 meV from dedicated MOs versus -9.47 meV obtained previously from bridging-ligand MOs taken from extended CASSCF calculations with, for instance, 10 electrons in 10 orbitals - both close to the DDCI benchmark, but the dedicated-MO route reaches it with a CI roughly 4% the size and, as the authors put it, avoids the convergence difficulties of the large CASSCF calculations. For a consumer choosing a space, this is a documented case where a bigger CAS was the thing being replaced rather than the thing being recommended.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2001 (excitation energy dedicated molecular orbitals, applications to magnetic systems)
notes: One of the magnetic systems used to demonstrate the excitation-energy dedicated molecular orbital method; one row each. Cu(II) and the d9 configuration follow from the magnetic-orbital description; d_electron_count carries the 3d shell prefix per policy. Basis set and program package are not stated in the extracted text.

geometry_source: stationary points and lowest-energy points on the singlet-singlet and triplet-triplet crossing seams optimized at CASSCF(14,12)/6-311+G(3df,2p); all stationary points characterized by harmonic vibrational frequencies
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 single points for dynamic valence-electron correlation; conical intersections optimized with the Anglada-Bofill algorithm
software: MOLCAS-6 (CASPT2 and CASSCF); a second program package also used for part of the work
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve molecular orbitals for several stationary points of the reacting system, built from the fragment orbitals of the two HOO radicals.
active_space_protocol: Per-species spaces set from MRDCI natural orbital fractional occupancies: (2,2) HOOH; (5,4) HOO*; (8,6) O2; (14,12) for several stationary points of the reacting system
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase bimolecular self-reaction of the hydroperoxyl radical, giving HOOH + O2. Adiabatic reaction paths on the lowest singlet and triplet surfaces are followed, and the lowest-energy points on the singlet-singlet and triplet-triplet crossing seams located. Natural orbitals of the CX1-S complex show two nearly singly occupied orbitals (au 0.9864, bg 1.0549 electrons) formed from the pi-type orbitals of each isolated HOO radical.
Other: Active spaces are derived rather than chosen: each stationary point's space follows the Anglada-Bofill procedure, from the fractional occupation of natural orbitals of an initial MRDCI wave function correlating all valence electrons. That yields a different (nel,norb) per species - (2,2) for HOOH up to (14,12) for several stationary points - so the numbers describe what the density said was strongly correlated, not a valence rule. The diagnostic value shows in the reaction complex: inspection of the CASSCF(14,12) natural orbitals for CX1-S found two nearly singly occupied orbitals, one au at 0.9864 and one bg at 1.0549 electrons, identifying them as the positive and negative combinations of the pi-type orbitals carrying each HOO radical's unpaired electron - i.e. the complex is a weakly coupled radical pair, read directly off the occupancies. Same methodology as the authors' CH3O2 + HO2 study.
reference_short: Anglada, Olivella & Sole, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007 (gas-phase bimolecular self-reaction of the HOO radical)

basis_set: not fully specified in the extracted text; MOLPRO default frozen core of O 1s2 and Y 4s2 4p6 used for the CASSCF-based methods
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space consisting of the O 2s2p and Y 5s4d shells, with the MOLPRO default frozen core of O 1s2 and Y 4s2 4p6. That is four orbitals per oxygen (2s and three 2p) plus six on yttrium (5s and five 4d), fourteen in total. For the most demanding MRCI runs the space was cut to four a1, two b1, three b2 and two a2 orbitals - eleven in total, with the highest a1 orbital of MOLPRO's default full valence space excluded and O 2s additionally frozen.
active_space_protocol: Full valence (O 2s2p + Y 5s4d, fourteen orbitals) used for all CASSCF, CASSCF/RSPT2, CASSCF/MRCI and RCCSD(T) calculations unless otherwise stated; reduced for the X~2B2 CASSCF/MRCI/G calculation to occ 8,3,6,2 over closed 4,1,3,0 - eleven active orbitals - because a full valence MRCI was computationally out of reach
electronic_structure_description: Neutral YO2 in its X~2B2 ground state. Low-lying electronic states characterized, and the geometry compared with BP86/LanL2DZ values and with IR matrix data giving frequencies near 702.0 and 618.6 cm-1 and a bond angle upper limit under 123 degrees estimated from the O16/O18 isotopic ratio.
Other: A candid account of a full valence space hitting a hard computational wall. With the full valence space the CASSCF on the anion X~1A1 state runs to over 2.25 million variables; the reduced eleven-orbital MRCI on the neutral X~2B2 state still produces more than 2.5e9 uncontracted and 43.8e6 internally contracted configurations, which the authors state are the largest calculations their computer systems could handle. Their conclusion is stated plainly: it is computationally too demanding to employ a full valence active space in CASSCF/MRCI on this system. So the reduced space here is a resource boundary, documented with the configuration counts that establish it, not a chemical judgement about which orbitals matter.
reference_short: Lee et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 4511 (low-lying electronic states of YO2 and Franck-Condon simulation)
notes: One of two species (neutral and anion) in a study of YO2 electronic states and photodetachment; one row each. active_space_norb=14 is the count of the orbitals in the stated full valence shells (O 2s2p on each oxygen plus Y 5s4d); active_space_nel is the corresponding valence electron count for this charge state. active_space_orbital_description: Six active electrons distributed among the pi and pi* orbitals of the two double bonds and the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the unique cyclopropane ring bond - a bond-localized description.
electronic_structure_description: Localized Cs geometry of the 1,5-disubstituted semibullvalene, the classical valence structure with an intact cyclopropane ring bond. Relative energies of the Cs and C2v geometries are compared across substituents; the paper finds that with R = F and -RR- = -O- the C2v equilibrium geometries do benefit from bishomoaromatic stabilization.
Other: Three active spaces, each composed to match the bonding picture being tested rather than by a uniform rule - and the contrast between the first two is the paper's argument. For the localized Cs semibullvalene the (6,6) holds the pi/pi* of the two double bonds plus the sigma/sigma* of the unique cyclopropane ring bond, i.e. a bond-localized description. For the delocalized C2v structure the same (6,6) count instead holds three filled and three empty benzene-like MOs formed from the two allylic pi systems, i.e. an aromatic description. Same size, entirely different orbitals, chosen to represent the two competing descriptions of the same molecule - which is precisely the question the title asks. Note also a practical limit stated outright: analytical CASPT2 gradients were not available, so full CASPT2 optimizations were impractical at this molecular size and only partial optimizations with fixed C2-C8 distances were done.

Substituent identity varies across the paper's series, so compound_name records the structural type rather than a single substituted example.

electronic_structure_description: Linear isomer of C6, one of the two most stable forms. CASPT2/CASSCF/ANO-L refined bond distances: R1 = R5 = 1.3127 A (outer bonds), R2 = R4 = 1.2926 A, R3 = 1.285 A (inner bonds). The Be rotational constant is 0.047770 cm-1, in good agreement with previous CCSD(T) data. Minimum energy geometries and excitation energies are reported for 19 electronic states across the study.
Other: The space size is stated outright as a resource ceiling rather than a chemical choice - '14 electrons and 14 orbitals, the largest one allowed by our computational capabilities' - so the (14,14) here should be read as the maximum affordable for a six-carbon system with an ANO-L C[4s3p2d1f] basis, not as a converged or recommended space. Note also the staged workflow: the cheaper survey work established that the linear and cyclic isomers are the stable ones, and only then were their geometries refined at CASPT2/CASSCF, so the expensive space was spent on two structures rather than the whole isomer manifold. Excitation energies for 19 electronic states are reported at this level.

geometry_source: RHF/6-31G** optimized ground-state geometries; for the chromophore inside the protein, the effective fragment potential QM/MM method was used to include the protein environment in the excitation energies
method: state-averaged CASSCF with equal weights for ground and excited states; TDDFT used initially and then re-done at CASSCF level
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons distributed over ten active orbitals. The initial active pi and pi* orbitals of the chromophore unit were selected MANUALLY, by inspecting graphs of the RHF orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state structures and vertical excitations of the chromophore of the kindling fluorescent protein asFP595, computed both in the gas phase and embedded in the protein. The CASSCF excitation energies, lacking dynamical correlation, show even larger discrepancies with the experimental band positions than the TDDFT values did, but are described as completely consistent with the qualitative picture.
Other: Two things worth carrying. First, the CASSCF work exists because of peer review: the authors state that an anonymous reviewer pointed out that TDDFT at RHF-optimized geometries could give serious errors for excitation energies, so Table 1 was recomputed at CASSCF(10/10). Second, and unusually for a modern paper, the active orbitals were selected by hand - by inspecting plots of the RHF orbitals - rather than by an occupancy criterion or an automated rule, which is worth knowing when judging reproducibility. The outcome is also candidly negative: bare state-averaged CASSCF without dynamical correlation gave LARGER discrepancies against experimental band positions than the method it was brought in to check, so the (10,10) space should not be read as delivering accurate excitation energies for this chromophore.
reference_short: Nemukhin et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2006 (ground-state structures and vertical excitations for asFP595)
notes: system_class=cluster-model: the chromophore is treated as a QM region embedded in the protein via effective fragment potentials, not as an isolated molecule. Related to but distinct from the asFP595 rows mined from 10.1021/jp804183w, which use larger occupancy-selected (16/14) spaces on isolated model chromophores in several protonation forms; this paper uses a manually selected (10/10) and includes the protein environment.

point_group: approximate C2v for both minima, but neither structure is planar; no symmetry restrictions imposed on wave functions or geometries
geometry_source: all geometry optimizations at SA-2-CAS(2/2), repeated in some cases at SA-2-CAS(14/12); several important geometries verified with the polarized 6-31G** basis
method: state-averaged CASSCF, abbreviated SA-N-CAS(n/m) where N is the number of states averaged, used to avoid a variational bias toward any particular electronic state
basis_set: 6-31G, with 6-31G** used to verify several important geometries
active_space_orbital_description: The larger space extends the minimal one by including contributions from the phenyl-ring pi and pi* molecular orbitals. The minimal SA-2-CAS(2/2) space consists of the pi2, pi pi* and pi*2 configurations built from the HOMO and LUMO, which are pi- and pi*-type on the ethylenic bond.
active_space_protocol: SA-2-CAS(2/2) - HOMO/LUMO pi and pi* of the central ethylenic bond, giving the pi2, pi pi* and pi*2 configurations - used for all geometry optimizations; extended to SA-2-CAS(14/12) by adding the phenyl-ring pi and pi* orbitals, and used to repeat some optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Cis-trans photoisomerization of stilbene, examined alongside ethylene to test how far the ethylene mechanism generalizes. Ground-state minima correspond to the trans and cis isomers; steric effects twist the cis isomer, with a C1-Ce-Ce'-C1' dihedral of 6 degrees and phenyl groups rotated 40 degrees out of plane, against gas-phase experimental values of 5 and 43 degrees. SA-2-CAS(2/2) S1 <- S0 excitation energies are 6.07 eV (cis) and 5.74 eV (trans). The paper concludes the picture developed for ethylene breaks down when both phenyl rings are present.
Other: State averaging is used for a stated methodological reason rather than convenience - to avoid a variational bias toward any particular electronic state - and the paper's SA-N-CAS(n/m) notation makes the number of averaged states explicit, which is worth preserving since two spaces of identical (n,m) can behave differently under different averaging. The two spaces map onto two physical hypotheses: (2/2) describes only the central ethylenic pi bond that twists, while (14/12) adds the phenyl-ring pi system, and the paper's conclusion is precisely that the phenyl rings matter - the ethylene-derived picture breaks down once both are present. Note the asymmetry in effort: optimizations were done at (2/2) and only repeated at (14/12) in some cases, so most reported geometries rest on the minimal space.
reference_short: Quenneville & Martinez, J. Phys. Chem. A 2003 (cis-trans photoisomerization in stilbene and ethylene)
notes: Condensed to one row for stilbene; the paper maps isomerization coordinates of a single molecule rather than distinct compounds. Ethylene is discussed extensively as the reference system from the authors' prior work, but this paper's calculations centre on stilbene, so no separate ethylene row is created. active_space_nel/norb record the larger (14/12) space with the (2/2) optimization space in active_space_protocol.

geometry_source: initial acrolein geometry from CASSCF optimization in vacuo with the ANO basis; excited-state CASPT2 geometry optimizations also performed; solvent structure from molecular dynamics with MOLDY using 214 TIP3P water molecules at fixed intramolecular geometry in a cubic box at the experimental density of water at 298 K

software: MOLCAS-5; MOLDY for the molecular dynamics

active_space_orbital_description: All configurations arising from six valence electrons in five orbitals (6e/5o). A larger (12e,11o) space was also tested for the excited-state geometry optimizations.
active_space_protocol: (6e,5o) used throughout for the reported vertical and adiabatic transitions; (12e,11o) used alongside it for CASPT2 excited-state geometry optimizations as a quality check
electronic_structure_description: Vertical and adiabatic electronic transitions of acrolein in water solution compared with the gas phase. CASPT2 excited-state geometry optimizations were run with both active spaces and vertical emission transitions evaluated at those geometries. The paper notes that in fluorescence spectra the vertical transition does not necessarily coincide with the band maximum, and that resolving the discrepancy against the experimental emission maximum would require Franck-Condon factors, which is outside its scope.
Other: A rare explicit null result on active space size: CASPT2 excited-state geometry optimizations were performed with both the (6e,5o) working space and a much larger (12e,11o), vertical emission transitions were evaluated at both geometries, and the authors report that no relevant differences were found relative to the (6e,5o) CASPT2//CASSCF calculation. So for this molecule and property the small space is validated by direct comparison rather than by assertion. The authors are equally clear about where the remaining discrepancy with experiment actually lies - not in the space, but in the neglect of Franck-Condon factors, since a vertical transition need not coincide with a fluorescence band maximum.
reference_short: Aguilar et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2007 (CASPT2//CASSCF study of acrolein in water solution)
notes: Condensed to one row for acrolein; the paper compares the same molecule in vacuo and in water rather than treating distinct compounds. Both active spaces are stated, with the working (6e,5o) recorded in active_space_nel/norb and the (12e,11o) check in active_space_protocol.

geometry_source: transition states first optimized at UHF/6-31G*, then reoptimized at CASSCF(4,6)/6-31G* using the UHF geometries and wave functions as the initial guess; CASSCF frequencies were not affordable, so harmonic frequencies came from UHF/6-31G* with ZPE corrections scaled by 0.89
method: CASSCF for the open-shell singlet transition states; B3LYP/6-31G* for the rest of the surface; transition state theory for rate constants
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons distributed over six orbitals in the (4,6) active space. The individual orbitals are not enumerated by the paper.
electronic_structure_description: Mechanisms of phenanthrene formation from biphenyl and naphthalene in combustion, across three competitive reaction pathways. CASSCF was applied specifically to six open-shell singlet transition states - TS4b, TS5b and TS11b of reaction network I, and TS5b, TS6b and TS14b of reaction network II. The highest barrier for one route is calculated at 45 kcal/mol, accessible at high temperatures; a naphthalene route involves two successive losses of ring hydrogen.
Other: CASSCF is deployed surgically rather than across the surface: only six specific open-shell singlet transition states get the multireference treatment, everything else being B3LYP, because those are the points where a single-determinant description fails. Two practical compromises are stated. The CASSCF was bootstrapped from UHF geometries and wave functions as the initial guess, so convergence to the intended solution depended on the broken-symmetry starting point. And CASSCF frequencies were unaffordable, so zero-point corrections on these multireference transition states come from UHF/6-31G* frequencies scaled by 0.89 - meaning the barrier heights combine a CASSCF electronic energy with a Hartree-Fock vibrational correction.
reference_short: Mebel et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2002 (phenanthrene synthesis from biphenyl and naphthalene)
notes: Condensed to one row for the phenanthrene-formation transition states: a single (4,6) space is applied to six open-shell singlet transition states across two reaction networks, and the paper does not assign distinct spaces to them. The remaining species on the surface are treated at B3LYP only and carry no active space, so they get no rows.

geometry_source: not stated in the extracted text; crystallographic references are cited
method: state-averaged CASSCF (over the lowest two or three states of a given symmetry); LS-CASPT2 (level-shift corrected CASPT2) to avoid intruder state problems
software: MOLCAS-3; a CCI program interfaced with the ASTERIX system for part of the model-system work
basis_set: atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis sets for the CASSCF/CASPT2 work
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons correlated in eleven active orbitals, or twelve when the bpy pi*(a2) orbital is included. The space comprises mainly the 3d orbitals together with the 4d orbitals that correlate them, the lowest bpy pi* orbitals of b2 and a2 local symmetry, and doubly occupied orbitals carrying a significant metal contribution. In the CASPT2 step only valence electrons - metal 3d and second-row 2s and 2p - were correlated.
active_space_protocol: (10,11) for Cr(CO)4(bpy), extended to (10,12) when the bpy pi*(a2) orbital is added; the reduced model system Cr(CO)4(dab) was treated with an 8-electron, 10-orbital space
electronic_structure_description: Lowest excited states of Cr(CO)4(2,2'-bipyridine). The excitations of interest originate in promotion of chromium d electrons to the lowest bpy pi* orbital of b2 local symmetry, with 3d -> 3d ligand-field excitations also considered. Dipole-allowed transitions and their intensities are analysed.
Other: The space is built around a specific excitation class rather than by a valence rule: the paper states its interest centres on 3d -> pi*(bpy) and 3d -> 3d excitations, so the space takes the 3d set, the 4d shell that correlates it - a double-shell correction, essential for 3d transition metals - the lowest bpy pi* orbitals, and any doubly occupied orbitals with significant metal character. The a2 bpy pi* orbital is optional, giving eleven or twelve orbitals for the same ten electrons depending on whether that state is targeted. Intruder states were a real problem here and were handled with a level-shifted CASPT2 rather than by respacing. Note the double-shell inclusion in particular: for a d-block complex this is a documented case where the 4d correlating orbitals were judged necessary, in contrast to several other transition-metal rows in this database where a bare metal-d space sufficed.
reference_short: Daniel et al., Inorg. Chem. 1997 (lowest excited states of Cr(CO)4(2,2'-bipyridine))
notes: The paper does not state a formal oxidation state for the chromium centre, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty rather than inferred from the carbonyl stoichiometry. Geometry source is not given in the extracted text.

geometry_source: CASSCF(9,9)/cc-pVDZ potential energy surface contour map for the initial processes as a function of the N(2D) position; MP2(full)/cc-pVTZ used to optimize the minima M1-M6, transition states TS1-TS5 and product fragments on the rest of the pathway
method: CASSCF for the initial approach surface; MP2(full) for the remaining reaction pathways

active_space_orbital_description: Nine electrons in nine active orbitals: the three nitrogen 2p orbitals, the CH sigma and CH sigma* orbitals, and two sets of CN pi and CN pi* orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Reaction of the excited nitrogen atom N(2D) with HCN. The initial approach is mapped as a two-dimensional CASSCF potential energy surface in the position of the attacking nitrogen; six minima and five transition states are then characterized along the full pathway, together with the product fragments.
Other: The space is composed atom-by-atom around what the reaction does: three N 2p orbitals to carry the 2D atomic state of the attacking nitrogen, the CH sigma/sigma* pair for the bond that may break, and both CN pi/pi* sets for the triple bond that must reorganize. That gives (9,9) with an odd electron count, as required for a doublet. Note the division of labour, which bounds what the space describes: CASSCF is used only for the initial approach surface where the atom-plus-molecule interaction is multireference, while everything downstream - all six minima, five transition states and the product fragments - comes from single-reference MP2(full) with a larger cc-pVTZ basis. Same authors' N(2D) + CH4 study uses the analogous construction at (5,5), the difference being the CN pi system that HCN adds.
reference_short: Kurosaki & Takayanagi, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999 (ab initio study of the N(2D) + HCN reaction)
notes: Condensed to one row for the N(2D) + HCN reaction system; the CASSCF treatment covers the initial approach surface specifically, with the rest of the pathway at MP2 and therefore carrying no active space. Space size and full orbital composition stated explicitly.

ligand_set: three bridging hydroxo groups between two Cr(III) centres
method: CASSCF (state-optimized) and SA-CASSCF with equal-weight averaging over the lowest root of each spin multiplicity; broken-symmetry DFT for comparison
basis_set: Ahlrichs Def2 family, with a larger set on the metals and SVP on the ligands, denoted QZVP-SVP; SVP used for the CASSCF orbital analyses
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in ten orbitals - the six singly occupied magnetic orbitals of the two Cr(III) d3 centres extended by the remaining 3d orbitals. A smaller CASSCF(6,6) using only the magnetic orbitals was examined first, with its natural orbital occupation numbers reported.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(6,6)/SVP over the six magnetic orbitals for the S = 0 state, with natural orbital occupation numbers inspected; extended to CASSCF(6,10) by including the remaining 3d orbitals, run both state-optimized and state-averaged over the lowest root of each spin multiplicity
electronic_structure_description: Zero-field splitting constants of an antiferromagnetically coupled tris-hydroxo bridged chromium(III) dimer with an S = 0 ground state and a spin ladder above it. In the S = 0 state each active orbital has an occupancy of about 1, the dominant configuration state function carries a coefficient of only 0.28, and the next twenty most significant CSFs have coefficients around 0.1. The S = 1 and S = 2 states show a similar picture.
Other: The paper supplies a quantitative diagnosis of why a minimal space is not enough here, which is more useful than the space size itself: in the S = 0 state every active orbital of the CASSCF(6,6) has an occupancy near 1, the leading CSF has a coefficient of only 0.28, and roughly twenty further CSFs sit near 0.1 - a textbook signature of a strongly multiconfigurational wave function with no dominant reference. That is what motivated extending to CASSCF(6,10) by bringing in the remaining 3d orbitals, run both state-optimized and state-averaged with equal weights over the lowest root of each spin multiplicity. So (6,6) here is the magnetic-orbital minimum and (6,10) the metal-d completion; the occupancy and CSF-coefficient numbers are the evidence for preferring the latter and are worth carrying alongside the space.
reference_short: Neese et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2012, 8, 4915 (electronic and magnetic properties of Kremer's tris-hydroxo bridged chromium dimer)
notes: Condensed to one row for the dimer; the paper treats one compound across its spin ladder rather than distinct compounds. Cr(III) is stated by the paper and the d3 count follows from it; d_electron_count carries the 3d shell prefix per policy. active_space_nel/norb record the (6,10) space used to characterize the spin states, with the (6,6) magnetic-orbital space in active_space_protocol.

geometry_source: all species (bicbut, g-but, t-but, con_TS, dis_TS, gt_TS) optimized at CASSCF(10,10)/cc-pVDZ, characterized by harmonic frequency analysis, with IRC calculations at the same level to confirm each transition state connects the correct minima; CR-CC(2,3)/cc-pVTZ single points for the reported enthalpies

basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF geometries; cc-pVTZ for the CR-CC(2,3) single points
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals: five doubly occupied molecular orbitals correlating with the C1-C2, C1-C3, C2-C3, C2-C4 and C3-C4 sigma bonds, together with the corresponding antibonding MOs. The space was constructed to account for all changes in the bicyclobutane ring system along the conrotatory and disrotatory pathways.
electronic_structure_description: Conrotatory and disrotatory isomerization channels of bicyclo[1.1.0]butane to trans-buta-1,3-diene. Six stationary points are characterized: the bicyclobutane reactant, gauche and trans butadiene products, the conrotatory and disrotatory transition states, and a gauche-to-trans transition state. Enthalpies relative to the reactant are reported at CR-CC(2,3)/cc-pVTZ//CASSCF(10,10)/cc-pVDZ and compared with available experimental values.
Other: The space is enumerated bond by bond rather than by a valence count: five sigma bonding MOs of the bicyclobutane ring skeleton - C1-C2, C1-C3, C2-C3, C2-C4 and C3-C4 - with their five antibonding partners, chosen explicitly so that every bond that changes along either isomerization channel is described. That is why it is (10,10) and not a smaller pi-type space: the reaction is a sigma-framework rearrangement, and the ring bonds that break and form must all be active. Note also the deliberate split of roles: CASSCF supplies geometries and IRC connectivity while the reported energetics come from CR-CC(2,3), because the paper states the dynamic correlation effects cannot be recovered by CASSCF(10,10) alone.
reference_short: Kinal & Piecuch, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 734
notes: Condensed to one row for the isomerization system; the paper's six stationary points share a single stated active space of identical composition. The bond-by-bond orbital list is given explicitly in the text.

method: CASSCF
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: 6-311G* for K, N and O atoms; 6-31G for the remaining C and H skeleton
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eight orbitals. The enlarged space was built by adding, to the four SOMO-derived magnetic orbitals of the reduced CASSCF(4,4), the next lower MOs from the canonical set of that first calculation. Those added orbitals look like the original ones rotated by 90 degrees, giving antibonding MOs parallel to the reference plane. The four magnetic orbitals of the (4,4) space originate from the symmetry-adapted SOMO states of each TEMPOL fragment and are roughly described as pi-perpendicular combinations, N1-(px_O - px_N), with local z axes along the NO bonds and x axes perpendicular to the mean plane of the six-membered rings.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(4,4) over the four symmetry-adapted SOMO-derived magnetic orbitals of the TEMPO fragments; enlarged to CASSCF(12,8) by taking the next lower MOs from the canonical set of the (4,4) result
multiplicities_studied: states of four coupled S = 1/2 spins
electronic_structure_description: Supramolecular assembly of four S = 1/2 nitroxide spins around a diamagnetic Y(III) centre. Exchange parameters fitted to magnetic susceptibility give Ja = -5.1 cm-1 and Jb = -3.4 cm-1 for the edges with Jd imposed as 0 for the diagonal. The CASSCF(12,8) ab initio results are Ja = -4.83 cm-1, Jb = -3.44 cm-1 and Jd = -0.07 cm-1. The 10 K EPR spectrum is consistent, within the dipolar approximation, with four interacting spins at the nodes of the assembly.
Other: The active space is grown by a specific procedure worth recording: the enlarged (12,8) was constructed by taking the next lower MOs from the canonical set produced by the reduced (4,4) calculation, so the extension is defined by the first calculation's own orbitals rather than chosen independently - and the added orbitals turn out to be the magnetic orbitals rotated by 90 degrees, giving in-plane antibonding partners. More striking is the use the authors make of the result: magnetic susceptibility fitting admitted SEVERAL versions of multiple solutions with acceptable goodness of fit, and the ab initio J values were used to select among them. The paper raises this explicitly as a methodological caveat about the artifacts of automatic best-fit parameters given the relative blindness of magnetic susceptibility modeling. Here the CASSCF is the arbiter of an experimental fit, not the other way round.
reference_short: Inorg. Chem. 2007 (spin coupling in a tetra(quinoline-TEMPO)yttrium(III) complex)
notes: Condensed to one row for the tetraradical complex. d_electron_count is left EMPTY: Y(III) is d0 and diamagnetic, and the magnetism is entirely ligand-centred on the four nitroxide radicals, so recording a metal d count would misdescribe where the spins live. The program package is not named in the extracted text.

geometry_source: equilibrium geometries of stable molecules and transition states optimized at CASSCF/cc-pVTZ; MRCI-level optimization performed for one channel using a reduced active space; single-point energies at MRCI+Davidson/aug-cc-pV(Q+d)Z on the CASSCF geometries
method: CASSCF; MRCI with the Davidson correction; transition state theory for the derived rate expressions
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; aug-cc-pV(Q+d)Z for the MRCI single points
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space containing nineteen electrons distributed in thirteen orbitals, used unless otherwise noted. For MRCI geometry optimization of one channel this was cut to nine valence electrons in eight orbitals by downgrading five doubly occupied valence orbitals into the inactive space.
active_space_protocol: Full valence (19,13) for the potential energy surface characterization; reduced to (9,8) for MRCI geometry optimization by moving into the inactive space the five doubly occupied valence orbitals whose occupation numbers exceeded 1.997 in the full valence CASSCF
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy surface of the SH + O2 reaction on the doublet ground surface. Several product channels are considered and three-parameter Arrhenius expressions derived for the kinetically favoured ones. For reaction channel R3, MRCI optimization lowered the electronic energies by about 1 kJ/mol relative to CASSCF geometries, a discrepancy of less than 2 percent with respect to the geometry variation, so CASSCF was taken to reproduce the MRCI transition state geometries accurately.
Other: A clean, numerically justified space reduction. The full valence space is (19,13), but MRCI geometry optimization at that size was prohibitive, so five doubly occupied valence orbitals were downgraded to inactive using an explicit occupation-number criterion - each had occupancy greater than 1.997 in the full valence CASSCF, i.e. essentially closed - leaving (9,8). The authors then validated the reduction rather than assuming it: MRCI optimization changed the electronic energies by only about 1 kJ/mol against the CASSCF geometries, under 2 percent with respect to the geometry variation, which is why the reported energetics use MRCI+Davidson single points on CASSCF geometries. This is a worked example of both how to prune an active space by occupancy and how to check that the pruning did not matter.
reference_short: Zhou, Sendt & Haynes, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009 (computational study of the reaction SH + O2)
notes: Condensed to one row for the SH + O2 reaction system; the paper characterizes multiple channels of the same doublet surface with one stated full valence space. Both the full valence (19,13) and the occupancy-pruned (9,8) are recorded, the latter in active_space_protocol. The program package is not named in the extracted text.

method: state-averaged CASSCF; conical intersections optimized in the (f-2)-dimensional intersection space by the method of Bearpark et al.
basis_set: 6-311G(d) for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; 6-311G(d,p) also used in the study
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in eleven orbitals: nine p-pi orbitals plus two nonbonding orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Photochemical isomerization of indoxazene, followed on the S0 and S1 surfaces. Stationary points are characterized by analytic CASSCF harmonic frequencies and conical intersections located in the (f-2)-dimensional intersection space.
Other: Two spaces built by the same explicit recipe applied to two ring sizes: all the p-pi orbitals of the ring system plus exactly two nonbonding orbitals. That gives nine p-pi + two nonbonding for the bicyclic indoxazene, i.e. (14,11), and five p-pi + two nonbonding for the monocyclic isoxazole, i.e. (10,7). The recipe is what transfers between the two molecules, not the numbers - a consumer reading (14,11) or (10,7) alone would not see that both are the same construction scaled to the conjugated system present. State averaging is used specifically to obtain geometries on the intersection space, since the conical intersections are the objects of interest and a state-specific description would bias one surface.
reference_short: Ming-Der Su, J. Org. Chem. 2009, 74, 6055
notes: One of two heterocycles whose photoisomerizations are compared in the same paper; one row each since the active space scales with the conjugated system. Both spaces are stated with full orbital composition.

compound_name: FeO+ + H2 reaction species (intermediates and transition states)
method: CASSCF with a full-valence reference space; CASPT2 (RSPT2) and diagonal CASPT2 (CASPT2D/RSPT2D) on top; DFT for comparison
basis_set: a series of basis sets was assessed, including a triple-zeta set with a dedicated hydrogen basis and an atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis
active_space_orbital_description: Fifteen electrons in twelve orbitals, the full-valence space for the intermediates and transition states of the FeO+ + H2 reaction shown in the paper's Figure 1.
active_space_protocol: Full-valence CAS per species: (2,2) H2, (8,6) H2O, (7,6) Fe+(6D), (7,5) Fe+(4F), (13,10) FeO+, (15,12) the reaction species; Fe+ additionally computed at (7,11) for 6D and (7,10) for 4F to test the 4d shell effect
multiplicities_studied: multiple spin states along the reaction
electronic_structure_description: Species along the H2 activation pathway by FeO+, giving the FeO+ + H2 to Fe+ + H2O transformation. All bonds change drastically along the reaction, which is the paper's stated reason for requiring a full-valence reference throughout.
Other: The governing principle is stated outright and is unusually clear: because all bonds change drastically along this reaction, a FULL-VALENCE CAS is described as the only chemically sensible choice of reference space. Every species therefore gets its own full-valence space rather than a shared one - (2,2) for H2, (8,6) for H2O, (7,6) and (7,5) for the two Fe+ states, (13,10) for FeO+, and (15,12) for the reaction species - so the numbers vary with the molecule rather than with any tuning decision. Separately, the paper runs an explicit 3d double-shell test on the iron cation: enlarging Fe+ from (7,6) to (7,11) for 6D and from (7,5) to (7,10) for 4F specifically to probe the effect of the 4d shell on the atomic excitation energy. That makes this one of the clearer documented cases of the 4d-correlating-shell question being posed and measured rather than assumed.
reference_short: J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2014 (correlated ab initio and density functional studies on H2 activation by FeO+)
notes: One of six species in a full-valence CASSCF/CASPT2 study of H2 activation by FeO+; one row each because each carries its own stated full-valence space. The paper does not state formal oxidation states, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty for the iron-containing rows.

Other: The governing principle is stated outright and is unusually clear: because all bonds change drastically along this reaction, a FULL-VALENCE CAS is described as the only chemically sensible choice of reference space. Every species therefore gets its own full-valence space rather than a shared one - (2,2) for H2, (8,6) for H2O, (7,6) and (7,5) for the two Fe+ states, (13,10) for FeO+, and (15,12) for the reaction species - so the numbers vary with the molecule rather than with any tuning decision. Separately, the paper runs an explicit 3d double-shell test on the iron cation: enlarging Fe+ from (7,6) to (7,11) for 6D and from (7,5) to (7,10) for 4F specifically to probe the effect of the 4d shell on the atomic excitation energy. That makes this one of the clearer documented cases of the 4d-correlating-shell question being posed and measured rather than assumed.

active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two molecular orbitals, the sigma_g and sigma_u active MOs of the ground state. These are re-expressed in an orthogonal valence bond basis of orthogonalized atomic orbitals a and b to give the VB reading of the CASSCF wave function.
multiplicities_studied: singlet (with the 3Sigma_u+ neutral and 1Sigma_u+ ionic excited states quoted for comparison)
electronic_structure_description: Ground 1Sigma_g+ state of H2 treated at several levels. CASSCF 2/2 with the cc-pVQZ basis gives a bond length of 1.426 and an energy of -1.152099 hartree, against the exact values of 1.401 and -1.174475. Valence bond, MO-SCF and 2x2 CI results are tabulated alongside; the paper notes these can be obtained equivalently by a 2x2 CI in the non-orthogonal VB approach, the orthogonal VB approach, or the MO scheme.
Other: A pedagogical rather than production calculation, and the row should be read that way: this is a Journal of Chemical Education article whose purpose is to show that the same two-electron-in-two-orbital wave function can be read either as molecular orbital theory or as valence bond theory. The sigma_g and sigma_u active MOs of the CASSCF are re-expressed in a basis of orthogonalized atomic orbitals to give the VB reading, and the paper demonstrates that the non-orthogonal VB, orthogonal VB and MO schemes all yield the same 2x2 CI result. The (2,2) here is therefore the minimum space that makes the equivalence demonstrable, not a recommendation for treating H2 - the tabulated CASSCF energy of -1.152099 hartree against the exact -1.174475 shows plainly how far a minimal space falls short even for the simplest molecule.

active_space_orbital_description: An (8,7) active space composed of the three valence metal d orbitals with their four electrons, the two filled chlorine pi orbitals with their electrons, and two empty CO pi* molecular orbitals of a' and a'' symmetry.
electronic_structure_description: Low-lying singlet and triplet states of the 16-electron d4 half-sandwich complex. Relative energies in kcal/mol against the 1A'-b reference: CASSCF gives 25.4, 0.0, 7.6 and 26.3 for the four low-energy states, compared with 21.3, 0.0, 3.4 and 24.4 at CCSD(T) and 20.0, 0.0, 4.1 and 25.1 at BPW91. The singlet states are distinguished by their occupations, 1A'-a being (1a')2(1a'')2 and 1A'-b being (1a')2(2a')2.
Other: The active space is assembled from three distinct ligand-field ingredients rather than a metal-only set, and the composition is spelled out: three valence metal d orbitals carrying four electrons, the two filled chlorine pi donor orbitals with their electrons, and two empty CO pi-acceptor orbitals of a' and a'' symmetry. That is a deliberate donor-metal-acceptor construction for a 16-electron complex where both pi donation from halide and back-donation to carbonyl matter. Worth noting the numerical outcome: CASSCF single points at B3LYP geometries put the excited singlet and triplet states consistently HIGHER than CCSD(T) does - 25.4 versus 21.3 and 7.6 versus 3.4 kcal/mol - so the missing dynamic correlation biases the state ordering gaps upward here, and CASSCF is the outlier among the four methods compared. Only the X = Cl member of the halide/CN/H/CH3 series received CASSCF treatment.

ligand_set: one terminal nitride and three fluoride
point_group: C3v (calculations run in Cs, all molecules converged to C3v)
geometry_source: geometries optimized at the CASPT2 level; vibrational frequencies from numerical gradients and Hessians
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 with the standard IPEA Hamiltonian and an imaginary shift of 0.1 to remove weak intruder states
basis_set: 5s4p2d1f for P, 4s3p2d1f for F and N, 6s5p3d2f1g for Cr
active_space_orbital_description: full valence active space of twelve electrons in twelve orbitals, used in place of the default bond-targeted space because the Cr-F bond is less ionic than in the Mo and W analogues
active_space_protocol: six electrons in six orbitals (three bonding, three antibonding) describing the M-N or M-P triple bond for all species except N(triple)CrF3, which used a full valence (12,12) space because of the less ionic Cr-F bond
electronic_structure_description: Terminal group 6 nitride complex studied by combined matrix-isolation experiment and CASPT2 theory. The M-N triple bond is the focus, with sigma and pi bonding analysed across the Cr, Mo and W series and compared with matrix infrared observations in argon and neon.
Other: The default space is bond-targeted rather than valence-complete: six active orbitals - three bonding and three antibonding - with six active electrons, chosen specifically to describe the M-triple-bond-N or M-triple-bond-P linkage. The exception is instructive and is the paper's own reasoning: for N(triple)CrF3 a FULL valence active space of twelve electrons in twelve orbitals was used instead, because the Cr-F bond has less ionic character than its Mo and W analogues, so the fluorines can no longer be treated as spectators outside the space. That is a documented case of ionicity, not size or row, deciding whether ligand orbitals must enter the active space. In the CASPT2 step all valence electrons plus the semicore 3s3p (Cr), 4s4p (Mo) and 5s5p (W) were correlated, so the correlation treatment extends well beyond the active orbitals.
reference_short: Andrews et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2008 (terminal group 6 nitride and phosphide complexes)
notes: One of six terminal group 6 nitride and phosphide complexes in the same study; one row each since the metal and pnictogen vary. This member uniquely uses the full valence (12,12) space rather than the bond-targeted (6,6), for the stated reason that its Cr-F bond is less ionic. The paper does not state formal oxidation states, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty.

active_space_orbital_description: Nineteen electrons in fifteen orbitals for the hydrogen-bonded complexes; a smaller (15,13) space was also used to explore them. Composition set from natural orbital fractional occupancies of an MRCI density matrix correlating all valence electrons.
active_space_protocol: (15,13) and (19,15) explored for the hydrogen-bonded complexes; (12,9) for O3; (7,6) for HO2; CASPT2 single points computed on a common CASSCF(19,15) reference for all stationary points
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase hydrogen-bonded complex between ozone and the hydroperoxyl radical. All stationary points were optimized at the CASSCF level, with CASPT2 single points on a common CASSCF(19,15) reference giving the relative stabilities.
Other: Spaces are set by the same natural-occupancy procedure the authors use elsewhere: composition chosen from the fractional occupation of natural orbitals of a first-order density matrix taken from an MRCI wave function correlating all valence electrons. What is distinctive here is the final step - although the hydrogen-bonded complexes were explored with two different spaces, (15,13) and (19,15), the CASPT2 energies were all computed on a COMMON CASSCF(19,15) reference. Using one shared reference across the stationary points is what makes the relative stabilities comparable; a per-species reference would leave the differences contaminated by differing zeroth orders. The individual fragments keep their own smaller spaces, (12,9) for ozone and (7,6) for the hydroperoxyl radical, for their isolated descriptions.
reference_short: Anglada et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2007 (gas-phase hydrogen-bonded complex between ozone and hydroperoxyl radical)
notes: One of three species in the ozone/hydroperoxyl complexation study, each with its own natural-occupancy-derived active space; one row each. Note the HO2 space here is (7,6), matching the same authors' HOO self-reaction and CH3O2+HO2 studies in this database only in method, not in size - there HO2 came out (5,4) - so the occupancy procedure does not always return the same space for the same fragment in different chemical contexts.
