compound_name: GFP chromophore with its proton wire (photoinduced multiple proton transfer)
geometry_source: structures from classical molecular dynamics of the solvated GFP protein (CHARMM), with eight structures corresponding to the eight possible protonation states of the proton wire
method: multiconfigurational CASSCF-based calculations; each of the three electronic states computed separately with no state averaging
software: MOLCAS 6; CHARMM (version 28b2) for the molecular dynamics
basis_set: 6-31++G(d,p) on the oxygen atoms of the wire and the three transferrable protons, 6-31G on the remaining atoms; diffuse functions are stated to be important for describing the 1(pi sigma*) charge-transfer state
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, but with a state-dependent composition. For the 1(pi pi*) state the space is the three highest occupied and three lowest unoccupied pi orbitals of the chromophore. For the 1(pi sigma*) state the highest-energy pi* orbital is substituted by the lowest unoccupied sigma orbital. The same (6,6) space is used for S0.
active_space_protocol: (6,6) with state-dependent composition - three occupied plus three unoccupied chromophore pi orbitals for S0 and 1(pi pi*), with the highest pi* swapped for the lowest sigma* to describe 1(pi sigma*); convergence checked with a (9,8) space of the four highest occupied and four lowest unoccupied pi orbitals plus the lowest unoccupied sigma orbital, this larger space kept identical across all three states
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy landscape of the photoinduced multiple proton transfer in the green fluorescent protein. Three electronic states are followed - the ground state S0, the locally excited 1(pi pi*) state, and the 1(pi sigma*) charge-transfer state in which the water molecule receives a net electron from the chromophore. Eight structures corresponding to the eight possible protonation states of the proton wire are examined.
Other: The (6,6) label conceals a state-dependent composition, which is the point worth carrying: for S0 and the locally excited 1(pi pi*) state the space is three occupied and three unoccupied chromophore pi orbitals, but for the 1(pi sigma*) charge-transfer state the highest pi* is swapped out for the lowest unoccupied sigma orbital, because that is the orbital the transferring electron actually enters. Same size, different orbitals, chosen per state. The authors then check that this swapping does not bias the comparison by recomputing all three states in a single common (9,8) space - four occupied pi, four unoccupied pi, plus the lowest sigma* - held identical across the states. Note also that the three states were computed separately with no state averaging, so each is variationally optimized for itself.
reference_short: Vendrell, Gelabert, Moreno & Lluch, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2006, 128, 3564
notes: system_class=cluster-model: the chromophore plus proton wire is a QM region taken from the solvated protein, not an isolated molecule. This is the source study whose CASPT2//CASSCF reference energies were reused in 10.1021/ja0666595 (the EVB proton-wire fitting paper), which was marked not_usable earlier in this session precisely because its multireference data came from here.

compound_name: oxy-myoglobin Fe-O2 active site (heme with bound dioxygen)
ligand_set: protoporphyrin IX macrocycle, proximal histidine, and bound dioxygen; His64 and protein polarization included via the MM environment
geometry_source: structure optimized for the singlet ground state at the B3LYP/MM B1 level; CASSCF single points at that geometry
method: CASSCF/MM (QM/MM) and CASSCF in the gas phase, denoted CASSCF(g); DFT/MM (B3LYP) for comparison
basis_set: the study's B1 basis for the DFT/MM optimization; the CASSCF basis is not separately specified in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve orbitals, tabulated individually by the paper: Fe 3d_xz; O2 pi; Fe 3d_yz + O2 pi_perp*; Fe 3d_z2 + O2 pi*; porphyrin N sigma + Fe 3d_x2-y2; Fe 3d_xy; O2 pi_perp; Fe 3d_yz - O2 pi_perp*; Fe 3d_x2-y2 - porphyrin N sigma; Fe 3d_z2 - O2 pi*; Fe 4d_xy; Fe 4d_xz. The z axis points along Fe-O and x and y along two nearly orthogonal Fe-N(porphyrin) directions.
electronic_structure_description: Nature of the Fe-O2 bonding in oxy-myoglobin and the effect of the protein environment. The CASSCF/MM singlet ground state is described by two dominant configurations carrying a total weight of about 90 percent, with the next most important configurations below 1 percent. Two low-lying triplet states T-1 and T-2 are also characterized. The paper notes that explicit treatment of His64 and protein polarization could substantially change the electronic configuration of the lowest triplet state, in the CASSCF description as well as the DFT one.
Other: A fully enumerated active space, which is rare and worth using: all twelve orbitals are tabulated individually rather than described by class, showing that the space is not simply metal-d but a set of Fe 3d / O2 pi bonding and antibonding COMBINATIONS - both the in-plane pi/pi* and the perpendicular pi_perp/pi_perp* of the O-O unit paired with Fe 3d_yz and 3d_z2 - plus two porphyrin-nitrogen sigma mixtures and, notably, two Fe 4d double-shell orbitals (4d_xy and 4d_xz). The double-shell inclusion places this alongside Cr(CO)4(bpy) in this database as a documented case where 4d correlating orbitals were judged necessary for a 3d centre. The multireference character is quantified rather than asserted: the singlet ground state needs two configurations for about 90 percent of its weight, so a single-determinant description is inadequate but the wave function is not pathologically mixed. Both a QM/MM and a gas-phase CASSCF were run at the same geometry, isolating the protein's effect on the wave function itself.
reference_short: Chen, Ikeda-Saito & Shaik, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2008, 130, 14778
notes: system_class=cluster-model: the QM region is a heme active site embedded in the protein via QM/MM, not an isolated molecule. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left EMPTY on purpose - the formal oxidation state of iron in oxy-myoglobin is the very question the Fe-O2 bonding analysis addresses, with Fe(II)-O2 and Fe(III)-superoxide descriptions both in play, so recording one would assert what the paper is investigating.

point_group: C2v at symmetric geometries, with symmetry breaking to Cs the object of study
geometry_source: equilibrium geometries determined for each electronic state; harmonic vibrational frequencies obtained by numerical differentiation of total energies at the respective equilibrium geometries
method: full valence CASSCF; internally contracted MRCI (ICMRCI) for static correlation; CISD, CCSD and CCSD(T) on ROHF references for the single-reference comparison
software: MOLPRO; ACES II for some harmonic frequencies
basis_set: correlation-consistent cc-pVXZ and aug-cc-pVXZ with X = T, Q, 5
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space of seventeen electrons in twelve orbitals, namely the 2s and 2p orbitals of nitrogen and both oxygens.
electronic_structure_description: Born-Oppenheimer symmetry breaking in the C-tilde state of NO2. The state lies at T0 = 46.0 kcal/mol (2.00 eV, 16100 cm-1) at the aug-cc-pV5Z/UCCSD(T) level, in good agreement with experiment, with an ONO angle of 109.7 degrees at the same level and an averaged NO bond distance of 1.329 angstroms.
Other: The full valence space is defined by shell rather than by count - the 2s and 2p orbitals of N and both O atoms - and the paper's purpose is to separate what static correlation contributes from what dynamic correlation contributes to a symmetry-breaking problem. That is why both branches are run in parallel on the same system: full valence CASSCF and ICMRCI for the static side, and CISD/CCSD/CCSD(T) on ROHF references for the single-reference side, with basis sets pushed to aug-cc-pV5Z so basis incompleteness cannot be confused with either. Symmetry breaking in doublet states like this is a classic case where a single-determinant reference can artificially localize, so the value of the (17,12) here is diagnostic - establishing whether the broken symmetry survives a properly multireference treatment - rather than as a recommended production space.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2008 (Born-Oppenheimer symmetry breaking in the C-tilde state of NO2)
notes: Condensed to one row for NO2; the paper studies one molecule across electronic states rather than distinct compounds. The full valence space and its shell composition are stated explicitly. Note this is a distinct paper from the existing NO2 row in the database (W1995927525), which covers bent and cyclic forms.

active_space_orbital_description: Six active orbitals with six electrons: the pi and pi* orbitals of allyl and of ethylene, together with the sigma and sigma* orbitals involved in the ene reaction, matching the space used for the propylene plus ethylene ene reaction in the authors' previous work.
active_space_protocol: (6,6) pi/pi* of allyl and ethylene plus the reacting sigma/sigma* for the reaction pathways; for the Li-allyl interaction specifically, CASSCF(4,4) with one a' orbital of Li plus three allyl pi(p) orbitals, extended to CASSCF(4,7) by adding three virtual orbitals of the Li atom so that both a' and a'' orbitals - all the valence atomic orbitals of Li - are active
electronic_structure_description: Ene reaction of allyl-Li with ethylene. The Li-allyl interaction in Cs symmetry has two components: the a'(s and/or p) orbital of lithium with the allyl 1pi orbital, and the a''(p) orbital of lithium with the allyl 2pi orbital. Reaction barriers at the MRMP2 level are significantly lower than for the corresponding metal-free ene reaction.
Other: Two spaces serving different questions in the same paper. The reaction pathways use a (6,6) transferred deliberately from the authors' earlier propylene-plus-ethylene ene study, so the metallo-ene barriers are computed in a space chosen for comparability with the metal-free reaction rather than re-optimized for these systems. Separately, to characterize the metal-allyl interaction itself, a CASSCF(4,4) of one Li a' orbital plus three allyl pi(p) orbitals was extended to CASSCF(4,7) by adding three Li virtual orbitals, so that all the valence atomic orbitals of lithium - both a' and a'' - are active. The paper's reason is explicit: there are two distinct Li-allyl interactions in Cs symmetry, a'(s and/or p) with the allyl 1pi and a''(p) with the allyl 2pi, and only the enlarged space can describe both. Barriers are reported at MRMP2 on these references and are significantly lower than for the metal-free ene reaction.
reference_short: Sakai & Hikida, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 10985
notes: One of two metallo-ene systems, Li and Na, compared in the same paper; one row each since the metal is the variable under study. metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left EMPTY: lithium and sodium are main-group s-block metals with no d electrons, and per policy d_electron_count applies only to d- and f-block centres. The program package is not named in the extracted text.

basis_set: correlation-consistent triple-zeta (cc-pVTZ), with pure angular momentum basis functions throughout; 266 basis functions for the dehydrophenylnitrenes and 280 for phenylnitrene
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals: seven pi and pi* molecular orbitals plus the in-plane p atomic orbital centred on nitrogen. This is the space introduced by Borden and co-workers for phenylnitrene, reused unchanged.
active_space_protocol: (8,8) phenylnitrene reference of Borden and co-workers - seven pi/pi* plus in-plane N p AO; (9,9) for the dehydrophenylnitrenes, adding the in-plane orbital at the dehydro carbon; (11,10) explored for 4-dehydrophenylnitrene by further adding the nitrogen nonbonding pair, giving very similar low-energy results; (6,6) benzene six pi/pi*; (7,7) phenyl radical adding the in-plane a1 MO; (5,5) 2-iminylpropan-1,3-diyl, four pi plus in-plane b2 at nitrogen
electronic_structure_description: Parent nitrene, included as the reference system against which the dehydro derivatives are compared.
Other: A worked example of building a space by systematic augmentation, with every step attributed and justified. The reference point is the (8,8) that Borden and co-workers introduced for phenylnitrene - seven pi/pi* MOs plus the in-plane p atomic orbital on nitrogen - reused here unchanged so results are comparable with that body of work. Removing a hydrogen to make a dehydrophenylnitrene adds one in-plane orbital at the dehydro carbon, giving (9,9); the increment is exactly the new radical centre. Benzene and the phenyl radical follow the same logic in miniature, (6,6) six pi/pi* and (7,7) adding the in-plane a1 orbital. The paper also reports a null result on further enlargement: an (11,10) space for 4-dehydrophenylnitrene, adding the nitrogen nonbonding electron pair, gave very similar results for the low-energy states considered - but the authors are careful to say such a larger space IS essential for higher excited states, which are outside their scope. That is a precise statement of where a space is and is not adequate.
reference_short: Bettinger & Sander, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2003 (dehydrophenylnitrenes: quartet versus doublet states)
notes: One of several species in a study of quartet versus doublet states of dehydrophenylnitrenes, all treated with spaces built by the same systematic augmentation; one row each since each carries its own stated (nel,norb). State-averaged CASSCF weighted the three states considered equally.

geometry_source: ground and excited state potential energy surfaces fully optimized at the CASSCF level; separated-fragment energies obtained by a supermolecule calculation with both fragments at large separation, using the same basis set and active space as the bound species
method: state-averaged CASSCF; RRKM theory for the dissociation rates
software: not named in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals, referred to by the paper as CAS(8,7). Arrived at by reduction: a literature space of sixteen valence electrons in eleven orbitals was cut by excluding the terminal N-N sigma orbital, which is doubly occupied with very low orbital energy, and then test CASSCF calculations with fourteen electrons in ten orbitals identified three further orbitals with occupancies near 2, which were deleted from the molecular orbital space.
active_space_protocol: Literature reference space of (16,11) reduced in two documented steps: the doubly occupied, low-energy terminal N-N sigma orbital excluded, giving (14,10); test calculations at that size then found three orbitals with occupancies near 2, which were deleted, leaving CAS(8,7). Also compared against CAS(14,10) with the cc-pVDZ basis.
electronic_structure_description: Photodissociation of hydrazoic acid at 248 nm and longer wavelengths. Ground and excited state surfaces are optimized and the dissociation rate computed with RRKM theory under the assumption that energy flows rapidly and randomly among the vibrational degrees of freedom.
Other: The space is reached by documented reduction from a published one rather than constructed from scratch, and each cut is justified by an orbital property. Starting from a literature (16,11), the terminal N-N sigma orbital is removed because it is doubly occupied with very low orbital energy; test calculations at the resulting (14,10) then reveal three more orbitals sitting at occupancies near 2, which are deleted, leaving (8,7). That is an occupancy-driven pruning like the SH + O2 case in this database, but performed against someone else's starting space. One methodological detail matters for anyone reusing these numbers: the separated-fragment energies come from a supermolecule calculation at large separation using the SAME basis and active space as the bound molecule, so dissociation energies are computed consistently rather than by subtracting independently optimized fragments.
reference_short: Fang et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2000 (photodissociation of HN3 at 248 nm and longer wavelength)
notes: Condensed to one row for HN3; the paper follows the dissociation of a single molecule across surfaces rather than treating distinct compounds. Both the final (8,7) and the intermediate (14,10) are stated, along with the reasoning for each reduction step. The program package is not named in the extracted text.

geometry_source: potential energy curve evaluated as a function of the shortest interfragment C-C distance; monomer SOMO shapes from UB3LYP/6-31+G(d)
method: CASSCF; MCQDPT on the CASSCF(2,2) reference; B3LYP for comparison
software: GAMESS-07 (CASSCF and MCQDPT); Gaussian 03 revision C.02 (B3LYP)
basis_set: 6-31+G(d) is stated for the B3LYP calculations; the basis used for the CASSCF and MCQDPT calculations is not separately stated
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals, the space comprising the two SOMO orbitals of the fragments at dissociation. This is stated to be the minimum that properly describes both the closed-shell singlet (CSS) and open-shell singlet (OSS) states arising from the interaction of the two doublet radical anions.
electronic_structure_description: Long, multicentre bonding in the tetracyanoquinodimethanide dimer dianion, observed in both the solid state and in solution. The isolated [TCNQ]2(2-) dimer is unbound at most levels, but a metastable minimum is found at the MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) level. Solid-state interactions were probed on the [cation]2[TCNQ]2 aggregate, the smallest unit containing all interactions present in the [K]2[TCNQ]2 crystal, and solution behaviour through {[TCNQ]2[H2O]n}2- and {[TCNQ]2[CH2Cl2]n}2- aggregates.
Other: A minimal (2,2) chosen for a specific representational reason rather than for accuracy: the space is the two fragment SOMOs at dissociation, which is exactly what is needed to describe both the closed-shell and open-shell singlet states that arise when two doublet radical anions interact. The authors justify the method by prior failure - B3LYP could not reproduce the diamagnetic ground state of the analogous [TCNE]2(2-) dimer, whereas MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) did - and note that MCQDPT on this reference captures the dispersion component of the interaction energy accurately, giving results similar to the more common CASPT2. The dependence on correlation treatment is stark here: the isolated dimer is unbound at most levels and only acquires a metastable minimum once MCQDPT is applied on top of the same (2,2) reference. This is the companion study to the same group's [TTF]2(2+) work already in this database, which used an identical (2,2) two-SOMO construction.
reference_short: Capdevila-Cortada, Novoa et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2009 (electronic structure of [TCNQ]2(2-))
notes: Condensed to one row for the dimer dianion; the crystal and solvated aggregates are environments for the same species rather than distinct compounds with their own active spaces. basis_set records only what the paper states: 6-31+G(d) is attributed specifically to the B3LYP work and no basis is given for the GAMESS CASSCF/MCQDPT calculations, exactly as in the companion [TTF]2(2+) paper.

The open-shell configuration is preferred in the lowest singlet state, with the closed-shell analogue lying 19.3 kcal/mol higher at CASPT2//CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G*. Reduced-space calculations gave open/closed gaps of 13.4, 24.2 and 5.3 kcal/mol at (8,7), (6,5) and (4,3) respectively, all agreeing on the open-shell preference.
Other: An unusually honest account of a space-size failure. Optimizing the closed-shell configuration proved impossible with the ideal active space - it collapsed to the open-shell solution - so reduced spaces were tried to force both configurations to converge. For 4-acetamidophenylnitrene the (8,7), (6,5) and (4,3) spaces gave open-shell/closed-shell gaps of 13.4, 24.2 and 5.3 kcal/mol, and the authors say plainly that this inconsistency is probably due to the lack of certain pi orbitals in the reduced spaces. The qualitative conclusion is robust across all of them - the open-shell configuration is consistently preferred - but the quantitative gap is not, and the authors state they were not able to obtain the exact energy difference this way. The final numbers, 19.3 and 20.4 kcal/mol, come from CASSCF(12,11) with a CASPT2 correction on the same space. A consumer should read the smaller spaces here as diagnostic attempts that failed quantitatively, not as alternatives.

The comparison it enables is worth noting: TD-DFT and CASPT2 agree closely on the lower transition (2.53 versus 2.44 eV) but diverge substantially on the higher one (3.20 versus 3.82 eV), so a consumer should not assume the two methods track each other across a spectrum. Other: A candid statement of a known inadequacy, kept deliberately. The authors say outright that this (18,12) space is NOT large enough to guarantee continuity of the pyrimidine potential energy surface on displacement from the C2v ground-state geometry in all modes, and that the intricacies of designing active spaces for pyrimidine are documented elsewhere. Their justification for accepting it is a division of labour: since CASSCF is not quantitatively reliable for excited-state energy differences anyway, they use it only to optimize geometries and report the more reliable CASPT2 energies, which makes the continuity problem of only minor significance. Second decision worth carrying: the space is held IDENTICAL for the bare molecule and for the hydrated complexes, justified by the pyrimidine orbitals lying well within the water band gap with no water orbitals participating in the transitions - so complexation shifts are computed at a constant active space rather than one that grows with the cluster.

CASSCF predicts expansion of the aromatic ring by 3 to 4 pm per bond on electronic excitation; the C4-C5 bond shortens by 2 pm in S1 while the C1-O bond length remains almost unchanged, the same behaviour found in calculations on phenol though experiment there predicts a bond shortening. Other: The paper tests whether its own space is larger than necessary and reports the evidence both ways. The (10,9) comprises all five occupied and four lowest unoccupied a'' pi orbitals, but the occupation number of the lowest-energy pi orbital stays close to two in both S0 and S1, indicating its contribution is small - and the authors corroborate this by repeating the calculation with a smaller (8,8) space and observing only a small lowering of the MCSCF energy. electronic_structure_description: The 1A2 singlet state of phenylphosphinidene, whose ring expansion is the subject of the study. Its singlet-triplet splitting is computed to be small.
Other: The (8/8) size is held constant across the reaction path while its COMPOSITION is re-chosen at every stationary point to match the bonding actually changing there. For the phosphinidene itself the eight orbitals are seven pi MOs plus the in-plane 2p AO on phosphorus - directly analogous to the phenylnitrene space of Borden and co-workers, which is the point of the comparison. At the transition structures the space instead holds six mainly-pi orbitals plus a sigma/sigma* pair for the bond being formed (going to the bicyclic intermediate) or broken (going on to the ring-expanded product). The intermediate reuses the transition-state composition, and the ring-expanded product switches again to the pi/pi* MOs of its four double bonds. Only the triene hydrogenation products drop to (6/6), the pi/pi* of three double bonds. So a consumer matching on '(8,8)' across this paper would be collapsing four different orbital sets; the constant size is what makes the relative energies comparable, not a constant space.

electronic_structure_description: The parent carborane anion and the radical formed on anodic oxidation. Its HOMO is degenerate at the C5v vertical geometry, making the neutral radical Jahn-Teller distorted. This is the species for which the CAS(3,2) approximation was validated against CAS(13,12).
Other: A minimal two-configuration space, adopted for a symmetry reason and then explicitly validated against a much larger one. The HOMO of these carborane anions is degenerate at the fivefold symmetric vertical geometry - or nearly degenerate when a methyl sits at position 1 or 12 - so on oxidation the radical ground state is Jahn-Teller unstable and a single determinant cannot describe it. The simplest valid treatment is therefore a two-configuration CAS(3,2). electronic_structure_description: Concerted and stepwise pathways for the Diels-Alder reaction of butadiene with ethene. Both a transition structure and a biradical intermediate were located for the stepwise pathway, in contrast to earlier CAS/4-31G work by Bernardi and co-workers which found neither. Other: The active space is not chosen by hand here but by an explicit published rule - the Pulay criterion was used to define the active space for each system - which is worth recording because it makes the choice reproducible and system-independent. What the rule delivers scales with the reaction: six electrons in six orbitals for butadiene plus ethene, eight in eight for both the butadiene and the cyclobutadiene dimerizations, since a second diene brings its own pi system into play. ligand_set: one chloride (X = Cl), one methyl, two carbonyl and one Me-DAB (1,4-dimethyl-1,4-diaza-1,3-butadiene) chelate
geometry_source: idealized structures of the complexes as depicted in the paper's Figure 1, with a chosen axis orientation
method: state-averaged CASSCF over the six lowest roots; CASPT2 with a level-shift corrected perturbation method; TD-DFT for comparison
basis_set: relativistic effective core potentials with associated valence basis sets: Ru (16 valence electrons) (8s,7p,6d)/[6s,5p,3d]; C (4 valence electrons) (4s,4p)/[2s,2p]; O (6 valence electrons) (4s,5p)/[2s,3p]; Cl and I (7 valence electrons each) (4s,5p)/[2s,3p]; H (7s)/[2s]
relativistic_treatment: relativistic effective core potentials on all heavy atoms
active_space_orbital_description: Sixteen electrons correlated in fifteen orbitals, listed individually by the paper: 3pz(X) and 3py(X) halide orbitals; the pi(DAB)/4dxy combination; 4dxy, 4dxz and 4dx2-y2 metal orbitals; the sigma1 and sigma2 X-Ru-Me bonding orbitals with their sigma1* and sigma2* antibonding partners; and 4d'/pi*(CO) combinations, four of them.
nroots_per_mult: total energy averaged over the six lowest roots
electronic_structure_description: Near-UV-visible spectrum of the chloride complex. CASSCF/CASPT2 assigns the lowest-lying transitions, with the halogen ligand influencing the state ordering. TD-DFT transition energies to the long-range charge transfer states disagree with the CASSCF/CASPT2 assignment, while the CASSCF/CASPT2 molecular orbitals are nearly identical to their DFT counterparts.
Other: The active space is enumerated orbital by orbital and its composition is the substance of the paper's comparison. It deliberately spans four distinct ligand and metal contributions at once - the halide 3p orbitals whose energy is what changes between the chloride and iodide complexes, the metal 4d set, the sigma/sigma* pairs of the X-Ru-Me axis, and the pi*(CO) acceptor combinations - so that halide-to-ligand, metal-to-ligand and sigma-bond excitations can all compete on an equal footing. Because the halide orbitals are IN the space, changing X from Cl to I shifts the state ordering without any change to the space itself, which is precisely the effect being studied. Two scope limits the authors state plainly: spin-orbit coupling, which they estimate at a few hundred wavenumbers and describe as potentially significant for these molecules, is NOT included and is deferred to a later paper; and TD-DFT is reported to disagree with CASSCF/CASPT2 specifically on the long-range charge transfer states.
reference_short: Zalis, Ben Amor, Daniel et al., Inorg. Chem. 2004, 43, 7978
notes: One of two halide complexes compared in the same paper; one row each since the halogen is the variable under study and its 3p orbitals sit inside the shared active space. The paper does not state a formal oxidation state for ruthenium, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty. Spin-orbit coupling is explicitly excluded from this work, hence soc_included=no.

Other: The active space is fixed by one rule applied consistently across four species: it holds the pi orbitals of whichever system is being treated. The same 4-31G basis is used throughout for the same reason.

compound_name: fulvene, S1/S0 degeneracy space along the exocyclic methylene twist
point_group: C2v planar starting structures, scanned in C2 symmetry up to C2v twisted structures

method: state-averaged CASSCF over S1 and S0 with equal weights
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, corresponding to the pi orbitals of fulvene.
electronic_structure_description: The S1/S0 degeneracy space of fulvene, revisited along the exocyclic methylene twist motion. Rather than locating a single minimum-energy conical intersection, the work characterizes and scans the continuous degeneracy seam from planar C2v structures through to twisted C2v structures.
Other: Two things bound how these numbers should be used, and the authors state both. First, the target is not a point but a seam: the paper characterizes the S1/S0 degeneracy space itself with a two-step optimization onto the seam, then scans along the methylene twist coordinate, so the (6,6) pi space has to describe both states equivalently across the whole scan - which is why the orbitals are state-averaged over S1 and S0 with equal weights rather than optimized for either. Second, the authors say plainly that their calculation is not definitive because CASSCF does not take dynamical electron correlation into account. That is an unusually direct caveat about what a bare pi-space CASSCF can settle, and it should travel with the geometry of the seam reported here.

notes: Condensed to one row for fulvene; the paper scans a degeneracy seam of a single molecule rather than treating distinct compounds. Hartree-Fock, Moller-Plesset, CASSCF and DFT methods all yield a C2-symmetric concerted transition state. A stepwise diradical process studied by UBLYP/6-31G* gives barriers of 30.1 and 13.0 kcal/mol. The barrier to pi-bond rotation in cis-cyclohexene is also predicted.
Other: The CASSCF here is one voice in a deliberate method chorus rather than the paper's primary tool, and that is its value: Hartree-Fock, Moller-Plesset, CASSCF(6,6) and several DFT functionals were all applied to the same transition state and every one of them returned a C2-symmetric concerted structure. Agreement across single-reference and multireference descriptions is the evidence the paper rests on, since a concerted-versus-stepwise question is exactly where methods usually diverge. Note the space is paired with a small 3-21G basis while the comparison methods use 6-31G*, so the CASSCF entry in the comparison table is not basis-matched to its neighbours - a caveat when reading the tabulated energies against each other. A two-configuration TCSCF is also used, and the stepwise diradical channel is handled by UBLYP rather than by enlarging the active space.
reference_short: J. Org. Chem. 2000, 65, 7134 (conformational selectivity in the Diels-Alder cycloaddition of s-trans-1,3-butadiene)
notes: Condensed to one row for the s-trans-butadiene cycloaddition system; the paper compares many methods on the same reaction rather than treating distinct compounds with distinct spaces. The (6,6) size is stated but its orbital composition is never enumerated, so active_space_orbital_description records that rather than assuming a pi assignment.

geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations with GAUSSIAN 94; CASPT2F single points at those geometries with MOLCAS; concerted surfaces also studied at HF/6-31G* and MP2/6-31G*
method: CASSCF for geometries; CASPT2F single points, described by the paper as the multiconfigurational equivalent of MP2; HF, MP2, MP3 and MP4 for comparison
software: GAUSSIAN 92 and GAUSSIAN 94 for the CASSCF work; MOLCAS for the CASPT2F single points
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals for the geometry optimizations: the two pi and two pi* molecular orbitals of the 2-azabutadiene together with the pi and pi* of the formaldehyde. For the CASPT2F single points this is enlarged to a valence space of ten electrons in ten orbitals by adding the two oxygen lone pairs with a corresponding pair of virtual orbitals.
active_space_protocol: (6,6) pi space of both reactants for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; enlarged to (10,10) for the CASPT2F single points by adding the two oxygen lone pairs and two corresponding virtuals, which the paper states was necessary for better correlation of the oxygen lone pairs
electronic_structure_description: Concerted potential energy surfaces for the thermal and Lewis acid catalyzed hetero-Diels-Alder reaction of 2-azabutadiene with formaldehyde. The Lewis acid catalyzed reaction with acetaldehyde was also studied at the HF/6-31G* level.
Other: The space is enlarged between steps for a specific, stated physical reason rather than for general convergence: the (6,6) pi space of the two reactants suffices to optimize geometries, but the CASPT2F single points use (10,10), adding the two oxygen lone pairs and two corresponding virtuals because that enlargement was necessary for better correlation of the oxygen lone pairs. This is a clean example of the geometry-adequate space and the energy-adequate space differing by a known chemical ingredient - the heteroatom lone pairs that a pure pi space omits. A consumer reading only the (6,6) would be taking the geometry space; the reported energetics rest on the larger one.
reference_short: J. Org. Chem. 1996 (Diels-Alder reactions of 2-azabutadienes with aldehydes)

geometry_source: conical intersection and intersystem crossing points between excited states computed at the CASSCF(6,5)/6-31G(d) level; solvent treated by a self-consistent reaction field with the polarized continuum overlapping spheres model (PCM)

electronic_structure_description: Excited state proton transfer dynamics of thioacetamide in the S2 (pi pi*) state. One intense UV absorption band is observed near 266 nm with oscillator strength 0.2255 in acetonitrile. Conical intersections and intersystem crossing points between excited states are located to explain the decay mechanism, with the role of dark excited states in the dynamics initiated from the light-absorbing state examined.
Other: CAUTION - THE SOURCE IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ABOUT THIS SPACE. Two consecutive sentences in the Computational section disagree: 'Seven active orbitals were used for the CASSCF calculations' is immediately followed by 'An active space with 6 electrons in 5 orbitals is referred to as CASSCF(6,5) hereafter'. The recorded (6,5) follows the explicit definition tied to the CASSCF(6,5) label the paper uses throughout, but the seven-orbital statement is not reconcilable with it and no orbital list is given to adjudicate. Anyone relying on this space should check the source directly. compound_name: 2H-benzopyrane open form (merocyanine), photochemical ring closure to spiropyran
geometry_source: full CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G(d) geometry optimizations without symmetry constraint; numerical frequency calculations to classify stationary points; intrinsic reaction coordinates computed to link the critical structures including conical intersections
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF(12,11) reference, using an average reference
software: Gaussian for the CASSCF calculations; MOLCAS 6.0 for the CASPT2
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF and for one set of CASPT2 single points; also cc-pVDZ, given as [9s4p1d/3s2p1d] for carbon and oxygen and [4s1p/2s1p] for hydrogen, for the more flexible CASPT2 single points
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals: the pi and pi* orbitals of the ethylene and carbonyl fragments together with the non-bonding pair of the oxygen atom of the carbonyl group.
electronic_structure_description: Ground state and lower singlet excited states of the open form of 2H-benzopyrane, supporting a proposed mechanism for the thermal and photochemical bleaching of merocyanine to spiropyran through an extended conical intersection seam. Merocyanine has eight stereoisomers; the cis conformation is the precursor for ring closure.
Other: The space pairs a pi manifold with a specific lone pair, and the reason is the reaction: ring closure forms a C-O bond, so the oxygen non-bonding pair of the carbonyl must be active alongside the ethylene and carbonyl pi/pi* orbitals. A pure pi space would describe the chromophore but not the bond being made. Note the deliberate separation of concerns in the basis: geometries and one CASPT2 set at 6-31G(d), with a second CASPT2 set at the more flexible cc-pVDZ, so basis sensitivity of the relative excited-state energies can be checked at fixed active space and fixed geometry. The target is an extended conical intersection seam rather than a single crossing point, which is why IRCs were run to connect the critical structures.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2006 (photochemical merocyanine-to-spiropyran ring closure through an extended conical intersection seam)
notes: Condensed to one row for the 2H-benzopyrane open form; the paper maps a reaction pathway of a single chromophore rather than distinct compounds. Active space stated with full orbital composition.

point_group: unconstrained optimizations plus a separate set under Cs symmetry constraints
geometry_source: geometry optimizations at SA-3-CAS(12,11)/6-31G(d,p) using a state average over the three lowest singlet states equally weighted, subsequently relaxing the appropriate root; Cs-constrained optimizations at SA-3-CAS(12,12)/6-31G(+)(d,p); preliminary single-state CAS(12,11)/6-31G(d) frequencies with GAMESS
method: state-averaged CASSCF; multistate CASPT2 single points on SA-5-CAS reference wave functions, with an imaginary level shift of 0.2 au to prevent intruder state effects
software: MOLCAS-6.2 for the main computations; GAMESS for preliminary single-state CAS and frequencies; MOLPRO for additional calculations
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for geometry optimizations; for the second-order correlated calculations both 6-31++G(d,p) and 6-31G(d,p) augmented with diffuse s and p functions (exponents 0.015 and 0.024) derived by Leutwyler and co-workers, denoted 6-31(+)G(d,p); the diffuse functions were placed on the N atom bearing the transferring H for minima, and on the moving H atom itself for transition states
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven active orbitals for the geometry work: the 6 valence pi orbitals and the 5 valence pi* orbitals of the 7-hydroxyquinoline ring. For the SA-5-CAS and MS-5-CASPT2 calculations the space instead comprises the 11 pi orbitals plus a sigma* Rydberg orbital, giving (12,12).
active_space_protocol: SA-3-CAS(12,11) over the 7HQ ring valence pi and pi* orbitals for unconstrained geometry optimization; SA-5-CAS(12,12) adding a sigma* Rydberg orbital as the reference for the MS-CASPT2 energies; SA-3-CAS(12,12)/6-31G(+)(d,p) for the Cs-constrained optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Hydrogen transfer versus proton transfer in the 7-hydroxyquinoline-(NH3)3 cluster. The 1(pi pi*) and 1(pi sigma*) states are followed along the transfer coordinate, their energies at the CASSCF stationary points refined by multistate CASPT2.
Other: The space CHANGES between the geometry step and the energy step for a state-specific reason: geometries use (12,11), the pure valence pi and pi* manifold of the 7HQ ring, but the CASPT2 references use (12,12), swapping in a sigma* Rydberg orbital. That extra orbital is what makes the 1(pi sigma*) state describable at all - it is the orbital the transferring hydrogen's electron enters - so a pi-only space can locate the geometries but cannot rank the two competing transfer mechanisms. The basis is placed with matching care: diffuse s and p functions are positioned on the N atom bearing the transferring hydrogen for minima, and on the moving hydrogen itself for transition states, since a Rydberg-like sigma* needs diffuse density exactly where the charge is going. The number of averaged states also changes with purpose, three for geometries and five for the CASPT2 references. An imaginary level shift of 0.2 au was applied throughout against intruder states.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2007 (hydrogen transfer versus proton transfer in 7-hydroxyquinoline-(NH3)3, a CASSCF/CASPT2 study)
notes: system_class=cluster-model: this is a hydrogen-bonded solute-solvent cluster of 7-hydroxyquinoline with three ammonia molecules, not an isolated molecule. Both active spaces are stated with their composition; active_space_nel/norb record the (12,11) used for geometry optimization, with the (12,12) CASPT2 reference space in active_space_protocol.

point_group: calculations performed under C2v symmetry restrictions, but the CASSCF wave functions display axial angular momentum symmetry with |Lambda| = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (sigma, pi, delta, phi, gamma)
geometry_source: potential energy curves across the internuclear coordinate; preliminary CASSCF calculations used to select the states examined
method: CASSCF; MRCI as CASSCF + single + double replacements, with internal contraction (icMRCI) to keep the computations tractable
software: not named in the extracted text
basis_set: ANO 21s16p9d6f4g for titanium; correlation-consistent cc-pVTZ contracted to 4s3p2d1f for boron, giving 96 spherical Gaussian functions in total with 5d and 7f components
active_space_orbital_description: A reference CAS space of ten orbital functions, six corresponding asymptotically to the valence-occupied space of Ti+ (4s + 3d) and the remainder to the valence space of the B atom (2s + 2p), with six electrons distributed among them. The resulting number of configuration functions ranges from about 600 to 1700 depending on the symmetry of the state.
multiplicities_studied: states spanning sigma, pi, delta, phi and gamma axial symmetries
electronic_structure_description: Bonding in the ground and low-lying states of the titanium boride cation, with potential energy curves computed across |Lambda| = 0 to 4. Valence correlation energy is extracted by single and double excitations out of the reference CAS space.
Other: Companion study to the same group's VB+ work already in this database, and the pair is instructive: both use a ten-orbital reference built the same way - the metal cation's 4s and 3d valence space plus the boron 2s and 2p - so the orbital count is identical while the electron count differs with the metal, six here for Ti+ against seven for V+. The authors note the method is essentially size consistent and size extensive precisely because the number of active electrons is small, and internal contraction (icMRCI) is used to keep the single-and-double expansion out of the reference space tractable.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 1998 (bonding investigation of the ground and low-lying states of the titanium boride cation TiB+)
notes: Condensed to one row for TiB+; the paper maps many electronic states of a single diatomic cation. point_group: C3v, with Jahn-Teller distortion of the degenerate X 2E state the object of study
geometry_source: initial molecular orbitals for the smallest CAS taken from a restricted Hartree-Fock calculation on the CH3S- anion; starting orbitals for the larger CASSCF calculations taken from the next smaller CAS, which the paper reports gave good convergence; doubly occupied orbitals were also optimized
method: state-averaged CASSCF; spin-orbit configuration interaction (SOCI); equation-of-motion coupled cluster used alongside
basis_set: triple-zeta and quadruple-zeta quality basis sets; the larger active spaces were studied only at the pVTZ level
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen electrons in eight orbitals, of symmetry 4a1 + 2e. The smallest space studied was five electrons in four orbitals with configuration (a1)2(e)3(a1)0, in which the e orbitals are interpreted as the sulfur 3p pi lone pairs and the a1 orbitals as the C-S sigma and sigma* molecular orbitals. A still larger space of thirteen electrons in eleven orbitals (5a1 + 3e) was also examined.
active_space_protocol: Three nested spaces: (5,4) with configuration (a1)2(e)3(a1)0 - S 3p pi lone pairs plus C-S sigma/sigma* - giving 20 configuration state functions; (13,8) as 4a1 + 2e, 168 CSFs, used for the SOCI calculations; (13,11) as 5a1 + 3e, 76230 CSFs. The two larger spaces were run only with the pVTZ basis.
electronic_structure_description: Jahn-Teller effect versus spin-orbit coupling in the X 2E state of the methylthio radical. The (13,8) space was carried into spin-orbit CI, generating as many as 13940178 single and double configurations by promoting one or two electrons from the active orbitals to all virtuals. Vibrational frequencies including nu3(A1) = 740 +/- 4 cm-1 are reported and compared with experiment.
Other: A nested sequence of three spaces where each one bootstraps the next: orbitals for the smallest (5,4) came from a restricted Hartree-Fock calculation on the CLOSED-SHELL ANION rather than the open-shell radical itself, and the starting orbitals for each larger space were taken from the converged smaller one, which the authors credit with good convergence of the CAS optimization. That cascade is the practical detail a reproducer needs, since converging a CASSCF on a Jahn-Teller degenerate state directly is the hard part. Note the cost gradient made explicit by the CSF counts - 20, 168 and 76230 for the (5,4), (13,8) and (13,11) spaces - and that only the smallest was affordable beyond pVTZ, so basis and space could not both be pushed. The (13,8) is the one carried into the spin-orbit CI, which then generates nearly 14 million single and double configurations, so the active space is the reference for a far larger correlation treatment rather than the final word itself.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2004 (Jahn-Teller effect versus spin-orbit coupling in X 2E CH3S)
notes: Condensed to one row for the methylthio radical; the paper treats one species across a Jahn-Teller distorted state manifold. All three nested spaces are stated with their symmetry decomposition and CSF counts; active_space_nel/norb record the (13,8) space used for the SOCI calculations, with the others in active_space_protocol.

compound_name: one-electron reduced methylcobalamin, base-on model (MeCbl(II) with axial imidazole)
ligand_set: complete corrin ring with all side chains replaced by hydrogens, a methyl group on cobalt, and imidazole as the axial base
geometry_source: CASSCF(9,7) geometry optimization with NWChem on a truncated model - complete corrin ring with side chains replaced by hydrogens - compared against HF and B3LYP optimized geometries
method: CASSCF (MCSCF) geometry optimization; HF and B3LYP for comparison
software: NWChem for the MCSCF geometry optimization; Gaussian 03 for part of the work
basis_set: 6-31G** for the cobalt atom and 6-31G for all other atoms; LANL2DZ used elsewhere in the study
active_space_orbital_description: Nine electrons in seven orbitals, written by the paper as CAS(9,7). The individual orbitals are not enumerated, but the analysis centres on state mixing involving the C-Co sigma* molecular orbital.
electronic_structure_description: Base-on model of the one-electron reduced methylcobalamin, with imidazole as the axial base. CASSCF gives an equilibrium Co-C bond distance of 2.164 angstroms against 1.969 from DFT, and an axial Co-N distance of 2.344 angstroms against 2.121 from DFT. Strong state mixing transfers about 0.3 electrons into the C-Co sigma* molecular orbital, and a pseudo-Jahn-Teller effect is considered possible in the reduced MeCbl(II) species relative to MeCbl(III).
Other: A case where the active space changes the GEOMETRY substantially, not just the energy - which is unusual and is the paper's central result. Going from DFT to CASSCF(9,7) lengthens the Co-C bond from 1.969 to 2.164 angstroms in the base-on model and from 1.938 to 2.144 in the base-off model, and stretches the axial Co-N bond from 2.121 to 2.344 angstroms; the remaining corrin ring distances are essentially unchanged between methods. The paper attributes the roughly 0.2 angstrom C-Co lengthening to strong state mixing that transfers about 0.3 electrons into the C-Co sigma* orbital, consistent with a pseudo-Jahn-Teller effect in the reduced Co(II) species. So the multireference character here is localized on exactly one bond, and a single-reference geometry is wrong by a chemically large margin on that coordinate while being fine elsewhere. The model is truncated in the usual way - full corrin ring with side chains replaced by hydrogens, imidazole standing in for the axial base - so the space describes the metal-corrin core rather than the intact cofactor.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. B 2006 (carbon-cobalt bond distance and cleavage in one-electron reduced methylcobalamin)
notes: One of two truncated models of one-electron reduced methylcobalamin differing in whether the axial base is present; one row each since the Co-C distances differ. The paper does not state a formal oxidation state in Roman numerals beyond the MeCbl(II)/MeCbl(III) shorthand, and does not give a d electron count, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty rather than inferred from the reduction.

compound_name: thioamide (thiopeptide bond) photoswitch, trans to cis photoisomerization
geometry_source: geometry optimizations with GAUSSIAN 98 using single-root CASSCF where possible, confirmed by analytic frequencies; the S2 minimum located with a two-root (S1,S2) state-averaged (0.5,0.5) CASSCF and confirmed numerically; four S0 transition states located with two-root (S0,S1) state-averaged (0.5,0.5) CASSCF because of wave function instability
method: CASSCF, single-root where stable and two-root state-averaged where not; CASPT2 single points to add dynamic correlation
software: GAUSSIAN 98 for the geometry optimizations; MOLCAS-5 for the CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the full N-C-S pi system (4 electrons in 3 pi orbitals), the sulfur p lone pair (2 electrons in 1 orbital), and the C-N and C-S bonds (4 electrons in 4 sigma orbitals).
electronic_structure_description: Trans to cis photoisomerization of a thioamide, proposed as a fast photoswitch that minimally perturbs a peptide backbone. Ground and excited state stationary points including an S2 minimum and four S0 transition states are located along the isomerization path.
Other: The sigma/sigma* orbitals were added to the space for a reason discovered by testing rather than assumed in advance: the authors report that test calculations showed the C-N and C-S sigma/sigma* orbitals MIX with the pi/pi* and lone pair systems once the geometry becomes highly pyramidalized. A pi-plus-lone-pair space would therefore be adequate near planarity and fail along the very coordinate the isomerization follows. Note also that the state-averaging is applied selectively rather than uniformly - single-root CASSCF wherever the wave function is stable, two-root (0.5,0.5) averaging only for the S2 minimum and for four S0 transition states where instability forced it - so different stationary points on the same surface rest on differently averaged references, which matters when comparing their relative energies.
reference_short: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2004 (a fast photoswitch for minimally perturbed peptides: trans to cis photoisomerization of a thioamide)
notes: Condensed to one row for the thioamide photoswitch; the paper follows one chromophore across an isomerization path rather than treating distinct compounds. Active space stated with a full electron-by-electron breakdown of its three components.

geometry_source: B3LYP-optimized geometries used for the CCSD(T) and CAS MP2 single points; CAS optimizations performed without restricting molecular symmetry
method: CASSCF for geometry optimization, spin-orbit coupling estimation and bound-state studies; CAS MP2 with a larger space for energies; CCSD(T) and B3LYP alongside
software: Gaussian 03 (natural population and natural bond orbital analysis; B3LYP geometries)
basis_set: 6-311G expanded with f functions for the transition metal centres; 6-31G for N, O and Ar centres; diffuse functions were deliberately NOT included in the CAS calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals, specified by symmetry label and index as (4a''-6a'')(15a'-19a') for this molecule. The orbitals are not described in chemical terms.
active_space_protocol: CAS(10,8) for the CAS optimizations, spin-orbit coupling estimation and bound-state studies, with full diagonalization of the CI matrix; enlarged to 12 electrons in 10 active orbitals for the CAS MP2 calculations, using Davidson diagonalization; spin-orbit and surface intersection calculations state-averaged over singlet and triplet with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: Intersystem crossings between triplet and singlet states of CuNO (copper mononitrosyl). Surface intersections and spin-orbit couplings are computed with state averaging over the singlet and triplet with equal weights, and bound states studied at the CAS level; charges obtained by natural population and natural bond orbital analysis to separate covalent from noncovalent effects.
Other: The active orbitals are specified by symmetry label and index rather than by chemical description, which makes the space exactly reproducible but opaque about what it contains: (4a''-6a'')(15a'-19a') for CuNO and (4a''-6a'')(14a'-18a') for CoNO. Two deliberate choices are worth carrying. Diffuse functions were excluded from the basis for the CAS calculations specifically, so the space describes valence rather than Rydberg character - a real constraint for excited states of a small metal nitrosyl. And the space is enlarged from (10,8) to (12,10) between the CASSCF stage and the CAS MP2 stage, with the diagonalization strategy changing too - full CI matrix diagonalization for the smaller space, Davidson for the larger - so the geometry and spin-orbit results and the correlated energies rest on different spaces. Spin-orbit and surface-intersection work is state-averaged over singlet and triplet with equal weights, which is what the intersystem crossing question requires.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2010 (intersystem crossings of triplet and singlet states in cobalt and copper mononitrosyls)
notes: One of two transition-metal mononitrosyls compared in the same paper; one row each since the active orbital indices differ between them. Both the CAS(10,8) and the enlarged CAS MP2 (12,10) space are recorded, the latter in active_space_protocol.

active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in four orbitals - the whole pi system corresponding to that of the parent cyclobutadiene.

The conversion proceeds via the HOMO-LUMO double electron excited 2 1A1 state; after transition from 1 1B1 to 2 1A1, the minimum-energy path at MRMP2//CASSCF leads most molecules to an ionic-like S1/S0 conical intersection that returns them to TB-CBD. Geometric parameters of the four-membered ring and Mulliken charges are tabulated across the stationary points.
Other: An explicit, reasoned compromise rather than a silent one. The authors state that twelve electrons in twelve orbitals would be PREFERABLE, to describe the six equivalent sigma bonds of the tetrahedrane accurately, but that such a space is demanding even for modern computers. They adopt CAS(4,4) - the parent cyclobutadiene pi system - and justify it with a specific scope argument: the paper does not deal with breakage of the sigma bonds that construct the original pi bonds of cyclobutadiene, so the reduced space is expected not to differ significantly for the chemistry actually being studied. geometry_source: systematic exploration of the potential energy surfaces first at the semiempirical MNDO level coupled to a full CI over 10 electrons in 10 orbitals (AMPAC 6.0, with a determinant selection scheme); stationary points then optimized at the CASSCF level, with one saddle point re-optimized using a full valence complete active space as a check

active_space_protocol: (10,10) comprising the nine C, N and O 2p orbitals plus the H 1s, used throughout; validated by re-optimizing one saddle point (labelled 20) with a full valence complete active space (FVCAS)

notes: Condensed to one row for the CH + NO reaction system; the paper explores many four-atom configurations of the same CHNO system with a single stated active space. Space composition stated explicitly, and its adequacy checked against a full valence space.

compound_name: housane (bicyclo[2.1.0]pentane) radical cation and its cyclopentane-1,3-diyl intermediate
geometry_source: stationary points optimized at CASSCF(5,6)/6-31G*, with some structures reoptimized at MP2/6-31G*; state-averaged CASSCF used for the Jahn-Teller-like region around the conical intersection
method: CASSCF, including state-averaged CASSCF for the Jahn-Teller-like surface; MP2 for selected reoptimizations
active_space_orbital_description: Five electrons in six orbitals, written by the paper as CASSCF(5,6). The individual orbitals are not enumerated in the main text.
electronic_structure_description: 1,2 rearrangement of housane radical cations. The ground-state potential energy surface is centred on a planar, symmetric cyclopentane-1,3-diyl geometry, and formation of that planar diyl intermediate is the rate-determining step of the sigmatropic-like reaction. Competing paths II and III are inactive because of larger barriers. The paper presents the system as a fully documented example of an organic molecule whose ground-state surface topology is organized around a conical intersection and its surrounding Jahn-Teller-type surface.
Other: An odd-electron space, (5,6), reflecting that this is a radical cation - so the space cannot be a simple set of filled bonding pairs and must accommodate the open shell. The substantive point is what the space is used to characterize: the ground-state potential energy surface topology here is centred on a conical intersection with a surrounding Jahn-Teller-type region, which is why state-averaged CASSCF was needed for that part of the surface rather than a state-specific treatment. A single-reference description would not merely be inaccurate near that region, it would miss the topology the paper's whole reactivity model rests on. The orbital composition is not enumerated in the main text, so the space is reproducible only by size and by the reference geometries deposited in the Supporting Information.
reference_short: Zuev, Sheridan, Bernardi, Olivucci, Robb et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1999 (1,2 rearrangement of housane radical cations)
notes: Condensed to one row for the housane radical cation rearrangement; the paper maps one surface including the diyl intermediate rather than treating distinct compounds with distinct spaces. geometry_source: ground-state geometry optimized with MOLCAS 7.2 at the all-electron MP2 and B3LYP levels
method: state-averaged CASSCF with equal weights over the two lowest states; CASPT2 and multistate CASPT2 with the default IPEA zero-order Hamiltonian unless otherwise stated; quantum Monte Carlo (variational and diffusion) on CAS-based Jastrow trial wave functions; CC2 and CCSD single points
software: MOLCAS 7.2 for the all-electron CASSCF, CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 and for the MP2 and B3LYP ground-state geometries; Gaussian 03 for the full retinal model geometry; CHAMP for the quantum Monte Carlo
basis_set: atomic natural orbital ANO-L-VxZP sets using the MOLCAS contraction schemes; a D+ basis for the QMC trial wave functions
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six pi orbitals for the reference calculations. The number of active pi orbitals was systematically increased from 6 to 18 in CAS(6,m) expansions to test convergence, the electron count being held at six throughout.
active_space_protocol: CAS(6,6) as the working reference; CAS(6,m) with m increased from 6 to 18 active pi orbitals to test the sensitivity of the excitation energies and of the IPEA dependence; QMC trial wave functions built from CAS(6,6) expansions on weighted-average CASSCF natural orbitals, truncated at thresholds varied from 0.01 to 0.08
electronic_structure_description: Minimal model of the retinal chromophore, extensively studied in the literature and used here as the reference system for the QMC and CASPT2 comparisons. Planar in the ground state. Vertical excitation energies computed by SA-CASSCF, CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 alongside variational and diffusion quantum Monte Carlo.
Other: The most quantitatively useful active-space sensitivity data in this batch, because the space size and the zero-order Hamiltonian are varied against each other. With CAS(6,6) the excitation energy differs by about 0.3 eV between the standard IPEA Hamiltonian and IPEA set to zero, and that difference is independent of basis set. Enlarging the active pi space from 6 to 18 orbitals at fixed electron count reduces the IPEA sensitivity to 0.2 eV - the dependence on the zero-order Hamiltonian shrinks as the wave function improves, exactly as expected. Crucially the two settings respond to space size in opposite ways: with IPEA set to zero the vertical energies rise by 0.07-0.12 eV as m goes from 6 to 18, whereas with the standard IPEA Hamiltonian they are stable, falling only 0.02-0.04 eV. So a CAS(6,6) with the standard IPEA shift is already near-converged with respect to space size, while the same space without IPEA is not - a consumer cannot judge whether (6,6) suffices for a polyene chromophore without also knowing which zero-order Hamiltonian is in use.
reference_short: Valsson & Filippi, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2010 (photoisomerization of model retinal chromophores from quantum Monte Carlo and multiconfigurational perturbation theory)
notes: One of five retinal chromophore models of increasing size compared in the same paper; one row each since the conjugated chain length is the variable under study. All share the CAS(6,6) reference and the systematic CAS(6,m) enlargement to 18 pi orbitals. Note this is a distinct and larger model series from the graded PSB models mined from 10.1021/jp800244h and the PSB3 benchmark from 10.1021/ct3003139.

method: CASSCF; CASPT2 and multistate CASPT2; MRCI

active_space_orbital_description: 1 electrons in the 5 metal 3d orbitals - the minimal ligand-field space for this 3d1 centre. A double-shell alternative with 10 active d orbitals per metal was tested and found not to change the excitation energies significantly.
active_space_protocol: Standard space of 5 active d orbitals per transition-metal atom holding that metal's d electrons; a double-shell space of 10 active d orbitals per metal was also tested and found not to change the excitation energies significantly
multiplicities_studied: spin-allowed and spin-forbidden d-d states of the relevant multiplicity manifold
electronic_structure_description: Ligand field d-d transitions of the octahedral 3d1 complex, with an average metal-ligand bond length of 2.099 angstroms. Computed transitions correlate with experiment mostly within 0.5 eV, with consistent trends for the intensities of spin-allowed and spin-forbidden transitions. Modelled as a cluster analogue of hematite and related transition-metal oxides of interest for solar fuels.
Other: Directly tests the double-shell question and answers it in the negative for these systems. The paper compares the standard space of 5 active d orbitals per transition-metal atom against a double-shell space of 10 active d orbitals, and reports that the larger active space does NOT significantly change the excitation energies - concluding that reasonable accuracy is achievable with MR methods on transition-metal oxide clusters using MINIMAL active spaces. That is a useful counterweight to the two entries elsewhere in this database, Cr(CO)4(bpy) and oxy-myoglobin, where 4d correlating orbitals were judged necessary; the difference appears to be the chemistry rather than the metal row, since ligand-field d-d transitions in a symmetric aqua cage are less sensitive to radial correlation than metal-ligand bonding or charge-transfer states are. The paper also documents a case where the method fails despite the space being adequate: for [Fe(H2O)6]3+ ALL calculations overestimate the d-d transition energies at about 3.0 eV against roughly 1.5 eV experimentally assigned, even though the same theory correctly gives the Fe3+ atomic ion d-d transition (~4.4 eV), the t2g-eg splitting (~1.4 eV) and the LMCT energy. The authors argue their ~3 eV result should in fact be right and question the experimental assignment, raising Fe(II) and low-spin Fe(III) impurities as possible origins.

method: CASSCF for geometries; MRCI single points at the CASSCF-optimized geometries
active_space_orbital_description: A full valence active space, with the N 1s and the Ar 1s, 2s and 2p atomic orbitals kept inactive but allowed to relax during the geometry optimizations. The resulting wave functions comprise up to 32000 configuration state functions. The paper does not state explicit electron or orbital counts for this space.
multiplicities_studied: singlet and triplet states of the dicationic system
electronic_structure_description: Bond-forming reactions of the argon dication with ammonia, producing ArNH+ and ArN+. This is reported as the first experimental observation of a triatomic product ion following a chemical reaction of a rare gas dication with a neutral. ArNH+ intensity falls with increasing collision energy while ArN+ rises, indicating ArN+ forms by dissociation of ArNH+; the computed pathway to 3ArN+ + H+ + 2H supports that sequential mechanism.
Other: Multireference methods were adopted here not by preference but by diagnosis: the authors state that their single-reference wave function was not accurately describing the system, and therefore employed multireference methods in ALL of the calculations reported. The space is then specified by rule rather than by count - full valence, with only the N 1s and the Ar 1s, 2s and 2p cores held inactive though still allowed to relax during optimization. Note the subtlety in that phrasing: inactive but relaxing cores are not frozen, so the orbitals outside the active space still respond to geometry changes. Scale is given only indirectly, as wave functions of up to 32000 configuration state functions, and no explicit (nel,norb) appears anywhere in the text - so this space is reproducible from the rule but not from a pair of integers.
reference_short: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2004 (bond-forming reactions of atomic dications with neutral molecules: ArNH+ and ArN+ from Ar2+ + NH3)

active_space_protocol: CAS(6,6) - 7ag, 7bu, 5au, 5bg, 8ag, 8bu - for the CASSCF calculations and as one MR-CISD/MR-AQCC reference; CAS(4,4) - 7bu, 5au, 5bg, 8ag - as the second reference, described as containing the most important configurations, with 7ag demoted to doubly occupied and 8bu promoted to virtual

Other: Two reference spaces used side by side, and the reduction is defined by orbital moves rather than by a new selection: going from CAS(6,6) to CAS(4,4) demotes the 7ag orbital into the doubly occupied reference set and promotes 8bu into the virtual space, leaving the four orbitals that carry the most important configurations. Because both references feed the same MR-CISD and MR-AQCC treatment, the pair isolates how much the reference space alone matters at fixed correlation method - which is the point, since these are among the first full geometry optimizations at MR-CISD and MR-AQCC level using analytic gradients. The active orbitals are given by symmetry label rather than by chemical description, and are taken from earlier CASSCF work by Dupuis and co-workers, so the space is reproducible but only against that prior orbital classification. software: MOLCAS 3 for the CASSCF and CASPT2; GAUSSIAN 94 for the local-minimum calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve molecular orbitals throughout, holding twelve electrons in the C2v and C2 point groups and sixteen electrons in Cs. The active orbitals are (2-3a2, 2-9b1, 12-13b2) in C2v, (22-23a, 13-22b) in C2, and (32-33a', 1-10a'') in Cs.
active_space_protocol: Twelve orbitals throughout; twelve active electrons for C2v and C2 symmetry structures and sixteen for Cs structures. The space was designed by maximizing the weight of the CASSCF reference in the first-order CASPT2 wave function.
electronic_structure_description: Intramolecular charge transfer in DMABN, examined along minimum energy paths connecting the locally excited state to charge-transfer structures including the rehybridized-ICT (RICT) state formed by rehybridization of the cyano group. Harmonic frequencies for the S0, La and RICT states are tabulated.
Other: The active space here is chosen by an explicit optimization criterion rather than by chemical inspection: it was DESIGNED by maximizing the weight of the CASSCF reference in the first-order CASPT2 wave function. That makes the selection objective and reproducible, and it also ties the space directly to the quality of the subsequent perturbation treatment rather than to a valence argument. The consequence is a space whose electron count varies with molecular symmetry while the orbital count stays fixed: twelve electrons in twelve orbitals for the C2v and C2 point groups, but SIXTEEN electrons in the same twelve orbitals for Cs. Since the reaction coordinate passes through structures of different symmetry, different points on the same path are described by spaces of different electron count - a fact a single (nel,norb) label cannot express. The active orbitals are listed by symmetry label per point group: (2-3a2, 2-9b1, 12-13b2) in C2v, (22-23a, 13-22b) in C2, and (32-33a', 1-10a'') in Cs.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 1998 (reaction pathways for intramolecular charge transfer in dimethylaniline derivatives)
notes: One of two dimethylaniline derivatives compared in the same paper; one row each since the substituent is the variable under study. active_space_nel records the twelve-electron count applying to the C2v and C2 structures; the sixteen-electron Cs variant is recorded in active_space_protocol and Other. This is a third, independent DMABN entry in the database alongside 10.1021/ja0490572 (12e/11o SVP) and 10.1021/jp015513m (12,12 ANO-L), each with a different space and selection rationale.

geometry_source: equilibrium and transition state geometries determined with analytic energy gradients at the CASSCF/6-31G(d,p) level; frequency calculations to classify stationary points; IRC followed from each transition state toward both reactants and products
method: CASSCF; CAS-MP2 single points at the CASSCF-optimized structures; CiLC-IRC (CI / localized molecular orbital / CASSCF along the intrinsic reaction coordinate) bonding analysis
software: GAMESS; Gaussian 98 for part of the work
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for the CASSCF and CiLC-IRC; 6-31G(d,p) and 6-311+G(d,p) for the CAS-MP2 single points
active_space_orbital_description: Six active orbitals relating to the reactions, with all configurations in the active space generated. The paper does not state the number of active electrons, and does not identify the individual orbitals here.
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy surfaces for the ene reactions of propene and cyclopropene with ethylene and cyclopropene, with propene plus ethylene as the parent reaction. Concerted and stepwise pathways were located for the parent reaction and the barriers compared; reactions of cyclopropene with propene and ethylene are found to occur through their own characteristic pathways.
Other: The active space is specified only by orbital count - six active orbitals relating to the reactions - with no electron count and no orbital list given, so this row carries an empty active_space_nel. That gap is worth reading alongside the same author's metallo-ene study already in this database (10.1021/jp806506g), which uses the analogous construction for allyl-metal plus ethylene and states it fully as six electrons in six orbitals comprising the pi and pi* of both alkene fragments plus the sigma and sigma* of the reacting bond. The two papers almost certainly share that construction, but this one does not say so, and the row records what is stated rather than what is likely. Note also that the space serves double duty here: it supplies the geometries and, through CiLC-IRC, the localized-orbital basis in which the concerted-versus-stepwise character is diagnosed along the reaction coordinate.

compound_name: TT stacked DNA nucleobase dimer (thymine-thymine), radical anion
ligand_set: one-strand stack of two nucleobases in the 5'-TT-3' arrangement
geometry_source: experimental idealized atomic coordinates of the nucleobases from high-resolution X-ray and neutron studies, used to generate the stacked structures; the same neutral-stack geometries are used for the radical anion calculations for consistency with the Koopmans-based scheme
method: state-averaged CASSCF with equal weights; CASPT2 and multistate MS-CASPT2 with a real level shift of 0.3
software: Gaussian 03 for the CASSCF; MOLCAS 5.4 for the CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen electrons in twelve orbitals, built as six orbitals per nucleobase across the stacked dimer. The odd electron count reflects the radical anion character of the excess-electron system. The construction follows the strategy the authors established in earlier work on radical cations of similar stacks.
electronic_structure_description: Excess electron transfer in the thymine-thymine stack, treated as a radical anion. Ground and excited state energies, state dipole moments and the transition dipole moment between the two states are obtained from a single state-averaged calculation and refined at CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2. Electronic couplings for excess electron transfer are derived from these energy differences and dipole matrix elements. The CT and TC stacks show the largest couplings, reaching a maximal value of 0.17 eV. In the TT stack the thymines are separated by 3.38 angstroms.
Other: The space is defined by a per-fragment rule rather than a global count: six orbitals per nucleobase, giving twelve orbitals for a stacked dimer, with thirteen electrons because the system is a radical ANION - the odd electron is the excess electron whose transfer is being studied. That construction makes the space transferable across every stack combination without re-selection, which is what allows the seven dimers to be compared on identical footing, and it follows a strategy the authors had already established for radical cations of similar systems. Two supporting choices are stated. All state energies, dipole moments and transition dipole moments come from a SINGLE state-averaged calculation with equal weights, so the coupling matrix elements are internally consistent rather than assembled from separately optimized states. And a real level shift of 0.3 was applied in CASPT2, with the authors verifying it worked: the weights of the CASSCF reference in the CASPT2 functions of the ground and excited states differed by 0.001 or less in every case - a quantitative check that the level shift did not bias one state relative to the other.
reference_short: Blancafort & Voityuk, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007 (MS-CASPT2 calculation of excess electron transfer in stacked DNA nucleobases)
notes: One of seven stacked nucleobase dimers compared in the same paper; one row each since the base composition and stacking order are the variables under study. system_class=cluster-model: these are two-base stacks standing in for DNA rather than isolated molecules. All share the same (13,12) space built as six orbitals per nucleobase. Note the stacking order matters - CT and TC are distinct entries because the 5' to 3' arrangement differs.

active_space_orbital_description: Eight active electrons in eight active orbitals. The paper does not enumerate the individual orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Dissociation of disilane along the Si-Si coordinate, part of a broader kinetics study of the SiH2 + Si2H6 and SiH3 + Si2H5 reactions and related unimolecular decompositions. Rate constants are reported for channels forming Si3H8, SiH2 + Si2H6, SiH4 + SiH3SiH, H2 + Si(SiH3)2 and H2 + SiH3SiH2SiH.
Other: Multireference treatment is applied here for a structural reason rather than a general one: the fragmentation has NO intrinsic transition state, so there is no saddle point to characterize and the dissociation potential had to be computed variationally along the Si-Si coordinate instead. A barrierless bond fission passes continuously from a closed-shell molecule to two open-shell radicals, which is precisely where a single-determinant description breaks down, so CASPT2//CASSCF is used for this one coordinate while the rest of the kinetics study rests on other methods. The (8,8) covers the scan from 2.344 out to 6.5 angstroms in 0.1 angstrom steps with all other parameters relaxed, so the space must remain balanced across the whole dissociation - a stronger requirement than describing either endpoint alone. The orbital composition is not enumerated.
