notes: Condensed to one row for the barrierless Si-Si dissociation, which is the only part of this kinetics study treated with a stated active space; the remaining stationary points and rate calculations use other methods and carry no active space.

geometry_source: geometric parameters optimized at the ROHF/6-31G* level, with bond orders evaluated using HONDO
method: CASSCF for excited-state gradients; CIS and RPA used to identify which MOs the target states involve; ROHF for geometries
software: Gaussian 98; HONDO for bond order evaluation
basis_set: 6-31G*, with 6-31G(+*) noted from earlier work as adding polarization and diffuse functions
active_space_orbital_description: Three electrons in three orbitals. The paper's notation is (n,N) for n electrons in N molecular orbitals. Spaces as small as (1,3) and (3,3) were found to describe the excited-state curvature correctly; the complete space of all n and pi orbitals would be 17 electrons in 14 orbitals, which the authors describe as quasi-unrealistic for this molecule.
active_space_protocol: Spaces constructed to contain at least the MOs identified from CIS and RPA for the selected states, taken first as small as possible and then increased progressively until they span all MOs of the symmetry species involved in the transition; reported results use the smallest space whose spectrum does not differ significantly from the largest. Restricted spaces of (1,3) and (3,3) proved adequate; the full n-and-pi space would be (17,14).
electronic_structure_description: Anion radical of 4,4'-bipyridine. Resonance Raman intensities are simulated from CASSCF excited-state gradients, with results described as very satisfactory for this species. Its transient absorption spectrum resembles that of the biphenyl anion radical, which shows strong bands at 625 and 400 nm; the 550-600 and 385 nm bands of the bipyridine anion radical had been attributed to the analogous one-electron transitions.
Other: A deliberate minimal-space strategy, executed as a documented convergence protocol rather than a guess. Active spaces are built to contain at least the molecular orbitals identified from CIS and RPA calculations for the target states, taken first as small as possible to save time, then increased PROGRESSIVELY until they incorporate the whole set of MOs of the symmetry species involved in the transition. The results reported are those from the SMALLEST space giving a spectrum not significantly different from the largest - so every published number is backed by an explicit convergence check against a bigger space. The payoff is stated plainly: spaces as restricted as (1,3) and (3,3) correctly describe the excited-state curvature at the ground-state geometry, whereas a complete space containing all the n and pi orbitals would require 17 electrons in 14 orbitals and is described as quasi-unrealistic for a molecule this size. That is a concrete case of a two- or three-orbital space being sufficient for a specific property - resonance Raman intensities depend on the excited-state gradient at one geometry, not on the whole surface - and it should not be read as a claim that (1,3) describes these radicals generally.
reference_short: J. Phys. Chem. A 2002 (resonance Raman spectra simulation of the 4,4'-bipyridine anion radical and N-protonated radical)
notes: One of two 4,4'-bipyridine radical species treated in the same paper; one row each since the protonation state differs and the simulation quality differs with it. active_space_nel/norb record the (3,3) space; the smaller (1,3) and the full (17,14) reference are in active_space_protocol.

method: CASSCF for the singlet-triplet intersection surface; full-valence CASSCF and MRCI for the Ni atom and NiO electronic states; B3LYP, UB3LYP, CCSD and CCSD(T) for the reaction stationary points
software: Gaussian 98, with MOLPRO 2000 used for some calculations
basis_set: 6-311G** for the CASSCF(18,12) intersection-surface calculations; 6-311+G(3df) and 6-311+G(3df,2p) for the full-valence CASSCF/MRCI and the coupled-cluster work; 6-31G** and 6-31G* for the DFT geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Eighteen electrons in twelve orbitals for the singlet-triplet intersection surface calculations. A separate full-valence active space, whose electron and orbital counts are not stated, was used for the CASSCF and MRCI treatment of the Ni atom and NiO electronic states.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(18,12)/6-311G** for representative points on the singlet-triplet intersection surface; a separate full-valence active space, counts unstated, for CASSCF and MRCI on the Ni atom and NiO electronic states
multiplicities_studied: singlet and triplet, with the intersection between them the object of the multireference treatment
electronic_structure_description: Reaction of nickel oxide with dihydrogen to give Ni + H2O, followed on the triplet surface with singlet-triplet crossing points CI1 and CI2 located on the intersection surface. A water complex lies 3.8 kcal/mol below products and can dissociate without an exit barrier. Full-valence CASSCF and MRCI give 6.3-7.1 kcal/mol for the Ni atom singlet-triplet difference, reasonably matching experiment; the Ni 3d8 4s2 singlet lies below 1D 3d9 4s1 by 41.8 kcal/mol at B3LYP/6-31G*.
Other: Multireference treatment enters at two distinct places for two distinct reasons, and only one of them is a stated (nel,norb). Full-valence CASSCF and MRCI were used to settle the ATOMIC and diatomic reference energetics - the Ni singlet-triplet gap and the electronic states of NiO - because the near-degeneracy of the Ni 3d8 4s2 and 3d9 4s1 configurations makes single-reference comparisons unwarranted; that treatment is specified only as full valence, with no counts given, and yields 6.3-7.1 kcal/mol for the Ni singlet-triplet difference in reasonable agreement with experiment. Separately, CASSCF(18,12)/6-311G** was used to locate representative points on the SINGLET-TRIPLET INTERSECTION SURFACE, which is where the reaction changes spin and where no single-reference method can work at all. So the (18,12) recorded here describes the crossing seam specifically, while the reaction's stationary points come from UB3LYP geometries - a division of labour worth knowing before reusing the space.
reference_short: Hwang & Mebel, J. Phys. Chem. A 2002 (reaction mechanisms of NiO and NiS with H2)
notes: One of two nickel chalcogenide plus H2 reaction systems compared in the same paper; one row each since the chalcogen is the variable under study. The paper states no formal oxidation state for nickel, so metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are left empty, though the Ni atomic configurations 3d8 4s2 and 3d9 4s1 are discussed for the free atom. Note that the stated (18,12) applies to the singlet-triplet intersection surface; the full-valence space used for the Ni atom and NiO states carries no stated counts.

point_group: C2v (PD path, symmetric H-chelate); Cs (PT path, planar frame)
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G** optimized for the excited states (medium active space); MP2/6-31G** optimized for the ground state
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 single points at CASSCF/6-31G** geometries
software: GAMESS (CASSCF reaction paths); GAUSSIAN94 (analytic Hessian); MOLCAS-4 (CASPT2)
basis_set: 6-31G** for geometry optimization and Hessian; ANO-L (3s2p1d/2s1p) for the CASPT2 single points
active_space_orbital_description: "Medium" space, 10/8 (Table 1): the full set of pi orbitals (1-3b1 and 1-2a2 in C2v), the highest n lone-pair orbital (7b2), and a pair of sigma and sigma* orbitals (9a1 and 10a1) mostly localized on the O-H-O moiety. Two other spaces were also used: "small" 6/5 (pi orbitals only, 1-3b1 and 1-2a2; for the n-pi* state the n orbital is added) and "extended" 14/12 ([8-11a1, 1-3b1, 1-2a2, 6-8b2]), which adds four sigma-type orbitals to the medium space, two occupied and two virtual in the HF reference.
active_space_protocol: Active orbitals chosen from the canonical Hartree-Fock orbitals (Figure 2). The complete set of pi orbitals was included; the sigma space is deliberately incomplete, restricted to the orbitals "crucial for a qualitatively correct description of the PE profile for the PT reaction in the 1pipi* state" (the lone-pair orbital and the sigma* orbital with nodes on the OH bonds), with the totally symmetric sigma* partner added for completeness. Full-valence CASSCF is stated to be impossible for this molecule. The medium active space is used throughout unless specified otherwise; oscillator strengths combine CASSCF (extended space) transition dipole moments with CASPT2 energies.
electronic_structure_description: S0 ground state; S1 = 1npi* (B1 in C2v, dominated by the b2(n)a2(pi*) configuration); S2 = 1pipi* (B2, dominated by b1(pi)a2(pi*)). Vertical excitation energies at the MP2/6-31G** geometry: S1 (npi*) 3.83 eV, S2 (pipi*) 4.51 eV, with oscillator strengths 1e-4 and 0.244 respectively. The 0-0 line of the S1 (npi*) transition is predicted at about 3.38 eV and its band maximum at about 2.72 eV. Low-lying 1pisigma* and 1nsigma* states are identified which intersect the 1npi* and 1pipi* states; a low-lying conical intersection of S1 and S0 accounts for efficient internal conversion. The 1pipi* state has a barrierless hydrogen-transfer profile; the 1npi* state has a significant PT barrier.
Other: The paper's central active-space test (Figures 3, 4 and 8): with the SMALL (6/5, pi-only) space CASSCF predicts a spurious barrier for hydrogen transfer in the 1pipi* state, and the CASPT2 correction on that reference restores the single symmetric minimum but overestimates the stabilization of the C2v structure, giving too steep a rise along R-. With the MEDIUM (10/8) and EXTENDED (14/12) spaces the CASSCF and CASPT2 profiles converge successively toward each other, so the medium space already gives a qualitatively correct 1pipi* profile at the CASSCF level. Further extension of the sigma active space "does not noticeably change the results but significantly increases the cost". The added sigma orbitals contribute almost nothing to the CASSCF energy in their Hartree-Fock form but relax and localize onto the O-H-O moiety, a consequence of the incompleteness of the sigma active space; the pi orbitals do not localize because the complete pi set is included. For the 1npi* state, correlation beyond CASSCF noticeably reduces the PT barrier for all three active spaces.
reference_short: Sobolewski & Domcke, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 4494
notes: Photophysics of malonaldehyde: hydrogen transfer (R- = (R_O1H - R_O2H)/2) and hydrogen detachment (R+ = (R_O1H + R_O2H)/2) coordinates studied by coordinate-driven minimum-energy paths. Cs symmetry imposed on the PT path, C2v on the PD path. Analytic Hessians at the stationary points give harmonic frequencies for malonaldehyde-d0 and -d1 (Table 2); the C2v 1pipi* structure has one imaginary frequency (first-order saddle point) while the Cs S0 and S1 (npi*) structures are true minima. CASSCF and CASPT2 total energies, dipole moments and CASSCF reference weights are tabulated in Table 3. Nel/Norb for all three spaces are stated explicitly in Table 1 together with the orbital labels in C2v, C2 and Cs.

geometry_source: CASSCF(12e/11o)/6-31G* optimized; S1 minimum-energy path (MEP) computed at the same level
method: CASPT2//CASSCF (state-averaged CASSCF geometries and MEP, CASPT2 single points)
active_space_orbital_description: 12 electrons in 11 orbitals: the benzene pi/pi* orbitals, the oxygen atom lone pair (n) perpendicular to the average plane defined by the annular molecular skeleton, the C=C double bond pi/pi* orbitals, and the C-O bond sigma/sigma* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The same 12e/11o space is used for the CASSCF S1 MEP, for the ground- and excited-state equilibrium geometries and numerical frequencies, and as the zeroth-order wave function for the CASPT2 single points. The CASPT2 single points along selected MEP points use a three-root (S2, S1, S0) state-average CASSCF reference with equal weights (0.33, 0.33, 0.33).
nroots_per_mult: 3 (S0, S1, S2 state-averaged for the CASPT2 reference)
electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 (closed shell); S1 is a pi-pi* state at the Franck-Condon geometry and at the excited-state minimum M, changing to n-pi* along the M -> CI segment; S2 is a second excited singlet. CASPT2//CASSCF vertical excitation energies: S1 96.53 kcal/mol (296 nm computed, 314 nm experimental band maximum in n-hexane) with oscillator strength 0.015; S2 138.87 kcal/mol (206 nm computed, 267 nm experimental) with oscillator strength 0.004. The excited-state minimum M lies 5.5 kcal/mol below FC; the S1/S0 conical intersection CI, characterised by crossing of the S1 n-pi* and S0 surfaces, lies 43 kcal/mol below FC and provides a fully efficient radiationless decay channel. An S2/S1 avoided crossing exists along the S1 ring-opening coordinate.
Other: The S1 ring-opening path is barrierless at CASPT2 but NOT at CASSCF: the transition-state point TS along the coordinate "is defined by the top of the barrier located along the corresponding CASSCF profile", and on the CASPT2 profile "there is only limited change in energy from M up to the transition-state point TS" — i.e. dynamic correlation on top of the 12e/11o reference flattens a CASSCF barrier into a plateau, turning the mechanism from activated into (nearly) barrierless. The space itself was built to span the whole reaction: benzene pi/pi* alone would not do, because the C-O sigma/sigma* pair is required for the bond-breaking mode and the perpendicular oxygen lone pair is required for the S1 character change from pi-pi* at the excited-state minimum M to n-pi* at the S1/S0 conical intersection. Including both is what allows a single space to describe FC, M, TS and CI on one footing.
reference_short: Migani et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 8684
notes: Photochemical ring-opening of chromenes, whose quantum yield depends on which vibronic level is excited. The C9-O1-C2-C3 dihedral changes from 40.6 deg to 32.8 deg on FC -> M. Absolute CASSCF and absolute/relative CASPT2 energies are tabulated in Table 1. Vibronic intensities were simulated from S0 and S1 equilibrium structures and the S1 force field (numerical frequencies at CASSCF(12e/11o)/6-31G*).

Computed vertical excitation energies 298 nm (S0 -> S1) and 202 nm (S0 -> S2), against experimental transition maxima of 311 and 266 nm in 3-methylpentane; the S0 -> S1 oscillator strength is 0.019. The S1 energy profile along the ring-opening MEP (Figure 2) shows the same barrierless-or-nearly-barrierless descent to an S1/S0 conical intersection as for C.
Other: The S1 ring-opening path is barrierless at CASPT2 but NOT at CASSCF: the transition-state point TS along the coordinate "is defined by the top of the barrier located along the corresponding CASSCF profile", and on the CASPT2 profile "there is only limited change in energy from M up to the transition-state point TS" — i.e. dynamic correlation on top of the 12e/11o reference flattens a CASSCF barrier into a plateau, turning the mechanism from activated into (nearly) barrierless. The space itself was built to span the whole reaction: benzene pi/pi* alone would not do, because the C-O sigma/sigma* pair is required for the bond-breaking mode and the perpendicular oxygen lone pair is required for the S1 character change from pi-pi* at the excited-state minimum M to n-pi* at the S1/S0 conical intersection. Including both is what allows a single space to describe FC, M, TS and CI on one footing. For DEC specifically, the paper states that the presence of the two ethyl groups does not affect the pattern of the reaction coordinate obtained for C, so the same 12e/11o space transfers unchanged.
reference_short: Migani et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 8684
notes: 2,2-diethyl derivative of 2H-chromene, computed with the same CASPT2//CASSCF(12e/11o)/6-31G* protocol as C so the two can be compared directly; absolute CASSCF and CASPT2 energies for both are in Table 1. Studied in the exo-exo conformer. Vibronic-intensity simulations for DEC used a simplified model MDEC (ethyls replaced) whose vibrational frequencies deviate from those of DEC by no more than 10 cm-1; in DEC the low-frequency out-of-plane activity is spread over four modes rather than concentrated in one as in C.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 (MOLCAS-5) single points on the state-averaged CASSCF reference

compound_name: CO adsorbed on Cr2O3(0001) — Cr2O6(6-) embedded cluster model, CO a3Pi desorption intermediate
ligand_set: O2- (six oxide ions of the Cr2O6(6-) cluster) plus the adsorbed CO
point_group: C1 (general CO orientation above the surface)
geometry_source: Cr2O6(6-) cluster cut from the Cr2O3(0001) surface, embedded in a large point-charge field (+3 and -2 point charges); point charges adjacent to the cluster oxygens replaced by Al pseudopotentials. CO bond distance frozen at the experimental gas-phase equilibrium value 1.128 A; the 4D PES is scanned over CO position X, height Z and orientation (theta, phi).
method: State-averaged CASSCF; valence CI (VCI) in the same active space
software: Bochum suite of ab initio programs
basis_set: Wachters (14s 9p 5d) -> [9s 6p 4d] for Cr, augmented by an extra s function (zeta = 0.24877); Huzinaga (9s 5p) -> [6s 3p] for the cluster oxygens and for CO, with two d polarization functions (zeta = 1.0, 0.3) added on both C and O of CO
active_space_orbital_description: CAS 9o:8e — the six singly occupied 3d orbitals on the two chromium ions of the cluster plus the 5 sigma and the two-fold degenerate 2 pi* orbitals of CO, occupied by eight electrons. A smaller CO-only space, CAS 3o:2e (the 5 sigma and the two 2 pi* orbitals with two electrons), is defined as the minimum needed to describe the two-fold spatial degeneracy of the CO a3Pi state.
active_space_protocol: For each CO orientation (theta, phi) at a given position X and bond distance Z above the surface, a state-averaged CASSCF calculation over the two lowest 9A states was performed to optimize the orbitals; those orbitals were then used for valence CI (VCI 9o:8e) with the same active space, in which nonet and septet states were considered with antiferromagnetic coupling allowed only for the two unpaired electrons of CO. The antiferromagnetic coupling between the two Cr ions is neglected (a0 = 4.954 A), so the Cr2O6(6-) cluster is treated as a single-reference open-shell high-spin septet and its six unpaired 3d electrons are kept with parallel spins. Interaction energies are corrected for BSSE by the Boys-Bernardi counterpoise scheme.
multiplicities_studied: nonet (2 lowest 9A states, state-averaged); septet also treated in the VCI
nroots_per_mult: 2 (nonet)
electronic_structure_description: Each Cr3+ ion has three unpaired 3d electrons; in an octahedral field the lowest term is the spatially non-degenerate 4A2g (t2g3 eg0), and at the surface the ground state of each Cr ion remains a quartet. Neglecting the weak antiferromagnetic coupling, the Cr2O6(6-) cluster ground state is a high-spin septet. The desorption intermediate is the CO a3Pi state, generated by 5 sigma -> 2 pi* excitation from the CO ...3sigma2 4sigma2 1pi4 5sigma2 ground configuration; gas-phase excitation energies are 6.0 eV (a3Pi) and 8.1 eV (A1Pi). Coupled to the septet cluster this gives the two lowest nonet states, corresponding to the doubly degenerate 3Pi state of CO interacting with the cluster. The gas-phase degeneracy of a3Pi is lifted at the surface: the splitting is 12.7 kJ/mol in the Franck-Condon region and 28.8 kJ/mol at the excited-state PES minimum (state-averaged CASSCF values). VCI shows the PES topologies of the a3Pi- and A1Pi-like states are essentially identical.
Other: The paper is explicit that the active space cannot stop at CO: describing the two-fold spatial degeneracy of the a3Pi state needs at least CAS 3o:2e (5 sigma + the two 2 pi*), because a single-determinant approach cannot represent it — but the six singly occupied Cr 3d orbitals must be added as well, giving CAS 9o:8e, in order to couple the CO excitation to the open-shell cluster and reach the nonet states. The paper also quantifies the cost of state-averaging over that space rather than optimizing a single component: the a3Pi splitting is 12.7 kJ/mol state-averaged vs 20.7 kJ/mol from separate SCF optimizations in the Franck-Condon region, and 28.8 vs 33.7 kJ/mol at the PES minimum, i.e. an error of ~8 kJ/mol falling to ~5 kJ/mol near the minimum. State-averaging was chosen deliberately anyway, to keep a uniform treatment of the whole 4D coordinate space (avoiding steps or kinks in the PES) and to avoid the SCF convergence problems seen where the a3Pi splitting is small.
reference_short: Pykavy, Thiel & Kluner, J. Phys. Chem. B 2002, 106, 12556
notes: Four-dimensional PES (X, Z, theta, phi) for an intermediate excited state in the laser-induced (DIET) desorption of CO from Cr2O3(0001), computed for wave-packet dynamics. Carbon-down adsorption is more favourable because the 5 sigma lone pair holds only one electron in the excited state, reducing Pauli repulsion. The change of symmetry of the CO quadrupole moment on excitation is identified as responsible for the PES topology. The CO internal stretch is frozen; the paper notes the CO bond length changes by only 0.06 A on 5 sigma -> 2 pi* excitation in the gas phase. Active space sizes are given in the paper's own o:e notation (CAS 3o:2e, CAS 9o:8e, VCI 9o:8e), which is orbitals-first — transcribed here as 8 electrons in 9 orbitals.
correlation_correction: Valence CI (VCI) in the same 9o:8e active space, on state-averaged CASSCF orbitals

geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G(d) optimized separately for the triplet and the two lowest singlet states
method: CASSCF; CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF optimized geometries
active_space_orbital_description: (14/14): the bonding and nonbonding pi MOs of the diradical together with the same number of antibonding pi* MOs as there are bonding pi MOs.
active_space_protocol: Full pi-valence prescription: the electrons in the bonding and nonbonding pi MOs are correlated using all possible configurations formed by exciting electrons into the same number of antibonding pi* MOs as there are bonding pi MOs. Geometries of the triplet and the two lowest singlet states were each optimized separately at CASSCF/6-31G(d); single-point CASPT2 was then run at those geometries with the same space. The CASPT2 calculations use IPEA shift = 0.25 in MOLCAS.
electronic_structure_description: Non-Kekule alternant hydrocarbon diradical. Ground state 3B2 (triplet). Relative energies in kcal/mol: CASSCF 1A1 19.8, 1B2 13.8, 1B1 14.8; CASPT2 1A1 18.9, 1B2 11.8, 1B1 14.4. The 1B1 state has a methylene group twisted out of conjugation with the rest of the pi system. The a2 and b1 nonbonding MOs of the 1B2 state are more localized in different regions of space than the corresponding NBMOs of the 3B2 state; because the pi MOs of the singlet states differ from the triplet and from each other, the C-C bond lengths in the 3B2, 1A1 and 1B2 states are all different (Figure 1).
Other: The CASPT2 correction on top of the full-pi space is modest but state-selective, so the space alone does not fix the ordering: relative to the 3B2 ground state, CASSCF -> CASPT2 moves the 1A1/1B2/1B1 states of 2 from 19.8/13.8/14.8 to 18.9/11.8/14.4 kcal/mol and those of 4 from 19.8/20.2/14.6 to 19.3/19.9/14.9 kcal/mol — the 1B2 state of 2 is stabilized by 2.0 kcal/mol while the 1B1 state of 4 is destabilized by 0.3, i.e. dynamic correlation changes the singlet-singlet gaps by up to ~2 kcal/mol without changing which state is lowest. The paper also flags an explicit CASPT2-parameter sensitivity in ref 11k: its CASPT2 numbers for trimethylenemethane differ from the earlier tabulation in ref 11j purely because the earlier values used IPEA shift = 0.0 in MOLCAS while these use IPEA shift = 0.25 — a warning that CASPT2 diradical splittings from this group are not comparable across papers unless the IPEA shift matches. A related (6/6)CASSCF/6-31G(d) check on 2,4-dimethylenecyclobutane-1,3-diyl (6, ref 25b,c) shows a much larger correlation effect in the same family: 19.8 and 27.1 kcal/mol at CASSCF fall to 18.0 and 18.6 kcal/mol at CASPT2.
reference_short: Dong, Hrovat, Quast & Borden, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 895
notes: Diradical 2 can be viewed either as trimethylenemethane (3) fused to carbons C1 and C8 of a naphtho substituent, or as 1,8-naphthoquinodimethane (4) bridged by vinylidene; the paper's point is how these ferromagnetic coupling groups modulate the three lowest state energies. The most dramatic effect is a 30.4 kcal/mol change in the relative energies of the 1A1 and 1B2 states on adding the vinylidene bridge to 4 to give 2. It is a hydrocarbon analogue of the triaza diradical 1, whose trialkyl derivative was generated and characterized by EPR. Table 1 also lists (4/4)CASSCF and CASPT2 numbers for trimethylenemethane (3), but those are taken from ref 11k rather than computed here, so no row is entered for 3.

geometry_source: CAS(14,11)/6-31G* fully optimized for each of the seven lowest electronic states (after preliminary CAS(10,8)/6-31G); B3LYP structures also computed for the ground and triplet states
method: CASSCF (full optimization of all seven lowest states); two-root state-averaged CASSCF for the surface intersections; B3LYP and CPMD/ADMP alongside
basis_set: 6-31G* for CAS(14,11); 6-31G for the preliminary CAS(10,8) and for the state-averaged intersection searches
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(14,11): the carbonyl C8=O11 and C12=O13 pi orbitals and the C8=O11 pi* orbital, the para-hydroxy O7 and the O11 nonbonding orbitals, and three pi and three pi* orbitals of the aromatic ring. For the T3 and S2 surfaces the C8=O11 pi* and O11 nonbonding orbitals are REPLACED by the C12=O13 antibonding and O13 nonbonding orbitals, so the (14,11) space is state-dependent. A smaller CAS(10,8) space was used for preliminary work and for the intersection searches.
active_space_protocol: Preliminary CASSCF at CAS(10,8)/6-31G, then all stationary structures re-optimized at CAS(14,11)/6-31G*. Equilibrium geometries on S0, S1, S3, T1 and T2 use the 14e/11o space as listed; T3 and S2 use the swapped variant. Surface-intersection structures were optimized with two-root state-averaged CASSCF, but only at CAS(10,8) because the state-averaged calculations were too time-consuming and memory-limited at (14,11). CSF counts are given: 1176 for CAS(10,8) and 54615 for CAS(14,11) in the singlets; 1512 and 76230 respectively in the triplets.
nroots_per_mult: 4 singlet (S0-S3) and 3 triplet (T1-T3) optimized individually; 2-root state-averaging at the intersections
electronic_structure_description: Seven lowest states optimized: S0, S1, S2, S3, T1, T2, T3. Relative energies at CAS(14,11)/6-31G* (kcal/mol, S0 = 0.0): T1(3npi*) 73.5, T2(3pipi*) 76.1, S1(1npi*) 77.3, T3(3npi*) 92.7, S2(1npi*) 98.4, S3(1pipi*) 107.3. In the isolated molecule the T2(3pipi*) minimum lies sandwiched between T1(3npi*) and S1(1npi*).
Other: Two active-space caveats are stated outright. (i) The (14,11) space is NOT one fixed space across states: on the T3 and S2 surfaces the C8=O11 pi* and O11 nonbonding orbitals are swapped out for the C12=O13 antibonding and O13 nonbonding orbitals, so energies for those two states rest on a different 11-orbital selection than S0/S1/S3/T1/T2 — a trap when comparing the seven relative energies of Table 1 on one scale. (ii) The surface crossings are computed at a SMALLER space than the minima: two-root state-averaged CASSCF at (14,11) was unaffordable (memory and time), so the crossing seams were located at CAS(10,8)/6-31G, and the quoted barrier of about 5.15 kcal/mol from the S1(1npi*) minimum to the T1/T2 (S1/T2) intersection is a (10,8) number placed against (14,11) minima. The size gap between the two spaces is large: 1176 vs 54615 singlet CSFs, 1512 vs 76230 triplet CSFs. The preliminary (10,8) work was superseded by re-optimizing every stationary structure at (14,11).
reference_short: Chen, Ma, Kwok, Guan, Du & Phillips, J. Phys. Chem. B 2007, 111, 11832
notes: p-Hydroxyphenacyl caged phototrigger; the paper's question is how explicit hydrogen bonding to water promotes photodeprotection and the subsequent rearrangement. Only HPA and HPA-4W were treated with CASSCF; the diethyl phosphate (HPDP) and diphenyl phosphate (HPPP) analogues and their water complexes were treated with B3LYP only, so no multireference rows are entered for them. Car-Parrinello (ADMP) dynamics were run on the computed surfaces. The second numeric column of Table 1 is not unambiguously labelled in the extracted text and has not been transcribed.

point_group: C1 (the CASSCF calculations were performed WITHOUT symmetry, to avoid artificial symmetry breaking from the Abelian-only symmetry groups in Molcas 7.0)
geometry_source: B3LYP geometry optimization and vibrational frequencies in the aqueous phase with the conductor-like polarizable continuum model and UAHF radii (Gaussian 03); all structures confirmed as minima with no imaginary frequency
method: CASSCF with spin-orbit coupling by the variation-perturbation scheme (RASSI-SO), used to correct spin-free unrestricted B3LYP Gibbs energies
basis_set: Small-core effective core potentials on Pu (60 core electrons) and O (2 core electrons) with the corresponding basis sets; the most diffuse Pu functions (exponent 0.005) omitted, a d function added on oxygen, and a 5s -> [3s] basis on hydrogen. The spin-orbit calculations were done at the ECP level using the integral mapping procedure.
relativistic_treatment: Small-core relativistic effective core potentials (60 electrons in the Pu core)
active_space_orbital_description: The spin-orbit matrix consisted of all states generated by distributing one f electron in the seven f shells, i.e. a single 5f electron in the seven 5f orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A minimal f-shell space is used deliberately: the paper argues that in plutonium complexes multireference effects arise only for systems with more than one unpaired 5f electron, so with Pu(VIII) f0 and Pu(VII) f1 the multireference effect can be neglected and the CASSCF is needed only to get spin-orbit coupling right. Spin-orbit coupling is likewise neglected entirely for the closed-shell Pu(VIII) partner. The spin-orbit effect is assumed additive: the ground-state energy lowering from CASSCF/RASSI-SO is added to the spin-free unrestricted B3LYP Gibbs energies. CASSCF is run without symmetry because the spin-orbit effect is sensitive to degeneracies.
nroots_per_mult: 7 (all states from one f electron in seven f orbitals)
electronic_structure_description: Pu(VII), 5f1, one unpaired 5f electron; the ground state is a doublet and the spin-orbit manifold is the set of states from one f electron in seven 5f orbitals. The CASSCF/RASSI-SO ground-state energy lowering due to spin-orbit coupling is 58.4 kJ/mol for this species (bare ion, no ligand field). The Pu(VIII) oxidation partner is closed shell (5f0), so both spin-orbit coupling and multireference effects are neglected for it.
Other: The paper's own sensitivity test is not about enlarging the space but about what surrounds it. The same (1,7) f-shell CASSCF/RASSI-SO gives a ground-state spin-orbit lowering of 58.4, 49.6, 24.1 and 0.3 kJ/mol for the BARE PuO2(3+), PuO3(+), PuO4(-) and PuO5(3-) ions, but only 31.4, 0.3, 4.8 and 6.6 kJ/mol for the corresponding hydroxide clusters PuO2(OH)4(-), PuO3(OH)3(2-), PuO4(OH)2(3-) and PuO5(OH)(4-) — the effect "drops drastically when the ligands are included in the molecular models", by a factor of ~2 for the dioxo species and by more than two orders of magnitude for the trioxo. The reason given is that in Pu(VII) the extra electron relative to closed-shell Pu(VIII) goes mainly to the LIGAND, not the metal, so unlike the isoelectronic f1 UO2(+) case (where the electron stays on the metal and bare-ion and hydrated spin-orbit values agree) it is NOT safe to compute the spin-orbit correction on the bare ion. The active space itself is justified by an electron count, not converged: >1 unpaired 5f electron would make the system strongly multiconfigurational and the unrestricted B3LYP energies unreliable, and the whole approach rests on Pu(VII)/Pu(VIII) being f1/f0.
reference_short: Tsushima, J. Phys. Chem. B 2008, 112, 13059
notes: One of the Pu(VII) species in a study of the Pu(VII)/Pu(VIII) redox potential in alkaline solution; 2 Pu-O oxo bonds. The number of oxo bonds was varied from 2 to 5, and the redox potential (relative to the standard hydrogen electrode) drops from 4.36 to 1.06 V as it increases; the potential is insensitive to the type of coordinating ligand (carbonate vs hydroxide give essentially the same value) but sensitive to coordination number. The tetra-oxo pair PuO4(OH)2(3-)/PuO4(OH)2(2-) gives 1.54 V. Only the spin-orbit correction is CASSCF here (58.4 kJ/mol for this species); geometries, frequencies, solvation and the spin-free Gibbs energies are unrestricted B3LYP/CPCM. The coordination number and stoichiometry were assumed equal within each redox pair, which the author flags as possibly farfetched.
correlation_correction: None on top of CASSCF; dynamic correlation comes from the B3LYP spin-free Gibbs energies to which the CASSCF spin-orbit lowering is added

The CASSCF/RASSI-SO ground-state energy lowering due to spin-orbit coupling is 49.6 kJ/mol for this species (bare ion, no ligand field). The Pu(VIII) oxidation partner is closed shell (5f0), so both spin-orbit coupling and multireference effects are neglected for it.
Other: The paper's own sensitivity test is not about enlarging the space but about what surrounds it. The same (1,7) f-shell CASSCF/RASSI-SO gives a ground-state spin-orbit lowering of 58.4, 49.6, 24.1 and 0.3 kJ/mol for the BARE PuO2(3+), PuO3(+), PuO4(-) and PuO5(3-) ions, but only 31.4, 0.3, 4.8 and 6.6 kJ/mol for the corresponding hydroxide clusters PuO2(OH)4(-), PuO3(OH)3(2-), PuO4(OH)2(3-) and PuO5(OH)(4-) — the effect "drops drastically when the ligands are included in the molecular models", by a factor of ~2 for the dioxo species and by more than two orders of magnitude for the trioxo. The reason given is that in Pu(VII) the extra electron relative to closed-shell Pu(VIII) goes mainly to the LIGAND, not the metal, so unlike the isoelectronic f1 UO2(+) case (where the electron stays on the metal and bare-ion and hydrated spin-orbit values agree) it is NOT safe to compute the spin-orbit correction on the bare ion. The active space itself is justified by an electron count, not converged: >1 unpaired 5f electron would make the system strongly multiconfigurational and the unrestricted B3LYP energies unreliable, and the whole approach rests on Pu(VII)/Pu(VIII) being f1/f0.
reference_short: Tsushima, J. Phys. Chem. B 2008, 112, 13059
notes: One of the Pu(VII) species in a study of the Pu(VII)/Pu(VIII) redox potential in alkaline solution; 3 Pu-O oxo bonds. The number of oxo bonds was varied from 2 to 5, and the redox potential (relative to the standard hydrogen electrode) drops from 4.36 to 1.06 V as it increases; the potential is insensitive to the type of coordinating ligand (carbonate vs hydroxide give essentially the same value) but sensitive to coordination number. The tetra-oxo pair PuO4(OH)2(3-)/PuO4(OH)2(2-) gives 1.54 V. Only the spin-orbit correction is CASSCF here (49.6 kJ/mol for this species); geometries, frequencies, solvation and the spin-free Gibbs energies are unrestricted B3LYP/CPCM. The coordination number and stoichiometry were assumed equal within each redox pair, which the author flags as possibly farfetched.

method: Quasi-classical CASSCF surface-hopping dynamics (trajectory surface hop following Groenhof and Robb)

nroots_per_mult: 2 (S1 and S0, with surface hopping between them)
electronic_structure_description: S0 ground state and the covalent S1 state on which trajectories are initiated; the Franck-Condon energy on S1 is +173.3 kcal/mol relative to s-cis-1,3-butadiene on S0 (-153.101643 hartree at CAS(4,4)/STO-3G). Other: Both the space and the basis are minimal by necessity, and the paper argues the case explicitly rather than testing convergence. CAS(4,4)/STO-3G was chosen because 0.8 million (= 4000 x 100 x 2) CAS energies, gradients and Hessians had to be evaluated; the defence is that "the main topological features of the CAS(4,4)/STO-3G potential energy surfaces are identical to those computed at higher levels of theory" — the FC point lying tens of kcal/mol above the S1 minimum, an S1 relaxation coordinate dominated by single/double bond reversal with a twisting nonadiabatic coordinate, and an S1/S0 seam accessible over a wide range of the C-C-C-C torsion. Two known biases are acknowledged: a minimal basis pushes the dynamics toward longer excited-state lifetimes and lower conversion rates (established for a protonated Schiff base model chromophore) without changing the mechanism, and the 1(1Bu) ionic state is not properly balanced against the 2(1Ag) covalent state at this level — justified by the very short S2 lifetime and by highly correlated post-CASSCF calculations finding the two states similar in energy at the Franck-Condon geometry. Because the study tests a DIFFERENCE (deuterium substitution) computed with an identical space for both isotopologues, these absolute biases cancel; the same numbers should not be read as converged absolute lifetimes or yields.
reference_short: Montagnese, Ogliaro, Wilsey & Bearpark, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 13239
notes: Reference (undeuterated) system for an inertial-effect study. Bicyclobutane (4) is also identified as a possible product region on the surface. compound_name: p-3A: para-linked PBPB dimer, planar form, iPr on P and tBu on B

geometry_source: B3LYP/6-31G(d) optimized with frequency analysis; the planar (A) conformations of the H-substituted models were obtained by restricting the optimization to the corresponding symmetry point group, because all H-substituted models have the bis(bicyclic) form as their ground state
method: CASSCF(4,4); RAS-2SF (restricted active space double spin-flip) and coupled-cluster perfect pairing (PP) alongside
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(4,4): four electrons in the four frontier orbitals of the tetraradicaloid (the four orbitals shown in Figure 5, whose totally symmetric combination of four unpaired electrons gives the MS = 0 quintet).
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(4,4) is used to obtain the one-particle density matrix from which the effective number of unpaired electrons NU is computed, and to inspect frontier-orbital occupations and the T4 cluster-operator single amplitudes. It is compared directly against perfect pairing with two active pairs, perfect pairing with five active pairs (which additionally correlates the six benzene-ring pi electrons), perfect quadruples (PQ) and RAS-2SF. All RAS-2SF calculations use the (hole, particle) truncation with a restricted open-shell high-spin QUINTET reference to reach the MS = 0 states.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet ground state, with the S1 state built mainly from similar contributions of doubly excited closed-shell configurations relative to the Hartree-Fock-like ground determinant. The two lowest triplets T1 and T2 lie 20-25 kcal/mol above the singlet ground state. The MS = 0 quintet is the totally symmetric combination of four unpaired electrons in the four frontier orbitals. In p-3A (and p-3AH) the two lowest triplets are 3B3u and 3A1g, separated by close to 4 kcal/mol; the highest triplet corresponds to a doubly excited configuration of B3u symmetry. Computed effective number of unpaired electrons NU at CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G(d): 0.77 (against 0.75-0.77 from two-pair PP, 0.87-0.92 from five-pair PP and 0.88-0.89 from RAS-2SF for the same four molecules).
Other: This paper is itself an active-space sensitivity study of radical character. The effective unpaired-electron count NU of the planar dimers is 0.75-0.77 with perfect pairing over TWO active pairs and 0.87-0.92 with FIVE pairs — the extra ~0.15 electron appearing purely because the six pi electrons of the benzene linker are brought into the correlated space. CASSCF(4,4), whose four frontier orbitals correspond to the two PBPB pairs and nothing else, tracks the two-pair PP numbers closely (0.76-0.79), while RAS-2SF tracks the five-pair numbers (0.88-0.89). So the answer to "how tetraradicaloid is this molecule?" moves by ~15% of an electron depending on whether the linker pi system is in the space, and a (4,4) space systematically UNDERSTATES the count relative to methods that include it. The absolute values remain far below the theoretical NU limit of four unpaired electrons, which the authors give as the likely reason for these species' unusual stability. Two further cautions are stated: RAS-2SF lacks dynamical correlation and its vertical transition energies should not be taken as benchmarks, though its balanced treatment of low-lying radicaloid states makes it suitable for energy GAPS; and the para/meta and H-/alkyl-substituted variants give nearly identical NU, so substituent and topology effects on radical character are negligible compared with the active-space choice.
reference_short: Bell, Casanova & Head-Gordon, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2010, 132, 11314
notes: Fully substituted (R = iPr on phosphorus, R' = tBu on boron) para isomer. 'A' denotes the planar 1,3-diborata-2,4-diphosphoniocyclobutane-1,3-diyl form and 'B' the bicyclic 1,3-diborata-2,4-diphosphoniobicyclo[1.1.0]butane rearrangement; only the planar A forms are radicaloid and treated here. The molecular formula is not transcribed because the paper specifies the substituents only as R = iPr and R' = tBu in Figure 1 without writing a formula. Interest in these species comes from the prospect of antiferromagnetic low-spin polymers with half-filled bands and undoped metallic conduction; the parent 1,3-diborata-2,4-diphosphoniocyclobutane-1,3-diyl is a localized singlet diradical indefinitely stable at room temperature. Planar-to-bicyclic energetics for these compounds are in Table 5 and NU values in Table 6.

compound_name: p-3AH: para-linked PBPB dimer, planar form, H-substituted model
point_group: D2h-like for the para isomers (3B3u / 3A1g triplet labels); C2v-like for the meta isomers (3A1 / 3B1 triplet labels)
geometry_source: B3LYP/6-31G(d) optimized with frequency analysis; the planar (A) conformations of the H-substituted models were obtained by restricting the optimization to the corresponding symmetry point group, because all H-substituted models have the bis(bicyclic) form as their ground state
method: CASSCF(4,4); RAS-2SF (restricted active space double spin-flip) and coupled-cluster perfect pairing (PP) alongside
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(4,4): four electrons in the four frontier orbitals of the tetraradicaloid (the four orbitals shown in Figure 5, whose totally symmetric combination of four unpaired electrons gives the MS = 0 quintet).
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(4,4) is used to obtain the one-particle density matrix from which the effective number of unpaired electrons NU is computed, and to inspect frontier-orbital occupations and the T4 cluster-operator single amplitudes. It is compared directly against perfect pairing with two active pairs, perfect pairing with five active pairs (which additionally correlates the six benzene-ring pi electrons), perfect quadruples (PQ) and RAS-2SF. All RAS-2SF calculations use the (hole, particle) truncation with a restricted open-shell high-spin QUINTET reference to reach the MS = 0 states.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet ground state, with the S1 state built mainly from similar contributions of doubly excited closed-shell configurations relative to the Hartree-Fock-like ground determinant. The two lowest triplets T1 and T2 lie 20-25 kcal/mol above the singlet ground state. The MS = 0 quintet is the totally symmetric combination of four unpaired electrons in the four frontier orbitals. In p-3AH the two lowest triplets are 3B3u and 3A1g, separated by close to 4 kcal/mol. Computed effective number of unpaired electrons NU at CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G(d): 0.79 (against 0.75-0.77 from two-pair PP, 0.87-0.92 from five-pair PP and 0.88-0.89 from RAS-2SF for the same four molecules).
Other: This paper is itself an active-space sensitivity study of radical character. The effective unpaired-electron count NU of the planar dimers is 0.75-0.77 with perfect pairing over TWO active pairs and 0.87-0.92 with FIVE pairs — the extra ~0.15 electron appearing purely because the six pi electrons of the benzene linker are brought into the correlated space. CASSCF(4,4), whose four frontier orbitals correspond to the two PBPB pairs and nothing else, tracks the two-pair PP numbers closely (0.76-0.79), while RAS-2SF tracks the five-pair numbers (0.88-0.89). So the answer to "how tetraradicaloid is this molecule?" moves by ~15% of an electron depending on whether the linker pi system is in the space, and a (4,4) space systematically UNDERSTATES the count relative to methods that include it. The absolute values remain far below the theoretical NU limit of four unpaired electrons, which the authors give as the likely reason for these species' unusual stability. Two further cautions are stated: RAS-2SF lacks dynamical correlation and its vertical transition energies should not be taken as benchmarks, though its balanced treatment of low-lying radicaloid states makes it suitable for energy GAPS; and the para/meta and H-/alkyl-substituted variants give nearly identical NU, so substituent and topology effects on radical character are negligible compared with the active-space choice.

compound_name: 1,2-Dioxetane (parent), thermal decomposition on S0 and T1
point_group: C1 (gauche and anti biradical structures; C2v/Cs only at the closed ring)
geometry_source: CASSCF optimized: CAS(8,6)/6-31G* routinely, CAS(12,10)/6-31+G* for the improved surface, and GVB-CAS(12,12)/6-31G* where the (12,12) space is too large for CASSCF optimization. Crossing points located with the conical-intersection algorithm in Gaussian 94, which optimizes the lowest point on the (n-2)-dimensional intersection hyperline; state-averaged orbitals were used for both the intersection optimizations and the spin-orbit couplings.
method: CASSCF, GVB-CAS, and multireference MP2 single points (CASMP2 by the method of Peasley et al. for the (8,6) and (8,8) spaces; CASPT2 by the method of Roos for the (12,10) space)
basis_set: 6-31G* for the routine CAS(8,6) and GVB-CAS(12,12) work; 6-31+G* for CAS(12,10); cc-pVDZ for recomputed CAS(8,6) barrier heights
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,10) = the minimal (8,6) space (Chart 1) extended by the C-O sigma/sigma* orbitals (Chart 2). Related spaces used in the same paper: (8,6), the stated minimum needed to describe the topology of the surfaces; (12,12), obtained by adding a pair of 'virtual' n* orbitals to (12,10); (8,8), the (12,12) space minus the sigma/sigma* orbitals, used for MP2 single points on GVB-CAS(12,12) geometries; and (4,4), the (8,6) space without the doubly occupied oxygen orbitals, used for frequencies.
active_space_protocol: Deliberate hierarchy rather than one space. An (8,6) space is stated to be the MINIMUM needed to describe the topology of the surfaces, and its energetics can be corrected by CASMP2 single points — but CASMP2 gradients are unavailable, so improving the GEOMETRIES requires enlarging the space instead, which is why the C-O sigma/sigma* orbitals were added to give (12,10). The further (12,12) space (adding two virtual n* orbitals) is too large for CASSCF geometry optimization, so those structures were optimized with GVB-CAS keeping the four C-O sigma orbitals in the GVB space, and CAS(8,8)/MP2 energies (without the sigma/sigma*) were computed at those structures. Frequencies at every critical point used a (4,4) space at CASSCF/6-31G*, with (8,6) frequencies at four selected points (a, b, m, q) for the thermal corrections in Table 1. Spin-orbit couplings use a one-electron operator with the effective nuclear charges of Koseki et al. (C 3.6, O 5.6).
electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 and lowest triplet T1, labelled by pi-electron count: the 1(4pi) singlet biradical surface, the 3(3pi) triplet biradical surface (about 2 kcal/mol below 1(4pi)) and the 2pi singlet/triplet states. Ring-opening barrier TS1 (a gauche structure, b) has an activation energy of ca. 17.6 kcal/mol uncorrected, 16.3 kcal/mol thermally corrected, against an experimental threshold of 22 kcal/mol for unsubstituted dioxetane. A syn MAXS saddle point lies some 6 kcal/mol above TS1. The lowest 1(4pi) biradical BIRS (anti, structure j) lies 9 kcal/mol below TS1 and is unstable to C-C cleavage — its fragmentation barrier could not be fully optimized. The anti minimum on the 3(3pi) surface, BIRT (structure m), lies 5-6 kcal/mol below TS1. At the best level (CAS(12,10)/6-31+G* + MP2 + thermal correction) the triplet fragmentation transition state TS2 (structure q) lies 20.3 kcal/mol above the reactant, 16.5 kcal/mol thermally corrected, so TS1 and TS2 are both about 16.5 kcal/mol. Spin-orbit coupling is large, ca. 60 cm-1, throughout the singlet/triplet crossing region, implying facile intersystem crossing along a crossing 'line' spanning the ground-state O-O cleavage valley a few kcal/mol above it.
Other: The paper is built around the fact that a bigger active space and a perturbative correction are not interchangeable here. CASMP2 on an (8,6) reference fixes the energies but cannot fix the GEOMETRIES, because CASMP2 gradients do not exist — so dynamic correlation had to be smuggled into the optimization by enlarging the space instead, adding the C-O sigma/sigma* pair to reach (12,10). Pushing further to (12,12) with two virtual n* orbitals broke CASSCF optimization entirely and forced a GVB-CAS compromise in which the four C-O sigma orbitals sit in the GVB rather than the CAS space, with the subsequent MP2 energies then computed in a (8,8) space that DROPS the sigma/sigma* orbitals again — so the (12,12) geometries and the (8,8) energies do not share an active space. A second trap: the two multireference MP2 corrections used are not the same method — CASMP2 (Peasley et al.) for the (8,6) and (8,8) spaces and CASPT2 (Roos) for (12,10), differing mainly in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian, so numbers from different rows of Tables 1 and 2 are not strictly comparable. Frequencies rest on a much smaller (4,4) space than the energies, and near surface degeneracies made some of them unreliable (flagged in the table). Even at the best level the O-O cleavage barrier converges to ~16.5 kcal/mol against an experimental 22 kcal/mol, so the remaining error is not removed by any of these active-space extensions.
reference_short: Wilsey, Bernardi, Olivucci, Robb, Murphy & Adam, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 1669
notes: Reinvestigation of the classic dioxetane chemiluminescence mechanism. The mechanism supported by the computed surfaces is: (i) activation energy around 16.5 kcal/mol, (ii) a very unstable 1(4pi) biradical intermediate BIRS that fragments immediately, (iii) a triplet 3(3pi) biradical intermediate BIRT, and (iv) a triplet fragmentation barrier TS2 of the same magnitude as the S0 O-O cleavage barrier TS1 — much better agreement with experiment than the earlier computational work, which predicted two very different activation energies with the triplet surface 20 kcal/mol higher. Experimental context: 22 kcal/mol for unsubstituted dioxetane, with measurements on tetramethyldioxetane (TMD) and cis-diethoxy-1,2-dioxetane (DED). Absolute energies in hartrees with kcal/mol values relative to the S0 reactant are in Tables 1 and 2.
correlation_correction: Multireference MP2 single points: CASMP2 (Peasley et al.) on the (8,6) and (8,8) references, CASPT2 (Roos) on the (12,10) reference

geometry_source: All stationary points optimized at CASSCF/cc-pVTZ, with harmonic vibrational wavenumbers for the ZPVE computed subsequently at the same level
method: CASSCF/cc-pVTZ optimizations and frequencies; CASPT2/cc-pVTZ single points on the CASSCF reference, replaced by CCSD(T)/6-311G(2d,2p) wherever CASPT2 gave negative activation barriers
basis_set: cc-pVTZ, contracted to (4s3p2d1f) on first-row atoms and (3s2p1d) on hydrogen; 6-311G(2d,2p) for the CCSD(T) corrections
active_space_orbital_description: (10,9): all spin- and symmetry-allowed distributions of 10 active electrons among 9 active orbitals, spanning 5292 configuration state functions. On fragmentation the space is split so the fragments carry matching subspaces: (8,7) + (2,2) between (fluoro)carbonyl oxide and formaldehyde (or formyl fluoride), (6,5) + (4,4) between fluorooxirane and singlet oxygen (1-Delta-g), and (8,7) + (2,2) between fluorodioxirane and formaldehyde.
active_space_protocol: The (10,9) space was kept throughout the whole reaction profile so that this study is a direct sequel to the authors' earlier treatment of the initial 1,3-bipolar addition. Its adequacy is judged against the Anglada-Bofill criterion that active occupancies lie in the range 0.02-1.98: inspection of the active orbital occupancies at every stationary point showed that in no instance did the (10,9) space need extension. Consistency across the reaction path was checked by requiring an unambiguous one-to-one correspondence between the active orbitals of adjacent stationary structures. CASPT2 uses the full (non-block-diagonal) Fock matrix and freezes the 1s core shells of O, C and F, because cc-pVTZ was not designed for core-valence correlation.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet throughout. The primary ozonide formed by 1,3-bipolar addition of ozone to fluoroethene decomposes unimolecularly; on cleavage the fluorine can end up on either the aldehyde or the carbonyl oxide moiety, designated the a- and b-type configurational mechanisms, with syn or anti conformations distinguished by the position of the fluorine relative to the terminal oxygen of the carbonyl oxide. The most favourable route is a concerted cleavage to carbonyl oxide (CO) plus formyl fluoride (FF) with the fragments anti; RRKM unimolecular rate constants put this CO-FF channel at 98% of the decomposition, matching the upper bound of experimental estimates. Competing channels give fluorooxirane plus singlet oxygen (1-Delta-g) and fluorodioxirane plus formaldehyde.
Other: The active space is defended by an occupancy test, not by enlargement: the Anglada-Bofill criterion (active occupancies between 0.02 and 1.98) was applied at every stationary point and "in no instance did there arise the need for an extension of the (10,9) active space", and the same space was carried unchanged from the earlier 1,3-bipolar-addition study so the two reaction profiles join without a discontinuity. The real difficulty is fragmentation: a nine-atom parent cannot keep one space when it breaks apart, so (10,9) is SPLIT channel by channel — (8,7)+(2,2) for carbonyl oxide plus formaldehyde or formyl fluoride, (6,5)+(4,4) for fluorooxirane plus singlet O2, (8,7)+(2,2) for fluorodioxirane plus formaldehyde — with a one-to-one correspondence between the active orbitals of adjacent structures enforced by hand to keep the profile consistent. Even with a space that passes the occupancy test, the perturbative correction on top of it fails locally: "in certain cases the CASPT2 correction was found to overestimate the stabilization energies of some transition states to the extent of placing them below those of the preceding minima", i.e. producing negative activation barriers, and those points had to be recomputed with CCSD(T)/6-311G(2d,2p) instead. So the reported profile mixes two correlation treatments, and CASPT2 numbers for the affected transition states are not usable as published.
reference_short: Ljubic & Sabljic, J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 2381
notes: Tropospheric ozonolysis chemistry: ozone, OH and NO3 are the main oxidants consuming anthropogenic pollutants, so ozonolysis rates bear on pollutant persistence. A single halogen substitution greatly multiplies the decomposition pathways relative to ethene ozonolysis, because the fluorine position becomes an extra branching variable. The study builds directly on the authors' earlier account of the initial 1,3-bipolar addition of ozone to ethene, fluoroethene and chloroethene, whose barrier alone determines the comparable kinetic parameters, and uses the ethene ozonolysis mechanism of Anglada et al. as a guide. CASSCF/CASPT2 was chosen because the balance of nondynamic and dynamic correlation is critical for ozone, and the approach had been shown comparable to CCSD(T) for carbonyl-oxide unimolecular decomposition.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/cc-pVTZ, substituted by CCSD(T)/6-311G(2d,2p) where CASPT2 produced negative activation barriers

compound_name: H + FH -> HF + H transition state (FH2)
geometry_source: Geometries taken from ref 19 at the QCISD/MG3 level; reactants and products treated as supermolecules with the moieties separated by 100 A to avoid MRMP2 size-consistency issues
method: CASSCF and CASCI reference wave functions with MRMP2 and MRMP2-ISA second-order corrections (Hirao formalism)
software: In-house CASSCF/CASCI and MRMP2/MRMP2-ISA codes interfaced with Gaussian 03 (which supplied the AO integrals, HF, BLYP, B3LYP and stability calculations)
basis_set: MG3S (the MG3 basis, i.e. 6-311++G(3d2f,2df,2p) for H-Si with an extended basis for P-Ar, minus the diffuse functions on H); cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ also surveyed
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence shell orbitals of all atoms. The paper states the rule rather than per-system counts; the electron and orbital numbers here follow arithmetically from it (see notes).
active_space_protocol: A HF or KS calculation is run first, followed by a wave function stability analysis and, where necessary, reoptimization. For stable wave functions the spin-restricted orbitals (closed- or open-shell as appropriate) seed the CASSCF; where instabilities were found the spin-unrestricted natural orbitals were used instead. The SAME initial orbitals, WITHOUT further optimization, define the CASCI target state used in the MRMP2 calculations — the point of the paper being to skip the CASSCF orbital optimization entirely. Orbital sets tested: CASSCF, HF, BLYP and B3LYP, giving MRMP2(CASSCF), MRMP2(HF), MRMP2(BLYP) and MRMP2(B3LYP). Intruder-state avoidance (ISA) uses the recommended shift parameter b = 0.02.
electronic_structure_description: Doublet surface (overall spin s = 1/2). Symmetric hydrogen-transfer barrier: database reference value 42.18 kcal/mol for both forward and reverse. Computed: CASSCF 55.08 (error +12.90), MRMP2(CASSCF) 41.62 (-0.56), MRMP2-ISA(CASSCF) 41.77 (-0.41). At the CASCI reference level: CASCI(HF) 41.96 (-0.22), CASCI(B3LYP) 57.42 (+15.24), CASCI(BLYP) 56.14 (+13.96).
Other: The paper's whole subject is what happens when the orbitals defining the active space are NOT optimized. With a full-valence space, MRMP2(CASSCF) reaches a mean absolute error of 0.57 kcal/mol over the ten barriers (0.53 with ISA), but replacing the CASSCF orbitals by unoptimized HF or KS orbitals in a CASCI reference degrades this to 1.43 (HF), 1.40 (B3LYP) and 1.87 (BLYP) kcal/mol. At the reference level before the perturbative correction the orbital choice matters far more: CASCI with KS orbitals typically halves the average error and cuts the maximum error by about a factor of three relative to CASCI with HF orbitals — yet for reaction 1 the ordering reverses completely (CASCI(HF) errs by -0.22 kcal/mol against +15.24 for CASCI(B3LYP) and +13.96 for CASCI(BLYP)), so no orbital set is uniformly safe. The diagnostic case is reaction 6: comparing the CASCI CI vectors against the CASSCF one shows that in HCN the determinants describing the doubly degenerate pi -> pi* excitation are UNDERWEIGHTED by every CASCI variant, and only orbital optimization recovers them — a concrete signature of when a CASSCF step cannot be skipped. On intruder states, the ISA shift changes the barriers only slightly, which the authors read as evidence of no major intruder problems here; they note that where an intruder contribution is significant the shift will NOT fix it and one must instead expand the reference space to include the intruder state or move to a multistate method. Bare CASSCF itself is far off (MAE 8.15 kcal/mol, max 12.90) — the full valence space alone buys nothing without the dynamic correlation on top.
reference_short: Robinson & McDouall, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2007, 3, 1306
notes: One of six reactions taken from the Zhao, Gonzalez-Garcia & Truhlar Minnesota database of barrier heights for heavy-atom transfer, nucleophilic substitution, and unimolecular and association reactions; forward and reverse together give ten barriers for comparison. Reference values come from W1 theory and include relativistic, core-correlation and spin-orbit corrections, whose net effect over these reactions averages under 0.07 kcal/mol (maximum 0.43 kcal/mol, for reaction 3), so direct comparison with the computed values is legitimate. compound_name: cis-1,3-Buta-1,4-dione model, fully reduced protonated form (QH2) + triplet O2 — reaction 1
point_group: C1 (full geometry optimization with no symmetry constraints)
geometry_source: Full gradient geometry optimization with no symmetry constraints at CASSCF/6-31+G(d) (also at UHF and ROHF); BSSE estimated by the method of Chalasinski et al. using the generalized counterpoise scheme of Boys and Bernardi, which separates the distortion energies of the interacting fragments
method: CASSCF with single-point MRMP (multireference Moller-Plesset) dynamic correlation; ROHF/RMP2 and UHF/UMP2 alongside, plus AM1 and PM3 semiempirical
active_space_orbital_description: Eight orbitals. For the isolated substrates the active-space orbitals correspond to the HOMO-LUMO pair of the organic molecule together with the pi/pi* and the sigma(O-O)/sigma*(O-O) pairs of the oxygen molecule.
active_space_protocol: The active space is fixed at 8 orbitals for every system, with 10 electrons for reactions 1 and 2 and 11 for reactions 3 and 4 as printed in the methods, giving the (10,8) and (11,8) spaces. Initial orbitals come from ROHF or UHF; proper spin multiplicity was rigorously maintained in all the ab initio calculations except UHF, where multiplicity is only approximately defined. Dynamic correlation is added as single-point MRMP at the CASSCF geometries. Active-space adequacy is judged from natural-orbital occupation numbers: on electron transfer only the donor frontier orbital (2.0 -> 1.0, or 1.0 -> 0.0) and one O2 pi*(2p) orbital (1.0 -> 2.0) change, while the occupations of the remaining active orbitals do not vary remarkably.
electronic_structure_description: Reaction 1: electron transfer from QH2 to 3O2. Energies at 6-31+G(d) (BSSE-corrected in parentheses): CASSCF +28.8 (+30.1), MRMP +1.5 (+4.7) kcal/mol; at 6-31G(d): CASSCF +31.1 (+32.6), MRMP +2.2 (+5.9). Endoenergetic at every level of theory, matching the experimentally observed diminished reductive properties of hydroquinone derivatives at low pH. Thermodynamics from the MRMP energies at 6-31+G(d): Delta-H +3.5 (+6.7), Delta-G +2.0 (+5.2) kcal/mol.
Other: Two things to know before reusing these numbers. First, the sensitivity: the reaction energies are NOT converged without dynamic correlation on top of the (10,8)/(11,8) reference, and the correction is enormous and sign-changing. For the buta-1,4-dione model at 6-31+G(d), bare CASSCF gives +28.8, -12.0, -13.6 and -3.2 kcal/mol for reactions 1-4, while MRMP on the same reference gives +1.5, -41.4, -17.9 and -6.8 — reaction 2 moves by nearly 30 kcal/mol. The authors state outright that "inclusion of diffuse functions in the basis set and dynamic correlation at the CASSCF level appears essential", and that the conclusion that reaction 2 is more exoenergetic than reaction 3 "is obtained only after dynamic correlation is included" — at CASSCF alone the two reactions look almost equally favourable. The single-reference routes do not substitute: ROHF and UHF disagree with each other and with MRMP, and adding MP2 to them makes the energies diverge FURTHER from MRMP, with UHF wrongly predicting reaction 3 to be strongly endoenergetic. Second, a trap in the source: the methods section pairs the electron counts as 10 electrons for reactions 1 and 2 and 11 for reactions 3 and 4, and the multiplicities as triplet for reactions 1 and 3 and doublet for reactions 2 and 4 — but the results section says the donor frontier orbital is initially DOUBLY occupied in reactions 1 and 3 and SINGLY occupied in reactions 2 and 4, which does not line up with the abstract's own definitions (1 = QH2, 2 = QH-, 3 = QH radical, 4 = Q radical anion, of which the first two are closed shell and the last two are radicals). All three groupings are transcribed here exactly as printed and have NOT been reconciled; anyone reusing the per-row electron count or multiplicity should check them against the paper's equations 1-4.

notes: Models the one-electron reduction of triplet (3-Sigma-g) dioxygen by reduced mitochondrial ubiquinone, believed to be the main source of the superoxide anion radical O2(.-) and the hydroperoxide radical OOH(.) in NADH dehydrogenase (complex I) and cytochrome bc1 (complex III). Four reactions are defined: 1 = fully reduced protonated quinol QH2, 2 = its deprotonated form QH-, 3 = the semiquinone radical QH(.), 4 = the semiquinone anion radical Q(.-). Values in parentheses in Tables 1 and 2 are BSSE-corrected. point_group: C2h at the planar trans minimum; C2 along the CNNC torsion; Cs along the single CNN bend; C2h along the concerted CNN bend
geometry_source: Relaxed surface scans optimized for the second root (S1) at the state-specific CAS(6,6)/4-31G level along three coordinates; the S0/S1 conical intersection fully optimized at the state-averaged CAS(6,6)/4-31G level. Force constants at CAS(6,6)/4-31G, single-point energies at CAS(6,6)/cc-pVDZ.
method: State-specific CASSCF for the relaxed scans; state-averaged CASSCF for the conical-intersection optimization
basis_set: 4-31G for optimizations and frequencies; cc-pVDZ for single-point energies
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(6,6): the CAS(6,4) core of n-, pi, n+ and pi* extended by two more virtual orbitals chosen per coordinate — two pi* for the rotation channel, or pi* + sigma* for the inversion channels. By symmetry block the selected orbitals are 3a + 3b for the CNNC torsional scan (C2), 3a' + 3a'' for the CNN bending scan (Cs), and ag + au + 2bg + 2bu for the concerted CNN bending scan (C2h).
active_space_protocol: Following earlier azomethane work, the active space must include at least six electrons in four orbitals (n-, pi, n+, pi*) to describe the PES along the rotational isomerization coordinate; two further virtual orbitals were added because delocalized pi* and sigma* orbitals matter for the other coordinates, giving CAS(6,6). The extra pair is chosen DIFFERENTLY for each reaction coordinate (two pi* for rotation, pi* + sigma* for inversion). Scans are state-specific on the second root; only the conical intersection is state-averaged. Solvent was checked and dismissed: TD-B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) with PCM lowers the vertical excitation energy by only 0.01 eV in hexane and 0.05 eV in DMSO, far below the ~0.2 eV uncertainty of the calculations, so everything is gas phase.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (state-averaged, for the conical intersection); state-specific second root for the scans
electronic_structure_description: S0 ground state (C2h, 1Ag) and the S1(n,pi*) excited state. Relative energies including ZPE, in kcal/mol at CAS(6,6)/4-31G and CAS(6,6)/cc-pVDZ respectively: S1 at the Franck-Condon geometry 59.6 / 63.4 (experimental S1 absorption maximum 450 nm = 63.5); S1(C2h, 1Bg) 47.1 / 51.1; S1(C2, 1B) 47.7 / 50.1 (experimental absorption tail 560 nm ~ 51); S1(Cs, 1A'') 45.0 / 50.7 at a CNN angle of 129.4 deg; the semilinear S1-180(Cs) species 61.0 / 68.1; the rotational conical intersection S0/S1 CI-rot 42.2 / 47.8 at a CNNC angle of 92.1 deg; and the concerted-inversion conical intersection S0/S1 CI-inv 68.9 / 77.5 at CNN angles near 157 deg. The inversion channel carries a substantial barrier: S1-180(Cs) lies close to 20 kcal/mol above S1(Cs), the S0-S1 gap exceeds 10 kcal/mol beyond 180 deg (21.2 kcal/mol at the state-averaged cc-pVDZ level at the semilinear geometry), and force constants there give THREE imaginary frequencies, making the semilinear structure a high-order saddle point. The rotation channel is essentially barrierless with the conical intersection close to the midpoint of the torsion.
Other: The active space is not one space but three: the (6,4) n-/pi/n+/pi* core is fixed, while the two orbitals added to reach CAS(6,6) are chosen per reaction coordinate — two pi* for the rotation scan versus pi* + sigma* for the inversion scans — with the symmetry blocks listed separately for C2, Cs and C2h. Energies from the three scans therefore rest on three different six-orbital selections and are not strictly on one footing, which matters because the paper's conclusion is a comparison BETWEEN those channels. The basis, not the space, carries the largest single shift: going from 4-31G to cc-pVDZ at fixed CAS(6,6) raises the concerted-inversion conical intersection from 68.9 to 77.5 kcal/mol (8.6) and the semilinear saddle from 61.0 to 68.1 (7.1), while moving the rotational CI only from 42.2 to 47.8 — so the relative ordering of the inversion and rotation funnels is basis-sensitive at this active space. The state-specific versus state-averaged choice also moves numbers: the S0-S1 gap at the semilinear geometry is quoted as >10 kcal/mol from the state-specific scan but 21.2 kcal/mol from a state-averaged CAS(6,6)/cc-pVDZ calculation. The authors put the overall uncertainty of the surface-scan energies at about 4 kcal/mol (0.2 eV), which is the right scale to judge any of these differences against.

notes: Addresses the long-running rotation-versus-inversion controversy for azobenzene photoisomerization by scanning three coordinates: CNN bending (inversion), CNNC torsion (rotation) and concerted CNN bending (concerted inversion). compound_name: Water dimer radical cation (H2O)2+, hemi-bonded vs proton-transferred isomers
point_group: C2h for the three-electron hemi-bonded isomer (2Bu ground state); Cs for the proton-transferred isomer (2A'' ground state)
geometry_source: Both isomers fully optimized at the CAS(11/10) level; DFT optimizations with many exchange-correlation functionals performed alongside
method: CASSCF with single-point second-order multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory (MCQDPT2) at the CASSCF geometries
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(11/10): all of the valence electrons and all of the valence orbitals except the oxygen 2s orbitals — 11 electrons in 10 orbitals. (The paper states the exclusion as 'the oxygen 2s orbitals' in a passage covering both the (H2O)2+ and (H2S)2+ systems; the same 11/10 count is used for both.)
active_space_protocol: A single full-valence-minus-2s space, CAS(11/10), is used for the geometry optimizations of both isomers of both dimer cations, with MCQDPT2 single points added at those geometries purely to recover dynamic correlation. No space variation is reported; the paper's comparisons are between CASSCF, MCQDPT2, MP2, CCSD(T), ROHF/UHF and a large set of DFT functionals at fixed active space.
electronic_structure_description: Doublet radical cation. The three-electron hemi-bonded isomer has a 2Bu ground state; the proton-transferred isomer has a 2A'' ground state. Most DFT exchange-correlation functionals instead make the hemi-bonded isomer more stable; the exceptions are BHHLYP and full-HF-exchange-with-local-correlation combinations such as HLYP and HOP, which give -19.8 and -22.7 kcal/mol and deviate from the MCQDPT2 value of -1.9 more than the -8.4 kcal/mol from half-and-half exchange with local correlation.
Other: A clean demonstration that a full-valence active space without dynamic correlation is the wrong tool for two-centre three-electron bonds. reference_short: Ghanty & Ghosh, J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 11815
notes: Two lowest stationary structures reachable by ionizing the neutral water dimer: a two-centre three-electron hemi-bonded O-O structure and a proton-transferred structure (essentially H3O+ .. point_group: C2v (all geometries optimized under C2v symmetry constraint)
geometry_source: CASSCF/BSI optimized under C2v symmetry (MOLPRO); LDA+GC (DFT) geometries optimized separately with GAUSSIAN-92/DFT for comparison
method: CASSCF; internally contracted MR-SDCI (MRCI) with all single and double excitations from the CASSCF reference, plus the Davidson correction (+DC) for quadruple excitations
basis_set: BSI for geometries: Hay-Wadt ECP basis sets (5s5p5d/3s3p3d) for Sc and Co, (5s5p4d/3s3p3d) for Rh, (5s5p3d/3s3p3d) for Ir, with 6-31G on H, B and O. BSII (used for the energetics) is BSI augmented with f functions on the metal (exponents 1.335 Sc, 1.50 Co, 0.35 Rh, 0.20 Ir), d on B (0.401) and O (0.626) and p on H (0.75). BSIII recontracts the metal basis as 4s4p3d1f.
relativistic_treatment: Hay-Wadt effective core potentials, which include relativistic effects only for the second- and third-row metals (Rh, Ir); for the first-row complexes the nonrelativistic ECP is used and the paper notes this probably underestimates binding energies by a few kcal/mol
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence reference space, the paper's (3/10) notation for 3 electrons in 10 orbitals: all (s and five d) valence electrons and orbitals of Sc, one vacant d* orbital corresponding to the doubly occupied d orbital (2a2 in Figure 1), and the a1, b1 and b2 orbitals plus one a1 electron from the BH2 ligand.
active_space_protocol: Full valence reference active space, in the paper's (m/n) notation for m electrons in n orbitals, in the coordinate system of Figure 1: all (s and five d) valence electrons and orbitals of the metal, together with one vacant d* orbital corresponding to the doubly occupied d orbital (the 2a2 orbital of Figure 1), plus the a1, b1 and b2 orbitals and one a1 electron from the BR2 ligand. The same reference space is used for the subsequent internally contracted MR-SDCI. Active natural orbital occupancies and the partitioning of each active orbital between M and BH2 are tabulated per state in Table 3. Binding energies are computed at the MR-SDCI level as the difference between the equilibrium structure and a 'supermolecule' with the fragments held 15.0 A apart, with the Davidson correction added.
electronic_structure_description: Doublet ground state arising from the interaction of Sc+ 3D(s1d1) with BH2(2A1). Relative energies (kcal/mol) at CASSCF/MRCI/MRCI+DC with BSII, referenced to 2A1 (total energy -71.571821 / -71.576916 / -71.576953 hartree): 2B1 5.5 / 6.1 / 6.1; 2B2 1.1 / 1.0 / 1.0; 2A2 -2.2 / 0.0 / 0.1. For ScBH2+ the 2A2 state goes from -2.2 to +0.1. The paper also reports a striking geometry result: MR-SDCI+DC binding energies computed at the DFT-optimized geometries come out LARGER than those at the CASSCF-optimized geometries, which the authors read as evidence that "the DFT geometries are more reliable than the CASSCF geometries" — i.e. the full-valence CASSCF surface is not good enough to optimize on even when it is good enough as an MRCI reference. On the atomic asymptotes the same reference is systematically biased: MR-SDCI-CASSCF+DC overestimates the stability of s2dn over s1dn+1 for the atoms and of s1dn over s0dn+1 for the cations in every case, with mean absolute deviations from experiment of 0.50 eV (atoms) and 0.26 eV (cations). One transcription trap: the Calculation Procedure assigns (9/10) to MBR2+ and (10/10) to MBR2, but Table 4 labels RhB(OH)2+ as (10/10); the per-row values here follow Table 4 where it is explicit and the methods rule otherwise.
reference_short: Musaev & Morokuma, J. Phys. Chem. 1996, 100, 6509
notes: Part of a study of transition-metal-boryl complexes prompted by metal-catalysed alkene hydroboration, whose proposed catalytic cycle involves oxidative addition of a B-H bond to the metal. MR-SDCI+DC binding energies (kcal/mol): ScBH2+ 49.3, CoBH2+ 52.8, RhBH2+ 64.3, IrBH2+ 87.5; ScBH2 37.8, CoBH2 51.0, RhBH2 74.1, IrBH2 84.5. basis_set: BSI for geometries: Hay-Wadt ECP basis sets (5s5p5d/3s3p3d) for Sc and Co, (5s5p4d/3s3p3d) for Rh, (5s5p3d/3s3p3d) for Ir, with 6-31G on H, B and O.
