relativistic_treatment: Hay-Wadt effective core potentials, which include relativistic effects only for the second- and third-row metals (Rh, Ir); for the first-row complexes the nonrelativistic ECP is used and the paper notes this probably underestimates binding energies by a few kcal/mol
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence reference space, the paper's (9/10) notation for 9 electrons in 10 orbitals: all (s and five d) valence electrons and orbitals of Ir, one vacant d* orbital corresponding to the doubly occupied d orbital (2a2 in Figure 1), and the a1, b1 and b2 orbitals plus one a1 electron from the BH2 ligand.
active_space_protocol: Full valence reference active space, in the paper's (m/n) notation for m electrons in n orbitals, in the coordinate system of Figure 1: all (s and five d) valence electrons and orbitals of the metal, together with one vacant d* orbital corresponding to the doubly occupied d orbital (the 2a2 orbital of Figure 1), plus the a1, b1 and b2 orbitals and one a1 electron from the BR2 ligand. The same reference space is used for the subsequent internally contracted MR-SDCI. Active natural orbital occupancies and the partitioning of each active orbital between M and BH2 are tabulated per state in Table 3. Binding energies are computed at the MR-SDCI level as the difference between the equilibrium structure and a 'supermolecule' with the fragments held 15.0 A apart, with the Davidson correction added.
electronic_structure_description: Nearly degenerate quartet ground state derived from Ir+ 5F(s1d7) and BH2(2A1). Relative energies at CASSCF/MRCI/MRCI+DC with BSII, referenced to 4B1 (-129.433635 / -129.495288 / -129.497533 hartree): 4B2 3.6 / 0.7 / 0.5; 4A2 0.4 / 0.2 / 0.2; 4A1 21.7 / 27.8 / 21.3; 2A1 14.0 / 16.7 / 17.6. MR-SDCI+DC binding energy 87.5 kcal/mol, the largest in the series.
Other: The full-valence CASSCF reference gets the STATE ORDERING wrong for several of these complexes, and only the MR-SDCI+DC correction on top of it fixes them — the reorderings are large and change the chemical conclusion. For IrBH2 the 3A1 state sits 8.1 kcal/mol BELOW the 3B2 reference at CASSCF/BSII but 2.3 kcal/mol ABOVE it at MRCI+DC, and 3A2 moves from -4.7 to +12.2 kcal/mol — a swing of ~17 kcal/mol that flips the ground state. For CoBH2 the 3A2 state moves from +12.4 (CASSCF) to -0.4 (MRCI+DC) and becomes the lowest. For ScBH2 the CASSCF ordering makes 3A2 the ground state by 2.9 kcal/mol, while at MRCI+DC the 1A1, 3A1 and 3A2 states collapse into a 0.5 kcal/mol cluster. For ScBH2+ the 2A2 state goes from -2.2 to +0.1. The paper also reports a striking geometry result: MR-SDCI+DC binding energies computed at the DFT-optimized geometries come out LARGER than those at the CASSCF-optimized geometries, which the authors read as evidence that "the DFT geometries are more reliable than the CASSCF geometries" — i.e. the full-valence CASSCF surface is not good enough to optimize on even when it is good enough as an MRCI reference. On the atomic asymptotes the same reference is systematically biased: MR-SDCI-CASSCF+DC overestimates the stability of s2dn over s1dn+1 for the atoms and of s1dn over s0dn+1 for the cations in every case, with mean absolute deviations from experiment of 0.50 eV (atoms) and 0.26 eV (cations). One transcription trap: the Calculation Procedure assigns (9/10) to MBR2+ and (10/10) to MBR2, but Table 4 labels RhB(OH)2+ as (10/10); the per-row values here follow Table 4 where it is explicit and the methods rule otherwise.
reference_short: Musaev & Morokuma, J. Phys. Chem. 1996, 100, 6509
notes: Part of a study of transition-metal-boryl complexes prompted by metal-catalysed alkene hydroboration, whose proposed catalytic cycle involves oxidative addition of a B-H bond to the metal. MR-SDCI+DC binding energies (kcal/mol): ScBH2+ 49.3, CoBH2+ 52.8, RhBH2+ 64.3, IrBH2+ 87.5; ScBH2 37.8, CoBH2 51.0, RhBH2 74.1, IrBH2 84.5. Total energies for reference states and relative energies for the rest are in Table 6 (BSII); CASSCF/BSI geometries in Table 4; active natural orbital occupancies in Table 3. The paper does not assign formal oxidation states, working instead from the M/M+ atomic configurations; the oxidation state and d-electron count recorded here follow the usual convention of boryl as a monoanionic X-type ligand.

compound_name: Stacked guanine dimer radical cation (G5'G3')+, hole transfer between the two guanines
geometry_source: X-ray structure of the TC3 transposase-DNA complex (PDB 1TC3, residues Gua-A7 and Gua-A8) as the reference geometry, with the six intermolecular stacking parameters scanned around it; interaction energies of the stationary points computed at MP2/6-31G(d(0.2)) with counterpoise BSSE correction
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by internally contracted MRCI; state-averaged RASSCF followed by RASPT2 (RS2)
software: MOLPRO (CASSCF, RASSCF, MRCI, RASPT2); Gaussian 03 (MP2 interaction energies)
basis_set: 6-31G(d(0.2)) — 6-31G augmented by diffuse polarization functions with exponent 0.2
active_space_orbital_description: Minimal space [5,3]_3: five electrons distributed among the three highest occupied molecular orbitals (HOMO, HOMO-1 and HOMO-2), state-averaged over three states. These three orbitals are identified as the minimal active space for describing the electron transfer, because the three lowest states of (GG)+ each have a dominant configuration corresponding to the singly occupied HOMO, HOMO-1 and HOMO-2 respectively. Two enlargements are used: a validation CASSCF with 11 electrons in 10 orbitals, and the RASSCF space {R1[0,0]; R2[5,3]; R3[2,1]}_3, which keeps [5,3] as RAS2 and adds a single RAS3 orbital reachable by double excitations.
active_space_protocol: The choice of states entering the state averaging "was found to be particularly important and required careful investigation" so that both charge repartitions G5'+G3' and G5'G3'+ and all interacting states are properly represented; the main configuration state functions defining these states are accounted for in a restricted active orbital space correlating a minimal number of electrons. The 36 lowest occupied MOs (the 1s and 2s orbitals of O, C and N) were frozen at the SCF level rather than variationally optimized, cutting the CPU time by a factor of three without significant loss of accuracy, leaving 75 closed-shell orbitals plus the 3 active ones. The MRCI multireference wave function corresponds exactly to the CASSCF wave function, with all single and double excitations from the active orbitals into the external space, reaching 1e5 contracted CSFs (denoted CASSCF/MRCI(5), correlating the five active electrons). All RASSCF calculations start from the optimized [5,3]_3 CASSCF orbitals and keep the same doubly occupied core; RAS3 was sized by test calculations reported in the Supporting Information, which found one orbital to be the most efficient choice consistent with the CASSCF/MRCI(5) results. For RASPT2 (the RS2 approach) the occupied space from which excitations are allowed was extended to the 32-orbital maximum the MOLPRO code permits, correlating 61 electrons and recovering 1.16 hartree of correlation energy relative to RASSCF at the 1TC3 geometry, with a configuration space of 7e7 contracted CSFs at 3.5x the CPU cost of the [5,3]_3 CASSCF reference (denoted RASSCF/RASPT2(61)).
nroots_per_mult: 3 (state-averaged over the ground and two lowest excited states)
electronic_structure_description: Doublet radical cation. The three lowest states are each dominated by a configuration with the singly occupied HOMO, HOMO-1 and HOMO-2 respectively, and configuration mixing occurs among all three. The ground-to-first-excited gap at the reference geometry is 6.35 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 4.72 kcal/mol at CASSCF/MRCI(5); an extended CASSCF with 11 electrons in 10 orbitals gives 4.40 kcal/mol, confirming the MRCI value. Along the optimized charge-transfer reaction path at RASSCF/RASPT2(61) the potential energy barrier is 7.33 kcal/mol and the electronic coupling near the avoided crossing is 3.6 kcal/mol; the barrier separating the two minima M1 and M2 reaches 4.48 kcal/mol. Mulliken atomic populations locate the positive charge on one or the other guanine, defining the two charge repartitions G5'+G3' and G5'G3'+.
Other: Two distinct sensitivities, both quantified. First, correlation on top of the minimal space does not merely shift the gap — it INVERTS the answer: "the Mulliken atomic populations calculated for these states show that the repartitions of the positive charge in the stacked dimer (GG)+ are inverted for the MRCI results" relative to CASSCF, i.e. which guanine carries the hole in the ground state changes when dynamical correlation is added to the [5,3] reference. The gap itself moves from 6.35 (CASSCF) to 4.72 kcal/mol (MRCI). The authors validate the small space rather than assume it: an extended CASSCF with 11 electrons in 10 orbitals gives 4.40 kcal/mol, agreeing with the MRCI(5) value and confirming that the interaction between the three lowest states and higher excited states is captured, at 2.5x LESS CPU time than the 11-electron CASSCF. Second, they are explicit that perturbation theory is fussier about the reference than CI is: "the results of PT2 calculations are more sensitive to the choice of the MCSCF reference wave function, and convergence problems can occur if the active orbital space is not adequately chosen". Because the MRCI analysis revealed couplings between the reference configurations and doubly excited configurations in the external space, the space had to be enlarged with HF-unoccupied orbitals before PT2 could be applied — which is why the RASSCF {R1[0,0]; R2[5,3]; R3[2,1]} construction exists at all, and why RAS3 was sized by explicit test calculations rather than guessed. The state-averaging choice is flagged as needing careful investigation in its own right, since both charge-localized states and every state interacting with them must be in the average.

notes: Models hole transfer between stacked guanines in DNA, the key step in oxidative damage migration. Geometry taken from the TC3 transposase-DNA X-ray structure (PDB 1TC3), residues Gua-A7 and Gua-A8, with each of the six intermolecular stacking parameters (translations and rotations of G5' relative to G3') scanned to map how stacking geometry controls charge migration; energy maps for the ground and first excited states are given at RASSCF/RASPT2(61)/6-31G(d(0.2)). An initial CIS test calculation and a large number of MRCI test calculations with different configuration sets both indicate that the charge transfer proceeds by progressive passage from the ground configuration to the first excited configuration. The 6-31G(d(0.2)) basis was shown in the authors' earlier work to reproduce stacking stability and the electronic changes on ionization as well as larger polarized and augmented basis sets, at lower cost. RASSCF/RASPT2(61) was the level used to optimize the charge-transfer reaction path.

active_space_protocol: Two spaces are used depending on what bond is breaking: 2,2-CAS (three singlet configurations) for the trimethylene stationary points and for ethylcarbene, and 4,4-CAS (20 singlet configurations) for the 1,2- and 1,3-H transfer saddle points 5 and 6, where the active space additionally includes the sigma and sigma* orbitals involved in bonding to the transferred hydrogen alongside the terminal p orbitals. To place the two on the same footing, structure 2 was reoptimized with 4,4-CAS/VTZ(2d,p) including the C2-H3 sigma and sigma* orbitals. Dynamic correlation is added by multireference CISD with all single and double excitations from the CASSCF reference, EXCLUDING excitations involving the lowest three occupied and highest three virtual orbitals, which are kept doubly occupied and unoccupied respectively. With VTZ(2d,p) in C1 symmetry this gives 1 031 945 singlet configurations for 2,2-CAS-CISD and 5 761 732 for 4,4-CAS-CISD.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet biradical. The two propene-forming saddle points, computed with 4,4-CAS, lie much higher: 5 (1,2-H transfer, 1562i cm-1) 16.03 / 7.94 / 6.91 and 6 (1,3-H transfer to ethylcarbene, 993i cm-1) 19.67 / 10.17 / 12.37. At structure 5 the natural orbitals resemble trimethylene — a doubly occupied C2-H3 sigma orbital plus biradical-like terminal p orbitals with occupations 1.69 and 0.31. Structure 2 is the formal trimethylene reactant for 1,2-H transfer, the IRC connecting 5 to 2.
Other: The two active spaces used here do NOT share an energy scale, and the paper handles this by fiat rather than by computation: Table 1's footnote f states that the 4,4-CAS entry for structure 2 is "defined to have the same Delta-E relative to 1 as 2,2-CAS in order to place them on the same scale", with all other 4,4-CAS entries then referred to that defined value. So the 16.03 and 19.67 kcal/mol CAS barriers for the 1,2- and 1,3-H transfer saddle points 5 and 6 are anchored to an assumption, not to a computed 2,2/4,4 offset — the raw total energies differ by about 16 kcal/mol (-117.027652 vs -117.043606 hartree for the same structure 2). Reoptimizing 2 in the larger space changes the geometry negligibly apart from the expected lengthening of the C2-H3 bond from 1.094 to 1.115 A, which is what justifies the splice. Separately, the CISD correction on top of the 4,4 space is enormous for exactly the structures that needed the bigger space: the 1,2-H transfer barrier falls from 16.03 (CAS) to 7.94 (CISD) kcal/mol and the 1,3-H transfer barrier from 19.67 to 10.17 — both roughly halved — whereas the purely biradical stationary points 1-4 move by only a few tenths of a kcal/mol between CAS and CISD. The active space was sized by inspecting natural orbitals rather than assumed: at structure 5 the biradical-like terminal orbitals carry occupation numbers 1.69 and 0.31, "implying considerable bonding character", while at structure 6 the natural orbitals resemble ethylcarbene (a doubly occupied C3-H1 sigma orbital plus a carbene lone pair on C1) rather than trimethylene, consistent with the Hammond postulate.

point_group: Cs for the ylidene 1 (1A' ground state) and its cation 1(.+) (2A'); C2v for pyridine 2 and its cation 2(.+) (2A1)
geometry_source: CASSCF-optimized geometries; MP2 and B3LYP/6-31G** optimizations and frequencies also performed, with MP2 harmonic frequencies used for the ZPE corrections applied to the CASSCF-MP2 energies
method: CASSCF with multireference MP2 (CASSCF-MP2) single points, as implemented in Gaussian 94; MP2/PMP2 and B3LYP alongside
active_space_orbital_description: Seven orbitals: the six pi and pi* orbitals plus the lone pair at nitrogen or at carbon, whichever is appropriate for the species. Eight electrons for the neutral molecules, seven for the radical cations.
active_space_protocol: A single fixed seven-orbital space is used for all four species so the two isomers and their cations can be compared on one footing, with only the electron count changing on ionization (8 -> 7). CASSCF-MP2 energies are computed at CASSCF-optimized geometries, with ZPE corrections taken from MP2 harmonic frequencies rather than from CASSCF.
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 1A' singlet. The lowest triplet (3A'') lies 44.2 kcal/mol higher at MP2 and 35.6 at B3LYP, but the MP2 triplet wave function is severely spin contaminated (<S2> = 2.395); the CASSCF-MP2 singlet-triplet gap is 36.4 kcal/mol. This carbene is less stable than its pyridine isomer by 50.2 (MP2/6-31G**), 49.0 (CASSCF-MP2/6-31G**) and 46.8 (B3LYP/6-31G**) kcal/mol.
Other: The active space earns its keep on the triplet, where the single-reference route demonstrably fails. The MP2 wave function for the 3A'' state of the ylidene 1 is severely spin contaminated (<S2> = 2.395), "which renders the corresponding triplet energy a bit questionable", and MP2 puts the triplet 44.2 kcal/mol above the singlet. The CASSCF-MP2 singlet-triplet gap built on the (8,7) pi + lone-pair space is 36.4 kcal/mol, almost identical to the B3LYP value of 35.6 and clearly smaller than MP2 — so the multireference treatment and DFT agree against the spin-contaminated single-reference result. For the closed-shell comparisons the space changes little: the neutral 1-versus-2 energy difference is 50.2 (MP2), 49.0 (CASSCF-MP2) and 46.8 (B3LYP) kcal/mol, i.e. the methods agree within about 3 kcal/mol. The cations are the delicate case, and here the three methods DISAGREE ON THE SIGN: MP2 and CASSCF-MP2 make the ylid cation 1(.+) more stable than the pyridine cation 2(.+) by 5.5 and 7.4 kcal/mol respectively, while B3LYP puts 1(.+) 1.1 kcal/mol ABOVE 2(.+) — and the authors note that even the B3LYP ordering emerges only after ZPE is included, the uncorrected total energies slightly favouring 1(.+). Anyone using the cation ordering should treat the ~8 kcal/mol spread between these levels as the real uncertainty. Note also that ZPE corrections applied to the CASSCF-MP2 numbers come from MP2 frequencies, not from the CASSCF surface.
reference_short: Lavorato, Terlouw, Dargel, Koch, McGibbon & Schwarz, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1996, 118, 11898
notes: Gas-phase generation and observation of the Hammick intermediate, azacyclohexatriene-2-ylidene (1) — the 2-ylidene isomer of pyridine (2) — by one-electron reduction of the ylid radical cation 1(.+) using neutralization-reionization mass spectrometry (NRMS). The radical cation is formed by dissociative ionization of 2-picolinic acid and its methyl and ethyl esters; CID mass spectra of the m/z 79 ions from metastable dissociation and from source CO2 loss are identical, indicating a single isomer rather than a mixture. The experimental heat of formation Delta-Hf(1(.+)) = 237 +/- 5 kcal/mol agrees with the theoretical 237-242 kcal/mol derived from the calculated energies. The 1(.+) -> 2(.+) isomerization barrier is 62 (MP2) and 57 (B3LYP) kcal/mol relative to 1(.+), larger than the 38 kcal/mol required for the corresponding neutral transformation at both levels. All four species are genuine minima with positive definite Hessians at MP2 and B3LYP. Computed singlet-triplet gaps are in line with other amino carbenes (50 kcal/mol for amino carbene, 78 for imidazol-2-ylidene). CASSCF-MP2 results are in Table 2.

geometry_source: (8,8)-CASSCF optimizations with the polarized continuum model: S0 and the globally stable S1 geometry in DMSO (S0/DMSO, S1/DMSO) and in cyclohexane (S0/CHEX, S1/CHEX), plus a bare-molecule S0 optimization without PCM (S0-bare). Free-energy curves in S1 versus the tau2 torsion were built by scanning tau2 from 0 to 90 deg with all other geometrical parameters frozen at each of the four optimized structures.

basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta augmented with polarization functions on the N atoms (alpha_d = 0.80) and on the central ethylenic C atoms (alpha_d = 0.75). The diffuse functions placed on the ethylenic carbons in the author's previous work were found less important here and were removed.
active_space_orbital_description: (8,8): the highest four occupied and the lowest four unoccupied orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space was cut down from the author's previous CASSCF study on the explicit grounds that "the present interest of S1 with respect to the tau2-torsional coordinate is well described by the configuration state functions within the excitations between the highest four occupied and the lowest four unoccupied orbitals". Free energy is decomposed as F_i(tau2) = E_i(int)(tau2) + E_i(ES)(tau2), separating internal energy from electrostatic interaction so the skeletal-relaxation and torsional contributions can be analysed independently.
electronic_structure_description: S0 ground state and the S1 charge-transfer state. In the polar solvent DMSO the globally stable S1 geometry is a twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) conformation with the dimethylanilino group at tau2 = 90 deg relative to the 4-cyanostyryl group; in nonpolar cyclohexane the stable S1 form is NONTWISTED (tau2 = 0.9 deg). Skeletal relaxation accompanies both: the amino wagging angle collapses from about 35-38 deg in S0 to ~0.1-0.3 deg in S1, the N-C4 bond contracts from 1.408-1.411 A (S0) to 1.336-1.340 A (S1), and the CaCa' ethylenic bond lengthens from 1.331 A (S0) to 1.447 A (S1/CHEX) or 1.374 A (S1/DMSO) — i.e. the aromatic rings acquire bond alternation. The S1 dipole moment grows from 18.4 D for the bare molecule at the S0 geometry to 27.6 D at S1/CHEX and 38.3 D at S1/DMSO, with the Mulliken charge on the dimethylanilino fragment rising from +0.42 to +0.60 and +0.81 respectively. Other: The (8,8) space is a deliberate reduction from the author's earlier CASSCF treatment, justified not by a convergence test but by the claim that the S1 tau2-torsional coordinate is already well described by excitations within the highest four occupied and lowest four unoccupied orbitals; the diffuse functions previously carried on the ethylenic carbons were likewise dropped as unimportant for this coordinate. Because the whole model rests on CASSCF, which includes static but effectively no dynamic correlation, the paper tests it directly: MRMP2 single points at eight important conformations lower the S1 energies by 1.0-1.4 eV, but the correction is "almost constant at 1-1.3 eV, irrespective of conformations", so the RELATIVE free-energy landscape that carries the mechanism survives even though every absolute excitation energy is off by more than an electronvolt. notes: The paper's thesis is that skeletal relaxation — the loss of aromaticity and onset of bond alternation in the rings — is a factor in charge-transfer state formation alongside the conventional TICT picture of dimethylanilino torsion plus solvent polarity, and that a conventional TICT model alone is incomplete. geometry_source: Fully optimized at CASSCF/6-31G(d) and at B3LYP/6-31G(d), with frequencies at both levels
method: CASSCF (full geometry optimization and frequencies); DFT-B3LYP alongside, including single points at the CASSCF critical points
active_space_orbital_description: (6,6): all pi orbitals of the two fragments — six electrons in six orbitals — following ref 13.
active_space_protocol: Used for the whole cycloaddition surface: attack of ethylene on the 3(pi-pi*) enone, the triplet and singlet 1,4-biradical intermediates and their anti/gauche conformers, and the transition states connecting them. electronic_structure_description: Reaction begins on the 3(pi-pi*) triplet state (t1) of the enone. compound_name: Ni(C2H4)2 — bis(ethylene)nickel(0), D2d / C2v(planar) / C2v(bent) / D2h critical points
point_group: D2d (minimum), C2v(planar), C2v(bent) and D2h — four symmetry-distinct critical points on the same surface
geometry_source: CASSCF gradient optimization of each structure with the (14,10) space; CASPT2 single points at those CASSCF-optimized geometries. DFT (LSD/DZVP, and LANL2DZ ECP) optimizations performed for comparison with B3LYP, BLYP and BP86.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with CASPT2 single points (Andersson et al. multireference perturbation approach)
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis of Bauschlicher et al. for nickel and Dunning cc-pVDZ for carbon and hydrogen: primitives (Ni 20s15p10d6f), (C 7s6p4d2f), (H 4s1p) contracted to [Ni 7s6p4d2f], [C 3s2p1d], [H 2s1p)
active_space_orbital_description: (14,10) for the CASSCF geometry optimizations: the pi and pi* orbitals of the two ethylene moieties plus the 4s and 3d orbitals of the nickel atom — all the orbitals required to describe the forming Ni-C bonds and the low-lying states of the metal atom. The space is ENLARGED for the CASPT2 single points by adding a correlating 4d orbital for each doubly occupied 3d orbital not taking part in the bonding, following Pierloot, Persson and Roos: this gives 14 electrons in 12 orbitals for the D2d, C2v(planar) and C2v(bent) structures and 14 electrons in 13 orbitals for the D2h structure.
active_space_protocol: Two-stage: a (14,10) space carries the geometry optimizations, then the space is extended with 3d-correlating 4d orbitals for the single-point CASPT2 energies. The number of added 4d orbitals is structure-dependent, because it is set by how many 3d orbitals remain doubly occupied and non-bonding in each symmetry — hence (14,12) for three structures and (14,13) for D2h. The adequacy criterion is stated numerically: with this extended space "the perturbation contributions are all smaller than 1.0 kcal/mol".
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet d10 nickel(0) complex. Four critical points, with relative energies in kcal/mol at CASSCF and (in the CASPT2 column E(2)) at CASPT2: D2d 0.00 / 0.00, C2v(planar) 6.89 / 5.07, C2v(bent) 18.05 / 17.31, D2h 36.56 / 18.96. Absolute energies of the D2d structure are -1663.01454 (CASSCF) and -1664.27375 (CASPT2) hartree. D2d is the only genuine minimum (all real frequencies); C2v(planar) is a saddle point of index 1 connecting two equivalent D2d structures, C2v(bent) has index 2 and D2h index 3. Geometrical parameters are barely affected by structure: Ni-C distances 2.021 A (D2d) lengthening to 2.121 A (D2h), C=C 1.399 A (D2d) shortening to 1.373 A (D2h), and the ethylene pyramidalization angle epsilon 18.8 deg in D2d, 18.5/20.2 deg in C2v(planar), 18.7 deg in C2v(bent), falling to 11.6 deg in the planar D2h form.
Other: A textbook double-shell case with a structure-dependent twist. The (14,10) space that suffices for geometries does NOT suffice for energies: for every 3d orbital that stays doubly occupied and out of the bonding, a correlating 4d orbital must be added for the CASPT2 step (the Pierloot-Persson-Roos prescription), and because the count of such orbitals depends on symmetry the extended space is (14,12) for D2d, C2v(planar) and C2v(bent) but (14,13) for D2h. The payoff is quantified — with the extended space "the perturbation contributions are all smaller than 1.0 kcal/mol" — and the effect on the answer is highly non-uniform: adding dynamic correlation barely moves the D2d-C2v(planar) and D2d-C2v(bent) gaps (6.89 -> 5.07 and 18.05 -> 17.31 kcal/mol) but nearly HALVES the D2d-D2h gap, from 36.56 to 18.96 kcal/mol. So a (14,10) CASSCF number for the planar D2h form is wrong by 17.6 kcal/mol, while the same space is good to ~2 kcal/mol for the other two — the structure needing the extra 4d orbital is exactly the one whose energy is most wrong without it. The topology of the surface nonetheless survives: the energetic ORDER of the four critical points is unchanged by correlation, only the gaps move. The DFT comparison lands closer to CASPT2 than to CASSCF for the D2d-C2v(planar) gap (5.03-5.64 kcal/mol across B3LYP, BLYP and BP86 against 5.07 at CASPT2) but spreads widely for the D2h gap (12.84 kcal/mol at B3LYP/DZVP, 14.53 at BLYP, 15.94 at BP86).

active_space_orbital_description: CASPT2(14,12): all pi-pi* orbitals except those related to the deepest canonical orbital, plus two lone-pair orbitals. Other, unstated active spaces were used for the geometry optimizations.
electronic_structure_description: Vertical transitions in eV, CASSCF then CASPT2 (oscillator strength in parentheses), with band origins Te CASSCF/CASPT2 and radiative lifetime: 1(n-pi*) 5.95 -> 4.96 (0.004), Te 4.88/4.52, 334 ns; 1(Lb pi-pi*) 5.56 -> 5.16 (0.004), Te 4.92/4.83, 251 ns; 1(La pi-pi*) 7.03 -> 5.35 (0.175), whose geometry optimization leads directly to a ground-state conical intersection at 4.0 eV; 3(La pi-pi*) 3.77 -> 4.00, Te 3.52/3.36, 359 ms (experimental phosphorescence origin and maximum in solution/glasses 3.43 and 3.05 eV); 3(n-pi*) 5.38 -> 4.91, Te 4.84/4.41; 3(pi-pi*) 5.07 -> 4.95. Two singlet-triplet crossings lie along the 1(La pi-pi*) MEP: one at 5.2 eV with the 3(n-pi*) state and one at 4.0 eV near the methanamine-like ground-state conical intersection, the latter connecting directly to the lowest 3(pi-pi*) T1 state and sharing the envelope-puckered geometry with a stretched, twisted C2=N3 bond. In the Franck-Condon region direct 1(pi-pi*) to 3(pi-pi*) transfer is unlikely — large gap and SOC below 0.1 cm-1 — but the SOC rises to 15 cm-1 at the relevant crossing, making the ISC toward 3(pi-pi*) very favourable.
Other: The active spaces were fixed by backward compatibility, not by convergence: "for the sake of consistency with previous calculations on the singlet states of the systems, the same one-electron basis sets and active spaces were employed". That freezes two different protocols side by side in one paper — CASPT2(14,10) with ANO-S C,N,O[3s2p1d]/H[2s1p] for the pyrimidines T, U and C, versus CASPT2(14,12) with 6-31G(d,p) for the purines A and G — so cross-comparisons between a purine and a pyrimidine in this work vary the space AND the basis at once. The purine space is also defined by exclusion (all pi-pi* orbitals EXCEPT those from the deepest canonical orbital, plus two lone pairs) rather than by a full-valence rule. A second trap: "other active spaces were employed in the optimization procedures, following a strategy which was proved successful previously", with details relegated to the Supporting Information and to earlier papers — so the reported CASPT2(14,10)/(14,12) energies sit on geometries obtained in DIFFERENT, unstated spaces. The CASSCF-to-CASPT2 shifts show why the perturbative step is indispensable rather than cosmetic, and are strongly state-dependent: for adenine the 1(La pi-pi*) vertical transition falls from 7.03 to 5.35 eV (-1.68) while the 3(La pi-pi*) RISES from 3.77 to 4.00 eV (+0.23); for guanine 1(La pi-pi*) falls 6.36 -> 4.93 and 1(Lb pi-pi*) 7.04 -> 5.72, while 3(La pi-pi*) rises 3.97 -> 4.11; for thymine 1(pi-pi* La) falls 6.52 -> 4.89 and its band origin 6.07 -> 4.49. CASSCF alone would therefore invert the singlet state orderings that the whole singlet-triplet crossing analysis depends on.
reference_short: Gonzalez-Luque, Climent, Gonzalez-Ramirez, Merchan & Serrano-Andres, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2010, 6, 2103
notes: Determines the singlet-triplet crossing (STC) regions and decay paths for the lowest singlet and triplet states of the five natural DNA/RNA nucleobases after near-UV irradiation, to explain how the triplet manifold gets populated. Central result: all five bases have a low-energy, easily accessible STC at the end of the main 1(pi-pi*) minimum energy path, near the conical intersection of that state with the ground state, directly connecting the lowest singlet and triplet pi-pi* states. Adenine, thymine and uracil additionally show higher-energy crossings mediated by low-lying singlet and triplet n-pi* states; these funnels are absent in guanine and cytosine, whose bright 1(pi-pi*) state lies lower and whose n-pi* states are less accessible. Radiative lifetimes come from the Strickler-Berg relationship and are only indicative. The authors stress that an accessible crossing is necessary but not sufficient for efficient intersystem crossing — vibronic contributions to the rates and dynamics calculations are still needed. New results are presented for the purines A and G; the pyrimidine results draw on the group's earlier work with new complementary calculations on cytosine.

compound_name: Difluoromethyl radical (CHF2), ground and first two excited electronic states
point_group: Cs (pyramidal ground state; the second excited B state is planar with a 180 deg dihedral)
geometry_source: CASSCF(19,13) and MRCI(3,4) geometry optimizations for the second excited state (convergence 3e-4 RMS gradient, 5e-4 maximum component); the first excited state has no locatable minimum, so it was characterized by two-dimensional relaxed-coordinate potential surface scans. Ground-state and barrier geometries come from MP2 and CCSD(T).
method: CASSCF(19,13) for surface scans and excited-state optimizations; MRCI with three electrons in four active orbitals for selected scans and optimizations; CIS, MP2 and CCSD(T) alongside
software: MOLPRO (CASSCF, MRCI); Gaussian 94 rev E.6 and Gaussian 98 rev A.7 (MP2, CCSD(T), CIS)
basis_set: 6-31+G* and 6-311++G** for the CASSCF and MRCI work; aug-cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ also used at MP2, CCSD(T) and CIS
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(19,13): the 10 occupied valence orbitals of the ground-state main configuration (six of a' symmetry and four of a'' symmetry) together with the lowest three unoccupied orbitals (two a' and one a''), holding 19 valence electrons. This gives 51 112 configuration state functions for states of A' symmetry (the ground and first excited states) and 51 992 for A'' symmetry (the second excited state). A far smaller MRCI space of three electrons in four active orbitals, MRCI(3,4), was used for selected scans and optimizations.
active_space_protocol: The CASSCF space is built by taking the entire occupied valence manifold of the ground-state configuration plus the three lowest virtuals, rather than by selecting orbitals around a particular bond. The 1s orbitals of carbon and the two fluorines are kept in the core. Because no minimum could be located on the first excited state by standard optimization, that state was mapped by two-dimensional scans in which the C-H distance and out-of-plane dihedral were varied (C-F fixed at 1.30 A, H-C-F fixed at 115 deg), and separately the H-C-F and out-of-plane dihedral angles were varied (C-H fixed at 2.0 A, C-F at 1.30 A).
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state main configuration (core)3a'2 2a''2 4a'2 5a'2 3a''2 6a'2 4a''2 5a''2 7a'2 8a'1, with the core comprising the carbon and fluorine 1s orbitals; the singly occupied 8a' HOMO has C-F pi* antibonding character. CIS vertical excitation energies (cm-1, oscillator strength) at 6-31+G* / 6-311++G** / aug-cc-pVDZ / aug-cc-pVTZ: A state 64 065 (0.031) / 62 532 (0.028) / 62 250 (0.029) / 61 355 (0.028); B state 68 226 (0.015) / 67 880 (0.012) / 67 162 (0.010) / 66 944 (0.010); C state 71 372 (0.003) / 70 573 (0.002) / 69 485 (0.003) / 69 065 (0.003). The first excited (A) state has no true minimum: CASSCF(19,13)/6-31+G* scans show an apparent minimum near a C-H distance of 2.0 A with a dihedral above 148 deg, and MRCI(3,4) gives a similar picture at 2.0 A and 144 deg. Two shallow local minima appear in the angular scan — one about 130 cm-1 deep at H-C-F 96 deg and dihedral 116 deg, lying 38 700 cm-1 above the ground-state minimum, and a deeper one about 3400 cm-1 deep at H-C-F 120 deg and dihedral above 160 deg, lying 35 400 cm-1 up — but full optimization from either fails, and the state may simply be dissociative as CIS suggests. The second excited (B) state IS a bound planar minimum: CASSCF(19,13)/6-31+G* gives r(H-C) 1.0606 A, r(C-F) 1.4588 A, H-C-F 133.89 deg, F-C-F 92.22 deg, dihedral 180.00 deg and an adiabatic transition energy of 49 904 cm-1; CASSCF(19,13)/6-311++G** gives 1.0606, 1.4501, 133.71, 92.58, 180.00 and 49 476 cm-1; MRCI(3,4)/6-31+G* gives 1.0877, 1.4107, 132.24, 95.52, 180.00 and 51 757 cm-1. The large CASSCF(19,13) space and the tiny MRCI(3,4) space locate the same features on the first excited state — an apparent minimum at a C-H distance of 2.0 A, with the dihedral coming out at above 148 deg from CASSCF and 144 deg from MRCI — and give closely similar geometries for the second excited state (C-H 1.0606 vs 1.0877 A, F-C-F 92.22 vs 95.52 deg). active_space_orbital_description: For the C2v structures (molecule in the yz plane), 10 electrons in 10 orbitals: the two in-plane pi-parallel orbitals (9a1, 8b2), the three out-of-plane pi-perpendicular orbitals (1b1, 1a2, 2b1) and the five corresponding virtual orbitals (2a2, 10a1, 9b2, 3b1, 3a2) of the enediyne moiety. Along the reaction coordinate the two in-plane pi orbitals transform into the a1 sigma orbital of the new C-C bond and the b2 sigma orbital localized on the radical centres. The CASMP2 step uses a reduced 8-electron/8-orbital space obtained by excluding the 1b1 and 3a2 MOs for this structure.
active_space_protocol: The space is chosen so that it follows the bonds being made and broken: the in-plane pi orbitals of the enediyne become the sigma orbital of the forming C-C bond and the sigma orbital on the radical centres, so one 10-orbital selection spans reactant, transition state and product. CASMP2 single points were performed at the optimized CASSCF geometry, but only with eight active electrons because of program limitations, the 8e/8o reference being generated from the 10e/10o CAS by excluding the most and least occupied orbitals at each point along the surface. MRSDCI, referenced on the configurations contributing above 99% of the CASSCF wave function, was used to test for relevant configurations outside the active space.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell 1(1A1) singlet ground state with substantial diradical character already present: effectively unpaired electrons per atom from the CASSCF wave function are 0.26 at C1/C6, 0.23 at C2/C5 and 0.18 at C3/C4 in the 1(1A1) state (0.27 unpaired electrons per pi bond is quoted as typical), rising to 0.43, 0.25 and 0.80 in the 1(3B2) triplet. The first six vertical excited states are describable as linear combinations of weakly interacting ethylene and acetylene configurations; the 1(1B1) and 1(1A2) states are localized at the alkyne units and the S0 -> 1(1A2) transition is symmetry forbidden. The singlet-triplet gap [S0 to 1(3B2)] is 2.1 eV in 1a. Thermally, cyclization has Delta-G(double dagger)/Delta-H(double dagger)/T-Delta-S(double dagger) of 44.18/41.86/-2.69 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 26.86/24.22/-2.63 at CASMP2, against experimental barriers of 28 and 32 kcal/mol.
Other: The CASSCF(10,10) space gets the barrier badly wrong, and the paper diagnoses exactly why. CASSCF gives Delta-H(double dagger) = 41.9 kcal/mol and Delta-H(rxn) = 25.9 kcal/mol against experimental values of 32 (or 28) and 14 (or 8 +/- 3) — because "CASSCF overestimates the radical contribution to the TS wave function and underestimates the ion pair contribution, thereby elevating the TS energy". Adding dynamic correlation for the ionic contributors through CASMP2 brings the barrier down to 24.2 kcal/mol and flips the reaction from strongly endothermic (+25.9) to exothermic (-4.9) — a swing of nearly 31 kcal/mol in the reaction enthalpy from the same reference. This is a case where the deficiency is not a missing orbital but a missing weighting of ionic configurations, so enlarging the space would not have helped. Worse, the CASMP2 correction could NOT be run in the reference space it corrects: "because of CASMP2 program limitations, the calculation could only be performed with eight active electrons", so the 8e/8o reference was carved out of the 10e/10o CAS by excluding the most and least occupied orbitals at each point — and the orbitals dropped differ by structure, 1b1 and 3a2 for the reactant and transition state but 1a1 and 2b2 for the diradical product. The reported CASMP2 reaction profile therefore rests on a space whose composition changes along the reaction coordinate. The active space was at least checked rather than assumed: MRSDCI calculations, using as reference every configuration contributing more than 99% of the CASSCF wave function, were run specifically to test for relevant configurations lying outside the active space. UDFT lands closer to experiment than CASSCF on the barrier (UB3LYP 29.9, UBPW91 22.2 kcal/mol) but needs the sum-formula correction for triplet spin contamination in the singlet diradical.

geometry_source: Geometries taken from the X-ray diffraction work and constrained to Cs symmetry, with the Cr-C(carbonyl) distances averaged
method: CASSCF(6,6) with a configuration interaction expansion of 175 spin-adapted configurations; HFSCF and DFT (LDA) alongside, with NBO analysis on both the HF and CASSCF wave functions
basis_set: Cr: (14,9,6)/[8,4,3] contraction (626*1/5112/411), with 14s9p primitives from Wachters and 6d functions from Goddard. N, O, C, H: split-valence double-zeta 6-31G. DFT uses a double numerical basis augmented with polarization functions (DNP).
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(6,6): the six orbitals of the Cr=C(carbene) double-bond region — three occupied (pi1 = the Cr-C(carbene) pi bond, sigma = Cr-C sigma, pi2 = the pi bond of C(carbene)-X) and three unoccupied (pi1*, sigma*, pi2*), where X = O or N. The CI expansion within these six orbitals comprises 175 spin-adapted configurations.
active_space_protocol: The space is confined deliberately to the Cr=C(carbene) bond region rather than spanning the metal d manifold, because the question being asked is the nature of that one bond. A SECOND CASSCF(6,6) calculation was run with the (CO)5Cr and carbene fragments separated by 6 A, to obtain the orbital correlation diagram and the bond dissociation energy. reference_short: Wang, Wang, Liu, Lin, Chou & Chan, J. Phys. Chem. A 1997, 101, 8887
notes: Combined X-ray charge-density and molecular-orbital study of four pentacarbonylchromium carbene complexes (CO)5CrC(XR')R, with one (XR' = OCH3, R = -(C=CPh)) measured extensively at 110 K with Mo K-alpha radiation. point_group: Cs (the carbene plane bisects the C-Cr-C angle); the Cr(CO)5 fragment is assumed to be C4v
geometry_source: Geometries taken from the X-ray diffraction work and constrained to Cs symmetry, with the Cr-C(carbonyl) distances averaged
method: CASSCF(6,6) with a configuration interaction expansion of 175 spin-adapted configurations; HFSCF and DFT (LDA) alongside, with NBO analysis on both the HF and CASSCF wave functions
basis_set: Cr: (14,9,6)/[8,4,3] contraction (626*1/5112/411), with 14s9p primitives from Wachters and 6d functions from Goddard. N, O, C, H: split-valence double-zeta 6-31G. DFT uses a double numerical basis augmented with polarization functions (DNP).

The CI expansion within these six orbitals comprises 175 spin-adapted configurations.
active_space_protocol: The space is confined deliberately to the Cr=C(carbene) bond region rather than spanning the metal d manifold, because the question being asked is the nature of that one bond. NBO analysis (NAO -> NHO -> NBO -> NLMO transformations) was applied to both the HF and the CASSCF wave functions to extract net atomic charges, orbital populations and bond orders.

compound_name: Ni(PH3)2 + H2 oxidative addition to cis-Ni(H)2(PH3)2
ligand_set: two PH3 plus the incoming H2 (dihydride in the product)
geometry_source: DFT(B3LYP)/Wa-TZ(f)-optimized geometries along the IRC reaction coordinate; the CASSCF, CASPT2, CCSD(T), Bs-MP2 to Bs-MP4(SDTQ) and DFT potential energy curves are all single points on those structures
method: CASSCF and CASPT2; CCSD(T), broken-symmetry MP2 to MP4(SDTQ) and DFT for comparison
software: MOLCAS 5.4 (CASSCF, CASPT2); Gaussian 03 (DFT, Bs-MP2 to MP4(SDTQ), CCSD(T)); MOLEKEL for orbital plots
basis_set: (21s15p10d6f)/[6s5p4d2f] ANO basis for Ni in the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations, cc-pVDZ on the other atoms. Many alternatives were surveyed for Ni elsewhere in the paper: cc-pVTZ, Wachters (14s9p5d1f)/[9s5p3d1f] augmented with an f function (Wa-TZ(f)), 6-31G(f), the Stuttgart-Dresden-Bonn ECP basis (311111/22111/411/1) (SDB), and the Christiansen-Ermler shape-consistent ECP bases CE-DZ (761/681/51/1) and CE-TZ (7511/6711/411/1). The all-electron sets are nonrelativistic; the ECP sets carry relativistic effects in their potentials.
relativistic_treatment: None in the ANO/CASPT2 route (nonrelativistic all-electron basis); relativistic effects enter only through the SDB and CE ECP basis sets used in the comparison calculations
active_space_orbital_description: (10e 10a): the five occupied Ni 3d orbitals plus the five second, outer 3d' orbitals — a full double-shell space. Two other spaces were tested. (4e 4a) comprises occupied Ni(d), Ni(d)+H(1s), unoccupied Ni(d) and Ni(d)-H(1s). (12e 12a) adds the occupied 3p(z) and unoccupied 4p(z) orbitals to the (10e 10a) space, motivated by the reported importance of 3p-3d correlation.
active_space_protocol: Three active spaces were compared systematically on the same DFT geometries. Two orbital-migration observations guided the choice: in the (4e 4a) calculation the Ni(d-sigma)+H2(sigma) canonical orbital that was deliberately included CHANGED into a Ni(d) orbital during the CASSCF optimization, which the authors read as evidence that intra-3d-shell correlation dominates; and in the (12e 12a) calculation the included canonical MO-18a likewise changed into NO-15a, meaning 3p-3d correlation matters more than correlation involving the dihydrogen sigma orbital. Natural orbital populations from CASSCF(10e 10a) were inspected along the reaction coordinate to identify which orbitals actually do the work.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet d10 nickel(0) phosphine complex adding H2. Four natural orbitals change population appreciably along the path — NO-15b, NO-16b, NO-18a and NO-19a — while the rest barely move. Configuration 2, a two-electron excitation from NO-15b to NO-16b (the Ni(d)+H(1s) bonding combination and its antibonding counterpart), rises sharply in weight around the transition state as the Ni-H bond forms, while configuration 3 falls; configuration 3 is a one-electron excitation from NO-18a to NO-19a combined with NO-15b to NO-16b, where NO-18a and NO-19a are mainly the 3d and outer 3d' orbitals, so it carries both Ni-H bond correlation and intra-3d-shell correlation. The reaction is endothermic: about 8.5 kcal/mol at CASPT2(10e 10a)/ANO and 7 kcal/mol at CCSD(T)/ANO, the latter smaller by roughly 1.5 kcal/mol. The product cis-Ni(H)2(PH3)2 optimizes at DFT(B3LYP)/Wa-TZ(f) but becomes LESS stable than the transition state once a better basis set is used.
Other: A clean, deliberate active-space convergence study on a 3d metal, with the double shell as the decisive ingredient. CASSCF(4e 4a) gives a DOWNHILL potential energy curve — the wrong sign for the reaction — while CASSCF(10e 10a) and CASSCF(12e 12a) both give uphill curves; the authors conclude outright that "(10e 10a) is necessary to incorporate well nondynamic correlation effects in this reaction but (4e 4a) is too small". The (10e 10a) space is nothing but the five 3d orbitals plus their five outer 3d' correlating partners, so the double-shell effect alone is what fixes the curve. Enlarging further to (12e 12a) by adding 3p(z)/4p(z) changes essentially nothing — "(10e 10a) and (12e 12a) active spaces present almost the same PECs in both CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations" — so the space is converged at the double shell. Two orbital-rotation diagnostics reinforce this: an orbital deliberately placed in the (4e 4a) space as Ni(d-sigma)+H2(sigma) rotated into a pure Ni(d) orbital during optimization, and in the (12e 12a) space the added canonical MO-18a rotated into NO-15a, showing the variational procedure preferring intra-3d and 3p-3d correlation over dihydrogen sigma correlation. Dynamic correlation on top is separately essential and NOT interchangeable with space size: CASPT2(4e 4a) gives a completely uphill curve "totally different from the CASSCF(4e 4a) calculation", i.e. a too-small space plus PT2 accidentally repairs the sign, and CASPT2(10e 10a) and CASPT2(12e 12a) are more uphill still than their CASSCF counterparts. The converged CASPT2(10e 10a)/ANO answer is corroborated externally by CCSD(T)/ANO to within about 1.5 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Ohnishi, Nakao, Sato & Sakaki, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 7915
notes: Benchmark of computational methods for oxidative addition to a nickel(0) complex, motivated by the difficulty of activating strong bonds and by the absence of prior multireference treatments of nickel organometallic reactions with an adequately selected active space. Basis-set effects on Ni are large and are surveyed exhaustively: the CCSD(T) endothermicity is 7 kcal/mol with ANO but shifts to about 6.7 kcal/mol with cc-pVTZ and changes completely with poorer sets, and improving the ligand basis from cc-pVDZ to cc-pVTZ lowers it by a further ~2 kcal/mol to 4.8. Broken-symmetry MP4(SDTQ) reproduces the CASPT2(10e 10a)/ANO curve reasonably but is not smooth around the transition state (the non-smoothness is under 0.5 kcal/mol). The companion reaction, oxidative addition of MeCN to Ni(PH3)2, was treated only with CCSD(T) and DFT — no CASSCF or CASPT2 — so no row is entered for it; its activation barrier is about 35-37 kcal/mol with Delta-E1 = -15.8 and Delta-E2 = +14.7 kcal/mol at CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ (Table 1). Population analysis follows the method of Weinhold et al.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF reference, computed for all three active spaces (4e 4a), (10e 10a) and (12e 12a)

point_group: C3v (the CASSCF calculations keep C3v symmetry; orbitals are labelled in the Cs subgroup as a'/a'')
geometry_source: B3LYP-optimized structure (Gaussian 03); the CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 calculations are single points on it. Experimental gas-phase electron-diffraction geometry gives Re-C 2.060 A, Re-O 1.709 A, C-Re-O 106 deg and O-Re-O 113 deg, against 2.069/1.693/105/112 at B3LYP and 2.098/1.715/107/113 at PW91.
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by MS-CASPT2 with a level shift; TD-DFT (PW91, GRAC, BP, B3LYP, LB94) for comparison
basis_set: Dolg effective core potential (Z = 15.0) on Re with the associated (8s,7p,6d) valence basis; ANO all-electron basis sets on the light atoms — (10s,6p,3d) contracted to [4s,3p,2d] for C and O, (7s,3p) contracted to [3s,2p] for H
relativistic_treatment: Dolg relativistic effective core potential on rhenium
active_space_orbital_description: 14 electrons correlated in 10 active orbitals. The orbitals carrying the reported transitions are 15a', 16a', 17a', 18a' and their a'' partners 7a'' and 9a'' — the oxygen lone pairs, the Re d manifold (pi*(Re-O)) and the sigma*(Re-C) orbital; 7a''/9a'' are the second components of the E sets in C3v and are closely similar to the Kohn-Sham 8e and 9e orbitals.
active_space_protocol: State-averaged CASSCF over 6 roots for a given spin, keeping C3v symmetry and using SUPERSYMMETRY plus cleaning of orbital coefficients to hold the orbital classification fixed during the optimization. The resulting wave functions are the reference for MS-CASPT2, computed with the level-shift corrected perturbation method using a shift of 0.3.
nroots_per_mult: 6 (state-averaged)
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell d0 Re(VII) ground state. CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 singlet excitation energies, with the dominant one-electron excitation, its weight and the experimental band maximum: b(1A1) at 4.81 eV / 257 nm, f = 0.0066, 15a' -> 17a' (44.1%) plus 7a'' -> 9a'' (26.4%), a pO -> dRe(pi*(Re-O)) charge transfer, against an observed band at 260 nm; c(1E) at 5.16 eV / 240 nm, f = 0.0059, 16a' -> 17a' (43.6%) plus 7a'' -> 9a'' (16.9%), pO and dRe -> dRe(pi*(Re-O)), observed at 231 nm; d(1E) at 5.84 eV / 212 nm, f = 0.0320, 15a' -> 18a' (40.4%) plus 16a' -> 17a' (12.7%), pO -> dRe(sigma*(Re-C)), observed at 205 nm. A further very weak excitation at 287 nm with oscillator strength 0.0003 is found but not tabulated. Photochemistry is Re-C homolytic cleavage on irradiation; a PW91 Walsh diagram along the Re-C coordinate shows the sigma*(Re-C) 10a1 orbital stabilizing as the bond lengthens while 9a1 rises, the latter losing Re p character and becoming more d(z2) and bonding.
Other: The multireference result is used here as the arbiter that settles a state assignment the single-reference methods get subtly wrong, and the composition percentages are what carry the argument. The 260 nm band is confirmed as an oxygen-lone-pair to Re d(pi*(Re-O)) charge transfer, overturning the long-standing empirical assignment of it as sigma(Re-C) -> pi*(Re-O), which the paper states plainly "was wrong". More pointedly, for the 240 nm transition the TD-DFT and MS-CASPT2 descriptions disagree in character even though they agree in energy: "the MS-CASPT2 calculations show that the methyl participation is overestimated and the Re participation is underestimated" by TD-DFT, the true transition being mainly pO and dRe -> dRe(pi*(Re-O)) rather than pO, pC -> dRe(pi*(Re-O)). The 14e/10o wave functions are strongly multiconfigurational in the relevant states — the leading configuration carries only 44.1%, 43.6% and 40.4% of b(1A1), c(1E) and d(1E) respectively, with a second configuration adding 26.4%, 16.9% and 12.7% — so no single-determinant description of these excitations is adequate in principle, whatever the energies come out at. A practical note on the protocol: the space is held together only by supersymmetry constraints and orbital-coefficient cleaning within C3v, and the MS-CASPT2 step needs a 0.3 level shift, indicating intruder-state pressure on this reference. Functional choice matters for the comparison: B3LYP agrees best with both experiment and MS-CASPT2 (its weak 277 nm / f = 0.0001 excitation matching the CASPT2 287 nm / f = 0.0003), whereas BP, GRAC and PW91 place that excitation at 285 nm with non-negligible oscillator strength, and LB94 performs worst.
reference_short: Costa et al., Organometallics 2006, 25, 5235
notes: Re-examination of the UV-vis spectra and photochemical reactivity of methyltrioxorhenium, the first modern quantum-chemical treatment of MTO photochemistry; earlier work had addressed Re-C homolysis but not the photochemistry itself. Solvent effects were included through COSMO in the ADF calculations. The Walsh diagram for Re-C stretching closely matches an earlier extended-Huckel picture and indicates the importance of the sigma/sigma*(Re-C) levels once the bond is stretched, though the paper is explicit that these results are insufficient for definitive conclusions about the photoprocess dynamics. The study was extended to RReO3 with R = C2H5, C6H5 and C6H3(CH3)3, all of which show the same Re-C homolytic cleavage on irradiation, but those larger species were treated with TD-DFT (PW91) only — no CASSCF or MS-CASPT2 — so no rows are entered for them. TD-DFT results are summarized in Tables 5 and 7; the CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 excitation energies are in Table 6.
correlation_correction: MS-CASPT2 (multi-state CASPT2) with the level-shift corrected perturbation method, level shift 0.3

compound_name: CH + O2 reaction surface: HCOO (IM1), the C-O-O ring intermediate IM2, and the transition states along the path
point_group: Cs (planar) for IM1 and several transition states; C1 for the nonplanar ring intermediate IM2
geometry_source: CASSCF(7,7) geometry optimization (Gaussian 94W) with CASPT2 single points at those geometries (MOLCAS 5.0); B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) reaction paths with IRC calculations provide the reference mechanism
method: CASSCF(7,7) geometry optimizations with CASPT2//CASSCF single points; (U)B3LYP with four basis sets as the primary method
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for the reported CASSCF and CASPT2 results; CASSCF optimizations were also attempted with 6-311G(d,p), 6-311+G(d,p) and 6-311++G(d,p)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(7,7): seven electrons in seven orbitals. The paper does not enumerate the orbitals; it identifies the full-valence space for this system as (17,13) and states that this would be the right uniform choice but is too large.
active_space_protocol: A single (7,7) space was carried across the whole reaction path, but it does not transfer cleanly: CASSCF optimizations located all the intermediates and transition states of the B3LYP path EXCEPT TS2 and TS5, IM1 could be located only with the 6-31G(d,p) basis, and IM3b was a minimum at 6-31G(d,p) but a transition state with a ~2800i cm-1 imaginary frequency at all three larger basis sets. Only the 6-31G(d,p) results are therefore reported. The leading-configuration coefficients of every CASSCF wave function were inspected as a multireference diagnostic.
electronic_structure_description: Doublet surface from CH + O2(X 3Sigma-g). Relative energies including CASSCF(7,7)/6-31G(d,p) ZPE corrections, given as CASSCF / CASPT2 in kcal/mol with the leading CASSCF configuration coefficient in parentheses: CH + O2 0.0 / 0.0; IM1 (HCOO, 2A') -79.8 / -8.0 (0.964); TS1 -59.4 / -19.6 (0.935); IM2 (C-O-O ring, nonplanar) -89.5 / -57.0 (0.957); TS3 -157.1 / -137.2 (0.969); TS4 -137.0 / -116.3 (0.975); IM4 -203.7 / -143.1 (0.974). Products: CO2 + H at -192.2 (CASSCF) / -152.3 (CASPT2), against -175.0 at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) and an experimental Delta-H of -184.0 kcal/mol; CO + OH at -165.1 / -129.9, against -146.7 and an experimental -159.0. TS2 and TS5 could not be located at the CASSCF level at all. TS1 carries the lowest leading coefficient (0.935) and is the one point on the path where static correlation is judged somewhat important.
Other: An unusually candid failure report, and the paper diagnoses the cause as the active space itself. The CASSCF(7,7) and CASPT2//CASSCF relative energies disagree with B3LYP by 4-26 and 17-45 kcal/mol respectively, and the CASPT2 magnitudes are systematically too SMALL against experiment: CO2 + H comes out at -152.3 kcal/mol against a B3LYP value of -175.0 and an experimental Delta-H of -184.0, and CO + OH at -129.9 against -146.7 and an experimental -159.0. Worse than the energetics, the (7,7) space gets a qualitative fact wrong — CASPT2 makes IM3a (2B2) more stable than IM3b (2A1), contradicting both experiment and B3LYP. Geometries are off too: the CASSCF C-H bond in TS3 is 0.237 A SHORTER than the B3LYP value and the HCO1 angle in IM1 is 14 deg smaller. The space is also not robust to the basis: IM1 could only be located at 6-31G(d,p), and IM3b flips from a minimum to a transition state with a ~2800i cm-1 imaginary frequency on going to any larger basis. The authors' own explanation is that the space is too small and cannot be made uniform along the path: the stationary points span Cs(planar), C1, Cs(nonplanar) and C2v symmetries, so "it is difficult to find correlations between the molecular orbitals in the electronic structures of all the IMs and TSs", and "the full-valence active space (17,13) should be a good choice for the uniform active space in the path calculations. However, such an active space is somewhat too large." The final irony is recorded in Table 3: the leading CASSCF configuration coefficients are 0.935-0.975 throughout, so "the static electron correlation might be somewhat important only for TS1" — the system barely needed a multireference treatment, and the undersized space it received made the answers worse than DFT rather than better.
reference_short: Huang, Chen & Wang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 5490
notes: Mechanistic study of the combustion-relevant reactions CH + O2(X 3Sigma-g) -> CO2 + H (1) and -> CO + OH (2), explored primarily with (U)B3LYP using 6-31G(d,p), 6-311G(d,p), 6-311+G(d,p) and 6-311++G(d,p), with IRC calculations and <S2> values below 0.775 along all paths. Mechanism: the CH radical side-attacks one oxygen of O2 to give HCOO (IM1, 2A'), a strongly exothermic step with no transition state; the C atom then bonds to the distal oxygen through TS1 to give the nonplanar C-O-O ring intermediate IM2; ring opening (O-O rupture) gives the formyloxyl radical HCO2 in its 2B2 state (IM3a), which converts readily to the 2A1 formyloxyl radical (IM3b) either through TS5 (2A') or through the 2B2-2A1 surface crossing; the final products follow from IM3b by H dissociation (channel 1) or by the channel-2 process. CASSCF locates the 2A1/2B2 crossing at an OCO angle of 130 deg against 128 deg from B3LYP. B3LYP energies and geometries are in Tables 1 and 2, the CASSCF/CASPT2 values in Table 3.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/6-31G(d,p) single points at the CASSCF(7,7)/6-31G(d,p) geometries

geometry_source: CASSCF(7,7) geometry optimization (Gaussian 94W) with CASPT2 single points at those geometries (MOLCAS 5.0); B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) reaction paths with IRC calculations provide the reference mechanism
method: CASSCF(7,7) geometry optimizations with CASPT2//CASSCF single points; (U)B3LYP with four basis sets as the primary method
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for the reported CASSCF and CASPT2 results; CASSCF optimizations were also attempted with 6-311G(d,p), 6-311+G(d,p) and 6-311++G(d,p)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(7,7): seven electrons in seven orbitals. The paper does not enumerate the orbitals; it identifies the full-valence space for this system as (17,13) and states that this would be the right uniform choice but is too large.
active_space_protocol: A single (7,7) space was carried across the whole reaction path, but it does not transfer cleanly: CASSCF optimizations located all the intermediates and transition states of the B3LYP path EXCEPT TS2 and TS5, IM1 could be located only with the 6-31G(d,p) basis, and IM3b was a minimum at 6-31G(d,p) but a transition state with a ~2800i cm-1 imaginary frequency at all three larger basis sets. Only the 6-31G(d,p) results are therefore reported. The leading-configuration coefficients of every CASSCF wave function were inspected as a multireference diagnostic.
electronic_structure_description: Planar formyloxyl radical, formed by O-O ring opening in IM2 and existing as two close-lying doublet states. Relative energies including ZPE, CASSCF(7,7)/6-31G(d,p) / CASPT2/6-31G(d,p) in kcal/mol with leading CASSCF coefficients in parentheses: IM3a (2B2) -161.6 / -136.4 (0.966); IM3b (2A1) -152.6 / -133.3 (0.954). Both multireference levels therefore place the 2B2 state BELOW the 2A1 state, contradicting both the experimental facts and the B3LYP prediction that 2A1 is the more stable. The 2A1/2B2 surface crossing is located at an OCO angle of 130 deg by CASSCF against 128 deg by B3LYP. IM3a converts easily to IM3b either through TS5 (2A') — which CASSCF could not locate — or directly through that crossing. At the B3LYP level the identity of the 2A1 stationary point is itself basis-dependent, and at CASSCF(7,7) IM3b is a minimum only with 6-31G(d,p), becoming a transition state with a ~2800i cm-1 imaginary frequency in every larger basis.
Other: An unusually candid failure report, and the paper diagnoses the cause as the active space itself. The CASSCF(7,7) and CASPT2//CASSCF relative energies disagree with B3LYP by 4-26 and 17-45 kcal/mol respectively, and the CASPT2 magnitudes are systematically too SMALL against experiment: CO2 + H comes out at -152.3 kcal/mol against a B3LYP value of -175.0 and an experimental Delta-H of -184.0, and CO + OH at -129.9 against -146.7 and an experimental -159.0. Worse than the energetics, the (7,7) space gets a qualitative fact wrong — CASPT2 makes IM3a (2B2) more stable than IM3b (2A1), contradicting both experiment and B3LYP. Geometries are off too: the CASSCF C-H bond in TS3 is 0.237 A SHORTER than the B3LYP value and the HCO1 angle in IM1 is 14 deg smaller. The space is also not robust to the basis: IM1 could only be located at 6-31G(d,p), and IM3b flips from a minimum to a transition state with a ~2800i cm-1 imaginary frequency on going to any larger basis. The authors' own explanation is that the space is too small and cannot be made uniform along the path: the stationary points span Cs(planar), C1, Cs(nonplanar) and C2v symmetries, so "it is difficult to find correlations between the molecular orbitals in the electronic structures of all the IMs and TSs", and "the full-valence active space (17,13) should be a good choice for the uniform active space in the path calculations. However, such an active space is somewhat too large." The final irony is recorded in Table 3: the leading CASSCF configuration coefficients are 0.935-0.975 throughout, so "the static electron correlation might be somewhat important only for TS1" — the system barely needed a multireference treatment, and the undersized space it received made the answers worse than DFT rather than better.
reference_short: Huang, Chen & Wang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 5490
notes: Mechanistic study of the combustion-relevant reactions CH + O2(X 3Sigma-g) -> CO2 + H (1) and -> CO + OH (2), explored primarily with (U)B3LYP using 6-31G(d,p), 6-311G(d,p), 6-311+G(d,p) and 6-311++G(d,p), with IRC calculations and <S2> values below 0.775 along all paths. Mechanism: the CH radical side-attacks one oxygen of O2 to give HCOO (IM1, 2A'), a strongly exothermic step with no transition state; the C atom then bonds to the distal oxygen through TS1 to give the nonplanar C-O-O ring intermediate IM2; ring opening (O-O rupture) gives the formyloxyl radical HCO2 in its 2B2 state (IM3a), which converts readily to the 2A1 formyloxyl radical (IM3b) either through TS5 (2A') or through the 2B2-2A1 surface crossing; the final products follow from IM3b by H dissociation (channel 1) or by the channel-2 process. CASSCF locates the 2A1/2B2 crossing at an OCO angle of 130 deg against 128 deg from B3LYP. B3LYP energies and geometries are in Tables 1 and 2, the CASSCF/CASPT2 values in Table 3. The formyloxyl radical is the key branching intermediate of both channels and the species where the (7,7) space most clearly fails, inverting the 2A1/2B2 ordering relative to experiment. Earlier CASPT2 work by Rauk et al. on the three low-lying HCO2 states is discussed in the paper for comparison but is not this paper's own calculation.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/6-31G(d,p) single points at the CASSCF(7,7)/6-31G(d,p) geometries

compound_name: (6-4) photolyase active site, protonated His365 model ((6-4)I) — flavin/photoproduct/adenine cluster
geometry_source: Active-site cluster models built from the CPD and (6-4) photolyase crystal structures, with hydrogens added in HyperChem and the sugar-phosphate part of the FADH- cofactor omitted; geometries optimized at B3LYP/6-31G(d) and found to agree well with the parent PDB models, with a planar flavin ring system in every case. The (6-4)Int and (6-4)Repaired models were obtained from (6-4) by following the OH-transfer reaction coordinate.
method: State-averaged CASSCF using the principal orbital CASSCF (POCAS) approach, with XMCQDPT2 for dynamic correlation; CIS used first to identify the lowest excited states; R-/U-B3LYP for comparison
software: Firefly (partially based on the GAMESS US source code)
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the excitation-energy calculations; B3LYP/TZVP for the separate two-base photoproduct models
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(2,2) for the closed-shell-singlet versus biradical comparison: the HOMO, localized on flavin, and the LUMO, localized on either the 3'base or the 5'base of the (6-4) photoproduct. The excitation-spectrum calculations use the larger principal orbital CASSCF (POCAS) space, whose size is given only in the Supporting Information.
active_space_protocol: State-averaged CASSCF with EQUAL weights for all roots, using the second-order MCSCF optimization implemented in Firefly and the POCAS (principal orbital CASSCF) orbital-selection scheme. The two-electron/two-orbital space is used specifically so that closed-shell singlet and biradical states can be put on one energy scale; the corresponding broken-symmetry U-B3LYP calculations of the (6-4)II and (6-4)Int models describe the same HOMO-LUMO biradicals. CIS is used as a pre-screen to identify which excited states to recompute.
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over all roots with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet reference state for the protonated (6-4) photolyase active site, taken as the zero of the relative ground-state energies at all three levels (R-/U-B3LYP, CASSCF(2,2) and XMCQDPT2). The excitation spectrum contains two flavin local excitations plus electron-transfer states: the ET state of protonated His365 lies at 2.53 eV, and the excitation energy of the (6-4) photoproduct radical anion — the (ET 3'base)-(ET 5'base) gap — is 1.6 eV in this model, against 1.1 eV in the protonated-adenine model (6-4)III, showing the gap is sensitive to the photoproduct environment. In the protonated-adenine model the three adenine ET states lie at 1.61, 2.82 and 3.01 eV.
Other: The minimal (2,2) HOMO-LUMO space is used for exactly one job — putting closed-shell singlet and biradical states on a common scale — and the paper's own numbers show how much that choice costs. For the protonated (6-4) active sites, the (6-4)II biradical lies below (6-4)I by 28.3 kcal/mol (1.23 eV) at R-/U-B3LYP, 22.1 kcal/mol (0.96 eV) at CASSCF(2,2), and 40.4 kcal/mol (1.70 eV) at XMCQDPT2 — a spread of 18 kcal/mol across three levels on the same geometries, with CASSCF(2,2) at one extreme and its own XMCQDPT2 correction at the other. For the neutral two-histidine models the ordering of the disagreement reverses: (6-4)Int sits 54.6 kcal/mol (2.37 eV) above (6-4) at B3LYP, 65.2 kcal/mol (2.82 eV) at CASSCF(2,2), but only 42.4 kcal/mol (1.83 eV) at XMCQDPT2 — so the bare (2,2) space overshoots here by 23 kcal/mol where it undershot by 18 before. In both cases dynamic correlation moves the answer by more than the difference between the states being compared, so no conclusion about which tautomer or intermediate is populated survives at the CASSCF(2,2) level alone. The excitation spectra are handled with a different and larger space chosen by the POCAS (principal orbital CASSCF) scheme rather than by hand, and its size is not stated in the main text — so the ground-state energetics in Tables 2 and 3 and the excitation energies discussed alongside them do NOT come from the same active space. A useful internal consistency check the paper does report: the two flavin hydroquinone local-excitation energies come out at 2.65 and 3.32-3.34 eV in every model with a closed-shell ground state, so the POCAS/XMCQDPT2 protocol is at least stable across cluster models.
reference_short: Domratcheva, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2011, 133, 18172
notes: Quantum-chemical study of photoinduced electron transfer in DNA photolyases, the light-activated enzymes that repair UV-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimer (CPD) and (6-4) pyrimidine-pyrimidone photoproducts. The models are large active-site clusters including the flavin, the photoproduct, adenine and nearby residues, built from the respective crystal structures. Computed flavin hydroquinone anion absorptions of 2.65 eV (f = 0.07, ~470 nm) and 3.32 eV (f = 0.28, ~375 nm) agree well with the observed FADH- spectrum in photolyase, which peaks near 380 nm with a red shoulder extending to about 500 nm; these are HOMO-LUMO and HOMO-(LUMO+1) transitions of the flavin hydroquinone. Vertical electron affinities of the CPD and (6-4) photoproducts were computed separately on two-base N1-methylthymine models at B3LYP/TZVP (Table 1). Full data for each model are in the Supporting Information Tables S2 and S9-S11.
correlation_correction: XMCQDPT2 (extended multiconfiguration quasi-degenerate perturbation theory to second order) on the state-averaged CASSCF reference

geometry_source: Model built on the experimental structures of Cs4V(H2O)6(SO4)2.6H2O and Cs3VCl6.4H2O with a V-O distance of 1.97 A; the M-O distance is then scanned along the totally symmetric Delta-Q(a1g) coordinate to build the potential energy curves
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2
basis_set: Generally contracted atomic natural orbital (ANO) sets: (17s,12p,9d,4f) contracted to [5s,4p,3d] for the metal; (10s,6p,3d) contracted to [3s,2p,1d] for oxygen; (7s,3p) for hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen active orbitals: the five 3d orbitals of the metal centre, the 3d correlating (second) shell, and some diffuse orbitals delocalized over the oxygen atoms and the metal centre. The SAME 13-orbital space is used for both complexes so their computed spectroscopic properties can be compared directly; only the electron count differs (2 for V3+, 8 for Ni2+).
active_space_protocol: Two electrons correlated in the 13 active orbitals. Averaged CASSCF generates the zero-order wave functions used as references for CASPT2. The correlated calculations were driven in D2h symmetry. No level shift was needed for this complex; the CASPT2 reference weight stays nearly constant at about 0.70 across all electronic states and geometries examined.
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over the low-lying triplet crystal-field states generated by single and double excitations within the 3d manifold
electronic_structure_description: d2 ion with a 3T1g(3F) electronic ground state, (3dxy)(2/3)(3dxz)(2/3)(3dyz)(2/3)(3dx2-y2)(0)(3dz2)(0), i.e. (t2g)2(eg)0 in Oh. Triplet crystal-field states along Delta-Q(a1g), given as Delta-Q(a1g,min) / E(min) / harmonic frequency, CASSCF then CASPT2 (experimental values in parentheses): 3T1g(3F) 0 / 0 / 124 cm-1, then 0 / 0 / 253 cm-1 (experimental 530 cm-1); 3T2g -0.71 A / 9660 cm-1 / 227 cm-1, then +0.23 A / 9830 cm-1 (experimental ~13 400) / 320 cm-1; 3T1g(3P) -0.73 A / 23 680 cm-1 / 222 cm-1, then +0.19 A / 19 930 cm-1 (experimental ~20 700) / 318 cm-1. Crystal-field parameters for this complex are Dq = 1860 cm-1.
Other: The most striking result is that CASSCF in this 13-orbital space gets the excited-state GEOMETRIES qualitatively wrong for the d2 complex and only CASPT2 repairs them. For [V(H2O)6]3+, CASSCF places the 3T2g and 3T1g(3P) minima at Delta-Q(a1g) = -0.71 and -0.73 A — i.e. it predicts the M-O bonds CONTRACT on d-d excitation — whereas CASPT2 gives +0.23 and +0.19 A, the physically expected elongation. The harmonic frequencies move correspondingly, roughly doubling from 124-227 cm-1 at CASSCF to 253-320 cm-1 at CASPT2. Nothing comparable happens in the d8 complex: for [Ni(H2O)6]2+ the CASSCF and CASPT2 minima agree in sign and to within 0.05 A (0.12-0.17 vs 0.17-0.23 A) and the frequencies shift by only ~10-20 cm-1. So the same space, differing only in electron count, is adequate at CASSCF level for d8 but not for d2 — the sensitivity is a property of the electron configuration, not of the orbital selection. Excitation energies improve markedly too for vanadium: the 3T1g(3P) origin falls from 23 680 cm-1 (CASSCF) to 19 930 (CASPT2) against an experimental ~20 700. The space itself is built deliberately around correlation rather than around bonding: beyond the five 3d orbitals it carries the full 3d correlating (double) shell plus diffuse orbitals spanning the oxygens and metal. Two protocol caveats are stated: a level shift of 0.4 was needed for the nickel complex to eliminate intruder states, and because CASPT2 is essentially monoconfigurational the authors flag state mixing as "a potentially serious problem in the nickel complex", arguing stability from the nearly constant reference weights of about 0.70 (V) and 0.76 (Ni) across all states and geometries. Spin-orbit coupling was deliberately omitted as a few hundred cm-1 effect against nonadiabatic couplings of thousands.
reference_short: Landry-Hum, Bussiere, Daniel & Reber, Inorg. Chem. 2001, 40, 2595
notes: Octahedral d2 and d8 complexes have triplet manifolds with identical T2g, A2g, T1g(3F) and T1g(3P) symmetry labels, which the paper exploits to compare their absorption spectroscopy on a common footing. Geometries are based on the experimental structures of Ni(H2O)6(NO3)2 and NiCl2(H2O)4, and Cs4V(H2O)6(SO4)2.6H2O and Cs3VCl6.4H2O, with M-O distances of 2.06 A (Ni-O) and 1.97 A (V-O); O-H is fixed at 1.04 A and H-O-H at 104.5 deg, and the water orientation is not varied. Potential energy curves are computed along the totally symmetric average M-O elongation Delta-Q(a1g), identified from the experimental spectra as the dominant deformation mode, with the origin at the ground-state equilibrium geometry. Tanabe-Sugano diagrams for both complexes are given, including the effect of setting the off-diagonal element coupling the two 3T1g states to zero. Anisotropic pi bonding, which could split the 3T2g states depending on the water hydrogen positions, is not explored in these model calculations.
