geometry_source: Model built on the experimental structures of Ni(H2O)6(NO3)2 and NiCl2(H2O)4 with an Ni-O distance of 2.06 A; the M-O distance is scanned along Delta-Q(a1g)
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2
basis_set: Generally contracted atomic natural orbital (ANO) sets: (17s,12p,9d,4f) contracted to [5s,4p,3d] for the metal; (10s,6p,3d) contracted to [3s,2p,1d] for oxygen; (7s,3p) for hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen active orbitals: the five 3d orbitals of the metal centre, the 3d correlating (second) shell, and some diffuse orbitals delocalized over the oxygen atoms and the metal centre. The SAME 13-orbital space is used for both complexes so their computed spectroscopic properties can be compared directly; only the electron count differs (2 for V3+, 8 for Ni2+).
active_space_protocol: Eight electrons correlated in the same 13 active orbitals as the vanadium complex. Averaged CASSCF references followed by CASPT2, driven in D2h symmetry, with a LEVEL SHIFT of 0.4 applied to eliminate intruder states. The CASPT2 reference weight stays nearly constant at about 0.76 across all states and geometries.
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over the low-lying triplet crystal-field states generated by single and double excitations within the 3d manifold
electronic_structure_description: d8 ion with a 3A2g electronic ground state, (3dxy)2(3dxz)2(3dyz)2(3dx2-y2)1(3dz2)1, i.e. (t2g)6(eg)2 in Oh. Triplet crystal-field states along Delta-Q(a1g), given as Delta-Q(a1g,min) / E(min) / harmonic frequency, CASSCF then CASPT2 (experimental in parentheses): 3A2g 0 / 0 / 318 cm-1, then 0 / 0 / 300 cm-1 (Raman at 77 K, 397 cm-1); 3T2g 0.12 A / 5678 cm-1 / 346 cm-1, then 0.17 A / 7039 cm-1 (~6600) / 332 cm-1; 3T1g(3F) 0.17 A / 8308 cm-1 / 356 cm-1, then 0.23 A / 9724 cm-1 (~11 300) / 343 cm-1 (experimental 350); 3T1g(3P) 0.14 A / 24 850 cm-1 / 350 cm-1, then 0.18 A / 23 703 cm-1 (~23 000) / 337 cm-1. Crystal-field parameters for this complex are Dq = 910 cm-1, B = 950 cm-1, C/B = 4, with a spin-orbit coupling constant of -270 cm-1 used in the separate crystal-field calculations.
Other: The most striking result is that CASSCF in this 13-orbital space gets the excited-state GEOMETRIES qualitatively wrong for the d2 complex and only CASPT2 repairs them. For [V(H2O)6]3+, CASSCF places the 3T2g and 3T1g(3P) minima at Delta-Q(a1g) = -0.71 and -0.73 A — i.e. it predicts the M-O bonds CONTRACT on d-d excitation — whereas CASPT2 gives +0.23 and +0.19 A, the physically expected elongation. The harmonic frequencies move correspondingly, roughly doubling from 124-227 cm-1 at CASSCF to 253-320 cm-1 at CASPT2. Nothing comparable happens in the d8 complex: for [Ni(H2O)6]2+ the CASSCF and CASPT2 minima agree in sign and to within 0.05 A (0.12-0.17 vs 0.17-0.23 A) and the frequencies shift by only ~10-20 cm-1. So the same space, differing only in electron count, is adequate at CASSCF level for d8 but not for d2 — the sensitivity is a property of the electron configuration, not of the orbital selection. Excitation energies improve markedly too for vanadium: the 3T1g(3P) origin falls from 23 680 cm-1 (CASSCF) to 19 930 (CASPT2) against an experimental ~20 700. The space itself is built deliberately around correlation rather than around bonding: beyond the five 3d orbitals it carries the full 3d correlating (double) shell plus diffuse orbitals spanning the oxygens and metal. Two protocol caveats are stated: a level shift of 0.4 was needed for the nickel complex to eliminate intruder states, and because CASPT2 is essentially monoconfigurational the authors flag state mixing as "a potentially serious problem in the nickel complex", arguing stability from the nearly constant reference weights of about 0.70 (V) and 0.76 (Ni) across all states and geometries. Spin-orbit coupling was deliberately omitted as a few hundred cm-1 effect against nonadiabatic couplings of thousands.
reference_short: Landry-Hum, Bussiere, Daniel & Reber, Inorg. Chem. 2001, 40, 2595
notes: Octahedral d2 and d8 complexes have triplet manifolds with identical T2g, A2g, T1g(3F) and T1g(3P) symmetry labels, which the paper exploits to compare their absorption spectroscopy on a common footing. Geometries are based on the experimental structures of Ni(H2O)6(NO3)2 and NiCl2(H2O)4, and Cs4V(H2O)6(SO4)2.6H2O and Cs3VCl6.4H2O, with M-O distances of 2.06 A (Ni-O) and 1.97 A (V-O); O-H is fixed at 1.04 A and H-O-H at 104.5 deg, and the water orientation is not varied. Potential energy curves are computed along the totally symmetric average M-O elongation Delta-Q(a1g), identified from the experimental spectra as the dominant deformation mode, with the origin at the ground-state equilibrium geometry. Tanabe-Sugano diagrams for both complexes are given, including the effect of setting the off-diagonal element coupling the two 3T1g states to zero. Anisotropic pi bonding, which could split the 3T2g states depending on the water hydrogen positions, is not explored in these model calculations.

compound_name: Phosphirane, ring-chain rearrangement to vinylphosphine by hydrogen migration (H1 -> H1/H2 transition state)
geometry_source: MP2-optimized geometries; the transition state was NOT reoptimized at the CASSCF level (see protocol). B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) geometries and PCM solvation, and GIAO/B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p) chemical shifts, were computed separately.
method: CASSCF(10,10) with CASPT2 single points at MP2 geometries; HF, MP2, B3LYP, CCSD and CCSD(T) for comparison
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis of quality comparable to 6-31G(d,p) for the CASSCF/CASPT2 work; 6-31G(d,p) for the other methods
active_space_orbital_description: (10,10): simply the five highest occupied and five lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals generated from the corresponding SCF wave function. The paper is explicit that the orbitals could not be characterized chemically — "because the system does not have any symmetry and the orbitals are strongly mixed, it is rather difficult to clearly identify their nature" — so the space is defined by energetic ordering rather than by which bonds it spans. The most important active orbitals at the transition state are its HOMO-2, HOMO-1, HOMO and LUMO.
active_space_protocol: Ten electrons in the five HOMOs plus five LUMOs of the SCF wave function, justified on the grounds that these "largely cover the important orbitals involved in the electronic reorganization accompanying the process". CASPT2 single points were taken at MP2 geometries. Attempts to reoptimize the minimum and transition state at the CASSCF level FAILED: "despite many attempts, we were unfortunately not successful in locating the TS because of the lack of analytical Hessians of the CASSCF energy in the Molcas-4 program". As a substitute diagnostic, the internal stability of the RHF wave functions was tested by mixing orbitals and allowing the restricted scheme to become unrestricted; the RHF wave function of the phosphirane ring itself is stable under that perturbation.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet reactant with a transition state showing appreciable biradical character. At the H1/H2 transition state the CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers are 1.95 for the HOMO and 0.33 for the LUMO, and in the CAS wave function the Hartree-Fock reference carries weight 0.82 against 0.15 for the doubly excited HOMO-to-LUMO configuration — an electronic distribution the authors read as indicating "significant biradical character" in the ring-opening transition state. Energy barriers including zero-point corrections (ZPEs of H1 and H1/H2 are 39.8 and 37.1 kcal/mol) with the 6-31G(d,p) basis: HF//HF 62.65, MP2//MP2 66.09, B3LYP//B3LYP 55.55, CCSD//MP2 65.28, CCSD(T)//MP2 61.84, CASSCF(10,10)//MP2 54.00 and CASPT2(10,10)//MP2 51.4 kcal/mol. Total energy of H1 at CASSCF(10,10)//MP2 is -419.459868 hartree and at CASPT2 -419.778431 hartree.
Other: The (10,10) space is chosen by orbital ENERGY ORDER, not by chemistry — five HOMOs plus five LUMOs — precisely because the molecule has no symmetry and the orbitals are too strongly mixed to identify individually. That choice is defensible here, since the diagnostic it delivers is the point of the calculation: HOMO/LUMO occupations of 1.95/0.33 and a CAS wave function that is 0.82 Hartree-Fock reference plus 0.15 doubly excited establish real biradical character in the transition state that no single-reference argument would have shown. But the space cannot be used for what it was ultimately wanted for. Reoptimizing the transition state at CASSCF failed outright for a purely technical reason — MOLCAS-4 has no analytical CASSCF Hessians — so the biradical contribution to the barrier could never be quantified, and every multireference number quoted rests on MP2 geometries. The methods then disagree in a way the space cannot resolve: CASPT2(10,10) gives 51.4 kcal/mol while CCSD(T) gives 61.84, about 10 kcal/mol higher, and the paper notes that B3LYP (55.55) lands closest to the CASSCF value (54.00) rather than to either correlated benchmark. The authors' own resolution is to abandon precision, concluding the true barrier is around 45 kcal/mol with an expected error of +/- 5 kcal/mol after allowing for a further ~3 kcal/mol lowering from geometry relaxation. Cost is recorded too: relative CPU times for single-point energies are HF 1, B3LYP 3, MP2 4, CASSCF/CASPT2 10, CCSD(T) 100, with the lack of symmetry noted as a disadvantage.
reference_short: Matrai, Dransfeld, Veszpremi & Nguyen, J. Org. Chem. 2001, 66, 5671
notes: Studies the ring-chain rearrangement of C-halogenated phosphiranes to vinylphosphines for X = H, F, Cl and Br, confirming a one-step mechanism in which C-P bond cleavage and X-sigmatropic migration from carbon to phosphorus occur together. The CASSCF/CASPT2 treatment was applied ONLY to the unsubstituted (X = H) system as a check on higher excitations and multireference character; the halogenated species were treated with HF, MP2, CCSD(T) and B3LYP, so no multireference rows are entered for them. Halogen substitution lowers the barrier by at most 3 kcal/mol (fluorine case) relative to the parent, while the largest difference between H1/H2 and F1/F2 is 3.1 kcal/mol and between H1/H2 and F1/F3 is 7.2 kcal/mol. A separate related result quoted for comparison is a silicon analogue barrier of about 24 kcal/mol at CASSCF(12,12)/CASPT2/6-31G(d,p), and a literature QCISD(T)/6-311G(d,p)+ZPE value of 56 kcal/mol. PCM at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) probes bulk solvent effects and GIAO/B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p) gives 31P chemical shifts correlating phosphiranes with XCH2PH2 phosphines. Optimized geometries and energies are in the Supporting Information.

compound_name: Diazetine (parent, compound 5) — N2 extrusion through TS1a
point_group: C1 at the transition state TS1a (Cs is slightly broken, N-N-C-C dihedral 14.9 deg); the Cs-constrained TS1a' is a second-order saddle point
geometry_source: CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G* optimized, with CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* and CASSCF(2,2)/6-311+G(2d,p) checks; BCCD(T) single points at the CASSCF geometries
method: CASSCF geometry optimizations with BCCD(T) single-point energies (Brueckner doubles with a triples contribution)
basis_set: mainly 6-31G(d), with 6-311+G(2d,p) used to test basis dependence
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(2,2) for the production geometries, with CASSCF(4,4) run as a check on the active-space choice. The initial orbitals for CASSCF are the natural orbitals generated from the unrestricted Hartree-Fock wave functions.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF is used for geometry optimization only, because it accounts for the nondynamic correlation these biradicaloid transition states require; energies come from BCCD(T)//CASSCF single points. CASPT2 was tested and REJECTED — "the calculated results were unreasonable (e.g., negative activation energies)" — which the authors attribute to CASPT2's known systematic errors when the number of unpaired electrons changes along a reaction path, and to size-consistency problems of the CI ansatz for larger systems. CCSD(T) was avoided in turn because coupled-cluster solutions can be unstable for low-symmetry biradicals, so Brueckner-orbital BCCD(T) was used instead; BCCD incorporates more fifth-order terms than CCSD or QCISD. The symmetry-breaking conclusion was tested against both the active space (CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G*) and the basis (CASSCF(2,2)/6-311+G(2d,p)).
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet reactant decomposing concertedly to N2 plus alkene. The transition state TS1a has strong biradical character, with natural orbital occupations (1.5006, 0.4994). It does NOT have Cs symmetry: the Cs-constrained structure TS1a' carries TWO imaginary frequencies, 342.2i cm-1 (the expected C-N bond scission mode) and 217.5i cm-1 (an out-of-plane bending mode); following the second mode gives the true transition state TS1a with a single imaginary frequency of 361.8i cm-1 and an N-N-C-C dihedral of 14.9 deg. The reactant geometry has bond lengths 1.471, 1.229, 1.471 and 1.538 A (parameters a-d of Table 1). The Woodward-Hoffmann rule is therefore broken for this path. The isomer 6 lies higher in energy than TS1a, so 5 decomposes directly to product without isomerizing.
Other: Two active-space findings, one about adequacy and one about what the space reveals. First, the paper's central claim — that the diazetine decomposition transition state BREAKS Cs symmetry and therefore violates the Woodward-Hoffmann rule — was explicitly stress-tested against the active space and the basis, because it is a surprising result: "one is the set of active electrons and orbitals in the CASSCF space. CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* data are shown in Table 1. The other is the basis set dependence. CASSCF(2,2)/6-311+G(2d,p) data are shown. Even by these examinations, the contrast between C1-symmetry TS1a and Cs-symmetry TS2a was confirmed." So (2,2) is sufficient here and enlarging to (4,4) changes nothing. Second, the natural orbital occupations show why any multiconfigurational treatment was needed at all: TS1a and TS2a have occupations of (1.5006, 0.4994) and (1.5325, 0.4675), i.e. very nearly the (1.5, 0.5) of a pure biradical, so these transition states cannot be described by a single determinant. The important negative result is on the CORRELATION side rather than the space: CASPT2 on this CASSCF reference produced NEGATIVE activation energies and was abandoned, attributed to CASPT2's systematic errors when the number of unpaired electrons changes along the path and to size-consistency problems of the CI ansatz — a documented case where the standard CASSCF-plus-CASPT2 recipe fails on a bond-breaking path and a Brueckner-orbital coupled-cluster correction had to be substituted. Method dependence of the resulting energetics is large where the space is not: reaction energies without thermal corrections for the tetramethyl (parent) system are -48.3 (-58.9) kcal/mol at BCCD(T)/6-31G*, -63.5 (-67.6) at RHF, -49.4 (-50.4) at B3LYP and -51.8 (-60.0) at MP2, while the C-C distance is essentially method-independent at 1.571-1.587 A (1.537-1.545 A).
reference_short: Yamabe & Minato, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 7281
notes: N2 extrusion from the smallest monocyclic azoalkane, diazetine, its tetramethyl derivative, and their three-membered cyclic isomers. Orbital correlation diagrams predict that routes conserving the Cs point group are symmetry allowed; the calculations find that the three-membered isomers obey the Woodward-Hoffmann rule but the diazetines do NOT, and the paper proposes a dual orbital-mixing rule to explain the contrast. No biradical intermediates were located and the 5 -> 6 isomerization channel was found to be absent, so decomposition is concerted. A model dicyanodiazetine (8) was also examined for the orbital-mixing analysis in Table 2, and the tetramethyl three-membered isomer (4) decomposes through TS2b. Geometric parameters are in Table 1 and orbital-energy changes in Table 2.

point_group: Cs (planar structures assumed, 29 degrees of freedom)
geometry_source: CASSCF-optimized ground and excited-state geometries under Cs symmetry (29 degrees of freedom); HF/6-31G(d) and MP2/6-31G(d) ground-state geometries computed for comparison
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2
software: MOLCAS (CASSCF/CASPT2); Gaussian 94 (HF and MP2 geometry optimizations)
basis_set: ANO valence basis contracted C,N,O[4s3p1d]/H[2s], 192 basis functions; supplemented for the Rydberg state with custom 1s1p1d Rydberg sets contracted from 8s8p8d primitives and placed at the average charge centroid of the 1(2A'') pi-hole cation. 6-31G(d) for the comparison HF and MP2 optimizations.
active_space_orbital_description: pi-valence space (denoted 0-10): all 10 pi active orbitals of a'' symmetry holding 12 pi active electrons — the 'pi-CASSCF' wave function — used for the singlet and triplet A' states. Three variants: for the 1,3(A'') n-pi* states the space additionally includes either the oxygen or the nitrogen lone pair as appropriate (denoted 1-10, 14 active electrons); the same spaces with one electron removed (11 and 13 active electrons) give the vertical ionization potentials to the 1(2A'') pi-hole and 1,2(2A') n-hole states; and for the 1A''(pi -> 3s) Rydberg state the pi-valence space is enlarged (denoted 1-12) with an additional a' orbital, 12 active electrons.
active_space_protocol: The ground-state space includes all pi-valence electrons; excited-state geometry optimizations reuse the same active spaces defined for the corresponding vertical excitations. Molecular orbitals for the excited states come from STATE-AVERAGED CASSCF averaging over all states of interest of a given symmetry. The heteroatom lone pairs are deliberately left INACTIVE for the pi-pi* states, justified empirically: "it is found that the occupation numbers are close to 2.0 when they are treated as active". The relative energy of each excited state is referred to a ground-state energy computed with the SAME active space. Carbon, nitrogen and oxygen 1s electrons are frozen in the ground-state HF form and are inactive during the pi-CASSCF geometry optimizations; all electrons except the core are correlated at the CASPT2 level. Oscillator strengths use CASPT2 vertical excitation energies.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, triplet; doublet cations for the ionization potentials
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over all states of interest of each symmetry (counts given in the paper's Table 1)
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet ground state; the HF description of C6H6N2O2 has (30-6) occupied orbitals of (a'-a'') symmetry with the pi orbitals in a''. The vertical absorption spectrum up to 6.9 eV is dominated by three pi-pi* transitions at 4.93 eV (oscillator strength 0.120), 5.40 eV (0.343) and 6.00 eV (0.324); taking 6a'' as HOMO and 7a'' as LUMO, the excitations H->L, H->L+1 and H-1->L are the main contributors to these three A' singlets, with H->L dominating the 3(1A') state which carries the largest oscillator strength. Doubly excited configurations contribute importantly, especially to the 2(1A') state. The low-lying n-pi* excitation is at 5.12 eV (f = 0.0005), mainly the single excitation 30a' -> 7a'' from a lone pair localized on the carbonyl oxygen; the second n-pi* transition, to 2(1A''), is at 6.86 eV with trivially small oscillator strength and promotes an electron from the sigma lone pair of the ring nitrogen. The pi -> 3s Rydberg transition is at 5.47 eV (f = 0.054). Vertical ionization potentials, CASSCF then CASPT2 (MP2-geometry values in parentheses): 1(2A'') pi-hole 7.80 (7.73) -> 8.33 (8.29) eV; 1(2A') nN-hole 9.26 (9.16) -> 10.16 (10.15); 2(2A') nO-hole 9.10 (8.96) -> 10.18 (10.13).
Other: The active space is sized by an occupation-number test rather than by inclusion of everything plausible: the heteroatom lone pairs are kept INACTIVE for the pi-pi* states because "the occupation numbers are close to 2.0 when they are treated as active", and they are switched in only for the n-pi* states that actually need them. Because different states use different spaces, the paper takes the necessary precaution that "the relative energy of each excited state is referred to a ground-state energy computed with the same active space" — without that, the (12,10), (14,11) and Rydberg-enlarged numbers would not be comparable. The revealing sensitivity here is to GEOMETRY rather than to space size, and it is strongly state- and isomer-dependent. Comparing MP2 with CASSCF geometries for the trans isomer, singlet vertical excitation energies shift by up to 0.42 eV at CASSCF and 0.31 eV after the CASPT2 correction, while triplet n-pi* excitations "show huge differences at the CASSCF level (1.01 eV, 0.60 eV), but this disparity largely disappears with the inclusion of dynamical correlation" — so CASPT2 absorbs most of a 1 eV geometry artefact that the bare CASSCF space cannot. For the cis isomer the same comparison gives a quantitatively IDENTICAL spectrum from both geometry sets despite an rms bond-length difference of 0.075 A. Ionization potentials show the same pattern at larger magnitude: CASSCF underestimates them badly and CASPT2 raises them by 0.5-1.3 eV, most dramatically the cis pi-hole value from 7.03 to 8.33 eV. Finally, the wave functions themselves justify the multiconfigurational treatment unevenly between isomers: the trans low-lying pi-pi* states carry an important contribution of doubly excited configurations, especially the 2(1A') state, whereas the two lowest pi-pi* singlets of the cis isomer are each dominated by a SINGLE configuration (H -> L and H-1 -> L), with doubles becoming important only in its 3(1A') and 4(1A') states at 23% and 38%.
reference_short: Page, Merchan, Serrano-Andres et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 9864
notes: CASPT2 study of the lowest excited states of urocanic acid, the skin chromophore implicated in UV-induced immunosuppression, in both geometric isomers. Ground-state geometries were optimized at CASSCF, HF/6-31G(d) and MP2/6-31G(d) for comparison (Table 3), and excited-state geometries at CASSCF (Table 4); the discussion is restricted to the CASSCF geometries because MP2 overestimates conjugation, with deviations between the correlated methods as large as 0.03 A in the highly delocalized regions and around the carboxylic acid group. Vertical ionization potentials at both geometries are in Table 2, vertical excitation energies with oscillator strengths, dipole moments and transition moment directions in Table 5, and CASSCF wave function contributions in Table 6. The lowest ionization involves a pi-hole, so the lowest singlet Rydberg state is 1A''(pi -> 3s); its position well above the intense valence transitions in both isomers means Rydberg states play only a minor role in the photochemistry.

method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2
software: MOLCAS (CASSCF/CASPT2); Gaussian 94 (HF and MP2 geometry optimizations)
basis_set: ANO valence basis contracted C,N,O[4s3p1d]/H[2s], 192 basis functions; supplemented for the Rydberg state with custom 1s1p1d Rydberg sets contracted from 8s8p8d primitives and placed at the average charge centroid of the 1(2A'') pi-hole cation. 6-31G(d) for the comparison HF and MP2 optimizations.

compound_name: CO2+ radical cation, predissociation of the C(2 Sigma-g+) state
point_group: D-infinity-h for the X, A, B and C states, treated in the D2h subgroup; C2v for the Renner-Teller-split 1(4Pi-u) components (C2 axis bisecting the OCO angle, denoted C2v(b)); C-infinity-v for the 1(4 Sigma-g-) state and throughout the O-loss dissociation, treated in the C2v(a) subgroup with the C2 axis along a C-O bond
geometry_source: CASPT2 geometry optimization for all six states, with CASSCF geometry optimization and frequency analysis performed alongside to confirm the stationary points; vertical energies computed at the experimental ground-state CO2 geometry
method: CASPT2 based on CASSCF; CASSCF minimum energy crossing point (MECP) searches with CASSCF spin-orbit coupling evaluation at the MECPs
basis_set: Contracted atomic natural orbital ANO-L, C(5s4p3d2f)/O(5s4p3d2f)
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space: 15 active electrons in the 3(sigma-g+)-5(sigma-g+), 2(sigma-u+)-4(sigma-u+), 1(pi-u)-2(pi-u) and 1(pi-g) orbitals of D-infinity-h. Written in the D2h subgroup ordering (Ag, B3u, B2u, B1g, B1u, B2g, B3g, Au) the space is (32203110); in the C2v(b) ordering (A1, B1, B2, A2) it is (5241); and for the O-loss dissociation, where the same full valence space comprises the 4(sigma+)-9(sigma+) and 1(pi)-3(pi) orbitals of C-infinity-v, it is (6330) in the C2v(a) ordering. The reference HF/6-31G configuration of neutral CO2 is (1su+)2(1sg+)2(2sg+)2(3sg+)2(2su+)2(4sg+)2(3su+)2(1pu)4(1pg)4(2pu)0(5sg+)0(4su+)0.
active_space_protocol: Full valence active spaces are used throughout, for the CO2+ ion and for every related species in the dissociation asymptotes (the CO molecule, the CO+ and O+ ions, and the O atom), so reactant and product energies are computed on a consistent footing. CASPT2 computes the first-order wave function and second-order energy in the FULL space. The reliability check reported is that the weight of the CASSCF reference function in the first-order wave function exceeded 0.85 in every CASPT2 calculation. Adiabatic T0 values are CASPT2 energies corrected with CASSCF zero-point energies. MECPs were located at the CASSCF level in C-infinity-v, Cs and C2v symmetries, with spin-orbit couplings evaluated there.
nroots_per_mult: six states computed in total: X(2 Pi-g), A(2 Pi-u), B(2 Sigma-u+), C(2 Sigma-g+), 1(4 Sigma-g-) and 1(4 Pi-u)
electronic_structure_description: Six electronic states of CO2+ were computed. CASPT2 vertical energies Tv' relative to X(2 Pi-g): A(2 Pi-u) 3.73 eV, B(2 Sigma-u+) 4.14 eV, C(2 Sigma-g+) 5.33 eV — respectively 0.09, 0.16 and 0.28 eV below the experimental values — plus 1(4 Pi-u) at 8.26 eV and 1(4 Sigma-g-) at 10.22 eV, for which no experimental values exist. CASPT2 adiabatic T0 values: A(2 Pi-u) 3.49 eV, B(2 Sigma-u+) 4.15 eV, C(2 Sigma-g+) 5.45 eV, respectively 0.04, 0.14 and 0.15 eV below experiment, with C-O bond lengths 0.002-0.008 A shorter than the experimental values. Geometries: the X, A, B and C states are all linear (D-infinity-h); Renner-Teller splitting of 1(4 Pi-u) gives two C2v states, 1(4A1) and 1(4B1), with OCO angles near 110 deg and a large T0 splitting between them; and 1(4 Sigma-g-) has a C-infinity-v geometry with one long C-O bond of 2.021 A, so it is not purely repulsive. The X, A, B and C states correlate with the first, second, second, third, third and fourth dissociation limits. CASPT2 sum energies for the O-loss product groups are 5.29, 5.84, 7.81 and 8.39 eV, within 0.20 eV of the experimental values.
Other: This is a full-valence study, so the interest is not in space size but in what full valence buys and where the reference still strains. The same full valence prescription is applied not only to CO2+ but to every asymptotic fragment — CO, CO+, O+ and O — which is what makes the dissociation energetics internally consistent: the CASPT2 sum energy of the 1(4 Sigma-g-) asymptote products (5.29 eV) matches the separately computed CASPT2 energy of that asymptote (5.42 eV), and the O + CO+ product energies (5.86 and 5.81 eV) agree with the sum energy 5.84 eV. Reference quality is reported rather than assumed: the CASSCF reference weight in the first-order wave function exceeded 0.85 in every CASPT2 calculation. The active space had to be relabelled three times for the three symmetry regimes traversed — (32203110) in D2h for the linear states, (5241) in C2v(b) for the Renner-Teller-bent quartet components, and (6330) in C2v(a) along the O-loss coordinate — the kind of bookkeeping that has to be right for a path spanning changing symmetry, and the paper spells it out explicitly. The residual CASPT2 error is systematic and one-signed: every computed Tv' and T0 falls BELOW experiment, by 0.09-0.28 eV vertically and 0.04-0.15 eV adiabatically, and every C-O bond length is 0.002-0.008 A short. The paper also criticizes earlier work on exactly this ground, noting that the CASSCF potential energy curves of ref 5 "did not well converge to the dissociation product groups" — a failure the full-valence-everywhere protocol here is designed to avoid.
reference_short: Meng, Huang et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 12825
notes: Tests the predissociation mechanism proposed for the C(2 Sigma-g+) state of CO2+ by Praet et al. (1982), against later experiments by Liu et al. and Yang et al. All the MECPs required by that mechanism — including the C(2 Sigma-g+)/1(4 Pi-u) (1 4B1) crossing — were located, and the spin-orbit couplings computed there are not small, so the calculations support the Praet mechanism. The paper concludes that the C state populated in the [1+1] photodissociation experiments predissociates through one channel while that populated in the earlier VUV-PFI-PE experiments predissociates through another. CASSCF frequencies were computed to confirm the nature of the stationary points but are not reported, being judged insufficiently accurate. O-loss dissociation potential energy curves were computed for all six states.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 with the first-order wave function and second-order energy computed in the full space

ligand_set: beta-diiminato (nacnac-type) chelate plus a phenylimido (NPh) ligand
point_group: C2v (states classified in the four irreducible representations A1, A2, B1, B2)
geometry_source: PW91 DFT-optimized ground-state geometry for the vertical excitation energies; the Co-N(imido) distance was subsequently reoptimized at the CASPT2 level (1.632 A, against 1.653 A from PW91), and calculations were also run at the PW91-optimized 3B2 geometry with a Co-N(imido) distance of 1.70 A
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 with Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals (CD-CASPT2); DFT with several functionals for comparison
basis_set: Generally contracted ANO-RCC basis sets including scalar relativistic effects. Smaller VDZP set: Co 5s4p2d1f, N/C 3s2p1d, H 2s, 406 functions total. Larger VTZP set: Co 6s5p3d2f1g, N/C 4s3p2d1f, H 2s1p, 869 functions total, used only with the Cholesky approximation.
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic effects included at all levels through the ANO-RCC basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: (10in10): the five Co 3d orbitals plus the two pi orbitals (pi-x and pi-y) of the imido nitrogen, with three 4d orbitals added to account for the DOUBLE SHELL effect of the doubly occupied 3d orbitals (3dz2, 3dyz and 3dx2-y2). CASSCF natural orbitals for the 1A1 ground state are shown in the paper's Figure 2, with the three weakly occupied 4d orbitals omitted from the plot.
active_space_protocol: Several active spaces were tested before settling on (10in10). A larger space including the lone-pair orbitals of the diiminato nitrogens was tried and rejected on occupation numbers: they came out "very close to two, which shows that they are not needed in the active space as long as the electronic states of interest do not involve charge-transfer excitations". Starting orbitals came from an SCF calculation whose occupied and virtual orbitals were then separately localized within each symmetry by the Cholesky localization technique, which "considerably simplified the selection of the physically appropriate orbitals for the active space", especially among the virtuals. Single-root CASSCF was used where possible; state-averaged CASSCF where more than one root was needed, and in some cases a second state was obtained by locking the occupied-orbital count. In the CASPT2 step all 132 valence electrons plus the Co 3s and 3p electrons were correlated, using the standard IPEA Hamiltonian and an imaginary level shift of 0.1 to remove weak intruder states.
nroots_per_mult: the two lowest singlet, triplet and quintet states in each of the four irreducible representations — 24 electronic states in all
electronic_structure_description: Diamagnetic 1A1 ground state with configuration (3dz2)2(3dx2-y2)2(3dyz)2(b1)2(b2)2. Its bonding is unusual: there is a Co-N(imido) DOUBLE bond made of two pi-bonding orbitals but NO net sigma bond, because double occupancy of 3dz2 is energetically preferred over using it for sigma bonding; moving electrons out of 3dz2 into b1 or b2 would create a sigma bond at the cost of the pi bonds, and some low-lying excited states (e.g. 2 3B1) do exactly that, giving a partial sigma bond and weaker pi bonding. The ground-state wave function is somewhat multiconfigurational, with antibonding natural orbital occupations of 0.13 and 0.22. Vertical excitation energies at the PW91 geometry (CASPT2-optimized Co-N distance values in parentheses), in eV: 3B2 (3dx2-y2 -> b2*) 0.14 (0.16); 3B1 (3dxy -> b2*) 0.24 (0.26); 5A2 (3dx2-y2 3dz2 -> b1* b2*) 0.52 (0.57); 5A1 (3dz2 3dxy -> (b2*)(b2*)) 0.60 (0.65); 3A2 (3dz2 3dxy -> (b2*)2) 1.11 (1.19); 5B1 (3dx2-y2 3dxy -> (b1*)(b2*)) 1.64 (1.77); 5B2 (3dxy b2 -> b1* b2*) 1.85 (1.99); 3A1 (b2 -> (b2*)) 1.85 (1.93). All 24 computed states lie below 4 eV of the ground state. The two lowest triplets are separated from the ground state by only 0.14 and 0.24 eV — within the error limits of CASPT2 — so reoptimizing their geometries could well change the ordering.
Other: The (10in10) space is built around the double-shell effect: beyond the five Co 3d orbitals and the two imido-nitrogen pi orbitals, THREE 4d orbitals are added specifically to correlate the doubly occupied 3dz2, 3dyz and 3dx2-y2. The space was then bounded from above by an occupation test rather than by cost — adding the diiminato nitrogen lone pairs gave occupation numbers "very close to two, which shows that they are not needed in the active space as long as the electronic states of interest do not involve charge-transfer excitations", an important scope condition since a charge-transfer state would invalidate the choice. A methodological point specific to this paper is that Cholesky LOCALIZATION of the SCF orbitals, applied separately to occupieds and virtuals within each symmetry, is what made the active orbitals identifiable at all in a system this size; the authors say it "considerably simplified the selection of the physically appropriate orbitals", especially among the virtuals. The remaining sensitivity is geometric rather than orbital: reoptimizing the Co-N(imido) distance at CASPT2 shortens it from 1.653 to 1.632 A and raises every excitation energy by 0.02-0.14 eV, and the triplet-singlet gaps of 0.14 and 0.24 eV are explicitly stated to lie within CASPT2's own error bars, so the state ordering is not established. Cost figures are given for the Cholesky approximation: with the 406-function basis, generating Cholesky vectors took 56 minutes against 151 minutes for the full integral set, and the 869-function calculation took 3.5 hours.
reference_short: Aquilante, Malmqvist, Pedersen, Ghosh & Roos, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2008, 4, 694
notes: Introduces Cholesky-decomposition-based CASPT2 (CD-CASPT2) as a route to multiconfigurational calculations on systems too large for conventional integral handling, demonstrated on the spin-state energetics of a low-coordinate cobalt(III) imido complex. The model is a slightly simplified version of the experimentally characterized CoIII(nacnac)(NAd), where nacnac is the anion of 2,4-bis(2,6-disubstituted-phenylimido)pentane; the S = 0 ground state and its (3dz2)2(3dx2-y2)2(3dxy)2 configuration had been assigned by DFT. The chemical question is how far the triplet and quintet states lie above the experimentally observed diamagnetic ground state, as a calibration of DFT spin-state energetics. Of the functionals tested, best agreement with the ab initio results comes from a modified B3LYP containing a reduced 15% Hartree-Fock exchange. Cholesky thresholds of 1e-4 and 1e-8 were both tested against conventional integrals with the smaller basis. The molecular formula is not transcribed because the paper specifies the model only through Figure 1 and the nacnac abbreviation, without writing one.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 correlating all 132 valence electrons plus Co 3s and 3p, with the standard IPEA Hamiltonian and an imaginary level shift of 0.1

compound_name: Ethylene — twisted-pyramidalized and ethylidene S1/S0 conical intersections
geometry_source: MECI geometries optimized at the CAS, MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI levels by the paper's penalty-constrained scheme
method: State-averaged CASSCF, MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI minimal-energy conical intersection (MECI) optimization by a new sequential penalty-constrained scheme with a smoothing function, requiring no derivative coupling vectors
basis_set: 6-31G** unless otherwise noted (6-31G* for the acrolein MDCI work)
active_space_orbital_description: SA-2-CAS(2/2): two active electrons in two active orbitals, state-averaged over the two lowest singlets. The same (2/2) reference space is used for the MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI calculations.
active_space_protocol: MECI geometries optimized separately at CAS, MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI levels on the same SA-2-CAS(2/2) reference, so the three can be compared directly. All valence orbitals are correlated. MRSDCI optimizations were carried out without analytic gradients, which are not implemented in MolPro.
electronic_structure_description: Energies in eV relative to the Franck-Condon point of each respective level of theory, given as CAS / MS-CASPT2 / MRSDCI for S0 and S1. Franck-Condon point: S1 at 10.27 / 8.67 / 9.33. Twisted-pyramidalized MECI: S0 5.62 / 4.81 / 5.11 and S1 5.65 / 4.82 / 5.14. Ethylidene MECI: S0 4.47 / 4.71 / 4.75 and S1 4.49 / 4.73 / 4.76. The two MECIs therefore REORDER between methods — CAS places ethylidene well below twisted-pyramidalized, while MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI place it slightly above, making the two nearly degenerate at MS-CASPT2.
Other: This paper exists because MECI optimization normally needs derivative coupling vectors, which are unavailable for MS-CASPT2; the new penalty-constrained scheme removes that requirement and so allows the SAME small reference space to be optimized at CAS, MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI and the three compared directly. The result is that geometries agree far better than energies. For ethylene and formaldiminium at SA-2-CAS(2/2) the MECI geometries are essentially identical across the three methods, the sole exception being the twisted formaldiminium MECI, where CASSCF and MRSDCI give a purely twisted structure while CASPT2 gives a slightly pyramidalized one — read as a sign of a flat intersection seam rather than a real disagreement. Energies move much more: the ethylene Franck-Condon S1 excitation drops from 10.27 eV (CAS) to 8.67 (MS-CASPT2) and 9.33 (MRSDCI), and the twisted-pyramidalized and ethylidene MECIs REORDER — CAS puts ethylidene 1.15 eV below twist-pyr, MS-CASPT2 and MRSDCI put it 0.10 and 0.36 eV ABOVE. The most consequential case is stilbene, where at SA-3-CAS(2/2) the S1/S0 MECI sits slightly above the S1 minimum (<0.1 eV) but MS-CASPT2 makes the MECI the absolute minimum of the S1 surface, which "might imply a large difference in the excited-state lifetimes which would be predicted by CAS and MS-CASPT2". A related diagnosis is offered for butadiene: pyramidalization seen in the S2/S1 MECI at CAS level "may be related to the unbalanced treatment of charge transfer states due to the neglect of dynamic electron correlation in CAS". Two practical caveats run through the work: the reference spaces are deliberately minimal — (2/2) for ethylene, formaldiminium, stilbene and the GFP chromophore — and for stilbene and the GFP chromophore 36 orbitals were left UNCORRELATED in the MS-CASPT2 step to contain the cost, so those numbers are not full-valence MS-CASPT2. MRSDCI optimizations were performed without analytic gradients, which exist in the literature but are not implemented in MolPro.

notes: Introduces a method for optimizing minimal-energy conical intersections (MECIs) and minimal-distance conical intersections (MDCIs) without derivative coupling vectors, using a sequential penalty-constrained optimization with a smoothing function, and applies it to MS-CASPT2 for the first time. compound_name: Potassium trimer K3 (doublet), on the surface of argon clusters
point_group: C2v (obtuse isosceles global minimum, 2B2); scans performed along the Qx normal coordinate at fixed Qs
geometry_source: UCCSD(T) ground-state scan with further geometry optimization locates the absolute minimum at an obtuse isosceles C2v geometry with bond length b = 4.322 A and bond angle 74.0 deg (Qs = 4.59 A, Qx = -0.61 A, Qy = 0); the CASSCF scans of the excited states are taken over Qx with Qs fixed at that global-minimum value of 4.59 A
method: CASSCF (Werner-Knowles) scans of the lowest 12 electronic states, with CASPT2 used to validate the atomic excitation energies; UCCSD(T) for the ground-state surface
basis_set: Relativistic small-core effective core potential basis ECP10MDF of the Stuttgart/Cologne group, augmented with three additional diffuse (s,p,d) functions generated by the even-tempered scheme in MOLPRO from the ratio of the two smallest original exponents; fully uncontracted this is (12s,12p,6d,3f)
active_space_orbital_description: [3,23]-CASSCF: the three valence electrons of the potassium trimer distributed over 23 active orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A [3,23]-CASSCF scan over the Qx coordinate at fixed Qs = 4.59 A generates the lowest 12 electronic states. The finite-active-space error is estimated EXPLICITLY and then corrected: scanning Qs out to 30 A (with Qx = Qy = 0), the trimer states correlating to the 4P atomic asymptote converge to 11 550 cm-1, which is 1493 cm-1 BELOW the spin-orbit-averaged experimental atomic value, so that difference is added back to all states except 1(2B2) and 1(2A1) to force consistency with the experimental asymptote. Basis-set accuracy was gauged separately on atomic K and on K2: UCCSD(T) reproduces the atomic polarizability (290.7 against an experimental 290.2 +/- 8), the singlet K2 bond length (3.93 A, exact) and its binding energy (4299 against 4450 cm-1), with counterpoise BSSE correction; and CASSCF with CASPT2 corrections reproduces the atomic 4s-4p, 4s-5s and 4s-3d excitations to within +5, -73 and +76 cm-1 of the spin-orbit-averaged experimental values.
nroots_per_mult: 12 (the lowest 12 electronic states scanned)
electronic_structure_description: Doublet alkali trimer with a Jahn-Teller-distorted C2v ground state, 2B2, at an obtuse isosceles geometry (b = 4.322 A, angle 74.0 deg). A second C2v stationary point lies 165 cm-1 above the absolute minimum at b = 4.783 A and angle 51.8 deg but is a saddle point on the three-dimensional surface. The computed level structure of the lowest 12 doublet states along Qx closely resembles published Na3 results. Assignments of the observed cluster-beam depletion spectrum, observed versus calculated: 3(2A1) below 11 000 cm-1 / 10 230 cm-1; 1(2A2) 11 350 / 11 280 cm-1; 4(2A1) 12 400 / 12 690 cm-1; 3(2B2) 13 470 / 13 830 cm-1. The electronic states of alkali dimers and trimers scale between Na and K by a factor of 1.302 derived from the atomic 3s-3p and 4s-4p excitation energies, and the scaled Na3 depletion spectrum matches the measured K3 spectrum in both structure and peak intensity.
Other: An unusually explicit and quantitative treatment of finite-active-space error. Rather than converging the space, the authors MEASURE its residual error against a known limit: scanning the symmetric-stretch coordinate out to 30 A, the [3,23]-CASSCF states correlating to the 4P atomic asymptote converge to 11 550 cm-1, 1493 cm-1 below the spin-orbit-averaged experimental atomic value, and that shortfall is taken as the active-space error. They then correct for it by hand, adding 1493 cm-1 to every state EXCEPT 1(2B2) and 1(2A1) — so the excited-state energies reported are shifted values, not raw CASSCF output, and the two lowest states are on a different footing from the other ten. The 23-orbital space is large but carries only three electrons, so its cost is modest while its asymptotic behaviour is still not exact. The basis rather than the space was validated in the usual way, on atomic K and K2, where CASSCF plus CASPT2 reproduces the atomic 4s-4p, 4s-5s and 4s-3d excitations to +5, -73 and +76 cm-1 — errors an order of magnitude smaller than the trimer's asymptotic shortfall, which locates the problem in the molecular active space rather than in the one-electron basis. The authors are candid that the resulting spectral assignment is provisional: agreement with experiment is good, but "the possibility of cluster-induced shifts has of course to be considered; thus alternative assignments should not be excluded", since the argon cluster perturbs the energies by amounts comparable to the differences being used to assign.
reference_short: Callegari et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 12377
notes: Combined experimental and theoretical study of potassium-doped argon clusters (average size about 2000 atoms) produced by supersonic expansion and doped with alkali metal by a pickup technique, investigated by beam-depletion spectroscopy. Spectral contributions are attributed to the potassium atom, dimer and doublet trimer residing on the cluster surface; the CASSCF calculations were performed specifically to support the trimer assignment. The paper notes that a definite assignment is not possible because the energy shifts due to perturbation by the argon cluster are comparable to the spacings involved. Molecular dynamics with pairwise K-Ar and Ar-Ar potentials (Lennard-Jones and Morse parameters in Table 1) models the cluster. Density functional results of Martins et al. for K3 give b = 4.0 A and 77 deg for the minimum and b = 5.4 A, 41 deg for the saddle point with a 160 cm-1 separation, close to this work's 165 cm-1. Full details of the electronic structure calculations were to be published separately.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 used to validate atomic excitation energies; the trimer excited-state scans are CASSCF with an empirical asymptotic shift

ligand_set: two bridging sulfides (S*) and four SCH3 thiolate terminal ligands
geometry_source: RISM-CASSCF and RISM-MRMP optimized geometries in DMSO solution; the MRMP Fe-S* and Fe-S distances come out 0.1-0.2 A shorter than the CASSCF ones
method: RISM-CASSCF (reference interaction site model self-consistent field) with MRMP multireference second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory; MC-QDPT where more than one state is treated
basis_set: Stevens et al. effective core potentials and basis sets for Fe and S, augmented with diffuse s and p functions on S, giving contracted (8s8p6d)/[4s4p3d] for Fe and (5s5p1d)/[4s4p1d] for S; 6-31G for C and H
relativistic_treatment: Effective core potentials of Stevens et al. on Fe and S
active_space_orbital_description: Two spaces are used. The 10-orbital space consists of orbitals mainly localized on the Fe 3d orbitals. The 13-orbital space adds three orbitals mainly composed of bridging-sulfide S* 3p atomic orbitals: (py + py) of b2u symmetry, (pz + pz) of b1u and (pz - pz) of b3g.
active_space_protocol: The 10-orbital Fe-3d space is used for the geometry optimizations of both oxidation states; the space is enlarged to 13 by adding the three S* 3p combinations "to obtain more reliable energy estimates". For the reduced state's low-spin geometry optimization, CASSCF was run with 10 SYMMETRY-BROKEN active orbitals even at a D2h geometry. The MRMP step uses the intruder state avoidance method with a parameter of 0.02, and the authors note that changing this parameter little affected the results. Solvation is treated by RISM with the hypernetted-chain closure; partial charges on solute sites come from grid points generated by the Spackman method, and Lennard-Jones parameters for Fe had to be substituted since none were available.
multiplicities_studied: the full spin ladder from S = 0 to S = 5 arising from antiferromagnetic coupling of two high-spin Fe3+ centres
electronic_structure_description: Two high-spin Fe3+ (3d5) centres antiferromagnetically coupled, giving a ladder of spin states from S = 0 to S = 5. The exchange coupling |J| extracted from the spin-state energies is 53 cm-1 at RISM-CASSCF and 203 cm-1 at MRMP; taking instead the S = 1 to S = 0 energy difference gives 268 cm-1. Experimental |J| values for comparison are 180 cm-1 (spinach ferredoxin), 182 cm-1 (Spirulina maxima) and 149 cm-1 (a synthetic analogue), so the MRMP result is in the right range while the CASSCF one is far too small. Energy gaps between the bonding and antibonding combinations of each d orbital pair, estimated from the CASSCF canonical orbitals of this oxidized state, are 1.11, 2.76, 1.01, 0.30 and 3.55 eV for the dxy, dyz, dzx, dx2-z2 and dy2 pairs respectively — the dx2-z2 gap being the smallest and the dy2 gap the largest.
Other: Enlarging the space from 10 Fe-3d orbitals to 13 by adding the three bridging-sulfide S* 3p combinations changes the electronic description qualitatively, not just quantitatively. With 10 active orbitals the ground state of the reduced cluster has the (dx2-z2 + dx2-z2) orbital occupied by 2 electrons and every other active orbital by 1, while the 2Ag state has the (dx2-z2 - dx2-z2) orbital doubly occupied — a fully valence-localized picture. With 13 orbitals BOTH dx2-z2 occupation numbers become 1.5, because the S = 1/2 wave function is a linear combination of the Fe2+Fe3+ and Fe3+Fe2+ localized configurations at D2h geometry and "the mixing of S* orbitals with Fe 3d ones is allowed so as to stabilize the Fe ions by including the S* orbitals into the active space". So whether this cluster looks valence-trapped or delocalized is an artefact of leaving the bridging sulfur out. Worse for the smaller space, the CASSCF wave function is UNSTABLE with respect to symmetry breaking of the orbitals: relaxing the D2h restriction lowers the 10-orbital CASSCF energy by 2.1 eV and produces two dx2-z2 orbitals localized on different Fe atoms with occupations of 2 and 1 — an enormous variational collapse that the symmetry-constrained calculation hides. Dynamic correlation is separately decisive for the spin ladder: CASSCF spin-state gaps are much smaller than MRMP ones "because the dynamic correlation energy becomes larger with decreasing S", and the exchange coupling |J| moves from 53 cm-1 at RISM-CASSCF to 203 cm-1 at MRMP, the latter comparable to experimental ferredoxin values of 149-182 cm-1. The same pattern holds for the redox thermodynamics, where "the CASSCF redox potentials are considerably small" against MC-QDPT values of 2.72-2.87 eV.

point_group: C2v for the localized low-spin (S = 1/2) optimized geometry; D2h for the delocalized high-spin (S = 9/2) geometry

method: RISM-CASSCF (reference interaction site model self-consistent field) with MRMP multireference second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory; MC-QDPT where more than one state is treated

compound_name: anti-Orthogonene (1-a), tetracyclo[8.2.2.0(2,7).0(3,10)]tetradecene-2(3) — a nearly orthogonally twisted alkene
point_group: D2 for the idealized anti stereoisomer (the symmetry label refers to an idealized symmetric structure)
geometry_source: CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* geometry optimizations followed by frequency calculations at the same level to confirm the nature of each stationary point and to obtain zero-point energies; uncorrected ZPE added to the raw energy
method: CASSCF(4,4) geometry optimizations and frequencies, with CASSCF-MP2 single points at the CASSCF geometries
software: Gaussian 03 (structures and frequencies visualized with GaussView 3.0)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(4,4): occupied orbitals C1-C5 (sigma) and C1-C2 (pi), with the unoccupied C1-C5 (sigma*) and C1-C2 (pi*) orbitals available for excitation. The cation uses the same four orbitals with one electron fewer, CASSCF(3,4).
active_space_protocol: The space is chosen from the assumed reaction: because twisted alkenes are known to isomerize to carbenes by a 1,2-alkyl shift, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the MIGRATING C1-C5 bond are included alongside the pi and pi* of the twisted double bond, so one (4,4) space spans reactant, transition state and carbene product. CASSCF was chosen as "the standard one for treating singlet diradicals" since twisting the double bond uncouples the two pi electrons. Dynamic correlation is added by Gaussian's CASSCF-MP2 procedure at the CASSCF geometries; the author acknowledges this "can be unreliable in some cases compared to the more common CASPT2N method" but validates it against the ethene torsional barrier and the rearrangement of bicyclo[2.1.1]hex-1(2)-ene to 2-carbenabicyclo[2.1.1]hexane. The vertical ionization energy comes from comparing the CASSCF(4,4) neutral with the CASSCF(3,4) cation at the neutral geometry, with no ZPE correction.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet diradicaloid arising from a double bond twisted through 88.2 deg, which almost completely uncouples the two pi electrons. The C1-C2 'double bond' length of 1.454 A is only slightly shorter than the 1.48 A sp2-sp2 central single bond of 1,3-butadiene, and its computed stretching frequencies of 1499-1519 cm-1 (coupled to C-H bending) compare with 1815 cm-1 computed for tetramethylethylene at CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G* with a C=C length of 1.350 A; scaling by the experimental 1650/1815 = 0.91 predicts a stretch near 1374 cm-1 for this compound. The singlet and triplet states are essentially degenerate: relative to the singlet, the triplet lies -0.18 kJ/mol at CASSCF and -1.2 kJ/mol at CASMP2 (absolute values with ZPE: singlet -541.33563 and triplet -541.33570 hartree at CASSCF/6-31G*; -543.16878 and -543.16924 at CASMP2//CASSCF). Rearrangement to the carbene 3c proceeds through transition state 2t with a barrier of about 200 kJ/mol, the carbene lying roughly 95-150 kJ/mol below 1-a (-150.1 kJ/mol at one level). The vertical ionization energy is 0.19364 hartree or 5.3 eV — comparable to lithium and sodium and far below the 8.3-8.8 eV typical of alkenes — a direct consequence of the uncoupled p orbitals.
Other: The (4,4) space is small but purpose-built rather than minimal: it deliberately pairs the pi/pi* of the twisted double bond with the sigma/sigma* of the C1-C5 bond that migrates in the 1,2-alkyl shift, so a single space describes the alkene, the transition state and the carbene product on one footing — the reason a (2,2) pi-only space would not have sufficed for this reaction path. The space is also what makes the singlet-triplet question answerable at all, since twisting to 88 deg produces a singlet diradical that no closed-shell method describes; the two states come out degenerate to within 0.2 kJ/mol at CASSCF and 1.2 kJ/mol at CASMP2, well inside the error of either method, so the multiplicity is genuinely undetermined by these calculations rather than resolved by them. The author is explicit about the weak point of the correlation treatment: Gaussian's CASSCF-MP2 "can be unreliable in some cases compared to the more common CASPT2N method", and rather than assert otherwise he validates it on two external cases — the ethene torsional barrier and a known twisted-alkene-to-carbene rearrangement — before trusting it here. The correction it applies is nonetheless large enough to matter for the chemistry: the bare CASSCF barrier of roughly 200 kJ/mol and the carbene stability of 95-150 kJ/mol below the alkene bracket a range wide enough that the synthetic verdict rests on the perturbative step, not on the CASSCF surface alone.
reference_short: Lewars, J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 9827
notes: Orthogonene is the highly twisted alkene proposed by Jeffrey and Maier, who attempted its synthesis and performed semiempirical calculations two decades earlier. It can exist as several stereoisomers differing in the relative orientations of the bridgehead C-H bonds: the syn ('up-up/up-up') isomer 1-s has C2 symmetry and a B3LYP/6-31G* double-bond torsion of 83 deg and was concluded in earlier work to rearrange with a very low barrier to a carbene or possibly a cyclopropane; this paper shows the ANTI ('up-up/down-down') isomer 1-a is far more stable, with a ~200 kJ/mol rearrangement barrier, making it a realistic synthetic objective. The syn isomer was not treated with CASSCF here, so no row is entered for it. The near-degeneracy and the low-symmetry distortion are attributed to singlet diradical character imposing a Jahn-Teller-type distortion. Computed sp2-sp3 C-C stretches fall at about 1240-1280 cm-1 and sp3-sp3 stretches at about 800-1100 cm-1, with a framework breathing mode at 746 cm-1 that also stretches the double bond. Structures and relative energies are in Figure 4 and Table 1, singlet/triplet energies in Table 2.
correlation_correction: CASSCF-MP2 (Gaussian implementation) single points at the CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* geometries

compound_name: Thymine monomer — reference for the pi-stacked dimer excited states
geometry_source: Monomer geometry; excitation energies at large separation serve as the asymptotic reference for the dimer scans
method: CASSCF; CIS, CIS(2), EOM-CCSD and TDDFT (LSDA, B3LYP, PBE1PBE) used alongside for comparison
software: GAMESS (CIS and CASSCF); Gaussian 03 (TDDFT); Priroda (CIS(2)); NWChem (EOM-CCSD)
basis_set: 6-31G(d), omitting the p polarization functions on hydrogen since they were found to have minimal effect on excitation energies
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(8,6) for the monomer: pi orbitals together with a lone pair on one of the oxygens (nO), the latter included because it is known to be involved in the lowest excited state of thymine.
active_space_protocol: A (8,6) space is used for the isolated monomer and is doubled to (16,12) for the dimer, so the dimer space is exactly two monomer spaces and the monomer excitation energies appear as the large-R limit of the dimer curves. The paper uses the (m,n) convention in which m is the number of electrons and n the number of orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet excited states of the isolated thymine base, computed as the R -> infinity limit of the dimer scans at every level of theory. Oscillator strengths and excitation energies at various levels for comparison: CASSCF/6-31G(d) gives 4.7640 eV with oscillator strength 0.6299, against EOM-CCSD/6-31G(d) 3.2020 eV (0.2239), CIS(2)/cc-pVDZ 3.5609 eV (0.2824), CIS(2)/cc-pVDZ+diff 3.5886 eV (0.2749), CIS/aug-cc-pVDZ 4.1146 eV (0.0481 for the bright S1), TD-LSDA 1.9546 eV (0.0670), TD-B3LYP 2.5815 eV (0.1282) and TD-PBE1PBE 2.7079 eV (0.1449). Literature values quoted for the same quantity include CASSCF/CASPT2 0.17, CASPT2 0.334, CC2 0.182, CCSD 0.222 and TD-B3LYP 0.1388. CASSCF therefore overshoots the pi-pi* excitation energy by more than 1.5 eV relative to EOM-CCSD and roughly triples the oscillator strength.
Other: This paper is a candid account of a small active space being the limiting factor. CASSCF places the pi-pi* states "much higher in energy ... since dynamical correlation is not included, and only a limited active space is used", and its dimer binding energy comes out similar to bare CIS and smaller than CIS(2) — the authors' explanation being that "nondynamical correlation will not compensate for the lack of dynamical correlation", a useful negative result about what a CASSCF-only treatment buys. Against that, the (16,12) space delivers something no single-reference method in the comparison can: an extra DOUBLY EXCITED state in which both thymine molecules are excited simultaneously, appearing as S5 for R > 5.5 A and S4 for R < 5.5 A. That state has been assigned elsewhere as responsible for the thymine dimer photochemical pathway, and "since this is a doubly excited state it cannot be predicted by the single reference methods used here". Its energy, however, is not reliable at this level — "in our CASSCF results the small active space and low level of theory do not allow for accurate assessment of this energy" — so the space is adequate to reveal the state's existence and position qualitatively but not to quantify it. A second structural result the space does get right is that the n-pi* states show no coupling at any separation (S1 and S2 remain degenerate at all R) while the pi-pi* states split, which is the physical content of the coupling analysis. BSSE corrections were deliberately omitted throughout, justified on the grounds that the effect largely cancels in the excited-state energy differences of interest; literature estimates for a cytosine dimer put ground-state BSSE at about 0.2 eV but the ground-state to S1 difference below 0.03 eV.
reference_short: Kozak, Kistler et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2010, 114, 1674
notes: Study of singlet excited states of two pi-stacked thymine molecules and their splittings due to electronic coupling, as a model for how excitation delocalizes between stacked bases in DNA — relevant because excited-state lifetimes in DNA differ from those of the isolated monomers. Energies were scanned as a function of the interplane separation R with several methods (CIS, CIS(2), EOM-CCSD, TDDFT and CASSCF) so their performance could be compared; CIS(2) turns out to give results very similar to EOM-CCSD, and adding diffuse functions matters more than the extra correlation in CCSD relative to CIS(2). Excited states of cytosine and adenine pi-stacked dimers were also obtained for a broader picture, but the CASSCF treatment reported here covers thymine. The coupling is very sensitive to the relative position and orientation of the bases, implying wide variation in the degree of excitation delocalization in natural DNA. Binding energies on the lowest pi-pi* state vary strongly by method: 0.1 eV at CIS (both basis sets), 0.66 and 0.81 eV at CIS(2)/cc-pVDZ and CIS(2)/cc-pVDZ+diff, and 0.31 eV at EOM-CCSD.

method: CASSCF; CIS, CIS(2), EOM-CCSD and TDDFT (LSDA, B3LYP, PBE1PBE) used alongside for comparison

compound_name: Benzene — valence and lower Rydberg excited states
point_group: D6h; all calculations performed in the D2h subgroup for technical reasons, but with the orbitals CONSTRAINED to full D6h symmetry to avoid symmetry-breaking solutions that occurred for some excited states
geometry_source: Fixed benzene geometry; the study concerns vertical excitation energies rather than optimized excited-state structures
method: CASSCF with contracted CI (CCI) on the CASSCF orbitals
basis_set: Three basis sets, giving CASSCF1/CASSCF2/CASSCF3. All use van Duijneveldt's 7s set contracted to three functions on hydrogen, with no hydrogen polarization functions. Carbon starts from a modified and extended Dunning double-zeta set whose outermost 2p function was optimized in full-valence CASSCF on the carbon atom ground state, plus three additional diffuse functions whose exponents were optimized in CASSCF on the (3p,1p) Rydberg state of carbon (SCF1/CASSCF1). CASSCF2 adds one set of 3d functions per carbon (exponent 0.63), giving 132 contracted Gaussians; CASSCF3 further extends the diffuse p set.
active_space_orbital_description: Six pi electrons distributed among 12 orbitals: the six valence pi orbitals plus a SECOND SHELL of six pi orbitals. The six-orbital valence-only pi space is stated to be inadequate because it "does not allow for any treatment of the Rydberg excited states, and does not include any radial correlation effects in the pi system", which is precisely why the second shell was added.
active_space_protocol: All calculations run in D2h but with orbitals constrained to full D6h symmetry, achieved by using a carefully symmetrized set of starting orbitals and allowing only rotations between orbitals of the correct symmetry during optimization — necessary because symmetry-breaking solutions appeared for some excited states. Three CASSCF calculations were performed for each state, one per basis set: CASSCF1 covers the valence and first Rydberg excited states, while CASSCF2 and CASSCF3 examine the effect of polarization and diffuse functions on the valence excited states. Because every orbital is optimized, full relaxation of the sigma electrons is achieved automatically for each state independently — in contrast to earlier work using a common set of sigma orbitals from a single SCF calculation. No sigma orbitals are active, so no sigma-pi correlation enters the CASSCF wave function; that is recovered in the subsequent contracted CI, which includes all single and double excitations out of a predetermined set of reference configurations built on the CASSCF2 orbitals.
electronic_structure_description: 1A1g ground state, whose wave function comprises 4022 configuration state functions in D2h symmetry; the SCF pi configuration (1a2u)2(1e1g)4 carries a weight of 87.9% at CASSCF1, rising slightly to 88.7% at CASSCF2 when 3d functions are added. Ground-state total energies and pi correlation energies: -230.7359 hartree / 2.36 eV (CASSCF1), -230.8133 / 2.35 eV (CASSCF2), -230.8136 / 2.32 eV (CASSCF3), against -230.7234 hartree and 2.24 eV from the earlier selected (1+2+3)-CI of Hay and Shavitt; the CCI ground-state energy is -231.1131 hartree. Vertical excitation energies in eV at CASSCF1 / CASSCF2 / CASSCF3 with experimental values: 4.9 / 4.9 / 4.9 against 4.9-5.0; 7.7 / 7.4 / 7.4 against 6.2-6.3; 8.6 / 8.3 / 7.8 against 6.98-7.0; 8.1 / 8.1 / 8.1 against 7.3; 3.9 / 3.9 / 3.9 against 3.9; 5.0 / 4.9 / 4.9 against 4.7; 7.1 / 7.0 / 6.7 against 5.6; 7.2 / 7.2 / 7.2 against 6.55. Ground and excited state quadrupole moments Qzz (a.u.) are also reported: 1A1g -6.14 (CASSCF1) and -6.47 (CASSCF2) against an experimental -7.4, with valence excited states spanning -4.96 to -8.92 and Rydberg states -19.2 to -35.1.
Other: The paper's explicit reason for its active space is that the obvious one will not do: the six valence pi orbitals "do not allow for any treatment of the Rydberg excited states, and do not include any radial correlation effects in the pi system", so a SECOND SHELL of six pi orbitals was added, giving six electrons in twelve orbitals. The advantages claimed for a complete pi space are specific — the wave function contains every pi configuration and is therefore "completely free of any bias" in selecting configurations, which matters because multiply excited configurations are known to be important in some benzene valence states, and because optimizing all orbitals gives full independent sigma relaxation for each electronic state rather than the common SCF sigma set used in earlier work. The cost of leaving sigma inactive is stated equally plainly: "without active sigma orbitals no sigma-pi correlation is included into the wave function", which is what the subsequent contracted CI has to recover. The residual errors are large and state-specific, and enlarging the basis does not fix them: the lowest state is reproduced exactly (4.9 eV) but the ionic states remain 1.1-1.3 eV above experiment even at CASSCF3, and the authors conclude that "it seems to be very difficult to achieve a better accuracy than around 0.5 eV for the most ionic states". Basis effects are separable from correlation effects by design — the diffuse and polarization functions were optimized in atomic CASSCF calculations first, and the atomic 3p Rydberg states come out within 0.03 to -0.17 eV — and for the 1E2g state "no basis set effect was detected" between CASSCF2 and CASSCF3. A practical caution: symmetry-breaking solutions appeared for some excited states and had to be suppressed by constraining orbitals to full D6h, so unconstrained optimization in the D2h working subgroup would have given different answers.
reference_short: Matos, Roos & Malmqvist, J. Chem. Phys. 1987, 86, 1458
notes: A CASSCF-CCI study of the benzene pi-electron spectrum, which mixes valence and Rydberg excited states and so requires careful excited-state orbital optimization. active_space_protocol: The space was built up in stages. electronic_structure_description: Open-shell singlet ground state arising from mixing of Yb f13 and f14 (and f12) configurations with the bipyridine pi* manifold. Energies of the four lowest singlet states relative to the 100% f13 triplet, in eV: at CASSCF, SS1 -0.06, SS2 +0.52, SS3 +1.03, SS4 +2.27; at CASSCF-MP2, SS1 -0.28, SS2 +0.30, SS3 +0.81, SS4 +2.05. The ground-state singlet composition resembles the earlier Cp2Yb(bipy) calculation: about 90% open-shell character, made up of 80% f13 and 10% f12. At the CASSCF level only one singlet lies below the triplet; CASSCF-MP2 lowers all the singlets relative to it. DFT (B3PW91) instead predicts a triplet f13,v(pi*)1,v ground state, which the authors attribute to the self-interaction error in the exchange-correlation energy.
Other: Adding the third bipyridine pi* orbital is what makes these calculations usable at all, and the paper says so directly: "an important effect of adding the pi3* orbital is to push the third-lowest lying singlet state (SS3) well above SS2, as they are nearly degenerate when pi3* is not included. This effect avoids the so-called 'intruder state problem' which otherwise would render these results unusable." A second, quantitative consequence is that SS2 rises by about 0.2 eV in the 4-Me-bipy complex once pi3* is in the space. The same intruder problem could not be escaped for the dimethyl-substituted complexes, which is why this study is restricted to the mono-methyl adducts — an active-space limitation that determined the scope of the paper. Dynamic correlation on top then changes the answer qualitatively rather than merely shifting it: at the CASSCF level only ONE singlet lies below the triplet in every complex, but CASSCF-MP2 lowers all the singlets, and the first EXCITED singlet drops below the triplet for the 5-Me and 6-Me complexes though not for bipy or 4-Me-bipy — so the number of sub-triplet singlet states, and hence the tautomeric equilibrium being modelled, depends on the perturbative step. The state configuration fractions are unchanged by that step. notes: Establishes multiconfigurational, intermediate-valent ground states in methyl-substituted decamethylytterbocene bipyridine complexes, combining magnetic susceptibility (SQUID), Yb L(III)-edge EXAFS and XANES with the calculations. compound_name: 1,2-Dihydronaphthalene oxide — photochemical conical intersections and T1/S0 crossing
geometry_source: CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G(d) conical intersection optimizations using the opt=conical algorithm; normal mode analyses performed at the located geometries
method: CASSCF conical intersection optimization
active_space_orbital_description: Three different CAS(4,4) spaces were used, chosen per target intersection. Active space I: the two benzylic sigma/sigma* orbital pairs of the epoxide moiety, known to dissociate in some aryloxiranes under photolysis. Active space II: modelled on the singlet 1,3-diradical usually proposed as the primary intermediate in aryloxirane photochemistry, matching spaces commonly used to locate hydrogen-allyl-type conical intersections. Active space III: the corresponding alkyl-allyl-type space. A fourth space comprising the two unshared valence orbitals of the carbenic carbon was used for the T1/S0 crossing. The aromatic pi system was deliberately EXCLUDED from all of them.
active_space_protocol: The aromatic pi orbitals were left out of every active space on the explicit grounds that "accurate reaction energetics, excitation energies, and energy barriers were not within the scope of this work", the aromatic system being treated as a 'photon antenna' that gathers light and supplies excitation to the oxirane moiety. The paper states the reason directly in a footnote: "the requisite CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G(d) calculations on this system are beyond the capacity of our current computational facilities." Each of the three (4,4) spaces successfully located a conical intersection.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (the degenerate pair at each intersection)
electronic_structure_description: Four crossing points were located. CCCI, from active space I, is an S1/S0 conical intersection whose geometry corresponds to complete dissociation of both benzylic sigma bonds of the aryloxirane ring, giving an aryl carbene plus a formyl group. TSC is a structurally similar T1/S0 surface crossing (intersystem crossing) located with the carbenic-carbon space, so the carbenic-aldehyde structure is accessible by either a singlet or a triplet pathway from the initial excited state. HACI, from active space II, is a hydrogen-allyl-type conical intersection with extreme lengthening of the C1-H1 bond (1.732 A) and lateral displacement toward oxygen (r(O-H) = 1.756 A); the hydrogen sits virtually centred over the C-O bond, with the benzylic centre interacting with the aromatic pi system rather than with the hydrogen, and the O-C1, C1-C2 and C2-C3 sigma bonds shorten, indicating a developing C1=C2 double bond. Normal mode analysis makes HACI a SECOND-ORDER saddle point, with imaginary frequencies for homolytic hydrogen dissociation and for hydrogen migration between O and C1, so it functions as the equivalent of a transition state for the 1,2-hydrogen migration typical of 1,3-diradicals. AACI1 and AACI2, from active space III, are two distinct alkyl-allyl-type conical intersections with C2-C3 lengthened to 2.24 and 2.23 A respectively, both also second-order saddle points. The triplet carbene plus CO lies within 0.05 kcal/mol of the relevant comparison energy, implying highly efficient intersystem crossing followed by ring closure to indan.
Other: An explicit, reasoned decision to use an active space known to be too small for energetics. The aromatic pi orbitals are omitted from all three (4,4) spaces because "the requisite CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G(d) calculations on this system are beyond the capacity of our current computational facilities", with the aromatic ring treated instead as a 'photon antenna' that collects the light and hands excitation to the oxirane. The authors bound their own claims accordingly, stating that accurate reaction energetics, excitation energies and energy barriers "were not within the scope of this work" — so the geometries and topologies of the located intersections are the deliverable and no energy from these calculations should be reused quantitatively. The compensating strategy is to run THREE different (4,4) spaces, each built around a different proposed mechanism (benzylic sigma/sigma* dissociation, hydrogen-allyl, alkyl-allyl) rather than one compromise space, and all three successfully converged to conical intersections — meaning the choice of space determines which intersection is found, and finding an intersection with a given space is not evidence that the corresponding pathway dominates. A useful internal check on the located structures is that the C-H and C-C distances at HACI (1.732 A) and at AACI1/AACI2 (2.24 and 2.23 A) match values reported for hydrogen-allyl and alkyl-allyl intersections elsewhere, and that normal mode analysis identifies all three as second-order saddle points rather than minima on the seam.

notes: Re-examination of the 254 nm photochemistry of 1,2-dihydronaphthalene oxide, in which indan is shown to be a PRIMARY photoproduct as well as the traditionally assumed secondary one. The proposed carbenic route runs through the carbene-aldehyde structure, whose triplet abstracts the aldehydic hydrogen (dissociation energy 86.0 kcal/mol, comparable to a benzylic hydrogen at 88.0) leading to decarbonylation and then intersystem crossing and ring closure to indan. Formation of indanyl dimers is suggested by two high-boiling GC/MS components with base peaks at m/e 145. Active spaces are depicted in the paper's Figure 3 and the intersection geometries in Figures 4, 5 and 7-9.
