method: CASSCF geometry optimization and crossing-point location; B3LYP and CCSD(T) single points at the CASSCF geometries; CASSCF spin-orbit couplings
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in five orbitals: the pi and pi* orbitals of the C=C fragment together with the pi, pi* and n orbitals of the C=O fragment.
active_space_protocol: A single (6,5) space is used for every molecule in the series so the four enones can be compared directly, and the same space serves the S0 minimum, the 3(n-pi*) and 3(pi-pi*) minima, the 3(pi-pi*)/3(n-pi*) conical intersection and the T1/S0 crossing. Crossing points are located with state-averaged orbitals (50%/50% for T1/S0). Spin-orbit couplings are computed at the T1/S0 crossing point I in a one-electron approximation using the effective charges of Koseki et al. (O 5.6, C 3.6). Single-point B3LYP and CCSD(T) triplet energies were taken at the CASSCF geometries to gauge dynamic correlation on the B-to-I energy difference, an approximation the authors flag explicitly because "neither B3LYP or CCSD(T) can be used to reoptimize the crossing".
nroots_per_mult: 2 (state-averaged at the crossings)
electronic_structure_description: Triplet decay pathway of an alpha,beta-enone, with all energies in kcal/mol relative to the twisted 3(pi-pi*) minimum B: A, the S0 planar minimum, at -71.06; G, the 3(pi-pi*)/3(n-pi*) conical intersection, at +8.79; C, the 3(n-pi*) planar minimum, at +3.95; B itself at 0.00; and I, the 3(pi-pi*)/S0 intersection, at +6.64. Delta-U, the triplet-singlet energy gap at the geometry of B, is -28.74 kcal/mol. B is the lowest-energy T1 structure. This compound is the most rigid ring in the series, with the smallest twist at B (C4-C3-C2-C1 dihedral -23 deg) and by far the largest B-to-I gap, hence the longest triplet lifetime. The computed spin-orbit coupling at the crossing point I is below 1 cm-1, as for every molecule in the series.
Other: The same (6,5) space — C=C pi/pi* plus C=O pi/pi*/n — is carried unchanged across the whole series, which is what makes the paper's central correlation meaningful: the energy gap Delta-E between the twisted 3(pi-pi*) minimum B and the 3(pi-pi*)/S0 intersection I varies from 0.16 kcal/mol (cycloheptenone) to 6.64 (cyclopentenone) purely with ring flexibility, not with any change of method or space, and correlates with the natural logarithm of the experimental triplet lifetimes. The one place the space is knowingly inadequate is dynamic correlation, and the authors both test and bound it: B3LYP and CCSD(T) single points were run at the CASSCF geometries B and I specifically to estimate that effect, with the explicit caveat that CASSCF geometries had to be used "because neither B3LYP or CCSD(T) can be used to reoptimize the crossing" — so the crossing geometry itself rests entirely on the (6,5) CASSCF surface with no correlated check available. A second finding is a genuine negative result on spin-orbit coupling: computed in the one-electron approximation at the crossing point I, the couplings are ALL below 1 cm-1 across the series, so "differences in spin-orbit coupling are unlikely to affect the 3(pi-pi*) lifetime", and unlike the case of alkenes "there appears to be almost no such variation with the one-electron approximation used here for alpha,beta-enones". For comparison, the same one-electron treatment gives 65 cm-1 at the corresponding acrolein point K. Including spin-orbit coupling makes the triplet/singlet crossing weakly avoided, introducing a small barrier on the 3(pi-pi*)-to-S0 pathway that the bare CASSCF crossing does not show.
reference_short: Garcia-Exposito, Bearpark, Ortuno, Branchadell, Robb & Wilsey, J. Org. Chem. 2001, 66, 8811
notes: Explains why cyclic alpha,beta-enones have such different triplet lifetimes by locating the T1 3(pi-pi*)/S0 intersections of cyclopentenone, cyclohexenone and cycloheptenone, with methyl vinyl ketone as an unconstrained acyclic comparison and acrolein data taken from earlier work. The relaxation path follows the S1 1(n-pi*) state through intersystem crossing to the triplet surface. Structures on the path are labelled A (S0 planar minimum), G (3(pi-pi*)/3(n-pi*) conical intersection), C (3(n-pi*) planar minimum), B (3(pi-pi*) twisted minimum) and I (3(pi-pi*)/S0 intersection); Delta-E is the B-to-I gap and Delta-U the triplet-singlet gap at geometry B. As ring flexibility decreases, the C4-C3-C2-C1 dihedral at B falls from -64 deg for cycloheptenone to -23 deg for cyclopentenone (acrolein's value is near 90 deg), and the intersections are always more twisted than the corresponding minima, so a stiffer ring must travel further to reach the funnel. Experimental lifetimes used for the correlation were measured in cyclohexane. All energies are in Table 1 and spin-orbit couplings in Table 2.

point_group: All calculations carried out in the C2v point group. Seven geometries considered: trigonal bipyramid (D3h), edge-capped tetrahedron (C2v), square pyramid (C4v), planar pentagon (D5h), square planar (D4h), linear (D-infinity-h) and tetrahedral (Td).

method: CASSCF and RASSCF geometry optimization followed by MRSDCI with the multireference Davidson correction (MRSDCI+Q)
software: GAMESS and a modified version of ALCHEMY II (CASSCF); ALCHEMY II (MRSDCI)
basis_set: (3s3p) basis for tin augmented with one set of 3d-type diffuse functions (exponent 0.2423), giving (3s3p1d), used uniformly for all electronic states
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potentials on tin with the outer 5s2 5p2 shells in the valence space
active_space_orbital_description: Full active space of 15 orbitals labelled by C2v irrep as 5442-CAS — five a1, four b2, four b1 and two a2 — for the C2v, D3h, C4v, D4h and Td structures; 5352 orbitals for D5h and 5532 for the linear structure. All five valence s orbitals are kept INACTIVE in the sense that no excitations from them are allowed at the CASSCF stage, though they are allowed to relax. Because including all 15 orbitals gives too many configurations, a RESTRICTED active space (RASSCF) of 3221 — three a1, two b2, two b1 and one a2 — was used instead.
active_space_protocol: The nominal full valence space of 15 orbitals proved unaffordable — "inclusion of all 15 orbitals in the active space leads to too large number of configurations for the CASSCF calculation" — so a RASSCF restriction to a 3221 subset was adopted. The five valence s orbitals are frozen against excitation at the CASSCF stage but allowed to relax. Crucially the s orbitals are RESTORED at the correlation stage: the MRSDCI computations include excitations from all five valence s orbitals as well as the valence p orbitals. Reference configurations for the MRSDCI are all CASSCF configurations with coefficients of 0.1 or greater, with single and double excitations from them; unlinked quadruple clusters are estimated by the multireference Davidson correction. The CASSCF calculations reached up to 384 configuration spin functions while the MRSDCI reached up to 3.62 million.

electronic_structure_description: The 1A1' state with trigonal bipyramidal (D3h) geometry is the ground state of Sn5 at the CASSCF, MRSDCI and MRSDCI+Q levels alike, with several low-lying excited triplet states. The Jahn-Teller distortion of the D3h 3E'' state gives an edge-capped tetrahedron: the 3B2 and 3B1 components lie at 0.62 (CASSCF), 0.45 (MRSDCI) and 0.47 eV (MRSDCI+Q), against 0.53 eV at MRSDCI for the undistorted D3h state, so the stabilization is modest. Correlation lowers the excited-state separations substantially — computed separations are 0.3-0.5 eV lower than the corresponding CASSCF values. Two orderings actually invert with correlation: the 3A2' state with D5h symmetry lies 0.07 eV BELOW the 1A2g state with D4h symmetry at CASSCF, but 0.11 and 0.06 eV ABOVE it at MRSDCI and MRSDCI+Q. Dissociation of two Sn atoms from the edge-capped tetrahedral structure costs 123 kcal/mol (MRSDCI) and 128 (MRSDCI+Q); combined with the Sn3 atomization energy of 93 and 100 kcal/mol, the Sn5 atomization energy is 216 kcal/mol at MRSDCI, taken as a lower bound since higher-order correlation would stabilize the cluster further by an estimated 12 kcal/mol.
Other: An explicit case of the intended active space being unaffordable and the fallback being documented. The full valence space for Sn5 is 15 orbitals (5442 by C2v irrep for most geometries, 5352 for D5h, 5532 for linear), but "inclusion of all 15 orbitals in the active space leads to too large number of configurations for the CASSCF calculation", so a restricted active space of 3221 was used instead — a reduction from 15 to 8 orbitals. The size gap between the two stages is stark — up to 384 configuration spin functions at CASSCF against up to 3.62 million at MRSDCI — which is a fair measure of how much of the correlation this system's answer depends on. And it does depend on it: the excited-state separations computed at the correlated level are 0.3-0.5 eV LOWER than the CASSCF ones, and two state orderings actually invert, the D5h 3A2' state moving from 0.07 eV below the D4h 1A2g state at CASSCF to 0.06-0.11 eV above it at MRSDCI and MRSDCI+Q. Geometry, by contrast, is insensitive: MRSDCI-optimized structures "were found to be quite close to the CASSCF geometries", which is what justified using CASSCF geometries for the edge-capped tetrahedron.

Other: The paper contains a deliberate active-space control experiment aimed at a specific disagreement with DFT. CASSCF/CASPT2 gives high-lying orbitals of nearly pure 4d(Ru) character, whereas the Kohn-Sham orbitals of the same complexes are mixed 3p(Cl)/4d(Ru) — a difference that changes the assignment of the lowest absorption from predominantly Ru->DAB MLCT (CASPT2) to something with substantial chloride character (TD-DFT). To test whether the pure-4d character is merely an artefact of a too-small space, TWO extra calculations were run on [Ru(Cl)(Me)(CO)2(Me-DAB)]: 14 electrons in 14 orbitals averaged over 12 roots, and 16 electrons in 15 orbitals averaged over 6 roots. The orbital character survived, so the discrepancy is a real methodological difference rather than an active-space limitation. A second, quieter space decision is recorded with its justification: the sigma bonding orbital between the chlorines and the Ru 5p(x) "is too low in energy to be included in the active space and keeps the occupation number of 1.98 at the CASPT2 level" — an occupancy check confirming the omission is safe. The dichloride complex needed a differently constructed 10-orbital space (dropping the axial sigma/sigma* pairs of the other complexes in favour of the sigma(ClRuCl) bonding orbital and its antibonding counterpart), so its space is not simply a subset of the others. The broader finding recorded across the series is that CASSCF/CASPT2 orbitals are more LOCALIZED than the TD-DFT ones yet CASPT2 predicts SMALLER electron density redistribution on excitation — the two effects run opposite to naive expectation. Agreement between the two methods is described as remarkably good for the non-halide complexes and poor once chloride is present, which is the paper's main conclusion. notes: UV-visible absorption spectra of [Ru(E)(E')(CO)2(iPr-DAB)] complexes analysed with CASSCF/CASPT2 and TD-DFT on the model complexes [Ru(E)(E')(CO)2(Me-DAB)], where DAB is a 1,4-diaza-1,3-butadiene chelate. The lowest-energy visible absorption of the halide complexes occurs at higher energy than for the stannyl complexes (459 and 469 nm, 21 790 cm-1, against 529-539 nm), a blue shift that CASSCF/CASPT2 reproduces well. The first metal-centred (MC) transition computed for this dichloride complex is discussed separately in the paper. Its active electron count is not stated, so only the orbital count is recorded here.
Other: The paper contains a deliberate active-space control experiment aimed at a specific disagreement with DFT. CASSCF/CASPT2 gives high-lying orbitals of nearly pure 4d(Ru) character, whereas the Kohn-Sham orbitals of the same complexes are mixed 3p(Cl)/4d(Ru) — a difference that changes the assignment of the lowest absorption from predominantly Ru->DAB MLCT (CASPT2) to something with substantial chloride character (TD-DFT). To test whether the pure-4d character is merely an artefact of a too-small space, TWO extra calculations were run on [Ru(Cl)(Me)(CO)2(Me-DAB)]: 14 electrons in 14 orbitals averaged over 12 roots, and 16 electrons in 15 orbitals averaged over 6 roots. The orbital character survived, so the discrepancy is a real methodological difference rather than an active-space limitation. A second, quieter space decision is recorded with its justification: the sigma bonding orbital between the chlorines and the Ru 5p(x) "is too low in energy to be included in the active space and keeps the occupation number of 1.98 at the CASPT2 level" — an occupancy check confirming the omission is safe. The dichloride complex needed a differently constructed 10-orbital space (dropping the axial sigma/sigma* pairs of the other complexes in favour of the sigma(ClRuCl) bonding orbital and its antibonding counterpart), so its space is not simply a subset of the others. The broader finding recorded across the series is that CASSCF/CASPT2 orbitals are more LOCALIZED than the TD-DFT ones yet CASPT2 predicts SMALLER electron density redistribution on excitation — the two effects run opposite to naive expectation. Agreement between the two methods is described as remarkably good for the non-halide complexes and poor once chloride is present, which is the paper's main conclusion. A stated limitation on every number here: spin-orbit coupling, expected to be very important for these third-row-metal complexes, is omitted entirely.
reference_short: Turki, Daniel, Zalis, Vlcek, van Slageren & Stufkens, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2001, 123, 11431

The aim is threefold: assign the observed bands, compare halide with stannyl ligands, and benchmark CASSCF/CASPT2 against TD-DFT for organometallic spectra. Experimental absorption maxima for the iPr-DAB complexes: [Ru(SnPh3)2(CO)2(iPr-DAB)] shows a strong band at 529 nm (18 900 cm-1), a weak broad band near 400 nm (25 000 cm-1) and a strong sharp band at 310 nm (32 260 cm-1); the mixed stannyl-methyl complex absorbs at 539 nm (18 550 cm-1) with a shoulder at 450 nm and a distinct band at 394 nm (25 380 cm-1); the halide complexes absorb at higher energy, 459 and 469 nm (21 790 cm-1). compound_name: Formaldehyde (H2CO) in aqueous solution — pi* -> n fluorescence transition
point_group: C2v at the ground-state geometry; the S1(n,pi*) state relaxes to a pyramidalized structure
geometry_source: Excited-state geometry optimized with analytical gradients for the state-averaged CASSCF wave function (nontrivial because SA-CASSCF is nonvariational); because the second CASSI root is close but not identical to the second SA-CASSCF root, the CASSI-optimal structure was established by a zero-order method comparing energies of nearby structures. Solvent configurations come from Monte Carlo simulation with the QMSTAT model.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with the complete active space state interaction (CASSI) method; CASPT2 used to build the reference solute-solvent potential
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis in two contractions: Ano.s(I), C and O 5s4p1d with H 3s2p; and Ano.s(II), C and O 7s6p3d with H 4s3p
active_space_orbital_description: Four active electrons in the pi, n and pi* orbitals of formaldehyde.
active_space_protocol: State-averaged CASSCF with EQUAL weight on the ground state and the S1(n,pi*) state. To generate the input set of state functions for CASSI, seven SA-CASSCF calculations were run: one field-free plus one with a homogeneous electric field of strength 0.003 au directed along each of the three axes in both directions. These yield fourteen states, some significantly overlapping, from which CASSI produces fourteen eigenstates of the unperturbed Hamiltonian — the two lowest being good estimates of the ground and first excited states, with the remaining twelve needed to describe their polarization by the solvent. CASSI is used in place of CASSCF at each Monte Carlo step because a full CASSCF, dominated by two-electron integral transformation, would be prohibitive; the CASSI ansatz is argued to adequately emulate CASSCF. The solute-solvent potential is fitted to counterpoise-corrected CASPT2 supermolecular potentials, since dispersion in the QMSTAT interaction requires dynamic correlation.
nroots_per_mult: 2 state-averaged in each SA-CASSCF; 14 states passed to CASSI, yielding 14 eigenstates
electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 and the S1(n,pi*) excited state; the fluorescence studied is the pi* -> n emission from the relaxed excited state. The dipole moment of the final state is greater than that of the initial state by almost a factor of two. Computed solvent-shift distributions for the pi* -> n transition average almost exactly 0 eV for both basis sets, with the difference between them not statistically significant; both distributions are slightly asymmetric with a tail toward negative (red) shifts, and the larger Ano.s(II) basis gives a noticeably wider distribution. A dielectric-continuum treatment would instead predict an average shift toward shorter wavelengths, because of the larger final-state dipole. Since the nonelectrostatic perturbation contributes at most a minor shift in either direction, packing strain cannot explain the absence of a net shift; specific solute-solvent interactions, in particular strong hydrogen bonding to the ground state, are identified as the likeliest cause.
Other: A minimal (4,3) pi/n/pi* space is used, and the paper's methodological interest is in what has to be built AROUND it rather than in enlarging it. Because a CASSCF would have to be re-solved at every Monte Carlo step and its cost is dominated by two-electron integral transformation, the wave function is instead assembled by CASSI from a precomputed basis of state functions: seven SA-CASSCF calculations (field-free plus a 0.003 au field along each axis in both directions) give fourteen states, and CASSI turns these into fourteen eigenstates of which the lowest two are the physical ground and excited states while "the remaining 12 will be needed in the description of the polarization of the former". So twelve of the fourteen states exist purely to let the small active space respond to the solvent field — polarization that a larger active space would otherwise have had to carry. The consequence is an inconsistency the authors flag themselves: the second CASSI root is "close but not exactly equal to the second root to the SA-CASSCF equations since some further correlation is introduced through the CASSI procedure", so the excited-state geometry could not simply be optimized and had to be re-established by comparing energies of nearby structures. Dynamic correlation enters only through the fitted potential, not the wave function: CASPT2 supermolecular potentials with counterpoise correction are the reference because dispersion in the solute-solvent interaction demands it, while the solute itself is described at the CASSI/CASSCF level throughout. Basis-set sensitivity shows up not in the mean but in the WIDTH of the solvent-shift distribution — the average shift is ~0 eV in both basis sets and the difference is not statistically significant, but Ano.s(II) gives a wider spread, attributed to the excited state being more diverse in the larger basis.
reference_short: Ohrn & Karlstrom, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 1934
notes: Combined quantum-chemical and statistical-mechanical study of the solvent shift to formaldehyde's pi* -> n fluorescence in water, using the QMSTAT model in which an explicit discrete set of solvent molecules perturbs the solute through both an electrostatic and a NONELECTROSTATIC operator. The nonelectrostatic term V(nel) partly models charge overlap and was needed because problems arose in solving the polarization equations without it. Monte Carlo simulations sampled solvent configurations with every hundredth step stored. A joint configuration-space/wave-function-space test was performed by taking configurations stored from the large-basis simulation and re-solving the quantum problem in the small basis (labelled 'Ano.s(I)[II-set]' in Figure 6), noting that those configurations no longer follow the correct Boltzmann distribution. The correlation between shifts computed with and without the nonelectrostatic perturbation is shown in Figure 7 for both basis sets. The n -> pi* solvent shift in aldehydes and ketones is discussed against the classical Bayliss-McRae framework.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 counterpoise-corrected supermolecular potentials used as the reference for fitting the QMSTAT solute-solvent interaction; the solute wave function itself is CASSI/CASSCF

electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet. The CASPT2//CASSCF torsional potential energy curve of the S0-A state makes the NONPLANAR structure (torsional angle 56.4 deg by CASSCF optimization) the most stable form, lying 1.8 and 3.6 kcal/mol below s-trans-HFBD and s-cis-HFBD respectively; earlier Hartree-Fock work gave 1.8 and 5.7 kcal/mol for the same quantities. MS-CASPT2 vertical excitation energies in eV with oscillator strengths and character: S1-A 6.2 (0.0014), pi-pi*, HOMO-1 -> LUMO mixed with HOMO -> LUMO+1; S2-B 6.5 (0.3054), pi-pi*, HOMO -> LUMO, experimental 6.3; S3-A 7.5 (0.2647), pi-pi*, HOMO-1 -> LUMO mixed with HOMO -> LUMO+1, experimental 7.6; S4-B 7.8 (0.2167), pi-pi*, HOMO-1 -> LUMO+1; S5-A 8.6 (0.0411), pi-pi*, HOMO -> LUMO+2 mixed with HOMO -> LUMO. For comparison CIS gives only 7.5 eV (f = 0.47) and 9.6 eV (f = 0.37) for the two observed bands.
Other: The neutral and cationic spaces are deliberately matched — 12-in-10 for HFBD and 11-in-10 for HFBD+ — so that the first ionization potential and the torsional curves of neutral and cation are computed in the same orbital space and differ only by the removed electron. That matching is what lets the paper connect ionization of the nonplanar neutral to relaxation of the initially 'hot' nonplanar cation into the two planar isomers, since the neutral and cation torsional potential energy curves are directly comparable. The value added by the multireference treatment shows up against the single-reference alternative in Table 3: for the neutral, MS-CASPT2 places the strongly allowed pi-pi* S2-B state at 6.5 eV against an experimental 6.3, and S3-A at 7.5 against 7.6, whereas CIS puts the corresponding states at 7.5 and 9.6 eV — errors of 1.2 and 2.0 eV. CIS also misses the weak S1-A state at 6.2 eV entirely, and several of these states are two-configurational (HOMO-1 -> LUMO mixed with HOMO -> LUMO+1), which is why a single-reference method cannot order them. For the cations the MS-CASPT2 excitation energies land within 0.1-0.4 eV of the measured values across both isomers. The multistate formulation matters here because the low-lying cation states of the same symmetry (1- and 2-2Au, 1- and 2-2B1) are close enough to interact through the dynamic correlation. One geometric caveat carried by the same space: the CASSCF optimization gives a nonplanar neutral with a torsional angle of 56.4 degrees as the most stable form, 1.8 and 3.6 kcal/mol below the s-trans and s-cis planar structures respectively, where earlier Hartree-Fock work gave 1.8 and 5.7 — so the s-cis relative energy is method-sensitive by about 2 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Kubozono et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 5192
notes: Combined ESR and computational study of the cis-to-trans photoisomerization of the hexafluoro-1,3-butadiene radical cation, produced by gamma-irradiation at 77 K in halocarbon matrices and photoisomerized with visible light from a 500 W xenon lamp. The neutral HFBD sample was verified free of impurities by Raman spectroscopy at 400 Torr, matching the published spectrum of nonplanar s-cis-HFBD. ESR shows two cation isomers, s-cis-HFBD+ and s-trans-HFBD+, whose relative abundances shift toward s-trans on illumination — the reverse isomerization was not observed. 19F isotropic and anisotropic hyperfine couplings were computed by B3LYP//B3LYP and MP2//B3LYP and compared with experiment in Table 1. The mechanistic picture is that ionizing radiation ionizes the nonplanar neutral and the resulting 'hot' nonplanar cation relaxes into the two planar isomers, which the torsional potential energy curves of both species are used to rationalize.

compound_name: InSb2 trimer and its cation InSb2+
point_group: C2v for the bent isosceles structures; C-infinity-v for the linear In-Sb-Sb permutational isomer
geometry_source: CASSCF and MRSDCI optimized bond lengths and bending angles; bending potential energy curves computed for the 2B2, 2A1 and 2B1 states
method: CASSCF (restricted active spaces, labelled ijkl-CAS by the number of a1, b2, b1 and a2 active orbitals) followed by multireference singles and doubles CI (MRSDCI)
software: A modified version of the ALCHEMY II codes, extended to include relativistic effective core potentials
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence space of five a1, four b2, two b1 and one a2 orbital (12 orbitals) holding the 13 outer electrons — too large for the MCSCF codes, so restricted subspaces were used: 5210-CAS (five a1, two b2, one b1, no a2) for the potential energy surfaces and 5320-CAS for geometries and energy separations. For the bent-versus-linear comparison, 4321-CAS was used for the C2v structure against a compatible 4330-CAS for the linear isomer, with the symmetric combination of the Sb s orbitals kept inactive and the highest b2 omitted.
active_space_protocol: Restricted active spaces throughout at the CASSCF stage, with the truncation chosen to follow the pattern established for GaAs2; all valence electrons including the frozen group V s electrons were restored to the active space at the MRCI level. CASSCF calculations on the InSb2 isomers reached up to 7000 configurations and the MRSDCI up to 420 000.
multiplicities_studied: doublet and quartet for the neutral trimers; singlet or triplet for the cations
electronic_structure_description: Bent 2B2 ground state, contrary to an earlier report of a linear ground state. Geometries and energies at CASSCF then MRSDCI (In-Sb bond length in A, apex angle in deg, energy in eV): 2B2 3.149/48.7/0 then 3.154/49.0/0; linear In-Sb-Sb (2-Pi) 2.901/-/0.15 then 2.878/-/0.56, with Sb-Sb bond lengths of 2.638 and 2.633 A; 2A1 2.781/59.6/0.62 then 2.803/60.5/0.67; 2B1 3.132/53.4/1.20 then 3.141/53.3/1.38. The InSb2+ cation has a closed-shell 1A1 ground state at 3.820/38.3/5.25 (CASSCF) and 3.846/38.9/5.83 (MRSDCI), giving an adiabatic ionization potential of 5.83 eV. The 2A1 surface crosses the 2B2 ground-state surface, so InSb2 cannot be stable in the 2A1 electronic state; a state lying 15.5 kcal/mol above the ground state will relax through spin-orbit coupling.
Other: A worked example of restricting an unaffordable active space and then documenting exactly what was dropped and where it was restored. Distributing the 13 outer electrons of InSb2 over the full valence space — five a1, four b2, two b1 and one a2 orbital — "resulted in a configuration space that is too large for our MCSCF codes", so the space was cut following a procedure established for GaAs2, where the most important subspace was found to be four a1, two b2 and one b1, with the fifth a1 (bonding) orbital important and the 3b2 and 2b1 orbitals less so. Different truncations are then used for different purposes, which matters when comparing numbers within the paper: potential energy surfaces at 5210-CAS, geometries and energy separations at 5320-CAS. For the crucial bent-versus-linear energy comparison a SEPARATE and deliberately matched pair of calculations was run — 4321-CAS for the C2v isosceles structures against 4330-CAS for the linear permutational isomers — with the symmetric combination of the group V s orbitals frozen in both and the highest b2 omitted, precisely so that the two geometries are treated compatibly. The authors are explicit that this compatibility, not absolute space size, is what makes the isomer energy difference meaningful. The frozen s electrons are not lost: "all valence electrons including the As 4s electrons were kept active at the MRCI level", so the CASSCF truncation affects only the reference. The scale of what the correlation step adds is visible in the configuration counts — up to 7000 CASSCF configurations against 420 000 MRSDCI for the InSb2 isomers, and 1000 against 241 000 for SbIn2. Correlation changes the answer qualitatively for InSb2: at CASSCF the linear In-Sb-Sb (2-Pi) isomer lies only 0.15 eV above the bent 2B2 ground state, but MRSDCI pushes it to 0.56 eV, and the paper's headline result — that the ground state of InSb2 is a BENT 2B2 state rather than the linear structure reported earlier — depends on that shift.
reference_short: Das & Balasubramanian, J. Chem. Phys. 1991, 94, 6620
notes: Systematic study of the geometries, potential energy curves and ionization potentials of the mixed III-V trimers InSb2, SbIn2, GaAs2 and AsGa2 (Ga2As) and their cations, motivated by mass-spectrometric observations of anomalous abundance and dramatic odd-even alternation in the ionization potentials of these clusters, which deviate significantly from group IV cluster patterns. Bending potential energy curves were computed for the low-lying doublet states. A previous study had reported a LINEAR ground state for InSb2 with r(Sb-Sb) = 2.82 A and r(In-Sb) = 3.15 A; this work shows the ground state is instead a bent 2B2 state. Dipole moments for the low-lying bent states are in Table V and leading configurations for each species in Tables VI-VIII.
correlation_correction: MRSDCI using the best CASSCF orbitals, with all CASSCF-CI configurations of coefficient greater than 0.07 as references; ALL valence electrons, including the group V s electrons frozen at the CASSCF stage, were kept active at the MRCI level

electronic_structure_description: The 4-Sigma- state is the ground state. active_space_protocol: One uniform pi space of 12 electrons in 11 orbitals serves the ground state and every pi-pi* state, with no symmetry restrictions imposed anywhere in the calculations. The standard zeroth-order CASPT2 Hamiltonian was used together with an IMAGINARY level-shift parameter of 0.1 au to circumvent intruder states. Radiative lifetimes were obtained from the Strickler-Berg relationship using CASSCF transition dipole moments together with CASPT2 band origin energies — the two levels are deliberately combined for that purpose.
electronic_structure_description: The two lowest singlet excitations are pi-pi* states of 1Lb and 1La character. Computed properties, CASSCF then CASPT2 (oscillator strength in parentheses): 1(pi-pi*)-Lb vertical absorption 4.15 then 3.80 eV (f = 0.0008), band origin 3.86 then 3.50 eV, vertical emission 3.66 then 3.44 eV, dipole moment 1.36 D, transition dipole orientation -15 deg from the inertial long axis, radiative lifetime 2754 ns. 1(pi-pi*)-La vertical absorption 5.78 then 4.35 eV (f = 0.0481), band origin 4.95 then 3.69 eV, vertical emission 4.27 then 3.20 eV, dipole moment 4.59 D, transition dipole orientation 77 deg, radiative lifetime 64 ns. Triplets: 3(pi-pi*)-La vertical absorption 2.92 then 2.83 eV, band origin 2.47 then 2.35 eV, vertical emission 2.06 then 2.09 eV, dipole 1.33 D, radiative lifetime 0.1 ms; 3(pi-pi*)-Lb vertical absorption 4.19 then 3.63 eV, dipole 1.43 D. The calculations place the 1Lb band origin BELOW that of 1La (3.50 against 3.69 eV), and give 1La a substantially higher oscillator strength than 1Lb. The measured LIF band origin in a supersonic jet is 3.73 eV (30 045 cm-1), short-axis polarized; magnetic circular dichroism in hexane gives band maxima at 3.90 and 4.17 eV, a gap of 2200 cm-1. A 1La/S0 conical intersection is located 0.7 eV above the 1La minimum, and a higher-lying singlet observed above 40 000 cm-1 (4.96 eV) is calculated at 5.18 eV. The ground-state dipole moment is 1.20 D.
Other: A single 12-electron, 11-orbital pi space is carried across the ground state and every pi-pi* state, which is what makes the 1La/1Lb ordering — the whole point of the study — a like-for-like comparison rather than an artefact of differently constructed spaces. The reason that matters here is that the two states respond to dynamic correlation utterly differently: at CASSCF the vertical absorptions are 4.15 eV (1Lb) and 5.78 eV (1La), a 1.63 eV gap, but CASPT2 pulls 1La down by 1.43 eV and 1Lb by only 0.35 eV, collapsing the gap to 0.55 eV. The band origins behave the same way — 3.86 and 4.95 eV at CASSCF against 3.50 and 3.69 eV at CASPT2 — so bare CASSCF in this space would overstate the 1La-1Lb separation by more than an electronvolt and misrepresent the state coupling that the paper exists to characterize. The 1La state's much larger dipole moment (4.59 D against 1.36 D, with a ground state of 1.20 D) is the underlying reason for its far greater correlation sensitivity. Two protocol details bear on reuse of these numbers: an IMAGINARY level shift of 0.1 au was needed to circumvent intruder states, and the radiative lifetimes mix levels by construction, combining CASSCF transition dipole moments with CASPT2 band origins in the Strickler-Berg formula. Finally, the conical intersections were not left at their CASSCF geometries — CASPT2 explorations of nearby structures were used to locate minimum energy CASPT2 crossing points, since a CASSCF crossing need not coincide with the CASPT2 one.

notes: Combined femtosecond time-resolved experimental and CASPT2//CASSCF theoretical study of 1-aminonaphthalene photophysics. Context: in naphthalene itself the populated 1La state internally converts to the lower 1Lb in 30 fs through a conical intersection, and donor or acceptor substituents can alter the relative energies and coupling of these states. Rotationally resolved fluorescence excitation work by Berden et al. had revealed a b-type transition suggesting a REVERSAL of the 1Lb/1La ordering in AMN relative to naphthalene, and studies of substituted 1-aminonaphthalenes highlighted the role of the amino twist angle in the 1La/1Lb coupling. Other: The active space is only PARTLY specified by the authors: "two nonbonding orbitals of O atom and the sigma orbital of the C-O bond were included in the CAS(9,7) active space while other active orbitals and electrons were chosen by the program automatically." So three of the seven orbitals are chosen on physical grounds — the two oxygen lone pairs whose splitting defines the X and A states of an alkoxy radical, plus the C-O sigma — and the remaining four are whatever the automatic selection produced, following the same recipe as the group's earlier alkoxy work. That makes the space reproducible only by re-running the same program with the same defaults, not from the paper's description, and means the four unspecified orbitals may differ between the five isomers. The paper runs TD-UB3LYP in parallel for the same B-X excitation energies, so the two methods serve as a mutual check on the assignment; the B3LYP level alone supplies the ground-state geometries and the relative conformer energies, meaning the CASSCF numbers sit on DFT structures throughout.

notes: Jet-cooled laser-induced fluorescence study of five dimethyl-substituted cyclohexoxy radicals — 3,4-, 3,5-, 2,3-, 2,5- and 2,6-dimethylcyclohexoxy — examining how methyl substitution position affects the LIF spectrum of the parent cyclohexoxy radical. compound_name: 9H-Adenine — radiationless decay of the lowest 1npi* and 1pipi* excited singlet states
point_group: Cs for the constrained excited-state optimizations, then relaxed to C1; the ground state has a pyramidalized amino group and C1 symmetry
geometry_source: Ground-state geometry optimized at MP2/6-31G(d,p); excited-state minima optimized at CASSCF first under Cs constraint and then reoptimized in C1 using the Cs structures and their canonical orbitals as initial guesses; nonplanar saddle points located without symmetry constraints; conical intersections optimized in Gaussian 98. Stationary points verified by Hessian calculation and harmonic frequency analysis. Reaction paths built as linearly interpolated internal coordinate (LIIC) paths connecting each excited-state minimum to a conical intersection.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and LIIC reaction paths with CASPT2 single points; LS-CASPT2 with an imaginary level shift
software: GAMESS (geometry optimizations, frequencies); Gaussian 98 (conical intersection searches); MOLCAS-4 (LIIC single points and CASPT2)
basis_set: ANO-L (3s2p1d/2s1p) split-valence double-zeta with polarization functions on all atoms for the LIIC single points; 6-31G(d,p) for the MP2 ground-state optimization
active_space_orbital_description: FOUR different active spaces are used for four different tasks. (i) For the 1pipi* geometry optimization: 10 orbitals of pi character. (ii) For the 1npi* equilibrium structure: the same space with the LOWEST-ENERGY pi orbital REPLACED by a lone-pair (n) orbital. (iii) For the nonplanar saddle-point search: nine orbitals nominally of pi character plus one orbital of n character, with no symmetry constraints. (iv) For the conical intersection searches: reduced to 6 electrons in 6 orbitals, built from the three HOMOs and three LUMOs of an RHF calculation at the guessed intersection geometry. The LIIC single-point energies use 12 electrons in 10 orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Cs symmetry is exploited to distinguish a''(pi) from a'(sigma/n) orbitals and to block the excited states into A' and A'' symmetries. Excited-state minima were first optimized under Cs constraint, then the constraint was relaxed and the geometries reoptimized in C1 starting from those structures and their canonical orbitals. For the LIIC single points, the six lowest electronic states were included in the CASSCF energy functional with EQUAL weights. Continuity of excited-state character along each path was verified by computing ground-to-excited transition dipole moments and by analysing the electronic configurations composing the CASSCF wave functions. The final CASPT2 single points rest on a state-averaged CASSCF over the THREE lowest states with equal weights — a different averaging from the six-state functional used for the paths — and use the LS-CASPT2 approach with an imaginary level shift of 0.3 au to mitigate intruder states. Oscillator strengths combine CASSCF transition dipole moments with CASPT2 energies.
nroots_per_mult: 6 state-averaged with equal weights for the LIIC paths; 3 state-averaged with equal weights for the CASPT2 single points
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies at the MP2/6-31G(d,p) ground-state C1 geometry, CASSCF then CASPT2, with dipole moment and oscillator strength: S1 1pipi*(1Lb) 5.226 then 4.852 eV, 2.700 D, f = 0.0064; S2 1pipi*(1La) 6.859 then 4.902 eV, 4.653 D, f = 0.1416; S3 1npi* 6.193 then 5.503 eV, 1.628 D, f = 0.0039; S4 1npi* 6.674 then 5.685 eV, 1.622 D, f = 0.0061; S5 1pipi* 7.232 then 6.098 eV, 1.203 D, f = 0.0374. At the respective CASSCF-optimized excited-state geometries the 0-0 excitation energies are: 1npi* 5.175 (CASSCF) then 4.476 eV (CASPT2) against an experimental 4.40 eV, dipole 2.776 D, f = 0.0035; 1pipi*(1Lb) 5.149 then 4.685 eV against an experimental 4.48 eV, dipole 2.461 D, f = 0.0057. Experimental values are from R2PI spectroscopy of jet-cooled adenine, whose 0-0 bands are separated by 0.08 eV. The ground-state dipole moment is 2.71 D. The 1npi* equilibrium structure is distorted out of plane. Two novel photochemical pathways leading to conical intersections with the ground state were identified, reached by stretching and twisting one of the two C-N bonds of the six-membered ring.
Other: Four different active spaces are used for four different jobs, and the substitutions are stated precisely enough to reuse. The 1pipi* optimization uses ten pi orbitals; the 1npi* optimization uses the SAME space with the lowest-energy pi orbital swapped out for a lone pair; the nonplanar saddle-point search uses nine nominally-pi orbitals plus one n orbital; and the LIIC single points use 12 electrons in 10 orbitals. So the two excited-state minima whose 0-0 energies are compared against experiment (4.476 and 4.685 eV against 4.40 and 4.48) were optimized in DIFFERENT orbital spaces — legitimate, since each space is tailored to the state it describes, but it means the 0.21 eV computed gap is not a single-space quantity. The conical-intersection searches are the weak link and the paper says why: "due to internal limitations of this program, the active space for the CASSCF calculations had to be reduced to 6 electrons distributed in 6 orbitals", assembled from the three RHF HOMOs and three LUMOs at the guessed geometry. The intersections that carry the paper's mechanistic conclusions therefore rest on a (6,6) space while the energies along the paths to them come from a (12,10) space. State averaging also changes between stages — six states with equal weights for the LIIC paths but only three for the final CASPT2 single points — and an imaginary level shift of 0.3 au was needed to suppress intruder states. The correlation correction is highly state-specific: CASSCF places 1pipi*(1La) 1.63 eV above 1pipi*(1Lb), but CASPT2 collapses that to 0.05 eV, a 1.96 eV differential shift, so the bright/dark state ordering is entirely a dynamic-correlation effect. One barrier could not be located at the CASSCF level at all because the states were too strongly mixed there; the paper infers it is probably very low.
reference_short: Perun, Sobolewski & Domcke, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 6257
notes: Investigates how the 1npi* and 1pipi* excited singlet states of the 9H tautomer of adenine deactivate so rapidly, identifying two novel photochemical pathways to conical intersections with the ground state. The conical-intersection guess geometries were built by stretching and twisting a C-N bond of the six-membered ring, following the authors' earlier experience with benzene, pyrazine and the guanine-cytosine base pair. The geometry at the maximum of the lowest excited singlet's LIIC energy profile served as the initial guess for the saddle-point search on that path. Comparison with earlier work: TDDFT gave 0-0 energies of 4.75 and 5.05 eV for the lowest 1npi* and 1pipi* states, another calculation gave 3.77 and 4.71 eV, and Broo predicted 1npi* and 1pipi* fluorescence band maxima at 3.32 and 4.02 eV — the present results suggest those earlier calculations overestimated the 0-0 gap between the 1npi* and 1Lb states. The reversal of state ordering on excited-state geometry optimization had been noted previously by several authors.
correlation_correction: LS-CASPT2 with an imaginary level shift of 0.3 au, on a state-averaged CASSCF reference over the three lowest states

compound_name: Succinonitrile (NC-CH2-CH2-CN) decomposition — singlet biradicals and near-degenerate transition states
geometry_source: CASSCF/DZP optimized geometries and frequencies for the multireference species; G2 geometries for the single-reference ones
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with CASPT2 single points; Gaussian-2 (G2) theory and MRCI used alongside
basis_set: Dunning double-zeta plus polarization (DZP) for the CASSCF geometries and frequencies; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 single points; VTZ2P (cc-pVTZ with the 4f functions removed from heavy atoms and the 3d from hydrogen, leaving valence triple-zeta with two polarization sets) for the larger CASPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Reference states for the succinonitrile decomposition range from CASSCF(6/6) to CASSCF(10/10) depending on the stationary point; the paper's notation is CASSCF(nel/nao). The largest space, (10/10), was used with the VTZ2P basis for selected pathways. The orbitals composing each space are not enumerated.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF/DZP geometries and vibrational frequencies for singlet biradical species and for transition states showing appreciable near-degeneracy, with CASPT2 single points at those geometries using cc-pVDZ; selected pathways recomputed at CASPT2 with a CASSCF(10/10) reference and the VTZ2P basis. G2 was used for all species where a single-reference expansion is valid, but cannot be used for singlet biradicals at all.
electronic_structure_description: Decomposition proceeds in part through singlet biradical species and through transition states with appreciable near-degeneracy, neither of which G2 can treat — singlet biradicals because the method rests on a single-reference expansion, and the near-degenerate transition states because of the multiconfigurational character. Contrary to the authors' initial expectation, G2 nonetheless performed well for most transition state energies. Agreement between G2 and CASPT2 relative energies is generally good for species of the same spin state; the systematic disagreement appears when comparing states of different multiplicity, where CASPT2 predicts carbene singlet-triplet separations 30 kJ/mol larger than G2. CC fission in succinonitrile yields cyanomethyl radicals.
Other: The paper is unusually explicit about apportioning blame between basis set and active space, and it benchmarks the multireference route against experiment rather than assuming it. Spaces are chosen per species — ranging from CASSCF(3/4) to CASSCF(10/10) overall, CASSCF(6/6) to CASSCF(10/10) for the succinonitrile decomposition, and (8/8) for acrylonitrile — with CASSCF used specifically where a single-reference expansion fails: singlet biradicals and transition states showing appreciable near-degeneracy. The calibration against small carbenes (:CH2, :CF2, :CHF), where experiment is available, gives a clean statement of systematic error: G2 UNDERestimates the relative stability of triplets by 10 kJ/mol while CASPT2 OVERestimates it by 20 kJ/mol, and CASPT2 consistently predicts carbene singlet-triplet separations 30 kJ/mol larger than G2. MRCI with the same basis as the CASPT2 work agrees closely with experiment, so the error is attributable to the perturbative treatment rather than to the reference — though tellingly MRCI and CASPT2 both underestimate the lowest singlet-to-triplet vertical excitation of ethylene by the same 20 kJ/mol, while G2 overestimates it by 10. The active-space contribution is then isolated directly on acrylonitrile: CASPT2/cc-pVDZ with an (8/8) space sits systematically 15 kJ/mol above G2, enlarging both the basis (to VTZ2P) and the space (to (10/10)) cuts that to 11 kJ/mol, and comparing CASPT2 against QCISD(T) in the SAME VTZ2P basis leaves only 6.6 kJ/mol. The authors' conclusion is that the discrepancy is "the result of a combination of factors, such as the obvious differences in basis sets as well as the choice of active space" — neither alone. Agreement between G2 and CASPT2 is described as good for species of the same spin state and poorer for acrylonitrile than for succinonitrile.
reference_short: Sendt, Ikeda, Bacskay & Mackie, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 1054
notes: Combined single-pulse shock tube experiments and ab initio study of acetonitrile pyrolysis, dilute in argon at 1400-2100 K and an average pressure of 12 atm. Principal products are HCN, C2H2, CH4 and H2, with HCCCN, H2CCHCN, C2H4 and C4H2 as minor products. G2 theory was used wherever a single-reference expansion is valid and CASSCF/CASPT2 where it is not — singlet biradicals, for which G2 cannot be used at all, and transition states with appreciable near-degeneracy. For the larger systems G2 was modified to be affordable: the Delta-E(2df) correction taken at MP2 rather than MP4, and the MP2/6-311+G(3df,2p) energy estimated additively; tested on smaller systems this modified G2 agreed with full G2 to an average of 3 kJ/mol. Succinonitrile was not detected in the shock tube pyrolyses of acetonitrile despite being observed in acetonitrile pyrolysis elsewhere, and only traces were identified by GC/MS. The computed C-H bond dissociation enthalpy of acetonitrile is 79.1 kJ/mol against an experimental 73.9 +/- 0.8, giving a cyanomethyl heat of formation of 267 kJ/mol; measured Arrhenius parameters for CH3CN dissociation are A = 10^14.6+/-0.3 s-1 and Ea = 397 kJ/mol.

geometry_source: CASSCF optimized geometries; the modified G2 procedure supplied energies for the single-reference species
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with CASPT2 single points; Gaussian-2 (G2) theory and MRCI used alongside
basis_set: Dunning double-zeta plus polarization (DZP) for the CASSCF geometries and frequencies; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 single points; VTZ2P (cc-pVTZ with the 4f functions removed from heavy atoms and the 3d from hydrogen, leaving valence triple-zeta with two polarization sets) for the larger CASPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Eight active electrons in eight orbitals for the CASPT2/cc-pVDZ calculations, enlarged to a (10/10) space for the VTZ2P calculations. The orbitals are not enumerated in the paper.
active_space_protocol: CASPT2 single points at CASSCF geometries with (8/8) and cc-pVDZ, then repeated with the larger (10/10) space and the VTZ2P basis to separate active-space effects from basis-set effects; QCISD(T)/VTZ2P computed for the same structures as a third point of comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Decomposition pathways of acrylonitrile, treated with both G2 and CASPT2. Agreement between the two is notably POORER than for succinonitrile: CASPT2/cc-pVDZ places intermediates, transition states and products relative to acrylonitrile systematically 15 kJ/mol above the G2 values. Enlarging both the basis to VTZ2P and the active space to (10/10) reduces the discrepancy to 11 kJ/mol, and comparing CASPT2 with QCISD(T) in the same VTZ2P basis brings it down to 6.6 kJ/mol — locating most of the residual difference in basis-set and active-space choices rather than in the correlation treatment itself.
Other: The paper is unusually explicit about apportioning blame between basis set and active space, and it benchmarks the multireference route against experiment rather than assuming it. Spaces are chosen per species — ranging from CASSCF(3/4) to CASSCF(10/10) overall, CASSCF(6/6) to CASSCF(10/10) for the succinonitrile decomposition, and (8/8) for acrylonitrile — with CASSCF used specifically where a single-reference expansion fails: singlet biradicals and transition states showing appreciable near-degeneracy. The calibration against small carbenes (:CH2, :CF2, :CHF), where experiment is available, gives a clean statement of systematic error: G2 UNDERestimates the relative stability of triplets by 10 kJ/mol while CASPT2 OVERestimates it by 20 kJ/mol, and CASPT2 consistently predicts carbene singlet-triplet separations 30 kJ/mol larger than G2. MRCI with the same basis as the CASPT2 work agrees closely with experiment, so the error is attributable to the perturbative treatment rather than to the reference — though tellingly MRCI and CASPT2 both underestimate the lowest singlet-to-triplet vertical excitation of ethylene by the same 20 kJ/mol, while G2 overestimates it by 10. The active-space contribution is then isolated directly on acrylonitrile: CASPT2/cc-pVDZ with an (8/8) space sits systematically 15 kJ/mol above G2, enlarging both the basis (to VTZ2P) and the space (to (10/10)) cuts that to 11 kJ/mol, and comparing CASPT2 against QCISD(T) in the SAME VTZ2P basis leaves only 6.6 kJ/mol. The authors' conclusion is that the discrepancy is "the result of a combination of factors, such as the obvious differences in basis sets as well as the choice of active space" — neither alone. Agreement between G2 and CASPT2 is described as good for species of the same spin state and poorer for acrylonitrile than for succinonitrile.

geometry_source: Geometry optimized by DFT (UB3LYP/6-31G* with SCRF dipole); CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* used as a single-point diagnostic at that structure
method: CASSCF(4,4) configuration-interaction coefficient analysis at optimized geometries; UB3LYP and RB3LYP with SCRF (dipole) for the energetics, CISD for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF and B3LYP calculations; 6-31+G(d) for the CISD comparison
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(4,4) spanning the HOMO/LUMO pair of the forming biradical and their partners; the doubly excited configuration examined is (HOMO -> LUMO, HOMO -> LUMO).
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* is used narrowly and diagnostically — not for energetics but to read off the configuration-interaction coefficients at geometries optimized by other methods, in order to decide whether each intermediate is a singlet BIRADICAL or a closed-shell ZWITTERION. Relative energies come from UB3LYP/6-31G* and RB3LYP/6-31G* with an SCRF dipole solvation model; a CISD/6-31+G(d) calculation provides an independent coefficient for comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet biradical formed from o-benzyne and tropothione without any activation barrier, with a trans C16-C15-S1-C2 arrangement; one radical spin density is localized at C16 of the six-membered ring and the other delocalized over the seven-membered ring. It is a biradical rather than a zwitterion because the CI weight is not confined to the adiabatic electron configuration: at CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* the adiabatic configuration coefficient is -0.706 and the doubly excited one 0.689 (CISD/6-31+G(d) gives 0.871 for the adiabatic coefficient). Energetically it lies 13.7 kcal/mol below the separated reagents at UB3LYP/6-31G* SCRF = dipole, and 6.2 kcal/mol below the corresponding closed-shell species at RB3LYP/6-31G* SCRF = dipole. It isomerizes through TS(11 -> 12) by alpha-hydrogen abstraction from the tropothione ring by the benzyne radical centre, giving the closed-shell cumulene species 12.
Other: A textbook use of a minimal active space as a DIAGNOSTIC rather than an energy method. CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* is run purely to read the configuration-interaction coefficients and settle whether each intermediate is a singlet biradical or a zwitterion — a question no single-reference calculation can answer, since the distinguishing feature is precisely the weight of the doubly excited configuration. The numbers make the distinction sharp: for intermediate 11 the adiabatic configuration carries a coefficient of -0.706 against 0.689 for the doubly excited (HOMO->LUMO, HOMO->LUMO) configuration, and for intermediate 17 the values are -0.702 and 0.689 — near-equal weights, hence genuine singlet biradicals. For intermediate 18 the adiabatic coefficient is 0.997, leaving essentially nothing for the double excitation, so that species is a zwitterion described adequately by a Hartree-Fock configuration. The same molecule therefore reacts as a biradical or an ionic reagent depending on the partner, and only the CI weights reveal which. The paper also flags a method dependence in the diagnostic itself: CISD/6-31+G(d) gives 0.871 for the adiabatic coefficient of 11 where CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* gives -0.706, so the absolute weight is sensitive to the correlation treatment even though the qualitative biradical assignment is not. Because the space is used only for this purpose, none of the reported reaction energies are CASSCF numbers — they come from UB3LYP and RB3LYP with SCRF dipole solvation, e.g. biradical 11 lying 13.7 kcal/mol below the separated reagents at UB3LYP and 6.2 kcal/mol below the corresponding closed-shell species at RB3LYP.
reference_short: Yamabe, Minato, Ishiwata, Irinamihira & Machiguchi, J. Org. Chem. 2007, 72, 2832
notes: Mechanistic study of the reaction of o-benzyne with tropothione, showing that it proceeds through biradical rather than concerted pathways. A singlet biradical intermediate (11) composed of the two reagents forms with NO activation barrier, with a trans C16-C15-S1-C2 moiety, one radical spin density localized at C16 of the six-membered ring and the other delocalized over the seven-membered ring. It then undergoes an unusual isomerization in which the alpha hydrogen of the tropothione ring is snapped off by the benzyne radical centre — driven by formation of the C-H bond in the benzyne ring — giving a closed-shell cumulene-containing species 12; the paper notes such C-H scission in cyclic conjugated compounds is unprecedented. The comparison with olefin reactions (e.g. H2C=C(OMe)2) establishes that o-benzyne is basically a biradical reagent. The 'triple' bond of o-benzyne is spectroscopically established as intermediate between a double and triple bond, since the rigid directionality of the two in-plane sp2 orbitals prevents a typical acetylene-like triple bond with a large pi-pi* gap.

geometry_source: Conical intersection geometry optimized at CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G*; excited-state minima optimized at TD-B3LYP/6-31G(d)
method: CASSCF conical intersection and intersystem crossing point optimization; TD-B3LYP for excited-state minima and vertical excitations
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(8,7) for the S1(1npi*)/S2(1pipi*) conical intersection: seven active orbitals comprising one nO, one sigma(C-N), two pi, two pi* and one sigma*(C-N).
active_space_protocol: CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* used specifically to locate the conical intersection between the two lowest excited singlets, with the sigma(C-N)/sigma*(C-N) pair included in the space because the crossing involves that bond. No higher-level check of the intersection was possible for want of computational resources. All other quantities — excited-state minima, vertical excitations, Raman intensities — come from TD-B3LYP/6-31G(d).
electronic_structure_description: The Sn/Spi conical intersection lies 130 kcal/mol above S0 at CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G(d) and is located NEAR the Franck-Condon region. Strong Sn-Spi vibronic coupling there is what produces the A-band resonance Raman spectrum, whose structural dynamics run along the C2=O/C4=O symmetric stretch (nu7) and the C2=O/C4=O antisymmetric stretch plus C5=C6 stretch (nu8) modes. For context from TD-B3LYP, the Sn and Spi minima lie 93 and 107 kcal/mol above S0, respectively 14.9 and 10.3 kcal/mol below their Franck-Condon geometries; Sn is a relatively pure 1npi* state while Spi is noticeably mixed with Sn.
Other: Two DIFFERENT (8,7) spaces are used for the two crossing points, each built around the orbitals the specific crossing needs, and the substitution is stated explicitly. For the S1(1npi*)/S2(1pipi*) CONICAL INTERSECTION the seven orbitals are one nO, one sigma(C-N), two pi, two pi* and one sigma*(C-N) — the sigma/sigma* pair being included because the intersection involves C-N stretching. For the S1(1npi*)/T1(3pipi*) INTERSYSTEM CROSSING the seven orbitals are instead one nO, three pi, two pi* and one RYDBERG orbital, dropping the sigma/sigma* pair entirely and adding a diffuse function. So the two crossing energies quoted on the same kcal/mol scale relative to S0 — 130 for the conical intersection and 85.5 for the intersystem crossing — come from different orbital selections and are not strictly one surface. The paper is candid about the limit on validating this: "due to the limited computational resources, we are unable to check the Sn/Spi conical intersection point at any higher theoretical level", so no convergence test against a larger space or a correlated method was performed for the intersection that carries the mechanistic argument. Everything else in the study rests on TD-B3LYP rather than CASSCF — the excited-state minima, the vertical excitation energies and the resonance Raman intensity analysis — with CASSCF used only where a single-reference method cannot go, namely at the two crossing points. Note the resulting scale mismatch: the Sn and Spi minima are placed 93 and 107 kcal/mol above S0 by TD-B3LYP while the crossings between them are placed at 130 and 85.5 kcal/mol by CASSCF, so the relative ordering of minima and funnels mixes two levels of theory.
reference_short: Li, Liu, Zhao, Pei, Wang, Zheng & Fang, J. Phys. Chem. B 2013, 117, 11660
notes: Resonance Raman and quantum chemical study of the excited-state structures and decay dynamics of 1,3-dimethyluracil (DMU) and 5-bromo-1,3-dimethyluracil (5BrDMU) in acetonitrile, methanol and water. DMU shows lambda-max = 266 nm in water, red-shifted 7 nm from uracil's 259 nm because of hyperconjugation between the methyl group and the pi(H) orbital; 5BrDMU absorbs at 280 nm in acetonitrile, a further 16 nm red shift attributed to the antibonding interaction between the bromine p(z) orbital and the DMU pi orbital raising the donor orbital energy. Computed singlet transitions at 232 nm (f = 0.1495) and 201 nm (f = 0.1273) correlate with the observed A-band at 264 nm (f = 0.2369) and B-band at 206 nm (f = 0.3695). Both molecules have 48 normal modes, and this work provides the first vibrational assignments for either. compound_name: Chloroethene radical cation (C2H3Cl+) — low-lying states and Cl-loss photodissociation
point_group: Cs (the C2H3Cl+ system is assumed to remain in Cs symmetry throughout)
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations for all four ionic states at BOTH the CASSCF and the CASPT2 level, with frequency analyses at the CASSCF level at the CASSCF-optimized geometries; Cl-loss potential energy curves computed at fixed R(C2-Cl) values
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 geometry optimization and single points; Cl-loss potential energy curves at the CASPT2//CASSCF level
basis_set: Contracted atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis, Cl[6s4p3d1f] / C[5s3p2d1f] / H[3s2p1d]
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(13,11): all eleven orbitals — seven occupied plus four virtual — appearing in the ground-state electron configuration of the NEUTRAL C2H3Cl molecule, [...(9a')2 (10a')2 (11a')2 (12a')2 (2a'')2 (13a')2 (3a'')2 (14a')0 (15a')0 (16a')0 (4a'')0...] as determined by HF/6-311+G(d,p), holding 13 active electrons in the cation.
active_space_protocol: The active space is derived from the electron configuration of the neutral parent molecule rather than being selected orbital by orbital, following the authors' previous CAS studies on molecular ions: every orbital in the frontier block of the neutral's HF configuration — seven occupied and four virtual — becomes active. The stated adequacy criterion is that this space "should be large enough for the CAS calculations of the lowest-lying two 2A' and two 2A'' states of the ion". CASPT2 computes the first-order wave function and second-order energy in the FULL space; reference quality is reported, with CASSCF reference weights in the first-order wave functions exceeding 0.87 in every case. compound_name: Pyridinium-N-phenoxide betaine dye (PNP) — S1 excited state in gas phase and aqueous solution
point_group: C2 imposed on the ground-state optimizations (each ring constrained planar); the S1 calculation is run in C1 but at the C2-optimized ground-state geometry
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized at the RHF level — in the gas phase directly, and in aqueous solution by the RISM-SCF method at RHF level. The S1 excited-state calculations use those ground-state structures. Throughout all optimizations both the pyridinium and the phenoxide ring were constrained planar with C2 symmetry in each ring.
method: CASSCF, coupled self-consistently to the reference interaction site model self-consistent field (RISM-SCF) procedure for the solution-phase calculations
basis_set: (9s5p1d/4s1p) contracted to [3s2p1d/2s1p], of valence double-zeta plus polarization (DZP) quality
active_space_orbital_description: Eleven active orbitals holding twelve electrons, constructed from the pi and pi* orbitals of the pyridinium and phenoxide ring moieties — six pi-valence active orbitals — together with the nonbonding (n) orbital on the oxygen.
active_space_protocol: The paper documents a convergence FAILURE and the workaround adopted for it: "with the present active space set, we could not obtain convergence for the pure S1 state with an optimized geometry in C1 symmetry from the ground-state at the RHF level." Rather than enlarge the space — explicitly rejected as "much more time-consuming" — the authors first verified that the state-averaged CASSCF wave function gave the SAME dominant configuration state function for S1 at both the C2 and the C1 optimized geometries, with molecular orbital symmetry switched off. Having established that, they ran the S1 calculation under C1 symmetry but on the geometry optimized under C2 constraint at the RHF ground-state level, describing this as a reasonable compromise between completeness and computational effort given that only the inter-ring torsion angle is of interest. Solvation is handled by RISM-SCF fully self-consistently with the CASSCF wave function, with solute site partial charges evaluated on roughly 45 000 Lebedev grid points around the solute.
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged CASSCF used to verify the S1 configuration; the production S1 calculation is state-specific
electronic_structure_description: PNP is charge-separated in its ground state, with an anionic phenoxide ring and a cationic pyridinium ring. The CASSCF wave function for the vertically excited S1 state is described mainly by a pi -> pi*-like transition transferring charge directly from phenoxide-ring orbitals to pyridinium-ring orbitals without change of nuclear geometry, so that charge separation is REDUCED in S1; the wave function also carries some n -> pi* character with smaller weight. The computed vertical transition energy is 2.26 eV, in very close agreement with an experimental estimate of 18 509 cm-1 (2.29 eV) for PNP in vacuum. The gas-phase torsional potential energy surface of S1 decreases monotonically with the inter-ring torsion angle, reaching a minimum at 90 degrees, with an energy difference of about 10.7 kcal/mol between 0 and 90 degrees. Ring twisting enhances the shift in charge-transfer character on excitation.
Other: The (12,11) pi + n(O) space is adequate for the vertical excitation — it gives 2.26 eV against an experimental 2.29 eV — but NOT adequate to optimize on: "with the present active space set, we could not obtain convergence for the pure S1 state with an optimized geometry in C1 symmetry." The authors state plainly that they declined to enlarge it, calling a bigger space "much more time-consuming", and instead validated a substitute protocol: they checked that the state-averaged CASSCF wave function contains the same dominant configuration state function for S1 at both the C2- and C1-optimized geometries with orbital symmetry turned off, then computed S1 in C1 on a geometry optimized under C2 constraint at the RHF level. So the entire S1 torsional surface — the paper's central result, running from 0 to 90 degrees with a 10.7 kcal/mol drop — rests on ground-state RHF geometries rather than relaxed excited-state ones, and the justification is a configuration-identity check rather than an energy convergence test. The authors bound the claim accordingly, noting that they focus only on the inter-ring torsion angle. A second consequence of the small space is that the S1 wave function mixes pi->pi* charge transfer with a smaller n->pi* component, which is precisely why the oxygen lone pair had to be in the space alongside the six pi-valence orbitals; a pi-only space would have missed that admixture entirely.

notes: Studies the strong coupling between solvation and electronic structure in the excited state of the betaine dye pyridinium-N-phenoxide (PNP), the chromophore family underlying the ET(30) solvent polarity scale. The gas-phase torsional surface is in Figure 3 and the charge-transfer scheme in Figure 2.

method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with CASPT2N single points
basis_set: 6-31G* for geometry optimizations and frequencies; single points also with cc-pVDZ and 6-311G(2d,p) (valence triple-zeta, two d sets on C and N, one p set on H)
active_space_orbital_description: (8,8) for phenylnitrene: seven pi and pi* molecular orbitals plus the in-plane p atomic orbital on nitrogen.
active_space_protocol: An eight-electron, eight-orbital space is used for every species on the surface to keep the active space a constant SIZE, with its composition adapted per structure. Vibrational frequencies computed at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* verify each stationary point as a minimum or transition state, and the unscaled CASSCF(8,8) frequencies supply the zero-point corrections. Single points were recomputed at the CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* geometries with cc-pVDZ and 6-311G(2d,p).
electronic_structure_description: Triplet ground state (3A2), with the lowest singlet 1A2 lying 18 kcal/mol above it by experiment. Singlet 1a has never been directly observed; it either intersystem crosses to the triplet ground state or isomerizes thermally to ketenimine 3a, and those two channels compete. Ring expansion from the 1A2 state proceeds through the bicyclic azirine 2a with a rate-determining barrier of about 6 kcal/mol, matching the experimental value revised upward from about 3 kcal/mol. Ketenimine 3a reverts thermally to triplet 1a in solution at ambient temperature, and both triplet 1a and 3a can be interconverted photochemically.
Other: A deliberate constant-size (8,8) space is imposed across the ENTIRE singlet surface so that reactant, intermediates, transition states and product are comparable — "an eight-electron, eight-orbital active space, hereafter designated (8,8), was used for all species" — but the eight orbitals are composed differently at every stationary point, and the paper enumerates each. Phenylnitrene 1a: seven pi and pi* MOs plus the in-plane p atomic orbital on nitrogen. Ketenimine 3a: the four pi and four pi* MOs of the double bonds. The two transition states TS1a and TS2a: six mainly-pi orbitals plus a sigma/sigma* pair for the partially formed or broken bond. Azacycloheptatrienylidene 4a: seven pi and pi* MOs plus the in-plane hybrid on the carbene carbon. The interesting case is the bicyclic azirine 2a, where the authors say the choice "was somewhat problematic": six pi orbitals are obvious, but the sigma/sigma* pair could be either the bridgehead C-C bond or the azirine C-N bond, and "might seem arbitrary, since the pathways that connect 2a to 1a and to 3a each involve breaking a different one of these two bonds". They resolve it on two independent grounds rather than by preference — the RHF/6-31G* C-N bond is much longer (1.530 A) than the bridgehead C-C bond (1.445 A), implying it is weaker; and because 2a is nonplanar, the C-N bond orientation mixes considerably more with the six pi MOs than the C-C bond does. This is an unusually explicit record of how a sigma/sigma* pair gets chosen when the reaction coordinate is ambiguous. Consistency of space size is what makes the reported relative energies meaningful; the accompanying caution is that a constant COUNT does not mean a constant space, so any reuse of these numbers inherits five different orbital selections.
reference_short: Karney & Borden, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1997, 119, 1378
notes: Ab initio study of the ring expansion of phenylnitrene, compared with the analogous ring expansion of phenylcarbene. Singlet 1a has never been directly observed and neither has 2a, though nucleophilic trapping products point to its intermediacy. Isodesmic reactions used to dissect the energetic differences are in Table 2 and all relative energies in Table 1.
