compound_name: Aniline — low-lying singlet and triplet excited states
point_group: Cs (states classified as A' and A'')
geometry_source: Geometries optimized by DFT (B3LYP; UB3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) for open-shell systems), with CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 applied afterwards for the excitation energies. Vibrational frequencies obtained at both UB3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) and CASSCF levels, but the normal modes were analysed from the UB3LYP results.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 and multistate MS-CASPT2 for excitation energies; RASSCF used to screen the Rydberg orbital content; UB3LYP alongside
basis_set: ANO-S atomic natural orbital sets, C([10s6p3d]/3s2p1d), N([10s6p3d]/3s2p1d), H([7s]/2s), supplemented by Rydberg 3s and 3p functions with exponents 0.024624 and 0.042335 placed at the centre of charge; 6-311++G(d,p) for the UB3LYP calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons of variable occupancy in 12 active orbitals, comprising 8 a' and 4 a'' orbitals. The space carries 3s- and 3p-Rydberg orbitals but deliberately NO 3d-Rydberg orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The Rydberg content of the space was decided by an explicit screening step rather than by assumption. Rydberg basis functions were generated by first running a CASSCF calculation on aniline with one electron removed, at the B3LYP-optimized geometry, to locate the centre of charge, and adding the functions there. Earlier SAC/SAC-CI work indicated no d-Rydberg orbital is involved up to the 18th singlet excited state; the authors then verified this for themselves by inspecting the RASSCF orbitals and finding that 3d-Rydberg basis functions make no contribution to the orbitals from LUMO through LUMO+10. On that basis only 3s and 3p Rydberg orbitals were included. MS-CASPT2 energies were then constructed for four roots of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in each of the a' and a'' symmetries. The same threshold and level shift were used in every CASSCF/CASPT2 calculation of singlet and triplet states, so the two spin manifolds are treated identically.
nroots_per_mult: 4 roots per symmetry (a' and a'') for each spin
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in eV with the dominant configuration (|C| > 0.3), compared against SAC-CI and experiment. Singlets: 1(1A'') (S1) pi -> pi*, 4.33 (SAC-CI 4.20, experiment 4.22); 1(1A') (S2) pi -> Rydberg(s), 4.85 (4.53, 4.60); 2(1A') (S3) pi -> pi*, 5.54 (5.34, 5.39); 2(1A'') (S4) pi -> Rydberg(pz), 5.92 (5.57); 3(1A') (S5) pi -> Rydberg(s,pz), 5.99 (6.06); 3(1A'') (S6) pi -> Rydberg(s), 6.28 (6.39); 4(1A') (S7) pi -> Rydberg(px), 6.38 (6.26); 4(1A'') pi -> pi*, 6.92 (6.62, 6.40). Triplets: 1(3A') (T1) pi -> pi*, 3.74; 1(3A'') (T2) pi -> pi*, 3.82; 2(3A') (T3) pi -> pi*, 4.40; 3(3A') (T4) pi -> Rydberg(s), 4.60; 2(3A'') (T5) pi -> pi*, 5.31; 4(3A') (T6) pi -> Rydberg(py), 5.86; 3(3A'') (T7) pi -> Rydberg(pz), 5.88; 4(3A'') pi -> Rydberg(s), 6.22. Both T1 (3.74 eV) and T2 (3.82 eV) lie BELOW the S1 singlet at 4.33 eV. The experimental S1-T1 gap is about 7200 cm-1 (0.89 eV), and an observed 1A' state at 37 104 cm-1 (4.62 eV, 0.38 eV above S1) had been assigned as a 3s-Rydberg state.
Other: The 3d-Rydberg question is settled by inspection rather than by assumption, and the paper documents both halves of the check: prior SAC/SAC-CI work suggested no d-Rydberg orbital participates up to the 18th singlet excited state, and the authors independently confirmed it by examining RASSCF orbitals and finding 3d-Rydberg basis functions contribute nothing to LUMO through LUMO+10. Only then were 3s and 3p Rydberg orbitals kept, holding the space to (10,12) — 8 a' plus 4 a'' — instead of the much larger space that d-Rydberg inclusion would have forced. The Rydberg functions themselves are not placed arbitrarily: a CASSCF calculation on the aniline CATION locates the centre of charge, and the diffuse functions are added there. The payoff is visible in the assignments, since five of the eight computed singlets and four of the eight triplets are Rydberg in character and could not have been described at all without those orbitals. Accuracy against experiment is good for the valence states — 4.33 eV computed against 4.22 for S1 and 5.54 against 5.39 for S3 — while the Rydberg states run 0.2-0.35 eV above the SAC-CI values. A methodological point the paper makes explicitly is that the same threshold and level shift were used for every singlet and triplet CASSCF/CASPT2 calculation, which is what licenses the direct comparison showing T1 and T2 both falling below S1. Note that all these numbers rest on DFT-optimized geometries rather than CASSCF ones, and that the vibrational normal modes were analysed from UB3LYP rather than from the CASSCF frequencies that were also computed.
reference_short: Hou, Quan, Holtzl et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 10396
notes: Determines the vertical low-lying singlet and triplet states of aniline, motivated by the fast decay of its triplet state and by the assignment of an observed band at 4.62 eV to a 3s-Rydberg state. Vertical gaps are computed as total-energy differences at the ground singlet optimized geometry, and adiabatic gaps as differences between singlet and triplet states at their respective relaxed geometries. The gas-phase proton affinity of aniline in the T1 state was computed as the difference between the ZPE-corrected total energies of aniline and protonated aniline, with geometries and frequencies of aniline protonated at different ring positions optimized at UB3LYP/6-311++G(d,p). Electron distribution in the high-spin state was analysed by several approaches. Reported literature S1-T1 gaps vary from 3.41 to 3.45 eV across studies.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 and multistate MS-CASPT2 on the CASSCF reference, with a common threshold and level shift across all singlet and triplet calculations

point_group: C1 for the asymmetric transition states and intermediates; Cs and C2 products located for the disilene reaction
geometry_source: All equilibrium and transition-state geometries optimized with analytically calculated energy gradients at CASSCF/6-31G(d); frequency calculations at the CASSCF level determine the nature of each stationary point and supply zero-point corrections; intrinsic reaction coordinates followed from each transition state toward both reactants and products
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with CASPT2 single points; CiLC-IRC (configuration interaction / localized molecular orbital / CASSCF along the IRC) analysis
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF optimizations, frequencies and CiLC-IRC; CASPT2 single points with both 6-31G(d) and 6-311++G(d,p)
active_space_orbital_description: Six orbitals relating to the reaction were included in the active space, with all configurations generated among them — the standard Diels-Alder space of the diene pi system plus the dienophile pi/pi* pair.
active_space_protocol: One six-orbital space is used for every stationary point on both reaction surfaces so that concerted and stepwise pathways are directly comparable. Beyond the energetics, the space is exploited diagnostically through CiLC-IRC: a CASSCF calculation supplies a starting set of orbitals which are then localized, and a configuration-interaction analysis in that localized basis is carried out at points along the IRC to classify the electronic character of each pathway as concerted or stepwise.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet surface with an asymmetric concerted transition state that is almost stepwise, plus two genuine stepwise routes. Relative energies in kcal/mol at CASSCF/6-31G(d), CASPT2/6-31G(d) and CASPT2/6-311++G(d,p), with ZPE-corrected values in parentheses: reactants 0.0/0.0/0.0; concerted TS(CSi) 14.96 (16.20) / 3.41 (4.66) / 0.85 (2.09); stepwise C-Si route TS(CSi-Si)-1 14.30 (15.55) / 3.66 (4.91) / 1.74 (2.99), intermediate inter(CSi-Si) 5.24 (6.47) / -2.28 (-1.05) / -4.42 (-3.19), TS(CSi-Si)-2 6.88 (8.13) / -0.56 (0.68) / -3.06 (-1.81); stepwise C-C route TS(CSi-C)-1 23.10 (25.17) / 12.19 (14.26) / 10.82 (12.89), inter(CSi-C) 6.62 (10.30) / -4.87 (-1.19) / -5.33 (-1.65), TS(CSi-C)-2 9.59 (13.23) / -2.10 (1.54) / -2.92 (0.72); product -53.86 (-46.87) / -68.64 (-61.64) / -68.89 (-61.90). The concerted barrier is only 0.89 kcal/mol below the first stepwise C-Si transition state at the CASPT2 level, and the first step of the C-Si stepwise route lies 9.9 kcal/mol below the corresponding C-C route.
Other: The six-orbital space is held constant across every stationary point of both reactions, which is what makes the concerted-versus-stepwise comparison meaningful — but the comparison it enables is also one that the CASSCF level alone would get badly wrong. Dynamic correlation shifts every barrier down enormously and NOT uniformly, so the mechanistic conclusion changes with the correlation treatment. For butadiene + silaethylene the concerted transition state TS(CSi) falls from 14.96 kcal/mol at CASSCF/6-31G(d) to 3.41 at CASPT2/6-31G(d) and 0.85 at CASPT2/6-311++G(d,p), while the competing first stepwise transition state TS(CSi-Si)-1 falls from 14.30 to 3.66 to 1.74. At CASSCF the stepwise path is FAVOURED by 0.66 kcal/mol; at CASPT2 the ordering reverses and the concerted path leads by 0.25 kcal/mol at the small basis and 0.89 at the large one — the paper's headline number. A margin under 1 kcal/mol between two mechanisms is well inside the uncertainty of the method, which is why the authors also bring the CiLC-IRC electronic analysis to bear rather than resting the assignment on energies. The disilene case is more dramatic still: the stepwise TS(SiSi)-1 drops from 9.44 kcal/mol at CASSCF to -2.97 and then -4.61 at CASPT2, so "the energy barrier of the first step of the stepwise reaction disappears" entirely — a barrier that exists at CASSCF and does not exist after correlation is added. Reaction exothermicities move by about 15 kcal/mol on the same correction (-53.86 to -68.89 for silaethylene), confirming that the (6,6) space captures the bond reorganization but leaves a large and structure-dependent dynamic-correlation deficit.
reference_short: Wakayama & Sakai, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 13575
notes: Study of the concerted and stepwise mechanisms of the Diels-Alder [4+2] cycloadditions of butadiene with silaethylene (H2Si=CH2) and with disilene (H2Si=SiH2). For butadiene + silaethylene an asymmetric concerted process — described as almost stepwise — and two stepwise processes were located, and C-Si bond formation is more favourable than C-C bond formation for the first step of the stepwise route. Energies in parentheses in Table 1 include the zero-point correction. Reaction pathways are analysed electronically by the CiLC-IRC method, whose details follow the authors' earlier papers.

compound_name: Formaldiminoxy radical (CH2NO) and its isomers — dissociation reactions
point_group: Cs for the CH2NO(2A') ground state; C1 for most transition states
geometry_source: Transition state and stationary point geometries optimized at CASSCF(11/11)/cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 and QCISD(T) single points; G2 energies taken at MP2/6-31G(d) geometries. Zero-point corrections come from CASSCF(11/11) for the CASPT2 and QCISD(T) numbers and from G2 for the G2 numbers.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with CASPT2 single points; Gaussian-2 (G2) and QCISD(T) for comparison
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; cc-pVTZ for the CASPT2 and QCISD(T) single points; 6-311+G(3df,2p) within the G2 procedure
active_space_orbital_description: Eleven electrons treated as active in a space of eleven active orbitals, denoted 11/11 in the paper. The individual orbitals are not enumerated.
active_space_protocol: A single 11/11 space is used for every stationary point on the dissociation surface, so all 24 dissociation reactions of the 11 isomers are treated on one footing. The explicit justification for using CASSCF at all is bond fission: "since the transition states of the dissociation reactions involve bond fissions, CASSCF is expected to provide a more accurate description of such a process than MP2 (as used in G2)" — the multireference treatment is applied precisely where the single-reference G2 procedure is expected to fail. Geometries come from CASSCF/cc-pVDZ and energies from CASPT2/cc-pVTZ, with QCISD(T)/cc-pVTZ at the same geometries as an independent check.
multiplicities_studied: doublet (the radical and its isomers); singlet and triplet fragments among the products
electronic_structure_description: Doublet radical, CH2NO(2A') = isomer I1, with a G2 total energy of -168.930826 Eh (ZPE 18.43 kcal/mol), CASPT2(11/11)/cc-pVTZ -168.928014 Eh and QCISD(T)/cc-pVTZ -168.919733 Eh (CASSCF ZPE 18.87 kcal/mol). Formed by association of triplet methylene with nitric oxide, exothermic by about 76.5 kcal/mol — energy that can drive subsequent isomerization and dissociation if not thermally equilibrated. Twenty-four dissociation reactions of eleven isomers were characterized. Notable features: the N-O bond is very weak, with one dissociation having a critical energy of only 2.7 kcal/mol and being 20 kcal/mol exothermic; three conformers are separated by 6 kcal/mol barriers; isomer I4 has a NEGATIVE computed barrier of 2.1 kcal/mol for one channel, suggesting it may not be a stable species. CASSCF and MP2 disagree on which transition states exist — TS27.1, found by CASSCF, appears nonexistent at the MP2 level, and it lies about 1 kcal/mol above TS27 but connects different isomers, so the two methods predict different products from HCN + OH recombination.
Other: The 11/11 space is deployed selectively and for a stated reason: "since the transition states of the dissociation reactions involve bond fissions, CASSCF is expected to provide a more accurate description of such a process than MP2 (as used in G2)". The multireference treatment is therefore aimed at exactly the structures where the single-reference G2 route is least trustworthy, rather than applied uniformly. Its value shows up topologically rather than only energetically: the transition state TS27.1 is located at the CASSCF level but "appears to be nonexistent at the MP2 level", and because TS27 and TS27.1 connect DIFFERENT isomers to the products, the two levels of theory predict different outcomes for HCN + OH recombination — a qualitative difference in the reaction network, not a shifted barrier. The paper's confidence argument rests on triangulation rather than on the active space alone: "given the level of consistency among the G2, CASPT2, and QCISD(T) energies, as well as the more extensive basis sets used in this study, we expect our results to be more reliable" than earlier multireference CI work with a 6-311+G(d,p) basis, which gave critical energies significantly higher at 28.6 and 35.3 kcal/mol. Two practical limits are recorded honestly: the CASSCF geometry for TS48 could not be found at all ("we were unsuccessful in our initial attempts", not pursued because the reaction is minor), and CASPT2 energies rest on cc-pVDZ CASSCF geometries while G2 energies rest on MP2/6-31G(d) ones, so the three methods being compared do not share geometries.
reference_short: Shapley & Bacskay, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 4514
notes: Second paper of a pair, following the authors' study of the ISOMERIZATION reactions of the formaldiminoxy radical; this one treats decomposition. A total of 24 dissociation reactions of 11 isomers were characterized. Conclusions: because the NCO-chain isomers are highly stable and the energy needed to isomerize CH2NO into species such as NH2CO, NC(H)OH, HNCOH and HNC(H)O is relatively low, decomposition of those to HCN, HNC, OH, NH2, CO, HNCO and H is very favourable; the CNO-chain isomerizations and dissociations are generally more energetic and are not expected to compete strongly. Comparison with experiment is limited — only CO was detected in the experiments of Grussdorf et al., whereas the calculations suggest comparable quantities of HNCO, NH2 and HOCN should also appear, and the authors call for a kinetic modelling study to resolve the discrepancy. Energies are in Tables 1 and 2.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/cc-pVTZ single points on the CASSCF(11/11)/cc-pVDZ reference; QCISD(T)/cc-pVTZ at the same geometries as an independent check

compound_name: Chlorosilylene HSiCl (and DSiCl) — X(1A') and A(1A'') states
point_group: Cs (bent silylene; states classified as A' and A'')
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations at RCCSD(T) and CASSCF/MRCI for the X(1A') state and at CASSCF/MRCI only for the A(1A'') state, with complete-basis-set extrapolation and core-correlation corrections applied to the optimized parameters
method: CASSCF followed by MRCI with Davidson correction (MRCI+D); RCCSD(T) for the closed-shell ground state; Franck-Condon factor calculations including anharmonicity and Duschinsky rotation on the resulting potential energy functions
basis_set: aug-cc-pVQZ (AVQZ), aug-cc-pV5Z (AV5Z) and aug-cc-pwCVQZ (ACVQZ) quality. Standard aug-cc-pVQZ and aug-cc-pV5Z on hydrogen; aug-cc-pV(Q+d)Z and aug-cc-pV(5+d)Z on Si and Cl for the AVQZ/AV5Z sets; aug-cc-pwCVQZ on Si and Cl for the ACVQZ sets.
active_space_orbital_description: A FULL VALENCE active space was employed in the CASSCF and MRCI calculations. The paper states the rule but does not give the electron or orbital counts, so they are not recorded here.
active_space_protocol: All CASSCF/MRCI calculations are SINGLE STATE, not state-averaged: the CASSCF molecular orbitals and reference configurations feeding each MRCI calculation are optimized for the one state concerned, so the wave functions are optimal for that state rather than compromised across several. The default frozen core was used with the AVQZ and AV5Z sets; with the ACVQZ sets both the default frozen core and a core freezing only the Si 1s2 and Cl 1s2 electrons were run, so that the effect of correlating the Si and Cl 2s2 2p6 electrons could be isolated. Complete-basis-set contributions were estimated two independent ways — taking half the AVQZ-to-AV5Z difference, and applying the 1/X^3 formula to the same pair — and Davidson corrections were added to give MRCI+D.
multiplicities_studied: singlet (X(1A') and A(1A'')); a(3A'') triplet examined in preliminary calculations
nroots_per_mult: 1 (single-state CASSCF/MRCI for each state separately)
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell X(1A') ground state and open-shell singlet A(1A'') excited state. Computed adiabatic excitation energies Te in eV (cm-1 in parentheses): CASSCF/MRCI/AVQZ 2.6602 (21456.3); CASSCF/MRCI+D/AVQZ 2.6306 (21217.4); CASSCF/MRCI+D/ACVQZ (frozen core) 2.6291 (21205.3); CASSCF/MRCI/AV5Z 2.6533 (21400.3); CASSCF/MRCI+D/AV5Z 2.6311 (21220.9). The best theoretical Te value after all corrections is 2.564 +/- 0.067 eV (20683 +/- 538 cm-1). Multireference character in the X state is negligible: T1 diagnostics from RCCSD(T) are below 0.013 in all cases and the CI coefficient of the main ground-state configuration exceeds 0.92 in the CASSCF and MRCI wave functions. Simulated absorption and experimental LIF spectra agree very well, as do simulated and observed A(0,0,0) -> X single vibronic level emission spectra for both HSiCl and DSiCl; agreement is poorer for the DSiCl A(0,1,0) and A(0,2,1) emissions. Preliminary calculations on low-lying excited states suggest vibronic interaction between low vibrational levels of A(1A'') and highly excited vibrational levels of a(3A''), which could change the character of those levels and perturb the emission spectra.
Other: The paper decides WHICH method to trust on the basis of measured multireference character rather than by preference, and says so explicitly. For the closed-shell X(1A') state, T1 diagnostics below 0.013 and a leading CI coefficient above 0.92 show that "multireference character is negligibly small", from which the authors conclude that "the size-consistent, single-reference RCCSD(T) method should be the more suitable, and more reliable than the size-inconsistent MRCI method" for that state — an unusual case of a multireference calculation being run and then deliberately set aside in favour of coupled cluster on diagnostic grounds. CASSCF/MRCI is nonetheless carried out for X as well, purely so that the X-to-A energy separation can be computed consistently, because the A(1A'') state is an open-shell singlet that "cannot be adequately treated by a single electronic configuration and hence requires a multireference method". The active space is full valence and the CASSCF is SINGLE STATE for each state separately rather than state-averaged, so each wave function is variationally optimal for its own state — the opposite trade-off from the state-averaged protocols common elsewhere, buying accuracy per state at the cost of a common orbital basis. Convergence is bounded rather than assumed: the Davidson correction moves Te by about 240 cm-1 (2.6602 to 2.6306 at AVQZ), the AVQZ-to-AV5Z basis change moves MRCI+D by only 3.5 cm-1, and core correlation of the Si and Cl 2s2 2p6 electrons was isolated by running the ACVQZ basis with two different frozen cores. The final quoted uncertainty of +/- 538 cm-1 on Te is far larger than any of these individual increments, which is an honest reflection of the residual error rather than of basis-set convergence.
reference_short: Mok, Lee, Chau & Dyke, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2009, 5, 565
notes: Franck-Condon simulations including anharmonicity and Duschinsky rotation for the A(1A'')-X(1A') absorption and single vibronic level emission spectra of HSiCl and DSiCl, part of a continuing study of carbenes, silylenes and germylenes as reactive intermediates. The FC factors were computed on RCCSD(T) and CASSCF/MRCI potential energy functions. The work follows a closely related combined ab initio/FC study on DSiF, where good agreement was obtained for most bands but discrepancies appeared for the A(0,1,0) emission; on the basis of computed FC factors, minor revisions of previous vibrational assignments were suggested. The A(1A'') state had received less high-level attention than the X state before this work. Simulated and observed band positions are tabulated in the paper, e.g. observed 21281.64 cm-1 against 21287.0 and 21288.3 for the (0,1,0) band.
correlation_correction: MRCI with Davidson correction (MRCI+D) on the CASSCF reference, with complete-basis-set extrapolation by two independent schemes and an explicit core-correlation correction

compound_name: Menshutkin SN2 reaction NH3 + CH3Cl -> CH3NH3+ + Cl-, gas phase and aqueous solution
point_group: C3v maintained for all geometries studied
geometry_source: Two-dimensional energy surface scanned in the N-C and C-Cl distances as independent coordinates, with the N-H distance (1.002 A), C-H distance (1.062 A) and HNC angle (110.8 deg) held fixed throughout
method: CASSCF combined with the polarizable continuum model (PCM), the solvent reaction field inserted into the CASSCF Hamiltonian through a mean-field approximation; Hartree-Fock with the same PCM for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Four valence electrons in four orbitals, all of a1 type in the maintained C3v symmetry. The space is chosen so that it correctly reproduces, for the REACTANTS, a nitrogen lone pair, a diffuse orbital on nitrogen, and the C-Cl bonding and antibonding pair; and for the PRODUCTS, a chlorine lone pair, a diffuse orbital on chlorine, and the C-N bonding and antibonding pair.
active_space_protocol: The gas-phase reaction was studied FIRST for the express purpose of choosing the active space — "the reaction was considered first in the gas phase in order to make the choice of the active space for the MCSCF calculation" — with C3v symmetry restricting the active orbitals to a1 type. The identical space is then carried into the aqueous-solution calculations. Solvation uses PCM including electrostatic, repulsion and dispersion solute-solvent terms, with the reaction field entering the CASSCF Hamiltonian by a mean-field approximation. Cavity radii: H 1.0 A when bonded to nitrogen and 1.2 A when bonded to carbon, C 1.7 A, N 1.6 A, Cl 1.7 A, scaled by 1.2 for the quantum-mechanical part of the solvation free energy and used unscaled for the cavitation term (Pierotti-Claverie formula).
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet SN2 reaction converting a neutral reactant pair into an ion pair, so the wave function must describe both a covalent C-Cl bond plus nitrogen lone pair at one end and a covalent C-N bond plus chloride lone pair at the other. Gas phase at 25 C, CAS(4,4)/6-311G**: reaction energy 114.2 kcal/mol and barrier 38.6 kcal/mol, with transition-state geometry R(C-N) 1.878 A, R(C-Cl) 2.522 A and HCCl angle 83.9 deg; these compare with MP2/6-31G** values of 121.0 and 38.4, MP3 118.5 and 38.8, MP4 114.0 and 32.1, and DFT 116.5 and 32.6. Adding 13 kcal/mol to the barrier and 7.5 kcal/mol to the reaction energy converts these into gas-phase free energies. In water at 25 C, CAS(4,4)/6-311G**: reaction free energy -29.1 kcal/mol and activation free energy 20.5 kcal/mol, with transition state R(C-N) 2.167 A, R(C-Cl) 2.317 A and HCCl 90.4 deg. The experimental reaction free energy is -34 +/- 10 kcal/mol and the experimental activation free energy for the analogous NH3 + CH3I reaction is 23.5 kcal/mol.
Other: The active space is selected by a stated CHEMICAL criterion applied at both ends of the reaction coordinate rather than by size: four a1 electrons in four a1 orbitals, chosen because that space "was able to correctly reproduce, for reactants, a lone-pair and a diffuse orbital on nitrogen and a bonding and an antibonding orbital between carbon and chlorine, and, for products, a lone-pair and a diffuse orbital on chlorine and a bonding and an antibonding orbital between carbon and nitrogen". A space that described only the reactant side would fail at the product side of an SN2 reaction where the bond being broken and the bond being formed are different, so this dual criterion is the substantive constraint. C3v symmetry, maintained throughout, is what makes the restriction to a1 orbitals legitimate. geometry_source: Geometries from (U)B3LYP/6-31G(d) and from CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G(d), which are in excellent agreement for this state
method: CASSCF(8,8) single points and geometry comparison; (U)B3LYP for geometries, frequencies and thermochemistry
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF calculations; 6-31G(d) and 6-311+G(d,p) for the (U)B3LYP work
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight active orbitals: the six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair (pN), and the sigma orbital located at the divalent carbon atom C1.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF was run for an explicitly diagnostic purpose — "to check the viability of such a single-determinant approach and to describe the nature of the singlet and triplet H2NC6H4+" — after the bulk of the study had been done at B3LYP. The test is the weight of the ground-state reference determinant in the CASSCF wave function, read from the coefficient of the lowest eigenvector and from the fractional populations of the eight active orbitals. The same test had been applied to the parent phenyl cation, where the reference determinant contributes more than 90% (eigenvector coefficients 0.94 for the singlet and 0.95 for the triplet), justifying B3LYP there.
electronic_structure_description: Triplet ground state, at least 10 kcal/mol below the singlet in the gas phase by both CASSCF and B3LYP. The CASSCF wave function is dominated by a single configuration, with the leading eigenvector coefficient above 0.93 and active orbital populations close to 0, 1 and 2. Two orbitals are singly occupied: the sigma orbital at the divalent carbon C1 and one pi orbital. The sigma electron is highly localized on C1 while the pi electron is delocalized over the ring and onto the nitrogen, giving 65% diradical and 35% carbene character at C1. UB3LYP spin densities corroborate this, with nitrogen carrying the second highest spin density at 0.35. The largest positive charge sits on C4 at +0.37, so there is NO cation at C1 — which is why this state does not react with neutral sigma nucleophiles but adds readily to pi nucleophiles as an electrophilic radical. Both ring and nitrogen remain planar.
Other: The (8,8) space — six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair, and the sigma orbital on the divalent carbon — is used to answer a single question: can a single-determinant method be trusted for this ion? The answer differs by spin state, and that difference is the paper's finding. For the 3B2 triplet the CASSCF wave function is dominated by one configuration, with the leading coefficient above 0.93 and fractional populations of the eight active orbitals close to 0, 1 and 2 — so B3LYP is adequate there, and indeed the CASSCF and UB3LYP geometries and charges "are in excellent agreement only for the 3B2 state". For the 1A' singlet the wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and "cannot be properly described by a single-determinant" treatment, so the B3LYP singlet results are not reliable. This is a clean case of an active space being used to bound the validity of a cheaper method rather than to produce numbers. The orbital populations also carry chemical content that a single-determinant picture would hide: in the triplet, the sigma and one pi orbital are each singly occupied, with the sigma electron highly localized on C1 but the pi electron delocalized over the ring and onto nitrogen. Combined with UB3LYP spin densities showing nitrogen carrying the second highest spin density (0.35), this makes the triplet "65% diradical, 35% carbene character at divalent C1" — which explains why it does not react with neutral sigma nucleophiles (there is no cation at C1, the largest positive charge being +0.37 on C4) but adds readily to pi nucleophiles as an electrophilic radical. For the parent phenyl cation the same diagnostic gave >90% single-reference character for BOTH states, so amino substitution is what breaks the single-determinant description of the singlet.

The test is the weight of the ground-state reference determinant in the CASSCF wave function, read from the coefficient of the lowest eigenvector and from the fractional populations of the eight active orbitals. The same test had been applied to the parent phenyl cation, where the reference determinant contributes more than 90% (eigenvector coefficients 0.94 for the singlet and 0.95 for the triplet), justifying B3LYP there.
electronic_structure_description: Excited singlet lying at least 10 kcal/mol above the triplet in the gas phase. compound_name: Cyclopropyl radical ring-opening to allyl radical
geometry_source: CASSCF(3,3)/cc-pVTZ optimized geometries taken from earlier work
method: CAS-BCCC4 (block correlated coupled cluster at the four-block correlation level with a CASSCF reference), benchmarked against CASSCF, CASPT2 and MR-CISD
active_space_orbital_description: (3,3) throughout the reaction path. For the reactant and transition state the space contains the radical orbital plus the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the breaking C-C bond; along the path these transform into the three pi orbitals of the allyl radical product.
active_space_protocol: A single (3,3) space is carried along the whole reaction coordinate, with its orbitals changing character continuously from radical-plus-sigma/sigma* at the reactant to the allyl pi system at the product. electronic_structure_description: The simplest electrocyclic reaction of a free radical, passing through a TRIRADICAL transition state. Other: A benchmark paper whose most transferable result is a direct measurement of active-space sensitivity on the same systems with three different multireference methods. compound_name: Br(2P)...H2(1 Sigma+) van der Waals pre-reactive complex — three lowest adiabatic and diabatic potential energy surfaces
point_group: C2v for the T-shaped arrangement and C-infinity-v for the collinear one, with Cs for general geometries; described in Jacobi coordinates (R, r, theta)
geometry_source: Rigid scans over the Jacobi coordinates: R (distance from the H2 centre of mass to Br), the H2 stretching coordinate r, and the angle theta, computed for several values of r over a wide range of R and theta
method: State-averaged CASSCF for the nonadiabatic coupling and the off-diagonal (fourth) diabatic surface; R-UCCSD(T) on ROHF orbitals for the diagonal diabatic interaction energies
basis_set: Bare aug-cc-pVQZ (without bond functions) for the CASSCF calculations; a large basis with bond functions and counterpoise correction for the benchmark CCSD(T) interaction energies
relativistic_treatment: Spin-orbit coupling included afterwards through the Alexander-Manolopoulos-Werner formalism using empirical splitting parameters
active_space_orbital_description: Default space: the Br 1s orbital frozen; the 2s, 2p, 3s and 3p orbitals doubly occupied; the 4s and 4p orbitals active; plus the sigma-g and sigma-u* molecular orbitals of hydrogen also in the active space. A larger test space was also run with 1s, 2s and 2p frozen, 3s, 3p, 3d, 4s, 4p(x) and 4p(y) doubly occupied and 4p(z) active. The CASSCF calculations "require neither the self-consistency corrections nor the counterpoise correction", unlike the supermolecular CCSD(T) interaction energies. electronic_structure_description: Open-shell doublet van der Waals complex of Br(2P) with H2, in the entry channel of the Br + H2 reaction. Three low-lying electronic states (1A', 2A' and 1A'') arise from the three orientations of the bromine 2P hole relative to H2, and their coupling produces a Sigma-Pi conical intersection at theta = 0 degrees. The approach exploits the oblate shape of H2, which makes the interaction anisotropy relatively simple, and follows earlier treatments of F + H2 and Cl + H2. Spin-orbit coupling cannot be neglected near the van der Waals minimum and significantly alters both the depth and position of the well. A test of inner-shell correlation on the A1-state global-minimum interaction energy gives 167.7 cm-1 with the extended space against a default-space value differing by 2.7 cm-1, less than 2%.

notes: Constructs three-dimensional adiabatic and diabatic potential energy surfaces for the Br(2P) + H2 pre-reactive van der Waals complex. notes: Study of the radiationless decay mechanisms of cyclic alkenes CnH2n-2 (n = 4, 5, 6), norbornene and their phenyl-substituted derivatives, aiming to explain the correlation between triplet lifetime and ring strain and the anomalously short triplet lifetime of norbornene (250 ns). Two decay pathways are considered: a twist coordinate with local C2 symmetry (theta2 = theta3) and an anti-pyramidalization coordinate (theta2 != theta3). Phenyl substitution of vinylic hydrogen lengthens the T1 lifetime substantially, paralleling the acyclic series (stilbene 50 ns, triphenylethylene 100 ns, tetraphenylethylene 175 ns). Rates are computed as products of Franck-Condon factors and squared spin-orbit matrix elements; test calculations with different reduced moments give lifetimes within 20%. Excitation energies and dihedral angles are in Table 1 and the Franck-Condon analysis in Tables 2 and 3.

The count is inherited from the requirement at the CH2 + SO dissociation limit.
active_space_protocol: The eight-electron six-orbital count is set by the CH2 + SO fragments and then applied uniformly to every species in the thermochemical cycle so that errors cancel in the energy differences. Geometries and vibrational frequencies come from RHF/DZP; the correlated energies use the DZ(2df,2d,p) basis. The CAS-CI expansion has 48 reference configurations (57 configuration functions) and a total dimension of 9 867 864 for the Cs systems, with the Pople size-extensivity correction applied.

electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet with a cumulated C=S=O framework. The CAS-CI heat of formation is Delta-Hf = -3 +/- 14 kJ/mol at 0 K, with a recommended 298 K value of -9 kJ/mol — a significant upward revision from an earlier estimate of -51 +/- 22 kJ/mol and from other ab initio values of -18 and -30 kJ/mol. Derived properties: proton affinity 787 kJ/mol at 298 K; C-S bond strength 405 kJ/mol and S-O bond strength 364 kJ/mol. Both bonds are much weaker than in the isolated subsystems CH2=S (562 kJ/mol) and S=O (521 kJ/mol) despite having almost the same bond lengths, and the sulfine S-O bond is comparable in strength to that in dimethyl sulfoxide (394 kJ/mol).
Other: The active space is fixed by the DISSOCIATION LIMIT and then held constant for everything else, which is the design decision that makes the thermochemistry work. The requirement comes from the CH2 + SO fragments, where near-degeneracy (pi -> pi* excitation in the linear molecules) forces a multiconfigurational treatment: the active orbitals must include the 2pi and 3pi shells of SO (four MOs) plus the singly occupied 3a1 and the 1b2 lone pair of CH2, giving eight electrons in six MOs — "which should then also be taken for all other systems". For the Cs-symmetry species CH2SO, CH2SOH+ and HC(=O)SH the same eight-electron six-orbital count is realized as three sigma and three pi MOs, of which two sigma and two pi are occupied in the Hartree-Fock determinant. Because near-degeneracy is expected to be severe only in the linear fragments, all active MOs were deliberately placed on those and on CH2, while H2O, H2S and H2 are noted as well described by plain HF-SDCI and need no such treatment. This is an unusually explicit statement that the space is sized by the hardest species in the thermochemical cycle rather than by the molecule of interest — necessary because a heat of formation is a difference across species, and an inconsistent space would not cancel. The resulting CAS-CI has 48 reference configurations (57 configuration functions) and a total dimension of 9 867 864 for the Cs systems. Accuracy is bounded empirically rather than asserted: across the anchor set the mean deviation is 18 kJ/mol and the root-mean-square deviation 14 kJ/mol, which is where the quoted +/- 14 kJ/mol uncertainty comes from. A separate warning concerns geometry rather than the space: the G2 procedure's MP2(FULL)/6-31G* optimization does not reproduce the experimental structure of sulfine, and only a larger MP2/6-311+G(2df,2p) basis gives the correct structure.

The CAS-CI result is -3 +/- 14 kJ/mol at 0 K, and the recommended 298 K value of -9 kJ/mol represents a significant upward revision. G2 gives a somewhat lower heat of formation but falls just within the stated theoretical error; with a larger basis for the geometry optimization G2 gives -2 kJ/mol. Combining the computed neutral heat of formation with the measured Delta-Hf of CH2SOH+ gives a 298 K proton affinity of 787 kJ/mol. On protonation the S-O bond lengthens by 0.157 A while the C-S bond is unchanged.

compound_name: Singlet phenylnitrene (parent) — cyclization to bicyclic azirine

method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries

active_space_protocol: An eight-electron, eight-orbital space is used for all species so the substituted derivatives can be compared with the parent, with the orbital composition switching between the reactant form and the transition-state/product form as the azirine C-N bond forms.
electronic_structure_description: Open-shell singlet nitrene, the reference compound for the series. Cyclization energies relative to the reactant, in kcal/mol including ZPE: CASSCF transition structure 8.9 and product 4.7; CASPT2 transition structure 8.6 and product 1.6. The two ortho carbons are equivalent so there is only one cyclization mode.

This is the same construction the group used for parent phenylnitrene, which is what allows the substituted barriers to be placed on that earlier scale. point_group: D2h at the S0 minimum; C2h at the globally stable trans-bent S1 geometry; lower symmetry at the conical intersection
geometry_source: State-specific (10,10)CASSCF optimization of the S0 minimum, then optimization of the Franck-Condon-region excited-state minima, the conical intersection and the globally stable S1 and T1 geometries; vibrational analyses at several important conformations for direct comparison with experiment; the reaction path from the FC region to the globally stable S1 structure was followed explicitly
method: CASSCF for geometries and surface scanning, with MRMP2 (second-order multireference Moller-Plesset) energy corrections
software: GAMESS, except the conical intersection location which used Gaussian 03
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta augmented with polarization functions
active_space_orbital_description: (10,10): the highest five occupied pi orbitals and the lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals. The full pi space would be (16,16) — all excitations from the eight pi-type occupied orbitals into the lowest eight unoccupied ones.
active_space_protocol: The space was chosen by an explicit two-stage screening rather than by cost alone. The desirable space is stated to be (16,16), but that is "practically prohibited even on a high-performance computer, especially in the case of a global search of potential energy surfaces, geometry optimizations, and vibrational analyses". So preliminary CI calculations were run at a range of geometries covering the conformations relevant to the photochemistry, establishing two things: (i) the low-lying excited states at every sampled conformation are well described by configuration state functions built from excitations among the highest five occupied pi and lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals, and (ii) the character of those ten pi-type orbitals is INVARIANT with conformation. Only then was (10,10) adopted for the global surface scan. The same strategy had been used by the authors for polyenes and polyynes. Geometry optimization of S0 used a STATE-SPECIFIC (10,10)CASSCF.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell S0(Ag) ground state of D2h symmetry, with the leading closed-shell configuration carrying weight 0.923. Vertical excitation energies at the S0 geometry, CASSCF with MRMP2-corrected values in parentheses, and oscillator strengths in velocity form: S1(B2u) 6.056 (4.054) eV, f = 1e-6, a strongly mixed state with leading CSF coefficients 0.520 and -0.508; S2(B3g) 6.061 (4.052) eV, f = 0.0, similarly two-configurational; S3(B1u) 6.407 (4.507) eV, f = 0.873, dominated by the single HOMO-LUMO excitation with coefficient 0.925; S4(Au) 6.688 (4.847) eV, f = 0.0, coefficient 0.940. The main transition is therefore to S3(B1u), the only state with significant oscillator strength. The globally stable S1 structure is a TRANS-BENT form of Au symmetry under C2h, with the C1-Ca-Ca' angle bent to 127.9 degrees from 180.0 in S0 and the Ca-Ca' bond elongated from 1.204 to 1.357 A; the S1 state there is well described by a HOMO-to-LUMO excitation and has diradical character. The S2/S1 conical intersection is intermediate, with an angle of 157.5 degrees and a 1.298 A triple-bond distance. The T1 geometry remains linear with a 1.251 A Ca-Ca' bond.
Other: An unusually well-documented reduction of an unaffordable space, with the screening criterion stated and checked at multiple geometries. Rather than simply truncating, the authors ran preliminary CI at a spread of geometries covering the relevant conformations and established two conditions before committing: that the low-lying states are well described within the highest five occupied pi and lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals, and — critically for a surface scan — that "the nature of a set of these 10 pi-type orbitals is invariant irrespective of the conformations". The second condition is what licenses using one fixed space across geometries as different as linear D2h and trans-bent C2h. reference_short: Amatatsu & Hosokawa, J. Phys. Chem. A 2004, 108, 10238
notes: Examines the photochemical behaviour of diphenylacetylene in its low-lying excited states, comparing with phenylacetylene and with other pi-conjugated systems studied by the same group. Characteristic optimized geometrical parameters for all eight structures (S0, the four FC-region excited states, the trans-bent S1, the S2/S1 conical intersection and T1) are collected in Table 2, with rotational constants in Table 3 and atom numbering in Figure 2. The dynamical picture is that DPA excited into S3(B1u) relaxes toward the trans-bent S1 geometry.
correlation_correction: MRMP2 (second-order multireference Moller-Plesset) energy corrections on the CASSCF reference

compound_name: NH + NO potential energy surface — HNNO complex, N2 + OH and H + N2O channels
point_group: Cs (states classified as 2A' and 2A'' with respect to the molecular plane); planar transition state for N2 + OH production
geometry_source: CASSCF gradient optimizations of stationary point geometries and frequencies, followed by CCI single points at those geometries
method: CASSCF gradient calculations for geometries and frequencies, with contracted CI (CCI) energies on a selected reference list
basis_set: For the CASSCF gradients, the Dunning-Hay polarized double zeta set: (9s5p)/[3s2p] on N and O augmented with a single 3d function (exponents 0.80 for N, 0.85 for O), and (4s)/[2s] on H augmented with a single 2p function (exponent 1.00). For the CI calculations, the Dunning correlation-consistent triple zeta double polarization basis, [4s3p2d1f] on N and O and [3s2p1d] on H.
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen electrons distributed among 8 a' and 3 a'' orbitals. The active electrons are those of the bonding configurations plus the 2s electron pair on the CENTRAL nitrogen. The ten inactive electrons are the two N 1s pairs, the O 1s and 2s pairs, and the N 2s pair on the terminal nitrogen.
active_space_protocol: The inclusion of one N 2s pair is a deliberate choice driven by a specific region of the surface: "one N 2s pair has to be active to describe certain regions of the surface (e.g. H + N2O) where the N 2s electrons on the central N are used in bonding". In the subsequent CCI calculations all electrons except the N 1s and O 1s are correlated, and a SELECTED reference list is used with a configuration coefficient cutoff of 0.04. Two different basis sets are used by design — a smaller polarized double zeta for the gradient work and a correlation-consistent triple zeta double polarization set for the CI energies.
multiplicities_studied: doublet (2A' and 2A'' surfaces); the NH reactant is a triplet X(3 Sigma-) and NH(1 Delta) is also discussed
electronic_structure_description: Two doublet surfaces arise from NH + NO and behave completely differently. The 2A' surface correlates with N2 + OH or H + N2O products but has barriers to addition of 3.2 kcal/mol for the trans approach and 6.3 kcal/mol for the cis, with experimental support for these barriers. The 2A'' surface has NO barrier to addition but does NOT correlate with products, so surface crossings between the barrierless 2A'' and the reactive 2A' surface may control the kinetics. Mechanistically, NH + NO forms an HNNO complex in cis or trans orientation, which undergoes a 1,3-hydrogen shift over a barrier to give an NNOH species that is unstable and dissociates to N2 + OH; HNNO can alternatively dissociate over a barrier to H + N2O. Production of N2 + OH is predicted to occur through a planar transition state. The ground X(3 Sigma-) state of NH leads to N2 + OH, while an excited surface — involving a doubly occupied N 2p orbital perpendicular to the plane, analogous to the configuration for O(1D) insertion into H2 — correlates with H + N2O and probably accounts for the N2O observed by Yamasaki et al. in the NH(1 Delta) + NO reaction. Results differ from the earlier work of Melius and Binkley by as much as 8 kcal/mol in the detailed energetics.
Other: The active space is enlarged for one specific reason, stated plainly: "one N 2s pair has to be active to describe certain regions of the surface (e.g. H + N2O) where the N 2s electrons on the central N are used in bonding". Without it the space would fail in a region the study exists to characterize, so the 2s pair on the central nitrogen is promoted while the terminal-nitrogen 2s pair, the O 1s and 2s pairs and both N 1s pairs stay inactive — an asymmetric treatment of two chemically similar orbitals, justified by which one participates in bonding along the reaction path. Getting both surfaces on the same footing is what makes the proposed 2A''-to-2A' surface crossing mechanism arguable at all. Two further protocol points bear on reuse: the correlated step uses a SELECTED reference list with a coefficient cutoff of 0.04 rather than the full CASSCF reference, and geometries come from a smaller polarized double zeta basis than the triple zeta double polarization basis used for the energies. The scale of the residual uncertainty is indicated by comparison with earlier work — differences as large as 8 kcal/mol against Melius and Binkley.
reference_short: Walch, J. Chem. Phys. 1993, 98, 1170
notes: Characterizes the potential energy surface for NH + NO, a reaction of combustion interest with two exothermic product channels, N2 + OH and H + N2O. The reverse process H + N2O -> N2 + OH is also relevant. Experimental context includes work suggesting the HNNO complex may not be fully equilibrated, since observed OH excitation is lower than a statistical model predicts, and the observation of N2O production by Yamasaki et al. in the NH(1 Delta) + NO reaction. Most calculations were run on the NASA Ames Cray Y-MP.
correlation_correction: Contracted CI (CCI) correlating all electrons except N 1s and O 1s, using a selected reference list with a 0.04 coefficient cutoff

compound_name: syn-ClC(O)SCl — ground and low-lying excited states
geometry_source: CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ optimized, with MP2/cc-pVDZ and B3LYP/cc-pVDZ structures for comparison and frequency analyses confirming minima
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with MR-CI single points; MP2 and B3LYP for ground-state structures
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,8): ten electrons in eight orbitals. The active ORBITALS are varied with the stationary structure rather than held fixed. The frontier orbitals involved are the HOMO and HOMO-1, nonbonding orbitals localized mainly on sulfur and oxygen respectively, and the LUMO and LUMO+1, which are sigma*(S-Cl) and pi*(C=O) in nature.
active_space_protocol: The paper states the ideal and why it was not met: "in principle, all valence electrons and orbitals of a system should be included in the active space for the CASSCF calculations. However, it is impossible for ClC(O)SCl due to the limited computational capability." The compromise is a fixed COUNT of ten electrons in eight orbitals with the orbital composition varied per stationary structure, so that whichever bonds are breaking or which excitation is relevant at a given geometry is represented. Relative energies are then refined by MR-CI single points on the CAS(10,8) wave functions. Ground-state structures were also optimized at MP2 and B3LYP for comparison, with frequency analyses confirming minima.
electronic_structure_description: The predominant gas-phase rotamer, planar in the ground state. Its CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ C-S bond length is 1.781 A against an experimental 1.791 A from electron diffraction, shorter than a normal C-S single bond (1.82 A) and so showing partial double-bond character. The frontier orbitals are the HOMO and HOMO-1 (nonbonding, localized on S and O respectively) and the LUMO and LUMO+1 (sigma*(S-Cl) and pi*(C=O)). From the MR-CI configuration coefficients, S1 arises mainly from a HOMO-to-LUMO one-electron transition and is n(S) -> sigma*(S-Cl) in character, while S2 is a HOMO-1 to LUMO+1 promotion and is 1n(O)pi*(C=O). MR-CI vertical excitation energies at the CAS(10,8)-optimized syn geometry are 98.7 kcal/mol to S1 and 134.7 kcal/mol to S2, comparable to observed absorption peaks at 300 nm (95.3 kcal/mol) and 220 nm (130.0 kcal/mol); the resulting band assignment differs from that of a previous study. On the S2 surface a rotational isomerization barrier of 7.7 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) rises to 10.2 kcal/mol at MR-CI, and on T2 the corresponding barrier is 9.3 rising to 10.0 kcal/mol.
Other: An explicitly acknowledged compromise, with the ideal stated first: "in principle, all valence electrons and orbitals of a system should be included in the active space for the CASSCF calculations. However, it is impossible for ClC(O)SCl due to the limited computational capability." The chosen CAS(10,8) keeps the electron and orbital COUNT fixed while letting the orbital composition vary with the stationary structure — so a single label covers several different eight-orbital selections across the surface, and relative energies drawn from different regions inherit that. This is the same trade-off as a constant-size space with per-structure composition, but here it is applied across excited-state minima, transition states and dissociation channels rather than along a single reaction coordinate. The MR-CI correction on top is substantial and not uniform: the S2 rotational isomerization barrier moves from 7.7 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) to 10.2 at MR-CI, the T2 barrier from 9.3 to 10.0, and a pair of excited-state structures from 106.3 and a companion value down to 93.5 and 97.3 kcal/mol — shifts of up to about 13 kcal/mol, so the CASSCF energies alone would not support the mechanistic conclusions. Where the space can be checked against experiment it performs well: the CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ C-S bond length of 1.781 A matches the electron-diffraction value of 1.791 A, and the MR-CI vertical excitation energies of 98.7 and 134.7 kcal/mol to S1 and S2 are comparable to the observed absorption peaks at 300 nm (95.3 kcal/mol) and 220 nm (130.0 kcal/mol). Notably the resulting band assignment differs from that in a previous study, so the multireference treatment changes the interpretation of the spectrum rather than merely refining it.
reference_short: Lin, Ding, Fang & Liu, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 8744
notes: Characterizes all possible unimolecular photolysis processes of ClC(O)SCl in the UV-visible region through optimized stationary structures and potential energy profiles. Six channels are considered: syn-to-anti isomerization, CO + SCl2, SCO + Cl2, ClC(O)S + Cl, C(O)SCl + Cl, and ClCO + SCl. Experimentally the molecule exists in the gas phase as a mixture of syn and anti isomers with the syn form predominant; both are planar minima and their computed structures agree well with electron diffraction. The C-S bond is shorter than a normal C-S single bond (1.82 A), showing partial double-bond character attributed to donation from the low-electronegativity sulfur lone pairs. The ground-state rotational isomerization barrier is 12.3 kcal/mol at MP2/cc-pVDZ and 12.7 at B3LYP/cc-pVDZ, with the syn-anti energy difference 3.2 and 3.6 kcal/mol at the two levels; a barrier above 5.0 kcal/mol is sufficient to suppress interconversion.

geometry_source: (8,8)CASSCF/6-31G* optimized stationary points with numerical frequency calculations to classify each as a minimum or transition state and to give zero-point energy differences; transition structures confirmed by their transition vectors and by intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations
method: (8,8)CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with (8,8)CASPT2 single points
basis_set: 6-31G* for both the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: (8,8): the four sigma and pi bonding orbitals involved in the rearrangement together with their four antibonding counterparts.
active_space_protocol: A single (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals is used for every stationary point on the surface, so reactant, both transition structures, the diradical intermediate and the product are directly comparable. The paper notes explicitly that structures 10, 11 and the diradical intermediate 12 were optimized "with the correct active space orbitals in each case", i.e. orbital identity was verified rather than assumed at each optimization. Dynamic correlation enters as (8,8)CASPT2 single points at all stationary points, and reported enthalpy differences are zero-point corrected using the CASSCF numerical frequencies.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet reactant of the conformationally restricted allenyl Cope rearrangement, optimized as an energy minimum at (8,8)CASSCF/6-31G* with the correct active space orbitals. It rearranges to triene 11 through either of two transition structures — 13 and 15 — which differ by 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy and both lead to the common diradical intermediate 12. Passing through the lower-energy structure 13, the terminal methylene group rotates in only one direction, whereas through 15 it appears free to rotate either way; this asymmetry is consistent with the 90% stereoselectivity observed in the thermal rearrangements of the dimethyl derivatives. A separate structure lies 32.7 kcal/mol above 10 with a large associated H term.
Other: A uniform (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals across every stationary point, which is what allows a two-transition-state mechanism to be established at all — the two structures 13 and 15 differ by only 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy, a margin that would be meaningless if the two had been computed in differently composed spaces. The paper also records that the reactant, product and diradical intermediate were optimized "with the correct active space orbitals in each case", i.e. orbital identity was checked at each optimization rather than assumed to persist — the failure mode being that an (8,8) optimization can converge onto a different set of eight orbitals at a distant geometry and silently break the comparison. The mechanistic conclusion depends on dynamic correlation being added on top: an earlier study at CASSCF level alone gave a different picture for the parent system, and it was "the inclusion of dynamic electron correlation at the (8,8)CASPT2/6-31G* level" that located allylic-stabilized structures and changed the pathway. The result here — two separate transition structures both leading to a common diradical intermediate — differs substantially from the parent 1,2,6-heptatriene rearrangement, which has a single transition structure that either proceeds to the diradical or bypasses it entirely. That contrast between a conformationally restricted system and its flexible parent, computed with the same space and the same correction, is the paper's central point.
reference_short: Duncan, Wulf et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1999, 121, 12029
notes: Computational study of the conformationally restricted allenyl Cope rearrangement of syn-7-allenylnorbornene (10) to triene 11, undertaken to explain stereoselectivity observed experimentally in the thermal Cope rearrangements of dimethyl allenylnorbornene derivatives. The rearrangement involves TWO separate transition structures, 13 and 15, differing by 2.1 kcal/mol in enthalpy, both leading to a common diradical intermediate 12 — substantially different from the parent 1,2,6-heptatriene to 3-methylene-1,5-hexadiene rearrangement, which proceeds through a single transition structure that either forms the diradical or bypasses it. The terminal methylene group rotates in only one direction through the lower-energy transition structure 13 but appears to rotate freely in either direction through 15, a finding described as remarkably consistent with the 90% stereoselectivity observed experimentally. Direct participation of the terminal allenyl pi bond is also addressed. Carbon-carbon bond lengths for all stationary points are in Table 1 and the zero-point-corrected reaction coordinate diagram in Figure 3.

Other: A uniform (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals across every stationary point, which is what allows a two-transition-state mechanism to be established at all — the two structures 13 and 15 differ by only 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy, a margin that would be meaningless if the two had been computed in differently composed spaces. The mechanistic conclusion depends on dynamic correlation being added on top: an earlier study at CASSCF level alone gave a different picture for the parent system, and it was "the inclusion of dynamic electron correlation at the (8,8)CASPT2/6-31G* level" that located allylic-stabilized structures and changed the pathway. That contrast between a conformationally restricted system and its flexible parent, computed with the same space and the same correction, is the paper's central point.
reference_short: Duncan, Wulf et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1999, 121, 12029
notes: Computational study of the conformationally restricted allenyl Cope rearrangement of syn-7-allenylnorbornene (10) to triene 11, undertaken to explain stereoselectivity observed experimentally in the thermal Cope rearrangements of dimethyl allenylnorbornene derivatives. Direct participation of the terminal allenyl pi bond is also addressed. compound_name: Thiophene (C4H4S) — ultrafast S1 deactivation by trajectory surface hopping
point_group: C2v at the S0 minimum; the S1(1pi-pi*) minimum is NONPLANAR; the CI(1pi-pi*/1pi-sigma*) conical intersection has Cs symmetry
geometry_source: CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* optimized minima and conical intersections; B3LYP geometries used for the DFT/MRCI comparison. Molecular dynamics trajectories propagated on CASSCF(8,7)/cc-pVDZ energies, gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with multistate multireference CASPT2 (MS-MR-CASPT2) single points; ab initio trajectory surface-hopping dynamics; DFT/MRCI for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(8,7): three occupied pi orbitals and two unoccupied pi* orbitals, plus the bonding and antibonding sigma and sigma* orbitals of one C-S bond. Equivalently, two pairs of pi electrons plus the sulfur lone pair (n orbital), with the C-S sigma/sigma* pair added.
active_space_protocol: The paper states the selection criterion explicitly — "selection of the active space in the CASSCF calculations is crucial" — and then gives two separate requirements. First, two pairs of pi electrons and the sulfur lone pair must be present to describe thiophene's low-lying electronic states at all. Second, one C-S sigma/sigma* pair must be added "since the C-S bond is broken in the decay process", i.e. the space is extended specifically to cover the ring-opening coordinate the dynamics traverses. State averaging uses EQUAL weights over the two states involved. The dynamics run to a maximum of 200 fs per trajectory with a 0.5 fs integration step; trajectories that hop to S0 and remain there for more than 5 fs are terminated, and some stop early because of convergence problems.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (state-averaged with equal weights)
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell S0 ground state. The S1 state is 1(pi-pi*) in the Franck-Condon region, and its minimum MIN(S1(1pi-pi*)) is nonplanar. Because it originates from a pi -> pi* transition, the ring bonds lengthen relative to MIN(S0); notably the S1-C5 bond is 0.043 A longer than the S1-C2 bond, and the sigma* orbital makes a small contribution, so the structure already tends toward MIN(S1(1pi-sigma*)) where the S-C bond is broken. The S0 -> S1 vertical transition energy is 5.74 eV at MS-MR-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ against an experimental 5.3-5.4 eV; DFT/MRCI on the B3LYP structure gives 5.4 eV, in excellent agreement with experiment. Near the Franck-Condon region there is an important CI(1pi-pi*/1pi-sigma*) conical intersection of Cs symmetry, predicted to lie 0.02 eV above the S1 minimum, which plays a key role in the S1(1pi-pi*) to S0 internal conversion. Trajectory kinetic-energy analysis gives around 1.0 eV per vibrational mode, with maxima of 1.8-2.4 eV and minima of 0.2-0.4 eV depending on the mode initially excited.
Other: The active space is sized by the reaction coordinate rather than by the spectroscopy alone, and the paper separates the two requirements. Describing thiophene's low-lying states needs only the pi manifold plus the sulfur lone pair; the C-S sigma/sigma* pair is added on top "since the C-S bond is broken in the decay process", so the (8,7) space is built to remain valid along a ring-opening coordinate that a purely pi space would not span. The consequence is visible in the results — the S1(1pi-pi*) minimum already shows a small sigma* contribution and an asymmetric pair of S-C bonds differing by 0.043 A, tending toward the 1(pi-sigma*) ring-opened structure, which a pi-only space could not have revealed. The paper is equally explicit about what this space costs and why it was accepted anyway: "the CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* calculation overestimates the excitation energy due to the limited inclusion of the electronic correlation effect" — 5.74 eV at MS-MR-CASPT2 and higher still at bare CASSCF, against 5.3-5.4 eV experimental and 5.4 eV from DFT/MRCI — but "the state-averaged CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* method can provide a balanced description on topological structures of S0 and S1 potential energy surfaces". That is the operative justification for using it for dynamics: topology, not energetics. The alternatives are ruled out on opposite grounds — TDDFT "usually fails at predicting intersections correctly", while multireference methods such as MS-MR-CASPT2 "remain unaffordable for ab initio nonadiabatic dynamics simulations" — so CASSCF occupies the only tractable middle ground, with its known energy error accepted as the price.

notes: Ab initio trajectory surface-hopping study of the ultrafast deactivation of thiophene, a five-membered sulfur heterocycle. Dynamics were run on CASSCF(8,7)/cc-pVDZ surfaces for up to 200 fs per trajectory with a 0.5 fs step, terminating trajectories that reach S0 and remain there beyond 5 fs since only the ultrafast internal conversion is of interest. Trajectories were initiated with excitation in individual vibrational modes (VIB3, VIB6, VIB7, VIB8, VIB16, VIB17), giving mode-resolved kinetic energies around 1.0 eV each: 0.846 eV with VIB3, 0.887 with VIB6, 0.902 with VIB7, 0.942 with VIB8, 0.992 with VIB16 and 1.078 with VIB17. The active-space molecular orbitals are depicted in Figure 2 and the conical intersection structure in Figure 3.
correlation_correction: MS-MR-CASPT2 (multistate multireference CASPT2) single points, used where needed; DFT/MRCI as an independent check on the vertical excitation energy

compound_name: Acetone — photodissociation, intersystem crossing and nonadiabatic pathways to S0
point_group: C1 for most structures, with converged higher symmetries noted per structure in the paper
geometry_source: Minima, transition states and minimum-energy seam-of-crossing (MSX) structures optimized directly at the (8e,7o)-CASPT2/6-31+G* level, using CASPT2 energies and gradient vectors from MOLPRO 2006 fed to an external optimizer in the GRRM program; MSX structures optimized by combining gradient projection with rational function optimization. Some paths were followed at the (8e,7o)-CASSCF/6-31+G* level with MOLPRO 2008.
method: CASPT2 geometry optimization — multistate CASPT2 for the singlet states and single-state CASPT2 for the triplet — with an IPEA-type shift; CASSCF for comparison and for path following
software: MOLPRO 2006 and MOLPRO 2008 (CASPT2 and CASSCF energies and gradients); GRRM (external optimizer)
basis_set: 6-31+G* for the CASPT2 optimizations; 6-31G* for some CASSCF comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: (8e,7o). The stated minimum requirement is (4e,3o) — the pi, n and pi* orbitals — which "is necessary to describe the n -> pi* transition". Two sigma and two sigma* orbitals are then added "to represent CC bond breaking and proton transfer", giving eight electrons in seven orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is built in two stages with each stage justified by what it must describe: the (4e,3o) pi/n/pi* core for the n -> pi* excitation itself, extended by two sigma and two sigma* orbitals for the C-C bond breaking and proton transfer that occur along the dissociation pathways. Multistate CASPT2 is applied to the singlet states and single-state CASPT2 to the triplet. A shift parameter of 0.3 was applied in the CASPT2 calculations to avoid the intruder state problem. Critically, the geometries themselves are optimized AT the CASPT2 level rather than at CASSCF and corrected afterwards.
nroots_per_mult: multistate CASPT2 for the singlets; single-state for the triplet
electronic_structure_description: S0 ground state with S1 reached by n -> pi* photoexcitation; T1 accessible by intersystem crossing. The total energy at S0-MIN1 is -192.526348 hartree, the reference for all relative energies. After n -> pi* excitation the system oscillates around the bottom of S1-MIN1. At the earlier (8e,7o)-CASSCF/6-31G* level an S1/T1 minimum-energy seam-of-crossing structure was known to lie very close in geometry to S1-MIN1 and slightly below T1-TS1, and intersystem crossing through it was believed dominant when the excitation energy is insufficient to reach S1-TS1. At the CASPT2 level that picture collapses: optimization starting from the CASSCF MSX structure converges instead to S1/T1-MSX1 with the C-O bond lengthened from 1.586 to 1.794 A and a considerable increase in energy, so no crossing exists in the low-energy region of the S1-MIN1 basin. The authors instead propose that the S1 -> T1 transition occurs by trickling down from S1 to T1 while the molecule remains in the S1 state, which accounts for the experimentally slow intersystem crossing. Optimization from the reported high-energy CASSCF S0/S1-MSX5 with a very long C-O bond likewise converged to a different structure, S0/S1-MSX2, at the CASPT2 level.
Other: The decisive methodological choice is optimizing the crossing GEOMETRIES at CASPT2 rather than locating them at CASSCF and correcting the energies afterwards — and the two levels give qualitatively different answers, which is the paper's central result. Starting from the previously reported (8e,7o)-CASSCF S1/T1 MSX structure, CASPT2 optimization does not merely shift it: it converges to a different structure, S1/T1-MSX1, with the C-O bond elongated from 1.586 to 1.794 A and a considerable rise in energy. The same happens for the S0/S1 crossing, where the reported CASSCF structure converges to S0/S1-MSX2 at CASPT2 level. The consequence is mechanistic, not numerical: at CASSCF the S1/T1 crossing sits close to the S1 minimum and below T1-TS1, making intersystem crossing through it the presumed dominant channel at low excitation energy, whereas at CASPT2 "no crossing exists in the low energy region of basin of S1-MIN1" and a different mechanism — trickling down from S1 to T1 — has to be invoked to explain the observed slow intersystem crossing. Structures the paper marks as newly located, or as very different from CASSCF, are flagged with asterisks in its Figure 1. The active space itself is layered by function: (4e,3o) of pi, n and pi* is stated as the minimum needed for the n -> pi* transition, with two sigma and two sigma* orbitals added specifically for C-C bond breaking and proton transfer. reference_short: Maeda, Ohno & Morokuma, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2010, 1, 1841
notes: Reports new potential energy profiles for the S0, S1 and T1 states of acetone, addressing why intersystem crossing is experimentally slow and exploring nonadiabatic routes back to the ground state. Dissociation is understood to proceed on the T1 surface at low excitation energies, with the relevant stationary structures previously characterized. Optimized MIN, TS and MSX structures are collected in Figure 1 with C-C and C-O bond lengths and rearranging bonds marked; Cartesian coordinates are in the Supporting Information. Comparison is drawn with earlier extensive studies of formaldehyde.
correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2 for the singlets and single-state CASPT2 for the triplet, with a 0.3 shift parameter against intruder states; energies AND gradients computed at this level so geometries are CASPT2-optimized

compound_name: Ethylene + ethylene — model system for [2+2] cyclobutane thymine dimer (T<>T) formation
point_group: D2 (all calculations performed in D2 symmetry)
geometry_source: State-averaged RIGID scan over two coordinates: the C5-C6-C6-C5 dihedral angle (eta) and the ethylene-ethylene separation distance (d). No geometry optimization; bond lengths within each ethylene are held fixed.
method: State-averaged CASSCF
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(4,12): four electrons in twelve orbitals, chosen in accord with the CASSCF(2,6) ethylene MONOMER space of Ben-Nun et al. — i.e. the monomer space doubled for the dimer. It includes some of the low-lying 3s and 3p carbon RYDBERG orbitals as well as the necessary pi* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The dimer space is constructed by doubling an established monomer space rather than being selected afresh, so the two-ethylene results connect to the known CASSCF(2,6) description of isolated ethylene. Rydberg 3s and 3p carbon orbitals are deliberately included alongside the valence pi* orbitals. Fifteen states were monitored in a state-averaged rigid scan over the dihedral angle and separation distance, and all calculations were run in D2 symmetry.
nroots_per_mult: 15 states monitored in the state average
electronic_structure_description: Model for the [2+2] photocycloaddition forming the cyclobutane thymine dimer. At infinite separation there are four degenerate (pi) states. As the ethylenes approach, one state falls steeply with decreasing separation d and eventually becomes the ground state at 2.0 A, producing a conical intersection between these states. The crossing distance depends weakly on the dihedral angle, ranging from 2.2 A at small dihedral angles to 2.0 A at large ones. The doubly excited (pi*)2 state is implicated in the mechanism: an eventual transition to it leads toward product. The surface shows little dependence on dihedral angle over a wide range, though there is a gradient toward zero dihedral angle at short separation. The paper notes that the mechanism's dependence on the dihedral angle eta had never previously been discussed, earlier work by Bernardi and others having considered only the separation coordinate, and that previous studies chose to limit the dihedral angle.
Other: The active space is inherited by construction rather than chosen: CASSCF(4,12) for the ethylene dimer is the CASSCF(2,6) monomer space of Ben-Nun et al. doubled, which is what makes the dimer surface comparable to the established isolated-ethylene description. Its notable feature is the deliberate inclusion of low-lying 3s and 3p carbon RYDBERG orbitals alongside the valence pi* orbitals — a twelve-orbital space for only four electrons, so most of it is virtual and exists to let the excited states be described correctly rather than to correlate electrons. That matters because the mechanism turns on a doubly excited (pi*)2 state and on state crossings among fifteen monitored roots; a compact valence-only space would not support either. The calculation is a RIGID two-dimensional scan in D2 symmetry, with only the intermolecular separation and the inter-ethylene dihedral varied, so the surface is a slice rather than a relaxed path — the paper is explicit that in reality photoexcitation occurs at geometries away from this slice, and that if the internal bond distances were allowed to change the picture would differ. Its own contribution is to add the dihedral coordinate that previous work had fixed or limited: the conical intersection distance moves only from 2.2 to 2.0 A across the full dihedral range, so the crossing is robust to that coordinate even though the reaction efficiency in DNA is conformationally controlled.
reference_short: McCullagh, Hariharan, Lewis, Markovitsi, Douki & Schatz, J. Phys. Chem. B 2010, 114, 5215
notes: A molecular dynamics study of conformational control of thymine-thymine dimerization in DNA conjugates, reporting quantum yields for [2+2] and 6-4 photodimerization of TT steps. The bulk of the work uses the CHARMM27 force field in NAMD; the CASSCF calculations on the ethylene + ethylene model system serve to characterize the electronic surface underlying the [2+2] cyclobutane dimer formation. The reaction coordinate is described by the ethylene separation d and the absolute value of the C5-C6-C6-C5 dihedral angle. The authors' earlier work on alkane-linked mini-hairpins established that no dimer forms when the base pair domain is absent, and dimerization occurs exclusively for intrastrand TT steps. Both previously published mechanistic models assume two excited states are needed, but recent experiments complicate that picture.

point_group: C1 (ion pairs taken directly from the X-ray crystal structure)
geometry_source: All pair exchange calculations performed on the X-ray diffraction crystal structure of salt 3, with no geometry optimization
method: CASSCF for the high-spin/low-spin energy splitting; broken-symmetry (BS) UB3LYP and UPBE0 for comparison
basis_set: Ahlrichs TZV on Cr, 6-31G(d) on the Cp* ligands, and 6-31+G(d) on the C, N and S atoms of the radical anion; the broken-symmetry DFT used 6-31+G(d) or 6-31G depending on the pair
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(10,10): four occupied pi molecular orbitals, two pi-SOMOs and four vacant pi* molecular orbitals, taken from the two radical anions.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled from the pi manifolds of both interacting radical anions so that the high- and low-spin states of the PAIR are described on one footing. Calculations were performed on the unmodified X-ray structure of salt 3, and each of the five crystallographically unique pairs within 10 A was treated separately.
multiplicities_studied: singlet (low spin) and triplet (high spin) of the radical anion pair
electronic_structure_description: Two pi-heterocyclic radical anions, each contributing one unpaired electron, coupled antiferromagnetically. Five unique pairs with S...S distances from 3.52 to 8.76 A were examined; the shortest contact is slightly below the 3.62 A van der Waals sum. Both CASSCF and broken-symmetry DFT agree that the pair with the shortest S...S distance dominates the exchange, but differ fourfold in magnitude: CASSCF(10,10)/6-31+G(d) gives J = -15.3 cm-1 while BS UB3LYP/6-31+G(d) gives -61 cm-1, against an experimental J1 = -40 +/- 9 cm-1 that lies between them.

Three different active spaces are built, one per pair type, each assembled from the orbitals the two interacting fragments actually contribute: (8,8) for the radical-anion/cation pair, (10,10) for the radical-anion pair, and (14,14) for the cation pair — the last being the seven-orbital set of one cation taken twice, so the pair spaces are constructed additively from monomer contributions rather than chosen ad hoc. For the [1]-...[1]- pairs both methods agree that pair 1, with the shortest S...S contact, dominates, but "the value obtained with the CASSCF method is 4 times smaller than that obtained with the BS approach" — CASSCF(10,10) gives -15.3 cm-1 against BS UB3LYP -61 cm-1, with experiment at -40 +/- 9 cm-1 sitting between them.
