Experimental exchange parameters are J1 = -40 +/- 9 cm-1 for the radical-anion pair and J2 = -0.58 +/- 0.03 cm-1 for the cation pair, with a paramagnetic impurity fraction p = 1.7 +/- 0.4%. Three pair types must be considered in the exchange calculations: [1]-...[1]-, [2]+...[2]+ and the mixed [1]-...[2]+. Five unique radical-anion pairs with S...S distances within 10 A are identified in the crystal, ranging from 3.52 to 8.76 A; the shortest is slightly below the 3.62 A sum of sulfur van der Waals radii. Eight unique mixed pairs lie within 10 A. Exchange parameters for the radical-anion pairs are in Table 1 and for the mixed pairs in Supporting Information Table S1.

compound_name: Staudinger reaction of ketenes with alpha,beta-unsaturated imines — TS(beta) and TS(delta) periselectivity
geometry_source: Transition structures optimized at HF/3-21G, HF/6-31G*, Becke3LYP/6-31G* and CASSCF(2,2)/3-21G, with SCRF solvent variants; CASSCF single points also taken at HF/3-21G geometries
method: CASSCF(2,2) and CASSCF(4,4) geometry optimization and single points; HF, MP2, Becke3LYP and semiempirical AM1 for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(2,2): the sigma(34) and sigma*(34) natural orbitals of the forming C(3)-C(4) bond. A CASSCF(4,4) surface was also explored.
active_space_protocol: The minimal two-orbital space is centred on the bond whose formation defines the [2+2] pathway. Attempts to optimize the competing TS(delta) saddle point at CASSCF/3-21G were made on BOTH the (2,2) and (4,4) surfaces and were explored extensively; all attempts failed, always collapsing to structures close to TS(beta), to the zwitterionic intermediates, or to the products. CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G* single points were therefore taken at HF/3-21G geometries for the substituted series.
electronic_structure_description: Competing transition structures for the Staudinger reaction: TS(beta) leading to [2+2] cycloadducts (cis-beta-lactams) and TS(delta) leading to the [4+2] products. At CASSCF(2,2)/3-21G the sigma(34) and sigma*(34) natural orbitals of TS(beta) have occupancies of 1.425 and 0.575, values customarily taken to indicate significant biradicaloid character. The C(3)-C(4) distance in TS(beta) is longest at CASSCF(2,2)/3-21G among all levels examined; HF/3-21G and HF/6-31G* give very similar geometries, Becke3LYP lengthens the distance relative to HF, and including solvent through SCRF gives a slightly earlier transition structure. TS(delta) is earlier than TS(beta) at every level, with longer C(3)-C(4) and shorter C(2)-C(3) distances. Dipole moments at HF/3-21G and CASSCF/3-21G are 2.466 and 1.470 D respectively. For the substituted series, MP2/6-31G*//HF/3-21G and CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G*//HF/3-21G both place TS(beta)b and TS(beta)d lowest, giving cis-beta-lactams 3b and 3d in agreement with experiment; torquoelectronic effects are more important in the TS(beta) structures than in their TS(delta) analogues.
Other: A documented failure of a minimal active space, stated as a conclusion rather than a caveat: "from these data it is clear that the CASSCF(2,2) method overestimates the biradical character of TS(beta) transition structures, predicting monotonously exclusive formation of [2+2] cycloadducts." Every other level in the study — HF, MP2, Becke3LYP, AM1 — predicts the observed periselectivity, while CASSCF(2,2) alone predicts exclusive [2+2] product, and it does so consistently across substrates rather than erratically. The mechanism of the error is visible in the orbital occupancies themselves: 1.425 and 0.575 in the sigma(34)/sigma*(34) pair, which look like genuine biradicaloid character but are an artefact of a space that contains ONLY that bond pair, so the sigma-to-sigma* excitation has nothing to compete with and is necessarily overweighted. Enlarging to (4,4) did not rescue the calculation — the competing TS(delta) saddle point could not be located on either the (2,2) or the (4,4) surface despite extensive exploration, all attempts collapsing to TS(beta), to zwitterionic intermediates, or to the products, so the smaller space cannot even represent the alternative pathway it is being asked to compare against. The geometric signature is consistent: the CASSCF(2,2) C(3)-C(4) distance is the longest of any method tested, and the CASSCF dipole moment (1.470 D) is far below the HF value (2.466 D), both reflecting the same overstated biradical and understated zwitterionic character.
reference_short: Lecea, Arrastia, Arrieta, Roa, Lopez, Arriortua, Ugalde & Cossio, J. Org. Chem. 1996, 61, 3070
notes: Combined theoretical and experimental study of solvent and substituent effects on the periselectivity of the Staudinger reaction between ketenes and alpha,beta-unsaturated imines, which can give either [2+2] beta-lactams or [4+2] products. The abstract records that HF/AM1 and CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G* methods tend to overestimate the stability and the biradical character of the relevant transition structures. Solvent effects were included through a self-consistent reaction field. Transition structure geometries are in Figures 3 and 4, energies in Table 1 and in Tables 2-5 of the supporting information. The molecular formula is not transcribed because the study covers a substituted series (a through e and beyond) rather than a single compound.

compound_name: Cyclopropanone — photodissociation and fluorescence disappearance below 365 nm
point_group: C2v at the S0 minimum; Cs at the S1 minimum and at two of the crossing points; C1 at the other two
geometry_source: CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ optimized minima, transition state, minimum-energy conical intersections (MECIs) and minimum-energy crossing points (MECPs), with frequency analysis at the same level to confirm the nature of each structure and to supply ZPE corrections
method: State-averaged CASSCF for critical-point optimization, with multistate multireference CASPT2 (MS-MR-CASPT2) single points; ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics by Tully surface hopping
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,8): one pair of pi electrons (pi and pi* orbitals), two pairs of n electrons (the oxygen lone pairs), and two pairs of sigma electrons (sigma and sigma* orbitals).
active_space_protocol: The paper states the criterion plainly — "choosing the active space for CASSCF calculations is crucial" — and builds the space from three components: the carbonyl pi system, both oxygen lone pairs, and two sigma/sigma* pairs for the ring bonds that break. In MECI optimizations, equal state averaging over the two states involved was used whenever possible. The choice is then VALIDATED against two independent references before being used for dynamics (see Other). MS-MR-CASPT2 single points refine the CASSCF energies at the CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ geometries with ZPE corrections computed at the CASSCF level.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (equal state averaging over the two states involved in each crossing optimization)
electronic_structure_description: S0 ground state of C2v symmetry taken as the ZPE-corrected reference. The S1 minimum (S1-CS) has Cs symmetry, formed by pyramidalization of the carbonyl carbon — an sp2 to sp3 transformation accompanied by an increase in the C1-O2-C3-C4 dihedral angle. Its relative energy is 68.9 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ against an experimentally predicted 72 kcal/mol, and 61.0 kcal/mol at MS-MR-CASPT2. The vertical excitation energy in the Franck-Condon region is 93.8 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ, consistent with the CCSD value of 90.0 kcal/mol from Kongsted et al., and 84.6 kcal/mol at MS-MR-CASPT2. Four critical points in the intersection space were located: SS-CS and SS-C1 are MECIs between S0 and S1, while ST-CS and ST-C1 are MECPs between T1 and S0; the CS-labelled pair has Cs symmetry and the C1-labelled pair C1. Conical intersections between states of the same spin span an (n-2)-dimensional hyperspace while crossings between different spin states span (n-1). SS-CS, lying close to the S1 minimum, is identified as responsible for the disappearance of fluorescence below 365 nm through efficient internal conversion.
Other: The active space is validated against two independent external references before being trusted for dynamics, and the paper says so explicitly: the CAS(10,8) S1 relative energy of 68.9 kcal/mol sits close to the experimentally predicted 72 kcal/mol, and the vertical excitation energy of 93.8 kcal/mol agrees with an independent CCSD value of 90.0 kcal/mol, which together "provide evidence of our selected CAS(10,8) being feasible to describe the photodissociation dynamics of cyclopropanone". That is a stronger justification than the usual assertion, because it checks the space against both experiment and a single-reference correlated method rather than only against a larger multireference calculation. The known deficiency is stated in the same breath: "although the CASSCF wave function has sufficient flexibility to model the large changes in electronic structure that can occur during chemical reactions, its energy unfortunately does not possess sufficient accuracy" — hence MS-MR-CASPT2 single points. The correction is large and roughly uniform: the S1 minimum drops from 68.9 to 61.0 kcal/mol and the vertical excitation from 93.8 to 84.6, both by about 8-9 kcal/mol, so the CASSCF surface topology survives even though the absolute energies do not. Interestingly the bare CASSCF numbers are CLOSER to experiment and to CCSD than the CASPT2 ones here, which the paper does not remark on but is worth noting for anyone reusing either set. The space composition is dictated by the reaction: two sigma/sigma* pairs are included alongside the carbonyl pi and both oxygen lone pairs precisely because ring C-C bonds break during photodissociation.
reference_short: Cui, Ai & Fang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 730
notes: Explores cyclopropanone photodissociation dynamics with CASSCF calculations and ab initio nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, filling in details of the S1 fluorescence behaviour that were previously missing at the electronic structure level. The MECI near the S1 minimum provides an efficient internal conversion channel, explaining why fluorescence disappears below 365 nm; the internal conversion event was subsequently observed directly in the trajectory simulations. Surface hopping follows the Tully technique, with the state vectors of S1 and S0 at successive steps compared to judge whether the system is passing through the intersection. Three sets of trajectories were run with 5, 10 and 20 kcal/mol of vibrational energy, distributed over selected modes; four modes involving heavy atoms were sampled between 0 and 5 kcal/mol. Geometry parameters for all critical points are in Table 1 and the structures in Figure 1.
correlation_correction: MS-MR-CASPT2 single points at the CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ geometries with CASSCF-level ZPE corrections

compound_name: BZT2 — 2-(2'-hydroxyphenyl)triazole, model for benzotriazole UV absorbers (ESIPT photostability)
point_group: Planar (Cs) enol and keto structures; nonplanar/twisted structures for the charge-transfer minimum and the conical intersections; npi* stationary points optimized under an A'' symmetry constraint
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G* optimized minima, transition states and conical intersections, with the active space varying by structure — see the protocol column; analytical frequencies computed where the space was small enough
method: CASSCF (state-averaged where states are near-degenerate) and RASSCF; conical intersection and minimum-energy crossing point optimization; initial relaxation direction (IRD) method for ground-state reaction channels; spin-exchange density (Pij) and localized one-electron density (Dii) analysis with Boys-localized active orbitals
software: Development version of Gaussian (TD-B3LYP comparisons with Gaussian 98 revision C.1)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS1, the benchmark space: the full pi-electron active space, 14 pi electrons distributed in all possible ways over the 12 p-pi molecular orbitals; 314,028 configurations. Five further spaces are used: CAS2 = CAS(16,13), the full npi* space, CAS1 plus the oxygen n-orbital, 828,828 configurations; CAS3 = CAS(14,12), obtained from CAS2 by swapping the oxygen pi orbital (occupation 1.999 in all states) out for the nitrogen n orbital; CAS4 = CAS(12,11) after removing a further quasi-inactive orbital, 106,953 configurations; CAS5 = a reduced CAS(10,8) pi space and CAS6 = a different reduced CAS(10,8) npi* space, each 1176 configurations. A RASSCF space of (14, 5+5+2)[1,1] — all single excitations from a CAS(7,5) reference — spans the same 14 electrons in 12 orbitals as CAS1/CAS3 but with only 2115 configurations.
active_space_protocol: A deliberate, documented ladder of spaces rather than one fixed choice. The full pi space CAS(14,12) is used for two purposes only: as a CALIBRATION benchmark for the cheaper spaces, and to extract spin-exchange densities, which require a space that large. Geometry optimization with it is described as 'only just feasible' and analytical frequencies as out of reach, so reduced spaces were derived by inspecting the one-electron density matrix from a large-active-space single point and demoting quasi-inactive (occupation near 2.0) and quasi-virtual (near 0.0) orbitals. The oxygen pi orbital has occupation 1.999 in ALL states and was removed on that basis. CAS(12,11) was used for nonplanar optimizations when the choice of further orbitals to remove was not obvious; CAS(10,8) was used wherever analytical frequencies were needed, with DIFFERENT (10,8) spaces for the pipi* and npi* manifolds. The RASSCF space reintroduces the orbitals discarded in CAS5/CAS6 while keeping the CI dimension manageable, and serves both to calibrate those reduced spaces and to check the proximity of pipi* states along the npi* reaction path. State-averaged orbitals were used at the nonplanar keto minimum where S1 and S0 come close. At the top of the ladder the BZT2 model itself is validated by comparing its CASSCF(14,12) vertical excitations against TD-B3LYP for both BZT2 and the full BZT1 molecule.
nroots_per_mult: Up to ~5-6 singlet states characterized in the Franck-Condon region; two-state averaging where S1 and S0 are near-degenerate
electronic_structure_description: Ground state is the planar intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded enol. CASSCF(14,12)/6-31G* vertical excitations: pipi* intraphenyl locally excited state 4.79 eV, pipi* charge transfer (phenol to triazole) CT1 5.94 eV, second pipi* CT 7.26 eV; the npi* state at 5.67 eV comes from the (16,13) space and so cannot be compared directly with the pipi* numbers. TD-B3LYP on the full BZT1 molecule gives 3.60 eV (expt 3.6), 4.20 eV (expt 4.1) and 4.26 eV (expt 4.1). Relative to the S0 enol minimum: S1 pipi*(LE) 113.0, S2 pipi*(CT) 139.3, S1/S2 conical intersection 121.3, pipi*(LE) planar minimum 106.7, pipi*(CT) nonplanar enol minimum 132.1, and pipi*(CT)/npi* avoided crossing 134.3 kcal/mol. The mechanism is ultrafast deactivation through coupled proton and electron transfer triggered by the charge-transfer state, with the S1 keto state a diradical-like open-shell state; a barrierless ground-state relaxation then recovers the enol. An alternative phenyl-localized channel resembling benzene channel-3 decay is also documented.
Other: This paper is an unusually explicit case study in active-space reduction, and quantifies exactly how much accuracy is lost at each step. Table 2 gives the same vertical excitations across six spaces plus RASSCF: the intraphenyl pipi* LE state is remarkably stable — 4.79 (CAS1, 14,12 full pi), 4.81 (CAS2, 16,13), 4.82 (CAS3), 4.86 (CAS4, 12,11), 4.87 eV (CAS5, reduced 10,8) — a spread of only 0.08 eV across a fourfold reduction in orbital count. The charge-transfer pipi* state is far more fragile: 5.94, 5.91, 6.01, 6.44, 5.88 eV across the same sequence, so the intermediate CAS(12,11) is WORSE for it (+0.50 eV) than the much smaller reduced CAS(10,8) (-0.06 eV), a non-monotonic failure that shows orbital count alone does not predict quality. The second CT state moves 7.26 to 7.30 to 6.94 eV. The npi* state is well behaved at 5.67/5.65/5.77 eV. Two structural lessons follow. First, a single reduced space cannot serve both manifolds: different (10,8) spaces were needed for pipi* and npi*, which means energies in Table 3 must be read together with their footnotes because they come from different spaces and are not mutually comparable as absolute numbers. Second, the selection criterion is occupation-number based and quantitative — the oxygen pi orbital was dropped only after being shown to have occupation 1.999 in every state considered. The RASSCF construction is the elegant escape: (14, 5+5+2)[1,1] recovers the full CAS(14,12) orbital span while cutting the configuration count from 314,028 to 2,115, and is used both to calibrate the reduced CAS(10,8) spaces and to verify that no pipi* state intrudes along the npi* path — a check the reduced spaces themselves cannot perform. Note also that the full pi space is NOT reserved for energetics here: it is required to obtain the spin-exchange density matrix elements Pij used for the valence-bond bonding analysis, so the largest space is justified by a property, not by an energy.
reference_short: Paterson, Robb, Blancafort & DeBellis, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2004, 126, 2912
notes: BZT1 is the full 2-(2'-hydroxyphenyl)benzotriazole; BZT2 is the truncated 2-(2'-hydroxyphenyl)triazole model actually treated at the CASSCF level, validated against BZT1 by TD-B3LYP comparison. The truncation deliberately drops a local excitation on the benzotriazole moiety of BZT1. TD-DFT analysis of both is stated to be not unambiguous because of considerable configurational mixing. Absolute CASSCF energies for every stationary point are tabulated in Table 3a with the space used for each; some entries are single points (marked s.p.) in one space at a geometry optimized in another. No dynamic correlation correction is applied anywhere in the study.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF/RASSCF energies only; no perturbative correction applied

compound_name: BZT phenolate anion — deprotonated BZT2 model, twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) state
point_group: Cs at both the S1 twisted minimum and the adjacent S1/S0 conical intersection, with the two rings perpendicular to each other
geometry_source: CAS(14,12)/6-31G* optimized S1 minimum and adjacent S1/S0 conical intersection
method: CASSCF (state-averaged where states are near-degenerate) and RASSCF; conical intersection and minimum-energy crossing point optimization; initial relaxation direction (IRD) method for ground-state reaction channels; spin-exchange density (Pij) and localized one-electron density (Dii) analysis with Boys-localized active orbitals
software: Development version of Gaussian (TD-B3LYP comparisons with Gaussian 98 revision C.1)
active_space_orbital_description: The CAS1 space of the neutral study: the full pi-electron active space, 14 pi electrons in 12 p-pi molecular orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The full pi space is used directly and without reduction here, and the paper gives the reason explicitly: 'the CAS1 active space discussed above is suitable for this study because the npi* state no longer plays a role in the excited-state reactivity.' Removing the deprotonated hydroxyl removes the state that forced the larger (16,13) space and the separate npi* reduced spaces in the neutral, so a single pure pi space suffices for the whole problem.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1)
electronic_structure_description: A minimum on S1 and an adjacent S1/S0 conical intersection were located, both twisted with the rings perpendicular. The excitation is a charge transfer from the phenolate anion to the triazole group, making the S1 species a TICT state, as had been suggested experimentally. The ground state of the anion has negligible double-bond character in the central bond, so twisting alone is NOT sufficient to induce degeneracy with the TICT state — the anion does not conform to the biradicaloid charge-transfer model; the decay point is reached principally along a bond-recoupling coordinate instead. The conical intersection lies 17 kcal/mol above the excited-state minimum, and that substantial barrier accounts for the long blue-fluorescence lifetimes.
Other: A clean example of the active space being sized by which states participate rather than by system size. The neutral BZT2 needed a ladder of six spaces up to CAS(16,13) because the oxygen npi* state had to be described on a balanced footing with the pipi* states; deprotonating the phenol removes that state from the photochemistry entirely, and the authors say so as their justification for using the unmodified CAS1 pi space throughout. The consequence is that the anion results carry no space-to-space inconsistency at all, whereas the neutral energetics in Table 3 must be read with per-entry footnotes naming which space produced each number. Also worth noting: the twisted S1/S0 degeneracy here is NOT delivered by the usual biradicaloid mechanism, so anyone reusing this space for a twisted charge-transfer system should not assume twisting about the central bond is the relevant degeneracy-lifting coordinate.
reference_short: Paterson, Robb, Blancafort & DeBellis, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2004, 126, 2912
notes: Studied to explain the blue emission near 420 nm from the open (non-hydrogen-bonded) form of BZT absorbers in polar hydrogen-bond-accepting solvents such as DMSO, where the solvent is believed to accept the hydroxy proton and leave the phenolate anion. Only the closed hydrogen-bonded form exists in nonpolar media, and it generally does not emit. Structures shown in Figure 9.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF/RASSCF energies only; no perturbative correction applied

compound_name: Positronium hydride (PsH) — mixed positronic-electronic wavefunction by NEO-FCI/NEO-CASSCF
formula: PsH (a proton, two electrons and a positron)
geometry_source: Single-centre system; no geometry optimization required for PsH (the companion e+LiH potential energy surface was scanned along the Li-H distance at the NEO-MP2 level only)
method: Nuclear-electronic orbital method modified for positrons: NEO-HF, NEO-MP2, NEO-CASSCF and its all-orbital limit NEO-FCI, with electron-positron annihilation rates evaluated from each wavefunction
software: GAMESS (the existing NEO implementation, modified for positrons)
basis_set: Gaussian basis sets optimized variationally at the NEO-FCI level, the SAME size for the electronic and positronic wavefunctions: [6s], [6s1p], [6s2p], [6s3p], [6s2p1d] and [6s3p1d]. Even-tempered electronic and positronic sets were also optimized, giving [9s5p4d] for H-, [13s6p4d] for Li and [6s4p4d] positronic for PsH.
active_space_orbital_description: NEO-CASSCF defines SEPARATE positronic and electronic active spaces, and minimizes the energy with respect to both the molecular orbitals and the CI coefficients over all configurations arising from those two spaces. All calculations actually reported here are at the NEO-FCI limit of that method, defined in the paper as the case where 'all of the quantum particles (i.e., electrons and positrons) in the system are active and the active space includes all of the available MOs' — for PsH that is two electrons plus one positron, three quantum particles in total, in every orbital the basis set provides. In that limit the energy is minimized with respect to only the CI coefficients.
active_space_protocol: No orbital selection was made: the study is deliberately run at the full-CI limit of NEO-CASSCF so that the active space is fixed by the basis set alone, and basis set size is then the sole convergence parameter. Basis function exponents for both the electrons and the positron were optimized variationally at the NEO-FCI level, in sizes chosen for direct comparison with Tachikawa's fully variational CI results. Because the electronic and positronic active spaces are complete, the multiconfigurational character of the wavefunction is read off from the natural orbital occupation numbers rather than being imposed.
nroots_per_mult: 1 (ground state)
electronic_structure_description: With the FCI-optimized basis sets, NEO-HF gives -0.666766 to -0.666872 Hartree across the series (essentially flat), NEO-MP2 -0.683835 to -0.728306 Hartree, and NEO-FCI -0.691010 to -0.758965 Hartree. NEO-MP2 recovers 70.4%, 73.9%, 71.9%, 71.7%, 66.9% and 66.7% of the NEO-FCI correlation energy across [6s] through [6s3p1d] — a fraction that DECREASES as the basis grows. Annihilation rates rise from 0.372 to 0.899 ns^-1 at NEO-FCI while NEO-HF stays pinned near 0.2977 ns^-1 throughout. The best NEO-FCI values, -0.758965 Hartree and 0.899299 ns^-1, are compared against a stochastic variational PsH energy of -0.78919674 Hartree with annihilation rate 2.47178 ns^-1 and an explicitly correlated Gaussian value of -0.78919765251 Hartree with rate 2.471406 ns^-1.
Other: The active space here is complete by construction, which turns the usual active-space question inside out: the limiting factor is not which orbitals are correlated but which orbitals the basis provides, and the paper measures exactly that. The highest positronic natural orbital occupation number falls from 0.9872 with [6s] to 0.8837 with [6s3p1d], a 10.4% decrease, meaning the wavefunction becomes MORE multiconfigurational as the basis grows — the multireference character is generated by the basis, not present at the outset, so a small-basis calculation would wrongly suggest a nearly single-configurational system. The consequence is severe and stated plainly: even at the full-CI limit of NEO-CASSCF the annihilation rate reaches only 0.899 ns^-1 against an accurate 2.471 ns^-1, is 'not yet converged in the present work', and 'converges very slowly with respect to the positronic basis set'; the energy is short of the accurate value by about 0.030 Hartree. The authors conclude that NEO-HF and NEO-MP2 'are not quantitatively accurate tools' for positronic systems, and note that Mitroy et al. found the same convergence trouble with more extensive CI on PsH. The perturbative diagnostic is equally instructive: the FRACTION of correlation energy recovered by NEO-MP2 falls from 73.9% to 66.7% as the basis improves, so extrapolating from a small basis would overstate how well perturbation theory does. Electron-positron correlation is the culprit — the second-order electron-positron contribution grows from -0.0064 to -0.0351 Hartree across the series while the electron-electron part only doubles — which is why the paper points to explicitly correlated approaches (NEO-XCHF with Gaussian-type geminals) rather than to a larger determinantal expansion as the way forward.
reference_short: Adamson, Duan, Burggraf, Pak, Swalina & Hammes-Schiffer, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 1346
notes: A method-development paper: the NEO framework is extended to positrons simply by replacing the proton mass with the positron mass, and strategies for computing electron-positron annihilation rates from NEO-HF, NEO-MP2 and NEO-FCI wavefunctions are derived. NEO-CASSCF is formulated and implemented but every number reported is at NEO-HF, NEO-MP2 or the NEO-FCI limit — no reduced NEO-CASSCF active space is used numerically, so no such space is recorded here. The companion e+LiH study is NEO-MP2 only and gets no row: it gives R0 = 1.6691 A and a vibrational energy of 1160 cm^-1 (against 1.5957 A and 1406 cm^-1 experimentally for LiH), and a dissociation energy of 1.626 eV for e+LiH -> Li+ + PsH, well above the reference values of 0.77275 eV (stochastic variational), 1.03(7) eV (quantum Monte Carlo) and 0.99452 eV (non-Born-Oppenheimer explicitly correlated Gaussian). Whether positron basis functions belong on H alone or on both atoms of e+LiH was examined separately via LiPs.
correlation_correction: NEO-MP2 second-order perturbation theory is reported alongside, and is decomposed into separate electron-electron and electron-positron contributions; it is an alternative to, not a correction on top of, the NEO-FCI results

compound_name: PSB11 — 11-cis-6-s-cis protonated Schiff base of retinal (rhodopsin chromophore)
geometry_source: CASSCF-optimized cis ground-state structure; the CAS(12,12)/6-31G* optimization held the beta-ionone ring twist angle fixed at the HF value of 165 degrees. B3LYP, BP86, BH-LYP, MP2 and SCC-DFTB geometries were also compared, and QM/MM structures were built from bacteriorhodopsin PDB 1C3W optimized with SCC-DFTB/CHARMM.
method: SORCI (spectroscopy-oriented configuration interaction, a multireference CI / multireference perturbation hybrid) for excitation energies; CASSCF for ground-state geometry optimization; compared against TD-DFTB, TDDFT (BP86, B3LYP, BH-LYP), HF/CIS, AM1/CIS, OM2/CIS and OM2/MRCI
software: ORCA (SORCI); Gaussian 03 and Gaussian 98 (CASSCF); Turbomole (TDDFT, HF/CIS); MNDO99 v6.1 (OM2/MRCI); CHARMM and SCC-DFTB (QM/MM)
basis_set: SV(P) (Ahlrichs) for the complete chromophore; 6-31G* for the CASSCF geometry optimization
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,12) for the ground-state geometry optimization, including ALL pi orbitals of the chromophore in the active space. For SORCI the reference space is not given as an (n,m) pair: the orbitals are approximated natural orbitals obtained from a preliminary MRCI of difference-dedicated CI type 2 (DDCI2) form, state-averaged over three roots, started from canonical RHF orbitals plus improved virtual orbitals (IVOs).
active_space_protocol: The pi system defines the space — all pi orbitals are taken in for the CASSCF geometry optimization, with no further selection. SORCI deliberately avoids the active-space-selection problem in a different way: the paper notes that 'the use of approximated natural orbitals eliminates the problem of choosing a suitable single-particle basis whose quality would affect the final CI result', so orbital quality is determined by a preliminary state-averaged DDCI2 calculation rather than by a hand-picked CAS. Efficiency instead comes from four selection thresholds, and the convergence behaviour of each was determined individually (Supporting Information) to guarantee excitation energies within 0.1 eV of the method's limit. The comparison OM2/MRCISD uses an active orbital window of 19 occupied plus 19 virtual orbitals selected from a preliminary CI run, with no configuration selection.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (state-averaged natural orbitals over three roots for SORCI)
electronic_structure_description: S1 vertical excitation energy of PSB11 on the CASSCF-optimized cis ground-state geometry: 1.22 eV at TD-DFTB, 1.39 at BP86, 1.91 at B3LYP and 2.26 eV at SORCI (oscillator strength 1.03); a literature CASPT2 value of 2.41 eV is quoted for comparison. S0 to S1 excitation transfers part of the positive net charge from the Schiff base fragment to the allyl fragment, producing a large change in dipole moment; a counterion nearer the Schiff base than the allyl fragment therefore works against that charge transfer and gives a hypsochromic shift. Bond length alternation is the dominant geometric control on the S1 energy, since the S1 gradient at the Franck-Condon point is nearly collinear with the 1556 cm-1 stretching mode and essentially cancels the polyene BLA — so a structure with larger BLA is blue shifted.
Other: The central active-space lesson is a negative one, and the paper documents it quantitatively: CASSCF WITHOUT a dynamic-correlation correction is the worst-behaved method in the whole comparison. Against an external point charge placed 2.22 A from the Schiff base proton, the state-averaged CAS(10,10)/6-31G* S1 shift is 0.13, 0.96 and 1.59 eV at charges of 0, -0.5 and -1.1 au, versus 0.03, 0.28 and 0.58 eV at SORCI — an overestimate of nearly a factor of three at full charge, larger than the error of any of the DFT, CIS or semiempirical methods tested. The dipole moment change tells the same story: 14.7 D at CASSCF versus 6.0 D at SORCI and 2-4 D for the DFT methods. Worse, at charge -0.5 the CASSCF S1/S2 pair actually crosses and the two states mix their diabatic components, so no meaningful dipole moment can be extracted at all — a state-ordering failure of the reference itself, not merely an energy error. The structural consequence is stated as a general rule: HF and post-HF methods carrying mainly static correlation OVERestimate bond length alternation while LDA/GGA functionals UNDERestimate it, and adding a PT2 correction to a CASSCF reference reduces BLA. Since BLA controls the S1 energy directly, a bare CASSCF geometry is doubly wrong here. The authors' recommendation follows: use B3LYP (or SCC-DFTB, within 0.04 eV at the SORCI level) geometries, not CASSCF ones, and treat SORCI rather than CASSCF as the benchmark. Note that the CASPT2 numbers in Table 1 are taken from the literature (refs 23-25), not computed here.

Other: This is where the CASSCF failure is measured most directly. The state-averaged CAS(10,10)/6-31G* shifts of 0.13, 0.96 and 1.59 eV at charges of 0, -0.5 and -1.1 au 'largely overestimate' the SORCI reference of 0.03, 0.28 and 0.58 eV, and the CASSCF dipole moment change of 14.7 D against SORCI's 6.0 D shows why: without dynamic correlation the space exaggerates the ionic, charge-transfer character of S1, so the state responds far too strongly to an external field. The (14,11) choice is then validated against measured structure: the optimized bond parameters agree with experiment, which the authors state 'means that our selection of the active space is reliable'.

Natural orbital occupations for 1(1)Bg are 1.97, 1.99, 2.00, 1.95, 1.78, 1.21, 1.83, 0.44, 0.03, 0.01, 0.78, from which the authors conclude the CASSCF wavefunction has multireference character. Critical points relative to the S0 minimum (CASSCF then CASPT2, eV): S1 minimum 3.02/2.32, T1 minimum 3.06/2.16, T1-NNTS 6.76/5.79, T2 minimum 2.57/2.64, T2-NNTS 3.26/3.12, two H2CN(1(2)B2) fragments 1.80/2.28, H2CN(1(2)B2) plus H2CN(1(2)B1) 6.34/5.81, and the crossings S1/S0(1) 6.51/6.14, S1/S0(2) 6.42/5.99, S1/S0(3) 3.58/2.45, S1/T1/T2 3.26/3.18. The labels T1/T2 in Table 2 are therefore assigned on the CASSCF ordering, and the T1/T2 minima at 3.06/2.16 and 2.57/2.64 eV cross the same way. Any mechanistic statement about which triplet is reached first depends entirely on which level is trusted. Second, the largest correlation correction of all is on 1(1)Bu, which falls from 8.54 to 6.40 eV — a 2.14 eV shift, against 0.39-0.44 eV for the other singlets — so the bright state is precisely the one the CASSCF space describes worst. basis_set: 6-31+G* for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; ANO-L for the CASSCF(10,10) and CASPT2 energy splittings — 5s4p2d1f for P and Cl, 4s3p1d for C, N and F, 3s1p for H
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,10): the pi orbitals of the ring carbons together with the p-pi and p-sigma orbitals of the two radical centres. Orbitals pi1 to pi3 have occupation near 2 in all configurations and pi6 to pi8 near 0; the four relevant magnetic orbitals are pi+ (= pi4), pi- (= pi5), sigma+ (= sigma1) and sigma- (= sigma2). pi+ is the bonding and pi- the antibonding combination of the ligand p orbital with the ring pi system, so their degeneracy is lifted, in contrast to sigma+ and sigma-. Illustrated in Figure 2 for the bisphosphinidene/bisnitrene and Figure 3 (magnetic orbitals only) for the methylene analogues.
active_space_protocol: One space of CONSTANT COMPOSITION across all five molecules — ring pi plus the two radical-centre p-pi and p-sigma orbitals — so that substituent trends are not contaminated by changes in the space. The multiconfigurational treatment is not optional here: broken-symmetry UHF-DFT singlets come out with <S2> of 1.11-1.18 (1.66 for the bisphosphinidene), an almost equal mixture of singlet and triplet, and the paper states that 'a multiconfigurational treatment of these states is crucial for an accurate description of this molecule'. In the CASPT2 step all valence electrons were correlated (1s of H, 3s3p of P and Cl, 2s2p of C, N and F); a level shift between 0.1 and 0.3 au was needed in some cases to remove intruder states, and a g1-corrected zeroth-order Hamiltonian was applied 'to ensure a balanced treatment of wave functions dominated by closed-shell configurations versus those with open-shell configurations'.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies including DFT zero-point corrections, as UB3LYP / CASSCF / CASPT2 / CASPT2+g1 in kcal/mol: 1[sigma2pi2] (1Ag, D2h) ground state at 0 throughout; 3[sigma2pi2] (3B1u) at 5.14 / 2.27 / 2.29 / 1.78; 5[sigma2pi2] (5Ag) at 8.82 / 7.47 / 10.2 / 11.4. The quintet is exceptionally low lying — 9 kcal/mol — where the nitrene and methylene analogues place it 23-34 kcal/mol up. The CASSCF(10,10) open-shell singlet wavefunction is 29% pi+(2)sigma+(2) and 26% pi+(2)sigma-(2) with three further configurations involving excitation into pi- (9% sigma+(2)pi-(2), 8% sigma-(2)pi-(2)); the triplet is only 49% pi+(2)sigma+(1)sigma-(1) with 15% pi-(2)sigma+(1)sigma-(1) and 11% pi+(1)sigma+(2)pi-(1). Only the quintet has a single leading configuration. The P-C1 distance of 1.773 A is ambiguous, lying between a typical P-C double bond (1.68 A) and the P-C single bond of phenylphosphinidene (1.82 A); the quinoid distortion of the ring is the least pronounced of the series and the Mulliken electron deficiency on C1 is only 0.12 electrons against 0.31 for the nitrene.
Other: The clearest demonstration in the paper that DFT and a proper active space disagree by more than the quantity being measured. UB3LYP puts the singlet-triplet gap at 5.14 kcal/mol; CASPT2+g1 gives 1.78 kcal/mol — a factor of nearly three on a gap that is the whole point of the study. The reason is visible in the wavefunction: the singlet is only 29%/26% in its two leading configurations and the triplet only 49%, so the broken-symmetry UHF-DFT reference has an <S2> of 1.66, far worse than the 1.11-1.18 seen for the other four molecules. Switching to the pure BLYP functional reduces <S2> to 1.27 and shrinks the gap, which is diagnostic of the problem rather than a fix. The structural cause is chemical: three configurations involving excitation into pi- contribute here but not in the analogues, because phosphorus 3p conjugates poorly with carbon 2p, so the pi+/pi- splitting collapses — Table 3 gives pi- at only 3.42 eV above pi+ for P against 9.90 eV for N — and the sigma/pi- combinations gain weight. This is what drives the anomalously low quintet, and it means any space that omitted pi- would be qualitatively wrong for phosphorus while surviving for nitrogen. The same physics was reported for vinylnitrene versus vinylphosphinidene by Parasuk and Cramer.

The CASSCF singlet is 40% pi+(2)sigma+(2) and 38% pi+(2)sigma-(2) with 9% pi+(1)sigma+(1)sigma-(1)pi-(1); the triplet is 79% pi+(2)sigma+(1)sigma-(1) — much more single-configurational than the phosphinidene. Other: A textbook warning against reading agreement with experiment as validation of the space. The bare CASSCF(10,10) singlet-triplet gap of 0.72 kcal/mol falls squarely inside the measured 0.58-0.82 kcal/mol range, and the authors explicitly refuse to take the credit: 'it has to be emphasized that a crucial part of the correlation effects, namely the dynamic correlation, is still missing'. Adding it moves the gap AWAY from experiment, to 1.48 kcal/mol at CASPT2 and 1.84 at CASPT2+g1. The good CASSCF number is therefore error cancellation, and a study that stopped at CASSCF would have drawn the right conclusion for the wrong reason. The g1 correction is not a small technical detail either — it moves the quintet by 2.7 kcal/mol (32.7 to 30.0) and the triplet by 0.36 kcal/mol in the opposite direction, so it matters most exactly where closed-shell and open-shell configurations are being compared. Across the whole series the CASPT2+g1 singlet-triplet gap is always bracketed by the uncorrected and sum-method-corrected DFT values, which is a useful consistency check but no substitute for the multiconfigurational treatment.

All the X-C6H4-X species studied have a singlet diradical ground state and are therefore antiferromagnetic; the singlet-triplet separation relates to the Heisenberg coupling constant through dE(T-S) = -2J.

basis_set: 6-31+G* for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; ANO-L for the CASSCF(10,10) and CASPT2 energy splittings — 5s4p2d1f for P and Cl, 4s3p1d for C, N and F, 3s1p for H
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,10): the pi orbitals of the ring carbons together with the p-pi and p-sigma orbitals of the two radical centres. Orbitals pi1 to pi3 have occupation near 2 in all configurations and pi6 to pi8 near 0; the four relevant magnetic orbitals are pi+ (= pi4), pi- (= pi5), sigma+ (= sigma1) and sigma- (= sigma2). pi+ is the bonding and pi- the antibonding combination of the ligand p orbital with the ring pi system, so their degeneracy is lifted, in contrast to sigma+ and sigma-. Illustrated in Figure 2 for the bisphosphinidene/bisnitrene and Figure 3 (magnetic orbitals only) for the methylene analogues.
active_space_protocol: One space of CONSTANT COMPOSITION across all five molecules — ring pi plus the two radical-centre p-pi and p-sigma orbitals — so that substituent trends are not contaminated by changes in the space. The multiconfigurational treatment is not optional here: broken-symmetry UHF-DFT singlets come out with <S2> of 1.11-1.18 (1.66 for the bisphosphinidene), an almost equal mixture of singlet and triplet, and the paper states that 'a multiconfigurational treatment of these states is crucial for an accurate description of this molecule'. In the CASPT2 step all valence electrons were correlated (1s of H, 3s3p of P and Cl, 2s2p of C, N and F); a level shift between 0.1 and 0.3 au was needed in some cases to remove intruder states, and a g1-corrected zeroth-order Hamiltonian was applied 'to ensure a balanced treatment of wave functions dominated by closed-shell configurations versus those with open-shell configurations'.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies including DFT zero-point corrections, as UB3LYP / CASSCF / CASPT2 / CASPT2+g1 in kcal/mol: 1[sigma2pi2] (1Ag, C2h) at 0; 3[sigma2pi2] (3Bu, C2h) at 1.45 (2.30 corrected) / 1.61 / 2.17 / 2.00; 3[sigma3pi1] (3A'', Cs) at 19.4 (20.2) / 28.3 / 27.6 / 27.0; 5[sigma2pi2] (5Ag, C2h) at 25.9 (26.7) / 27.0 / 25.6 / 27.2; 1[sigma4] (1Ag, Ci) at 30.8 (31.6) by DFT only. The free-energy singlet-triplet difference is 0.87 kcal/mol (1.59 with the sum-method correction). The C-C1 bond of 1.354-1.356 A is a typical double bond. In the closed-shell 1[sigma4] state no ligand pi orbital is occupied, so only a single bond to the ring forms and the ring is left almost undisturbed, with the HC-C1 angle dropping from about 130 to 110 degrees; the 3[sigma3pi1] triplet is structurally intermediate, with one angle near 130 and the other near 110 degrees.
Other: The 3[sigma3pi1] triplet is where DFT and the (10,10) space part company most sharply: 19.4 kcal/mol at UB3LYP against 28.3 at CASSCF and 27.0 at CASPT2+g1, an 8 kcal/mol discrepancy, and the paper notes that the multiconfigurational treatment moves both 1[sigma4] and 3[sigma3pi1] to higher values without changing the state ORDER for this molecule, the chloro analogue or the nitrene. So for the well-behaved members of the series the space affects spacings but not conclusions — which is exactly what makes the fluorinated member (see the CF row) and the phosphinidene diagnostic rather than routine. The paper also uses the CASSCF geometries as an independent check on the questionable broken-symmetry DFT structures, warning the reader 'not to attach too much importance on the absolute values obtained from the pseudo-singlet DFT calculations, but rather on the qualitative trend', and reporting that the carbene pseudo-singlet structures very strongly resemble the CASSCF ones. Davidson's prediction that the quintet should be more stable than 1[sigma2pi2] is contradicted here by both theory and experiment.
reference_short: Flock, Pierloot, Nguyen & Vanquickenborne, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 4022
notes: The parent of the three methylene analogues. Only for the methylene ligands was it possible to optimize the closed-shell 1[sigma4] singlet and the unsymmetric 3[sigma3pi1] triplet at all. Characteristic IR band from the shorter exocyclic bond stretch at 1495 cm-1 (DFT, pseudo-singlet state), which distinguishes closed-shell from diradical singlets; ESR distinguishes singlet diradical from triplet since the singlet is ESR silent.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF(10,10)/ANO-L reference, reported both plain and with the g1-corrected zeroth-order Hamiltonian; level shifts of 0.1-0.3 au applied where intruder states appeared

electronic_structure_description: Relative energies including DFT zero-point corrections, as UB3LYP / CASSCF / CASPT2 / CASPT2+g1 in kcal/mol: 1[sigma2pi2] (1Ag, C2h) at 0; 3[sigma2pi2] (3Bu, C2h) at 1.58 (2.32 corrected) / 1.66 / 2.21 / 2.19; 3[sigma3pi1] (3A'', Cs) at 7.04 (7.78) / 17.4 / 14.2 / 14.2; 1[sigma4] (1Ag, Ci) at 9.29 (10.0) / 18.2 / 20.3 / 19.6; 5[sigma2pi2] (5Ag, C2h) at 23.7 (24.5) / 25.6 / 22.8 / 22.1. The free-energy singlet-triplet difference is 0.78 kcal/mol (1.52 with the sum-method correction). Chlorine substitution stabilizes both the 3[sigma3pi1] and 1[sigma4] states relative to the parent methylene, bringing them to only 7 and 9 kcal/mol above the ground state at the DFT level. Characteristic exocyclic stretch at 1606 cm-1.
Other: The most dramatic single number in the comparison sits here: the 1[sigma4] closed-shell singlet is 9.29 kcal/mol above the ground state at UB3LYP but 18.2 at CASSCF and 19.6 at CASPT2+g1 — DFT places it less than half as high. The 3[sigma3pi1] triplet behaves the same way (7.04 versus 17.4 and 14.2). Both errors run in the SAME direction, DFT over-stabilizing the states with doubly occupied sigma orbitals relative to the open-shell diradical, which is the mirror image of the CASPT2 bias described for the fluoro analogue. Since chlorine substitution is precisely what brings these states down toward the ground state, a DFT-only study would conclude the closed-shell singlet is nearly accessible in the chloro compound when the multiconfigurational treatment puts it twice as far away. The diradical singlet-triplet gap itself, by contrast, is almost method-independent (1.58 to 2.19 kcal/mol), so the sensitivity is specific to comparing states of different sigma/pi occupancy — exactly the imbalance the g1-corrected zeroth-order Hamiltonian was introduced to address.
reference_short: Flock, Pierloot, Nguyen & Vanquickenborne, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 4022
notes: One of the two halogenated methylene analogues, used to trace how substituent electronegativity moves the closed-shell singlet and the unsymmetric triplet relative to the diradical ground state.

electronic_structure_description: THE STATE ORDER DEPENDS ON THE METHOD. Relative energies including DFT zero-point corrections, as UB3LYP / CASSCF / CASPT2 / CASPT2+g1 in kcal/mol, listed on the DFT ordering: 1[sigma4] (1Ag, C2h) at 0 / 0 / 1.74 / 1.52; 3[sigma3pi1] (3A, C1) at 6.77 / 13.3 / 5.32 / 7.06; 1[sigma2pi2] (1Ag, C2h) at 8.71 (7.89 corrected) / 0.69 / 0 / 0; 3[sigma2pi2] (3Bu, C2h) at 10.1 / 2.12 / 1.80 / 1.82; 5[sigma2pi2] (5Ag, C2h) at 33.8 / 27.3 / 24.8 / 24.8. DFT and CASSCF both give a closed-shell 1[sigma4] ground state, in agreement with experiment, but CASSCF brings the diradical singlet down to only 0.69 kcal/mol above it, and CASPT2 or CASPT2+g1 inverts them so the diradical becomes the ground state by 1.52-1.74 kcal/mol. Fluorine is known to stabilize the closed-shell singlet carbene relative to high-spin states.
Other: This is the paper's own worked example of a method-driven wrong answer, and the authors say which method is at fault: 'this preference for the biradical state is a well-known inherent error of the CASPT2 treatment, and the energy differences obtained in this work are within the CASPT2 error limits'. The g1-corrected zeroth-order Hamiltonian 'helps but is not sufficient to obtain a balanced treatment of closed- and open-shell states in this case'. The remaining lever is the basis, not the space: augmenting F and C with one extra s, p, d and f function and H with another p shrinks the closed-shell-to-diradical separation to 0.74 kcal/mol, still with the wrong sign but half the magnitude. The conclusion drawn is symmetric and worth carrying forward — CASPT2 overemphasizes singlet diradical stability while DFT overestimates the stability of the closed-shell 1[sigma4] singlet, so the truth lies between two methods that bracket it, and the 1[sigma4] state is certainly the ground state with 1[sigma2pi2] very close by. The 3[sigma3pi1] triplet is equally unstable to the treatment, spanning 5.32 to 13.3 kcal/mol across the four levels. Note also that this molecule's CASSCF singlet-triplet separations are far more compressed than its analogues' (0.69 and 2.12 kcal/mol), so near-degeneracy rather than active space size is what makes it fragile.
reference_short: Flock, Pierloot, Nguyen & Vanquickenborne, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 4022
notes: The problematic case for the CASPT2 calculations, and the reason the study reports both plain and g1-corrected CASPT2 throughout. Its characteristic exocyclic stretch is at 1633 cm-1. Zuev and Sheridan reported weak IR bands in the region characteristic of the biradical and assigned them to combination bands of the 1[sigma4] structure; given the small computed energy difference between the two singlets, the authors suggest those bands may instead come from small amounts of the diradical actually being present.

compound_name: Formaldehyde (H2CO) — molecular dissociation to H2 + CO at medium photoexcitation energies
point_group: Cs for the planar regions and for the MSX crossing point; C1 for the lower-lying conical intersections and for radical dissociation to H + HCO
geometry_source: CASSCF full-valence (10,9)/6-31G* optimized stationary points, characterized by numerical frequencies; reoptimized in the reduced CAS(8,7) space for analytical frequencies and for minimum energy paths; some crossing points additionally checked in an augmented CAS(12,10). Singlet-triplet energy-difference minimizations and part of the seam MEP came from a development version of Gaussian.
method: CASSCF for the potential energy surfaces, with direct dynamics variational multiconfiguration Gaussian (DD-vMCG) wavepacket quantum dynamics on S1, T1 and S0; conical intersection and T1/S0 seam mapping by energy-difference minimization
software: Development version of GAUSSIAN; development version of the Heidelberg MCTDH package (DD-vMCG)
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space, 10 electrons in 9 orbitals, for energies and optimized structures. A reduced CAS(8,7) omitting one pair of CH2 sigma/sigma* orbitals was used for analytical frequencies and for the minimum energy paths, at reoptimized geometries. An augmented CAS(12,10) was used to check some of the crossing points.
active_space_protocol: Three spaces in a deliberate hierarchy, each justified by what it is used for and each checked against its neighbour. The full valence (10,9) is credited with capturing part of the DYNAMIC correlation as well, specifically the CO sigma to sigma* excitation — an unusual and explicit claim about what a valence space buys beyond static correlation. The reduced (8,7) exists because analytical frequencies and MEPs were not affordable in the larger space; the paper states that dropping the CH2 sigma/sigma* pair 'does not affect the structure or energetics significantly'. The augmented (12,10) is a spot check: 'the geometries do not change significantly, while the energies are typically lowered by about 2 kcal/mol'. CASSCF rather than CASPT2 had to be used for the dynamics because DD-vMCG needs a local quadratic representation of the surface, 'which is not yet feasible at the CASPT2 level' — a practical constraint that forced the level of theory rather than a judgement that CASSCF was sufficient.
electronic_structure_description: S1 is the n to pi* state. S1 and T1 run almost parallel in Cs regions with T1 about 10 kcal/mol below S1, and they close up as the symmetry drops from Cs to C1. The barrier to dissociation from the T1 minimum is 17 kcal/mol against 27 kcal/mol for the singlet, so with intersystem crossing available the dissociation dynamics is argued to be controlled by the T1 bottleneck. At the bottom of the S1/S0 seam, recalculated here with the full valence space, all three states S0, S1 and T1 are almost degenerate, which lets T1 formaldehyde deactivate to S0 and form molecular products. Two distinct sets of T1/S0 crossing points were located, one close to the original geometries on two parallel branches and a second on a separate segment of the seam with lower energies and longer CH bonds. The energy gap between S1 and T1 is no more than 10 kcal/mol.
Other: The paper quantifies its own CASSCF error rather than asserting sufficiency, and the numbers are not small: against the CASPT2 results of ref 14, relative to the S0 minimum, CASSCF is off by 6 kcal/mol at the S1 minimum, 7 kcal/mol at the S0/S1 C1 conical intersection and 9 kcal/mol at the T1 minimum. Those errors are systematic in sign (CASSCF too high) but not uniform in size, and one consequence is qualitative: the MSX point — an accessible minimum on the T1/S0 seam of Cs symmetry, characterized at MRCI and CASPT2 in refs 13 and 14 — IS NO LONGER A MINIMUM at the CASSCF level. A similar structure still on the seam, found by minimizing the T1/S0 energy difference, comes out 21 kcal/mol higher, so the energetic ORDER of that crossing point and the T1 transition state is reversed at CASSCF relative to the correlated methods. Anyone reading mechanistic conclusions off this surface has to know that. The active-space checks themselves are reassuring by comparison: enlarging from (10,9) to (12,10) leaves geometries alone and lowers energies by only about 2 kcal/mol, and shrinking to (8,7) by removing a CH2 sigma/sigma* pair changes neither structure nor energetics significantly — so the residual error is a dynamic-correlation problem, not an active-space-size problem, which is exactly why the (12,10) check does not rescue the MSX topology. The paper also notes a small barrier within the seam at post-CASSCF levels that CASSCF does not reproduce, though the degenerate asymptotes are ultimately lower either way.
reference_short: Araujo, Lasorne, Magalhaes, Worth, Bearpark & Robb, J. Chem. Phys. 2009, 131, 144301
notes: Proposes a previously unidentified channel to molecular products H2 + CO through T1, opening at medium energies near or above the T1 dissociation barrier but still below the S1 barrier, making T1 a shortcut between S1 formaldehyde and S0 molecular products. Builds on the authors' earlier proposal (J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 7489) of concerted internal conversion and dissociation through an S1/S0 conical intersection seam reached after an S1 transition barrier. The Cs region of the T1/S0 seam favours ground-state reactant regeneration, but two further portions of the seam are characterized here, one leading to radical dissociation and one to molecular dissociation. Reaching the seam from the T1 basin requires a change in the character of the dominant diabatic state — a generalized transition barrier that is in fact an avoided crossing — which may or may not involve passing through the optimized T1 transition state. Up to eight Gaussian wavepacket basis functions were used in the DD-vMCG runs.
correlation_correction: None applied — CASSCF energies throughout, with published CASPT2 (ref 14) and MRCI (ref 13) results used only as an external check on the CASSCF error

compound_name: TM-1' — model tictoid twisted pi-electron electro-optic chromophore (analogue of TM-1)
point_group: C2v at the fully twisted 90 degree geometry
geometry_source: Ground-state optimized geometries at fixed ring-ring dihedral twist angles; excitation energies computed at twist angles between 50 and 90 degrees
method: Three-state state-averaged CASSCF (SA3-CASSCF) with CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries; single-state CASSCF for the reference calibration; finite-field second derivative of the dipole moment for the hyperpolarizability
active_space_orbital_description: SA3-CASSCF(4,3): four pi electrons in three pi molecular orbitals, obtained by expanding a single-state CASSCF(2,2) to include the in-plane oxygen p atomic orbital and its electrons. The active orbitals are shown in Figure 10. A single-state CASSCF(14,13) calculation at the 90 degree geometry serves as the higher-quality reference.
active_space_protocol: Three levels are used for three distinct jobs. The minimal SS-CASSCF(2,2) covers the two inter-ring charge-transfer states; expanding it to SA3-CASSCF(4,3) by adding the in-plane oxygen p orbital and its electrons was necessary to bring in a THIRD state, and the surfaces are then state-averaged over three roots so that state ordering is maintained across the whole 50-90 degree twist scan. The much larger single-state CASSCF(14,13) is not used to build surfaces at all — it is run only at the 90 degree geometry, and the SA3-CASSCF energies are then rigidly SHIFTED BY 0.3 eV so their state separation matches it. Two further empirical corrections are layered on: the four ortho-methyl groups of TM-1 are left out of the state-averaged calculations and replaced by a model methyl-repulsion potential, derived by differencing TM-1' ground-state torsional potentials and zeroed at 90 degrees where the methyls interact least, then added to both ground and excited state energies. CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries test the space: 'the CASPT2 and CASSCF results differ by no more than 0.1 eV in all of these calculations; therefore, the CASSCF active space is adequate for the purpose of describing the differences in computed quantities.'
electronic_structure_description: At the 90 degree twisted geometry the lowest three states converge to a diradical ground state (D), a zwitterionic first excited state (Z), and a second excited state of n to pi* character. Each state was classified by inspecting its CI coefficients, molecular orbitals and dipole moment at the highly symmetric C2v twisted geometry. Potential energy surfaces for all three as a function of twist angle and applied longitudinal dipolar field (simulating a polar solvent) are given in Figure 11. The nonlinear response beta was computed at 90 degrees as the finite second derivative of the dipole moment with respect to an additional applied field. Crystallography on the target chromophores and their precursors gives consistently large, uniform arene-arene twist angles of 80-89 degrees, governed primarily by sterics and essentially independent of chromophore identity.
Other: Expanding the active space here changes the STATE COUNT, not just the energies: going from SS-CASSCF(2,2) to SA3-CASSCF(4,3) — the addition being the in-plane oxygen p atomic orbital and its two electrons — makes a second excited state appear 'fairly close in energy to the first excited state over a wide range of twist angles'. Since nonlinear response depends on differences between state energies, a state that only exists once the oxygen lone pair is in the space is not a detail; the minimal (2,2) space would have described the inter-ring charge transfer while being blind to a nearby competing state. Two cautions attach to reusing these energies. First, the CASPT2 agreement to within 0.1 eV is offered as proof the space is adequate, but it was measured only on the (4,3) surfaces — it does not license the (2,2), and it says nothing about whether a fourth state is missing. Second, the SA3-CASSCF surfaces as plotted are NOT raw: they carry a rigid 0.3 eV shift imposed so that the state separation reproduces a single-state CASSCF(14,13) calculation at 90 degrees, plus an added empirical methyl-repulsion potential standing in for the four ortho-methyl groups that were dropped from the model. The 0.3 eV shift is itself the size of the active-space error between (4,3) and (14,13) at one geometry, applied uniformly across the whole twist coordinate on the assumption it is geometry-independent — an assumption the paper does not test.
reference_short: Kang et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, 3267
notes: TM-1' is a computational model of chromophore TM-1, used to reduce cost; the real TM-1 carries four ortho-methyl groups that enforce the inter-ring twist and are represented in the calculations only by an added repulsion potential. The wider paper is largely synthetic and materials-focused: Suzuki coupling of 4-bromopyridine N-oxide with a boronic acid using a Pd(0)/DCPPP catalyst gives the tetra-ortho-methylphenylpyridine core in 53% yield, and the resulting tictoid chromophores show very large hyperpolarizabilities. Poled 5 wt % TMC-3/PVP guest-host films reach an effective r33 of 330 pm/V at 1310 nm by Teng-Man measurement, with strong aggregation limiting the response in less polar matrices. PGSE NMR aggregation numbers and EFISH-derived mu-beta data are reported as a function of concentration.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single-point energies at the CASSCF geometries; agreement within 0.1 eV throughout

geometry_source: Reactant, product and transition state fully optimized at CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) in the gas phase and in heptane, with frequencies at the same level; solution structures optimized with both SMD and IEFPCM
method: CASSCF for geometries and frequencies with second-order multireference perturbation theory (MRPT2) single points; continuum solvation by IEFPCM, self-consistent PCM (SC-PCM), SMD in Gaussian 09 and SMD in GESOL (SMD-G); equilibrium solvation path approximation for the potential of mean force
software: Gaussian 09 (CASSCF, IEFPCM, SMD); GAMESS (MRPT2); GESOL with Gaussian 03 (SMD-G solvation free energies)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(10,9): four pi bonds, the four corresponding antibonding orbitals, and one nitrogen lone pair.
active_space_protocol: A single fixed space is used for every structure, solvent model and complex in the study, which is what makes the solvent-model comparison in Table 2 internally consistent. Composition is by chemical function — the pi/pi* manifold that carries the excitation plus the nitrogen lone pair that donates the proton — not by an energy window. Frequencies at the same level confirm each stationary point (no imaginary frequencies for reactant and product, exactly one for the transition state). MRPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries supply the dynamic correlation; the potential of mean force along the reaction coordinate was built at MRPT2//SMD/CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) using 32 MRPT2 energy points.
electronic_structure_description: Excited-state double proton transfer (ESDPT) converting the normal form to the tautomer. Gas-phase CASSCF/6-31G(d,p) bond distances, reactant then transition state: N1-H10 0.998 then 1.288 A, O16-H10 2.147 then 1.187 A, O16-H17 0.951 then 1.035 A, N6-H17 2.112 then 1.557 A. Barrier heights in kcal/mol, CASSCF then MRPT2, with ZPE-corrected values in parentheses: gas phase 17.1 (13.7) then 8.71 (5.31); IEFPCM 19.5 (16.7) then 12.0 (9.12); SC-PCM 15.8 (12.9) then 8.23 (5.40); SMD 13.4 (10.6) then 5.83 (3.05); SMD-G 15.4 (12.6) then 7.87 (5.09). The transition state has a larger dipole moment than the reactant, so solvent should stabilize it preferentially and lower the barrier. Solvation increases the N-H distances and decreases the O-H distances at the transition state relative to gas phase, giving it more pronounced ion-pair character.
Other: Dynamic correlation on top of this space is not a refinement, it is most of the answer: the gas-phase barrier falls from 17.1 kcal/mol at CASSCF(10,9) to 8.71 at MRPT2, and from 13.7 to 5.31 with zero-point energies — roughly a factor of two in every solvent model tested. A CASSCF-only treatment with this space would put the barrier far too high to explain the observed kinetics, so the (10,9) space should be understood as a reference for MRPT2 rather than as a level of theory in its own right. The second, less expected finding concerns coupling the space to a continuum: the IEFPCM implementation in Gaussian 09 gave a POSITIVE solvation energy for the nonpolar solvent and barriers larger than gas phase — 'physically unreasonable' in the authors' words — because the reaction field is held fixed rather than equilibrated against the excited-state CASSCF wavefunction. The self-consistent SC-PCM external iteration against the solute CASSCF density fixes the sign and restores the expected trend, and the paper concludes it 'seems to be very important for excited-state calculations in solution with the IEFPCM model'. SMD in G09 inherits the same defect since its bulk electrostatic part is IEFPCM-based; only the GESOL SMD-G route avoids it. The residual warning is that both SC-PCM and SMD-G appear to UNDERestimate excited-state solvation energies with CASSCF, so the computed solvent lowering of the barrier (0.22 kcal/mol at SMD-G) is probably too small. notes: Multidimensional excited-state potentials of mean force in solution were generated for the first time at the MRPT2//SMD/CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) level, using the equilibrium solvation path approximation with 32 MRPT2 points along the minimum energy path and interpolated dual-level corrections. Heptane was chosen as a nonpolar solvent to allow comparison with the experiments of Kwon et al., who found the rate constants of 7AI-alcohol complexes to depend on alcohol acidity. The result that solution lowers the barrier is consistent with the experimental observation that excited-state tautomerization of the 1:1 7AI:alcohol complex is seen in solution but not in the gas phase.

geometry_source: Reactant, product and transition state fully optimized at CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) in the gas phase and in heptane, with frequencies at the same level; solution structures optimized with both SMD and IEFPCM
method: CASSCF for geometries and frequencies with second-order multireference perturbation theory (MRPT2) single points; continuum solvation by IEFPCM, self-consistent PCM (SC-PCM), SMD in Gaussian 09 and SMD in GESOL (SMD-G); equilibrium solvation path approximation for the potential of mean force

active_space_protocol: A single fixed space is used for every structure, solvent model and complex in the study, which is what makes the solvent-model comparison in Table 2 internally consistent. Composition is by chemical function — the pi/pi* manifold that carries the excitation plus the nitrogen lone pair that donates the proton — not by an energy window. Frequencies at the same level confirm each stationary point (no imaginary frequencies for reactant and product, exactly one for the transition state). MRPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries supply the dynamic correlation; the potential of mean force along the reaction coordinate was built at MRPT2//SMD/CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) using 32 MRPT2 energy points.
electronic_structure_description: Excited-state double proton transfer analogous to the methanol complex. Gas-phase CASSCF/6-31G(d,p) bond distances, reactant then transition state: N1-H10 0.998 then 1.292 A, O16-H10 2.147 then 1.184 A, O16-H17 0.951 then 1.029 A, N6-H17 2.117 then 1.578 A. Barrier heights in kcal/mol, CASSCF then MRPT2, ZPE-corrected in parentheses: gas phase 17.1 (13.8) then 8.79 (5.43); IEFPCM 22.7 (19.9) then 15.3 (12.5); SC-PCM 15.7 (12.9) then 8.26 (5.46); SMD 13.4 (10.6) then 5.93 (3.19); SMD-G 15.6 (12.8) then 8.14 (5.40). The ethanol complex has a slightly higher gas-phase barrier than the methanol complex, attributed to the proton affinity of ethanol relative to methanol.

That is a 7 kcal/mol swing produced purely by how the reaction field is coupled to the active-space wavefunction, with the geometry, basis and space unchanged — a reminder that for excited-state CASSCF in a continuum, the solvation algorithm can dominate any active-space consideration.
reference_short: Fang & Kim, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2013, 9, 3557
notes: Studied alongside the methanol complex to test the dependence of the excited-state proton transfer rate on alcohol acidity reported experimentally by Kwon et al. in heptane. Structures at the CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) level with SMD and IEFPCM are shown in Figure 1B; acidity and basicity values are tabulated in Supporting Information Table S2.
