geometry_source: CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* optimized critical points along the reaction pathway, with frequency analysis at the same level to confirm that each transition state is a real saddle point; surface crossings and conical intersections also optimized at the CASSCF level
method: CASSCF for geometries and surface crossings, CASPT2 for all energies, with spin-orbit coupling constants from a one-electron approximate spin-orbit Hamiltonian
software: Gaussian 03 (stationary point optimizations); Molpro 2006 (surface crossing optimizations at CASSCF and all CASPT2 energy evaluations); MOLCAS 7.4 (SOC constants)
basis_set: 6-31G* for the geometry optimizations; 6-311G** for the vertical transition energies; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 energies along the reaction pathway
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(8,7): all bonding and antibonding pi-type orbitals, the oxygen lone pair (n-type orbital) in the reactive fragment, and the additional orbitals — sigma orbitals in particular — relevant to the bonds being broken and made.
active_space_protocol: A single reaction-defined space of constant size across the whole surface: pi/pi* of the reactive fragment, the carbonyl oxygen lone pair, and whichever sigma orbitals participate in the bond that is breaking. Because paths A and B break DIFFERENT bonds (C1-C5 and C5-C6 respectively), holding the electron and orbital counts at (8,7) means the sigma orbitals entering the space differ between the two pathways while the count does not. Dynamic valence-electron correlation is added by CASPT2 with an imaginary shift of 0.4 au to moderate intruder states. The basis is stepped by purpose — 6-31G* for optimization, 6-311G** for vertical excitations, and cc-pVDZ for the pathway energies, the last justified by low cost and accuracy 'matchable with the results given by the 6-311G** basis set'.
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2 vertical excitations: 1(npi*) at 3.52 eV (f = 0.001, experiment 3.70 eV), 1(pipi*) at 4.87 eV (f = 0.020), 3(npi*) at 3.32 eV and 3(pipi*) at 3.56 eV. Under 320 nm irradiation only 1(npi*) is accessible — the bright 1(pipi*) state lies too high. The 3(pipi*) state comes from promoting a pi-type bonding orbital MIXED WITH the sigma orbital along the C1-C5 and C5-C6 bonds into the cyclopentenone pi* orbital, which is what makes it the state that drives C-C cleavage. In 1(npi*) the cyclopentenone C-O bond lengthens by 0.138 A; in 3(pipi*) the C3-C4, C2-C3, C2-O and C1-C5 bonds go from 1.343, 1.486, 1.205 and 1.508 A in the ground state to 1.511, 1.447, 1.237 and 1.535 A. The 1(npi*)/3(pipi*) surface crossing near the 1(npi*) minimum carries a spin-orbit coupling constant of 60.9 cm-1; the 1(npi*)min and 3(pipi*)min are nearly degenerate, differing by 0.1 kcal/mol. CASPT2 reaction energies in eV: path A, R to A-INT is 29.3 on S0 and -38.7 on 3(pipi*), A-INT to A-P has barriers of 11.1 (S0) and 22.5 (triplet) with energies -42.2 and 2.1; path B, R to B-INT-I 42.8 barrier and -6.2, B-INT to B-INT-I -50.0 and -34.2, B-INT-I to B-P-I barriers 60.6 and 56.7 with -10.0 and -7.5. SOC constants at the other crossings are much smaller: 0.54 cm-1 at S0/3(pipi*)-A-SC and 0.43 cm-1 at S0/3(pipi*)-B-SC.
Other: The active space is defined by the bond that breaks, and the paper's own results show why that matters: the reactive 3(pipi*) state is not a clean pi to pi* excitation at all but comes from an orbital of MIXED pi and sigma character delocalized along C1-C5 and C5-C6. A space built from the pi manifold and the carbonyl lone pair alone — the obvious choice for an enone — would misdescribe precisely the state that does the chemistry. Two cautions follow for reusing these numbers. First, the space is held at (8,7) for both pathways even though path A breaks C1-C5 and path B breaks C5-C6, so the sigma orbitals occupying those seven slots are not the same set in the two branches and the path A versus path B energetics rest on different orbital selections at constant size. Second, and stated explicitly by the authors, 'the energy evaluations in the CASSCF-optimized surface crossings at the CASPT2 level show that the two degenerate electronic states are SPLIT due to the dynamic valence-electron correlation at the position of the PES crossing point' — the crossing geometries were located where the CASSCF space makes the states degenerate, and correlation lifts that degeneracy, so the reported crossing points are CASSCF artifacts to a degree the CASPT2 energies quantify but do not correct. The intruder-state problem was real enough to need a 0.4 au imaginary shift. On the physics, the SOC constants span more than two orders of magnitude across the three crossings (60.9 versus 0.54 and 0.43 cm-1), so which decay channel is efficient is decided by spin-orbit coupling rather than by energetics.
reference_short: Chen, Rinkevicius, Luo, Agren & Cao, J. Phys. Chem. A 2011, 115, 7815
notes: Photolysis divides into two branches by which C-C bond ruptures. Path A (C1-C5 cleavage) gives the biradical intermediate A-INT with no barrier — a restricted optimization along the bond-rupture direction found the energy rising monotonically with no saddle point — followed by methyl migration from C6 to C1 through A-TS to product A-P, with C1-C6 contracting from 1.522 to 1.436 A. Path A is favoured on the triplet surface for both dynamic and thermodynamic reasons. Path B (C5-C6 cleavage) leads first to a relatively stable species and is described as the more facile route for the PYROLYTIC rather than photolytic reaction. On the ground state the overall reaction is exothermic by 12.9 kcal/mol. The vertical energy to 1(npi*) is 81.3 kcal/mol, matching the 320 nm irradiation energy, and relaxation to the 1(npi*) minimum is exoergic by 8.7 kcal/mol. No 3(npi*) minimum was found near the Franck-Condon region, but the 3(npi*/pipi*) conical intersection was optimized.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 with an imaginary level shift of 0.4 au to moderate intruder states; cc-pVDZ for the pathway energies and 6-311G** for the vertical excitations

compound_name: Benzoic acid monomer (C6H5COOH) — photophysics and photodissociation
point_group: Cs for the planar S0-a, S1, S2, T1 and T2 structures; C1 for the nonplanar S0-b conformer
geometry_source: CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ optimized structures for all five lowest states, with harmonic frequencies at the same level confirming each as a minimum or first-order saddle point; S0 and T1 additionally optimized at MP2 and B3LYP with cc-pVDZ
method: CASSCF for stationary structures on all five surfaces (T2, S1 and S2 by CASSCF only); MP2 and B3LYP for S0 and T1; RRKM rate constants for adiabatic and nonadiabatic unimolecular processes, with the nonadiabatic hopping probability from the Delos expression using the spin-orbit coupling matrix element and the gradients at the crossing
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,8). The paper first states what the space SHOULD contain on a localized-orbital picture — the three pi and three pi* orbitals of the aromatic ring, the C=O pi and pi* orbitals, and the oxygen nonbonding orbital of the carbonyl, which is ten orbitals — and then says the calculations use ten electrons in eight orbitals, 'with one of the pi* orbitals excluded from the active space'.
active_space_protocol: The selection is stated to be 'a crucial step for the CASSCF calculation' and is built from a localized-orbital analysis of which fragments carry the relevant excitations: the aromatic pi system for the pipi* states and the carbonyl pi/pi* plus oxygen lone pair for the npi* states. Both manifolds have to be described on a common footing because the mechanism turns on the ordering of 3(pipi*), 3(npi*) and 1(npi*). The same (10,8) space is used for all five states and for every stationary point, so relative energies are internally consistent. The space is validated indirectly: the CAS(10,8) C-C bond lengths in the ring come out near 1.40 A, matching MP2 and B3LYP, so 'the conjugation interaction in the aromatic ring is well described'.
electronic_structure_description: Five lowest states studied: S0, T1, T2, S1 and S2. Two ground-state minima were found — planar C6H5COOH(S0)-a with all atoms coplanar, and C6H5COOH(S0)-b, nonplanar with an H15-O14-C12-C1 dihedral of 11.5 degrees at MP2/cc-pVDZ and lying 6.6 kcal/mol higher; the barrier between them is 11.6 kcal/mol at MP2/cc-pVDZ. Relative to the S0 zero level, at CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ: T1 (3 pipi*, from pi to pi* excitation in the aromatic ring) at 73.8 kcal/mol (B3LYP gives 75.5); T2 (3 npi*) at 90.0 kcal/mol, 16.2 above T1 and 1.5 BELOW S1; S1 (1 npi*) at 91.5 kcal/mol (32002.6 cm-1), 17.7 above T1; S2 (1 pipi*) at 100.7 kcal/mol (35220.3 cm-1), 10.8 above S1 and comparable to the experimental band origin of 35923-35960 cm-1 (102.7 kcal/mol). The S1 state is a carbonyl-localized excitation in which the C12-O13 bond changes from double to single; S2 lengthens the ring C-C bonds from 1.40 to 1.44 A. Both the 3(pipi*) assignment of T1 and the 3(npi*) assignment of T2 lying between S1 and T1 confirm earlier experimental inferences.
Other: The space here is DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE and the paper says so: the localized-orbital analysis calls for three ring pi and three ring pi* orbitals plus the C=O pi/pi* pair and the oxygen lone pair, but one pi* orbital is dropped, giving (10,8) instead of the (10,10) that analysis implies. That truncation is unbalanced by construction — it removes virtual character from the ring pi manifold while leaving the carbonyl set intact — and the states whose relative order carries the whole mechanism are precisely one ring pipi* pair (T1, S2) against one carbonyl npi* pair (T2, S1). The T2-S1 gap comes out at only 1.5 kcal/mol, well inside what an unbalanced pi* truncation could move, so the reported ordering of those two states should be treated as suggestive rather than settled. No CASPT2 or other dynamic-correlation correction is applied anywhere, which matters more than usual for a pipi*/npi* competition, where correlation typically stabilizes pipi* states more. The paper's own validation is structural rather than energetic — ring C-C bond lengths near 1.40 A agreeing with MP2 and B3LYP — and structural agreement is a weak test of a space chosen to get state ordering right. What does support the assignments is external: T1 as 3(pipi*), T2 as 3(npi*) lying between S1 and T1, and the S2 adiabatic energy of 35220 cm-1 against an observed band origin of 35923-35960 cm-1 all match experiment independently.
reference_short: Li, Zhang & Fang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 7718
notes: Three reaction channels are explored on the ground and excited state surfaces, extending the authors' earlier work on formic and acetic acid photodissociation; phenyl substitution is expected to change the aliphatic mechanism because of conjugation between the ring and the carboxylic group. RRKM rate constants were computed for both adiabatic and nonadiabatic unimolecular processes, the latter treating the surface hop as a transition probability factor in the manner Miller uses for tunneling, with the hopping probability from Delos's expression in terms of the coupling matrix element V12, the effective reduced mass, the norm of the gradient difference and the geometric mean of the two gradient norms. Detailed structural parameters are in the Supporting Information.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF energies only; no perturbative correction applied

compound_name: 3H-Diazirine (cyclic CH2N2) — photochemical carbene formation and isomerization
point_group: C2v for the ground and excited state stationary points; Cs along the reaction coordinates to carbene and to diazomethane; C1 at the conical intersections
geometry_source: CASSCF(12,10)/cc-pVTZ optimized stationary points and conical intersections, characterized by analytic harmonic vibrational frequencies from the mass-weighted Cartesian Hessian; frequencies at the conical intersections computed instead from the PROJECTED Hessian, and used for zero-point corrections. Minima connected by each transition state confirmed by IRC.
method: CASSCF for geometries and crossing-surface optimizations with state-averaged orbitals; CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF references; ab initio direct semiclassical trajectory dynamics in the full coordinate space with Tully-Preston surface hopping
software: MOLCAS 5.0 (CASSCF, CASPT2); Gaussian 98 revision A.7 (direct dynamics); an in-house program for projecting zero-frequency modes out of the Hessian at conical intersections
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; 6-31G* for the direct dynamics trajectories
active_space_orbital_description: (12e,10o): all valence orbitals of the -CN2 chromophore. In the S0 minimum of diazirine these are one pi(N-N), one pi*(N-N), one sigma(N-N), one sigma*(N-N), two sigma(C-N), two sigma*(C-N), plus the 2s atomic orbitals of the two nitrogen atoms. One of the sigma(C-N)/sigma*(C-N) pairs transforms into a pi(N-N)/pi*(N-N) pair in the acyclic isomer, diazomethane. Illustrated in Figure 1. A reduced CASSCF(8,7) with 6-31G* was used for the direct dynamics trajectories.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by the CHROMOPHORE rather than by the molecule: all valence orbitals of -CN2, so the same twelve electrons in ten orbitals describe both the cyclic and acyclic isomers even though the orbitals themselves change character across the isomerization — one sigma(C-N)/sigma*(C-N) pair in diazirine becomes a pi(N-N)/pi*(N-N) pair in diazomethane. That is what makes a single space valid along the whole reaction coordinate. All crossing-surface computations use STATE-AVERAGED orbitals, chosen because they 'ensure a balanced description at the intersection geometries without imposing symmetry on the wave function and avoiding symmetry breaking'. CASPT2 uses the CASSCF wavefunctions as reference with the carbon and nitrogen 1s electrons frozen. The much smaller CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* space exists purely because the trajectory calculations need energy, gradient and Hessian at every step, and only a few representative trajectories are affordable even then.
nroots_per_mult: Up to four singlet states per isomer (S0 plus three excited states); state-averaged orbitals at the crossings
electronic_structure_description: Energies in hartrees (CASSCF then CASPT2, with reference weight): A1 diazirine ground state -148.05365 then -148.44749 (0.904); B1 -147.88929 then -148.30585 (0.891), band origin 322 nm and 0-0 transition 323 nm against an observed 325 nm; B2 -147.77301 then -148.22731 (0.860) at 207 nm; A2 -147.79754 then -148.21969 (0.888) at 200 nm, both against an observed 200 nm. The first excited state is an n to pi* excitation of B1 symmetry; it is NOT a minimum but a first-order saddle point on S1, whose imaginary mode leads to S1 diazomethane. An IRC from it ends at the S1/S0 conical intersection CI1 (-147.94963 then -148.39688, 900 nm without and 909 nm with ZPE relative to ground-state diazirine), which is the global minimum of the S1 n-pi* surface and the site of efficient radiationless decay. The strong 200 nm (6.20 eV) absorption is a pi to pi* (B2) saddle point at 207 nm, with a third sigma to pi* (A2) state above it at 200 nm that IS a minimum. Ground-state transition states: TS0 for diazirine-to-diazomethane isomerization at -147.98248 then -148.38024, and TS1 for N2 extrusion at -148.01573 then -148.39843. Methylene formation is favoured over isomerization on barrier heights. The computed isomerization reaction energy of 9.9 kcal/mol agrees with the experimental 8 plus or minus 5 kcal/mol.
Other: Two active-space decisions carry the result. First, the space is anchored on the -CN2 chromophore's full valence set rather than on any one geometry, which is what lets a SINGLE (12,10) space describe both isomers and the path between them: one sigma(C-N)/sigma*(C-N) pair simply becomes a pi(N-N)/pi*(N-N) pair as the ring opens. A space chosen from diazirine's orbital character alone would not survive the isomerization. Second, state-averaged orbitals are used for every crossing-surface computation specifically to avoid symmetry breaking, since the C2v stationary points sit adjacent to Cs and C1 crossings where a state-specific calculation would collapse onto one symmetry species. The quality checks are unusually complete: reference weights are tabulated for every critical point and stay in a narrow 0.860-0.904 band, so no point is contaminated by intruders, and the CASPT2 numbers are validated externally against three independent observables — a 323 nm computed 0-0 transition against 325 nm observed, 461 nm against 471 nm for diazomethane, and a 9.9 kcal/mol isomerization energy against 8 plus or minus 5 kcal/mol. Note the caveat for reuse: the dynamics were run in a much smaller CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G* space, not the (12,10)/cc-pVTZ space that produced the energetics, so trajectory results and surface energetics come from different levels. The lowest reference weight in the table, 0.860, belongs to the B2 pipi* state, the one carrying the strong 200 nm absorption.
reference_short: Arenas, Lopez-Tocon, Otero & Soto, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2002, 124, 1728
notes: The 0-0 transition wavelengths in Table 2 are reported both with and without ZPE correction; footnotes specify that TS and CI energies are relative to ground-state A1 diazirine. A valley-ridge inflection (bifurcation) point must exist along the minimum energy path between the two S1 saddle points, as shown mathematically by Castano et al.; it was located by computing analytical frequencies at each interpolation step and projecting seven zero-frequency directions (the energy gradient plus six translations and rotations) out of the Hessian. In the trajectory method the electrons are treated quantum mechanically and the nuclei classically, with no precomputed surface and no geometric restriction; after a surface hop the energy difference between the two electronic states is redistributed along the momentum parallel to the nonadiabatic coupling vector, so only trajectories orthogonal to the crossing seam and with sufficient velocity produce an effective hop.

software: Gaussian 98 revision A.7 (CASSCF optimizations, MEPs, analytical frequencies, conical intersection optimizations); MOLCAS 6.0 (CASPT2)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(8,8): the four pi-type orbitals of the two double bonds (two occupied and the two lowest unoccupied), plus four sigma-type orbitals of the central cyclobutane ring — its two highest occupied and two lowest unoccupied, chosen so that all four ring carbon atoms contribute equally. Equivalently 4e/4MO for the two double bonds and 4e/4MO for the ring. A CASSCF(6,6) containing only the pi-type orbitals was used for the CASPT2 numerical-gradient reoptimization of the biradical, and single points with up to 12 electrons in 12 orbitals were run as a test.
active_space_protocol: The sigma orbitals are in the space for a specific spectroscopic reason, argued from experiment before any calculation: hyperconjugation through the strained cyclobutane ring couples the two double bonds, pulling the S1 absorption to 300 nm from the 250 nm expected for two non-interacting double bonds, so 'the sigma molecular orbitals of the central cyclobutane ring must be enclosed in the active space'. Symmetry is respected in the selection — the sigma orbitals are taken with equal contribution from all four ring carbons. The choice is then tested from above: single points including up to 12 electrons in 12 orbitals, adding the remaining ring sigma electrons, found 'no significant contributions of the new configurations respect to using the 8MO,8e scheme, which validates the selection of the 8MO,8e active space'. Intruder states were policed explicitly — CASPT2 eigenvalues were examined to eliminate their contributions, and the reference weight exceeds 0.74 at every point in Table 1. State-averaged MEPs were used where conical intersections are the end point.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1; state-averaged where the MEP terminates at a conical intersection)
electronic_structure_description: The CASPT2 S0 to S1 excitation energy is 272 nm; zero-point correction stabilizes S1 by about 9 kcal/mol, giving 298 nm against an experimental 300 nm. Oscillator strength for the Franck-Condon S0 to S1 transition is 0.0851. At the Franck-Condon point the S1 Hessian has FIVE negative eigenvalues — -844, -761, -593 (twofold) and -322 cm-1, of D2, C2, Cs (twofold) and D2 symmetry — all with eigenvectors orthogonal to the gradient, so relaxation can proceed along a combination of five directions. MEPs started with a 0.03 amu^1/2 bohr distortion along each of these are almost coincident and converge on a common tetraradicaloid bifurcation point BP1 where both C3=C4 and C7=C8 have stretched to 1.5 A, a single-bond length, accompanied by expansion of the cyclobutane sigma bonds that stabilizes the system by through-bond coupling of the radical centres. Relative CASSCF energies in kcal/mol with CASPT2 in parentheses, referred to the S0 equilibrium geometry: TOD (D2d) S1 156.63 (105.26), and with ZPE 147.29 (95.92); BR (Cs) S0 -14.85 (1.08) and S1 51.53 (68.32); CI1 (D2) 55.08/57.04 (62.28/64.38); CI2 (C2) 41.50/42.06 (53.13/50.81); CI3 (C1) 45.62/45.98 (50.36/52.00); CI4 (Cs) 53.59/53.63 (60.74/61.68); CI5 (C1) 57.55/57.66 (60.21/64.59); CIM (C2) 39.71/39.90 (53.69/50.33); CIA (C2v) 11.61/16.83 (37.29/29.92). The activation energy out of BR is corrected to about 6 kcal/mol at CASPT2//CASSCF(8,8).
Other: Two lessons, one about how the space was chosen and one about how it was tested. The space is not built from a generic valence rule but from a spectroscopic anomaly: two isolated double bonds should absorb near 250 nm and TOD absorbs near 300 nm, and that 50 nm shift is hyperconjugation through the strained cyclobutane ring — so four ring sigma orbitals go into the space alongside the four pi orbitals. Leave them out and the coupling that defines the chromophore is gone. The test is the useful part for reuse: single points with up to 12 electrons in 12 orbitals, adding the rest of the ring sigma manifold, produced no significant new configurations, so the (8,8) is converged with respect to the obvious enlargement — a check most papers assert rather than perform. Two cautions remain. First, the BR reoptimization at CASPT2 used a SMALLER CASSCF(6,6) reference containing only pi orbitals, i.e. dropping precisely the sigma orbitals argued to be essential, so the conclusion that BR remains an S1 minimum at CASPT2 rests on a space the paper's own reasoning would reject for the Franck-Condon region; it is defensible only because BR is a biradical where the ring bonds have already expanded. Second, the reference weight floor is only 0.74, low enough that some points in Table 1 are noticeably more contaminated than others, and CASSCF-to-CASPT2 shifts are enormous and non-uniform — 156.63 to 105.26 kcal/mol at the Franck-Condon S1 but 11.61 to 37.29 at CIA, moving in OPPOSITE directions — so CASSCF relative energies cannot be used on their own anywhere on this surface.
reference_short: Frutos, Sancho, Garavelli, Olivucci & Castano, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 2830
notes: Establishes two properties of TOD photochemistry: simple low-lying intersection space domains can mediate different photoproducts, and TOD is probably mediated by TWO DISCONNECTED intersection space domains on different timescales — the first leading to cyclooctatetraene by barrierless pericyclic reactions, the second to semibulvalene through an excited-state biradical intermediate. Claimed as the first computationally documented case in single-molecule photochemistry where distinct low-lying intersection spaces play different chemical roles. Bifurcation points were located by diagonalizing the projected Hessian along the S1 MEP and identifying points with eigenvalues nearest zero. Ground-state relaxation after each funnel was explored from twenty initial relaxation directions equally spaced in the branching space. The intersection-space surface was obtained by fitting 1369 optimized points to a polynomial. Photoproducts are rationalized through branching space diagrams built from the derivative coupling and gradient difference vectors of each conical intersection.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/6-31G(d) single points at the CASSCF(8,8) geometries, with eigenvalues examined to remove intruder-state contributions (reference weight above 0.74 throughout); one CASPT2 numerical-gradient optimization over a CASSCF(6,6) pi-only reference

point_group: Cs-like and C2-symmetric conformers of the 1DR and 1DZ diradical species; C1 for the linear-axial conical intersection
geometry_source: CASSCF(12,10)/6-31G* unconstrained and constrained geometry optimizations; the ground-state relaxation coordinate from the linear-axial conical intersection obtained by determining the initial relaxation direction. Because the 1DZ potential energy surface is flat, transition structures could not be located by unconstrained optimization — the denitrogenation path (C1-N2 bond breaking) and the Cs-like to C2 conformational change (radical-centre inversion) were mapped by constrained optimization with the C-N bond length and the C-H inversion angle held fixed.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — single-point CASPT2 along the CASSCF reaction coordinate; classical trajectory computations on a DFT force field; a CASPT2 numerical-gradient constrained optimization (CASPT2-Opt) on a model system as a validation
software: GAUSSIAN 98 revision A.7 (CASSCF); MOLCAS-4 (CASPT2); GAUSSIAN 03 (DFT trajectories)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,10): the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the two DBH C-N bonds, the sigma, sigma*, pi and pi* orbitals of the N=N bond, and the two nitrogen lone pair (n) orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A bond-inventory space covering every orbital involved in extruding N2: both C-N sigma/sigma* pairs that break, the full N=N sigma/sigma*/pi/pi* set that becomes the N2 triple bond, and both nitrogen lone pairs. The same space is used for the entire reaction coordinate, since which C-N bond breaks first is exactly what the study is trying to resolve. CASPT2 is applied as single points along the CASSCF path rather than by reoptimization, because 'CASPT2 geometry optimization ... is still not practical for systems as large as DBH'; the approximation is validated on a smaller stand-in, the methyl diazenyl radical, where a full CASPT2 constrained optimization with numerical gradients gives transition structures and barriers similar to those from the CASSCF coordinate. The scheme is separately calibrated against experiment on two related azoalkanes.
electronic_structure_description: The primary photoproduct is an exo-axial conformer of the diazenyl diradical 1DZ, carrying a cyclopenta-1,3-diyl moiety with a Cs-like structure, generated selectively by decay at a linear-axial conical intersection. It sits in a shallow ground-state region giving access to five different reaction pathways, all located within 0.0-4.0 kcal/mol. Along the exo-axial 1DZ denitrogenation path, CASSCF places the energy maximum at a C1-N2 length of 1.59 A with effectively NO barrier, while CASPT2 gives 1.55 A and a barrier of 3.6 kcal/mol (1.6 kcal/mol after ZPE). Other computed barriers include 2.7 kcal/mol (2.3 after ZPE) and 2.2 kcal/mol. The intermediate dissipates roughly 50 kcal/mol.
Other: The single most important finding for anyone reusing a CASSCF surface of this kind: at the CASSCF level the denitrogenation of the exo-axial diazenyl diradical is EFFECTIVELY BARRIERLESS, and adding dynamic correlation creates a real barrier of 3.6 kcal/mol while moving the transition structure from a C1-N2 length of 1.59 to 1.55 A. On a surface whose five competing pathways all lie within 0.0-4.0 kcal/mol of each other, a spurious absence of a barrier is not a quantitative error but a change of mechanism — the whole stereoselectivity argument depends on barriers of this size. The authors could not fix it the obvious way, since CASPT2 optimization is impractical at this size, so they validated the CASPT2//CASSCF shortcut on a smaller model, the methyl diazenyl radical, where a genuine CASPT2 constrained optimization with numerical gradients reproduces the same transition structures and barriers. That is the right control, and it is worth noting it tests the GEOMETRY approximation, not the active space. External calibration is also given: the same strategy predicts 7.6 and 11.4 kcal/mol for alpha C-N cleavage in singlet-excited pyrazoline and diazabicyclo[2.2.2]octene against experimental ranges of 6-9 and 8.6-10.2 kcal/mol. A further practical warning is that the flatness of the 1DZ surface defeats unconstrained optimization entirely — constrained scans in the C-N length and the C-H inversion angle were required, so the reported transition structures are constrained ones.
reference_short: Sinicropi, Page, Adam & Olivucci, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2003, 125, 10947
notes: Explains the inversion stereoselectivity of housane formation. Reaction path analysis with classical trajectories indicates that inverted housane can only be produced by IMPULSIVE population of an axial-to-equatorial pathway, which is inconsistent with thermal equilibration of the primary 1DZ conformer; loss of inversion selectivity, and the retention (stereochemical memory) seen for suitably substituted DBHs, follow from dynamics in which the axial-to-equatorial impulsive motion is restrained by substituent inertia or steric hindrance. Two trajectories were released from the same point, one without initial velocity and one with a velocity proportional to the energy; both used a DFT force field. Energy profiles for the diazenyl denitrogenation are compared across CASSCF, CASPT2 and triplet DFT in Figure 3.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points along the CASSCF(12,10)/6-31G* reaction coordinate (the CASPT2//CASSCF scheme), validated against a full CASPT2 numerical-gradient constrained optimization on the methyl diazenyl radical model

compound_name: Model 4' — five-coordinate V(III) tristhiolato complex, simplified model of [V(PS3')(1-Me-Im)]
ligand_set: PS3-type tristhiolatophosphine (trianion of tris(2-thiophenyl)phosphine) plus one N-donor; simplified model of complex 4, [V(PS3')(1-Me-Im)]
geometry_source: Complete geometry optimization at BP86/TZV(P), in fairly good agreement with the available X-ray structures especially for the V-P and V-S bond distances; constrained models (geometry held at the crystallographic values) were also treated and gave slightly better results, so the discussion is based on those
method: State-averaged CASSCF with quasi-degenerate perturbation theory — the Born-Oppenheimer and spin-orbit coupling operators are diagonalized simultaneously in the basis of the SA-CASSCF roots — plus spin-spin coupling from the McWeeny-Mizuno equation applied to the multiconfigurational wavefunction; SORCI (spectroscopy-oriented CI) on top of the CASSCF reference for one case; BP86 DFT for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(2,5): the two d electrons of V(III) in the five vanadium 3d-based molecular orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Described as 'the smallest reasonable active space' — the minimal d-only space that can carry the full multiplet structure of a d2 ion. Orbitals were determined by averaging over ALL the states the configuration can produce: 10 triplet and 15 singlet roots, i.e. the complete d2 multiplet manifold, so no state is preferentially optimized. Those roots then enter an infinite-order spin-orbit treatment by quasi-degenerate perturbation theory, which the authors describe as 'an ab initio realization of a complete ligand-field theory that also takes care of differential orbital covalency'. The stated limitation is equally explicit: 'CASSCF is not a highly accurate method if metal-ligand bonds become considerably covalent' — a real concern with thiolate donors — and where it failed, SORCI on top of the same CAS(2,5) reference was used, with thresholds Tpre, Tnat and Tsel of 1e-5, 1e-5 and 1e-6 Eh.
nroots_per_mult: 10 triplet and 15 singlet roots (the full d2 multiplet manifold), all included in the spin-orbit treatment
electronic_structure_description: Trigonal bipyramidal C3v geometry gives a 3A2 ground state with dxz and dyz as the SOMOs. The important d-d single excitations are 1e(dxz,yz) to the unoccupied degenerate 2e(dx2-y2,xy) set, which with two possible spin couplings for two unpaired electrons in four orbitals produces three triplet excited states 3A1, 3A2 and 3E and three singlets 1A1, 1A2 and 1E; excitation from 1e to 1a1(dz2) gives a further set. Zero-field splitting parameters in cm-1, calculated (constrained model in parentheses) against Dexp = 1.80 and Eexp = 0.047: at CASSCF Dcal 3.5 (2.0), Ecal 0 (0), DSOC 2.5 (1.2), DSSC 1.0 (0.8). BP86 DFT gives Dcal 0.39 (0.37) with DSOC -0.24 (-0.23) and DSSC 0.63 (0.61). Individual state contributions to DSOC for the constrained model: 1A1(1e to 1e) at 19560 cm-1 contributing 1.4, 3E(1e to 2e) at 11160 cm-1 contributing 1.0, 1E(1e to 2e) at 20090 cm-1 contributing 0.6, 3E(1e to 1a1) at 27090 cm-1 contributing 0.6 and 1E(1e to 1a1) at 33820 cm-1 contributing 0.5, totalling 1.9 cm-1, with covalency reduction factors of about 0.79, 0.69 and 0.66.
Other: A minimal d-only CAS(2,5) and DFT disagree about the PHYSICS, not merely the numbers. The CASSCF spin-orbit contribution to the zero-field splitting is far larger than the DFT one and comes out with the OPPOSITE SIGN — DSOC of 2.5 (1.2 constrained) at CASSCF against -0.24 (-0.23) at BP86 — so at the multiconfigurational level SOC dominates the zfs whereas DFT makes spin-spin coupling dominant. Since the two effects are 'multiple, often counteracting' and the total |D| is only about 1 cm-1, this sign reversal decides the answer. The CAS(2,5) is honest about being the floor rather than a converged choice: it is 'the smallest reasonable active space', and its known weakness is exactly the one this chemistry stresses, since 'CASSCF is not a highly accurate method if metal-ligand bonds become considerably covalent' and the donors here are thiolates. The covalency is real and measurable in the reduction factors of 0.66-0.79 quoted for this model. What partly rescues the small space is the state averaging: all 10 triplet and 15 singlet roots of the d2 configuration are computed and fed into an infinite-order SOC treatment, so the multiplet structure is complete even though the orbital space is minimal — effectively an ab initio ligand-field calculation that still carries differential orbital covalency. Even so, CASSCF overshoots D by roughly a factor of two on the fully optimized geometry (3.5 against an experimental 1.80), improving to 2.0 on the constrained one, which is why the constrained models were preferred throughout.
reference_short: Ye, Neese, Ozarowski, Smirnov, Krzystek, Telser, Liao, Hung, Chu, Tsai, Wang, Chen & Hsu, Inorg. Chem. 2010, 49, 977
notes: Part of a family of V(III) complexes with the PS3 ligand (trianion of tris(2-thiophenyl)phosphine and its phenyl-substituted derivatives) of coordination number 5, 6 and 7, relevant as functional models of vanadium nitrogenase — the parent system reduces N2H4 to ammonia. Spin Hamiltonian parameters come from high-frequency and high-field EPR at 40 K supported by DC magnetic susceptibility. The V(III) ion, 3d2, is a non-Kramers system with S = 1. The precise atom-by-atom composition of model 4' is not spelled out in the text (unlike 7''), so no formula is recorded.
correlation_correction: None for the CASSCF results; SORCI (multireference CI with perturbative treatment of weak perturbers) applied on top of the CAS(2,5) reference for the seven-coordinate model 7''

compound_name: Model 6' — six-coordinate V(III) tristhiolato complex, simplified model of [V(PS3')(2,2'-bpy)]
ligand_set: N2PS3 donor set: PS3-type tristhiolatophosphine plus a bidentate 2,2'-bipyridine; simplified model of complex 6, [V(PS3')(2,2'-bpy)]
point_group: Distorted octahedral; effective C4v symmetry used to label the excited states

electronic_structure_description: The N2PS3 coordination sphere is distorted octahedral with three thiolates in the equatorial plane, which destabilizes the pi-antibonding dxy-based MO relative to the other two t2g orbitals. The SOMOs are therefore dxz and dyz, giving an orbitally NONDEGENERATE 3A2 ground state, so the spin-Hamiltonian formalism applies. Zero-field splitting parameters in cm-1, calculated (constrained model in parentheses) against Dexp = 1.70 and Eexp = 0.075: at CASSCF Dcal 3.9 (3.4), Ecal 0.8 (0.3), DSOC 2.5 (2.7), ESOC 0.4 (0.3), DSSC 1.6 (0.7), ESSC 0.4 (0). BP86 DFT gives Dcal 1.85 (0.33) with DSOC -0.15 (0) and DSSC 2.00 (0.33). The qualitative ligand-field analysis reproduces the CASSCF DSOC well: 2.4 against 2.7 cm-1 for the constrained model.
Other: Same minimal CAS(2,5), same sign reversal against DFT in the spin-orbit term — DSOC of 2.5 (2.7 constrained) at CASSCF versus -0.15 (0) at BP86 — confirming that the disagreement is systematic across coordination numbers rather than a quirk of one geometry. The useful positive result here is that the CASSCF spin-orbit contribution is reproduced almost exactly by a hand ligand-field analysis summing individual excited-state contributions (2.4 against 2.7 cm-1), which is a strong internal check that the d-only space is doing precisely what a d-only space should and nothing more. Its shortfall is correspondingly precise: CASSCF places Dcal at 3.9 (3.4) against an experimental 1.70, roughly double, and gives a non-zero E of 0.8 where the experiment finds 0.075. The overshoot is the same direction and magnitude as for the five-coordinate model, so with this space and this system a factor-of-two overestimate of D should be expected rather than diagnosed as a geometry problem. Note that the constrained (crystallographic-geometry) models consistently give better agreement than the fully optimized ones, and were adopted for the analysis on that basis.

notes: Complex 6 is [V(PS3')(2,2'-bpy)]; the bidentate bipyridine contributes two nitrogen donors, giving coordination number 6. As with 4', the atom-level composition of the simplified model 6' is not stated in the text.

electronic_structure_description: Zero-field splitting parameters in cm-1 against Dexp = 0.96 and Eexp = 0.19, with constrained-model values in parentheses. For model 7' at CASSCF: Dcal -1.0 (-0.5), Ecal 0.1 (0), DSOC -0.7 (-0.4), DSSC -0.4 (-0.1). For the further-simplified 7'' at CASSCF: Dcal -0.7 (-0.4), DSOC -0.5 (-0.3), DSSC -0.2 (-0.1). For 7'' at SORCI: Dcal 1.2 (1.1), DSOC -0.2 (0.1), DSSC 1.4 (1.0). BP86 DFT on 7' gives Dcal 0.23 (1.22) with DSOC 0.02 (0.35) and DSSC 0.21 (0.87). Relative to the five- and six-coordinate complexes the spin-orbit contribution is much reduced here, so the spin-spin term decides the sign of D.
Other: The clearest failure and repair of a minimal active space in the paper. CAS(2,5) gets the SIGN of D wrong for the seven-coordinate complex — -1.0 (or -0.7 for 7'') against an experimental +0.96 — and the reason is diagnosable: unlike the five- and six-coordinate cases where SOC dominates, here the SOC contribution collapses and the SPIN-SPIN term sets the sign, and it is the SSC contribution whose sign CASSCF gets backwards (-0.4/-0.2 at CASSCF against +1.4 at SORCI). Running SORCI on top of the SAME CAS(2,5) reference space fixes it completely, giving Dcal = 1.2 in excellent agreement with 0.96. So the error was not a missing orbital but missing dynamic correlation on top of an adequate reference — enlarging the d-only space would not have helped, and the multireference CI on the same reference did. The practical rule this supports: a minimal d-only CAS is serviceable while SOC dominates the zfs, and becomes unreliable exactly where the smaller SSC term takes over, because SSC is computed from the spin density and is far more sensitive to correlation than the SOC sum-over-states is. The model had to be truncated further to V(NH3)3(PH3)(SH)3 to make SORCI affordable, so the successful calculation and the failing one are not on quite the same structure, though 7' and 7'' agree closely at CASSCF.

Model 7' is the simplified version of it, and 7'' the further approximation V(NH3)3(PH3)(SH)3 in C3 symmetry adopted to make the SORCI calculation tractable. compound_name: Diels-Alder reaction of butadiene with ethylene (system I) — concerted and stepwise transition states
point_group: Cs for the concerted transition state; anti and gauche-out conformers of the nonconcerted transition state and the diradical intermediate
geometry_source: Stationary points for the concerted transition state (CTS), the anti and gauche-out nonconcerted transition states (NTS), the diradical intermediate (DI) and cyclohexene; relative energies include zero-point corrections
method: CASSCF and UNO CASCI (CAS configuration interaction over unrestricted natural orbitals), with MRMP2 and CASMP2(CI) dynamic correlation corrections; compared against broken-symmetry HF, MP2, QCISD(T), CCSD(T), BLYP, B2LYP and B3LYP with approximate spin projection; natural orbital occupation numbers used to define five chemical indices — spin density Q, unpaired electron density U, effective bond order b, information entropy I and diradical character y
software: GAMESS (CASSCF, MRMP2, UNO CASCI, CASMP2(CI)); Gaussian 94 revision E.3 (broken-symmetry HF, DFT and post-HF)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS{6,6} — six pi electrons in six pi natural orbitals — for the parent butadiene plus ethylene system. The paper's natural-orbital analysis determines the required space for the phenyl-substituted systems as well: {12,12} for 1-phenylbutadiene with ethylene and for butadiene with styrene, and {18,18} — eighteen pi electrons in eighteen pi natural orbitals — for 1-phenylbutadiene with styrene. Under UB3LYP, selecting only LUMOs with occupation at or above 0.005 reduces the space to {4,4} even for the anti nonconcerted transition state.
active_space_protocol: The active space is DIAGNOSED rather than assumed: unrestricted natural orbital occupation numbers from a broken-symmetry solution are inspected, and the orbitals with fractional occupation define the CAS that a symmetry-adapted calculation would need. That procedure is validated on the parent system, where UNO CASCI{6,6} and CASSCF{6,6} agree closely — 'the UNOs are not so different from NOs of CASSCF' — licensing its use on the substituted systems where CASSCF is out of reach. An occupation threshold of 0.005 on the LUMOs is used as the selection criterion under UB3LYP.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol including zero-point corrections, as UNO CASCI (CASSCF in parentheses) then CASMP2(CI) (MRMP2 in parentheses), against reactants at 0.0: concerted transition state 40.5 (45.1) then 19.8 (22.4), experiment 27.5 plus or minus 2; anti nonconcerted transition state 42.0 (46.6) then 26.0 (28.6); gauche-out nonconcerted transition state 43.0 (47.7) then 27.5 (30.1); diradical intermediate 40.5 (41.3) then 27.1 (27.0); cyclohexene -5.6 (-0.9) then -41.1 (-38.7), experiment -38.4. The concerted transition state is more stable than the nonconcerted ones by 1.5-2.5 kcal/mol and the diradical intermediate by 0.5-6.4 kcal/mol, consistent with CCSD(T). For the substituted systems, the HONO and LUNO of 1-phenylbutadiene plus ethylene are delocalized over the phenyl ring of the diene, those of butadiene plus styrene over the styrene phenyl ring, and those of the doubly substituted system over BOTH phenyl groups, giving synergic diradical stabilization — the reason the anti nonconcerted transition state becomes favourable in the latter two.

compound_name: Methoxy radical (CH3O) — Jahn-Teller coupling constants of the ground state
point_group: C3v at the symmetric point (a conical intersection); Cs at the distorted minimum (2A') and maximum (2A')
geometry_source: CASSCF(5,6)/6-31G* conical intersection optimization for the symmetric point X0; CASSCF geometry optimizations for the Jahn-Teller minimum Xmin, started near X0; the maximum Xmax sought by restarting from Xmin with the electronic state symmetry swapped (2A' minimum, 2A'' maximum in Cs). Each stationary point verified by a vibrational frequency calculation. Generalized restricted Hartree-Fock (GRHF) and ROHF geometries and frequencies from CADPAC with the same basis.
method: CASSCF, with the symmetric configuration located as a genuine conical intersection so that the Jahn-Teller stabilization energy follows from energies computed in one consistent active space; GRHF and ROHF for vibrational frequencies and normal modes; UHF, UMP2 and B3LYP for comparison at the distorted geometry
software: Gaussian 94 (CASSCF, UHF, UMP2, B3LYP); CADPAC (GRHF and ROHF, which has analytical second derivatives)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(5,6). The valence structure of the CX3Y radicals is [C-X sigma bonds][X lone pairs](1a1)2(2a1)2(1e)3(3a1)0[virtuals], where 1a1 is nominally the Y ns sigma lone pair, 2a1 the C-Y sigma bond, 1e the pair of Y np pi lone pairs and 3a1 the C-Y sigma* orbital. The active space comprises 2a1, 1e, 3a1 and one virtual orbital approximating the (n+1)p pi orbital of Y.
active_space_protocol: The space is built around the singly occupied degenerate 1e pair that causes the Jahn-Teller distortion, together with the C-Y sigma/sigma* pair that the distortion modulates, plus one correlating (n+1)p pi virtual. The methodological requirement is that THE SAME active space be used at the symmetric point, the minimum and the maximum, since only then does the difference of total energies give a meaningful Jahn-Teller stabilization energy — the paper makes this explicit as the basis of its algorithm, and the conical-intersection formulation is what makes the symmetric point's total energy meaningful in the first place. Space size and basis were both stress-tested on CH3O with smaller and larger active spaces and a 6-31G** basis: 'the predictions of the Jahn-Teller coupling constants were not significantly affected by the change in active space or basis set.'
nroots_per_mult: 2 degenerate components at the conical intersection
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF conical-intersection geometry against experiment: r(C-O) 1.426 A (experiment 1.37), r(C-X) 1.085 A (1.10), angle(Y-C-X) 109.4 degrees (110), angle(X-C-X) 109.6 degrees (109). Vibrational frequencies calculated then experimental, in cm-1: 2822, 1359/1422, 1051/1040, 2835/2891, 1417/1434, 1065/1082. Linear Jahn-Teller coupling constants (dimensionless) experimental then calculated: D4 0.02 then below 0.01, D5 0.075 then 0.02, D6 0.24 then 0.20. Linear stabilization energies in cm-1: 57 then 2 for mode 4, 106 then 33 for mode 5, 256 then 221 for mode 6; quadratic 2, 33 and 36 then 20; total 458 then 256. The Table 5 spin-orbit row lists only four values (-140, -145, -340, -360) across eight expt/calc columns; the first pair is most naturally read as CH3O but the mapping is not stated, so it is recorded here with that caveat. Jahn-Teller rotational corrections h1(JT) = 6e-4 and h2(JT) = 3.0e-2 cm-1 against experimental 3.38(3)e-4 and 7.81(2)e-2. Mode 6, nominally the methyl rocking motion or equivalently tilting of the O atom off the C3 axis, is the most Jahn-Teller active by both experiment and calculation. Largest geometric changes on distortion are in the bond ANGLES, so the angle-bending modes are expected to be the most Jahn-Teller active.
Other: CH3O is the one radical the authors used to test the space itself, and the test is the most useful result in the paper for active-space purposes: smaller AND larger active spaces than (5,6), plus a 6-31G** basis, left the Jahn-Teller coupling constants essentially unchanged. So the minimal space capturing the degenerate 1e pair, the C-Y sigma/sigma* pair and one correlating virtual is converged for this property — Jahn-Teller coupling constants are geometric derivatives of a degeneracy, far less sensitive to correlation than absolute energies are. The agreement bears this out where it matters: D6 = 0.20 calculated against 0.24 experimental, which the authors call 'probably better than could have been expected'. But the same space performs badly on the SMALL couplings, D5 at 0.02 against 0.075 and D4 below 0.01 against 0.02, and the total stabilization energy comes out 256 cm-1 against 458 — a factor of nearly two, driven almost entirely by the underestimated weak modes. The lesson is that the space is adequate for the dominant coupling and unreliable for minor ones, and the authors respond by omitting quadratic constants from their spectral simulations. The universal failure is worth stating once and applying to all four radicals: AT THE CASSCF LEVEL NO MAXIMUM ON THE MOAT COULD BE LOCATED FOR ANY of them, so the quadratic Jahn-Teller stabilization energies do not come from the active space at all — they were computed from the imaginary ROHF normal mode and the ROHF minimum-to-maximum energy difference. Linear parameters therefore rest on CASSCF and quadratic ones on ROHF, and the two should not be quoted as though they share a level of theory. The paper also reports quadratic stabilization energies rather than quadratic coupling constants Ki precisely because any error in the small linear constants D4 and D5 propagates into Ki.

notes: The reference radical of the series and the only one with a complete experimental Jahn-Teller analysis. The valence structure of the CX3Y radicals is [C-X sigma bonds][X lone pairs](1a1)2(2a1)2(1e)3(3a1)0[virtuals], where 1a1 is nominally the Y ns sigma lone pair, 2a1 the C-Y sigma bond, 1e the pair of Y np pi lone pairs and 3a1 the C-Y sigma* orbital. The active space comprises 2a1, 1e, 3a1 and one virtual orbital approximating the (n+1)p pi orbital of Y.
active_space_protocol: The space is built around the singly occupied degenerate 1e pair that causes the Jahn-Teller distortion, together with the C-Y sigma/sigma* pair that the distortion modulates, plus one correlating (n+1)p pi virtual. The methodological requirement is that THE SAME active space be used at the symmetric point, the minimum and the maximum, since only then does the difference of total energies give a meaningful Jahn-Teller stabilization energy — the paper makes this explicit as the basis of its algorithm, and the conical-intersection formulation is what makes the symmetric point's total energy meaningful in the first place. Space size and basis were both stress-tested on CH3O with smaller and larger active spaces and a 6-31G** basis: 'the predictions of the Jahn-Teller coupling constants were not significantly affected by the change in active space or basis set.'
nroots_per_mult: 2 degenerate components at the conical intersection
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF conical-intersection geometry against experiment: r(C-S) 1.817 A (experiment 1.767), r(C-X) 1.082 A (1.10, fixed at the ab initio value), angle(Y-C-X) 109.9 degrees (experiment 115.8), angle(X-C-X) 109.0 degrees (experiment 102.5). Vibrational frequencies calculated then experimental, in cm-1: 2851/2776, 1330/1313, 689/717, 2932, 1422, 913 (the last fixed at the ab initio value). Linear coupling constants experimental then calculated: D4 below 0.01, D5 0.02, D6 0.045 experimental then 0.16 calculated. Linear stabilization energies in cm-1: 6 for mode 4, 22 for mode 5, 41 experimental then 144 calculated for mode 6; total 41 experimental then 171 calculated. Spin-orbit constant not tabulated for this radical in the comparison.
Other: The worst case in the series, and the one that exposes the limit of the (5,6) space. The calculated D6 of 0.16 is nearly four times the experimental 0.045, and the total stabilization energy of 171 cm-1 overshoots 41 cm-1 by a factor of four — the opposite direction to CH3O's underestimate, so the errors are not correctable by any uniform scaling. The geometry gives the reason directly: the CASSCF conical intersection has angle(Y-C-X) = 109.9 and angle(X-C-X) = 109.0 degrees, essentially tetrahedral, while experiment finds 115.8 and 102.5 — a discrepancy of six to seven degrees in exactly the bond angles that the paper identifies as changing most on Jahn-Teller distortion and therefore as controlling which modes are Jahn-Teller active. When the symmetric point itself is wrong in the relevant coordinate, the coupling constants derived from it inherit the error. The C-S bond is also 0.05 A too long. Sulfur, with its more diffuse 3p lone pairs, is evidently not described adequately by a space and basis calibrated on the oxygen radicals, and the (5,6)/6-31G* combination should not be transferred to second-row Y atoms without re-testing. The universal failure is worth stating once and applying to all four radicals: AT THE CASSCF LEVEL NO MAXIMUM ON THE MOAT COULD BE LOCATED FOR ANY of them, so the quadratic Jahn-Teller stabilization energies do not come from the active space at all — they were computed from the imaginary ROHF normal mode and the ROHF minimum-to-maximum energy difference. Linear parameters therefore rest on CASSCF and quadratic ones on ROHF, and the two should not be quoted as though they share a level of theory. The paper also reports quadratic stabilization energies rather than quadratic coupling constants Ki precisely because any error in the small linear constants D4 and D5 propagates into Ki.
reference_short: Barckholtz & Miller, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 2321
notes: Experimental values for r(C-X) and the mode 6 frequency were fixed at the ab initio values in the experimental analysis rather than independently determined, so those comparisons are not independent tests. Jahn-Teller rotational corrections h1(JT) = 3e-5 and h2(JT) = 1.3e-2 cm-1.
