compound_name: G-4H — graphite-like carbon nanoparticle model cluster with one dehydrogenated edge
geometry_source: B3LYP/def2-TZVP optimized structures (TurboMole), unrestricted Kohn-Sham throughout, with broken-symmetry singlet and triplet states obtained for selected systems by a spin-flip procedure starting from the density matrix of the most stable high-multiplicity state. CASSCF energies were evaluated at the cluster geometry optimized for the lowest-energy eigenstate of each target-multiplicity manifold, obtained WITHOUT state averaging.
method: CASSCF with the initial wavefunction taken from the DFT calculation; unrestricted B3LYP for comparison; spin density and spin contamination analysis
basis_set: def2-TZVP (Ahlrichs triple-zeta split valence plus polarization)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(8,8), eight electrons in eight orbitals, for this graphite-like cluster. Two different sets of starting orbitals were tried: ORCA model guess orbitals (superposition of predetermined spherical neutral-atom densities) for the DFT-optimized TRIPLET structure, and restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham orbitals from a single-point calculation on the DFT-optimized QUINTET structure. An exploratory CASSCF(4,4) was also run and rejected.
active_space_protocol: The space size was determined by an explicit failure test rather than by assumption. Exploratory CASSCF(4,4) calculations 'provide an inadequate description of the cluster spin states, compared to the larger active space CASSCF(8,8) calculations, essentially lifting their pseudodegeneracy and proving that the large (8,8) active space is indeed needed'. Since pseudodegeneracy of the spin states IS the half-metallic property under investigation, a space that destroys it destroys the phenomenon. Starting-orbital dependence was also checked: two independent initial orbital sets, from the DFT triplet and quintet structures, gave qualitatively the same result. Energies are computed without state averaging, at the geometry optimized for the lowest eigenstate of each target multiplicity.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, triplet, quintet, septet (nonet and undecet at the DFT level)
nroots_per_mult: Six singlet, six triplet and one quintet eigenstate per target multiplicity
electronic_structure_description: The CASSCF lowest-energy structure corresponds to a QUINTET state, exactly as DFT predicts. The quintet, lowest triplet, second triplet and first singlet states lie within 1 kcal/mol of one another, and the six lowest states within 2 kcal/mol — the pseudodegeneracy that constitutes half-metallicity. B3LYP/def2-TZVP relative energies in kcal/mol with the spin contamination given in parentheses: broken-symmetry singlet 1.0 (2.02), triplet 1.0 (1.03), quintet 0.0 (0.31), septet 16.9 (0.08). The cluster is a reduced version of the C96H18 hexagulene used in previous DFT work, comprising two rows of aromatic rings with one dehydrogenated edge, which supplies conformational rigidity and additional stabilization of the high-multiplicity states by deep delocalization. Spin density is localized on the unoccupied edge sites. G-4H has a simpler electronic structure than the amorphous models and a smaller standard deviation in its C-C bond lengths.
Other: The (4,4)-versus-(8,8) comparison here is a rare case where a too-small active space produces a QUALITATIVELY WRONG PHYSICAL CONCLUSION rather than an energy error: CASSCF(4,4) lifts the pseudodegeneracy of the spin states, which would make the cluster ordinary rather than half-metallic. Since half-metallicity is defined as the near-equal stability of several spin states, and the states here lie within 1-2 kcal/mol, the space must be large enough to hold every configuration that participates in that near-degeneracy — four orbitals cannot. The paper's broader conclusion inverts the usual reading of a DFT diagnostic. Spin contamination in the unrestricted Kohn-Sham solutions runs as high as 2.02 for the broken-symmetry singlet, which would normally be treated as an error; comparison against CASSCF shows the single-reference DFT nonetheless gives the correct electronic structure of antiferromagnetically coupled pairs, and that 'spin contamination ... does not corrupt the energetics of the half-metallic systems and therefore does not preclude the applicability of DFT to such systems'. Here the contamination is a faithful reflection of genuine multiconfigurational character rather than a symptom of failure. One further robustness result: repeating the CASSCF on DFT-optimized rather than CASSCF-appropriate geometries changes only the number of configurations contributing to each eigenstate, not the pseudodegeneracy, so the conclusion is 'fairly insensitive to the choice of optimized geometry employed'.
reference_short: Khavryuchenko, Khavryuchenko & Peslherbe, J. Phys. Chem. A 2014, 118, 7052
notes: G stands for graphite-like and the -4 denotes the number of H atoms abstracted from the edge. The half-metallic behaviour of these small models reproduces that of the larger clusters of the authors' previous work, which is the point of designing them — they make CASSCF benchmarking of the DFT predictions affordable. Spin density distributions were visualized with UCSF Chimera.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF energies only, with no perturbative correction applied

compound_name: A16H — amorphous-domain carbon nanoparticle model with three carbene centres linked by benzyne motifs
geometry_source: B3LYP/def2-TZVP optimized structures (TurboMole), unrestricted Kohn-Sham throughout, with broken-symmetry singlet and triplet states obtained for selected systems by a spin-flip procedure starting from the density matrix of the most stable high-multiplicity state. CASSCF energies were evaluated at the cluster geometry optimized for the lowest-energy eigenstate of each target-multiplicity manifold, obtained WITHOUT state averaging.
method: CASSCF with the initial wavefunction taken from the DFT calculation; unrestricted B3LYP for comparison; spin density and spin contamination analysis
basis_set: def2-TZVP (Ahlrichs triple-zeta split valence plus polarization)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(6,6), six electrons in six orbitals, used for the amorphous model clusters.
active_space_protocol: A smaller space than the graphite-like cluster's (8,8), matched to the three carbene spin centres of the amorphous models rather than to the delocalized edge states of the graphitic one. Energies are again computed without state averaging, at the geometry optimized for the lowest eigenstate of each target-multiplicity manifold, with the CASSCF initial wavefunction taken from DFT. The model itself is constructed to prescriptions established for the larger amorphous C92H18 cluster: an H/C atomic ratio near 0.2 as found experimentally for active carbon, two-coordinated carbene-type carbon sites that can be spin-active, and conjugation chains linking those spin sites.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, triplet, quintet, septet (nonet and undecet at the DFT level)
nroots_per_mult: Six singlet, six triplet, three quintet and one septet eigenstate per target multiplicity
electronic_structure_description: The CASSCF lowest-energy structure is a QUINTET, matching the DFT prediction, and the CASSCF calculations confirm the multiple pseudodegenerate spin states. B3LYP/def2-TZVP relative energies in kcal/mol with spin contamination in parentheses: broken-symmetry singlet 0.7 (2.09), triplet 0.0 (1.12), quintet 1.0 (0.05), septet 27.4 (0.03), nonet 62.3 (0.04), undecet 97.7 (0.05). The lowest-energy triplet eigenstate at the triplet-optimized geometry is built from a fair number of triplet configurations, some with high open-shell character (four SOMOs), while the NEXT triplet eigenstate, only 0.08 kcal/mol higher, is overwhelmingly dominated by a single open-shell configuration with four SOMOs at 57%. Quintet eigenstates generally involve fewer configurations with one highly dominant contribution. Eigenstates of multiplicity at or below the target one are multiconfigurational with the same orbital makeup and occupancy, differing only in magnetization. The cyclic carbene-containing clusters undergo Jahn-Teller distortion, worth 22-27 kcal/mol of additional stability, giving a larger standard deviation in C-C bond lengths than the graphite-like cluster.
Other: Two eigenstates 0.08 kcal/mol apart have completely different configurational structure — one spread over many triplet configurations, the next dominated by a single open-shell configuration at 57% — which is the sharpest available illustration of why the active space cannot be chosen by inspecting one state. Any space validated on the dominant-configuration eigenstate would be inadequate for its near-degenerate partner, and the two are indistinguishable energetically. A second point specific to this model: the (6,6) space here is SMALLER than the (8,8) shown to be necessary for the graphite-like cluster, and the (4,4) failure test that established the (8,8) requirement was performed only on G-4H. The paper does not repeat that test for the amorphous models, so the adequacy of (6,6) rests on the three-carbene-centre count rather than on a demonstration. Since these clusters also show Jahn-Teller distortion worth 22-27 kcal/mol — an effect absent from the graphite-like model — there is more electronic structure to describe here, not less. Set against that, the multiconfigurational character is genuine and matches what the DFT spin contamination (up to 2.09 for the broken-symmetry singlet) reports.
reference_short: Khavryuchenko, Khavryuchenko & Peslherbe, J. Phys. Chem. A 2014, 118, 7052
notes: A stands for amorphous and 16 for the number of H atoms. Built from the A6H moiety — a cyclic model of three carbene centres connected by three benzyne motifs — rigidly connected at the bottom by three aliphatic chains to a single central CH group. A6H alone could not be used: all its spin states up to the septet are pseudodegenerate, but on geometry relaxation every state below the septet collapses into a fullerene-like curved graphene bowl because oppositely polarized radicals on unsaturated carbons approach each other. That collapse is itself flagged as a possible mechanism for fullerene-like motif formation during carbonization of polymer precursors. Benzyne-type motifs (phenyl rings dehydrogenated on one side) were chosen because they provide spin conductivity, conformational rigidity and the lowest H/C ratio. A16H deviates from the target H/C ratio overall but retains the required dehydrogenation level in its upper three-site carbene cycle.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF energies only, with no perturbative correction applied

compound_name: A22H — amorphous-domain carbon nanoparticle model with carbene centres and fully hydrogen-saturated non-carbene carbons
geometry_source: B3LYP/def2-TZVP optimized structures (TurboMole), unrestricted Kohn-Sham throughout, with broken-symmetry singlet and triplet states obtained for selected systems by a spin-flip procedure starting from the density matrix of the most stable high-multiplicity state. CASSCF energies were evaluated at the cluster geometry optimized for the lowest-energy eigenstate of each target-multiplicity manifold, obtained WITHOUT state averaging.
method: CASSCF with the initial wavefunction taken from the DFT calculation; unrestricted B3LYP for comparison; spin density and spin contamination analysis
basis_set: def2-TZVP (Ahlrichs triple-zeta split valence plus polarization)
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(6,6), six electrons in six orbitals, the same space used for A16H.
active_space_protocol: Identical space and protocol to A16H — six electrons in six orbitals, no state averaging, initial wavefunction from DFT, energies at the geometry optimized for the lowest eigenstate of each target multiplicity — which is what makes the A16H versus A22H comparison meaningful: the two models differ only in how far the non-carbene carbons are hydrogenated, so any difference in their spin properties is chemical rather than methodological.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, triplet, quintet, septet (nonet and undecet at the DFT level)
nroots_per_mult: Six singlet, six triplet, three quintet and one septet eigenstate per target multiplicity
electronic_structure_description: B3LYP/def2-TZVP relative energies in kcal/mol with spin contamination in parentheses: broken-symmetry singlet 0.0 (1.15), triplet 1.8 (0.02), quintet 0.1 (0.04), septet 22.7 (0.03), nonet 105.7 (0.04), undecet 177.8 (0.07). CASSCF confirms the pseudodegeneracy of the low-lying spin states. Spin density in the quintet is distributed over the carbene carbons (Figure 2b). Like A16H, this cyclic carbene-containing cluster undergoes Jahn-Teller distortion. Its behaviour closely parallels A16H's.
Other: A22H is the control that isolates the effect of dehydrogenation, and it delivers a negative result with real consequences: it 'exhibits a similar behavior as A16H, and thus, benzyne links provide no enhancement or decrease of electronic delocalization in comparison to phenyl rings, suggesting that the high level of dehydrogenation observed in carbon materials is not so critical to their spin properties'. Because both models were run with the SAME (6,6) space, this conclusion is not confounded by an active-space change — the one methodological virtue that makes the comparison usable. The caveat carried over from A16H applies equally: the (4,4)-versus-(8,8) test that established how large the space must be to preserve pseudodegeneracy was done only on the graphite-like G-4H cluster, and a (6,6) is being used here for a system that additionally shows Jahn-Teller distortion. Since the entire finding rests on states separated by tenths of a kcal/mol, and the demonstrated failure mode of an undersized space is precisely to LIFT that degeneracy, the amorphous results would be more secure with the same failure test repeated. The DFT spin contamination pattern differs interestingly from A16H's: the broken-symmetry singlet is at 1.15 rather than 2.09 while the triplet drops to 0.02 from 1.12, so hydrogen saturation changes how the multiconfigurational character distributes across multiplicities even though it does not change the energetics.
reference_short: Khavryuchenko, Khavryuchenko & Peslherbe, J. Phys. Chem. A 2014, 118, 7052
notes: Constructed from the same cyclic carbene framework with all non-carbene carbon atoms saturated by hydrogens to the level of benzene, in order to reveal the properties of cyclic carbene-containing systems without benzyne links. Its DFT spin density distribution in the quintet state is shown in Figure 2b and suggests the spin resides on the carbene carbons.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF energies only, with no perturbative correction applied

compound_name: Thymine — conical intersections and radiationless decay of the lowest excited singlet states
point_group: Cs for the ground state (all atoms in the ring plane except two methyl hydrogens) and for the constrained excited-state optimizations; C1 for the reoptimized excited-state minima and for all three conical intersections
geometry_source: Ground state at MP2/cc-pVDZ. Excited-state minima of the lowest 1(pipi*) and 1(npi*) states optimized with CASSCF and with CC2 — first under a Cs constraint, which separates a''(pi) from a'(sigma/n) orbitals and splits the states into A' and A'' blocks, then reoptimized in C1 using the Cs structures as starting guesses. Conical intersections optimized at CASSCF/cc-pVDZ from initial guesses built by stretching and twisting the ring C-N bonds, following earlier DNA-base work.
method: CASSCF and state-averaged CASSCF with CASPT2 single points; CC2 (approximate coupled cluster singles and doubles) for geometries and energies; MP2 for the ground state; linearly interpolated internal coordinate (LIIC) reaction paths between excited-state minima and conical intersections
software: TURBOMOLE-5.7 (MP2 and CC2); GAMESS (CASSCF excited-state optimizations); MOLCAS-5 (CASSCF/CASPT2 single points); Gaussian 98 (conical intersection optimization)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ, ANO-L, def-SV(P) and TZVPP, compared systematically
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(12,10) for the excited-state minima and for all single-point energies along the reaction paths: eight pi plus two n valence orbitals. For locating the conical intersections the space was REDUCED to six electrons in six orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces for two jobs, with the reduction argued rather than assumed. The (12,10) pi-plus-lone-pair space covers both the 1(pipi*) and 1(npi*) manifolds on a common footing, and the LIIC path single points use state-averaged CASSCF with the six lowest electronic states carried at EQUAL weights so that state character is tracked continuously; continuity was verified independently by computing ground-to-excited transition dipole moments and by analyzing the configurational character of the CASSCF wavefunctions along each path. The 6-in-6 space used for the intersections is justified by prior results on DNA bases showing that 'the S0 and S1 wave functions at the S1-S0 conical intersections typically are of biradical character and are well represented by a rather compact active space' — biradicals need few orbitals. Enlarging the space with additional n orbitals was TRIED and reported as not helping (see Other).
nroots_per_mult: Six lowest electronic states in the state-averaged CASSCF energy functional with equal weights; five 1(pipi*) and five 1(npi*) states reported
electronic_structure_description: Ground state Cs with an MP2/cc-pVDZ dipole moment of 3.84 D. Vertical 1(pipi*) excitation energies in eV as CASSCF/cc-pVDZ, CASSCF/ANO-L, CASPT2/cc-pVDZ, CASPT2/ANO-L, CC2/def-SV(P), CC2/cc-pVDZ, CC2/TZVPP, against gas-phase absorption: state 1, 6.47, 6.16, 4.81, 4.68, 5.60, 5.52, 5.29 against 4.8; state 2, 7.24, 7.06, 5.99, 5.84, 6.70, 6.59, 6.39 against 5.7; state 3, 8.23, 7.87, 6.26, 6.06, 7.08, 7.03, 6.71 against 6.2; state 4, 9.19, 8.83, 7.08, 6.80, 7.99, 7.92, 7.56 against above 6.7; state 5, 9.35, 9.26, 7.99, 7.79, 8.37, 8.15, 7.70. The corresponding 1(npi*) values: state 1, 5.05, 4.95, 4.97, 5.02, 5.06, 5.00, 4.88; state 2, 6.62, 6.44, 6.51, 6.55, 6.47, 6.40, 6.25; state 3, 8.09, 8.01, 7.32, 7.29, 6.93, 6.85, 6.64; state 4, 8.28, 8.09, 7.05, 6.95, 7.34, 7.16, 6.74; state 5, 10.4, 10.3, 8.56, 8.44, 7.35, 7.30, 7.11. Three local minima of the S1-S0 intersection hypersurface were located, all with strongly out-of-plane distorted rings in which the H6 atom and the methyl group twist out of the ring plane. The lowest, CI1, is a crossing of the lowest 1(pipi*) state with S0, reached BARRIERLESSLY from the 1(pipi*) minimum, giving a direct fast quenching channel that explains the absence of sharp structure in the jet-cooled absorption spectrum. The other two involve the lowest 1(npi*) state crossing S0 and lie about 7.5 eV above the S0 minimum, so they are presumably irrelevant to decay of the lowest states but may matter at higher excess energy. A CASSCF-optimized excited-state geometry shows a slightly puckered C4C5C6 moiety with dihedrals of 5.32 and -156.6 degrees.
Other: The most useful active-space result here is a documented NON-fix. The authors' 1(npi*) excitation energies come out several tenths of an eV above those of Lorentzon et al., and they tried to close the gap by enlarging the active space with additional n orbitals and separately by adding diffuse functions — 'neither ... has led to a significant lowering of the 1(npi*) excitation energies'. The explanation is that the earlier work used a special procedure of putting diffuse functions in the basis and then DELETING the Rydberg-type orbitals from the active space, so the discrepancy comes from an orbital-deletion protocol that cannot be reproduced with standard spaces and bases. That is a warning about comparing CASPT2 numbers across papers: the space size alone does not define the calculation. On the raw performance of this space, bare CASSCF is unusable for the pipi* states — 6.47 eV against an experimental 4.8, an error of 1.67 eV that CASPT2 reduces to 0.01 eV — while for the npi* states CASSCF and CASPT2 agree within 0.1 eV, so the correlation demand is entirely concentrated in the pi manifold. The two methods also bracket experiment from opposite sides: CC2 energies are intrinsically too high and approach experiment from above as the basis improves, while CASPT2 pipi* energies fall BELOW experiment with large basis sets, so the frequently excellent CASPT2/small-basis agreement is partly cancellation. The compact 6-in-6 space used for the intersections rests on biradical character rather than on a convergence test, and the paper concludes that CC2 geometries with CASPT2 single points are a viable alternative to the whole CASSCF/CASPT2 protocol.
reference_short: Perun & Sobolewski, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 13238
notes: The 1(pipi*) excitation energies are markedly more basis-set dependent than the 1(npi*) ones — cc-pVDZ to ANO-L lowers CASSCF pipi* energies by about 0.3 eV and CASPT2 ones by about 0.2 eV, against roughly 0.1 eV and 0.05 eV for npi*. Higher transitions of either character are more basis-sensitive than the low-lying ones, reflecting their increasingly ionic character and the onset of valence-Rydberg mixing. The present CASPT2 pipi* results agree well with the earlier CASPT2 data of Lorentzon et al.; only the npi* states disagree. Cartesian coordinates of all optimized structures are in the Supporting Information; conical intersection geometries are shown in Figure 3.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF reference with cc-pVDZ and ANO-L; CC2 used as an independent correlated method rather than as a correction

compound_name: Dimethyldihydropyrene / cyclophanediene (DHP/CPD) — photochromic ring-opening and ring-closure
point_group: C2h imposed for all (16,16) geometry optimizations, the symmetry of both DHP and CPD ground-state structures; lower symmetry accessible only in the reduced (12,12) space
geometry_source: CASSCF(16,16)/cc-pVDZ energy minimizations under a C2h constraint; conical intersections and lower-symmetry structures optimized in the reduced (12,12) space; single points at linearly interpolated structures between stationary points to approximate the excited-state reaction paths
method: CASSCF for geometries and paths, CASPT2 single points on CASSCF(12,12) reference wavefunctions, and MRPT2 with the full (16,16) reference as a benchmark
software: MOLPRO and Gaussian (development version, revision B.07)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ, with aug-cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ used to check basis set effects and found to give small changes
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(16,16): sixteen pi electrons in sixteen pi orbitals, generating about 8.7 million electron configurations in C2h symmetry. A reduced CAS(12,12) was used for lower-symmetry work, for conical intersection optimization, for transition moments, and as the CASPT2 reference.
active_space_protocol: The space is the full pi system, and its size dictates everything else about the study. At (16,16) the configuration count reaches 8.7 million even in C2h, so 'the C2h symmetry had to be imposed at this level of calculation as reducing the symmetry would lead to an unworkable number of electron configurations' — only configurations of a given irreducible representation are generated per state. Anything requiring lower symmetry, conical intersections in particular, had to drop to (12,12). The CASPT2 reference is likewise (12,12), chosen 'to avoid the problem with the bottleneck of the CASPT2 method due to the large number of active orbitals', and its adequacy was then checked by benchmark MRPT2 calculations using the FULL (16,16) space as reference. A level shift of 0.4 hartree, in the Roos and Andersson form, was applied in all calculations to avoid intruder states in the excited-state manifold. CASPT2 geometry optimization was impossible for a system this size since no analytical gradients were available.
nroots_per_mult: 5 (ground state plus the first four singlet excited states)
electronic_structure_description: Two ground-state minima, DHP-GS and CPD-GS. In the DHP minimum the transannular bond is fully formed and the remaining 14 pi electrons delocalize over an almost planar (dihedral 177 degrees) [14]annulene outer ring. DHP lies 11.4 kcal/mol below CPD at CASSCF and 30.2 at CASPT2, bracketing DFT values of 23.2 and 20.6. The ground-state barrier connecting them is 44 (CASSCF) and 52 (CASPT2) kcal/mol against a DFT activation enthalpy of 43.5; the ring-CLOSURE barrier falls from 32.5 at CASSCF to 21.9 at CASPT2, against 20.3 from DFT and 22.4 experimentally. Four excited states, all intertwined with numerous surface crossings along the reaction coordinate (a dihedral measuring planarity), and all well separated from the ground state. LE state: vertical excitation 42.7 (CASPT2) / 40.9 (CASSCF) kcal/mol, with a closed-ring minimum DHP-LE almost at the Franck-Condon geometry so that vertical emission at 41.6 / 39.6 kcal/mol nearly coincides with absorption; a shallow CPD-LE minimum lies 70 kcal/mol above DHP-LE with a 1.4 kcal/mol ring-closure barrier at CASSCF that VANISHES at CASPT2. Z state (zwitterionic, mainly HOMO to LUMO): vertical excitation 61.1 kcal/mol, one minimum CPD-Z, barrierless ring closure at both levels as the Woodward-Hoffmann rule predicts. D state (doubly excited): 87.5 (89.4) kcal/mol, two C2h minima with the open-ring isomer higher and a barrier near 1 kcal/mol. B state (biradicaloid): 87.9 (89.5) kcal/mol, nearly degenerate with D at the Franck-Condon geometry, two C2h minima with the closed-ring one 5 kcal/mol above the open-ring at CASPT2 and a ring-closure barrier around 6 kcal/mol; CPD-B is a biradical with a transannular distance of 2.14 A resembling the ground-state transition state for homolytic transannular bond breaking.
Other: The zwitterionic Z state is the clean demonstration that a full pi space is not enough when ionic configurations dominate. At CASSCF the Z state comes out as the HIGHEST of the four computed excited states, and only CASPT2 puts it second — the paper states plainly that CASSCF 'describes the energies of this state very poorly on a quantitative level ... due to the fact that dynamic correlation is very important in such a state due to the important ionic configurations'. A (16,16) space covering every pi orbital in the molecule still gets the state ORDER wrong, because the deficiency is dynamic correlation of ionic configurations, which no enlargement of a valence pi space can supply. The same correlation dependence removes a mechanistic feature outright: the CPD-LE minimum's 1.4 kcal/mol ring-closure barrier at CASSCF vanishes entirely at CASPT2. Two structural constraints propagate through the whole study. Symmetry had to be IMPOSED because the 8.7 million configurations of the (16,16) space are only tractable when C2h blocks the CI space, so no lower-symmetry stationary point could be optimized at that level; and the CASPT2 reference had to be the smaller (12,12) because many active orbitals are the CASPT2 bottleneck, with MRPT2 on the full (16,16) reference run as a benchmark to justify the substitution. The authors' own verdict on the accuracy is worth carrying: 'even with perturbation theory, there is no guarantee that different states encountered along the same reaction pathway will be described equally well ... the results are expected to be only semiquantitative.' Basis effects, by contrast, are small (aug-cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ tested), so the residual uncertainty is correlation and space, not basis.
reference_short: Boggio-Pasqua, Bearpark & Robb, J. Org. Chem. 2007, 72, 4497
notes: A mechanism for the photochromism of dimethyldihydropyrenes. The triplet state was not studied in detail because experiment shows that although it is formed, it does not influence the isomerization quantum yields. The ground-state barriers are described as very approximate because no transition state was optimized. The relatively small ring-closure barrier compared with the ring-opening one accounts for the thermal ring-closure reaction, which is Woodward-Hoffmann forbidden. An attempt to use the molecular mechanics-valence bond (MMVB) method failed: the current version cannot treat DHP/CPD because it cannot describe all the electronic states involved, probably from poor parametrization for such states.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on CASSCF(12,12) reference wavefunctions at the CASSCF(16,16) geometries, with a 0.4 hartree Roos-Andersson level shift throughout; benchmarked against MRPT2 using the full (16,16) reference

compound_name: (6-4) Photolyase repair site — FADH- lumiflavin donor with the T(6-4)T thymine photoproduct acceptor, QM/MM electron-transfer states
geometry_source: QM/MM geometry optimization at the CASSCF(2,2)2 level from the crystal structure of (6-4) photolyase from Drosophila melanogaster bound to double-stranded DNA containing the T(6-4)T photoproduct (PDB 3CVU). Nearby MM residues (His365, His369, Tyr423, Gln299, Asn406, water W697, the ribityl and adenine fragments of FADH-, two deoxyriboses and the photoproduct phosphate) were relaxed at every QM step by microiterations; all other MM coordinates constrained. ESPF charges during optimization were computed from the state-averaged CASSCF density.
method: QM/MM with electrostatic embedding via the ESPF operator; state-averaged CASSCF with equal weights, followed by multistate CASPT2; energy decomposition of the QM/MM interaction
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(2,2)2 in the paper's notation, where m and n are the electrons and orbitals and k the number of states: two electrons in the flavin HOMO and the LUMO of the 3' thymine base, averaged over two states. Two larger spaces are also used — CASSCF(2,3)3 adding an orbital to carry the ET-HisH+ state alongside ET-3'T, and CASSCF(2,5)5 spanning the closed-shell ground state, the two lowest locally excited flavin states, and the ET-3'T and ET-5'T states.
active_space_protocol: The space is sized by the number of states that must be described rather than by any orbital-occupation criterion, and it grows only when a state intrudes. The minimal (2,2) with two-state averaging holds just the donor HOMO and the acceptor LUMO — the smallest space that can represent an electron transfer at all. It was expanded to (2,3) with three-state averaging ONLY for the two modified-environment models (MM-6.9 and MM-(2.7+7.7)) where the ET-HisH+ state dropped below ET-3'T and became the first excited state, so the two-state calculation would have tracked the wrong root. The (2,5) five-state space adds the flavin locally excited states and the second electron-transfer acceptor; being far more expensive, it was applied only to the smaller (D,A) QM part. All CASSCF calculations use state averaging with EQUAL weights over the states considered. MS-CASPT2 used the standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au and an imaginary shift of 0.1 au. QM part: 62 atoms for the (D,A) models, growing to 79 (HisH+) or 78 (His) atoms when the histidine side chain is included, its geometry optimized with force-field rather than quantum-mechanical parameters.
nroots_per_mult: 2, 3 or 5 depending on the space (state-averaged with equal weights in every case)
electronic_structure_description: The states of interest are the closed-shell ground state, two locally excited flavin states, and electron-transfer states to the 3' and 5' thymine bases. The two flavin LE states are HOMO to LUMO and HOMO to LUMO+1 pipi* transitions at about 2.95 eV (420 nm) and 3.40 eV (365 nm), with oscillator strengths of 0.02 and 0.52 — a weak lowest band and a strong second band, matching the UV-vis spectrum of FADH- in photolyases. The ET states are dark, carrying no absorption intensity; electron transfer to the DNA substrate is what quenches flavin fluorescence, whose lifetime drops markedly when the enzyme binds photodamaged DNA. In the modified environments MM-6.9 and MM-2Na+ the ET-HisH+ state falls below ET-3'T, with ET-HisH+ at 1.66 and 2.03 eV against ET-3'T at 2.47 and 3.34 eV. The same environmental change raises ET-HisH+ by 0.37 eV but ET-3'T by 0.97 eV, so His365H+ is a much less DNA-charge-sensitive electron acceptor than the 3' base. The DNA negative charge significantly increases the ET excitation energies, while protonation of the active site, screening or omitting the DNA charge, and extending the QM part all lower them.
Other: The most transferable result is a two-part cancellation. The ET-3'T excitation energy from the minimal CASSCF(2,2)2 is SMALLER than from CASSCF(2,5)5, but the differential dynamic correlation correction is correspondingly smaller for the two-state calculation, so 'after the (MS)CASPT2 correction very similar excitation energies are obtained with both methods'. In other words the minimal two-orbital donor-acceptor space is adequate for the electron-transfer energy PROVIDED CASPT2 is applied — its CASSCF error and its correlation correction offset, and Figure 6 shows the differential correlation energy separating cleanly into an ET trend and an LE trend, growing with excitation energy. The paper's wider conclusion is that dynamic correlation 'does not alter the energy trends', so the environmental effects the study is really after survive at the CASSCF level. Where the small space genuinely fails is state IDENTITY rather than energy: in two modified-environment models a third state, ET to the protonated histidine, drops below the target ET-3'T state, and only expanding to (2,3) with three-state averaging keeps the right root in view. That failure mode is invisible from within the (2,2) calculation, so it was caught by physical reasoning about a nearby acceptor, not by any internal diagnostic. Two further caveats for reuse: the five-state (2,5) results exist only for the smaller 62-atom (D,A) QM part, so the QM-size effect and the state-count effect were never varied together, and the histidine side chain added to the larger QM models had its geometry optimized with force-field parameters rather than quantum-mechanically.
reference_short: Moughal Shahi & Domratcheva, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2013, 9, 4644
notes: Studies how the excitation energies of the DNA repair site depend on the protonation state of the conserved His365, the distribution of DNA counterions, and the water solvent. Two QM/MM models were built, with protonated (HisH+) and neutral (His) His365. Setup: His19 protonated to satisfy a salt bridge with Glu224, all other His in the H-N-epsilon form, all Glu and Asp deprotonated, all Lys and Arg protonated, FADH- and DNA backbone phosphates deprotonated, all crystallographic waters retained, hydrogens added with Tinker, 15 or 16 Na+ counterions along the DNA backbone, and a 50 A water shell of 6000 molecules from Packmol. AMBER94 with TIP3P waters; force-field parameters and atomic charges for FADH- and T(6-4)T from earlier studies. Three hydrogen link atoms at the C1'-C2' bond of the ribityl chain and the two N1-C1' bonds to the deoxyriboses, with MM-boundary charges reassigned by the charge-shift scheme. The double-stranded DNA carries 28 negatively charged phosphates in the MM part, screened by protein, water and counterions. Cluster models from earlier work predict smaller ET energies than these QM/MM models.
correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2 with the standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au and an imaginary shift of 0.1 au

compound_name: Dihydrogen (H2) — full CI reference for domain-averaged Fermi hole analysis of a two-centre two-electron bond
geometry_source: Scan of internuclear distances from 0.5 to 3.0 A
method: CASSCF wavefunctions, from which one- and two-particle spinless density matrices in the natural orbital basis are extracted for domain-averaged Fermi hole (DAFH) analysis and shared-electron distribution indices (SEDI); RHF and restricted Kohn-Sham B3LYP for comparison, including a 'pseudo-RKS' scheme inserting RKS orbitals into the simplified RHF-level DAFH expression
software: MOLPRO (with the B3LYP alias b3lyp3); GAMESS-UK basis sets
basis_set: Triple-zeta valence plus polarization Cartesian Gaussians — TZVP in GAMESS-UK, GAMESS-PVTZ in MOLPRO, derived from Dunning's work — for H and F. No analogous internal Li set exists, so Dunning's [4s] contraction of a (10s) primitive set was taken from Table 5 of the original paper and augmented with a single p function of exponent 0.17.
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in twelve orbitals, which in this basis set corresponds to a FULL CI. Compared throughout against the authors' earlier two-electrons-in-two-orbitals CASSCF in the same basis.
active_space_protocol: The basis was chosen compact enough that a (2,12) CASSCF is a full CI, making H2 the calibration point for the whole study: it is the only system where the exact answer in the given basis is available, so the effect of dynamic correlation on the DAFH analysis can be isolated by comparing against the minimal (2,2) space. All analysis is carried out on valence electrons only, checked against all-electron analysis with no important differences in interpretation.
electronic_structure_description: Across all bond lengths from 0.5 to 3.0 A, DAFH analysis for a hydrogen atom returns a single dominant occupation number close to unity. At large separations the full-CI values are practically identical to those from the (2,2) CASSCF; at short separations the full-CI values are slightly lower — 0.994 falls to 0.991 at R = 1 A and 0.998 to 0.993 at R = 0.5 A. The corresponding DAFH function f1 resembles the 1-sigma-g molecular orbital delocalized over both atoms at short R, and localizes onto the analyzed atom to become H(1s) at dissociation. Near the equilibrium geometry the DAFH functions are still fairly symmetrical, and the overlap between DAFH functions for the two atomic domains shows very little tendency to decrease with R in that region.
Other: The quantitative answer to how much active space size matters for this kind of bonding analysis: going from a minimal (2,2) CASSCF to a full CI (2,12) in the same basis changes the dominant DAFH occupation number by 0.003 at R = 1 A and 0.005 at R = 0.5 A, and by essentially nothing at long range. The conclusion drawn is that 'the inclusion of dynamical electron correlation makes only small quantitative differences to the DAFH analysis relative to a somewhat cheaper calculation that mostly includes only nondynamical correlation. The basic descriptions are much the same.' Full-valence CASSCF is therefore validated as the working level for the larger systems in the study, where full CI is impossible — this row is what licenses the Li2, Li4 and F2 rows. The paper is equally clear about what does NOT work: the pseudo-RKS scheme of inserting restricted Kohn-Sham B3LYP orbitals into the simplified RHF-level DAFH expression is 'far less successful' for H2 and Li4, since that expression cannot take proper account of correlation effects. The authors state they prefer 'the use of the actual density matrices for correlated descriptions to schemes that rely on approximations that become exact at the RHF level', and note the pseudo-RKS shortcut is still fairly widely used — worth knowing before reusing published DAFH numbers of that provenance. The practical obstacle to doing it properly is that the required pair densities are not always readily available.
reference_short: Ponec & Cooper, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 11294
notes: DAFH analysis extracts bonding information from correlated wavefunctions, complementing AIM, ELF, NBO, population analyses and bond orders. The domain integrations are over AIM domains from partitioning the total electron density, but all analysis reported is for valence electrons only.
correlation_correction: None — the point of the study is to compare the correlation content of full CI, full-valence CASSCF, RHF and B3LYP descriptions directly, not to correct one with another

compound_name: Dilithium (Li2) — bond dissociation and non-nuclear attractor by DAFH analysis
geometry_source: Scan of bond lengths from 2.0 to 4.5 A
method: CASSCF wavefunctions, from which one- and two-particle spinless density matrices in the natural orbital basis are extracted for domain-averaged Fermi hole (DAFH) analysis and shared-electron distribution indices (SEDI); RHF and restricted Kohn-Sham B3LYP for comparison, including a 'pseudo-RKS' scheme inserting RKS orbitals into the simplified RHF-level DAFH expression
software: MOLPRO (with the B3LYP alias b3lyp3); GAMESS-UK basis sets
basis_set: Triple-zeta valence plus polarization Cartesian Gaussians — TZVP in GAMESS-UK, GAMESS-PVTZ in MOLPRO, derived from Dunning's work — for H and F. No analogous internal Li set exists, so Dunning's [4s] contraction of a (10s) primitive set was taken from Table 5 of the original paper and augmented with a single p function of exponent 0.17.
active_space_orbital_description: Full-valence CASSCF, two electrons in eight orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Full-valence prescription — every valence orbital active, no selection — applied uniformly to Li2, Li4 and F2 so the three systems are described on a common footing and can be compared directly. Its adequacy rests on the H2 full-CI comparison rather than on any convergence test here. Analysis restricted to valence electrons.
electronic_structure_description: Li2 features a NON-NUCLEAR ATTRACTOR in the electron density over a significant range of nuclear separations, so the AIM partitioning yields domains that do not correspond to atoms. The total extent of valence electron sharing is tracked by the sum of SEDI indices for both types of sharing with one lithium atom as a function of R. The relevant DAFH eigenvector evolves from a sigma-g-like molecular orbital at short separation to the appropriate 2p-sigma atomic orbital localized on one atom at the dissociated limit.
Other: The interesting feature for active-space purposes is that a full-valence space of only two electrons in eight orbitals must describe a density topology containing a non-nuclear attractor — a maximum of the electron density lying between the atoms with no nucleus under it — across a wide range of separations. Since DAFH analysis integrates over AIM domains, the domains themselves are not atomic here, and the analysis reports on electron sharing with the attractor basin as well as between the lithium atoms. That the same full-valence recipe handles this and the ordinary covalent cases is the point: the choice is dictated by consistency across the four systems rather than by anything specific to Li2, and its transferability was established on H2, where a (2,2)-to-full-CI comparison changed DAFH occupation numbers by at most 0.005. What this row cannot establish is whether the modest single p function added to Dunning's [4s] lithium contraction is sufficient to describe a non-nuclear attractor faithfully; no Li basis of matching quality was available in the packages used, so it was assembled by hand and not benchmarked.
reference_short: Ponec & Cooper, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 11294
notes: Li2 is examined to follow the electron reorganization accompanying bond dissociation in a system that also features a non-nuclear attractor. The lithium basis had to be constructed by hand because no analogous TZVP-quality set was stored internally in GAMESS-UK or MOLPRO.
correlation_correction: None — the point of the study is to compare the correlation content of full CI, full-valence CASSCF, RHF and B3LYP descriptions directly, not to correct one with another

compound_name: Tetralithium rhombus (Li4) — valence electron sharing among non-nuclear attractor domains
geometry_source: Planar rhombus with each side 5.552 bohr and the shortest across-ring distance Li1...Li2 of 4.936 bohr, taken from earlier work
method: CASSCF wavefunctions, from which one- and two-particle spinless density matrices in the natural orbital basis are extracted for domain-averaged Fermi hole (DAFH) analysis and shared-electron distribution indices (SEDI); RHF and restricted Kohn-Sham B3LYP for comparison, including a 'pseudo-RKS' scheme inserting RKS orbitals into the simplified RHF-level DAFH expression
software: MOLPRO (with the B3LYP alias b3lyp3); GAMESS-UK basis sets
basis_set: Triple-zeta valence plus polarization Cartesian Gaussians — TZVP in GAMESS-UK, GAMESS-PVTZ in MOLPRO, derived from Dunning's work — for H and F. No analogous internal Li set exists, so Dunning's [4s] contraction of a (10s) primitive set was taken from Table 5 of the original paper and augmented with a single p function of exponent 0.17.
active_space_orbital_description: Full-valence CASSCF, four electrons in sixteen orbitals — the analogue for the cluster of the (2,8) full-valence space used for Li2.
active_space_protocol: Full-valence again, scaled to the cluster: four valence electrons in all sixteen valence orbitals. Applying the identical prescription to Li2 and Li4 is what makes the monomer-to-cluster comparison of electron sharing meaningful. Valence-only analysis throughout.
electronic_structure_description: The rhombus contains non-nuclear attractors (labelled NNA1 and NNA2) whose domains participate in the sharing of valence electrons. Shared-electron distribution indices for the three levels of theory compared (as tabulated): SEDI(Li1,Li2) 0.012, 0.027, 0.017; SEDI(Li1,Li3) 0.037, 0.046, 0.037; SEDI(Li3,Li4) 0.070, 0.114, 0.082; SEDI(Li1,NNA1) 0.139, 0.132, 0.111; SEDI(Li3,NNA1) 0.565, 0.602, 0.622; SEDI(Li3,NNA2) 0.023, 0.064, 0.058; SEDI(NNA1,NNA2) 0.168, 0.158, 0.166. The dominant sharing is between Li3 and the first non-nuclear attractor at roughly 0.6, an order of magnitude larger than any direct Li-Li index.
Other: Li4 is where the pseudo-RKS shortcut is shown to fail on a real cluster, and the SEDI table quantifies it: direct lithium-lithium indices vary by up to a factor of 1.6 across the methods compared (SEDI(Li3,Li4) at 0.070, 0.114 and 0.082) while the dominant Li3-to-attractor index moves only from 0.565 to 0.622. So the weak, chemically ambiguous interactions are exactly the ones most sensitive to how correlation is treated, while the strong one is robust — a useful triage rule when deciding how much a bonding analysis can be trusted. The paper's summary is that inserting restricted Kohn-Sham orbitals into the RHF-level DAFH expression cannot properly capture key correlation effects, and the authors note this pseudo-RKS manipulation remains fairly widely used despite that. Note also that 'genuine' B3LYP SEDI values could not be calculated at all, since the required pair density is not available from a Kohn-Sham calculation — the pseudo scheme exists because of that gap, not as a considered approximation. The full-valence (4,16) space is transferred here from the H2 validation without a cluster-specific convergence test.
reference_short: Ponec & Cooper, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 11294
notes: The main object of the study: the role played by non-nuclear attractor domains in the sharing of valence electrons in a lithium cluster. The rhombus geometry is taken from earlier work rather than optimized here.
correlation_correction: None — the point of the study is to compare the correlation content of full CI, full-valence CASSCF, RHF and B3LYP descriptions directly, not to correct one with another

compound_name: Difluorine (F2) — dissociation of a weak homopolar bond by DAFH analysis
geometry_source: Scan of bond lengths from 1.25 to 2.50 A
method: CASSCF wavefunctions, from which one- and two-particle spinless density matrices in the natural orbital basis are extracted for domain-averaged Fermi hole (DAFH) analysis and shared-electron distribution indices (SEDI); RHF and restricted Kohn-Sham B3LYP for comparison, including a 'pseudo-RKS' scheme inserting RKS orbitals into the simplified RHF-level DAFH expression
software: MOLPRO (with the B3LYP alias b3lyp3); GAMESS-UK basis sets
basis_set: Triple-zeta valence plus polarization Cartesian Gaussians — TZVP in GAMESS-UK, GAMESS-PVTZ in MOLPRO, derived from Dunning's work — for H and F. No analogous internal Li set exists, so Dunning's [4s] contraction of a (10s) primitive set was taken from Table 5 of the original paper and augmented with a single p function of exponent 0.17.
active_space_orbital_description: Full-valence CASSCF, fourteen electrons distributed in just eight orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The full-valence prescription was adopted here 'mostly for consistency with the treatments of Li2 and Li4', and the authors say plainly what that costs: 'This is a relatively low-level of theory for this molecule, but it should be more than adequate to highlight the differences from H2.' Consistency across the four systems was preferred over accuracy on any one of them — the study is comparative, so a space chosen by a single rule everywhere is worth more than a space optimized per molecule.
electronic_structure_description: DAFH eigenvalues and their degeneracies for one F atom, by bond length: at 1.25 A, 1.984 (singly degenerate, sigma-like lone pair), 1.966 (doubly degenerate, pi-like lone pairs) and 0.995 (free valence); at 1.30 A, 1.983, 1.969 and 0.994; at 1.40 A, 1.983, 1.975 and 0.992; at 1.50 A, 1.983, 1.979 and 0.990; at 1.60 A, 1.985, 1.983 and 0.989; at 1.75 A, 1.988, 1.988 and 0.988; at 2.25 A, 1.996, 1.995 and 0.995, the last now interpreted as 2pz rather than free valence; at 2.50 A, 1.998, 1.996 and 0.998. The DAFH functions already show noticeable asymmetry near the equilibrium geometry, unlike H2 which stays fairly symmetrical there, and the equilibrium F-F distance (calculated or experimental) falls in a region where the overlap between the DAFH functions of the two domains is ALREADY decreasing fairly rapidly with R.
Other: The 14-electrons-in-8-orbitals full-valence space is unusually electron-rich for its orbital count — nearly two electrons per active orbital — and the eigenvalue table shows why that still works for this purpose: three of the four DAFH eigenvalues sit between 1.96 and 2.00 throughout, being lone pairs that barely change, while all the interesting physics lives in the single free-valence eigenvalue near 0.99. The analysis is therefore insensitive to how well the space describes the lone pairs, which is fortunate because the authors concede this is 'a relatively low-level of theory for this molecule'. The substantive result is that the weakness of the F-F bond shows up in DAFH analysis as the equilibrium geometry sitting in a region where the two domains' DAFH functions are already losing overlap — the bond is, roughly speaking, already partly broken at its own equilibrium distance, whereas H2's equilibrium lies in a flat region of the same curve. The paper flags that visual inspection of DAFH functions is 'rather subjective' and that the numerical domain-overlap measure, which behaves like a bond order, is the reliable version of the comparison. Anyone reusing these eigenvalues should note the interpretation of the fourth one CHANGES with distance, from free valence to 2pz between 1.75 and 2.25 A, so the table is not a single continuous quantity.
reference_short: Ponec & Cooper, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 11294
notes: F2 is included to determine how far DAFH analysis of a weak bond differs from a conventional homopolar bond such as H2. Comparisons with other systems also show F2 to be unusual. Figures 6 and 7 display the nonbonding DAFH eigenvectors at 1.50 A and the R-dependence of the broken-valence eigenvector, both at an isovalue of 0.12.
correlation_correction: None — the point of the study is to compare the correlation content of full CI, full-valence CASSCF, RHF and B3LYP descriptions directly, not to correct one with another

point_group: C1 — 16 conformers exist under a Cs constraint but NONE of them is a minimum; the local minima appear only when the symmetry constraint is released
geometry_source: CAS(10,9)/6-31G* optimized stationary structures on the S0, T1, S1, T2 and S2 surfaces; state-averaged CASSCF for intersections between states of the same multiplicity, and state-averaged CASSCF with SLATER DETERMINANTS for the singlet-triplet minimum energy crossing points. B3LYP/6-311G** was used for the S0 and T1 equilibrium and transition-state geometries, with analytical frequencies confirming each critical point and IRC calculations verifying the pathways.
method: CASSCF and state-averaged CASSCF; B3LYP and UB3LYP for the ground and lowest triplet surfaces; spin-orbit coupling from a one-electron approximation to the spin-orbit operator
basis_set: 6-31G* for all CASSCF; 6-31G* and 6-311G** for B3LYP
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,9): three pi and three pi* orbitals of the aromatic ring, the C=O pi and pi* orbitals, and one oxygen nonbonding orbital. For the 1,4-biradicals produced by the 1,5-H shift the space is reduced to 10 electrons in EIGHT orbitals, dropping the C=O pi* orbital from the (10,9) set.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF was chosen for the geometries 'because the CASSCF wave function has sufficient flexibility to model the changes in electronic structure upon electronic excitation' — the study spans npi* and pipi* states of both multiplicities, so both the carbonyl lone pair and the ring pi manifold must be active simultaneously. The space is then ADAPTED to the chemistry: once the 1,5-H shift has produced a 1,4-biradical the carbonyl is gone, so the C=O pi* orbital is removed and the space becomes (10,8) at constant electron count. Two different state-averaging protocols are used for the two kinds of crossing: ordinary state-averaged CASSCF for same-multiplicity intersections, and state averaging over SLATER DETERMINANTS for the singlet-triplet minimum energy crossing points, since spin eigenfunctions cannot describe both multiplicities in one average.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged over the states involved at each crossing (three states at the S1/T2/T1 intersection)
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic excitation energies at CAS(10,9)/6-31G*: T1(3npi*) 74.3, T2(3pipi*) 76.9, S1(1npi*) 77.0 and S2(1pipi*) 103.8 kcal/mol, against band origins of 73.9, 76.9, 77.9 and 101.2 kcal/mol for acetophenone. Because S1(1npi*), T1(3npi*) and T2(3pipi*) lie within 2.7 kcal/mol of one another they intersect in the Franck-Condon region, which the state-averaged CASSCF confirms. The optimized 1npi*/3pipi* and 3pipi*/3npi* crossing points turn out to be INDISTINGUISHABLE in structure and identical in energy, so all three surfaces meet at a single S1/T2/T1 three-surface intersection, only 2.5 kcal/mol above the S1 minimum. In the S1 and T1 structures the two singly occupied electrons sit mainly on the carbonyl C12 and O11 atoms; in T2 they sit mainly on the aromatic ring; at the intersection the electronic structure is intermediate, with one unpaired electron on O11 and one on the ring. There is no first-order spin-orbit coupling between S1(1npi*) and T1(3npi*), so direct intersystem crossing between them is inefficient; T2(3pipi*) acts as a relay, and the spin-orbit coupling matrix element at the S1/T2/T1 intersection is 52.9 cm-1. The 1,5-H shift has a barrier of 1.9 kcal/mol on the T1 pathway at UB3LYP/6-311G**, consistent with a rate constant near 1e10 s-1 inferred for o-alkylphenyl ketones.
Other: The active space is validated against experiment in an unusually direct way and then deliberately changed mid-mechanism. Validation: all four adiabatic excitation energies from CAS(10,9)/6-31G* — 74.3, 76.9, 77.0 and 103.8 kcal/mol — sit within 1 kcal/mol of the measured band origins of acetophenone (73.9, 76.9, 77.9, 101.2), including the ORDERING of the three near-degenerate low-lying states, which is the whole mechanistic question here. That is a stringent test, because the states span both npi* and pipi* character and both multiplicities, and a space biased toward either manifold would reorder them. The adaptation: for the 1,4-biradical formed after the 1,5-H shift, the C=O pi* orbital is dropped, giving (10,8). This keeps the electron count fixed while removing an orbital that no longer corresponds to a bond in the product, which is the right instinct but means biradical and reactant energies come from different spaces and are not directly comparable. A third point worth carrying: the singlet-triplet crossings could not be optimized with ordinary spin-adapted state averaging and required state-averaged CASSCF over Slater determinants instead — a protocol detail that determines whether a three-surface intersection can be located at all. The result that 1npi*/3pipi* and 3pipi*/3npi* optimize to the SAME structure and energy is what establishes the three-surface intersection, and the authors note this is a common feature of aromatic carbonyls with a nearly constant structure across compounds.
reference_short: Ding & Fang, J. Org. Chem. 2010, 75, 1630
notes: Near-UV irradiation at about 300 nm populates S1(1npi*), which relaxes and crosses efficiently to T1(3npi*) through the S1/T2/T1 three-surface intersection. The subsequent triplet reactions from the 1,4-biradical are improbable because the spin-conserving pathways have high barriers or are strongly endothermic, so intersystem crossing to the lowest singlet occurs first. Cyclization is prevented by the parent acid. Deuterated acids yielding deuterated products was earlier experimental evidence for the mechanism. Detailed structural parameters for the S1/T2/T1 structure are in the Supporting Information.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF energies; B3LYP/UB3LYP results are reported alongside as an independent method rather than as a correction

compound_name: Diels-Alder reaction of cyclopropene with butadiene — endo/exo selectivity
point_group: Cs enforced for the concerted transition states (a plane bisecting the butadiene central bond and the cyclopropene pi bond); all other optimizations unconstrained
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations of the concerted endo and exo transition states with D95 and D95V* basis sets, with a symmetry plane enforced; biradical intermediates optimized with the CASSCF option in GAMESS using D95V and the same active space as the transition state. HF/3-21G, D95 and D95* geometries computed for comparison. Input generated with PCMODEL and MOLDEN after preoptimization with the MMX force field.
method: CASSCF for geometries, with single-point QCISD(T) on each CASSCF-optimized structure; HF at several basis sets; AM1 with a 3x3 CI from an open-shell SCF wavefunction for the biradical paths; counterpoise correction for basis set superposition error by the Boys-Bernardi method including reagent distortion
software: Sirius and Abacus (CASSCF and MCSCF energy derivatives); GAMESS (CASSCF biradical optimizations); AMPAC 2.1 and 4.5 (AM1)
basis_set: D95, D95*, D95V and D95V* for CASSCF and QCISD(T); 3-21G, D95 and D95* for HF
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in the six pi orbitals of the reagents and the corresponding orbitals of the transition state.
active_space_protocol: The space follows the pi systems of the two reagents — four butadiene pi orbitals and two cyclopropene pi orbitals — and is carried unchanged onto the transition state and onto the biradical intermediates, so every point on both the concerted and stepwise pathways is described at constant space. A symmetry plane bisecting the butadiene central bond and the cyclopropene pi bond was enforced for the concerted transition states only; every other geometry optimization was unconstrained. CASSCF geometries then serve as the platform for single-point QCISD(T), with zero-point corrections to both the CASSCF and QCISD(T) numbers ASSUMED to be 90% of the corresponding HF/D95 and HF/D95* values rather than computed.
electronic_structure_description: Activation energies in kcal/mol, uncorrected then counterpoise- and ZPVE-corrected. Endo: HF/3-21G 25.16 then 36.33; HF/D95 32.90 then 36.60; HF/D95* 35.82 then 39.00; CASSCF/D95V 33.38 then 36.51; CASSCF/D95V* 33.82 then 36.79; QCISD(T)/D95V 14.57 then 24.91; QCISD(T)/D95V* 12.68 then 21.37. Exo values run about 2 kcal/mol higher throughout, giving corrected endo-exo differences of 1.93, 1.92, 1.88, 1.24, 1.22, 1.54 and 1.88 kcal/mol across the same seven levels — consistently under 2 kcal/mol and remarkably method-independent. Reaction energies are -75.08, -70.82 and -69.54 kcal/mol uncorrected, -68.50, -63.65 and -62.29 corrected. Geometrically the CASSCF forming C-C distances are 2.3027 A (endo) and 2.3013 A (exo) with D95, 2.2926 and 2.2937 A with D95*, slightly longer than the HF values. On the stepwise route the s-trans and s-cis biradicals lie 5 and 10 kcal/mol above the reagents at the level directly comparable with QCISD(T).
Other: The paper opens with the correct caveat — 'since CASSCF does not generally provide a balanced treatment of electron correlation, one might expect inconsistencies in the energetics' — citing Houk's finding that CASSCF overestimated reagent stability relative to products and transition states for butadiene plus ethylene, and noting that comparing RETRO-Diels-Alder activation energies instead would have brought the CASSCF numbers much closer to experiment. That imbalance shows up here as expected: corrected CASSCF barriers of 36.5-36.8 kcal/mol sit right on top of the Hartree-Fock values (36.6-39.0) and roughly 15 kcal/mol above the size-consistent QCISD(T) results of 21.4-24.9, which are the ones consistent with a fast reaction at 0 degrees C. A pi-only six-in-six space therefore buys essentially nothing over HF for the absolute barrier. What it does deliver is the SELECTIVITY: the corrected endo-exo difference is 1.2-1.9 kcal/mol at every level from HF/3-21G through CASSCF to QCISD(T), so the quantity of interest is insensitive to correlation treatment entirely, and 'surprisingly, the HF calculations give the same selectivities'. The second lesson is about a correction that is not the active space at all. Counterpoise corrections are 1.1-1.3 kcal/mol for CASSCF but 6.8-8.5 kcal/mol for QCISD(T) and 8.5-9.0 for the minimal 3-21G basis, so basis set superposition error 'fortuitously lowers the (uncorrected) activation energies' by far more than any method difference; the authors note that other reports of QCISD(T) Diels-Alder transition states have not made this correction and 'the reported activation energies reported in them should be treated with caution'. reference_short: Sodupe, Rios, Branchadell, Nicholas, Oliva & Dannenberg, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1997, 119, 4232
notes: Wiberg reported this reaction in 1960; Baldwin later found complete endo selectivity (within detection limits) at 0 degrees C for cyclopropene with 1(E)-dideuteriobutadiene. The reagents exclude secondary pi-orbital overlap as defined by Gleiter, which is the most popular explanation of endo preference, and transition-state polarity is also hard to invoke — making this a clean test case. The biradical mechanism is ruled out: no transition state for biradical formation could be located because GAMESS lacked efficient enough optimization procedures for the available resources, but an established relationship between the bond dissociation energy and the intrinsic C-C barrier predicts barriers near 27 (s-trans) and 29 (s-cis) kcal/mol, well above either concerted path, and the favoured s-trans biradical would additionally need about 15 kcal/mol to isomerize about the butadiene central bond before it could close. A proposed explanation of the endo preference is a stabilizing interaction between an H on C3 of cyclopropene and the incipient C2-C3 double bond of butadiene, present only in the endo transition state, analogous to interactions seen in some crystals and in H2O/acetylene complexes; this is consistent with Apeloig's observation that C3-substituted cyclopropenes give exo adducts. AM1 biradical optimization needed the BIRADICAL keyword (3x3 CI from an open-shell SCF wavefunction) because 2x2 CI with an RHF wavefunction would not converge.
correlation_correction: Single-point QCISD(T) — quadratic CI with singles, doubles and a perturbative estimate of triples — on each CASSCF-optimized structure; counterpoise correction for basis set superposition error applied throughout

compound_name: Sulfur dioxide (SO2) — ion-pair dissociation to SO+ + O- at 14.87-15.15 eV
point_group: Cs for the bent geometries used in the calculations; the ground state configuration is also given in C2v
geometry_source: Cuts through the potential energy surfaces rather than optimized structures: the bond angle was fixed at 119 degrees and one S-O bond length at 1.42 A, with the other S-O bond length scanned. Calculated PES energies were shifted DOWN by 4.7 eV so the ion-pair dissociation threshold matches the experimental value.
method: CASSCF potential energy surface cuts; velocity map imaging experiment measuring O- ion-pair yield spectra and angular distributions
active_space_orbital_description: Six active electrons in five active orbitals: (3a'')2 (12a')2 (13a')2 (4a'')0 (14a')0 in Cs symmetry for the bent molecule. The full ground-state configuration is (core)(5a1)2(3b2)2(6a1)2(4b2)2(7a1)2(2b1)2(1a2)2(5b2)2(8a1)2 in C2v, or (core)(7a')2(8a')2(9a')2(10a')2(11a')2(2a'')2(3a'')2(12a')2(13a')2 in Cs.
active_space_protocol: The space is chosen to be SMALL ON PURPOSE, which is unusual and is argued explicitly. Around the ion-pair energy region a large number of excited valence and Rydberg states coexist, and avoided crossings between ion-pair states and same-symmetry states make adiabatic surfaces of pure ion-pair character hard to follow, so the authors 'limited possible excited configurations by including only the main electronic configurations of the ion-pair states'. The consequence is stated directly: 'Small active space eliminates the mixing of ion-pair states with Rydberg states completely and some highly excited valence states. Any additional active orbital will result in a very large number of states that the calculations about ion-pair states become very difficult.' The space is therefore a diabatization device — it buys DIABATIC character by excluding the orbitals that would produce the avoided crossings.
nroots_per_mult: Multiple A' symmetry roots (states labelled up to 15A' are reported)
electronic_structure_description: Ion-pair states correlating with SO+(X 2Pi, v) + O-(2P_J). Near the crossing region, with S-O bond lengths of 1.7 and 1.4 A and a bond angle of 119 degrees, the A'-symmetry ion-pair configurations are: Sigma+ from (2pi)4(3pi)3(10sigma)2(4pi)1 with rSO 1.41 and 2.53 A at 180 degrees, corresponding to 15A' built from (3a'')2(12a')2(13a')1(4a'')0(14a')1 and (3a'')1(12a')2(13a')2(4a'')1(14a')0; Sigma- from the same parent configuration with rSO 1.41 and 2.58 A; Pi from (2pi)4(3pi)4(10sigma)1(4pi)1 with rSO 1.39 and 2.43 A, corresponding to 14A'; Delta from (2pi)4(3pi)3(10sigma)2(4pi)1 with rSO 1.42 and 2.45 A, corresponding to 13A'. The O- yield spectrum over 14.87-15.15 eV shows two very broad bands, assigned as vibrationally excited Rydberg states converging on the SO2+ ionic states C, D and E; the 14.94 eV band is assigned to a Rydberg state with ionic core D(2A1). Rydberg PESs were obtained by shifting the D 2A1 and C 2B1 ionic-state surfaces to the experimentally determined Rydberg energy levels. The SO+ vibrational population distributions are inverted.
Other: An unusually candid case of an active space chosen for what it EXCLUDES rather than what it includes. Because ion-pair states are embedded in a dense manifold of Rydberg and highly excited valence states of the same symmetry, an adiabatic calculation with a physically complete space would produce avoided crossings that destroy the ion-pair character of any single surface. The five-orbital space removes the orbitals that carry Rydberg character, so the computed surfaces stay diabatically ion-pair along the whole dissociation path — 'small active space eliminates the mixing of ion-pair states with Rydberg states completely'. Enlarging it is described as making the calculation not just costlier but harder to interpret, because of the state proliferation. The authors state the price plainly: 'the calculated electronic energies for the ion-pair states are expected to have large errors because the multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) method was not used ... the number of active electronic orbitals and active electrons was also limited', while arguing that the equilibrium geometries and the main PES characteristics survive. The 4.7 eV downward shift applied to align the computed threshold with experiment is the scale of the absolute error, so these surfaces are usable for topology and for the crossing analysis but not for energetics. The physics the small space is protecting is worth noting too: ion-pair states typically differ from the interacting Rydberg states by TWO orbitals, which rules out vibronic, spin-orbit and rotational coupling (all of which need a one-orbital difference) and leaves electrostatic coupling as the dominant interaction.
reference_short: Liu, Song, Kong, Li & Mo, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 9999
notes: Combined experiment and theory on ion-pair dissociation dynamics. The sample was 10% SO2 in He at about 1000 Torr stagnation pressure, with molecular beam source and ionization chamber pressures near 3e-5 and 1e-7 Torr. Energy calibration used F- images from ion-pair dissociation of F2 to F+(3P2,1,0) + F-(1S0), whose spin-orbit spacings are well determined. Rydberg state symmetries were determined experimentally from angular distributions: a transition dipole moment out of the molecular plane would force beta2 = -1, which is inconsistent with the measurements, so the moment must lie along y or z with A1 or B2 symmetry. Geometric parameters of the Rydberg ionic cores for the C, D and E states are quoted from CASPT2/ANO-L calculations of Li and Huang, not computed here. Figure 7 shows the PES cuts illustrating the predissociation mechanism.
correlation_correction: None — the paper notes explicitly that MRCI was NOT used and that the ion-pair energies therefore carry large errors

compound_name: Co(II) in an all-silicon zeolite six-ring — CoO6Si6H12(2+) / CoO6Si6(OH)12(2+) model
ligand_set: Six framework oxygens of a zeolite six-ring (three close OA, three distant OB), the ring completed by six Si and terminated by H or OH
point_group: C3v (run in Cs because MOLCAS accepts only Abelian groups)
geometry_source: CoNaA X-ray crystal structure with three close oxygens at 2.08 A and three distant at 2.94 A; then restricted BP86 optimizations in successive steps, each relaxing a further shell of atoms around cobalt while the dangling-bond positions and orientations stay frozen at crystal values
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with BP86 DFT geometry optimizations; spin-orbit coupling in one case via an effective one-electron operator with an effective charge
software: MOLCAS (CASSCF/CASPT2); Amsterdam Density Functional (BP86 geometry optimizations)
basis_set: [6s4p3d1f] for Co, [3s2p1d] for OA and OB, [4s3p] for Si and Al; [2s] for H in the small models, [2s1p] for OC and [1s] for H in the large models
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen electrons in eight orbitals of predominantly cobalt 3p and 3d character — the five Co 3d orbitals that carry the ligand field states plus the three Co 3p orbitals included for 3p-3d intershell correlation.
active_space_protocol: The active space discussion is explicit and tested. The MINIMAL space that can describe the ligand field spectrum is the five predominantly Co 3d orbitals, and the calculations confirm those five orbitals are indeed mainly Co 3d with only a small contribution from the nearby OA oxygens, so the computed states are genuine ligand field states. Ligand valence orbitals were considered for inclusion — which is CRUCIAL in transition metal complexes with strongly covalent bonds, to capture nondynamical correlation of the metal-ligand interaction — but here the Co-O bonds are IONIC, and when oxygen orbitals were added they either kept occupation numbers very close to 2 or rotated into Co 3p orbitals. That rotation is itself the diagnostic: 3p-3d intershell correlation governs the relative energies of terms arising from 3d(n) configurations in transition metal ions. The effect can largely be captured by correlating the 3p electrons at the CASPT2 stage, but slightly better results follow from putting the 3p orbitals in the CASSCF space, so the final choice is 13 electrons in 8 orbitals (Co 3p plus 3d). Test calculations with and without the Co 3p orbitals in the CASSCF space differed by never more than a few hundred cm-1, and the eight-orbital space was preferred simply because it costs little more. In the CASPT2 step all electrons from Co 3p and 3d, Si and Al 3s and 3p, O 2s and 2p, and H 1s are correlated — 87 electrons for the small models and 159 for the large ones. Correlating distant electrons on Si, Al and the terminating H or OH is not expected to matter but cannot be avoided with delocalized molecular orbitals, and that large electron count is what produces intruder states; a level shift of 0.3 hartree with back-correction was applied, a magnitude shown elsewhere not to significantly alter excitation energies in similar transition metal systems. Because MOLCAS accepts only Abelian point groups, the C3v models were run in Cs and the C3 models with no symmetry, with SUPSYM restrictions imposed to prevent mixing between orbitals of different parent-group representations. State-averaged CASSCF over all states of a given representation was used, followed by CASPT2 on each state.
multiplicities_studied: quartet (doublets added in one spin-orbit case)
nroots_per_mult: All states of the 4F ground and 4P first excited free-ion terms; state-averaged over each symmetry representation
electronic_structure_description: At the CoNaA crystal structure with C3v symmetry the free-ion terms split as 4F to 2x4E + 4A1 + 2x4A2 and 4P to 4E + 4A2. CASPT2 energies in cm-1 with individually optimized orbitals (column A) then state-averaged orbitals (column B): X 4A2 at 0/0; a 4E 273/313; a 4A1 1580/2063; b 4E 2793/3286; b 4A2 2734/3457; c 4E 14840/15906; c 4A2 20044/21777. The experimental free-ion 4P-4F splitting is 14561 cm-1. Optimization changes the structure substantially: Co-OA contracts from 2.08 to 2.01 A and Co-OB from 2.94 to 2.79 A by step 2, with the OA-Co-OA angle closing from 117.5 to 112.4 degrees. The largest spectral change accompanies step 2, where the 4F splitting increases by almost 2000 cm-1 over the crystal-structure result and both 4P-derived states rise about 1000 cm-1; later optimization steps change little, matching the small further structural changes.
Other: This model carries the paper's own estimate of its accuracy, obtained by varying the ORBITAL OPTIMIZATION protocol rather than the space. Two CASPT2 sets are reported for the same (13,8) space: one with individually optimized CASSCF orbitals per state, one with a single state-averaged set per symmetry representation. The difference grows with excitation energy and reaches 1700 cm-1 for the c 4A2 state, and the authors say this 'should be considered as an upper bound of the accuracy that can be expected from the present CASPT2 results'. Every other model in the study uses state-averaged orbitals only, so all cross-model comparisons should be read against column B here, and no other model has an independent error estimate. On the space itself, the (13,8) is minimal-plus-3p: adding ligand valence orbitals was tried and rejected because the ionic Co-O bonding leaves them at occupation near 2 or rotates them into Co 3p, and dropping the 3p from the CASSCF stage changes energies by at most a few hundred cm-1. So the space is genuinely converged for this bonding regime — the caveat being that the same reasoning would NOT hold for covalent metal-ligand bonds, where the paper notes ligand orbitals are crucial. The remaining error is geometric, not electronic: moving from the averaged crystal structure to DFT-optimized structures changes the 4F splitting by about 2000 cm-1, comparable to the entire spread of the low-lying states.
reference_short: Pierloot, Delabie & Ribbing, J. Phys. Chem. B 1998, 102, 10789
notes: The all-silicon reference member of the series, used to establish the effect of the crystal versus optimized geometry before aluminium substitution is considered. Its ground state is nondegenerate, contrary to the 4E'' (D3h) ground state proposed by Klier, though a low-lying 4E state is found at 313 cm-1.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF(13,8) reference correlating 87 (small models) or 159 (large models) electrons, with a 0.3 hartree level shift plus back-correction to control intruder states

electronic_structure_description: With no symmetry all states become 4A. CASPT2 energies in cm-1 at the crystal structure: X 4A 0; b 4A 36; c 4A 71; d 4A 2004; e 4A 2639; f 4A 3024; g 4A 3495; h 4A 15858; i 4A 16039; j 4A 22129. Across the whole model series the 4F state splits by at most 3500 cm-1 while the 4P-derived states appear near 15500 and 21000 cm-1. Substituting Si by Al at frozen geometry has little spectral effect: the largest change is 1000 cm-1 on the highest state as the Al/Si ratio goes from 0 to 1, with all other states shifting by 200 cm-1 or less. On optimization this ring is found to give the STRONGEST oxygen ligand field of the whole series, producing four strong cobalt-oxygen bonds of comparable length.
Other: The cleanest separation of electronic from structural effects in the paper, and it comes out decisively on the structural side. Holding every geometry frozen at the averaged crystal structure and changing only Si to Al moves the excitation energies by 200 cm-1 or less, except for the highest state which shifts 1000 cm-1 — negligible against the several-thousand-cm-1 features being assigned. So the chemical role of aluminium is entirely indirect: it changes where the oxygens sit, not the electronic structure at fixed geometry. Any study that substituted heteroatoms in a frozen framework and concluded they had little effect would therefore reach the wrong answer. For active-space purposes the same (13,8) Co 3p+3d space serves this C1 model as the symmetric ones, which is what makes the comparison valid — but note that with no symmetry, SUPSYM restrictions cannot separate representations and all states are averaged together as a single A block, so this model's orbitals are averaged over more states than the higher-symmetry members.
