software: MOLCAS (CASSCF/CASPT2); Amsterdam Density Functional (BP86 geometry optimizations)
basis_set: [6s4p3d1f] for Co, [3s2p1d] for OA and OB, [4s3p] for Si and Al; [2s] for H in the small models, [2s1p] for OC and [1s] for H in the large models
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen electrons in eight orbitals of predominantly cobalt 3p and 3d character — the five Co 3d orbitals that carry the ligand field states plus the three Co 3p orbitals included for 3p-3d intershell correlation.
active_space_protocol: The active space discussion is explicit and tested. The MINIMAL space that can describe the ligand field spectrum is the five predominantly Co 3d orbitals, and the calculations confirm those five orbitals are indeed mainly Co 3d with only a small contribution from the nearby OA oxygens, so the computed states are genuine ligand field states. Ligand valence orbitals were considered for inclusion — which is CRUCIAL in transition metal complexes with strongly covalent bonds, to capture nondynamical correlation of the metal-ligand interaction — but here the Co-O bonds are IONIC, and when oxygen orbitals were added they either kept occupation numbers very close to 2 or rotated into Co 3p orbitals. That rotation is itself the diagnostic: 3p-3d intershell correlation governs the relative energies of terms arising from 3d(n) configurations in transition metal ions. The effect can largely be captured by correlating the 3p electrons at the CASPT2 stage, but slightly better results follow from putting the 3p orbitals in the CASSCF space, so the final choice is 13 electrons in 8 orbitals (Co 3p plus 3d). Test calculations with and without the Co 3p orbitals in the CASSCF space differed by never more than a few hundred cm-1, and the eight-orbital space was preferred simply because it costs little more. In the CASPT2 step all electrons from Co 3p and 3d, Si and Al 3s and 3p, O 2s and 2p, and H 1s are correlated — 87 electrons for the small models and 159 for the large ones. Correlating distant electrons on Si, Al and the terminating H or OH is not expected to matter but cannot be avoided with delocalized molecular orbitals, and that large electron count is what produces intruder states; a level shift of 0.3 hartree with back-correction was applied, a magnitude shown elsewhere not to significantly alter excitation energies in similar transition metal systems. Because MOLCAS accepts only Abelian point groups, the C3v models were run in Cs and the C3 models with no symmetry, with SUPSYM restrictions imposed to prevent mixing between orbitals of different parent-group representations. State-averaged CASSCF over all states of a given representation was used, followed by CASPT2 on each state.
multiplicities_studied: quartet (doublets added in one spin-orbit case)
nroots_per_mult: All states of the 4F and 4P free-ion terms; in the spin-orbit calculation additionally the doublet states of the 2G, 2P, 2H and 2D free-ion terms
electronic_structure_description: Under Cs the C3v representations reduce as E to A'+A'', A1 to A', A2 to A''. CASPT2 energies at the crystal structure in cm-1: X 4A'' 0; b 4A'' 140; a 4A' 574; b 4A' 2326; c 4A' 3204; c 4A'' 3451; d 4A'' 3486; e 4A'' 15240; d 4A' 15981; f 4A'' 22411. On optimization the cobalt moves within the mirror plane away from OA1, giving two shorter Co-OA2 and one longer Co-OA1 bond differing by 0.06 A; from step 2 the two OB2 oxygens move strongly toward cobalt while OB1 moves away, the difference growing to close to 1 A by step 4. The final Co-OB2 distance of 2.52 A represents two weak bonds which, added to the three strong ones, make the ion FIVE-coordinate rather than three-coordinate; the OA1-Co-OA2 angles open to 124.1 degrees leaving only 98.7 degrees for OA2-Co-OA2. At the optimized structure the calculated 4F splitting reaches 6200 cm-1, and states are found at 16000 and 25000 cm-1 matching the experimental band maxima.
Other: The one model where the space was pushed further, and where its limits show. Spin-orbit coupling was added only here, requiring a protocol change: a single orbital set for all states, built from a weighted average of the density matrices of the CASSCF quartet calculations, with the interacting states then constructed by FULL CI within the same (13,8) space and CASPT2 energies used for the diagonal elements of the spin-orbit matrix. The effective one-electron spin-orbit operator used an effective charge Zeff = 15.2 au, obtained by scaling against the experimental free Co(2+) spectrum — an empirical calibration, not an ab initio result. The motivation was a genuine failure of the spin-free calculation: the two states near 16000 cm-1 are split by only 500 cm-1 against an experimental band splitting of several thousand, and only one nondegenerate state is found at 25000 cm-1 where experiment shows structure. So the (13,8) space with CASPT2 reproduces band POSITIONS well once DFT geometries are used, but not band SPLITTINGS, and spin-orbit coupling was invoked to close that gap. The resulting doublet-quartet mixings are extensive — individual spin-orbit states are reported as combinations of six to nine parent states with weights as low as 23% — so the ligand-field picture that justified the minimal d-based space does not survive spin-orbit coupling at higher energies.
reference_short: Pierloot, Delabie & Ribbing, J. Phys. Chem. B 1998, 102, 10789
notes: Two aluminiums mirrored by one of the C3v planes. The five-coordination reached on optimization is the paper's central structural finding for this composition, with the two extra Co-OB bonds considerably weaker than the three Co-OA bonds. The calculations suggest the observed splitting of the 16000 cm-1 band relates to structural variation among sites rather than to a single geometry.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF(13,8) reference correlating 87 (small models) or 159 (large models) electrons, with a 0.3 hartree level shift plus back-correction to control intruder states

compound_name: Co(II) in a Si3Al3 zeolite six-ring — CoO6Si3Al3H12(-) model
ligand_set: Six framework oxygens of a zeolite six-ring with three Si and three Al at alternating positions, terminated by H
point_group: C3 (run with no symmetry in MOLCAS, with SUPSYM restrictions)
geometry_source: CoNaA X-ray crystal structure; this composition proves the least distorted of the series on optimization, retaining a three-coordinate C3 structure
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, with BP86 DFT geometry optimizations; spin-orbit coupling in one case via an effective one-electron operator with an effective charge
software: MOLCAS (CASSCF/CASPT2); Amsterdam Density Functional (BP86 geometry optimizations)
basis_set: [6s4p3d1f] for Co, [3s2p1d] for OA and OB, [4s3p] for Si and Al; [2s] for H in the small models, [2s1p] for OC and [1s] for H in the large models

multiplicities_studied: quartet (doublets added in one spin-orbit case)
nroots_per_mult: All states of the 4F and 4P free-ion terms; state-averaged CASSCF orbitals
electronic_structure_description: With Si and Al alternating the symmetry falls from C3v to C3, with E going to E and both A1 and A2 going to A. CASPT2 energies at the crystal structure in cm-1: X 4A 0; a 4E 63; a 4A 2260; b 4E 3235; b 4A 3523; c 4E 15719; c 4A 22793. The ground state is nondegenerate with a low-lying 4E only 63 cm-1 above it. On optimization this is the LEAST distorted member of the series, keeping a three-coordinated C3 structure rather than developing the extra Co-OB bonds seen with two aluminiums.
Other: The maximum-aluminium member, and it disproves the natural expectation that more aluminium means a stronger ligand field — the paper states the opposite outright: 'This does not mean, however, that the strength of the oxygen ligand field increases with the number of aluminums present in the ring. On the contrary, the strongest field was calculated for a Si5Al ring.' With three aluminiums the alternating arrangement is too symmetric for cobalt to gain extra coordination, so the ion stays three-coordinate while the Si5Al and Si4Al2 rings distort to reach four- and five-coordination respectively. The same (13,8) Co 3p+3d space is used throughout, which is what allows this comparison to be attributed to structure rather than to method. The near-degeneracy of the ground state with a 4E state only 63 cm-1 above it is the tightest in the series and is worth noting for anyone reusing these energies: a state-averaged CASSCF over near-degenerate roots is the right protocol here, but the resulting 63 cm-1 gap sits well inside the 1700 cm-1 upper error bound the paper establishes from the orbital-optimization comparison on the all-silicon model.
reference_short: Pierloot, Delabie & Ribbing, J. Phys. Chem. B 1998, 102, 10789
notes: The five CASSCF active d orbitals illustrated in Figure 5 are taken from this model (step 5 structure). The paper states only that the Si and Al atoms are at alternating positions; no rule or rationale for that arrangement is given.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF(13,8) reference correlating 87 (small models) or 159 (large models) electrons, with a 0.3 hartree level shift plus back-correction to control intruder states

compound_name: Carbonyl oxide (H2COO) plus hydroxyl radical — reaction mechanism
point_group: C1 for the reaction stationary points; Cs (2A') for the syn- and anti-HCOO radical products
geometry_source: CASSCF(11,10) optimized stationary points with 6-31G(d,p) and 6-311+G(2df,2p), with harmonic frequencies at the larger basis to confirm minima and saddle points and to supply ZPE, enthalpy and free energy contributions; B3LYP/6-311+G(2df,2p) and QCISD/6-311+G(d,p) optimizations for comparison, with IRC verification of transition-state connectivity at the B3LYP level
method: CASSCF for geometries with CASPT2 single points; B3LYP, QCISD and CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ for comparison, monitored by the T1 diagnostic; counterpoise BSSE correction; AIM topological analysis of QCISD and CASSCF first-order density matrices
software: Gaussian, GAMESS, MOLCAS and MRD-CI; Molden for visualization; AIMPAC for the topological analysis
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) and 6-311+G(2df,2p) for CASSCF and CASPT2; 6-311+G(d,p) for QCISD; aug-cc-pVTZ for CCSD(T)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(11,10) for the geometry optimizations, giving 27720 configuration state functions in C1. The CASPT2 reference is a larger and common CASSCF(17,14), 2576574 CSFs in C1, chosen because '(17,14) corresponds to the sum of the appropriate active spaces describing H2COO (12,9) and HO (5,5)'. A schematic of the space composition is in the Supporting Information.
active_space_protocol: Two principles, both worth copying. First, the space for each structure is chosen NUMERICALLY rather than by chemical intuition: 'the active space for the CASSCF calculations of a given structure has been chosen according to the fractional occupation of the natural orbitals generated from a first-order density matrix of a MRD-CI wave function', itself based on correlating all valence electrons — so a separate correlated calculation supplies the occupation numbers that decide the space. Second, the CASPT2 reference is a COMMON (17,14) built additively from the two fragments' own spaces, H2COO (12,9) plus HO (5,5), so that reactants, complexes, transition states and products are all described in a space of identical composition and no artificial energy change arises from the space itself along the reaction coordinate. Multireference treatment is mandatory here because the reaction couples a molecule of partial biradical character to a radical. Single-reference results are policed by the T1 diagnostic, with CCSD wavefunctions above the Rienstra-Kiracofe threshold of 0.044 taken as unreliable.
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase H2COO is described mainly by the configurations 0.94(...10a'(2)1a''(2)2a''(2)) - 0.20(...10a'(2)1a''(2)3a''(2)), giving it a certain amount of biradical character; the a'' orbitals are pi, so carbonyl oxide is a four-pi-electron system and those electrons drive its reactivity. CASPT2 reaction energies: formation of H2CO plus HO2 is exothermic by 57.0 kcal/mol; formation of HCO plus two HO radicals exothermic by about 8 kcal/mol; formation of syn-HCOO plus H2O endothermic by 1.44 kcal/mol and anti-HCOO plus H2O exothermic by 6.52 kcal/mol. The hydrogen-bonded complex C1 lies 8.15 kcal/mol below the reactants at QCISD (7.52 with BSSE), on a flat surface — a 0.96 kcal/mol variation is noted — and TS1 lies 2.54 kcal/mol below the separated reactants. The anti-HCOO radical computed here (d(CO) 1.224 A, d(OO) 1.351 A, COO angle 121.5 degrees) resembles its carbonyl oxide precursor and differs sharply from the structure of Huang and co-workers (O-O 1.586 A, C-O 1.200 A, COO 97.6 degrees); additional calculations show the two correspond to DIFFERENT electronic states despite both having 2A' symmetry. The syn-HCOO radical had not been reported previously. T1 diagnostics of 0.0363, 0.0388, 0.0362 and 0.0362 are quoted for the structures checked, all below the 0.044 reliability threshold.
Other: The additive construction of the CASPT2 reference space is the transferable idea here: (17,14) is not chosen by inspection but as the exact SUM of the fragment spaces, H2COO (12,9) plus HO (5,5), so the space has the same composition at the reactant asymptote as at every complex, transition state and product. That removes the commonest artifact in reaction-path multireference work, where a space adequate near one geometry silently changes character elsewhere and injects spurious energy differences; the cost is a jump from 27720 to 2576574 CSFs, which is why the smaller (11,10) is used for geometries and the additive space only for single-point energies. Equally reusable is the space-SELECTION rule: fractional natural orbital occupations from an MRD-CI first-order density matrix, computed with all valence electrons correlated, decide which orbitals go in at each structure — an external, quantitative criterion rather than a chemical guess, applied per structure. The consistency of the whole picture is then cross-checked from the single-reference side with the T1 diagnostic, which comes out at 0.036-0.039 everywhere reported, safely under the 0.044 threshold, so the CCSD(T) numbers can be trusted alongside the CASPT2 ones — a mutual validation rather than either method standing alone. One caution for reuse: the (11,10) geometries and the (17,14) energies come from different spaces, so CASSCF and CASPT2 numbers in the tables are not a single consistent surface.
reference_short: Mansergas & Anglada, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 4001
notes: The reaction couples H2COO, which has partial biradical character, with the HO radical, hence the multireference requirement. Stationary points are labelled C for hydrogen-bonded complexes that are minima and TS for transition states. Three product channels are examined: H2CO + HO2, syn-/anti-HCOO + H2O, and HCO + 2 HO. Cartesian coordinates, absolute energies and AIM topological parameters at the bond critical points are in the Supporting Information. Small geometric changes on the flat C1 surface produce energy changes up to 3.36 kcal/mol.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points on a common CASSCF(17,14) reference at the CASSCF and QCISD geometries; CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ single points as an independent check

compound_name: Dimethylnitramine ((CH3)2NNO2, DMNA) — initial decomposition steps of a model nitramine energetic material
point_group: C1 — no symmetry restrictions were applied in any calculation
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations for the excited-state surfaces; ground-state decomposition geometries optimized at both MP2 and CASSCF with 6-31G(d) and 6-311G(d,p). Analytical frequencies and IRC minimum energy paths were computed in the REDUCED (10,7) space because the Gaussian 03 code cannot perform analytical frequency calculations with more than eight active orbitals.
method: CASSCF with state averaging over ground and excited states at equal weights for vertical excitation energies; conical intersection localization; MP2, QCISD(T) and B3LYP comparisons; pump-probe photofragmentation/fragment-detection experiments with TOFMS and LIF
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(14,11): one nitrogen nonbonding 2s_N orbital, two N-O bonding sigma_NO, two N-O antibonding sigma_NO*, one delocalized ONO pi-bonding, one delocalized ONO pi-antibonding, one N-N bonding sigma_NN, one N-N antibonding sigma_NN*, one pi-nonbonding n_pi(O) and one sigma-nonbonding n_sigma(O), shown in Figure 2. A reduced (10,7) space is also used.
active_space_protocol: The (14,11) space is taken over unchanged from Soto et al.'s work on NH2NO2, so the DMNA results are directly comparable with the published nitramine parent — a deliberate transfer rather than an independent construction. Its composition is a bond inventory of both dissociation channels at once: the N-N sigma/sigma* pair for NO2 elimination, both N-O sigma/sigma* pairs and the ONO pi system for nitro-nitrite isomerization, plus the oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs that carry the n-to-pi* excitations. The reduced (10,7) space exists for two separate reasons, one physical and one purely technical: 'to avoid convergence failure problems' in the excited-state calculations, and because the Gaussian 03 code cannot do analytical frequencies with more than eight active orbitals, so all frequency and IRC work — which needs initial force constants — had to run in (10,7) with the same basis. Vertical excitation energies come from state averaging over the ground and excited states with equal weights.
nroots_per_mult: At least 4 (S0 through S3), state-averaged with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(10,7)/6-31G(d) vertical excitation energies relative to the Franck-Condon geometry: S1 at 4.83 eV (n_sigma(O) to pi*), S2 at 5.65 eV (n_sigma(O) to pi*), S3 at 6.6 eV (n_pi(O) to pi*). Conical intersection energies on the same scale: (S1/S0)CI at 2.6 eV, (S2/S1)X at 4.8 eV and (S2/S1)CI at 4.2 eV. TWO S2/S1 intersections were located, one at short N-N distance labelled (S2/S1)X and one at long N-N distance labelled (S2/S1)CI. The (S2/S1)X intersection is strongly coupled with an adiabatic gap of 485 cm-1, while (S2/S1)CI and (S1/S0)CI are relatively weakly coupled. On the S1 surface beyond (S2/S1)CI there is a 3 kcal/mol barrier to NO2 elimination and NO barrier at all to nitro-nitrite isomerization. On the ground state at CASSCF(10,7)/6-31G(d), the N-NO2 bond dissociation energy is 30 kcal/mol, the nitro-nitrite isomerization barrier 57 kcal/mol, and the (S1/S0)CI barrier 60 kcal/mol. The adiabatic S0-S1 gap near (S1/S0)CI is only 11 cm-1. The nitro-nitrite transition state is LOOSE, not tight: at CASSCF(10,7)/6-31G(d) only a loose geometry could be found, whereas MP2/6-31G(d) gives a tight one at N1-N2 = 1.90 A with a 94.0 kcal/mol barrier and a loose one at 2.80 A with 69.0 kcal/mol.
Other: This paper documents a case where a single-reference method invents a stationary point that a multiconfigurational treatment shows does not exist. MP2 predicts a TIGHT nitro-nitrite isomerization transition state at N1-N2 = 1.90 A with a 94.0 kcal/mol barrier; neither CASSCF(10,7) nor CASSCF(14,11) can locate any tight transition state, finding only a loose one at 57 kcal/mol — and in the very region where MP2 puts its tight structure, both spaces locate an (S1/S0) conical intersection instead. The explanation, following Soto et al. on the parent NH2NO2, is that the nearby S1 surface 'repels the S0 surface down, destroying the tight TS', with the adiabatic gap collapsing to 11 cm-1. The authors' conclusion is blunt and worth carrying: monoconfigurational methods 'may overestimate the energy barrier of the tight nitro-nitrite isomerization TS because they cannot judge how the S0 surface topology can be affected by the proximity of the S1 surface', so 'only the CASSCF level of theory (or MRCI, CASPT2 approaches) will provide the most reasonable theoretical picture'. The MP2 barrier is wrong by 37 kcal/mol on a surface it cannot see. Two caveats attach to the numbers themselves. Nearly all reported energetics, including Table 2 and the ground-state barriers, come from the REDUCED (10,7) space, not the (14,11) the paper introduces — and the reduction is driven partly by a code limitation on analytical frequencies rather than by physics, so it was not chosen to preserve any particular property. And the (14,11) space was inherited from published work on a different molecule (NH2NO2), which aids comparability but means it was never validated for DMNA specifically; that both spaces agree on locating the (S1/S0) intersection is the only cross-check offered.
reference_short: Bhattacharya, Guo & Bernstein, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 811
notes: Combined experiment and theory. DMNA is excited by a single UV photon at 226 or 193 nm and the fragments detected by TOFMS or LIF. NO is the major product at 226 nm. Ground-state NO2 is ruled out as an intermediate: NO2 photodissociation near 226 nm shows a laser-intensity-dependent NO rotational temperature (about 30 K at low intensity through the 2 2B2 state, about 100 K at high intensity via Rydberg or ion-pair states), and no such dependence is seen for DMNA. Excited-state NO2 is also ruled out — no fluorescence with the characteristic 30-120 microsecond NO2 lifetime is observed, only NO LIF with about 200 ns lifetime and a hot rotational temperature near 120 K. Literature comparisons for the nitro-nitrite transition state across NH2NO2, CH3(H)NNO2 and (CH3)2NNO2 at DFT-GGA, MCSCF/4-31G, MP2, QCISD(T), CASPT2(14,11)/ANO-L and B3LYP levels are collected in Table 1. Which excited-state pathway dominates depends on the rate of intramolecular vibrational redistribution and on nonadiabatic transition rates through the different intersections, assessable only by dynamics such as MCTDH.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF results reported here; MP2, QCISD(T) and CASPT2(14,11)/ANO-L values from the literature are tabulated for comparison

compound_name: Ni(C2H4) — nickel-ethene complex, singlet and triplet potential surfaces
d_electron_count: 3d9 in the bound 1A1 state, arising from the Ni d(9)s (1)D asymptote (the free-atom ground state is d(8)s(2) 3F)
geometry_source: CASSCF potential surface scans varying the Ni-C and C-C bond lengths with all other parameters at their asymptotic values, then reoptimization around the equilibrium and transition state also varying the CH2 tilt angle; C-H bond and HCH angle held at free-ethene values (1.085 A, 120 degrees). Contracted CI single points at the CASSCF-optimized geometries.
method: CASSCF for the zeroth-order wavefunction, treating all spin couplings in the nickel 3d shell and giving correct dissociation, followed by contracted CI (CCI) for dynamic correlation; Davidson correction for unlinked clusters with the larger basis
basis_set: Nickel: Tatewaki-Huzinaga DZC-SET contracted (3,3,3,2,1/3,3,1,1/3,1) plus an added diffuse d exponent of 0.1641. Carbon: MIDI-3 plus a 3d polarization function (0.65). Hydrogen: Huzinaga 5s contracted to three functions plus a 2p (0.8). Double-zeta plus polarization in the valence shells with a minimal core description; cores frozen in free-atom form to avoid superposition errors. A larger nickel basis was also tested: Wachters 14s9p5d contracted to 8s4p2d plus two diffuse 4p and one diffuse 3d, giving 8s6p3d.
active_space_orbital_description: Seven active orbitals: the sigma, sigma*, pi and pi* orbitals of the C-C double bond, plus the nickel 3d(x2-y2-z2), 3d(xz) and 4s orbitals. The number of active electrons is not stated as a single figure in the text, so it is left blank; the CASSCF wavefunctions comprise 254 terms for 1A1 and 288 for 3A1. In the subsequent contracted CI the reference space consists of two configurations and 14 electrons are correlated — the 10 nickel valence electrons plus the electrons of the C-C sigma and pi bonds.
active_space_protocol: The space is derived from a list of REQUIREMENTS stated in advance and then verified. It must describe a weak double charge-transfer bond between nickel and ethene, allow proper dissociation of the C-C double bond (since C-C weakening in the complex is a central question), and give a proper description of the (1)D and (3)D states of the nickel atom. The seven-orbital choice was reached 'after some trial studies, using larger subspaces'. Each orbital is justified individually: the four C-C orbitals ensure correct C-C dissociation; nickel 3d(xz) binds to the ethene pi*, a weak bond that leaves both bonding and antibonding partners appreciably occupied so both must be active; and in the singlet the 4s and 3d(x2-y2-z2) hybridize, with occupation numbers that vary strongly with distance, so both must be active. The remaining 3d orbitals have occupation numbers very close to 2 and are kept inactive — a conclusion 'explicitly tested by calculating the most important points on the surface by using an active subspace which includes the remaining 3d orbitals'.
nroots_per_mult: 1 per state
electronic_structure_description: Singlet 1A1: with planar ethene, CASSCF gives a metastable complex 4.0 kcal/mol ABOVE the d(9)s (1)D dissociation limit (Ni-C 2.016 A, C-C 1.431 A) with a barrier to dissociation only 1.1 kcal/mol higher (transition state at 2.146/1.389 A, 5.1 kcal/mol). Optimizing the CH2 tilt angle changes the surface dramatically: the equilibrium drops 7.4 kcal/mol to -3.4 kcal/mol (Ni-C 1.972 A, C-C 1.454 A, tilt 21 degrees) and the barrier becomes 6.1 kcal/mol (transition state 2.205/1.390 A, tilt 9 degrees, 2.7 kcal/mol). Contracted CI at those geometries gives -8.2 kcal/mol at BOTH the equilibrium and the CASSCF transition state, so the barrier essentially disappears. The C-C bond lengthens from 1.354 A in free ethene to 1.454 A in the complex, and the hydrogens bend 21 degrees out of plane — close to experimental values for L2Ni(C2H4) complexes (C-C 1.46 A, Ni-C 1.99 A for (P(C6H5)3)2Ni(C2H4)). Back-donation from 3d(xz) to ethene pi* dominates, giving -0.18 electron on ethene and a b2 population of 1.39 electrons (charge transfer 0.61); 3d(xz) loses 0.64 electron. The nonbonded 11a1 orbital's occupation rises from 1.0 at large distance to 1.8 at equilibrium while its partner 12a1 falls from 1.0 to 0.2 — and 12a1 'would not be occupied at all in a closed-shell SCF description'. The computed (3)D-(1)D separation is 7.2 kcal/mol against an experimental 9.5. Triplet 3A1 is strongly REPULSIVE: 13.6 kcal/mol above the Ni d(9)s (3)D asymptote at the optimized geometry (Ni-C 2.1 A, C-C lengthened 0.03 A, tilt 6 degrees) at CASSCF, and 27 kcal/mol at CCI — more repulsive still. With the larger Wachters-based nickel basis the singlet CASSCF binding energy is 6.8 kcal/mol, rising to 14.3 at CCI and 19.8 with the Davidson correction, well below the d(8)s(2) 3F ground-state asymptote.
Other: An early and unusually rigorous piece of active-space reasoning: the space is specified by three physical requirements stated BEFORE the calculation (weak double charge transfer, correct C-C dissociation, correct Ni (1)D and (3)D description), narrowed by trial studies with larger subspaces, and then the exclusion of the remaining 3d orbitals is verified by actually recomputing the most important surface points with them included. The occupation-number evidence is given rather than asserted — the excluded 3d orbitals sit very close to 2, while the retained 12a1 varies from 1.0 to 0.2 across the surface and 'would not be occupied at all in a closed-shell SCF description', which is precisely why a single-reference treatment cannot describe this bonding. What the space alone does NOT deliver is energetics: CASSCF puts the singlet complex 3.4 kcal/mol below the (1)D limit, contracted CI deepens that to 8.2, the larger nickel basis plus CCI gives 14.3, and adding the Davidson correction 19.8 kcal/mol — a factor of six between the bare CASSCF number and the best estimate, and the authors say the 8.2 value 'is most probably a lower limit'. The dynamic correlation contribution to binding is substantial and, they note, still underestimated by the limited one-electron basis. compound_name: s-trans-Acrolein in water — conical intersections and singlet-triplet crossings for radiationless de-excitation
point_group: Planar for the S0, S1 and T2 minima and for the S1/T1 and T2/T1 crossings; twisted for the T1 minimum and for the T1/S0 and S1/S0 crossings
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G* optimization of acrolein in vacuum and in solution; minimum-energy conical intersection (MECI) and singlet-triplet crossing (MESTC) points located by a quasi-Newton search with a BFGS-updated approximate Hessian, starting in every case from the Franck-Condon (ground-state minimum) geometry. A point is accepted when the two-state energy gap falls below 0.002 au (1.3 kcal/mol) and both energy and geometry stabilize; in-solution values are averaged over the last 5 ASEP/MD cycles.
method: CASSCF within the ASEP/MD (averaged solvent electrostatic potential from molecular dynamics) framework, treating the solvent under both equilibrium and nonequilibrium (frozen-solvent) conditions
software: ASEP/MD, using data from Gaussian 98 and Moldy
active_space_orbital_description: All configurations arising from six valence electrons in five orbitals (6e/5o).
active_space_protocol: A single fixed (6,5) space is used for every state, every crossing point and both phases, which is what makes the vacuum-versus-solution comparison in Table 1 meaningful — any change in relative stability is attributable to the solvent rather than to the description of the solute. The odd orbital count reflects a space built around the n, pi and pi* manifold that carries both the n-to-pi* and pi-to-pi* excitations plus the ground state, so all four participating states (S0, S1, T1, T2) are described together. Crossing points are converged on a gap criterion of 0.002 au rather than to exact degeneracy, and in solution the results carry statistical uncertainty from the molecular dynamics, so they are reported as averages over the final five ASEP/MD cycles.
nroots_per_mult: 2 singlets (S0, S1) and 2 triplets (T1, T2)
electronic_structure_description: Four states participate: the ground state S0, the first singlet excited state S1 (n to pi*), and two triplets, T(pi to pi*) and T(n to pi*), labelled T1 and T2 respectively by the order of their absolute minima. Energies relative to the S1 Franck-Condon point (-190.6788 au) in kcal/mol, as vacuum then equilibrium-solution then nonequilibrium-solution: S0 minimum -90.8 / -95.8 (planar); S1 minimum -18.4 / -20.7 (planar); T2 minimum -21.5 / -22.3 (planar); T1 minimum -35.7 / -36.4 (twisted); S1/T1 STC -16.1 / -19.2 / -17.7 (planar); T2/T1 CI -16.7 / -19.1 / -18.4 (planar); T1/S0 STC -30.5 / -33.7 / -34.2 (twisted); S1/S0 CI +1.6 / -1.4 / +6.4 (twisted). Two gas-phase de-excitation paths had been proposed: direct S1/S0 internal conversion, or an indirect route beginning with S1/T1 intersystem crossing followed either by T1/S0 ISC or by T1/T2 internal conversion with weak phosphorescence from T2.
Other: The active space is held rigorously constant — one (6,5) for four electronic states, eight stationary and crossing points, and three solvent conditions — and that constancy is the entire basis of the paper's conclusion. Because nothing about the solute description changes, the observed shifts of 1.4 to 5.0 kcal/mol on going from vacuum to solution can be attributed to solvation, and the finding that 'the solvent modifies the relative stability of the different CI and STC but not enough as to alter the order of stability' is a statement about solvation rather than about method. The one point where the solvent matters qualitatively is the S1/S0 conical intersection, which moves from +1.6 kcal/mol above the Franck-Condon point in vacuum to -1.4 under equilibrium solvation but +6.4 under frozen-solvent (nonequilibrium) conditions — an 7.8 kcal/mol spread between the two solvation regimes, larger than any other entry, and the only one that changes sign. Anyone reusing these numbers must therefore specify which solvation condition applies. Two limits on precision are worth carrying: crossing points are converged only to a 0.002 au (1.3 kcal/mol) interstate gap rather than to true degeneracy, and the in-solution values are statistical averages over five ASEP/MD cycles, so differences smaller than a few kcal/mol are not resolved. reference_short: Munoz Losa, Fdez. Galvan, Sanchez et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2008, 112, 877
notes: Presents a method for locating minimum-energy conical intersection and singlet-triplet crossing points IN SOLUTION, combining high-level quantum treatment of the solute with a molecular dynamics description of solvent structure, usable under both equilibrium and nonequilibrium conditions. compound_name: Cyclobutadiene (1) — parent of the cyano-substituted series
geometry_source: Single-point CAS and CASPT2 calculations on CCSD/cc-pVDZ optimized geometries; B3LYP/6-31G* and B3LYP/6-311+G* structures also computed and found to show no significant differences from CCSD, with harmonic frequencies verifying all geometries as minima and supplying ZPVE
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 single points; CCSD and CCSD(T)/cc-pVDZ; B3LYP; natural bond orbital analysis at HF on the B3LYP geometries
software: MOLCAS (CAS and CASPT2); Gaussian 03 (DFT and CCSD(T)); ACES II MAB (CCSD); NBO 5.0
basis_set: ANO-L-VTZP for CASSCF and CASPT2; cc-pVDZ for CCSD and CCSD(T); 6-31G* and 6-311+G* for B3LYP
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(4,4): the four pz pi/pi* orbitals of the cyclobutadiene ring. For this parent the scaled CAS(x,x) and the fixed ring-only CAS(4,4) coincide.
active_space_protocol: Two nested space definitions are compared throughout. Sufficiency was tested by expanding further to include the py pi/pi* orbitals on the cyano substituents, giving CAS(8,8) for 2 and CAS(12,12) for the dicyano isomers; in each case the smaller space reproduced the singlet-triplet gap to within 0.3 kcal/mol, so the smaller was retained. Separately, a CONSTANT CAS(4,4) containing only the cyclobutadiene ring pz pi/pi* orbitals was run for every compound, to replicate the methodology of the MR-AQCC results of Eckert-Maksic et al. All CAS and CASPT2 calculations are single points on CCSD/cc-pVDZ geometries with the ANO-L-VTZP basis; ZPVE corrections come from B3LYP/6-311+G*.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet-triplet gaps in kcal/mol with ZPVE (negative means singlet ground state): B3LYP/6-31G* -4.1; B3LYP/6-311+G* -4.9; CCSD -9.5; CCSD(T) -11.2; CAS(x,x) -16.0; CAS(x,x)PT2 -10.3; CAS(4,4)PT2 -10.3; MR-AQCC -14.9. Reference configuration weights are 0.88 (singlet) and 0.92 (triplet) in both space definitions, since they are the same space here. The series-wide lesson is in Table 5: the reference-configuration weights for the scaled CAS(x,x) spaces FALL steadily with substitution — singlet 0.88, 0.84, 0.80, 0.81, 0.80, 0.77, 0.73 and triplet 0.92, 0.88, 0.84, 0.84, 0.84, 0.76, 0.76 from cyclobutadiene to tetracyano — while the fixed CAS(4,4) weights stay essentially flat near 0.87 (singlet) and 0.91-1.00 (triplet). The energetic price of getting this wrong is small — CAS(4,4)PT2 gaps run about 1 kcal/mol larger in magnitude than CAS(x,x)PT2 — so the diagnostic that matters is the reference weight, not the gap. compound_name: o-Dichlorobenzene (oDCB) — S1 state and cation vibrational spectroscopy
point_group: C2v for the DFT and CIS calculations; Cs for the CASSCF calculations
geometry_source: DFT geometries for the S0 neutral and D0 cation states at 6-311++G(d,p); the S1 excited state treated at CIS and CASSCF with the same basis
method: CASSCF and CIS for the first excited state; DFT for the ground and cation states; TD-DFT for higher excited states; natural bond orbital analysis of the cations; mass analyzed threshold ionization (MATI) spectroscopy via S1 intermediate states
active_space_orbital_description: Six pi orbitals containing six electrons: the three highest occupied pi orbitals of the aromatic ring and the three lowest unoccupied pi* orbitals. The chlorine lone pairs are deliberately excluded.
active_space_protocol: A pi-only six-in-six space, and the paper argues explicitly for the ORBITALS IT LEAVES OUT. The three highest occupied and three lowest unoccupied aromatic pi orbitals are taken; the chlorine lone pairs are excluded on the strength of experimental photoelectron data — 'from UV photoelectron spectra it is known that the lone-pair orbitals of the chlorine lie 1.5 eV under the aromatic pi orbitals, therefore they contribute only very weakly to the electronic excitation'. The corresponding assumption is stated up front: 'we assume for the electronic excitation a pi* from pi transition without any involvement of the lone-pair electrons of the chlorine atoms'. The assumption is then checked against the computed geometry change rather than left as an assertion: excitation lengthens the aromatic ring (weakening the pi bonds) while SHORTENING the C-Cl bonds through the mesomeric effect, which is the signature of a pi* from pi excitation. The same space and basis are used for all three isomers, so isomer differences cannot come from the space. Note that the CASSCF calculations run in Cs while the CIS and DFT comparisons are in C2v.
multiplicities_studied: singlet (neutral S0 and S1); doublet for the D0 cation, treated at DFT
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF electronic transition energy to the first excited state: 37122 cm-1 (4.6026 eV). Calculated ionization energy at the DFT level 9.0803 eV; the experimental adiabatic ionization energy from MATI is 73237 plus or minus 6 cm-1, identical for both the 35Cl2 and 35Cl37Cl isotopomers. Electronic excitation extends the aromatic ring through weakening of the pi bonds while the C-Cl bonds shorten, the chlorines stabilizing the ring by the mesomeric effect. NBO analysis of the cation places the positive charge primarily in a pi* orbital spanning C3-C4-C5-C6 — carbons that are NOT neighbours of the two chlorine atoms; the cation geometry shows further C-Cl shortening with C1-C2 elongation and C3-C4 compression. Franck-Condon overlaps for the ortho isomer are reported among the three isomers analysed.
Other: The ortho isomer is the one where excluding the chlorine lone pairs is least obviously safe, because the two chlorines are adjacent and their lone pairs are closest to one another — yet the paper reports 'no characteristic differences between the isomers' in the excitation-induced geometry change, which is the internal evidence that the pi-only (6,6) description holds across substitution patterns. The cation NBO result sharpens the point: the positive charge localizes on C3-C4-C5-C6, deliberately avoiding the chlorine-bearing carbons, so even in the ionized state the chlorine orbitals stay out of the singly occupied manifold. That said, the cation is described at DFT rather than CASSCF, so this is corroboration from a different method, not a test of the active space itself. The transferable point is that the space was bounded by an EXPERIMENTAL energy criterion rather than by an occupation-number threshold: chlorine lone pairs sit 1.5 eV below the aromatic pi orbitals in the UV photoelectron spectrum, so they are excluded, and the consistency of that choice is then confirmed by the computed geometry change on excitation (ring expansion with C-Cl contraction, the signature of pi* from pi). The exclusion is not obviously safe — the cation's NBO analysis shows the positive charge residing in a pi* orbital whose composition depends on where the chlorines sit — but the cation was treated at DFT, not CASSCF, so the active space is never asked to describe the ionized state. No dynamic-correlation correction is applied to the CASSCF results anywhere in this work.
reference_short: Gaber, Riese & Grotemeyer, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 425
notes: Vibrational spectra of the 35Cl2 and 35Cl37Cl isotopomers of the cation in the electronic ground state measured for the first time via S1 intermediate states by MATI. Wilson nomenclature is used for the vibrational assignments with Lord's numbering convention, and Herzberg (Mulliken) notation given in parentheses in the tables. Time-of-flight mass spectra show the three-peak chlorine isotopomer pattern with a theoretical 146:148:150 intensity ratio of 9.3:6.1:1.0; the heaviest isotopomer was too weak to record. TD-DFT at 6-311++G(d,p) was used to compute symmetries and energies of higher excited states in order to explain REMPI vibrations allowed by vibronic coupling.

geometry_source: CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G(d) optimization of the S0/S(pi) conical intersection for the 5FU-water system, and CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d) for the planar S(pi)/S(n) intersection; PCM ground and excited-state geometry optimizations in solution with UA0 cavity radii, followed by single points with UAHF radii; four explicit first-shell water molecules added in the aqueous calculations
method: CASSCF for conical intersection location, with PCM/TD-PBE0 for absorption, emission and potential energy surface exploration; polarizable continuum model for bulk solvent, supplemented by explicit first-shell water molecules
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF conical intersection work; 6-31G(d) and 6-311+G(2d,2p) for TD-PBE0
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(8,8) for the S0/S(pi) intersection: six pi molecular orbitals plus the two highest-energy n(O) valence orbitals, the lone pairs of the two carbonyl groups. A separate CASSCF(6,6) — five pi orbitals plus the highest n(O) — is used for the planar S(pi)/S(n) intersection.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces, each matched to the pair of states whose crossing is being located. For the S0/S(pi) conical intersection, CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G(d) with six pi molecular orbitals plus the two highest-energy n(O) valence orbitals, corresponding to the lone pairs of the two carbonyl groups. For the planar S(pi)/S(n) conical intersection, CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d) with five pi molecular orbitals plus the single highest-energy n(O) valence orbital. Intersections were located by the method of Bearpark et al. Both spaces are validated externally rather than internally: 'in both cases the CI structures are very similar to those obtained for uracil by Matsika at the MRCI(12/9) level (and checked by single-point calculations with larger active spaces) suggesting that our computational approach is fully adequate for the purposes of the present paper', that purpose being to obtain good CI STRUCTURES for subsequent PCM/TD-PBE0 energy analysis rather than accurate CI energies. All computed vibrational frequencies at the S0 and excited-state minima were checked to be positive.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (the two states forming each intersection)
electronic_structure_description: Two low-lying excited states: a bright S(pi) (pi to pi*) and a dark S(n) (n to pi*). Reaching the S0/S(pi) conical intersection CI(0pi) requires pyramidalization at C5 together with an out-of-plane distortion carrying the C5 substituent into a pseudoperpendicular arrangement relative to the molecular plane; including explicit water molecules does not significantly change the CI structure, so the ground-state recovery mechanism is solvent-independent. At TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) on the CI(0pi) geometry, S(pi) and S0 lie within 0.3 eV for all compounds studied. In ACETONITRILE, S(pi) and S(n) remain comparably stable along the planar path, and a planar CI(n-pi) between them — predicted by CASSCF in vacuo — is confirmed by PCM/TD-PBE0 with the two states within 1000 cm-1, so the wavepacket on S(pi) can be trapped in the dark S(n) state. In WATER the picture is completely different: S(n) is significantly less stable than S(pi) along the whole path from Franck-Condon to the S(pi) minimum, and an explicit calculation on CI(n-pi) with four first-shell waters puts S(pi) 0.35 eV below S(n), RULING OUT the crossing in aqueous solution. The path toward the S(pi) minimum is steeper in water than in acetonitrile.
Other: The two CASSCF spaces here are chosen per intersection rather than per molecule — (8,8) with both carbonyl lone pairs for the S0/S(pi) crossing, (6,6) with only the highest n(O) for the S(pi)/S(n) crossing — so the number of n orbitals tracks how many lone-pair-derived states have to be described at each crossing. That is a cleaner criterion than a single global space, but it means the two intersections in this study rest on different references and their energies are not on a common scale. The validation is external and honest about its scope: the structures reproduce Matsika's MRCI(12/9) results for uracil, and single points in larger spaces were run as a check, but the stated purpose is 'obtaining a good estimate of the CI structure to be used for the subsequent PCM/TD-PBE0 analysis' — CASSCF supplies geometry, TD-PBE0 supplies energy. The most striking result depends on that division: the CASSCF-predicted planar S(pi)/S(n) intersection EXISTS in vacuo and in acetonitrile but is destroyed in water, where four explicit first-shell waters push S(pi) 0.35 eV below S(n). A gas-phase active-space calculation alone would therefore predict a decay channel that does not operate in aqueous solution, which is exactly the case where the excited-state lifetime differs experimentally. The methodological point worth carrying is a division of labour between methods: the CASSCF spaces are used ONLY to obtain conical intersection GEOMETRIES, with the energies then supplied by PCM/TD-PBE0 at those structures. The authors are explicit that this is the criterion by which the spaces were judged adequate — agreement of the CI structures with Matsika's MRCI(12/9) results for uracil, plus single points in larger spaces — and not that the CASSCF energies themselves are reliable. The size of that gap is visible: at TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) on the CASSCF CI(0pi) geometry, the S(pi) and S0 surfaces are within 0.3 eV of each other for every compound, so dynamic correlation matters at the same scale as the state separations being discussed.
reference_short: Santoro, Barone, Gustavsson & Improta, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2006, 128, 16312
notes: The first comprehensive quantum mechanical study of solvent effects on the two lowest excited states of uracil derivatives, and the first unifying explanation of the experimental trend in 5-fluorouracil excited-state lifetime across solvents. PCM dielectric constants: 36.64 for acetonitrile, 78.39 for water. Solvent can modulate access to the dark n/pi* decay channel. Absorption and fluorescence energies computed with PCM/TD-PBE0 agree well with experiment; the 6-31G(d) and 6-311+G(2d,2p) discrepancies against experiment are noted in the text.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF results; dynamic correlation is brought in separately by TD-PBE0 single points on the CASSCF-optimized conical intersection geometries

electronic_structure_description: As for 5-fluorouracil, the S0/S(pi) conical intersection CI(0pi) is reached by pyramidalization at C5 and out-of-plane motion of the C5 substituent, and adding four explicit water molecules leaves its structure essentially unchanged. The solvent dependence, however, is OPPOSITE to 5FU's: for uracil S(pi) and S(n) are closer in WATER than in acetonitrile, so in acetonitrile the two states cross in a region far from the Franck-Condon point while in water they cross within the Franck-Condon region. S(n) is the most stable excited state for uracil at all levels, whereas for 5FU S(pi) becomes more stable in the nonequilibrium regime. In aqueous solution the equilibrium solvation shell of the S(n) state shows remarkable geometry changes relative to the ground state, which the authors take as strong evidence that this minimum is not relevant to the ultrafast decay of uracil-like molecules.
Other: Uracil is the control that shows the solvent effect is not generic: the same (8,8) and (6,6) spaces, the same solvent models and the same explicit-water treatment give a crossing that moves TOWARD the Franck-Condon region in water for uracil while being eliminated entirely in water for 5-fluorouracil. Because the active spaces are identical between the two molecules, that reversal is attributable to the 5-fluoro substitution rather than to any difference in electronic-structure treatment — which is the whole value of holding the space fixed across a substituent comparison. The CASSCF spaces are also the reason the comparison is possible at all: locating a conical intersection requires a balanced two-state description that TD-DFT cannot provide, so CASSCF geometries anchor the analysis while TD-PBE0 supplies the solvated energetics. Uracil additionally supplies the external benchmark for both spaces, since its CI structures are compared against Matsika's MRCI(12/9) results — so the validation was performed on this molecule and transferred to the fluorinated one. The methodological point worth carrying is a division of labour between methods: the CASSCF spaces are used ONLY to obtain conical intersection GEOMETRIES, with the energies then supplied by PCM/TD-PBE0 at those structures. The authors are explicit that this is the criterion by which the spaces were judged adequate — agreement of the CI structures with Matsika's MRCI(12/9) results for uracil, plus single points in larger spaces — and not that the CASSCF energies themselves are reliable. The size of that gap is visible: at TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) on the CASSCF CI(0pi) geometry, the S(pi) and S0 surfaces are within 0.3 eV of each other for every compound, so dynamic correlation matters at the same scale as the state separations being discussed.
reference_short: Santoro, Barone, Gustavsson & Improta, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2006, 128, 16312
notes: Studied alongside 5-fluorouracil to separate substituent effects from solvent effects. The conclusion that the out-of-plane motion of the 5-substituent drives ground-state recovery holds for both molecules and both solvents. Matsika's MRCI(12/9) conical intersection structures for uracil provide the external check on the CASSCF spaces used here.

compound_name: Valerophenone and its one-water complex — Norrish type reactions in aqueous solution
geometry_source: Iterative QM/MM optimization: the QM subsystem optimized at B3LYP/6-311G** or CAS(10,9)/6-31G* with the MM subsystem fixed, then electrostatic-potential fitting to obtain effective QM atomic charges, then MM optimization with the QM geometry fixed, cycling until the maximum force and its root-mean-square fall below 0.00045 and 0.0003 hartree/bohr. Bulk water modelled by a 32 x 27 x 27 A water box with the Amber force field.
method: CASSCF for the stationary structures of the lowest five electronic states with CASPT2 single points; B3LYP for comparison; combined QM/MM with Amber for the bulk solvent
software: Not stated in the extracted text (QM/MM with the Amber force field)
basis_set: 6-31G* for CASSCF and CASPT2; 6-311G** for B3LYP
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10,9): the three pi and three pi* orbitals of the aromatic ring, the C-O pi and pi* orbitals, and the oxygen nonbonding orbital.
active_space_protocol: One space, chosen so that it 'provides a balanced description of the minimum energy structures of the lowest five electronic states' — S0, S1, T1, S2 and T2 — which is necessary because the mechanism turns on the relative ordering of npi* and pipi* states of both multiplicities. Both manifolds are therefore represented at once: the ring pi system for the pipi* states and the carbonyl pi/pi* plus oxygen lone pair for the npi* states. CASPT2 single points are computed on the CASSCF reference with FIVE-ROOT state averaging at equal weights, so no state is preferentially optimized. The same space is applied to bare valerophenone, to the isolated one-water complex, and to the complex embedded in bulk water, which is what allows the hydrogen-bonding and bulk-electrostatic contributions to the solvent shift to be separated.
nroots_per_mult: 5 states total (S0, S1, T1, S2, T2), state-averaged with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic excitation energies in kcal/mol with dipole moments in Debye in parentheses and oscillator strengths, given as CAS for bare VP, then CAS, CAS/Amber and CASPT2//CAS/Amber for the VP-H2O complex: S0 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 (6.4); 3npi* 75.1, 77.1, 77.3, 78.2 (4.4), f = 9.2e-6; 3pipi* 75.5, 75.5, 74.2, 76.5 (7.2), f = 1.4e-4; 1npi* 78.7, 80.2, 80.4, 83.2 (4.3), f = 6.9e-5; 1pipi* 105.9, 105.6, 104.3, 98.8 (8.0), f = 0.47. In bare valerophenone 3npi* lies BELOW 3pipi* by 0.4 kcal/mol; forming the one-water complex INVERTS them, and CASPT2//CAS/Amber confirms 3pipi* as the lowest triplet with a 1.7 kcal/mol gap. The 1npi* state rises about 2.0 kcal/mol from the intermolecular hydrogen bond and is nearly unaffected by bulk water, while 1pipi* is barely changed by complexation but strongly lowered by the bulk. Vertical S0 to 1pipi* excitation raises the dipole moment from 6.2 to 9.4 D. In the 1npi* and 3npi* structures the two unpaired electrons sit on the carbonyl C7 and O12 atoms; in 3pipi* they sit on the aromatic ring; at the 1npi*/3pipi*/3npi* crossing the electronic structure is intermediate, with one unpaired electron on O12 and one on the ring. Experimentally the pi to pi* absorption maximum shifts from 237 nm in hexane to 239 nm in acetonitrile and 245 nm in water, while the n to pi* band in the UV-B region (280-315 nm) shows a blue shift.
Other: The single most useful result is a state-ordering inversion that only one solvent contribution produces. At CAS(10,9) bare valerophenone has 3npi* below 3pipi* by 0.4 kcal/mol; adding ONE explicit water molecule inverts them, and the bulk-water Amber environment leaves 3npi* essentially untouched (77.1 to 77.3 kcal/mol) while shifting 3pipi* by 1.3. So the two solvent mechanisms are cleanly separable and act on different states: hydrogen bonding raises the npi* states (the ground-state complex is stabilized more than the npi* excited complex because the H-bond weakens on n to pi* excitation), while bulk Coulomb interaction lowers the pipi* states because they carry the larger dipole moment. That separation is only trustworthy because the SAME (10,9) space is used at all three levels of environment — bare, complexed, and embedded — so nothing in the comparison comes from a changed reference. The correlation correction is not negligible and is state-specific: CASPT2 moves 1pipi* DOWN by 5.5 kcal/mol (104.3 to 98.8) while moving 3npi*, 3pipi* and 1npi* UP by 0.9, 2.3 and 2.8, so it changes the npi*-pipi* separations by several kcal/mol and cannot be omitted from a study whose conclusion is a 1.7 kcal/mol triplet gap. Five-root equal-weight state averaging is essential here for the same reason — a state-specific treatment could not maintain a balanced description of five states spanning 100 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Ding, Shen, Chen & Fang, J. Org. Chem. 2009, 74, 8956
notes: The 3pipi* state becoming the lowest triplet in water explains the long triplet lifetime observed for aqueous valerophenone. The 1npi*, 3pipi* and 3npi* states intersect in the same structural region, which the authors identify as the reason intersystem crossing from 1npi* to 3npi* is efficient for aqueous valerophenone photoexcited at 290-330 nm. Barrier heights reported include 14.9 kcal/mol for one ring pathway and a value 12.1 kcal/mol lower for alpha-C6-C7 cleavage; the C7-C8 cleavage barrier decreases by 0.5 kcal/mol on complexation, and a barrier of 4.6 kcal/mol for free valerophenone becomes 3.8 in the complex. Adiabatic excitation energies at all levels for both VP and VP-H2O, in gas phase and aqueous solution, are in the Supporting Information.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points on the CAS(10,9) reference wavefunctions, using five-root state averaging with equal weights

point_group: C2 at the most stable S0 geometry, with a Ci minimum only 0.015 eV higher; C2h imposed for the planar constrained scans; S1 geometries of C2 and Ci symmetry differ by only 0.001 eV
geometry_source: State-specific (14,12)CASSCF optimization of the S0 geometry, then phenyl torsional potentials in S0 and S1 scanned under C2 and/or Ci symmetry constraints, with C2h-constrained optimizations for comparison
method: State-specific CASSCF for geometry optimization and global potential energy surface scanning, with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP2) corrections including all valence and virtual orbitals; preliminary CI up to triple excitations used to select the active space
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta augmented by polarization functions: alpha_d = 0.75 for C, 0.55 for P, 0.80 for N
active_space_orbital_description: (14,12): the highest five occupied pi orbitals, the lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals, and the two nonbonding orbitals on the P atoms (for t-DPP) or N atoms (for t-AZB). The symmetric combination of the lone pairs is denoted n+; the antisymmetric combination n- is described as much less important.
active_space_protocol: The full space is defined first and then explicitly rejected on cost grounds. DPP has seven pi-type occupied orbitals with their corresponding pi* partners plus two phosphorus nonbonding orbitals, so allowing all excitations from the nine occupied into the lowest seven unoccupied orbitals would be an (18,16) CASSCF — 'quite unrealistic to scan the global potential energy surfaces', and the paper states plainly that 'reduction of active space is important'. The reduction is guided by a SEPARATE preliminary calculation rather than by inspection: configuration interaction including up to triple excitations from the closed-shell Hartree-Fock configuration was run first, and on that basis the highest five occupied pi, the lowest five pi*, and the two phosphorus nonbonding orbitals were judged 'enough to describe our present interest of S0 and S1 states at any geometries which possibly contribute to the photochemistry' — the qualifier AT ANY GEOMETRIES being the important one for a global surface scan. That gives (14,12), used for all surface scanning, with S0 geometries optimized by a STATE-SPECIFIC (14,12) CASSCF. MRMP2 corrections including all valence and virtual orbitals are applied to each electronic state where needed. The identical space and protocol are applied to t-AZB so the two molecules are directly comparable.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1)
electronic_structure_description: At the S0 geometry: S0 at 0.0 eV with a dipole moment of 0.025 D and a leading closed-shell configuration of coefficient 0.897; S1 at 3.544 eV CASSCF (2.759 eV with MRMP2), dipole 0.088 D, leading n+ to pi* configuration of coefficient 0.901. The experimental n+ to pi* absorption maximum is 2.695 eV (about 460 nm), well reproduced by MRMP2. Key geometric parameters, S0 then S1: P-P 2.056 then 2.153 A; P-C1 1.834 then 1.821 A; C1-P-P angle 103.1 then 109.0 degrees; C1-P-P-C1' dihedral -177.9 then -179.1 degrees; and the phenyl torsion phi 30.3 then 89.6 degrees. The S0 torsional potential has DOUBLE MINIMA at nonplanar conformations, phi = phi' = 30.3 degrees (C2) and phi = -phi' = 30.0 degrees (Ci). On excitation to S1 the phenyls twist to nearly perpendicular. Electron populations at phi = 30 degrees show that on n to pi* excitation the in-plane 3s, 3px and 3py populations fall from 0.936, 1.065 and 1.058 to 0.891, 0.828 and 0.963 while the out-of-plane 3pz rises from 0.994 to 1.398, and that 3pz population stays almost constant in S1 regardless of phi — the pi electron is localized on the P=P unit.
Other: This is a clean case of a reduced space being justified for a GLOBAL surface scan rather than for a single point, and the justification procedure is worth copying: a preliminary CI including up to triple excitations was run first, and the (14,12) subset was selected on the criterion that it describe S0 and S1 'at any geometries which possibly contribute to the photochemistry'. That geometry-independence requirement is exactly what a torsional scan from planar to perpendicular demands, and it is a stronger condition than adequacy at the Franck-Condon point. The full (18,16) was defined and rejected purely on the cost of scanning global surfaces, not on any claim that it would give the same answer. The compensating check is external: MRMP2 on this reference reproduces the observed 2.695 eV absorption to within 0.06 eV, whereas bare CASSCF is 0.85 eV too high. Note that the S1 phenyl torsion result — twisting to 89.6 degrees — is driven by an electron-population redistribution into the out-of-plane 3pz orbital, a property the active space must contain the relevant pi* orbitals to describe at all; the paper notes explicitly that P-C bond-length change alone 'is not persuasive enough' to explain the torsion. The general lesson is that the reduced space was validated against EXPERIMENT rather than against the larger space it replaced. Bare (14,12) CASSCF overestimates the n+ to pi* excitation energy substantially — 3.544 eV for t-DPP against an observed 2.695 eV, and 3.277 eV for t-AZB against 2.412 eV — while MRMP2 on the same reference gives 2.759 and 2.412 eV, essentially exact in both cases. The CASSCF error is nearly identical for the two molecules (0.85 and 0.87 eV), so the reduced space is BALANCED across the P/N comparison even though it is quantitatively poor on its own; that constancy is what makes the t-DPP versus t-AZB contrast trustworthy at the CASSCF level while the absolute energies are not. Both states are strongly single-configurational at the S0 geometry (leading CI coefficients 0.897-0.907 for S0 and 0.896-0.901 for S1), so the multiconfigurational treatment is needed for the surface topology and the excited-state ordering rather than for near-degeneracy at any one point.
reference_short: Amatatsu, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 8824
notes: An analogue of trans-azobenzene with P=P in place of N=N. P=P double bonds are of interest for electronic, optical and magnetic device materials; Protasiewicz and Simpson synthesized a diphosphene analogue of poly(p-phenylenevinylene). Standard reference bond distances computed at MP2 with the same basis (RHF values in parentheses): P=P 2.039 (2.002) in PH=PH, P-P 2.206 (2.214) in PH2-PH2, C=P 1.678 (1.653) in CH2=PH, C-P 1.860 (1.857) in CH3-PH2. The nonplanar S0 conformation is attributed to steric as well as electronic repulsion, and to the character of the P-C linkage bond compared with N-C.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP2) with all valence and virtual orbitals included

point_group: C1 — the 2A/1A conical intersection minimum structure is nonsymmetric
geometry_source: Relaxed 2A surface built by geometry optimization of the first excited state of a state-averaged CASSCF calculation over a grid of two active degrees of freedom q = (r, phi), with ALL other degrees of freedom relaxed at each grid point rather than frozen or treated as harmonic baths. One relaxed dihedral (xi) had to be frozen afterwards to remove an unphysical discontinuity (see notes).
method: State-averaged CASSCF over three states for the global potential energy surface; CASPT2 single points as a check; quantum-mechanical wavepacket dynamics on the resulting surface
software: MOLPRO (CASSCF surface); MOLCAS (larger active space and CASPT2 checks)
basis_set: Ahlrichs TZVP for the surface; 6-311G(2df,p) augmented with an additional diffuse p function on each carbon for the accuracy checks
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(6,6): two pairs of pi and pi* orbitals of cyclohexadiene and of hexatriene, together with the sigma and sigma* orbitals describing the bond cleavage in cyclohexadiene — orbitals which ADOPT PI CHARACTER in hexatriene. An extended CAS(8,12) was also tested.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by what the orbitals BECOME along the reaction rather than by what they are at either end: the sigma/sigma* pair that breaks in cyclohexadiene turns into pi character in hexatriene, so a single (6,6) describes both the closed and open forms and the path between them without changing composition. Three states (1A, 2A, 1B) are carried in the state-averaged CASSCF, matching the experimental mechanism in which the molecule passes through all three. Two independent accuracy checks were run: extension to CAS(8,12), and a much larger diffuse basis — 'these extensions did not lead to any significant differences for the first excited state'. CASPT2 was then computed on BOTH active spaces to add dynamic correlation.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (1A, 2A, 1B), state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: Experimentally, irradiation places the molecule in the second excited state 1B, which it leaves under steep gradients within about 50 fs to reach the dark 2A state where the population has a lifetime of 80 fs, after which the reaction completes on the ground state. The computed surface is that of the first excited state (2A) over the two active coordinates r and phi. The part of the 2A/1A conical intersection SEAM covered here had not previously been investigated. The nonsymmetric CI minimum structure obtained at CASSCF(6,6)/TZVP was compared against the published structure of Garavelli et al., which used the same active space with a smaller one-electron basis; detailed analysis showed 'differences well within the limits of the method and basis sets, and no systematic deviations'.
Other: Both of the obvious ways to challenge this space were tried and neither changed the answer: enlarging to CAS(8,12) and switching to a 6-311G(2df,p) basis augmented with diffuse p functions on every carbon 'did not lead to any significant differences for the first excited state'. That is a genuine two-axis convergence test, rare in surface-scanning work where the cost usually forbids it. What the space does NOT survive unchanged is dynamic correlation: CASPT2 on both spaces 'show larger deviations from the CASSCF results', though 'still qualitatively very similar'. The authors state the honest remedy and why it was unavailable — 'these differences could therefore be further minimized by a geometry optimization at the CASPT2 level. Due to the lack of analytical gradients for this method in the used programs this was not feasible' — so the surface the wavepacket propagates on is a CASSCF surface with a known, unremoved correlation error. The active-space construction itself is the transferable idea: the sigma/sigma* pair that breaks in the reactant becomes pi in the product, so choosing orbitals by their role ALONG the reaction rather than by their character at one geometry keeps a six-orbital space valid across an electrocyclic ring-opening. Independent corroboration comes from outside: the CI minimum structure matches Garavelli et al.'s at the same active space with a smaller basis, with no systematic deviation.
reference_short: Schonborn, Sielk & Hartke, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 4036
notes: A global ab initio potential energy surface for quantum wavepacket dynamics, aimed at interpreting femtosecond mass spectrometry data of Fuss et al. and Kosma et al. All passive degrees of freedom are RELAXED at each grid point rather than fixed or treated as harmonic baths, which the authors argue avoids the problems of frozen-coordinate reaction surfaces, on the assumption that passive-mode relaxation is faster than motion in the active coordinates. One relaxed dihedral angle xi produced a triangular-shaped step discontinuity at intermediate phi and large r, where an infinitesimal change in (r, phi) flips the molecule between two relaxed xi values; although energetically allowed, this instantaneous large-amplitude motion is unphysical and is presumably irrelevant below 100 fs, so xi was effectively frozen to remove the step. Wavepacket tests with opposite direction and different magnitudes of initial momentum are reported in the supporting sections.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points computed on both the CAS(6,6) and the extended CAS(8,12) references; no CASPT2 geometry optimization was possible for lack of analytical gradients in the programs used

geometry_source: Fully unconstrained CASSCF/6-31G* optimization of all critical points, with conical intersection funnels optimized using the methodology in Gaussian 03; CASPT2/6-31G* single points on the CASSCF reaction coordinate
method: CASPT2//CASSCF: the reaction coordinate computed at CASSCF and the energy profile re-evaluated at CASPT2 to recover dynamic correlation
active_space_orbital_description: Composition stated only: the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine moiety and the nitrogen lone pair. Electron and orbital counts are not given in the paper for this compound.
active_space_protocol: The space is described only by COMPOSITION, not by counts: 'the active space was chosen depending on the compounds considered but in each case included the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine and alkene moieties and the N lone pair. Depending on the alkene considered, the active space also included ketone pi and pi* orbitals, N or O lone pairs.' No electron or orbital totals are stated anywhere in the paper except for one enlargement test, so nel and norb are left blank on this row where they were not given. The CASPT2 zeroth-order wavefunction is a THREE-ROOT (S0, S1, S2) state-averaged CASSCF with 6-31G*, and the same state-averaged form was used elsewhere 'where necessary in order to avoid convergence problems'. Conical intersection funnels were optimized with the methodology in Gaussian 03 while the CASPT2 single points were run in MOLCAS-6.4.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (S0, S1, S2), state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: The key structural feature of the conical intersection is a TRIANGULAR C=N-O moiety, planar in the ground state; this deformation raises the ground-state energy while stabilizing the excited state, which is what creates the intersection. Most geometric parameters of the CI points for 3 and 4 agree to within 0.003 A. The distinguishing parameter is the C-O distance, 1.830 A in 3 against 1.818 A in 4. Because the CI point of 3 is low enough in energy, fast deactivation occurs and photocycloaddition — although energetically available — does not take place. Experimentally 3 is known not to photocycloadd to olefins.
Other: The whole mechanistic argument rests on an energy DIFFERENCE between two conical intersections whose geometries differ by no more than 0.003 A in most parameters and by 0.012 A in the one distance that matters — a resolution well inside what a CASPT2//CASSCF protocol can normally claim, and the paper offers no error estimate. The one active-space test performed is reassuring but was run on the other compound: enlarging compound 4's space to include the cyano pi orbitals, giving CAS(14,11), left 'both geometries and relative energies almost unaltered'. That result is used to justify the smaller spaces throughout, including for 3, which has no cyano group and therefore was never itself tested. The more serious limitation for reuse is that the paper never states electron or orbital counts for any space except that one enlargement, so these calculations cannot be reproduced from the text alone. Note also that the S1/S2 state averaging over three roots was applied 'where necessary in order to avoid convergence problems', so the reference is not uniform across all structures.
reference_short: Sampedro, Soldevilla, Campos, Ruiz et al., J. Org. Chem. 2008, 73, 8331
notes: One of two model isoxazolines whose experimentally opposite behaviour the calculations set out to explain: 3 shows fast deactivation while 4 undergoes photocycloaddition to give azetidines. Isoxazoline and the imine share a cyclic structure, which is why isoxazolines were chosen as models. A singlet excited state is reported in the literature to be involved in the photochemistry of these compounds.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/6-31G* single points on a three-root state-averaged CASSCF reference

active_space_orbital_description: The base space contains the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine moiety and the nitrogen lone pair, with counts not stated. The ENLARGED space, CAS(14,11), additionally includes the pi orbitals of the cyano group; this is the only active space in the paper for which explicit electron and orbital counts are given.
active_space_protocol: The space is described only by COMPOSITION, not by counts: 'the active space was chosen depending on the compounds considered but in each case included the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine and alkene moieties and the N lone pair. Depending on the alkene considered, the active space also included ketone pi and pi* orbitals, N or O lone pairs.' No electron or orbital totals are stated anywhere in the paper except for one enlargement test, so nel and norb are left blank on this row where they were not given. The CASPT2 zeroth-order wavefunction is a THREE-ROOT (S0, S1, S2) state-averaged CASSCF with 6-31G*, and the same state-averaged form was used elsewhere 'where necessary in order to avoid convergence problems'.
