nroots_per_mult: 3 (S0, S1, S2), state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: The electron-withdrawing cyano group, transmitted through the phenyl ring, puts a partial positive charge on the carbon of the C=N-O moiety. That partial positive charge interacts with the oxygen, shortening the C-O distance from 1.830 A in compound 3 to 1.818 A in 4. The authors suggest this deformation raises the energy of the conical intersection, so the system spends time in the excited state and photocycloaddition can occur. Experimentally 4 yields azetidines on irradiation. All other CI geometric parameters differ from those of 3 by no more than 0.003 A.
Other: This is the compound on which the paper's single active-space convergence test was run, and it is the right one to test: adding the cyano pi orbitals is the obvious worry for a substituent whose entire mechanistic role is electron withdrawal through the ring. The result — CAS(14,11) leaves 'both geometries and relative energies almost unaltered' — is a real check, and it matters because the mechanistic claim turns on a 0.012 A difference in one C-O distance between two otherwise near-identical conical intersections. Two caveats attach. First, the test confirms that the cyano pi orbitals need not be ACTIVE, not that the smaller space is accurate in absolute terms; no comparison against experiment or a higher method is offered for the CI energies themselves. Second, the mechanistic conclusion is stated tentatively by the authors — 'perhaps this deformation contributes to an increase in the energy of the CI point' — so the causal link from geometry to CI energy to reactivity is a proposal, not a computed result. CAS(14,11) is the only space in the paper with stated counts, so it is the only one recorded numerically here.
reference_short: Sampedro, Soldevilla, Campos, Ruiz et al., J. Org. Chem. 2008, 73, 8331
notes: The para-cyano substitution is the sole structural difference from compound 3, making the pair a clean test of substituent control over the competition between fast deactivation and photocycloaddition. Several 3-arylisoxazolines were synthesized and irradiated experimentally to confirm the theoretical predictions.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/6-31G* single points on a three-root state-averaged CASSCF reference

compound_name: 2-Isoxazoline (2) — [2+2] photocycloaddition regioselectivity with methyl vinyl ether, dimethyl vinyl amine and acrylaldehyde
geometry_source: Fully unconstrained CASSCF/6-31G* optimization of all critical points, with conical intersection funnels optimized using the methodology in Gaussian 03; CASPT2/6-31G* single points on the CASSCF reaction coordinate
method: CASPT2//CASSCF: the reaction coordinate computed at CASSCF and the energy profile re-evaluated at CASPT2 to recover dynamic correlation
active_space_orbital_description: Composition stated only: the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine and alkene moieties plus the nitrogen lone pair, extended depending on the alkene to include ketone pi and pi* orbitals and further N or O lone pairs. No electron or orbital counts are given.
active_space_protocol: The space is described only by COMPOSITION, not by counts: 'the active space was chosen depending on the compounds considered but in each case included the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine and alkene moieties and the N lone pair. Depending on the alkene considered, the active space also included ketone pi and pi* orbitals, N or O lone pairs.' No electron or orbital totals are stated anywhere in the paper except for one enlargement test, so nel and norb are left blank on this row where they were not given. The CASPT2 zeroth-order wavefunction is a THREE-ROOT (S0, S1, S2) state-averaged CASSCF with 6-31G*, and the same state-averaged form was used elsewhere 'where necessary in order to avoid convergence problems'. Conical intersection funnels were optimized with the methodology in Gaussian 03 while the CASPT2 single points were run in MOLCAS-6.4.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (S0, S1, S2), state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2/6-31G* relative energies in kcal/mol for the reaction with methyl vinyl ether, referred to the ground-state minimum: Franck-Condon S0 0.0, S1 158.4, S2 203.2; S1 minimum 124.5; CI-a S0 68.9 / S1 76.0; CI-b 85.3 / 88.7; CI-c 69.6 / 76.8; CI-d 82.5 / 85.5; products Prod-a -9.8, Prod-b -4.2, Prod-c -4.6, Prod-d -8.0. At the conical intersections both C=C (about 1.43 A) and C=N (about 1.36 A) lengthen relative to the ground state with clear pyramidalization at the atoms involved; the forming C-C bond is 2.09 A in the lower-energy CI-a and CI-c and 2.17 A in CI-b and CI-d, while the forming N-C bond runs from about 2.18 A in CI-a and CI-c to about 2.05 A in CI-b and CI-d. All four regiochemical outcomes are achievable, but there is a preference of at least 10 kcal/mol for the CI-a/CI-c regioisomer.
Other: Here the active space CHANGES with the alkene partner — ketone pi/pi* orbitals and additional N or O lone pairs are added as required — so the three alkene reactions studied with this isoxazoline are not described in a common space, and their CI energies are not strictly on one scale. That is a defensible choice, since each alkene contributes different orbitals to the forming bonds, but it means the comparison between methyl vinyl ether, dimethyl vinyl amine and acrylaldehyde carries an unquantified space-dependence on top of the chemistry. The regiochemical conclusion is robust to this concern because it compares four intersections WITHIN one reaction, where the space is fixed: CI-a and CI-c lie at 68.9 and 69.6 kcal/mol against 85.3 and 82.5 for CI-b and CI-d, a separation of 13-16 kcal/mol that no plausible space error would close. Compound 2 was chosen for the regioselectivity study because it behaves and deforms in the excited state like compound 4 while being smaller. As throughout the paper, no electron or orbital counts are stated, so the calculations cannot be reproduced from the text.
reference_short: Sampedro, Soldevilla, Campos, Ruiz et al., J. Org. Chem. 2008, 73, 8331
notes: Used for the regioselectivity study because of its similar excited-state behaviour and deformation to compound 4 and its smaller size. Reactions with methyl vinyl ether (Table 1 and Figure 3), dimethyl vinyl amine (Figure 4) and acrylaldehyde (Figure 5) are reported, with optimized CI geometries, CASPT2 S0/S1 relative energies and atomic charge distributions. Experimentally, 3-arylisoxazolines were irradiated in the presence of furan or ethyl acrylate (10 equivalents, 0.6 mmol substrate) to test the predictions.
correlation_correction: CASPT2/6-31G* single points on a three-root state-averaged CASSCF reference

compound_name: p-Benzosemiquinone radical anion — low-energy doublet states
point_group: D2h for the ground and all excited states; ground-state ROHF geometry re-optimized and frequencies computed under a C1 assumption to verify the D2h structure; a C1 test of the excited states gave only modest improvement
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized at ROHF (RHF for neutral p-benzoquinone) in D2h, with vibrational frequencies computed assuming C1 symmetry as a check; UHF was tried but rejected because the wavefunctions were contaminated by higher spin states. Excited-state geometries optimized at CASSCF assuming the same D2h symmetry as the ground state.
method: SCF-CI and CASSCF (also called FORS, fully optimized reaction space)
basis_set: Huzinaga (9s,5p) double-zeta contracted to [3s,2p] by the Dunning-Hay method; (3s)/[2s] for hydrogen; no diffuse functions
active_space_orbital_description: Seven doubly occupied molecular orbitals (1b2u, 1b1u, 1b3g, b3u, 2b1g, 1b2g and 2b1u), the singly occupied 2b3g orbital, and four unoccupied orbitals (au, 3b1u, 3b3g and 3b1g) — fifteen electrons in twelve orbitals. The 2b3g SOMO is a pi orbital with its largest contribution from oxygen, bonding between the carbons whose bonds shorten and antibonding between carbon and oxygen.
active_space_protocol: Chosen as 'the largest active space possible with current computational resources' — a resource-bounded rather than a physically converged selection, and the paper is explicit that this is a limitation. The orbitals are listed individually by symmetry label, so the space is fully auditable. Exploratory calculations probing the choice are reported rather than suppressed: lowering the symmetry to C1 gave only modest improvement in the vertical transition energies, and the authors state that 'including more pi-pi correlation by including more orbitals in the active space will probably give more accurate energies'.
nroots_per_mult: 6 doublet states reported
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 2B3g with a dominant configuration coefficient of 0.948. Vertical excitation energies in cm-1, CI then CASSCF: first 2B1u 26058 then 25578 (coefficient 0.783); 2Au 30277 then 26029 (0.915); second 2B1u 37738 then 37877 (0.733); 2B3u 25869 then 19837 (0.888); 2B1g 25893 then 22062 (0.893). The first symmetry-allowed transition, 2B3g to 2B1u, is a 2b1u to 2b3g pi excitation and falls within 9% (CASSCF) to 12% (CI) of the measured value. The second allowed transition, to 2Au at 26029 cm-1, agrees excellently with the experimental 27027 cm-1; the 4000 cm-1 gap between the CI and CASSCF values for this state implies a large electronic rearrangement on excitation. The third allowed transition, the second 2B1u at 37877 cm-1, is almost 20% above the measured 31746 cm-1. The symmetry-forbidden n to pi* transitions are computed at 19837 cm-1 (n+ to pi*), coinciding with a weak absorption observed near 18182-22222 cm-1. The n+(b3u) to n-(2b1g) orbital energy difference is 2480 cm-1. Adding an electron to p-benzoquinone lengthens the C-O and the shorter C-C bonds and contracts the longer C-C distances, consistent with the nodal properties of 2b3g; calculated unpaired spin densities are 0.182 at oxygen, 0.125 and 0.097 at successive carbons, against experimental 0.161-0.166, 0.149-0.154 and 0.092-0.093.
Other: The single most valuable result here is a documented state-ordering failure caused by removing ONE orbital: 'it was found that omitting the doubly occupied 1b2u orbital from the active space reversed the energy ordering of the 2Au and the first 2B1u excited states'. That is exactly the discrepancy the paper set out to resolve, since earlier CNDO/S work had also reversed those two states, so a one-orbital truncation reproduces a known semiempirical error. Any study of this system that trims the pi manifold must keep 1b2u. The authors are equally candid about where their own space is still too small: the second 2B1u state overshoots experiment by nearly 20% (37877 against 31746 cm-1), and they attribute it to the limited active space together with the fact that this state's CI expansion 'involves a number of large contributions in addition to the single excitation from 2b3g to 3b1u' — its reference coefficient of 0.733 is by far the lowest in the table, against 0.888-0.948 for every other state. So reference weight predicts which state the space fails on. Two further diagnostics are offered: no dynamic correlation is included anywhere, and the authors specifically recommend multireference CI, coupled cluster, or the CASSCF-based second-order perturbation method of Andersson, Malmqvist and Roos as the remedy; and although diffuse functions are known to improve anion transition energies, they judge the double-zeta basis sufficient here because the anion is delocalized. The 4000 cm-1 CI-to-CASSCF shift on the 2Au state shows that orbital relaxation, not just configuration mixing, matters for these excitations.
reference_short: Wheeler, J. Phys. Chem. 1993, 97, 1533
notes: p-Benzoquinones and their reduced semiquinone anions are ubiquitous in synthetic and biological electron-transfer assemblies, and absorption spectra are used to monitor charge transfer, which motivates characterizing the excited states. The experimental structure of the radical anion is unknown, so the calculated geometry is compared against electron and X-ray diffraction structures of neutral p-benzoquinone: the calculated C=O distance matches electron diffraction exactly, the C=C distance falls nearly midway between the electron and X-ray values, the C-C single bond is within 0.006 A of electron diffraction, and C-H is 0.018 A too short, described as typical for ab initio calculations. Experimental transition energies from UV-visible absorption, electron transmission spectroscopy, electron photodetachment and resonance Raman are compiled for comparison, with earlier PPP and CNDO semiempirical results. Hester and Williams and Harada and Inokuchi observed a weak absorption near 18182-22222 cm-1 attributed to a symmetry-forbidden n-pi* transition. Minimum-energy geometries are reported for every excited state calculated.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF and SCF-CI energies only; the paper recommends multireference CI, coupled cluster or CASSCF-based second-order perturbation theory as future improvements

compound_name: Uracil in water — solvent-induced shifts of the n-pi* and pi-pi* electronic excitations
point_group: Cs at the gas-phase equilibrium geometry; C1 in the solvated configurations sampled from dynamics
geometry_source: Ground-state CASSCF/cc-pVTZ optimized geometry for the gas-phase excitations. For the four monohydrated isomers, two parallel optimizations: full QM B3LYP/cc-pVDZ (used for the full QM calculations) and B3LYP/EFP1 with cc-pVDZ (used for the QM/EFP1 calculations). Bulk solvation sampled from a 5 ps molecular dynamics production phase with configurations taken every 100 fs.
method: Five-state state-averaged CASSCF with MCQDPT (multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory) corrections, interfaced to the effective fragment potential EFP1 water model; compared against full QM treatments where the water molecules sit in the QM region
software: Not stated in the extracted text (the SA-CASSCF/EFP and MCQDPT/EFP interfaces described are GAMESS features)
basis_set: cc-pVTZ for the excitation energies; cc-pVDZ for the B3LYP geometry optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in ten orbitals: two nitrogen lone pairs, one CC and two CO pi orbitals, three pi* orbitals, and the two CO lone-pair orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is taken over UNCHANGED from Merchan et al., and the reason given is specifically about geometry range rather than about the equilibrium structure: that work 'suggested that the large active space is necessary to describe the excited states of uracil when the geometry is away from the gas-phase equilibrium geometry, as will be the case in solution'. Since this study samples solvated configurations from molecular dynamics, geometric robustness of the space is the binding requirement. All MCQDPT calculations use a FIVE-STATE state-averaged CASSCF reference. State characters were verified individually — 'the n-pi* and pi-pi* excited states were confirmed by matching the gas-phase (excited state minus ground state) density differences'. In the QM/EFP1 treatment the water molecules do NOT contribute orbitals to the CASSCF active space; in the full QM comparison the occupied and unoccupied water orbitals are excluded from the active space too but ARE used in the MCQDPT perturbation corrections, so solvent-solute dynamic correlation enters only at the perturbative stage.
nroots_per_mult: 5 (five-state state averaging)
electronic_structure_description: Gas-phase vertical excitations with cc-pVTZ, as SA-CASSCF then MCQDPT, against experiment: n-pi* 5.32 then 4.85 eV (experimental range 4.4-5.16); pi-pi* 6.63 then 5.16 eV (experimental 5.08). Dipole moments: ground state 4.25 D, n-pi* 2.20 D, pi-pi* 6.39 D. Monohydrated n-pi* solvent shifts in eV for the four isomers, as SA-CASSCF QM/EFP then SA-CASSCF QM then MCQDPT QM/EFP then MCQDPT QM: isomer 1 -0.174, -0.183, 0.170, 0.244; isomer 2 -0.260, -0.268, 0.173, 0.195; isomer 3 -0.023, 0.004, 0.296, 0.322; isomer 4 0.019, -0.009, 0.362, 0.400. The EFP1 treatment recovers the full QM MCQDPT solvent shift to within 0.05 eV, with rms deviations of 0.045 eV for pi-pi* and 0.039 eV for n-pi*. In bulk water the maximum MCQDPT/EFP1 solvent shift is +0.45 eV for n-pi* and -0.20 eV for pi-pi*, the latter under-shifted by about 0.1 eV relative to experiment, attributed to neglected dispersion between the excited solute and nearby solvent. These shifts confirm that the two excited states CHANGE ORDER in solution, with pi-pi* becoming the lowest.
Other: The (14,10) space was adopted because of a property most active-space justifications ignore: robustness ACROSS GEOMETRIES rather than accuracy at one. Merchan et al.'s argument, quoted approvingly here, is that a large space 'is necessary to describe the excited states of uracil when the geometry is away from the gas-phase equilibrium geometry' — precisely the condition when configurations are drawn from a 5 ps molecular dynamics trajectory, where no structure is the optimized one. That makes geometric transferability the selection criterion, and it is the right one for solvent-sampling work. On the space's raw performance, bare SA-CASSCF is badly off for the bright state: 6.63 eV against an experimental 5.08, an error of 1.55 eV that MCQDPT reduces to 0.08 eV, while the n-pi* error falls from about 0.2-0.9 eV to within the experimental range. The correlation demand is therefore concentrated almost entirely in the pi manifold, mirroring what other nucleobase studies find. More striking is that CASSCF and MCQDPT disagree on the SIGN of the monohydrated solvent shifts: SA-CASSCF gives -0.174 to +0.019 eV for the four isomers while MCQDPT gives +0.170 to +0.362 eV — so the uncorrected space predicts the wrong direction of solvation for three of four isomers, and the conclusion that the two states swap order in solution rests entirely on the perturbative correction. Note also that the water molecules never enter the active space in any treatment; solvent-solute dynamic correlation appears only through the MCQDPT step, which is what makes the QM/EFP1 and full QM shifts agree to 0.05 eV.
reference_short: DeFusco, Ivanic, Schmidt & Gordon, J. Phys. Chem. A 2011, 115, 4574
notes: Motivated by understanding the photostability of DNA and RNA. Four monohydrated uracil isomers from the literature are used to validate the SA-CASSCF/EFP1 and MCQDPT/EFP1 interfaces against full QM calculations. Bulk solvation used 15 water molecules with configurations sampled every 100 fs over a 5 ps production phase. Computational cost scales steeply with QM-region size: one water in the QM region needs 120 min, two waters 3.0 GB/core and 200 min on 16 cores, and five waters close to 16 GB/core — forcing that run onto 2 cores for 2200 min, on 3.0 GHz Intel Xeon Harpertown processors. Two EFP coupling methods are compared; method 1 does not allow the EFP induced dipoles to relax in the field of the solute excited state. The ordering of the two excited states in solution may have consequences for the excited-state decay mechanism after photoexcitation to pi-pi*.
correlation_correction: MCQDPT (multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory) on the five-state SA-CASSCF reference, with solvent orbitals entering the perturbation corrections in the full QM calculations

compound_name: Benzene-OH-O2 peroxy radical (I2), cis-axial isomer (I2-c-ax) — bicyclisation to the bridged bicyclic peroxide
point_group: C1 (no spatial symmetry used except for O2, treated in D2h)
geometry_source: CASSCF/cc-pVDZ geometry optimizations followed by frequency calculations, with the negative-eigenvalue displacement vector inspected to verify transition-state connectivity; energies corrected with G3X zero-point energies
method: CASSCF with multireference Rayleigh-Schrodinger second-order perturbation theory (CASPT2); G3X(MP2) and G3X(MP2)-RAD composite methods for the full surface, with T1, D1 and spin-expectation diagnostics; master equation kinetics
software: MOLPRO (multireference calculations and UCCSD-ROHF); Gaussian 03 (UMP2/ROHF); MOLDEN (natural orbital visualization)
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for all CASSCF and CASPT2 — stated as 'the largest that our computational facilities would permit'
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(9,9): the pi and pi* orbitals deriving from the p orbitals of carbons 3-6, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C2-O15 and O15-O16 bonds, and the singly occupied molecular orbital localizing the radical on O16 of the peroxy group.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces, each built as a bond inventory of the specific rearrangement being described, and both validated by inspection at EVERY geometry rather than only at stationary points. For the bicyclisation paths the space is (9,9): the pi and pi* orbitals from the p orbitals of carbons 3-6, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C2-O15 and O15-O16 bonds, and the peroxy SOMO localized on O16. For the OOH channel it is (11,11): the pi and pi* orbitals of carbons 3-6, the peroxy SOMO, and sigma/sigma* pairs for O15-O16, C1-C2 and O12-H13. Consistency was enforced empirically: 'the natural orbitals obtained from diagonalization of the electron density matrix were visualized using MOLDEN to ensure that the active space remained consistent for all geometries', and every active orbital's natural occupation number stayed within 0.02 to 1.98. CASSCF geometry optimizations were followed by frequency calculations with the imaginary-mode displacement vector inspected to confirm each transition state connects the intended minima. In the CASPT2 step all excitations within the active space were considered and the electrons in all other non-core occupied orbitals were correlated through single and double excitations. Apart from O2, computed in 3-Sigma-g-minus symmetry, no spatial symmetry was used.

point_group: D-infinity-h/C-infinity-v linear for the 3-Sigma-minus ground state; Cs for the distorted 1A' component of the 1-Delta state

method: CASSCF, with unrestricted Hartree-Fock and UMP2 for comparison
software: HONDO-8 (CASSCF); GAUSSIAN-92 (unrestricted MP2), on a Convex C-240

relativistic_treatment: Effective core potentials of Stevens et al. for the inner electrons of zinc and tin
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight molecular orbitals: sigma(XH), sigma(HZn) and sigma(ZnX) together with their sigma antibonding partners, plus the open-shell pi(x,y) pair holding the two lone electrons.
active_space_protocol: A single space of constant composition for both molecules, defined by the sigma framework plus the open shell: the sigma(XH), sigma(HZn) and sigma(ZnX) bonding orbitals together with their sigma antibonding partners, plus the open-shell pi(x,y) pair holding the two lone electrons — eight electrons in eight molecular orbitals. Using the same recipe for HZnCH and HZnSnH is what allows the carbon-versus-tin comparison, since the space adapts to the substituted element by construction (sigma(XH) and sigma(ZnX) follow X) while the electron and orbital counts stay fixed. Geometries were optimized with analytical gradients and every stationary point characterized by computing and diagonalizing the Cartesian second-derivative matrix, transformed via the B matrix into internal symmetry coordinates to give physically meaningful force constants. Open shells were also treated at UHF with UMP2 correlation for comparison.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is a linear triplet 3-Sigma-minus at every level of theory, in agreement with experiment and previous theoretical work, in contrast to Hamilton et al. who found a bent structure at Hartree-Fock and linear only with correlation. Optimized bond distances in A for 3-Sigma-minus, as HF / MP2 / CASSCF / CISD (literature): Zn-C 1.9163 / 1.8633 / 1.9405 / 1.883; C-H 1.0761 / 1.0794 / 1.0960 / 1.083; Zn-H 1.5474 / 1.5010 / 1.5743 / 1.521. For the 1A' state: Zn-C 1.9973 / 1.9392 / 2.0651; C-H 1.0933 / 1.1027 / 1.1290; Zn-H 1.5585 / 1.5142 / 1.5922; HCZn angle 117 / 117 / 109 degrees; HZnC angle 174 / 172 / 173 degrees. The ground state arises from pairing the lone electron in the carbon sigma-sp orbital (the 3-sigma MO) of the CH 4-Sigma-minus state with the HZn sigma-sp electron, leaving two carbon pi(x,y) electrons in a pi MO. Those pi MOs correspond mainly to carbon px,y atomic orbitals, so the Zn-C bond is essentially SINGLE with no significant pi donation to the empty Zn px,y pair — consistent with a net spin population of 1.98 on carbon and a Zn-C bond order of 0.89, close to the 0.84 estimated for ZnCH2. Dissociation of the carbyne ground state does not correlate with the ground states of its fragments (HZn 2-Sigma-plus and CH 2-Pi, which give 1-Pi and 3-Pi) but correlates directly with the first excited 4-Sigma-minus state of CH. The first excited state is the singlet 1-Delta, which splits into A' and A'' components and shows a classical Renner-Teller distortion: both components rise at small bending angles, but after a low barrier the A' component stabilizes to a minimum near an HCZn angle of 120 degrees.
Other: The active space is built around the sigma framework plus the open-shell pi pair, and the paper shows directly what including the sigma ANTIBONDING orbitals costs: 'with respect to CASSCF results, a general lengthening of the bond distances is observed because of the inclusion of the sigma antibonding MOs in the active space'. That is a systematic geometric bias, visible in every bond — CASSCF gives Zn-C 1.9405 A against MP2's 1.8633 and CISD's 1.883, and Zn-H 1.5743 against 1.5010 and 1.521. So the space that is necessary to describe the dissociation and the open-shell coupling simultaneously overestimates bond lengths by 0.05-0.08 A relative to correlated single-reference methods, and CASSCF geometries from a space of this construction should be read with that offset in mind. The compensating strength is qualitative: the same space gets the LINEAR triplet ground state right at every level, whereas Hartree-Fock alone gave a bent structure in earlier work — a difference the authors attribute to nondynamical correlation, which is exactly what an eight-orbital sigma/sigma*/pi space captures. The space also has to span a dissociation whose asymptote is NOT the fragment ground states but the CH 4-Sigma-minus excited state, so a space chosen only from the equilibrium bonding picture would fail along the dissociation coordinate.

The second, '10e12a', correlates 10 electrons in 12 orbitals: ALL the 3d orbitals whether occupied or vacant in the ground state, the 3d correlating orbitals, the two low-lying pi*(bpy) orbitals, and two occupied orbitals with significant metal character. The second space is used ONLY for the metal-centred states corresponding to 3d-to-3d excitations.

Neither space alone could describe both manifolds, since MLCT states demand acceptor orbitals the MC space omits while MC states demand vacant 3d orbitals the MLCT space omits. Both CASSCF wavefunctions were optimized for a HIGH-SPIN state, S = 4, and then used as references for the correlated treatment. active_space_orbital_description: CAS(6,6): the six pi orbitals of the D6h ring holding six pi electrons.
active_space_protocol: A single CAS(6,6) pi space applied identically to all six D6h rings, which is the whole point: the systems are isoelectronic in the pi manifold, so holding the space fixed makes the comparison of bonding across first- and second-row elements attributable to the atoms rather than to the description. Geometries were optimized under a D6h CONSTRAINT 'whether or not this leads to the most stable structure', because the aim is to compare pi bonding at benzene-like geometries; frequency analysis then reports honestly which structures are genuine minima and which are not. The CASSCF wavefunction is invariant to nonsingular linear transformations of the six active orbitals, and the paper exploits that: the active orbitals are re-expressed either as orthogonal localized orbitals (the CiLC approach, with a subsequent CI over the same configuration list) or as NONORTHOGONAL valence-bond-like orbitals, giving alternative representations of one and the same CASSCF wavefunction. All calculations used 6-31G(d,p) in Cartesian form with six d components, run first in GAUSSIAN 98 and repeated in MOLPRO with identical results.

active_space_orbital_description: Active spaces are specified as symmetry-block orbital counts, not as electron/orbital totals. In the notation (a1 b2 b1 a2)/(closed a1 b2 b1 a2): 4-Sigma-minus used (8 2 2 0)/(2 0 0 0) for the valence states and (9 2 2 0)/(3 0 0 0) optimized for three Rydberg states; 4-Delta used (6 2 2 2)/(2 0 0 0) at short range and (7 2 2 1)/(2 0 0 0) at intermediate bond lengths to include the lowest sigma Rydberg orbital; 4-Pi used (6 4 3 0)/(2 0 0 0), adding three extra orbitals (two b1, one b2) to envelop the two lowest pi Rydberg orbitals; 4-Sigma-plus used (7 2 2 1)/(2 0 0 0); the doublet Sigma-minus, Sigma-plus and Delta states used (8 2 2 0)/(2 0 0 0) at short range and (6 2 2 0)/(2 0 0 0) beyond 1.26 A; 2-Pi used (6 4 3 0)/(2 0 0 0) and (6 2 2 0)/(2 0 0 0). active_space_protocol: The space is re-optimized PER STATE SYMMETRY and PER BOND-LENGTH REGIME rather than held fixed, because Rydberg states of different character dominate in different regions. The clearest case: for 4-Delta states the short-range space (6 2 2 2) is switched to (7 2 2 1) at intermediate bond lengths specifically because 'Rydberg states with cores corresponding to the electronically excited A' 3-Delta and A'' 3-Sigma-plus states of FO+ cross the nd-delta Rydberg states', so the lowest sigma Rydberg orbital must enter the space; the basis was adjusted in step, removing the most diffuse d and adding an s function. Similarly 4-Sigma-minus was computed from two spaces, one optimized for three Rydberg states and one for the valence states, with five states obtained in total. Quartets were computed first and used to guide the basis-set optimization, because 'these calculations demanded a larger basis set' and, since a 4-Sigma-plus state cannot be formed from the X 3-Sigma-minus ion core, quartet energies give the most efficient route to the ordering of the lowest Rydberg orbitals. All valence electrons were correlated with the 1s cores frozen, and the Davidson correction was applied to every MRCI energy. MOLPRO's MRCI is limited to five states of a given multiplicity and symmetry, which caps how many roots any one calculation can deliver.

electronic_structure_description: Valence and low-lying Rydberg states of FO computed as potential energy curves. The lowest quartet Rydberg states can only be built on the X 3-Sigma-minus core of FO+, whereas doublet states can also arise from the first and second excited core states of 1-Delta and 1-Sigma-plus symmetry — the three low-lying valence states of the XO+ ion core are what complicate the Rydberg pattern in halogen oxides. Because no 4-Sigma-plus state can be formed from the X 3-Sigma-minus core, the only 4A1 Rydberg states accessible at short range are 4-Delta states built from a d-delta Rydberg orbital on the 3-Sigma-minus ion. The A 2-Pi state, unlike in the other halogen monoxides, is calculated to be entirely repulsive for FO. States labelled f 4-Pi and g 4-Delta form part of the 3d complex. The computed ordering of Rydberg state symmetries DIFFERS from that computed for ClO, a consequence of the relative energies of the lowest electronic states of the FO+ and ClO+ cores. active_space_protocol: A single minimal CAS(4,4) used for every substrate: the pi and pi* orbitals of the alkene (or disilene) plus the HOMO and LUMO of CF2, i.e. exactly the four orbitals whose occupancy changes when the two new sigma bonds form. The definition is taken unchanged from the authors' earlier study, and the SAME space and basis (6-31G(d,p)) supply all geometries, zero-point energies and entropies for all six reactions, so substrate-to-substrate comparisons carry no space-dependence. Single-point energies were then computed at four levels on those geometries — CASSCF(4,4), MR-MP2(4,4), CR-CC(2,3) and UB3LYP — with basis sets from 3-21G up to 6-311++G(3d,p), which is what exposes the space's limitation (see Other). The paper reasons about the methods explicitly: MR-MP2 adds dynamic correlation perturbatively and so 'poses the risk of overestimating the stabilities for some less-diradical structures', while CR-CC(2,3), though single-reference, 'can balance the nondynamic and dynamic electron correlation effects in the different stages of reactions reasonably well'.
electronic_structure_description: At CASSCF(4,4)/6-311+G(d,p) the first barrier E1 for CF2 addition to substrates 1-5 falls in the range 15.5-21.6 kcal/mol; MR-MP2(4,4)/6-311+G(d,p) gives 6.7-15.2 and CR-CC(2,3)/6-311+G(d,p) gives 4.2-14.6 kcal/mol over the same set. The second barrier E2 is overestimated by CASSCF by 4.2-7.6 kcal/mol for every reaction studied. Earlier work by the same group, using CASSCF with 6-31+G(d) and 6-31G(d), found stepwise mechanisms with singlet diradical intermediates and E2 values of 0.1-5.7 kcal/mol for CF2 and C(OH)2 additions to ethylene and isobutene, and the stepwise mechanism for ethylene was already shown to become concerted once dynamic correlation is included.
Other: Ethylene is the simplest member and the one where the artificial stepwise mechanism had already been identified in earlier work, making it the calibration case for the whole series. The (4,4) space here is exactly the four orbitals that change occupancy — alkene pi and pi*, carbene HOMO and LUMO — so it cannot be faulted for omitting anything relevant; the failure is purely that CASSCF without dynamic correlation over-stabilizes the diradical it is designed to describe. A CAS(4,4) is the right space for the ORBITALS involved, and still the wrong level for the mechanism.

The definition is taken unchanged from the authors' earlier study, and the SAME space and basis (6-31G(d,p)) supply all geometries, zero-point energies and entropies for all six reactions, so substrate-to-substrate comparisons carry no space-dependence. Single-point energies were then computed at four levels on those geometries — CASSCF(4,4), MR-MP2(4,4), CR-CC(2,3) and UB3LYP — with basis sets from 3-21G up to 6-311++G(3d,p), which is what exposes the space's limitation (see Other). The paper reasons about the methods explicitly: MR-MP2 adds dynamic correlation perturbatively and so 'poses the risk of overestimating the stabilities for some less-diradical structures', while CR-CC(2,3), though single-reference, 'can balance the nondynamic and dynamic electron correlation effects in the different stages of reactions reasonably well'.
electronic_structure_description: The worked example in the text: ZPE-corrected energies at CASSCF(4,4)/6-311+G(d,p) predict the second barrier E2 to be 6.7 kcal/mol, whereas the same quantity is -0.2 kcal/mol at MR-MP2/6-311+G(d,p) and -0.7 kcal/mol at CR-CC(2,3)/6-311+G(d,p) — the CASSCF value is about 7.0 kcal/mol too high, and the correlated methods give a NEGATIVE barrier. E1 for this substrate lies within the 15.5-21.6 kcal/mol CASSCF range for the alkenes.
Other: This is the case the paper works through in detail, and it shows the failure at its sharpest: CASSCF gives a positive second barrier of 6.7 kcal/mol — a real intermediate with a real barrier to closure — while both correlated methods give -0.2 and -0.7 kcal/mol, meaning no barrier at all and hence no intermediate. The 7.0 kcal/mol overestimate is the largest in the series and sits at the top of the 4.2-7.6 kcal/mol range. A sign change in a barrier is not a quantitative error but a change of mechanism, and it happens here with the active space held fixed and only the correlation treatment varied. The headline finding is a MECHANISM created by the active space and destroyed by dynamic correlation. CASSCF(4,4) predicts that all six cycloadditions proceed stepwise through a singlet diradical intermediate, but the paper concludes that 'the stepwise mechanisms predicted at the CASSCF level are artificial because of their neglect of dynamic electron correlation', and that with 6-311G(d) or larger basis sets MR-MP2 and CR-CC(2,3) consistently give a CONCERTED mechanism. The error is quantified and systematic: the second barrier E2 is overestimated by CASSCF by 4.2-7.6 kcal/mol for every reaction in the set, and the first barrier E1 by comparable amounts (15.5-21.6 kcal/mol at CASSCF against 6.7-15.2 at MR-MP2 and 4.2-14.6 at CR-CC(2,3) for the alkenes). The authors connect this to a known pathology — 'a similar tendency of CASSCF to overstabilize singlet diradicals has been reported by several authors' — and it is the reason a minimal diradical-spanning space can manufacture an intermediate that does not exist. A CAS(4,4) is the right space for the ORBITALS involved, and still the wrong level for the mechanism.

compound_name: PO2 radical — ground and low-lying excited states, and anharmonic Franck-Condon simulation of single-vibrational-level emission
point_group: C2v for the bent states; the 1 2B1 state becomes LINEAR, with vibrational frequencies of sigma-g, pi-u and sigma-u symmetry
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations at RCCSD(T) and CASSCF levels for the relevant states, following earlier optimizations at other levels. Potential energy functions built from 34 single-point energies in the symmetric stretching coordinate and 29 in the bending coordinate — at RCCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVQZ for the X 2A1 state and at CASSCF/MRCI/aug-cc-pVQZ(no g) (second root only) for the 2 2A1 state — fitted to polynomial analytical forms and used to compute anharmonic vibrational wavefunctions.
method: CASSCF with internally contracted MRCI; RCCSD(T); CIS and MP2 for comparison; anharmonic Franck-Condon factor calculation including Duschinsky effects; iterative Franck-Condon analysis (IFCA)
basis_set: Basis sets up to aug-cc-pVQZ quality: aug-cc-pVQZ for the RCCSD(T) scans, aug-cc-pVQZ(no g) for the CASSCF/MRCI scans, cc-pVTZ and cc-pVQZ for selected Te values, 6-311G(2d) and 6-311+G(3df) for the CIS/MP2/CASSCF comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: Described only as a FULL VALENCE active space — 'all CASSCF calculations performed in this work had a full valence active space' — with no electron or orbital counts given anywhere in the paper, so nel and norb are left blank. All correlation calculations used the frozen core approximation. Configuration counts are quoted instead: over 1936 uncontracted and 8.96 million internally contracted configurations for the two-state calculations, and over 1487 and 7.3 million for the single-root ones.
active_space_protocol: The notable choice is not the space but the ROOT STRATEGY, and the paper argues both sides explicitly. For the reliable adiabatic energies Te, the CASSCF/MRCI calculations 'considered only the root of interest (the second root in the case of the 2 2A1 and 2 2B2 states) in both the CASSCF and MRCI stages', with two stated advantages: the CASSCF orbitals entering the MRCI are then optimized for the state concerned, whereas 'the averaged state CASSCF orbitals with equal weights for more than one root are not optimal for any state concerned, as they are a compromise of all states'; and the single-root CI space is significantly smaller, 7.3 against 8.96 million contracted configurations. Separately, TWO-state equal-weight calculations on X 2A1 and 2 2A1 were also run at both the CASSCF and MRCI stages for the vertical excitation energy and for one Te evaluation, so the same transition is computed both ways.
nroots_per_mult: Either one (the root of interest, state-specific) or two (X 2A1 and 2 2A1 with equal weights), depending on the quantity computed
electronic_structure_description: Ground state X 2A1, configuration (8a1)1. Geometries as re (A) and theta-e (degrees), with adiabatic Te in eV: X 2A1 gives 1.480/133.5 at CASSCF/6-311G(2d), 1.483/134.6 at RCCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ, 1.474/134.8 at RCCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVQZ, against experimental r0 values of 1.4665/135.3. Excited states with their configurations, Te in eV: 1 2B2 (5b2)1(8a1)2 at 1.39 (MP2) and 0.63 (MRDCI); 1 2A2 (1a2)1(8a1)2 at 2.29 (MP2) and 1.02 (MRDCI); 1 2B1 (8a1)0(3b1)1 at 3.80 (MP2), 3.53 (RCCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ) and 3.56 (MRDCI), becoming linear; 2 2B1 (2b1)1(8a1)2 at 3.51 (CASSCF/6-311G(2d)), 4.20 (MP2), 3.68 (RCCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ); 2 2A1 (7a1)1(8a1)2 at 3.89 (CASSCF/6-311G(2d)) against an experimental 3.77, with the MRCI/aug-cc-pVQZ(no g) potential energy function giving re = 1.574 A, theta-e = 115.8 degrees and frequencies 933 and 400 cm-1 against experimental 936 and 396; 2 2B2 (4b2)1(8a1)2 at 4.20 (CASSCF). Comparison of simulated and observed spectra led to REASSIGNMENT of the emitting single-vibrational-levels in the upper state, confirming the observed transition as 2 2A1 to X 2A1, revising the LIF excitation band assignments, and giving a revised T0 of 30660 cm-1 (against 30378 and 30392.8 cm-1 previously reported). The 2 2A1 equilibrium geometry is derived for the first time by iterative Franck-Condon analysis: re = 1.560 A, theta-e = 116.5 degrees.
Other: The instructive content here is a clearly reasoned argument for STATE-SPECIFIC rather than state-averaged orbitals, made in a case where the target is the second root of its symmetry. The paper's position is that averaged orbitals 'are not optimal for any state concerned, as they are a compromise of all states', so the reliable Te values come from single-root CASSCF/MRCI on the root of interest, with the side benefit of an 18% smaller contracted CI space (7.3 versus 8.96 million). Two-state equal-weight calculations were nonetheless run for the vertical excitation and one Te, so both strategies are represented — a useful pairing for anyone weighing the tradeoff, since state-specific optimization on an excited root risks root flipping while state averaging guarantees balance at the cost of accuracy for each state. The full-valence space itself is asserted rather than justified and its size is never stated, only its configuration counts. The most useful accuracy check is external and specific: the CASSCF/MRCI potential energy function for the 2 2A1 state reproduces the experimental vibrational frequencies to 3 and 4 cm-1 (933 and 400 against 936 and 396), whereas plain CASSCF/6-311G(2d) puts Te at 3.89 eV against an experimental 3.77 — so the MRCI correction on this full-valence reference is worth about 0.1 eV on the adiabatic energy while the shape of the surface is already excellent. Note that the derived 2 2A1 geometry (re = 1.560 A) comes from iterative Franck-Condon fitting to experiment, not from the ab initio calculation (1.574 A).
reference_short: Lee, Mok, Dyke et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 10130
notes: Motivated by the laser-induced fluorescence excitation and single-vibrational-level emission spectra of Lei et al., obtained from a mixture of PCl3 and O2 seeded in Ar, where earlier attempts at simulation gave 'in no case ... a satisfactory, even qualitatively correct, simulation of the experimental spectra'. Franck-Condon factors between the X 2A1 and 2 2A1 states were computed allowing for Duschinsky rotation and anharmonicity. Experimental geometrical parameters are r0 values from far-IR laser magnetic resonance and microwave work of Kawaguchi et al.; vibrational frequencies come from that work and from Hamilton (LIF), Qian et al. (IR laser absorption) and Lei et al. (LIF and dispersed fluorescence). MRDCI/TZ+2d+R results of Cai et al. are tabulated for comparison. The paper notes that CASSCF/MRCI is the appropriate method for these states but is computationally very demanding, so it was applied only where needed.
correlation_correction: Internally contracted MRCI on the full-valence CASSCF reference within the frozen core approximation; RCCSD(T) used independently for the ground state and selected excited states

compound_name: Oxyallyl (structure 1) — intermediate in the allene oxide to cyclopropanone rearrangement
geometry_source: All structures optimized with (U)B3LYP (6-31G* and 6-311G**) and with CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G*; harmonic frequencies at both levels characterize every stationary point and give zero-point energies; IRC calculations at (U)B3LYP/6-31G* and CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* confirm which minima each transition structure links
method: CASSCF for geometries and CASPT2N single points on a CASSCF(10,11) reference; (U)B3LYP; QCISD(T) and UQCISD(T) single points with Q1 diagnostics
software: GAUSSIAN 94 (most geometry optimizations); GAMESS 97 (CASSCF(4,4) optimizations of structures 1, 2 and 4); MOLCAS-4
basis_set: 6-31G* for CASSCF, CASPT2N, QCISD(T) and one DFT set; 6-311G** for the second DFT set
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(4,4) for the geometry optimizations and IRC paths. A separate CASSCF(10,11) — ten electrons in eleven orbitals — is the reference for the CASPT2N single points, chosen to include every natural orbital with occupation between 0.02 and 1.98 for each structure, plus additional orbitals for smooth convergence.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces with a division of labour. A CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* supplies geometries, frequencies and IRC paths for structures 1, 2 and 4, alongside parallel (U)B3LYP optimizations; unrestricted single-determinant forms were used throughout for structures 1, 4, 6 and 10 because the restricted solutions are unstable. A much larger CASSCF(10,11) then serves as the reference for single-point CASPT2N energies at the (U)B3LYP/6-31G* geometries, and its selection rule is quantitative and stated: 'on the basis of the results of several test calculations, the active space of 10 electrons and eleven orbitals was chosen, and it includes ALL NATURAL ORBITALS WITH OCCUPATION NUMBERS BETWEEN 0.02 AND 1.98 for each structure considered. Additional orbitals were included to ensure smooth convergence.' The molecular orbitals of the CASSCF wavefunction were fully optimized. Zero-point energies use unscaled frequencies — CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* for the CASSCF energies and (U)B3LYP/6-31G* for the DFT, QCISD(T), UQCISD(T) and CASPT2N single points. Multireference character is monitored independently by the Q1 diagnostic of Lee and co-workers.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol referred to cyclopropanone: 18.9 at CASSCF(4,4)//CASSCF(4,4); 12.6 at CASPT2N/CASSCF(10,11)//(U)B3LYP; 11.3 at (U)B3LYP/6-31G* and 12.0 with 6-311G**; 12.5 at both QCISD(T)//B3LYP and UQCISD(T)//UB3LYP. Q1 diagnostic values are 0.0303 (QCISD(T)) and 0.0231 (UQCISD(T)). The restricted solution is unstable, so unrestricted single-determinant forms were used. Oxyallyl has long been considered a potential intermediate in the rearrangement of allene oxide to cyclopropanone and in the ring-closing reactions of substituted cyclopropanones. The planar form is more stable than the perpendicular one by only 3.5 kcal/mol at the DFT geometries. The barrier to isomerization of substituted oxyallyls is about 16 kcal/mol.
Other: Oxyallyl is where the small and large spaces disagree most sharply in relative terms: CASSCF(4,4) puts it 18.9 kcal/mol above cyclopropanone while CASPT2N on the CASSCF(10,11) reference gives 12.6, and every other correlated method clusters at 11.3-12.5. The four-orbital space over-destabilizes the diradical intermediate by about 6 kcal/mol — the opposite sign to the diradical over-STABILIZATION documented for CASSCF elsewhere, and a reminder that the direction of the bias depends on what the intermediate is being compared against. Its Q1 diagnostic of 0.0303/0.0231 is modest, so the multireference character is real but not extreme, which is consistent with a (10,11) reference plus perturbation theory being sufficient. The occupation-window criterion (0.02 to 1.98) that defines that reference is the transferable part: it selects orbitals per structure rather than fixing a list, so the same eleven-orbital space follows the changing electronic structure along the whole rearrangement. The paper's central methodological verdict is that the SMALL space is the unreliable one, and it says so directly: 'one of the most striking aspects of these results is the close agreement of the energies calculated with the DFT and CASPT2N methods. Therefore one may conclude that the DFT method gives more reliable results than CASSCF(4,4).' Table 2 makes the size of the failure concrete — relative to cyclopropanone, CASSCF(4,4) places the six C3H4O species at 18.9, 24.0, 24.3, 41.2 and 28.7 kcal/mol where CASPT2N/CASSCF(10,11) gives 12.6, 30.6, 28.6, 41.8 and 38.9, with individual discrepancies up to 10 kcal/mol and errors in BOTH directions. A four-orbital space is enough to describe the oxyallyl diradical qualitatively but not to place it on a common energy scale with the closed-shell isomers, which is exactly the comparison the mechanism requires. The larger space is defined by an occupation-number window (0.02 to 1.98) applied structure by structure rather than by a fixed orbital list, so its composition adapts along the reaction while its size stays at (10,11).
reference_short: Hess, Eckart & Fabian, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1998, 120, 12310
notes: The rearrangement of allene oxide to cyclopropanone is found to proceed STEPWISE: allene oxide first converts to oxyallyl through a newly located transition structure (6), and the oxyallyl then closes disrotatorily through transition structure 4. Experimental context: oxidation of di-tert-butylallene gave the first isolable allene oxide, 1,3-di-tert-butylallene oxide, which rearranges to trans-2,3-di-tert-butylcyclopropanone. A Cs transition structure was also located that presumably links oxyallyl with the two cyclopropanones in a degenerate reaction, though no IRC was run to confirm it.

The rearrangement to 3-methylene-1,5-hexadiene is exothermic: the computed heat of reaction is -15.1 kcal/mol at CASSCF, -13.8 at CASPT2 and -11.5 at B3LYP, against -15.7 from group equivalents and -14.5 from Roth's experiments. Since the reactant lies above the product in energy, the transition state connecting the diradical to the reactant is the higher of the two, making passage over TS(1->2) rate-determining.

method: CASSCF for geometries with CASPT2 single points; RHF and MP2 also used
basis_set: ANO-L of split-valence double-zeta quality with polarization functions on heavy atoms, plus diffuse s and p Gaussians of exponent 0.02 at a floating center (or at the phenol ring centre of mass where the floating center was not optimized)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF geometry optimizations use 6 electrons in 6 orbitals: the six pi valence orbitals of phenol, except for the 1(pi-sigma*) state where the highest pi* orbital is replaced by the sigma* orbital. The CASPT2 single points use an enlarged space of 8 electrons in 8 orbitals — all valence pi orbitals of phenol plus the sigma* orbital — with one further pi orbital added for the clusters, localized mostly on the water oxygen or ammonia nitrogen.
active_space_protocol: Two different active spaces at two stages, with the CASPT2 space deliberately LARGER than the CASSCF one. For geometry optimization the space is six electrons in six orbitals: six pi valence orbitals of phenol for the 1(pipi*) state and the cation ground state, but for the 1(pi-sigma*) state 'the highest pi* orbital was replaced by the sigma* orbital'. For the CASPT2 single points 'the active space was enlarged to include all valence pi orbitals of phenol in addition to the sigma* orbital', giving eight electrons in eight orbitals; for the clusters an additional pi orbital, mostly on the water oxygen or ammonia nitrogen, was added on top. The same active space and basis were used for the excited-state and ground-state calculations of a given system, so state separations are internally consistent. A crucial technical device is a FLOATING CENTER carrying diffuse s and p Gaussians (exponent 0.02) to describe the diffuse sigma* orbital, its position optimized during geometry optimization of the 1(pi-sigma*) state; its effect on the S0 and pipi* states was negligible so it was omitted there, and in CASPT2 at non-sigma* geometries the diffuse functions were placed at the phenol ring centre of mass instead. Cs symmetry was imposed throughout, which is what prevents the 1(pi-sigma*) state (A'') from collapsing onto the ground or 1(pipi*) states (both A').

electronic_structure_description: CASPT2 vertical energies with adiabatic values in parentheses, in eV: 1(pipi*) 4.46 (4.24); 1(pi-sigma*) 5.77; cation ground state 2(pi) 8.46 (8.35). The adiabatic 1(pipi*) value is about 0.26 eV below the experimental 36346.7 cm-1 (4.50 eV); the 1(pi-sigma*) vertical energy of 5.77 eV matches Lorentzon et al.'s 5.78 eV, while the vertical ionization energy of 8.46 eV exceeds their 8.21 eV. Along the OH detachment coordinate the ground state, the 1(pipi*) state and the cation ground state all rise in approximately parallel fashion while the 1(pi-sigma*) profile is essentially REPULSIVE. At the ground-state equilibrium geometry the optimized 1(pipi*) state lies below the optimized 1(pi-sigma*) state, so 1(pipi*) is the lowest excited singlet; above a certain excess energy the repulsive 1(pi-sigma*) state predissociates it. In a multidimensional picture the 1(pipi*)/1(pi-sigma*) crossing becomes a conical intersection once out-of-plane A'' modes lift the accidental degeneracy, and the lower adiabatic sheet then carries a barrier near the intersection. The sigma* orbital is diffuse and largely localized near the hydroxyl proton, with antibonding character with respect to the O-H bond; its form at R(OH) = 1 A and 2 A is shown in Figure 2.

The 1(pi-sigma*) state is obtained by SUBSTITUTING sigma* for the highest pi* orbital rather than by enlarging the space, keeping the CASSCF optimization at (6,6) while changing its character entirely — possible only because Cs symmetry makes the state A'' and thus non-collapsible onto the A' ground and 1(pipi*) states. The sigma* orbital's diffuseness (Figure 2 shows it spreading well beyond the molecule at R(OH) = 2 A) is handled by a floating center carrying diffuse s and p functions, whose position is optimized only for that state because its effect elsewhere was 'negligibly small'. The CASPT2 space is then enlarged to (8,8), all valence pi plus sigma*, so the correlated energies rest on a larger reference than the geometries — a deliberate asymmetry, since the geometry only needs the state's shape while the energy needs its correlation. Accuracy check: the 1(pi-sigma*) vertical energy of 5.77 eV agrees to 0.01 eV with independent CASPT2 work, while the ionization potential differs by 0.25 eV, so the space is better calibrated for the neutral excited states than for the cation. The transferable device here is the orbital SUBSTITUTION rather than enlargement: for the 1(pi-sigma*) state the highest pi* orbital is swapped out for sigma*, keeping the space at (6,6) while completely changing what it describes. That works only because Cs symmetry is imposed — the 1(pi-sigma*) state transforms as A'' while the ground and 1(pipi*) states are A', so the excited state 'cannot collapse to the ground state or to the 1(pipi*) excited state' during optimization. Without that symmetry constraint a state-specific optimization of a repulsive, diffuse state embedded below a bound one would be unstable. The second device is the floating center: the sigma* orbital is so diffuse that ordinary atom-centred basis functions cannot describe it, so diffuse s and p Gaussians ride on an optimizable centre, which the authors verified matters only for the sigma* state and omitted elsewhere. compound_name: Vinylcyclopropane (parent) — rearrangement to cyclopentene and competing diradical stereoisomerization
point_group: C1, except where Cs is noted for individual stereoisomerization transition structures
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at (U)B3LYP/6-31G* with GAUSSIAN 94; closed-shell wavefunctions for reactants and products, open-shell for all other structures. CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* single points on those DFT geometries. For the parent system, fully optimized CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* structures were also obtained and used for single-point MRCI.
method: CASSCF(4,4) single points on (U)B3LYP geometries; MRCI single points for the parent system; Yamaguchi spin correction applied to open-shell singlet DFT energies; quasiclassical trajectory dynamics on a parametrized AM1 surface
basis_set: 6-31G* for DFT, CASSCF and one set of MRCI calculations; cc-pVDZ for the second MRCI set
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(4,4) — four electrons in four orbitals. The paper gives only the count; the identity of the four orbitals is not stated anywhere in the text, so no composition is recorded.
active_space_protocol: The active space is used only for SINGLE-POINT energies on DFT geometries: 'geometry optimizations using UB3LYP/6-31G* calculations were followed by CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* single point calculations'. Reactants and products were computed with closed-shell wavefunctions and all other structures with open-shell ones. Three energy scales are reported and kept distinct: E1 is (U)B3LYP/6-31G* with unscaled zero-point corrections; E2 is CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G*//(U)B3LYP/6-31G* WITHOUT zero-point correction; E2,ZPE adds the (U)B3LYP zero-point energy to E2. A fourth scale, E(SC), applies the Yamaguchi spin-correction to the open-shell singlet DFT energies, removing triplet contamination by mixing the triplet energy at the same geometry. The paper states the active space only as '(4,4)' and never lists which four orbitals it contains, so the orbital composition is not recorded here. Separately, single-point MRCI calculations with 6-31G* and cc-pVDZ were run on FULLY OPTIMIZED CASSCF(4,4) structures for the unsubstituted system.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol referred to transition structure 2 (the concerted si shift), given as E1 / E(SC) / E2 / E2+ZPE. Rearrangement structures: s-trans reactant t-1 at -46.9 / -42.8; gauche reactant g-1 at -45.2 / -41.1; product 5 at -67.7 / -63.6; transition structure 2 at 0.0 throughout; 3 at -1.6 / 1.2 / 1.6 / 1.1; 4 at -2.6 / 2.2 / 0.3 / -0.1. Stereoisomerization of gauche vinylcyclopropane: 6 at -5.0 / -0.4 / -3.1 / -3.7; 7 at -5.4 / -0.9 / -3.2 / -4.0. Stereoisomerization of s-trans vinylcyclopropane: 8 at -5.9 / -2.8 / -4.3 / -4.8; 9 at -6.1 / -3.3 / -4.0 / -4.4; 10 at -5.4 / -1.5 / -2.6 / -3.4; 11 at -5.9 / -1.7 / -3.5 / -4.4. The activation barrier is 46.9 kcal/mol (E1). Structure 2 is the transition state for the si shift; 3 and 4 are higher-energy transition structures involved in the ar (3), sr (4) and ai (3+4) pathways. Structure 8 lies 4.3 (4.8) kcal/mol below 2, and structure 10 has Cs symmetry. The C-C bond lengths of structure 2 are almost equal, as expected for an allyl radical.
Other: The parent is the only system for which MRCI was run, and it is therefore the calibration point for the whole study. Single-point MRCI on FULLY OPTIMIZED CASSCF(4,4) structures agrees generally with the CASSCF(4,4)//(U)B3LYP energies but not everywhere — structure 4 comes out 0.9 kcal/mol above transition structure 2 at MRCI against 0.2 and 0.3 kcal/mol by the other two methods — and carries about 1 kcal/mol of basis-set dependence between 6-31G* and cc-pVDZ. That matters because the entire mechanistic question here concerns energy differences of 0-3 kcal/mol among structures 2, 3 and 4. MRCI also reproduces the experimental barrier more closely than either (U)B3LYP or CASSCF, so on this surface the active space alone is not the accurate level. The quasiclassical trajectory work of Doubleday et al., built on an AM1 potential parametrized to the MRCI energies and the UB3LYP IRC and started from saddle points 2, 3 and 4, gave stereochemical predictions in close agreement with experiment — an independent validation that these three structures are the right ones. point_group: C1, except where Cs is noted for individual stereoisomerization transition structures
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at (U)B3LYP/6-31G* with GAUSSIAN 94; closed-shell wavefunctions for reactants and products, open-shell for all other structures. CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* single points on those DFT geometries. For the parent system, fully optimized CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* structures were also obtained and used for single-point MRCI.
method: CASSCF(4,4) single points on (U)B3LYP geometries; MRCI single points for the parent system; Yamaguchi spin correction applied to open-shell singlet DFT energies; quasiclassical trajectory dynamics on a parametrized AM1 surface
basis_set: 6-31G* for DFT, CASSCF and one set of MRCI calculations; cc-pVDZ for the second MRCI set
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(4,4) — four electrons in four orbitals. The paper gives only the count; the identity of the four orbitals is not stated anywhere in the text, so no composition is recorded.
active_space_protocol: The active space is used only for SINGLE-POINT energies on DFT geometries: 'geometry optimizations using UB3LYP/6-31G* calculations were followed by CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G* single point calculations'. Reactants and products were computed with closed-shell wavefunctions and all other structures with open-shell ones. Three energy scales are reported and kept distinct: E1 is (U)B3LYP/6-31G* with unscaled zero-point corrections; E2 is CASSCF(4,4)/6-31G*//(U)B3LYP/6-31G* WITHOUT zero-point correction; E2,ZPE adds the (U)B3LYP zero-point energy to E2. A fourth scale, E(SC), applies the Yamaguchi spin-correction to the open-shell singlet DFT energies, removing triplet contamination by mixing the triplet energy at the same geometry. The paper states the active space only as '(4,4)' and never lists which four orbitals it contains, so the orbital composition is not recorded here. Separately, single-point MRCI calculations with 6-31G* and cc-pVDZ were run on FULLY OPTIMIZED CASSCF(4,4) structures for the unsubstituted system.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol referred to transition structure 2, as E1 / E(SC) / E2 / E2+ZPE: reactant t-1 at -44.2 / -39.8 (lowest energy conformer); gauche reactant g-1 at -42.7 / -38.3 (lowest energy conformer); product 5 at -61.2 / -56.8, this being the lowest energy conformation, (3R,4S)-3,4-dimethylcyclopentene, with one diastereomer 0.7 kcal/mol higher and another 2.3 kcal/mol higher; 2 at 0.0 throughout, with a relative energy of 0.7 kcal/mol quoted for structure 12; 3 at -0.6 / 3.5 / 2.0 / 1.6; 4 at -1.8 / 3.2 / 1.4 / 1.1. Stereoisomerization: 7 at -5.0 / -0.2 / -2.5 / -3.3; 10 at -5.5 / -1.0 / -3.4 / -3.6; 11 at -5.2 / -0.4 / -3.0 / -3.8.
Other: The dimethyl case is the one where product stereochemistry is resolved, with three diastereomeric cyclopentenes spanning 2.3 kcal/mol — small enough that the choice of energy scale matters, since E2 carries no zero-point correction while E1 and E(SC) do. On the transition structures the pattern matches the rest of the series: raw DFT places 3 and 4 below the concerted transition structure 2 (-0.6 and -1.8 kcal/mol) while both the spin-corrected DFT (+3.5, +3.2) and the CASSCF(4,4) single points (+2.0, +1.4) place them above. The consistency of that sign flip across all four substrates, computed at one fixed (4,4) space, is the strongest evidence in the paper that the raw open-shell DFT energies are contaminated rather than that the active space is inadequate — though without MRCI on the substituted systems, that conclusion rests on transfer from the parent. On the parent system the relative energies of the three rearrangement transition structures come out as -1.6 and -2.6 kcal/mol at plain (U)B3LYP, +1.2 and +2.2 after the Yamaguchi spin correction, and +1.6 and +0.3 at CASSCF(4,4) — so uncorrected DFT puts structures 3 and 4 BELOW the concerted transition structure 2 while both the spin-corrected DFT and the active-space treatment put them above. compound_name: Phenol and phenoxyl radical — O-H bond strength as a reference test of correlation treatments
geometry_source: Full geometry optimizations at the B3LYP, UMP2 and CASSCF levels; the CASPT2 energy computed at the CASSCF-optimized geometry
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 (CASSCF plus full MP2-level correlation correction); B3LYP, UMP2, PUMP2, ROHF, UHF and PUHF for comparison, with spin projection applied to remove higher-spin contaminants from unrestricted doublet wavefunctions
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: 6-31G** for most calculations; 6-31G* for the CASSCF and CASPT2 bond-strength work and for CASSCF(10,10)
active_space_orbital_description: The FULL pi-electron active space: full configuration interaction of the 8 pi electrons of phenol and the 7 pi electrons of phenoxyl radical, in both cases within a subset of 7 pi molecular orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A full pi-electron space applied to both the closed-shell parent and the open-shell radical, so the bond dissociation energy is a difference between two calculations of identical construction. The stated deficiency is what the space OMITS: 'the full pi CASSCF approach considerably underestimates dynamic correlation effects in phenol, because it neglects sigma-pi correlation'. CASPT2 on the same reference supplies that missing correlation. Spin projection was applied separately to the unrestricted methods to remove higher-spin contamination from doublet wavefunctions.
electronic_structure_description: O-H bond strengths in kJ/mol for a set of reference molecules, as B3LYP/6-31G** / PUMP2/6-31G** / CASSCF/6-31G* / CASPT2/6-31G* against experiment: H-OH 501.4 / — / — / — against 498 plus or minus 4; H-OCH3 444.6 / — / — / — against 436.0 plus or minus 3.8; H-O2H 364.7 / — / — / — against 369.0 plus or minus 4.2; H-O2CH3 359.2 / — / — / — against 370.3 plus or minus 2.1; H-OC6H5 (phenol) 375.0 / 376.2 / 253.4 / 377.3 against 361.9 plus or minus 8. Taking zero-point energy into account lowers the predicted phenol O-H bond strength by about 33 kJ/mol. The p-alkyl substituent in cresol slightly weakens the O-H bond, consistent with p-cresol's lower redox potential than phenol. The reason the full pi space fails for phenol is stated to be the high delocalization of the corresponding orbital.
Other: This is one of the largest single active-space failures recorded in this database, and the paper flags it in its own table by underlining and bolding the value. A FULL pi-electron CASSCF — 8 electrons in 7 pi orbitals for phenol, the complete pi manifold — gives an O-H bond strength of 253.4 kJ/mol against an experimental 361.9, an error of 108 kJ/mol, while B3LYP gives 375.0, PUMP2 376.2 and CASPT2 377.3, all within about 15 kJ/mol of experiment. The diagnosis is precise and general: a full pi space 'considerably underestimates dynamic correlation effects in phenol, because it NEGLECTS SIGMA-PI CORRELATION', and the effect is amplified by the high delocalization of the relevant orbital. Since breaking an O-H bond is a sigma process while the space is entirely pi, the space cannot describe the correlation change that accompanies dissociation — completeness within the pi manifold is no protection when the reaction coordinate lies outside it. The remedy is CASPT2 on the same reference, which recovers the sigma-pi correlation and lands within 16 kJ/mol of experiment. The practical rule: a 'complete' active space is complete only with respect to the orbitals it contains, and for bond-breaking outside that subspace the uncorrected CASSCF energy can be worse than DFT by two orders of magnitude in accuracy.
reference_short: Shamovsky, Riopelle & Ross, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 1061
notes: Reference molecules used to validate the theoretical methods before applying them to tyrosine coupling. Bond strengths were obtained by computing the energy of homolytic dissociation. All levels except CASSCF/6-31G* show marked accuracy across the set. Hydrogen-bonded complexes of p-cresol with hydroperoxyl radical, tyrosyl radical and peroxynitrous acid were also studied at B3LYP/6-31G**; no barrier to hydrogen abstraction from p-cresol exists for hydroxyl radical, consistent with its extreme oxidative power.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 — CASSCF with a full MP2-level electron correlation correction — computed at the CASSCF-optimized geometry

compound_name: Stacked diphenoxyl dimer (VIIp) — pi-stacked dimer of two phenoxyl radicals
geometry_source: Full geometry optimization at CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G** for both monomer and dimer, with CASPT2(2,2)/6-31G** single points on those geometries; B3LYP/6-31G**, UMP2/6-31G** and Hartree-Fock optimizations for comparison. To avoid size-consistency problems in the CASSCF(2,2) and CASPT2(2,2) dimerization energies, the monomer energy was computed by separating the dimer into two non-interacting monomers 20 A apart.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 (CASSCF plus full MP2-level correlation correction); B3LYP, UMP2, PUMP2, ROHF, UHF and PUHF for comparison, with spin projection applied to remove higher-spin contaminants from unrestricted doublet wavefunctions
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: 6-31G** for most calculations; 6-31G* for the CASSCF and CASPT2 bond-strength work and for CASSCF(10,10)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(2,2): two pi orbitals of the dimer, its HOMO and LUMO. A larger CASSCF(10,10) was also run, its active space 'formed from five inner pi-MO of each phenoxyl unit'.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces of very different size are compared directly. The minimal (2,2) holds only the HOMO and LUMO of the dimer — the two orbitals whose occupancy changes on forming the stacked pair — and is the reference for CASPT2. The (10,10) is built symmetrically from five inner pi orbitals on each phenoxyl unit. The rationale for combining CASSCF(2,2) with MP2 is stated explicitly: 'the three-determinant CASPT2(2,2) method ensures that the resulting wave functions of both monomer and dimer are eigenvectors of the S2 operator, and that dynamic electron correlation effects are taken into account. The first component (CASSCF) recovers static electron correlation, whereas the second (MP2) evaluates dynamic electron correlation effects including sigma-pi correlation.' Size consistency was handled by computing the monomer as a 20 A separated dimer.
electronic_structure_description: Dimerization energies in kJ/mol relative to two isolated phenoxyl radicals, with the C-O bond length in the monomer in parentheses and dimer geometric parameters following: ROHF/6-31G** +86.8 (1.329), C-O 1.216, o-o' 2.694, O-p' 2.728, delta 2.67; UHF +266.0 (1.254), same geometry; PUHF +518.1 (1.254); UMP2 -330.2 (1.225), C-O 1.264, o-o' 2.543, O-p' 2.455, delta 2.52; PUMP2 -129.2 (1.225), same geometry; CASSCF(2,2) -18.7 (1.208), C-O 1.224, o-o' 2.710, O-p' 2.740, delta 2.68; CASPT2(2,2)//CASSCF(2,2) -65.8 (1.208), same geometry; CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G* -7.0 (1.256), o-o' greater than 2.8; B3LYP/6-31G** -15.9 (1.258), C-O 1.248, o-o' 2.765, O-p' 2.693, delta 2.74. Vibrational frequency calculations show the C2h stacked structure is a genuine minimum only at correlated levels (MP2/6-31G* and B3LYP/6-31G**); at HF/6-31G** it is a transition state with one imaginary frequency.
Other: The two active spaces disagree with each other and both disagree with the correlated treatments, in a way that isolates exactly what is missing. CASSCF(2,2) gives a dimerization energy of -18.7 kJ/mol and the much larger CASSCF(10,10) gives -7.0 — enlarging the pi space makes the binding WEAKER, not better — while CASPT2 on the (2,2) reference gives -65.8 and PUMP2 gives -129.2. The paper's explanation is the same as for the phenol bond strength: 'the CASSCF(2,2) and CASSCF(10,10) methods significantly underestimate the dimerization energy in comparison with the PUMP2 prediction' because a pure pi space neglects sigma-pi correlation, and 'the enormous difference between dimerization energies predicted by the CASSCF(2,2) and CASPT2(2,2) methods confirm that dynamic electron correlation effects are, in fact, extremely important'. So a tenfold enlargement of the active space buys nothing here while a perturbative correction on the minimal space changes the answer by a factor of 3.5 — the deficiency is a correlation deficiency, not a space-size deficiency, and no amount of pi orbitals fixes it. The geometry responds the same way: CASSCF(10,10) pushes the ortho-carbon separation beyond 2.8 A while the correlated methods contract it to 2.45-2.54 A. PUMP2 is flagged as potentially affected by residual spin contamination that could artifactually stabilize the dimer, which is why the CASPT2(2,2) route — guaranteed to give S2 eigenvectors for both monomer and dimer — was adopted as the arbiter.

notes: One of several dimeric structures derived from tyrosyl radicals whose relative stabilities are compared in Table 3. Dimerization causes significant geometric change in the phenoxyl moieties. The energy of two isolated phenoxyl radicals is the zero of the scale.

geometry_source: DFT geometry optimizations with analytical frequency calculations for neutral bithiophene and its radical cation in Gaussian 94; CASSCF geometry optimizations and vibrational analyses for the ground and selected excited states of both planar rotamers in DALTON
method: CASSCF with multiconfigurational linear response for transition energies and oscillator strengths; independent CASSCF calculations on the vertical excited states; DFT for comparison; resonance Raman and electronic absorption spectroscopy
active_space_orbital_description: Eleven active electrons in the 10 valence-pi orbitals, the space chosen on the basis of MP2 natural orbital occupation numbers.
active_space_protocol: The space is selected by a NUMERICAL criterion from an independent calculation: 'the active space was selected on the basis of MP2 natural orbital occupation numbers and comprised the 10 valence-pi orbitals containing 11 active electrons'. So the full valence pi manifold enters, with the MP2 natural orbital occupations used to confirm which orbitals qualify rather than a chemical guess. The same (11,10) space serves the ground state, the vertical excited states, the multiconfigurational linear response calculations, and the excited-state geometry optimizations of both rotamers, so all comparisons in the paper rest on one reference. Excited states were chosen for optimization on the basis of transition energies and oscillator strengths from linear response at the ground-state optimized geometries. Both a 'vertical Hessian' at the ground-state geometry and an 'adiabatic Hessian' at each optimized excited-state geometry were computed to establish which states are genuine minima.
nroots_per_mult: First three excited doublet states of each symmetry
electronic_structure_description: Ground state 1 2Bg. Vertical excitation energies from CASSCF linear response, with oscillator strengths in the dipole length and velocity representations: 1 2Au at 1.75 eV (14122 cm-1, 709 nm), f = 0.0032/0.0024; 2 2Au at 2.05 eV (16524 cm-1, 606 nm), f = 0.1906/0.1577; 3 2Au at 2.77 eV (22375 cm-1, 447 nm), f = 0.3564/0.3206. Dipole-forbidden Bg states at 2.22, 4.11 and 4.63 eV and Ag states at 6.83, 7.06 and 7.67 eV; Bu states at 7.06 eV (f = 0.0000/0.0005) and 7.25 eV (f = 0.0066/0.0085). Independent CASSCF calculations on the vertical excited states give 1.79, 2.28 and 3.42 eV for the three 2Au states. Experimental transition energies are 2.10 and 2.91 eV; the absorption spectrum shows a band at 590 nm and a strong one at 425 nm. The third 2Au state contains two main configurations with weights 0.27 and 0.45. The vertical Hessian is positive definite for 1 2Au but has one negative eigenvalue for 2 2Au and 3 2Au; at the optimized geometry the adiabatic Hessian for 3 2Au becomes positive definite, so optimization of 1 2Au and 3 2Au leads to real minima.
Other: The s-trans rotamer carries the paper's key methodological comparison, and the numbers are unambiguous: from the SAME (11,10) space, linear response gives errors of 2% and 5% against experiment while separately converged excited-state CASSCF gives 9% and 18%. State-specific orbital relaxation, which one might expect to improve an excited state, makes it markedly worse here because it destroys the balance between the states being compared. The active space itself is defensible — the full valence pi manifold, confirmed by MP2 natural orbital occupations — so the error is procedural rather than a space deficiency. A second useful detail is the Hessian bookkeeping: the vertical Hessian (computed at the ground-state geometry) is positive definite only for 1 2Au, while 2 2Au and 3 2Au each show one negative eigenvalue, and only after optimization does 3 2Au become a genuine minimum. Reporting both vertical and adiabatic Hessians is what distinguishes a real excited-state minimum from a saddle point here, and 2 2Au never becomes one. The paper measures the same excitation energies two ways from ONE active space and finds a large discrepancy between them, which is the transferable result. Multiconfigurational linear response on the (11,10) reference underestimates the experimental transition energies by 2% and 5%, while INDEPENDENT CASSCF calculations on the vertical excited states — the same space, but each state optimized separately — are in error by 9% and 18%. For the s-trans rotamer that is 1.79, 2.28 and 3.42 eV from the state-specific calculations against 1.75, 2.05 and 2.77 eV from linear response, with experimental values of 2.10 and 2.91 eV. The lesson is that with a fixed space the response-theory route is markedly more accurate for vertical excitations than separately converged excited-state CASSCF, because the latter allows each state its own orbital relaxation and so loses the balance between states. Anyone quoting excitation energies from a CASSCF calculation should therefore say which of the two procedures produced them.
reference_short: Keszthelyi, Grage, Offersgaard & Wilbrandt, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 2808
notes: The radical cation was generated radiolytically in a low-temperature glassy matrix and studied by electronic absorption and resonance Raman spectroscopy at 425 and 550 nm excitation, with a 248 nm 20 ns excimer pulse. Figure 5c gives the valence pi-orbital correlation diagram for s-cis to s-trans interconversion of the neutral, and Figure 5d the corresponding state correlation diagram for the radical cation, both with the C2 axis conserved.
