compound_name: Pyrene radical cation (Py+) — photostability via sloped conical intersections
point_group: D2h for all CASSCF geometry optimizations, matching the planar-constrained MMVB structures
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations within D2h symmetry for the D0, D1 and D2 minima. Conical intersections optimized at CASSCF in a REDUCED (13e,14o) active space, with full (15e,16o) CASSCF energies then computed at the resulting crossing structures. CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries. MMVB structures optimized with planar constraints.
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 as benchmarks for a hybrid QM/MM molecular mechanics-valence bond (MMVB) force field, for which an analytical energy gradient for cations was implemented in this work
basis_set: 6-31G*, including polarization d functions on the carbon atoms
active_space_orbital_description: The FULL pi active space: 15 pi electrons distributed in 16 valence pi orbitals. A reduced (13e,14o) space is used for conical intersection optimization and as the CASPT2 reference.
active_space_protocol: Three distinct uses of two spaces, each forced by a stated computational limit. The full (15e,16o) pi space is used for minima and for single-point energies, and the paper quantifies why it cannot be used everywhere: 'CASSCF presently has a practical limit of around 10^7 configuration state functions (e.g., Py+ with 15 electrons in 16 active orbitals and D2h point group symmetry)' — this molecule sits AT that limit. Conical intersections therefore had to be optimized in a reduced (13e,14o) space 'as computationally expensive orbital state-averaging procedures are required for such calculations', with full-space energies recomputed at the resulting geometries. For CASPT2 'we also had to reduce the reference space to (13e,14o), keeping the CASSCF optimized orbitals frozen with the (15e,16o) active space' — so the CASPT2 reference orbitals come from the large space while the reference configurations come from the small one. The choice of a multiconfigurational method is argued from first principles: the one-electron approximation 'is unreliable, because so many problems involve interaction of many configurations', and CASSCF 'fully accounts for configuration interactions within a pi-electron system'.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (D0, D1, D2); state averaging required for the conical intersection optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in kcal/mol as CASSCF / CASPT2 / MMVB: D1 at 22.9 / 23.7 / 21.5; D2 at 39.9 / 36.2 / 47.0, against an experimental D2 value of about 36 kcal/mol. At the D1 minimum the D0-D1 energy gap is 7.4 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 11.9 at CASPT2 (1.9 at MMVB). The D0/D1 conical intersection lies 1.9 kcal/mol above the D1 minimum at CASSCF (0.1 at MMVB). The D1/D2 conical intersection lies 8.1 kcal/mol above the D2 minimum at CASSCF and 7.9 at MMVB. Both conical intersections are SLOPED, with parallel gradients on the upper and lower states and equivalent gradient difference vectors at CASSCF and MMVB. Root-mean-square deviations of MMVB from CASSCF bond lengths over six distinct bonds are 0.006, 0.009 and 0.011 A for the D0, D1 and D2 minima (maximum errors under 0.01, 0.015 and 0.02 A), 0.010 A for the D0/D1 CI (maximum 0.015 A) and 0.017 A for the D1/D2 CI (maximum 0.030 A). The mechanism proposed is photoexcitation to an absorbing Dn state, rapid decay to D1 consistent with Kasha's rule, then ultrafast nonradiative decay to D0 at an easily accessible sloped D0/D1 conical intersection — accounting for the observed photostability.
Other: The most important caveat is one the authors state against their own conical intersections: 'at the CASSCF D0/D1 CI and D1/D2 CI optimized geometries, the two respective electronic states split by over 6 kcal/mol at the CASPT2 level, indicating that differential dynamic electron correlation is not negligible. We therefore do not know the real crossing energy and geometry at the CASPT2 level.' The crossings were located where the CASSCF space makes two states degenerate, and adding dynamic correlation lifts that degeneracy by more than 6 kcal/mol — so these are CASSCF crossing points, not true conical intersections of the correlated surface, and the paper says the same effect was seen for the naphthalene cation. It cannot be fixed here because CASPT2 geometry optimization is not available at this size. The second point concerns how the reduced space is used: conical intersections need state averaging, which is expensive enough that the space had to drop from (15e,16o) to (13e,14o) for those optimizations, and the CASPT2 reference is a hybrid — orbitals frozen from the large-space CASSCF, configurations from the small space. That is a defensible compromise but means the CASPT2 energies do not correspond to any single self-consistent active space. method: CASSCF for geometries, with internally contracted multireference singles and doubles CI on the CASSCF reference (MR-SDCI-CASSCF) plus a Davidson correction for quadruple excitations; SEAM program for the minimum on the singlet/triplet crossing seam
basis_set: Basis set I: (5s5p5d/3s3p3d) for Sc with Hay-Wadt effective core potentials treating the 3s3p4s3d shells explicitly, and 6-31G for C and H. Basis set II: BSI augmented with polarization functions f(Sc) alpha = 1.335, d(C) alpha = 0.626, p(H) alpha = 0.75.
relativistic_treatment: Hay-Wadt effective core potentials on scandium
active_space_orbital_description: (3/7) for both species: the sigma(Sc-X) bonding and sigma*(Sc-X) antibonding orbitals plus delta(dxy), delta(dx2-y2), pi(dxz), pi(dyz) and sigma(sd2z2-x2-y2) — that is, all the Sc+ valence orbitals together with the Sc-X bonding and antibonding pair. C2v notation is not used for these two species.
active_space_protocol: The most systematically constructed set of active spaces in this database: every species gets a space assembled ADDITIVELY from its fragments' spaces, and Table 1 lists the orbitals of each one explicitly. Sc+ takes (2/6), all the 4s and five 3d valence orbitals and electrons; H2 and CH2 each take (2/2); ScCH2+ takes (4/8), which 'consists of the (2/6) and (2/2) active spaces for Sc+ and CH2 fragments at the dissociation limit'; H2ScCH2+ and TS1 take (6/10) = ScCH2+ (4/8) plus H2 (2/2); ScH+ and ScCH3+ take (3/7), all Sc+ valence orbitals plus the Sc-X bonding and antibonding pair; HScCH3+ and TS2 take (4/8). The selection rule is stated as a principle: 'MOs corresponding to those bonds that are well described at the single-determinant level of theory and are not directly involved in the current step of reaction were excluded from the active space' — so (4/8) for HScCH3+ 'excludes from (6/10) the C-H bonding and antibonding orbitals and electrons to retain the symmetry of the CH3 group'. For the ENERGETICS a single common (6/10) reference is used throughout, chosen so that it reduces correctly at every dissociation limit — to ScCH2+ (4/8) plus H2 (2/2), and to Sc+ (2/6) plus CH4 (4/4). Dissociation limits themselves were computed as supermolecules at 15.0 A interfragment separation. Stationary points were confirmed by numerical Hessians at the CASSCF level, and the lowest point on the singlet/triplet crossing seam was located with the SEAM program using CASSCF gradients from GAMESS.
electronic_structure_description: Products of the channels ScH+ + CH3 and ScCH3+ + H from HScCH3+, which will dominate at higher temperatures. The (3/7) space is described as 'consistent with the (4/8) active space for HScCH3+'. For the MR-SDCI energies of these processes the reference is a CASSCF(6/10) consisting of (5/9) for ScH+ or ScCH3+ — the (3/7) plus one C-H bonding and antibonding orbital pair — combined with (1/1) for CH3 or H at the dissociation limit. For early transition metals these channels are more endothermic than the MCH2+ + H2 channel; for late transition metals the three endothermicities are similar.
Other: These two products complete the additive scheme and show it being applied in reverse: the (3/7) space is checked for CONSISTENCY with the (4/8) of the parent HScCH3+, so that bond dissociation energies are differences between spaces of matched construction rather than between independently chosen ones. The (6/10) reference for their formation energies is assembled as (5/9) + (1/1), a different decomposition of the same total size used elsewhere on the surface — the space size is held at (6/10) throughout while its fragment decomposition follows whichever bond is breaking. That is the clearest statement of the paper's discipline: constant total space, fragment-consistent composition, one correlated reference for all energies. It also means every energy on this surface is comparable, which is what supports the mechanistic conclusion that channel 1 dominates at low temperature and channels 2 and 3 at high temperature. The construction principle here is worth carrying: every active space is built ADDITIVELY from fragment spaces that are correct at the dissociation limit, and the single (6/10) reference used for all the energetics was chosen precisely because it reduces to ScCH2+ (4/8) + H2 (2/2) at one asymptote and to Sc+ (2/6) + CH4 (4/4) at another. That guarantees size-consistent comparison across the whole surface without the space changing character. Geometry optimizations then use smaller, species-specific spaces on an explicit criterion — orbitals for bonds 'well described at the single-determinant level of theory and not directly involved in the current step of reaction' are excluded — so the paper separates what a geometry needs from what an energy needs. Table 1 lists the individual orbitals of every space by symmetry label, which makes each one auditable. The authors are candid about accuracy: the same approach applied to Fe, Co and Rh gave 'qualitatively excellent agreement with the latest experiments, although quantitatively the calculated and measured energies are different up to several kcal/mol, especially for H-H bond activation barriers'.
reference_short: Musaev & Morokuma, J. Phys. Chem. 1996, 100, 11600
notes: Recorded together because the paper assigns them the same (3/7) active space and treats them in parallel. Their dissociation limits were computed as supermolecules HSc+--CH3 and H--ScCH3+ at 15.0 A interfragment distance.
correlation_correction: Internally contracted MR-SDCI-CASSCF on the (6/10) CASSCF reference with basis set II, plus the Davidson correction for quadruple excitations (+DC)

compound_name: H2 + O2 reaction system — kinetic stability of the hydrogen-oxygen mixture
point_group: C2 along the concerted addition pathway; Cs along the oxene-insertion route; no symmetry constraint on the rebound pathway
geometry_source: All critical species optimized at (14,10)CASSCF/6-31G*, with transition states located by the eigenvector-following algorithm and characterized by vibrational analyses at the same level; CASSCF zero-point energies used in all energy differences. Single-point MR-(S)DCI/cc-pVTZ energies computed at those geometries.
method: CASSCF for geometries and frequencies, with multireference singles and doubles CI (MR-(S)DCI) single points plus a Davidson correction for the energetics
active_space_orbital_description: (14,10) — all valence electrons and all valence orbitals of O2 and H2.
active_space_protocol: A full-valence space of the two reactants, held at (14,10) for every species on all three mechanistic pathways, so the concerted, oxene-insertion and rebound routes are compared in one reference. The choice of a multiconfigurational method is justified from the chemistry rather than assumed: 'since the oxygen molecule in its ground 3-Sigma-g-minus state and the lowest excited singlet 1-Delta-g state has an open electronic shell and since many of the reaction intermediates are typified by strong nondynamic correlation, the method of choice in this paper is the complete active space SCF calculation'. Symmetry is used to keep the two O2 states separate along each pathway: the triplet ground state becomes 3B in C2 and 3A'' in Cs, the 1-Delta-g excited singlet becomes 1A in C2 and 1A' in Cs, and those constraints were imposed on the symmetric species; for non-symmetric species the lowest triplet and singlet were computed directly.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies are quoted throughout as CASSCF without parentheses and MR-(S)DCI in parentheses. Key results: dissociation of H2O2 (1P3) to two OH radicals (1P5) is 42.8 kcal/mol at MR-(S)DCI against an experimental 48.9; dissociation to H + HO2 (1P1) is 80.5 against an experimental 89.5. The 3P5 to 3P4 difference of -15.3 kcal/mol at MR-(S)DCI matches an experimental enthalpy of -17.0 kcal/mol for OH + OH to H2O + O, and the computed -58.0 kcal/mol for H + HO2 to H2 + O2 matches an experimental -55.7. The H2 dissociation energy De is 96.1 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 108.5 at MR-(S)DCI, against an experimental 109. The barrier from H2O2 to two OH radicals is only 1.9 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 1.2 at MR-(S)DCI, with the reaction endothermic by 20.2 and 18.6 kcal/mol respectively. The concerted pathway is characterized by a huge barrier of about 130-140 kcal/mol. A diradicaloid state lies at 90.3 (85.7) kcal/mol and a symmetry-allowed one at 86.6 (73.5) kcal/mol. The H-abstraction step has a substantial barrier for both the triplet and singlet states of O2 and is highly endothermic, over 30 kcal/mol, so it is unlikely at ambient conditions; the lowest singlet state of O2 also has very high reaction barriers.
Other: The clearest quantitative lesson is that the correlation correction is state-dependent in a way that matters for mechanism: 'in general, the transition states are lower in the more extensive MR-(S)DCI treatment, which is expected because both types of correlation energy, static and dynamic, are accounted for to a larger extent than in the CASSCF procedure. Smaller discrepancies between the two methods are observed for the various minima'. So a full-valence CASSCF systematically overestimates barriers relative to minima on this surface, and the one exception noted is a minimum — 1P3, where MR-(S)DCI is 10 kcal/mol lower. The size of the effect is visible in the symmetry-allowed state, which drops from 86.6 to 73.5 kcal/mol, a 13.1 kcal/mol correction, against only 4.6 for the diradicaloid state at the same point. The full-valence space itself is validated externally against four independent experimental quantities — H2O2 dissociation to 2 OH (42.8 against 48.9), to H + HO2 (80.5 against 89.5), the OH + OH enthalpy (-15.3 against -17.0) and the H + HO2 enthalpy (-58.0 against -55.7) — plus the H2 dissociation energy, where CASSCF alone gives 96.1 against an experimental 109 and MR-(S)DCI recovers 108.5. That last comparison is the sharpest: a complete valence space captures only 88% of the H2 bond energy, and the missing 12.4 kcal/mol is pure dynamic correlation that no enlargement of a valence space would supply.
reference_short: Filatov, Reckien, Peyerimhoff & Shaik, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 12014
notes: Three mechanisms are examined for the reaction of H2 with O2: concerted addition, oxene insertion, and a 'rebound' mechanism, with trajectories defined in Scheme 1. The reactions are exothermic by at least -30 kcal/mol. Barriers on the singlet surface would in principle be expected lower than triplet barriers, but the calculations find the lowest singlet state of O2 has very high barriers for reaction. The conclusion is that the H-abstraction step carries a substantial barrier for both spin states and is highly endothermic, explaining the kinetic stability of H2/O2 mixtures at ambient conditions.
correlation_correction: Multireference singles and doubles CI (MR-(S)DCI) with the cc-pVTZ basis at the CASSCF geometries, with Davidson's correction added to the total energies

compound_name: meta-Xylylene biradical (MX, C8H8) and its radical cation — calibration system
geometry_source: Geometries initially optimized with UHF and UB3LYP using 6-311++G(3df,2p), with harmonic frequencies at the same level characterizing each structure; CASSCF optimizations with the ANO-L basis. Vibrational frequency computations were NOT possible at the CASSCF level, so zero-point corrections could only be applied to structures characterizable at the B3LYP level.
method: CASSCF with multistate MS-CASPT2 and multiconfigurational quasidegenerate perturbation theory (MCQDPT/MRMP2); B3LYP for high-spin states not severely affected by orbital degeneracy
basis_set: ANO-L for the MS-CASPT2/CASSCF calculations; 6-311G(d,p) for MCQDPT/CASSCF; 6-311++G(3df,2p) for the HF and B3LYP optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(10,9): nine orbitals comprising one a1, three a2 and five b1. The a1 orbital is of sigma character and the rest are pi. The b2 orbitals are excluded 'because they do not show significant contributions'. The two highest-energy molecular orbitals, 2a2 and 3b1, are the natural orbitals whose variable occupancy by two electrons generates the states.
active_space_protocol: An explicit case of choosing a LARGER space than needed for consistency across a redox pair. The paper states that 'although for the neutral biradical, an (8,8) active space is sufficient to describe the nondynamical correlation, we have rather chosen a (10,9) space because of the fact that, in the C8H8 radical cation, an electron could be removed from the a1 orbital, implying a set of 9 correlated electrons. For the sake of consistency, the (10,9) active space has been selected for both neutral and ionized systems.' So the space is sized by the ionized species and applied to both, making ionization energies differences between identically constructed calculations. Orbitals are selected by contribution: b2 orbitals are excluded on the grounds of insignificant contribution. The paper's stated reason for using MULTISTATE perturbation theory rather than single-state CASPT2 or MRMP2 is worth recording, because it applies to every near-degenerate system in this database: 'when applying separately a perturbative treatment to MCSCF states with very close energies, the states ordering could be reversed and the results become unphysical if the states are of the same symmetry, as in most cases, a root flipping occurs or the perturbation series diverges because of the existence of intruder states'. Intruder states arise because 'high-lying states within the complete active space frequently have zeroth-order energies that are quasidegenerate with zeroth-order states in the orthogonal space', and are said to be especially likely in MRMP treatment when the reference is a high-lying state and a diffuse basis is used. MS-CASPT2 and MCQDPT both couple the lower-lying states of the same symmetry and determine their energies simultaneously, which is exactly what a 1-3 kcal/mol doublet-quartet gap requires.
electronic_structure_description: MX is a formal C8H8 hydrocarbon biradical of C2v symmetry whose two highest molecular orbitals, 2a2 and 3b1, accommodate two electrons to give a triplet 3B2, an open-shell singlet 1B2 and a closed-shell singlet 1A1. CASSCF(10,9)/ANO and UB3LYP/6-311++G(3df,2p) geometries for the 3B2 triplet are nearly identical; the closed-shell 1A1 parameters are close to the triplet's, while the open-shell 1B2 differs significantly — its exocyclic C-C distance is 1.355 A against 1.401 A, close to a double bond. The proton affinity of DMX- computed as the energy difference to MX(3B2) is 401.4 kcal/mol, agreeing with an experimental 401 plus or minus 3 kcal/mol from proton-transfer bracketing. The protonated form, the MX radical cation C8H8+, shows a completely different electronic landscape from the neutral C8H7 triradical: forming the additional C-H bond gives it pure one-electron radical character.
Other: This is a clean, explicitly reasoned instance of oversizing an active space for CONSISTENCY rather than for accuracy. An (8,8) would suffice for the neutral biradical, but ionization removes an electron from the a1 orbital, so the cation needs nine correlated electrons; rather than use different spaces for the two species, the authors adopt (10,9) for both. The payoff is that the computed proton affinity — a difference between the anion and the neutral triplet — lands at 401.4 kcal/mol against an experimental 401 plus or minus 3, and the ionization quantities are differences between identically constructed references. The cost is a slightly larger calculation for the neutral than it strictly needs. The exclusion criterion is stated too: b2 orbitals are left out because they show no significant contribution, so the space is nine orbitals of a1, a2 and b1 symmetry chosen by inspection of the natural orbitals rather than by a fixed rule. electronic_structure_description: Derived from MX by dehydrogenation at C5. Three electrons occupy three open-shell sigma(1)pi(1)pi(1) orbitals of comparable energy, giving a doublet 2B2 with configuration (a1)1(b1)1(a2)1 and a quartet 4B2. The doublet is the ground state, lying 3.3 kcal/mol below the quartet in one treatment, with a smaller quartet-doublet gap of 1.9 kcal/mol from another and 2.0 kcal/mol in the ordering 2B2 (0.0) below a4B2 (2.0); the leading configuration in the 4B2 state contributes 0.82. The overall 4B2-2B2 separation is reported in the range 1-3 kcal/mol. The proton affinity of DMX, evaluated as the energy difference between DMX(2B2) and the MX radical cation (2B1), is 261 kcal/mol with a probable error of 3 kcal/mol.
Other: The whole conclusion of the paper rests on an energy gap of at most 2 kcal/mol between the doublet and quartet, which is smaller than the spread among the methods used to compute it — 3.3, 1.9 and 2.0 kcal/mol from different treatments. That is why the multistate perturbation machinery matters here rather than being a refinement: with two states of the SAME symmetry (2B2 and 4B2 both B2) separated by a couple of kcal/mol, single-state CASPT2 or MRMP2 would be at risk of root flipping or intruder-state divergence, and the paper says so explicitly before choosing MS-CASPT2 and MCQDPT. The result is chemically notable — the low-spin open-shell doublet lies below the high-spin quartet, 'another case of a breakdown of the Aufbau principle of electron occupancy in molecular orbitals and of Hund's rule' — and it is exactly the kind of claim that a 0.3 kcal/mol methodological artifact could overturn. A practical limitation for reuse: CASSCF frequencies were not feasible, so zero-point corrections exist only where B3LYP could characterize the structure. The paper's stated reason for using MULTISTATE perturbation theory rather than single-state CASPT2 or MRMP2 is worth recording, because it applies to every near-degenerate system in this database: 'when applying separately a perturbative treatment to MCSCF states with very close energies, the states ordering could be reversed and the results become unphysical if the states are of the same symmetry, as in most cases, a root flipping occurs or the perturbation series diverges because of the existence of intruder states'. Intruder states arise because 'high-lying states within the complete active space frequently have zeroth-order energies that are quasidegenerate with zeroth-order states in the orthogonal space', and are said to be especially likely in MRMP treatment when the reference is a high-lying state and a diffuse basis is used. MS-CASPT2 and MCQDPT both couple the lower-lying states of the same symmetry and determine their energies simultaneously, which is exactly what a 1-3 kcal/mol doublet-quartet gap requires.

active_space_protocol: The decision to include the nitrogen lone pairs was made by an explicit numerical test and is quantified. Separate state-averaged CASSCF computations on the two lowest states WITH and WITHOUT the N lone pairs showed the lone pairs 'were mostly doubly occupied in CASSCF wave functions, with an occupation number larger than 1.97' — which by a conventional occupation-window criterion would justify excluding them. But 'the resulting energy gaps from the two CASSCF sets differ by approximately 0.3 kcal/mol. Because the energy gaps are also small, approximately 2 kcal/mol, a variation of 0.3 kcal/mol already represents 15% of the gap. Therefore, it seems reasonable to incorporate the lone pair orbitals.' Since the relative importance of the a1 and b2 lone pairs could not be determined a priori, both were included. The authors acknowledge the risk: 'a doubly occupied orbital with an occupancy number larger than 1.97 could introduce redundant rotations during the iterative process, between the closed and active shells', though the CASSCF processes converged well here. The paper's stated reason for using MULTISTATE perturbation theory rather than single-state CASPT2 or MRMP2 is worth recording, because it applies to every near-degenerate system in this database: 'when applying separately a perturbative treatment to MCSCF states with very close energies, the states ordering could be reversed and the results become unphysical if the states are of the same symmetry, as in most cases, a root flipping occurs or the perturbation series diverges because of the existence of intruder states'. Intruder states arise because 'high-lying states within the complete active space frequently have zeroth-order energies that are quasidegenerate with zeroth-order states in the orthogonal space', and are said to be especially likely in MRMP treatment when the reference is a high-lying state and a diffuse basis is used. MS-CASPT2 and MCQDPT both couple the lower-lying states of the same symmetry and determine their energies simultaneously, which is exactly what a 1-3 kcal/mol doublet-quartet gap requires.

electronic_structure_description: Formed by replacing the CH groups at positions 4 and 6 of the six-membered ring with two nitrogen atoms, which introduces two lone pairs at each site; combination of the corresponding atomic orbitals gives a1 and b2 molecular orbitals. Like the parent triradical, the ground state is the doublet 2B2, lying 1 kcal/mol below the 4B2 quartet. Figure 6 shows the three orbitals (a1, b1 and a2) that determine the electronic state.
Other: This is the most instructive active-space decision in the paper, because it OVERRIDES the standard occupation-number rule with an error-budget argument. The nitrogen lone pairs have occupation numbers above 1.97 — comfortably inside the doubly-occupied regime that occupation-window criteria (typically 0.02 to 1.98) would exclude — yet including them shifts the doublet-quartet gap by 0.3 kcal/mol, which is 15% of a gap of about 2 kcal/mol. When the target quantity is small enough, an orbital that is 'inactive' by occupation can still carry a significant fraction of the answer. The authors accept the known cost of including near-doubly-occupied orbitals, redundant rotations between closed and active shells, and report that convergence held. The general rule this supports: occupation-number thresholds should be judged against the SIZE OF THE QUANTITY BEING COMPUTED, not applied absolutely. Note also that both lone-pair orbitals were included because their relative importance could not be established in advance — a symmetric choice rather than a tuned one. active_space_protocol: A minimal, purely metal-centred space — eight electrons in the five Ni 3d-based molecular orbitals — with the orbitals optimized by averaging over the COMPLETE d8 multiplet manifold: 10 triplet and 15 singlet roots. Spin-spin coupling contributions come from the Breit-Pauli spin-spin Hamiltonian with first-order perturbation theory, accelerated by the RI approximation with TZV/C auxiliary bases. Three levels are compared on the SAME (8,5) reference: plain SA-CASSCF, NEVPT2 (identical wavefunctions with state energies corrected to second order before entering the QDPT treatment), and SORCI as a more rigorous multireference CI, with thresholds Tpre, Tnat and Tsel of 1e-5, 1e-5 and 1e-6 Eh. The ZORA scalar relativistic approximation is used in every ab initio calculation with ZORA-TZV(2d,2p) for all elements — essential given the iodide complex.

The trigonally distorted tetrahedral C3v geometry gives a 3A2 ground state from single occupation of the degenerate dxz,yz-based pi* orbitals, but the SOMOs contain significant contribution from the other e-set (dxy, dx2-y2) because the metal centre is displaced about 1.1 A out of the equatorial plane defined by the three Tp nitrogen atoms. Relevant d-d excited states are 1E and 3E from 1a1 to 1e promotion, three triplets 3A1, 3A2 and 3E plus three singlets of the same symmetry from 1e to 2e, and two singlets 1A1 and 1E from spin-flip transitions within the degenerate SOMOs.
Other: The chloride is the one complex where the three methods disagree noticeably: CASSCF gives 3.9 cm-1 and NEVPT2 3.8, both matching the experimental 3.9 essentially exactly, while the more elaborate SORCI gives 2.0 at the optimized geometry and 4.9 at the crystal geometry — a spread of 2.9 cm-1 on a D value of 3.9, and a swing of nearly 75% between two geometries that the other two methods barely distinguish. The spin-spin contribution is zero to the precision reported, so for this complex the entire D value is spin-orbit in origin — unlike the iodide, where DSSC becomes visible. Across all three halides, plain SA-CASSCF and NEVPT2 differ by at most 0.5 cm-1 in D, so the second-order correction to the state energies is essentially irrelevant — which is the signature of a system whose physics is contained in the d-manifold multiplet structure rather than in metal-ligand covalency. active_space_orbital_description: CAS(10-in-9): ten electrons in nine orbitals, comprising all the pi orbitals of the six-membered ring, the N10 atom and the carbonyl group. CAS(12-in-10) additionally includes an oxygen lone pair and is used for the chemiluminescent state.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces used for two different questions, with the difference between them quantified rather than assumed. The working space is CAS(10-in-9) — ten electrons in nine orbitals — described as 'an optimal candidate for the calculations' for characterizing chemiluminescent and fluorescent properties, containing all the pi orbitals of the six-membered ring, the N10 atom and the carbonyl group. For the chemiluminescent state a second space CAS(12-in-10) adds the oxygen LONE PAIR, 'since it has been shown elsewhere that a lone pair of the oxygen atom may be relevant to the chemiluminescent reactivity'. The geometry-optimization strategy is stepwise and explicitly methodological: first a small pi-only space at CASSCF, then two separate modifications — adding the nO lone pair of O30, and switching to CASPT2 geometry optimization via numerical gradients — so the two effects can be separated. State averaging is a live constraint here: no low-lying state has charge-transfer character at the Franck-Condon geometry, and 'to find a state with charge-transfer character to the carbonyl group, more than 10 roots are needed in the State Averaged CASSCF wave function'.
nroots_per_mult: More than 10 roots in the state-averaged CASSCF are required to reach a charge-transfer state
electronic_structure_description: Vertical absorption at the ground-state minimum: the brightest state (S2, highest oscillator strength and therefore most populated on irradiation) requires 4.03 eV and the lowest-energy state appears at 3.25 eV. Both S1 and S2 involve transitions between natural orbitals delocalized over the pi-aromatic system. NONE of the lowest excited states has CTIL (charge-transfer-to-inner-ligand) character at the Franck-Condon geometry, even though the N10 atom is negatively charged and the system therefore has a lower oxidation potential; states with CTIL character require more than 10 roots in the state-averaged CASSCF and lie above 7 eV, corresponding to excitations from the SCF HOMO to the pi* orbital located mainly on the CO group. Excited-state minima: the S2 minimum lies 0.29 eV above the S1 surface with a vertical emission of 2.39 eV and f = 0.001; the S1 minimum gives a vertical emission of 2.13 eV with f = 0.043.
Other: The anion is where the lone-pair effect was measured, and the numbers are large enough to change conclusions: adding nO to the active space lengthens the CO bond by 0.12 A and lowers the vertical emission by 0.87 eV. The mechanism is identifiable — with the lone pair active, a new nO to pi*(CO) excitation contributes alongside the CTIL character, so the chemiluminescent state becomes genuinely more multiconfigurational rather than merely shifted. The second, independent constraint is on ROOTS rather than orbitals: at the ground-state geometry no CTIL state appears among the low-lying manifold at all, and more than 10 state-averaged roots are needed before one emerges above 7 eV. So the states responsible for chemiluminescence are inaccessible at the optimized ground-state geometry of this model, and a study that carried only a handful of roots would conclude, wrongly, that no such state exists. Both constraints are specific to the chemiluminescent state; the fluorescence properties are well described by the smaller pi-only space. The active-space finding here is quantified precisely. Adding the oxygen lone pair nO to the pi-only space — going from CAS(10-in-9) to CAS(12-in-10) — makes 'the multiconfigurational character of the CS become stronger', because a new nO to pi*(CO) excitation joins the charge-transfer-to-inner-ligand (CTIL) contribution. The structural and energetic consequences are large: the CO bond lengthens by 0.12 A, the vertical emission energy drops by 0.87 eV, and the O30-C20-N10-C40 dihedral changes by 7 degrees, while the C20-N10-C2-N3 angle is essentially unaffected. A single lone-pair orbital therefore changes both the geometry and the emission energy of the light-emitting state substantially, so a pi-only space cannot describe chemiluminescence in these systems even though it suffices for fluorescence. A second constraint is on the number of roots rather than orbitals: no CTIL state appears among the low-lying states at all, and more than 10 roots must be carried in the state-averaged CASSCF before one is found, at energies above 7 eV.

notes: A small model of the coelenterazine/coelenteramide and Cypridina luciferin/oxyluciferin bioluminescent systems. In those systems a peroxo intermediate decomposes to give coelenteramide (in aequorin and obelin) or Cypridina oxyluciferin (in Cypridina luciferase) in the excited state. Direct comparison with experimental coelenteramide absorption spectra is difficult because the transitions are mainly affected by the phenolate substituent of the pyrazine ring, which the model omits; two peaks are nonetheless found in the coelenteramide analogues studied by Shimomura and Teranishi. Efficient chemiluminescent systems are governed by a concerted CTIL mechanism, a charge transfer from an electron-donating part of the molecule to the dioxetanone moiety. The paper does not write out a molecular formula, so none is recorded.

point_group: The 1A1g label indicates a centrosymmetric point group; the open-shell singlets of the [n]cyclacene series display nearly D(nh) symmetry
geometry_source: Cyclacene geometries optimized at B3LYP/6-31G*; [6]cyclacene was additionally optimized at the CASSCF level, with its energy refined by MRMP2 single points
method: CASSCF with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP2); unrestricted broken-spin-symmetry DFT (UBS-DFT) and spin-restricted closed-shell B3LYP for comparison
software: GAMESS-US (all CASSCF and MRMP2); Gaussian 03 (all DFT)
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(8,8) — eight electrons in eight orbitals. The paper reports the natural orbital occupation numbers for the resulting wavefunction but does not name the individual orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Only [6]cyclacene, the smallest member of the series, receives the multiconfigurational treatment; the larger cyclacenes and short zigzag nanotubes are treated by unrestricted broken-spin-symmetry DFT, with the CASSCF/MRMP2 result on the smallest system serving as the benchmark that validates the UBS-DFT description for the rest. The singlet was described with open-shell UBS theory rather than the restricted closed-shell B3LYP approach, and the paper attributes previous incorrect ground-state assignments to that restricted treatment.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is the 1A1g open-shell singlet. The triplet lies 14.9 kcal/mol above it at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* and 7.4 kcal/mol above at MRMP2/6-31G*//CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G*. The CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers are 1.98, 1.93, 1.87, 1.46, 0.54, 0.14, 0.07 and 0.01. Open-shell singlet character is already apparent at [6]cyclacene and resembles that of long linear polyacenes rather than the triplet ground states previously reported. For [10]cyclacene the alpha-spin electrons are mainly localized on the zigzag edge carbon atoms. Even-numbered [n]cyclacenes are more stable than odd-numbered ones for the closed-shell singlets; the open-shell singlets display nearly D(nh) symmetry.
Other: The natural orbital occupations are the diagnostic that settles the question, and they are unusually clean: 1.98, 1.93, 1.87, 1.46, 0.54, 0.14, 0.07, 0.01. The near-symmetric 1.46/0.54 pair in the middle is the signature of a genuine open-shell singlet — an orbital half a electron away from single occupancy on each side — and the paper says these 'clearly indicate the significant multiconfiguration character of the singlet state'. Note that a conventional occupation-window criterion of 0.02 to 1.98 would admit all eight of these orbitals and exclude none, so the (8,8) is exactly the space the diagnostic calls for. The methodological point is that the restricted closed-shell B3LYP treatment does NOT reproduce these results and, as in previous work the authors describe as being 'at such inadequate levels', puts the triplet lower — so the earlier literature assignment of triplet ground states to cyclacenes is an artifact of imposing a closed-shell singlet reference. Dynamic correlation halves the singlet-triplet gap, from 14.9 kcal/mol at CASSCF to 7.4 at MRMP2, so the sign of the gap is robust to correlation while its magnitude is not. Only the smallest member was affordable at this level; the conclusion for larger cyclacenes and nanotubes rests on transferring the validated UBS-DFT description.
reference_short: Chen, Jiang, Lu, Bettinger, Dai et al., Org. Lett. 2007, 9, 5449
notes: [n]Cyclacenes have never been synthesized despite attempts going back decades; an effort to make [12]cyclacene yielded a hydrogenated derivative, and attempts at [8]cyclacene by stereospecific routes did not succeed. The systems are relevant to carbon nanotube research since cyclacenes are the shortest zigzag nanotube segments. Transannular CC and edge CCH bond behaviour across the series is analysed in the paper, along with the alternation in stability between even and odd [n]cyclacenes for the closed-shell singlets. The paper does not write out a molecular formula, so none is recorded.
correlation_correction: MRMP2/6-31G* single points at the CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* geometry

compound_name: 4-Dimethylamino-4'-cyanodiphenylacetylene (DCDPA) — photochemistry and twisted intramolecular charge transfer
point_group: C1; the S0 geometry is near-linear about the acetylenic unit, with the S1 trans-bent form strongly bent
geometry_source: State-specific (10,10)CASSCF optimization of the S0 geometry; S1-specific (10,10)CASSCF optimization of the S1 minimum in the Franck-Condon region and of the S1 trans-bent minimum. The charge-transfer/diradical conical intersection was determined with a reduced (4,4)CASSCF. Polarized continuum model calculations for the polar-solvent behaviour, with the MRMP2 free energy obtained as the sum of an MRMP2 internal energy and an electrostatic term.
method: CASSCF with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset (MRMP2) energy corrections; CIS and complete active space CI as preliminary orbital-selection tools; polarized continuum model for solvent
software: GAMESS for the standard (10,10)CASSCF work; Gaussian 03 for the determination of the CT/BR conical intersection
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta with polarization on the acetylenic carbons (alpha_d = 0.75) and the nitrogen atoms (alpha_d = 0.80), i.e. DZP quality on those centres and DZ elsewhere
active_space_orbital_description: (10,10)CASSCF: the highest five occupied pi and the lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals. The full pi manifold would be eight out-of-plane occupied orbitals, one dimethylamino lone pair and two in-plane orbitals of the triple bond, together with the corresponding eight out-of-plane and two in-plane pi* orbitals. The in-plane pi and pi* orbitals of the C-C triple bond are included within the ten. A reduced (4,4) space — the two occupied and two unoccupied orbitals correlating with pi(HOMO), pi*(LUMO), pi(ip) and pi*(ip) at the S0 geometry — was used to locate one conical intersection.
active_space_protocol: A three-stage, empirically driven reduction. The full pi space is defined first and rejected on cost: taking all pi-type occupied orbitals and the corresponding lowest pi* orbitals is 'practically prohibited even on a high-performance computer, especially in case of scanning of global potential energy surfaces'. Stage one is CIS at geometries spanning every region that could matter — trans-bent, dimethylamino-twisted, dimethylanilino-twisted and benzonitrile-twisted — which established that the low-lying states are well described by excitations among the highest five occupied pi and lowest five unoccupied pi* orbitals, and crucially that 'a set of the 10 orbitals are INVARIANT IRRESPECTIVE OF GEOMETRIES though the order among them interchanges in some cases'. Stage two verified multiple-excitation effects within those ten by (10,10)CASCI at various geometries. Only then was (10,10)CASSCF adopted for the global surface scan. State-specific optimization is used for each state separately, and the space is further cut to (4,4) for one conical intersection, justified by preliminary CI showing the two crossing states are well described by four orbitals.
nroots_per_mult: At least 4 (S0 through S4 characterized in the preliminary CI)
electronic_structure_description: DCDPA is mainly excited into an internal charge-transfer (ICT) state, the charge moving from the dimethylanilino group into the benzonitrile part. The first excited manifold consists of three states S1, S2 and S3, well described by linear combinations of two types of pi-pi* locally excited states in the benzene rings plus the CT state from the HOMO-LUMO single excitation; the transition from S0 is mainly to the CT state. S4 is a combination of pi(ip) to pi*(LUMO) and pi(HOMO) to pi*(ip) excitations; it is separate from the first excited manifold near the Franck-Condon and twisted regions but merges into it as the bending angles decrease from 180 degrees, and eventually becomes S1 in the strongly bent trans-bent region. S1 has two stable geometries: an ICT structure skeletally relaxed from S0, and a DIRADICAL structure in which DCDPA is trans-bent and the acetylenic C-C triple bond becomes an ethylenic double bond, as in parent diphenylacetylene. A conical intersection between the charge-transfer and diradical states lies on the path to the globally stable trans-bent form, behind a barrier of 0.115 eV. Twisting the dimethylamino group decreases the CT character while twisting the dimethylanilino group increases it. In polar solvent a twisted ICT (TICT) state forms with the dimethylanilino group perpendicular to the rest. At the S0 geometry the C-C bond is 1.203 A, a normal triple bond, and the benzene rings retain aromatic bond lengths near 1.4 A.
Other: The orbital-selection procedure here is unusually rigorous about a property most reductions ignore: GEOMETRIC INVARIANCE of the chosen set. CIS calculations were run first across four distinct structural regions — trans-bent, dimethylamino-twisted, dimethylanilino-twisted and benzonitrile-twisted — precisely because the study scans global potential surfaces, and the finding that 'a set of the 10 orbitals are invariant irrespective of geometries though the order among them interchanges in some cases' is what licenses a fixed (10,10) for the whole scan. The order interchanging while the set does not is the important detail: an energy-window selection applied at one geometry would pick different orbitals elsewhere. The full pi space was defined and rejected on cost grounds alone, not on any claim of equivalence. The one place the space is cut further, to (4,4) for a conical intersection, is again justified by preliminary CI identifying which four orbitals carry the two crossing states — and the authors note they checked the result. The consequence for reuse is that the (10,10) and (4,4) results are not on a common footing, and the 0.115 eV barrier to the CT/diradical intersection is small enough that this matters.
reference_short: Amatatsu, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 543
notes: Phenylethynyl-linked pi-conjugated systems are of interest in photofunctional material science; phenylethynyl-linked porphyrinic compounds serve as light-harvesting antennae mimicking chlorophyll. The trans-bent S1 form parallels behaviour already established for parent diphenylacetylene. Solvent was treated by a polarized continuum model, with the MRMP2 free energy formed as F(MP2) = E(intMP2) + E(S), applying the MRMP2 correction to the internal energy but not to the electrostatic term. Potential energy surfaces with respect to symmetric bending are given in Supporting Information Figure SI-1, and the state compositions in Table SI-1. The paper does not write out a molecular formula, so none is recorded.
correlation_correction: MRMP2 second-order multireference perturbation corrections applied to the CASSCF energies for quantitative discussion

compound_name: Trimethylenemethane (TMM) and methylenecyclopropane (MCP) — rearrangement potential energy surfaces
point_group: D3h for the triplet ground state (3A'2, or 3B2 in the C2v subgroup); C2v for the orthogonal 1B1 structure; Cs for a slightly pyramidalized alternative
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations with MRMP2 and MRCISD single points at those geometries; RCCSD(T) for MCP and UCCSD(T) for triplet TMM at the optimized CASSCF geometries
method: CASSCF with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MRMP2), multireference CI singles and doubles (MRCISD) including Davidson's correction for unlinked quadruples, and coupled-cluster singles and doubles with perturbative triples
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: 6-311G(d,p) for the CASSCF, MRMP2 and MRCISD results in Table 1
active_space_orbital_description: (4e,4o) for all parent TMM structures in this work. The literature comparison discussed in the paper spans (4e,4o)CASSCF/6-31G* and (10e,10o)CASSCF/cc-pVTZ treatments by other authors.
active_space_protocol: A (4e,4o) space for all the parent trimethylenemethane structures, with MRMP2 and MRCISD computed at the optimized CASSCF geometries. The paper is explicit about when CASSCF energy differences are and are not trustworthy, and the criterion is orbital CHARACTER rather than count: comparing TMM with methylenecyclopropane is unreliable because 'two pi-type active orbitals of TMM will transform to two sigma-type orbitals in MCP, the active space will be somewhat modified. In order to obtain reliable energy differences with the CASSCF method the MOs in the active spaces should be similar. Hence, the CASSCF energy differences between TMMs and MCP may not be reliable.' That comparison is therefore made with coupled-cluster instead — RCCSD(T) for MCP and UCCSD(T) for triplet TMM at the CASSCF geometries — while CASSCF and MRMP2 differences are retained for the biradical TMM structures, 'since the RCCSD(T) method suffers from triplet instabilities, while the UCCSD(T) method suffers from high spin contamination for singlet TMMs'. Each method is used only where the other fails.
nroots_per_mult: Four electronic states of TMM examined: 3A'2 (3B2 in C2v), 1A1, 1B1 and 1B2, plus the MCP ground state
electronic_structure_description: Zero-point-corrected relative energies in kcal/mol with the 6-311G(d,p) basis, referred to triplet TMM at 0.0, as (4e,4o)CASSCF / (4e,4o)MRMP2 / (4e,4o)MRCISD / CCSD(T): o1 13.7 / 14.9 / 12.7; s1 17.2 / 18.0 / 16.9; l1 16.7 / — / 16.7; MCP -13.0 / -16.2 / -21.2 / -22.5; TS(MCP/o1) 17.2 / 17.4; conrotatory 19.3 / 20.1; disrotatory 18.9 / 19.6. The MRCISD values include Davidson's correction. Triplet TMM is a minimum at D3h geometry. At CASSCF the orthogonal o1(1B1) structure in C2v is a transition state with an imaginary frequency of 264i cm-1 connecting two equivalent pyramidalized structures, and a Cs minimum was found with a 12.9 degree pyramidalized methylene; however o1(A'') is only 0.1 kcal/mol below o1(1B1) at CASSCF while o1(1B1) is 0.8 kcal/mol BELOW o1(A'') at MRMP2. The paper concludes that the pyramidalization is an ARTIFACT of the CASSCF method and the true geometry is C2v. A structure with pyramidalization in the unique methylene group lies 13.9 kcal/mol above the triplet minimum at MRCISD.
Other: Two distinct active-space lessons here. First, this paper identifies a CASSCF geometric artifact directly: the C2v orthogonal structure appears as a transition state with a 264i cm-1 imaginary frequency at CASSCF, with a pyramidalized Cs minimum 0.1 kcal/mol lower — but MRMP2 reverses the ordering by 0.8 kcal/mol, so 'pyramidalization is an artifact of the CASSCF method, and the actual geometry is C2v'. A 0.1 kcal/mol CASSCF preference is not evidence of anything, and the imaginary frequency it produces is spurious. Second, the paper states a criterion for when CASSCF energy differences may be compared at all, and it is about orbital CHARACTER not count: TMM and methylenecyclopropane cannot be compared at CASSCF because two pi-type active orbitals of TMM become sigma-type in MCP, so 'in order to obtain reliable energy differences with the CASSCF method the MOs in the active spaces should be similar'. The size of that failure is visible in Table 1 — CASSCF puts MCP at -13.0 kcal/mol while CCSD(T) gives -22.5, a 9.5 kcal/mol discrepancy, whereas the purely biradical TMM structures agree between methods to within about 2 kcal/mol. The paper's own literature review supplies a third data point: (4e,4o)CASSCF makes 1A1 TMM a saddle point with a 70i imaginary frequency while (10e,10o)CASSCF/cc-pVTZ makes it a minimum and 1B1 a transition structure — the same qualitative question answered differently by two space sizes.
reference_short: Bozkaya & Ozkan, J. Phys. Chem. A 2012, 116, 2309
notes: Structures are labelled s (short planar), l (long planar), o (orthogonal methylene) and c (cyclopropane ring), with subscripts 1-3 giving the position of the short bond, long bond, orthogonal methylene or cyclopropane ring; methylene carbons are numbered clockwise from the top. Dowd's ESR experiments gave a singlet-triplet separation of 7.8 plus or minus 0.3 kcal/mol from the temperature dependence of the rate of disappearance of the matrix-isolated triplet signal, on the assumption that intersystem crossing is rate-determining. Earlier predictions in the literature include Goddard's that the 1B2 state is unstable to methylene rotation, making it a maximum in two coordinates, Borden's (4e,4o)CASSCF/6-31G* finding that 1A1 is a saddle point connecting two equivalent C2 transition states, and Cramer's (10e,10o)CASSCF/cc-pVTZ finding that 1A1 is a minimum with a pyramidalized structure only 10 degrees from C2v.
correlation_correction: MRMP2 and MRCISD (with Davidson's correction for unlinked quadruple excitations) at the optimized CASSCF geometries; CCSD(T) used where the multireference comparison is unreliable

compound_name: 2-Mercaptopyridine (2MP) — S1 minimum in the excited-state proton transfer from 2-thiopyridone
point_group: C1 for the CASSCF S1 optimization; Cs was used for the DFT ground and lowest triplet states of both tautomers
geometry_source: CASSCF(6,8)/6-311+G(d,p) optimization of the S1 minimum energy structure in C1 symmetry; (U)B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p) with Cs symmetry for the ground and lowest triplet states of both tautomers, with vertical transitions from B3LYP-TD using a self-consistent reaction field and a polarized continuum overlapping-spheres model
method: CASSCF for the S1 minimum with CASPT2 single points; (U)B3LYP and B3LYP-TD for the remaining states; time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy
basis_set: 6-311+G(d,p) for the CASSCF and CASPT2 work and for most DFT; 6-311++G(d,p) for some B3LYP energies
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(6,8) — six electrons in eight orbitals. The paper does not identify which eight orbitals, so no composition is recorded.
active_space_protocol: The multiconfigurational treatment is applied narrowly: CASSCF(6,8) is used only to locate the S1 minimum energy structure of 2-mercaptopyridine, with a CASPT2 single point on top, while every other state of both tautomers — T1, S1 through S4 of 2-thiopyridone and T1, S1 through S3 of 2-mercaptopyridine — is treated by (U)B3LYP-TD. The reason for the narrow scope is stated as a practical limit rather than a methodological choice: the transition barriers between the S4 state of 2TP and the S1 state of 2MP 'are not presently determined due to the difficulty in CASSCF calculations'.
electronic_structure_description: The S1 minimum energy of 2-mercaptopyridine is 103 kcal/mol at CASPT2, close to the 105 kcal/mol vertical transition energy of the S4 state of 2-thiopyridone, making excited-state proton transfer between those two states energetically feasible. By contrast the ESPT reaction from the S2 state of 2TP to the S1 state of 2MP is greatly prohibited, since 108 kcal/mol is required. In the ground state 2MP lies 2.57 kcal/mol above 2TP at B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) with SCRF and PCM, and ground-state proton transfer is strongly inhibited by a very high barrier. Three decay channels to 2MP are proposed: internal conversion from S4 of 2TP to the S1 minimum of 2MP; intersystem crossing from S4 of 2TP to T1 of 2MP through a global T1 surface connecting both tautomers, feasible because the T1 transition state lies below the S4 state; and a route from T1 of 2TP to ground-state 2MP. The UV absorption spectrum of 2TP in water shows strong bands at 341.6 nm (f = 0.1145) and 270.4 nm (f = 0.1593).
Other: This is a case where the active space appears at exactly one point on an otherwise DFT surface, and the paper is candid that the limit is practical: the barriers connecting the S4 state of 2-thiopyridone to the S1 state of 2-mercaptopyridine 'are not presently determined due to the difficulty in CASSCF calculations'. The consequence is that the mechanistic conclusion rests on comparing a CASPT2 energy (103 kcal/mol for the 2MP S1 minimum) with a TD-DFT vertical energy (105 kcal/mol for the 2TP S4 state) — two quantities from different methods on a 2 kcal/mol margin. The authors offer a partial defence, arguing the barrier should be small because 'the corresponding orbitals are similar for two pi to pi* transitions of 2TP and 2MP', but that is an orbital-similarity argument rather than a computed result. The (6,8) space is never decomposed into named orbitals, so it cannot be reproduced or checked from the text; and with six electrons in eight orbitals there are two more orbitals than the pi system of a six-membered heterocycle would suggest, implying sulfur lone-pair or sigma* involvement that the paper does not spell out.
reference_short: Du, Liu, Zhao, Pei, Wang et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2011, 115, 8266
notes: Studied together with its tautomer 2-thiopyridone (2TP) by nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy with 266 nm pump and probe, alongside computation. Figure 8 gives the potential energy surface diagram for the excited-state proton transfer tautomerization, with vertical transition energies from (U)B3LYP-TD for T1 and S1 through S4 of 2TP and T1 and S1 through S3 of 2MP, and the 2MP S1 minimum from CASSCF(6,8). Computed Raman frequencies were scaled by 0.97 for comparison with experiment.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF(6,8)/6-311+G(d,p) reference

ligand_set: Cyclopentadienyl on chromium, three carbonyls on iron, bridging cyclooctatetraene dianion
geometry_source: Structure taken as established for this complex; the Cot ring is bent, so there are no degenerate pi orbitals and the orbitals are labelled by Cs symmetry
method: CASSCF, with DFT (B3LYP) used for geometry optimization of the dichromium complex
basis_set: Standard 3-21G for the ligands; Hay-Wadt effective core potentials with the corresponding valence basis sets for the metals
relativistic_treatment: Hay-Wadt effective core potentials on the metal centres
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(9/9) in the 5a'4a'' partition, the best of five compositions tested. Active orbital occupations and characters: 32a'' 0.07 (Cot pi to Cr(xz), M-Cot antibonding); 53a' 0.10 (Cot pi to Cr(yz), M-Cot antibonding); 31a'' 0.15 (Cr(xy) to Cot pi, antibonding); 52a' 0.49 (Cr(x2-y2) minus Fe(yz), M-M' antibonding); 51a' 1.00 (Cr(z2)); 50a' 1.51 (Cr(x2-y2) minus Fe(yz), M-M' bonding); 30a'' 1.85 (Cr(xy) to Cot pi bonding); 49a' 1.90 (Cot pi to Cr(yz) bonding); 29a'' 1.93 (Cot pi to Cr(xz) bonding). Three Fe-based orbitals — 48a' Fe(yz), 28a'' Fe(xz) and 47a' Fe(z2), all M-CO — remain inactive at occupation 2.00.
active_space_protocol: The desired space is defined, shown to be unaffordable, and the truncation is then validated by systematic VARIATION rather than by assertion. For the Cr/Fe complex the initial space held the singly occupied Cr(z2) orbital, the metal-metal bonding and antibonding orbitals, and Cr(xy), Fe(xy) and Fe(x2-y2), each with a correlation partner of the same symmetry usually representing the metal-ligand antibonding combination, giving nine electrons in nine orbitals. The paper states what would be desirable: adding the Fe(z2) orbital and the two highest occupied Cot(2-) pi orbitals plus their three metal-ligand antibonding counterparts, 'which would lead to a CAS(15/15) wave function, which is not feasible for calculation'. To test the truncation, CAS(9/9) calculations were run with the SYMMETRY COMPOSITION systematically varied across five partitions — 7a'2a'', 6a'3a'', 5a'4a'', 4a'5a'' and 3a'6a'' — with the lowest quartet and doublet sought for each, and because 'the results of CASSCF calculations are usually sensitive to the initial guess, different doublet, quartet, and sextet RHF wave functions were tested as starting orbitals for each active space'. The winning space is chosen on two criteria at once: lowest energy AND physical reasonableness of the resulting wavefunction.
nroots_per_mult: Lowest doublet and quartet computed for each of the five active-space partitions tested
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 2A', obtained by far the lowest in energy of all wavefunctions tested. The unpaired electron is localized on chromium in the Cr(z2) orbital at occupation exactly 1.00, so it should be only slightly affected by interaction with the second metal. The 50a'/52a' pair describes a DIRECT METAL-METAL BOND formed by overlap of the two formally singly occupied fragment orbitals Cr(x2-y2) and Fe(yz), of mainly sigma character given the relative orientation of the CpCr+ and (CO)3Fe+ fragments. Its formal bond order, taken as half the difference between bonding and antibonding populations, is only 0.5 — (1.51 minus 0.49)/2 — indicating a rather weak metal-metal bond. Orbital 30a'' is the metal-ligand bonding combination of Cr(xy), which with its antibonding counterpart 31a'' describes an electron pair mainly localized on chromium.
Other: The 0.49 occupation of the metal-metal antibonding orbital 52a' against 1.51 for its bonding partner is the quantitative heart of this system, and the paper immediately qualifies it: the formal bond order of 0.5 is a CASSCF number, and 'the inclusion of dynamical correlation effects, e.g., by means of a subsequent CASPT2 or MRCI calculation, would, in general, reduce somewhat the weight of the metal-metal antibonding configurations in the wave function and, therefore, predict a stronger metal-metal bond'. So the bond order derived from an uncorrelated active space is a lower bound, and the direction of the correction is known even though it was not computed. The truncation is equally well characterized: the two highest occupied Cot(2-) pi orbitals and the Fe(z2) orbital that a CAS(15/15) would have carried are simply absent, with three Fe-based orbitals sitting inactive at exactly 2.00 occupation. Since those inactive orbitals are pinned at 2.00, the space is not depriving itself of anything with fractional occupation — the useful check that the retained nine orbitals span all the correlation the reference can express. The transferable practice here is validating a forced truncation by varying the space's SYMMETRY COMPOSITION at fixed size. Five partitions of nine orbitals between a' and a'' symmetry were tried (7a'2a'' through 3a'6a''), each with the lowest doublet and quartet sought, and each started from several different RHF references because 'the results of CASSCF calculations are usually sensitive to the initial guess'. That is a genuine search over a discrete space rather than a single choice, and the selection criterion combines lowest energy with physical reasonableness of the wavefunction — the paper reports that the winning partition 'also yielded the only physically reasonable description of the electronic ground state of the system among all wave functions tested'. The desirable larger space, CAS(15/15) for the Cr/Fe complex and CAS(13/13) for the dichromium one, is stated explicitly and declared infeasible, so the reader knows precisely what is missing: the Cot(2-) pi donor orbitals and their antibonding partners, which appear in the INACTIVE space instead.
reference_short: Richter, Reinhold & Heck, Inorg. Chem. 2000, 39, 658
notes: One of two dinuclear Cot-bridged complexes studied. Metal-ligand interactions in bridged dinuclear systems are noted as a source of large nondynamical correlation effects, independent of the weak metal-metal bond. Figure 2 shows the frontier orbitals of the (CO)3M' fragment relative to the CpCr chromium centre; Figure 3 shows the Cot(2-) pi orbitals, which are non-degenerate because the ring is bent. The paper does not write out a molecular formula, so none is recorded.
correlation_correction: None applied. The paper notes that a subsequent CASPT2 or MRCI treatment 'would, in general, reduce somewhat the weight of the metal-metal antibonding configurations in the wave function and, therefore, predict a stronger metal-metal bond'.

To test the truncation, CAS(9/9) calculations were run with the SYMMETRY COMPOSITION systematically varied across five partitions — 7a'2a'', 6a'3a'', 5a'4a'', 4a'5a'' and 3a'6a'' — with the lowest quartet and doublet sought for each, and because 'the results of CASSCF calculations are usually sensitive to the initial guess, different doublet, quartet, and sextet RHF wave functions were tested as starting orbitals for each active space'. electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 4A''. The three unpaired electrons are localized on the chromium of the CpCr unit, occupying its z2, x2-y2 and xy orbitals at exactly 1.00 each — orbitals which, as in vanadocene, essentially represent the three formally nonbonding metal d orbitals. The other six active orbitals are the z2, x2-y2 and xy orbitals of the (CO)3Cr fragment and their metal-carbonyl antibonding counterparts. Within the active orbital set there is NO indication of a direct metal-metal bond, in contrast to the Cr/Fe complex. The two highest occupied Cot(2-) pi orbitals fall in the inactive space; because of the electron deficiency of the CpCr(2+) fragment the a'' pi orbital donates primarily into the xz orbital of Cr1, while the a' pi orbital donates into the yz orbitals of both metals, producing some electron density between them. Orbital 47a' therefore gives rise to a direct metal-metal binding interaction, but the metal contributions to it are very small so the interaction is extremely weak — consistent with the very small zero-field splitting seen by ESR and with the high reactivity of the complex.
Other: This complex illustrates a specific hazard of a truncated space: the only metal-metal bonding interaction it possesses lives in an INACTIVE orbital. Within the active set 'there is no indication of a direct metal-metal bond', and the binding contribution comes from 47a', a Cot pi donor orbital held doubly occupied outside the active space. A reader taking the active-space populations at face value would conclude there is no metal-metal interaction at all, when in fact there is a very weak one mediated by ligand donation into the yz orbitals of both metals. The desirable space is again stated and declared unaffordable — three singly occupied Cr1 orbitals, a metal-metal bonding/antibonding pair, the formally doubly occupied Cr2(z2) and Cr2(xy), the two highest Cot(2-) pi orbitals and four metal-ligand antibonding combinations, 'leading in all to 13 electrons in 13 active orbitals'. Five partitions of nine orbitals between a' and a'' symmetry were tried (7a'2a'' through 3a'6a''), each with the lowest doublet and quartet sought, and each started from several different RHF references because 'the results of CASSCF calculations are usually sensitive to the initial guess'. compound_name: Mn(H)(CO)3(H-DAB) — photodissociation and electronic spectroscopy of a manganese hydride diimine complex
point_group: Cs, enforced throughout the potential energy surface calculations
geometry_source: Two-dimensional potential energy surfaces V(qa,qb) with qa = Mn-H and qb = Mn-CO(axial), under a Cs symmetry constraint; 30 to 35 ab initio points computed per electronic state and the whole potentials fitted numerically by bicubic splines. Geometry optimizations with MOLCAS-3 or HONDO.
method: CASSCF averaged over five roots per spin and symmetry, supplemented by multireference contracted CI (MR-CCI); CASPT2 attempted for all states but successful only for two; spin-orbit coupling from a restricted full CI scheme with an effective one-electron operator on the metal; quantum wave packet dynamics on the fitted surfaces
software: MOLCAS-3 for the CASSCF/MR-CCI work; MOLCAS-3 or HONDO for geometry optimizations
basis_set: ANO sets: metal (17s,12p,9d) contracted to [6s,4p,3d]; second-row atoms (10s,6p,3d) to [3s,2p]; the metal-bound hydrogen (7s,3p) to [3s,1p]; other hydrogens (7s,3p) to [2s]
active_space_orbital_description: 8e10a: the occupied Mn 3d orbitals and the 3d orbitals that correlate them, the vacant 3d orbital, the bonding sigma(Mn-H) and antibonding sigma*(Mn-H) orbitals of the Mn-H bond, and the low-lying pi*(H-DAB) orbital.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by the EXCITATIONS of interest rather than by a valence rule: since the study centres on 3d to pi*(H-DAB), sigma(Mn-H) to pi*(H-DAB), and 3d to 3d excitations, 'the CASSCF active space is limited to' exactly the orbitals those three excitation types require — the occupied 3d set with correlating partners, the vacant 3d, the Mn-H sigma/sigma* pair, and the acceptor pi*(H-DAB). Averaging is over five roots of a given spin and symmetry for each of the four blocks (1,3A' and 1,3A''). The MR-CCI includes every configuration appearing with a coefficient above 0.08 in the CASSCF expansion, correlating eight electrons with single and double excitations to all virtuals except the carbonyl 1s and metal 1s, 2s, 2p counterparts. Kinetic coupling around avoided crossings was approximated by Lorentzians rather than differentiated numerically.
nroots_per_mult: 5 roots per spin and symmetry block (1A', 3A', 1A'', 3A'')
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF/MR-CCI excitation energies in cm-1 to the low-lying triplet states, with CASPT2 values where obtainable: a1A' to a3A' (3d(xz) to pi*(H-DAB)) 16100, CASPT2 16300; a1A' to a3A'' (3d(yz) to pi*) 17200; a1A' to b3A' (3d(x2-y2) to pi*) 19200, CASPT2 19000; a1A' to c3A' (3d(yz) to 3d(xy)) 26400; a1A' to d3A' (sigma(Mn-H) to pi*, the SBLCT state) 34400. A singlet SBLCT state from sigma(Mn-H) to pi*(H-DAB) is calculated at 35600 cm-1 with an oscillator strength of 0.11. The singlet-triplet gap is small (under 2000 cm-1) for states delocalized on the pi*(H-DAB) acceptor, whether MLCT or SBLCT, but large (over 5000 cm-1) for the metal-centred state. The 3d(xz) to pi* MLCT state is anomalous, with a 7000 cm-1 singlet-triplet gap caused by strong interaction between its singlet component and the electronic ground state — evidenced by a low principal-configuration CI coefficient of 0.75 for c1A' against about 0.85 for the other MLCT states.
Other: The most useful practical record here is a documented CASPT2 FAILURE on a system where MR-CCI succeeded. CASPT2 excitation energies could be obtained only for the a3A' and b3A' states; 'our attempt at performing reference CASPT2 calculations for the other states has failed either because of their less pure character, characterized by a large mixing of configurations at the CASSCF level, or because of the occurrence of intruder states'. Where both methods worked they agree essentially exactly — 16100 against 16300 and 19200 against 19000 cm-1 — so the MR-CCI numbers for the remaining states inherit that credibility even though they cannot be cross-checked. The two failure modes named are worth separating: configuration mixing is a property of the state, intruder states a property of the perturbation series, and only the second is in principle curable by level shifts. A related diagnostic runs through the paper: the CI coefficient on the principal configuration is used as a state-purity measure, and the one state with a coefficient of 0.75 rather than about 0.85 is precisely the one whose singlet-triplet gap is anomalous at 7000 cm-1 — so low CI coefficients flag both the CASPT2 difficulty and the physical ground-state interaction. Because the active space contains only the orbitals needed for three named excitation types, it cannot describe states outside that set, which is the deliberate trade for being able to compute 30-35 surface points per state.

notes: For the dynamics the molecule is modelled as pseudotriatomic with two collinear dissociative bonds, qa = Mn-H and qb = Mn-CO(axial), these being the coordinates most significantly affected on electronic excitation. Electronic dipole transition moments were estimated at the CASSCF level. Spin-orbit coupling between singlet and triplet states used a restricted full CI scheme with an effective one-electron operator acting on the metal in the L-S coupling scheme. Only the first-derivative part of the kinetic coupling is needed in the authors' nonadiabatic treatment. The paper does not write out a molecular formula, so none is recorded.

compound_name: n-Tetrasilane (n-Si4H10) — conformational dependence of the UV spectrum
point_group: C2h at the anti planar geometry (omega = 180 degrees), C2v at the syn planar geometry (omega = 0), C2 at intermediate twist angles where only a twofold axis survives
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized at MP2/6-31G**; the potential energy was mapped as a function of the SiSiSiSi dihedral angle omega by freezing omega at successive values and optimizing all other coordinates, with full optimization at the resulting local minima. Excitation energies and oscillator strengths were computed at those MP2 geometries.
method: 6-in-8 CASSCF for the excitation energies and oscillator strengths as a function of the backbone dihedral; CIS with a larger polarized basis for comparison; HF and MP2 for ground-state structures and vibrational spectra; matrix-isolation IR and vacuum-UV spectroscopy
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF; a polarized basis (H: 6s4p contracted to 3s2p; other atoms: 13s10p4d contracted to 7s5p2d) for the CIS; 6-31G** for the HF and MP2 work
active_space_orbital_description: 6-in-8: six electrons in eight orbitals. The paper does not enumerate the individual orbitals, though the states of interest are described as arising from sigma(SiSi) to sigma*(SiSi) and sigma(SiSi) to pi*(SiH) excitations.
active_space_protocol: The active space is applied uniformly across a full scan of the SiSiSiSi dihedral angle, which is what the study requires since the whole question is how the spectrum changes with conformation. The CASSCF results were checked against CIS with a substantially larger polarized basis, and the comparison is used to separate robust from fragile conclusions rather than to claim convergence.

electronic_structure_description: Four low-lying valence excited states — two of A and two of B symmetry — lie in the region of interest, arising from four singly excited configurations with considerable mixing within each symmetry pair at intermediate twist angles. Excitation energies to the two lowest (2A and 1B) change little with omega and those to 3A and 2B hardly at all, but the OSCILLATOR STRENGTHS vary remarkably. At the anti planar geometry (omega = 180 degrees) the transition to 1B(Bu), a sigma(SiSi) to sigma*(SiSi) state, is intense while the transition to 2B(Bg), sigma(SiSi) to pi*(SiH), is symmetry-forbidden; at the syn planar geometry (omega = 0) the transition to 1B(B1), now sigma to pi*(SiH), is extremely weak while 2B(B2), sigma to sigma*(SiSi), is intense. The lowest-energy transition thus has virtually no intensity at omega = 0 and is by far the most intense at omega = 180, while its energy differs by less than 0.1 eV. The cause is a set of AVOIDED CROSSINGS: at intermediate twist only a twofold axis survives, sigma and pi symmetry can no longer be distinguished, and the intended crossings are avoided — the lowest antibonding a1 MO starts as sigma* at omega = 0 and becomes pure pi*(au) at 180, while the lowest antibonding b1 starts as pi* and becomes pure sigma*(bu). Below omega = 30 degrees a further A-symmetry configuration (A2 at omega = 0) drops enough to dominate the 3A state, an excitation from a b2 sigma orbital with one node, strongly destabilized at small omega by a syn-periplanar interaction. Two ground-state conformers, anti and gauche, are found with almost the same energy.
Other: The authors draw an explicit and unusually careful line between what their active space settles and what it does not: 'the qualitative trends in the valence space are INDEPENDENT both of the size of the valence basis set and of the size of the CI space, but the quantitative aspects, such as the detailed shape of the state energy curves and even the ORDERING WITHIN THE LOWEST PAIR OF STATES, depend on the details of the calculation.' Concretely, the 6-in-8 CASSCF gives an Au rather than a Bu state lowest at the anti geometry, differing from the CIS result, and the paper presents the CASSCF curves anyway while stating 'it is uncertain that the Au below Bu order is correct'. They describe the results as 'still only preliminary' and plan to improve them with diffuse functions and a larger CI. That is the right posture for a system whose four low-lying states span a fraction of an eV and mix strongly at intermediate geometries. The robust physics — that oscillator strength migrates dramatically between states as the backbone twists while the state energies barely move, driven by avoided crossings that convert sigma* into pi* character — survives every level tested, and it is that qualitative result the spectral assignments rest on. A caution for reuse: the eight active orbitals are never enumerated, so the space cannot be reconstructed from the text.

notes: Matrix-isolation IR and UV spectra of Si3H8 and Si4H10 were measured, with the n-Si4H10 IR spectrum separated into anti and gauche conformer contributions and a qualitative separation of their UV spectra achieved. In a sigma-delocalized system oscillator strength is carried primarily by the one-electron sigma-sigma* excitation in which sigma and sigma* differ by a single node. Resonance integrals are negative for vicinal, geminal and syn-periplanar interactions and positive for anti-periplanar ones. The energy ordering of excited configurations from HOMO promotions does not follow the HF virtual orbital ordering, because a 1-sigma-pi* configuration lies below a 1-sigma-sigma* one for the same orbital energy difference, K(sigma,pi*) being smaller than K(sigma,sigma*) since sigma and pi* avoid each other in space.

compound_name: m-Phenylenediamine dication diradical (1(2+)) — aminium radical centres bridged by m-phenylene
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at ROHF (3B2, 1B2) or GVB (1A1) and then reoptimized at the CASSCF level; CAS(8,8) energies reported at both sets of geometries
method: CASSCF with CASPT2, following ROHF and GVB reference calculations
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(8,8), also called the pi-CAS: eight electrons in the eight Huckel pi molecular orbitals, namely 1b1, 1a2, 2b1, 3b1, 2a2, 4b1, 3a2 and 5b1 (with 4b1 and 3a2 inverted for the 1A1 state of the m-phenylenediamine dication).
active_space_protocol: A pi-only CAS(8,8) whose orbitals are enumerated explicitly: 1b1, 1a2, 2b1, 3b1, 2a2, 4b1, 3a2, 5b1, corresponding to the eight Huckel pi molecular orbitals — with the note that for the 1A1 state of the m-phenylenediamine dication the 4b1 and 3a2 orbitals are inverted. The paper also records a useful equivalence: 'the ROHF/GVB method is EQUIVALENT TO THE CAS(2,2) METHOD', so the GVB starting point sits on the same ladder as the CASSCF, with the (8,8) representing the full pi extension of it. CAS(8,8) energies were computed first at the ROHF/GVB optimized geometries and then all three states were reoptimized at the CASSCF level, so both the geometry effect and the correlation effect can be read off Table 2 separately.
