For 1B2: ROHF -340.0953 (9.0); CASSCF//ROHF -340.1828 (10.2); CASSCF//CASSCF -340.1835 (10.4); CASPT2 -341.0790 (11.2). For 1A1: GVB//GVB -340.1034 (3.9); CASSCF//GVB -340.1717 (17.2); CASSCF//CASSCF -340.1723 (17.4); CASPT2 -341.0957 (0.7). The singlet-triplet splitting is therefore 0.7 kcal/mol at CASPT2. The triplet has strong C-N pi-bonding character (1.292 A) from nitrogen substitution, in contrast to m-quinodimethane. The 1B2 state has an equilibrium geometry similar to the triplet, but unlike 3B2 its frontier electrons are not kept apart by the Pauli principle and are more localized on different regions of the benzene ring. The 1A1 state shows a cyanine-like distortion and is highly ionic.
Other: This is one of the largest single-state CASPT2 corrections recorded in this database: the 1A1 state falls from 17.4 kcal/mol above the triplet at CASSCF to 0.7 at CASPT2, a shift of 16.7 kcal/mol, while the 1B2 state moves only from 10.4 to 11.2. So the pi-CAS(8,8) treats the three states of one molecule very unevenly, and the reason is stated: 'the 1A1 state exhibits a cyanine-like distortion, and therefore has a highly ionic character compared with the 3B2 and 1B2 states', which is 'why this state is significantly stabilized by dynamic correlation compared with the other states'. A valence pi space is a covalent description; ionic configurations require the dynamic correlation it omits. The geometry effect is negligible by comparison — reoptimizing at CASSCF rather than at ROHF/GVB changes the relative energies by only 0.2 kcal/mol for every state — so essentially the entire CASSCF-to-CASPT2 difference is electronic rather than structural. A useful bookkeeping note: the paper states that ROHF/GVB is equivalent to CAS(2,2), placing the GVB reference on the same ladder as the CASSCF, and the GVB relative energy for 1A1 (3.9 kcal/mol) happens to be much closer to the CASPT2 answer than the CAS(8,8) value is — coincidence rather than accuracy, since GVB lacks both the correlation and the flexibility. The comparison between the two dications isolates a dynamic-correlation effect that a pi-only active space cannot itself capture, and the paper explains the mechanism. For the m-phenylenediamine dication the singlet-triplet gap collapses from 17.4 kcal/mol at CASSCF to 0.7 at CASPT2 — a 16.7 kcal/mol correction on a single state — while for the triazine dication the same quantity moves only from 12.8 to 12.5 kcal/mol. The cause is that the 1A1 state 'exhibits a cyanine-like distortion, and therefore has a highly ionic character compared with the 3B2 and 1B2 states', and ionic states are precisely what a valence pi space describes worst; in the triazine system 'charge polarization is reduced by dispersion over the triazine ring due to aza-substitution', so the same state is far less ionic and needs far less correction. The practical rule: a pi-CAS treats covalent and ionic states unequally, and the size of the CASPT2 correction on a given state is a direct measure of its ionic character.

compound_name: Protonated Schiff base model with three conjugated double bonds (molecule A)
geometry_source: Ground-state geometry from B3LYP/6-31G* optimization with Gaussian 98
method: State-averaged CASSCF as the reference for multireference CI (MRCI); HF/MRCI for comparison; B3LYP for ground-state geometries
software: COLUMBUS version 5.5 (SCF, CASSCF and MRCI), using routines from DALTON; Gaussian 98 for the B3LYP geometries; GAMESS for the excited-state CASSCF optimizations
basis_set: 6-31G in the first set of calculations and 6-31G* in the second, since 'polarization functions might be essential for a proper description of this system' and the same basis was used by Garavelli et al.
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(6,6): all excitations within an active space of six orbitals and six electrons, state-averaged over S0, S1 and S2. In the MRCI step the reference space comprised all single and double excitations from the two highest occupied into the two lowest virtual orbitals, giving 15 reference configurations.
active_space_protocol: The CASSCF(6,6) reference was chosen to be 'very similar to the calculation carried out by Garavelli et al.', making the comparison with that earlier conical-intersection work direct. Two basis sets were run: with 6-31G, six core and 14 virtual orbitals were frozen, giving 3.6 million configuration state functions; with 6-31G*, six core and 28 virtual orbitals (all with orbital energies above 1.5 au) were frozen, giving nearly 8 million CSFs. The reference space was verified post hoc — 'inspection of the results ensured that all configurations which show an expansion coefficient larger than 0.1 in the optimized CI wave functions are contained in the reference configurations'.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (S0, S1, S2) in the state-averaged CASSCF
electronic_structure_description: An S0/S1 crossing is found on a single rotation about the C=C double bond at the CASSCF level. The authors state they cannot determine from their method whether this is an avoided or a real crossing, but conclude from comparison with Garavelli et al. that it most likely corresponds to their conical intersection. This state crossing is LOST after the subsequent MRCI calculation.
Other: The smallest model is where the central methodological result is established: a CASSCF-level S0/S1 crossing on double-bond rotation vanishes when MRCI is performed on that same CASSCF reference. Since the reference space was verified to contain every configuration with a CI coefficient above 0.1, the disappearance is not a reference-space deficiency but a genuine effect of dynamic correlation on the state separation. The authors are careful about what their method can and cannot resolve — they cannot distinguish an avoided from a real crossing — and rely on comparison with Garavelli et al.'s independent work to identify the CASSCF feature as that group's conical intersection. Two basis sets were run precisely because polarization functions were suspected to matter, and the CSF count roughly doubles from 3.6 to 8 million between them, which bounds what is affordable at this reference size. The paper's central claim is a method-dependence of a QUALITATIVE feature: 'predictions of crossings of electronic states depend on the method of calculation and are different at the CASSCF and CASSCF/MRCI levels'. Specifically, an S0/S1 crossing found on rotation about the C=C double bond at the CASSCF level 'is LOST after the following MRCI calculation' — so a conical intersection present in the reference disappears once dynamic correlation is added on the same reference. That is the same phenomenon seen elsewhere in this database where CASPT2 splits CASSCF-located crossings, but here it is followed through to the mechanistic conclusion rather than noted as a caveat. A second layer: adding a counterion near the protonated Schiff base makes HF/MRCI and CASSCF/MRCI predict DIFFERENT regions for the S0/S1 crossing, so the reference choice matters as much as the correlation treatment once electrostatics are included. Throughout, the reference space was validated by the standard test that every configuration with a CI expansion coefficient of 0.1 or more appears among the reference configurations.

notes: The small model system continued from the authors' previous contribution, which had used an HF/MRCI approach. Structures of all the Schiff base model molecules are shown in Figure 1. geometry_source: All stationary points optimized at the CASSCF level with ANO-L; the most relevant ground-state structures additionally optimized at CASPT2. Minima and saddle points characterized by harmonic CASSCF/ANO-L frequencies; imaginary modes at Franck-Condon geometries obtained from the mass-weighted Cartesian force matrix after projecting out gradient, rotational and translational contributions. Transition states verified by intrinsic reaction paths; minimum energy paths from conical intersections started along the gradient difference and nonadiabatic coupling vectors. Conical intersections located with Gaussian 03.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF with multistate CASPT2 for vertical transitions; CASSI for transition dipole moments
software: MOLCAS 6.4 (CASSCF and CASPT2); Gaussian 03 (conical intersection location); MacMolPlt for visualization
basis_set: ANO-L with the C, N, O [4s3p2d1f] / H [3s2p1d] contraction scheme
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in eleven valence orbitals: 2s(O), 2s(N), sigma(XH), sigma(NN), pi(NO), sigma(NO), n(p)(N), pi*(NO), sigma*(NN), sigma*(NO) and sigma*(XH), where X is N or O depending on the tautomer.
active_space_protocol: A single (14,11) valence space, enumerated orbital by orbital and TRANSFERRED from the authors' earlier study of neutral nitrosamine: 2s(O), 2s(N), sigma(XH), sigma(NN), pi(NO), sigma(NO), n(p)(N), pi*(NO), sigma*(NN), sigma*(NO) and sigma*(XH), where X is N or O depending on which tautomer is being treated. The same space serves every conformer, tautomer, transition state and conical intersection, so the whole ground- and excited-state surface rests on one reference. CASPT2 is computed over the CASSCF reference with the 1s core orbitals of C, N and O frozen as optimized at the CASSCF level. An IMAGINARY LEVEL SHIFT was applied as the default in every linear-interpolation calculation, with the stated purpose of preventing situations 'in which the weight of the CASSCF wave function in the perturbative treatment results is too low, and as a consequence, the CASPT2 potential energy surface is not continuous. In such cases, the CASPT2 treatment would lack significance.' Transition dipole moments came from the CAS state interaction (CASSI) procedure with perturbatively modified PMCAS-CI reference functions built as linear combinations of all states in the MS-CASPT2 calculation.
nroots_per_mult: At least 2 (the SA-CASSCF zero-order wavefunction includes two states with equal weights)
electronic_structure_description: Two of the four stable conformers of protonated nitrosamine at both CASSCF and CASPT2 levels are trans-NH2NOH+ and cis-NH2NOH+, separated by about 6 kcal/mol. Mulliken analysis of neutral nitrosamine identifies two main protonation sites — the amino nitrogen at -0.42 e and the nitroso oxygen at -0.31 e — while the nitroso nitrogen carries only -0.01 e and is not favoured. Critical points located include the trans and cis minima, the cis-trans isomerization saddle point, an NH2 rotation saddle point, two S1/S0 conical intersections, and staggered, twisted and cis minima on S1. A transition state for NH2NOH+ to NH2NHO+ interconversion lies at 63.2 kcal/mol. On comparing MS-CASPT2 vertical transitions with the experimental low-temperature absorption of the nitrosamine-acid complex (bands at 3.39 eV / 367 nm, 3.63 eV / 342 nm and 3.74 eV / 333 nm), neither trans-NH2NOH+, cis-NH2NOH+ nor NH2NHO+ accounts for the observed lower absorption band, so all are discarded as the absorbing species. This tautomer is photochemically inert.
Other: The (14,11) space is unusually complete for a small molecule — it holds both nitrogen and oxygen 2s orbitals alongside the full sigma and pi valence manifold — and that completeness is what allows one space to describe two protonation isomers, four ground-state conformers, several transition states and two conical intersections without modification. Only the sigma(XH)/sigma*(XH) pair changes identity, following the proton between oxygen and nitrogen. The space was not designed here but transferred from the authors' earlier neutral-nitrosamine study, which is a defensible choice given the chromophore is unchanged, though it means no space-size test appears in this paper. Its adequacy is instead tested against experiment: the computed vertical transitions rule this tautomer out as the absorbing species, and independent agreement with the authors' earlier neutral nitrosamine (2.98 eV) and neutral NDMA (3.29 and 3.34 eV in gas phase and water) calculations supports the assignment. The methodological point worth carrying is the reason given for applying an imaginary level shift BY DEFAULT rather than as a remedy: it prevents the CASSCF reference weight in the perturbative treatment from dropping so low that 'the CASPT2 potential energy surface is not continuous. In such cases, the CASPT2 treatment would lack significance.' That reframes the level shift as a continuity requirement for surface scanning rather than merely an intruder-state fix — the relevant failure is a discontinuous surface, not a single bad energy. The (14,11) space is transferred wholesale from the authors' earlier neutral-nitrosamine work and applied unchanged across both tautomers, with only the sigma(XH)/sigma*(XH) pair shifting between N-H and O-H according to where the proton sits. That is the minimal adaptation needed to keep the space chemically equivalent between protonation isomers, and it is what makes the tautomer energy comparison meaningful.
reference_short: Pelaez, Arenas, Otero, Avila & Soto, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 8394
notes: Protonated nitrosamine exhibits four stable conformers at CASPT2 and CASSCF: trans-NH2NOH+, cis-NH2NOH+, cis-NH3NO+ and NH2NHO+, shown in Scheme 2. CASSCF critical points related to ground- and first-excited-state chemistry are collected in Figure 1, with imaginary modes on the saddle points and gradient difference and nonadiabatic derivative coupling vectors on the conical intersections. Experimental work has dealt exclusively with the first excited singlet state.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 and multistate CASPT2 over the CASSCF reference with 1s cores frozen, using an imaginary level shift throughout to control intruder states and preserve continuity of the perturbed surface

electronic_structure_description: cis-NH3NO+ is one of the four stable conformers and corresponds to an ADDUCT between NH3 and NO+ at both CASSCF and CASPT2 levels; trans-NH3NO+ is a first-order saddle point. The transition state for NH3NO+ to NH2NHO+ interconversion lies at 75.8 kcal/mol. Dissociation to a state at high energy (about 127 kcal/mol) makes that process inaccessible, while another state occurs 34.2 kcal/mol above the cis-NH3NO+ minimum. Its MS-CASPT2 vertical transition of 3.46 eV matches the experimentally observed new species formed on low-temperature excitation of the nitrosamine-acid complex, which has a tetrahedral amine conformation and absorbs at 3.19, 3.32 and 3.44 eV (391, 375 and 362 nm) and reverts on warming to the initial O-associated complex. compound_name: Carbon atom (3P ground state) — spin density at the nucleus from a CASSCF-to-full-CI series
geometry_source: Single atoms; no geometry optimization required
method: Full configuration interaction as the benchmark, with a systematic ladder of CASSCF calculations of increasing active-space size converging to it; spin polarization model results compared
software: GAMESS, with a determinant-based CI code by Ivanic and Ruedenberg for the full CI
basis_set: Chipman basis sets — segmented Dunning contractions of the Huzinaga (9s5p) primitive set, with the outer member of the innermost contraction uncontracted and diffuse s, p and one or more d functions added. Original Dunning sets with and without diffuse sp and d polarization functions were also used. Five-component spherical d functions throughout, since Cartesian d functions change results significantly by effectively adding an extra s function.
active_space_orbital_description: A ladder of complete active spaces built by adding shells, with the full CI reached at 22 orbitals: MCSCF(9) = 1s2s2p3s3p; MCSCF(13) = 1s2s2p3s3p4p4s; MCSCF(14) = 1s2s2p3s3p4p4s5s; MCSCF(15) = [1s2s2p]3s3p4s3d; MCSCF(18) = 1s2s2p3s3p4p4s3d; MCSCF(19) = 1s2s2p3s3p4p4s3d5s; and FCI = MCSCF(22) = 1s2s2p3s3p4p4s3d5s6p. The number in parentheses is the orbital count; electron counts are not given separately since all electrons are included at the FCI limit.
active_space_protocol: The study inverts the usual strategy and says so explicitly: 'instead of including a limited number of excitations within the space spanned by all basis functions, we include ALL excitations within a smaller space, and then gradually increase the size of that active space, UP TO FCI'. The authors stress that this is a genuine complete active space including every excitation within it, 'quite different from the spin polarization MCSCF wave function, which includes only a limited number of spin polarization configurations'. The ladder for carbon runs MCSCF(9) [1s2s2p3s3p], MCSCF(13) [+4p4s], MCSCF(14) [+5s], MCSCF(15) [1s2s2p 3s3p4s3d], MCSCF(18) [1s2s2p3s3p4p4s3d], MCSCF(19) [+5s], and finally FCI = MCSCF(22) [1s2s2p3s3p4p4s3d5s6p]. Because the ground states of B and C are 2P and 3P, the electron density was averaged over all degenerate components in every CASSCF calculation 'to ensure that the resulting wave function was a true L-squared (angular momentum) eigenfunction'. Full CI expansions ran to millions of determinants, handled by a determinant-based CI code of Ivanic and Ruedenberg.
nroots_per_mult: Density averaged over all degenerate components of the 3P ground state
electronic_structure_description: Convergence of the CASSCF spin density toward the full CI value with the [5s,2p]1sp1d basis (d exponent 0.40), given as energy in hartree then spin density: MCSCF(9) -24.570213, +0.0451845; MCSCF(13) -24.583678, -0.0132546; MCSCF(14) -24.584180, -0.0099208; MCSCF(15) -24.604076, -0.0056539; MCSCF(18) -24.604223, -0.0057322; MCSCF(19) -24.604663, -0.0011207; FCI = MCSCF(22) -24.604715, -0.0009381. The spin density therefore CHANGES SIGN between the smallest space and all larger ones, and the MCSCF(19) value — only three orbitals short of the full space — remains 20% away from the FCI result. The experimental values for boron and carbon are noted as not well established.
Other: This is the most direct measurement in the database of how slowly a complete active space converges to full CI for a property, and the answer is discouraging: three orbitals short of completeness, the spin density is still 20% off. Worse for practical purposes, the convergence is not even monotonic — the smallest space gives +0.045 while every larger one gives a negative value, and MCSCF(18) at -0.00573 is marginally FURTHER from FCI than the smaller MCSCF(15) at -0.00565 despite having three more orbitals. So neither the sign nor the trend of a small-space result can be extrapolated. The energies behave quite differently: MCSCF(15) already recovers -24.6041 against the FCI -24.6047, within 0.7 mhartree, while its spin density is six times too large. That decoupling is the core lesson — an active space converged for energy can be badly unconverged for a one-electron property sampled at a single point in space. The authors trace the cause to excitations into orbitals of very high angular momentum and conclude that 'including excitations within only a subspace of the complete space is not sufficient, even if all such excitations are included'. The conclusion is a direct verdict on active-space methodology for this property, and it is negative: 'the convergence of the spin density is very slow; the CASSCF value for an active space which is only THREE ORBITALS SHORT of the full space is still 20% off the FCI value ... we are forced to conclude that CASSCF calculations probably cannot be used as a substitute for FCI'. The general principle stated in the conclusions is broader still: 'it is unlikely that a method that does not account at least to some extent for excitations to ALL orbitals in the complete space of basis functions would be successful in correctly describing atomic spin densities at the nuclei. Including excitations within only a subspace of the complete space is not sufficient, EVEN IF ALL SUCH EXCITATIONS ARE INCLUDED.' That is the sharpest statement in this database of a property for which completeness within a subspace is structurally insufficient, and it is attributed to the need for excitations into orbitals of very high angular momentum. The convergence is also non-monotonic in sign, which rules out extrapolating a small-space result toward the exact answer.
reference_short: Pak & Gordon, J. Chem. Phys. 2000, 113, 4238
notes: Full CI provides the ultimate test of an atomic orbital basis set for spin density calculations, since it is exact for a given basis: any method giving better spin densities with the same basis is likely benefiting from fortuitous error cancellation. The paper concludes that the basis sets studied are largely inadequate for spin densities at the nuclei for boron and carbon, and that the spin polarization model may not be generally reliable. The FCI results are offered as benchmarks for testing cheaper approaches.
correlation_correction: None needed — full CI is the reference; the CASSCF series is the approximation being tested against it

compound_name: Water (H2O) — ground-state energy benchmark across three active spaces
geometry_source: Experimental geometries used for H2O, NH3 and CH4; for the supermolecule series the monomer bond lengths are 1.60, 1.50 and 1.50 A, with monomers separated by 200 A for N2 and F2 and 2000 A for HF to quench dipole-dipole interactions
method: A single-reference perturbation theory (SRPT1, SRPT2, SRPT3) built on ROHF or CASSCF orbitals, compared against CASSCF, MRCI, MRCI with Davidson correction (MRCI+Q), and multireference second- and third-order perturbation theory (MRPT2, MRPT3)
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for the total-energy comparisons; 6-31G also used in some supermolecule tests
active_space_orbital_description: Three complete active spaces used in parallel as references: CASSCF(2,2), CASSCF(4,4) and CASSCF(6,6). The largest, (6,6), is recorded in the numeric fields.
active_space_protocol: A methodological study in which the active space is a controlled VARIABLE rather than a modelling choice: CASSCF(2,2), CASSCF(4,4) and CASSCF(6,6) are each used as the reference for the same set of correlated methods, so the active-space dependence of every method can be read directly down the columns of Tables 2-4. For the size-extensivity tests the space is CASSCF(2,2) for the HF and F2 supermolecule series and CASSCF(2,2), (4,4) and (6,6) for the N2 dimer, specifically 'to investigate the impact of active spaces on SEE'; the fluorine 1s core is frozen. The CASSCF convergence threshold is 1e-8 hartree, which turns out to be the floor on the measurable size-extensivity errors themselves.
Other: Water shows the MRPT2 overshoot most starkly: at CASSCF(2,2) it gives -76.261841 hartree, LOWER than MRCI+Q's -76.232834 by 29 mhartree, and it climbs monotonically toward the variational answer as the space grows — -76.249367 at (4,4) and -76.234849 at (6,6). So the perturbative energy approaches the correct value FROM BELOW the variational bound, and a small-reference MRPT2 number that looks impressively low is in fact an artifact. MRCI moves only 15.5 mhartree across the same range of active spaces while CASSCF itself moves 80.9, which quantifies how much of the reference improvement MRCI already recovers by other means. The contrast with the single-reference series is equally instructive: SRPT1 changes by 0.6 mhartree across the three references and SRPT2 by 7.5, because those series 'consider only the ground-state configuration and its corresponding excitation configurations', so the nondynamical correlation in a larger CASSCF simply does not enter them. The systematic finding across all three molecules is that MRPT2 and MRPT3 depend strongly on the active space while MRCI barely does, and the dependence has a definite direction: 'MRPT2 overestimates the energies especially with a small complete active space like CASSCF(2,2) in comparison with MRCI results. MRPT3 counteracts these discrepancies significantly. As the complete active space increases from CASSCF(2,2) to CASSCF(6,6) the MRPT2 and MRPT3 results converge very closely to MRCI energies.' So a second-order multireference perturbation theory built on a minimal reference can OVERSHOOT the variational answer, and enlarging the space corrects it from above rather than from below. A second, independent result: the paper's single-reference perturbation energies are 'almost unchanged with respect to the three types of CASSCF wave functions', because the series considers only the ground-state configuration and its single and double excitations, so the nondynamical correlation carried by the CASSCF reference does not propagate into them.
reference_short: Chen, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2009, 5, 931
notes: Part of a methodological study introducing a single-reference perturbation theory beyond the Moller-Plesset partition, tested against established multireference methods. Experimental geometry used.
correlation_correction: MRCI, MRCI+Q, MRPT2 and MRPT3 on the CASSCF references, compared against the paper's own single-reference perturbation series

active_space_protocol: A methodological study in which the active space is a controlled VARIABLE rather than a modelling choice: CASSCF(2,2), CASSCF(4,4) and CASSCF(6,6) are each used as the reference for the same set of correlated methods, so the active-space dependence of every method can be read directly down the columns of Tables 2-4. compound_name: Sexithiophene dication (6T(2+)) — bipolaron versus polaron pair character
geometry_source: Geometry optimized at CASSCF/6-31G(d); CASSCF single points also computed on UB3LYP/6-31G(d) geometries
method: CASSCF with three active-space sizes; UB3LYP and B3LYP for geometries, charge distributions and comparison energies
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Active spaces of up to 10 electrons in 10 orbitals; CAS(4,4), CAS(6,6) and CAS(10,10) were each applied to every oligomer. The largest is recorded in the numeric fields. The paper does not enumerate the individual orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Three active spaces — CAS(4,4), CAS(6,6) and CAS(10,10) — were applied to every oligomer, so the active-space dependence of both the singlet-triplet gap and the electronic character can be read across Table 2 and the accompanying analysis. Geometries for the shorter oligomers 6T(2+) and 10T(2+) were optimized at CASSCF/6-31G(d); for the longer ones up to 12T(2+) the CASSCF calculations are single points on UB3LYP/6-31G(d) geometries. The electronic character is diagnosed by the number of ELECTRONS OUTSIDE CLOSED-SHELL BONDING ORBITALS, benchmarked against benzene, which has 0.13 electrons outside closed-shell bonding orbitals at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d).
electronic_structure_description: Triplet-minus-singlet energy differences in kcal/mol from CASSCF(m,m)/6-31G(d)//UB3LYP/6-31G(d), by active space: 33.2 at (4,4) [24.9 at the CASSCF-optimized geometry], 21.9 at (6,6), and 10.3 at (10,10) [15.4]. CASSCF single points give 0.09, 0.19 and 0.30 electrons outside closed-shell bonding orbitals for the (4,4), (6,6) and (10,10) spaces respectively — for comparison benzene has 0.13 electrons outside closed-shell bonding orbitals at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d). The electron distribution shows a significant contribution from the singlet BIPOLARON state with a smaller contribution from the singlet polaron-pair state, in agreement with the energies, bond-length alternation and charge distribution from B3LYP/6-31G(d).
Other: The shortest oligomer shows the largest active-space sensitivity in the series: the singlet-triplet gap falls from 33.2 to 10.3 kcal/mol between CAS(4,4) and CAS(10,10), a factor of three on the quantity the study is trying to establish. Geometry adds a further 5-6 kcal/mol of variation — the (4,4) gap is 33.2 at the DFT geometry but 24.9 at the CASSCF-optimized one, and the (10,10) gap moves the other way, 10.3 versus 15.4 — so geometry and active space do not shift the answer in a consistent direction. What IS robust is the character assignment: only 0.09-0.30 electrons lie outside closed-shell bonding orbitals at any space, bracketing benzene's 0.13, so this dication is essentially closed-shell bipolaronic on every treatment. The benzene calibration is the useful device here, giving an absolute reference for what 'negligible diradical character' looks like in the same diagnostic. The singlet-triplet gaps in Table 2 are strongly active-space dependent and the dependence is NOT systematic across chain length, which is the key caution for anyone reusing them. Across CAS(4,4), CAS(6,6) and CAS(10,10) the gaps run 33.2 / 21.9 / 10.3 kcal/mol for 6T(2+) — a factor of three — but 9.0 / 15.7 / 14.6 for 8T(2+), 1.1 / 6.8 / 9.7 for 10T(2+) and 11.1 / 4.8 / 1.9 for 12T(2+). So the gap falls monotonically with space size for the shortest and longest oligomers, rises for 10T(2+), and is non-monotonic for 8T(2+); no single active space gives a consistent trend along the series, and the CHAIN-LENGTH dependence of the gap changes qualitatively depending on which space is used. The diradical-character diagnostic is better behaved: electrons outside closed-shell bonding orbitals increase monotonically with space size for both oligomers reported (0.09 / 0.19 / 0.30 for 6T(2+) and 1.03 / 1.11 / 1.20 for 12T(2+)), so the qualitative assignment of bipolaron versus polaron-pair character is robust to the space even though the energies are not.

method: CASSCF for the S1 surface, B3LYP for the S0 and T1 surfaces and radicals, TD-B3LYP for vertical excitation energies; matrix-isolation infrared spectroscopy in low-temperature argon
basis_set: 6-31G** for the CASSCF; 6-31++G** for the DFT and TD-DFT
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(10,8): the three pi and three pi* orbitals of the pyridine ring, the amino nitrogen 2pz orbital, and the pyridine nitrogen nonbonding electrons.
active_space_protocol: A single fixed (10,8) space describes both tautomers and the transition structure connecting them on the S1 surface. Its composition mixes three kinds of orbital deliberately — the ring pi system that carries the excitation, the amino nitrogen 2pz that becomes the imino pi bond on tautomerization, and the pyridine nitrogen lone pair that accepts the migrating proton — so the space follows the chemistry of the hydrogen transfer rather than being a pure pi selection. The S0 and T1 surfaces are treated by DFT instead, so the S1 energetics in Figure 7 come from a different method than the surfaces they are compared against.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, triplet (the triplet at the DFT level only)
electronic_structure_description: In the S1 state the amino tautomer is LESS stable than the imino tautomer by 69.4 kJ/mol, and the tautomerization barrier from amino to imino is 164.6 kJ/mol at CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G**. This ordering and barrier follow the same trend as the keto-enol tautomerism between 2(1H)-pyridinone and 2-hydroxypyridine. The first irradiation wavelength used experimentally (340 > lambda >= 300 nm) is consistent with the S1-S0 transition energy of the amino tautomer. Bond lengths match those of 2-aminopyridine to within 0.01 A, showing no significant hyperconjugation of the methyl group with the ring. The molecular orbital phases at the LUMO of the imino tautomer are consistent with those of the amino tautomer, which would in principle allow the tautomerization to proceed in S1.
Other: The (10,8) space is built from three functionally distinct groups rather than as a uniform pi selection: three ring pi and three pi* orbitals for the excitation, the amino nitrogen 2pz which becomes the imino pi bond, and the pyridine nitrogen nonbonding pair which accepts the transferring proton. That composition is what allows one fixed space to describe both tautomers and the transition structure between them without changing character along the reaction coordinate — the amino 2pz and the pyridine lone pair exchange roles as the proton moves, but both remain in the space. The energetic conclusion is that the first irradiation, although resonant with the S1-S0 transition, carries insufficient energy to surmount the 164.6 kJ/mol S1 barrier, so the excited-state pathway is closed. Note that no dynamic-correlation correction was applied, and bare CASSCF typically overestimates barriers — which here reinforces rather than undermines the negative result. The methodological caution this paper illustrates is that a photochemical mechanism was RULED OUT on the strength of energetics assembled from three different methods. The S1 barrier of 164.6 kJ/mol comes from CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G**, the T1 barrier of 154.7 kJ/mol from B3LYP/6-31++G**, and the vertical excitation energies that set the accessible energy from TD-B3LYP/6-31++G**. The conclusion — that neither the S1 nor the T1 surface can carry the tautomerization, so it must occur during vibrational relaxation in S0 after internal conversion — depends on comparing a CASSCF barrier against a TD-DFT excitation energy, with no dynamic-correlation correction on the CASSCF side. Since bare CASSCF characteristically overestimates barriers relative to correlated treatments, the S1 barrier is likely an upper bound, which happens to strengthen rather than weaken the paper's negative conclusion.
reference_short: Akai, Harada, Shin-ya et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 6016
notes: Studied by infrared spectroscopy in a low-temperature argon matrix. No change from imino to amino occurs in darkness over at least 3 hours, which rules out a tunnelling mechanism and establishes that the tautomerism proceeds through electronically excited states. Its composition mixes three kinds of orbital deliberately — the ring pi system that carries the excitation, the amino nitrogen 2pz that becomes the imino pi bond on tautomerization, and the pyridine nitrogen lone pair that accepts the migrating proton — so the space follows the chemistry of the hydrogen transfer rather than being a pure pi selection. electronic_structure_description: The imino tautomer is the MORE stable of the two in the S1 state, lying 69.4 kJ/mol below the amino form at CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G** — an inversion of the ground-state ordering. The second irradiation wavelength used experimentally (420 > lambda >= 340 nm) is consistent with its S1-S0 transition energy, matching the behaviour of 2-aminopyridine. At the DFT level the trans imino tautomer is more stable than the amino tautomer by 30.4 kJ/mol in the T1 state. Its bond lengths agree with those of 2(1H)-pyridinimine to within 0.01 A.
Other: The imino tautomer is the photoproduct, and the fact that the SAME (10,8) space describes it and its amino precursor is what makes the 69.4 kJ/mol S1 stability difference meaningful — the amino nitrogen 2pz orbital that is a lone pair in one tautomer is part of the C=N pi bond in the other, and both situations are spanned because the space was chosen to contain the orbitals on both sides of the proton transfer. The excited-state stability ordering is inverted relative to the ground state, which is the electronic basis for the photoinduced tautomerism, and the two irradiation windows used experimentally map cleanly onto the two tautomers' S1-S0 transitions. The paper nevertheless concludes that neither the S1 nor the T1 surface carries the reaction, since the barriers exceed the available photon energy; the tautomerism is assigned instead to vibrational relaxation in the S0 state following internal conversion. The methodological caution this paper illustrates is that a photochemical mechanism was RULED OUT on the strength of energetics assembled from three different methods. The S1 barrier of 164.6 kJ/mol comes from CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G**, the T1 barrier of 154.7 kJ/mol from B3LYP/6-31++G**, and the vertical excitation energies that set the accessible energy from TD-B3LYP/6-31++G**. The conclusion — that neither the S1 nor the T1 surface can carry the tautomerization, so it must occur during vibrational relaxation in S0 after internal conversion — depends on comparing a CASSCF barrier against a TD-DFT excitation energy, with no dynamic-correlation correction on the CASSCF side. Since bare CASSCF characteristically overestimates barriers relative to correlated treatments, the S1 barrier is likely an upper bound, which happens to strengthen rather than weaken the paper's negative conclusion.

active_space_protocol: The paper's explicit methodological conclusion is about the relative importance of space size versus basis: 'the use of a LARGER ACTIVE SPACE IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN A HIGH LEVEL BASIS SET in order to get qualitatively correct state ordering for these biradicals when using CASSCF wave functions'. It is demonstrated by deliberately crude combinations — a CASSCF(8,8)/STO-3G* energy at a fixed ROHF/STO-3G* triplet geometry still gives the experimentally correct singlet-below-triplet ordering with a 1.1 kcal/mol gap, and CASSCF(6,6)/3-21G with separately optimized states gives 0.1 kcal/mol. A second practical rule is stated: 'if the same or nearly the same quinonoidal geometries are used for both the singlet and triplet states, CASSCF computations with sufficiently large orbital subspaces generally yield a near-degeneracy with a slight favoring of the singlet'. For the multireference CI the space had to be cut to (6,6) with 14 orbitals frozen — eight core plus six of the next-lowest — 'to conform to the limitations of 16 active orbitals inherent to MOLPRO', with the CASSCF(10,10) orbitals reused. Across the smaller molecules 2 and 3, 'where necessary, orbital reordering was carried out to ensure that the same active space orbitals were used for all states in each molecule'.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet-triplet (1Ag minus 3B1u) gaps in kcal/mol by method: CASSCF(8,8)/STO-3G* at a fixed ROHF/STO-3G* triplet geometry, 1.1; CASSCF(6,6)/3-21G with separately optimized states, 0.1; CASSCF(10,10)/cc-VTZ(2df,2p)//CASSCF(10,10)/D95**, 0.95; MRCISD/D95**, 1.2; MR-RSPT2/D95**, 2.0; MRCISD/cc-VTZ(2d,2p), 1.1; MRCISD/cc-VTZ(2df,2p), 1.0; RSPT2 with cc-VTZ(2d,2p) and cc-VTZ(2df,2p), 1.9 and 1.8. The largest calculations considered over 37 million configurations for the singlet and over 72 million for the triplet. The CASSCF(10,10)/D95** 1Ag ground state is essentially a TWO-CONFIGURATION wavefunction with coefficients 0.629 and -0.613 for double occupancy of the b2u and b3g orbitals; its four frontier natural orbital occupations are 1.80, 1.02, 0.98 and 0.21. The 3B1u state is largely single-determinantal with a leading coefficient of 0.886 and frontier occupations of 1.82, 1.00, 1.00 and 0.19. ESR Curie law studies of the triplet in frozen 2-methyltetrahydrofuran gave singlet-triplet gaps of 574 and 722 cal/mol. The aromatic quintet dinitrene states lie much higher, by an average of about 33 kcal/mol.
Other: The near-symmetric 1.02 / 0.98 pair of frontier natural orbital occupations in the singlet, against 1.00 / 1.00 in the triplet, is the numerical signature that both states are genuinely open-shell and that the singlet is a two-configuration wavefunction rather than a closed shell — the singlet's leading coefficients of 0.629 and -0.613 are almost equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. That is precisely the situation restricted DFT cannot represent, which is why RB3LYP gives 'artifactually high biradical singlet state energies' while unrestricted mixed-state UB3LYP recovers the correct ordering. On the multireference side, the MRCI had to be run in a (6,6) space rather than the (10,10) used for geometries, purely because of MOLPRO's 16-active-orbital limit, so the highest-level energies rest on a smaller reference than the structures they are computed at. The perturbative and variational treatments disagree systematically: RSPT2 overestimates the singlet's stability by about 0.8 kcal/mol against both MRCISD and experiment, which on a gap of roughly 1 kcal/mol is nearly the whole quantity — hence the recommendation of variational MRCISD for these systems. The general guidance the paper offers is that for these near-degenerate biradicals, active-space size matters more than basis quality — a CASSCF(8,8)/STO-3G* calculation at a fixed ROHF/STO-3G* geometry already reproduces the experimental singlet-below-triplet ordering, whereas the state ordering is what fails when the space is too small. It also finds that restricted B3LYP 'gives artifactually high biradical singlet state energies relative to the triplet biradical states', while unrestricted mixed-state UB3LYP correctly places the singlet slightly below the triplet and gives geometries comparable to the best CASSCF results — so for these systems the spin-restriction of the DFT reference, not the functional, is what decides the answer. A further caution concerns the perturbative correction: 'the RSPT2 calculations at all levels appear to overestimate the stability of the 1Ag state by about 0.8 kcal/mol in comparison to the variational results and the experimental singlet-to-triplet gap', so for gaps of order 1 kcal/mol 'variational MRCISD methods are superior'.

compound_name: Tryptophan zwitterion — quenching of 1(pi,pi*) fluorescence by intramolecular hydrogen abstraction
geometry_source: Started from the HF/6-31G* optimized zwitterionic ground-state conformer with the protonated ammonium closest to the benzene moiety of the indole chromophore, prearranged for proton transfer to the ring. All stationary points — minima, transition structures and conical intersections — optimized at CASSCF with a development version of Gaussian 98. S0-Taut optimized at HF/6-31G* and the decarboxylated pair S0-Degr at B3LYP/6-31G*, both then recomputed at CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G* with state-averaged orbitals.
method: CASSCF with state-averaged orbitals and CAS-MP2 single points using a procedure based on localization of the active space orbitals; valence-bond analysis of the localized active orbitals via one-electron density diagonal elements and spin-exchange density matrix elements; intrinsic reaction coordinate and initial relaxation direction calculations
software: Development version of Gaussian 98 (also cited as Gaussian 99 revision C.1)
active_space_orbital_description: The base active space is 10 electrons in nine orbitals, with NO Rydberg orbitals included. It is enlarged to (12,11) by adding the sigma(N-H) and sigma*(N-H) orbitals for the hydrogen-transfer transition structure, and reduced to (8,8) for frequency calculations and for the final conical-intersection characterization.
active_space_protocol: The active space is changed FOUR TIMES along one reaction path, each change justified by what the chemistry requires at that point. The base (10,9) covers the indole chromophore. For the hydrogen-transfer transition structure S1-TS-H 'the active space was extended to (12,11) by inclusion of the sigma(N-H) and sigma*(N-H) orbitals'. The IRC forward from that transition state ran with the full (12,11) but used FORCE CONSTANTS FROM A REDUCED (8,8) space, a cost-saving split between the energy and the Hessian. The IRC was then 'interrupted at a point of near degeneracy between the excited and the ground state, where the optimization fails to converge'; at that point 'the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the newly formed carbon-hydrogen bond were removed from the active space (OCCUPATIONS CLOSE TO 2 AND 0, respectively)', returning to (10,9) to optimize the intersection — an explicit occupation-based removal criterion. Finally 'the pi orbital with highest occupation was removed from the active space, and the intersection was reoptimized with the remaining (8,8) active space SOLVING THE COUPLED MCSCF EQUATIONS', the larger space having required an approximation in which those equations were not solved. Analytical frequencies for the transition structures were computed in the reduced (8,8).
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged over at least three states, with weights of 0.33/0.33 used for the orbitals of the second and third excited states
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G* vertical excitation energies are 4.98 eV for 1Lb and 6.19 eV for 1La, with 0-0 excitations of 4.63 and 5.46 eV; the third excited state 1Bb has a vertical excitation of 6.34 eV. Experimentally the 1Lb origin is near 286 nm (4.32 eV) with six close-lying bands assigned to six side-chain conformers; the 1La origin is undetermined but a vertical value of 4.7 eV can be estimated by assuming the same 0.4 eV state separation as in indole. The experimental 1Bb value is 5.58 eV for 3-methylindole and 5.80-6.02 eV for indole. Valence-bond analysis shows S1 is a benzene-benzene type excitation while S2 and S3 are ionic and biradical respectively; the three lowest excited valence states come out in the correct order at the Franck-Condon geometry. S1 is purely ionic at the geometries of S1-Exc and S1-TS-H. The S1/S0 intersection is rigorously characterized as PEAKED in Ruedenberg's terminology. Ground-state decarboxylation from CI-S1/S0 is barrierless. Adding a loosely hydrogen-bonded water molecule to the carboxylate and reoptimizing the intersection at CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G* gave essentially the same result, the only difference being a more stretched carbon-carbon bond (1.84 A) from stabilization of the closed-shell ionic tautomer state.
Other: This is the most elaborate example of a DYNAMICALLY ADAPTED active space in the database — four different spaces along a single reaction path, each with a stated criterion. The two most transferable moves are the removal rules. When the IRC reached near-degeneracy and stopped converging, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the newly formed C-H bond were dropped 'occupations close to 2 and 0, respectively' — the standard occupation-window criterion applied mid-path to shrink a space that had done its job. Then the pi orbital with highest occupation was removed to reach (8,8), and the stated reason is computational rather than physical: only at that size could the coupled MCSCF equations be solved rather than approximated, and only with them solved could the intersection be rigorously characterized as peaked. So the smallest space produced the most rigorous result. The paper is also candid about a systematic failure the space cannot fix: the 1La state is overestimated relative to 1Lb by 0.7-0.8 eV (16-18 kcal/mol), matching a known deviation in comparable CASSCF work on indole, and 'inclusion of the MP2 correlation energy did NOT correct this deviation' — accurate values require adding Rydberg-type orbitals or doubling the active space together with the MP2 correction. The authors accept the error rather than chase it, noting that the ionic state's poor reproduction stems partly from contaminating Rydberg states whose energies will rise once the hydrogen bond forms, so the hydrogen-transfer results should remain reliable.

The full list of CASSCF and CAS-MP2 energies is in Supporting Information Table S1. The water-complex calculation was performed specifically to exclude the possibility that the decarboxylation path is an artifact of mistreating the carboxylate negative charge.

active_space_protocol: A minimal bond-pair space containing exactly the three bonds that can break: Al-H and both Al-CH3. Since every decomposition pathway studied involves cleaving one of these, the same (6,6) describes reactant, every transition state and every dissociation asymptote without changing composition, which is what allows the competing channels to be compared on one footing. The SAME active space is reused for the internally contracted CI, with a selected reference list of configurations having CI coefficients above 0.05 and a multireference Davidson correction (ICCI+Q). Energetics come from CCSD(T) rather than from the multireference treatment, with the aluminium 10-electron neon core left uncorrelated.

electronic_structure_description: Decomposition channels of the monomer with their barriers: elimination to CH3AlCH2 + H2 has a barrier of 71.1 kcal/mol; dissociation to CH3AlH + CH3 is barrierless other than its exoergicity of 82.2 kcal/mol; formation of CH3Al + CH4 has a barrier of 90.4 kcal/mol. A validation case gives 73.6 kcal/mol from the cc-pVnZ extrapolation against an experimental 73.1 kcal/mol. Earlier work by others computed barriers of 28 and 22 kcal/mol for related processes and a binding energy of 32 kcal/mol for the DMAlH dimer, the latter also obtained at the MP2 level in independent work. Elimination to CH3AlCH2 + H2 has a lower barrier than simple bond-breaking from the monomer.
Other: The active space here is defined purely by the BONDS THAT BREAK — the Al-H and two Al-CH3 pairs, six electrons in six orbitals — which is the minimal construction that keeps every decomposition channel describable in one space. Because all three competing pathways cleave orbitals inside that space, the barriers of 71.1, 90.4 and the barrierless 82.2 kcal/mol channel are computed against a common reference and can be compared directly, which is the whole point of the study. Notably the multireference machinery is used for STRUCTURE, not energy: CASSCF supplies geometries and frequencies and ICCI+Q reuses the same space with a 0.05 coefficient threshold on the reference list, but the reported energetics come from CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ extrapolated to the complete basis set limit via MP2. The accuracy claim rests on external work — Dunning and Peterson found MP2 extrapolation of augmented cc-pVTZ results gives an average error of 0.72 kcal/mol in dissociation energies for AB molecules, and since dissociation energies are argued to be harder than barrier heights, the barriers should be good to well within 1 kcal/mol. That is validated in one case at 73.6 against an experimental 73.1 kcal/mol. The aluminium neon core was left uncorrelated throughout.

geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations with state averaging over the ground and target excited state at equal weights; NH dissociation pathways optimized under Cs symmetry restriction, all other geometries without symmetry constraint. Conical intersection geometries optimized at CASSCF were further corrected to approximate the CASPT2 intersection.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF geometry optimization with single-point internally contracted CASPT2 for dynamical correlation
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: For the deformation-path CASPT2, a (10s6p1d/5s1p)/[5s3p1d/3s1p] set of triple-zeta plus polarization quality; for the NH dissociation paths a triple-zeta set augmented with the same diffuse functions used in the double-zeta CASSCF optimizations

active_space_protocol: The paper uses SEVERAL DIFFERENT active spaces for different electronic states and reaction paths, and states each one and its reason. For out-of-plane deformation of the 7H-keto-amino and 7H-keto-imino tautomers: 16 electrons in 12 orbitals, being 11 pi orbitals plus one nitrogen lone pair (N3 for keto-amino, N10 for keto-imino). For the 7H-enol-amino tautomer a smaller (12,10) was necessary 'because the optimizations with 12 active orbitals COULD NOT BE PROPERLY CONVERGED due to the mixing of the orbitals', and for the same reason different orbital sets were used for different structures of that tautomer: 10 pi orbitals for the 1(pipi*) minimum; for the CI32 intersection the lowest pi orbital was REPLACED by the N3 lone pair; and for CI16 a further pi orbital was replaced by the N1 lone pair. For NH dissociation the space is 14 electrons in 11 pi orbitals, with one sigma* RYDBERG orbital added for the 1(pi-sigma*) state. CASPT2 single points used 16 electrons in 12 orbitals for the deformation paths and 14 electrons in 12 orbitals (11 pi plus one sigma*) for dissociation, with the enol-amino CASPT2 space taken as 10 pi orbitals plus BOTH the N1 and N3 lone pairs. CASSCF orbitals were state-averaged over two states with equal weights for the optimizations and over the lowest four singlets for the CASPT2 references; a level shift of 0.3 was used.
nroots_per_mult: 2 for the CASSCF optimizations (ground state plus target excited state, equal weights); lowest 4 singlets for the CASPT2 references
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2//CASSCF vertical excitation energies with oscillator strengths and dipole moments: ground state dipole 1.9 D; 1(pipi*) 1La at 4.37 eV, f = 0.142, 3.4 D; 1(pipi*) 1Lb at 5.11 eV, f = 0.009, 2.1 D; 1(n_O pi*) at 5.24 eV, f = 0.001, 5.2 D; 1(pi-sigma*) at 5.09 eV, f = 0.003, 12.0 D. The S0-S1 conical intersection CI32 lies at 4.02 eV above the ground-state minimum. At CI32 the N3C2 bond is strongly twisted with a C4N3C2N1 dihedral of 71.1 degrees, and the amino group is greatly distorted out of plane with a C4N3C2N10 dihedral of -146.6 degrees. The N3C2 bond is the primary candidate for twisting because twisting of the C4C5 double bond is hindered by the five-membered ring.
Other: The 1(pi-sigma*) state carries a dipole moment of 12.0 D against 1.9-5.2 D for every other state listed, which is the charge-separated signature that makes the sigma* Rydberg orbital essential — a space without it simply cannot represent this state. That is why the NH dissociation space explicitly adds one sigma* orbital to the 11 pi orbitals. The conical intersection is reached by twisting the N3C2 bond, and the space contains the N3 lone pair alongside the pi manifold precisely because that nitrogen's electronic environment changes as the bond twists. Note that the CI32 energy of 4.02 eV sits just below the 1La vertical excitation of 4.37 eV, so the intersection is energetically accessible directly from the bright state. Two active-space findings run through this paper. First, an explicit CONVERGENCE FAILURE drove the space size down: for the 7H-enol-amino tautomer the (16,12) used for the other two tautomers 'could not be properly converged due to the mixing of the orbitals', forcing a (12,10) and, beyond that, DIFFERENT ORBITAL SETS FOR DIFFERENT STRUCTURES of the same tautomer — the lowest pi orbital swapped for the N3 lone pair at one intersection and a further pi swapped for the N1 lone pair at another. So within a single tautomer the space composition varies from structure to structure, and its energies are correspondingly not all on one footing. Second, the conical intersections located at CASSCF are not intersections at CASPT2: 'the CASPT2 energy gaps of about 0.5 eV at the CASSCF geometries were reduced to less than 0.3 eV by the correction', so even after geometry correction a 0.3 eV gap remains where the CASSCF surfaces touch. The paper also notes its CASSCF state ordering differs from previous studies and attributes the discrepancy to 'difference of computational levels (basis set, active space, and ...)'.
reference_short: Yamazaki & Domcke, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 7090
notes: One of three guanine tautomers studied. Structures optimized at MP2 for the ground state are almost identical for the keto-amino and enol-amino tautomers. Atom labelling is given in Figure 1 and the corrected CI geometries in Figure 2.

compound_name: Acrolein (2-propenal), s-trans and s-cis conformers — excited-state surface crossings
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G* geometry optimizations with analytical frequency computations to confirm the nature of equilibrium geometries and transition states. Surface crossing points obtained by full optimization of the lowest energy points of crossing between the four relevant states (S0, S1, T1, T2); further well-defined points on the crossing seams obtained by constrained optimization at the CCCO torsion angle phi = 0 and phi = 90 degrees, plus grids in the R(C=O), R(C-C) and phi coordinates.
method: CASSCF, with state-averaged MC-SCF (orbitals optimized for an average of the two states involved) used for optimizations on the intersection space
software: Gaussian 92, plus a development version of the Gaussian package for the surface-crossing optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons distributed in five orbitals, originating from the pi and pi* orbitals of the C=C fragment and the pi, pi* and n orbitals of the C=O fragment.
active_space_protocol: A single fragment-additive space is used throughout: the pi system of the C=C fragment (pi, pi*) plus the pi system and oxygen lone pair of the C=O fragment (pi, pi*, n), giving (6,5). State-averaged MC-SCF, averaging the two states involved, is required for the geometry optimizations on the intersection space because ordinary state-specific orbitals cannot describe two degenerate states even-handedly. The paper states the accuracy limitation explicitly: 'CASSCF will give a balanced representation of the excited states computed in this work that would not be possible with SCF methods. Thus, the surface topology (minima, transition states, and crossings) should be quite reliable. However, the detailed energetics will be sensitive to the inclusion of dynamic correlation.'
nroots_per_mult: Four states followed (S0, S1, T1, T2); two-state averaging used for the intersection-space optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Three low-lying excited states are followed: 1(n-pi*), 3(n-pi*) and 3(pi-pi*). For s-trans-acrolein at the planar S0 minimum (R(C=O) 1.21, R(C-C) 1.48, R(C=C) 1.34 A) the vertical energies above S0 are T1 3(n-pi*) 3A'' 85.84, T2 3(pi-pi*) 3A' 89.73 and S1 1(n-pi*) 1A'' 90.80 kcal/mol. Key stationary points (relative energies in kcal/mol): twisted T1 3(pi-pi*) minimum at phi = 90 degrees 60.18; planar T1 3(n-pi*) minimum 69.34; planar T2 3(pi-pi*) transition state at phi = 0, 71.54; rotated 3(n-pi*) transition state at phi = 90, 84.15; planar S1 1(n-pi*) minimum 72.48. Crossings: T1/T2 conical intersection at phi = 0, 74.30; S0/T1 3(pi-pi*) intersection at 60.36/60.49; S0/S1 1(n-pi*) conical intersection minimum at phi = 90, 87.91/89.73, with an extreme bond-length reversal (R(C-O) 1.40 and R(C-C) 1.30 single-bond-like, R(C=C) 1.49 a fully formed double bond); the phi = 0 constrained S0/S1 intersection lies very high at 126-128 kcal/mol and is not accessible; the S1 1(n-pi*)/T2 3(pi-pi*) crossing minimum at phi = 0, 75.99/76.24. For s-cis-acrolein the S0 minimum lies 1.57 kcal/mol above the s-trans one, the S1 minimum at 71.72 and the S0/S1 conical intersection at phi = 90 at 81.64/82.39. Computed vertical excitation to 1(n-pi*) is 90.8 kcal/mol (about 315 nm, the middle of the experimental n-pi* absorption band); computed 0-0 energies of 72 and 69 kcal/mol for 1(n-pi*) and 3(n-pi*) compare with experimental 74 and 70 kcal/mol.
Other: The authors draw an explicit line between what this small (6,5) space can and cannot deliver: 'the surface topology (minima, transition states, and crossings) should be quite reliable. However, the detailed energetics will be sensitive to the inclusion of dynamic correlation.' That is a topology-converged-but-energetics-not verdict, and it matters here because the paper's central conclusion turns on a 2 kcal/mol margin — the phi = 90 S0/S1 conical intersection minimum J lies 'only 2 kcal mol-1 below the S1 1(n-pi*) vertical excitation energy', which the paper uses to argue that 300 nm irradiation cannot supply enough excess energy to reach it. A dynamic-correlation shift of a few kcal/mol would flip that argument, and no CASPT2 or comparably correlated check is reported. The space itself is built additively by fragment (C=C pi/pi* plus C=O pi/pi*/n) rather than by any occupation-number criterion, so it holds exactly the orbitals that the n-pi* and pi-pi* labels require and nothing more — it can name the states but carries no sigma correlation and no room for the extra orbitals that the extreme bond-length reversal at the conical intersection (a single C-O bond and a fully formed C=C bond) would arguably call for. The internal accuracy check offered is geometric and spectroscopic rather than variational: ground-state bond lengths agree with experiment to 0.01 A, excited-state ones to about 0.03 A, and the 0-0 energies are underestimated by only a few kcal/mol.

Model II: reactant optimized at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G*, transition state and intermediate located by single-point CASPT2/6-31G* scans in 0.025 A increments of the C(1)-C(6) (or C(1)-C(7)) distance with all other parameters CASSCF-optimized. X-ray structure of 9a available for comparison.
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 (CASPT2[0] and CASPT2[g1])
software: MOLCAS Version 3 and Version 4 (University of Lund); Gaussian 98 Revision A.5
basis_set: 6-31G*, with 6-31G** used as a check on selected energies
active_space_protocol: An (8,8) space is used throughout, but its ORBITAL CONTENT IS SWITCHED ALONG THE REACTION COORDINATE to follow the bonding change. For the closed-shell reactants 9a-c the space contains all of the in-plane and out-of-plane pi and pi* orbitals. For every other stationary point (transition states and biradical intermediates) 'the in-plane pi and pi* orbitals were replaced by the newly formed sigma and sigma* orbitals and the combinations of the nonbonding sigma orbitals belonging to the irreducible representations Ag and Au'. The size therefore stays at (8,8) while the composition tracks the in-plane pi -> sigma transformation. Two protocols are compared: Model I optimizes every structure at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G*; Model II optimizes only the reactants at CASSCF and locates the transition states and intermediates from single-point CASPT2/6-31G* scans along the C(1)-C(6) (or C(1)-C(7)) distance in 0.025 A increments with all other parameters CASSCF-optimized. Model IIa uses the CASPT2[0] and Model IIb the CASPT2[g1] zeroth-order Hamiltonian. All electrons except the heavy-atom 1s cores are correlated in the CASPT2.
electronic_structure_description: 1,6-ring closure 9a -> 10a -> 11a, energies relative to 9a in kcal/mol: CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* (model I) 43.0 and 40.9; CASPT2[0]/6-31G* (IIa) 21.1 and 14.1; CASPT2[g1]/6-31G* (IIb) 21.4 and 15.1; CASPT2[0]/6-31G** 21.0 and 13.8; CASPT2[g1]/6-31G** 21.3 and 14.8. Experimental gas-phase activation enthalpy 28.9 kcal/mol. 1,7-ring closure 9a -> 12a -> 13a: 49.2 and 48.1 (I), 27.6 and 23.2 (IIa), 28.0 and 24.0 (IIb) — the 1,7 transition state lies 7 kcal/mol above 10a and 13a is 9 kcal/mol above 11a. Along the reaction coordinate the in-plane pi combinations 17ag(pi+), 18au(pi-), 19ag(pi*+) and 20au(pi*-) transform into the C(1)-C(6) sigma (17ag) and sigma* (20au) plus two nonbonding orbitals 18au and 19ag. CASSCF(8,8) occupation numbers of the frontier pair 18au/19ag as a function of the C(1)-C(6) distance: 1.933/0.059 at 3.296 A (9a), 1.925/0.060 at 2.700, 1.905/0.093 at 2.300, 1.876/0.126 at 2.100, 1.796/0.208 at 1.925 (10a), 1.776/0.228 at 1.900, 1.554/0.450 at 1.700 and 1.394/0.610 at 1.525 A (11a). Transition state geometry at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* for 10a and CASPT2 model IIa: the C(1)-C(6) distance is 1.925 A (model I) and closer to 11a than to 9a in both models, a late transition state. 11a has C(1)-C(6) 1.564 A at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G*. Other: The occupation-number table is the paper's own biradical-character meter, and it shows the (8,8) space doing exactly the job it was designed for: 18au/19ag move from 1.933/0.059 in the closed-shell reactant to 1.394/0.610 in the biradical, never reaching the 1.0/1.0 of a perfect biradical. The residual imbalance (18au still above 19ag) is what the authors use to argue that through-bond coupling stabilizes the singlet, and it is confirmed independently by the 9.7 kcal/mol singlet-triplet gap. Note the diagnostic value of the 3.296 A entry: at the reactant geometry the second frontier orbital holds only 0.059 electrons, well inside the range that would normally justify leaving it out — so the space is sized for the PRODUCT end of the reaction coordinate, not the reactant end, which is the correct choice for a reaction path but means the reactant is described in a space larger than it needs and, as the geometry comparison shows, worse than Hartree-Fock describes it. Two distinct active-space effects are documented, and they point in opposite directions. First, an explicit admission that the space is too small for the reactant geometry: the RHF/3-21G bond lengths of 9a agree better with the X-ray structure than the CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* ones, and the authors write 'we ascribe this to our limitation of the active space (8/8). Second, and much larger, the space alone gets the energetics badly wrong: CASSCF(8,8) puts the 9a barrier at 43.0 kcal/mol against an experimental 28.9, and adding CASPT2 on the SAME space brings it to 21.1-21.4. Dynamic correlation is worth over 20 kcal/mol here, more than the residual error, so the biradical energetics are set by the correlation treatment rather than by the active space. The authors note CASPT2 'overestimates the dynamic correlation energy', which is consistent with every CASPT2 barrier in Table 6 falling BELOW experiment. The choice of zeroth-order Hamiltonian is by contrast almost irrelevant: CASPT2[0] and CASPT2[g1] differ by 0.3-1.0 kcal/mol, and switching 6-31G* to 6-31G** changes energies by only 0.1-0.3 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Haberhauer & Gleiter, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1999, 121, 4664
notes: 9a is the parent 10-membered cyclic diyne. point_group: None — all optimizations start near the S0 minimum releasing any symmetry constraints
geometry_source: ONIOM(CASSCF:UFF) minimum-energy conical intersection optimizations started near the S0 minimum with all symmetry constraints released; the chromophore is the high-level moiety and the substituents the low-level one, with microiterations relaxing the low-level region between high-level steps. The unsubstituted parent is optimized at the fully QM CASSCF level for comparison. Initial and optimized Cartesian coordinates are in the Supporting Information.
method: ONIOM(QM:MM) minimum-energy conical intersection optimization with state-averaged CASSCF as the high level and UFF as the low level, using projected-gradient algorithms (CG, CG-CS and DNR-CS) with microiterations
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: A (6,6) space on the fulvene chromophore; the substituents are outside the QM region entirely and are described by UFF.
active_space_protocol: The active space is fixed by CHROMOPHORE, not by molecule: (6,6) for the fulvene, benzene and ergosterol calculations, (4,4) for butadiene, and (12,12) for DPDBF. The substituents are never in the space — they are the ONIOM low-level (UFF) layer, so the same space is reused unchanged across all derivatives of a given parent chromophore. The high level is state-averaged CASSCF/6-31G**, the low level UFF without partial charges, and there are no QM:MM electrostatic cross terms (the MM atoms carry no partial charges and the interaction is treated purely sterically/mechanically). All CASSCF gradients include the coupled-perturbed multiconfiguration self-consistent field corrections EXCEPT for DPDBF.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, state-averaged)
electronic_structure_description: S0/S1 minimum-energy conical intersections located for the parent fulvene and five derivatives. Number of optimization cycles by algorithm (CG / CG-CS / DNR-CS): fulvene itself (fully QM CASSCF) 26 / 25 / 23; 3 x t-butyl (1a) 56 / 32 / 17; 6 x methyl (1b) 19 / 19 / 18; 6 x phenyl (1c) 19 / 14 / 25; 6 x ethyl (1d) 23 / 23 / 23; 2 x trimethylene (1e) 24 / 20 / 29. All optimizations complete within 60 steps, and in several cases the substituted systems converge in fewer steps than the unsubstituted parent at full QM.
Other: The most direct active-space message here is negative and useful: for the fulvene series the SAME (6,6) chromophore space describes six chemically distinct molecules, because the substituents are removed from the QM region by construction rather than being judged unimportant orbital by orbital. The validity condition is stated as a locality condition on the excitation, not an occupation-number one. Whether the (6,6) can be transferred like this is verified only indirectly, by the substituted MECIs converging in a similar number of steps to the fully QM parent — an efficiency check, not an accuracy check. Note also that the derivative with the largest algorithm-to-algorithm spread (1a, 56 versus 17 steps) is the bulkiest one, showing the convergence behaviour is governed by the MM sterics outside the space rather than by anything inside it. The design premise of the whole study is that a small active space on a chromophore fragment is sufficient provided the excitation stays localized there. The paper is explicit about when that holds: for the phenyl-substituted molecules 'the excitation is well localized on the fulvene, benzene or butadiene chromophore ... because the phenyl rings are rotated with respect to the chromophore, and the electronic coupling is weak', and for the DPDBF crystal because 'the excitonic coupling between the different molecules is weak, and the excitation is localized on a single molecule'. So the active space is not sized by any occupation-number or energy criterion but by a locality argument that has to be checked case by case — a rotated phenyl is outside the space, a conjugated one would not be. The correspondingly required approximation is that the QM:MM coupling be purely steric: the UFF layer has no partial charges and there is no electrostatic embedding, which the authors state limits the method to systems 'where the interaction between the chromophore and the rest of the system is dominated by steric effects, and charge interactions can be neglected'.
reference_short: Ruiz-Barragan, Morokuma & Blancafort, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2015, 11, 1585
notes: Part of a 14-molecule test set for three projected-gradient MECI algorithms. On average CG-CS is the most efficient (25.7 steps) against CG (28.4) and DNR-CS (28.0).
correlation_correction: None — state-averaged CASSCF only; no perturbative correction is applied

software: Gaussian 98 for the optimizations; MOLPRO for the MR-CI single-point energies
active_space_orbital_description: At the S0 and S1 equilibrium geometries: the three pi and three pi* orbitals of the aromatic ring, plus the nitrogen nonbonding orbital and the oxygen 2pz electrons. At the S1 transition states the O-H and N-H sigma and sigma* orbitals are included instead, with some pi electrons demoted to filled closed-shell orbitals to keep the space at (10,8).
active_space_protocol: The space is stated as a construction rather than a size: 'To describe the low-lying electronic states of 2HP, the three pi and three pi* orbitals on the aromatic ring should be used as the active orbitals for the CASSCF calculations. Meanwhile, the nitrogen nonbonding orbital and the oxygen 2pz electrons are also included in the active space. This leads to the active space with 10 electrons in 8 orbitals, referred to as CAS(10,8).' Crucially, the CONTENT CHANGES at the transition states without the size changing: 'The tautomerization processes involve the formation and breakage of the O-H and N-H bonds; the O-H and N-H sigma and sigma* orbitals are included in the active space for the CAS(10,8) optimizations of the S1 transition states. Some of the pi electrons were treated as filled closed-shell orbitals with no recovery of correlation energy.' The justification for the equilibrium-geometry space is orbital-energy based: 'The orbital energies of the sigma orbitals are much lower than those of the conjugation pi orbitals and oxygen and nitrogen n orbitals for the equilibrium geometries of 2HP and 2PY in the S0 and S1 states. The near-degenerate orbitals are included in the (10,8) active space for the S0 and S1 equilibrium geometries.' Relative energies are then refined by internally contracted MR-CI including all single and double excitations relative to the CAS(10,8) reference wave function.
electronic_structure_description: 2HP is the more stable tautomer in the ground state by 0.1, 2.4 and 0.1 kcal/mol at B3LYP, MP2 and CAS(10,8)/6-31G** respectively, against an experimental free-energy difference of about 0.02-0.04 eV. In the EXCITED state the ordering reverses: 2PY* lies 17.2 kcal/mol below 2HP* at MR-CI, against an experimental exothermicity of 6500 cm-1 (18.6 kcal/mol). Adiabatic 0-0 energies with ZPE correction: 2HP 109.3 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) and 111.1 at MR-CI, against the experimental S0-S1 band origin of 36118.7 cm-1 (103.3 kcal/mol); 2PY 86.9 at CAS(10,8) and 94.2 at MR-CI, against experimental pi-pi* origins at 29832 (85.3) and 29935 cm-1 (85.6 kcal/mol). Ground-state tautomerization barrier 34.4 kcal/mol at MP2/6-31G** (experimental estimate 45 kcal/mol, 16000 cm-1); in the 2HP-TS structure the H8-O7 distance is 1.382 A and N1-H8 1.273 A at MP2. Excited-state barrier 18.2 kcal/mol at MR-CI, with 2HP*-TS at 1.195 A (H8-O7) and 1.365 A (N1-H8) — a reactant-like transition state, consistent with an exothermic S1 reaction. Relative to the S0 minimum, 2HP*-TS lies at 129.3 kcal/mol, so S1 tautomerization is NOT accessible on photoexcitation at 277 nm (103 kcal/mol). CAS(10,8) optimized N1-C2, C2-O7 and O7-H8 bond lengths are 0.02-0.04 A shorter than the MP2 values while the remaining ring bonds are nearly unchanged. Scaled O-H stretching frequency 3703 cm-1 for 2HP and 3695 for 2HP*; for 2PY the N-H mode is 3453/3431 cm-1 (experimental 3448) and the C=O mode collapses from 1733 in S0 to 1215 cm-1 in S1 (experimental S0 value 1721).
Other: The single most transferable observation here is the collapse of the 2PY C=O stretch from 1733 to 1215 cm-1 on excitation, computed in a space that contains the oxygen 2pz and the ring pi system — a 500 cm-1 shift that only a space carrying both the carbonyl pi and its correlating pi* can produce, and a useful check that the (10,8) is adequate at the equilibrium geometries even though it is not at the transition states. This paper contains an unusually clean statement of a fixed-size, variable-content active space failing, together with the authors' own diagnosis of why. At the S0 and S1 EQUILIBRIUM geometries the (10,8) holds the three ring pi, three pi*, the nitrogen lone pair and the oxygen 2pz — the near-degenerate set, with the sigma orbitals lying much lower — and the resulting adiabatic excitation energies are good. At the S1 TRANSITION STATES the O-H and N-H sigma and sigma* orbitals must go in because bonds are breaking, and since the size is held at (10,8) some pi electrons are demoted to closed shells 'with no recovery of correlation energy'. The consequence is stated outright: 'Therefore, the CAS(10,8) calculations overestimate the barrier to the S1 tautomerization, which is significantly improved by the MR-CI calculations.' The trap for anyone reusing these numbers is that the same space is NOT uniformly better or worse: MR-CI fixes the barriers but makes the 2PY 0-0 energies worse, moving them from 86.9/86.1/87.8 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) — within about 1.5 kcal/mol of the experimental 85.3/87.1/87.9 — out to 94.2/96.0/94.0, an overestimate the authors themselves acknowledge. Barriers and excitation energies from this study therefore come from different levels and should never be combined into a single profile without saying so; the paper's own Figure 4 mixes MP2 ground-state energies with MR-CI excited-state energies for exactly this reason.

electronic_structure_description: One of three simple systems (1-3) investigated as possible new candidates for photoheterolysis. CASSCF-optimized ground-state minimum, first singlet excited-state minimum and the S0/S1 conical intersection were located; the results place it among the cations with high-energy, distant conical intersections relative to the excited-state minimum, i.e. NOT photochemically favored. It is also included in the TD-DFT survey (with cations 36-39) to show the vertical gap of 'normal' conjugated cations, indicating that such structures do not have a favorable conical intersection in the default case.
Other: The allyl cation is the paper's baseline for what a complete-pi active space gives for an ordinary, well-stabilized conjugated cation: a high-energy conical intersection far from the excited-state minimum. Its value in the set is as a null result — it shows that the complete-pi rule does not automatically manufacture a low-lying intersection, so the low intersections found for cations 9, 14, 16 and 20 are properties of those systems rather than artefacts of the space-selection rule. The active-space rule here is complete-pi, applied uniformly so that cations of very different stability can be compared on the same footing — the whole argument of the paper is a comparison of conical-intersection energies ACROSS cations, which only works if the space is defined by the same rule for each. First, the rule is not quite uniform: empty sigma orbitals had to be added for the dicoordinate p-aminophenyl cation, because a sigma-type empty orbital at the formally cationic carbon is not in the pi manifold at all — so the systems being compared do not all have spaces of the same character. geometry_source: Gradient CASSCF optimizations under Cs symmetry for the a1A' ground state and the low-lying b1A', c1A' and d1A' singlet excited states, starting from the gas-phase electron diffraction staggered geometry; also optimized at DFT (B3LYP). The ground-state CASSCF geometry obtained with the large 10e14a space was used for the Franck-Condon energies and transition dipole moments.

software: MOLCAS-4 for the multiconfigurational calculations; GAUSSIAN-98 for the TD-DFT

active_space_orbital_description: The 10e14a space: ten electrons in fourteen orbitals, comprising the highest occupied piCp orbitals, the occupied and vacant 3d(Mn) orbitals, the 3d orbitals of correlation (the double-shell set), and the low-lying pi*(CO) orbitals. The smaller 10e10a space is the same set WITHOUT the four low-lying pi*(CO) orbitals.
active_space_protocol: Two active spaces of the SAME electron count are compared directly. The 10e14a space (10 electrons, 14 orbitals) contains the high-lying piCp occupied orbitals, occupied and vacant 3d(Mn), a 3d correlating shell and the four low-lying pi*(CO) orbitals; it is described as 'a good starting point for the addition of dynamical correlation effects by CASPT2 treatment in the multistate approach (with a level shift correction of 0.5)'. The 10e10a space is exactly the 10e14a space with the four pi*(CO) orbitals removed, and was used for CASSCF geometry optimizations specifically 'in order to study the effect of the quality of the CASSCF wave function on the calculated bond lengths and angles'. CASSCF wave functions used in the subsequent MS-CASPT2 are averaged over several roots of a given spin and symmetry. Transition dipole moments were estimated at the CASSCF level.
