electronic_structure_description: The a1A' ground state has the closed-shell occupation (20a')2 (21a')2 (22a')2 (12a'')2 (13a'')2, i.e. (3dz2)2 (3dx2-y2)2 (2piCp)2 (3dxy)2 (1piCp)2, with the low-lying virtuals being 3dyz (23a'), 3dxz (14a'') and pi*CO (24a', 25a', 15a'' and 16a''). MS-CASPT2 vertical excitation energies (CASSCF value in parentheses, then CASSCF oscillator strength): a1A'' 24972 cm-1, 3.10 eV (32021, 3.97 eV) f = 0.0110; b1A' 25733 cm-1, 3.22 eV (34678, 4.33 eV) f = 0.0069; b1A'' 26024 cm-1, 3.23 eV (30779, 3.82 eV) f = 0.0085; c1A' 26470 cm-1, 3.30 eV (32488, 4.06 eV) f = 0.0157; c1A'' 29949 cm-1, 3.71 eV (37882, 4.70 eV) f = 0.0002; d1A' 30366 cm-1, 3.80 eV (38396, 4.80 eV) f = 0.0015 — these are all 3d(Mn) -> 3d(Mn) metal-centred states. The MLCT band, 3d(Mn) -> pi*(CO): e1A' 36075 cm-1 (41149), d1A'' 37410 (40249), f1A' 40690 cm-1, 5.09 eV (47733) f = 0.0040, g1A' 41175 cm-1, 5.15 eV (46629) f = 0.0052, e1A'' 42346 (43278), f1A'' 45019 (47939). The reference CASSCF weight is 0.720-0.733 for every state. Experimentally the first band runs to about 375 nm with a maximum at 30769 cm-1 (325 nm) and the second peaks near 250 nm (40000 cm-1). Optimized geometries (10e10a values in parentheses): ground state Mn-Cip 1.810 (1.830), Mn-Cop 1.806 (1.831), Mn-Cring 2.231 (2.215), C-O 1.148 (1.146) A, against gas-phase 1.808, 1.808, 2.149, 1.148 A. In the dissociative c1A' state Mn-Cip stretches to 2.846 A (2.249 A with 10e10a) with the Cop-Mn-Cop angle opening to 106.5 degrees.
Other: This paper is a controlled experiment on ONE question: what do the four pi*(CO) orbitals do? The electron count is held at 10 and only the orbital count changes, 10 to 14, so the comparison is not confounded by a change in the reference. Two effects are documented. On GEOMETRY, adding the pi*(CO) orbitals lets the d(pi)-p(pi) Mn-CO back-donation be described, which brings the Mn-CO bond lengths into perfect agreement with the gas-phase values and, as a knock-on, lengthens Mn-Cring — the largest deviation anywhere, and the paper states that Mn-Cop and the average Mn-Cring 'are both very sensitive to the CASSCF active space'. Note the direction: the LARGER space makes Mn-Cring worse relative to experiment (2.231 versus 2.215 A against 2.149 experimental), because it improves the competing back-donation. Both spaces and DFT underestimate the Mn-Cp interaction. On the DISSOCIATIVE c1A' state the space difference is enormous — Mn-Cip comes out at 2.846 A with 10e14a but only 2.249 A with 10e10a, a 0.6 A discrepancy in the very coordinate that defines the photochemistry, because carbonyl loss cannot be described without the pi*(CO) orbitals that accept the back-donation being broken. A trap for reuse: this optimization never converged (values are after 20 cycles), so neither number is a stationary point. Finally, CASSCF alone overestimates every excitation energy by 5000-9000 cm-1 (0.6-1.1 eV) and MS-CASPT2 also REORDERS the states — at CASSCF b1A'' lies lowest at 30779 cm-1 but at MS-CASPT2 a1A'' is lowest at 24972 — so the CASSCF ordering must not be used. The reference weight is a uniform 0.72-0.73 across all states, which is the paper's evidence that the perturbation is balanced despite its size.

TD-DFT agrees well with MS-CASPT2 for the low-lying metal-centred states but underestimates the MLCT band by more than 2000 cm-1, which the authors attribute to the functional handling delocalized charge-transfer situations poorly. The 3d(Mn) -> pi*(Cp) MLCT states are placed above 45000 cm-1 and do not contribute to the visible or UV spectrum.

active_space_orbital_description: Nine pi electrons in the nine pi orbitals — the full pi manifold. Three of these are the nonbonding MOs (NBMOs) that carry the unpaired electrons.
active_space_protocol: Full pi active spaces: (9,9)CASSCF for the neutral 1 and (10,9)CASSCF for the anion 1-, i.e. all nine pi orbitals with nine or ten electrons. Two separate correlation treatments are applied on top at the CASSCF/6-31G* geometries. CASPT2N supplies second-order perturbative sigma-pi correlation. MR-CI(pi-SD,sigma-S)+Q generates configurations 'by allowing simultaneous single excitations in both the sigma and pi spaces, as well as double excitations in the pi space, from several reference configurations', with a Davidson correction for neglected quadruples; canonical CASSCF MOs are imported from MOLCAS into MELDF-X. The MR-CI reference space for each state consists of the most important CASSCF configurations, and the paper reports the CUMULATIVE WEIGHT of that reference space explicitly — about 80% of the CASSCF wave function for most states. For D3h calculations MOLCAS v.3 uses only the C2v subgroup, so the SUPSYM option in RASSCF was used to keep the a2'' and ey'' MOs from mixing and to maintain true D3h symmetry of the pi MOs. Where the MR-CI configuration lists exceeded 2 GB, second-order perturbation theory eliminated configurations below a threshold of typically 1e-7 hartree, discarding only 0.20 +/- 0.05% of the perturbatively predicted correlation energy, with the energy corrected for the loss; test calculations showed this affects relative energies by less than 0.1 kcal/mol.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is the quartet 4A1'' at D3h. Relative energies in kcal/mol (CASSCF / CASPT2N / MR-CI+Q, 6-31G*): 4A1'' D3h 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0; 1(2)B1 C2v 15.9 / 13.7 / 16.5; 1(2)A2 C2v 15.7 / 13.8 / 14.7; 1(2)Ey''(B1) D3h 18.3 / 14.2 / 19.2; 1(2)Ex''(A2) D3h 18.3 / 14.2 / 17.2; 2(2)B1 C2v 36.0 / 29.2; 2(2)A2 C2v 35.0 / 31.5; 2(2)Ey''(B1) D3h 37.9 / 29.4; 2(2)Ex''(A2) D3h 37.9 / 29.5; 2A1''(A2) D3h 57.2 / 48.3; 2A2''(B1) D3h 111.6 / 62.8. The doublet-quartet gap is quoted as 14 +/- 1 kcal/mol. Jahn-Teller distortion of the 2E'' state stabilizes it by about 2.5 kcal/mol, with both the 2Ex''(2A2) and 2Ey''(2B1) components stabilized; the C2v distorted doublets lie only 0.2 kcal/mol below the pure D3h 2E'' at the CASSCF level. Geometry optimization of 1(2)E'' within D3h gave an energy 0.3 kcal/mol lower than the value computed at the 4A1'' geometry. UB3LYP/6-31+G* unscaled frequencies for the e' modes of 4A1'' are 296, 509, 944, 1063, 1229, 1422, 1511 and 1528 cm-1. The 2A2'' state, in which two electrons occupy the same e'' NBMO, has a highly ionic pi wave function — reflected in the enormous 111.6 to 62.8 kcal/mol drop from CASSCF to CASPT2N.
Other: The single most striking number in Table 1 is the 2A2'' state falling from 111.6 kcal/mol at CASSCF to 62.8 at CASPT2N — a 49 kcal/mol correction, against 2-5 kcal/mol for every other state. The paper explains why: in 2A2'' two electrons occupy the same e'' nonbonding MO, giving 'a highly ionic pi wave function', and ionic states are exactly where a pi-only active space omits the sigma relaxation that screens the charge separation. This is a clean illustration that the adequacy of a full-pi space is state-dependent, not molecule-dependent: the same (9,9) that needs a few kcal/mol of correction for the covalent states needs fifty for the ionic one. Anyone using a full-valence-pi space for a non-Kekule system should treat doubly-occupied-NBMO states as outside its reach without a correlation treatment. The transferable lesson here is not about the size of the CASSCF space — that is fixed at the full pi manifold — but about the REFERENCE SPACE of the correlation treatment built on it, and it is one of the clearest worked examples in the literature. The 4A1'' quartet is well described by a single configuration constituting 80% of its CASSCF wave function, while each component of the doublet 1(2)E'' has only about 70% in its two-configuration reference. The authors state the consequence directly: 'Having ca. 10% less of the CASSCF wave function in the reference space for 1(2)E'' leads to its MR-CI(pi-SD,sigma-S)+Q energy being calculated too high, relative to that of 4A1''.' Enlarging the reference space to restore parity then broke the degeneracy it was meant to fix — adding configurations contaminated the 1(2)Ex'' reference with an A1''-symmetry configuration, so the two components of what must be an exactly degenerate E'' pair came out 2 kcal/mol apart. The resolution is a parity argument rather than a convergence argument: the extra reference configurations for 1(2)Ex'' are the SAME ones used for 4A1'', so 'since 1(2)Ex'' is treated in a manner which is equivalent to 4A1'' in the MR-CI calculations, the relative energies of these two states should be reliable'. This is why the paper's headline number carries an explicit uncertainty of 14 +/- 1 kcal/mol. Two further cautions come from the same analysis: the CASSCF ordering and the correlated ordering differ throughout (compare the CAS, CASPT2N and CI+Q columns of Tables 1 and 2), and UB3LYP disagrees with both CASSCF and MR-CI on which state is the anion ground state.
reference_short: Kemnitz, Squires & Borden, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1997, 119, 6564
notes: A high-spin non-Kekule hydrocarbon of interest for organic magnetic materials. The C2v doublet states arise from six possible e' distortions of the D3h 2E'' state, with pseudorotation interconverting them in a potential well around the D3h 2E'' maximum. Because MOLCAS v.3 works in the C2v subgroup, states should strictly be labelled by their C2v rather than D3h symmetry unless artifactual symmetry breaking is prevented.

point_group: D3h for the 3E' and 1A1' states; C2v for the Jahn-Teller distorted components
geometry_source: C2v geometries optimized at (9,9)CASSCF/6-31G* for the neutral and at (10,9)CASSCF/6-31G* and (10,9)CASSCF/6-31+G* for the anion. All D3h calculations on the neutral were performed at the optimized geometry of 4A1''; those on the anion at the optimized geometry of 1A1'. Full UB3LYP/6-31+G* optimizations were also carried out.

notes: The paper's purpose is to predict the negative-ion photoelectron spectrum of 1-. geometry_source: Geometry optimizations at UB3LYP and/or (6/6)CASSCF with the 6-31G(d) basis set; all stationary points and transition states located and confirmed by vibrational analysis. The multireference MP2 correction is a single point at the CASSCF geometry with no re-optimization.
method: (6/6)CASSCF with multireference MP2 single points; UB3LYP for comparison and for the systems not treated multiconfigurationally
basis_set: 6-31G(d); for Ge the footnote to Table 1 reads 'LANTZ2 basis set was used for Ge'
active_space_orbital_description: A (6/6) space — six electrons in six orbitals. The article does not state which orbitals were selected.
active_space_protocol: A single (6/6)CASSCF space with the 6-31G(d) basis is used for every diradical, alongside UB3LYP; the article does not state which six orbitals it contains. Dynamic correlation is added by a multireference MP2 algorithm implemented in Gaussian, applied to the CASSCF energetics WITHOUT re-optimizing the geometries. The paper's own discussion is conducted on the spin-corrected UDFT energies rather than the CASSCF ones, on the stated grounds that spin-corrected UDFT gaps 'are known to be close to the energy gaps computed at a multiconfiguration self-consistent field method such as CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations'. UDFT singlet-triplet gaps are corrected for spin contamination in the singlet using Yamaguchi and Houk's formula. Geometries are optimized at UB3LYP and/or (6/6)CASSCF, with vibrational analyses at all stationary points and transition states.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet-triplet energy gap dEST = E(singlet) - E(triplet) in kcal/mol: -5.2 at spin-corrected UB3LYP/6-31G(d), -3.8 at (6/6)CASSCF/6-31G(d), -1.0 at MP2/6-31G(d)//(6/6)CASSCF/6-31G(d). A negative value means the SINGLET is the ground state. The singlet lies below the triplet even with only hydrogen substituents at silicon, in contrast to the carbon analogue DR1 (M = C, X = H) which has dEST = +1.3 kcal/mol at UB3LYP, i.e. a triplet ground state. This reference value defines the substituent scale ddEST(Si,X) = -5.2 - dEST(Si,X).
Other: The parent silicon diyl is where the three methods disagree most in relative terms: -5.2 (UDFT), -3.8 (CASSCF), -1.0 (MP2//CASSCF). The MP2 correction moves the gap in the OPPOSITE direction to what the UDFT reference implies, reducing the singlet stabilization to a fifth of the UDFT value. Since the singlet stabilization mechanism is delocalization of the in-phase nonbonding MO into the low-lying Si-H sigma* orbitals, and this is the system with the fewest and simplest such acceptors, it is also the case where a six-orbital space is least likely to hold them. Treat the -1.0 value with particular caution.  The active-space finding here is a warning the authors put in a footnote and then act on: 'UDFT calculations are known to reproduce closely the results calculated by CASPT2 level of theory. However, CASSCF energies were reported to be largely deviated from CASPT2 calculations.' Having said that, they base the entire discussion on spin-corrected UDFT rather than on their own (6/6)CASSCF numbers, and use MP2//CASSCF only as a check. The Table 1 data bear the warning out: for the silicon series the CASSCF gaps are uniformly SMALLER in magnitude than the UDFT ones (-3.8 vs -5.2 for X = H, -3.1 vs -5.7 for Me, -7.5 vs -11.3 for F, -5.5 vs -8.1 for OH, -0.7 vs -1.6 for SiH3), i.e. a bare (6/6) systematically underestimates the singlet stabilization by roughly a third, and adding MP2 correlation does not simply close the gap — it overshoots for X = Me (-3.7 against -3.1 CASSCF and -5.7 UDFT) and for X = F (-10.8) while undershooting for X = H (-1.0 against -3.8 CASSCF). The physical reason the small space struggles is stated in the chemistry: the singlet is stabilized by HYPERCONJUGATION of the in-phase nonbonding MO into the low-lying Si-X sigma* orbitals, and those sigma* orbitals are exactly the ones a six-orbital diradical space is unlikely to contain. So the substituent effect being measured lives partly outside the active space, which is the most likely explanation for both the systematic underestimate and the erratic MP2 correction.
reference_short: Abe, Ishihara & Tagegami, J. Org. Chem. 2004, 69, 7250
notes: Reference compound for the silicon series. Its carbon analogue DR1 (M = C, X = H) has dEST = +1.3 kcal/mol at UB3LYP, a triplet ground state, taken from the authors' previous work.

method: CASSCF (FORS) with MRMP2 (multireference Moller-Plesset second-order perturbation theory) single points
basis_set: 6-311G(3df) on Be, O and N — the standard 6-311G basis supplemented with three d and one f polarization functions (alpha = 1.02, 0.255, 0.06375 and 0.260 on Be); a single polarization and a diffuse function on N and O, i.e. 6-311+G(d), to allow for electron transfer from the metal atom
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in the twelve orbitals [8a'-15a', 1a''-4a''] in Cs symmetry.
active_space_protocol: The active space is specified by ORBITAL LABEL rather than by a description of orbital character, in Cs symmetry: [8a'-15a', 1a''-4a''] for Be, [12a'-19a', 2a''-5a''] for Mg and [16a'-23a', 3a''-6a''] for Ca. Each is twelve orbitals holding twelve electrons, i.e. CASSCF(12/12), and each is the same COUNT of orbitals shifted up the manifold to follow the metal — a constant-composition space across the series, which is what makes the Be/Mg/Ca barriers comparable. The wave functions are described as CASSCF (FORS) type; state-averaged CASSCF natural orbitals are used for the key-MO occupation analysis. Dynamical electron correlation is added by MRMP2 with all electrons except 1s correlated. One exception is documented: the calcium singlet-triplet crossing structure V(Ca,S/T) was optimized at CASSCF(6/6), not (12/12).
electronic_structure_description: MRMP2 energies relative to the entrance complex I(Be,S), in kcal/mol, at CASSCF(12/12) geometries (bond lengths r1 = N-N, r2 = N-O, r3 = M...O in angstroms): I(Be,S) 0.0 with r3 = 4.602 A, a very weakly bound complex; TS(Be,S,cis) 9.5 (classical barrier quoted as 8.9 kcal/mol with zero-point correction) at r3 = 1.783 A; TS(Be,S,trans) 16.0 (15.5 kcal/mol above I with ZPE); exit-channel complex II(Be,S) -97.6. On the triplet surface: I(Be,T) 49.3 with a much shorter M...O distance of 1.818 A; TS(Be,T) 45.9; III(Be,T) -51.2; the ionic-region minimum IV(Be,T) -3.3 and TS(Be,a,T) 13.8, giving a 17.0 kcal/mol barrier from IV. The calculated singlet barriers decrease down the group in the same order as the metal ionization potentials fall: IP(Be) 9.32 > IP(Mg) 7.65 > IP(Ca) 6.11 eV.
Other: Beryllium is the extreme of the series and shows most clearly what the constant-orbital-count space is buying. The entrance complex sits at a Be...O distance of 4.602 A on the singlet surface but only 1.818 A on the triplet — a 2.8 A difference between two states described by the same twelve orbitals, which is only possible because the space is defined by orbital index rather than by a fixed chemical picture of the bonding. The triplet entrance complex lies 49.3 kcal/mol up, so the singlet channel dominates. No previous report of the Be + N2O reaction existed, so these numbers have no independent check — worth remembering given that the analogous Mg surface came out qualitatively different from the earlier single-reference treatment.  The paper contains a direct methodological claim about why the active space matters here: an earlier MP2/CCSD(T) study of Mg + N2O found a TWO-STEP mechanism through a stable cyclic NNOMg intermediate, whereas the CASSCF(12/12) surface is a SINGLE-STEP process. The authors' reasoning is that 'at least two electronic configurations are important in the intermediate regions ... single-configuration-based methods may result in highly distorted PESs', and they point at the natural-orbital occupation numbers of the key MOs as the evidence. The physical origin is a charge transfer: passing over the barrier, the ground adiabatic state changes from a neutral configuration to an ionic one in which an electron moves from the metal s or p orbital into the in-plane 2p-pi orbital of N2O, so the wave function in the barrier region is 'dominated by BOTH the neutral and the ionic configurations'. A space that cannot hold both descriptions at once will place the barrier and, as here, can invent or destroy an intermediate. Two cautions for reuse. First, the small CASSCF(12/12) barriers on the TRIPLET surface (I(T) -> TS(T)) disappear entirely once MRMP2 dynamic correlation is applied, so the triplet channel is barrierless and the CASSCF triplet barriers are artefacts. Second, the singlet-triplet crossing structures V(S/T) were located at CASSCF with MRMP2 energies evaluated afterwards, and the authors warn that 're-optimization of the corresponding structures at the correlated levels of theory might lower their energies with respect to the asymptotes' — so the crossing-point energies are upper bounds, and the calcium one was found with a smaller (6/6) space still.

active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in the twelve orbitals [16a'-23a', 3a''-6a''] in Cs symmetry.
active_space_protocol: The active space is specified by ORBITAL LABEL rather than by a description of orbital character, in Cs symmetry: [8a'-15a', 1a''-4a''] for Be, [12a'-19a', 2a''-5a''] for Mg and [16a'-23a', 3a''-6a''] for Ca. Each is twelve orbitals holding twelve electrons, i.e. CASSCF(12/12), and each is the same COUNT of orbitals shifted up the manifold to follow the metal — a constant-composition space across the series, which is what makes the Be/Mg/Ca barriers comparable. The wave functions are described as CASSCF (FORS) type; state-averaged CASSCF natural orbitals are used for the key-MO occupation analysis. Dynamical electron correlation is added by MRMP2 with all electrons except 1s correlated. One exception is documented: the calcium singlet-triplet crossing structure V(Ca,S/T) was optimized at CASSCF(6/6), not (12/12).
electronic_structure_description: MRMP2 energies relative to I(Ca,S) in kcal/mol at CASSCF(12/12) geometries: I(Ca,S) 0.0 at r3 = 5.157 A; TS(Ca,S,cis) 2.2 (classical barrier 1.2 kcal/mol with ZPE, against 1.6 kcal/mol derived from kinetic data) at r3 = 2.349 A; TS(Ca,S,trans) 5.0 (3.9 above I with ZPE). Triplet surface: I(Ca,T) 36.0 at r3 = 3.370 A; TS(Ca,T) 34.5; IV(Ca,T) -1.0 and TS(Ca,a,T) 3.9, a barrier of 4.8 kcal/mol from IV. The singlet-triplet crossing structure V(Ca,S/T), optimized at CASSCF(6/6), lies at r1 = 1.294, r2 = 1.268, r3 = 2.200 A and 6.8 kcal/mol above I(Ca,S), i.e. only 4.5 kcal/mol above the lowest saddle point TS(Ca,S,cis), so unlike the magnesium case it could form part of the reaction mechanism. The Ca reaction shows pronounced non-Arrhenius behaviour; a two-channel fit to the kinetic data gives barriers of 1.2 and 5.4 kcal/mol.
Other: Calcium is the one system where the paper reduces the space, and it does so exactly where the reduction matters most: the singlet-triplet crossing structure V(Ca,S/T) was optimized at CASSCF(6/6) rather than (12/12), and that structure is the one that decides whether the spin-forbidden channel participates — at 4.5 kcal/mol above the lowest saddle point it plausibly does, whereas the magnesium analogue at 24 kcal/mol clearly does not. So the qualitative conclusion that distinguishes calcium from magnesium rests on a structure located in a quarter of the orbital space used everywhere else, with only a subsequent MRMP2 energy on top and the authors' own warning that re-optimization at a correlated level might lower it. The agreement of the computed 1.2 kcal/mol barrier with the 1.6 kcal/mol from kinetics is excellent, and the two-channel fit value of 5.4 kcal/mol matches the higher trans channel at 3.9-5.0, so the singlet surface itself is well described.  The paper contains a direct methodological claim about why the active space matters here: an earlier MP2/CCSD(T) study of Mg + N2O found a TWO-STEP mechanism through a stable cyclic NNOMg intermediate, whereas the CASSCF(12/12) surface is a SINGLE-STEP process. The authors' reasoning is that 'at least two electronic configurations are important in the intermediate regions ... single-configuration-based methods may result in highly distorted PESs', and they point at the natural-orbital occupation numbers of the key MOs as the evidence. The physical origin is a charge transfer: passing over the barrier, the ground adiabatic state changes from a neutral configuration to an ionic one in which an electron moves from the metal s or p orbital into the in-plane 2p-pi orbital of N2O, so the wave function in the barrier region is 'dominated by BOTH the neutral and the ionic configurations'. A space that cannot hold both descriptions at once will place the barrier and, as here, can invent or destroy an intermediate. Two cautions for reuse. First, the small CASSCF(12/12) barriers on the TRIPLET surface (I(T) -> TS(T)) disappear entirely once MRMP2 dynamic correlation is applied, so the triplet channel is barrierless and the CASSCF triplet barriers are artefacts. Second, the singlet-triplet crossing structures V(S/T) were located at CASSCF with MRMP2 energies evaluated afterwards, and the authors warn that 're-optimization of the corresponding structures at the correlated levels of theory might lower their energies with respect to the asymptotes' — so the crossing-point energies are upper bounds, and the calcium one was found with a smaller (6/6) space still.
reference_short: Tishchenko, Vinckier, Ceulemans & Nguyen, J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 6099
notes: Absolute MRMP2 reference energy E(I(Ca,S)) with the ECP = -36.098282 au. Calcium is the only member of the series treated with an effective core potential. compound_name: P-Phenylphosphirane (1) — thermal fragmentation to phenylphosphinidene plus ethylene
point_group: The lowest-energy conformation of 1 has a plane of symmetry (Cs); the concerted transition structure 2TS has only C1 symmetry
geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G(d) geometry optimizations of all stationary points with vibrational frequencies to classify them and to supply zero-point and thermal corrections at 298 K; (U)B3LYP reoptimizations started from the CASSCF geometries; CCSD(T) single points at the CASSCF geometries.
method: (10/10)CASSCF with CASPT2 single points; (U)B3LYP and CCSD(T) as independent checks
software: Gaussian 98 Revision A.7 and MOLCAS version 5.4
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals: the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the two P-C bonds, plus the three bonding pi orbitals of the benzene ring and their three antibonding counterparts.
active_space_protocol: A (10/10)CASSCF space is used for P-phenylphosphirane and the ring-opened diradicals derived from it, and it is defined by ORBITAL CORRELATION between reactant and product rather than by any threshold. For the reactant 1 it consists of the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the two P-C bonds plus the three bonding pi orbitals of the benzene ring and their antibonding counterparts. In the products the same ten orbitals correlate with the pi and pi* of ethylene, three bonding, three antibonding and one nonbonding pi orbital of phenylphosphinidene, and a nonbonding sigma orbital on phosphorus. That correlation is what keeps reactant and product energies on a common footing across a bond-breaking reaction. CASSCF/6-31G(d) vibrational frequencies were computed at every stationary point to classify it and to supply zero-point and thermal corrections at 298 K, with internal rotations approximated by harmonic oscillator partition functions. CASPT2 single points were then performed at each CASSCF stationary point; (U)B3LYP reoptimizations from the CASSCF geometries and CCSD(T) single points at the CASSCF geometries were used as independent checks.
ground_state_mult: 1 for P-phenylphosphirane; the phosphinidene product has a triplet (3A2) ground state
electronic_structure_description: Enthalpies in kcal/mol relative to 1 (CASSCF / CASPT2 / (U)B3LYP): PhP(1A1) + C2H4 49.1 / 63.3; PhP(1A2) + C2H4 46.0 / 59.3; PhP(3A2) + C2H4 21.8 / 38.0 / 38.7; concerted transition structure 2TS(1A) 49.5 / 59.9; singlet diradical transition structures 3aTS(1A'') 37.2 / 42.6, 3bTS(1A) 37.6 / 43.1, 3cTS(1A') 37.1 / 42.8; the shallow singlet minimum 3d(1A) 37.6 / 43.7; triplet diradical intermediates 4a(3A'') 35.7 / 41.1 / 38.9 and 4b(3A) 37.1 / 42.4 / 39.7; triplet fragmentation transition structures 5aTS(3A) 43.7 / 49.2 / 47.3 and 5bTS(3A) 43.2 / 47.7 / 46.5; ring-closure transition structures 6aTS(3A') 36.5 / 42.2 / 40.1 and 6bTS(3A) 36.9 / 41.8 / 40.2. The concerted path is 59.9 kcal/mol, essentially equal to the 59.3 kcal/mol reaction enthalpy, so the reverse addition of 1A2 PhP to ethylene is almost barrierless (0.6 kcal/mol) and 2TS is a very late transition structure with P-C distances of 3.172 and 3.143 A. The stepwise triplet route is 21 kcal/mol less endothermic and has a 12 kcal/mol lower barrier. Because the ground state of 1 is A' in Cs and the lowest singlet of PhP is A'', the A' and A'' surfaces must cross along a Cs-constrained coordinate, giving a conical intersection — but the lowest-energy path avoids it by breaking symmetry to C1. The three singlet diradical transition structures 3aTS-3cTS lie within 0.5 kcal/mol of each other; (10/10)CASPT2 triplet single points at those geometries lie 2.1, 0.8 and 0.7 kcal/mol BELOW the corresponding singlets, so 42-43 kcal/mol is an upper limit and 41-42 kcal/mol a lower limit for the activation enthalpy of intersystem crossing.
Other: Beyond the CASSCF-versus-correlated calibration, the most reusable result here is that the (10/10) space supports a state-crossing analysis that a single-reference method could not perform at all: the closed-shell reactant is A' and the open-shell singlet product A'' in Cs, so a symmetry-conserving path must pass through a conical intersection, and the calculation shows the molecule avoids it by dropping to C1. The occupation-number evidence is the striking part — by the time the C1 transition structure 2TS is reached, the wave function has already lost the open-shell character it has in the PhP reactant, with the 3p(sigma)/3p(pi) occupancy ratio at 6 against 3 in the genuinely closed-shell 1A1 state. The paper explains this through orbital interactions: 3p(pi) mixes with the filled ethylene pi (destabilizing it) while 3p(sigma) mixes with the empty pi* (stabilizing it). Note also footnote 25: conrotatory C-C rather than C-P bond breaking gives a 1,3-dipolar intermediate 1.5 kcal/mol below 3cTS, whereas in unsubstituted phosphirane the analogous intermediate lies 17.5 kcal/mol below its transition structure — a large substituent effect on the surface topology that a reader comparing to the parent system must not overlook.  This paper opens with an explicit CALIBRATION of the active space against two independent methods, and the result is a 16 kcal/mol indictment of bare CASSCF. The enthalpy of triplet PhP plus ethylene relative to 1 is 21.8 kcal/mol at (10/10)CASSCF but 38.0 at CASPT2, 38.7 at (U)B3LYP and 40.3 at CCSD(T) — three unrelated correlated methods clustering within 2.3 kcal/mol of each other and 16-18 kcal/mol away from CASSCF. The authors accordingly base every subsequent discussion on the CASPT2 energies. The lesson generalizes: a (10/10) space chosen by reactant-product orbital correlation gives the right STRUCTURES and the right topology but not the right reaction enthalpy, because the dominant error is differential dynamic correlation between a strained ring and two separated fragments. A second, subtler effect is that dynamic correlation reshapes the surface, not just its energies. At CASSCF the intermediate 3d lies 0.3 kcal/mol below the transition structure 3cTS, but at CASPT2 their energies are essentially equal, and the paper concludes that 'the CASPT2 energies suggest that there are no singlet diradical intermediates, but only transition structures' — in direct analogy with cyclopropane ring opening, where dynamic correlation is known to flatten the surface. A trap for anyone using Table 1: because 3d has one more real vibrational mode than 3cTS, its zero-point energy and heat capacity are larger, so within the harmonic approximation its ENTHALPY is computed to be higher than that of the transition structure at both levels. The active space also supports a direct wave function diagnostic — the natural orbital occupation numbers of the two phosphorus 3p orbitals — which shows that at the concerted transition structure 2TS the 3p(sigma)/3p(pi) occupancy ratio is 6, against only 3 in the closed-shell 1A1 state of PhP itself, so 2TS 'has more closed-shell character than the closed-shell singlet state of the reactant'.
reference_short: Lam, Gaspar, Hrovat, Trieber, Davidson & Borden, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 9886
notes: Written to answer whether arylphosphinidenes have actually been generated by thermal fragmentation of P-arylphosphiranes. Passage over 3aTS involves rotation about the P-C bond and preserves C-C stereochemistry; 3bTS involves rotation about the C-C bond. 3cTS was found by optimizing a Cs geometry and has one imaginary frequency that both pyramidalizes and rotates the C(1) methylene, connecting two mirror-image diradicals. In 3d the singly occupied orbital on C(1) hyperconjugates with a C-H bond at C(2).

Relative to P-phenylphosphirane the products lie at (CASSCF / CASPT2): PhP(3A2) + C2H4 21.8 / 38.0 (with (U)B3LYP 38.7 and CCSD(T) 40.3); PhP(1A2) + C2H4 46.0 / 59.3; PhP(1A1) + C2H4 49.1 / 63.3. geometry_source: CASSCF/6-31G* geometry optimizations; for systems V1, V2, V3, W1, W2 and W3 the geometries were optimized at STO-3G with single points at 4-31G. No zero-point corrections were applied because frequency calculations were too expensive for the large bicyclic and tricyclic systems. Activation energies are transition structure minus reactant; reaction energies are products minus reactants.
method: CASSCF, with UHF and UB3LYP comparisons for the bicyclic and tricyclic systems
basis_set: 6-31G*; STO-3G geometries with 4-31G single points for systems V1-V3 and W1-W3
active_space_orbital_description: Three electrons in three orbitals: the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-C bond that is cleaved, plus the singly occupied nonbonding orbital (SOMO) on oxygen. These evolve into the C=O pi and pi* orbitals and the SOMO of the departing alkyl fragment.
active_space_protocol: The active space is sized by HOW MANY BONDS CAN BREAK, and grown only when the chemistry requires it. For the acyclic systems A-O and the monocyclic systems P-S the space contains the sigma orbitals of the single bond that is cleaved plus the singly occupied nonbonding orbital (SOMO) on oxygen — three electrons in three orbitals, CAS(3,3). For the bicyclic and tricyclic systems T-W, where TWO bonds (a and b in Scheme 1) can be cleaved, the space is CAS(5,5): the sigma orbitals of both candidate bonds plus the oxygen SOMO. The paper states what those orbitals become: 'These orbitals eventually evolve into the C=O pi and pi* orbitals and the SOMO on the alkyl fragment in the products.' For the alkene-containing systems U, W, W1, W2 and W3 the pi and pi* of the C=C bond are added as well, giving CAS(7,7). In every case the lowest energy doublet state was studied. Energies are NOT zero-point corrected, because frequency calculations proved too expensive for the large T-W systems.
nroots_per_mult: 1 (the lowest energy doublet state in each case)
electronic_structure_description: Loss of hydrogen, methyl, ethyl, isopropyl and tert-butyl radicals was examined for each of the five primary alkoxy radicals. The plot of activation energy against reaction energy is linear with r-squared greater than 0.98, and the slope — the fraction of product stabilization that appears in the transition state — is 0.79, the largest of the three substitution classes. For a primary alkoxy radical the activation energy for cleavage is LOWER than for a secondary or tertiary cleavage of the same endothermicity. Drawing lines instead through systems sharing the same leaving alkyl radical gives slopes between 0.16 and 0.21 for all leaving groups except hydrogen, where the slope is 0.38. Loss of radicals with a low ionization potential occurs with a lower activation energy than formation of radicals with higher IP at the same heat of reaction, consistent with a polarized transition state. Computed reaction energies are 4-5 kcal/mol more exothermic and activation energies 4-8 kcal/mol higher than Benson's estimates from experimental data.
Other: The primary series has the largest transition-state/product coupling of the three (slope 0.79 versus 0.65 and 0.56), which is the paper's central structure-reactivity result and is exactly the kind of quantity that survives a systematically-shifted absolute barrier. Worth noting that the three-orbital space contains no oxygen lone pair other than the SOMO, yet the transition state is described as polarized with charge separation toward the leaving alkyl group — that polarization is carried by the orbital relaxation of the closed-shell part of the wave function rather than by the active space, so the IP-dependence result is a CASSCF orbital effect, not a configurational one.  The active space here is defined by the reaction coordinate rather than by the molecule, and the paper is unusually explicit about scaling it: (3,3) when one bond can break, (5,5) when two can, (7,7) when a C=C must also be described. That keeps the orbital content constant per breaking bond across thirty-odd systems, which is what makes the linear free-energy correlations meaningful — the slopes of 0.79, 0.65 and 0.56 for primary, secondary and tertiary radicals are differences measured against a fixed methodological background. The cost is stated plainly: 'CASSCF energies are known to lack some dynamic correlation, and therefore activation energies tend to be overestimated. However, these errors are expected to be consistent such that the trends are not expected to be affected by this error.' The size of that systematic error is quantified against experiment — reaction energies come out 4-5 kcal/mol too exothermic and activation energies 4-8 kcal/mol too high relative to Benson's estimates — so absolute barriers from this work should be shifted, while relative barriers and correlations can be used as given. The most valuable methodological result is the comparison in Table 1, where CASSCF, UHF and UB3LYP are applied to the same bond-selectivity question: UB3LYP/6-31G* optimizes the bicyclic reactants with an exceptionally long bond b (1.71 A) and gives bond-b barriers of only 0.1-0.2 kcal/mol, a 'strong predisposition' that is absent from both the UHF and the CASSCF reactants (barriers of about 8 and 5 kcal/mol respectively). For a homolysis where two nearly degenerate sigma bonds compete, that is a case of a single-reference functional pre-committing the geometry — and the (5,5) space, which holds both sigma bonds explicitly, is what avoids it.
reference_short: Wilsey, Dowd & Houk, J. Org. Chem. 1999, 64, 8801
notes: Systems 15-19 in Figure 1. The IP dependence at fixed heat of reaction reproduces an earlier result of Benson.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF only; the paper notes that the missing dynamic correlation makes activation energies too high by 4-8 kcal/mol but expects the error to be systematic

electronic_structure_description: Loss of hydrogen, methyl, ethyl, isopropyl and tert-butyl radicals examined. The activation energy versus reaction energy plot is linear with r-squared above 0.98 and a slope of 0.65, intermediate between the primary (0.79) and tertiary (0.56) series. As the leaving group becomes more substituted, both the transition state and the products are stabilized.
Other: The monotonic fall of the slope from 0.79 (primary) to 0.65 (secondary) to 0.56 (tertiary) means that as the alkoxy carbon becomes more substituted, less of the product stabilization is felt at the transition state — the transition state becomes earlier. That trend is computed on an identical (3,3) space for all fifteen acyclic radicals, so it cannot be an artefact of differing active spaces, which is the strongest argument the paper can make for it given that every absolute barrier is 4-8 kcal/mol too high.  The active space here is defined by the reaction coordinate rather than by the molecule, and the paper is unusually explicit about scaling it: (3,3) when one bond can break, (5,5) when two can, (7,7) when a C=C must also be described. That keeps the orbital content constant per breaking bond across thirty-odd systems, which is what makes the linear free-energy correlations meaningful — the slopes of 0.79, 0.65 and 0.56 for primary, secondary and tertiary radicals are differences measured against a fixed methodological background. The cost is stated plainly: 'CASSCF energies are known to lack some dynamic correlation, and therefore activation energies tend to be overestimated. However, these errors are expected to be consistent such that the trends are not expected to be affected by this error.' The size of that systematic error is quantified against experiment — reaction energies come out 4-5 kcal/mol too exothermic and activation energies 4-8 kcal/mol too high relative to Benson's estimates — so absolute barriers from this work should be shifted, while relative barriers and correlations can be used as given. The most valuable methodological result is the comparison in Table 1, where CASSCF, UHF and UB3LYP are applied to the same bond-selectivity question: UB3LYP/6-31G* optimizes the bicyclic reactants with an exceptionally long bond b (1.71 A) and gives bond-b barriers of only 0.1-0.2 kcal/mol, a 'strong predisposition' that is absent from both the UHF and the CASSCF reactants (barriers of about 8 and 5 kcal/mol respectively). For a homolysis where two nearly degenerate sigma bonds compete, that is a case of a single-reference functional pre-committing the geometry — and the (5,5) space, which holds both sigma bonds explicitly, is what avoids it.

electronic_structure_description: Ring cleavage of 36 to 38 through transition structure 37 is exothermic by only 4.3 kcal/mol because of the small ring strain in the reactant, and the activation barrier is 15.4 kcal/mol — much higher than for either cyclopropoxy or cyclobutoxy. compound_name: 2-Hydroxy allyl vinyl ether — Claisen rearrangement transition structure
geometry_source: Geometry optimization and vibrational frequency calculation at CASSCF/6-31G*; all stationary points characterized by frequency calculations. Force constants were fed to the program Quiver to obtain theoretical isotope effects. software: GAMESS and GAUSSIAN 94 for the CASSCF; GAUSSIAN 92/DFT for the RHF and Becke3LYP; MacroModel 4.5 for the conformational search; Quiver for the isotope effects

Activation energies are taken from RHF and DFT; CASSCF is used for geometry and KIEs.
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF/6-31G* activation energy 32.6 kcal/mol, against 39.8 at RHF/6-31G* and 20.1 at Becke3LYP/6-31G*; the experimental value for the 2-(trimethylsiloxy) analogue is a free energy of activation of about 23.8 kcal/mol. RHF gives 1.156/0.860 and Becke3LYP 1.120/0.898 at 25 degrees C. The CASSCF/6-31G* transition structure has O3-C4 = 2.023 A and C1-C6 = 2.605 A; for the parent allyl vinyl ether the corresponding CASSCF distances are 2.100 and 2.564 A, so hydroxyl substitution at C2 gives slightly more bond-breaking at C4 and more bond-making at C6. Relative activation energies of parent versus 2-OH are 9.1 (RHF), 6.7 (Becke3LYP) and 9.9 (CASSCF) kcal/mol, against an experimental 8 kcal/mol. At RHF the transition state has enolate/allyl cation character with a charge separation of 0.31 electron in the parent; the 2-hydroxy system shows only a 0.03 electron increase in charge separation, a value CASSCF/6-31G* reproduces exactly.
Other: This paper draws an unusually sharp line between what the (6,6) space is needed for and what it is not. It is needed for GEOMETRY-DERIVED observables: only CASSCF reproduces the secondary deuterium kinetic isotope effects, giving 1.413 at 25 degrees C against an experimental 1.48, where RHF (1.156) and Becke3LYP (1.120) both fall well short. software: MOLCAS-3 for the CASSCF(7,7) energies; GAUSSIAN-94 for the B3LYP calculations and the CASSCF(5,6) optimizations
basis_set: 6-31G* (additional diffuse functions led to convergence problems)
active_space_orbital_description: Seven electrons in seven orbitals for the energy calculations, obtained by selecting the SDCI natural orbitals with occupation numbers between 0.02 and 1.98 at each point separately. The reduced space used for geometry optimization is five electrons in six orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The active space is chosen by an OCCUPATION-NUMBER WINDOW applied point by point: 'the active space in each point was chosen by selecting those SDCI (singles and doubles configuration interaction) natural orbitals with occupation numbers between 0.02 and 1.98. The resulting active space includes seven electrons in seven orbitals for all the cases.' So the (7,7) is an OUTCOME of the 0.02-1.98 criterion rather than an imposed size, and the criterion happened to return the same count at every stationary point. electronic_structure_description: Energies relative to propene + NO3 in kcal/mol, B3LYP/6-31G* with CASSCF(7,7)/6-31G* in parentheses. The Markownikoff adduct MO is at -15.90 (-35.07) and the contra-Markownikoff adduct MOp at -14.20 (-27.67); MO is more stable by 1.70 kcal/mol at B3LYP because of hyperconjugative stabilization by the methyl donor group. A separate transition state TScM at -2.53 (+5.33) with a 152i cm-1 imaginary frequency leads from reactants to MOp; in it the NO3 radical sits with two oxygen atoms in a bridged conformation over the double bond, in a plane perpendicular to it, with the propene double bond eclipsed. An estimate of the Markownikoff transition state TSM was obtained by fixing the O'-C distance, giving -2.38 (-2.15) kcal/mol relative to reactants; a true TSM search gave two imaginary frequencies, the second only 28i cm-1 and corresponding to relative fragment orientation, so it can be neglected. In MO the largest negative charge is on C'' because of the methyl donor character, while the spin density is mainly on C' — confirming the experimental suggestion of electrophilic addition to the double bond. In MOp the spin density is mainly on C and is not stabilized by donor groups. In TScM the spin density is on O' and C, so radical character is delocalized over both the NO3 fragment and the pi system. In the atmosphere both adducts would be oxidized on the carbon carrying the largest spin density (C' for MO, C for MOp) to give peroxides, as found experimentally.
Other: The entrance channel is the one place where the two methods agree, and the reason is instructive: reactants and the entrance transition state are electronically similar, so whatever seven orbitals the 0.02-1.98 window selects at one geometry are essentially the same seven it selects at the other, and the shifting-space problem cancels in the difference. Both give about -2.2 to -2.4 kcal/mol against an experimental 2.32. Once the adduct forms, agreement collapses: MO is at -15.90 (B3LYP) but -35.07 (CASSCF(7,7)), a 19 kcal/mol discrepancy, and MOp likewise -14.20 versus -27.67. That the CASSCF is far MORE exothermic tells you the space describes the adduct's localized radical better than it describes the delocalized reactant pair — exactly the imbalance an occupation-number criterion applied independently at each point will produce.  This paper is one of the clearest published statements that an occupation-number-selected active space can fail as a REACTION-PATH method even when it succeeds at every individual point. The 0.02-1.98 SDCI natural-orbital window returned exactly seven electrons in seven orbitals at every stationary point — apparently a consistent space — yet the authors' final verdict is that 'B3LYP/6-31G* calculations seem to be more reliable than CASSCF(7,7)/6-31G* ones, since in the latter case it is very difficult to define an active space coherent all along the potential energy hypersurface.' A constant SIZE is not the same as a constant space: the seven orbitals that pass the occupation test at an adduct are not the same seven that pass at a ring closure, so relative energies along the path are computed in shifting orbital sets. The damage is visible and large. B3LYP reproduces the experimental reaction enthalpies within 5 kcal/mol for every product except propenol, whereas CASSCF(7,7) does not, and individual barriers differ by tens of kcal/mol between the two methods with the sign of the disagreement varying from step to step. The authors diagnose one case explicitly — the CASSCF(7,7) energy of the five-membered ring M2 is 'too high' because of a poor description of that ring structure — and the M2 barriers even come out NEGATIVE at CASSCF(7,7) (-18.23 and -29.67 kcal/mol), which is physically impossible for a barrier and marks the space as inconsistent between M2 and its transition states. The one number both methods agree on is the entrance barrier, -2.38 (B3LYP) versus -2.15 kcal/mol (CASSCF(7,7)) against an experimental activation energy of about 2.32 kcal/mol — the step where reactants and transition state are electronically most alike, and therefore where the shifting-space problem is smallest. Note separately that the CASSCF(5,6) geometries validate B3LYP well (mean absolute differences of 0.8 degrees and 0.011 A), so the geometric side of the small space is sound; it is the ENERGIES from the larger occupation-selected space that are not transferable.

notes: Both adducts are experimentally relevant intermediates in the tropospheric oxidation of propene by the nitrate radical. Only the entrance-channel barriers control the measured rate of reactant disappearance.
correlation_correction: None on the CASSCF; SDCI was used only to generate the natural orbitals from which the active space was selected

electronic_structure_description: The linear SiCO 3Sigma- state is the global ground state of the [Si,C,O] system. The 3Sigma- / 1Delta separation is 17.26 kcal/mol at CASSCF-MP2, against 18.2-20.8 kcal/mol from three DFT methods and 19.8 from MP2; MP4 and CCSD(T) estimates are very close to the CASSCF-MP2 value, so about 17 kcal/mol is judged reliable. A (4,6) space containing the C-O pi and pi* is structurally right — the bond length is excellent — but a harmonic frequency is a second derivative and is far more sensitive to the missing dynamic correlation than the minimum position is. The (4,6) is built from a state-counting argument — all the states of interest come from redistributing two pi electrons over two degenerate pi orbitals — and it delivers geometries that match much more expensive methods: the ground-state Si-C bond length of 1.835 A is identical to CISD/DZ+P and within 0.010 A of CCSD(T)/cc-pVQZ. The authors attribute this to a specific and avoidable cause — 'this discrepancy should be attributed to the use of the CASSCF geometries instead of the CASSCF-MP2 geometries. Although the former method can produce the correct electronic configurations and yield accurate geometric parameters ... it may yield larger deviation for the relevant energy quantities perhaps because it does not include the electron correlation correction' — and predict that direct optimization at CASSCF-MP2 would fix it. So the transferable warning is about the //CASSCF part of a CASSCF-MP2//CASSCF protocol, not about the space: a bond length can be right to 0.01 A while the energy at that geometry is wrong by 16 kcal/mol, because the dissociation energy samples the flat part of the curve where the missing correlation accumulates. One quantity escapes this: the vertical ionization potential, where 'the CASSCF-MP2 value is almost equal to the CCSD(T) one' and all methods agree to within 7%, because ionization is a vertical process at a single geometry and the geometry error cancels.

notes: The large singlet-triplet gap of about 20 kcal/mol is attributed to the absence of the C-O bond. The singlet state of this isomer had not been studied before this work.
correlation_correction: CASSCF(4,6)-MP2(full) single-point correction with all electrons correlated

compound_name: Thymine-acrylamide radical anion complex — proton-coupled electron transfer
point_group: Cs (imposed during the geometry optimization to maintain planarity and hence maximize the electronic coupling between thymine and acrylamide)
geometry_source: Geometry of the NEUTRAL thymine-acrylamide complex optimized with B3LYP/6-31G* under Cs symmetry, giving an N-O proton donor-acceptor distance of 2.85 A; using the neutral geometry is consistent with the assumption that electron transfer is faster than geometry relaxation. The negatively charged complex was also optimized, increasing N-O to 3.0 A without altering the qualitative conclusions. For the CASSCF energy profiles all solute nuclei except the transferring proton were held at the neutral optimized geometry, and the adiabatic energies were computed on a one-dimensional grid in the proton coordinate.
method: State-averaged CASSCF for the adiabatic energies and electronic coupling, with the generalized Mulliken-Hush approach for the diabatic couplings; B3LYP/6-31G* for the geometry; CHELPG for atomic charges; FRCM for solvent reorganization energies
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF energies and couplings; Gaussian 98 for the B3LYP geometry optimization and the CHELPG charges
active_space_orbital_description: Nine electrons in eight molecular orbitals, FOUR of them localized on thymine and four localized on acrylamide — a deliberately fragment-balanced space. A much smaller CASSCF with one electron in two molecular orbitals (one localized on thymine, one on acrylamide) was used separately to generate the valence-bond state wave functions for the CHELPG atomic charges.
active_space_protocol: The space is constructed to be SYMMETRIC BETWEEN THE TWO FRAGMENTS: four orbitals localized on thymine and four on acrylamide, holding nine electrons, so neither the donor nor the acceptor is better described than the other. The lowest two electronic states are equally weighted in the state averaging. A second, minimal (1,2) space with one orbital on each fragment is used for the valence-bond charge distributions. The choice of basis set was driven by the active space rather than the reverse: diffuse functions 'resulted in difficulties choosing the physically relevant active space for the CASSCF calculations when the transferring proton is bonded to acrylamide', while CASSCF excitation energies were similar for 6-31G* and 6-31+G* when the proton is bonded to thymine, so 6-31G* was adopted. Further reasons given against diffuse functions: the negative vertical electron affinity of neutral thymine at B3LYP/6-31+G* suggests diffuse functions may be unreliable, and they may be inappropriate for solvation properties because the solvent restricts electronic density for open-shell systems.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (the lowest two electronic states, equally weighted in the state average)
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic energies were computed along a one-dimensional proton coordinate connecting the two proton-transfer states. The singly occupied molecular orbital is LOCALIZED ON THYMINE when the proton is bonded to thymine, and localized on acrylamide when the proton is bonded to acrylamide. Electronic couplings from the generalized Mulliken-Hush approach, using the adiabatic energy splitting, the transition dipole moment and the adiabatic dipole moment difference, are 0.7 kcal/mol with the proton bonded to thymine and 0.8 kcal/mol with the proton midway between donor and acceptor; the electron transfer coupling is therefore taken as V(ET) = 0.8 kcal/mol. That is comparable to the thermal energy at room temperature, placing this electron transfer in the intermediate regime between the electronically adiabatic and nonadiabatic limits. CHELPG partial charges for the five-site empirical valence bond model, for VB states 1a / 1b / 2a / 2b: donor -0.8/-0.9/0.2/0.1; N -0.6/-0.9/-0.7/-1.0; H 0.4/0.4/0.4/0.4; O -0.7/-0.6/-0.6/-0.5; acceptor 0.7/1.0/-0.3/0.0. Morse parameters D(NH) = 93 and D(OH) = 102 kcal/mol with beta(NH) = beta(OH) = 2.35 A-1. Solvent reorganization is smaller for pure proton transfer than for PCET and larger for pure electron transfer than for PCET. In the gas phase the 2b VB state lies below 2a, but on solvation the ordering reverses, so the dominant charge transfer would be concerted electron-proton transfer in the gas phase but pure electron transfer in solution.
Other: This paper resolves a published disagreement by attributing it to the METHOD rather than to the basis set, and the active space is the instrument. Earlier DFT work at B3LYP/6-31+G* found the unpaired spin delocalized over both thymine and acrylamide when the proton sits on thymine; the CASSCF(9,8) here finds it cleanly localized on thymine. The authors ruled out the basis set by reproducing the DFT delocalization at B3LYP/6-31G* and the CASSCF localization at CASSCF/6-31+G*, and further reproduced the localized result at MP2/6-31G* — so two wave-function methods agree with each other and disagree with DFT, the classic signature of self-interaction-driven over-delocalization in a charge-localized open-shell system. The fragment-balanced construction of the space (four orbitals on each molecule) is what makes that conclusion credible: an asymmetric space would itself bias where the SOMO sits, so the localization could have been an artefact. A second, less common lesson: the ACTIVE SPACE dictated the basis set here, not the other way round — diffuse functions made it impossible to identify a physically relevant space when the proton was on acrylamide, and that practical obstacle, together with two physical arguments, is why 6-31G* was used throughout. Finally, note that the 0.7-0.8 kcal/mol coupling is at the scale of kT, so the qualitative regime assignment (intermediate between adiabatic and nonadiabatic) is robust while the number itself is not something to quote to two significant figures from an (9,8) space with no dynamic correlation.
reference_short: Carra, Iordanova & Hammes-Schiffer, J. Phys. Chem. B 2002, 106, 8415
notes: Model for proton-coupled electron transfer in DNA-acrylamide complexes, analyzed with multistate continuum theory and a four-state valence bond model. The FRCM solvent reorganization energy matrix elements were insensitive to whether the VB-state atomic charges came from CASSCF(1,2) or from B3LYP/6-31G* CHELPG calculations on the separate fragments, indicating the results do not depend on the details of the charge distribution. Sevilla and co-workers had separately investigated basis set effects for DNA bases.
correlation_correction: None on the CASSCF; MP2/6-31G* was used separately only to check the SOMO localization

compound_name: Pyrazine — vibrational structure of the singlet and triplet excited states
point_group: D2h at the symmetric geometry; C2v wave functions examined for symmetry-breaking instabilities
geometry_source: Analytical second-derivative frequency calculations at the CASSCF level, plus numerical and diagonal-anharmonic frequencies obtained by analysing the potential surfaces along the CASSCF analytical normal modes. Geometry optimizations in C2v symmetry were performed both with and without state averaging: with state averaging the geometry relaxed to a fully symmetric D2h structure, without it did not. Ground-state vibrational analyses at SCF, SVWN, B3LYP, MP2 and CASSCF(10,8).
method: CASSCF and CASPT2, with CIS, MP2, SVWN, B3LYP, TD-DFT and EOM-CCSD(T) for comparison
software: MOLCAS for the CASSCF and CASPT2 energies; DALTON for the CASSCF analytical frequencies; MOLPRO for some multirepresentation state-average calculations; GAUSSIAN-94 for the CIS and MP2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: The base (10,8) space contains the two nitrogen lone-pair orbitals and all six valence pi orbitals. Larger spaces of (12,9) and (12,10) are used for particular mode symmetries; the paper notes that the residual discontinuity arises because the lone pairs mix with other sigma orbitals, which would also have to be included.
active_space_protocol: A DIFFERENT active space and state-averaging scheme is used for each vibrational mode symmetry, because different distortions couple T1 to different partner states. Table 1 lists them: analytical frequencies for T1(3B3u) with (10,8); ag modes with (12,9) single-state; b2g modes with (12,10) averaged over T1(3B3u) + T2(3B1u); b1g modes with (12,10) single-state; b1u modes with (10,8) averaged over T1(3B3u) + T5(3B2g); au and b3u modes with (12,10) single-state. Equal weights are used in each state average. The rationale is that continuity of the potential energy surface requires the state that T1 interacts with along a given distortion to be included in the average — b1u distortions mix T1(3B3u) with T5(3B2g), and b2g distortions mix it with T2(3B1u).
nroots_per_mult: 1 or 2 depending on the mode symmetry — equal-weight two-state averages over T1(3B3u)+T5(3B2g) for b1u modes and T1(3B3u)+T2(3B1u) for b2g modes, single-state otherwise
electronic_structure_description: T1(3B3u) vibrational frequencies in cm-1 (observed / CASSCF analytical / CASSCF numerical / CASSCF anharmonic / CASPT2 numerical / CASPT2 anharmonic / B3LYP analytical): ag,8a 1234 / 1663 / 1664 / 1664 / 1617 / 1587 / 1571; ag,9a 1149 / 1266 / 1266 / 1270 / 1196 / 1201 / 1191; ag,1 986 / 1053 / 1053 / 1052 / 1051 / 1022 / 1029; ag,6a 620 / 643 / 644 / 645 / 604 / 604 / 617; b1u,12 690 / 2723 (discontinuous) / 1347 / 1373 / 1594 / 1546 / 667; au,16a 406 / 457 / 461 / 463 / 389 / 393 / 448; b1g,10a 254 / 370 / 280 / 503 / 203 / 392 / 84i; b2g,5 295 / 834 (discontinuous) / 853 / 878 / 720 / 755 / 834; b2g,4 236 / 2343i (discontinuous) / 1229 / 1091 / 2069 / 1824 / 371; b3u,16b -- / 311 / 321 / 332 / 197 / 225 / 266. UMP2 analytical frequencies are pathological where the single-determinant wave function is unstable: 2380 cm-1 for b1u,12, 22042 cm-1 for b1g,10a, and 1260 and 803 cm-1 for b2g,4 and b2g,5 — the last two plausible-looking but wrong, and apparently switched in order relative to the ground state. The CASSCF(10,8) surface for T1 along mode 12 has a nonzero energy change of -0.0064 eV at Q = 0 and a pronounced derivative discontinuity. Ground-state RMS frequency errors after optimized scaling range from 20 to 43 cm-1, with scale factors of 0.90 (SCF), 0.99 (SVWN), 0.97 (B3LYP), 0.96 (MP2) and 0.92 (CASSCF). The Duschinsky mapping of normal modes between methods is smooth except that the order of the b2u modes nu14 and nu18b differs between SCF/CASSCF and the dynamically correlated methods MP2, SVWN and B3LYP — modes whose observed frequencies differ by only 86 cm-1.
Other: This paper's central result is an active-space failure that no amount of correlation can repair, and it is stated bluntly in the abstract: 'no practicable CASSCF methodology producing a continuous potential energy surface for T1. While CASPT2 (and also MRCI) methods can correct for erroneous CASSCF state energies, they are not capable of removing the effects of erroneous CASSCF conical intersections.' The mechanism is worth understanding. A (10,8) containing both nitrogen lone pairs and all six valence pi orbitals should in principle give a continuous surface, and the authors say so — but a small discontinuity survives because the lone pairs mix with sigma orbitals that are NOT in the space, so the wave function breaks symmetry from D2h to C2v as the lone-pair localization mode nu12 is displaced. Because a perturbative correction is built on the CASSCF reference, it inherits the reference's spurious intersection: the CASPT2 surface has its minimum at Q = 0 but is still not continuous there. The practical remedies and their costs are both documented. STATE AVERAGING restores continuity — averaging T1(3B3u) with T5(3B2g) for b1u distortions and with T2(3B1u) for b2g distortions makes those surfaces continuous, and a C2v geometry optimization with state averaging relaxes back to D2h while one without does not. But averaging 'modifies the wave function from that which would otherwise be thought of as optimal': the single-state curves show a double minimum and the state-averaged curve a single minimum, and only the CASPT2 test settles that the averaged description is right. There is also a methodological warning of general value: analytical frequency codes assume the wave function is stable to symmetry lowering and report numbers regardless. The UMP2 b2g frequencies of 1260 and 803 cm-1 look entirely plausible and are wrong — and 'the naive application of results such as this to resolve that controversy would have led to the incorrect conclusion'. Test the wave function for stability before interpreting any excited-state analytical frequency. Note finally that B3LYP outperforms every CASSCF-based method here on both qualitative and quantitative grounds, an unusual verdict that follows directly from the discontinuity problem rather than from any deficiency of the multiconfigurational treatment per se.
reference_short: Weber & Reimers, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 9830
notes: Companion paper considers a range of excited-state DFT methods. Less extensive calculations were also performed for the ground state, three excited singlet states and five other triplet states. Frequencies marked with an asterisk in Table 4 indicate that the potential energy surface is not a continuous function of that mode. The study verifies the current assignments of the strongly vibronically active modes nu4, nu5 and nu10a, predicts vibronic activity for nu12, reproduces the anomalous behaviour of nu16a and nu16b, and reassigns nu8a. The vibrational pattern for perdeuteropyrazine is noted to be significantly different.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF references; the paper reports that CASPT2 and MRCI can correct erroneous CASSCF state energies but cannot remove the effects of erroneous CASSCF conical intersections

geometry_source: SS-CASSCF(8,8)pi/6-31G* optimization; for the bond-stretch search the annelated C(1)-C(2) distance was held fixed at successive values while all other independent structural parameters were optimized at the SS-CASSCF(pi)/6-31G* level, followed by single-point HF, SS-CASSCF(8,8)pi, SS-CASPT2(pi) and SS-CASPT2(pi)+sigma calculations in cc-pVDZ. MP2(fc)/6-31G*, MP2(fc)/cc-pVDZ and B3LYP/6-31G* geometries computed for comparison; X-ray data available for a heavily substituted derivative in a molecular crystal.
method: Single-state and two-state CASSCF with single-state and two-state CASPT2, correlating either the pi electrons alone or all valence electrons; HF, B3LYP and MP2(fc) for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF geometries; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 single points, with cc-pVTZ used to extrapolate correlation energies to the infinite basis set limit
active_space_orbital_description: An (8,8) space over the pi orbitals only, denoted CASSCF(8,8)pi.
active_space_protocol: Two axes are varied independently. FIRST, the number of STATES in the reference: single-state SS-CASSCF/SS-CASPT2 versus two-state TWS-CASSCF/TWS-CASPT2, in which both states are treated simultaneously with equal weight and the solution obtained from the generalized Bloch equation. The two-state treatment is described as indispensable where several electronic states of the same symmetry are strongly coupled. SECOND, the electrons included in the PERTURBATIVE correction: CASPT2(pi), correlating only the pi electrons, versus CASPT2(pi)+sigma, correlating all valence electrons. The active space itself is pi-only in both cases — (8,8)pi for benzocyclobutene and (10,10)pi for benzo[1,2:4,5]dicyclobutadiene. The paper defines its correlation energies explicitly with a positive-is-larger sign convention: E(corr) = E(ND) + E(D), with the nondynamical part E(ND) = E(HF) - E(CASSCF) and the dynamical part E(D) = E(CASSCF) - E(CASPT2). Geometries along the bond-stretch coordinate were obtained by fixing the annelated C(1)-C(2) distance and optimizing all remaining parameters at the CASSCF(pi) level, with single-point HF, CASSCF, CASPT2(pi) and CASPT2(pi)+sigma energies in cc-pVDZ. Weightings other than 50:50 (40:60 and 60:40) were tried in the two-state calculations to test the sensitivity of the result.
nroots_per_mult: 1 for the single-state calculations; 2 with equal weights for the two-state calculations, with 40:60 and 60:40 weightings also tested
electronic_structure_description: HF/6-31G*, B3LYP/6-31G* and MP2(fc)/6-31G* all locate TWO minima, 1 and 1b, but the CASSCF(8,8)pi/6-31G* method shows 1b to be a FALSE minimum, leaving a single structure. All three single-configuration methods nonetheless correctly identify 1 as the global minimum, more stable than the spurious critical point 1b by 49.3, 46.7 and 49.0 kcal/mol respectively. Artificially stretching the annelated CC bond to very large distances does not produce another isomer, and the same electron configuration remains dominant throughout — so benzocyclobutene has no bond-stretch isomer corresponding to a pseudo-cyclic 8 pi-electron pattern. The CASSCF(8,8)pi picture amplifies the Mills-Nixon distortion (shortened exo C(2)-C(3) bonds, lengthened fused C(1)-C(2) bond). Loewdin pi-bond orders from SS-CASSCF(8,8)pi/6-31G*: 0.19 for the C(1)/C(2)-C(7)/C(8) bonds, 0.74-0.82 for C(2)-C(3), C(4)-C(5) and C(7)-C(8), and an intermediate 0.43 for the meta C(3)-C(4) and C(5)-C(6) bonds. Correlation energies in cc-pVDZ: E(ND)pi = 66.9, E(D)pi = 24.7 and E(D)(pi)+sigma = 581.3 kcal/mol; extrapolated to the infinite basis set these become 66.3, 37.9 and 808.5 kcal/mol. Additivity formulas give 65.6, 37.1 and 808.9 kcal/mol, in good agreement.
Other: The most quantitatively useful result here is the basis-set behaviour of the two correlation components, measured separately on the same molecule. The NONDYNAMICAL pi correlation energy — the part the active space is responsible for — is essentially basis-set independent: 66.9 kcal/mol in cc-pVDZ against 66.3 extrapolated to the infinite basis, a 1% change. The DYNAMICAL part is not: E(D)pi runs 24.7, 31.5 and 37.9 kcal/mol for cc-pVDZ, cc-pVTZ and the extrapolated limit, and E(D)(pi)+sigma runs 581.2, 717.2 and 808.5 kcal/mol — a 39% increase. This is a clean justification for the common practice of choosing an active space with a modest basis and then converging the perturbative correction separately, and a warning that any CASPT2 energy quoted in a double-zeta basis is missing hundreds of kcal/mol of valence correlation. Separately, this molecule is the paper's negative control for bond-stretch isomerism: a deliberate scan to large annelated CC distances finds no second minimum and no change in the dominant configuration, which is what makes the contrasting behaviour of benzo[1,2:4,5]dicyclobutadiene meaningful. Note also that HF, B3LYP and MP2 all produce a spurious second minimum 1b that the (8,8)pi space eliminates — an early demonstration in this paper that single-configuration methods manufacture bond-stretch isomers.
reference_short: Despotovic, Eckert-Maksic, Maksic & Smith, J. Phys. Chem. A 2003, 107, 10396
notes: Some NMR data had been advanced in favour of structure 1b; Schulman et al. showed the HF/6-31G* GIAO proton chemical shifts are fully compatible with structure 1 instead. The Mills-Nixon effect in 1 has two contributions: in-plane rehybridization of the junction carbons and the out-of-plane pi density distribution.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 in single-state and two-state forms, correlating either only the pi electrons or all valence electrons; correlation energies extrapolated to the infinite basis set limit using cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ

compound_name: Benzo[1,2:4,5]dicyclobutadiene — putative bond-stretch isomers 2 (localized) and 3 (delocalized pseudo-[10]annulene)
geometry_source: TWS-CASSCF(10,10)pi/6-31G* along the C(1)-C(2) bond-stretch coordinate, with the distance parametrically fixed and the remaining parameters optimized; TWS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ single points at those geometries. The transition state could not be located as a stationary point because critical points cannot currently be calculated by the CASPT2 method, so the point at d[C(1)-C(2)] = 1.496 A is called a transition state only conditionally. Zero-point energies were taken from MP2(fc)/cc-pVDZ with a 0.94 scaling factor, since geometry optimization and frequencies are not possible at TWS-CASPT2 and neither TWS-CASSCF nor MP2 yields a transition state at all.
method: Single-state and two-state CASSCF with single-state and two-state CASPT2, correlating either the pi electrons alone or all valence electrons; HF, B3LYP and MP2(fc) for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF geometries; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 single points, with cc-pVTZ used to extrapolate correlation energies to the infinite basis set limit
active_space_orbital_description: A (10,10) space over the pi orbitals only, denoted CASSCF(10,10)pi. The two orbitals that change most along the isomerization are the Au and B1g pair.
active_space_protocol: Two axes are varied independently. FIRST, the number of STATES in the reference: single-state SS-CASSCF/SS-CASPT2 versus two-state TWS-CASSCF/TWS-CASPT2, in which both states are treated simultaneously with equal weight and the solution obtained from the generalized Bloch equation. The two-state treatment is described as indispensable where several electronic states of the same symmetry are strongly coupled. SECOND, the electrons included in the PERTURBATIVE correction: CASPT2(pi), correlating only the pi electrons, versus CASPT2(pi)+sigma, correlating all valence electrons. The active space itself is pi-only in both cases — (8,8)pi for benzocyclobutene and (10,10)pi for benzo[1,2:4,5]dicyclobutadiene. The paper defines its correlation energies explicitly with a positive-is-larger sign convention: E(corr) = E(ND) + E(D), with the nondynamical part E(ND) = E(HF) - E(CASSCF) and the dynamical part E(D) = E(CASSCF) - E(CASPT2). Geometries along the bond-stretch coordinate were obtained by fixing the annelated C(1)-C(2) distance and optimizing all remaining parameters at the CASSCF(pi) level, with single-point HF, CASSCF, CASPT2(pi) and CASPT2(pi)+sigma energies in cc-pVDZ. Weightings other than 50:50 (40:60 and 60:40) were tried in the two-state calculations to test the sensitivity of the result.
nroots_per_mult: 1 for the single-state calculations; 2 with equal weights for the two-state calculations, with 40:60 and 60:40 weightings also tested
electronic_structure_description: Isomers 2 and 3 have INTERCONVERTED HOMO and LUMO: their pi ground-state configurations are (B3u)2(B3u)2(B2g)2(Au)2(B1g)2 and (B3u)2(B3u)2(B2g)2(B1g)2(Au)2, so the ground configuration of 2 is the first excited configuration of 3 and vice versa. Relative stabilities, positive meaning 2 more stable: SS-CASSCF(10,10)pi/6-31G* +5 kcal/mol; TWS-CASSCF(10,10)pi/6-31G* +5.7; TWS-CASPT2(10,10)pi/cc-pVDZ +3.8 (energies -382.17563 and -382.16951 au); TWS-CASPT2(10,10)(pi)+sigma/cc-pVDZ//TWS-CASSCF(10,10)pi/6-31G* REVERSES the order, with 3 more stable by 3.2 kcal/mol. B3LYP/cc-pVDZ and MP2(fc)/cc-pVDZ also favour 3, by 2.6 and 5.0 kcal/mol (3.7 kcal/mol at MP2(fc)/6-31G*). The barrier relative to 2 and 3 is 3.4 and 6.6 kcal/mol. Energy minima occur at C(1)-C(2) distances of 1.430 A (isomer 2) and 1.554 A (isomer 3), the latter extremely long for two sp2 carbons, with the conditional transition state near 1.496 A. TWS-CASSCF(10,10)pi natural orbital occupations along the coordinate (Au / B1g) are 0.36/1.64 at 1.430 A, 0.74/1.26 at 1.494, 0.79/1.21 at 1.496, 0.90/1.10 at 1.498, 1.14/0.86 at 1.4985, 1.18/0.82 at 1.499, 1.22/0.78 at 1.500 and 1.54/0.45 at 1.554 A — the turnover occurring just below 1.4985 A. MP2(fc)/cc-pVDZ shows a DISCONTINUOUS jump between two separate curves at d = 1.532 A, with a 14.3 kcal/mol gap between the upper curve at 1.531 A and the lower at 1.532 A. Scaled MP2 zero-point energies are 69.6 and 71.9 kcal/mol for 2 and 3, reducing their separation to 2.3 kcal/mol and, by analogy with cyclobutadiene and cyclobutadieno-p-benzoquinone where ZPVE lowered barriers by 2.6 and 2.4 kcal/mol, leaving a barrier of only about 0.4-1.0 kcal/mol.
Other: Three separate active-space lessons sit in this one system. FIRST, the sign of the answer depends on which ELECTRONS the perturbation correlates, not on the active space: TWS-CASPT2 correlating only pi electrons makes 2 more stable by 3.8 kcal/mol, and TWS-CASPT2 correlating all valence electrons reverses this to 3 more stable by 3.2 kcal/mol. The (10,10)pi space is identical in both. As the authors put it, 'the dynamical correlation energy of sigma electrons plays a very important role in phenylenes' — a pi-only space with a pi-only correction gets the qualitative answer backwards. SECOND, the occupation-number table is a direct measure of when a single-reference method must fail: the Au/B1g populations pass through 0.79/1.21 at the transition state and cross near 1.4985 A, so at the barrier both configurations are of almost equal weight. MP2 works well at both equilibrium geometries — where the multiconfigurational character is only moderate, 0.36/1.64 and 1.54/0.45 — because its double excitations mimic that character, but it 'completely fails in reproducing the transition structure', jumping discontinuously between two curves with a 14.3 kcal/mol gap. THIRD, and unusually candid, the two-state treatment does not fully cure the problem: the TWS-CASPT2 cross-section 'exhibits an unphysical cusp in the vicinity of TS', and reweighting the two states 40:60 and 60:40 changes the answers by only 0.2-0.5 kcal/mol, showing the cusp 'is inherent in the TWS-CASPT2 wave functions'. The authors accordingly label their own conclusion tentative — a caveat emptor that anyone reusing the 3.2 kcal/mol preference or the sub-kcal/mol barrier must carry with it.
reference_short: Despotovic, Eckert-Maksic, Maksic & Smith, J. Phys. Chem. A 2003, 107, 10396
notes: The paper concludes, tentatively, that benzo[1,2:4,5]dicyclobutadiene exists as a fully delocalized 10 pi-electron pseudo-[10]annulene rather than as two distinguishable bond-stretch isomers, consistent with some experimental evidence. The Mills-Nixon effect is less pronounced than in benzocyclobutene because of the higher symmetry, so the benzene ring is better preserved; the peripheral four-membered ring pi bonds participate little in the conjugation in 2, while pi density is almost evenly distributed over the perimeter CC bonds in 3. Substituted derivatives (including 4,5,9,10-tetraethenyl analogues 2b and 3b) were examined at MP2(fc)/cc-pVDZ and B3LYP levels only, not with CASSCF.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 in single-state and two-state forms, correlating either only the pi electrons or all valence electrons; correlation energies extrapolated to the infinite basis set limit using cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ

point_group: 6A optimized under the constraint of linear NC2O units; 6B, 6C and 6D optimized without constraint
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations and vibrational analysis of HNC4O2 at various levels, with structure 6A constrained to linear NC2O units and 6B-6D unconstrained; the B3PW91/6-31G** geometries are shown in Figure 3.
method: CASSCF, alongside B3PW91, HF, MP2 and CI
software: MOLCAS for the multiconfigurational calculations; Gaussian 94/98 and NWChem for the other levels
active_space_orbital_description: Not stated in the text — the article reports CASSCF/6-31G** energies without specifying the number of active electrons or orbitals.
active_space_protocol: No active space specification is given anywhere in the article; the Computational Details section states only that 'the multiconfigurational calculations were performed with MOLCAS'. The CASSCF results are used solely as a check that the DFT conformer ordering survives at a correlated multiconfigurational level.
electronic_structure_description: Relative conformer energies in kcal/mol. At B3PW91/6-31G**: 6A 9.00, 6B 0.91, 6C 0.67, 6D 0.00 (total energies -357.90053, -357.91336, -357.91375 and -357.91481 au). At HF/6-31G**: 6B 3.55, 6C 1.72, 6D 0.00 (-356.01219, -356.01511, -356.01785 au). At CASSCF/6-31G**: 6B 1.74, 6C 1.59, 6D 0.00 (-356.05480, -356.05511, -356.05765 au). 6D is the global minimum at all three levels, but 6B, 6C and 6D are all very close in energy. All of these geometries are described as singlet states 'quite well represented by single determinants', with the triplet state at least 20 kcal/mol higher and of similar geometry to 6C. Given a zero-point vibrational energy of about 30 kcal/mol, the paper concludes it is difficult to settle the definitive geometry of HNC4O2 without a dynamical analysis.
