In other words, it is almost impossible to predict what will happen from one active space to the next.' The authors' explanation is that the three isomers improve at DIFFERENT RATES as the space grows, so the errors do not cancel in the difference — which is precisely why relative energies between structurally dissimilar isomers are the quantity most vulnerable to space truncation. The numbers make the point starkly. At CASSCF the 1t-2s separation runs -12.5, -4.4, -7.9, -4.3 and +2.3 kcal/mol across (8,8), (10,10), (12,12), (14,14) and FORS(16,16) — non-monotonic, spanning 15 kcal/mol, and changing sign only at the full valence space. At MRPT2 the swings are smaller but still non-monotonic, and 3s and 1t exchange places between (12,12) and (14,14) and then swap back at FORS(16,16). Two structural lessons follow. First, a nested ladder of spaces derived from full-valence natural orbital occupations does NOT guarantee monotonic convergence, so testing two or three space sizes and extrapolating is unsound. Second, the full valence space is preferred here on a BALANCE argument rather than a size argument — it contains all valence orbitals for every isomer, so no isomer is favoured by the selection. Note also the resolution of a literature dispute: the earlier MRMP2(12,11)/aug-cc-pVDZ prediction that 1t is the global minimum by 4.4 kcal/mol survives a basis-set change (still 1t lowest at 6-31G(d) and cc-pCVQZ) and therefore was not a basis-set artefact as had been suggested, but it does not survive going to the full valence space. Core 1s excitations shift things by only 0.1-0.5 kcal/mol but are described as 'not large but play a non-negligible role in such a sensitive system'.

compound_name: Hypoxanthine (keto-N9H form) — vertical singlet electronic transitions
point_group: Cs (planar, imposed for the CASSCF calculations and found at every level of ground-state optimization)
geometry_source: CASSCF vertical transitions computed at the MP2/6-311++G(d,p) ground-state optimized geometry under planar Cs symmetry. Ground-state geometries also optimized at HF and B3LYP with 6-311++G(d,p), all planar. The lowest singlet pipi* excited-state geometries of the isolated and hydrated forms were optimized at the CIS level, with harmonic frequency analysis confirming the nature of the stationary points in both ground and excited states. A hydrated form with three water molecules in the first solvation shell was optimized at HF and B3LYP.
method: CASSCF with MCQDPT2 dynamic correlation correction; CIS and TD-B3LYP for comparison
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 94 and Gaussian 98 for everything else; gOpenMol for the electrostatic potential mapping
basis_set: 6-31+G(d) for the CASSCF; 6-311++G(d,p) for all other calculations
active_space_orbital_description: The paper states the active space as '2 sigma, 6 pi, and 4 pi* orbitals', with the sigma orbitals present specifically to allow the n-pi* transitions to be computed. Twelve orbitals in total; the electron count of 16 follows arithmetically from the eight occupied orbitals (2 sigma plus 6 pi) and is not stated in the text.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled by transition type: 6 pi and 4 pi* orbitals for the pipi* manifold, plus 2 sigma (lone pair) orbitals added expressly so that the n-pi* transitions can be described. The state weighting is NON-UNIFORM and the reason is a convergence failure: 'The CASSCF energies were obtained by giving 100% weight to each state except for the third and fifth singlet pipi* excited states, for which the weight factors were 88 and 96.5%, respectively. Several attempts were made to compute these states with 100% weight, but convergence was not obtained.' Dynamic correlation was then added by MCQDPT2 on those references.
nroots_per_mult: Five singlet pipi* and two n-pi* states; state-specific (100% weight) except for the third and fifth pipi* states at 88% and 96.5%
electronic_structure_description: Vertical singlet transition energies in eV (MCQDPT2 / CASSCF), with CASSCF oscillator strengths and Tinoco-DeVoe transition moment directions in degrees. pipi*: 4.63 / 5.62 (f = 0.247, -61 deg); 5.35 / 6.55 (f = 0.362, 56 deg); 5.48 / 6.92 (f = 0.045, 24 deg); 5.78 / 7.97 (f = 0.102, 20 deg); 6.31 / 8.40 (f = 0.034, 77 deg). n-pi*: 5.75 / 6.62 (f = 0.0001) and 6.06 / 7.19 (f = 0.0036). Ground-state dipole moment 4.72 D at CASSCF/6-31+G(d)//MP2/6-311++G(d,p), against 5.13, 5.07 and 5.22 D at the other levels; the CASSCF value is relatively closer to experiment. Excited-state CASSCF dipole moments range from 2.66 to 6.83 D. The MCQDPT2 energies of 4.63, 5.35, 5.78 and 6.31 eV agree within about 0.2 eV with the vapour-phase absorption transitions of 9-methylhypoxanthine (4.41, 5.19, 6.05 and 6.42 eV). CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers, ground state: lone pairs 1.998 and 1.998; occupied pi 1.994, 1.988, 1.949, 1.940, 1.957, 1.911; virtual pi 0.041, 0.075, 0.082, 0.067. In the first pipi* state the 8pi occupation falls to 1.378 with 10pi rising to 0.620; in the second pipi* state 7pi and 8pi fall to 1.657 and 1.170 with 9pi and 10pi at 0.805 and 0.383. In the first n-pi* state the 1n occupation falls to 1.048 and 9pi rises to 0.978; in the second n-pi* state the two lone pairs become 1.693 and 1.306, i.e. strongly mixed.
Other: Two things in this paper bear directly on active-space practice. First, the ground-state occupation numbers show the space is only marginally justified by the usual criterion: the four virtual pi orbitals carry 0.041, 0.075, 0.082 and 0.067 electrons, all just above the conventional 0.02 cutoff, while the most correlated occupied orbital sits at 1.911, comfortably below 1.98. So the space is defensible in the ground state but is really sized for the EXCITED states, where occupations swing dramatically — 8pi drops to 1.378 and 10pi rises to 0.620 in the first pipi* state. Judging this space from the ground state alone would have suggested trimming it. Second, and more cautionary, the two highest pipi* states could not be converged with equal state weighting and were computed at 88% and 96.5% weight instead. That means the third and fifth pipi* energies rest on differently weighted references from the other three, so the five pipi* transitions are NOT all on the same footing, and comparisons among them carry that caveat. It is consistent with the paper's own observation that the first two pipi* energies agree well with scaled CIS and experiment while 'the higher transitions show significant error'. Note finally the sheer size of the MCQDPT2 correction: 0.99, 1.20, 1.44, 2.19 and 2.09 eV for the five pipi* states, growing with excitation energy — a bare CASSCF spectrum from this space is unusable, and the correction is not a uniform shift.

compound_name: 9H-Adenine — S0, 1(n-pi*) and 1Lb excited-state geometries and vibronic activities

compound_name: pH-BDI — para-unsubstituted neutral benzylidene-imidazolinone GFP chromophore model
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized on the MP2 potential energy surface with the cc-pVDZ basis set; all subsequent SA-CASSCF calculations performed at those geometries.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with self-consistent thermostatistical (Boltzmann) weighting of the state-average weights, analysed in a complete-active-space valence-bond (CASVB) representation over Boys-localized active orbitals
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in three orbitals: after Boys localization, one orbital on the benzyl ring, one on the bridge and one on the imidazoloxy ring, with similar nodal structure for every dye in the series.
active_space_protocol: A deliberately MINIMAL CAS(4,3) is used for every member of the series, and the paper argues at length that this is not merely economical but BETTER than intermediate spaces. 'This active space was chosen because it is the minimal complete quantum many-body model that can describe coherent transfer of an excess electronic charge and a covalent bond pair.' The justification against enlarging it is explicit: 'the same three-orbital, four-electron CAS provides a more balanced description of the low-energy electronic structure than is possible with larger active spaces short of the full pi-electron space. The reason is that the aromaticity of the rings changes for different structures involved, and these correlations are deep. They are sufficiently deep to break the symmetry if they are not treated completely for both rings. The four-electron, three-orbital CASSCF approximation was shown to constitute a Pauling point, where further increases in the size of the CAS made things worse before making them better.' The state averaging is not the usual equal-weight scheme: a self-consistent THERMOSTATISTICAL equilibration of the SA-CASSCF weights is used, so the converged ensemble is a canonical Boltzmann state with the converged effective Hamiltonian as sufficient statistic. All states generated by the active space are included in the ensemble support. An electronic 'temperature' of beta^-1 = 2.75 +/- 0.25 eV is used, chosen to span most of the emission band of pH-BDI; results were scanned over 2.5-3.0 eV to give error bars. The active orbitals are Boys-localized onto the benzyl ring, the bridge and the imidazoloxy ring, and are qualitatively identical across all dyes — an ISOLOBAL ANALOGY that lets the CASVB states of differently substituted molecules be identified with a single abstract set of states in a shared Hilbert space, which is what makes the Hammett LFER analysis possible.
nroots_per_mult: All states generated by the (4,3) active space are included in the thermostatistical ensemble support, weighted by a Boltzmann distribution at an electronic temperature of beta^-1 = 2.75 eV
electronic_structure_description: The reference member of the series, defining the zero of the Hammett sigma-p scale. The ground state is unambiguously dominated by the unpolarized covalent CASVB structure |211>, which is the lowest diabatic state for every molecule in the series and is separated from the next state by a significant gap. Four diabatic CASVB states are clustered within a 2 eV window above the lowest diabatic gap for pH-BDI, in the order |121>, |220>, |202>, |112>. The covalent charge-transfer configuration |112> lies HIGHER than any CASVB state associated with a locally excited structure, so pH-BDI is expected to have an adiabatic excited state of dominant LE character with ionic biradicaloid structure localized to the ground-state bond pairing. The 1,3-diradical state |121> is the lowest diabatic excited state for all the dyes but does not appreciably contribute to adiabatic S0 or S1, being high in energy and more weakly coupled to the ground state than other CASVB states; it mixes significantly only into S2 and above. The most significant couplings (greater than 1.0 eV) correspond to one-electron transfers between nearest-neighbour orbitals; the direct inter-ring coupling <211|H|112> is only about 0.4 eV at beta^-1 = 2.75 eV, indicating that models neglecting it may be useful, and all other couplings are mostly below 0.1 eV. The dependence of the CASVB couplings on sigma-p is significantly weaker than that of the CASVB state energies.
Other: pH-BDI is the LE-dominant end of the series and the reference that defines the abstract CASVB basis. Its electronic temperature of beta^-1 = 2.75 eV was chosen to span most of its own emission band, so the ensemble weighting for the whole series is calibrated on this molecule. The diabatic congestion here — four states within a 2 eV window — is what makes a balanced active space essential: with states that close together, any asymmetry in how the two rings are correlated would reorder them.  The active-space argument in this paper runs opposite to the usual direction and is worth recording carefully. Rather than treating (4,3) as a compromise forced by cost, the author argues it is a PAULING POINT: enlarging the CAS beyond three orbitals but short of the full pi space makes the description WORSE before it improves, because ring aromaticity changes between the structures involved and those correlations are deep enough to break the symmetry unless treated completely for BOTH rings. A partially enlarged space treats one ring better than the other and so biases the very charge-transfer asymmetry the study is measuring. This is the balance argument in its sharpest form: what matters is not how many orbitals are correlated but whether the two competing fragments are correlated equivalently. The minimal space also buys something no larger space could: because the three Boys-localized active orbitals have the same qualitative structure for every dye in the series, the CASVB states of different molecules can be mapped onto one abstract basis, and differences between molecules become meaningful as free-energy differences correlating with the Hammett sigma-p scale. An isolobal analogy of this kind would be much harder to sustain across a larger, less transferable space. One internal check is reported: the 1,3-diradical CASVB state |121> was found to mix significantly only into S2 and above, and 'this was also upheld in calculations with a larger active space, where the corresponding state could be reliably identified for comparison.' The caveat for reuse is that this is a diabatic, model-Hamiltonian study — the reported quantities are CASVB diabatic state energies and couplings, not adiabatic excitation energies, and the paper notes separately that ab initio models typically overestimate the pOH-BDI gap by several tenths of an eV.
reference_short: Olsen, J. Phys. Chem. B 2015, 119, 2566
notes: pR-BDI denotes para-substituted benzylidene-dimethyl-imidazolinone GFP chromophore models. The CASVB labels |211>, |121>, |112>, |220>, |202>, |022> give the occupations of the benzyl, bridge and imidazoloxy localized orbitals respectively.

geometry_source: All stationary points located by (4/4)CASSCF/6-31G* optimization, with a (4/4)CASSCF vibrational analysis at each to classify it as a minimum, transition structure or hilltop and to give enthalpies at 298 K; transition vectors followed in both directions to establish connectivity. Single-point CASPT2 energies computed at those geometries with both 6-31G* and 6-311+G(2df,2p).
method: (4/4)CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with single-point CASPT2
software: Gaussian 03 for the CASSCF calculations; MOLCAS for the CASPT2
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF; CASPT2 single points with both 6-31G* and 6-311+G(2df,2p)
active_space_orbital_description: For reactant 9: the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the scissile sigma bond plus the pi and pi* MOs. For all other stationary points: the four MOs formed by mixing the sigma, sigma*, pi and pi* orbitals of 9 upon ring opening.
active_space_protocol: A (4/4)CASSCF space is used throughout, but its ORBITAL CONTENT is redefined as the reaction proceeds. For the reactant 9 the four active orbitals are the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the scissile sigma bond plus the pi and pi* MOs. 'For other stationary points on the potential energy surface, the orbitals in the active space consisted of the four MOs, formed by the mixing of the sigma, sigma*, pi, and pi* orbitals of 9 upon ring opening.' The size therefore stays at (4,4) while the composition follows the sigma-to-pi transformation of ring opening — the same fixed-size, variable-content strategy used for the parent hydrocarbon rearrangement. A (4/4)CASSCF vibrational analysis was performed at every stationary point to classify it as a minimum, transition structure or hilltop and to supply enthalpies at 298 K; each transition vector was followed in both directions to identify which pair of minima it connects. Single-point CASPT2 was then computed at every CASSCF stationary point, with BOTH the 6-31G* and the much larger 6-311+G(2df,2p) basis sets.
electronic_structure_description: Relative electronic energies with enthalpies at 298 K in parentheses, kcal/mol, at (4/4)CASSCF/6-31G* geometries. Format CASSCF/6-31G*, CASPT2/6-31G*, CASSCF/6-311+G(2df,2p), CASPT2/6-311+G(2df,2p): reactant 9 is the zero. Diradical 10: 21.7 (19.8), 21.8 (20.0), 21.4 (19.6), 21.4 (19.5). Diradical 10': 21.4 (20.4), 22.8 (21.7), 21.9 (20.8), 24.0 (22.8). TS(10/10'): 25.7 (23.3), 25.1 (22.7), 26.0 (23.5), 25.1 (22.6). Product 11: -4.8 (-4.4), -8.6 (-8.3), -4.9 (-4.6), -9.2 (-8.8). TS-12 (ring opening of 9 to 10, the rate-determining step): 30.7 (29.3), 31.9 (30.5), 29.4 (28.1), 31.3 (30.0). TS-13: 23.7 (22.4), 25.4 (24.1), 24.1 (22.8), 27.0 (25.7). TS-14 (ring closure of 10 to 11 with CF2 inversion): 25.5 (23.2), 28.0 (25.6), 25.6 (23.3), 28.4 (26.1). Diradical 15: 25.4 (23.6), 28.3 (26.6), 25.4 (23.7), 28.8 (27.1). TS-16: 31.6 (29.2), 28.6 (26.2), 30.5 (28.2), 26.4 (24.1). TS-17 (ring closure of 10' to 11 with retention): 31.4 (29.0), 33.0 (30.6), 30.6 (28.2), 32.0 (29.6). Structures 18, 19 and their triplets lie between 27.5 and 36.1. The CASPT2 activation enthalpy Ea = dH(double dagger) + RT = 30.0 + 0.8 = 30.8 kcal/mol agrees very well with the measured Ea = 29.6 +/- 1 kcal/mol (150-160 degrees C). active_space_orbital_description: Sixteen electrons in ten orbitals: the platinum s orbital, the six Cartesian d orbitals and the three p-type functions of the fluorine atom being attacked. With no C-H bond present, only the C-F activation composition applies.
active_space_protocol: Two different space sizes are used across the study, and the composition of the smaller one is REDEFINED according to which bond is being activated. For Pt + CH3F a FULL VALENCE active space of 24 electrons in 13 orbitals was used. For every other interaction the potential-energy curves used 16 electrons in 10 orbitals, and 'the dimension of the active space was kept fixed throughout all calculations on the different potential-energy curves'. The invariant core of the space is the platinum s orbital and the six Cartesian d orbitals, present in all cases. Beyond that, for C-F bond activation the space also includes the three p-type functions of the fluorine atom, while for C-H insertion it instead uses the s-type functions of the hydrogen and carbon atoms plus a p function of a fluorine atom. MRMP2 calculations were performed at selected points of each CASSCF potential-energy curve, using the CASSCF active orbitals as the MRMP2 active space. Because a non-gradient geometry optimization algorithm was used, curves for the Cs states were computed with the platinum atom constrained to lie in the F-C-H plane.
electronic_structure_description: Linear C-Pt-F approach: 3A' at -0.25 (CASSCF) and +0.27 kcal/mol (MRMP2) — the ONLY entry in Table 1 where MRMP2 raises the energy above the dissociation limit — with r(Pt-F) = 2.85 and r(C-F) = 1.39 A; 1A' at +8.08 (CASSCF) and -2.08 kcal/mol (MRMP2) with r(Pt-F) = 3.50 and r(C-F) = 1.38 A. The C-F insertion product PtCF4 1A' has a C-Pt-F angle of 104.7 degrees with r(Pt-F) = 1.99, r(Pt-C) = 1.92 and r(C-F) = 3.11 A. All C-F insertion products show a significant elongation of the C-F bond. A small energy barrier of 2.6 kcal/mol separates the potential-energy wells for the more stable insertion products arising from the high multiplicity states.
Other: CF4 is the clean C-F-only endpoint of the series: with no C-H bond, the (16,10) space carries the Pt s and d set plus the three fluorine p functions and nothing else, so it is the member whose space composition is least ambiguous. It is also the weakest interaction — the triplet is the only state in Table 1 that MRMP2 places ABOVE the dissociation limit (+0.27 kcal/mol) and the singlet is bound by only 2.08 kcal/mol, against 11.90 for CH3F. The trend across the series is monotone at CASSCF (singlet linear approach at +4.57, +4.98, +6.78, +8.08 for n = 1 to 4) and monotone in the opposite direction after correlation is added, which is a reminder that for weakly bound metal-substrate complexes the bare CASSCF trend can invert entirely under MRMP2.  The active-space design here is explicitly bond-directed: the same ten orbitals are not the same ten orbitals from one reaction to the next. Platinum's s and six Cartesian d orbitals are always active, but the ligand contribution switches between the three fluorine p functions (for C-F activation) and the carbon and hydrogen s functions plus one fluorine p (for C-H activation). Holding the DIMENSION fixed at (16,10) across the whole series is what makes the C-H versus C-F comparison and the n = 1 to 4 trend meaningful, since every curve carries the same number of correlated electrons and orbitals; but the composition change means a C-H and a C-F curve for the same molecule are not strictly the same calculation, and the difference between them absorbs some of the space difference. The one exception undercuts this slightly: Pt + CH3F was treated with a FULL VALENCE (24,13) space, not the (16,10) used for everything else, so the best-characterized member of the series is the one least comparable with the rest. The magnitude of the correlation correction warns against using the CASSCF curves directly: for the linear Pt...F approach the singlet states move from +4.57 to -11.90 kcal/mol (CH3F), +4.98 to -7.66 (CH2F2), +6.78 to -7.18 (CHF3) and +8.08 to -2.08 (CF4) on adding MRMP2 — corrections of 10 to 16 kcal/mol that change every singlet from unbound to bound. The triplets shift by only 0.5 to 3 kcal/mol. That differential is the crux: a space of this size describes the open-shell triplet adequately but leaves the closed-shell singlet badly under-correlated, so the singlet-triplet ordering at CASSCF is not to be trusted. The paper states the same for the insertion barriers, which are 'significantly decreased after inclusion of the electron correlation'.
reference_short: Colmenares & Torrens, J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 10587
notes: CH4-nFn with n = 4. Only C-F activation is possible for this substrate. The greater stabilization calculated for the products of the Pt + CH2F2 and related reactions is discussed in comparison.
correlation_correction: MRMP2 at selected points on the CASSCF potential-energy curves, using the CASSCF active orbitals

compound_name: Bicyclo[4,1,0]hept-2-ene (2-norcarene) — singlet and triplet photoisomerization pathways
geometry_source: CASSCF(8,8)/6-311G(d) optimization of all stationary points on the S0, S1 and T1 surfaces; state-averaged CASSCF(8,8) used to determine geometries in the intersection space. Every stationary point characterized by analytically computed harmonic frequencies (all real for minima, one imaginary for transition states). Optimizations terminated when the maximum force and its RMS fell below 0.00045 and 0.00005 hartree/bohr. Minima, transition states and crossing minima were all located in CARTESIAN coordinates, so the results do not depend on any particular choice of internal variables. Transition-state connectivity verified by following the intrinsic reaction coordinate in both directions.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with multireference Moller-Plesset (MP2-CAS) single-point energies
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals. For the general photoisomerization the space comprises two p-pi orbitals plus three sigma(C-C) and three sigma*(C-C) orbitals. For reactions such as the hydrogen migration a DIFFERENT (8,8) is used: pi, sigma, sigma, pi*, sigma*, sigma* of the cycloheptene ring plus the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-H bond.
active_space_protocol: A fixed-size (8,8) space whose composition is chosen to match the bonds being made and broken in each reaction type. The default set is two p-pi orbitals plus three sigma(C-C)/sigma*(C-C) pairs, which covers ring opening and closing at the cyclopropane bonds. Where a C-H bond is involved — notably the 1,2-hydrogen migration — two of those orbitals are replaced by the sigma and sigma* of the C-H bond, leaving pi, sigma, sigma, pi*, sigma*, sigma* on the cycloheptene ring. State-averaged CASSCF(8,8) is used for geometries in the intersection space. Dynamic correlation is added by multireference Moller-Plesset (MP2-CAS) single points at the CASSCF geometries; unless stated otherwise all relative energies quoted are MP2-CAS-(8,8)/6-311G(d)//CAS(8,8)/6-311G(d).
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged for the intersection-space optimizations
electronic_structure_description: SINGLET pathways. Decay from S1 to S0 occurs via two conical intersections, CI-1 and CI-2, both arising from breaking of cyclopropane bonds. Path I proceeds S0 + h-nu -> FC-S -> CI-1 -> Int-1 and then over four competing S0 transition states to four photoproducts: TS-3 (52 kcal/mol, imaginary frequency 1729i cm-1) to bicyclo[3.2.0]hept-2-ene (2) by intramolecular C-C ring closure; TS-4 (32 kcal/mol, 3180i cm-1) to 1,2,6-heptatriene (3) by 1,2-hydrogen migration with C-C bond breaking; TS-5 (6.9 kcal/mol, 1727i cm-1) to 1,4-cycloheptadiene (4); and TS-6 (8.7 kcal/mol, 1775i cm-1) to 1,3-cycloheptadiene (5). Path II proceeds via CI-2 to Int-2, which lies 63 kcal/mol below CI-2 and has a methylcycloheptene-like structure with two unpaired electrons on C1 and C7; from Int-2 three pathways lead to photoproducts 6, 7 and 8 over TS-7 (9.0 kcal/mol), TS-8 (60 kcal/mol) and TS-9 (18 kcal/mol). The barrier to path II-1 is the smallest of all the reaction pathways at only 3.8 kcal/mol, making it the most favourable and giving 1,3,6-heptatriene (6) as the product. TRIPLET pathways. The vertical S0 to T1 excitation at the S0 geometry is 95 kcal/mol; T1 lies about 61 kcal/mol above the ground-state minimum. Two triplet routes are found: path III via TS-10 and path IV via C-C bond breaking between C1 and C7 via TS-11, with barriers of 16 and 12 kcal/mol respectively. The T1/S0-1 crossing point lies 36 kcal/mol below the FC-T point and 59 kcal/mol above the ground-state minimum; T1/S0-2 lies 28 kcal/mol below FC-T and 67 kcal/mol above the ground-state minimum. MP2-CAS gives TS-13 (20 kcal/mol) above TS-12 (8.0 kcal/mol) relative to the ground-state minimum, so path III is preferred over path IV.
Other: The interesting active-space decision here is that the (8,8) is not one space but two, selected by reaction type at fixed size. The default set — two p-pi plus three sigma(C-C)/sigma*(C-C) pairs — is built for the cyclopropane ring openings that generate both conical intersections. For the 1,2-hydrogen migration the C-H sigma and sigma* are swapped in, since a space containing no C-H orbitals cannot describe a hydrogen shift at all. That swap is necessary but it means the four path-I barriers are NOT all computed in the same orbital space: TS-4, the hydrogen migration at 32 kcal/mol, uses the C-H variant while TS-3, TS-5 and TS-6 use the C-C variant. Since the paper's conclusion is a ranking of these barriers (TS-3 > TS-4 > TS-6 > TS-5), the position of TS-4 in that ranking carries a caveat the others do not. Two further diagnostics support the choice of space. First, the imaginary frequency of TS-4 is 3180i cm-1, nearly twice that of the three C-C transition states (1727-1775i cm-1), exactly as expected for a hydrogen-motion transition vector and confirming the C-H orbitals are doing the work they were added for. Second, all stationary points and crossing minima were located in Cartesian rather than internal coordinates, so the intersection geometries are not biased by a coordinate choice. Note finally that the paper quotes both MP2-CAS and bare CASSCF energies throughout (the latter in parentheses in Figures 1 and 5), and bases every conclusion on the MP2-CAS values.
reference_short: Su, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 381
notes: 2-Norcarene photoisomerization is experimentally known to give a wide variety of products. The mechanisms are grouped as cycloheptene ring expansion (paths I and III) and cyclohexene ring contraction (paths II and IV). Products identified are bicyclo[3.2.0]hept-2-ene (2), 1,2,6-heptatriene (3), 1,4-cycloheptadiene (4), 1,3-cycloheptadiene (5), 1,3,6-heptatriene (6), and products 7 and 8.
correlation_correction: Multireference Moller-Plesset (MP2-CAS) single points at the CASSCF geometries

compound_name: Anti n-tetrasilane — valence and Rydberg singlet excited states
geometry_source: Vertical excitation energies at the ground-state geometry of the anti conformer; the Rydberg functions were placed at the charge centroid of the ground state of the positive ion.
method: Average CASSCF with single-state CASPT2 and multistate MS-CASPT2; CASSCF State Interaction (CASSI) for transition dipole moments
basis_set: ANO-type from Si(17s12p5d)/H(8s4p) primitives, contracted Si[6s5p2d]/H[2s1p], supplemented for the Rydberg states with a 1s1p1d set of Rydberg functions contracted from 8s8p8d primitives placed at the charge centroid of the ground state of the cation
active_space_orbital_description: Six active electrons throughout, corresponding to the three Si-Si bonds of the sigma-conjugated system. The base space is the sigma and sigma* Si-Si bond orbitals, denoted (3;3;0;0) in the ag, bu, au, bg irreducible representations of C2h — six orbitals. This is extended per symmetry class to include the relevant Rydberg orbitals and the pi*-symmetry Si-H antibonding orbital combinations: (8;3;0;0) for 1Ag with 11 orbitals, (3;5;0;0) for 1Bu with 8, (3;3;2;0) for 1Au with 8, and (3;3;0;3) for 1Bg with 9. Frozen orbitals (2;2;0;0); inactive (9;9;4;4); occupied SCF MOs (13;12;4;4).
active_space_protocol: The electron count is fixed at SIX for every calculation, one pair per Si-Si bond, and the paper justifies this as 'a natural truncation, inspired by the semiempirical Sandorfy C and ladder C models of electronic structure of saturated systems'. The authors state explicitly what they would have preferred and why they could not do it: 'The next better choice would be to also treat as active the 20 electrons of the ten Si-H bonds (in analogy to the Sandorfy H and ladder H models), but we cannot afford to assign all valence electrons in a molecule of this size into the active category and will attempt to treat them with perturbation theory.' The ORBITAL count then varies by symmetry class, extending the base (3;3;0;0) sigma/sigma* set with whichever Rydberg orbitals and pi*-symmetry Si-H antibonding combinations are needed for the states of that symmetry. Molecular orbitals come from average CASSCF over all states of the given symmetry (7 states for 1Ag, 4 for 1Bu, 2 for 1Au, 3 for 1Bg); the four 1s core orbitals are frozen at the Hartree-Fock form and not correlated at second order. MS-CASPT2 builds an effective Hamiltonian whose diagonal elements are the CASPT2 energies and whose off-diagonal elements introduce coupling to second order in the dynamic correlation.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged over all states of each symmetry: 7 (1Ag), 4 (1Bu), 2 (1Au) and 3 (1Bg) with the Rydberg-augmented basis
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in eV with oscillator strengths and the expectation value of R-squared in atomic units (ground state <R2> = 127.3), at CASSCF / CASPT2 / MS-CASPT2. VALENCE states: 1(1Bu) 8.50 (f 1.098) / 6.90 (0.891) / 6.33 (1.115), <R2> 144.9; 2(1Ag) 6.94 / 7.12 / 6.55, <R2> 158.5; 1(1Au) 7.58 (0.003) / 6.86 (0.003) / 6.68 (0.005), <R2> 131.5; 3(1Ag) 6.46 / 6.76 / 6.87, <R2> 163.4; 2(1Bu) 8.81 (0.275) / 7.50 (0.234) / 6.96 (0.154), <R2> 180.1; 1(1Bg) 8.06 / 7.51 / 7.10, <R2> 137.7. RYDBERG states: 4(1Ag) HOMO to 4s 7.10 / 7.33 / 7.40, <R2> 263.1; 3(1Bu) HOMO to 4p 7.76 (0.051) / 7.09 (0.046) / 7.46 (0.006), <R2> 237.2; 2(1Au) 7.60 / 7.28 / 7.46, <R2> 242.4; 5(1Ag) HOMO to 3d 7.29 / 7.87 / 7.86, <R2> 326.1; 4(1Bu) HOMO to 4p 7.79 (0.279) / 7.13 (0.255) / 7.87 (0.029), <R2> 266.5; 2(1Bg) 7.78 / 7.74 / 7.93, <R2> 310.3; 6(1Ag) 7.61 / 7.70 / 7.99, <R2> 352.6; 3(1Bg) 7.84 / 7.84 / 8.10, <R2> 336.8; 7(1Ag) 7.76 / 8.09 / 8.22, <R2> 333.8. Six valence states lie below the lowest Rydberg state at MS-CASPT2; four resemble states found previously at lower levels, while 2(1Bu) and 3(1Ag) are new. All the states are one-electron promotions from the 13ag HOMO, which is bonding across each of the three Si-Si bonds with nodes at the two internal silicon atoms. The strongly allowed 1(1Bu) sigma-sigma* transition at 6.33 eV with f = 1.12 has its transition moment along the silicon backbone and matches the experimental matrix band at 6.14 eV; the 2(1Bu) transition at 6.96 eV with f = 0.15 has its moment along the central Si-Si bond and contributes to the intense band observed at 6.89 eV; the weakly allowed out-of-plane 1(1Au) at 6.68 eV lies at the red edge of the second band.
Other: This paper is a controlled demonstration that valence-Rydberg mixing is an ACTIVE-SPACE-LEVEL artefact that a single-reference perturbative correction cannot remove. Average CASSCF over the states of a symmetry class produces strongly mixed valence and Rydberg wave functions; single-state CASPT2 does not fix it; only MS-CASPT2, which couples the states through an effective Hamiltonian built to second order in the dynamic correlation, separates them cleanly. The evidence is in the numbers: the 4(1Bu) Rydberg state has an oscillator strength of 0.279 at CASSCF and 0.255 at CASPT2 but only 0.029 at MS-CASPT2, i.e. it was carrying nearly all its intensity by borrowing from the valence 1(1Bu), and the intensity returns to the valence state (1.098 to 1.115) once the states are decoupled. The <R2> column is the diagnostic that makes this checkable: valence states cluster at 132-180 a.u. against a ground-state 127.3, while Rydberg states run 237-353. The CASSCF errors are enormous and NON-UNIFORM — 1(1Bu) falls 2.17 eV from CASSCF to MS-CASPT2 while 3(1Ag) RISES 0.41 eV — so no scaling of the CASSCF spectrum could reproduce the final ordering, which differs from the CASSCF ordering entirely. A second, quieter lesson concerns the electron count. Fixing six active electrons on the three Si-Si bonds is a principled truncation borrowed from the Sandorfy C model, but the authors are candid that the twenty Si-H bonding electrons ought to be active too and are relegated to perturbation theory purely for cost. That the resulting valence energies match the matrix spectrum to about 0.2 eV suggests the relegation is tolerable here, but it is the identified weak point of the model rather than a defended choice.
reference_short: Crespo, Merchan & Michl, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 8593
notes: MS-CASPT2 oscillator strengths were computed from perturbation-modified CAS (PMCAS) reference functions, i.e. linear combinations of all CAS states in the multistate calculation, whereas CASSCF and CASPT2 oscillator strengths both used the CASSCF transition dipole moments with the respective energy differences. The character and ordering of states in Table 2 are those from MS-CASPT2. Values in parentheses in Table 2 were obtained with the valence-only Si[6s5p2d]/H[2s1p] basis. Strong valence-Rydberg interaction at the CASSCF level is noted as a well-known problem for ethene and butadiene. The bulk of the second observed matrix band is attributed to the gauche conformer rather than the anti conformer studied here.
correlation_correction: Single-state CASPT2 and the multistate extension MS-CASPT2; the 1s electrons were not correlated at second order

compound_name: CH2CH2O biradical from O(3P) + ethylene — singlet-triplet spin-orbit coupling at crossing geometries
geometry_source: Spin-orbit matrix elements evaluated at selected singlet-triplet crossing point geometries detected in sample trajectories from the direct-dynamics trajectory surface hopping simulation; the underlying potential energy surface was generated on the fly at unrestricted B3LYP/6-31G(d,p). Six different crossing point geometries were sampled.
method: Twelve-state state-averaged CASSCF used to generate orbitals for Breit-Pauli spin-orbit coupling matrix elements; the reaction dynamics themselves use quasiclassical trajectory surface hopping on UB3LYP/6-31G(d,p) surfaces
software: GAMESS, using the Breit-Pauli spin-orbit implementation of Fedorov and Gordon
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF; 6-31G(d,p) for the B3LYP dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight active orbitals. The individual orbitals are not itemized in the text.
active_space_protocol: A single (8,8) space used purely to generate orbitals for the spin-orbit coupling evaluation, with a TWELVE-STATE state average. The state list was chosen from the states actually involved in intersystem crossing: 'the states that are close in energy and thus are actively involved in ISC processes are the first 6 triplet states 1(3A) (Ms = 0, +/-1), 2(3A) (Ms = 0, +/-1), and the first 2 singlet states 1(1A) (Ms = 0), 2(1A) (Ms = 0)'. Because the singlet-triplet matrix elements are complex, the three components of each triplet were combined into symmetry-adapted triplet wave functions following Hoffmann and Schatz, making all elements real.
nroots_per_mult: 12 states in the average: the first 6 triplet states (two 3A states with Ms = 0 and +/-1) and the first 2 singlet states
electronic_structure_description: In the symmetry-adapted triplet representation the singlet-triplet spin-orbit matrix elements are all real and range from 0 to 70 cm-1. Close inspection of the coupling matrix shows the triplet wave functions can be further linearly combined so that the first singlet 1(1A) couples strongly to only three of the six triplets and the second singlet 2(1A) couples to the other three. An average spin-orbit coupling was defined by summing the squares of the twelve singlet-triplet coupling elements and dividing by six, the number of nonzero elements after this decoupling; calculations at six different crossing point geometries give an average SOC of about 35 cm-1. Rather than use that value directly, the dynamics were run with SOC values of 70, 50 and 30 cm-1 to test sensitivity, with 70 cm-1 producing excess singlet formation. For the CH2CH2O biradical the triplet and singlet relative energies are -30.4 and -33.7 kcal/mol on the B3LYP surface but -24.0 and -25.9 kcal/mol at the CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q level of an earlier study, i.e. B3LYP stationary points are lower by up to 8 kcal/mol, an especially prominent discrepancy for the saddle points and reaction intermediates on the triplet surface. The triplet and singlet curves lie very close over a wide range of C-O distances (1.3-1.7 A) in the biradical region, so there are numerous singlet-triplet surface crossings after the biradical forms and the overall ISC probability for a long-lived intermediate can be large even though each individual hop probability is small. Unlike the multireference CASPT2 curves of the earlier work, the barrier to O addition is barely visible on the B3LYP surface.
Other: The active space here is doing an unusual job: it is not used for energetics at all, only to supply orbitals of sufficient quality for a Breit-Pauli spin-orbit calculation, and the design constraint is therefore not correlation recovery but BALANCED description of all the states that participate in the crossing. Hence the twelve-state average over the six triplet components and two singlets rather than a state-specific calculation — with singlet and triplet manifolds nearly degenerate over C-O distances of 1.3 to 1.7 A, a state-specific (8,8) would describe one manifold better than the other and bias the very couplings being measured. The paper also demonstrates why this matters quantitatively: individual matrix elements span the full range 0 to 70 cm-1 depending on which pair of states is taken, and only after the triplets are linearly recombined does the structure become clear (each singlet couples to just three of the six triplets), giving a meaningful average of about 35 cm-1. Quoting any single element would have been arbitrary. The corresponding caution about the surfaces is that the B3LYP energetics used for the dynamics differ from the earlier CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q values by up to 8 kcal/mol in the biradical region and, more seriously, the B3LYP surface loses the O-addition barrier that the multireference CASPT2 curves show — the paper accepts this because 'the relative significance of the primary reaction pathways is largely preserved'.
reference_short: Hu, Lendvay, Maiti & Schatz, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 2093
notes: The main study is a quasiclassical trajectory surface hopping simulation of O(3P) + C2H4 with the potential generated on the fly at UB3LYP/6-31G(d,p); nonadiabatic transitions were only considered where the singlet surface intersects the triplet. The CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q and CASPT2 comparisons are taken from reference 16 of the paper and are not this work's own calculations. Two transition states exist for direct H abstraction, TS1a of 3A'' and TS1b of 3A' symmetry, within 5-6 kcal/mol at B3LYP. A single fixed SOC value was used throughout the trajectories, an approximation justified on the grounds that most T-S crossings occur near the CH2CH2O biradical where the SOC matrix elements vary little with geometry.
correlation_correction: None on the CASSCF used for the spin-orbit couplings; the cited CASSCF(8,8)+MR-CISD+Q energetics are from an earlier study

geometry_source: All stationary and transition structures of the ground and excited states of the M-1 model optimized at CAS(10,8)/6-31G(d), with harmonic vibrational frequencies computed to verify minima and transition states along the reaction path. Conical intersections optimized at the same level. Initial geometries of the (6-4) and Dewar photoproducts taken from the literature. For the aqueous work, a water solvent box was built within 8 A of M-1 using the xleap module of Amber and treated by the CASPT2//CASSCF/Amber QM/MM protocol.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with CASPT2 single points; CASPT2//CASSCF/Amber (QM/MM) for the aqueous surfaces; B3LYP and UB3LYP for the larger M-2 model
software: Gaussian and MOLCAS for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Tinker for the Amber MM subsystem; the QM/MM interface coded by Ferre and co-workers; VMD for the figures
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight molecular orbitals: six bonding and antibonding pi orbitals plus two sigma MOs of the pyrimidone ring. Only the pyrimidone ring, where the reaction coordinate lies, is included.
active_space_protocol: A single CAS(10,8) is used for every stationary point, transition state and conical intersection of the M-1 model, and its size is justified by the reaction coordinate rather than by the molecule: 'Because the main reaction coordinate lies on one ring of the 2 pyrimidines, 10 electrons and 8 molecular orbitals as the active space, labeled as CAS(10,8), was used.' Its composition is six bonding and antibonding pi orbitals plus two sigma MOs of the pyrimidone ring — the sigma pair being what allows the N3'-C6' bond cleavage to be described. So only ONE of the two pyrimidine rings is correlated; the other is left to the inactive space. Minima and transition states were verified by harmonic frequency calculations. CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries supply dynamic correlation. For the larger M-2 model, which adds the surrounding residues, the active space was abandoned entirely: 'because of the computational limitation, the B3LYP and UB3LYP were employed'. Solvation was handled two ways: a CASPT2//CASSCF/Amber QM/MM protocol with an explicit water box within 8 A of M-1, and an IEF-PCM continuum with dielectric constant 4 for M-2.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies at the CASPT2 level with respect to the S0 of T(6-4)T: the T1 state at 2.9 eV, the S1 n-pi* state (labelled S(n)) at 3.2 eV and the S2 pi-pi* state (labelled S(pi)) at 3.6 eV. In the T1 state the pyrimidone ring is noticeably expanded relative to S0 and the C6'-H bends out of the ring plane. The S1 state has a considerably lengthened C2'=O bond at 1.345 A, giving it n-pi* character; the S2 pi-pi* excitation is mainly localized in the pyrimidone ring. A ground-state transition structure S0-TS for N3'-C6' bond cleavage lies at a barrier of 3.7 eV. Two conical intersections were located, S0/T1 and S0/S2, similar in structure but different in energy: in both the pyrimidine ring resembles the ground state while the pyrimidone ring is strongly deformed, with C4'-C3' lengthening from 1.272 A in the ground state to about 1.414 A and N3'-C6' contracting to about 2.535 A, producing out-of-plane deformation of the pyrimidone. The S0/T1 conical intersection lies at 3.1 eV. Upon UV excitation at 313-280 nm the lesion is first promoted to the pi-pi* S(pi) state, then reaches the S0/S(pi) conical intersection which lies only 0.2 eV above the S0-TS, leading to the Dewar photoproduct. In aqueous solution the barrier for N3'-C6' cleavage on the S(n) surface falls from 1 eV in the gas phase to 0.6 eV.
Other: The most useful geometric result from this space is the conical-intersection structure: N3'-C6' at about 2.535 A, effectively a broken bond, held in a space that contains exactly two sigma MOs for that bond. That the (10,8) can follow the coordinate all the way from 1.49 A to 2.54 A confirms the sigma pair was the right addition to the six pi orbitals. The 0.2 eV margin between the S0/S(pi) conical intersection and the ground-state transition structure is the paper's central mechanistic number and is small enough to be within the uncertainty of a CASPT2 correction on a single-ring space, so the qualitative conclusion (the intersection is accessible) is safer than the number.  The active-space decision here is an asymmetric one that is easy to miss: the (10,8) covers ONE pyrimidine ring only, chosen because the reaction coordinate lies there, so the second ring of this bipyrimidine lesion is described at the closed-shell level throughout. That is defensible for the N3'-C6' bond cleavage but means any state with amplitude on the other ring cannot be represented — and the paper does assign the S1 of the Dewar photoproduct as an n-pi* 'localized in the pyrimidine ring', i.e. on the ring that is largely outside the active space. The inclusion of two sigma MOs alongside the six pi orbitals is the essential piece: a pi-only space could not describe the sigma bond that breaks, and this is the same fixed-size, mixed sigma/pi construction that recurs in ring-opening photochemistry. The paper also illustrates the limit of what an active space can be scaled to. The M-1 model gets CASSCF/CASPT2; the M-2 model with surrounding residues gets B3LYP/UB3LYP because the space could not be afforded, so the two models cannot be compared at a common level of theory — and their barriers do differ, 1.2 eV for neutral M-2 against roughly 1.4 eV for M-1 in the ground state, with the radical anion barriers at 0.7 and 0.8 eV respectively. active_space_protocol: A single CAS(10,8) is used for every stationary point, transition state and conical intersection of the M-1 model, and its size is justified by the reaction coordinate rather than by the molecule: 'Because the main reaction coordinate lies on one ring of the 2 pyrimidines, 10 electrons and 8 molecular orbitals as the active space, labeled as CAS(10,8), was used.' So only ONE of the two pyrimidine rings is correlated; the other is left to the inactive space. Minima and transition states were verified by harmonic frequency calculations. CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries supply dynamic correlation. active_space_orbital_description: Active spaces are built by a fixed RULE rather than a fixed size: all 3d Fe-based molecular orbitals, all O2-originating valence orbitals, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the substrate C-H bond, and all valence orbitals of the water molecule where one is present. Applying this rule to the nine reaction pathways gives spaces from (26e,20o) to (35e,26o): (26e,20o) for pathways 1 and 4, (26e,22o) for pathway 2, (34e,26o) for pathway 3, (26e,21o) for pathway 5, (27e,20o) for pathways 6 and 8, (27e,21o) for pathway 7 and (35e,26o) for pathway 9. The entry lists the (26e,22o) of pathway 2, the mechanistically favoured route.
active_space_protocol: The DMRG replaces the CAS-CI step and lifts the conventional ceiling: the paper notes that costs scale exponentially with active space size in conventional CASSCF/CASPT2, 'which makes the conventional calculations prohibitively expensive for an active space larger than approximately 15 electrons in 15 orbitals (15e,15o)', whereas DMRG permits CAS(100e,100o) or larger in favourable cases. Active orbitals were localized with the Pipek-Mezey scheme and ORDERED according to spatial localization, following the fragment sequence FeA (with the O-H group in water-assisted pathways), FeB, the (H)O-O moiety, and the C10-H sigma and sigma* orbitals; for the remaining transition states and all products the ordering is FeA, (H)O on FeA, FeB, (H)O or H2O on FeB (and O-H), then H-C10 or C10. Orbital optimizations used M = 256 spin-adapted renormalized basis functions, with final wave functions from a CAS-CI solved at M = 512. Pathway 2 (1,1-mu hydroperoxo diferric, CAS(26e,22o)): TS2 86.6 then 54.9; P2 35.1 then 3.4; the alternative 'hydroxylated' TS2 lies well above 90 and the hydroxylated product P2 at -273.8 then -254.6. Pathway 3 (water-assisted, CAS(34e,26o)): TS3 286.6 then 150.3; P3 123.7 then 9.4. Pathway 4 (CAS(26e,20o)): TS4 126.0 then 118.1; P4 109.5 then 14.3. Pathway 5 (1,2-mu hydroperoxo, CAS(26e,21o)): TS5 103.9 then 41.9; P5 285.9 then 154.7. Pathway 6 (1e-reduced superoxo, CAS(27e,20o)): TS6 161.8 then 40.3; P6 139.6 then 0.4. Pathway 7 (mixed-valence hydroperoxo, CAS(27e,21o)): TS7 31.4 then 64.9; P7 -25.5 then -78.6. Pathway 8 (CAS(27e,20o)): TS8 -3.7 then -6.0, a negative barrier indicating no barrier at all; P8 -42.4 then -63.9. Pathway 9 (CAS(35e,26o)): TS9 226.9 then 86.9; P9 131.1 then -67.7. In P2 the resulting FeA(IV)=O unit is favourably oriented toward C9-H with an O to H(C9) distance of 2.88 A, allowing a second hydrogen abstraction. Pathway 1 has an in vacuo barrier of 90 kJ/mol or more, rising above 115 kJ/mol with QM/MM corrections, well above experiment.
Other: The point of this paper is that the active space required for a binuclear non-heme iron site is simply larger than conventional CASSCF can reach, and DMRG is what makes it accessible: the conventional ceiling is put at about (15e,15o) while these calculations run from (26e,20o) to (35e,26o). Crucially the space is defined by a CHEMICAL RULE applied uniformly — all Fe 3d orbitals, all O2-derived valence orbitals, the substrate C-H sigma/sigma*, and all water valence orbitals when a water is present — so the nine competing pathways are compared on a consistent footing even though their spaces differ in size. method: CASSCF with subsequent relocalization of the valence molecular orbitals into atomic-like orbitals for a valence-bond type analysis
basis_set: ANO-RCC atomic natural orbitals with contractions [7s6p5d3f2g1h] for Fe, [3s2p1d] for C, [4s3p1d] for N, [4s3p1d] for O, [3s3p1d] for S and [1s] for H
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in twelve orbitals: the five mainly Fe 3d orbitals, five virtual orbitals of the same symmetry forming the 3d' double shell, and two occupied eg-like orbitals of mainly ligand character.
active_space_protocol: A single CAS[10,12] is used for every complex, and its composition is the standard spin-crossover recipe stated explicitly: '(i) the mainly Fe 3d character orbitals extended with a set of virtual orbitals of the same symmetry (so-called 3d' orbitals) and (ii) two occupied eg-like symmetry orbitals with mainly ligand character. Thus, a CAS[10,12] including 10 electrons in 12 active orbitals is used in the calculations.' That is the five 3d orbitals plus a full DOUBLE SHELL of five 3d' correlating orbitals, plus two ligand-based eg-like orbitals that carry the sigma donation. Calculations are performed on the ISOLATED BASIC UNIT of each compound taken from the experimental low-spin and high-spin X-ray structures, not on optimized geometries. After convergence the valence MOs are RELOCALIZED into atomic-like orbitals to expose the charge-transfer contributions in the wave function expansion; this transformation leaves any observable expectation value unchanged and affords a valence-bond type analysis from which configuration amplitudes and atomic charges are derived. The paper stresses that finely balanced basis sets are necessary to describe spin-crossover energetics correctly.

ground_state_mult: 1 in the low-spin phase, 5 in the high-spin phase
electronic_structure_description: Spin crossover between a low-spin S = 0 and a high-spin S = 2 state, with 2RT(1/2) = 425 K and an experimental thermal hysteresis width of 40 K. Relocalized-CASSCF atomic charges (atomic units): in the low-spin state Q(Fe) = 1.45, Q(N) = -0.36 for the thiocyanate nitrogen and Q(N') = -0.18 for the pm-pea nitrogens; in the high-spin state Q(Fe) = 1.92, Q(N) = -0.48 and Q(N') = -0.24. The thiocyanate nitrogen carries roughly twice the negative charge of the pm-pea nitrogens. Average on-site potential differences between iron and nitrogen positions are 6.32e-5 au in the low-spin phase and -2.14e-3 au in the high-spin phase, the latter corresponding to about -700 K and large enough to polarize the Fe-N bonds. The van der Waals contribution to the intermolecular cooperative parameter, obtained from pi-stacking energies as 2E(LS,HS) - E(LS,LS) - E(HS,HS), is about 115 K, giving a cooperativity factor of only 0.27 — incompatible with the observed 40 K hysteresis. Adding the polarization term Gamma(pol) = 329 K gives a total Gamma = 444 K and a cooperativity factor of 0.78, consistent with hysteretic behaviour; the polarization contribution accounts for about 74% of the total (Gamma(pol)/Gamma about 0.74).
Other: Compound 1 is where the whole argument is calibrated, and the decisive number comes straight out of the active space: the iron charge rises from 1.45 to 1.92 on going low spin to high spin. That 0.47 e redistribution is only meaningful because the CAS[10,12] contains both the 3d' double shell (balancing radial correlation between the two spin states) and the two ligand eg-like orbitals (letting sigma donation vary), so the charge is a physical result rather than a partition artefact. The consequence is stark: the van der Waals treatment alone gives a cooperativity factor of 0.27, which cannot produce the observed 40 K hysteresis, while including the polarization derived from these charges raises it to 0.78. In other words, the entire explanation of the memory effect rests on a charge difference extracted from a twelve-orbital wave function.  The active space here is the canonical spin-crossover construction and the paper uses it for an unusual purpose: not to compute a spin-state energy gap but to extract ATOMIC CHARGES for a Madelung-field model of crystal cooperativity. Two features of the CAS[10,12] make that possible. The double shell of 3d' correlating orbitals is what keeps the high-spin and low-spin states balanced — without it the differential radial correlation between a t2g(6) and a t2g(4)eg(2) configuration is not recovered and any derived charge difference would be biased toward one state. The two ligand-based eg-like orbitals are what let sigma donation appear explicitly in the wave function, so that the metal charge is a computed quantity rather than an artefact of the orbital partition. The relocalization step is the second essential piece: because it is a unitary transformation it changes no observable, yet it converts the delocalized CASSCF orbitals into atomic-like ones from which valence-bond configuration weights and charges can be read directly. The resulting charge redistribution is large — on iron, 1.45 in the low-spin state against 1.92 in the high-spin state for compound 1, a change of 0.47 e — and it is precisely this difference that drives the polarization term. The methodological caution for reuse is that these are single-point calculations on experimental X-ray geometries of the isolated molecular unit, so the charges carry whatever the crystal structure determination carried, and the Madelung analysis then reintroduces the environment as fixed point charges rather than self-consistently.

compound_name: Dioxirane (1) — low-lying electronic states and ring opening
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at the MRD-CI/BS1 level by a numerical Newton-Raphson procedure, except the ring-opening transition structure TS1 which was optimized at CASSCF(6,4)/BS1. Harmonic frequencies obtained by diagonalizing the analytically computed mass-weighted Cartesian force constant matrix with BS1; zero-point energies from frequencies scaled by 0.8929. Vertical excitation energies computed at MRD-CI+Q/BS2 at the MRD-CI/BS1 ground-state geometry; adiabatic energies from MRD-CI+Q/BS2 at MRD-CI/BS1 optimized geometries of each state.
method: CASSCF(6,4) for the transition-structure geometry and harmonic frequencies, with multireference single- and double-excitation configuration interaction including a Davidson correction (MRD-CI+Q) for all energies
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; Gaussian 94 for the harmonic frequency calculations
basis_set: Two basis sets denoted BS1 and BS2; BS2 is the more flexible and gives results reasonably close to experiment, while BS1 deviates by about 0.3 eV. MRD-CI selection thresholds were 2 microhartree (BS1) and 3 microhartree (BS2), generating CI spaces of roughly 6e5 to 22e6 configurations.
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons distributed in the 6a1, 2b1, 1a2 and 4b2 molecular orbitals: the O-O sigma bond (6a1), the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of the out-of-plane oxygen nonbonding p orbitals (2b1 and 1a2), and the O-O sigma* orbital (4b2, the SCF LUMO).
active_space_protocol: The CASSCF space is deliberately MINIMAL and defined by naming the four orbitals: 'The CASSCF wave function of each electronic state was obtained by distributing six electrons in the 6a1, 2b1, 1a2, and 4b2 MOs', which the authors describe as 'the smallest active space that can describe the low-lying electronic states of each symmetry and multiplicity'. In the dioxirane ground-state description the 5a1 and 3b2 orbitals are the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of the two C-O sigma bonds, 6a1 is the O-O sigma bond, 2b1 and 1a2 are the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of the out-of-plane oxygen lone pairs (the pi manifold), and 4b2 is the O-O sigma* orbital, the SCF LUMO. So the (6,4) contains the O-O sigma/sigma* pair plus the two oxygen pi orbitals — exactly what is needed for ring opening at the O-O bond and for the pi-to-sigma* excitations, and nothing more. The CASSCF is used only for geometry optimization of the transition structure TS1 and for harmonic frequencies (scaled by 0.8929); all energies come from separate multireference single- and double-excitation configuration interaction (MRD-CI) calculations with a Davidson correction, whose CI spaces ranged from about 6e5 to 22e6 configurations with selection thresholds of 2 microhartree (BS1) and 3 microhartree (BS2).
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is a closed-shell singlet with four pi electrons, 1(1A1), of C2v symmetry, with the configuration having 5a1, 6a1, 3b2, 2b1 and 1a2 doubly occupied and 4b2 empty; it is 87.80% single-configurational in the MRD-CI/BS1 expansion. Vertical excitation energies at MRD-CI+Q/BS2 in eV, with dipole moments in debye and oscillator strengths: 1(3B1)(3pi) 3.07, 2.55 D; 1(1B1)(3pi) 4.23, 2.57 D, f = 0.0005; 1(3A2)(3pi) 5.72, 3.30 D; 1(1A2)(3pi) 6.14, 3.38 D, forbidden; 1(3B2)(4pi) 6.39, 2.90 D; 2(1A1)(2pi) 8.44, 2.54 D, f = 0.005; 2(3B2)(2pi) 9.91, 2.73 D; 1(1B2)(4pi) 9.97, 2.23 D, f = 0.1; 2(3B1)(3pi) 11.81; 2(3A2)(3pi) 11.95; 2(1B1)(3pi) 12.42, f = 0.00001; 2(1A2)(3pi) 13.11, forbidden. The first four excited states are the B1 and A2 triplet and singlet pairs dominated by the singly excited configurations 1a2 to 4b2 and 2b1 to 4b2. The 1(1B1)(3pi) vertical excitation of 4.23 eV agrees with an earlier CASPT2 value of 4.1 eV. The singlet-triplet splitting for the B2(4pi) pair is 3.58 eV, far larger than the 1.16 and 0.42 eV found for the B1(3pi) and A2(3pi) pairs, which the authors rationalize by the larger exchange integral for the 6a1-4b2 orbital pair than for 1a2-4b2 or 2b1-4b2. The remaining excited states between 8.44 and 13.11 eV all arise from double excitations relative to the ground-state configuration. The ring-opening barrier to dioxymethane is 22.6 kcal/mol at the MRD-CI/BS2 level, against earlier values of 15.2 and 25.8 kcal/mol; with zero-point correction it becomes 21.4 kcal/mol. Along the O-C-O angle the 1(1A1) and 2(1A1) potential curves do not cross at the MRD-CI level, in contrast to earlier work at other levels including CASPT2 which predicted a crossing at O-C-O angles of 102 and 100 degrees; instead the character of the two wave functions reverses abruptly, the ground state changing from the 4-pi-electron configuration to a 2-pi-electron one. At the CASSCF(6,4)-optimized transition structure TS1 the 1A1(4pi) state lies only 0.1 kcal/mol above the 1A1(2pi) state. The electronic spectrum of dioxirane is not known experimentally, although dimethyl- and bis(trifluoromethyl)dioxirane absorb at 335 nm in solution.

At the transition structure the two states are 0.1 kcal/mol apart — well inside the uncertainty of either method — so which picture is right cannot be settled from these energies. The practical lesson is that the (6,4) space contains both configurations by construction (it holds the O-O sigma, both oxygen pi combinations and the sigma*), so the disagreement is not about what the space can represent but about how the correlation on top of it is balanced. Note also that the ground state's 87.8% leading weight makes it look single-reference, while six of the twelve excited states are dominated by DOUBLE excitations from that configuration — the ratio a small space handles worst. The (6,4) supplies the transition-structure geometry and the frequencies, while every reported excitation energy, barrier and dissociation energy comes from MRD-CI+Q with a much larger CI expansion. The reason is visible in Table 4: the ground state is 87.8% one configuration, but the excited states carry substantial weight in doubly excited configurations, and six of the twelve reported excited states 'arise from double excitations relative to the dominant configuration of the ground state'. A four-orbital space can generate those doubles but cannot balance their dynamic correlation against the ground state's. The crossing behaviour is the sharpest illustration: along the O-C-O angle the MRD-CI wave functions of 1(1A1) and 2(1A1) exchange character abruptly, the ground state switching from a 4-pi-electron to a 2-pi-electron description, and at the CASSCF(6,4)-optimized transition structure the two states lie only 0.1 kcal/mol apart. Earlier CASPT2 work placed this crossing at an O-C-O angle of 100-102 degrees, and the present MRD-CI treatment finds the states avoid crossing throughout — a qualitative disagreement between two multireference treatments on the same small orbital set.

compound_name: Uracil (U) — S1/S0 conical intersection and excited-state decay
geometry_source: S1/S0 conical intersections located at CASSCF(8/8)/6-31G(d) using the method of Bearpark et al. Ground- and excited-state minima optimized with PCM/TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) in aqueous solution, with all frequencies verified positive — analytical second derivatives for S0 and numerical differentiation of analytic gradients for S1. Two-dimensional S1 surfaces built at PCM/TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) between the S1 minimum and the conical intersection.
method: CASSCF for conical intersection optimization; PCM/TD-DFT with the PBE0 hybrid functional for excited-state energetics and surfaces in aqueous solution
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals: six pi molecular orbitals plus the two oxygen lone-pair (nO) valence orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A CASSCF(8/8) space is used solely to LOCATE the S1/S0 conical intersection, not for any energetics. Its composition is stated: 'including 6 pi molecular orbital and the two nO valence orbitals'. The size was chosen by benchmarking against a larger published space rather than by a threshold: 'The geometry of the CI is very similar to that obtained for uracil at the CASSCF(12/9) level, including all the 8 pi orbitals and 1 nO valence orbital. This latter structure has been shown to be reliable by single-point CASSCF calculation with larger expansion, suggesting that our approach should be fully adequate to the purposes of the present paper.' The intersection was optimized by the method of Bearpark et al. All subsequent energetics — the two-dimensional S1 surfaces connecting the S1 minimum to the conical intersection — were computed at PCM/TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) in aqueous solution, not with the active space. The two surface coordinates are the out-of-plane motion of the C5 substituent (an improper dihedral) and a collective coordinate defined by linear interpolation of all remaining internal coordinates between the S1 minimum and the conical intersection.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, at the conical intersection)
electronic_structure_description: The S1/S0 conical intersection is reached by pyramidalization at C5 together with out-of-plane motion of the H5 hydrogen, bringing the C5 substituent into a pseudo-perpendicular arrangement with respect to the molecular plane. Near the intersection the S0 and S1 surfaces lie within 0.2 eV (1.6e3 cm-1) of each other in both gas phase and aqueous solution. The S1 surface connecting the S1 minimum to the conical intersection is flat, with a barrier of only about 0.1 eV (8e2 cm-1), consistent with the very short measured fluorescence lifetime. The excited-state geometry in aqueous solution is a nonplanar boat-like structure with altered C4-C5 and C5-C6 bond lengths, consistent with a Stokes shift of about 1 eV (8e3 cm-1). The measured mean fluorescence decay time is 96 +/- 3 fs, with a Strickler-Berg radiative lifetime of 7.01 ns. The relevant transition throughout is pi/pi*, which is always the S1 state, with an anisotropy close to 0.4.
Other: Uracil is the reference against which the (8/8) space was validated: its intersection geometry from six pi plus two nO orbitals matches the published CASSCF(12/9) result built from eight pi plus one nO, and that agreement is the paper's entire justification for the smaller space. Because the two spaces differ in WHICH orbitals they keep rather than merely in size, the match is evidence that the intersection structure is governed by the carbonyl lone-pair to pi* interaction and the C5 pyramidalization, not by the outer reaches of the pi manifold. Uracil also has the flattest surface of the three studied — a 0.1 eV barrier — so it is the case where the accuracy of the intersection geometry matters least for the mechanism and most for the lifetime ordering.  The active space here is deployed for GEOMETRY ONLY, and the paper is explicit that this is a deliberate division of labour: CASSCF(8/8) locates the conical intersection, then PCM/TD-PBE0 maps the surface between it and the S1 minimum, because the study needs solvation and a wide region of the surface rather than a high-accuracy point energy. The space was validated by comparison rather than by convergence testing — its intersection geometry matches one obtained at CASSCF(12/9) with all eight pi orbitals and one nO, which had itself been checked against a larger expansion. That is a defensible economy for a structure, and the paper says so, but it means no energy in this study rests on the multiconfigurational treatment. The choice of which orbitals to drop is the interesting part: the (8/8) keeps SIX pi orbitals and TWO oxygen lone pairs, while the reference (12/9) keeps EIGHT pi and ONE lone pair. The two spaces trade two pi orbitals for one nO and still give the same intersection geometry, which suggests the intersection structure is controlled by the nO/pi* balance rather than by the full pi manifold. There is also a documented CASSCF failure worth recording: in the gas phase, CASSCF calculations 'fail to locate a true minimum on the pi/pi* surface' — the planar minimum exists only under a Cs constraint and becomes a saddle point when planarity is relaxed, with out-of-plane motion leading to a conical intersection with the more stable n/pi* state. Preliminary gas-phase TD-DFT gives the same picture, with the n/pi* state always below the pi/pi*. The pi/pi* minimum these compounds fluoresce from is therefore a solution-phase feature that neither method finds in vacuum.

active_space_protocol: A CASSCF(8/8) space is used solely to LOCATE the S1/S0 conical intersection, not for any energetics. Its composition is stated: 'including 6 pi molecular orbital and the two nO valence orbitals'. The size was chosen by benchmarking against a larger published space rather than by a threshold: 'The geometry of the CI is very similar to that obtained for uracil at the CASSCF(12/9) level, including all the 8 pi orbitals and 1 nO valence orbital. This latter structure has been shown to be reliable by single-point CASSCF calculation with larger expansion, suggesting that our approach should be fully adequate to the purposes of the present paper.' The intersection was optimized by the method of Bearpark et al. All subsequent energetics — the two-dimensional S1 surfaces connecting the S1 minimum to the conical intersection — were computed at PCM/TD-PBE0/6-31G(d) in aqueous solution, not with the active space. The two surface coordinates are the out-of-plane motion of the C5 substituent (an improper dihedral) and a collective coordinate defined by linear interpolation of all remaining internal coordinates between the S1 minimum and the conical intersection.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, at the conical intersection)
electronic_structure_description: The S1/S0 conical intersection is reached by the same motions as in uracil — pyramidalization at C5 and out-of-plane displacement of the C5 substituent, here a methyl group, toward a pseudo-perpendicular arrangement. The barrier separating the S1 minimum from the conical intersection is estimated at about 0.2 eV (1.6e3 cm-1), roughly twice that of uracil, so the out-of-plane motion is more difficult. Measured fluorescence decay: a fast component of 195 +/- 17 fs with amplitude 0.56 +/- 0.02 and a slow component of 633 +/- 18 fs, giving a mean decay time of 388 +/- 13 fs; the Strickler-Berg radiative lifetime is 7.72 ns and the derived fluorescence lifetime 0.78 ps. Only 5-substituted compounds show this more complex biexponential behaviour; the experimental lifetime ordering across the series is U < TFT < 5ClU < T, 1MT < 5F1,3DMU < 5FU.
Other: Thymine is the middle point of the three-compound CASSCF set and the one that establishes the trend: identical (8/8) space, identical intersection topology, but a barrier roughly double that of uracil and a mean lifetime four times longer. Since the space composition is unchanged and only the C5 substituent differs, the substituent effect on the barrier is measured against a fixed methodological background — the same control logic that makes a rule-based space valuable in a substituent series. Note the division of labour though: the barrier itself comes from PCM/TD-PBE0 surfaces, and only the intersection endpoint comes from the active space, so the 0.2 eV value inherits the functional's errors rather than the CASSCF's.  The active space here is deployed for GEOMETRY ONLY, and the paper is explicit that this is a deliberate division of labour: CASSCF(8/8) locates the conical intersection, then PCM/TD-PBE0 maps the surface between it and the S1 minimum, because the study needs solvation and a wide region of the surface rather than a high-accuracy point energy. The space was validated by comparison rather than by convergence testing — its intersection geometry matches one obtained at CASSCF(12/9) with all eight pi orbitals and one nO, which had itself been checked against a larger expansion. That is a defensible economy for a structure, and the paper says so, but it means no energy in this study rests on the multiconfigurational treatment. The choice of which orbitals to drop is the interesting part: the (8/8) keeps SIX pi orbitals and TWO oxygen lone pairs, while the reference (12/9) keeps EIGHT pi and ONE lone pair. The two spaces trade two pi orbitals for one nO and still give the same intersection geometry, which suggests the intersection structure is controlled by the nO/pi* balance rather than by the full pi manifold. There is also a documented CASSCF failure worth recording: in the gas phase, CASSCF calculations 'fail to locate a true minimum on the pi/pi* surface' — the planar minimum exists only under a Cs constraint and becomes a saddle point when planarity is relaxed, with out-of-plane motion leading to a conical intersection with the more stable n/pi* state. Preliminary gas-phase TD-DFT gives the same picture, with the n/pi* state always below the pi/pi*. The pi/pi* minimum these compounds fluoresce from is therefore a solution-phase feature that neither method finds in vacuum.
reference_short: Gustavsson, Banyasz, Lazzarotto, Markovitsi, Scalmani, Frisch, Barone & Improta, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2006, 128, 607
notes: Thymine is 5-methyluracil. The dependence of the excited-state lifetime on the C5 position is explained by the weight of that atom in the HOMO; involvement of the n/pi* state would instead require pyramidalization of a carbonyl carbon and would be less sensitive to the C5 substituent.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF; dynamical correlation and solvent were introduced separately through PCM/TD-PBE0

compound_name: 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) — S1/S0 conical intersection and excited-state decay
geometry_source: S1/S0 conical intersections located at CASSCF(8/8)/6-31G(d) using the method of Bearpark et al. method: CASSCF for conical intersection optimization; PCM/TD-DFT with the PBE0 hybrid functional for excited-state energetics and surfaces in aqueous solution
