compound_name: Phenol blue (PB) — ultrafast photochemical reaction dynamics
geometry_source: S0 minimum optimized at SA2-CASSCF(2,2) and, for comparison, at MP2 and B3LYP. The S1/S0 conical intersection was optimized at SA2-CASSCF(2,2) and characterized by the topography in its branching plane. Minimum energy paths were computed on the S1 surface from the Franck-Condon point and on the S0 surface from the conical intersection minimum. Because no experimental structure of phenol blue exists, an indoaniline-derived calix[4]arene containing the phenol blue skeleton (Cambridge Structural Database refcode TEYGOT), whose X-ray structure is known, was computed at HF, MP2 and B3LYP as a structural benchmark.
method: State-averaged CASSCF over two states, with multistate multireference second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MS-CASPT2) on that reference; trajectory surface hopping nonadiabatic molecular dynamics driven by ab initio CASSCF energies, gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors; TD-DFT(B3LYP) and SAC-CI for comparison
basis_set: 6-31G*, with a 6-31G(d on N/O) variant giving no significant differences in vertical excitation energies or oscillator strengths
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals: the HOMO, which is clearly localized on the aniline ring, and the LUMO, localized on the quinoneimine ring. The HOMO-to-LUMO excitation is therefore an electron transfer from the aniline to the quinoneimine ring.
active_space_protocol: A minimal two-electron, two-orbital space averaged over two states (S0 and S1) with equal weights, denoted SA2-CASSCF(2,2), is used for EVERY calculation in the study — the ground-state minimum, the conical intersection optimization, the minimum energy paths, and the trajectory surface hopping dynamics. The choice is dictated by the dynamics: nonadiabatic trajectories require energies, gradients AND nonadiabatic coupling vectors on the fly, which restricts the affordable space. Its accuracy was checked separately rather than assumed: MP2 and B3LYP were used for the S0 geometry, and MS-CAS(2,2)PT2, TD-DFT(B3LYP) and SAC-CI for the vertical excitation energies and dipole moments. The equal-weight two-state average is what makes the S0 and S1 surfaces balanced enough for the conical intersection and the surface hops.
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, equal weights)
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies from S0 in vacuum, in eV with oscillator strengths in parentheses, at the 6-31G* level. S1, of pi(HOMO) to pi*(LUMO) character: SA2-CASSCF(2,2) 3.38 (f 0.89); MS-CAS(2,2)PT2 2.15 (0.57); TD-DFT(B3LYP) 2.33 (0.39); SAC-CI(level2) 2.27 (0.34); experimental absorption maximum 2.16 eV in benzene and 2.25 eV in cyclohexane. The bare SA2-CASSCF(2,2) value is more than 1 eV above experiment. TD-DFT and SAC-CI assign S1, S2 and S3 as pi(HOMO) to pi*(LUMO), n(O) to pi*(LUMO) and n(N) to pi*(LUMO) respectively, with transitions to S1 and S3 allowed and that to S2 almost forbidden. Averaged permanent dipole moments: MS-CAS(2,2)PT2 and TD-DFT(B3LYP) values are about 1.0 D LARGER for S0 and 2.0-3.0 D SMALLER for the S1 Franck-Condon state than the SA2-CASSCF(2,2) values, meaning dynamical correlation mixes the quinonoid (Q) character of S0 with the zwitterionic (Z-like) character of S1 and vice versa. The experimental S0 dipole moment in benzene is 5.8 D, about 2 D below the MS-CASPT2 and B3LYP values, with the caveat that B3LYP may overestimate charge-transfer dipole moments through self-interaction error. The ground state has two equivalent mirror-image minima distinguished by the sign of the C5-N8-C9-C10 dihedral. The S1/S0 conical intersection minimum is a branching point, as established by computing minimum energy paths away from it. Trajectory surface hopping from the S1 Franck-Condon point gives nonadiabatic transitions to the ground state mostly at 110-120 fs, reaching the vicinity of the S0 minimum at 200-300 fs, in good agreement with the fast ground-state recovery component seen by pump-probe spectroscopy in solvents. After decay the trajectories show a coherent bending vibration between the quinoneimine and aniline rings at 43 cm-1, matching a low-frequency coherently excited mode observed experimentally.
Other: This paper is an unusually clear case of a minimal active space being wrong about energies and right about dynamics, with the authors quantifying both. The bare SA2-CASSCF(2,2) vertical excitation energy is 3.38 eV against an experimental 2.16-2.25 eV — an error exceeding 1 eV — and MS-CAS(2,2)PT2 on the SAME two orbitals brings it to 2.15 eV, essentially exact. So the (2,2) contains the right two orbitals; what it lacks is dynamical correlation, and adding it perturbatively suffices. The dipole moments show the physical content of that correction precisely: correlation raises the S0 dipole by about 1 D and lowers the S1 dipole by 2-3 D, i.e. it mixes quinonoid character into the zwitterionic excited state and vice versa, which a two-configuration wave function cannot do on its own. The consequence for reuse is sharp — the excited-state charge separation is OVERESTIMATED at bare CASSCF, and since the trajectory surface hopping dynamics run on uncorrected SA2-CASSCF(2,2) surfaces, the simulated trajectories evolve on a surface whose excited state is too ionic and too high by over 1 eV. That the resulting 110-120 fs hopping times and the 43 cm-1 coherent bending mode nonetheless match experiment suggests the TOPOGRAPHY around the conical intersection is captured even where the energetics are not, which is the usual justification for minimal-space dynamics and here is supported by direct comparison rather than assumed.
reference_short: Kobayashi, Shiga, Murakami & Nakamura, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2007, 129, 6405
notes: Phenol blue consists of an electron-donor dimethylaniline moiety linked to a quinoneimine acceptor. The Q (quinonoid) and Z (zwitterionic) resonance structures are the two limiting descriptions of its ground state. Cis and trans forms are defined by the C4-C5-N8-C9 dihedral and R/L forms by the C5-N8-C9-C10 dihedral; because C4 and C6 are equivalent in reality, the cis and trans labels are a bookkeeping convenience. No experimental structure of phenol blue itself is available. Pump-probe measurements in solvents report fast and slow decay components, with reported fast time constants of about 200 fs and of 30 fs in two separate studies.
correlation_correction: Multistate multireference second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MS-CAS(2,2)PT2) on the SA2-CASSCF(2,2) reference, applied to vertical excitation energies and dipole moments only — not to the dynamics

compound_name: Manganese trifluoride, MnF3 — Jahn-Teller distorted free molecule
point_group: C2v (planar) for both low-lying quintet states; no stationary point of C3v symmetry could be located, and the D3h reference geometry is Jahn-Teller unstable
geometry_source: Many different geometrical arrangements of both triplet and quintet MnF3 were surveyed with CASSCF; gradient methods located stationary points on the quintet surface. Larger-space CASSCF and CASPT2 single points were then computed at those geometries. Vibrational frequencies and force fields for the two low-lying quintet states were computed with SCF and DFT (unrestricted, giving analytic second derivatives) rather than CASSCF, since the CAS calculations showed both states are dominated by a single configuration. Gas-phase electron diffraction patterns of a commercial MnF3 sample were recorded for comparison.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 for the electronic structure survey; SCF, MP2 and DFT (B3LYP, BLYP, BP86) for geometries and vibrational frequencies; gas-phase electron diffraction
software: MOLCAS 3 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 92-DFT for the SCF, MP2 and DFT calculations
basis_set: For the CASSCF work, pseudopotentials on both Mn and F with seven valence electrons treated explicitly for fluorine and fifteen for neutral manganese (so the 3s and 3p orbitals are in the valence region); Gaussian bases of double-zeta quality for F (4s,5p contracted to 2s,3p) augmented with diffuse p functions, and approximately triple-zeta for Mn (8s,7p,6d,1f contracted to 6s,5p,3d,1f) with f polarization. For the frequency work, all-electron bases: F as a triple-zeta contraction of Huzinaga's 10s,6p with diffuse s and p (exponents 0.10 and 0.07) and a d polarization function (0.8), giving [5+1s,3+1p,1d]; Mn s and p from Wachters' 14s,9p contracted to 8s,6p with an added diffuse p (0.15), a (6/3) triple-zeta d set, and an f polarization function (0.6), with spherical harmonic d and f functions.
relativistic_treatment: Pseudopotentials on Mn and F in the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: The initial survey correlated 6 electrons in 8 orbitals, giving 108 configuration state functions; the refined calculations used 8 electrons in 10 orbitals, giving 2000 configuration state functions. Orbital selection was based on the populations of the natural orbitals obtained from an MCPF calculation.
active_space_protocol: A two-stage protocol with the space chosen from natural orbital populations rather than assumed: 'In the initial phase we correlated 6 electrons in 8 orbitals, to give 108 CSF. The selection criteria were based upon the populations of the natural orbitals obtained from an MCPF calculation.' The smaller space was used to survey many geometrical arrangements of both triplet and quintet states and to locate stationary points by gradient methods; then 'further CASSCF calculations were then performed, using a larger active space (8 electrons in 10 orbitals, to give 2000 CSF) and the geometries already located', followed by CASPT2 at the same structures. The active space was subsequently ABANDONED for the vibrational analysis: 'The CAS calculations showed, as expected, that a single configuration dominates in both of these species; the weight of the HF-reference configuration always exceeded 99%. We therefore adopted SCF and DFT methods for these vibrational frequency calculations, since they are less computationally demanding than the CASSCF variety.' Separately, the MP2 calculations excluded excitations out of the eight lowest MOs and into their virtual counterparts, a choice that keeps the 3s- and 3p-like manganese orbitals active in order to capture part of the core-valence correlation.
electronic_structure_description: Three planar C2v quintet states were located, of A1, B1 and B2 symmetry, differing chiefly in bond angles: two small angles of 106 degrees in 5A1, two large angles of 128 degrees in 5B2, and all angles close to 120 degrees in 5B1. With the (6,8) space the 5A1 state lies 25.7 kJ/mol below 5B2 and 173 kJ/mol below 5B1. Enlarging to (8,10) at the same geometries keeps 5A1 lowest but cuts its margin over 5B2 to only 10 kJ/mol, and adding CASPT2 reduces it further to just 6.4 kJ/mol — the ordering is unchanged throughout. No C3v stationary point could be found. The 5A1 state has two long and one short bond while 5B2 has the reverse pattern, with a total bond-length variation of about 0.04 A; this is exactly the pattern expected for two states linked by a Jahn-Teller distortion along the in-plane e' bending mode from a D3h reference, where the phase of the distortion determines whether one angle opens with two bonds lengthening or two angles open with one bond lengthening. Four triplet states of C2v planar geometry were characterized, 3B1 being most stable, then 3A2, 3A1 and 3B2, lying 280, 358, 366 and 485 kJ/mol above the 5A1 ground state with the six-electron space — all substantially above the lowest quintet. Optimized geometries and 5A1-to-5B2 separations (r(Mn-F2), r(Mn-F3), angle F2-Mn-F3 for 5A1, then the same for 5B2, then dE in kJ/mol): SCF 1.734, 1.749, 107.4 and 1.774, 1.734, 127.5, dE 8.7; B3LYP 1.734, 1.755, 106.6 and 1.770, 1.741, 128.4, dE 7.7; BLYP 1.752, 1.775, 106.9 and 1.781, 1.760, 128.4, dE 5.8; BP86 1.739, 1.763, 106.6 and 1.771, 1.747, 128.8, dE 6.4; MP2 1.726, 1.752, 105.7 and 1.773, 1.731, 129.1, dE 8.9. Spin contamination in the unrestricted calculations was negligible, with S-squared never exceeding 6.03. Electron diffraction confirms a Jahn-Teller-type distortion: a non-distorted MnF3 would require an implausibly large shrinkage effect.
Other: MnF3 is a clean demonstration that enlarging an active space can collapse an energy gap without changing the answer. Going from (6,8) to (8,10) at fixed geometry cuts the 5A1-5B2 separation from 25.7 to 10 kJ/mol, and CASPT2 takes it to 6.4 — a factor of four reduction — while the state ordering survives every step. Two states related by a Jahn-Teller distortion of a common D3h parent are exactly the case where this should be expected: they differ only in the phase of the same e' distortion, so their correlation requirements are nearly identical and most of the initial gap was differential correlation error rather than physics. The authors' emphasis that 'the relative ordering was not affected' is the right thing to check, since with a final gap of 6.4 kJ/mol the identification of the ground state rests on a margin smaller than the correction that produced it. The second lesson runs the other way: having established with the active space that both quintets are over 99% single-configurational at the HF reference, the authors DROP the CASSCF for the vibrational analysis and use SCF and DFT instead. That is the correct inference from a multiconfigurational calculation — using it as a diagnostic to license a cheaper method — and the five methods in Table 1 then agree on the gap to within 3 kJ/mol and on the angles to within about 1.5 degrees. Note that the survey space was itself chosen from MCPF natural orbital populations rather than by chemical intuition, so the whole chain from orbital selection to method selection is evidence-driven.
reference_short: Hargittai, Reffy, Kolonits, Marsden & Heully, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1997, 119, 9042
notes: Computed harmonic wavenumbers with infrared intensities in parentheses (SCF then B3LYP) against experimental matrix and estimated gas-phase values: b2 811(313)/788(260) versus 752 in Kr, 759 in Ar and 778 in Ne; a1 757(166)/749(129) versus 705, 712, 732; a1 695(28)/666(9) versus 644; b1 210(104)/181(58) versus 182, 185, 186; a1 194(45)/180(21) versus 186, 190; b2 205(8)/173(3) versus 180. Electron diffraction patterns were recorded from a Sigma-Aldrich MnF3 sample at 60 kV. Geometry optimization among the triplets was performed only for 3B1, since the ground-state geometry was the focus. The two lowest quintet bond lengths could not be resolved in the electron diffraction radial distribution.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 at the CASSCF geometries; MP2 with the eight lowest MOs and their virtual counterparts excluded from the excitation space

compound_name: O(3P) + C2H2 reaction system — triplet 3A'' and 3A' potential energy surfaces
geometry_source: All stationary points in the reaction scheme were REOPTIMIZED at CASSCF(8,8)/6-311++G(d,p) with analytical Hessian calculations, specifically to test for multiconfigurational character. The reference energetics come from CCSD(T), QCISD, CBS-QCI/APNO, CBS-QB3, G2M(CC,MP2), G3B3, G3 and B3LYP calculations. Intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations at B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) established the connections between reaction intermediates.
method: CASSCF used as a multireference diagnostic alongside single-reference composite methods (CCSD(T), QCISD, CBS-QCI/APNO, CBS-QB3, G2M(CC,MP2), G3B3, G3) and B3LYP
software: Dalton and MOLPRO for the CASSCF geometries and vibrational frequencies; Gaussian 03 for all the single-reference and composite calculations
basis_set: 6-311++G(d,p) for the CASSCF; various basis sets for the composite single-reference methods
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals. The individual orbitals are not itemized in the text.
active_space_protocol: The active space is deployed purely as a DIAGNOSTIC rather than as a production method. Every stationary point on the two lowest triplet surfaces — including, importantly, the transition structures — was reoptimized at CASSCF(8,8)/6-311++G(d,p) with analytical Hessians, for the stated purpose of checking 'the effects of multiconfiguration or near-degeneracies of the wave functions for stationary points and particularly for the transition structures'. The outcome licenses the single-reference treatment used for all the reported energetics: 'The CASSCF calculations confirmed that for each of the species considered in this paper the HF-wave function is dominant (i.e., the CI-coefficient of the most important configuration is >0.9), indicating that a single-reference method should give fair results in all cases.' No CASSCF energies are reported; the entire potential energy surface is built from composite single-reference methods.
electronic_structure_description: Two lowest-lying triplet electronic surfaces, 3A'' and 3A', for the O(3P) + C2H2 reaction. The pathway proceeds from O(3P) + C2H2 to the triplet :CHCHO adduct Int1, with a route via TS7 involving a 1,2-hydrogen migration over a barrier of 49.4 kcal/mol leading to triplet ketene (Int3), which then dissociates. Ground-state ketene H2CCO (C2v, X 1A1) lies at -125.6, -122.4, -124.2 and -121.7 kcal/mol at the various composite levels. A pathway leading to triplet HCCOH was also characterized, but was found to lie very high in energy on the triplet surface. Conversion of the excited Int1-ex to the lowest-lying triplet Int1 is described as very facile. One species is a first-order saddle point at the B3LYP, MP2 and CASSCF levels alike. Refined treatments increase the absolute yield of triplet CH2 by only a small amount, with the relative change in triplet CH2 yield being 0.4%; CH2(X 3B1) + CO is formed from activated triplet ketene. CBS-QCI/APNO results agree well with CCSD(T) and with experiment, though a discrepancy of about 1 kcal/mol against experiment remains for fragment radicals whose experimental heats of formation carry uncertainties of at least 1 kcal/mol.
Other: This paper is a clean example of an active space used to EARN a single-reference treatment rather than to replace it. The authors' concern was specifically the transition structures, where near-degeneracies are most likely and where a spuriously single-reference-looking minimum would not protect the barrier heights; so every stationary point, not just the minima, was reoptimized at CASSCF(8,8) with analytical Hessians. The criterion applied is the leading CI coefficient, and the reported threshold is explicit and uniform: greater than 0.9 for every species. That is a stronger check than the more common practice of testing only a few suspect geometries or quoting a T1 diagnostic, and it is what justifies building the whole two-surface reaction scheme from CCSD(T) and composite methods. The limitation to record for reuse is that no CASSCF or CASPT2 energies exist here at all — the active space contributes geometries, frequencies and a validity certificate, and every energy in the paper is single-reference. Anyone wanting a multireference barrier height for this system will not find one in this work, only the assurance that a single-reference one is defensible.
reference_short: Nguyen, Vereecken & Peeters, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 6696
notes: Acetylene is a major intermediate in almost all hydrocarbon-fuelled flames, and O(3P) has a triplet ground state, so the reaction proceeds on triplet surfaces. Product radicals include HCCO and triplet and singlet CH2. Rate coefficients on the adiabatic triplet surface were obtained by solution of the master equation. The paper notes that transition state theory fails for certain intermediate steps. All CASSCF results for the individual species are given in the Supporting Information; IRC analyses appear in Figures S9-S16.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF; dynamic correlation is handled entirely by the separate single-reference composite methods

compound_name: para-Methylbenzonitrile (PMBN, 1) — photoisomerization to meta and ortho isomers
point_group: No symmetry constraints were introduced in any geometry optimization
geometry_source: Ground-state structures optimized at both B3LYP and CAS(10,8); S1 state optimized at CAS(10,8). Substituted benzvalene, carbene, conical crossing and ground-state transition structures optimized at CAS(8,7). CASPT2 single points on the CAS(10,10) wave function at those geometries.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF, with B3LYP and UB3LYP, TD-B3LYP and CCSD-EOM for comparison

active_space_orbital_description: Ten valence electrons distributed in all possible ways among the eight low-energy pi orbitals for the S0 and S1 geometry optimizations; the reduced CAS(8,7) and the enlarged CAS(10,10) used for ground-state structures and for CASPT2 energies respectively are also pi spaces.
active_space_protocol: THREE different active spaces are used for three different jobs, and the paper says why for each. Geometry optimization of the ground and first excited states uses CAS(10,8): 'In this case, 10 valence electrons are allowed to distribute in all possible ways into eight low-energy pi orbitals, denoted as CAS(10,8). At the same CASSCF level, the first excited states (S1) have been optimized.' A SMALLER CAS(8,7) is used for the more numerous ground-state structures: 'To reduce computational costs, the substituted benzvalene, carbene, conical crossing, and transition-state structures on the ground-state PES have been optimized at the CAS(8,7) level. Test calculations indicate that use of relatively small active space was still adequate for geometry optimization.' A LARGER CAS(10,10) carries the energetics: 'In order to validate estimation of relative energies, CASPT2 calculations were carried out on the basis of the CAS(10,10) wave function at the CASSCF-optimized geometries. The absorption and fluorescence spectra were computed by the CASPT2 approach in combination of the state-averaged CAS(10,10) calculations at the CAS(10,8)-optimized geometries.' No symmetry constraints were imposed in any geometry optimization. Where CASSCF optimization failed to converge — for one transition structure on the methylanisole S1 surface — CIS was substituted.

electronic_structure_description: Vertical transition energies in eV with oscillator strengths, gas phase (TD-B3LYP / CCSD / CASSCF / CASPT2, with CASPT2/6-31+G(d) in parentheses, against experiment): S1 5.11 (f 0.0021) / 5.09 / 4.77 / 4.79 (4.78) with f 0.0009, experimental 4.63; S2 5.50 (f 0.3137) / 6.35 / 7.47 / 6.67 (6.33) with f 0.0670, experimental 5.34. The CASSCF and CASPT2 S1 values agree closely at 4.77 and 4.79 eV (260 and 259 nm). The S2 CASSCF wave function includes partial double excitation configurations and shows a dipole increment of 50-100% over the ground state, indicating charge-transfer character; benzonitrile may be stabilized by 0.77 eV in polar solvent, which is invoked to reconcile the computed 6.33 eV with the measured 5.34 eV (232 nm) in acetonitrile. Only the S1 state is accessible at the irradiation wavelength, at 4.88 eV (112.5 kcal/mol). The S1 equilibrium geometry gives a predicted fluorescence emission at 4.37 eV (100.8 kcal/mol) and an adiabatic S1 transition energy of 4.46 eV (102.9 kcal/mol). The photochemistry proceeds through a prefulvene-like S1/S0 conical intersection to prefulvene biradical intermediates, which evolve to substituted benzvalenes; a prebenzvalene structure serves as an intermediate. Re-aromatization of the substituted benzvalenes requires relatively high barriers. The barrier from the S1 Franck-Condon structure to the S1/S0 conical intersection is about 5 kcal/mol lower than in p-methylanisole.
Other: PMBN is the photochemically ACTIVE reference of the comparison, and the property that makes it active is a low barrier to reach the S1/S0 conical intersection — about 5 kcal/mol below the methylanisole value. It is also the compound where the three-space protocol is most exposed: the CAS(10,8) gives the S1 geometry, the CAS(8,7) gives the benzvalene and biradical structures, and the CAS(10,10) CASPT2 gives every energy joining them, so the reaction profile is assembled across three orbital sets. The S1 numbers survive this well (CASSCF 4.77 and CASPT2 4.79 eV, within 0.16 eV of the 4.63 eV measurement), but the S2 does not: 7.47 eV at CASSCF against 6.67 at CASPT2 and 5.34 measured. The footnote explains why — partial double excitations and a 50-100% dipole increase mark it as a charge-transfer state — and this is the standard signature of a state whose energy a pi-only space places badly regardless of size.  The three-space protocol here is worth recording as a template: a mid-sized (10,8) pi space for the states that matter structurally, a trimmed (8,7) for the many ground-state stationary points where 'test calculations indicate that use of relatively small active space was still adequate for geometry optimization', and an enlarged (10,10) carrying every reported energy through CASPT2. Geometry and energy are decoupled deliberately, and the smallest space is used only where its adequacy was checked. The failure mode the paper documents is at the top end rather than the bottom: the S2 state is flagged in a table footnote because 'The CASSCF wave function of the S2 state includes partial double excitation configurations, and it exhibits a large dipole increment (increase of 50-100%) relative to the ground state, showing the character of charge transfer.' That double-excitation and charge-transfer character is exactly what wrecks the single-reference comparisons — for PMBN the S2 comes out at 5.50 eV (TD-B3LYP), 6.35 (CCSD), 7.47 (CASSCF) and 6.67 (CASPT2) against 5.34 eV measured, a spread of 2 eV — while the S1, a well-behaved state, is reproduced to within 0.2 eV by every method. A second practical caution: a CASSCF optimization simply did not converge for the methylanisole S1-to-conical-intersection transition structure, and CIS was used instead, so the 10.7 kcal/mol barrier that carries the paper's central conclusion rests on a CASPT2 energy at a CIS geometry.
reference_short: Xu, Cao & Zhang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 5775
notes: One of three methylbenzonitrile isomers (para, meta, ortho) whose photochemical interconversion is observed experimentally. The biradical channel operates here, in contrast to the carbene channel in methylanisoles. B3LYP relative energetics for the conversion of PMBN to MMBN and OMBN via the benzvalene mechanism coupled with prefulvene biradicals are given in Figure 4, with CASPT2 values in parentheses. A 1,2-carbon shift mechanism was found to be less relevant to the photoisomerization.

electronic_structure_description: The meta and ortho isomers are the photoproducts of para-methylbenzonitrile irradiation. All three isomers are close in energy. Photoisomerization proceeds from the S1/S0 conical intersection through prefulvene biradical structures which evolve into substituted benzvalenes; the conical intersection can evolve into two other substituted structures whose interconversion, followed by re-aromatization, returns the substituted benzonitriles. Prefulvene biradicals form as the primary photochemical event and evolve to benzvalenes almost without energy requirement, while re-aromatization of the substituted benzvalenes requires relatively high barriers. UB3LYP calculations describe the interconversion of the substituted biradicals. Isotope labeling experiments show the transposition is highly specific.

Like PMBN, p-methylanisole shows a large S1-S2 gap and the S1 is the only accessible excited state at 254 nm despite its relatively small oscillator strength; the S1 comprises two excitation configurations. Fluorescence emission is estimated at 4.35 eV and the adiabatic S1 transition energy at 4.47 eV, comparable with the rotationally resolved S0-to-S1 fluorescence excitation spectrum of m-methylanisole (4.47 eV cis, 4.48 eV trans). The S1/S0 conical intersection (A6) has a prefulvene-like structure like PMBN, but NO prefulvene biradical could be located — every optimization attempt converged instead to a carbene (A11) or a substituted prebenzvalene (A7). The paper attributes this to the lack of conjugative interaction between C4 and the OCH3 group, which destabilizes the biradical, while the oxygen lone pairs push the C4 single electron to couple with that at C2, giving the prebenzvalene. C4-C5 bond cleavage instead gives a more stable carbene in which C4 offers an empty orbital to share the oxygen lone pair. CASPT2 barriers: 4.1 kcal/mol from carbene A11 to benzvalene A8, 17.1 kcal/mol in reverse, 6.9 kcal/mol for carbene interconversion A11 to A13 (lower than the benzvalene interconversion barrier), and 7.8 kcal/mol for A11 returning to A2 via A14TS. notes: Methylanisole isomers are experimentally unreactive relative to methylbenzonitriles, and photochemical interconversion of methylanisoles has not been observed at 254 nm. The ground-state structures of p-, m- and o-methylanisole (A1, A2/A3, A4) are all close in energy. The substituted benzvalene A8 should be the primary product from the conical intersection owing to its stability, but carbenes A11 and A13 are argued to be the important intermediates for isomer interconversion because both re-aromatization and benzvalene interconversion face large barriers. Variable temperature fluorescence studies are also cited in support.

active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons distributed in six active orbitals, used in a state-averaged CASSCF for the n-pi* transition. The individual orbitals are not itemized.
active_space_protocol: A minimal state-averaged space of TWO electrons in SIX orbitals, s/a-CASSCF(2,6), is used for the n-pi* transition, with CASPT2 on the same reference. The state averaging is what makes a two-electron space workable for a symmetry-forbidden transition. The space is applied identically to bare acetone and to every acetone-water complex, so the hydrogen-bonding shift is measured at constant orbital content — the water molecules contribute no active orbitals. CIS with three basis sets (6-31G**, 6-311G**, 6-311+G**) was run first as a preliminary survey, and CASSCF/CASPT2 with 6-31G** only for the more accurate work; for the larger two- and three-water complexes only CASSCF was affordable, with CASPT2 restricted to acetone and the one-water complexes. Geometries come from B3LYP/6-311G** with zero-point corrections scaled by 0.963, and complexation energetics from G2M.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged; the number of states is not stated
electronic_structure_description: The n-pi* transition is the symmetry-forbidden 1A1 to 1A2 excitation, with zero oscillator strength. Vertical excitation energies in eV (oscillator strengths in parentheses) for the most stable conformer 0a: CIS 5.2012 (0) with 6-31G**, 5.1974 (0) with 6-311G**, 5.2131 (0) with 6-311+G**; CASSCF/6-31G** 4.3481 (0); CASPT2/6-31G** 4.3781 (0). The CASPT2 value of 4.38 eV reproduces the experimental value; CASSCF slightly underestimates it but agreement is still good; CIS overestimates by about 0.8 eV and does not improve with increasing basis set. Structure 0a is the most stable at B3LYP/6-311G** with zero-point correction and has no imaginary frequencies; it is stabilized by two intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen (natural charge -0.55 e) and methyl hydrogens (natural charge +0.22 e) with O...H distances of 2.52 A and a Wiberg bond index of 0.005.
Other: Bare acetone is the calibration point, and it establishes two things about the two-electron space. First, it is sufficient: CASPT2 at 4.378 eV matches experiment and CASSCF at 4.348 eV is only 0.03 eV below it, so the dynamic correlation missing from s/a-CASSCF(2,6) is negligible for this transition. Second, the comparison with CIS is the sharper lesson — CIS overestimates by 0.8 eV and that error is completely insensitive to basis set, moving by only 0.016 eV across 6-31G**, 6-311G** and 6-311+G**. An n-pi* excitation of a carbonyl is a case where the deficiency is in the treatment of correlation between the two states, not in the one-particle space, and no amount of basis-set enlargement addresses it.  This paper measures a SOLVENT SHIFT at fixed active space, which is the right design for the question and worth noting as a pattern. The s/a-CASSCF(2,6) sits entirely on the acetone carbonyl; the one, two and three water molecules that hydrogen-bond to it contribute no active orbitals at all, so the computed blue shifts of 0.25-0.40 eV are a response of a FIXED chromophore wave function to an electrostatic and geometric perturbation rather than a change in the correlated space. The internal validation is unusually direct: CASSCF and CASPT2 agree to within 0.1 eV on the complexes where both were run, and their oscillator strengths are close too, which is what licenses the authors to 'analyze the whole set of data based on the CASSCF/6-31G** results' for the larger complexes where CASPT2 was not affordable. That agreement also bounds what the two-electron space is missing: for bare acetone CASPT2 gives 4.378 eV against a CASSCF 4.348, so dynamic correlation is worth only 0.03 eV here — the space contains the essential n and pi* orbitals and the perturbative correction has little left to do. The contrast with CIS is the useful calibration: CIS overestimates the excitation by about 0.8 eV and, tellingly, that error does not improve at all with basis set (5.2012, 5.1974 and 5.2131 eV across three bases). A single-reference excited-state method fails here by an amount no basis-set improvement can touch, while a two-electron multiconfigurational space reproduces experiment. One caution for reuse: because the shifts are differences of order 0.25 eV computed from absolute energies that CASSCF places about 0.03 eV low, the shift magnitudes are more reliable than the absolute transition energies, and the CASPT2 shift for the one-water complex (0.16 eV) differs noticeably from the CASSCF one (0.25 eV) — so even a well-converged absolute energy does not guarantee a converged difference.

Relative to bare acetone the transition is blue-shifted by 0.25 eV in 1a at the CASSCF level and by 0.16 eV at CASPT2. Going from 1a to 1b the energy increases by 0.066 eV at CASSCF and 0.117 eV at CASPT2. Complexation with the first water molecule brings an energy gain of 3.5 kcal/mol at the G2M level. Red shifts of up to 358 cm-1 are predicted for the OH stretching vibrations, the HOH bending vibrations are blue-shifted and the CO stretching frequencies red-shifted in the complexes. The forbidden transition acquires nonzero intensity on complexation because the water breaks the acetone symmetry.

geometry_source: Geometry optimizations on QM-only clusters and on SIMOMM (surface integrated molecular orbital molecular mechanics) QM/MM embedded clusters, with the QM region treated multiconfigurationally and the surrounding silicon treated by molecular mechanics. Analytic Hessians were available for the QM-only clusters and seminumerical Hessians for the hybrid QM/MM SIMOMM models; because the Hessian is costly for larger clusters, dimer buckling mode frequencies were examined only for the smallest two-dimer system.
method: Full CASSCF (FORS), occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field (ORMAS) with several partitioning schemes, and generalized valence bond perfect pairing (GVB-PP), with SIMOMM QM/MM embedding
basis_set: SBKJC effective core potentials augmented with a set of d polarization functions, SBKJC ECP(d)
active_space_orbital_description: The pi and pi* orbitals of the single Si-Si surface dimer.
active_space_protocol: The paper's subject IS the active space: it tests occupation restricted multiple active space (ORMAS) partitionings against full CASSCF for Si(100) surface clusters. The physical basis is that each surface dimer contributes a pi/pi* (and optionally sigma/sigma*) pair, so a CAS grows as (4n,4n) with the number of dimers n and rapidly becomes intractable — the stated practical ceiling for FORS/CASSCF being about (16,16) because determinant counts scale factorially. ORMAS partitions the same orbital set into user-defined subspaces with minimum and maximum electron occupations, eliminating configurations that contribute negligibly ('deadwood'). The worked illustration: a two-dimer CAS(4,4) of two pi/pi* sets has 36 determinants; splitting it into two (2,2) subspaces, one per dimer, with minimum and maximum occupation both fixed at 2, leaves 18 determinants and forbids any interdimer electronic excitation. Three partitioning schemes are compared: grouping each dimer's orbitals into its own subspace (number of subspaces equal to the number of dimers), and finer groupings with two subspaces per dimer (pi/pi* and sigma/sigma* separated). All groupings set the minimum occupation equal to the maximum. The justification for the partition is measured first: CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers for one-, two- and three-dimer clusters show the dimers are only weakly coupled, so interdimer excitations can be dropped with little cost.
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers for the pi and pi* orbitals: 1.65 and 0.35. These values, far from 2 and 0, indicate significant diradical character in the surface dimer and are the basis for requiring a multiconfigurational description of the Si(100) surface. The experimental Si-Si dimer bond length is 2.26 +/- 0.1 A.
Other: The single-dimer cluster establishes the diagnostic that the whole study rests on: pi/pi* occupation numbers of 1.65/0.35 for one isolated surface dimer. Roughly a third of an electron in the nominally empty pi* is well outside anything a single determinant can represent, and the paper states the general rule — 'a NOON that is significantly larger than 0 for a supposedly unoccupied orbital is a good indicator that a multiconfiguration description is needed'. Equally important is what these numbers do NOT change: for two- and three-dimer clusters the corresponding values stay at 1.64/1.64 with 0.38/0.34 and 1.65/1.64/1.62 with 0.40/0.35/0.34. The near-invariance across cluster size is the evidence that dimers are weakly coupled and hence that an ORMAS partition forbidding interdimer excitations will be nearly exact.  This is a systematic study of when an active space can be PARTITIONED rather than merely truncated, and the criterion is physical: the CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers of the Si(100) dimers barely change as clusters grow (pi around 1.62-1.65, pi* around 0.34-0.40 for one, two and three dimers), showing the dimers are electronically almost independent. Because they are, forbidding interdimer excitations costs almost nothing while removing orders of magnitude of determinants — for the four-dimer QM cluster, ORMAS cuts a 165-million-determinant CASSCF(16,16) Hamiltonian by two to three orders of magnitude with a largest energy error of about 2.4 mhartree, and the best partition errs by well under 1 mhartree. The occupation numbers themselves are the headline diagnostic: pi/pi* NOONs of roughly 1.66/0.33 for the surface dimers indicate substantial diradical character and are the reason a multiconfigurational description is needed at all, since a NOON far from 2 for a nominally occupied orbital or far from 0 for a nominally empty one is the standard signal. The comparison against GVB-PP sharpens the point about how far one can go: when only (2,2) subspaces are used, ORMAS and GVB-PP agree closely, but larger ORMAS subspaces cut the error against full CASSCF substantially while the GVB-PP error stays large — for the 2x2 QM/MM (16,16) cluster, ORMAS errs by 1.7-2.2 mhartree against GVB-PP's 21 mhartree, an order of magnitude worse. The limit is reached honestly: the nine-dimer CASSCF(18,18) would need more than 2.3 billion determinants and is simply not performed, so for that cluster ORMAS is validated only by agreement with trends from the smaller systems it could be checked against. A final caveat the authors state themselves: the conclusion that the Si(100) surface is symmetric in the ground state comes from calculations that 'do not include dynamic correlation'.

geometry_source: Geometry optimizations on QM-only clusters and on SIMOMM (surface integrated molecular orbital molecular mechanics) QM/MM embedded clusters, with the QM region treated multiconfigurationally and the surrounding silicon treated by molecular mechanics. Analytic Hessians were available for the QM-only clusters and seminumerical Hessians for the hybrid QM/MM SIMOMM models; because the Hessian is costly for larger clusters, dimer buckling mode frequencies were examined only for the smallest two-dimer system.
method: Full CASSCF (FORS), occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field (ORMAS) with several partitioning schemes, and generalized valence bond perfect pairing (GVB-PP), with SIMOMM QM/MM embedding
basis_set: SBKJC effective core potentials augmented with a set of d polarization functions, SBKJC ECP(d)
active_space_orbital_description: Sixteen electrons in sixteen orbitals: four pi/pi* sets and four sigma/sigma* sets, one pair of each per Si-Si dimer. ORMAS partitions this either as four (pi pi*) subspaces plus four (sigma sigma*) subspaces, or as four combined (pi pi* sigma sigma*) subspaces.
active_space_protocol: The paper's subject IS the active space: it tests occupation restricted multiple active space (ORMAS) partitionings against full CASSCF for Si(100) surface clusters. The physical basis is that each surface dimer contributes a pi/pi* (and optionally sigma/sigma*) pair, so a CAS grows as (4n,4n) with the number of dimers n and rapidly becomes intractable — the stated practical ceiling for FORS/CASSCF being about (16,16) because determinant counts scale factorially. ORMAS partitions the same orbital set into user-defined subspaces with minimum and maximum electron occupations, eliminating configurations that contribute negligibly ('deadwood'). The worked illustration: a two-dimer CAS(4,4) of two pi/pi* sets has 36 determinants; splitting it into two (2,2) subspaces, one per dimer, with minimum and maximum occupation both fixed at 2, leaves 18 determinants and forbids any interdimer electronic excitation. Three partitioning schemes are compared: grouping each dimer's orbitals into its own subspace (number of subspaces equal to the number of dimers), and finer groupings with two subspaces per dimer (pi/pi* and sigma/sigma* separated). All groupings set the minimum occupation equal to the maximum. The justification for the partition is measured first: CASSCF natural orbital occupation numbers for one-, two- and three-dimer clusters show the dimers are only weakly coupled, so interdimer excitations can be dropped with little cost.
electronic_structure_description: For the QM/MM 2x2 cluster, CASSCF(8,8) gives pi occupations 1.64, 1.64, 1.63, 1.62 and pi* 0.39, 0.39, 0.35, 0.35 with a dimer bond length of 2.30 A from 4900 determinants; the ORMAS 4(pi pi*)2 partition gives 1.63 x4 and 0.37 x4 with the same bond length from only 454 determinants and an energy error of 0.36 mhartree; GVB-PP(4) gives identical occupations and bond length with an error of 0.46 mhartree. For CASSCF(16,16) the reference requires 165,636,900 determinants and gives pi 1.70, 1.70, 1.69, 1.69, pi* 0.32, 0.32, 0.29, 0.29, sigma 1.98 x4, sigma* 0.02 x4 and a bond length of 2.32 A. The ORMAS 4(pi pi*)2 4(sigma sigma*)2 partition needs 411,462 determinants with an error of 2.23 mhartree; the 4(pi pi* sigma sigma*) partition needs 6,297,030 determinants with an error of 1.74 mhartree; both reproduce the occupation numbers and the 2.32 A bond length. GVB-PP(8) errs by 21.13 mhartree and gives noticeably different occupations (pi 1.61, pi* 0.39) and a bond length of 2.33 A. The experimental dimer bond length is 2.26 +/- 0.1 A. Across the three ORMAS partitioning schemes applied to the four-dimer QM cluster, the largest energy error is about 2.4 mhartree and the most accurate partition errs by much less than 1 mhartree.

GVB-PP restricts to strictly paired (2,2) subspaces, so it cannot capture the correlation ORMAS retains within its larger subspaces — this is the concrete demonstration that HOW a space is partitioned matters more than how many orbitals it nominally contains. Note also the systematic effect of adding the sigma orbitals: going from (8,8) to (16,16) shifts every pi occupation up by about 0.06 and every pi* down by about 0.07, so the apparent diradical character depends on whether the sigma framework is correlated alongside it. A final caveat the authors state themselves: the conclusion that the Si(100) surface is symmetric in the ground state comes from calculations that 'do not include dynamic correlation'.

notes: Studied as a QM-only four-dimer cluster (Si42H34 in the 1x4 arrangement) and as a 2x2 SIMOMM embedded cluster with QM region Si33H32 in an MM region of Si267H116. Correlating both the pi and sigma orbitals of a four-dimer cluster at full CASSCF would create a Hamiltonian of more than 165 million determinants.

compound_name: Adenine — 1La, 1Lb and 1(n-pi*) excited states and low-energy deactivation channels
point_group: Planar except for a slightly pyramidalized amino group
geometry_source: Fully unconstrained CASSCF geometry optimizations and minimum energy path computations on the relevant potential energy surfaces, with CASPT2 energy corrections added at those geometries. Excited-state geometries were optimized with equal-weight state averaging over the first nine roots to avoid root flipping; the N-H photocleavage study used thirteen-root state averaging.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF, with multistate CASPT2 (MSPT2) used to correct the state mixing; CASSI for transition dipole moments
basis_set: 6-31+G**, chosen because the p functions on hydrogen give a better description of the sigma* orbitals
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals: the 2 lone pairs on the pyrimidine-ring nitrogen atoms, 4 pi orbitals, and either 4 pi* plus 1 sigma*, or alternatively 3 pi* plus 2 sigma* — the latter being the sigma*(N9-H) and sigma*(N10-H) antibonding orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The paper devotes a dedicated section (2.2 Active Space Selection) to justifying and then CORRECTING its space, and the correction is the point. Most geometry optimizations use CAS(12,11): the 11 orbitals are the 2 nitrogen lone pairs of the pyrimidine ring, 4 pi, and then either 4 pi* plus 1 sigma*, or alternatively 3 pi* plus 2 sigma* — the latter being the sigma*(N9-H) and sigma*(N10-H) antibonding orbitals. For the 1La intrinsic reaction coordinate a CAS(12,10) of pi and pi* only was used instead, explicitly 'to avoid the problems arising from the contamination of 1La with npi*, nsigma*, and psigma* states'. A third space, CAS(12,9), was used to recompute the 1La MEP and the npi* and 1Lb minima, excluding the sigma*(N9H) and sigma*(N10H) orbitals in order 'to eliminate the 1n-sigma(N9H)* and 1n-sigma(N10H)* configurations that incorrectly mix up and perturb the 1La state'. State averaging over the first NINE roots with equal weights was used generally to avoid root flipping, extended to THIRTEEN roots for the N-H photocleavage study so as to include higher-lying Bb and n-sigma* states. An imaginary level shift of 0.25 au was applied in all CASPT2 calculations to remove intruder states. Transition dipole moments came from CASSI and oscillator strengths were evaluated with CASPT2 excitation energies.
nroots_per_mult: 9 equally weighted roots generally; 13 roots for the N-H photocleavage paths
electronic_structure_description: The CASSCF/6-31+G** S0 minimum is planar except for a pyramidalized amino group, with the two N10 hydrogens 21 and 19 degrees out of plane, in agreement with vibrational transition moment angle measurements; the amino inversion barrier is only 0.01 eV so the hydrogens oscillate between the two minima, consistent with the small inertial defect of -0.2 from microwave spectra. The three lowest excited states 1(n-pi*), 1La and 1Lb lie close together, from about 4.4 eV (1(n-pi*) origin) to about 5.0 eV (1La vertical). Oscillator strengths for the 1(n-pi*) and 1Lb transitions are very small (about 1e-2 and 1e-3) and therefore markedly geometry dependent. The S0-to-1La oscillator strength is 0.22 at the CASSCF(12,9) level, against an observed 0.24, and accounts for most of the absorption near 5 eV; at CASSCF(12,11) the same quantity collapses to 0.08. The computed 1La vertical excitation energy is 5.45 eV with the (12,11) space and 5.20 eV with (12,9), against experimental absorption maxima of 4.98 eV in vapour (249 nm) and about 4.92 eV in a supersonic beam (252 nm). Optimizing 1Lb enlarges the hexagonal ring while keeping the molecule planar and lowers the 1Lb energy. At CASSCF(12,11) two 1(n-sigma*) states appear slightly BELOW 1La, an ordering that CASPT2 corrects.
Other: Adenine here is the case where a larger active space makes one state worse. The (12,11) space carries the sigma*(N-H) orbitals required for the dissociative channel, but they allow 1(n-sigma*) configurations to contaminate 1La — visible as an oscillator strength of 0.08 against a measured 0.24, a spurious barrier on the 1La path incompatible with the subpicosecond lifetime, and 1(n-sigma*) states spuriously below 1La at the CASSCF level. Deleting the two sigma*(N-H) orbitals to give (12,9) restores an oscillator strength of 0.22 and lowers the 1La path by about 10 kcal/mol, and multistate CASPT2 on the (12,11) reference reaches the same place independently. The 1Lb and 1(n-pi*) curves are unchanged by either fix, so the defect is state-specific. Note also that the 1La vertical energy is 0.25 eV lower with the smaller space (5.20 versus 5.45 eV) and closer to the 4.92-4.98 eV measurements — the reverse of the usual expectation that enlarging a space improves an excitation energy.  This is one of the most explicit published accounts of an active space being too large in the wrong direction. The CAS(12,11) contains the sigma*(N-H) orbitals needed for the dissociative pi-sigma* channel, but their presence lets 1n-sigma* configurations mix into 1La, and the authors detect this through OBSERVABLES rather than by inspection: the computed S0-to-1La oscillator strength collapses to 0.08 against a measured 0.24, the S0-to-1n-sigma* oscillator strength is correspondingly overestimated, and the 1La minimum energy path acquires a spurious barrier incompatible with the observed subpicosecond 1La lifetime. Their verdict is blunt — 'within the CASSCF(12,11) active space, 1La is not described on the same accuracy as the other states.' Two independent fixes are applied and cross-checked. Multistate CASPT2 mixes the CASSCF wave functions at the perturbative level and corrects the energies; separately, a CAS(12,9) that DELETES the two sigma*(N-H) orbitals removes the offending configurations at the reference level. That the two give similar answers — a 1La path about 10 kcal/mol below the CASPT2//CASSCF(12,11) one — is what makes the diagnosis credible rather than a fitted correction. Crucially, the other states are unaffected: 'the energy curves of the other electronic states, in particular, of the 1Lb and 1npi* states, tend to remain unchanged'. So the space is adequate for most of the spectrum and defective for exactly one state, which is why no single space serves the whole study and three are used. The reusable lesson is that adding orbitals to describe one channel (here N-H dissociation) can degrade an unrelated state through spurious configuration mixing, and that oscillator strengths against experiment are a more sensitive diagnostic of this than energies are.
reference_short: Conti, Garavelli & Orlandi, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2009, 131, 16108
notes: Adenine excited-state decay has two experimental lifetime components; the path associated with the roughly 1 ps tau-2 lifetime was not fully understood. Two decay hypotheses are examined: direct barrierless decay from 1La to a low-energy 1La/S0 conical intersection, and mediation by dissociative 1(pi-sigma*) states leading to N-H bond cleavage. Table 1 of the paper gives CASPT2 S0-Si excitation energies up to 6.5 eV.

compound_name: N(2D) + ethylene reaction — addition versus insertion entrance channels
geometry_source: Saddle point structures for the N(2D) addition and insertion entrance channels fully optimized at CASSCF(5,5)/cc-pVDZ, with harmonic vibrational frequencies at the same level to characterize them as saddle points. Single-point CASSCF(7,7) energies were then computed at those structures. The remainder of the reaction diagram — reactants, products, intermediates and transition states — was optimized at MP2/cc-pVDZ with frequencies, and refined by spin-projected fourth-order Moller-Plesset single points including single, double, triple and quadruple substitutions.
method: CASSCF for the entrance-channel saddle points, with MP2 and PMP4(SDTQ) for the full reaction energy diagram and RRKM/transition state theory for kinetics
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF and MP2 work; cc-pVTZ for the PMP4(SDTQ) single points
active_space_orbital_description: Five electrons in five orbitals: the three nitrogen 2p orbitals plus the C-C pi and C-C pi* orbitals of ethylene. The enlarged space adds the highest C-H sigma and lowest C-H sigma* orbitals with two more electrons, giving (7,7).
active_space_protocol: The multiconfigurational treatment is required by the reactant itself: N(2D) has a (2p) valence configuration that 'cannot be described by the single-determinant HF theory', and unrestricted HF gives a wave function with considerable spin contamination. The base CASSCF(5,5) is assembled from the three nitrogen 2p orbitals and the ethylene C-C pi/pi* pair — exactly the orbitals involved in ADDITION across the double bond. The authors then identify the resulting bias explicitly and correct it: because the (5,5) 'does not include the CH sigma- and sigma*-orbitals', the insertion channel, which breaks a C-H bond, is not described on the same footing, so single-point CASSCF(7,7) calculations 'including the highest CH sigma- and lowest CH sigma*-orbitals, and two more electrons' were performed at the same geometries.
electronic_structure_description: At CASSCF(5,5)/cc-pVDZ the classical barrier for ADDITION of N(2D) to the C=C bond is 3.2 kcal/mol, while the barrier for INSERTION into a C-H bond is 13.0 kcal/mol — a difference of 9.8 kcal/mol. Adding the C-H sigma and sigma* orbitals to give CASSCF(7,7) reduces this difference to 7.3 kcal/mol, so addition remains the lower-barrier channel and the insertion mechanism can be ignored under normal thermal conditions. The N-H internuclear distance at the insertion saddle point is 1.512 A, comparable with the 1.516 A reported for N(2D) + CH4. The paper cautions that the CASSCF barrier heights are not quantitatively reliable because CASSCF omits dynamical electron correlation, which is generally important for reaction barrier heights, and that an MRCI treatment would be needed for accurate values. Transition state theory rate constants were computed using a reaction path degeneracy of 2 for the addition reaction, with electronic-state contributions handled by a separate degeneracy factor rather than in the partition functions. active_space_protocol: A FULL-VALENCE space is used with no selection at all: 'All 15 valence electrons were correlated in all 12 valence orbitals.' Applying the same full-valence space to every stationary point on the P2N doublet surface means the four isomers are compared with no orbital-selection freedom whatsoever. For the electronic transition energy a separate multireference averaged coupled pair functional (ACPF) treatment was built on top, with a reference space selected by amplitude threshold and then ITERATIVELY EXPANDED: 'All configuration state functions (CSFs) with amplitudes >0.025 in a full-valence CASSCF calculation — with orbitals averaged over the 2-Pi-g and 2-Sigma-u+ states — were included in the reference space ... method: CASSCF geometry optimization with state-averaged CASSCF and multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2); B3LYP, MP2 and TD-OLYP for comparison
software: GAMESS for the DFT and MP2 geometries and frequencies
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 calculations; 6-31+G(d), 6-31G(d,p) and 6-311+G(2d,p) for the DFT and MP2 work; TZ2P(DZP) for TD-OLYP
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals spanning a configuration space of dimension 1764: four orbitals (bonding and matching antibonding) localized chiefly on the carbonyl part of the amide and acetyl functional groups, and four originating from the degenerate e1g and e2u HOMO and LUMO of the benzene ring of the phenylalanine side chain.
active_space_protocol: A single CASSCF(8,8) is used for all four conformers, and its content is stated orbital by orbital: 'Four of the active orbitals (bonding and the matching antibonding interactions) were localized chiefly in the region of the carbonyl part of the amide and acetyl functional groups, whereas the remaining four originate from the benzene degenerate e1g and e2u highest occupied (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied (LUMO) molecular orbitals.' The space spans a configuration space of dimension 1764 and 'effectively encompassed all of the chromophores of interest for describing a few lowest excited states'. Geometries were reoptimized at CASSCF/cc-pVDZ, then state-averaged CASSCF over the FOUR lowest equally weighted roots was performed at those geometries; SA-CASSCF optimizations of the second-root geometries gave the adiabatic S1 energies. Three separate numerical safeguards were applied at the MS-CASPT2 stage: the C, N and O 1s cores were frozen; an IMAGINARY level shift of 0.10 au removed intruder states 'emerging mostly in the first and the third excited state', after which 'the reference weights in the excited states approached to within 7% of that in the ground state (around 0.60)'; and an IPEA shift of 0.10 au — deliberately BELOW the recommended 0.25 au — was used 'to mitigate the problems of overestimating the stability of open shells in CASPT2'. Oscillator strengths combine CASSCF transition dipole moments in the length representation with MS-CASPT2 energy differences.
nroots_per_mult: 4 equally weighted roots in the state-averaged CASSCF
electronic_structure_description: The extended beta-strand conformer. CASSCF(8,8)/MS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ excitation energies in eV with oscillator strengths (length representation, x100, in parentheses): vertical T(v) for state 1 is 4.827 (0.25), state 2 is 5.946 (5.00) and state 3 is 6.809 (88.5); the adiabatic T(0) for state 1 is 4.707. The experimental value for state 1 is 4.650 eV. TD-OLYP/TZ2P(DZP) gives a vertical energy of 5.133 eV (0.64) for the corresponding state. The dominant intensity lies in state 3, whose oscillator strength of 0.885 is more than two orders of magnitude above that of the lowest state. Geometric parameters at B3LYP/6-31+G(d), B3LYP/6-311+G(2d,p) and MP2/6-311+G(2d,p) are tabulated. Amide A band frequencies at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p), harmonic then anharmonic: NH(Phe) 3587/3403, symmetric NH2 3582/3421, antisymmetric NH2 3721/3539 cm-1. Amide I frequencies: amide I(1) harmonic 1729 with intensity 355 and anharmonic 1698 cm-1, dominated by CO(1) stretch (0.76); amide I(2) harmonic 1760 with intensity 269 and anharmonic 1732 cm-1, dominated by CO(2) stretch (0.70).
Other: The beta(a) conformer gives the best agreement with the measured origin, 4.707 eV adiabatic against 4.650 eV observed, a 0.057 eV error that is about as good as MS-CASPT2 on an (8,8) can be expected to deliver for a system this size. What makes the comparison meaningful across conformers is that the eight orbitals — four carbonyl bonding/antibonding pairs from the amide and acetyl groups, four benzene e1g/e2u frontier orbitals — are the same set at every geometry, so conformer-to-conformer differences in excitation energy reflect the hydrogen-bonding environment rather than any change in the correlated space. The spread across all four conformers is only 0.086 eV vertically, which is precisely why a consistent space matters: a differently constructed space per conformer could easily produce artificial differences of that size.  The most valuable thing in this paper is that the active space is used to DISPROVE a set of states predicted by another method. TD-DFT with GGA functionals returns 14 of its 15 lowest excited states as charge-transfer states appearing in quasi-degenerate pairs, reflecting quasi-degeneracies among the phenylalanine antibonding orbitals. The authors dismiss these as artefacts with an argument that turns entirely on the space: 'These low-lying CT states must be considered illusive, knowing that the CASSCF active space comprises all of the orbitals necessary for describing them and that they are still absent from the CASSCF/MS-CASPT2 spectrum in the 4.8-7.0 eV region.' That is a genuinely strong form of negative evidence — a state absent from a calculation whose space demonstrably CONTAINS the orbitals required to build it. It works only because the eight orbitals were chosen and documented as the amide/acetyl carbonyl set plus the benzene e1g/e2u frontier pair, i.e. exactly the donor and acceptor orbitals any peptide-to-phenyl charge transfer would need. The reference weight of about 0.60 in the ground state is worth noting as a caution in the other direction: that is low in absolute terms, and it is only the CONSISTENCY across states (excited states within 7% of the ground state) that makes the MS-CASPT2 energy differences trustworthy. Achieving that consistency required the imaginary level shift; without it the first and third excited states suffered intruders. The reduced IPEA shift of 0.10 au against the recommended 0.25 au is a second deliberate departure, chosen because the standard value overstabilizes open shells — a reminder that the CASPT2 zeroth-order Hamiltonian is itself a tunable part of the protocol and must be reported alongside the space.
