active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the sigma(O2), two pi and two pi* orbitals and the sigma*(O2) orbital of molecular oxygen, together with the HOMO-LUMO pair of ethylene.
active_space_protocol: The (10e,8o) space is used for all geometry optimizations, with MRMP2 optimizations of the local minima as a check on whether CASSCF geometries suffice. For the single-point ENERGIES the authors deliberately avoid multireference perturbation theory because of its active-space sensitivity, and state the reasoning explicitly: 'It is well-known that the single-point energy calculations performed by MRPT encounter several problems, e.g., the intruder state problem, so an appropriate CASSCF wave function should be prepared for perturbation calculations. Maranzana et al. indicated that two counterparts of the oxygen lone-pair orbitals should be included in the active space for the single-point energy calculations to improve convergence. In this way, calculated relative energies heavily depend on the selection of the active space. Instead, we performed Mukherjee's state-specific MRCC for single-point energy calculations because it is intruder free.' The MkCCSD single points use a much smaller (2e,2o) active space with LOCALIZED active orbitals, chosen so the MkCCSD energy is size consistent.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet oxygen (1-Delta-g) adds to ethylene in a stepwise mechanism through two transition structures, giving the 1,4-diradical intermediate I via TS1 and then 1,2-dioxetane (P) via TS2. Relative energies in kcal/mol for reactant, TS1, I, TS2 and P: MkCCSD(2e,2o)//CASSCF(10e,8o) gives 0.0, 21.8, 7.0, 16.0 and -31.3; CASPT2(10e,10o)//CASSCF(10e,8o) gives 0.0, 17.5, 8.3, 16.4 and -31.7; experiment gives 0.0, about 21 and about -35.5. The molecular beam experiment estimates the TS1 barrier at about 21 kcal/mol, which MkCCSD reproduces. Uncorrected broken-symmetry singlet-triplet gaps fall in the range 10.6-13.2 kcal/mol, about half the experimental 22.5 kcal/mol, and are corrected by the approximate spin projection. CASSCF(10e,8o) geometric parameters at TS1 (r1, r2, r3 in angstroms, then two angles and a dihedral in degrees): S = 1 gives 1.426, 1.765, 1.283, 109.0, 111.9, 76.0 and S = 0 gives 1.404, 1.847, 1.276, 98.0, 113.6, -102.3; at the intermediate I, S = 1 gives 1.483, 1.489, 1.341, 111.5, 109.4, -70.5 and S = 0 gives 1.482, 1.484, 1.337, 106.9, 110.9, -99.4. The spin-projected DFT parameters are generally similar to those of CASSCF(10e,8o), and the corrected ordering of the key distance recovers TS1 > I > TS2 in accordance with CASSCF, whereas all broken-symmetry calculations without correction wrongly predict the TS2 barrier to exceed the TS1 barrier and so fail to reproduce the early transition state. A functional containing at least 25% Hartree-Fock exchange plus the AP energy correction is needed to reproduce the accurate ab initio results qualitatively.
Other: This paper is unusual in choosing its correlation method specifically to ESCAPE active-space sensitivity. The authors note that multireference perturbation theory on this system suffers intruder states, that Maranzana et al. found the two oxygen lone-pair counterpart orbitals must be added to the space for the perturbation to converge, and that consequently 'calculated relative energies heavily depend on the selection of the active space'. Rather than enlarge the space and hope, they switch to Mukherjee's state-specific MRCC, which is intruder free, and run it in a minimal (2e,2o) with localized orbitals for size consistency. The payoff is visible in the numbers: MkCCSD gives a TS1 barrier of 21.8 kcal/mol against the molecular beam value of about 21, while CASPT2 with a (10e,10o) reference gives 17.5 — a 4.3 kcal/mol discrepancy on the rate-determining step, precisely the quantity the active-space dependence was expected to damage. Note the division of labour: the (10e,8o) space is retained for GEOMETRIES, where MRMP2 optimizations of the minima confirmed CASSCF suffices, while the energies come from a much smaller space with a method immune to the intruder problem. The CASSCF geometries also serve as the structural reference that exposes the broken-symmetry DFT failure — every uncorrected BS calculation inverts the TS1/TS2 barrier ordering, and only after spin projection does the geometric trend TS1 > I > TS2 agree with CASSCF.
reference_short: Saito, Nishihara, Kataoka, Nakanishi, Kitagawa, Kawakami, Yamanaka, Okumura & Yamaguchi, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 7967
notes: The reaction of singlet oxygen with ethylene proceeds stepwise rather than concertedly. The paper's main purpose is to assess the approximate spin projection method against multireference coupled cluster. Barrier height training sets NHTBH38/04 (38 non-hydrogen-transfer barriers) and HTBH38/04 (38 hydrogen-transfer barriers) are used to calibrate the functionals. The AP-corrected hybrid DFT approach is proposed as an alternative to the MRCC//CASSCF strategy provided spin projection is applied, though quantitative estimation of the rate-limiting TS1 barrier remains difficult.
correlation_correction: MkCCSD(2e,2o) single points at the CASSCF(10e,8o) geometries, chosen over multireference perturbation theory because it is intruder free; CASPT2(10e,10o) values quoted from earlier work for comparison

compound_name: Pt + O2 to PtO2 — calibration of oxygen reduction on a single platinum atom
d_electron_count: 5d9 in the atomic configuration assumed for the cluster models (6s1 5d9)
ligand_set: Molecular oxygen, intact in the outer minimum and dissociated into two Pt-O bonds in the inner minimum
point_group: Cs (the CASSCF/MRCI calculations were carried out in Cs symmetry for the 3A'' state)
geometry_source: Structures taken from DFT calculations with the LANL2DZ+1f/cc-pVDZ basis set, with the same geometry used at all levels of calculation except MP2, where geometries were reoptimized at the MP2 level. Extended PtO calculations with cc-pVTZ basis sets, uncontracting the 5s and 5p shells and optimizing a (1s1p1d) correlating shell, were used to extrapolate the PtO2 results.
method: CASSCF with multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) for calibration; DFT with the B3LYP hybrid functional for the production calculations, and MP2 for comparison
software: MOLPRO for the CASSCF/MRCI calculations; Gaussian 03 for the DFT and MP2 calculations
basis_set: cc-pVDZ/ECP for Pt developed by Peterson with the Stuttgart 60-core-electron relativistic ECP, and aug-cc-pVDZ for O. For the extended PtO work, cc-pVTZ with uncontracted 5s and 5p shells and an added (1s1p1d) correlating shell. The DFT calculations used LANL2 and LANL1 ECPs with LANL2DZ+1f/cc-pVDZ and related basis sets, the f exponent of 0.5 being nearly optimal for B3LYP and 1.0 for MP2.
relativistic_treatment: Stuttgart 60 core-electron relativistic effective core potential on Pt for the CASSCF/MRCI; LANL2 and LANL1 ECPs for the DFT work
active_space_orbital_description: A 5/1 active space in Cs symmetry for the 3A'' state — five orbitals of a' symmetry and one of a'' symmetry, as printed in the paper. The electron count is not stated. Only the Pt 6s and 5d levels could be correlated.
active_space_protocol: The active space is specified by symmetry-block counts, '5/1 active space in Cs symmetry (3A'' state)', and its size was set by a SOFTWARE LIMIT rather than by chemistry: 'We were only able to correlate the 6s and 5d levels of the Pt atom because of restrictions on the number of active orbitals in MOLPRO.' The 5s and 5p semicore levels, which the authors would have wished to correlate, were therefore excluded from the CASSCF/MRCI on PtO2 and were instead studied separately on the smaller PtO molecule, where cc-pVTZ basis sets with uncontracted 5s and 5p shells and an optimized (1s1p1d) correlating shell made the calculation affordable. Those PtO results were then used to EXTRAPOLATE the PtO2 energetics: core-valence correlation and the larger basis together raised the PtO bond strength by 0.10 eV (0.06 eV from the basis set, 0.04 eV from core-valence correlation), and assuming twice that effect for PtO2 gave a 0.2 eV correction added to every structure.
multiplicities_studied: triplet for the CASSCF/MRCI calibration; singlet and triplet for Pt2; spin multiplicity 11 assumed for the Pt10 cluster model
electronic_structure_description: Energetics for Pt + O2 in eV at the outer minimum, saddle point and inner minimum. CASSCF/MRCI with cc-pVDZ/aug-cc-pVDZ: -0.4, 1.1, -0.8. CASSCF/MRCI extrapolated to cc-pVTZ with core-valence correlation based on PtO: -0.6, 0.9, -1.0. DFT cc-pVDZ/aug-cc-pVDZ: -0.9, 0.9, -1.4. DFT cc-pVDZ/cc-pVDZ: -1.0, 0.9, -1.4. DFT LANL2DZ/cc-pVDZ: -0.7, 1.1, -0.5. DFT LANL2DZ+1f/cc-pVDZ: -0.8, 1.0, -1.5. DFT LANL2DZ+2f/cc-pVDZ: -0.9, 0.9, -1.6. MP2 LANL2DZ+1f*/cc-pVDZ: 0.0, 2.6, -0.4. The CASSCF/MRCI surface shows O2 bound to Pt by 0.4 eV in the outer minimum with the O-O bond intact, a barrier of 1.1 eV relative to reactants (1.5 eV relative to the outer minimum), and an inner well bound by 0.8 eV in which the O-O bond has been replaced by two Pt-O bonds. The outer minimum is a physisorbed state whose bonding is a dative interaction between an oxygen lone pair and the 5d9 Pt configuration. Comparing at the same basis set, DFT gives the inner minimum 0.9 eV where CASSCF/MRCI gives 0.4, more than a factor of two, and DFT is judged to overestimate binding energies by more than a factor of 2. MP2 fails qualitatively: the outer well is not bound at all, the barrier is more than a factor of 2 too high, and the inner minimum is bound by a factor of 2 less. For Pt2 at a bond length of 4.75 bohr, CASSCF/MRCI places the singlet state — which has a Pt-Pt 5d sigma bond — only 0.15 eV below the triplet, which has the 5d electrons in delta orbitals.
Other: The active space here was capped by the program rather than chosen: 'We were only able to correlate the 6s and 5d levels of the Pt atom because of restrictions on the number of active orbitals in MOLPRO.' The 5s and 5p semicore levels the authors wanted are absent, and rather than leave that as an unquantified caveat they measured its size on the smaller PtO molecule — core-valence correlation is worth 0.04 eV and the larger basis 0.06 eV — then transferred twice that as a flat 0.2 eV correction to every PtO2 structure. That is a defensible extrapolation and, unusually, it is reported alongside the raw numbers so a reader can undo it. The scientific payoff is a clean diagnosis of MP2's failure: the outer well unbound, the barrier more than doubled, the inner minimum half as deep, which the authors attribute to 'an inability of perturbation theory based methods to accurately represent a potential energy surface with a large amount of multireference character'. The Pt2 result quantifies that character directly — singlet and triplet within 0.15 eV, with quite different 5d couplings — which is why the cluster models had to assume a high-spin 6s1 5d9 configuration, the authors noting that low-spin coupling 'would require a broken symmetry UHF based calculation to get physically meaningful results'. The CASSCF/MRCI is used as the calibration standard against which DFT is judged to overbind by more than a factor of two, so the entire DFT-based mechanism rests on this one multireference anchor point.
reference_short: Walch, Dhanda, Aryanpour & Pitsch, J. Phys. Chem. C 2008, 112, 8464
notes: Part of a study of the oxygen reduction reaction at the cathode of a PEM fuel cell. Larger cluster models were used for the production DFT work: Pt10 and Pt16 for the (111) surface and Pt8 and Pt14 for the (100) surface, plus a Pt20 three-layer model, all built around a central Pt2 unit with a Pt-Pt distance of 2.77 A. Rate constants were computed from conventional transition state theory with tunneling included for hydrogen transfer reactions. For the Pt2O2 twofold site the present work gives De = 1.3 eV, r(O-O) = 1.37 A and an O-O frequency of 873 cm-1, against experimental values of 0.4 and 0.5 eV, 1.377 A and 842-875 cm-1.
correlation_correction: MRCI on the CASSCF reference; core-valence correlation and basis-set effects estimated separately on PtO and extrapolated to PtO2 as a 0.2 eV correction

compound_name: Cyclic ozone (D3h isomer) — active space selection study
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations; the 12/12 selection was too large to permit geometry optimization, so the 18/12 geometry was used for its single-point energy. Vibrational frequencies and zero-point energies computed at the CASSCF level with the 12/9 selection.
method: CASSCF, with Hartree-Fock and MP2 for comparison; the Laplacian of the charge density used to identify the natural orbitals
software: HONDO-8 for the CASSCF calculations; GAUSSIAN-92 for the other methods; the PAC series of programs for the charge density analysis
basis_set: 6-31G* for the geometry optimizations, with 6-311G(d,p) used for the highly correlated treatments
active_space_orbital_description: The balanced 12/12 selection: the same orbitals as the conventional 12/9(a) space plus three extra vacant orbitals of p symmetry, added to correlate the three doubly occupied p orbitals of the Hartree-Fock configuration. Orbitals are labelled by the oxygen atomic orbitals participating and the symmetry of the combination in D3h, with the y axis perpendicular to the molecular plane.
active_space_protocol: This paper contains an extended, explicit comparison of SIX different active-space selections for cyclic ozone, tabulated with energies, geometries, natural orbital occupation numbers and configuration counts. The central problem is stated clearly: in cyclic (D3h) ozone all the p-type orbitals perpendicular to the molecular plane are FILLED in the Hartree-Fock configuration, so 'no correlating vacant orbitals of this symmetry exist when an 18/12 or a 12/9 active space selection is carried out' — the widely used spaces contain no py correlation at all. The occupation numbers make the failure visible: in the 18/12 space the sigma orbitals from 2s combinations are poorly correlated as expected, 'but py orbitals are even less correlated'. Substituting the p orbitals by the 2s orbitals, giving the 12/9(b) selection instead of 12/9(a), actually LOWERS the energy — evidence that the p orbitals in the conventional space were doing nothing. The properly balanced choice is 12/12, which adds three extra orbitals to correlate the three doubly occupied p orbitals, 'a well balanced situation involving doubly occupied and vacant orbitals and between sigma and pi electron clouds', but at 56928 configurations it is too large for geometry optimization. The compromise is 10/9, obtained by removing the a2'' orbital whose role is 'clearly less important than that of the e'' orbitals', which gives a BETTER energy than the 18/12 selection with a third as many configurations. For the Li+ complexes the 1s orbital of Li+ was frozen and its vacant 2s and 2p orbitals excluded, after single-point tests over a range of geometries confirmed no important configurations transfer an electron to or from lithium — giving the same active space for the neutral molecule and the complexes.
electronic_structure_description: Comparison of six active space selections for cyclic ozone, giving r(O-O) in angstroms, total energy in hartree and number of configurations: 12/9(a) 1.4545, -224.48488, 666; 12/9(b) 1.4562, -224.49552, 1280; 18/12 1.4554, -224.49795, 4067; 12/12 (geometry not optimized, the 18/12 geometry used) -224.56149, 56928; 10/9 1.4514, -224.51290, 1374; 14/11 1.4528, -224.52311, 8346. Natural orbital occupation numbers across the selections: a1'(2s) 1.9980-1.9982; the two e'(2s) 1.9949-1.9955; a2''(2py) 1.9913-1.9993; the two e''(2py) 1.9807-1.9971; a1'(2px,2pz) 1.9282-1.9337; the two e'(2px,2pz) 1.9016-1.9107; the vacant a2'(2px,2pz) 0.1091-0.1256; the two vacant e'(2px,2pz) 0.0725-0.0795; and, only in the p-correlating selections, a1''(3py) 0.0138-0.0182 and two e''(3py) 0.0100. The 10/9 selection gives a lower energy than 18/12 despite having three times fewer configurations. The dominant electron promotions correlate bonding occupied orbitals with vacant antibonding orbitals of similar character, matching the bond regions where the Laplacian of the charge density changes sign.
Other: Cyclic ozone is where the conventional space fails by symmetry rather than by size. Every p orbital perpendicular to the plane is doubly occupied at Hartree-Fock, so the standard 18/12 and 12/9 selections — taking only the three lowest vacant orbitals — include NO vacant orbital of p symmetry and allow no p correlation at all. The occupation numbers prove it: the py orbitals come out less correlated than the 2s combinations, which are proverbially inert. The decisive demonstration is that swapping the inert p orbitals for the 2s orbitals, going from 12/9(a) to 12/9(b), LOWERS the energy by 0.011 hartree — the p orbitals in the conventional space were contributing nothing. The properly balanced 12/12 that adds three vacant p orbitals recovers 0.066 hartree over 12/9(a) but needs 56,928 configurations against 666, ruling out geometry optimization. The practical resolution is the 10/9 selection, built by dropping the a2'' orbital whose role is clearly minor, which beats 18/12 on energy with a third of the configurations.  Cyclic ozone is a textbook case of a conventional active space being not merely small but WRONG BY SYMMETRY. In the D3h isomer every p orbital perpendicular to the plane is doubly occupied in the Hartree-Fock configuration, so the standard 18/12 and 12/9 selections — which take only the lowest three vacant orbitals — contain no vacant orbital of that symmetry and permit no p correlation whatsoever. The paper proves this two ways. The occupation numbers show the py orbitals are LESS correlated than the notoriously inert 2s combinations, and swapping the useless p orbitals out for the 2s ones (12/9(a) to 12/9(b)) improves the energy by 0.011 hartree. An active space can therefore contain orbitals that contribute nothing while excluding the ones that would. The remedy — 12/12, adding three vacant p-symmetry orbitals — is correct but costs 56,928 configurations against 1,280, too many for geometry optimization, so a 10/9 compromise is adopted that beats the 18/12 energy with a third the configurations. That inversion is the practical lesson: a smaller, symmetry-appropriate space outperforms a larger, symmetry-blind one. Two further traps are documented. Selecting only ONE of a degenerate e' or e'' pair 'will give different weighting to the oxygen atoms in the molecule, leading to the incorrect prediction of an asymmetric structure' — a symmetry-broken space manufactures a symmetry-broken geometry. And once Li+ sits above the plane, reducing the system to Cs, sigma and pi orbitals mix and 'there is no way now to select s-like or p-like orbitals based on symmetry criteria', so the automatic selection in the 12/9 approach silently swaps a py orbital for a 2s one and produces 'a spurious asymmetric geometry for the complex'. The fix was to force the 2s(e') orbitals into the space for all orientations, giving 14/11.
reference_short: Alcami, Cooper, Mo & Yanez, J. Chem. Phys. 1995, 103, 253
notes: The cyclic D3h isomer is contrasted with the open-chain C2v form, where sigma and pi occupied orbitals can both be promoted into vacant orbitals of the same symmetry, so the conventional selections are properly balanced there. The 3p-type correlating orbitals (a1''(3py) and e''(3py)) appear with occupations of 0.010-0.018 only when the space is enlarged to admit them. Figure 1(b) of the paper shows the Laplacian of the charge density for each natural orbital.
correlation_correction: None reported beyond the CASSCF itself; MP2 was used separately for comparison

compound_name: Open-chain ozone (C2v isomer) and its Li+ complexes
point_group: C2v for the neutral open-chain isomer; the Li+ complexes are lower in symmetry, with structure 1c obtained by imposing C2v during optimization
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations; the 12/12 selection was too large to permit geometry optimization, so the 18/12 geometry was used for its single-point energy. Vibrational frequencies and zero-point energies computed at the CASSCF level with the 12/9 selection.
method: CASSCF, with Hartree-Fock and MP2 for comparison; the Laplacian of the charge density used to identify the natural orbitals
software: HONDO-8 for the CASSCF calculations; GAUSSIAN-92 for the other methods; the PAC series of programs for the charge density analysis
basis_set: 6-31G* for the geometry optimizations, with 6-311G(d,p) used for the highly correlated treatments
active_space_orbital_description: The 12/9 selection, comprising 1280 configurations in Cs symmetry, used for all complex calculations. For complexes with D3h ozone this implies using combinations of 2s orbitals rather than 2py orbitals in the active space. The Li+ 1s orbital is frozen and its vacant 2s and 2p orbitals are excluded, giving the same active space for the neutral molecule and the complexes.

The dominant excitations are from the highest occupied b2 to the vacant a1, or from the highest occupied a1 to the vacant b2. Four structures were considered for Li+ interacting with open-chain ozone: attachment to a terminal oxygen (1a), a bridged structure involving terminal oxygens (1b), a link to the central oxygen (1c, obtained by imposing C2v symmetry, which dissociates at the RHF level), and insertion into one of the O-O bonds (1d). The open-chain forms lie more than 50 kcal/mol below the cyclic ones, with several forms within an energy range of less than 3.0 kcal/mol; one structure is just 1 kcal/mol less stable than 1b. Structures corresponding to attachment to terminal oxygens and to insertion of Li+ into an O-O bond lie about 1 kcal/mol apart. An energy gap of 22.8 kcal/mol separates 1d from another form, and a computed value of 3.5 kcal/mol is compared with an experimental 23.06 kcal/mol for a related quantity. Single-point calculations over a range of geometries showed no important configurations transferring an electron to or from the lithium orbitals, confirming the interactions are mainly electrostatic. Reference values for the cyclic-to-open-chain gap in the literature are around 28.7 kcal/mol.

compound_name: Cyclopropene (1) — photoisomerization to allene and propyne
geometry_source: Stationary points on the S0 and S1 surfaces optimized at CASSCF/6-311G(d), with state-averaged CASSCF(6,6) for geometries in the intersection space and conical intersections optimized by the Bearpark method. All stationary points characterized by analytical harmonic frequencies (all real for minima, one imaginary for transition states), with optimization converged when the maximum force and its RMS fell below 0.00045 and 0.00005 hartree/bohr. Every transition state was verified by a CASSCF IRC calculation. All localizations and IRC mapping performed in mass-weighted Cartesian coordinates.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with multireference Moller-Plesset (MP2-CAS) single-point energies
basis_set: 6-311G(d) for the CASSCF geometries; 6-311G(d,p) for the MP2-CAS single points
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals: two p-pi orbitals plus two sigma(C-C) and two sigma*(C-C) orbitals. For hydrogen-shift processes one C-C sigma/sigma* pair is replaced by the C-H sigma and sigma* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: A fixed-SIZE (6,6) space is used throughout, but its ORBITAL CONTENT is chosen to match the bonds broken in each reaction type. For the ring-opening photoisomerizations the six orbitals are 'two p-pi orbitals plus two sigma(C-C) and two sigma*(C-C) orbitals'. For hydrogen-shift processes the composition changes: 'In some hydrogen shift molecules, their active space is chosen as two p-pi orbitals plus two sigma (i.e., C-C and C-H) and two sigma* (i.e., C-C and C-H) orbitals' — one C-C sigma/sigma* pair is swapped for a C-H pair so the migrating hydrogen's bond is active. State-averaged CASSCF(6,6) was used for geometries in the intersection space, with conical intersections optimized in the (f-2)-dimensional intersection space by the method of Bearpark et al. Every stationary point was characterized by analytically computed harmonic frequencies, and every transition state was confirmed by an IRC calculation at the CASSCF level. Localization of minima, transition states, conical intersection minima and the IRC mapping was performed in MASS-WEIGHTED CARTESIAN coordinates 'therefore, the results are independent of any specific choice of internal variables'. Dynamic correlation was added by the multireference Moller-Plesset algorithm (MP2-CAS) at the CASSCF geometries.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged for the intersection-space optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol at MP2-CAS(6,6)/6-311G(d,p)//CAS(6,6)/6-311G(d), with bare CASSCF values in parentheses, referenced to cyclopropene: FC-1 (S1) 168.9 (199.6); Int-1 (S1) 108.6 (94.57); TS-1 (S1) 120.8 (109.2); CI-t-1 (S1/S0) 67.23 (50.83); TS-1' (S1) 120.5 (106.3); CI-c-1 (S1/S0) 65.47 (49.20); Int-t-2 (S0) 53.78 (35.44); Int-c-2 (S0) 52.71 (69.23); TS-t-2 (S0) 70.46 (62.64); TS-c-2 (S0) 60.89 (52.20); TS-t-3 (S0) 31.61 (42.12); TS-c-3 (S0) 61.54 (65.42); allene (2) -13.15 (-15.32); propyne (3) -25.84 (-32.18). The photoisomerization proceeds from the Franck-Condon point through Int-1 and a transition state to a conical intersection, then relaxes to the ground state where 1,2-hydrogen migration through TS-c-2 or TS-t-2 gives allene or propyne. Barriers of 17 kcal/mol for allene formation (path 2) and 8.2 kcal/mol for propyne formation (path 1) were computed, with products more stable than the reactant by 13 and 26 kcal/mol. The barrier to path 1 exceeds that for path 2 by 8.5 kcal/mol, so path 2 is favoured and allene should be formed in higher quantum yield. Two thermal (dark) pathways were also characterized: TS-c-3 lies 62 kcal/mol above the ground-state minimum and only 4.0 kcal/mol below the conical intersection CI-c-1, while TS-t-3 connecting cyclopropene to propyne lies 32 kcal/mol above, making thermal path 3 the more favourable. The vertical excitation is 173 kcal/mol at CAS(6,6) dropping to 152 kcal/mol after MP2-CAS correction, against an observed absorption band at 193 nm (148 kcal/mol).
Other: Cyclopropene shows the MP2-CAS correction acting in OPPOSITE directions on different parts of the same surface, which rules out any uniform rescaling of the CASSCF energies. Among the ground-state intermediates the split is starker still: Int-c-2 drops 16.5 kcal/mol while its trans partner Int-t-2 rises 18.3, a 35 kcal/mol relative swing between two structures differing only in configuration. That keeps every barrier on the same six-orbital footing while ensuring the bond actually breaking is always active. What makes this paper quantitatively useful is that both CASSCF and MP2-CAS energies are tabulated for every stationary point, so the size of the correlation correction can be read off directly — and it is neither small nor uniform. For cyclopropene the Franck-Condon point drops 30.7 kcal/mol on adding MP2-CAS (199.6 to 168.9), while the conical intersections RISE by about 16 kcal/mol (49.20 to 65.47 and 50.83 to 67.23). Several ground-state structures move in opposite directions: Int-c-2 falls 16.5 kcal/mol while Int-t-2 rises 18.3. The consequence is that no uniform shift maps the CASSCF surface onto the correlated one, and at least one qualitative conclusion changes with it — for trimethylcyclopropene the CI-3 intersection sits at 85.95 kcal/mol at CASSCF but 61.93 at MP2-CAS, a 24 kcal/mol drop that moves it from clearly inaccessible to competitive with CI-2. notes: Thermolysis of cyclopropenes is known to give products consistent with initial ring opening to vinylcarbene intermediates. Figures 2 and 3 show the CASSCF geometries with the gradient difference and derivative coupling vectors at the conical intersections.

geometry_source: Stationary points on the S0 and S1 surfaces optimized at CASSCF/6-311G(d), with state-averaged CASSCF(6,6) for geometries in the intersection space and conical intersections optimized by the Bearpark method. All stationary points characterized by analytical harmonic frequencies (all real for minima, one imaginary for transition states), with optimization converged when the maximum force and its RMS fell below 0.00045 and 0.00005 hartree/bohr. Every transition state was verified by a CASSCF IRC calculation. All localizations and IRC mapping performed in mass-weighted Cartesian coordinates.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies with multireference Moller-Plesset (MP2-CAS) single-point energies
basis_set: 6-311G(d) for the CASSCF geometries; 6-311G(d,p) for the MP2-CAS single points
active_space_orbital_description: The same six-electron, six-orbital construction as for the parent: two p-pi orbitals plus two sigma and two sigma* orbitals, with the sigma pairs chosen as C-C for ring opening or including a C-H pair for hydrogen-shift processes.
active_space_protocol: A fixed-SIZE (6,6) space is used throughout, but its ORBITAL CONTENT is chosen to match the bonds broken in each reaction type. For hydrogen-shift processes the composition changes: 'In some hydrogen shift molecules, their active space is chosen as two p-pi orbitals plus two sigma (i.e., C-C and C-H) and two sigma* (i.e., C-C and C-H) orbitals' — one C-C sigma/sigma* pair is swapped for a C-H pair so the migrating hydrogen's bond is active. compound_name: Cyclohexene — conical intersections leading to carbene formation via [1,2]-hydrogen and [1,2]-carbon shifts
geometry_source: Conical intersections optimized at CAS(6,6)/6-31G* using the Gaussian94 algorithm that locates the lowest energy point on an (n-2)-dimensional crossing seam, with state-averaged orbitals weighted 0.5:0.5 at all intersection structures. Reactant-region stationary points optimized at CAS(8,8)/6-31G*. Gradient difference and derivative coupling vectors were produced as part of the intersection optimization and indicate the ground-state reaction paths available after decay.
method: CASSCF (complete active space SCF) with two different active spaces for the intersection and reactant regions
active_space_orbital_description: For the conical intersections, six electrons in six orbitals: the pi, pi*, sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C=C bond plus the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-H or C-C bond being cleaved. For the reactant region, eight electrons in eight orbitals: the same four C=C orbitals plus the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the two adjacent C-C or C-H sigma bonds.
active_space_protocol: TWO active spaces of different size are used for two different regions of the surface, and within the larger one the composition is varied deliberately. Conical intersections following alpha-cleavage of either C-C or C-H bonds were optimized with a (6,6): 'The six active orbitals included the pi-, pi*-, sigma-, and sigma*-orbitals in the C=C bond and the sigma- and sigma*-orbitals in the C-H or C-C bond that is cleaved.' The REACTANT regions used a (8,8): 'The pi-, pi*-, sigma-, and sigma*-orbitals in the double bond were included, along with the sigma- and sigma*-orbitals of the two adjacent C-C or C-H sigma bonds.' Crucially, in the reactant region the two variants were run SEPARATELY and both reported — Table 2 gives values 'in regular type' for geometries optimized with an active space containing the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the adjacent C-C bonds and 'in italic type' for those containing the adjacent C-H bonds, so the same structure appears twice with different active orbitals. State-averaged orbitals with 0.5:0.5 weighting were used at all conical intersection structures. Intersections were optimized on the (n-2)-dimensional crossing seam with the gradient difference and derivative coupling vectors produced as part of the procedure. The lack of dynamic correlation is acknowledged and defended: 'previous results by the Martinez group have shown that the qualitative features of the potential energy surfaces are unchanged when this is taken into consideration ... we believe that the inclusion of dynamic correlation will not greatly affect our overall conclusions.'
nroots_per_mult: 2, state-averaged with 0.5:0.5 weighting at the conical intersections
electronic_structure_description: CAS(6,6)/6-31G* relative energies in kcal/mol, with S1 then S0 values at each intersection, referenced to the ground-state reactant. HYDROGEN SHIFT: type I conical intersection (1a) 130.7 and 130.7; type III (1b) 135.1 and 135.0; type II (1c) 134.5 and 134.5; carbene product 78.0. CARBON SHIFT: type III (3a) 127.0 and 126.9, and a second type III (3b) 127.3 and 127.2; type II (3c) 128.3 and 128.3; carbene products 88.2 (cis) and 89.0 (trans). For comparison, ethene at the same level gives type I at 127.5/127.2, type II at 146.7/146.7 and a carbene product at 80.6. In the hydrogen migration series the degree of migration is indicated by the H5C3C2 angle, varying from 46 degrees in the type I structure to 116 degrees in the type II structure, closely matching the 47 and 113 degrees found for ethene; the breaking C-H bond is 1.22 A in the cyclohexene type I intersection against 1.23 A in ethene. From Table 2, the S1 second-order saddle point lies at 198.1 kcal/mol with the C-C sigma orbitals in the active space and 196.6 with the C-H orbitals, and the Z/V conical intersection (5e) at 161.5 (S2) and 161.4 (S1) kcal/mol. Three types of conical intersection minimum were located — type I near the excited-state reactant after partial hydrogen migration, type II near the carbene product, and a type III at intermediate geometries arising most probably from steric constraints — indicating a HYPERLINE of crossing points extending from reactant to carbene product, along which decay can in principle occur anywhere.
Other: Cyclohexene is where the two-space design shows its logic most clearly. The intersections need only the breaking bond and the double bond, so a (6,6) suffices; the reactant region has two adjacent sigma bonds either of which could break, so an (8,8) is used and — importantly — is run in both compositions, once with the adjacent C-C sigma/sigma* pair active and once with the C-H pair. The second-order saddle point comes out at 198.1 and 196.6 kcal/mol respectively, a 1.5 kcal/mol difference, and publishing both is what demonstrates the choice is immaterial rather than merely asserting it. The three intersection types spanning 127 to 135 kcal/mol for cyclohexene establish a continuous crossing seam rather than isolated funnels, which is the paper's central structural claim and one that only a space following the migrating bond could reveal. Note that the carbon-shift intersections (126-128 kcal/mol) all lie BELOW the hydrogen-shift ones (130-135), the reverse of the product stabilities (88-89 versus 78 kcal/mol), so kinetic and thermodynamic preferences oppose each other here.  The methodological point worth recording here is that the same stationary point is computed TWICE with different active orbitals and both numbers are published. In the reactant region the (8,8) can contain either the adjacent C-C sigma/sigma* pair or the adjacent C-H pair, and Table 2 reports both: the cyclohexene second-order saddle point comes out at 198.1 kcal/mol with C-C orbitals active and 196.6 with C-H, and the norbornene one at 190.6 versus 189.3. A 1.3-1.5 kcal/mol spread is small, and reporting it rather than picking one is what lets a reader see that the choice does not matter here. The rest of the protocol is the familiar reaction-coordinate-matched design: the (6,6) at the intersections always contains the sigma/sigma* pair of the bond actually being cleaved, so a C-H shift and a C-C shift are described by analogous but not identical spaces. That is necessary — a space without the breaking bond cannot follow the migration — but it means the C-shift and H-shift columns of Table 1 are not strictly the same calculation, and their comparison carries that caveat. The authors are explicit that dynamic correlation is absent and defend the omission on the grounds that they are 'primarily interested in the existence of the crossing points and the mechanisms involved in reaching them' rather than in precise relative energies, citing Martinez group results that the qualitative surface features survive. Given the 20 kcal/mol gaps the conclusions rest on, that is a reasonable position, but every energy in this work is bare CASSCF. The comparison against ethene at the same level is the internal control: the type I intersection geometries agree closely (H5C3C2 angles of 47 and 46 degrees, breaking C-H bonds of 1.23 and 1.22 A), confirming that the ring systems are being described consistently with the reference molecule.
reference_short: Wilsey & Houk, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2002, 124, 11182
notes: The conical intersections located here are described as very different from the H/allyl and alkyl/allyl structures found previously. Figures 1 and 3 show the CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* optimized structures for the hydrogen and carbon shifts respectively, with gradient difference and derivative coupling vectors. Experimental conical intersection energies of 118 kcal/mol for cyclohexene are referenced, about 20 kcal/mol below the computed structures.
correlation_correction: None — CASSCF only; the authors argue from earlier work that qualitative surface features are unchanged by dynamic correlation

compound_name: Naphthalene radical cation — excited-state decay through sloped conical intersections
point_group: D2h; the pi-electronic states belong to the Au, B1u, B3g and B2g irreducible representations
geometry_source: CASSCF(9,10)/6-31G* geometry optimizations started from CASSCF/STO-3G optimized geometries. The D1 minimum was optimized with state-averaged orbitals equally weighting D0 and D1 to prevent root flipping, then re-optimized without state averaging by constraining the molecule to D2h and the state to B1u. The D0 and D2 minima were confirmed as true minima by numerical frequency calculations; this was not feasible for D1 because the symmetry constraint needed to optimize it would be broken by the numerical frequencies. Conical intersection optimizations require state-averaged orbitals. CASSCF energies were recomputed with cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVTZ without re-optimizing geometries.
method: CASSCF with single-point pi-MRCI and CASPT2 for dynamic correlation
software: Gaussian (without symmetry restrictions) and MOLPRO (with symmetry restrictions); the symmetry-restricted MOLPRO results are the ones quoted for energy, geometry and gradient vectors
basis_set: 6-31G* for the geometry optimizations, chosen as flexible enough for a good qualitative description of covalent excited states; cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVTZ for single-point energies and basis-set convergence analysis
active_space_orbital_description: Nine pi electrons distributed in the ten valence pi orbitals — the full pi valence space of the naphthalene cation.
active_space_protocol: A full pi-valence CASSCF(9,10) is used throughout, so the space itself has no selection freedom. Dynamic correlation is then probed by TWO different multireference methods chosen so their difference is diagnostic: pi-MRCI uses single and double excitations out of the valence pi orbitals only, while CASPT2 uses single and double excitations out of the FULL valence space. 'Comparison between the two multireference methods allowed analysis of the contribution from excitations between the sigma- and pi-orbitals (sigma-pi polarization).' Both were run with 6-31G*, cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVTZ to check basis-set convergence, since large polarized basis sets are known to matter for recovering dynamic correlation.
nroots_per_mult: 2, state-averaged with equal weights for the D1 minimum and for all conical intersection optimizations
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(9,10)/6-31G* energies in kcal/mol relative to D0 at the optimized D0 minimum, given as D0, D1, D2, D3 then the adiabatic excitation energy Te: at the D0 minimum 0.0, 18.8, 47.6, 67.2, Te 0.0; at the D1 minimum 8.0, 10.8, 51.3, 69.0, Te 10.8; at the D2 minimum 3.5, 18.1, 44.0, 70.2, Te 44.0; at the D3 minimum 2.4, 15.0, 48.8, 65.6, Te 65.6; at the D0/D1 conical intersection 12.4, 12.4, 54.0, 70.8; at the D1/D2 conical intersection 31.1, 68.0, 68.0, 88.4. Comparative energies across methods (CASSCF(9,10) then pi-MRCI then CASPT2, each with 6-31G* and cc-pVTZ): D0 to D1 vertical 18.8/18.6, 20.7/21.1, 23.5/23.4; D0 to D1 adiabatic 10.8 (12.2 state-averaged)/10.6, 13.0/13.5, 16.7/16.9; the D1-D0 gap at the D1 minimum 2.9/2.3, 2.6/5.0 and 5.5, 10.0/10.2; the D1-D0 gap at the D0/D1 intersection 0.0/0.3, 2.1/2.6, 7.5/7.8; D0 to D2 vertical 47.6/46.8, 48.9, 47.6/46.9; D0 to D2 adiabatic 44.0/43.5, 45.4, 43.7/43.4; the D2-D1 gap at the D2 minimum 25.8/24.7, 24.5, 20.1/19.4; the D2-D1 gap at the D1/D2 intersection 0.0/0.3, -1.6, -6.0/-6.6. Both the D0/D1 and D1/D2 crossings are found to be SLOPED, with the two states having almost parallel energy gradients. The CASPT2 D0 to D1 adiabatic excitation energy of 16.9 kcal/mol lies within 1 kcal/mol of the experimental I2-I1 photoelectron ionization energy of 17.9 kcal/mol. Analysis of the excited-state wave functions shows the three lowest states arise from occupation of different valence pi orbitals; the percentage contributions of the major configurations to D0 through D3 are given for the five valence bonding pi orbitals.
Other: The full pi-valence (9,10) leaves no orbital-selection question, so this paper turns the diagnostic elsewhere: it runs pi-MRCI and CASPT2 side by side specifically because their difference isolates sigma-pi polarization — pi-MRCI correlates only within the pi space while CASPT2 correlates the full valence. The answer is that sigma-pi polarization dominates. At the D1 minimum the D1-D0 gap is 2.9 kcal/mol at CASSCF, 5.0 at pi-MRCI and 10.0 at CASPT2, and at the D0/D1 intersection it goes 0.0, 2.1, 7.5 — so the pi-only correction recovers roughly a third of the effect and the sigma-pi part supplies the rest, with the authors noting this suggests 'some extra ionic character in these states'. The consequence for the mechanism is severe and honestly reported: the CASSCF D1/D2 crossing is degenerate by construction, but at CASPT2 the gap at that same geometry OPENS to -6.0 kcal/mol, meaning the CASSCF-optimized crossing point is not a crossing at the correlated level. Because the two states have near-parallel gradients there, the authors estimate by linear interpolation that the true CASPT2 crossing lies more than 10 kcal/mol lower, and state plainly that resolving it 'would require CASPT2 re-optimization of the D1/D2 crossing geometry. However, at the present time, there are no available, implemented procedures for optimization of conical intersection geometries using CASPT2 gradients.' That is the general limitation this row records: a conical intersection optimized on a CASSCF surface can move substantially once dynamic correlation is added, and for sloped crossings with parallel gradients the displacement is largest and least correctable.
reference_short: Hall, Boggio-Pasqua, Bearpark & Robb, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 13591
notes: Sloped conical intersections, in which the two states have almost parallel gradients, are associated with photostability because decay through them returns population to the excited state rather than funnelling it to the ground state. A similar dynamic correlation effect was seen in the ionic S2 state of pyracylene. Several matrix-isolated electronic spectra of the naphthalene cation are available for comparison. The largest geometric change along the path to the D0/D1 intersection is described as a remarkable compression, with distortions increasing progressively along the reaction path. The unusually high energy of the D1/D2 crossing structure is discussed in terms of its geometry.
correlation_correction: Single-point pi-MRCI (single and double excitations from the valence pi orbitals) and CASPT2 (single and double excitations from the full valence space), each with three basis sets

compound_name: Glyoxal (S1) with argon — collision-induced intersystem crossing
point_group: C2h (planar in the S0, S1 and T1 states)
geometry_source: Geometries of the S0, S1 and T1 states optimized with the eight-in-six CASSCF method, with zero-point energies from the same level. For the interaction calculations the glyoxal geometry was FIXED at the isolated-molecule S1 optimized structure, since the region of interest is where the interaction energy is sufficiently low. Roughly 150 points were sampled over a quarter sphere by symmetry: r from 3.0 to 6.0 A in 0.5 A steps, theta from 0 to 90 degrees and phi from -90 to 90 degrees, both in 30 degree steps.
method: CASSCF with multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) including Davidson and Pople corrections; full CI within the same active space for the T1 interaction energies; Breit-Pauli spin-orbit interaction calculations on the resulting CI wave functions
basis_set: Gaussian basis sets of double-zeta plus polarization quality: Dunning-Raffenetti [9s5p1d/3s2p1d]/(3s1p/2s1p) for glyoxal and [12s8p/5s3p] for the argon atom
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in six orbitals. The individual orbitals are not itemized in the text.
active_space_protocol: A single eight-in-six CASSCF space is used for the geometries, frequencies and vibrational basis sets of both the S1 and T1 states. For the glyoxal-argon interaction energies the S1 orbitals were computed at this level and then a FULL CI was carried out within the same active space to obtain the T1 interaction energies — the paper notes 'the results for S1 by the full-CI calculations are identical as those by the eight-in-six CASSCF', so the full CI is exact within the space and serves to put both spin states on precisely the same orbital footing. The resulting CI wave functions for S1 and T1 were used directly in the spin-orbit interaction calculations. Separately, MRCI with Davidson or Pople corrections was used to improve the S0/S1/T1 energy differences.
electronic_structure_description: Optimized geometries (bond lengths in angstroms, angles in degrees), calculated then experimental: S0 r(C-H) 1.088 vs 1.132, r(C-C) 1.508 vs 1.526, r(C-O) 1.208 vs 1.212, angle CCH 116.2 vs 112.2, angle CCO 121.1 vs 121.2; S1 r(C-H) 1.077 vs 1.115, r(C-C) 1.419 vs 1.460, r(C-O) 1.281 vs 1.252, angle CCH 121.1 vs 114.0, angle CCO 120.4 vs 123.7; T1 r(C-H) 1.076, r(C-C) 1.435, r(C-O) 1.265, angle CCH 120.9, angle CCO 119.8. The discrepancy between calculated and experimental S1 geometries is 'attributed to the instability problem, i.e., the symmetry-broken solutions with a lower symmetry than the C2h nuclear framework exist in the CASSCF wave functions for the excited states. reference_short: Nakajima & Kato, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 10657
notes: The study computes cross sections for the S1 to T1 transition in glyoxal induced by collision with argon, combining the interaction potential with the spin-orbit interaction. Vibronic basis sets were constructed from the CASSCF vibrational analysis, and Franck-Condon factors between the S1 and T1 manifolds were required. correlation_correction: MRCI with Davidson or Pople energy corrections; full CI within the active space for the T1 interaction energies

compound_name: Protonated water H3O+ and H3O — dissociative recombination dynamics
point_group: C3v at the H3O+ equilibrium geometry; most trajectories are sampled in C1 symmetry
geometry_source: Trajectories propagated with a fourth-order symplectic integrator at a time step of 0.043 fs, with energies, forces and transition matrix elements computed on the fly. Initial geometries for 500 trajectories were sampled according to the vibrational normal modes of H3O+ at room temperature. The H3O+ equilibrium structure was also optimized at CCSD/aug-cc-pVTZ for calibration.
method: State-averaged CASSCF for on-the-fly surface-hopping molecular dynamics, with a separate minimal-space CASSCF for the initial conditions; CCSD and CCSD(T) used as calibration references
basis_set: 6-311G(d,p) for the full-valence trajectory calculations; 6-31G(d) for the CAS(2,2) initial conditions; aug-cc-pVTZ for the CCSD and CCSD(T) calibration
active_space_orbital_description: The trajectory space is the full valence space, stated as seven electrons in six orbitals, chosen so that all possible dissociation limits of H3O are described correctly. The initial-conditions space is a minimal two electrons in two orbitals.
active_space_protocol: TWO different active spaces are used deliberately, and the reason is a documented CASSCF failure mode for systems differing in electron count. The trajectory propagation uses a FULL VALENCE space: 'The CASSCF method contains seven electrons and six orbitals, that is, a CAS(7,6)/6-311G(d,p) method. The full valence electrons are active in self-consistent field calculations so that all possible dissociation limits of H3O can be described correctly.' (The paper also refers to this same full-valence trajectory space as CAS(6,7) elsewhere in the text.) The INITIAL CONDITIONS instead use a minimal CAS(2,2)/6-31G(d), because of an imbalance identified in earlier work: 'the CASSCF method poorly balances the correlation energy between H3O+ and H3O because of the different number of electrons. As a result, their relative energy cannot be accurately represented by a consistent CASSCF approach. In order to get better vertical potential energies, instead of the CAS(6,6)/6-311G(d,p) method, we used the CAS(2,2)/6-31G(d) method to compute the potential energy surfaces and forces of both H3O+ and e--H3O+ systems.' The minimal space was not assumed adequate but CALIBRATED: 'The specific combination was selected by comparing the equilibrium geometry of H3O+ and its vertical affinity potentials with those calculated with a high-level ab initio method CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ.' The division of labour is stated explicitly: 'the CAS(2,2) method is used only for the initial conditions of H3O+ while the trajectory calculations are performed by use of the full valence electron CAS(6,7) method. At the beginning of each trajectory, the H3O+ ion vibrates near its equilibrium structure, where the potential energy surface of CAS(2,2) is as good as that of CCSD(T) except for a vertical energy shift.' State-averaged CASSCF supplies energies, forces and transition matrix elements on the fly; surface hopping is limited to the propagating state and its two adjacent states in energy, so only those nonadiabatic coupling elements are needed.
multiplicities_studied: singlet for H3O+; doublet for H3O
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged; surface hopping restricted to the propagating state and its two energetically adjacent states
electronic_structure_description: CAS(2,2)/6-31G(d) gives a ground-state H3O+ (X 1A1) electronic energy of -76.30673489 au with equilibrium geometry r(OH) = 0.9705 A and angle HOH = 111.7 degrees in C3v symmetry. At CAS(7,6)/6-311G(d,p) the vertical affinity potentials of H3O+ to the low-lying doublets of H3O are 4.958, 2.094, 2.094 and -4.914 eV; the second and third states are a doubly degenerate E state that splits into two A states in C1 symmetry, giving four vibrationally averaged levels. CCSD/aug-cc-pVTZ gives r(OH) = 0.9758 A and angle HOH = 111.7 degrees with a vertical affinity potential of 5.208 eV for ground-state H3O, and CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ at that geometry gives 5.261 eV, in good agreement with the CAS values. Four product channels are open for dissociative recombination. Calculated branching fractions, compared with earlier calculations and four experiments: H2O + H 0.230 (this work) against 0.10 and 1.0 calculated and 0.18, 0.25, 0.33, 0.05 measured; OH + H2 0.108 against 0.015 and 0.0 calculated and 0.11, 0.14, 0.18, 0.36 measured; OH + 2H 0.660 against 0.87 and 0.0 calculated and 0.67, 0.60, 0.48, 0.29 measured; O + H + H2 0.002 against 0.015 and 0.0 calculated and 0.04, 0.01, 0.01, 0.30 measured. Total energies are conserved within 0.05 eV. The affinity potentials to excited states are about 1.83 and 2.45 eV. The eliminated hydrogen atoms show a bimodal kinetic energy distribution: atoms with kinetic energy above 3.5 eV are directly eliminated leaving vibrationally cold H2O, while a slower channel gives vibrationally excited intermediates that undergo unimolecular dissociation into OH and H, producing vibrationally cold OH and a slow hydrogen atom. One trajectory survived 88 fs before dissociating into OH and H at 102 fs. A major peak appears at 1.5 eV in the kinetic energy distribution.
Other: This paper documents a rarely stated CASSCF limitation: the method 'poorly balances the correlation energy between H3O+ and H3O because of the different number of electrons', so a single consistent CASSCF cannot give their relative energy accurately. Since a dissociative recombination calculation is precisely a comparison between an ion and its neutral, that imbalance strikes the central quantity — the vertical affinity potential. The fix adopted is a deliberate SPLIT: a minimal CAS(2,2) for the initial conditions of H3O+, calibrated against CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ and found to differ only by a vertical energy shift near equilibrium, and the full valence CAS(7,6) for the trajectories, chosen so that every dissociation limit of H3O is representable. That is the general principle worth carrying: a full valence space is needed to describe bond breaking, but a full valence space applied to two species with different electron counts recovers different fractions of correlation for each, so an ion-neutral energy gap should be taken from a calibrated smaller space or from a single-reference benchmark instead. The calibration is real — CAS gives 4.958 eV for the vertical affinity against CCSD 5.208 and CCSD(T) 5.261 — and the payoff is branching fractions (0.230, 0.108, 0.660, 0.002) that track three of the four experimental sets closely, with the paper noting the OH + 2H fraction remains overestimated. Note also a labelling inconsistency in the source: the same full-valence trajectory space is written as CAS(7,6) in the methods and CAS(6,7) later, and the space being replaced for initial conditions is called CAS(6,6).
reference_short: Yu, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 6555
notes: The method is a spherical electron cloud hopping molecular dynamics simulation. Restricting surface hopping to the propagating state and its two adjacent states follows earlier work by Taketsugu and co-workers and saves computing only the nearby nonadiabatic coupling matrix elements. The third excited state of H3O always lies above the ground state of H3O+ at the sampled geometries. Trajectories violating energy conservation by more than about 0.05 eV were discarded. The sequential hydrogen elimination mechanism is compared with earlier work on H3O+(H2O)n cluster ions.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF itself; CCSD and CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ were used to calibrate the choice of the smaller active space

compound_name: cis-Penta-2,4-dieniminium cation (model 1) — retinal protonated Schiff base model with and without acetate counterion
geometry_source: Reaction paths and geometry optimizations at the CASPT2//CASSCF/6-31G* level, with the reaction coordinate computed at CASSCF and the energy profile from single-point CASPT2 at selected points and stationary structures. Minimum energy paths computed in mass-weighted coordinates using the full set of vibrational degrees of freedom.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF reaction paths and geometries with single-point CASPT2 energies
basis_set: 6-31G*, validated against 6-31+G* which showed no appreciable difference in energetics or force field
active_space_orbital_description: The full pi system of the protonated Schiff base. The acetate counterion contributes no active orbitals — its full set of orbitals is placed in the core and virtual space.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by a chemical rule and the counterion is deliberately EXCLUDED from it: 'The selected CAS active space comprises the full pi-system of the PSB. On the other hand, the full set of acetate anion orbitals are enclosed in the core and virtual space.' For the longer model the space is the pi 8e/8o. Because the acetate contributes no active orbitals, the counterion acts on the chromophore purely through its electrostatic field and through geometry, and the same space describes the isolated chromophore and every counterion arrangement. The state averaging is varied as needed rather than fixed: 'The single-state CASSCF computations have been used for excited states when possible, while a state average procedure between two (S0, S1) or three (S0, S1, S2) roots has been used (with identical weights) in all other cases to avoid CASSCF convergence problems.' The CASPT2 zeroth-order wave functions are three-root (S0, S1, S2) state-averaged CASSCF unless stated otherwise, with core orbitals always frozen. The basis set was calibrated against the active space rather than assumed: 'A preliminary calibration analysis performed by comparing calculations with a diffuse functions expanded basis set (6-31+G*) has shown that no appreciable differences exist on both the energetics and the force field, justifying the use of the less demanding 6-31G* basis set.' Reaction coordinates are minimum energy paths in mass-weighted coordinates using the full set of vibrational degrees of freedom.
nroots_per_mult: Single-state where possible; two-root (S0, S1) or three-root (S0, S1, S2) equal-weight state averaging elsewhere to avoid convergence problems. CASPT2 zeroth-order wave functions are three-root state-averaged unless stated otherwise
electronic_structure_description: CASPT2 energies with CASSCF reference weights and relative energies in eV (kcal/mol in parentheses) for the isolated model 1: Franck-Condon point FC1 with S0 at -248.97481 au (weight 0.81, 0.00), S1 at -248.82949 (0.78, 3.95 eV / 91.2 kcal/mol), S2 at -248.77806 (0.79, 5.35 eV / 123.5); stationary point SP1 with S0 -248.95472 (0.80, 0.55 / 12.6), S1 -248.83946 (0.78, 3.68 / 84.9), S2 -248.80134 (0.79, 4.72 / 108.9); twisted minimum TM21 with S0 -248.88532 (0.80, 2.44 / 56.2), S1 -248.83888 (0.79, 3.70 / 85.3), S2 -248.79128 (0.69, 4.99 / 115.2); conical intersection CI1 with S0 -248.88909 (0.79, 2.33 / 53.8), S1 -248.88728 (0.80, 2.38 / 54.9), S2 -248.76610 (0.78, 5.68 / 131.0); twisted minimum TM11 with S0 -248.90188 (0.79, 1.98 / 45.8), S1 -248.85088 (0.78, 3.37 / 77.8), S2 -248.75701 (0.70, 5.93 / 136.7). Three counterion arrangements were studied: Central, above the chromophore backbone (1a); closer to the C-tail (1b); and closer to the N-head (1c). The shorter models 1a, 1b and 1c give results similar to the longer models.
Other: Model 1 establishes the counterion-free reference against which every environmental effect in the study is measured, and its value depends on the space containing only the chromophore pi system. Two features of the tabulated data deserve attention. The S1 and S0 energies at CI1 differ by only 0.05 eV (1.1 kcal/mol) at CASPT2, so the CASSCF-optimized intersection survives the perturbative correction here — unlike many cases where a correlated treatment opens the gap substantially. And the CASPT2 reference weights fall to 0.69-0.70 for S2 at the two twisted minima TM21 and TM11 while remaining 0.78-0.81 elsewhere, marking those points as where the three-root reference is under most strain.  The design decision that carries this study is excluding the acetate counterion from the active space entirely — 'the full set of acetate anion orbitals are enclosed in the core and virtual space' — so that the space is the full pi system of the chromophore and nothing else. That is what makes the counterion effects measurable: every model, isolated or with acetate in any of the three positions, is described by an identical set of active orbitals, so differences in excitation energy, barrier height and intersection topology are attributable to the electrostatic field and geometry rather than to a changing correlated space. The cost is that no charge transfer between chromophore and counterion can appear in the wave function, which is a real restriction for an ion pair; the paper's own finding that the relaxed planar structure in one arrangement 'has a charge-transfer character' is therefore describing intramolecular charge transfer within the pi system, not chromophore-to-acetate transfer. The CASPT2 reference weights are reported for every state and structure, running 0.69 to 0.81, and the lowest values (0.69-0.72) occur consistently for S2 at the twisted geometries — so the perturbative correction is least secure exactly where the states are most strongly mixed. The state-average protocol is honest about being pragmatic: single-state where possible, two- or three-root averaging elsewhere 'to avoid CASSCF convergence problems', with the details relegated to tables. That means not every energy in the paper rests on the same reference, and comparisons across structures should be checked against those tables.

notes: The shorter of two retinal protonated Schiff base models. Reference structures for the intrinsic photochemistry of the chromophore in the absence of environmental effects. Detailed results for 1a, 1b and 1c are given in the Supporting Information; the longer model 2 series is documented extensively in the main text.

compound_name: E-Azobenzene — photoisomerization from the n-pi* and pi-pi* singlets
geometry_source: Fully unconstrained CASSCF geometry optimizations and minimum energy path computations, with single-point CASPT2 on the optimized structures. Conical intersections located by minimizing the two-root state-averaged CASSCF energy in the (n-2)-dimensional intersection space orthogonal to the branching-space directions x1 and x2.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF optimizations and minimum energy paths with single-point CASPT2 corrections; CASSI for transition dipole moments
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve orbitals: ten pi-system orbitals and electrons plus the two doubly occupied nitrogen lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: The paper opens its active space discussion with a statement of principle — 'The active space choice is a crucial step in a CASSCF calculation' — and then gives the composition: 'our choice was to include 10 orbitals and electrons of the pi system plus the two doubly occupied nitrogen lone pairs, resulting in an active space of 12 orbitals and 14 electrons.' So (14,12): the full azo/phenyl pi manifold plus BOTH nitrogen lone pairs, the latter being what makes the n-pi* states representable alongside the pi-pi* ones. The state-averaging protocol is layered. Geometry optimizations and minimum energy paths use single-state CASSCF 'when possible; otherwise, when root flipping problems occurred, state average calculations have been the choice'. CASPT2 and CASSCF relative energies in kcal/mol with the CASSCF dominant-configuration weight, referenced to the ground-state minimum: E-Min S1 with S0 at 17.0/16.1 (weight 0.63) and S1 at 46.3/59.1; E-TS S1 with S0 30.7/35.6 and S1 47.7/62.0; the torsional conical intersections CItors-1 with S0 52.1/61.1 and S1 47.4/56.8, CItors-2 with S0 50.9/59.3 and S1 45.2/56.2, CItors-3 with S0 58.7/70.8 and S1 51.6/64.6; the inversion intersections E-CIinv with S0 74.0/87.0 and S1 70.3/80.9, and E-CId-inv with S0 85.6/92.9 and S1 71.0/84.7; the S3/S2 intersection E-CI with S0 9.0/13.7, S1 64.6/83.1, S2 92.3/129.6 and S3 93.4/110.7; the S2/S1 intersections E-1-CI with S1 88.0/107.7 and S2 89.3/107.5, and E-2-CI with S1 83.9/108.0 and S2 88.5/108.2; Min S2 with S0 47.7/64.4, S1 38.3/48.5 and S2 57.8/76.0; E-Min 2Bu with S0 9.4/15.4, S1 63.8/83.0, S2 88.9/116.4, S3 89.6/114.4 and S4 92.5/136.7. Those are different wave functions, so an intersection located under one average is being described energetically under another. That is standard practice and the paper is explicit about it, but it means the degeneracy at a CI structure is not guaranteed to be exactly reproduced in the tabulated nine-root energies — and indeed several tabulated S1/S0 pairs at the CItors structures differ by 3-7 kcal/mol.

Table 2 gives the vertical transition energies, wave function compositions and oscillator strengths of the lowest excited singlets at the planar Franck-Condon geometry.
