compound_name: Ga.N2 van der Waals complex — (1)2Delta excited state and low-lying quartet states
d_electron_count: The singly occupied delta orbitals of the 2Delta state originate essentially from the Ga 4d atomic orbitals, which are unoccupied in the ground-state configuration of atomic gallium
ligand_set: Molecular nitrogen bound as a van der Waals partner
point_group: C2v symmetry labels used for the orbital classification; linear and T-shaped structures both examined
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations and harmonic vibrational frequency calculations at CASSCF(3,6), UB3LYP, UMP2, UQCISD and UCCSD(T) levels for the 4Sigma- state, plus symmetry-equivalent restricted-spin Hartree-Fock (SERHF). Vertical excitation energies computed at CASSCF/MRCI and RCCSD(T) levels at higher-quality basis sets. Franck-Condon factors including Duschinsky rotation were computed from the force constants; one-dimensional anharmonic Franck-Condon factors were obtained by solving the vibrational problem with the program LEVEL on RCCSD(T) curves.
method: CASSCF with internally contracted MRCI (with Davidson correction) for the excited states; RCCSD and RCCSD(T) for benchmark energetics; SERHF, UB3LYP, UMP2 and UQCISD for comparison
software: MOLPRO for the CASSCF/MRCI and RCCSD(T) calculations; Gaussian98 for the DFT and other single-reference methods; GAMESS-UK for the SERHF calculations; LEVEL for the vibrational problem
basis_set: For the CASSCF/MRCI, an ECP[10s8p5d] basis for Ga with uncontracted 9s, 7p and 5d functions (highest exponents and ratios: s 0.65 and 2.75, p 0.9 and 3.0, d 0.25 and 3.0) with aug-cc-pVTZ (no f) on N. For RCCSD(T), ECP[11s10p6d5f] and ECP[11s10p6d5f3g] on Ga with aug-cc-pVQZ on N. For the SERHF work, Dunning-Hay split-valence sets [6s4p1d] for Ga and [3s2p] for N augmented with diffuse s, p, sp and d functions on Ga and s, p and d functions on N, the added Ga d functions designed to describe the 4d atomic orbital.
active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen valence electrons. For the X 2Pi and 4Sigma- states the space is seven sigma orbitals plus three sets of pi orbitals (b1 and b2 in C2v), i.e. thirteen orbitals. For the 2Delta state one set of pi is replaced by two delta orbitals (a2 in C2v), giving seven sigma, two sets of pi and two delta.
active_space_protocol: The active space is chosen SEPARATELY FOR EACH ELECTRONIC STATE according to which orbitals that state actually occupies, and the two choices are stated explicitly. 'The CASSCF calculations on the X 2Pi and 4Sigma- states considered 13 valence electrons within an active space of seven sigma and three sets of pi (b1 and b2 symmetry in the C2v point group) molecular orbitals. For the 2Delta state, an active space of seven sigma, two sets of pi, and two delta (a2 symmetry in the C2v point group) molecular orbitals was employed.' The reason is that the 2Delta state has a ...sigma(2)delta(1) configuration whose singly occupied doubly degenerate delta molecular orbitals 'originate essentially from the 4d atomic orbitals of Ga, which are unoccupied in the ground-state electronic configuration of atomic gallium' — so a space built for the ground state contains no delta orbital at all and cannot represent the excited state. One set of pi orbitals is traded for the two delta orbitals to keep the space size manageable. The internally contracted MRCI on each state uses 'the CASSCF orbitals of the corresponding state as the many-particle basis', so each state is correlated on its own optimized reference, with more than 430 uncontracted and 4.1 million internally contracted configurations per state. The basis set was designed around the same requirement: augmented d functions on Ga 'were designed to account adequately for the 4d atomic orbital of Ga, as shown from the wave function of an ROHF calculation on the 2Delta state'.
nroots_per_mult: Root 5 was targeted in the CASSCF(3,6) geometry optimizations of the 2Delta state
electronic_structure_description: Optimized geometries (angstroms) and harmonic frequencies (cm-1) of the ...sigma(2)delta(1) 2Delta state at four levels, given as r(GaN), r(NN), omega1(NN), omega2(sigma), omega3(pi): SERHF 3.1574, 1.0771, 2730.1, 71.3, 104.7; CASSCF(3,6, root 5)/6-31+G(2d)+diff 3.1669, 1.1071, 2752.2, 64.3, 120.7; CASSCF(3,6, root 5)/6-311+G(3d)+diff 3.2464, 1.0668, 2727.3, 62.1, 81.2; RCCSD(T)/ECP[7s7p5d2f], aug-cc-pVTZ 2.9626, 1.1032, with 85.0 cm-1 from a one-dimensional scan (the corresponding X 2Pi value being 47.0 cm-1). The X 2Pi geometries at those same levels are r(GaN) = 3.5329, 3.9015, 4.0090 and 3.3229 A. Vertical excitation energies from the X 2Pi state in eV and cm-1 for the 2Delta, 4Sigma- and 4Pi states: MRCI gives 3.832 (30904) for 2Delta and 3.237 (26107) for 4Sigma-; MRCI+Davidson gives 3.978 (32082) and 3.940 (31782); RCCSD at the same basis gives 3.988 (32162) and 4.214 (33988); RCCSD(T) 3.997 (32236) and 4.238 (34185). With the larger ECP[11s10p6d5f]/aug-cc-pVQZ(no g) basis, RCCSD(T) gives 3.937 (31751), 4.215 (33997) and 4.402 (35501) for the three states; with ECP[11s10p6d5f3g]/aug-cc-pVQZ, 3.936 (31748) and 4.217 (34016), and in a further variant 3.919 (31611), 4.187 (33773) and 4.463 (35999). The experimental values are 4.192 eV (33814 cm-1) and 4.727 eV (38123 cm-1). The computed Te for the 2Delta state is 3.92 eV (31617 cm-1) against an observed LIF band onset of 4.15 eV (33468 cm-1), agreement within about 0.2 eV. The counterpoise-corrected dissociation energy De of the 2Delta state is 1363.7 cm-1, agreeing very well with the D0' of 1270 +/- 60 cm-1 from a Birge-Sponer plot. Computed vertical excitation energies at different levels agree to within about 0.1 eV.
Other: Ga.N2 is a clean case of the active space having to be rebuilt for a different electronic state because the orbitals the state occupies are simply absent from the ground-state space. The 2Delta state has its unpaired electron in doubly degenerate delta orbitals that 'originate essentially from the 4d atomic orbitals of Ga, which are unoccupied in the ground-state electronic configuration of atomic gallium' — so the seven-sigma-plus-three-pi space used for X 2Pi and 4Sigma- contains no delta orbital and cannot represent 2Delta at all. The solution is to trade one set of pi orbitals for the two delta orbitals, keeping thirteen electrons and a comparable space size while making the target state representable. The consequence for interpretation is that the 2Delta and 4Sigma- vertical excitation energies come from DIFFERENT active spaces, so their MRCI values are not strictly comparable to each other — and indeed MRCI places 4Sigma- 0.6 eV below 2Delta while every coupled-cluster level places it 0.2-0.3 eV ABOVE, a reordering that the Davidson correction largely repairs (3.978 versus 3.940 eV). The basis set was designed to the same requirement, with augmented Ga d functions added specifically to describe the 4d orbital, verified against an ROHF wave function for the 2Delta state. Note also that the paper flags a general concern about mixing levels: the force constants for the multidimensional Franck-Condon factors came from CASSCF, 'a method which lacks dynamic electron correlation', while the one-dimensional anharmonic factors used higher-level RCCSD(T) curves, and the two simulations give vibrational intervals differing by about 30 cm-1.
reference_short: Lee, Dyke, Mok, Claridge & Chau, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 9533
notes: The study simulates the laser-induced fluorescence spectrum of Ga.N2 to test the assignment by Ellis et al. of two observed bands. The van der Waals potential was fitted to the form V = De - C5/R5 + C6/R6. A number of low-lying quartet states of both linear and T-shaped structures were also studied. The MRCI calculations used more than 430 uncontracted and 4.1 million internally contracted configurations per state.
correlation_correction: Internally contracted MRCI with Davidson correction on state-specific CASSCF orbitals; RCCSD and RCCSD(T) as independent benchmarks, with full counterpoise correction for BSSE in the dissociation energy

point_group: Cs imposed on the initial anti-conformation with flat methylenes rotated 90 degrees out of the CCOC plane; the conformational scan spans lower symmetry
geometry_source: The initial triplet geometry, constrained to Cs symmetry in an anti-conformation, was optimized at MP2/6-311+G(d). Spin-orbit coupling was mapped as a function of three torsional angles — alpha about C1-C2, beta about C2-O3 and gamma about O3-C4 — on a 15 degree grid, refined to 10 or 5 degrees in some regions. For the singlet-triplet gap the triplet geometry was reoptimized by a relaxed scan in beta from 0 to 180 degrees in 15 degree steps at MP2/6-311+G(d), with triplet and vertical singlet energies then computed at those geometries.
method: State-averaged MCSCF with a one-electron spin-orbit Hamiltonian using parametrized effective nuclear charges (Robb implementation), compared against complete one- and two-electron Breit-Pauli spin-orbit coupling with a fully optimized MCSCF triplet wave function and frozen-core singlet (Furlani implementation); CASSCF(6,6)-MP2 for the singlet-triplet energy separations
software: Gaussian 98 Revision A.6 and GAMESS; the Gaussian 98 spin-orbit integral module L319 was modified to update the effective nuclear charges
relativistic_treatment: Breit-Pauli spin-orbit Hamiltonian in the full one- and two-electron form, and a one-electron form with parametrized effective nuclear charges
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, chosen 'to include the two odd electrons and two oxygen lone pairs'.
active_space_protocol: A single (6,6) space is used for both the spin-orbit coupling calculations and the CASSCF-MP2 singlet-triplet gaps, and its composition is stated by function: the two odd electrons of the diradical plus the two oxygen lone pairs. The size was established by an explicit CONVERGENCE TEST reported in a footnote: 'Active space of 4-in-4 was clearly not sufficient; increasing it to 8-in-8 did not produce noticeable changes in calculated SOC values.' So (6,6) is a demonstrated plateau rather than a guess — too small at (4,4), converged by (6,6), and unimproved at (8,8). The same space is used at every point of a three-dimensional torsional scan, so conformational trends in spin-orbit coupling are measured against a fixed orbital description.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged MCSCF for the Gaussian 98 approach; a fully optimized MCSCF triplet with a frozen-core singlet for the GAMESS approach
electronic_structure_description: Spin-orbit coupling was mapped over three torsional coordinates. In the cisoid conformation of the C-C-O-C fragment the coupling has a clear maximum at (105;0;30) degrees, with a second peak at the enantiomeric geometry; as beta increases the maximum shifts toward smaller alpha as the C1 odd-electron orbital follows the C4 orbital. Two distinct regions of elevated spin-orbit coupling were identified. Comparing the two Hamiltonians, the full one- and two-electron coupling SOC(12) is about 55% of the one-electron value SOC(1), a uniform 45% reduction attributed mainly to one-centre two-electron contributions; the correlation between the two data sets is R-squared 0.96, supporting the view that two-centre one- and two-electron terms approximately cancel for light elements and justifying the effective-charge approach. Gaussian 98 values deviate from the GAMESS SOC(12) values by only 4% on average with R-squared 0.77, so the much cheaper state-averaged MCSCF with effective nuclear charges gives sensible results; the full treatment required about 3-4 times more CPU time per point. On the CASSCF(6,6)-MP2/6-311+G(d) triplet surface the gauche conformer at beta near 70 degrees, which is also a minimum spin-orbit coupling conformation, lies about 2 kcal/mol from the singlet surface. Barriers on the triplet surface are about 4 kcal/mol at beta = 0 and 2 kcal/mol at beta = 120 degrees, both surmountable at room temperature; the apparent high energy near beta = 0 in the rigid scan is an artefact of steric crowding, the relaxed barrier being about 4 kcal/mol. Rotation in beta toward either barrier simultaneously reduces the singlet-triplet gap and increases the spin-orbit matrix element, so the most favourable conditions for intersystem crossing are predicted at beta = 15-25 degrees and near 120 degrees. NBO population analysis shows considerable depletion of electron density in the oxygen 2p orbital for conformations with small gamma, coupled with increased spin density.
Other: This paper is unusually explicit about how its active space size was settled, and the answer is a bracketing test rather than an assertion: '(4,4) was clearly not sufficient; increasing it to (8,8) did not produce noticeable changes in calculated SOC values.' A (6,6) is therefore a demonstrated plateau — bounded below by a space that fails and above by one that changes nothing — which is the strongest justification a fixed space can have and is rarely reported. The composition follows the physics of the problem: the two odd electrons plus the two oxygen lone pairs, since the mechanism of spin-orbit coupling here is the roughly 90-degree alignment between an oxygen 2p orbital and the half-filled p orbital at the adjacent carbon, so the lone pairs are load-bearing rather than decorative. Holding that space fixed across a three-dimensional torsional scan is what makes the conformational map interpretable — every point in the (alpha, beta, gamma) space is described by the same orbitals, so the peaks and valleys reflect geometry alone. The paper also quantifies a separate approximation that often goes untested: the full one- and two-electron Breit-Pauli coupling is a uniform 55% of the one-electron effective-charge value with R-squared 0.96, confirming that the cheaper parametrized approach captures the conformational behaviour even though it overestimates the magnitude, because the missing one-centre two-electron contributions involve two core and two valence orbitals and so vary with geometry in the same way.
reference_short: Kutateladze, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2001, 123, 9279
notes: Paterno-Buchi photocycloaddition forms oxetanes via 1,4-diradicals detected experimentally in transient studies. Intersystem crossing in these diradicals is controlled by spin-orbit coupling, which is argued to dominate over electron-nuclear hyperfine coupling even in longer 1,n-diradicals. Two effects raise the coupling: a resonance shortening the average distance between unpaired electrons, and conformations giving roughly 90 degrees between the oxygen 2p orbital and the adjacent half-filled p orbital. The maximum spin-orbit coupling conformation is compared with that of trimethylene.
correlation_correction: CASSCF(6,6)-MP2 (multireference MP2 on the CASSCF reference) for the singlet-triplet energy separations

compound_name: 2,4,6-Tricyano-N,N-dimethylaniline (TCDMA) — absence of an excited-state intramolecular charge transfer reaction
point_group: C2 for the ground-state optimized geometry
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations performed using symmetry at the CASSCF and RASSCF levels with the 6-31G(d) basis set; harmonic frequencies computed with Gaussian. CASPT2 energies evaluated at the best RASSCF geometries with the cc-pVDZ basis. Solvent effects were not included.
method: CASSCF and RASSCF geometry optimization with CASPT2 single-point energies on a (6e,5o) reference
software: MOLPRO for the symmetry-based calculations; Gaussian for the harmonic frequencies
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF and RASSCF calculations; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2
active_space_orbital_description: A (6e,5o) CAS for the twisted structures and (4e,4o) for the nontwisted ones, following the precedent established for DMABN and ABN. These are embedded in RASSCF(20, 7+5+7)[2,2] or RASSCF(18, 7+4+7)[2,2] depending on whether the amino nitrogen lone pair is included, with up to double excitations allowed in the seven-orbital subspaces on either side. The chemically complete space would be (20e,19o), comprising six benzene pi orbitals, the amino nitrogen lone pair and twelve cyano pi orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The paper opens by stating what the CHEMICALLY correct space would be and then explains why it cannot be used: 'CASSCF calculations for TCDMA and TCA would require a (20e,19o) active space including the six benzene pi orbitals, the amino nitrogen lone pair, and the 12 cyano pi orbitals. This size of active space is well beyond current computational resources, and a different approach is therefore needed.' The retreat is justified by precedent: 'Dreyer and Kummrow have shown that active spaces of (4e,4o) and (6e,5o) were sufficient to describe qualitatively the nontwisted and twisted structures of DMABN and ABN. We employed a similar active space to optimize the structures corresponding to the different electronic states of TCDMA and TCA.' compound_name: Pd(2-thienylpyridine)2 — cyclometalated palladium(II) complex electronic spectrum
ligand_set: Two cyclometalated 2-thienylpyridine (thpy-) ligands, each formally negative and binding through carbon and nitrogen
point_group: C2v structures used for the spectral calculations; BP86-DFT optimizations performed in both C2v and C2
geometry_source: BP86-DFT geometry optimizations of the ground state in both C2v and C2 symmetry; the C2v structures were used for the electronic spectra. The molecules were placed in the yz plane so that sigma-type orbitals fall in a1 and b2 and pi orbitals in b1 and a2.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2, using the level-shifted LS-CASPT2 variant to handle intruder states; BP86-DFT for geometries
basis_set: Relativistic core ab initio model potentials (AIMP) replacing 30 electrons for Pd and 62 for Pt, with the corresponding [3s3p4d] valence basis sets of Barandiaran and Casarrubios. ANO-S basis sets of Pierloot for the remaining atoms, contracted to [3s2p1d] for C and N bound to the metal, [3s2p] for other C, [4s3p1d] for S and [2s] for H, giving 292 contracted basis functions in total; enlarged to [3s2p1d] on all C for the free thpyH calculations.
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic core ab initio model potentials (AIMP) on Pd and Pt
active_space_orbital_description: Sixteen electrons in twelve orbitals partitioned by symmetry as 4 a1, 3 b1, 2 b2 and 3 a2. The orbitals are the bonding and antibonding combinations of thpy sigma (mainly carbon lone pairs) with the metal d(yz) in b2 and with the metal s orbital in a1, the remaining four metal d orbitals (2 a1, b1, a2), and the HOMO-LUMO pair of thpy pi orbitals (2 b1, 2 a2). The full thpy pi valence set would require 14 more orbitals, giving 26 in total.
active_space_protocol: The paper states the two requirements an active space must satisfy — '(1) the resulting CASSCF wave function should include the most important correlation effects, and (2) orbitals involved in the excited states of interest should be included' — and then builds the space accordingly. For covalent metal-ligand interactions 'both the bonding and antibonding combination of metal and ligand orbitals have to be included', which here means the bonding and antibonding combinations of thpy sigma (mainly the carbon lone pairs) with Pd 4dyz or Pt 5dyz in b2 symmetry, and of thpy sigma with Pd 5s or Pt 6s in a1. Added to these are the remaining four d orbitals (2 a1, b1, a2) and the HOMO-LUMO pair of thpy pi orbitals (2 b1, 2 a2). This gives 'a total of 12 active orbitals (4 a1, 3 b1, 2 b2, 3 a2), populated with 16 electrons.' The paper is explicit about what it would rather have done: 'Ideally, one would of course like to include in the active space all thpy pi valence orbitals in order to get a better description of pi-pi* correlation effects and of the ligand centered excited states. This would, however, mean adding 14 more active orbitals, leading to an active space of 26 orbitals, which is far beyond the reach of today's computer power.' The resulting error was then MEASURED on a smaller system: 'To check the uncertainty on the excitation energies connected with the use of a limited thpy active space, test calculations on the lowest excited states of free C-protonated thpyH were performed with both a HOMO-LUMO (2 electrons in 2 orbitals) and a full valence pi (12 electrons in 11 orbitals) active space.' In the CASPT2 step 122 electrons are correlated, from Pd 4p and 4d or Pt 5p and 5d, C and N 2s and 2p, S 3s and 3p, and H 1s. 'As a result of limitations in the 12 orbital active space, quite strongly interacting intruder states appear in the CASPT2 calculations of some of the excited states', handled by the LS-CASPT2 level-shift technique with test calculations at several shift values. Reference wave functions were built from individually optimized CASSCF orbitals for each excited state in almost all cases.
nroots_per_mult: Individually optimized CASSCF orbitals for each excited state in almost all cases
electronic_structure_description: BP86-DFT ground-state structure: r(Pd-C) 2.01 A in C2v and 2.00 in C2, r(Pd-N) 2.24 and 2.20 A, C-Pd-C 97.1 and 97.3 degrees, C-Pd-N 80.3 and 80.7, N-Pd-N 102.4 and 103.9. Calculated excitation energies in cm-1 at CASSCF then CASPT2, with the dominant configurations and Mulliken metal populations: the a 3A1 state at 30903 CASSCF and 19689 CASPT2, ligand-centred, 8b1 to 10b1 (56%) and 7a2 to 9a2 (35%), with populations 4.86, 3.76 and 8.62; a 3B2 at 30784 and 19957, ligand-centred, 7a2 to 10b1 (57%) and 8b1 to 9a2 (34%), populations 4.86, 3.77 and 8.63; B 1B2 at 52648 and 31240 with oscillator strength 0.0324, ligand-centred, 7a2 to 10b1 (73%) and 38a1 to 37b2 (9%), populations 4.93, 3.47 and 8.40; B 1A at 55392 and 32022 with oscillator strength 0.2985 (computed with a 0.3 au level shift rather than the 0.2 au used elsewhere), ligand-centred, 8b1 to 10b1 (74%), populations 4.97, 3.44 and 8.41. Metal-to-ligand charge transfer transitions involve excitation from a metal orbital (37 or 38 a1) into a thpy pi* orbital (10b1 or 9a2). The lowest a 3A1 state is confirmed as ligand-centred. Mulliken populations for the Pd complex fall around 8.29 for the relevant analysis, against 8.09-8.12 for the Pt complex, showing that the separation between ligand-centred and charge-transfer character is not sharp and that CT admixture into the LC states is smaller in the Pd complex than in the Pt one. Absorption spectra were recorded between 250 and 450 nm; features below 340 nm (above 29000 cm-1) are assigned to weakly perturbed ligand-centred transitions since the lowest absorption band of the C-protonated thpyH ligand appears in the same region, with dominating LC bands around 32000 cm-1.
Other: The palladium complex is the less strongly mixed of the pair, with only modest MLCT admixture into its ligand-centred states, so the truncated thpy pi space costs it less. Even so the paper attributes deviations between calculated and experimental band positions to three sources it names together: the restricted CASSCF active space, the uncertainties from the level shift, and the state assignments themselves. The level shift is not uniform across states — 0.2 au for most but 0.3 au for the intense B 1A transition — which means the strongest band in the spectrum is computed under a different zeroth-order Hamiltonian from the others, a detail easy to overlook when comparing calculated intensities.  This paper does what is too often skipped: it quantifies the error introduced by the active space it was forced to truncate. The ideal space would carry all thpy pi valence orbitals, requiring 26 orbitals and being 'far beyond the reach of today's computer power', so a 12-orbital space is used instead — and the cost is then measured directly on free C-protonated thpyH, where both the minimal HOMO-LUMO (2,2) and the full valence pi (12,11) spaces are affordable. The answer is instructive and not what one would guess: the error changes SIGN between spin states. 'Somewhat surprisingly, the sign of the error is different for the lowest singlet and triplet state. For the 3A' state we find that the PT2A calculations systematically overestimate the excitation energy, by 700-1500 cm-1. On the other hand, the excitation energy of the A 1A' state is considerably underestimated, by 2700 cm-1, at the PT2A level.' A truncated pi space therefore cannot be corrected by a single offset, and singlet-triplet gaps computed with it inherit the full 3400-4200 cm-1 spread. The truncation has a second consequence the authors trace explicitly: 'As a result of limitations in the 12 orbital active space, quite strongly interacting intruder states appear in the CASPT2 calculations of some of the excited states.' Intruder states here are a symptom of the missing orbitals, not an independent numerical nuisance, and are treated with LS-CASPT2 level shifts of 0.2 au for most states and 0.3 au for the strongest transitions. The requirement stated at the outset — that BOTH bonding and antibonding combinations of metal and ligand orbitals be active to capture nondynamical correlation in covalent metal-ligand bonds — is the general principle worth carrying from this work for transition metal complexes.

basis_set: Relativistic core ab initio model potentials (AIMP) replacing 30 electrons for Pd and 62 for Pt, with the corresponding [3s3p4d] valence basis sets of Barandiaran and Casarrubios. ANO-S basis sets of Pierloot for the remaining atoms, contracted to [3s2p1d] for C and N bound to the metal, [3s2p] for other C, [4s3p1d] for S and [2s] for H, giving 292 contracted basis functions in total; enlarged to [3s2p1d] on all C for the free thpyH calculations.
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic core ab initio model potentials (AIMP) on Pd and Pt
active_space_orbital_description: Two active spaces compared on the same molecule: a minimal HOMO-LUMO space of 2 electrons in 2 orbitals (denoted PT2A) and the full valence pi space of 12 electrons in 11 orbitals (denoted PT2B).
active_space_protocol: The paper states the two requirements an active space must satisfy — '(1) the resulting CASSCF wave function should include the most important correlation effects, and (2) orbitals involved in the excited states of interest should be included' — and then builds the space accordingly. For covalent metal-ligand interactions 'both the bonding and antibonding combination of metal and ligand orbitals have to be included', which here means the bonding and antibonding combinations of thpy sigma (mainly the carbon lone pairs) with Pd 4dyz or Pt 5dyz in b2 symmetry, and of thpy sigma with Pd 5s or Pt 6s in a1. Added to these are the remaining four d orbitals (2 a1, b1, a2) and the HOMO-LUMO pair of thpy pi orbitals (2 b1, 2 a2). This gives 'a total of 12 active orbitals (4 a1, 3 b1, 2 b2, 3 a2), populated with 16 electrons.' The paper is explicit about what it would rather have done: 'Ideally, one would of course like to include in the active space all thpy pi valence orbitals in order to get a better description of pi-pi* correlation effects and of the ligand centered excited states. This would, however, mean adding 14 more active orbitals, leading to an active space of 26 orbitals, which is far beyond the reach of today's computer power.' The resulting error was then MEASURED on a smaller system: 'To check the uncertainty on the excitation energies connected with the use of a limited thpy active space, test calculations on the lowest excited states of free C-protonated thpyH were performed with both a HOMO-LUMO (2 electrons in 2 orbitals) and a full valence pi (12 electrons in 11 orbitals) active space.' In the CASPT2 step 122 electrons are correlated, from Pd 4p and 4d or Pt 5p and 5d, C and N 2s and 2p, S 3s and 3p, and H 1s. 'As a result of limitations in the 12 orbital active space, quite strongly interacting intruder states appear in the CASPT2 calculations of some of the excited states', handled by the LS-CASPT2 level-shift technique with test calculations at several shift values. Reference wave functions were built from individually optimized CASSCF orbitals for each excited state in almost all cases.
nroots_per_mult: Individually optimized CASSCF orbitals for each excited state in almost all cases
electronic_structure_description: Calculated excitation energies in cm-1 for the lowest singlet and triplet excited states of neutral thpyH, comparing the minimal and full-valence-pi references. For the a 3A' state: vertical excitation 23691 (PT2A), 22137 (PT2B) and 22509 (DFT); 0-0 transition energy 19921, 19196 and 19610; phosphorescence maximum 17179, 16453 and 16855. For the A 1A' state: vertical excitation 30468 (PT2A) and 33147 (PT2B). The experimental emission range is 16600-20600 cm-1. The PT2A minimal-space calculations OVERESTIMATE the triplet excitation energy by 700-1500 cm-1 but UNDERESTIMATE the singlet by 2700 cm-1, so the sign of the error differs between spin states. The PT2B value of 33147 cm-1 for the singlet corresponds nicely to the lowest absorption maximum in the experimental spectrum. The calculated phosphorescence maximum and 0-0 transition energy span the experimental emission range, though the computed 0-0 energy is about 1000 cm-1 below the highest recorded value of 20600 cm-1. BP86-DFT performs well for the lowest triplet, placing it about 400 cm-1 above the PT2B result, but standard DFT is restricted to the lowest state of each spin and symmetry and so could not treat the lowest excited singlet of thpyH nor the complexes.
Other: This row exists because the free ligand is the CALIBRATION EXPERIMENT for the metal complexes: it is small enough that both the minimal HOMO-LUMO space forced on the complexes and the full valence pi space one would prefer can be run on the same molecule, so the truncation error can be measured rather than guessed. The result is the paper's most transferable finding — the error reverses sign between spin states, overestimating the triplet by 700-1500 cm-1 and underestimating the singlet by 2700 cm-1. That rules out correcting a truncated pi space by any single shift, and it means singlet-triplet gaps are the quantity most damaged, carrying the sum of the two errors. It is also worth noting that the full-valence-pi singlet at 33147 cm-1 matches the experimental absorption maximum while the minimal-space value at 30468 does not, so on this molecule the larger space is demonstrably right rather than merely larger.  This paper does what is too often skipped: it quantifies the error introduced by the active space it was forced to truncate. The ideal space would carry all thpy pi valence orbitals, requiring 26 orbitals and being 'far beyond the reach of today's computer power', so a 12-orbital space is used instead — and the cost is then measured directly on free C-protonated thpyH, where both the minimal HOMO-LUMO (2,2) and the full valence pi (12,11) spaces are affordable. The answer is instructive and not what one would guess: the error changes SIGN between spin states. 'Somewhat surprisingly, the sign of the error is different for the lowest singlet and triplet state. For the 3A' state we find that the PT2A calculations systematically overestimate the excitation energy, by 700-1500 cm-1. On the other hand, the excitation energy of the A 1A' state is considerably underestimated, by 2700 cm-1, at the PT2A level.' A truncated pi space therefore cannot be corrected by a single offset, and singlet-triplet gaps computed with it inherit the full 3400-4200 cm-1 spread. The truncation has a second consequence the authors trace explicitly: 'As a result of limitations in the 12 orbital active space, quite strongly interacting intruder states appear in the CASPT2 calculations of some of the excited states.' Intruder states here are a symptom of the missing orbitals, not an independent numerical nuisance, and are treated with LS-CASPT2 level shifts of 0.2 au for most states and 0.3 au for the strongest transitions. The requirement stated at the outset — that BOTH bonding and antibonding combinations of metal and ligand orbitals be active to capture nondynamical correlation in covalent metal-ligand bonds — is the general principle worth carrying from this work for transition metal complexes.
reference_short: Pierloot & Ceulemans, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 4374
notes: The C-protonated form of the 2-thienylpyridine ligand, used as a neutral closed-shell model of the coordinated thpy- ligand. The basis set was enlarged to [3s2p1d] on all carbons for these calculations to obtain a balanced description of the free molecule.
correlation_correction: LS-CASPT2 with level shifts of 0.2 au for most states and 0.3 au for the strongest transitions, correlating 122 electrons

point_group: Cis, trans and perpendicular conformers of HO-ONO
geometry_source: CASSCF(12,10)/6-311+G(d,p) geometry optimizations of the cis-2 and trans-2 biradicaloid minima, compared against UB3LYP/6-311+G(3df,2p) structures. Single-point Brueckner Doubles calculations were performed at both the DFT and the CASSCF geometries to test their equivalence. Basis set superposition error was examined by the counterpoise method because the O-O distances in the metastable states exceed 2 A.
method: CASSCF with MRCI and CIPT2 correlation corrections, alongside UB3LYP, spin-corrected UB3LYP, UQCISD(T), G3B3 and Brueckner Doubles UBD(TQ)
software: Gaussian 03 (used for the COSMO solvent corrections; other program details not stated in the extracted text)
basis_set: 6-311+G(d,p) for the CASSCF, MRCI and CIPT2 calculations; 6-311+G(3df,2p) for the DFT work
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in ten orbitals. The occupied set comprises the three sigma bonds of the O-O, O-N and N-O framework, an in-plane lone pair on oxygen, and the two highest pi orbitals. The virtual set comprises the three antibonding sigma orbitals and one pi orbital.
active_space_protocol: The active space was assembled to answer a specific diagnostic question rather than as a production method. Broken-symmetry DFT gave S-squared expectation values of 0.77 and 0.73 for the cis-2 and trans-2 states, 'suggesting a significant contamination of the singlet wave function with triplet character', and 'a complete active space (CASSCF) calculation was used to assess the multireference character of the wave function'. Its composition follows the bonding directly: the three sigma bonds of the O-O-N-O framework with their three antibonding partners, an in-plane oxygen lone pair, and the two highest pi orbitals with one pi*. The CASSCF geometries were then validated against DFT by comparing single-point Brueckner Doubles energies computed at each: UBD(TQ)/6-311+G(d,p) gives a GS-to-cis-2 gap of 15.1 kcal/mol at the DFT geometry and 14.3 at the CASSCF geometry, and 13.6 versus 12.1 kcal/mol for trans-2. Correlation was then added two ways on the same space — CIPT2, and an MRCI expansion of 6.8 million contracted configurations.
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol referenced to cis-HO-ONO. At UB3LYP/6-311+G(3df,2p) without zero-point correction (ZPVE-corrected values in parentheses): perp-HO-ONO 1.4 (1.0); trans-HO-ONO 2.6 (1.6); TScis-1 14.6 (12.5) with S-squared 0.52; cis-2 14.4 (12.2) with S-squared 0.77; TS-3 14.8 (12.2) with S-squared 0.87; trans-2 12.9 (10.9) with S-squared 0.73; TStrans-2 13.2 (11.5) with S-squared 0.43; the hydrogen-bonded complexes 4A 16.2 (12.9) and 4B 15.8 (13.1), both with S-squared near 1.01. Spin-corrected UB3LYP gives cis-2 at 8.2 (5.8) and trans-2 at 6.7 (4.6). MRCI on the CAS(12,10) reference gives 11.7 for cis-2 and 9.0 for trans-2, with CIPT2 in parentheses giving 12.7 and 4.9 respectively. G3B3 gives 18.0 and 17.3, spin-corrected 10.2 and 7.5. UBD(TQ) gives 11.4 (14.3) for cis-2 and 12.3 (12.1) for trans-2. The CIPT2 value of 4.9 kcal/mol for the perp-to-trans-2 gap agrees well with the spin-corrected DFT and G3B3 values. Interconversion between the two terminal oxygens proceeds essentially without barrier through TS-3, with a ZPVE-corrected barrier of 0.01 kcal/mol and an imaginary frequency of 112.0i cm-1. The O-O bond dissociation energy of HO-ONO is 19.1 kcal/mol at one level and 19.0 at G3B3, with binding energies of 17.4 and 17.6. Dissociation limits with zero-point correction are 15.3, 14.3 and 13.4 kcal/mol; the 15.3 kcal/mol limit for ground-state cis-HO-ONO compares with an experimental activation energy of 18 +/- 1 kcal/mol for peroxynitrite isomerization. The O-O distances in the metastable biradicaloid states exceed 2 A. In water media the energies increase to 14.3 and 12.7 kcal/mol, or 15.4 and 14.2 with an alternative treatment, and water molecules exhibit very little effect on the perp-2 complex, changing energies by only 0.3 kcal/mol.
Other: The active space here exists to adjudicate a diagnosis that broken-symmetry DFT could only flag. S-squared values of 0.77 and 0.73 for the two biradicaloid minima signal heavy triplet contamination but cannot say whether the states are genuinely multiconfigurational, so a CAS(12,10) built from the three framework sigma/sigma* pairs plus an oxygen lone pair and the pi manifold was constructed specifically 'to assess the multireference character of the wave function'. The validation strategy is worth noting: rather than trusting either geometry, the authors computed the SAME Brueckner Doubles energies at both the DFT and CASSCF structures and found gaps agreeing to 0.8-1.5 kcal/mol, establishing that the two methods locate essentially the same minima. What the space cannot settle is the energetics, and the spread across methods on the identical structures is the caution to carry: for trans-2 the relative energy runs 12.9 (raw UB3LYP), 6.7 (spin-corrected), 17.3 (G3B3), 9.0 (MRCI), 4.9 (CIPT2) and 12.3 (UBD(TQ)) kcal/mol. MRCI and CIPT2 use the SAME CAS(12,10) reference yet differ by 4.1 kcal/mol, so the choice of correlation treatment on a fixed space matters as much here as the space itself. The 6.8 million contracted configurations of the MRCI mark the practical ceiling for this ten-orbital space.
reference_short: Bach, Dmitrenko & Estevez, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 3140
notes: Peroxynitrous acid is relevant to the oxidation of hydrocarbons, sulfides and selenides. Hydrogen-bonded complexes 4A and 4B lie several kcal/mol above the biradicaloid states at highly correlated levels but are 1.4 kcal/mol more stable than cis-2 at one DFT level and 6.4 kcal/mol less stable with G3B3 spin corrections. Counterpoise BSSE tests were performed given the long O-O distances. COSMO water solvent corrections were applied and hydrated complexes with three water molecules were examined.
correlation_correction: MRCI with 6.8 million contracted configurations, and CIPT2, both applied to the CAS(12,10)/6-311+G(d,p) reference

point_group: Cs or C1 after Jahn-Teller distortion; C5v optimizations also performed for the Jahn-Teller stabilization energy
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at the Hartree-Fock/6-31G** level — restricted HF for the closed-shell neutral, singlet dianion and tetraanion, unrestricted HF for the open-shell monoanion, triplet dianion and trianion. Anion symmetries constrained to Cs or C1 as expected after Jahn-Teller distortion; the neutral fixed at C5v. Separate C5v optimizations of the monoanion and trianion were performed to obtain Jahn-Teller stabilization energies. All CASSCF and MP2 results are single points at these HF geometries.
method: CASSCF single points at HF geometries, with MP2 single points for comparison
software: Gaussian 94 Revision D.3 and Gaussian 98 Revision A.5
active_space_orbital_description: Five electrons in either four orbitals (CAS(5,4)) or six orbitals (CAS(5,6)), both reported. The relevant frontier orbitals derive from the corannulene e2 HOMO and e1 LUMO of the C5v parent, which map onto a' and a'' in Cs.
active_space_protocol: Each anion gets its OWN active space, sized to its own electron count, and each is computed in TWO sizes so the sensitivity is visible: 'We chose the active space spanned by four and six orbitals with five electrons (CAS(5,4) and CAS(5,6)) for 1-, four and six orbitals with six electrons (CAS(6,4) and CAS(6,6)) for 1(2-), and three and four orbitals with three electrons (CAS(3,3) and CAS(3,4)) for 1(3-), respectively.' All CASSCF calculations are single points at HF/6-31G** optimized geometries — restricted HF for the closed-shell neutral, singlet dianion and tetraanion, unrestricted HF for the open-shell monoanion, triplet dianion and trianion. Symmetry was constrained to Cs or C1 for the anions as expected after Jahn-Teller distortion, with the neutral fixed at C5v; C5v optimizations of the monoanion and trianion were also performed specifically to extract Jahn-Teller stabilization energies as the C5v-minus-Cs difference. Every CASSCF result in the paper is reported for both the smaller and the larger space side by side, in Tables 3, 4 and 5.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, doublet and triplet depending on the charge state
electronic_structure_description: Total ground-state energy -20767.514361 eV at HF/6-31G**, -20835.694577 eV at MP2//HF, -20766.882577 eV at CAS(5,4) and -20767.611828 eV at CAS(5,6), against -20767.886817 eV (HF) for the neutral. Relative energies of the two lowest states with respect to the ground state, in eV: the 2A' state with configuration [10](37a') at 0.0 (HF), 0.0 (MP2), 0.044621 (CAS(5,4)) and 0.309226 (CAS(5,6)); the 2A'' state with configuration [10](30a'') at 0.017650 (HF), 0.289492 (MP2), 0.0 (CAS(5,4)) and 0.0 (CAS(5,6)). So HF and MP2 place 2A' lowest while both CASSCF spaces place 2A'' lowest. The Jahn-Teller stabilization energy, defined as the C5v minus Cs energy difference, is 0.313240 eV at HF/6-31G** and 0.494175 eV at MP2//HF. Hydrogen atoms of the neutral are positively charged. Jahn-Teller stabilization in these systems is larger than the roughly 0.04 eV reported for a comparison system.
Other: The monoanion shows the sharpest space-size sensitivity in the paper: the 2A'-2A'' gap grows from 0.045 eV at CAS(5,4) to 0.309 eV at CAS(5,6), a sevenfold increase from adding two orbitals to a five-electron space. The state ORDERING happens to be stable — 2A'' is lowest in both — but the magnitude is not, and 0.045 eV is small enough that a reader taking only the smaller space might reasonably call the two states degenerate while the larger space makes them clearly separated. Note also that both CASSCF spaces disagree with HF and MP2, which put 2A' lowest; since the correlated single-reference and the multiconfigurational treatments give opposite orderings, this is a genuine multireference situation rather than a correlation-magnitude question. The Jahn-Teller stabilization energies quoted (0.31 eV at HF, 0.49 at MP2) come from neither CASSCF space.  The design here is to report EVERY CASSCF number twice, once in a smaller space and once in a larger one, and the resulting comparison is the paper's most useful methodological content because the two sizes frequently disagree about which state is the ground state. For the monoanion the 2A' state lies 0.045 eV above 2A'' at CAS(5,4) but 0.309 eV above it at CAS(5,6) — a sevenfold change in the gap from adding two orbitals. For the dianion the ordering REVERSES outright: at CAS(6,4) the [10](30a'')2 configuration is lowest with 1A' at 0.038 eV above, while at CAS(6,6) the 1A' configuration is lowest and [10](30a'')2 sits 0.268 eV above it. For the trianion the 2A' state is 0.094 eV above 2A'' at CAS(3,3) and 0.066 eV above at CAS(3,4), a smaller but still 30% shift. Comparing across methods makes the same point: for the trianion, HF puts 2A' lowest while 'the MP2 and CASSCF calculations' put 2A'' lowest, so the ground-state assignment depends on both the correlation treatment and the space size. The dianion singlet-triplet gap is the one quantity that survives reasonably: 0.538 eV at CASSCF(6,4) and 0.580 at CASSCF(6,6), a 7% change, against 0.202 eV at ROHF and 1.614 at MP2 — the two CASSCF values bracket neither of the single-reference results, and the eightfold spread between ROHF and MP2 shows why a multiconfigurational treatment was needed at all. A caution for reuse: these are single points at Hartree-Fock geometries, so none of the reported CASSCF energies corresponds to a CASSCF-optimized structure, and the Jahn-Teller stabilization energies of 0.31-1.17 eV come from HF and MP2 rather than from the correlated spaces.
reference_short: Sato, Yamamoto & Yamabe, J. Phys. Chem. A 2000, 104, 130
notes: The Hueckel HOMO of corannulene is an e2 state and the LUMO an e1 state; the symmetry compatibility between C5v and Cs governs the a'/a'' labels. Corannulene has 9A1 + 7A2 + 16E1 + 18E2 vibrational modes.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF; MP2 single points computed separately at the same HF geometries

Other: The trianion is the most stable case of the three: both spaces agree on the ground state and the 2A'-2A'' gap changes only from 0.094 to 0.066 eV between CAS(3,3) and CAS(3,4), a 30% shift on a small number. The interesting disagreement here is method rather than space — Hartree-Fock places 2A' lowest by 0.437 eV while MP2 and both CASSCF spaces place 2A'' lowest, a complete reversal that the paper notes explicitly. With only three electrons the space cannot vary much, which is presumably why it is the best behaved of the three anions. Its Jahn-Teller stabilization energy is two to three times that of the monoanion (0.91 versus 0.31 eV at HF), making it a strongly Jahn-Teller-coupled system, though again those energies come from HF and MP2 rather than from the CASSCF spaces.  The design here is to report EVERY CASSCF number twice, once in a smaller space and once in a larger one, and the resulting comparison is the paper's most useful methodological content because the two sizes frequently disagree about which state is the ground state. For the monoanion the 2A' state lies 0.045 eV above 2A'' at CAS(5,4) but 0.309 eV above it at CAS(5,6) — a sevenfold change in the gap from adding two orbitals. For the dianion the ordering REVERSES outright: at CAS(6,4) the [10](30a'')2 configuration is lowest with 1A' at 0.038 eV above, while at CAS(6,6) the 1A' configuration is lowest and [10](30a'')2 sits 0.268 eV above it. For the trianion the 2A' state is 0.094 eV above 2A'' at CAS(3,3) and 0.066 eV above at CAS(3,4), a smaller but still 30% shift. Comparing across methods makes the same point: for the trianion, HF puts 2A' lowest while 'the MP2 and CASSCF calculations' put 2A'' lowest, so the ground-state assignment depends on both the correlation treatment and the space size. The dianion singlet-triplet gap is the one quantity that survives reasonably: 0.538 eV at CASSCF(6,4) and 0.580 at CASSCF(6,6), a 7% change, against 0.202 eV at ROHF and 1.614 at MP2 — the two CASSCF values bracket neither of the single-reference results, and the eightfold spread between ROHF and MP2 shows why a multiconfigurational treatment was needed at all. A caution for reuse: these are single points at Hartree-Fock geometries, so none of the reported CASSCF energies corresponds to a CASSCF-optimized structure, and the Jahn-Teller stabilization energies of 0.31-1.17 eV come from HF and MP2 rather than from the correlated spaces.

compound_name: Linear OBeO and its cation and anion
point_group: D-infinity-h for the linear symmetric species
geometry_source: Geometries and harmonic frequencies computed at MP2, B3LYP and CASSCF levels for comparison against matrix infrared spectra of laser-ablated metal atoms codeposited with oxygen in argon or nitrogen.
method: CASSCF, compared against MP2, B3LYP density functional theory and, for CaO2, CCSD(T)
software: SIRIUS/ABACUS for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 92/DFT for the DFT and MP2 calculations
basis_set: 6-31+G** of Pople and co-workers for most atoms; 6-311+G** for Ar; a Hay-Wadt relativistic effective core potential with a (5s6p5d)/[4s3p3d] valence basis for Sr; a (12s8p5d)/[8s6p3d] set for Ca; a (10s7p1d)/[5s4p1d] oxygen set for the CaOxNy and SrO2 calculations. Calibration used the augmented correlation-consistent polarized valence triple-zeta oxygen set with the diffuse f function deleted, a (20s15p5d3f)/[8s8p4d3f] Ca set from a Partridge primitive set, and a (26s19p10d)/[13s12p6d] all-electron Sr set.

active_space_orbital_description: Built from the Be 2s and 2p orbitals and the oxygen 2p orbitals, giving two sigma-g, two sigma-u, two pi-u and one pi-g orbital, with a second pi-g orbital added to correlate the oxygen pi-g lone pair electrons. Results are reported for both a smaller and a larger version of this space.
active_space_protocol: For the linear OBeO systems the space is built from the atomic valence orbitals: 'The active space includes the Be 2s and 2p orbitals and the oxygen 2p orbitals, which leads to two sigma-g, two sigma-u, two pi-u, and one pi-g orbitals. A second pi-g orbital is added to the active space to correlate the oxygen pi-g lone pair electrons.' The paper reports results for both this space and a smaller one, labelled 'small' and 'big' in Table 6. For CaO2 a FULL VALENCE CASSCF was used, and the paper states plainly why this approach could not be carried through the whole study: 'the CASSCF approach can lead to prohibitively large calculations for large active spaces. For example, while full valence CASSCF calculations are possible for CaO2, they would not be practical for N2CaO2. Thus using the CASSCF approach, it will be difficult to find an accurate and equivalent description for all systems of interest.' The rationale for using a multiconfigurational method at all is stated up front: 'The metal oxides are poorly described by the SCF treatment, in large part because it underestimates electron affinities of O and O2. Neglect of electron correlation can lead to symmetry breaking ... The CASSCF approach can account for near-degeneracy effects, which lead to symmetry breaking, but might not contain sufficient dynamical correlation to yield an accurate description of these systems.' CASSCF calculations used SIRIUS/ABACUS while the DFT and MP2 work used Gaussian 92/DFT.
electronic_structure_description: Harmonic frequencies in cm-1 with infrared intensities in km/mol, at MP2, B3LYP, and CASSCF in the small and big active spaces, against experiment. Neutral OBeO: pi-u 294 (intensity 335), 227 (268), 323 (361) and no experimental value; sigma-g 767 (0), 722 (0), 680 (0); sigma-u 1599 (8), 1372 (311), 1428 (231) against an experimental 1413.2 cm-1 in argon. Anion OBeO-: pi-u 517.5 (1956), 395 (213), 434 (235); sigma-g 789 (0), 739 (0), 691 (0); sigma-u with MP2 showing symmetry breaking, then 1219 (826) and 1550 (3759). Cation OBeO+: pi-u 196 (305), 185 (324), 205 (198); sigma-g 602 (0), 602 (0.0), 586 (0); sigma-u 996 (676), then imaginary frequencies of 10006i and 1868i cm-1 in the small and big CASSCF spaces respectively. For the neutral molecule the CASSCF and B3LYP methods give relatively similar results, and for the sigma-u mode CASSCF is in best agreement with experiment while MP2 is significantly too large. Previous spin-restricted MP2 calculations gave a harmonic frequency in much better agreement with experiment. The ions show a much larger spread between methods. The B3LYP/DFT value for OBeO gives 226.7, 722.0 and 1372.1 cm-1 for a 3-Sigma-g- ground state at a Be-O distance of 1.441 A, with cyclic BeO2 1A1 lying 11 kcal/mol higher and cyclic 3A2 29 kcal/mol higher. A 1412.4 cm-1 absorption is assigned to the OBeO molecule.
Other: OBeO is the clearest case in this paper of the same active space succeeding and failing on the same molecule depending only on its charge. For the neutral, CASSCF gives the best sigma-u frequency of any method — 1428 cm-1 against an experimental 1413.2, with MP2 'significantly too large' at 1599. For the cation it fails outright: 'the CASSCF method shows symmetry breaking for the positive ion FOR ALL OF THE ACTIVE SPACES TESTED', producing sigma-u imaginary frequencies of 10006i cm-1 in the small space and 1868i in the big one. Both are unphysical, and enlarging the space changes the magnitude fivefold without changing the sign, which is the diagnostic point: this symmetry breaking is not the kind a larger space repairs. MP2 breaks symmetry for the ANION instead, so neither method is uniformly safe across the charge states. Since near-degeneracy-driven symmetry breaking was the stated reason for invoking CASSCF in the first place, its failure precisely where it was most needed is a substantive negative result.  This paper is a calibration study whose conclusion is to ABANDON the multiconfigurational approach, and the reasoning is worth recording precisely. The authors need one method applicable to every species from BeO2 up to N2CaO2, and they state that 'while full valence CASSCF calculations are possible for CaO2, they would not be practical for N2CaO2', so a consistent CASSCF description across the series is unattainable. Since comparing frequencies across a family of related molecules is the entire point, an equivalently-applicable single-reference method beats a better method applied unevenly. The other finding is that CASSCF does not always cure symmetry breaking, which was the main reason for invoking it. 'The MP2 shows symmetry breaking for the negative ion and the CASSCF method shows symmetry breaking for the positive ion FOR ALL OF THE ACTIVE SPACES TESTED.' The OBeO+ sigma-u mode comes out as an imaginary frequency of 10006i cm-1 in the small space and 1868i in the big one — both unphysical, and the fact that enlarging the space changes the magnitude by a factor of five while leaving the sign unchanged shows the problem is not one a bigger space fixes. Where CASSCF does work it works well: for the neutral OBeO sigma-u mode it gives 1428 cm-1 against an experimental 1413.2, the closest of any method, with MP2 'significantly too large' at 1599. So the paper documents both a success and a failure of the same space on the same molecule differing only by charge. metal_ox_state: Formally V(5+) and Mo(6+) before reduction; ten reducing electrons are distributed over the metal centres
ligand_set: Oxo and polyoxometalate framework oxygens; eight vanadium centres in a ring and eight molybdenum centres
geometry_source: Geometry of the closed-shell electronic configuration optimized with DFT/BP86; CASSCF calculations performed with the same double-zeta basis set as the B3LYP calculations.
method: CASSCF, compared against DFT with the BP86 and B3LYP functionals
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Double-zeta, the same basis used for the B3LYP calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in twelve orbitals. The active orbitals are linear combinations of either vanadium 3d or molybdenum 4d atomic orbitals. Sixteen such combinations could in principle be constructed from the 8 Mo-4d and 8 V-3d atomic orbitals, but the space was limited to the twelve lowest in energy, excluding the four out-of-phase combinations of Mo-4d orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is constructed from the metal d manifold and then truncated by orbital energy: 'In principle, 16 linear combinations can be constructed with these atomic d-orbitals (8 Mo-4d and 8 V-3d). However, the active space has been limited to the 12 molecular orbitals that are lowest in energy, excluding the four out-of-phase linear combinations of Mo-4d orbitals.' The purpose of the multiconfigurational treatment is explicitly to remove method bias in deciding where the reducing electrons sit: 'The optimization of both the CI expansion and the molecular orbital coefficients ensures an unbiased treatment of the different electron distributions over V and Mo.' The authors also state their justification for not adding dynamic correlation: 'the CASSCF approach is usually sufficient for an accurate description of the electron distribution of a given N-electron state. The dynamical electron correlation can have a strong effect on the relative energy of different states but does not change the character of these states.' They note that no such correction was applied given the size of the molecule, which also precludes treating the electron-electron cusp properly in the CASSCF wave function. Calculations were performed on both the high-spin S = 5 and the low-spin singlet coupled states.
multiplicities_studied: Singlet and the high-spin S = 5 undecaplet
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF on the high-spin state gives an 8/2 distribution of the ten unpaired electrons over the vanadium and molybdenum centres. Mulliken spin populations are 0.98 e for each of the two distinct vanadium centres, corresponding to eight unpaired electrons in the V8 ring, and 0.22 for molybdenum, consistent with two electrons delocalized over the eight Mo centres. The singlet state lies 1.2 kcal/mol below the undecaplet, a gap expected to widen once dynamical correlation is included. Mulliken spin populations are identically zero for a singlet spin eigenfunction, so the singlet character was instead assessed from the active orbitals and natural occupation numbers, which show an antiferromagnetic alignment of ten unpaired electrons with the same 8/2 spin distribution; the alpha spin density shows each vanadium carrying an equivalent number of unpaired alpha electrons with smaller spin density on molybdenum. The singlet CI expansion contains 80 configuration state functions with squared coefficients above 0.05, and the largest CI coefficient is only 0.1737, less than 3% of the total wave function. DFT/BP86 gives a different answer, delocalizing six of the ten metal electrons over the V ring and four over the Mo centres (6/4 sharing), whereas both B3LYP and CASSCF give the 8/2 configuration expected from the assumption that V(5+) is reduced before Mo(6+).
Other: This is one of the most extreme multiconfigurational cases likely to appear in this database: the singlet wave function has 80 configuration state functions with weight above 0.05 and its LARGEST CI coefficient is 0.1737, under 3% of the total. There is no dominant configuration at all, which makes any single-reference description of this state meaningless in principle and is the strongest possible justification for the CASSCF treatment. The active space was built to be unbiased between the two metals — all twelve orbitals are linear combinations of V 3d and Mo 4d, and 'the optimization of both the CI expansion and the molecular orbital coefficients ensures an unbiased treatment of the different electron distributions over V and Mo' — which is exactly what is needed when the question being asked is where ten reducing electrons localize. The payoff is a methodological correction: DFT/BP86 gives 6/4 sharing between the V ring and the Mo centres while both B3LYP and CASSCF give 8/2, and the authors conclude that 'although most of the theoretical studies reported on polyoxoanions have been carried out using the BP86 functional the present results suggest that mixed vanadium-molybdenum anions are better described through a hybrid functional'. Note two acknowledged limitations: the truncation from 16 possible d combinations to the 12 lowest excludes the out-of-phase Mo-4d set, and no dynamic correlation was added, so the 1.2 kcal/mol singlet-undecaplet gap is explicitly expected to grow.
reference_short: Lopez, de Graaf, Maestre, Benard, Rohmer, Bo & Poblet, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2005, 1, 856
notes: Highly reduced polyoxometalates containing both vanadium and molybdenum. The conventional assumption is that V(5+) ions are reduced before Mo(6+) centres, which the B3LYP and CASSCF results support against the BP86 outcome. The size of the molecule prevents proper treatment of the electron-electron cusp in the CASSCF wave function.
correlation_correction: None applied; the authors argue dynamical correlation affects relative state energies but not state character, and note the singlet-undecaplet gap would be expected to increase with it

point_group: Cs in all three states (S0, S1 and D0), with two methyl hydrogens and the water hydrogens above and below the molecular symmetry plane
geometry_source: Optimized structures from the acetanilide monomer study were used as starting geometries with the water molecule attached to the NH binding site and the methyl group in different orientations. This complex geometry was assumed to be the most stable on the basis of studies on similar systems, and only this isomer was pursued. The paper notes that for acetamide the methyl group orientation showed a strong dependence on the level of theory and basis set, and that the methyl alignment in acetanilide-water could not be investigated further because only relatively low levels of theory and small basis sets were computationally feasible.
method: CASSCF, with MP2 and zero-point energy corrections applied to the ionization energy
basis_set: Not stated in the extracted text; the paper notes only small basis sets were computationally feasible
active_space_orbital_description: The paper describes the space as consisting of 'the six benzene type pi orbitals and the oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs of a'' symmetry: a (10/9,8) active space', with the notation reproduced as printed. No orbitals from the water moiety were included.
active_space_protocol: The active space is built entirely from the SOLUTE and deliberately excludes the solvent: 'The HF molecular orbitals included in the active space consisted of the six benzene type pi orbitals and the oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs of a'' symmetry: a (10/9,8) active space. No orbitals from the water moiety were included.' The same space is therefore used for the isolated monomer and for the hydrated complex, so hydration effects are measured against a fixed orbital description of the chromophore. The space is used for the neutral ground and excited states and for the cation, with the notation apparently encoding the differing electron counts of the neutral and ionized species.
multiplicities_studied: singlet for S0 and S1; doublet for the D0 cation
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF predicts Cs symmetry for the complex in all three states. In the neutral states one methyl hydrogen faces the oxygen of the water moiety, whereas in the cation the methyl group is rotated by 60 degrees so that one methyl hydrogen points toward the amide oxygen — the methyl orientation in the complex therefore differs from that in the monomer. Geometric parameters of the side chain are very similar in monomer and complex, with bond distances and angles slightly smaller in the complex except for the C14-O15 bond and N2-C14-O15 angle. Upon excitation CASSCF predicts only minor changes in side-chain distances and angles, becoming considerably more pronounced in the cation, corresponding mainly to displacements along the in-plane bending and side-chain stretching coordinates. The hydrogen bond H13...O20 shortens from 2.216 A in S0 to 2.105 A in S1 and 1.906 A in D0; the angle between the C2v axis of the water and the hydrogen bond increases from 173.7 to 176.7 degrees on excitation and to 185.7 degrees on ionization. Partial atomic charges show that in the cationic monomer 40% of the positive excess charge delocalizes onto the side chain (32% onto the amide group), and the complex shows a similar 42%, indicating that hydration of the amide group does not influence the overall ability for electron density redistribution. The experimental ionization energy is 62633 +/- 5 cm-1, a red shift of 2904 +/- 5 cm-1 relative to the monomer; CASSCF predicts 53388 cm-1 with a red shift of 3482 cm-1, becoming 62040 and 3246 cm-1 once MP2 and zero-point corrections are included. The S1 origin lies at 36052 +/- 0.2 cm-1 for a possible second origin band. A side-chain torsion predicted at 37 cm-1 by CASSCF was observed. The methyl rotor barrier was determined as 320 cm-1 for V3 by simulating eigenvalues in a V3-V6 potential.
Other: The design decision here is that the active space contains no water orbitals at all — six benzene pi orbitals plus the oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs, and nothing from the solvent molecule. That makes the hydration shift a property of a FIXED chromophore wave function responding to a hydrogen bond, exactly the same logic as the retinal counterion and acetone-water studies, and it means the monomer and complex are directly comparable. The internal evidence that this is adequate is the charge delocalization: 40% of the cation excess charge goes onto the side chain in the monomer and 42% in the complex, so the water is not accepting charge and needs no active orbitals to describe. The limitation is visible in the raw ionization energy: bare CASSCF gives 53388 cm-1 against a measured 62633, an error of over 9000 cm-1 (1.15 eV), which only falls into line at 62040 cm-1 after MP2 and zero-point corrections are added. The RED SHIFT, being a difference between monomer and complex computed in the same space, is far better behaved — 3482 cm-1 bare and 3246 corrected against 2904 measured. That contrast is the useful one: an absolute ionization energy from a space of this size is unusable, while a solvation shift from the same calculation is good to about 10%. Note also the paper's caution that methyl group orientation in the related acetamide 'showed a strong dependence on the level of theory and basis set used' and could not be tested here because larger calculations were not feasible.
reference_short: Ullrich & Muller-Dethlefs, J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 9188
notes: Two-colour REMPI and ZEKE spectra were recorded in a supersonic jet, extending previous work on the acetanilide monomer. The complex is bound at the NH site. Because of the large hydrogen-bond geometry changes, the intermolecular in-plane bend, stretch and possibly another intermolecular mode are expected to be prominent in the spectra. No higher clusters were detected in the mass spectrum.
correlation_correction: MP2 and zero-point energy corrections applied to the CASSCF ionization energy

compound_name: Singlet molecular oxygen O2(1-Delta-g) + ethylene — peroxirane and dioxetane reaction paths
point_group: C2v assumed for paths 2 and 3; Cs for paths 4 and 5
geometry_source: Preliminary calculations with a double-zeta basis, with the intermolecular distance and the oxygen bond length varied explicitly as reaction coordinates while the carbon-carbon bond length and hydrogen tilt angle were optimized at each point and the remaining parameters held fixed. Equilibrium geometries were then reoptimized with the double-zeta basis augmented by a single d function on carbon and oxygen, and small nets of points around the transition states on paths 4 and 5 were recomputed with the augmented basis to refine the barrier heights. Several hundred points on the energy surface were computed in total.
method: CASSCF (complete active space SCF) solved by the super-CI technique, with contracted CI (CCI) at key points using the most important CASSCF configurations as reference states
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Double-zeta: a (9s5p) primitive set contracted to (4s2p) for carbon and oxygen following Dunning, and a (4s) set contracted to (2s) for hydrogen with exponents scaled by 1.24. Final calculations augmented with a single d function on carbon and oxygen, exponents 0.750 for C and 0.861 for O, optimized for the separated molecules at their experimental geometries.
active_space_orbital_description: Eight active orbitals. In terms of the separated molecules these are the ethylene pi and pi* orbitals, the bonding and antibonding oxygen sigma orbitals 3-sigma-g and 3-sigma-u, and the oxygen pi bonding and lone-pair orbitals 1-pi-u and 1-pi-g. These are the orbitals needed to describe formation of the C-O bonds from the O-O and C-C pi bonds and the restructuring of the oxygen lone pairs. A six-orbital subset (3-pi-g, 3-sigma-u, 1-pi-u and 1-pi-g) was used in some O2 tests, and adding a further 2-sigma-u orbital was tested separately.
active_space_protocol: The paper sets out the CAS philosophy explicitly — the one-electron space is divided into primary orbitals (inactive, doubly occupied in all configurations, plus active orbitals that 'describe the changes during the chemical process') and secondary orbitals, with the CI wave function complete in the active subspace, so that 'the sometimes difficult choice of important configurations is avoided, and the only remaining chemical problem is the choice of the active orbitals'. The eight orbitals were chosen as exactly those needed for the bond reorganization. The paper then states its own limitation and the reason for accepting it: 'Obviously, this active space is rather limited, in particular as it is lacking the important 2-pi-u orbital. The present study, however, includes calculations of four reaction paths for the O2 + C2H4 reaction, and a large number of independent calculations (several hundred points on the energy surface) have been performed. With such a prospect in mind it is necessary to limit the size of each calculation as much as possible. Important parts of the energy hypersurface can afterward be studied with higher accuracy.' The cost of the truncation was quantified on the isolated O2 molecule by adding the missing orbital and watching the dissociation energy. Contracted CI at the key points used about 1100 configurations for path 4 and about 1000 for path 5, built on seven reference configurations.
electronic_structure_description: Four reaction paths were studied. Neither C2v path was found feasible: the equilibrium geometry of peroxirane has lower symmetry than C2v, ruling out path 2. In Cs symmetry the barrier for formation of the peroxirane intermediate is 149 kJ/mol, lower than the 169 kJ/mol barrier for the Cs transition state leading to dioxetane via a biradical species. The latter transition state is analogous to the C2v one, showing formation of even the second C-O bond at a rather early stage. No other low-energy transition states leading to dioxetane via a biradical were found. Constrained to Cs symmetry, peroxirane lies 115 kJ/mol above the reactants and 170 kJ/mol above dioxetane at the CASSCF level; at the contracted CI level the C-O distance increases and the energy at the CASSCF optimum becomes 133 kJ/mol above reactants and 260 kJ/mol above dioxetane, reflecting a large energy lowering of dioxetane from CI effects. For the isolated reactants, ethylene is described realistically with the present active space and both basis sets, but the optimized oxygen bond distance is 10 pm longer than the experimental 122.55 pm at the double-zeta level; adding one d function with exponent 0.861 and using the six active orbitals 3-pi-g, 3-sigma-u, 1-pi-u and 1-pi-g gives a much better 123 pm. The O2 dissociation energy improves from 0.05885 au (1.60 eV) to 0.10648 au (2.90 eV) with the d function, and further to 0.1376 au (3.75 eV) on adding the 2-sigma-u orbital to the active space, against an experimental 4.20 eV for O2(1-Delta-g).
Other: This 1983 paper is an early and unusually frank account of trading active-space quality for surface coverage. The eight orbitals are exactly those required for the bond reorganization, and the authors immediately concede what is missing: 'this active space is rather limited, in particular as it is lacking the important 2-pi-u orbital'. Their justification is coverage — four reaction paths and several hundred points on the surface — with the explicit expectation that 'important parts of the energy hypersurface can afterward be studied with higher accuracy'. That is the correct framing for an exploratory surface study and is stated rather than hidden. The cost is then MEASURED on the isolated O2 molecule, where the same orbital can be added cheaply: the dissociation energy runs 1.60 eV (double zeta, six orbitals), 2.90 eV (with a d function), 3.75 eV (adding 2-sigma-u), against 4.20 eV experimental. So the missing orbital is worth 0.85 eV on a diatomic dissociation energy and the residual basis-set error a further 0.45 eV — a 2.6 eV total shortfall on the reactant asymptote, which the authors nonetheless argue does not overturn the relative barrier ordering. The 20 kJ/mol difference between the peroxirane and biradical barriers on which the mechanistic conclusion rests is much smaller than that absolute error, so the conclusion depends on cancellation between paths computed in the same space rather than on absolute accuracy.

geometry_source: All stationary structures optimized at the CASSCF level with 12 electrons in 10 orbitals; state-averaged CASSCF used to determine the geometry of the intersection space. C-Cl bond cleavage along six state pathways was scanned by MR-CI stepwise calculations with all other bond parameters held at ground-state equilibrium values. Molecular dynamics on the CASSCF potential surfaces used the Hessian-based integration method of Helgaker.
method: CASSCF, with internally contracted MR-CI single-point energies including all single and double excitations relative to the CASSCF reference; ab initio molecular dynamics on the CASSCF surfaces

active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in ten orbitals. The six occupied orbitals derive from the C=S pi orbital, the sulfur nonbonding orbital, the 3pz orbitals of the two chlorine atoms and the two C-Cl sigma orbitals; the virtual set comprises the C-S pi*, C-Cl and C-S sigma* orbitals. The paper notes that the three sigma* orbitals are actually delocalized over the whole molecular backbone with marked antibonding character in the C-Cl or C-S regions. A smaller preliminary CAS(8,7) omitted the two C-Cl sigma orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The paper opens with the principle — 'The selection of the active space is a crucial step for the CASSCF calculations' — and then documents a deliberate enlargement driven by the chemistry being studied. Preliminary calculations used CAS(8,7), whose eight electrons come from the C=S pi orbital, the sulfur nonbonding orbital and the 3pz orbitals of the two chlorine atoms, and which 'give a good description of the equilibrium structures and relative energies of the S0, T1, and S1 states'. But 'for a balanced description of the C-Cl dissociation process, the two C-Cl sigma orbitals should be added to the active space', so all stationary structures were optimized with CAS(12,10) instead. The enlargement is therefore not a general refinement but a targeted addition of the bonds that break. State-averaged CASSCF was used for the intersection-space geometries, and MR-CI with 24 correlated valence electrons refined the relative energies.

electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic excitation energies from S0 to T1, S1, T2 and S2 are 51.9, 54.4, 63.2 and 113.4 kcal/mol at CAS(12,10)/6-311G*, becoming 50.5, 54.0, 61.6 and 106.1 kcal/mol at MR-CI/cc-pVTZ. Experimentally the T1 and S1 origins were assigned at 17492 cm-1 (50.0 kcal/mol) and 18716 cm-1 (53.5 kcal/mol) from vibrational analysis, with a further band at about 20340 cm-1 (58.2 kcal/mol) and the S2 origin in the range 97.2-103.0 kcal/mol. The C-S bond lengthens to 1.793 A in S1 at CAS(12,10)/6-311G*. A barrier for molecular inversion on the S1 and T1 surfaces was calculated as 1383 cm-1 at the MR-CI level, against an experimental value revised upward to 1495 cm-1. For dissociation into ClCS and Cl, the S2 (1-pi-pi*) state correlates adiabatically with Cl(X 2P) and ClCS(A 2A''); a transition state TS(S2) has a C-Cl bond of 1.935 A, slightly longer than in the S2 equilibrium geometry, consistent with an early transition state since S2 dissociation is exothermic by 24.2 kcal/mol. The barrier to C-Cl cleavage on the S2 pathway is 6.3 kcal/mol at CAS(12,10)/6-311G* and 6.0 kcal/mol at MR-CI/cc-pVTZ. The S2-S0 fluorescence excitation spectrum breaks off at a vibrational energy of 1450 +/- 50 cm-1 above the S2 zero point, attributed to C-Cl dissociation, with loss of fluorescence under free jet expansion at about 1700 cm-1 above the S2 origin. An attempt to locate an S3 structure at the CAS(12,10)/6-311G* level was unsuccessful.
Other: Thiophosgene is a textbook case of an active space enlarged for one specific reason, stated explicitly. The preliminary CAS(8,7) — C=S pi, sulfur lone pair and the two chlorine 3pz orbitals — was found to 'give a good description of the equilibrium structures and relative energies of the S0, T1, and S1 states', so it was adequate for the spectroscopy. It was enlarged to CAS(12,10) solely because 'for a balanced description of the C-Cl dissociation process, the two C-Cl sigma orbitals should be added'. A space that describes vertical spectroscopy well can be blind to a dissociation channel, and the fix is to add the specific bonding orbitals that break rather than to enlarge generally. An interesting complication the paper records is that the three sigma* orbitals brought in are 'actually delocalized into the whole molecular backbone, with remarkable antibonding characteristics in the C-Cl or C-S region' — so the added orbitals are not cleanly localized C-Cl antibonds and serve both dissociation channels at once. The CASSCF and MR-CI results agree closely for the low-lying states (51.9 versus 50.5 and 54.4 versus 54.0 kcal/mol for T1 and S1) but diverge sharply for S2 (113.4 versus 106.1), a 7.3 kcal/mol correction on the state that actually dissociates — while the S2 dissociation BARRIER is essentially unchanged at 6.3 versus 6.0 kcal/mol, so the correlation error largely cancels along the reaction coordinate even though it does not cancel in the vertical excitation.

notes: Photodissociation dynamics of Cl2CS at 235 nm have been studied experimentally.
