compound_name: Iodide-water clusters I-(H2O)2-5 — charge-transfer-to-solvent excited-state dynamics
geometry_source: Initial structures were the ground-state minimum-energy geometries of I-(H2O)2-5 optimized at the CASSCF/aug-cc-pVDZ+(2s2p/2s) level, then vertically excited. Excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics simulations ran for 800 fs (n = 2-4) and 600 fs (n = 5) with a 0.2 fs time step, plus shorter 300 fs runs for n = 5 with a 0.1 fs step. Initial kinetic energies of 0 and 300 K were used, extended to 0, 100, 200, 300 and 400 K for the more complex I-(H2O)5 dynamics, along with somewhat different initial geometries.
method: CASSCF excited-state ab initio molecular dynamics, with CASPT2, CIS, TD-DFT and SAC-CI single points for the vertical CTTS energies
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ+(2s2p/2s) for O and H, found reliable after testing an X(3s3p/3s) extra diffuse set with exponents 0.01, 0.00125 and 0.000015625; the CRENBL effective core pseudopotential basis for iodine, since aug-cc-pVDZ is unavailable for it
relativistic_treatment: CRENBL effective core pseudopotential on iodine
active_space_orbital_description: For clusters up to three waters, six electrons in six orbitals. For four and five waters a reduced CAS(4,4) was used, containing the iodine p orbital pointing toward the water cluster (distinct from the other two p orbitals) together with the delocalized water-cluster orbital that accepts the excess electron — the essential orbitals for the photoexcitation and the subsequent rearrangement. CAS(4,3) was also tested.
active_space_protocol: The active space is REDUCED for the larger clusters on the basis of two explicitly stated and separately justified assumptions. For clusters of up to three water molecules a CAS(6,6) was used. 'Because ES-AIMD simulations require enormous computing time for four and five water molecules, the optimal choice of the active space for the reduction of computational resources is needed, even though the computational accuracy is slightly sacrificed.' Assumption (i) is an empirical test: 'We performed CASSCF ES-AIMD simulations for the I-(H2O)3 complex using different active spaces [CAS(4,3), CAS(4,4), CAS(6,6)]. The results of these simulations are almost identical.' Assumption (ii) is a physical argument: the charge-transfer-to-solvent states arise from excitation of an electron localized on the iodide into a more delocalized state on the water cluster; 'since the promotion energies are larger than the electron affinities for the iodine atom, and the iodine's p-orbital pointing toward the water cluster is different from that of the other two p orbitals, the active space of CAS(4,4) contains the essential MOs involved in the photoexcitation and the rearrangement of the water cluster including the excess electron.' The authors then state the limitation plainly: 'for the reliable understanding of the dissociation phenomena of I-(H2O)n=4,5, CAS(4,4) is the only feasible and yet the most up-to-date approach currently available.' They also note what the CASSCF level itself omits: 'At the CASSCF level the dynamical correlation effects are not taken [into account]', and that dispersion energy is important for these clusters.
electronic_structure_description: Charge-transfer-to-solvent energies in eV across methods (CIS, TD-DFT, CASSCF, CASPT2, SAC-CI, experiment): I-(H2O)2 5.07, 3.53, 4.36, 4.26, 4.47 against 3.95 measured; I-(H2O)3 5.46, 4.16, 4.94, 4.70, 4.82 against 4.25; I-(H2O)4 5.60, 4.35, 5.11, 4.86, 4.93 against 4.50; I-(H2O)5 5.63, 4.18, 5.02, 4.83, 4.81 with no experimental value. The CTTS states arise from excitation of an electron localized on the iodide anion into a more delocalized state on the water cluster, corresponding to a HOMO to LUMO transition. The CTTS energies of I-(H2O)2-5 (4.0-4.5 eV experimentally) exceed by 0.5-1 eV the sum of the iodine electron affinity (3.06 eV) and the iodine-water binding energy (0.5 eV), so the excited cluster tends to dissociate almost fully into an iodine radical and water. Simulations show simple dissociation for the smaller clusters while I-(H2O)5 shows drastic rearrangement. Temperature rises by several hundred K (several kcal/mol) within the first 30 fs of simulation. The dissociation energy of the water cluster is around 3 kcal/mol at 0 K and a comparable value at 230 K, so only colder clusters retain the original water cluster size without dissociating into smaller ones; the simulations therefore start in an NVE-like ensemble whose temperature decreases with time toward a heat bath value.
Other: This paper handles a space reduction the way it should be handled: by testing it rather than asserting it. Three spaces — CAS(4,3), CAS(4,4) and CAS(6,6) — were run on the SAME I-(H2O)3 cluster through full excited-state dynamics, and 'the results of these simulations are almost identical', which is what licenses CAS(4,4) for the four- and five-water clusters where CAS(6,6) dynamics would be unaffordable. The physical argument backing this is specific rather than generic: the CTTS excitation removes an electron from the one iodine p orbital pointing at the water cluster, which is inequivalent to the other two, so a four-orbital space containing that orbital and the accepting cluster orbital holds everything the photoexcitation and the subsequent water rearrangement require. The authors are also candid that this is a floor rather than a choice — 'CAS(4,4) is the only feasible and yet the most up-to-date approach currently available'. The cost shows in Table 1: CASSCF overestimates every CTTS energy by 0.4-0.8 eV against experiment, and CASPT2 on the same reference recovers only about a third of that (4.94 to 4.70 eV for the trimer against 4.25 measured), so dynamical correlation and the dispersion the authors flag as important are not fully recovered even perturbatively. Since the dynamics run on the uncorrected CASSCF surfaces, the simulated excess energy driving dissociation is systematically too large.
reference_short: Kolaski, Lee, Pak & Kim, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2008, 130, 103
notes: The basis set dependence was investigated in terms of extra diffuse functions and polarization functions on oxygen and hydrogen. The authors note that the CASSCF dynamics assume a separation that 'may be violated when the energy splitting between states is small', and that incorporating a better treatment is not presently possible. Time evolutions of kinetic energies, iodine-oxygen distances and natural orbital populations were tracked through the simulations.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points for the vertical CTTS energies; no correction applied during the dynamics, which run on CASSCF surfaces

active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals: the metal-metal bonding sigma-d, pi-1d, pi-2d and delta-d together with their antibonding counterparts sigma-d*, pi-1d*, pi-2d* and delta-d*. The d(x2-y2) orbital is excluded because it lies much higher in energy through strong antibonding interaction with the ligand lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: The eight active orbitals are named individually and are exactly the metal-metal bonding and antibonding set: 'eight electrons in the eight orbitals sigma-d, pi-1d, pi-2d, delta-d, sigma-d*, pi-1d*, pi-2d*, and delta-d* were taken as active space because these orbitals exist around the HOMO and LUMO'. One d orbital is deliberately EXCLUDED with a stated reason: 'The d(x2-y2) orbital was excluded from the active space because it exists at much higher energy due to the strong antibonding interaction with the lone pair orbitals of ligands.' The choice is anchored to precedent: 'This active space is the same as those of CASPT2 and MRMP2 calculations of dinuclear Re complex, [Re2Cl8]2-, bearing a Re-Re quadruple bond.' The multiconfigurational treatment is embedded in an ONIOM scheme: DFT for the whole system and either CASSCF or MRMP2 for the high-quality region, giving ONIOM(CASSCF:DFT) and ONIOM(MRMP2:DFT). Geometries were optimized at various fixed Cr-Cr distances in the singlet spin state with B3LYP, and MRMP2 potential energy surfaces were built on the CASSCF reference. Core electrons of Cr up to 2p were replaced with an effective core potential. A small model M1 with all alkyl substituents replaced by hydrogen was used in preliminary calculations alongside the real system R1.
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(8,8) natural orbital occupation numbers at a Cr-Cr distance of 1.85 A: sigma-d 1.740, pi-1d 1.707, pi-2d 1.713, delta-d 1.372, delta-d* 0.629, pi-2d* 0.294, pi-1d* 0.287, sigma-d* 0.259. Component bond orders, defined as half the difference between bonding and antibonding occupations, are sigma-d 0.741, pi-d 1.420 and delta-d 0.372, giving a total Cr-Cr bond order of 2.532 — much smaller than the formal quadruple-bond value of 4.0. At R(Cr-Cr) = 1.850 A the bond order is 2.53, and evaluated with the CASSCF(8,8) method it is 2.40 for the real complex. The model takes C2v symmetry. The small bond order arises from the occupations of the antibonding orbitals, reflecting large nondynamical correlation, with the difference in occupation number between delta-d and delta-d* being especially pronounced.
Other: The model complex is where the occupation numbers do their real work. With all four metal-metal bonding orbitals and all four antibonding partners active, the natural orbital occupations are not a diagnostic to be checked but the primary result: delta-d at 1.372 against delta-d* at 0.629 means the delta component contributes a bond order of only 0.372 out of a formal 1.0, and the total collapses from a nominal quadruple bond to 2.53. Every part of that number is read directly off the eight-orbital space, which is why the orbital-by-orbital naming of the space matters. The excluded d(x2-y2) orbital is justified by its strong antibonding interaction with ligand lone pairs placing it much higher in energy — a reasonable argument, though it is asserted from orbital energies and precedent on [Re2Cl8]2- rather than tested by enlarging the space here.  The value of this study for active-space practice is that the eight orbitals are precisely the metal-metal bonding manifold and their occupation numbers become the RESULT rather than a diagnostic. Because sigma-d, two pi-d and delta-d with their antibonding partners are all active, the bond order can be defined directly as half the difference between bonding and antibonding natural orbital occupations, and it comes out at 2.53 for the model complex against a formal quadruple-bond value of 4.0. That deficit is entirely attributable to occupation of the antibonding orbitals — delta-d* alone carries 0.629 electrons — which is what 'large nondynamical correlation' means concretely here and is invisible to any single-determinant treatment. The exclusion of d(x2-y2) is the notable judgement call: it is left out because ligand lone-pair antibonding pushes it to much higher energy, so the space covers the metal-metal interaction and nothing of the metal-ligand framework. That is defensible for a bond-order analysis but means the space cannot describe any process involving the ligand sphere, and the choice rests partly on precedent from [Re2Cl8]2- rather than on a test within this system. Note also that the same eight-orbital space applied to the real substituted complex versus the hydrogen-substituted model resolves a purely geometric effect: the pi-d and delta-d bond orders drop by 0.045 and 0.073 on going from the C2v model to the C2 real complex because the d-pi and d-delta atomic orbitals twist relative to one another, while the sigma-d bond order barely moves (0.017). A fixed space is what makes that decomposition meaningful.

compound_name: Ethene and its radical anion (C2H4 and C2H4-) — monomer reference for polyacetylene electron transfer
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at UHF, UMP2 and CASSCF levels. At all symmetric geometries the symmetry was lowered to C2 and a nonsymmetric density matrix supplied as input, so that localized solutions were obtained in all SCF methods. The reaction path was constructed by locating the minimum for the symmetric configuration Qa = Qb and then approximating the orthogonal trajectory to the energy surface by a power law.
method: pi-CASSCF with CASPT2 and the CASSCF State Interaction (CASSI) method; UHF and UMP2 for comparison
software: MOLCAS-93 for the CASSCF, CASPT2 and CASSI calculations; GAUSSIAN-92 for the UHF and MP2 calculations
basis_set: D951 with polarization functions on carbon for the pi-CASSCF, pi-CASPT2 and CASSI calculations; 6-31G and D95 for the UHF and MP2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Four pi orbitals, established as sufficient by testing against a two-orbital space and against larger spaces. The pi and pi* orbitals belong to the b2u and b3g irreducible representations respectively in D2h.
active_space_protocol: The space is restricted to pi orbitals throughout ('pi-CASSCF'), with two different sizes tested and the adequacy of the larger one established two independent ways. For the monomer, two- and four-pi-orbital spaces were compared: 'For C2H4- the increase to four pi-orbitals in the active space affected the CC bond length and the wave function significantly. The energy of the ground state was improved by about 3.748 eV. Larger active space calculations were performed for C2H4-, but no substantial improvement was achieved. We may conclude that a four pi-orbital active space is enough to describe the electronic structure of the C2H4-.' CASPT2 was then used as a DIAGNOSTIC for what the space is missing: 'CASPT2 can be used to see which inactive orbitals should be included in the active space to take into account additional electronic correlation.' Occupation numbers of the natural orbitals lying outside the active space were inspected, with those above 0.005 listed explicitly — 4ag (0.016), 5ag (0.008), 6ag (0.007), 2b3u (0.016), 3b3u (0.009), 3b2u (0.006), 3b1u (0.021), 4b1u (0.014), 5b1u (0.006) and 2b2g (0.016) — all small enough to justify leaving them inactive. For the dimer the same test was applied: 'CASPT2 does not give significant differences for the occupation numbers of the natural orbitals, with respect to the CASSCF function, and this implies that the four orbital active space is adequate to treat the dimeric system and that no a large improvement is expected by enlarging the active space.' At symmetric geometries the symmetry was lowered to C2 and a nonsymmetric density matrix used as input, deliberately producing localized solutions in all SCF methods. The dimer active orbitals were 9a, 10a and others in the C2 point group with a 1(2B) ground state.
multiplicities_studied: singlet for the neutral, doublet for the anion
nroots_per_mult: Two roots in the CASSI calculation for the dimer
electronic_structure_description: For a single ethene molecule the single-determinant ground-state configuration is 1ag(2) 1b1u(2) 2ag(2) 2b1u(2) 1b3u(2) 3ag(2) 1b2g(2) 1b2u(2). With the inactive orbitals denoted k(2), the neutral form is described by +0.977|k(2) 1b2u(2)| - 0.212|k(2) 1b3g(2)| with the two-orbital space and +0.969|k(2) 1b2u(2)| - 0.242|k(2) 1b3g(2)| with the four-orbital space. Enlarging from two to four pi orbitals changed the C2H4- CC bond length and wave function significantly and improved the ground-state energy by about 3.748 eV; larger spaces gave no substantial further improvement. The CC bond length change on reduction, dR, is 0.105, 0.090 and a third value at the various levels with four pi orbitals in the active space; increasing the space beyond four orbitals did not change the neutral CC bond length. UMP2/6-31G is noted to give overly long bond lengths, and both UHF and MP2 geometries for neutral ethene differ from experiment, but the quantity that matters for electron transfer is dR, the difference between the neutral and anion CC bond lengths. CASPT2 natural orbital occupation numbers for orbitals outside the active space are all below 0.021, the largest being 3b1u (0.021), 4ag (0.016), 2b3u (0.016), 2b2g (0.016) and 4b1u (0.014).
Other: The monomer establishes the space by two complementary tests. Going from two to four pi orbitals lowers the anion ground-state energy by 3.748 eV and materially changes both the CC bond length and the wave function, so two orbitals are demonstrably insufficient; going beyond four changes nothing, so four is a plateau. The second test is the more transferable one: CASPT2 is used explicitly 'to see which inactive orbitals should be included in the active space', and the natural orbital occupations of every orbital outside the space are listed, the largest being 0.021. That is a direct measurement of what the truncation costs rather than an assumption, and it is the same logic later formalized as occupation-number-window selection. Note the quantity being targeted is a DIFFERENCE — the CC bond length change between neutral and anion — which the authors point out is what matters for the reorganization energy even though the absolute geometries from UHF and UMP2 are poor.
reference_short: Rodriguez-Monge & Larsson, J. Phys. Chem. 1996, 100, 6298
notes: Part 3 of a series on conductivity in polyacetylene. The monomer geometries feed a two-site model for electron transfer. Orbital symmetries are referenced to the molecular plane in xy with the CC bond along y.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the pi-CASSCF reference, used both for energies and as a diagnostic of which inactive orbitals carry significant occupation

compound_name: Ethene dimer radical anion (C2H4)2- — two-site model for electron transfer in polyacetylene
point_group: C2 assumed, with a 1(2B) ground state
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at UHF, UMP2 and CASSCF levels. At all symmetric geometries the symmetry was lowered to C2 and a nonsymmetric density matrix supplied as input, so that localized solutions were obtained in all SCF methods. active_space_orbital_description: Four pi orbitals in the C2 point group, the active orbitals including 9a and 10a. Five active orbitals were used for the dimer in one of the tabulated cases.
active_space_protocol: The space is restricted to pi orbitals throughout ('pi-CASSCF'), with two different sizes tested and the adequacy of the larger one established two independent ways. For the monomer, two- and four-pi-orbital spaces were compared: 'For C2H4- the increase to four pi-orbitals in the active space affected the CC bond length and the wave function significantly. The energy of the ground state was improved by about 3.748 eV. Larger active space calculations were performed for C2H4-, but no substantial improvement was achieved. We may conclude that a four pi-orbital active space is enough to describe the electronic structure of the C2H4-.' CASPT2 was then used as a DIAGNOSTIC for what the space is missing: 'CASPT2 can be used to see which inactive orbitals should be included in the active space to take into account additional electronic correlation.' Occupation numbers of the natural orbitals lying outside the active space were inspected, with those above 0.005 listed explicitly — 4ag (0.016), 5ag (0.008), 6ag (0.007), 2b3u (0.016), 3b3u (0.009), 3b2u (0.006), 3b1u (0.021), 4b1u (0.014), 5b1u (0.006) and 2b2g (0.016) — all small enough to justify leaving them inactive. For the dimer the same test was applied: 'CASPT2 does not give significant differences for the occupation numbers of the natural orbitals, with respect to the CASSCF function, and this implies that the four orbital active space is adequate to treat the dimeric system and that no a large improvement is expected by enlarging the active space.' multiplicities_studied: singlet for the neutral, doublet for the anion
nroots_per_mult: Two roots in the CASSI calculation for the dimer
electronic_structure_description: The principal contribution to both the CASSCF and CASPT2 wave functions is the configuration |k(2) 9a(2) 10a(2) 7b(1)|. Localized solutions were obtained in all SCF methods by lowering the symmetry to C2 and supplying a nonsymmetric density matrix. The CASSCF localized solutions give very similar wave functions at the equilibrium and transition points of the ground state. CASPT2 gives no significant difference in the natural orbital occupation numbers relative to CASSCF, confirming the four-orbital space is adequate for the dimer. Perpendicular sections of the two CASSI roots were computed for a monomer separation of 5.9 A, giving an electronic coupling of 0.104 eV. The reaction paths from UHF, UMP2, CASSCF and CASSI all differ. The UHF, UMP2 and CASSCF energy curves have a CUSP at the transition point whereas the CASSI curve changes smoothly. The authors attribute this to UHF and CASSCF being non-linear variation methods that give localized solutions even at the transition point, i.e. symmetry breaking: 'for all values of Ra and Rb there are two local minima which do not know of each other and are degenerate for Ra = Rb. Nonlinear variation methods therefore cannot be used to calculate the Marcus curves.' The potential surfaces can be represented as interacting parabolic-well potentials only in the case of CASSI. Symmetry-adapted wave functions at the transition point give a different energy from the symmetry-broken ones, but the electronic coupling is believed to be correctly obtained as a state energy difference by CASSCF with symmetry-adapted wave functions.
Other: The dimer is where an adequate active space turns out not to be sufficient, because the problem is the variational principle rather than the correlation treatment. CASPT2 confirms the four-orbital space is fine — occupation numbers essentially unchanged from CASSCF — yet the CASSCF energy curve still has an unphysical cusp at the transition point, exactly as UHF and UMP2 do. The diagnosis is precise and general: UHF and CASSCF 'are not linear variation methods and therefore lead to localized solutions even at the transition point', so 'for all values of Ra and Rb there are two local minima which do not know of each other', and 'nonlinear variation methods therefore cannot be used to calculate the Marcus curves'. Only CASSI, which diagonalizes in a basis of separately optimized states, gives the smooth interacting-parabola form the Marcus picture requires. The practical lesson for symmetric electron-transfer systems is that no enlargement of the active space fixes a cusp of this kind — a state-interaction step is needed on top. Note the supporting evidence the authors offer: the CASSCF wave functions at the equilibrium and transition points are almost identical, which is precisely what a localized solution that never delocalizes would look like.

notes: The dimer models a two-site electron transfer relevant to K-doped polyacetylene, whose X-ray diffraction spectra motivated the assumed geometry. The electronic coupling was also estimated by Koopmans' theorem applied to the LUMO and LUMO+1 of the neutral system, a route with no symmetry breaking.

compound_name: [TCNE]2(2-) pi-dimer in dichloromethane — tetracyanoethylene radical anion dimer
point_group: D2h for the isolated dimer; fully optimized structures show small deviations from D2h without symmetry being imposed
geometry_source: Geometries optimized with RB3LYP for the closed-shell singlet and UB3LYP/6-31+G(d) for the open-shell singlet and triplet, without imposing symmetry; the minimum-energy nature of all structures was confirmed by vibrational analysis. CASSCF(2,2) and MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) energies were then computed along the interanion distance using these geometries.
method: CASSCF(2,2) with MCQDPT (multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory), alongside B3LYP in restricted and unrestricted forms and UMP2 for the solvent interaction
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals: the bonding and antibonding combinations of the singly occupied pi* orbitals of the two [TCNE] radical anions. The closed-shell singlet places both electrons in the bonding combination and none in the antibonding; the open-shell singlet and triplet place one in each.
active_space_protocol: A minimal CASSCF(2,2) is used, containing the bonding and antibonding combinations of the two singly occupied pi* orbitals of the [TCNE] radical anions — 'Closed-shell singlet: two electrons in the bonding combination and none in the antibonding. Open-shell singlet and triplet states: one [in each].' The multiconfigurational step is invoked for a specific physical reason: MCQDPT on the CASSCF(2,2) reference is 'a high-level multiconfigurational perturbative calculation, similar to a CASPT2 calculation, which properly includes the dispersion component' — dispersion being what binds the dianion dimer against Coulomb repulsion. The two-orbital space is validated against DFT by comparing natural orbital occupations: at the optimum closed-shell geometry the CASSCF(2,2) occupations for the four orbitals nearest the HOMO are 2.0, 1.62, 0.38, 0.0, essentially identical to the UB3LYP values, and at the open-shell geometry CASSCF(2,2) gives 2.0, 1.02, 0.98, 0.0 against UB3LYP 2.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0. Closed-shell curves were computed at RB3LYP optimum geometries and open-shell curves at UB3LYP/6-31+G(d) geometries, with CASSCF(2,2) and MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) energies evaluated along each.
electronic_structure_description: Experimentally the dimers in solution have an interaction enthalpy of -33.1 kJ/mol, but an isolated D2h pi-[TCNE]2(2-) at an intradimer separation of 3.05 A is unstable against dissociation into monomers by 59.8 kcal/mol (250 kJ/mol) at B3LYP/6-31+G(d) and by 37.7 kcal/mol (157.7 kJ/mol) at MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2). Natural orbital occupations for the four orbitals nearest the HOMO: at the optimum closed-shell geometry, RB3LYP gives 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0 while UB3LYP gives 2.0, 1.62, 0.38, 0.0 and CASSCF(2,2) gives the same 2.0, 1.62, 0.38, 0.0; at the optimum open-shell geometry UB3LYP gives 2.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0 and CASSCF(2,2) gives 2.0, 1.02, 0.98, 0.0. The RB3LYP wave function is purely monodeterminantal while the UB3LYP is multideterminantal, so the two are describing different electronic structures. Interanion distances differ markedly between states: 3.033 A in the closed-shell singlet, 5.227 A in the open-shell singlet and 5.232 A in the triplet, so only in the closed-shell singlet are the two anions close enough to interact. For the [TCNE]2(2-)(CH2Cl2)4 aggregate the CASSCF(2,2) curve has only one minimum, of open-shell singlet type, whereas the MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) curve has its only minimum at 2.75 A and is closed-shell — so once dispersion is properly included the aggregate has a diamagnetic-like closed-shell singlet ground state, in agreement with the experimental behaviour of [TCNE] radical anion dichloromethane solutions at low temperature. That MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) minimum is energetically stable by -24.0 kcal/mol (101 kJ/mol), consistent with the dimers dissociating only on warming. The [TCNE] radical anion to CH2Cl2 interactions contribute 48 kcal/mol and overcompensate the anion-anion repulsion; a counterpoise-corrected interaction energy of -6 kcal/mol (-25 kJ/mol) is reported for a single solvent contact.
Other: A two-orbital active space is about as small as a multiconfigurational treatment gets, and this paper shows both why it suffices and why it is not enough on its own. It suffices because the chemistry is entirely the pairing of two singly occupied pi* orbitals — the CASSCF(2,2) natural occupations reproduce the UB3LYP values essentially exactly at both the closed-shell (2.0, 1.62, 0.38, 0.0) and open-shell (2.0, 1.02, 0.98, 0.0) geometries, so nothing outside those two orbitals is doing anything. It is not enough on its own because the binding is dispersive: the bare CASSCF(2,2) curve for the solvated aggregate has only an OPEN-SHELL minimum, and only when MCQDPT is added does a closed-shell minimum appear at 2.75 A — the correct answer against experiment. So the space identifies the right two states and the perturbative correction decides between them, and using either alone would give the wrong ground state. The paper is also a clean demonstration that a natural-occupation comparison can diagnose what a DFT calculation is doing: RB3LYP gives 2.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0 and is monodeterminantal while UB3LYP gives 2.0, 1.62, 0.38, 0.0 at the same geometry and is multideterminantal, so the two functionals are describing different electronic structures rather than the same one at different accuracy.
reference_short: Garcia-Yoldi, Miller & Novoa, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 8020
notes: The stability of the dianion dimers in solution is attributed to [TCNE] radical anion to solvent interactions overcompensating the anion-anion repulsion, demonstrated with [TCNE]2(2-)(solvent)4 aggregates whose minimum-energy structures are stable against dissociation. The aggregate geometry resembles that found in crystals. The extra stabilization from bulk solvent beyond the four explicit molecules could not be evaluated at the MCQDPT/CASSCF(2,2) level.
correlation_correction: MCQDPT (multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory) on the CASSCF(2,2) reference, described as similar to CASPT2 and as the step that properly includes dispersion

compound_name: p-Aminobenzonitrile (ABN) — aqueous solvation of the excited states
point_group: Cs imposed for the CASSCF and MC-QDPT2 calculations
geometry_source: Geometries at each condition (isolated molecule, in methanol, and eight solvent-density conditions) fully optimized with DFT (B3LYP)/cc-pVDZ. State-specific CASSCF and MC-QDPT2 were then carried out under Cs symmetry at those geometries; CASSCF-optimized geometries were also used for comparison. In the RISM-SCF-SEDD calculations for the excited states, the RISM procedure was converged with respect to the wave function of each state.
method: State-specific CASSCF with MC-QDPT2, coupled to the RISM-SCF-SEDD solvation theory (reference interaction site model self-consistent field with spatial electron density distribution)
software: Not stated in the extracted text beyond a modified package used to implement RISM-SCF-SEDD
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the DFT geometry optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: Nine active orbitals holding ten electrons: three pi and three pi* orbitals of the benzene ring, the pi and pi* of the C-N triple bond, and the lone pair of the amino group. Nine chemical core orbitals were frozen in the subsequent perturbation step.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled fragment by fragment to cover exactly the three moieties whose interplay defines the photophysics: the benzene ring (three pi and three pi*), the cyano acceptor (pi and pi*) and the amino donor (lone pair). That is the minimum set able to represent both locally excited benzene states and any donor-to-acceptor charge transfer. State-specific rather than state-averaged CASSCF was used, with the Cs point group imposed so the A' and A'' states are separately optimized. Nine chemical core orbitals were frozen at the MC-QDPT2 stage. The same space is applied to the isolated molecule and to every solvent density condition, so solvation shifts are measured against a fixed orbital description of the solute.
nroots_per_mult: State-specific
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in eV in the gas phase for S0, S1 (1B2) and S2 (2A1). At the DFT geometry, CASSCF gives 0.00 (-377.599556 au), 4.73 and 6.32; at the CASSCF geometry 0.00 (-377.601692 au), 4.78 and 6.52. MC-QDPT2 gives 0.00 (-378.754131 au), 4.26 and 4.93 at the DFT geometry and 0.00 (-378.751058 au), 4.32 and 5.09 at the CASSCF geometry. Literature comparisons: 4.15 eV for the 0-0 transition (Gibson et al.), 4.01 and 4.44 eV (Serrano-Andres et al., CASPT2), 4.26 and 4.98 eV (Sobolewski et al., CASPT2), 4.27 and 5.13 eV (Parusel et al., STEOM). Dipole moments in debye for the three states: CASSCF gives 6.04, 5.76 and 12.14 at the DFT geometry and 5.69, 5.47 and 11.80 at the CASSCF geometry; MC-QDPT2 gives 6.19, 6.58 and 10.71 at the DFT geometry and 5.83, 6.23 and 10.34 at the CASSCF geometry, against experimental values of 6.6, 8.0 to 8.5 (Schuddeboom et al.) and 6.41, 7.20 (Borst et al.). The S1 state is a mixture of various pi-pi* transitions and lies about 15 kcal/mol below S2 in the gas phase. In the UV spectrum the peak corresponds to 1La (the S2, A' state) and the shoulder to 1Lb (the S1, A'' state). With increasing solvent density both excitation energies red shift; the S2 state shows remarkable density dependence indicating strong solvation, with the change in solvation free energy responsible for the main red shift, while the S1 state behaves similarly to the ground state. The cyano group draws further electron density as the solvent density increases.
Other: The nine-orbital space is built by fragment — three pi and three pi* on the ring, pi and pi* on the nitrile, and the amino lone pair — which is exactly what a donor-acceptor aromatic needs if both locally excited and charge-transfer states are to be representable in one space. The internal evidence that this matters is the dipole moments: 6.04, 5.76 and 12.14 D for S0, S1 and S2 at CASSCF, so S2 is the charge-transfer state carrying twice the ground-state dipole while S1 is essentially locally excited. Only a space containing both the amino lone pair (the donor) and the nitrile pi* (the acceptor) can produce that 12 D state at all. The perturbative correction acts very unevenly between the two: MC-QDPT2 lowers S1 by 0.47 eV but S2 by 1.39 eV, closing the S1-S2 gap from 1.59 to 0.67 eV, so the near-degeneracy that the paper emphasizes (about 15 kcal/mol) is a product of dynamical correlation rather than of the reference. The dipole moments move in the opposite direction under correlation — S2 falls from 12.14 to 10.71 D while S1 rises from 5.76 to 6.58 — meaning the CASSCF reference overstates the charge separation of the CT state and understates it for the locally excited one. Since the whole study measures solvation shifts driven by these dipoles across eight solvent densities, and the same space is used throughout, the density trends are internally consistent even though the absolute dipoles carry that method dependence.
reference_short: Yokogawa, Sato, Sakaki & Kimura, J. Phys. Chem. B 2010, 114, 910
notes: RISM-SCF-SEDD combines ab initio electronic structure theory with the reference interaction site model, using the hypernetted chain closure, and is essentially free from statistical error. The study examines excitation energies and solvation structure across eight reduced solvent densities plus the isolated molecule and methanol. Previous studies noted a slight geometry dependence of the excitation energies with respect to amino group wagging and twist angle.
correlation_correction: MC-QDPT2 (multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory) with nine chemical core orbitals frozen

geometry_source: Geometries optimized at the CASSCF level with the pVTZ (ANO-L) basis set, initially under the highest possible molecular symmetry (C2v or Cs); states with imaginary frequencies were reoptimized under reduced symmetry constraints where possible. Energies include an unscaled zero-point correction. States that could not be optimized without symmetry (root switching and conical intersections were encountered) are reported at the symmetry-optimized geometry together with a CASPT2 vertical energy from the ground-state optimized geometry.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF (CASPT2 single points at CASSCF-optimized geometries), with CCSD(T), CBS-Q and B3LYP as single-reference corroboration for the closed-shell single-reference states
software: MOLCAS 7.4 for all CASPT2/CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 09 for CCSD(T), B3LYP and CBS-Q; orbitals inspected with Molden
basis_set: ANO-L basis set of Widmark et al., of polarized valence triple-zeta (pVTZ) quality; cc-pVDZ for the CCSD(T) comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in nine orbitals. The active space comprised all of the pi and pi* orbitals, the in-plane oxygen p orbital, and any lone pair electrons and sigma orbitals on nitrogen atoms. In the few cases where the lone pair of electrons does not contribute significantly (electron population about 2), the orbital containing the lone pair was sometimes replaced with a sigma orbital of identical symmetry, also with an occupation of about 2.
active_space_protocol: The recipe is stated as a rule rather than a per-molecule choice: all pi and pi* orbitals, the in-plane oxygen p orbital, and any nitrogen lone pair electrons and sigma orbitals. Applied to a monoaza ring this yields (10,9) uniformly for the 2-, 3- and 4-pyridinyl ions, so the three isomers can be compared on absolute energies. The space is not frozen in composition: all active orbitals were inspected with Molden, and where a lone pair turned out to carry an occupation of about 2 (i.e. not correlating) it was replaced by a sigma orbital of the same symmetry and similar occupation, keeping the size fixed while swapping in an orbital that does work. The method was calibrated beforehand on the phenyl oxenium ion (singlet-triplet gap -22.1 kcal/mol against -19.8 experimental) and on isoelectronic phenyl nitrene (+17.2 and +31.4 kcal/mol against 18 and 30 experimental).
nroots_per_mult: The lowest state of each irreducible representation at the highest molecular symmetry was computed
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies, adiabatic (vertical in parentheses), in kcal/mol under Cs: 1(1A') 0; 1(1A'') 23.8; 1(3A') 36.3 with an imaginary frequency upon optimization under symmetry (49.0 vertical); 1(3A'') 16.4. The singlet-triplet gap (1A'-3A'') is 16.4 kcal/mol between the closed-shell singlet and an n,pi* triplet state, so the ground state is the closed-shell singlet. A very short C-O bond length of 1.205 A for the ground singlet state implicates a quinoidal structure with significant charge on the carbon para to the oxygen, resembling an azacyclohexadienonyl cation. These two states are identical to the lowest energy states of the phenyl oxenium ion but with the gap reduced by 6 kcal/mol (phenyl oxenium is -22.1 kcal/mol between 1A1 and 3A2 at the same level). Compared with the 4-pyridinyl isomer the singlet of 2 is more stable by 67 kcal/mol, offset by the triplet being stabilized by 53 kcal/mol.
Other: Because the same (10,9) rule-based space is applied to all three pyridinyl isomers, and they are isomers of each other, absolute CASPT2 energies can be compared directly across them -- which is how the paper isolates singlet destabilization rather than triplet stabilization as the cause of the changing gaps. That analysis is only legitimate because the space is defined by a composition rule (all pi/pi*, in-plane O p, nitrogen lone pairs and sigma) instead of being tuned per molecule; a per-isomer space would have made the absolute energies incommensurable. The space is validated externally rather than by internal enlargement: the identical protocol gives -22.1 kcal/mol for phenyl oxenium against -19.8 experimental, and +17.2 / +31.4 kcal/mol for isoelectronic phenyl nitrene against 18 / 30 experimental. For this ion, whose lowest singlet is essentially single-determinantal, CCSD(T)/cc-pVDZ and CBS-Q reproduce the CASPT2 gap to within 5 kcal/mol, whereas B3LYP underestimates the singlet energy by more than 10 kcal/mol.
reference_short: Hanway & Winter, J. Phys. Chem. A 2012, 116, 9398
notes: Most of the states can be reasonably well represented as a single determinant, so the major determinant is used to label the configurations. States are designated by the irreducible representation at the highest possible molecular symmetry even when the optimized structure for that configuration is nonplanar.

The (12,10) space itself proved insufficient for one state: the 3B1 root required expansion to (12,12) merely to converge, so the nominal space size is not uniform across the state manifold of this ion. That is only visible because all active orbitals were inspected in Molden rather than assumed from the construction rule, and it means the (12,10) space must carry both lone-pair combinations, not one lone pair plus a spectator. The consequence is a near-triple degeneracy of 1A', 3A'' and 1A'' within 3.9 kcal/mol, which is far below any reasonable error bar for CASPT2 on a (12,10) reference; the paper accordingly declines to assign a ground state. compound_name: 2-Methylfuran (model for the triplet-state photoisomerization of furans)
geometry_source: Stationary point structures on the S0 and T1 surfaces optimized at the CASSCF level with the 6-311G(d) basis set. Every stationary point was characterized by analytic harmonic frequencies at the CASSCF level (minima all real, transition states one imaginary frequency). Optimization converged when the maximum force and its rms were below 0.00045 and 0.00005 hartree/bohr. Minima, transition states and crossing minima were located in Cartesian coordinates, so the results are independent of any specific choice of internal variables. The state-averaged CASSCF(10,8) method was used to determine geometries on the intersection space.
method: CASSCF(10,8) for geometries and state-averaged CASSCF(10,8) for the intersection space, with MP2-CAS (multireference Moller-Plesset) single points for dynamic correlation
basis_set: 6-311G(d) for the CASSCF optimizations and MP2-CAS single points; the abstract and Table 1 caption also cite 6-311G(d,p)
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: five p pi orbitals, one lone pair orbital, plus the sigma(C-C) and sigma*(C-C) orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled to cover both the chromophore and the bond that breaks. The five ring pi orbitals and the oxygen lone pair describe the n-pi* triplet reached by photoexcitation; the sigma(C-C) and sigma*(C-C) pair is added because the isomerization proceeds by ring opening and contraction, and a sigma bond cannot be broken correctly if its bonding and antibonding partners are outside the space. State-averaged CASSCF over the same (10,8) space is used where the T1 and S0 surfaces intersect, since a state-specific wave function is not usable at a crossing. The same space is carried through every stationary point of all three reaction paths so the whole profile is on one footing, and MP2-CAS(10,8) single points at the CASSCF(10,8) geometries supply the dynamic correlation.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged CASSCF used for the intersection space
electronic_structure_description: Energies in kcal/mol relative to 2-methylfuran at MP2-CAS(10,8)/6-311G(d,p) with CASSCF(10,8)/6-311G(d) in parentheses. Rea-1 (S0) 0.0 (0.0); FC 123.1 (145.4); T1-Rea (T1) 96.31 (114.5); TS-1 (T1) 116.4 (117.2); T1/S0-1 crossing 91.37 (92.07); Int-T (T1) 78.31 (57.68); Int-S (S0) 69.36 (50.82); TS-2 (S0) 77.47 (80.52); Int-3 (S0) 59.34 (70.34); TS-3 (S0) 75.10 (90.02); Pro-1 (S0) -18.06 (-22.08); Int-2 (S0) 41.35 (43.78); TS-4 (S0) 81.76 (60.76); TS-5 (S0) 88.64 (49.75); 3-methylfuran (Pro-2, S0) 9.068 (1.079). The computed triplet vertical excitation energy is 123 kcal/mol at MP2-CAS(10,8)/6-311G(d) against an experimental value of 113 kcal/mol (254 nm). T1-Rea is a slightly nonplanar minimum with an O1C2C3C4 dihedral of about 11 degrees and ring bonds longer than in the ground state; TS-1 for O-C bond breaking has an imaginary frequency of 830i per cm and lies 20 kcal/mol above T1-Rea. The T1/S0-1 intersection is nonplanar with an O1C2C3C4 dihedral of about 36 degrees, lying 91 kcal/mol above Rea-1 and 32 kcal/mol below FC; intersystem crossing from 3(n,pi*) to 1(n,pi*) occurs there. Int-T and Int-S both have a carbene-like structure with two unpaired electrons on the same carbon atom and are separated by about 9.0 kcal/mol with the triplet above the singlet.
Other: Table 1 reports both levels for every critical point, which turns this into a direct measure of what the (10,8) reference alone gets wrong: dynamic correlation does not shift the profile uniformly but reorders it. At CASSCF, TS-4 (60.76) and TS-5 (49.75) sit below the intermediate Int-2 and near Int-S, while at MP2-CAS they rise to 81.76 and 88.64 -- swings of 21 and 39 kcal/mol that convert apparently barrierless steps into real barriers and change which of paths A, B and C is competitive. Int-3 and TS-3 move the other way (70.34 to 59.34 and 90.02 to 75.10), and the vertical triplet excitation falls from 145.4 to 123.1, the latter matching the 113 kcal/mol experimental value far better. Meanwhile points where the two levels agree closely -- TS-1 (117.2 vs 116.4) and the T1/S0-1 crossing (92.07 vs 91.37) -- show the (10,8) reference is adequate where the wave function is dominated by the ring-opening coordinate it was built for. The failures cluster at the carbene-like biradical structures (Int-T, Int-S) and the late ground-state transition states, where an eight-orbital space with only one sigma/sigma* pair is thinnest. Note also that the two carbene-like intermediates differ by only 9 kcal/mol at MP2-CAS but 6.9 kcal/mol at CASSCF, so the singlet-triplet ordering there is stable while the barriers around them are not.
reference_short: Su, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 194
notes: 2-Methylfuran serves as the model system for furan photoisomerization from the triplet state. Three reaction paths are traced: path A to Pro-1, path B back to Rea-1, and path C to 3-methylfuran (Pro-2). Cartesian coordinates and energetics at both levels are in the Supporting Information. The basis set is quoted as 6-311G(d) in the methods section but as 6-311G(d,p) in the abstract and Table 1 caption; both are transcribed as printed.

compound_name: Hydroxyl acetylene (H-C#C-OH) adsorbed on the Si(100)-2x1 surface
formula: C2OSi9H14 quantum region embedded in a C2OSi48H38 cluster
point_group: All computations were done without imposing symmetry unless otherwise specified
geometry_source: Geometries fully optimized at the SIMOMM:CASSCF/6-31G(d) level with the channel-specific active spaces; geometric data throughout are from the CASSCF results. Each stationary point was characterized by computing and diagonalizing the Hessian matrix. Minimum energy paths (intrinsic reaction coordinates) were followed with the Gonzalez-Schlegel second-order method using a step size of 0.3 amu^(1/2) bohr.
method: SIMOMM (surface integrated molecular orbital molecular mechanics) QM/MM with CASSCF for the quantum region and MRMP2 single points; the MRMP2 implementation used is MCQDPT2 (multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory). MM3 parameters for the molecular mechanics part.
basis_set: All-electron 6-31G(d) throughout; 6-31G(d,p) tested in the preliminary comparison and found to have very little effect
active_space_orbital_description: Six different active spaces, one per reaction channel (Table 2). pi-complex channel (6,6): two electrons in the pi and pi* orbitals of the C#C bond plus four electrons in the pi, pi*, sigma and sigma* orbitals of the surface Si dimer. O-H bond activation channel (8,6): two electrons in the pi and pi* orbitals of the surface Si dimer, two electrons in the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the O-H bond, and four electrons in the two nonbonding orbitals of oxygen. C-O bond activation channel (8,6): two electrons in the pi and pi* of the surface Si dimer, two electrons in the sigma and sigma* of the C-O bond, and four electrons in the two nonbonding orbitals of oxygen. C-H bond activation channel (4,4): two electrons in the sigma and sigma* of the C-H bond plus two electrons in the pi and pi* of the surface Si dimer. Isomerization to the surface hydroxylated product (10,8): two electrons in the sigma and sigma* of the C-O bond, four electrons in the sigma and sigma* orbitals of two Si-C bonds, and four electrons in the two nonbonding orbitals of oxygen. Isomerization to the surface ketene product (8,6): two electrons in the sigma and sigma* of the Si-C bond, two electrons in the sigma and sigma* of the O-H bond, and four electrons in the two nonbonding orbitals of oxygen. A large common (10,10) space was used to recompute all product stabilities: two electrons in the pi and pi* of C#C, two electrons in the pi and pi* of the surface Si dimer, and six electrons in the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-O, C-H and O-H bonds.
active_space_protocol: Rather than one space for the whole surface chemistry, six channel-specific spaces were designed, each containing the surface Si dimer pi/pi* plus exactly the bond being made or broken in that channel (C#C pi for the pi-complex, O-H sigma/sigma* for O-H activation, C-O sigma/sigma* for C-O activation, C-H sigma/sigma* for C-H activation), with the two oxygen nonbonding orbitals added wherever oxygen is involved. Sizes range from (4,4) to (10,8). Because relative energies computed with different spaces are not strictly comparable, all product stabilities were recomputed with a single large common (10,10) space containing every bond that any channel touches, and the two sets were compared. The choice of CASSCF over single-reference methods was itself justified by a preliminary three-point test on the [2+2] channel.
electronic_structure_description: Preliminary comparison for three stationary points of the [2+2] cycloaddition channel (R, TS2, P1) in kcal/mol: SIMOMM:MP2/6-31G(d) 0.0, -2.4, -77.8; SIMOMM:MP2/6-31G(d,p) 0.0, -2.2, -77.5; SIMOMM:CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d) 0.0, 18.1, -64.4; SIMOMM:CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d,p) 0.0, 18.2, -64.0; SIMOMM:MRMP2(6,6)/6-31G(d) 0.0, 9.5, -63.7; SIMOMM:MRMP2(6,6)/6-31G(d,p) 0.0, 9.7, -64.1; SIMOMM:B3LYP/6-311G(d) 0.0, -3.2, -77.2; SIMOMM:B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) 0.0, -4.7, -77.5. Relative energies of the surface products in kcal/mol, with the individual channel active spaces and then with the common (10,10) space: P1 -63.7 / -66.9; P2 -59.6 / -66.2; P3 -79.9 / -85.6; P4 -50.9 / -56.6; P5 -63.1 / -66.3; P6 -102.2 / -102.8. Four initial adsorption channels were found ([2+2] cycloaddition, O-H, C-O and C-H bond cleavage) plus two subsequent isomerizations of the [2+2] product P1: to the surface hydroxylated product P3 via TS7 (internal barrier -7.0 kcal/mol) and the alkylidene carbene intermediate I4, and to the surface ketene product P6 via the bond-rotation transition state TS9 and hydrogen transfer TS10 (internal barrier -17.9 kcal/mol). P6 is the most stable product of all channels.
Other: Two separate active-space findings sit on top of each other here. First, the decision to use CASSCF at all rests on a diagnostic rather than a preference: for the [2+2] transition state TS2, single-reference MP2 and B3LYP give negative barriers (-2.4 and -3.2 kcal/mol) while CASSCF(6,6) and MRMP2(6,6) give positive ones (18.1 and 9.5), and the single-reference methods also overestimate the binding energy of P1 by about 14 kcal/mol (-77.8 vs -63.7). A sign change in a barrier is not a quantitative discrepancy, so the multiconfigurational treatment is load-bearing for the mechanism. Second, using six different channel-tailored spaces makes the energies of different channels formally incommensurable, and the paper tests exactly that by recomputing every product with one common (10,10) space: the individual-space and (10,10) values agree to about 5 kcal/mol, but not uniformly -- P2 shifts by 6.6 and P3 by 5.7 kcal/mol while P6 shifts by only 0.6. The spread is systematic and one-signed (the larger space always stabilizes the product), so the relative ordering of products survives even though the absolute stabilities do not, which is what licenses the mechanistic conclusions. Note the caption of Table 3 refers the reader to Table 1 for the individual active spaces, while they are actually given in Table 2.
reference_short: Ghosh & Choi, J. Phys. Chem. C 2010, 114, 14187
notes: The QM/MM model embeds a C2OSi9H14 quantum region in a C2OSi48H38 cluster, with one surface Si dimer in the QM region and three in the MM region. Relative energies are measured against separated H-C#C-OH plus the bare surface using the active space of the corresponding channel. Basis set and cluster size effects were studied systematically and 6-31G(d) was found to perform well against larger basis sets.
