software: COLUMBUS program package (used for the SD-CI rotational curve)
basis_set: Standard Huzinaga (9s5p) Gaussian set for the heavy atoms in a Dunning [4s2p] contraction, plus two d functions with exponents 1.4 and 0.35 on carbon and 1.7 and 0.425 on oxygen, and a p function with exponent 0.059 on oxygen; for hydrogen the (5s) basis of Whitten et al. in a [2s] contraction with scaling factor eta^2 = 2.0, plus polarization p functions with exponent 0.735
active_space_orbital_description: Eight active electrons -- the four p electrons on oxygen and the pi and sigma(CC) electrons on ethene -- distributed among eight active orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The CASSCF is used only to generate molecular orbitals as the one-particle basis for the MRD-CI, not for the energetics. The eight electrons chosen are exactly those that change bonding character along the reaction coordinate: the four oxygen p electrons that split into in-plane and out-of-plane sets as the atom approaches, and the ethene pi and sigma(CC) electrons that reorganize as the attacked carbon rehybridizes from sp2 to sp3. The MRD-CI on top used six reference configurations, with configuration spaces from single and double excitations of the order of 30 million, secular equations of the order of 20000 at a configuration selection threshold of 3.5 microhartree, and an estimated full CI correction. The carbon and oxygen 1s orbitals were always kept doubly occupied and the same number of highest virtual orbitals discarded in the MRD-CI. For the CH2 rotational potential, where multireference effects were not expected to matter, plain SD-CI was used instead.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 3A''(pi,sigma) with configuration 1a'^2 ... 9a'^2 10a' 1a''^2 2a''^2 3a''. At the ground state minimum the total CASSCF energy is -152.9308 hartree, the MRD-CI energy -153.2905 hartree and the estimated full CI energy -153.3250 hartree. The OC2H4 biradical is stable relative to dissociation into O(3P) + C2H4 at every level: the energy difference between fragments and product is 14.4 kcal/mol at estimated full CI, 12.6 kcal/mol at MRD-CI and 9.0 kcal/mol at CASSCF. A definite barrier separates fragments and product: CASSCF predicts a transition state 8.9 kcal/mol above the reactants while the estimated full CI gives an activation energy of only 4.7 kcal/mol, against an experimental value of 2 kcal/mol; the earlier MCSCF work of Dupuis et al. gave 16 kcal/mol. The barrier top is at R(CO) about 2.1 A, and vibrational effects reduce the calculated barrier by 0.5 kcal/mol. Relative energies of the low-lying 3OCH2CH2 diradical states in kcal/mol, SCF then estimated full CI: 3A''(pi,sigma) 0.0 / 0.0; the same with 90 degree rotation 0.5 / 3.9; 3A'(sigma,sigma) ...8a'^2 9a'^2 10a' 3a''^2 2.1 / 3.6; that state with 90 degree rotation 1.2 / 4.8. The first excited state (9a' to 3a''), which correlates with the electronic ground state of the 3CH2 + C2H4 surface, lies only 3.6 kcal/mol above the minimum at estimated full CI because the excitation is between two orbitals primarily localized on oxygen; the two states are degenerate at the dissociation limit. Charge transfer from ethene to oxygen peaks at R(CO) = 1.8 A, and the top of the SCF barrier coincides with the change from the electrophilic to the nucleophilic phase.
Other: The barrier is where the reference level fails hardest, and the paper quantifies it three ways: 16 kcal/mol from the earlier MCSCF work, 8.9 kcal/mol at CASSCF(8,8) here, 4.7 kcal/mol at estimated full CI, against 2 kcal/mol experimental. Each successive treatment of dynamical correlation halves the barrier, so the eight-orbital reference on its own is not merely imprecise but wrong by a factor of four -- the authors state plainly that proper inclusion of electron correlation is very important for the description of the barrier height. The well depth is far less sensitive (9.0 / 12.6 / 14.4 kcal/mol), which is the expected pattern: the reference space describes the bound biradical adequately but not the partially ionic O(-)C2H4(+) character that develops at the barrier, where an avoided crossing between ionic and covalent states occurs. The paper notes this mixing happens at the MO level rather than the configuration level because of the low symmetry, which is precisely why orbital choice matters here. A second sensitivity appears in the state ordering: at SCF the 3A'(sigma,sigma) state lies 2.1 kcal/mol above the ground state and the 90-degree-rotated 3A''(pi,sigma) only 0.5 kcal/mol, but at estimated full CI these become 3.6 and 3.9 kcal/mol, reversing which of the two is the lower excited structure. The rotational barrier of 5-6 kcal/mol was computed at plain SD-CI on the explicit judgement that multireference effects are not important for that distortion.
reference_short: Wortmann-Saleh, Engels & Peyerimhoff, J. Phys. Chem. 1994, 98, 9541
notes: The labels (pi,sigma) describe the orientation of the unpaired electrons: the first character refers to the unpaired electron on the terminal carbon, the second to the one on oxygen, with sigma meaning in the CCO plane and pi out of plane. The study compares OC2H4 with the isoelectronic CH2C2H4, whose ground state is 3A' rather than 3A'' because the degeneracy of the attacking fragment's p orbitals is already lifted in the CH2 fragmentation channel.
correlation_correction: MRD-CI with six reference configurations plus an estimated full CI (multireference Davidson) correction

geometry_source: Three sets of equilibrium geometries for the S0, S1 and D0 states, all with cc-pVDZ: (8,7)-CASSCF/cc-pVDZ optimizations with normal-mode analyses taken from Watkins et al. (ref 17); internally contracted MRCI/cc-pVDZ optimizations performed here on top of those state-specific CASSCF wave functions; and SACCI/cc-pVDZ optimizations using the full valence space as active space, started from the (8,7)-CASSCF geometries and stopped after three macroiterations.
method: State-specific (8,7)-CASSCF, internally contracted MRCI built on those CASSCF wave functions, and SACCI, each used to generate geometries for rotational band-contour and Franck-Condon simulations of the REMPI and ZEKE/MATI spectra
software: MOLPRO version 2002.6 for the MRCI calculations; Gaussian 03 for the SACCI calculations; Asymmetric Rotor Simulation (A.R.S.) program of M. S. Ford for the rotational simulations
active_space_orbital_description: An (8,7) active space, the same active space employed for the phenol monomer in the earlier work of Schumm et al. The individual orbitals are not enumerated in this paper.
active_space_protocol: The cluster inherits its active space unchanged from the phenol monomer: the (8,7) space used by Schumm et al. for bare phenol was applied to phenol-nitrogen on the assumption that the N2 partner does not participate in the S0, S1 or D0 electronic structure. State-specific CASSCF wave functions were optimized separately for each of the three states and then used as the reference for internally contracted MRCI (4723992 uncontracted CSFs internally contracted to 241332 configurations for S0 and S1; 5276334 contracted to 251622 for D0). The SACCI calculations deliberately abandon this restricted space and use the full valence space instead, providing an independent check of whether the seven-orbital description is the limiting approximation.
nroots_per_mult: State-specific for S0, S1 and D0
electronic_structure_description: Rotational constants in MHz from the equilibrium geometries (CASSCF / MRCI / SACCI, with two sets of experimental values). S0: A 4067.3 / 4087.9 / 4105.4, expt 4072.2 and 4046.6 +/- 4.2; B 620.3 / 620.8 / 616.8, expt 648.0 and 587.4 +/- 2.3; C 538.2 / 538.9 / 536.2, expt 559.3 and 538.4 +/- 0.5. S1: A 3931.6 / 3963.3 / 4014.2, expt 3930.7 and 4011.9 +/- 4.5; B 615.9 / 616.8 / 627.1, expt 663.7 and 631.7 +/- 2.7; C 532.5 / 533.7 / 542.4, expt 567.8 and 524.7 +/- 0.9. D0: A 4266.8 / 4282.5 / 4271.4; B 679.1 / 679.6 / 671.3; C 585.9 / 586.5 / 580.1. On S0 to S1 excitation, CASSCF and MRCI predict changes in A of -135.7 and -124.5 MHz, close to experiment, but predict both B and C to decrease, whereas experiment shows the opposite; SACCI underestimates the change in A (-91.2 MHz) but reproduces the changes in B and C (+10.3 and +6.2 MHz). Bond length changes on S0 to S1 (in pm) include C-OH -0.7, ring C1-C2a +3.7, C2a-C3a +3.4, C3a-C4 +4.1, C3b-C4 +3.5, C2b-C3b +4.2, C1-C2b +2.9, with N1-N2 unchanged at 0.0. On S1 to D0 the H-N1 hydrogen bond contracts by 40.3 pm and C-OH by 7.7 pm. The predicted S0-S1 geometry changes of phenol itself are not greatly affected by the N2 moiety at the levels of theory used.
Other: The decisive observation is that adding dynamical correlation on top of the (8,7) reference changes essentially nothing: the internally contracted MRCI geometries, built on nearly five million CSFs from those same state-specific CASSCF wave functions, give rotational constants within about 20 MHz of CASSCF and Franck-Condon simulations that are almost identical to it, failing in exactly the same way -- the intensities in mode 6a are wrong and both methods predict the B and C rotational constants to decrease on excitation when experiment shows them increasing. SACCI, which uses the full valence space rather than seven orbitals, fixes both the sign of the B and C changes and the mode 6a intensities. Since MRCI corrects correlation but keeps the seven-orbital reference while SACCI changes the space, the residual error is attributable to the space rather than to the correlation treatment. This matters because the earlier work on bare phenol had already found the same thing and had patched it by hand -- manually shortening the S1 C-O bond and elongating along mode 6a to force agreement -- and the paper notes that vibronic transition intensities are extremely sensitive to the upper and lower state geometries, so Franck-Condon simulation is being used here as a diagnostic of active-space quality. Caveat on the SACCI side: the geometries after three macroiterations are not operator-guess-independent converged, so its advantage is real but not fully converged either.
reference_short: Pugliesi, Watkins & Muller-Dethlefs, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 4668
notes: The (8,7)-CASSCF geometries and normal modes are taken from Watkins, Muller-Dethlefs & Cockett, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2000, 2, 5528, which in turn used the phenol monomer active space of Schumm et al., Chem. Phys. Lett. 1996, 263, 126. The SACCI calculations included all single excitation operators in the linked terms with a level two perturbation selection for the linked doubles and no R2S2-type unlinked operators, giving 43586 operators for the SAC wave function, 30962 for the S1 SACCI and 7233 for the D0 SACCI.
correlation_correction: Internally contracted MRCI on the state-specific CASSCF wave functions; SACCI as an independent single-reference-based correlated treatment

compound_name: Lithium fluoride (LiF) dissociation and the ionic-covalent avoided crossing
geometry_source: Potential energy curves computed as a function of the LiF bond length from about 2 to 18 bohr; the equilibrium ground state distance is quoted as 2.98 bohr.
method: ORMAS-PT (quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory on an occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field reference), benchmarked against full CAS-based MRMP/MCQDPT
software: GAMESS (General Atomic and Molecular Electronic Structure System); ORMAS-PT implemented there
basis_set: 6-311++G(3df,3pd) for all MCQDPT and ORMAS-PT calculations
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(6,9) in C2v symmetry: 4a1, 5a1, 6a1, 1b1, 2b1, 3b1, 1b2, 2b2, 3b2. Molecular orbitals 1a1, 2a1 and 3a1 correspond to the fluorine 1s and 2s and the lithium 1s atomic orbitals; these are chemically inactive and remain in the core. For ORMAS the same nine orbitals are partitioned into three three-orbital subspaces {4a1,5a1,6a1}, {1b1,2b1,3b1} and {1b2,2b2,3b2}, each restricted to a minimum and maximum of 2 electrons.
active_space_protocol: The complete space is chosen along symmetry lines -- three orbitals in each of the a1, b1 and b2 blocks -- and the ORMAS partition then simply makes each symmetry block its own subspace with exactly two electrons, which is the natural partition for a diatomic where the two pi-like blocks are equivalent. Orbitals are state-averaged over the two lowest 1Sigma+ states so that both the ionic and the covalent state are described on an equal footing across the avoided crossing. The test asks whether truncating the CI expansion this way still reproduces the avoided crossing that the full CAS(6,9) reference produces.
nroots_per_mult: Two lowest 1Sigma+ states, state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: The two lowest 1Sigma+ states are examined. Near the equilibrium geometry the lower state is ionic or at least highly polar and the higher state covalent; after the avoided crossing, around 12-13 bohr, the characters swap. ORMAS-PT and MCQDPT curves overlap so closely that they are difficult to distinguish, and ORMAS-PT reproduces both the equilibrium geometry and the avoided crossing. Beyond 2.9 bohr the ORMAS-PT singlet-singlet energy splitting differs from MCQDPT by less than 0.2 kcal/mol; at the two shortest bond distances ORMAS-PT overestimates the splitting by 2.4 and 3.0 kcal/mol.
Other: The one place the occupation-restricted reference fails is at short bond length, where the error in the singlet-singlet splitting jumps to 2.4-3.0 kcal/mol against less than 0.2 kcal/mol everywhere beyond 2.9 bohr. The authors attribute this directly to the reference rather than to the perturbation: ORMAS does not give an adequate reference wave function for both 1Sigma+ states at compressed geometries, and that deficiency carries over into ORMAS-PT. Their prescribed remedy is to relax the subspace occupation restrictions, i.e. move back toward the complete space, which makes the point that the two-electrons-per-symmetry-block restriction is a geometry-dependent approximation: it is harmless where the states are cleanly ionic or covalent but fails where compression mixes the blocks. Note the restriction excludes exactly the configurations that transfer charge between symmetry blocks, which is why the ionic-covalent avoided crossing itself -- an a1-block phenomenon -- survives intact.
reference_short: Roskop & Gordon, J. Chem. Phys. 2011, 135, 044101
notes: The two lowest 1Sigma+ states are examined at the LiF ground state equilibrium geometry and along the dissociation coordinate.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory in quasi-degenerate form, built on the ORMAS reference and compared against MRMP/MCQDPT on the corresponding complete active space

compound_name: Si15H16 cluster model of the Si(100) surface, buckling modes of the surface dimers
geometry_source: Si15H16 optimized at both the FORS/CASSCF and ORMAS-SCF levels with cc-pVDZ; the Hessian was then diagonalized to determine the vibrational modes, and geometric distortions were made along the two buckling modes with MRPT single-point energies computed along them.
method: ORMAS-PT (quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory on an occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field reference), benchmarked against full CAS-based MRMP/MCQDPT
software: GAMESS (General Atomic and Molecular Electronic Structure System); ORMAS-PT implemented there
active_space_orbital_description: The CASSCF active space includes one sigma/sigma* and one pi/pi* pair from each surface dimer, giving 8 electrons in 8 molecular orbitals. For ORMAS-SCF each dimer is given its own subspace, producing two subspaces of four orbitals each (one sigma/sigma* and one pi/pi* pair), with reference occupation restrictions of a minimum and maximum of 4 electrons per subspace.
active_space_protocol: The space is built one dimer at a time -- sigma, sigma*, pi, pi* per dimer -- so it scales linearly with the number of surface dimers treated, and the ORMAS partition follows the same physical decomposition by giving each dimer its own subspace with its own four electrons. The restriction therefore forbids charge transfer between dimers while retaining full flexibility within each one. The question being tested is whether the buckled or symmetric dimer geometry is the ground state, which is unresolved because highly correlated methods are impractical on the large surface models needed to eliminate edge effects.
electronic_structure_description: Two buckling modes are identified. Their frequencies are 159.4 cm-1 (CASSCF) and 159.0 cm-1 (ORMAS) for mode-1, and 154.8 cm-1 (CASSCF) and 154.1 cm-1 (ORMAS) for mode-2. Displacements along both buckling modes show that the ORMAS-PT surface agrees with the MRMP result that the MRPT energy increases as the atoms are displaced along the buckling modes, over displacements up to 40 percent and energies up to about 0.2 kcal/mol.
Other: Forbidding inter-dimer charge transfer costs almost nothing here: the buckling frequencies shift by only 0.4 and 0.7 cm-1 between CASSCF(8,8) and the two-subspace ORMAS, and the MRPT energy profiles along both modes overlay the MRMP ones. That is a meaningful statement about the physics rather than about the method -- the surface dimers are electronically independent enough that a wave function which never lets electrons move between them reproduces the full CAS result. The corollary is that the (8,8) space itself contains no inter-dimer correlation worth having, so the linear-scaling per-dimer construction is safe to extend to the larger clusters actually needed to eliminate edge effects, which is the whole motivation given for the test. Both surfaces agree that the energy rises on displacement along the buckling coordinates.
reference_short: Roskop & Gordon, J. Chem. Phys. 2011, 135, 044101
notes: Whether Si(100) ground state surface dimers are buckled is described as an unresolved matter; small surface clusters are routinely used to circumvent the expense of large cluster models.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory in quasi-degenerate form, built on the ORMAS reference and compared against MRMP/MCQDPT on the corresponding complete active space

compound_name: oxoMn(salen), neutral singlet and triplet states
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations on the singlet (neutral) species with the 6-31G(d) basis set. The triplet MCSCF state spontaneously dissociates the oxygen atom upon optimization from the bound singlet geometry, so triplet calculations were done at the corresponding optimized singlet geometries. ORMAS-PT singlet-triplet splittings were computed at both the CASSCF and the ORMAS optimized geometries.
method: ORMAS-PT (quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory on an occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field reference), benchmarked against full CAS-based MRMP/MCQDPT
software: GAMESS (General Atomic and Molecular Electronic Structure System); ORMAS-PT implemented there
active_space_orbital_description: The complete active space is 12 electrons in 11 orbitals: dMn, sigma, sigma*, pi1, pi1*, pi2, pi2*, piL, piL*, piR, piR*. ORMAS-3 partitions these into three subspaces {piL,piL*}, {piR,piR*} and {pi1,pi1*,pi2,pi2*,sigma,sigma*,dMn} with electron occupations restricted to a minimum and maximum of 2, 2 and 8. ORMAS-6 partitions them into six subspaces {piL,piL*}, {piR,piR*}, {pi1,pi1*}, {pi2,pi2*}, {sigma,sigma*} and {dMn} with minimum occupations 1,2,2,2,2,2 and maximum occupations 2,4,4,4,2,2.
active_space_protocol: Three treatments of the same 11 orbitals are compared: the full CAS(12,11), a coarse three-subspace ORMAS that keeps the metal d orbital together with the sigma/sigma* and the two pi/pi* pairs of the oxo-manganese core while isolating the left and right salen ligand pi systems, and a fine six-subspace ORMAS that additionally separates every pi/pi* pair, the sigma/sigma* pair and the metal d orbital from one another. The coarse partition preserves correlation between the metal and the orbitals it bonds through; the fine one does not. Determinant counts fall from 213444 (CAS singlet) to 34104 (ORMAS-3) to 11520 (ORMAS-6), and the perturbation-correction time from 209 to 42 to 16 minutes.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet-triplet splittings in kcal/mol (MCSCF then MRPT) for the 3A state relative to the 1A state: CAS(12,11) -0.3 and -2.2, with 152460 determinants and 293 minutes for the PT correction; ORMAS-3//CAS -0.3 and -0.4 (24948 determinants, 51 min); ORMAS-6//CAS -1.3 and +0.3 (8742 determinants, 19 min); ORMAS-3 at its own geometry -0.2 and -2.3 (24948 determinants, 51 min); ORMAS-6 at its own geometry -1.0 and +0.4 (8742 determinants, 19 min). Determinant counts for the singlet are 213444 (CAS), 34104 (ORMAS-3) and 11520 (ORMAS-6), with PT correction times of 209, 42 and 16 minutes.
Other: This is the case where the partition changes the answer qualitatively. Against the CAS MRPT benchmark of -2.2 kcal/mol, the coarse ORMAS-3 partition gives -2.3 kcal/mol at its own optimized geometry (0.1 kcal/mol error) but -0.4 kcal/mol at the CAS geometry (1.8 kcal/mol error) -- so the reference and the geometry have to be matched, and using an ORMAS reference at a CASSCF geometry is worse than using it self-consistently. The fine ORMAS-6 partition gives +0.3 and +0.4 kcal/mol, which is not merely 2.5 kcal/mol off but the wrong sign: it places the singlet below the triplet, reversing the state ordering. The difference between the two partitions is exactly whether the manganese d orbital is allowed to correlate with the sigma/sigma* and pi/pi* orbitals it bonds through; isolating dMn in its own one-orbital subspace destroys that, and the paper concludes a more complete active space is needed. The triplet state also spontaneously dissociates the oxygen upon MCSCF optimization from the bound singlet geometry, which is why it is treated at the singlet geometry throughout.
reference_short: Roskop & Gordon, J. Chem. Phys. 2011, 135, 044101
notes: Determinant counts and timings are for two dual-quad-core Intel Xeon R5420 nodes. The system was previously studied with the CAS MRPT method and is reexamined here to test ORMAS-PT on a transition metal complex.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory in quasi-degenerate form, built on the ORMAS reference and compared against MRMP/MCQDPT on the corresponding complete active space

compound_name: oxoMn(salen) anion, doublet and quartet states
ligand_set: salen (N,N'-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine) with an oxo ligand; anionic species
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations on the doublet and quartet (ionic) species with the 6-31G(d) basis set. ORMAS-PT doublet-quartet splittings were computed at the ORMAS optimized geometries only.
method: ORMAS-PT (quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory on an occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field reference), benchmarked against full CAS-based MRMP/MCQDPT
software: GAMESS (General Atomic and Molecular Electronic Structure System); ORMAS-PT implemented there
active_space_orbital_description: FORS/CASSCF active space of 13 electrons in the same 11 orbitals used for the neutral species (dMn, sigma, sigma*, pi1, pi1*, pi2, pi2*, piL, piL*, piR, piR*). The ORMAS subspaces are partitioned exactly as for the neutral species; only the electron occupation restrictions differ. ORMAS-3 subspaces {piL,piL*}, {piR,piR*}, {pi1,pi1*,pi2,pi2*,sigma,sigma*,dMn} are restricted to a minimum and maximum of 2, 2 and 9 electrons; ORMAS-6 uses the same restrictions as the neutral species, minimum 1,2,2,2,2,2 and maximum 2,4,4,4,2,2.
active_space_protocol: The anion is treated by keeping both the orbital set and the subspace partitioning identical to the neutral molecule and changing only the occupation restrictions to accommodate the extra electron, which places it in the large core subspace for ORMAS-3 (8 to 9 electrons) and lets the ORMAS-6 restrictions absorb it unchanged. Holding the partition fixed across the two charge states is what makes the neutral and anionic errors comparable and is the paper's argument that ORMAS provides a reliable reference for the MRPT correction.
electronic_structure_description: Doublet-quartet splittings in kcal/mol (MCSCF then MRPT) for the 4A state relative to the 2A state: CAS(13,11) -6.9 and -10.8, with 76230 determinants for the quartet and 157 minutes for the PT correction; ORMAS-3 -6.7 and -10.2 (11193 determinants, 25 min); ORMAS-6 -7.9 and -10.4 (6972 determinants, 16 min). Determinant counts for the doublet are 152460 (CAS), 21336 (ORMAS-3) and 12582 (ORMAS-6), with PT correction times of 313, 47 and 28 minutes. Both ORMAS-3 PT and ORMAS-6 PT splittings agree with CAS MRPT to within about 0.6 kcal/mol, and the doublet-quartet splitting is much larger than the singlet-triplet splitting of the neutral species.
Other: The contrast with the neutral molecule is the finding. Here the same six-subspace partition that reversed the state ordering in the neutral case reproduces the CAS MRPT splitting to 0.4 kcal/mol, and even the coarse-to-fine difference is only 0.2 kcal/mol at the perturbation level. The reason is scale: the doublet-quartet gap of -10.8 kcal/mol is an order of magnitude larger than the neutral singlet-triplet gap of -2.2 kcal/mol, so the roughly 2.5 kcal/mol error the fine partition introduces is invisible here and decisive there. The practical rule this establishes is that the acceptable severity of an occupation restriction is set by the size of the energy difference being computed, not by the system or the orbital set -- both are identical between this row and the neutral one. Note also that the MCSCF-level splittings track the MRPT ones much better here (-6.9 vs -10.8 for CAS, -7.9 vs -10.4 for ORMAS-6) than in the neutral case, where the MCSCF gap was near zero.
reference_short: Roskop & Gordon, J. Chem. Phys. 2011, 135, 044101
notes: Determinant counts and timings are for two dual-quad-core Intel Xeon R5420 nodes. For the open shell systems ORMAS-PT uses about one to two orders of magnitude fewer determinants and about one order of magnitude less CPU time than CAS MRPT, with correspondingly reduced memory requirements.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory in quasi-degenerate form, built on the ORMAS reference and compared against MRMP/MCQDPT on the corresponding complete active space

compound_name: trans-Polyacetylene oligomers of 2 to 8 ethylene subunits, vertical ionization potentials
geometry_source: The energies of the ionized species are calculated at the optimized geometries of the corresponding neutral species (vertical ionization potentials).
method: ORMAS-PT (quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory on an occupation restricted multiple active space self-consistent field reference), benchmarked against full CAS-based MRMP/MCQDPT
software: GAMESS (General Atomic and Molecular Electronic Structure System); ORMAS-PT implemented there
active_space_orbital_description: For the MRMP reference, a complete active space of size (2n,2n) where n is the number of ethylene subunits: (4,4), (6,6), (8,8), (10,10), (12,12), (14,14) and (16,16) for n = 2 to 8. Since these systems are highly conjugated, the active space is constructed around the pi orbitals and pi electrons. For ORMAS-PT the same active orbitals are partitioned into two subspaces: with respect to the RHF determinant, space 1 holds the occupied pi molecular orbitals and space 2 the unoccupied pi* orbitals, with reference occupation restrictions of minimum (maximum) 2n-MAX and 0 for space 1 and 2n and MAX for space 2, where MAX = 2, 3 or 4 is the maximum number of electrons allowed to excite from space 1 to space 2.
active_space_protocol: The complete space grows as (2n,2n) with oligomer length and becomes impractical, so ORMAS replaces it by an occupied-pi / virtual-pi* split truncated at a fixed excitation level MAX = 2, 3 or 4. This turns a size-scaling problem into a convergence question: for each oligomer length the ORMAS-PT ionization potential can be watched as MAX is raised, and compared with the full MRMP value. The active space is confined to the pi system throughout because the oligomers are highly conjugated.
Other: Both MCSCF and MRPT ionization potentials fall monotonically with chain length, but the MCSCF values fall below experiment (CASSCF 8.47, 7.78 and 7.35 eV against 9.09, 8.29-8.45 and 7.8-8.1 eV for n = 2, 3, 4) while the MRMP values reproduce it (9.11, 8.34, 7.88 eV) -- so on a pure pi active space of the full (2n,2n) size, dynamic correlation is worth 0.5-0.6 eV and is essential, whatever the reference. Within the perturbative treatment the truncation converges cleanly for the longer chains: raising MAX from 2 to 4 shrinks the error against MRMP from 0.08-0.11 eV to 0.01-0.05 eV for n = 4-8. But the short chain n = 3 goes the other way, with errors growing as MAX increases (8.32, 8.59, 8.62 against 8.34), and at n = 2 the two-electron truncation actually beats MRMP against experiment (9.23 vs 9.11 against 9.09). Convergence in the truncation level is therefore not monotonic at small system size, and the agreement seen there partly reflects error cancellation. Note also that ORMAS-SCF and CASSCF ionization potentials agree to about 0.02 eV at MAX = 4 even where the corresponding perturbative values still differ, so reference-level agreement does not guarantee agreement after the perturbation.
reference_short: Roskop & Gordon, J. Chem. Phys. 2011, 135, 044101
notes: The (16,16) CASSCF and MRMP values for n = 8 were not computed, which is the point of the exercise: ORMAS-PT uses one to two orders of magnitude fewer determinants and is presented as an efficient approach for polymers of length 8 or larger. Experimental ionization potentials are available only for n = 2, 3, 4.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation theory in quasi-degenerate form, built on the ORMAS reference and compared against MRMP/MCQDPT on the corresponding complete active space

geometry_source: Geometries of the reactant complex, product complex and transition state in the excited electronic state optimized at CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p). Minimum energy paths obtained in mass-scaled coordinates (1 amu) at the same level using the Euler steepest descent method and the reoriented generalized-transition-state-theory dividing surface algorithm with a step size of 0.01 amu^(1/2) bohr. Frequencies along the MEP computed at the same level and scaled by 0.9. The interpolated VTST by mapping (IVTST-M) algorithm was used with 31 Hessian and 310 gradient points (IVTST-M-31/310), and the S1 potential energy curve was corrected by 31 interpolated single point energies from MRPT2, chosen every 0.1 bohr between -2.3 and 0.8 bohr along the MEP.
method: CASSCF(10,9) with second-order multireference perturbation theory (MRPT2) single points, used as a dual-level MRPT2//CASSCF surface for variational transition state theory with multidimensional tunneling (VTST/MT); IEFPCM polarizable continuum calculations at the CASSCF level for the solvent study
software: Gaussian 03 for the CASSCF optimizations and MEPs; GAMESS for all MRPT2 calculations; Gaussian 09 for the solvent effect calculations
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(10,9). The individual active orbitals are not enumerated in this paper; the space is adopted from the CASSCF(10,9)/DZP work of Chaban and Gordon on the same complex.
active_space_protocol: The space is inherited rather than constructed: CASSCF(10,9)/DZP was the highest level previously reported in the literature for the 1:1 7AI:H2O complex, and this work adopts the same (10,9) space while changing the basis to 6-31G(d,p). The basis change was forced by practice rather than accuracy -- at nonstationary points along the excited-state MEP the DZP calculations sometimes failed to reach SCF convergence, and a smoothly convergent surface is a prerequisite for the interpolated-VTST machinery. The paper states outright that the quality of the CASSCF calculations strongly depends on the choice of active space and basis sets, and cites the smaller CASSCF(8,8) space used in an earlier instanton study as an example of that dependence going wrong. Single-level MRPT2 optimization and MRPT2 frequencies were practically impossible, so the surface is necessarily dual-level.
electronic_structure_description: Barrier heights (delta V) and reaction energies (delta E) in kcal/mol for the excited-state double proton transfer, with zero-point-corrected values in parentheses: CIS/6-31G(d) 26.94, -18.15; CIS/6-31G(d,p) 25.19, -17.67; CIS/6-31+G(d,p) 27.15, -15.58; TD-B3LYP//CIS/6-31G(d) 6.42, -21.47; CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G(d) 20.64 (22.07), -33.19; CASSCF(10,9)/sDZP 16.90 (13.5), -32.20 (-31.7); CASSCF(10,9)/DZP(d,p) 18.20 (14.7), -31.80 (-31.2); CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) 18.08 (14.39), -28.56 (-27.92); MCQDPT2//CASSCF(10,9)/DZP 9.80 (6.3), -18.00 (-17.4); MRPT2//CASSCF(10,9)/6-31G(d,p) 9.72 (6.39), -18.95 (-18.31). The two protons are transferred concertedly but asynchronously. The variational transition state is very different from the conventional transition state and is highly dependent on isotopic substitution; the adiabatic energy maximum is at s = -0.79 bohr rather than at s = 0. CVT rate constants for HH transfer without tunneling are 3.9 to 7.6 times smaller than TST values, while the CVT and TST rate constants for DD transfer differ little. Rate constants including tunneling (10^6 s-1): HH at 250, 298, 300, 311 and 350 K are 0.56, 4.14, 4.44, 6.41 and 19.5 with SCT coefficients 2.99, 2.20, 2.17, 2.07 and 1.79; DD at the same temperatures 0.11, 1.04, 1.12, 1.67 and 5.63 with SCT coefficients 1.53, 1.35, 1.34, 1.31 and 1.24. In water (IEFPCM/UFF and IEFPCM/UA0) the noncyclic 1:1 complex lies 1.91 and 2.20 kcal/mol above the cyclic one and the TS at 16.64 (16.01 with nonelectrostatic terms) and 16.78 kcal/mol.
Other: Enlarging the space from (8,8) to (10,9) does not merely shift the barrier from 20.6 to 18.2 kcal/mol -- it reverses the mechanism. At CASSCF(10,9)/DZP the N-H bond in the five-membered ring moves first toward the water while the O-H is nearly unchanged, giving an H3O+-like moiety in the transition state; at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G(d) the O-H moves first toward the six-membered ring while the N-H is nearly unchanged, giving an OH--like moiety. The order of the protons in flight is inverted, and the paper argues from experiment (7AI becomes acidic in S1 upon pi-pi* excitation, so the N-H should break easily) that the (10,9) picture is the correct one and that the earlier instanton study built on the (8,8) transition state was therefore working from an inappropriate structure. A second, independent sign of reference-level trouble in the smaller space: the ZPE correction raises the CASSCF(8,8) barrier by 1.5 kcal/mol but lowers the CASSCF(10,9) barrier by 3.5 kcal/mol, and the authors note it is very unusual for a ZPE correction to increase a barrier height. Dynamic correlation on top of the (10,9) reference then halves the barrier (18.08 to 9.72 kcal/mol), consistent with CIS and CASSCF systematically overestimating excited-state barriers, and the MRPT2 result with 6-31G(d,p) matches the independently computed MCQDPT2/DZP value of 9.80 kcal/mol -- so the basis set is interchangeable in a way the active space is not.
reference_short: Duong & Kim, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 3403
notes: Experimental rate constants for 7AI tautomerization in water are of order 10^9 s-1 at room temperature, a few hundred times larger than the gas-phase values computed here; the fluorescence lifetime of 8 ns measured in cold beams implies the tautomerization rate cannot exceed about 10^7 s-1, consistent with this work. Experimental HH/DD KIEs in aqueous solution are 3.4-3.9 at room temperature. IEFPCM calculations show solvation brings H10 about 0.1 A closer to O16 and lengthens the N7-H18 hydrogen bond by about 0.2 A, increasing ion-pair character and asynchronicity, but attempts to locate an ion-pair intermediate collapsed to reactant or product, so the mechanism remains concerted in water.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference perturbation theory (MRPT2) single points, interpolated along the MEP as 31 interpolated single point energies (ISPE)

compound_name: C2H4Si isomer manifold: silacyclopropene (1), vinylsilylene (2), silylvinylidene (3), 1-silaallene (4), silylacetylene (5), diradical 6, and the transition states connecting them
geometry_source: Species-dependent optimizations, all with 6-31G*. Closed-shell molecules 1, 4, 5 and 8 optimized by RHF with MP2 single points. Silylene 7 optimized by (2,2)CASSCF with a (2,2)CASPT2 single point. Species 2, 3 and 6 optimized by (4,4)CASSCF with (4,4)CASPT2 single points. Transition states TS1 and TS2 located with (6,6)CASSCF; TS2 was also reoptimized with (10,10)CASSCF. TS3 to TS6 located with (4,4)CASSCF. Analytical vibrational frequencies were computed at each stationary point at the same level at which the geometry was optimized, and zero-point energies evaluated from the unscaled frequencies.
method: CASPT2N//CASSCF with species-dependent active spaces, plus a uniform (12,12)CASSCF/(12,12)CASPT2 treatment for all species, and B3LYP as an independent check
software: Gaussian 94 and MOLCAS, except the (10,10)CASSCF calculations on TS2 which were carried out with GAMESS
active_space_orbital_description: Several spaces are used. (2,2) for silylene 7. (4,4) for species 2, 3 and 6, correlating the pair of nonbonding electrons and the pair of pi electrons in each double bond. (6,6) for transition states TS1 and TS2, adding to the two pairs of the (4,4) space the pair of electrons in the breaking R-H bond (R = Si in TS1, R = C in TS2). (10,10)CASSCF for the reoptimization of TS2. The largest space, (12,12), correlates the 12 electrons in the six highest filled MOs using the corresponding six virtual orbitals, and was applied to all species in Scheme 1 except 7, 8 and TS6.
active_space_protocol: Each stationary point first gets the smallest space that describes its own bond reorganization -- two electrons for the silylene lone pair, four for the nonbonding plus pi pairs, six once an R-H bond is breaking -- which keeps every optimization affordable but leaves the relative energies of different species computed at different levels. To make them comparable, a single uniform space is then applied across the whole manifold: the 12 electrons in the six highest occupied MOs correlated in the six corresponding virtuals. The authors state that all 16 valence electrons in 16 orbitals would have been the ideal but was impossible with the hardware available, so (12,12) is an explicit compromise, not the converged answer. TS2 was separately reoptimized at (10,10)CASSCF specifically so that an IRC could establish which minima it connects.
electronic_structure_description: Relative CASPT2 energies in kcal/mol with the 6-31G* basis, relative to silacyclopropene (1), listed as delta E at the species-specific space, then (6,6), then (12,12), then the (12,12) value with ZPE correction where given. Species 2: 1.9 / - / 0.2 / 0.7. Species 3: 34.9 / - / 31.5 / 27.6. Species 4: 14.3 / - / 7.2 / 6.4. Species 5: -8.8 / - / -12.8 / -14.9. Species 6: 30.5 / - / 29.4 / 26.7. 7 + 8: 54.3. TS1: 38.9 / 41.4 / 35.7 / 32.2. TS2: 46.8 / 49.3 / 43.0 / 38.7. TS3: 42.2 / 40.3 / 35.3 / 32.3. TS4-H: 43.5 / 42.8 / 39.1 / 32.6. TS4-Si: 29.8 / - / 25.5. TS5: 69.4 / 68.0 / 61.4. Zero-point energies range from 25.1 to 32.2 kcal/mol. Imaginary frequencies: TS1 1184i, TS2 1025i, TS3 1513i, TS4-H 1265i, TS4-Si 194i, TS5 2133i, TS6 1182i cm-1. The ZPE-corrected barriers to concerted ring opening of 1 to vinylsilylene 2 and to forming silylacetylene 5 are 32.2 and 38.7 kcal/mol by (12,12)CASPT2, against 35.8 and 42.2 kcal/mol by B3LYP. Ring closure of 2 to 1 is 31.5 kcal/mol by (12,12)CASPT2 and 31.7 by B3LYP, essentially the same as the barrier for rearrangement of 2 to 1-silaallene 4 at CASPT2, whereas B3LYP puts formation of 4 about 3 kcal/mol lower. Interconversion of 4 and 5 by two consecutive [1,2]-hydrogen shifts via diradical 6 is prevented by barriers above 70 kcal/mol. Corresponding B3LYP relative energies with ZPE correction: 2 at 4.1, 3 at 29.9, 4 at 8.9, 5 at -8.9, 7+8 at 50.8, TS1 35.8, TS2 42.2, TS3 32.3, TS4-H 36.4 kcal/mol.
Other: The paper explicitly sets out to gauge active-space dependence, and Table 1 answers it: the relative CASPT2 energies are fairly independent of the size of the space chosen for each species, and moving to the uniform (12,12) space produces a systematic lowering of everything relative to 1 with no reordering of the sequence. The largest shifts, about 7 kcal/mol, are for silaallene 4 (14.3 to 7.2) and TS3 leading to it (42.2 to 35.3) -- the two structures where cumulated double-bond character means the smaller spaces miss the most pi correlation. The direction of the shift is uniform because recovering correlation variationally at (12,12)CASPT2 rather than perturbatively at MP2 favors every less-saturated structure over the closed-shell ring 1. Two caveats attach to the (12,12) result: it is not the converged space (all 16 valence electrons in 16 orbitals was the stated ideal, ruled out by hardware), and it is defined by orbital energy ordering (six highest filled and their virtual counterparts) rather than by chemical identification, so its composition can change between species. Independent support comes from B3LYP, which agrees with (12,12)CASPT2 to within a few kcal/mol on every barrier but disagrees qualitatively on one competition, placing formation of 4 from 2 about 3 kcal/mol below closure of 2 to 1 where CASPT2 makes them equal. Separately, the (4,4) and (6,6) energies for TS5 came out so high that (6,6)CASPT2 was skipped for it and CASPT2 was skipped entirely for TS6 -- a case where a small-space energy is used to decide that a larger-space calculation is not worth running.
reference_short: Skancke, Hrovat & Borden, J. Phys. Chem. A 1999, 103, 4043
notes: The species-specific level n used for the delta E(n,n) column is n = 0 (MP2//RHF) for 1, 4 and 5; n = 4 for 2, 3, 6, TS3, TS4-H and TS5; and n = 6 for TS1 and TS2. The 7 + 8 value is based on CASPT2//(2,2)CASSCF for 7 plus MP2//RHF for 8. IRC calculations at the (10,10)CASSCF level demonstrated unequivocally that TS2 connects 1 to 3, contradicting an earlier assignment connecting 1 and 5. The results support the hypothesis that equal amounts of the two isotopomers of 1 formed from monodeuterated 2 arise from a kinetically competitive equilibrium between 2 and 4.
correlation_correction: CASPT2N single points at the CASSCF geometries, with MP2//RHF used for the closed-shell species at the smallest level

compound_name: Model protonated Schiff base of 9-cis retinal (isorhodopsin chromophore), photoisomerization dynamics
point_group: No restrictions for symmetry are placed
geometry_source: Ground-state geometry optimized at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G. Minima and saddle points on S1 located by combining the geometry optimization subroutines of Gaussian 03 with state-specific energies, gradients and nonadiabatic coupling matrix elements from Molpro 2006.1 through Gaussian's External feature. Vibrational frequencies from numerically evaluated Hessians in Molpro were used to confirm zero imaginary frequencies at minima and one at saddle points, and IRC path following was used to track the minima connected by saddle points. The activation energy estimates at the larger levels are based on fully optimized structures of the minimum and saddle point at the respective level of theory, not on single points at the CASSCF(6,6) geometries. The two methyl groups were replaced by two hydrogen atoms to save computational cost.
method: On-the-fly nonadiabatic ab initio molecular dynamics with state-averaged CASSCF, surface hopping treated by Zhu-Nakamura theory; CASSCF(10,10) and CASPT2(10,10) used to check the excited-state barrier
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six active orbitals, all of pi character. No restrictions for symmetry or orbital occupations are placed when the six active orbitals are chosen. For the barrier check the space was expanded by four more electrons and four more active orbitals to (10,10).
active_space_protocol: The (6,6) pi space is chosen explicitly as a compromise between a reasonable description of the dynamics and computational feasibility, since the space must be reevaluated at every step of 71 trajectories run with a 0.5 fs time step. The known consequences are stated up front: a CASSCF treatment of retinal overestimates bond alternation, the torsion angle between the backbone and the beta-ionone ring, and the excitation energy, though the bond alternation and torsion angle are qualitatively reproduced. Two lowest states are averaged. The conditions are held identical to the authors' earlier 11-cis calculation on the same 12-pi system so the two isomers can be compared. Because the excited-state barrier is the mechanistic conclusion of the paper, it is separately re-derived at CASSCF(10,10) and CASPT2(10,10), each with its own fully optimized minimum and saddle point rather than by single points on the (6,6) geometries.
nroots_per_mult: Two lowest states, state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: On S1 there are two saddle points and two minimal energy conical intersection points, which bifurcate to the all-trans product and the 9-cis reactant; one saddle point and one conical intersection are twisted clockwise in the phi9 dihedral and the others counterclockwise. Both saddle points give a barrier of about 10 kcal/mol (9.8 clockwise and 10.0 counterclockwise) along a mixed coordinate of twist in phi9 and complementary bond order changes in the C9 to C13 polyene chain. The CASSCF(10,10) barrier is 6.2 kcal/mol and the CASPT2(10,10) barrier 1.7 kcal/mol. The experimentally derived solvent-phase activation energy for isorhodopsin to bathorhodopsin is 0.09-0.25 kcal/mol, two orders of magnitude below the CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G gas-phase value, with the wavelength-independent quantum yield 0.22 at ambient temperature. Seventy-one trajectories were run with a 0.5 fs time step from a Wigner distribution at T = 0 K after excitation to S1. Photoisomerization of 9-cis retinal proceeds more slowly and at lower quantum yield than the 11-cis analogue; the excited-state barrier impedes elongation and twist of the C9=C10 stretch and torsion coordinates, trapping trajectories so that transitions occur at smaller twist angles of the C8-C9=C10-C11 dihedral, which regenerates the 9-cis reactant. An asynchronous bicycle pedal or crankshaft mechanism is found to operate.
Other: The barrier that carries the entire mechanistic argument shrinks by a factor of six as the treatment improves: 10 kcal/mol at CASSCF(6,6), 6.2 at CASSCF(10,10), 1.7 at CASPT2(10,10), against 0.09-0.25 kcal/mol from experiment in the protein. Enlarging the pi space and adding dynamical correlation each remove a comparable slice, so neither alone accounts for the (6,6) error, and even CASPT2(10,10) remains an order of magnitude above experiment -- though part of that gap is attributed to the opsin environment rather than to the wave function. What saves the conclusion is that the saddle points survive at every level: the paper's own defense is that a barrier as small as 0.6 kcal/mol is enough to trap trajectories partially and produce multiexponential decay, so the qualitative dynamics is robust to the overestimate even though the timescale is not. Importantly, the higher-level barriers were obtained from fully reoptimized minima and saddle points at each level rather than from single points on the (6,6) geometries, so the reduction is a real change in the surface and not just an energy shift. The known systematic errors of a pure pi CASSCF space on retinal -- overestimated bond alternation, beta-ionone torsion angle and excitation energy -- are stated as accepted costs of running on-the-fly dynamics.
reference_short: Chung, Nanbu & Ishida, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 8190
notes: Surface hopping uses the Zhu-Nakamura theory: when the energy gap between adjacent adiabatic surfaces reaches a local minimum the nonadiabatic coupling vector is computed, one-dimensional adiabatic curves are calculated along it, the crossing is classified as nonadiabatic-tunneling or Landau-Zener type, and the transition probability is compared with a uniform random number. The simulation is in vacuo, which the authors take as evidence that the excited-state barrier and the photoisomerization are intrinsic properties of the chromophore.
correlation_correction: CASPT2(10,10) single-level check of the excited-state barrier

compound_name: Lumiflavin-thiomethanol complex, model of the flavin mononucleotide cofactor and reactive cysteine in the LOV blue-light receptor
geometry_source: All structures optimized by state-specific CASSCF(2,2)/6-31G(d): the ground-state complex R (dark-adapted LOV absorbing at 447 nm), R-photo optimized in the triplet state with the S-C4a distance fixed at 4.5 A (the triplet intermediate absorbing at 660 and 715 nm), the H-transfer transition state TS-photo in the triplet state, the triplet Biradical complex optimized with the S-C4a distance fixed at 3.40 A, the S-C4a covalent adduct Add in the ground state (photoproduct absorbing at 390 nm), and TS-dark in the ground state. Some distances were fixed during optimization; unrestrained optimization of the biradical moved the SCH3 fragment aside.
method: State-specific and state-averaged CASSCF with MCQDPT2 single points; MRCI-SD on CASSCF orbitals used specifically to validate the choice of active space
software: PC GAMESS version of GAMESS (U.S.); Molekel for figures
basis_set: 6-31G(d), a standard Gaussian basis containing polarization d functions on the heavy atoms
active_space_orbital_description: The state-specific CASSCF(2,2) space contains the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (HOMO and LUMO) of the ground-state Hartree-Fock configuration. The CASSCF(4,4) space adds a pair of pi,pi* MOs localized on the dimethylbenzene ring, identified from the MRCI analysis. A CASSCF(4,3) space of four electrons in three MOs was used for the state-averaged S0/T1 crossing calculations. The lumiflavin-thiomethanol complex has 160 electrons described by 351 molecular orbitals in this basis; in the MRCI-SD calculations 65 MOs were treated as core and 256 as virtual, leaving an excitation window of 30 MOs with 30 electrons containing all pi MOs (7 pi and 7 pi*).
active_space_protocol: The smallest possible space is used and then tested rather than assumed. Starting from HOMO/LUMO only, MRCI-SD calculations using the CASSCF(2,2) orbitals were run to find out whether any configuration outside the space carries weight. The answer was that all such CSFs have MRCI coefficients no greater than 0.1 (largest 0.12, for S1 at the R geometry) and that they correspond to excitations within a pi,pi* pair on the dimethylbenzene ring; those two orbitals were then promoted into the space to give CASSCF(4,4), and the comparison run. Separately, for the S0/T1 crossing region a state-averaged CASSCF(4,3) space was chosen, again on the basis of MRCI analysis of the state-averaged wave function, as the smallest space describing both states simultaneously. State-averaged CASSCF with equal 0.5/0.5 weights on the two states involved was used for transition energies.
nroots_per_mult: State-specific for the energy profile; two states with weights 0.5 and 0.5 for the transition energies
electronic_structure_description: Total energies in hartree at the CASSCF(2,2) / MCQDPT2 / MRCI-SD levels for the structures R(S0), R(S1), R(T1), R-photo(T1), TS-photo(T1), Biradical(T1), Biradical(S0), Add(S0) and TS-dark(S0): CAS(2,2) -1304.576423, -1304.398784, -1304.443019, -1304.467340, -1304.424206, -1304.515333, -1304.520331, -1304.565059, -1304.479388; MCQDPT2 -1307.440091, -1307.319140, -1307.346847, -1307.360405, -1307.342207, -1307.402101, -1307.411409, -1307.460488, -1307.394552; MRCI-SD -1304.627336, -1304.424324, -1304.503981, -1304.525280, -1304.479042, -1304.575831, -1304.557026, -1304.565597, -1304.525402. The CASSCF(2,2) wave functions are essentially single-determinantal for R in S0 and S1 and for Add in S0, while Biradical and TS-dark in S0 need a two-configurational description to account for the dissociated S-C4a bond; the triplet CASSCF(2,2) solutions are identical to ROHF. Relative energies with respect to R in S0: vertical excitation to S1 costs 75.9 kcal/mol, the vertical T1 energy is 58.5 kcal/mol, and the relaxed triplet complex R-photo lies at 50.1 kcal/mol; relaxation elongates N5-C4a from 1.27 to 1.38 A and shortens N5-C5 from 1.37 to 1.29 A. The triplet H transfer between S-H and N5 has a barrier of 11.3 kcal/mol (14.5 kcal/mol at MCQDPT2/CASSCF(4,4)), at TS-photo with S-H and H-N5 distances of 1.49 and 1.35 A. Electronic transition energies in eV, CASSCF (oscillator strength) then MCQDPT2 then experiment: R (S0-S1) 4.53 (0.655), 2.86, 2.77; R-photo (T1-T2) 1.99 (0.010), 1.64, 1.73 and 1.88; Add (S0-S1) 5.13 (0.476), 3.37, 3.18; free lumiflavin (S0-S1) 4.56 (0.670), 2.88, 2.80; free lumiflavin (T1-T2) 2.20 (0.011), 1.49, 1.95. At the Biradical geometry with S-C4a of 3.40 A the MCQDPT2/CASSCF(4,3) S0-T1 gap is 4.6 kcal/mol, falling to 1.4 kcal/mol at 3.40 to 4.5 A, near the S0/T1 crossing.
Other: This paper uses MRCI-SD not for energies but as an instrument for choosing the active space, and reports the diagnostic explicitly: with CASSCF(2,2) orbitals, every configuration outside the two-orbital space has an MRCI coefficient of at most 0.12, and those few live in a pi,pi* pair on the dimethylbenzene ring. Promoting exactly those two orbitals gives CASSCF(4,4), and the test then shows the enlargement lowers absolute energies without significantly changing relative energies (agreement 0.5-3.3 kcal/mol), CI coefficients or Lowdin charges -- so (2,2) is declared sufficient. Two caveats sit inside that conclusion. The (4,4) calculation would not converge at all for the covalent adduct Add, so the space that was validated is not actually available at every point on the profile; for Add the validation rests instead on CASSCF(2,2) and MRCI-SD agreeing to 0.3 kcal/mol. And the one quantity that does move is the barrier that matters: the triplet H-transfer barrier is 11.3 kcal/mol at MCQDPT2/CASSCF(2,2) but 14.5 at MCQDPT2/CASSCF(4,4), a 28 percent change, because dynamic correlation lowers the transition states TS-photo and TS-dark more than the reactants and products. Separately, the reference alone is badly off for spectra -- CASSCF puts the S0-S1 transition of R at 4.53 eV against 2.77 eV experimental, corrected to 2.86 eV by MCQDPT2 -- so the space that suffices for relative energies does not suffice for excitation energies without the perturbative correction. The crossing region needed its own space again, a state-averaged (4,3) chosen by the same MRCI criterion.
reference_short: Domratcheva, Fedorov & Schlichting, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2006, 2, 1565
notes: The CSF labels used in Table 1 are occupancy numbers within the (4,4) space: (1) 2200, (2) 2110, (3) 2020, (4) 2101, (5) 1210, (6) 1111, (7) 1111, (8) 0112, (9) 0211, (10) 0202, (11) 0022. Lowdin charges are reported in preference to Mulliken because the latter came out somewhat overestimated, though both were consistent. The free complex results are compared throughout with an earlier QM/MM study of LOV in which the same lumiflavin-thiomethanol geometry was restrained by a molecular-mechanical model of the protein; that model found a similar triplet intermediate with an 18 kcal/mol intersystem crossing barrier.
correlation_correction: MCQDPT2 single points on the CASSCF(2,2) and CASSCF(4,4) references; MRCI-SD with CASSCF orbitals as an independent check

compound_name: 1,2-Bis(3-thienyl)ethene (mod-DAE), model diarylethene for the photochromic cyclization/cycloreversion
point_group: No symmetry constraints imposed during geometry optimizations
geometry_source: Stationary points on the S0 and T1 surfaces optimized at the CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G* level with no symmetry constraints; analytical frequency calculations at the same level and at the optimized geometries were used to identify the nature of the stationary points. The same structures were also optimized at the UB3LYP/6-31G* level for comparison, and the structures obtained at both levels are in very good agreement.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 single-point corrections, compared against UB3LYP; CASSCF(8,8) used separately to evaluate S0/T1 spin-orbit coupling
software: MOLCAS revision 3.0 for the CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 98 for the remaining calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten orbitals, defined as those allowed variable occupancies between 2.0 and 0.0, holding ten electrons. For the open-ring isomer the ten orbitals are the 10 pi, pi* orbitals; for the closed-ring isomer they are 8 pi, pi* orbitals plus the 2 sigma, sigma* orbitals describing the sigma bond broken during the cycloreversion photoprocess. A reduced CASSCF(8,8) space was used for the spin-orbit coupling calculations.
active_space_protocol: The size of the space is held at ten orbitals along the whole reaction coordinate while its contents change: two pi/pi* orbitals of the open-ring isomer are replaced by the sigma/sigma* pair of the bond that is formed on ring closure. That substitution is what makes a single space able to describe both isomers and the transition state between them, since the sigma bond does not exist on one side of the coordinate and the two pi orbitals are consumed on the other. The model system mod-DAE was chosen deliberately as a small surrogate that conserves the essential pi system undergoing the electronic rearrangement, so that the full surfaces could be explored at a cost impossible for the real diarylethene. The spin-orbit coupling calculations had to drop to (8,8), which the authors attribute to the algorithm used requiring full diagonalization of the CI matrix.
electronic_structure_description: On the ground-state surface the open-ring minimum Ogs, the closed-ring minimum Cgs and the transition state TSgs were located; the two isomers have very similar energies. At the CASSCF level the S0/T1 gap is typically 20 kcal/mol larger than at DFT, so no S0/T1 crossings appear in the transition-state region and T1 lies well above S0, and the barrier on T1 is much higher, with TSt 22 kcal/mol above Ot. CASPT2 corrections lower TSgs to only 39 kcal/mol above Ogs and lower the T1 surface overall, bringing the surfaces into excellent agreement with the UB3LYP/6-31G* results, which put TSgs 45 kcal/mol above the open-ring minimum. Selected UB3LYP/6-31G* values for mod-DAE: Ogs, absolute energy -1888.3090 hartree with spin contamination 0.000 (-1887.9674), relative energy 0.0, triplet -1888.2233 with spin contamination 2.001 at 53.8 kcal/mol; TSgs -1888.2363 with spin contamination 0.548 (-1887.8969) at 45.6 kcal/mol, triplet -1888.2325 with spin contamination 2.002 at 48.0 kcal/mol, giving a 2.4 kcal/mol S0-T1 separation. Spin-orbit coupling between S0 and T1 at the CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G* level is strongly geometry dependent: 8.3 cm-1 at the Ct minimum and 1.5 cm-1 at the Ot minimum, so intersystem crossing is expected in the transition-state region where the two surfaces are nearly degenerate, on the closed-ring side of TSt.
Other: Two findings sit on the same space. First, the composition of the fixed ten-orbital space has to change identity along the coordinate: 10 pi/pi* for the open-ring isomer, but 8 pi/pi* plus the sigma/sigma* of the forming bond for the closed one. Keeping the size fixed while swapping contents is what lets one space span a photochromic reaction in which a sigma bond appears. Second, and more consequential, the bare CASSCF reference gets the mechanism qualitatively wrong: it puts the S0/T1 gap about 20 kcal/mol too high, which erases the S0/T1 crossings in the transition-state region entirely and inflates the T1 barrier to 22 kcal/mol above Ot. Since the paper's whole argument is a nonadiabatic pathway through an S0/T1 crossing seam, that is not a quantitative error but a missing mechanism, and CASPT2 restores it -- bringing TSgs down to 39 kcal/mol above Ogs, in line with the 45 kcal/mol from UB3LYP. Conversely, DFT struggles precisely where CASSCF is at its best: the open-ring transition state has reactant and product configurations of equal weight in the CASSCF wave function, and the resulting multiconfigurational character shows up in DFT as prominent spin contamination (0.548 at TSgs against 0.000 at Ogs). Finally, the spin-orbit coupling had to be computed in a smaller (8,8) space for algorithmic reasons, and the authors themselves warn that this reduction may unbalance the description of the electronic states, defending the extrapolation only on the grounds that SOC tracks spin density delocalization, whose variation along the coordinate is shared by mod-DAE and the real system.

notes: mod-DAE is the small model system; the paper's main subjects are the larger 1,2-bis(2-methylbenzothiophene-3-yl)maleimide model DAE and two dyads containing ruthenium(II) polypyridine units, which were treated by DFT only. The CASSCF//CASPT2 calculations on mod-DAE serve as assessment calculations to benchmark the DFT results and to demonstrate the generality of the main topological features. mod-DAE lacks the maleimide fragment of DAE.

compound_name: 7-Hydroxyquinoline and its 1:2 complex with methanol, triple proton transfer in the ground and first excited states
point_group: Cs planar structures for the N and T forms
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized at SCF, SCRF and MP2 levels; excited-state geometries obtained by first optimizing with configuration interaction with single excitations (CIS) using the 3-21G basis set, then performing CASSCF optimization with the CIS structures as the initial guess. Vibrational frequency calculations confirmed the N and T minima with all real frequencies. Zero-point vibrational energy corrections used a scale factor of 0.85. Ground-state geometries were reoptimized with the SCRF method using 3-21G, 6-31+G and 6-31G* basis sets; energies were then recalculated at the MP2/3-21G ground-state and CASSCF(14,10)/3-21G excited-state geometries with solvent effects included.
method: CASSCF(14,10) for the excited-state surface, with CIS, HF, SCRF and MP2 for comparison; solvent treated by the self-consistent reaction field method with a dielectric constant of 31.2 for methanol and a spherical cavity of radius 5.4 A based on the calculated complex volume
basis_set: 3-21G for the CASSCF(14,10) calculations; 3-21G, 6-31+G and 6-31G* used for the ground state
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in ten orbitals. The obvious choice for describing the first excited singlet state of 7HQ would be 10 electrons in the 5 pi molecular orbitals and 4 electrons in the 2 nonbonding orbitals located at the O and N atoms. Initial test CASSCF(14,12) calculations showed only three antibonding pi orbitals with occupation numbers larger than 0.05, so the space was reduced to 14 electrons in 10 orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space was chosen by testing rather than by counting: a chemically motivated (14,12) space -- five pi and their antibonding partners plus the oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs -- was run first, the natural orbital occupation numbers inspected, and the two antibonding pi orbitals whose occupations fell below 0.05 were removed, giving (14,10). The electron count is unchanged by this because the discarded orbitals were essentially empty. The 3-21G basis was accepted as adequate on the grounds that a similar basis had been used successfully for first excited states of valence character; the size of the system forced this choice. Excited-state optimizations started from CIS geometries.
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic excitation energies at CASSCF(14,10)/3-21G, computed at MP2 ground-state and CASSCF excited-state geometries: 98.6 kcal/mol in solution for the N form, an overestimate of about 15 kcal/mol against experiment, and 62.1 kcal/mol for the T form, in agreement with the experimental estimate. Vertical excitation and emission energies of the complex are 4.68 and 3.08 eV for the N form and 3.41 and 1.88 eV for the T form, in accord with the monomer values. The CIS transition moment and oscillator strength are 1.32 au and 0.20 for the N-form complex and 1.34 au and 0.3 for the T form. For the N* state the CASSCF and CIS wave functions agree, both dominated by the HOMO to LUMO and HOMO-1 to LUMO+1 single excitations, since HOMO and HOMO-1 and LUMO and LUMO+1 lie close in energy. For the T* form the double excitation from HOMO to LUMO contributes more than 50 percent for both the bare molecule and the complex, and the CASSCF wave function is characterized as the asymmetric combination of the ground-state configuration and its doubly excited configuration. The excited-state triple proton transfer is exothermic by 13.9 kcal/mol at CIS and 20.4 kcal/mol at CASSCF, becoming 21.3 kcal/mol with solvent effects, with T* the more stable form. The excited-state barrier is 1.4 kcal/mol at CASSCF, reduced to 0.2 kcal/mol by solute-solvent interaction, against 5.8 kcal/mol at CIS and an experimental activation energy of 0.54 kcal/mol from the temperature dependence of the T* fluorescence rise time. Ground-state values at HF/3-21G, HF/6-31G* and MP2 include reaction endothermicities of 12.0, 10.8 and 9.2 kcal/mol against a measured enthalpy difference of 9.7 kcal/mol, and forward barriers of 14.1, 12.9 and 10.3 kcal/mol with reverse barriers of 9.1, 12.9 and 9.9 kcal/mol against an experimental estimate of 5.4 kcal/mol.
Other: The active space was fixed by natural-orbital occupation numbers from a larger trial: the chemically obvious (14,12) space -- five ring pi orbitals with their antibonding partners plus the oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs -- showed only three antibonding pi orbitals with occupation above 0.05, so two were dropped to give (14,10) with the electron count unchanged. The multireference character that justifies this whole treatment is state-dependent and lives entirely in the product: for N* the CASSCF and CIS wave functions agree because both are dominated by two single excitations, but for T* the HOMO-to-LUMO double excitation carries more than 50 percent of the weight, so the CASSCF function is the asymmetric combination of the ground configuration and its double, and CIS cannot represent it at all. That is exactly why CIS overestimates the excited-state barrier by a factor of four (5.8 vs 1.4 kcal/mol) while CASSCF lands near the 0.54 kcal/mol experimental activation energy -- the single-reference method describes the reactant but not the product side of the transfer. A separate accuracy caveat sits in the same numbers: the CASSCF(14,10)/3-21G adiabatic excitation energy is 15 kcal/mol too high for the N form but correct for the T form, so the space and basis are unbalanced between the two tautomers even though the barrier between them comes out right.
reference_short: Fang, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1998, 120, 7568
notes: The reaction studied is the concerted triple proton transfer converting the 7-hydroxyquinoline (N) form to the 7-quinolone (T) tautomer in a hydrogen-bonded complex with methanol. Attempts to find an intermediate on the ground- or excited-state pathway were unsuccessful. The authors caution that the excited-state reaction is so rapid that the solvent molecules do not have time to reorient, so equilibrium between the solute electronic state and the reaction field cannot be assumed and the calculated change in barrier from gas phase to solution is only a qualitative estimate.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF energies; MP2 used separately for the ground state

point_group: Cs, with the symmetry plane being the molecular plane
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations for the ground state and the low-lying excited states of both n-pi* and pi-pi* character carried out at the pi-CASSCF level with the ANO C,O[3s2p1d]/H[2s] basis set, all constrained to Cs symmetry. The ground-state C1O distance was also optimized at the pi-CASPT2 level, giving 1.232 A against 1.204 A at CASSCF and 1.231 A at MP2 with the same basis set. Optimized C1O distances: 1.204 (ground state), 1.343 (1 3A''), 1.231 (1 3A'), 1.354 (1 1A''), 1.214 (2 1A') A.
method: Average CASSCF reference wave functions with single-state CASPT2 and the extended multistate MS-CASPT2; transition dipole moments from perturbation-modified CAS (PMCAS-CI) reference functions via the CASSI protocol
basis_set: Generally contracted atomic natural orbital (ANO) sets from the C,O(14s9p4d)/H(8s) primitives with the C,O[3s2p1d]/H[2s] contraction, supplemented with two s-, two p- and two d-type diffuse functions placed at the charge centroid of the cation
active_space_orbital_description: A different space for each class of state, given as (number of a' orbitals, number of a'' orbitals, number of electrons, number of configurations, number of states averaged): 1A'(pi-pi*) 0, 8, 8, 1764, 8; 3A'(pi-pi*) 0, 8, 8, 2352, 1; 1A''(n to pi*) 1, 8, 10, 2352, 1; 3A''(n to pi*) 1, 8, 10, 3696, 1; 1A'(pi to 3pz, 3dxz, 3dyz) 0, 11, 8, 32670, 10; 1A''(n to 3pz, 3dxz, 3dyz) 1, 11, 10, 76230, 6; 1A''(pi to 3s, 3px, 3py, 3dxy, 3dx2-y2, 3dz2) 9, 4, 4, 1140, 9; 1A'(n to 3s, 3px, 3py, 3dxy, 3dx2-y2, 3dz2) 10, 4, 6, 20925, 9.
active_space_protocol: The space is rebuilt for each symmetry and state class rather than fixed once. The base is the valence pi orbitals and pi electrons (eight of each) for pi-pi* states; the oxygen lone pair orbital is added, raising the electron count to ten, whenever the states involve that lone pair. Rydberg orbitals are then appended as appropriate for each Rydberg series. Where the Rydberg orbital belongs to the a' irreducible representation of Cs, the valence part is cut back to only four pi orbitals with four pi electrons, so that adding nine or ten a' Rydberg orbitals stays tractable -- a deliberate trade of valence correlation for Rydberg flexibility in exactly the states that need it. All reference functions come from average CASSCF including all states of interest for a given symmetry, and the MS-CASPT2 step is used specifically so that possibly erroneous valence-Rydberg mixing can be removed at the correlated level.
nroots_per_mult: Between 1 and 10 states averaged depending on the symmetry and state class, as listed in the orbital description
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies from MS-CASPT2. The n-pi* 1 1A'' state is placed vertically at 3.71 eV and assigned to the lowest band; it is the expected weak dipole-forbidden transition. The 1 1A' to 2 1A' and 1 1A' to 3 1A' transitions, of pi-pi* nature, are at 4.33 and 4.89 eV and account for the second and third energy bands. The most intense feature involves the 4 1A' and 5 1A' pi-pi* states, calculated 5.98 and 6.23 eV above the ground state, one of which has a computed oscillator strength of 0.55 and is predicted to be the most intense. A state near 3.27 eV and one with oscillator strength 0.33 are also reported, and a state at 7.58 eV carries a nonnegligible oscillator strength with further states between 7.8 and 8.6 eV having small oscillator strengths. Experimental bands lie at 4.51 eV (oscillator strength given in the text), a band with oscillator strength 0.26, and a fourth band with a maximum around 6.36 eV. Excited states of the low-lying Rydberg series are related to the available experimental data.
Other: The paper solves the valence-Rydberg problem in two different ways at once, and the choice depends on the symmetry of the Rydberg orbital. Where the Rydberg orbitals are a'' (3pz, 3dxz, 3dyz) they are simply appended to the full eight-orbital valence pi space, giving spaces of up to 76230 configurations. Where they are a' (3s, 3px, 3py and the remaining d set) that is not affordable, so the valence part is cut from eight pi orbitals with eight electrons down to four with four -- the Rydberg states get their diffuse orbitals at the price of half the valence correlation. The resulting energies for a' and a'' Rydberg series are therefore not computed on an equal footing, which matters because valence-Rydberg mixing is precisely what the study is trying to resolve. The second mechanism is the MS-CASPT2 step itself, chosen explicitly because it lets the states be treated simultaneously with correlation on the reference functions included, so that erroneous valence-Rydberg mixing present at the CASSCF level can be removed. Note also that the reference-level geometry is not reliable for the carbonyl: the ground-state C1O distance is 1.204 A at pi-CASSCF but 1.232 A at pi-CASPT2, agreeing with MP2 at 1.231 A, so the 0.03 A error sits in the bond whose n and pi* orbitals define the lowest excited state.
reference_short: Molina & Merchan, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 3745
notes: The same basis set and methodology had been applied by the group to biphenyl, stilbene, styrene and 1-phenylpyrrole. In the MS-CASPT2 effective Hamiltonian the diagonal elements are the CASPT2 energies and the off-diagonal elements introduce coupling to second order in the dynamic correlation energy.
correlation_correction: Single-state CASPT2 and extended multistate MS-CASPT2 on the average CASSCF reference functions

point_group: Pseudo C4 (the highest g value direction of the ground microstate is quite far from the pseudo C4 axis)
geometry_source: Geometries taken from the crystal structures, determined at around 100 K, and not optimised. Five layers of point charges were included to assess the effect of charges further away, i.e. neighbouring molecules in the lattice.
method: CASSCF for the spin-free wave functions, followed by RASSI for the spin-orbit multiplets; the resulting energies and wave functions were projected onto the ground Russell-Saunders multiplet to extract mJ compositions of the microstates and crystal field splitting parameters. Magnetic susceptibility computed from the Van Vleck equation; FIR spectra computed by convoluting transition energies and Boltzmann-weighted transition probabilities with a lineshape function.
basis_set: Not specified in the main text beyond a reference to the effects of the necessarily limited size of the employed basis sets, and a comparison of energy changes going from a double to a triple zeta basis set
relativistic_treatment: Spin-orbit multiplets obtained in a second step by RASSI
active_space_orbital_description: The seven 4f orbitals as active space. The number of active electrons is not stated in the main text.
active_space_protocol: The space is the minimal chemically meaningful one for a lanthanide ion: the seven 4f orbitals and nothing else, applied identically to all three metals so that Dy, Ho and Er are treated on the same footing. Everything outside it is handled by other means -- spin-orbit coupling by a subsequent RASSI step, the surrounding lattice by five explicit layers of point charges, and the residual error by a single semi-empirical scaling factor per compound. The authors attribute the need for that scaling to the necessarily limited size of the basis sets, unaccounted dynamical correlation and possible differences between the low-temperature structure and the roughly 100 K crystal structure used, and note the direction of the scaling agrees with the energy change on going from a double to a triple zeta basis.
electronic_structure_description: The CASSCF calculations find a ground doublet predominantly |+/-13/2>: 0.93|+/-13/2> + 0.31|+/-15/2> + 0.21|+/-11/2>, with the first excited state predominantly |+/-11/2>: 0.91|+/-11/2> + 0.34|+/-9/2> + 0.21|+/-13/2>. The resulting calculated energy gap is 52.3 cm-1. Including five layers of point charges changed the energies by at most about 10 percent. Calculated energies were semi-empirically scaled by 0.68 to match the experimentally observed transition energies, with absolute accuracies in the range 10-20 cm-1. The FIR spectra and dc susceptibility can be simulated well using the crystal field parameters found in the CASSCF calculations.
Other: The seven-4f-orbital space gets the wave function composition right but the energies wrong by a fixed factor: the calculated gap of 52.3 cm-1 needs scaling by 0.68 to match experiment, and the scaling is different in both magnitude and direction from the 1.31 and 1.27 needed for the holmium and erbium analogues in the same paper with the identical space. Since the space, method and treatment are held constant across the three metals, that spread is a direct measurement of what the minimal 4f-only space leaves out and how unevenly it does so across the lanthanide series. The authors test the alternative explanations and largely exclude them: five layers of point charges shift energies by at most 10 percent, and varying the interligand distance by +/-0.05 A produces changes comparable to the discrepancy but in a non-monotonic direction, while the g-tensors of the lowest doublet barely move -- so the wave functions are stable even where the energies are not. That stability is the paper's actual argument: CASSCF supplies the state compositions and spectroscopy supplies the accurate energies, because neither alone is sufficient.

notes: The number of active electrons is not stated; the space is described only as the seven 4f orbitals. The 4f9 count follows from the Dy(III) oxidation state. Simulations based on crystal field parameters previously reported by Ishikawa et al. and Gaita Arino et al. are given for comparison.
