electronic_structure_description: Three independent peaks were observed in the holmium derivative, enabling derivation of crystal field splitting parameters. The energy level diagram obtained from the spectroscopic data is very well reproduced by the CASSCF calculations assuming a scaling factor of 1.31. The calculations find that all microstates of the ground multiplet are heavily mixed. Holmium has an integer angular momentum quantum number and is not subject to Kramers' theorem, so twofold degeneracy is not necessarily maintained; the calculations find energy splittings of up to about 1 cm-1 between pairs of states that can be considered quasi-doublets. The compositions of the wave functions strongly depend on the choice of quantisation axis; the highest g value direction of the ground microstate was chosen, and that direction is quite far from the pseudo C4 axis, consistent with single crystal SQUID measurements. Assuming a |+/-6> rather than a |+/-5> ground doublet leads to almost equally good fits of susceptibility, magnetization and FIR data. Excellent fits of the field and temperature dependence of the FIR spectra and of the dc susceptibility are obtained from the CASSCF crystal field parameters. Five layers of point charges were included and the effect of small distortions of the molecule on the energy spectrum was examined.
Other: Here the seven-orbital 4f space produces a result whose interpretation is not even basis-independent in the ordinary sense: because holmium has integer J and is not protected by Kramers' theorem, the calculation splits the nominal doublets by up to about 1 cm-1, and the mJ compositions of the heavily mixed microstates depend strongly on which quantisation axis is chosen. The authors pick the highest-g direction of the ground microstate, which turns out to lie far from the pseudo C4 axis -- so the state labels themselves are a post-processing choice rather than an output of the wave function. Compounding this, the spectroscopy cannot discriminate: a |+/-6> ground doublet fits susceptibility, magnetization and FIR almost as well as |+/-5>, and it is the CASSCF composition that breaks the tie. The energies again need a scaling factor, 1.31, in the opposite direction from the 0.68 required for the dysprosium analogue with the identical space, which the authors reconcile with the direction of the double-to-triple-zeta basis set shift.

electronic_structure_description: CASSCF gives a ground doublet with 99 percent |+/-1/2> character and a first excited doublet with 98 percent |+/-3/2> character. The calculated zero-field gap between them is 58.7 cm-1, smaller than the experimentally observed 74 cm-1, so a scaling factor of 1.27 is applied; the experimental value is in turn clearly smaller than the 102 cm-1 derived by Ishikawa et al. Two FIR features are observed, one at 74 cm-1 in zero field assigned to the |+/-1/2> to |+/-3/2> transition, and a low-energy one assigned to the |-1/2> to |+1/2> transition within the ground doublet, which enters the spectral window only above 3 T because of the large g-perpendicular of the ground doublet, expected to be about 9 for a pure |+/-1/2> Kramers doublet. X-band EPR gives a single resonance with g-perpendicular 9.59 (g-parallel not observed) and the FIR measurements give g = 9.01 for the ground doublet. Using that value and the observed splitting of the high-frequency line, the effective g value of the excited multiplet is almost zero, in accordance with the CASSCF calculations. The CASSCF crystal field parameters give an excellent simulation of the FIR spectra and susceptibility data.
Other: Erbium is the case where the minimal 4f space works cleanly on composition: the ground and first excited doublets come out 99 and 98 percent pure |+/-1/2> and |+/-3/2>, and the near-zero effective g of the excited multiplet predicted from that purity is confirmed by the field splitting of the FIR line. The energy is another matter -- 58.7 cm-1 calculated against 74 cm-1 observed, requiring a 1.27 scaling factor, close to the 1.31 needed for holmium but opposite in direction to the 0.68 needed for dysprosium. Across three isostructural complexes treated with the identical seven-orbital space and identical protocol, the required correction therefore spans 0.68 to 1.31, which sets the honest error bar on unscaled 4f-only CASSCF/RASSI crystal field energies at roughly a factor of two. Worth noting that the experimental gap of 74 cm-1 also disagrees with the 102 cm-1 previously derived from magnetic data alone, so the calculation is closer to the direct spectroscopy than the older parameterisation was.

compound_name: Wild-type 11-cis retinal protonated Schiff base chromophore in the rhodopsin binding pocket
geometry_source: Chromophore geometries obtained after relaxation inside the rhodopsin binding pocket from molecular dynamics runs (10 MD runs and 10 optimized structures per model, with internal coordinates and error margins in the Supporting Information). For the electronic structure calculations the chromophores were reduced to five-double-bond systems by omitting the beta-ionone ring, and the counterion was reduced to the formate anion HCOO- together with wat2b.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 second-order perturbation corrections for specified states; transition dipole moments from the CAS state interaction method, combined with the CASPT2 energies to obtain oscillator and rotatory strengths
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital (ANO) set consisting of 4s3p1d for carbon and nitrogen and 2s for hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: All valence pi electrons and as many orbitals. The numeric electron and orbital counts are not stated in the paper; the chromophores were truncated to five-double-bond systems for these calculations.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by a rule rather than by a count -- all valence pi electrons in an equal number of orbitals -- so it adapts automatically to each of the five chromophores without any per-molecule tuning, which is what makes the calculated spectral shifts between analogues comparable. The cost of the method forced the chemistry instead: the beta-ionone ring was cut off so that every chromophore is a five-double-bond system, and the protein counterion Glu113 was reduced to formate plus one water. That truncation is the dominant approximation and its direction is known and stated -- shortened chromophores give systematically higher excitation energies.
electronic_structure_description: Across all five chromophores the electronic structure follows the same pattern: the ground state S0 is configurationally rather pure (75 percent closed shell); the first excited state has high HOMO-LUMO character (65 percent), high oscillator strength and a very unsymmetric charge distribution with a dipole moment above 18 D in every case; the next state is configurationally mixed, combining the HOMO to LUMO+1 and HOMO-1 to LUMO single excitations with the HOMO to LUMO double excitation, and is spectrally silent with neither oscillator nor rotatory strength. Wild type: S0 -670.7365 au with dipole moment 9.77 D; S1 at 2.86 eV (434 nm) with oscillator strength 0.89, rotatory strength 0.66 au and dipole moment 19.1 D; S2 at 3.10 eV (400 nm) with oscillator strength 0.00, rotatory strength -0.00 au and dipole moment 9.43 D. compound_name: Thymine, photodynamics of the relaxation into the first excited singlet state
geometry_source: Ground- and excited-state minima and minima on the crossing seam optimized at the SA-3-CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G* level, with analytic energy gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors. RI-CC2 geometries were optimized at the RI-CC2 level itself. MS-CASPT2 and MR-CISD single points used the CASSCF geometries. Initial geometries and velocities for the dynamics were generated by a Wigner distribution treating each nuclear coordinate as a harmonic oscillator in the ground state. Structures were analyzed with Cremer-Pople parameters using the Boeyen conformer classification scheme.
method: Mixed quantum-classical surface-hopping dynamics on SA-3-CASSCF(10,8) surfaces, with MS-CASPT2, MR-CIS, MR-CISD+Q and RI-CC2 static benchmarks
software: NEWTON-X for the dynamics, COLUMBUS for the MRCI calculations, MOLCAS for MS-CASPT2, TURBOMOLE for RI-CC2, PLATON for the Cremer-Pople parameters
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF and dynamics; 6-311G** for the larger MS-CASPT2 calculations; SV(P) and TZVPP for RI-CC2
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals. At the ground-state minimum geometry these are one n, four pi and three pi* orbitals. The MR-CISD and MR-CIS reference space is smaller, six electrons in five orbitals, obtained from the CAS(10,8) space by a selection scheme based on natural-orbital occupation numbers in which orbitals with occupation larger than 0.9 were moved to the doubly occupied space and those below 0.1 to the virtual space.

The multireference CI reference space is not chosen independently but derived from that same space by an automatic occupation-number cut at 0.9 and 0.1, which reduces (10,8) to (6,5); this keeps the MR-CISD reference consistent with the surfaces the dynamics actually ran on. MS-CASPT2 reuses the CAS(10,8) space unchanged, with an IPEA shift of 0.25 unless stated otherwise, so the benchmarks differ from the dynamics only in the correlation treatment and basis, never in the orbital selection.

At the lowest crossing point MXS 3,6B: S0 2.87, 2.50 (2.42), 2.38, 2.34, 2.52; S1/S2 5.74, 5.01 (4.85), about 5.3, about 5.2, 5.31. method: CASSCF for geometries and harmonic frequencies with CASPT2 single-point corrections as formulated by Roos et al.; conventional transition-state theory for the kinetics
software: MOLCAS 4.1 and MOLCAS 5.0; POLYRATE version 7.8 for the kinetics and thermodynamics

Core electrons were left uncorrelated (frozen) throughout because the basis is inadequate for core-valence and core-core correlation.

This space is the ozone share of the common (10,9) space used for the transition states and addition products, chosen so that the energy scales properly on separation. An alternative full outer valence (12,9) space was also considered.
active_space_protocol: The active space is fixed at (10,9) for every transition state and addition product, following the empirical prescription of Anglada and Bofill, and the spaces for the separated reactants are then not free choices: they are dictated by that decision, since the energy must scale properly on dissociation. Partitioning the common (10,9) space gives (2,2) on the alkene -- the pi bonding and antibonding orbitals, 3 CSFs -- and (8,7) on ozone, 490 CSFs. The authors note explicitly that this partitioning differs from the alternative used elsewhere, where the optimal spaces were built from a diagonalized MRCI density matrix by keeping all natural orbitals with occupancies between 0.02 and 1.98, which for the same chemistry yields (2,2) on ethene but (12,9) on ozone. Orbital composition was tracked by monitoring the changes in the occupation numbers of the active orbitals during the optimizations.
electronic_structure_description: Geometric parameters at CASSCF(8,7)/cc-pVTZ are in fairly good agreement with experiment. The calculated harmonic wavenumbers are in the wrong order: the asymmetric mode is placed above the symmetric one and the experimental value is overestimated by 201 cm-1. Increasing the active space to the full outer valence (12,9) does not result in a convincing approach of the calculated geometric parameters toward the experimental values.
Other: Ozone is the classic case where a bigger space does not help, and this paper measures that directly: going from (8,7) to the full outer valence (12,9) produces no convincing improvement in the geometry, while the harmonic frequencies remain misordered with the asymmetric mode above the symmetric one and a 201 cm-1 overestimate. The diagnosis given is that the failure belongs to dynamical correlation, not to the reference space -- the CASSCF(8,7)/cc-pVTZ calculation includes only a small fraction of it -- and that correctly ordered frequencies were obtained only recently by reduced multireference coupled cluster including all three spin-adapted references of a (2,2) space, which unconstrains the symmetry adaptation. So the cure for ozone is a different correlation treatment on a deliberately smaller reference, not a larger CAS. The (8,7) space used here is not chosen for ozone's own sake anyway: it is whatever the common (10,9) transition-state space leaves for the ozone fragment once proper energy scaling on dissociation is imposed.

But the price is visible in the reactant geometry: with only the (2,2) pi pair on the alkene, the C-F bond comes out 0.022 A short and the C-Cl bond 0.012 A long, because the space contains no density on the carbon-halogen bond at all and the calculation is, in the authors' words, just a small step away from Hartree-Fock for everything except the C-C pi system. Since the whole chemical question is how the halogen's resonance and inductive effects redistribute charge and thereby set the ozonolysis rate, the space omits exactly the bonds that carry the substituent effect and recovers it only indirectly through the pi density. The syn/anti energetics turn on the same charge distribution -- charge transfer leaves ozone negative and steers it away from the negative region of the haloalkene -- so the conformational preference is a property of a density the reactant-level space does not describe well.

notes: The scarcity of experimental data for fluoroethene ozonolysis diminishes the relevance of comparing calculated and experimental values.

ligand_set: eight or nine water molecules in the first hydration shell
point_group: C1 as optimized; also symmetrized to C4 for the excited-state analysis
geometry_source: Geometry optimized at the B3LYP level with no symmetry constraints, using an SCF energy convergence of 1e-6 and an Ultrafine integration grid in Gaussian03. The CASSCF calculations were single points at these C1 B3LYP geometries. For the excited-state analysis the small-core C1 geometry was symmetrized to C4, which raises the total electronic energy by 3.33 kcal/mol at B3LYP.
method: CASSCF used to test the multiconfigurational character of the wave function, on B3LYP-optimized geometries; the thermodynamics and structures themselves were obtained with DFT, MP2 single points and PCM solvation
basis_set: Stuttgart small-core RSC28 segmented effective core potential on Ce(III), replacing 28 inner-shell electrons and accounting for scalar relativistic effects, with a [9s,8p,5d,4f,3g] basis describing the 4s2 4p6 5s2 4d10 5p6 4f1 valence electrons; the most diffuse s function was omitted because of linear dependency. The large-core RLC47 ECP with a [5s,4p,3d] basis for the 5s2 5p6 valence electrons was used in the large-core calculations. All H and O atoms used aug-cc-pVDZ.
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic effects accounted for through the Stuttgart effective core potentials; spin-orbit coupling was ignored, although calculated spin-orbit coupling constants for the bare Ce3+ ion are known to be 600-700 cm-1
active_space_orbital_description: A minimal active space of the one 4f electron in the seven 4f orbitals, (1,7), reflecting the 4f1 valence electronic configuration of Ce(III). A (1,1) space, one electron in one f orbital, was also run; this is equivalent to an ROHF calculation. Natural orbitals from Lowdin orthogonalization of the C1 molecular orbitals were used as the initial guess.
active_space_protocol: The space is used as a diagnostic instrument rather than as a production method. Two calculations bracket the question: (1,1), which is equivalent to ROHF and gives the total electronic energy with no correlation from excited-state mixing at all, and (1,7), which permits every possible placement of the single electron among the seven 4f orbitals. The difference between the two is by construction the entire multiconfigurational contribution available within the f manifold, so if it vanishes the wave function is single-determinantal and DFT is licensed for the rest of the study. The CASSCF calculations were run at the C1 B3LYP optimized geometries, and their computational expense is given as the reason for not pursuing them further once the diagnostic came back negative.
electronic_structure_description: The (1,1) and (1,7) CASSCF total ground-state electronic energies differ by less than 0.0001 millihartree, and the (1,7) wave function consists of a single configuration with a coefficient of 0.99998. The singly occupied Lowdin natural orbitals from both the (1,1) and (1,7) CASSCF show significant mixing of the 4f orbitals, similar to the mixing seen in the singly occupied Kohn-Sham orbital from B3LYP, where the f-character orbital has large contributions from the fz3, fxz2 and fxyz atomic orbitals. Natural bond order analysis found no covalent bonding interactions between the Ce and OH2 units.
Other: This is a negative result reported as such, and it is the point of the calculation: expanding from (1,1) -- which is just ROHF for a single f electron -- to the full (1,7) f manifold changes the total energy by under 0.0001 millihartree and leaves a wave function that is 0.99998 a single configuration. Since (1,7) exhausts every rearrangement of the one valence electron among the seven 4f orbitals, there is no multiconfigurational character available in the f shell to find, and the authors use that to license DFT for the rest of the thermodynamic study. What the CASSCF does not certify is the orbital picture: the singly occupied natural orbital is heavily mixed among fz3, fxz2 and fxyz at both CASSCF levels just as it is in the Kohn-Sham orbital, so the single determinant is single in the CI sense while its orbital is a strong mixture in the atomic-f basis -- the near-degeneracy of the seven 4f orbitals shows up in the orbital shape, not in the CI expansion. Spin-orbit coupling, which for the bare Ce3+ ion runs 600-700 cm-1 and would mix these states, was ignored throughout.
reference_short: Dinescu & Clark, J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 11198
notes: Ce(III), with a single f electron, is presented as the simplest test case for benchmarking hydrated Ln(III) properties against varying density functionals and reaction field models. Counterpoise corrections of Boys and Bernardi were used to evaluate basis set superposition error on adding one water to this species, applied a posteriori with fragment relaxation energy terms included. Hydration free energies were corrected with the polarizable continuum model using UA0, UFF, UAHF, UAKS and partially scaled Pauling radii cavity models.
correlation_correction: MP2 single points at the optimized B3LYP geometries with the Stuttgart RSC28 basis on Ce(III); no correlation correction applied on top of the CASSCF

compound_name: Nitromethane / methyl nitrite rearrangement: the transition structure for 1,2-methyl migration and the CH3 + NO2 dissociation limit
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations with B3LYP (analytical gradients and Hessians) and CCSD(T) (numerical gradients and Hessians with the eigenvector following technique) using cc-pVDZ, and with CASSCF(10,10) using a modified (aug)-cc-pVTZ basis in which diffuse functions were placed on C, N and O but not on hydrogen. Vibrational frequencies at B3LYP/cc-pVDZ characterized the stationary points and gave the zero-point corrections. Core orbitals were kept frozen in the electron correlation calculations.
method: CASSCF(10,10) geometry optimization with CASPT2(10,10) and internally contracted MRCISD(10,10)+Q single points, alongside HF, MP2, CCSD(T), B3LYP and a modified G2M treatment
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Modified (aug)-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF, with diffuse functions on C, N and O but not on H; cc-pVDZ for the B3LYP and CCSD(T) geometries; 4-31G and 6-31G(d,p) used when reproducing the earlier smaller-space work; basis sets from 6-311G(d,p) to 6-311G(3df,2p) for the MPn and CCSD(T) energetics
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons distributed over ten orbitals, selected by considering the most relevant orbitals of both the nitrogen dioxide and methyl radical fragments together with the interacting orbitals between them. The shapes of the ten active natural orbitals and their occupation numbers are shown in Figure 1. A (4,4) space matching that used in the earlier literature was also tested.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled fragment-wise -- the important orbitals of NO2, those of CH3, and the orbitals through which the two interact -- so that both the tight transition structure and the fully separated radical pair are representable in one space. The immediate purpose is to test a literature claim: two earlier studies using MCSCF(4,4) had located a loose transition state with C-N and C-O distances of 3.4 and 3.7 A, and this work asks whether that structure survives a larger space. The (4,4) space and the smaller 4-31G and 6-31G(d,p) basis sets of those studies were reproduced here as controls. The same (10,10) space was reused unchanged as the reference for the internally contracted MRCISD calculations.
electronic_structure_description: Only a tight transition structure could be located for the methyl migration linking nitromethane and methyl nitrite. All single-reference methods (HF, MP2, CCSD(T)) and B3LYP give a tight transition state. Despite extensive attempts with different optimization techniques, starting points and Hessians, no loose transition state could be reproduced with CASSCF(10,10)/(aug)-cc-pVTZ; at interfragment distances beyond 3.5 A some first-order saddle points were found but they correspond to methyl configurational changes rather than to methyl migration. Repeating the search with a (4,4) space and the 4-31G and 6-31G(d,p) basis sets of the earlier studies also failed to locate a loose transition state, as did a search for a transition state resembling CH3 + NO2 recombination. The CASSCF wave function of the tight transition state is effectively dominated by the Hartree-Fock configuration with C0 greater than 0.93, and all occupied natural orbitals have occupation numbers above 1.9. Geometric parameters of the tight transition state agree across CCSD(T)/cc-pVDZ, B3LYP/cc-pVDZ and CASSCF(10,10)/(aug)-cc-pVTZ, with the most sensitive parameters, the C-N and C-O interdistances, varying by only 0.05-0.06 A between levels. The transition state lies consistently above the CH3 + NO2 dissociation limit at every level; lower levels give differences up to 15-18 kcal/mol and significantly smaller C-N bond dissociation energies, while the smallest gap, 3.9 kcal/mol, comes from the G2M approach, comparable to 2.7 kcal/mol from a previous G2MP2 study. At MRCISD(10,10)+Q/(aug)-cc-pVTZ//CASSCF(10,10)/cc-pVDZ + ZPE the difference between the tight transition state and CH3 + NO2 is 10.5 kcal/mol and the C-N bond energy 59.2 kcal/mol. The C-N bond dissociation energy is 68.0 kcal/mol at CASSCF(10,10), 51.8 at CASPT2(10,10) and 59.9 at MRCISD, so the quadruple correction is rather small; other estimates are 62.3 kcal/mol from G2M, 63.0 from CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ and 61.9 from a previous G2MP2 calculation. The recommended value is 60 +/- 2 kcal/mol, with the migration barrier via the tight transition state at least 6 kcal/mol higher.
Other: The whole point of enlarging the space is a structure that turns out not to exist: two earlier MCSCF(4,4) studies had located a loose transition state at C-N and C-O distances of 3.4 and 3.7 A, and with (10,10) it cannot be found, no matter the starting geometry, Hessian or optimization technique. Crucially, the authors then went back and reran the (4,4) space with the original 4-31G and 6-31G(d,p) basis sets and still could not reproduce it, so the discrepancy is not simply space size. The internal evidence that (10,10) is adequate is that it is barely needed at all at the tight transition state: the CASSCF wave function there is dominated by the Hartree-Fock configuration with C0 above 0.93 and every occupied natural orbital sits above 1.9 electrons, which is why the CASSCF, CCSD(T) and B3LYP geometries agree to 0.05-0.06 A on the sensitive C-N and C-O distances. Where the space does matter is the dissociation energy, and there the spread is large and one-directional: CASSCF(10,10) gives 68.0 kcal/mol, CASPT2(10,10) overshoots downward to 51.8, and MRCISD lands at 59.9 with a small Davidson correction bringing 59.2 -- a 16 kcal/mol swing across three treatments of the identical reference, with the perturbative result the worst of the three.

notes: The earlier work of Saxon and Yoshimine used MCSCF(4,4) with a 4-31G basis without polarization functions and obtained a loose transition state, giving a barrier of 56.7 kcal/mol for the 1,2-methyl shift from MCSCF-CI(7)/6-31G(d) single points. In the loose structure the predominant configuration has the three unpaired electrons of NO2 distributed in the nitrogen lone pair orbital (a') and the two pi combinations of oxygen lone pairs (a''). The possibility of heavy atom tunneling accelerating the migration is raised.

active_space_protocol: Correlated ab initio calculations on the entire polyoxometalate were prohibited by its size, so the chemistry was reduced to six-coordinate CrO6(3-) model complexes and the question of what the rest of the structure does was answered by varying the model rather than the space. compound_name: Phenoxy radical (C6H5O), ground and low-lying electronic states and thermal decomposition
geometry_source: Ground-state geometry optimized at the CASSCF(9e/8o)/6-31G* level and compared with UHF, UMP2, B3LYP and literature CASSCF(7e/7o) results with the same basis. Geometries of some intermediates and transition states were also optimized with B3LYP. Vertical excitation energies were computed at the CASSCF(9e/8o)/6-31G* ground state geometry. Planar UMP2/6-31G* structures were obtained for the 2B1, 1 2A2 and 1 2B2 states.
method: State-specific and state-averaged CASSCF(9e/8o) for the electronic states, with G2M(rcc,MP2) and a simplified G2M(rcc,MP2*) scheme built from UMP2 and RCCSD(T) for the decomposition energetics, and multistep RRKM calculations for the rate constants
software: Gaussian 92/DFT for the UHF, B3LYP, UMP2 and UMP4 calculations; MOLPRO 92 and 94 for the CASSCF and RCCSD(T) calculations
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF; 6-31G(d,p), 6-311G(d,p) and 6-311+G(3df,2p) in the composite G2M schemes
active_space_orbital_description: Nine electrons in eight orbitals: the pi active space augmented with the lone pair orbital of the oxygen, so the nine electrons are seven pi electrons plus two lone pair electrons distributed over eight active orbitals. Earlier literature used a CASSCF(7e/7o) pi-only space.
active_space_protocol: The pi-only (7,7) space of earlier work is enlarged by one orbital and two electrons to bring in the oxygen lone pair, specifically because the low-lying states of the phenoxy radical differ in the symmetry of the singly occupied orbital and some of them are n-type -- a pure pi space cannot describe them. The paper reports the geometric consequence explicitly: including the lone pair had no effect on the optimized structure, so the enlargement buys state coverage rather than accuracy for the ground state. Six non-totally-symmetric states (1-2 2B1, 1-2 2A1 and 1-2 2A2) were included with equal weight in the state-averaged calculations, and state-specific results were computed alongside for comparison.
nroots_per_mult: Six states with equal weight in the state-averaged calculations, plus state-specific calculations
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in kcal/mol from state-specific CASSCF(9e/8o)/6-31G* with state-averaged values in parentheses: 30.2 (33.1) for 1 2B2, 59.3 (62.4) for 1 2A2, 79.2 (77.6) for 1 2B1, 117.0 (120.0) for 2 2B2, and 139.7 (144.7) for 2 2A2. State-specific and state-averaged calculations give qualitatively the same energy ordering, with the state-averaged values 3-5 kcal/mol larger. Experimental transitions are 24.4 +/- 1.2 kcal/mol (1200 nm) for the first excited state from ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy of phenide, 46.1 kcal/mol (611 nm), 71.5 kcal/mol (395 nm), 96.8 kcal/mol (292 nm) and 119.9 kcal/mol (240 nm) from gas phase and nitrogen matrix absorption. The proposed assignment is 1200 nm to 1 2B2, 611 nm to 1 2A2, 395 nm to 2 2B1, 292 nm to 2 2B2 and 240 nm to 2 2A2. Inclusion of the lone pair orbital in the active space had no effect on the optimized structure, and the CASSCF structural features agree with the UMP2 and B3LYP results. The earlier CASPT2/CASSCF study of Olivella et al. gave an activation energy of 53.9 kcal/mol at their best level, about 10 kcal/mol higher than the experimentally derived value, with a theoretical preexponential A factor substantially larger than experiment.
Other: Enlarging the space from the literature's pi-only (7,7) to (9,8) by adding the oxygen lone pair changes nothing about the ground-state geometry -- the paper says so directly -- but it is what makes the excited states accessible at all, since the low-lying states differ in the symmetry of the singly occupied orbital and some involve the lone pair. What the enlargement does not fix is the energies: every computed vertical excitation lies above experiment, by about 10 kcal/mol for the lower states (1 2B1, 1 2B2, 1 2A2) and about 20 kcal/mol for the higher ones (2 2B2, 2 2A2). The authors attribute this partly to compact basis functions where the higher states need diffuse ones, but identify the more essential cause as incomplete recovery of dynamic correlation, and state plainly that the straightforward cures -- SDCI on top of the CASSCF wave function, or CASPT2 -- were prohibitively expensive for a molecule of this size. So this is a case where the space is known to be adequate and the correlation treatment is known to be the limiting factor, with the fix explicitly out of reach rather than merely untried. State averaging over six states costs a further 3-5 kcal/mol of upward shift relative to state-specific calculations without changing the ordering. A caveat on the assignment itself: the 2B1 to 2B2 transition assigned to the 292 nm band is symmetry forbidden under C2v, though that band is observed to be weak and nearly obscured.
reference_short: Liu, Morokuma, Mebel & Lin, J. Phys. Chem. 1996, 100, 9314
notes: A previous CIS/3-21G calculation on the 1 2A2 state gives an excitation energy 3 eV larger than CASSCF with the same basis and is described as totally unreliable. The simplified G2M(rcc,MP2*) scheme, which involves only UMP2 and RCCSD(T) calculations, still needs calibration and testing but gives results close to G2M(rcc,MP2) for this reaction. The computed energies and molecular parameters were used in multistep RRKM calculations of the reaction rate constant.

geometry_source: All stationary points optimized at the CASSCF/6-31G* level with the indicated active space, with analytical or numerical vibrational analyses to characterize them as minima or transition structures and to obtain zero-point energy differences; B3LYP/6-31G* geometries were obtained in parallel.
method: CASSCF for all stationary points with CASPT2/6-31G*//CASSCF/6-31G* single points for dynamic electron correlation, run in parallel with B3LYP/6-31G*
software: Gaussian 98 and Gaussian 03 for the CASSCF and B3LYP calculations; Molcas 6.4 for the CASPT2 calculations; MacMolPlt for the structural and molecular orbital representations with the contour value set at 0.08
basis_set: 6-31G* throughout for all CASSCF, CASPT2 and B3LYP calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in nine orbitals for 3, 4 and TS(3->4), covering the conjugated pi system including the terminal allenyl C-C pi bond together with the nitrogen lone pair. The same (10,9) space was used for the constrained planar transition structure.
active_space_protocol: Each rearrangement gets the space that covers exactly its own pi system and heteroatom lone pair, so the sizes run (6,6) for the all-carbon triene, (8,7) for the aza-trienes, (8,8) for the allenyl tetraene and (10,9) for the aza-allenyl tetraene. The whole argument of the paper is a comparison of activation enthalpies across this series -- the allene moiety is worth so many kcal/mol, the nitrogen lone pair so many more -- so the spaces are deliberately built by the same rule (all participating pi bonds plus the nitrogen lone pair where present) rather than fixed at one size, and each addition to the space corresponds to the structural feature being tested. CASPT2 single points at every CASSCF stationary point supply dynamic correlation, and B3LYP is run in parallel throughout as an independent check.
electronic_structure_description: The presence of the allene moiety lowers the activation enthalpy of TS(3->4) relative to TS(10->11) by 7.1 kcal/mol at CASPT2//CASSCF and 6.8 kcal/mol at B3LYP. TS(3->4) lies 4.9 (6.1) kcal/mol below TS(5->6), whereas if only the C-N pi bond and not the nitrogen lone pair participated it would be expected about 7 kcal/mol above; this energy lowering of 11.8 (13.2) kcal/mol parallels the 17.2 (16.7) kcal/mol difference between TS(9->11) and TS(10->11). The B3LYP activation barrier for the 3 to 4 electrocyclization is 13.9 kcal/mol against 24.4 kcal/mol for the 12 to 4 one, a difference of 10.5 kcal/mol, while the difference in reaction enthalpy between the two is only 0.1 kcal/mol; based on activation energies rather than enthalpies the difference is 10.7 kcal/mol. TS(3->4) is flatter than TS(7->8), with a C3-C4-C5-N1 dihedral of 23.5 degrees against 30.6 degrees. The C-N pi bond is 0.4 A longer in TS(12->4)-B3LYP than in TS(3->4)-B3LYP. A hypothetical fully planar TS(3->4), with all relevant dihedral angles frozen and only the CH2 hydrogens free, was located at (10,9)CASSCF/6-31G* with zero forces and one imaginary frequency at 1020 cm-1; it lies 6.8 kcal/mol above the unconstrained TS(3->4), only 1.1 kcal/mol per frozen dihedral angle. Its molecular orbitals look almost identical to those of TS(3->4) except that the atomic orbitals are less hybridized (more p-like) and less tilted, so even with the nitrogen lone pair and terminal C-C pi bond perfectly aligned the reaction is not pseudopericyclic with two orbital disconnections. Fixing both H-C7-C2-C3 dihedral angles at 90 degrees gives a second-order saddle point. All rearrangements studied are exothermic.
Other: The series is constructed so that each step up in active space size isolates one structural feature, and the resulting energy differences are the paper's evidence. Adding the allene moiety lowers the activation enthalpy of TS(3->4) relative to TS(10->11) by 7.1 kcal/mol at CASPT2//CASSCF and 6.8 at B3LYP, and of TS(5->6) relative to TS(7->8) by 12.5 and 10.3 kcal/mol. Adding the nitrogen lone pair in a position where it can reach the bonding site lowers TS(10->11) relative to TS(9->11) by 17.2 (16.7) kcal/mol, and since the two reactions differ in reaction enthalpy by a negligible 0.6 (0.3) kcal/mol, that cannot be a Hammond effect. The two levels agree closely -- activation enthalpies differ by only 0.4-1.4 kcal/mol between CASPT2//CASSCF and B3LYP, except for the hypothetical planar transition structure -- so the conclusions do not hinge on the perturbative correction. Structural corroboration comes from within the active space itself: the C-N bond is 1.35 A in TS(9->11) but 1.31 A in TS(10->11) at (8,7)CASSCF, showing less C-N pi participation exactly where the lone pair takes over. The one place the two methods diverge is the constrained planar transition structure, which warns that the CASPT2 correction and B3LYP respond differently once geometry is frozen.
reference_short: Duncan, Calkins & Chavarha, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2008, 130, 6740
notes: Correlation diagrams constructed entirely from localized complete active space molecular orbitals were used to explore the roles of the terminal allenyl pi bond and the nitrogen lone-pair orbital. Compound 12 is the Z isomer of 3 and rearranges to the same product 4.

compound_name: SrOSr, the hypermetallic strontium oxide molecule
ligand_set: a single central oxygen bridging two Sr atoms; the bonding is predominantly ionic Sr+ O2- Sr+
point_group: D-infinity-h at linearity; calculations performed in D2h, C2v and Cs subgroups
geometry_source: Three-dimensional potential energy and dipole moment surfaces computed on a grid: energies and dipole moments at 55 geometries for the ground state and 56 for the first triplet, with Sr-O bond lengths from 2.00 to 2.35 A and bond angles from 180 to 115 degrees, chosen to cover energies up to 1500 cm-1 above each minimum with uniform grid spacing. The common singlet and triplet equilibrium geometry is a linear SrOSr angle with r(Sr-O) = 2.15 A. Least-squares fits of the surfaces had standard deviations of 9.5 and 5.0 cm-1 for the ground and first triplet states.
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by internally contracted MRCISD with the Davidson correction (+Q), combined with a modified CASPT2 (RS2C) of Celani and Werner; variational MORBID calculations on the resulting surfaces for rovibrational term values and infrared spectra
software: MOLPRO 2010.1 for all electronic structure calculations; the MORBID program system for the rovibrational calculations
basis_set: Sadlej pVTZ for Sr and O, with a modified Sadlej pVTZ for the singlet-triplet matrix element calculations
relativistic_treatment: Stuttgart small-core relativistic effective core potential ECP28MDF on strontium; the Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian used for the singlet-triplet electronic matrix element calculations
active_space_orbital_description: For the potential energy surfaces, 28 electrons (1s2 2s2 2p4 on O and 4s2 4p6 5s2 on each Sr) distributed in 15 molecular orbitals (7-11 sigma-g, 7-10 sigma-u, 4-5 pi-u and 4 pi-g), written by the authors as CAS(15,28) with the orbital count first. In C2v this is seven orbitals of A1, two of B1, five of B2 and one of A2 symmetry; in Cs it is twelve of A' and three of A''. For the vertical excitation spectra a different space of 12 orbitals holding 10 electrons was used: nine orbitals (7-9 sigma-g, 7-8 sigma-u, 4 pi-u and 4 pi-g) were closed, and the 10-12 sigma-g, 9-11 sigma-u, 5-6 pi-u and 5 pi-g orbitals formed the active space. The singlet-triplet matrix elements used a 14-orbital, 26-electron space.
active_space_protocol: Test calculations with different active spaces were carried out before adopting one, and they established a specific requirement: correct description of the ground and first triplet states demands correlation of the core 4s and 4p electrons of strontium, which is why 28 electrons rather than the valence count are correlated. Two states, 1 1A1 and 1 3B2, are state-averaged with equal weights for the surfaces. Because the chosen space still excludes the valence antibonding orbitals, the energies are assembled from three separate calculations: the MRCISD+Q energy plus the difference between two RS2C runs, one in which the 5 pi-g antibonding orbital (the antisymmetric combination of the Sr 5px,y orbitals) is correlated and one in which it is not, so that core-valence correlation and the antibonding orbitals are recovered without enlarging the reference. An energy shift of 0.1 hartree was applied in the RS2C calculations to avoid intruder states, and the energies corrected for it. The vertical spectra use a separate, smaller reference averaged over eleven singlet and nine triplet states.
nroots_per_mult: Two states with equal weights for the surfaces; eleven singlet states (two Ag, two B3u, two B2u, one B1u, two B2g, two B3g) and nine triplet states (two B3u, two B2u, one B1u, two B2g, two B3g) for the vertical spectra
electronic_structure_description: The ground X 1Sigma-g+ state requires a multiconfigurational treatment: its two most important configurations are |... 8sigma-g2 7sigma-u2 9sigma-g2 8sigma-u2 4pi-u4 4pi-g4 10sigma-g2 9sigma-u2 5pi-u4 11sigma-g2> and |... 5pi-u4 10sigma-u2>, with CI coefficients 0.72 and -0.60 at linearity. The a 3Sigma-u+ state is well described by a single reference, |... 5pi-u4 11sigma-g1 10sigma-u1>, with a coefficient of 0.94. Vertical excitation energies in cm-1 at the common equilibrium geometry, from state-averaged CAS(12,10)-MRCISD+Q: singlets X 1Sigma-g+ 0 (0.74 |5pi-u4 11sigma-g2> - 0.56 |5pi-u4 10sigma-u2>), A 1Sigma-u+ 11391, B 1Sigma-g+ 12910 (0.70 |5pi-u4 10sigma-u2> + 0.52 |5pi-u4 11sigma-g2>), C 1Pi-g 13337, E 1Pi-u 14109, D 1Pi-g 27932, F 1Pi-u 33297; triplets a 3Sigma-u+ 0, b 3Pi-g 15701, d 3Pi-u 16451, c 3Pi-g 27457, e 3Pi-u 31967. Transition dipole moments in au: 1.17 for A 1Sigma-u+, 2.53 for E 1Pi-u, 0.49 for F 1Pi-u, 2.94 for b 3Pi-g and 0.45 for c 3Pi-g. These predict a strong triplet absorption band centered near 640 nm and a strong singlet band near 710 nm, which do not agree well with the bands observed by Gaydon at 595 and 605 nm in strontium arc spectra. The molecular orbital ordering differs from MgOMg and CaOCa: the orbitals built from Sr 4p combinations (8 sigma-u, 4 pi-u, 4 pi-g, 10 sigma-g) lie energetically between the 9 sigma-g and 9 sigma-u orbitals. The atomization energy from the ground state, computed at CAS(15,28)-MRCISD+Q by comparing the equilibrium geometry with both Sr atoms placed 15 and 20 A away, is 199.6 kcal/mol against an experimental 194 +/- 6 kcal/mol. The singlet-triplet perturbation matrix elements between close-lying vibronic states turn out to be very small.
Other: Two independent findings about the space, both established by explicit testing. First, test calculations with different active spaces showed that the ground and first triplet states cannot be described correctly unless the strontium 4s and 4p core electrons are correlated, which is why 28 electrons are carried rather than a valence count -- a genuine core-valence requirement rather than a precaution. Second, the space that results is still incomplete in the other direction, missing the valence antibonding orbitals, and rather than enlarge the reference the authors compose the final energy from three calculations: MRCISD+Q plus the difference between two RS2C runs differing only in whether the 5 pi-g antibonding orbital is correlated. That construction isolates the antibonding contribution as an additive correction, and it is necessary precisely because the ground state is strongly multiconfigurational -- CI coefficients of 0.72 and -0.60 for two configurations at linearity -- while the first triplet is essentially single-reference at 0.94. The two states therefore demand very different treatments even though they are averaged together with equal weights. A separate and smaller 12-orbital, 10-electron space averaged over eleven singlets and nine triplets is used for the vertical spectra, so the excitation energies and the surfaces do not rest on the same reference. Note the paper writes its spaces orbital-count-first, as CAS(15,28), CAS(12,10) and CAS(14,26). The predicted bands at 640 and 710 nm do not match Gaydon's observed 595 and 605 nm features, which Gaydon had suggested might belong to Sr2O2 instead.

The MORBID variational calculations on the fitted surfaces give rovibrational term values, transition wavenumbers and spectral intensities. The y axis lies along the molecular axis in the reported transition moment components.

point_group: Cs, kept planar in all calculations on the C-Br fragmentation
geometry_source: Constrained ground-state geometry optimizations with the C-Br internal degree of freedom frozen at values from about 1.3 to 4.0 A, all other degrees of freedom optimized within the molecular point group. Geometries of certain low-lying excited states were obtained from optimizations constrained to the same symmetry as the ground state.
method: CASSCF for geometry optimizations and reference wave functions, with multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) single points for vertical excitation energies; combined with femtosecond laser spectroscopy
basis_set: ANO-S atomic natural orbital sets with contractions (7s3p)/[2s1p] for hydrogen, (10s6p3d)/[3s2p1d] for carbon and (10s6p3d)/[3s2p1d] for fluorine; for bromine a relativistic effective core potential basis with seven electrons, contraction (9s8p4d)/[1s1p2d], of Barandiaran and co-workers
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potential on bromine
active_space_orbital_description: Labelled as (a' occupied, a'' occupied)(a' virtual, a'' virtual): (2, 4)(2, 4) with 12 active electrons.
active_space_protocol: Each molecule gets its own space, specified orbital-by-orbital per irreducible representation rather than as a single (n,m) count, so that the same physical set of orbitals is captured despite the differing symmetry. The requirement driving the choice is stated explicitly: all lower excitation energies correspond to n/pi to pi*/sigma* transitions and all orbitals involved in those transitions are included, so no root corresponding to an observed 0-0 transition can be missing. Symmetry is imposed and held fixed through the whole C-Br fragmentation coordinate -- Cs for the 2- and 3-isomers, C2v for the rest -- which assumes the mirror planes of the relaxed ground state survive dissociation. Geometries come from constrained ground-state optimizations with the C-Br distance frozen between about 1.3 and 4.0 A and everything else relaxed, then MS-CASPT2 single points including the three lowest roots in each irreducible representation for both multiplicities.
nroots_per_mult: Three lowest roots in each irreducible representation for both singlet and triplet multiplicity: 24 states for the C2v molecules and 12 for the Cs ones
electronic_structure_description: Calculated CASPT2 vertical excitation energies with experimental absorbance maxima, across 2-BrFPh, 3-BrFPh, 4-BrFPh, 1-Br-2,6-FPh, 1-Br-3,5-FPh and BrF5Ph. First 3-pi-pi*: 3.84, 3.88, 3.83, 3.86, 3.94, 3.85 eV. Second 3-pi-pi*: 4.40, 4.45, 4.11, 4.45, 4.48, 4.51 eV. Third 3-pi-pi*: 4.46, 4.51, 4.44, 4.49, 4.57, 4.52 eV. First 1-pi-pi* (calculated then experimental in eV): 4.62 and 4.60, 4.67 and 4.57, 4.51 and 4.50, 4.65 and 4.64, 4.69 and 4.62, 4.68 and 4.70, with an RMSD of 0.055 eV. 3-pi-sigma*: 5.51, 5.48, 5.58, 5.37, 5.44, 4.91 eV. 1-pi-sigma* (calculated then experimental): 5.85 and 5.74, 6.49 and 5.71, 5.96 and 5.83, 5.78 and 5.66, 5.23 and 5.17, with RMSD 0.327 eV including the 3-fluoro compound. Higher 1-pi-pi* (calculated then experimental): 6.30 and 6.75, 5.80 and 5.74, 5.80 and 5.74, 5.84 and 5.97, with RMSD 0.088 eV excluding the 3-fluoro compound. The lowest excited singlet varies over a narrow range, from 4.51 eV for 4-BrFPh to 4.68 eV for BrF5Ph. For 2-BrFPh the 0-0 transition of the 1La band is located at 271.0 nm. The energy of the crossing point between the S1-B1 state and T1 (3-pi-sigma*) is 0.24 eV. A second time constant is observed for this molecule, indicating that an additional electronic state is initially excited. The spectra show a band between 200 and 230 nm and a less intense band between 245 and 280 nm with vibronic features; the 1La band corresponds to the first singlet pi-pi* state and the 1Lb band to the second.
Other: The active spaces are defined per irreducible representation rather than by a single size, and the completeness criterion is spectroscopic rather than energetic: because every n/pi to pi*/sigma* orbital involved in the low-lying transitions is inside the space, no observed 0-0 band can correspond to a missing root, which is what licenses assigning experimental peaks purely by the energetic order of the CASPT2 roots. The accuracy this buys is measured: RMSD of 0.055 eV against experimental 0-0 transitions for the first excited state and 0.088 eV for the second, far better than the 0.3 eV generally expected of the method. But the same tables show where it breaks down. The 1-pi-sigma* states, which are the dissociative ones that carry the entire photochemistry, have an RMSD of 0.327 eV -- six times worse than the bound pi-pi* states -- and 3-BrFPh had to be excluded from the second-state analysis as anomalous. That matters because the mechanism rests on crossings between the bound S1 and repulsive T states, computed at 0.24, 0.21 and 0.14 eV for the 2-, 3- and 4-isomers, differences smaller than the error bar on the repulsive states themselves. The authors accordingly conclude that the crossing point energies do not correlate with the measured dissociation rates and that some other coupling mechanism, not represented in these one-dimensional curves, must dominate. A further structural assumption is that the imposed symmetry survives the whole C-Br fragmentation, which forces the calculated states to remain symmetry-classified along a coordinate where the molecule is breaking apart.
reference_short: Borg, Liu, Persson, Lunell, Karlsson, Kadi & Davidsson, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 7045
notes: The disubstituted molecules all resemble fluorobenzene in the 1La band, showing three significant peaks. The dissociation channel common to all disubstituted bromofluorobenzenes corresponds to a transition between the bound S1 state and a repulsive T state, the same channel observed earlier for many halobenzenes.

compound_name: Spirooxazine / merocyanine model system (Model-1) for photochemical and thermal ring-opening and closure
geometry_source: Full geometry optimizations at CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G(d) without any symmetry constraint to locate the critical points on the ground and excited state surfaces. Numerical frequency calculations determined the nature of the stationary points, and intrinsic reaction coordinates were computed to establish the pathways linking critical structures including conical intersections. Conical intersections were optimized at the CASSCF level. CASPT2 single points were then computed at the CASSCF-optimized geometries.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 and multistate MS-CASPT2 single points; a larger Model-2 with explicit water molecules was treated by DFT (B3LYP) for the ground-state reaction only
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals for the ring-opening reaction coordinate: the six benzenoid orbitals, the pi and pi* orbitals of the N-C double bond, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-O single bond, and the orbital of the nonbonding pair of the oxygen atom, which is conjugated with the aromatic ring (a pO in the spirooxazine form but an nO in the merocyanine isomer). Some calculations used a larger space of 14 electrons in 12 orbitals, obtained by adding the nonbonding pair orbital of the nitrogen atom.
active_space_protocol: The core space is chosen so that a single orbital set spans both isomers: it contains the sigma and sigma* of the C-O bond that breaks, the pi and pi* of the N-C bond that forms, the benzenoid set, and one oxygen lone pair whose character changes identity along the coordinate, being a pO perpendicular to the ring in the closed form and an nO in the open merocyanine. The valence-bond rationale is explicit -- excitation from pO to sigma*(O-C2) simultaneously forms the pi(O-C10) bond and breaks the sigma(O-C2) bond, and that excited state correlates with the merocyanine ground state. The nitrogen lone pair is added, giving (14,12), only for the vertical excitation spectrum and the final energetics, because one of the three lowest excited states at the Franck-Condon geometry is of nN-pi* character. It is then deliberately removed again for the exploratory surface scans, on the stated grounds that the nN-pi* state is not expected to participate in the opening reaction, which makes the calculations cheaper at the cost of that state disappearing from those results.
nroots_per_mult: Nine lowest excited states characterized at the Franck-Condon geometry
electronic_structure_description: Thermal reaction on the ground state surface: the colorless spirooxazine reactant is 27.6 kcal/mol more stable than trans-merocyanine, which in turn is 9.5 kcal/mol more stable than cis-merocyanine. The transition state connecting spirooxazine with cis-merocyanine has an O-C2 distance of 2.063 A and a CASPT2 barrier of 40.8 kcal/mol, precluding thermal ring opening under usual conditions, while the reverse barrier is only 3.8 kcal/mol above the cis-merocyanine minimum. No transition state for trans/cis isomerization could be located; at the CASPT2 level the cis-merocyanine minimum shifts to a different geometry from the CASSCF one, lying 8.9 kcal/mol above trans-merocyanine, and the cis to trans path appears almost barrierless, with the trans to cis barrier at 9.1 kcal/mol. Nine lowest excited states at the Franck-Condon geometry from MS-CASPT2//CASSCF(14,12), with energies in kcal/mol relative to the spirooxazine ground state minimum at -697.370 au and oscillator strengths: S1 pi-pi* and pO-sigma* 95.3 (0.100); S2 nN-pi* and pi-pi* 109.6 (0.041); S3 nN-pi*, pi-pi* and pO-pi* 119.2 (0.025); S4 pi-pi* and pO-pi* 141.4 (0.135); S5 pi-pi* and pO-pi* 154.4 (0.308); S6 pi-pi* and pO-sigma* 159.3 (0.020); S7 pi-pi* 178.8 (0.081); S8 nN-pi* 185.8 (0.003); S9 pi-pi* 189.2 (0.064). Gradients at the Franck-Condon region on both the S1 and S3 CASSCF surfaces involve elongation of the N-C3 bond and shortening of the O-C10 bond. Relaxation on S1 leads to a minimum 87.7 kcal/mol above the ground state minimum, from which a transition state with an O-C2 distance of 1.617 A lies only 3.8 kcal/mol higher on the path to the S1/S0 conical intersection. Relaxation on S3 decreases continuously in energy, crossing the S2 surface and reaching a conical intersection with S1 located 102.6 kcal/mol above the ground state minimum by a barrierless path. The S1/S0 conical intersection optimized at CASSCF lies 57.3 kcal/mol (average value) above the S0 minimum when recalculated at MS-CASPT2(14,12), with an S0-S1 energy difference of only 1.0 kcal/mol there.

The size of the system rules out exploring the surfaces at CASPT2 directly. The consequences are visible in the numbers: the cis-merocyanine minimum moves to a different geometry between the two levels, changing its energy from 9.5 to 8.9 kcal/mol above trans, and the S1/S0 conical intersection optimized at CASSCF sits at 57.3 kcal/mol at MS-CASPT2 -- roughly half the 102.6 kcal/mol of the S3/S1 crossing on the CASSCF surface. What rescues the conical intersection is a self-consistency check rather than reoptimization: at the CASSCF-optimized geometry the MS-CASPT2 S0-S1 gap is only 1.0 kcal/mol, so the CASSCF description of that particular structure is judged adequate. Separately, the space is not held constant: the nitrogen lone pair is included for the vertical spectrum, giving (14,12), then dropped for the surface exploration to save time on the argument that the nN-pi* state does not participate in ring opening -- which means the S2 state is simply absent from the exploratory results, and the S2/S3 crossing the mechanism invokes is inferred rather than located. The single oxygen lone-pair orbital in the space changes character from pO to nO between the two isomers, which is what allows one space to span the whole reaction.

notes: Model-1 is the smaller model used for the CASSCF/CASPT2 study of the mechanism; a larger Model-2 including all heteroatoms of the photochromic active site plus explicit water molecules was studied by DFT only, because of its size and because only the ground state reaction was needed there. The experimental observation that merocyanine structures revert to spirooxazine on a timescale of seconds to minutes in nonpolar solvents even at low temperatures, while the forward reaction requires photoexcitation, matches the computed 40.8 versus 3.8 kcal/mol barriers.

compound_name: SnCl2+ cation, low-lying doublet and quartet states
geometry_source: CASSCF and CASSCF/MRCI vertical ionization energies were computed at the RCCSD(T)/A optimized geometry of the X 1A1 state of neutral SnCl2 taken from the authors' previous study. Adiabatic ionization energies used geometries optimized at the RCCSD(T) level with the various basis sets.
method: CASSCF and CASSCF/MRCI with the Davidson correction as initial survey calculations, followed by restricted coupled-cluster singles-doubles with perturbative triples (RCCSD(T)) with larger basis sets for the production results; Franck-Condon factor calculations for simulating the photoelectron band
basis_set: A series of basis sets for Sn with the ECP28MDF small-core effective core potential accounting for the 1s2s2p3s3p3d shells: sets A and Af for the CASSCF and MRCI survey calculations, and A1, A2, A3, B, B1 and B2 of up to aug-cc-pV5Z quality for the RCCSD(T) calculations, with aug-cc-pV(5+d)Z on Cl and the standard aug-cc-pwCVQZ set for core correlation. In the Af set the g functions on both Sn and Cl were removed; only the s, p and d functions of the standard basis sets were used in the CASSCF spin-orbit interaction calculations.
relativistic_treatment: ECP28MDF small-core relativistic effective core potential on Sn; scalar relativistic effects included, with off-diagonal spin-orbit interaction evaluated separately
active_space_orbital_description: A full valence active space; the numerical electron and orbital counts are not stated. With the small-core ECP28MDF potential the X 1A1 state of neutral SnCl2 has the valence electronic configuration ...(12a1)2 (4b1)2 (9b2)2 (3a2)2.
active_space_protocol: The multiconfigurational treatment is used as a survey and a diagnostic rather than for the final numbers. A full valence space with relatively small basis sets (A and Af) gives CASSCF and CASSCF/MRCI vertical ionization energies for the eight lowest doublet states, and the MRCI wave functions are then inspected to decide whether a single-reference method suffices. Two different averaging schemes were used: average-state CASSCF over eight states, being the two lowest doublet cationic states of each C2v symmetry, for the Af calculations, and two-state CASSCF/MRCI for each symmetry separately for the A calculations. Once the diagnostic came back negative for strong multireference character, the accurate work switched to RCCSD(T) with basis sets up to aug-cc-pV5Z, core correlation on both Sn and Cl, and extrapolation to the complete basis set limit.
nroots_per_mult: Eight states in the average-state CASSCF (two lowest doublets of each C2v symmetry); two states per symmetry in the CASSCF/MRCI calculations
electronic_structure_description: Vertical ionization energies in eV for eight low-lying doublet states of SnCl2+, given as CAS/Af, CAS/A, MRCI/A, MRCI+D/A, then the largest MRCI CI coefficient: 2A1 (12a1)1 9.15, 9.11, 9.72, 9.89, 0.891; 2B2 (9b2)1 9.98, 10.05, 10.67, 10.86, 0.752; 2A2 (3a2)1 10.27, 10.41, 10.95, 11.08, 0.883; 2B1 (4b1)1 10.81, 10.97, 11.49, 11.62, 0.876; 2A1 (11a1)1(12a1)2 10.95, 11.04, 11.59, 11.72, 0.863; 2B2 (8b2)1(9b2)2 11.55, 11.65, 12.22, 12.40, 0.728; 2B1 (11a1)2(12a1)0(4b1)2(5b1)1 12.66, 12.69, 13.41, 13.59, 0.849; 2A2 (12a1)1(4b1)2(5b1)1(9b2)1 13.02, 13.09, 13.82, 13.99, 0.877. The reference-configuration weights from the MRCI calculations are larger than 0.93 for all states. For the four lowest states the vertical ionization energies at MRCI/A are 9.86, 10.90, 11.08 and 11.71 eV; at MRCI+D/A 10.03, 11.07, 11.23 and 11.87; at RCCSD(T)/A 10.22, 11.19, 11.47 and 11.97; at RCCSD(T)/B2 10.38, 11.24, 11.53 and 12.08; with best estimates of 10.40 +/- 0.02, 11.30 +/- 0.07, 11.61 +/- 0.07 and 12.17 +/- 0.08 eV. T1 diagnostics from all RCCSD calculations are below 0.0253 for the doublet states and 0.0268 for the quartets. The best adiabatic ionization energy including zero-point vibrational correction is 10.09 eV. The four low-lying quartet states lie above about 14.4 eV, roughly 2 eV higher than the six lowest doublets reachable by one-electron ionization, so spin-orbit interaction between low-lying doublet and quartet states should be negligibly small in the vertical ionization region. The results confirm assignment of the first photoelectron band of SnCl2 to ionization to the X 2A1 state, the second band to both (1)2B2 and (1)2A2, the third to both (1)2B1 and (2)2A1, and the fourth to (2)2B2.
Other: The full valence CASSCF/MRCI here exists to answer one question -- is a single-reference method safe? -- and the answer is read directly off the CI coefficients: every state accessible in the vertical ionization region has a single dominant reference configuration with C0 above 0.72, reference weights above 0.93, and RCCSD T1 diagnostics below 0.0253, so nondynamic correlation is judged unimportant and the accurate work proceeds at RCCSD(T). The multireference numbers are nonetheless systematically too low: MRCI/A gives 9.86 eV for the first ionization against a best estimate of 10.40 eV, and the Davidson correction recovers only 0.17 eV of that 0.54 eV gap, with the remainder coming from basis set extension and core correlation rather than from anything the reference could supply. Two states, (2)2A1 and (2)2B2, are excited states inaccessible to the restricted-Hartree-Fock-based RCCSD(T) method, so for those the MRCI values are the only ones available -- which means the two states with the weakest single-reference character in the set (C0 of 0.863 and 0.728) are precisely the ones that could not be cross-checked by coupled cluster. The quartet states were computed for a specific reason, to test whether spin-orbit mixing with the doublets matters for a fourth-row element, and the answer is no because they sit about 2 eV higher.
reference_short: Lee, Dyke, Chow, Mok & Chau, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 13193
notes: The computational strategy follows the authors' previous study on the low-lying neutral states of SnCl2. The assignments agree with those of three earlier references but disagree with two others. Franck-Condon factors were computed and used to simulate the first photoelectron band of SnCl2; no experimental adiabatic ionization energy position has been reported because the observed band shows no resolvable vibrational structure.
correlation_correction: MRCI with the Davidson correction (+D) on the CASSCF references; RCCSD(T) with core correlation and complete-basis-set extrapolation for the production values

compound_name: Cr(H2O)6(2+), the divalent hexaquochromium complex and its Jahn-Teller distortion
ligand_set: six water ligands in an approximately octahedral first coordination sphere
point_group: Oh idealized; the effective geometry at all three minima is D2h
geometry_source: Potential energy surfaces mapped along the two eg normal modes by state-averaged CASSCF on a grid, with a second finer grid of 16 x 42 = 672 points. Geometry optimizations were also performed with the B3LYP and BP86 functionals and the TZVP basis set, giving two sets of bond distances; the difference between theory and experiment is about 0.01 A for the axial Cr-O bonds and at most about 0.049 A for the equatorial ones.
method: State-averaged CASSCF for mapping the potential energy surfaces along the eg normal modes, with multireference difference dedicated configuration interaction (MR-DDCI2) and spectroscopy-oriented configuration interaction (SORCI) at the stationary points for the D tensor; quasi-degenerate perturbation theory and second-order perturbation theory both used to extract D and E
basis_set: TZVP and the more extensively polarized TZVPP
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic treatment; the Breit-Pauli two-electron spin-orbit coupling operator approximated by the spin-orbit mean field (SOMF) approach
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in the five metal d-based orbitals, CAS(4,5). For the Table 2 CASSCF calculations the 4 d electrons were used together with the 5 d orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is the five metal d-based orbitals and nothing else, with the electron count set by the oxidation state, so the two complexes differ only in occupancy and can be compared directly. Everything the space omits is recovered by other means rather than by enlargement: dynamic correlation by MR-DDCI2 and SORCI single points at the stationary points of the CASSCF surface, spin-orbit coupling by the spin-orbit mean field approximation, and spin-spin coupling separately. The state averaging is deliberately exhaustive at first -- all 10 quartet and 35 doublet roots for Cr(III), all 5 quintet and 35 triplet roots for Cr(II) -- and only then truncated for the fine grid, where the five quintets and the eight most important triplets were kept so that a 16 x 42 = 672-point surface became affordable. Individually selecting MR thresholds were Tsel 1e-6 Eh, Tpre 1e-4 and Tnat 1e-5 Eh.
nroots_per_mult: All five quintet and 35 triplet states on the initial grid; the five quintets and the eight most important triplets on the finer 672-point grid
electronic_structure_description: Jahn-Teller stabilization energy and the splitting of the 5Eg ground term at the minimum of the CASSCF/TZVPP surface, in cm-1: CASSCF/TZVP 954 and 3984; CASSCF/TZVPP 1082 and 4625; MRDDCI2/TZVP 1188 and 4318; MRDDCI2/TZVPP 1457 and 4483; SORCI/TZVP 1340 and 4485; SORCI/TZVPP 1708 and 4630; experimental about 1600 and about 6500. When a SORCI calculation is performed at the experimentally determined Jahn-Teller radius rather than the computed one, the splitting rises to 6600 cm-1, in excellent agreement with the observed transition near 8000 cm-1 (of which about 1500 cm-1 is attributed to strain effects). The zero-field splitting D at the CASSCF/TZVPP minimum is -2.45 cm-1 at SORCI/TZVPP against an experimental -2.2 cm-1; at the experimentally determined Jahn-Teller radius it is -2.34 cm-1, taken as the best theoretical result. The computed E is 0.04 cm-1 against an experimental estimate below 0.1 cm-1; a finite E cannot be explained within sigma bonding alone, where zero would be obtained. Decomposition of D gives spin-orbit quintet contributions of -1.067, -1.020 and -1.105 cm-1 and a spin-spin contribution of -0.371, -0.360 and -0.364 cm-1, with totals of -2.45, -2.448 and -2.532 cm-1 against an experimental value of about -2.3. The spin-spin contribution is essentially geometry independent and is about 15 percent of the total D. Second-order perturbation theory reproduces the exact D to within 1.4 percent or 0.033 cm-1 across the theta normal mode. In D2h both the Oh T1g and T2g states map onto B1g + B2g + B3g and can spin-orbit-couple with the ground state.
Other: The five-orbital d-only space with four electrons gets the zero-field splitting right and the Jahn-Teller surface wrong, and the paper separates the two failures cleanly. On the surface, CASSCF/TZVPP underestimates both the Jahn-Teller energy (1082 against about 1600 cm-1) and the 5Eg splitting (4625 against about 6500 cm-1); adding dynamic correlation improves both monotonically -- MRDDCI2 to 1457 and SORCI to 1708 cm-1 for EJT -- but the splitting stays too small because the calculated Jahn-Teller radius is too short. Evaluating SORCI at the experimental radius instead raises the splitting to 6600 cm-1 and brings it into excellent agreement, so the residual error is geometric rather than electronic. Crucially, this does not contaminate the property of interest: by symmetry the 5Eg state contributes nothing to D, so its underestimated splitting is harmless. The D value itself is reproduced to -2.45 cm-1 at SORCI/TZVPP against -2.2 cm-1 experimental, and the authors note explicitly that the decomposition results are unchanged when MR-DDCI2 or SORCI replaces state-averaged CASSCF -- so for D the minimal space suffices and the correlation treatment is not load-bearing, the reverse of the situation for the surface. The spin-spin contribution is 15 percent of the total, needed for quantitative accuracy but ignorable qualitatively, and second-order perturbation theory reproduces the full quasi-degenerate treatment to 1.4 percent.
reference_short: Liakos, Ganyushin & Neese, Inorg. Chem. 2009, 48, 10572
notes: The experimentally observed optical transition near 8000 cm-1 is assigned to the transition between the tetragonally split components of the 5Eg (Oh) ground term. State averaging over all five quintets and 35 triplets was used on the first grid and reduced to the eight most important triplets on the finer grid with the larger basis.

Geometry optimizations gave Cr-O distances of 2.0 A. Second-order perturbation theory reproduces the exact D to within 10.4 percent or 0.08 cm-1. Other: With an orbitally nondegenerate 4A2g ground term there is no Jahn-Teller distortion to map, so the same CAS(3,5) space is used purely to compute how the zero-field splitting responds to imposed geometric distortion -- and the answer is that 0.02 A of distortion produces the entire experimental D of 0.1 cm-1. That sensitivity is the finding: the property is so small and so steeply geometry-dependent that the calculation cannot be used to predict D from an optimized structure, only to invert the measured D into a statement about the average solution geometry. The perturbative treatment is also noticeably worse here than for the divalent complex, 10.4 percent error against 1.4 percent, though the absolute deviation is comparable (0.08 versus 0.033 cm-1) because D itself is twenty times smaller. compound_name: [HIPTN3N]MoL with L = N2, the Jahn-Teller-active dinitrogen complex
ligand_set: the HIPTN3N triamidoamine ligand (truncated to models 1' and 1'') with an axial dinitrogen ligand
point_group: C3v at the symmetric limit; distorted by the pseudo-Jahn-Teller effect
geometry_source: Model 1' geometries optimized with a CASSCF(3,2) wave function together with a scalar relativistic ZORA treatment using the model potential of van Wuellen and the SARC-TZVP basis. Two sets were obtained: one optimized to the fully C3v-symmetric limit as a reference and one allowing pseudo-Jahn-Teller distortion. Model 1'' geometries were fully optimized with the BP86 functional together with ZORA, SARC-TZVP for molybdenum and nitrogen and SARC-SV(P) for carbon and hydrogen, using spin-unrestricted Kohn-Sham determinants. Model 1, the full complex with HIPT substituents, could only be treated at the DFT level and served as reference for the truncated models.
method: State-averaged CASSCF references with MR-DDCI2 for property and final energy calculations; molecular g-tensors from the Gerloch-McMeeking formalism as an infinite-order quasi-degenerate perturbation theory solution with respect to spin-orbit coupling in a finite number of scalar-relativistic eigenstates, with first-order Zeeman perturbation theory on top
software: ORCA version 2.6.35, including the ORCA-MRCI program
basis_set: SARC-TZVP (scalar relativistically recontracted all-electron triple-zeta valence polarization) for the CASSCF geometry optimizations; TZVP for the property and final energy calculations; TZVP for Mo and N with SV(P) for C and H in the model 1'' calculations
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic zeroth-order regular approximation (ZORA) with the model potential of van Wuellen; spin-orbit coupling treated by the spin-orbit mean-field Hamiltonian within quasi-degenerate perturbation theory
active_space_orbital_description: Three electrons in the five metal d-based orbitals for the state-averaged CASSCF(3,5) reference used in the MR-DDCI2 property calculations, taking 30 roots. A smaller CASSCF(3,2) space, three electrons in the two frontier d-pi orbitals with two roots, was used for the geometry optimizations and for the two-state model.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces are used for two purposes. Geometry optimization and the two-state vibronic model use CASSCF(3,2), the minimal space spanning the degenerate d-pi doublet whose splitting is the Jahn-Teller effect itself. Property calculations use CASSCF(3,5), almost all multiplets arising from distributing three electrons over all five metal d orbitals, with 30 roots rather than two in the quasi-degenerate perturbation theory step; the justification is that the ligands are made of light atoms with very small spin-orbit coupling, so multiplets within the metal d manifold can safely be expected to dominate the g-values. MR-DDCI2 is then layered on the (3,5) reference to recover dynamic correlation and more realistic covalencies. The choice of a multiconfigurational route is forced rather than preferred: the 2E ground state has very strong in-state spin-orbit coupling and cannot be represented by two-component DFT.
nroots_per_mult: Two roots in the CASSCF(3,2) model; 30 roots in the CASSCF(3,5) and MR-DDCI2 calculations
electronic_structure_description: Calculated d-d transition energies in cm-1 from scalar relativistic ZORA MR-DDCI2 on top of the SA-CASSCF(3,5) reference with the SARC-TZVP basis, for [Mo]N2, [Mo]CO and [Mo]NH3 respectively: 2Ea (2e)3 at 0, 0, 0; 4Ea (2e)2(3e)1 at 16979, 20644, 9188; 4A1 (2e)2(3a1)1 at 30297, 32501, 18739; 2Eb (2e)2(3e)1 at 23569, 26420, 21067; 2A1 (2e)2(3a1)1 at 32947, 35454, 28692. Experimental g-values are g-perpendicular 1.51 < 2 < g-parallel 3.03. Calculated g-values at model 1' geometries with the TZVP basis and ZORA, listed as CAS(3,2) with 2 roots, CAS(3,5) with 30 roots, then MR-DDCI2 with 30 roots: g1 1.14, 1.26, 1.17; g2 1.14, 1.33, 1.19; g3 3.50, 3.30, 2.75; pseudo-Jahn-Teller splitting 714, 735, 682 cm-1. At the model 1'' geometries: g1 1.77, g2 1.81, g3 2.66, with a pseudo-Jahn-Teller splitting of 1309 cm-1 calculated against 1200 cm-1 from the two-orbital model. Inclusion of dynamic correlation shifts g3 down by about 0.55 for this complex, the largest such effect in the study. Pi-backbonding significantly stabilizes the 2e orbitals. The splitting of the two lowest Kramers doublets increases rapidly with geometric distortion, reaching about 600 cm-1 at the calculated Jahn-Teller distorted geometry, which explains why EPR detects only a single Kramers doublet. Metal and ligand contributions: 15.2 percent on the L = N2 ligand for one orbital and 18.4 percent for another, with 3.9 and 4.2 percent on the equatorial ligands. Taking r = 1.2, a spin-orbit parameter of 800 cm-1 for Mo(III) and a force constant of 0.15 mdyn/A gives a linear Jahn-Teller coupling parameter of 3.1e3 cm-1/A and a pseudo-Jahn-Teller distortion of about 0.08 A, small against the Mo-N bond length of about 2 A. Jahn-Teller stabilization energies are calculated as 850-1300 cm-1.
Other: The paper isolates the effect of enlarging the space from the effect of adding correlation, and finds the space matters for a reason other than the one expected. Going from CASSCF(3,2), the two frontier d-pi orbitals, to CASSCF(3,5), all five metal d orbitals with 30 roots instead of 2, changes g-values by up to 0.26 -- and the authors trace this not to the extra spin-orbit pathways the larger root space allows (indirect coupling of the 2Ea ground components to 2Eb and 4Ea via the x and y components of the SOC operator, impossible in the two-state model) but to the influence of the extended five-orbital space on the pseudo-Jahn-Teller splitting of the 2E ground state itself. Adding dynamic correlation at MR-DDCI2 on the same (3,5) reference then shifts g3 of [Mo]N2 down by about 0.55, the largest single change in the study. Both effects are strongly ligand-dependent: [Mo]NH3 is almost unaffected by either the extended space or dynamic correlation, while the N2 and CO complexes respond to both. Two limitations are stated rather than fixed. First, DFT is disqualified at the outset: the 2E ground state has very strong in-state spin-orbit coupling and cannot be correctly represented by two-component DFT because a single Slater determinant does not account for the genuine multireference character, so the multiconfigurational route is not a refinement but a requirement. Second, the CASSCF calculations on truncated models substantially underestimate the vibronic coupling -- the computed pseudo-Jahn-Teller splittings fall noticeably below the two-orbital model estimates -- because the bulky HIPT substituents and the solvent are absent, so the roughly 600 cm-1 splitting at the calculated distorted geometry is itself probably an underestimate. Symmetry sets a hard constraint the calculations respect: at C3v geometries the g-tensor must remain axial, and deviations from axiality appear only once the Jahn-Teller distortion is present.

notes: [Mo]N2 is the dinitrogen complex central to the catalytic nitrogen reduction cycle; the earlier EPR work identified the singly occupied d-pi doublet. The Jahn-Teller-active mode is a composite of all e modes with non-zero Jahn-Teller coupling.
correlation_correction: MR-DDCI2 (difference dedicated configuration interaction) on the state-averaged CASSCF(3,5) reference
