compound_name: 1,5-Diaza-1,3-pentadiene, intramolecular NH...N proton transfer in the ground and low-lying excited states
point_group: Cs for the equilibrium (E) structure and C2v for the transition state (TS); the CASSCF calculations were limited to planar-constrained structures
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations within a multiconfigurational CASSCF wave function, limited to planar-constrained structures; transition state optimizations performed under the presumption of C2v symmetry. Separate SCF, CIS and CIS-MP2 optimizations were carried out with 4-31G and 6-31+G** for comparison, and some excited states have nonplanar minimum energy structures which were examined alongside the planarity-constrained ones to allow direct comparison with isoelectronic systems such as malonaldehyde and glyoxalmonohydrazone. Reaction paths were computed as intrinsic reaction coordinates by the Gonzalez-Schlegel algorithm with a step size of 0.1 amu^(1/2) bohr in mass-weighted internal coordinates, using the 4-31G basis.
method: CASSCF, compared against CIS and CIS-MP2
basis_set: 4-31G for the CASSCF and the reaction paths; 6-31+G** also used at the CIS and CIS-MP2 levels
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in seven orbitals, constructed from canonical SCF molecular orbitals as three occupied and four virtual. The three occupied orbitals are those from which single excitations contribute appreciably to the CIS energy, with a coefficient greater than about 0.3: the two highest occupied orbitals of pi character (17a'' and 19a'' in the equilibrium structure, 17a2 and 19b2 in the transition state) and the highest occupied orbital of n character (18a' in E, 18b1 in TS). The four virtual orbitals are the lowest of pi* character (20a'', 23a'', 34a'', 36a'' in E and 20a2, 23b2, 33b2, 36a2 in TS). A second active space was built by replacing two of the virtual pi* orbitals with two virtual orbitals of sigma* character.
active_space_protocol: The occupied part of the space is selected by a numerical criterion rather than by inspection of orbital character alone: orbitals from which single excitations enter the CIS wave function with a coefficient of at least 0.3 are promoted into the space, which for this molecule picks out two pi and one n orbital. The virtual part is chosen by argument -- since all excited states of interest are of pi-pi* character it is called a natural choice to include only pi* orbitals -- and that argument is then tested directly by rebuilding the space with two of the pi* orbitals swapped for two sigma* orbitals and rerunning the ground state and the lowest triplet. The resulting shifts are reported explicitly as an estimate of the uncertainty associated with the choice of active space.
electronic_structure_description: Total CASSCF(6,7)/4-31G energies in hartree for the planar equilibrium and transition state structures, with adiabatic excitation energies in kcal/mol: S0 -225.6907075 (E) and -225.6527408 (TS); 3pi-pi* -225.5891636 and -225.5305432, AEE 63.72 and 76.7; 3n-pi* -225.5670023 and -225.4979672, AEE 77.63 and 97.1; 1n-pi* -225.5567291 and -225.4851928, AEE 84.07 and 105.1; 1pi-pi* -225.4856670 (a non-fully-optimized structure with total RMS gradient 0.01) and -225.4524778, AEE 128.66 and 125.7. Proton transfer barriers in kcal/mol for 1pi-pi*, S0, 3n-pi*, 1n-pi* and 3pi-pi*: CIS/4-31G 6.53, 13.84, 26.75, 29.13, 34.14; CIS/6-31+G** 11.03, 16.81, 27.17, 30.03, 34.84; CIS-MP2/4-31G -3.52, 8.87, 8.19, 5.34, 8.95; CIS-MP2/6-31+G** -0.87, 8.12, 6.79, 1.24, 3.47; CASSCF(6,7)/4-31G 20.83, 23.82, 36.78, 44.89, 43.32. The number of configurations generated in the S0, 3pi-pi*, 3n-pi*, 1pi-pi* and 3n-pi* states is 280, 294, 294, 210 and 280 for the E structure in Cs symmetry and 149, 153, 147, 105 and 131 for the transition state in C2v. With the modified active space containing two sigma* orbitals, the configuration counts fall to 254 and 288 in E and 136 and 150 in TS for the S0 and 3pi-pi* states; the 3pi-pi* excitation energies rise to 66.6 (E) and 84.6 (TS) kcal/mol and the transfer barriers increase to 24.6 and 42.6 kcal/mol for S0 and 3pi-pi* respectively. Both CIS and CASSCF predict the 1pi-pi* transfer barrier to be smaller than the ground state one, and the order of increasing barrier is essentially the same at both levels, but this order conflicts with the CIS-MP2 treatment of correlation. CASSCF and CIS adiabatic excitation energies are similar for the two pi-pi* states, but CASSCF is 20-30 kcal/mol smaller than CIS for the n-pi* states. Frequencies computed at CIS/6-31+G** gave an imaginary frequency of 512i cm-1 for one 3pi-pi* structure; other imaginary frequencies of 778i cm-1 were found, all corresponding to out-of-plane displacements.
Other: The authors run the active-space test explicitly and report the result as an error bar rather than as a correction. Replacing two of the four virtual pi* orbitals with two sigma* orbitals -- keeping the size at (6,7) -- raises the ground state proton transfer barrier from 23.82 to 24.6 kcal/mol but the 3pi-pi* barrier from 43.32 to 42.6, and shifts the 3pi-pi* excitation energies to 66.6 and 84.6 kcal/mol, and these numbers are presented as an estimate of the uncertainty associated with the choice of active space. The motive is a discrepancy the paper cannot resolve: CASSCF barriers exceed CIS-MP2 ones by as much as 40 kcal/mol, and the authors consider two possible causes -- that their particular choice of orbitals gives an unbalanced account of correlation between the equilibrium and transition state structures, or that orbitals important to the proton transfer are simply missing from the space -- while also noting that CIS-MP2 is not a true MP2 procedure since it is not based on a single configuration. They state plainly that CASSCF results can be very sensitive to the choice of active space orbitals. Crucially, adding dynamic correlation by second-order perturbation theory is known to lower such barriers dramatically, which is exactly what CIS-MP2 does relative to CIS, so the large CASSCF barriers are described as not unexpected. The selection rule used for the occupied orbitals -- a CIS single-excitation coefficient above about 0.3 -- makes the space reproducible but ties it to the quality of the CIS wave function it is meant to improve upon.
reference_short: Rovira & Scheiner, J. Phys. Chem. 1995, 99, 9854
notes: The 1pi-pi* state is clearly the first excited state, but the ordering of the higher states depends on the level of theory. A correlation is noted between hydrogen bond strength and proton transfer barrier: the stronger the H bond, the lower the barrier. The r(NH) internitrogen distance and the a(NNH) angle account for most of the contribution to the eigenvector with negative eigenvalue at the saddle point. The 1pi-pi* equilibrium structure was not fully optimized at the CASSCF level, carrying a total RMS gradient of 0.01.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF energies; CIS-MP2 (second-order Moller-Plesset correction to the CIS energies) computed separately, with core electrons of C and N excluded from the correlation correction

compound_name: [FeCp*2]+ ... [TCNE]- radical pairs in the organic-based ferromagnet decamethylferrocenium tetracyanoethenide
ligand_set: two pentamethylcyclopentadienyl ligands on the iron cation, paired with a tetracyanoethenide radical anion
geometry_source: The crystal geometry of each A-B radical pair, taken from the refined structures of the temperature-dependent polymorphs; no optimization.
method: CASSCF with MCQDPT second-order perturbative correction (a multireference perturbation approach similar to CASPT2 but using a different zeroth-order Hamiltonian); spin-orbit coupling added afterwards by computing and diagonalizing the matrix representation of the SOC Hamiltonian using the CASSCF wave function, with one-electron terms only
software: GAMESS-06; Gaussian 03 revision C.02 used elsewhere in the study
basis_set: Ahlrichs TZV on Fe, 6-31G on all Cp ligands, and 6-31+G on the [TCNE]- anions
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals: four Fe 3d orbitals (all but the Fe dz2 orbital, which test calculations with larger active spaces gave an occupation of 1.99 electrons, suggesting it should be moved to the core), the two occupied pi orbitals from each Cp fragment that can interact with the dxz and dyz orbitals of Fe, and the SOMO of the TCNE fragment.
active_space_protocol: Three different active spaces are used for three kinds of radical pair, each sized so that the high- and low-spin states of that pair are properly described and so that the quality is comparable across pairs. That comparability is the design constraint, since the magnetic topology is assembled from J values computed for different pair types. Two of the three choices are justified by explicit tests: the Fe dz2 orbital was excluded from the (8,7) space because test calculations with larger spaces gave it an occupation of 1.99 electrons, so it belongs in the core; and the (2,2) space for the anion-anion pairs was validated against CASSCF(6,6), whose six active orbitals came out at occupations 1.93, 1.93, 1.00, 1.00, 0.07 and 0.07, with both spaces giving the same J of -0.16 cm-1. The largest pairs, cation-cation with about 540 basis functions and no symmetry, could only be run at CASSCF(14,12) with no perturbative correction. All calculations used the crystal geometry of each pair.
nroots_per_mult: Two state-averaged CASSCF calculations, one for each of the two triplets and the two singlets
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF and MCQDPT energies in cm-1 relative to T1, for the T1, T2, S1 and S2 states of each unique pair. Pair 1: CASSCF 0.0, 17.31, 53.34, 71.07; MCQDPT 0.0, 40.15, 90.51, 133.82. Pair 2: CASSCF 0.0, 8.50, 33.84, 39.28; MCQDPT 0.0, 21.34, 55.85, 68.54. Pair 3: CASSCF 0.0, 26.99, 0.17, 27.15; MCQDPT 0.0, 54.52, 0.34, 54.84. Pair 4: CASSCF 0.0, 7.05, -0.02, 7.04; MCQDPT 0.0, 6.46, -0.07, 6.39. Pair 5: CASSCF 0.0, 22.64, 0.0, 22.65; MCQDPT 0.0, 54.47, 0.0, 54.48. Pair 8: CASSCF 0.0, 31.72, -0.02, 31.73; MCQDPT 0.0, 70.05, -0.09, 70.04. Exchange couplings in cm-1 as isotropic JAB(1), JAB(2), then anisotropic JAB-parallel and JAB-perpendicular: pair 1 +45.25, +46.84, +30.6, +1.6; pair 2 +27.93, +23.60, +17.04, +3.78; pair 3 +0.17, +0.16, +0.12, +0.01; pair 4 -0.04, -0.03, -0.03, -0.08; pair 5 0.00, +0.01, 0.00, 0.00; pair 8 -0.05, -0.01, -0.03, -0.02. No single isotropic JAB Hamiltonian fits the whole energy spectrum, so two coupling constants are used, defined as JAB(i) = [ES(i) - ET(i)]/2. Center-to-center distances are 5.209, 5.323, 7.804, 8.278, 8.097 and 7.408 A for pairs 1-5 and 8, with nearest Fe-N distances of 5.582, 5.600, 5.042, 5.311, 5.594 and 5.563 A. The dominant interaction JAB(1) is ferromagnetic with a triplet ground state; the CASSCF(8,7) wave function has three SOMOs with occupations 1.5, 1.5 and 1.0, the two at 1.5 being nonbonding Fe dxy and dx2-y2 orbitals and the one at 1.0 a bonding combination, with all other orbitals close to 2.0 or 0.0. Interchain interaction 3 is also ferromagnetic, coupling the chains into (101) sheets, while interactions 4, 6 and 8 between the sheets are antiferromagnetic. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling does not affect the order of magnitude of the interactions, their relative strength, or their strong anisotropy. All JAB interactions were computed with an expected error smaller than +/- 0.01 cm-1.
Other: The Fe dz2 orbital was removed from the space on the strength of an occupation number: test calculations with larger active spaces gave it 1.99 electrons, so it was demoted to the core, yielding (8,7) rather than a larger space that would have carried a doubly occupied passenger. The resulting wave function has exactly three partly occupied orbitals -- 1.5, 1.5 and 1.0 -- with everything else at 2.0 or 0.0, which is the internal confirmation that the space is neither too small nor padded. The perturbative correction matters enormously for the energies but much less for the couplings: MCQDPT roughly doubles most of the excitation energies relative to CASSCF (pair 1 goes from 17.31, 53.34, 71.07 to 40.15, 90.51, 133.82 cm-1) yet the sign and relative ordering of every JAB survive, which is what the magnetic topology actually depends on. A structural limitation is stated rather than solved: the CASSCF energies alone do not fit a single isotropic Hamiltonian, so two coupling constants per pair are needed, and the spin-orbit correction is applied after the fact using only one-electron terms, on the grounds that including two-electron terms by modifying nuclear charges does not change the exchange couplings. Note the space differs from those used for the other pair types in the same study -- (14,12) for cation-cation and (2,2) for anion-anion -- so cross-pair comparability rests on each space being separately validated rather than on uniformity.

notes: There are two nearly degenerate singlets and two equally nearly degenerate triplets, giving rise to two nearly similar JAB values; only the smallest is reported in some places. Sixteen states arise when spin-orbit coupling is included.

electronic_structure_description: Only one triplet and one open-shell singlet state exist for these pairs, and spin-orbit corrections are not required because no Fe atom is present. Only pair 6 has nonnegligible energies: CASSCF(2,2) gives 0.00 and -0.16 cm-1 for the T and S states, in good agreement with the CASSCF(2,2)/MCQDPT values of 0.00 and -0.30 cm-1. CASSCF(6,6) on one of the dimer triplets returns occupations of 1.93, 1.93, 1.00, 1.00, 0.07 and 0.07 -- two orbitals essentially doubly occupied, two essentially empty, and exactly two singly occupied -- from which the authors conclude that a (2,2) space must give the same answer, and then confirm it by computing JAB at both levels and obtaining -0.16 cm-1 either way. software: GAMESS-06; Gaussian 03 revision C.02 used elsewhere in the study
basis_set: Ahlrichs TZV on Fe, 6-31G on all Cp ligands, and 6-31+G on the [TCNE]- anions
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve orbitals. Because of their size, about 540 basis functions, and their lack of symmetry, these pairs were computed by CASSCF(14,12) only, with no MCQDPT correction.
active_space_protocol: Three different active spaces are used for three kinds of radical pair, each sized so that the high- and low-spin states of that pair are properly described and so that the quality is comparable across pairs. That comparability is the design constraint, since the magnetic topology is assembled from J values computed for different pair types. Two of the three choices are justified by explicit tests: the Fe dz2 orbital was excluded from the (8,7) space because test calculations with larger spaces gave it an occupation of 1.99 electrons, so it belongs in the core; and the (2,2) space for the anion-anion pairs was validated against CASSCF(6,6), whose six active orbitals came out at occupations 1.93, 1.93, 1.00, 1.00, 0.07 and 0.07, with both spaces giving the same J of -0.16 cm-1. The largest pairs, cation-cation with about 540 basis functions and no symmetry, could only be run at CASSCF(14,12) with no perturbative correction. All calculations used the crystal geometry of each pair.
nroots_per_mult: Four open-shell singlet and four triplet states, becoming 16 states when spin-orbit coupling is included
electronic_structure_description: Four open-shell singlet and four triplet states arise for each pair, becoming 16 states with spin-orbit coupling included. In these triplets all of the singly occupied molecular orbitals are degenerate, so to a first approximation all four triplets are expected to be degenerate. At the CASSCF(14,12) level all of these states are nearly degenerate for all unique cation-cation pairs, so their isotropic JAB is negligible at about 0.00 cm-1. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling does not lift the degeneracy, so the computed anisotropic JAB-parallel and JAB-perpendicular values are also negligible. There are also eight closed-shell singlet states obtained by placing two electrons on the half-filled orbitals, not considered because their energy is much higher, being ionic states. The one unique pair listed, pair 7, has a center-to-center distance of 8.205 A with a nearest C-C contact of 3.946 A.
Other: This is the pair type where the space was set by what was affordable rather than by what the chemistry demanded: about 540 basis functions and no symmetry meant CASSCF(14,12) with no MCQDPT correction at all, unlike every other pair type in the study. The result is defensible only because it is a null: all four triplets and their singlet partners come out nearly degenerate, so JAB is about 0.00 cm-1 and spin-orbit coupling does not lift the degeneracy either. A degeneracy is far more robust to missing dynamic correlation than a small splitting would be -- had these states been split by a few wavenumbers, the absence of the perturbative correction that doubles the cation-anion splittings elsewhere in the same paper would have left the sign unreliable. Eight closed-shell singlet states were excluded on energetic grounds as ionic states lying much higher, so the (14,12) space is used only for the neutral-type manifold.
reference_short: Her, Stephens, Ribas-Arino, Novoa, Shum & Miller, Inorg. Chem. 2009, 48, 3296
notes: The total magnetic topology results from the various cation-anion, anion-anion and cation-cation pairs. The structural network has a three-dimensional topology, but interactions within a single chain are much stronger than those between chains.
correlation_correction: MCQDPT second-order multireference perturbation theory on the CASSCF wave functions; not applied to the cation-cation pairs

point_group: C2v for the ground state minimum and the Franck-Condon S1 stationary point; C2 for the twisted S1 minimum
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations for ground- and excited-state intermediates, transition states, singlet/singlet and triplet/triplet conical intersections and singlet/triplet crossing points, using the MCSCF program in Gaussian98 with a 6-31G* basis. Crossing points were optimized with the state-averaged CASSCF method. Frequency calculations were performed for all stationary points to obtain zero-point energies and to verify their nature. The ground state minimum M1-S0 has N-N and C-N bond lengths of 1.263 and 1.527 A. Three ground-state minima M2-S0, M3-S0 and M4-S0 were optimized at the CASSCF(4,4) level.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF: CASSCF geometry optimizations with single-point CASPT2 for dynamic correlation, plus spin-orbit coupling constants from the full Breit-Pauli spin-orbit operator
software: Gaussian98 revision A.9 for the CASSCF optimizations; MOLPRO2000 for the CASPT2 and spin-orbit coupling calculations
basis_set: 6-31G* throughout, with single-point CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations also performed with the larger polarized triple-zeta 6-311G* basis at all stationary and crossing points to check basis set dependence
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in ten orbitals: both pairs of C-N sigma and sigma* orbitals, needed to describe cleavage of the two C-N bonds, and six orbitals from the N2 fragment (pi, pi*, two n orbitals, sigma and sigma*). The N2 sigma and sigma* orbitals are included because the N-N bond length varies significantly during deazotation. In regions of the surface near the diazenyl diradicals the lone pair orbital of the nitrogen atom of the broken C-N bond is nearly doubly occupied in all states studied, so it was deleted to give a (10,9) space there. Three ground-state minima were optimized with a CASSCF(4,4) space.
active_space_protocol: The space is built from the bonds that break and the fragment that leaves: both C-N sigma/sigma* pairs for the two bonds cleaved, plus the full N2 valence set including sigma and sigma* because the N-N distance changes substantially along the deazotation coordinate. The space is then deliberately shrunk in part of the coordinate space, not enlarged: near the diazenyl diradicals the nitrogen lone pair of the broken C-N bond becomes nearly doubly occupied in every state, and the authors note that including orbitals with occupancies near 2 or 0 dramatically deteriorates CASSCF convergence, so that orbital is dropped to give (10,9). They acknowledge the resulting inconsistency directly -- comparing CASSCF energies across regions computed with different spaces introduces small errors -- but argue that after the perturbative corrections are added the two spaces give energies that can be compared directly. A level shift was used in all CASPT2 calculations to avoid intruder states.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged CASSCF for the crossing point optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol as CASSCF/6-31G*, CASPT2/6-31G* and CASPT2/6-311G*, with ZPE-corrected values in parentheses. At M1-S0: T1 (n-pi*) 78.5, 59.0, 57.9; T2 (pi-pi*) 124.5, 114.6, 113.7; S1 (n-pi*) 96.1, 76.7, 75.2. TS1-S1 94.9, 76.1 (74.0), 74.8 (72.7). M-S1 93.9, 73.8 (72.3), 72.2 (70.7). M-T1 66.2, 51.3 (50.0), 50.5 (49.2). TS1-T1 75.5, 56.2 (54.7), 55.2 (53.7). TS-T2 86.5, 80.3 (78.0), 80.8 (78.5). ISC-T2/S1: T2 100.7, 91.7, 91.4 and S1 100.7, 81.1, 80.2. IC-T2/T1: T2 92.2, 83.0, 83.2 and T1 92.2, 72.5, 72.0. TS2-S1 99.0, 86.0 (83.2), 84.6 (81.8). TS2-T1 72.7, 62.2 (59.0), 60.8 (57.6). The four-surface crossing X-T3/T1/S1/S0 has S0 at 76.6, 76.6, 75.1 with S1, T1 and T2 all within 1 kcal/mol of it. IC-T3/T1: T1 96.9, 81.5, 79.9 and T2 (n-sigma*) 96.9, 90.7, 88.9. ISC-T3/S1: S1 107.7, 91.5, 89.7 and T2 107.7, 99.6, 97.5. Ground state minima M2, M3 and M4 lie at 41.0/49.1/46.4, 40.0/48.4/45.6 and 41.1/49.2/46.4. On direct photolysis at 366 nm (78.1 kcal/mol) and triplet-sensitized photolysis at 313 nm (91.3 kcal/mol) only the T1 and S1 states are accessible. The Franck-Condon S1 stationary point of C2v symmetry with r(N-N) = 1.286 A is a transition state whose imaginary mode is twisting of the C-N=N-C bridge; following it gives a C2 minimum 2.3 kcal/mol lower with a C-N=N-C dihedral of 29.4 degrees, so the C2v transition state links the minimum and its enantiomer. Calculated 0-0 transitions are 73.8 and 51.3 kcal/mol against experimental values of 76.4 and 51.9 +/- 0.6 kcal/mol. A calculated value of 11.1 kcal/mol accounts well for the roughly 10 kcal/mol half-width of the emission band. At TS1-T1 the pi-pi* state lies 55.1 kcal/mol above the n-pi* state, whereas at TS-T2 it lies 12.9 kcal/mol below it.
Other: The interesting decision here is a deliberate reduction of the space in part of the surface. Near the diazenyl diradicals the nitrogen lone pair of the broken C-N bond becomes nearly doubly occupied in every state considered, and since orbitals with occupancies near 2 or 0 dramatically deteriorate CASSCF convergence, it is removed, giving (10,9) in that region against (12,10) elsewhere. The authors state plainly that this makes CASSCF energies from different regions not directly comparable, and rely on the perturbative correction to restore comparability -- an assumption the tables let you inspect, since CASPT2 moves individual points by as much as 19 kcal/mol (S1 at the Franck-Condon geometry falls from 96.1 to 76.7) and by very different amounts for different states (T2 drops only 9.9 kcal/mol while T1 drops 19.5). Three ground-state minima were optimized at a still smaller (4,4) space, giving a third level in the same energy table. Against this, the basis set dependence is genuinely small, under 3.0 kcal/mol between 6-31G* and 6-311G*, so the basis is not the limiting factor. The independent validation is spectroscopic: the CASPT2 0-0 transitions of 73.8 and 51.3 kcal/mol match the measured 76.4 and 51.9 +/- 0.6 kcal/mol, and the computed 11.1 kcal/mol reorganization matches the roughly 10 kcal/mol emission half-width. The active space design itself is dictated by the coordinate: both C-N sigma/sigma* pairs because two bonds break, and the N2 sigma/sigma* pair because the N-N distance changes markedly as N2 departs.
reference_short: Chen & Li, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 13190
notes: Conical intersections are treated as the main locus of internal conversion and singlet/triplet crossings as the main locus of intersystem crossing. The study addresses the origin of the extremely long-lived fluorescence from the lowest excited singlet state of DBO and the rapid radiationless decay of its triplet state. For DBH, which is slightly more rigid than DBO, a twisted C-N=N-C minimum exists only on T1 and not on S1. On twisting the bridge, the n and pi orbitals of the N-N moiety slightly mix in the S1 state.
correlation_correction: Single-point CASPT2 with the same basis set and active space at the CASSCF-optimized geometries, using a level shift to avoid intruder states

compound_name: Dysprosium(III) in the Dy(hfac)3(NITC6H4-OEt)2 molecular chain compound, local magnetic anisotropy in a low-symmetry environment
ligand_set: three hexafluoroacetylacetonate (hfac-) ligands and two nitronyl nitroxide radicals (NITC6H4-OEt); in the computational model the fluorides of hfac- were replaced by H atoms and the NITC6H4-OEt radicals by NIT-CH3, with H atoms added to the external oxygen atoms of the radicals to make them closed-shell
geometry_source: A simplified molecular model built from the experimental structure to reduce computational time: the fluorides in the hfac- ligands replaced by H atoms, the NITC6H4-OEt radicals replaced by NIT-CH3, and H atoms added to the external oxygen atoms of the radicals to transform them into closed-shell molecules. The justification given is that, in view of the internal nature of the 4f orbitals, those orbitals should be the most sensitive to ionic interactions.
method: CASSCF with RASSI-SO state interaction for the spin-orbit splitting, compared with single-crystal angular-resolved magnetic susceptibility measurements
basis_set: Atomic natural orbitals from the ANO-RCC library with contractions [8s7p4d3f2g] for Dy, [3s2p] for O, C and N, and [2s] for H
relativistic_treatment: ANO-RCC relativistic basis sets; spin-orbit coupling introduced through the RASSI-SO state interaction
active_space_orbital_description: The Dy 4f orbitals, containing nine electrons in seven orbitals, CASSCF(9,7).
active_space_protocol: The space is the minimal 4f manifold, and the design effort goes into the ligand model and the root selection rather than the orbitals. The ligands are chemically simplified -- fluorines to hydrogens, the aryl radicals to NIT-CH3, and the radicals capped to closed shell -- explicitly so that the CASSCF active space can stay small, with the argument that the internal 4f orbitals respond mainly to the ionic environment. State averaging was pushed as far as hardware allowed: all 21 sextet roots, all 224 quadruplet roots, and 200 of the 490 doublet roots. Four separate RASSI state interactions were then compared to test how much the higher multiplets matter: A included everything within 40000 cm-1 of the 6H15/2 multiplet (the 6H, 6F and 6P sextets, 108 quadruplets and 32 doublets); B only the three sextets; C only the 6H multiplet; and D used only the 11 roots of the 6H multiplet in the CASSCF state average itself as well as in the RASSI-SO step.
nroots_per_mult: All 21 sextets, all 224 quadruplets, and 200 of 490 doublets in the CASSCF state average; four different RASSI subsets labelled A to D
electronic_structure_description: The 6H15/2 ground electronic state of Dy(III) has gJ = 4/3, and the crystal field interaction removes the (2J+1) degeneracy to give eight Kramers doublets. The energy pattern of the split 6H15/2 levels is basically the same in RASSI calculations A, B and C, indicating a small mixture of the 6H multiplet with the others through spin-orbit coupling, which is why calculation D restricting the CASSCF state average itself to the 11 roots of 6H was performed. The calculations indicate a strong Ising-type magnetic anisotropy at low temperature. In the Ising limit the ground doublet is reasonably approximated by mJ = +/- 15/2 with the first excited doublet about 60 K higher, so low-temperature data can be interpreted with only the ground Kramers doublet, treated with Seff = 1/2, gz-effective = 2 x (15/2) x gJ = 20 and gx,y-effective = 0; these values agree well with the computed column D results. The angle between the ab initio computed magnetization easy axis and the experimentally determined one is only 7 degrees. The magnetization plateau value of 9.9 Bohr magnetons is very close to the expected 10. Magnetic simulations used JNN = -13.7 cm-1, JNNN = 15 cm-1 and gDy of either 19.7 or 18.4.
Other: The systematic test here is on which spin-orbit states are allowed to interact, not on the orbital space, which is fixed at the minimal 4f manifold. Four RASSI variants were run: everything within 40000 cm-1 of the ground multiplet, then the three sextets only, then the 6H multiplet only, then a version where even the CASSCF state average was restricted to the 11 roots of 6H. The energy pattern of the split ground multiplet comes out basically the same in all of them, which is the finding -- spin-orbit mixing of 6H with the higher multiplets is small, so the expensive averaging over 224 quadruplets and 200 doublets buys little for this property. That justifies the cheapest treatment, and the resulting easy axis lands within 7 degrees of the experimentally determined one. Two constraints on the result are worth recording. The doublet averaging was already incomplete for hardware reasons, 200 of 490 roots, so variant A is not the converged limit it might appear. And the ligand model is chemically altered rather than merely truncated -- fluorines replaced by hydrogens and the nitronyl nitroxide radicals capped to closed-shell species -- which changes the charge distribution around a lanthanide whose anisotropy is set by exactly that electrostatic environment; the defence offered is that the 4f orbitals are internal and respond to ionic interactions, not that the model is faithful.
reference_short: Bernot, Luzon, Bogani, Etienne, Sangregorio, Shanmugam, Caneschi, Sessoli & Gatteschi, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2009, 131, 5573
notes: The numerical body of Table 1, giving the computed energies of the split 6H15/2 levels and the principal g values of the ground Kramers doublet for calculations A to D, was not recoverable from the text extraction; only the qualitative statement that the four calculations give basically the same energy pattern is transcribed here. Single-crystal susceptibility was measured by rotation around the a axis with theta = 0 and 90 degrees corresponding to b' and c*.
correlation_correction: None; spin-orbit coupling treated by RASSI-SO state interaction on the CASSCF states

compound_name: Benzene, the prefulvene extended conical intersection seam
point_group: Critical points on the seam belong to Cs, C2, C2v, C2h and D3d point groups
geometry_source: Conical intersection critical points located and characterized at the CAS(6,6)/cc-pVDZ level, with characterization done by computing intersection space frequencies. Branching space vectors were computed at the CASSCF level for all critical points on the seam.
method: CASSCF for locating and characterizing the conical intersection critical points, with valence bond analysis of the electronic states carried out numerically by the MMVB method
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, the six pi orbitals of benzene.
active_space_protocol: The space is the canonical six-pi-electron set of benzene, the minimum that can carry the covalent valence bond structures whose crossings define the seam. That choice is what makes the valence bond mapping possible: the same six orbitals underlie both the CASSCF wave function and the VB spin-exchange density, so the numerical MMVB results can be compared directly with the ab initio branching space vectors. Ionic configurations are noted to play no role in the seam, which is why a purely covalent VB description of the same six orbitals suffices. Critical points are characterized by intersection space frequencies rather than ordinary Hessians, since the objects being characterized are intersections rather than minima.
electronic_structure_description: The permutational isomers of the prefulvene-like minimum energy conical intersection lie on an extended seam and are connected by higher symmetry structures. The prefulvene-like CI-Cs structure is the lowest minimum energy conical intersection; it lies very close to an S1 transition state arising from an avoided crossing of the anti-Kekule state A-B and an antiquinoid structure C-E of A'' symmetry in Cs, which can couple because they belong to the same irreducible representation. The intersection considered is between state I = A+B and state II = A-B+C-E, where state II has a benzvalene-like noncanonical valence bond structure. The valence bond argument predicts that the saddle point connecting two prefulvene isomers whose prow is rotated by 60 degrees must have a benzvalene-like geometry with VB function A+D, and CASSCF confirms a conical intersection CI-C2 of C2 symmetry lying 0.75 eV above CI-Cs, with two imaginary intersection space frequencies that interconvert two permutational isomers of CI-Cs; CI-C2 both rotates the prow by 60 degrees and inverts it with respect to the ring plane. The 180 degree isomers can be connected by a C2v intersection, where the two outward-bent carbon atoms point in the same direction, or by a C2h one where the 180 degree rotation occurs together with inversion of the prow. A conical intersection of D3d symmetry, 4.2 eV above CI-Cs, connects three equivalent structures of CI-C2h. Analysis of the computed spin-exchange densities shows that CI-C2v involves an intersection between A-B and a state dominated by D with a small admixture of A+B, the predominance of D being understandable because the antiquinoid structure is stabilized by the 1,4 interaction between the two out-of-plane carbon atoms, whereas CI-C2h involves only the Kekule state A+B and the anti-Kekule state. Branching space vectors from the valence bond model are in good agreement with the CASSCF-computed vectors.
Other: The six-orbital pi space is doing something unusual here: it is being used as a bridge between two descriptions rather than as an approximation to be converged. Because the CASSCF wave function and the valence bond spin-exchange density span the same six benzene pi orbitals, the VB bonding patterns can be read directly out of the ab initio result, and the branching space vectors predicted by the VB model come out in good agreement with the CASSCF ones -- which is the paper's validation that the VB picture is faithful rather than merely suggestive. That validation then pays off predictively: the VB argument says the saddle point interconverting two prefulvene isomers must have a benzvalene-like A+D structure, and a CASSCF search confirms a C2 conical intersection 0.75 eV above the minimum with the required two imaginary intersection space frequencies, a geometry the authors describe as rather counterintuitive and which they credit to the heuristic value of the VB reasoning. The space is legitimate at this size precisely because ionic configurations play no role in this seam, so nothing outside the covalent six-electron manifold is needed. Note that critical points are characterized by intersection space frequencies rather than conventional Hessians, and that structures higher on the seam reach 4.2 eV above the lowest intersection, so the seam spans an energy range over which a fixed pi-only space is being asked to remain balanced.
reference_short: Blancafort & Robb, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2012, 8, 4922
notes: The valence bond method has been shown to work here because ionic valence bond functions play no role in the conical intersection seam of benzene. The computational details for locating and characterizing the conical intersection critical points are given in the authors' preceding study; the C2v and C2h intersections were described there, while the D3d intersection is new to this work and appears in the Supporting Information.
correlation_correction: None applied beyond the CASSCF level

geometry_source: Geometry optimizations at both CASSCF(10,10) and RASSCF(2) under D2h symmetry, with the optimized geometries confirmed as minimum energy points by vibrational frequency analysis using numerical RASSCF derivatives.
method: RASSCF with the configuration expansion truncated at two electron excitations (RASSCF(2)) or four (RASSCF(4)), and full CASSCF where affordable, all within a complete pi orbital space
active_space_orbital_description: All 10 pi electrons active, distributed over 5 bonding pi and 5 antibonding pi* orbitals, giving a nominal (10,10) complete pi space with the configuration expansion truncated by excitation level. The paper states the rule as n pi electrons in n/2 bonding and n/2 antibonding pi orbitals for a system of n carbon atoms and writes it as the Gaussian keyword CASSCF(n, n, RASSCF(0,0,2,n/2)); for this molecule the paper writes the spaces explicitly as CASSCF(10,10) and CASSCF(10,10,RASSCF(0,0,2,5)).
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by a rule applied uniformly across the whole series: for a system with n carbon atoms, all n pi electrons are active, distributed over n/2 bonding pi and n/2 antibonding pi* orbitals, giving a nominal (n,n) complete space. Because that space is intractable for the larger members, the CI expansion rather than the orbital set is truncated -- the configuration state functions are restricted to at most two electron excitations from the reference determinant, entered as the Gaussian keyword CASSCF(n, n, RASSCF(0,0,2,n/2)) and called RASSCF(2) here; a four-excitation variant, RASSCF(4), was also run for anthracene and phenanthrene. This separates the two questions that a smaller CAS would conflate: the orbital space is complete for the pi system in every case, and only the excitation level varies. Geometries were optimized and numerical RASSCF vibrational frequencies computed at each level.
electronic_structure_description: Both the CASSCF and RASSCF(2) optimized geometries under D2h are minima. Calculated bond lengths at both levels are in good agreement with experiment, and the calculated infrared spectra by RASSCF(2) are similar to those by CASSCF, with the CASSCF spectra in good agreement with experiment when the vibrational frequencies are scaled by 0.9. Wave function diagnostics from Table 3, giving the coefficient of the main configuration C0, the HONO and LUNO occupation numbers, and the unpaired electron measures N(T) and N(H): naphthalene CASSCF 0.90, 1.87, 0.14, 1.57, 0.82 and RASSCF(2) 0.93, 1.92, 0.09, 1.03, 0.53; anthracene RASSCF(2) 0.92, 1.92, 0.08, 1.15, 0.59, RASSCF(4) 0.87, 1.85, 0.16, 2.08, 1.09 and CASSCF(cc) 0.86, 1.84, 0.17, 2.25, 1.19; naphtacene RASSCF(2) 0.90, 1.92, 0.09, 1.46, 0.75; pentacene RASSCF(2) 0.89, 1.92, 0.08, 1.62, 0.83; perylene RASSCF(2) 0.94, 1.95, 0.05, 0.96, 0.49; phenanthrene RASSCF(4) 0.90, 1.88, 0.12, 1.99, 1.04; picene RASSCF(2) 0.90, 1.94, 0.06, 1.53, 0.78.
Other: Because the orbital space is held complete for the pi system and only the excitation level is truncated, this study isolates the effect of CI truncation cleanly -- and for anthracene it is decisive. The energy difference between the D2h and Cs optimized geometries is 0.3 kcal/mol at RASSCF(2), 16.8 kcal/mol at RASSCF(4) and 26.5 kcal/mol at full CASSCF: two excitations barely register the symmetry breaking that four excitations and the complete expansion make substantial. The wave function diagnostics move in step, with the leading coefficient falling from 0.93 to 0.87 to 0.86, the HONO occupation from 1.92 to 1.85 to 1.84, and the unpaired electron measure N(T) rising from 1.15 to 2.08 to 2.25 -- so the two-excitation treatment systematically understates the polyradical character that drives the distortion. The direction is consistent, RASSCF(2) always the most closed-shell and full CASSCF the least, with RASSCF(4) close to CASSCF; that convergence pattern is what licenses using RASSCF(2) for the larger members where CASSCF is impossible. Against this, the properties the paper actually reports are insensitive: bond lengths and infrared spectra from RASSCF(2), RASSCF(4) and CASSCF all agree well with experiment, and the RASSCF(2) infrared spectra are described as similar to the RASSCF(4) ones. The practical lesson is that the truncation level matters for relative energies between competing symmetries and for unpaired-electron descriptors, while structures and vibrational spectra survive it.
reference_short: Aiga, J. Phys. Chem. A 2012, 116, 663
notes: Naphthalene is the one molecule for which both full CASSCF and RASSCF were performed with vibrational frequency analysis, serving as the calibration case for the series.

point_group: Cs at the minimum; D2h stationary point has two imaginary frequencies
geometry_source: Geometry optimizations at RASSCF(2), RASSCF(4) and CASSCF under D2h symmetry, all of which gave two imaginary frequencies, followed by reoptimization under Cs symmetry which gave minimum energy points at every level. The CASSCF geometry optimization was performed without vibrational frequency analysis.
method: RASSCF with the configuration expansion truncated at two electron excitations (RASSCF(2)) or four (RASSCF(4)), and full CASSCF where affordable, all within a complete pi orbital space
active_space_orbital_description: All 14 pi electrons active, distributed over 7 bonding pi and 7 antibonding pi* orbitals, giving a nominal (14,14) complete pi space with the configuration expansion truncated by excitation level. The paper states the rule as n pi electrons in n/2 bonding and n/2 antibonding pi orbitals for a system of n carbon atoms and writes it as the Gaussian keyword CASSCF(n, n, RASSCF(0,0,2,n/2)); The electron and orbital counts here follow arithmetically from the rule stated in the paper together with the carbon count of this molecule; they are not printed as a numeral in the text except for naphthalene.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by a rule applied uniformly across the whole series: for a system with n carbon atoms, all n pi electrons are active, distributed over n/2 bonding pi and n/2 antibonding pi* orbitals, giving a nominal (n,n) complete space. Because that space is intractable for the larger members, the CI expansion rather than the orbital set is truncated -- the configuration state functions are restricted to at most two electron excitations from the reference determinant, entered as the Gaussian keyword CASSCF(n, n, RASSCF(0,0,2,n/2)) and called RASSCF(2) here; a four-excitation variant, RASSCF(4), was also run for anthracene and phenanthrene. This separates the two questions that a smaller CAS would conflate: the orbital space is complete for the pi system in every case, and only the excitation level varies. Geometries were optimized and numerical RASSCF vibrational frequencies computed at each level.
electronic_structure_description: Under D2h symmetry two imaginary frequencies were found at every level; under Cs symmetry the optimized geometries are minima. Calculated energies in hartree at the D2h and Cs geometries with the energy difference in kcal/mol: RASSCF(2) -536.1245 and -536.1249, difference 0.3; RASSCF(4) -536.1450 and -536.1717, difference 16.8; CASSCF(cc) -536.1706 and -536.2129, difference 26.5. Selected bond lengths in angstroms at RASSCF(2), RASSCF(4), CASSCF(cc) and experiment: a 1.43405, 1.43430, 1.43584, 1.431; j 1.43778, 1.43435, 1.43583, 1.431; b 1.35697, 1.36329, 1.36729, 1.396. compound_name: p-Nitrobenzenediazonium cation and the corresponding diazenyl radical (compound 1, p-NO2)
geometry_source: Geometries of the arenediazonium cations and the corresponding diazenyl radicals optimized by standard gradient methods at the pi-CASSCF/6-31G* level, alongside HF, DFT and MP2 optimizations. Frequency analysis of the optimized HF/6-31G* cation and neutral geometries revealed no negative frequencies; memory considerations precluded completing these at MP2/6-31G*.
method: Full pi-complete active space SCF (pi-CASSCF), compared against UHF, ROHF, MP2, B3LYP and B3PW91 for inner-sphere reorganization energies of the arenediazonium/diazenyl couple
software: PC GAMESS version of the GAMESS (US) package for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 92 and 94 for the HF and DFT calculations
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF; a TZP basis built from Dunning and Huzinaga contractions with a double-zeta core and full triple-zeta valence shell plus one set of Cartesian d polarization functions (exponent 0.80 on nitrogen, 1.1 on hydrogen) for the DFT calculations
active_space_orbital_description: A full pi-complete active space, comprising the entire pi system of the arenediazonium ion. The numbers of active electrons and orbitals are not stated.
active_space_protocol: The space is specified by chemical class rather than by count: the complete pi system, applied uniformly across the substituted series so that reorganization energies can be compared substituent by substituent. That uniformity is the whole point, since the quantity of interest is a trend with donor and acceptor strength. The choice is a compromise the authors state openly -- full valence CASSCF is what they and others found necessary for small molecules like NO and NO2, but it is computationally intractable for these arenediazonium systems, so a simpler model had to be used. compound_name: Retinal protonated Schiff base in bacteriorhodopsin, thermal dark-adaptation isomerization about the 13-14 and 15-N bonds
geometry_source: Retinal conformations taken from molecular dynamics trajectories of the protein, with methyl groups removed for the ab initio calculations. In situ isomerization was modelled along a predefined reaction coordinate: retinal was gradually rotated about the 13-14 and 15-N bonds simultaneously in bicycle pedal fashion, in steps of 5 degrees with those dihedrals constrained, while all remaining retinal degrees of freedom were relaxed on the empirical potential. The protein environment was represented by explicit point charges in the electronic Hamiltonian using the CHARGE statement in Gaussian.
method: CASSCF(8,8) single-point calculations on conformations from classical molecular dynamics, with the protein entering as point charges
basis_set: 6-31G; sample calculations with the doubly polarized 6-31G** basis were performed on a smaller retinal analogue
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals: the four highest occupied and four lowest unoccupied orbitals of retinal displaying strong pi character. Molecular orbitals from an unrestricted Hartree-Fock SCF calculation were used as the initial guess for the CASSCF.
active_space_protocol: The space is selected by energetic ordering plus a character filter -- the four HOMOs and four LUMOs that show strong pi character -- rather than by identifying particular bonds, which keeps the selection automatic across the thousands of geometries sampled from the molecular dynamics trajectory. That automation is the constraint: the same recipe has to work at every point along a bicycle-pedal rotation in 5 degree steps and at every snapshot of a fluctuating protein, so a hand-picked space is not an option. The basis set was tested rather than assumed: sample calculations on a smaller retinal analogue with 6-31G** showed that rotation barriers about the double bonds of protonated Schiff bases essentially do not change on going beyond 6-31G at the CASSCF(8,8) level. A convergence criterion of 1e-4 hartree was used throughout.
electronic_structure_description: Isomerization barrier heights fluctuate significantly with the instantaneous protein and retinal geometry, ranging from 20 to 70 kcal/mol with the majority of points between 30 and 60 kcal/mol. The average barrier is 51 kcal/mol for the deprotonated state of Asp-85 and 43 kcal/mol for the protonated state. The difference between in situ and in vacuo barriers varies in sign and magnitude and rarely exceeds 10 kcal/mol, so the barrier height is controlled mainly by the internal geometry of retinal. Dihedral energy fluctuations amount to about 6 kcal/mol, with average dihedral energies of 19 kcal/mol for deprotonated and 16 kcal/mol for protonated Asp-85; the lower average dihedral energy for the deprotonated state correlates with its lower average isomerization barrier. One sampled surface shows an isomerization barrier 18 kcal/mol lower than another because of the different environments generated by the two protonation states. Coulomb interactions increase the barrier by 9 kcal/mol in the deprotonated case and lower it by 10 kcal/mol in the protonated case, changing it by about 10 kcal/mol either way; the exchange-correlation-like contribution has a negligible effect.
Other: The active space is chosen so that it can be applied blindly: four highest occupied and four lowest unoccupied orbitals filtered on strong pi character, which is a rule a program can follow at every one of thousands of molecular dynamics snapshots and every 5 degree step of a constrained bicycle-pedal rotation. Nothing about the space is tuned to a particular geometry, which is what makes the barrier distribution meaningful as a distribution. The paper does test the other axis: 6-31G** calculations on a smaller retinal analogue show that rotation barriers about protonated Schiff base double bonds essentially do not change beyond 6-31G at CASSCF(8,8), so the basis is not the limiting approximation. What the paper flags as the real limitation is the absence of dynamic correlation, naming multireference perturbation methods such as CASPT2 as the promising alternative -- which matters because the computed barriers of 43-51 kcal/mol are far above what a thermal process on the observed timescale would require. The internal consistency check that does work is the environmental one: in situ and in vacuo barriers differ by at most about 10 kcal/mol and vary in sign, so the eight-orbital pi description of the isolated chromophore, not the point-charge protein field, is what sets the barrier.
reference_short: Logunov & Schulten, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1996, 118, 9727
notes: Charges were derived using the Breneman-Wiberg, Singh-Kollman and Besler-Merz-Kollman schemes. The study addresses how the protonation state of Asp-85 controls the rate of thermal dark adaptation. The authors list the accuracy of the ab initio level, the treatment of the protein environment, the procedure for computing barriers, and the limited statistics as the factors limiting the overall rate estimate.
correlation_correction: None; the paper identifies multireference perturbation methods such as CASPT2 as a promising alternative but does not apply them

compound_name: 4-cis-Nona-2,4,6,8-tetraeniminium cation (model 1), unlocked model of the PSB11 retinal chromophore
geometry_source: Fully unconstrained structure optimization and relaxation path mapping. Relaxation paths computed as minimum energy paths in mass-weighted coordinates using the initial relaxation direction (IRD) methodology. Ground state energy minima and transition structures optimized with a single-root CASSCF wave function; first excited state minima and transition structures optimized with a two-root (S0, S1) state-averaged CASSCF wave function with equal weights of 0.5 and 0.5. The S1 and S0 surfaces were connected through optimized conical intersections.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF: reaction coordinates computed at the CASSCF level with the energy profiles re-evaluated by multiconfigurational second-order perturbation theory
software: GAUSSIAN98 for all geometry optimizations; MOLCAS-5 for the CASPT2 calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals, comprising the full pi system of the chromophore model.
active_space_protocol: The full pi system is taken as the active space for every model, so that the seven- and eight-membered ring locks change the geometry and strain of the chromophore without changing the composition of the space. Ground-state stationary points use a single-root CASSCF; excited-state stationary points use a two-root state average over S0 and S1 with equal weights, which is necessary in the region of the conical intersections that terminate the paths. Dynamic correlation enters only as a CASPT2 re-evaluation on the CASSCF coordinate.
nroots_per_mult: Single root for ground-state optimizations; two roots (S0, S1) state-averaged with weights 0.5 and 0.5 for excited-state optimizations
electronic_structure_description: The unlocked model admits a single planar conformer. Its S1 energy surface has a two-mode structure: the coordinate is asymmetric and dominated by a cis-trans isomerization motion initiated after depopulation of a very flat planar energy minimum (SP), and evolution along that mode leads to a conical intersection funnel where the chromophore has a roughly 90 degree twisted central double bond and fully efficient decay to the ground state occurs. Initial relaxation out of the Franck-Condon region is characterized by stretching alone. The path connects two degenerate S1 to S0 decay channels entered by clockwise and counterclockwise torsional deformation.
Other: A single (10,10) full-pi space is applied to all three chromophore models -- unlocked, seven-membered-ring locked and eight-membered-ring locked -- which is what makes the comparison the paper rests on legitimate: the differences between the S1 surfaces have to come from ring strain rather than from differing orbital descriptions. Because the space is the complete pi system rather than a truncation, adding or removing a saturated alkyl bridge does not change what is in it, so the models are strictly commensurable. The protocol is split by state in a way that matters for a photochemical path: ground-state minima and transition structures use a single-root CASSCF, while excited-state stationary points use a two-root state average with equal weights, because near the conical intersection a state-specific wave function is not usable. The CASPT2//CASSCF strategy is stated as a requirement rather than a refinement -- the reaction coordinate must be built at CASSCF and the profile re-evaluated at CASPT2 -- so the topological features (the flat plateau, the SP metastable minimum, the TSex transition structure separating the two decay funnels) are CASSCF objects whose energies alone are corrected. That is the load-bearing assumption here, since the mechanistic conclusion turns on whether a barrier exists along the S1 path, and a barrier located on an uncorrected surface can survive or vanish under the correction.
reference_short: De Vico, Garavelli, Bernardi & Olivucci, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 2433
notes: Model 1 is the reference unlocked chromophore against which the two ring-locked models are compared. The initial relaxation is pure stretching, unlike the locked model 3.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 re-evaluation of the CASSCF energy profiles

point_group: C2 for the conrotatory and Cs for the disrotatory transition state
geometry_source: Geometries and frequencies of all stationary points determined with analytically calculated energy gradients at the CASSCF/6-31G(d) level.
method: CASSCF with CiLC analysis (CASSCF orbitals Boys-localized, then full CI at the determinant level in the localized basis) to evaluate the index of deviation from aromaticity (IDA); CASPT2N used for one comparison
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: All active spaces corresponding to the valence pi, pi*, sigma and sigma* orbitals relating to each reaction were included, and all configurations in the active spaces were generated. The numbers of active electrons and orbitals are not stated for any individual reaction.
active_space_protocol: The space is specified by a rule applied per reaction: every valence pi, pi*, sigma and sigma* orbital involved in that particular transformation enters the space, with the full configuration list generated. The CASSCF wave function then serves as the starting point for Boys localization to orbitals of highly atomic character, and a full CI at the determinant level in that localized basis generates the electronic structures and relative configuration weights used to compute the aromaticity index; the CI total energy is checked to correspond well with the CASSCF energy.
electronic_structure_description: For the three polyene electrocyclizations the index of deviation from aromaticity orders the symmetry-allowed transition states as butadiene greater than hexatriene greater than octatetraene, matching the order of their CASSCF/6-31G(d) activation barriers of 52.6, 36.8 and 21.4 kcal/mol respectively. In every case the symmetry-allowed transition state is more aromatic (smaller index) than the symmetry-forbidden one. By contrast the NICS values of the same allowed transition states are -12.3, -25.4 and -6.6 to -12.3, which would make hexatriene the most aromatic of the three, so the magnetically derived aromaticity does not reflect the stabilization energy. For butadiene the index of the C2 transition state is less than one half that of the Cs one, corresponding to the reactivity of the symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden reactions. The Cs transition state for the butadiene electrocyclic reaction is not a real transition state, having two negative eigenvalues of the force constant matrix, unlike the corresponding structures for hexatriene and octatetraene. The symmetry-allowed activation barrier is 52.6 kcal/mol, the highest of the three polyenes, and its NICS value is -12.3.
Other: The active space is defined by a reaction-specific rule rather than a fixed count -- all valence pi, pi*, sigma and sigma* orbitals relating to each particular reaction, with all configurations in the space generated -- so the space grows and changes composition from one pericyclic reaction to the next while the selection criterion stays identical. That uniformity of criterion is what allows the derived aromaticity index to be compared across electrocyclizations, cycloadditions and sigmatropic shifts. The space also has a second job here: the CASSCF orbitals are Boys-localized to give orbitals of highly atomic character, and a full CI at the determinant level is then run in that localized basis to extract valence-bond-like configuration weights, with the check that the CI total energy corresponds well to the CASSCF energy. So the space must be large enough to support a meaningful localized-orbital decomposition, not merely to give a converged energy. Where the index and the energetics can be compared directly the agreement is close but not exact: for the [1,5]-sigmatropic carbon shift the retention transition state lies 0.3 kcal/mol above the inversion one at CASSCF but 0.5 kcal/mol below it at CASPT2N, a reversal of ordering under dynamic correlation, while the two differ in index by only 0.02 -- so a 0.8 kcal/mol swing from the perturbative correction is enough to invert a preference that the reference-level index cannot resolve.

notes: Butadiene is the only one of the three polyenes whose disrotatory Cs structure is a second-order saddle point rather than a genuine transition state.

compound_name: Benzoic acid monomer (BAM), wavelength-dependent photodissociation by C-O fission
point_group: Planar structures for the ground state and most excited states
geometry_source: Ground and excited state geometries optimized at the CASSCF level with the ANO-RCC-VDZP basis; the most stable ground state conformer, with OH and C=O trans, was optimized at CAS(14,12)/ANO-RCC-VDZP. Dissociation coordinates in every state were optimized at the CASSCF level with CASPT2 applied afterwards. Harmonic vibrational frequencies were computed at the CASSCF level.
method: CASSCF for optimizations and harmonic vibrational frequencies, with CASPT2 and multistate MS-CASPT2 single points for the energies
basis_set: Relativistic atomic natural orbital basis ANO-RCC contracted to H/2s1p, C/3s2p1d and O/3s2p1d, denoted ANO-RCC-VDZP
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve orbitals: three pi and three pi* orbitals of the phenyl ring, the C=O pi and pi* orbitals, one nonbonding orbital on each oxygen, and the C-O sigma and sigma* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled to cover the chromophore and the bond that breaks: the full ring pi manifold and the carbonyl pi system carry the excitation, both oxygen lone pairs give access to the n-pi* states, and the C-O sigma/sigma* pair is included because that is the bond undergoing fission. Corresponding spaces are built for each dissociation fragment by the same logic so that the potential energy curves connect properly. Previous work on this molecule used a smaller CAS(10,8) with a cc-pVDZ basis.
nroots_per_mult: Vertical energies computed for S1-A'', S2-A', S3-A', T1-A'', T2-A'' and T3-A'
electronic_structure_description: Two stable planar conformers of the ground state exist, differing in the relative positions of OH and C=O; the trans one is more stable. The present CAS(14,12)/ANO-RCC-VDZP ground-state geometry is closer to experiment than both the previous CASSCF geometry and a DFT structure. Vertical transition energies were computed for S1-A'', S2-A', S3-A', T1-A'', T2-A'' and T3-A'' by MS-CASPT2//CASSCF. The CASPT2 adiabatic excitation energy T0 of the second excited state S2 with a 0.25 IPEA shift is 0.17 eV above the only available experimental value. The rotation barrier of the hydroxyl group is very small, less than 3 kcal/mol, which was exploited to save computer time. As OH leaves, the energy separation of two groups of states becomes nearly the same at 0.79 eV, matching a computed first excited state of the C6H5CO radical at 0.80 eV. The S2-A' and T3-A' states dissociate to C6H5CO + OH if the requisite energy is available. The T1 state was ruled out as the dissociating state, and channel 3 rather than channel 2 was identified as the operative dissociation route. Photodissociation is discussed for excitation energies below 266 nm (4.66 eV) and in the 266-295 nm range.
Other: Three separate spaces are used, one per fragment, each built from the same principle -- every orbital whose occupancy changes along the C-O fission coordinate, plus the aromatic pi system that carries the excitation -- so that the parent molecule and its two dissociation products are described consistently. The parent's (14,12) contains the C-O sigma and sigma* pair that actually breaks; the acyl radical's (11,10) replaces those with the singly occupied carbon orbital left behind; the hydroxyl radical's (7,7) is a full valence set plus two secondary orbitals. That last addition matters: a bare valence space on OH would not describe the radical on the same correlation footing as the large aromatic fragment, and the dissociation energies compared across the three spaces are only meaningful if they are. The enlargement over previous work is substantial and measurable -- earlier CAS(10,8)/cc-pVDZ optimizations are superseded here by CAS(14,12)/ANO-RCC-VDZP, and the resulting ground-state geometry is stated to be closer to experiment than both the earlier CASSCF and a DFT structure. The perturbative correction was itself tuned rather than taken on default: test calculations led to an IPEA shift of 0.15 on important geometries instead of the MOLCAS default 0.25, and the remaining error against the one available experimental number is 0.17 eV in the S2 adiabatic excitation energy at the default shift. An imaginary shift of 0.05 was needed for the T2 transition state to remove an intruder state, so the perturbation is not uniformly well behaved across the surface.
reference_short: Fang & Liu, J. Phys. Chem. A 2010, 114, 680
notes: The [He] cores for O and C were frozen in all CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 computations. The small hydroxyl rotation barrier allowed an approximation that saved considerable CPU time.
