compound_name: Formic acid and its one-water complex HCOOH-H2O, solvent effects on photodissociation
geometry_source: Structures of the HCOOH-H2O complexes in the S0, T1 and S1 states optimized with the CAS(10,8) method and the cc-pVTZ basis; harmonic frequencies were examined after convergence to confirm each structure as a true minimum or saddle point. Structures and energies of the complexes in S0 and T1 were also computed at the B3LYP level for comparison. Bulk solvent effects were added by optimizing the complexes in the three lowest states at the CAS(10,8) level within the polarizable continuum model, using a dielectric constant of 78.93 for water and a cavity built from overlapping spheres with united atom radii.
method: CASSCF for geometries and frequencies, with internally contracted MR-CI single-point energies including all single and double excitations; DFT (B3LYP) and PCM used alongside
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the C=O pi and pi* orbitals, the C-O and C-H sigma and sigma* orbitals, and the two oxygen nonbonding orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space was chosen by a documented comparison rather than by construction alone. Earlier work on gas-phase formic acid photodissociation used three spaces -- (18,13) containing all 18 valence electrons of HCOOH, (10,8) and (8,7) -- and found that the CAS(10,8) optimized structural parameters and relative energies for the S0, S1 and T1 states are very close to those from the full-valence CAS(18,13). That result is what licenses using (10,8) here. Its composition is dictated by the chemistry: the carbonyl pi system and both oxygen lone pairs for the n-pi* excitation, and the C-O and C-H sigma/sigma* pairs for the two bond cleavage channels. The same space is used for the free molecule, the explicit one-water complex, and the complex in a continuum, so the hydrogen-bonding and bulk contributions to the solvent shift are separated without any change in the electronic description.
electronic_structure_description: MR-CI single points on the CAS(10,8) optimized structures give an S0 to S1 adiabatic excitation energy of 110.2 kcal/mol for the HCOOH-H2O complex against 107.7 kcal/mol for free HCOOH, an increase of 2.5 kcal/mol on complex formation; adding bulk water through PCM at the CAS(10,8) level increases it by a further 0.5 kcal/mol. The T1 state lies at 105.8 kcal/mol for the free molecule and 108.0 kcal/mol for the one-water complex relative to the S0 zero level. Experimentally the gas-phase S0 to S1 band origin is 37413.4 cm-1 (107.0 kcal/mol), and in aqueous solution the absorption maximum is at 207 nm, blue shifted by 8 nm (0.2 eV) from the gas phase; earlier CAS(2,2)/CASPT2 work on HCOOH-(H2O)n complexes with n = 1 to 5 predicted a blue shift of 0.2 to 0.4 eV. A transition state TS1-H2O(S1) was located for dissociation of the complex, at which the C1-O4 bond is nearly broken, with a barrier computed as 14.4 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) and 14.8 kcal/mol at MR-CI; another quantity is 41.5 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) and 36.5 kcal/mol at MR-CI. For the free molecule no barrier was found above the endothermic character of the H2O + HCO channel. Hydrogen bonding is much weaker in the T1 complex than in the S0 complex; the H5...O6 distance contracts from 1.968 A in the gas-phase S1 complex to 1.824 A in the aqueous S1 complex.
Other: The choice of a (10,8) space rests on a published three-way comparison rather than on judgement: earlier gas-phase work ran (18,13) containing all valence electrons of formic acid, (10,8) and (8,7), and found the (10,8) geometries and S0/S1/T1 relative energies very close to the full-valence result. That is a stronger warrant than an occupation-number argument, because it tests the property of interest directly. The value of keeping the space fixed shows up in the solvent analysis: the same (10,8) description is applied to the free molecule, the explicit one-water complex and the complex in a continuum, so the 2.5 kcal/mol shift from hydrogen bonding and the further 0.5 kcal/mol from bulk water are separated cleanly, and both reproduce the experimentally observed blue shift. Dynamic correlation matters unevenly across the surface: the S1 dissociation barrier of the complex is 14.4 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8) and 14.8 at MR-CI, essentially unchanged, while another reported energy moves from 41.5 to 36.5 kcal/mol, a 5 kcal/mol drop. So the reference space is adequate where the wave function stays close to the reference configuration and less so elsewhere. Note also that earlier work on the same solvent shift used a drastically smaller CAS(2,2) with CASPT2 and obtained a comparable 0.2 to 0.4 eV blue shift, which suggests the shift itself is not a sensitive test of the space.
reference_short: Tian & Fang, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 11704
notes: Solvent effects are treated as a combination of explicit hydrogen bonding to a water molecule and bulk effects through the polarizable continuum model. In neutral complexes of acetic acid with several partners, the weaker of two hydrogen bonds opens and the stronger shortens with increasing solvent polarity, a pattern relevant to the behaviour seen here.
correlation_correction: Internally contracted MR-CI including all single and double excitations, as single-point energies on the CASSCF geometries

compound_name: HBDI, the green fluorescent protein chromophore (anionic form), photodynamics and vibrational activity in solvent
geometry_source: Ground and excited state structures relaxed at the CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G* level with solvent effects included through the PCM method. The excited-state reaction path was computed with an S0/S1 state-averaged approach to prevent convergence problems in the energy calculations. Vibrational frequencies at the CASSCF(12,11)-optimized S0 geometry were computed with a reduced (10,8) active space. Ground-state structures at HF/6-31+G* and CIS(S1)/6-31+G* levels were also used for comparison.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF with PCM solvent effects, used for both photoreaction paths and simulated Raman and resonance Raman spectra
software: Gaussian 98 revision A.6 and Gaussian 03 revision B.01; MOLCAS-5 for the CASPT2 calculations
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; 6-31+G* for the HF and CIS calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals, selected from the complete pi system of HBDI which contains sixteen electrons in fourteen orbitals. Three orbitals are excluded: one localized on the amidic nitrogen, and the highest and lowest energy pi orbitals of the benzene ring. A further reduced (10,8) space was used for the vibrational frequency calculations at the CASSCF(12,11) S0 geometry.
active_space_protocol: The complete pi system, sixteen electrons in fourteen orbitals, is too large for CASSCF, so (12,11) is chosen as the stated best compromise between computer speed and accuracy, with three specific orbitals dropped: the amidic nitrogen orbital and the highest and lowest benzene ring pi orbitals. The paper then states exactly which properties that truncation is and is not safe for -- it does not influence the quality and details of the reaction path, but it does affect vibrational frequencies and activities, because the benzenic region ends up described in a somewhat unbalanced way and modes partially localized there are predicted less accurately. State averaging over S0 and S1 was required to prevent convergence problems along the excited-state path. A separate compromise was forced in the correlation step: CASPT2 with PCM would not converge, so the perturbative correction was computed in vacuo and added to the PCM-corrected CASSCF energies.
nroots_per_mult: S0/S1 state-averaged for the excited-state reaction path
electronic_structure_description: Upon excitation the out-of-phase change of the exocyclic CC bonds drives the chromophore from a markedly alternated Franck-Condon structure with well-defined single and double bonds to a fully relaxed structure in which both exocyclic CC bond lengths are comparable and close to 1.43 A at the CASSCF level. This is remarkably different from the gas phase, where the Franck-Condon structure is the more delocalized one and the relaxed structure shows a 0.03 A difference between the two exocyclic CC bonds. The excited surface is remarkably flat in the relaxed region, from which the system can deactivate radiatively, rotate about the more double exocyclic CC bond to a twisted intermediate TW2 giving the double bond flip mechanism, rotate about the more single one to a twisted intermediate TW1 giving the single bond flip mechanism, or rotate about both simultaneously to a hula-twist intermediate HT. Emission from the relaxed structure is computed at 504 nm against an experimental value of about 490 nm; the PCM correction on the CASSCF portion of the CASPT2 calculation shifts this from 518 to 504 nm, and the residual underestimate is attributed to the lack of PCM correction in the perturbative part. The hula-twist intermediate, obtained by simultaneous 90 degree rotation of both exocyclic bonds, shows an S0-S1 surface touching but lies 11 kcal/mol above the relaxed structure and about 8 kcal/mol above the Franck-Condon structure at CASPT2. The charge distribution and S1 wave function hardly change along the Franck-Condon to relaxed-structure path, and excitation relocates charge from the phenolic to the imidazolinone ring.
Other: This is an unusually explicit statement of property-dependent active space adequacy. Dropping three orbitals from the complete sixteen-electron, fourteen-orbital pi system -- the amidic nitrogen orbital and the outermost two benzene ring pi orbitals -- is declared not to influence the quality or details of the reaction path, but explicitly not safe for vibrational frequencies and activities, because the benzenic region is then described in a somewhat unbalanced way and modes partially localized there come out less accurately. The authors go further and warn that the CASSCF-simulated resonance Raman spectra are therefore not expected to be superior to CIS-based simulations, despite CASSCF being generally the better method -- a rare case of a paper telling the reader that its more sophisticated calculation is the less reliable one for a particular observable. The space is reduced again, to (10,8), just for the frequency calculations. A second compromise compounds this: CASPT2 with PCM would not converge, so the perturbative correction was taken from in vacuo calculations and added to PCM-corrected CASSCF energies, and the residual 14 nm underestimate of the emission wavelength is attributed to exactly that missing PCM correction in the PT2 part. The lowest conical intersection of the hula-twist conformation could not be located at all because of problems in the algorithm in the presence of PCM corrections.
reference_short: Altoe, Bernardi, Garavelli, Orlandi & Negri, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2005, 127, 3952
notes: Solvent effects on the photoexcited reaction path were investigated only for the anionic form of the chromophore; Raman and resonance Raman spectra were simulated for the cationic, neutral and anionic forms. Detailed simulations of resonance Raman intensities had not previously been reported for this system.
correlation_correction: Single-point CASPT2, computed in vacuo and added to the PCM-corrected CASSCF energies because CASPT2 with PCM would not converge

compound_name: Pyridine, anharmonic Franck-Condon simulation of the absorption and fluorescence spectra of the S1 and S2 states
geometry_source: Equilibrium geometries of the S0, S1 and S2 states optimized at CASSCF(8,7)/6-311++G** and CASSCF(8,7)/aug-cc-pVDZ using both Gaussian03 and MOLCAS 7.2, which give basically the same results. All 27 normal-mode frequencies were computed for the three electronic states to verify the optimized geometries as true minima on their respective potential energy surfaces.
method: CASSCF for geometries, frequencies and anharmonic constants, feeding an analytic anharmonic Franck-Condon treatment of the absorption and fluorescence coefficients
active_space_orbital_description: Eight active electrons in seven active orbitals, comprising four doubly occupied orbitals and three virtual orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is chosen so that the ground state and both low-lying excited states are treated on an equal footing, which is a requirement rather than a convenience here because the Franck-Condon simulation needs geometries, all 27 normal-mode frequencies and anharmonic constants for all three states from the same electronic description. The selection is described as having been fully analysed and its validity verified in earlier work, and the resulting geometries are checked against Roos's calculations, which used the biggest active space and the most active orbitals. Two basis sets and two program packages were run in parallel as a consistency check and gave essentially the same results.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state S0(1A1) is planar with C2v symmetry, in agreement with electron diffraction and microwave measurements, and the computed bond lengths and angles agree with other theoretical work and with Roos's larger-active-space calculations. The first excited state is 1B1, arising from an A1 to B1 excitation, an n to pi* transition in which the excited orbital is located mostly on nitrogen and the antibonding pi orbital has nodes between C4, C5 and N11, C2; on excitation the C1-N11-C2 angle rises by 10 degrees and the C4-C5 and N11-C2 bond lengths rise by about 0.03 A. The second excited state S2(1B2) is also optimized within C2v symmetry. For the vertical n to pi* transition, experimental assignments range from 4.44 eV (Villa et al.) to 4.59 eV (Goodman et al.), with 4.74 eV extrapolated by Cai and Reimers from fluorescence excitation; the CASSCF value of 5.68 eV is too large, while other cited methods agree well with experiment. For the vertical pi to pi* transition to S2, the experimental band maximum is at 4.99 eV, rising to 5.13 eV with zero-point correction; here CASSCF shows the best agreement with experiment, while TDDFT overestimates at 5.47 and 5.58 eV and CASPT2, CCSD and SAC-CI all underestimate. Vertical excitation energies from calculation can be either larger or smaller than experiment depending on the method, while adiabatic excitation energies are larger than experiment for the S1(1B1) state.
Other: The same (8,7) space gives the best agreement of any method for one state and the worst for the other: CASSCF puts the pi to pi* vertical transition closest to the experimental 4.99 eV, better than TDDFT, CASPT2, CCSD and SAC-CI, while its n to pi* vertical energy of 5.68 eV is described outright as too large against experimental assignments spanning 4.44 to 4.74 eV. Four doubly occupied and three virtual orbitals cannot balance a nitrogen lone pair excitation and a ring pi-pi* excitation equally well, and the error is roughly 1 eV on one and near zero on the other -- yet the space must be shared, because the Franck-Condon machinery requires geometries, all 27 frequencies and anharmonic constants for S0, S1 and S2 from one consistent description. The paper's own resolution of the residual discrepancy is not to enlarge the space but to argue that part of the gap between computed adiabatic energies and observed excitation energies is a dynamic anharmonic contribution absent from any static electronic structure calculation. Two independent checks on the space are reported: geometries agree with Roos's calculations using the biggest active space and most active orbitals, and running both 6-311++G** and aug-cc-pVDZ in two different program packages gives basically the same results, so neither basis nor implementation is limiting.
reference_short: Wang, Zhu, Yu & Lin, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 14407
notes: The n to pi* transition appears experimentally as a shoulder on the pi to pi* band, which is why its assignment is controversial. The anharmonic constants are described as not large in themselves but able to make a remarkable contribution to the spectra, and the signs entering the anharmonic expressions differ between absorption and fluorescence, which breaks the mirror-image relationship between the two spectra.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF; CASPT2, CCSD, SAC-CI and TDDFT values are quoted for comparison

compound_name: Acetamide (CH3CONH2), mechanistic photochemistry and dissociation pathways
point_group: The x-y plane is the molecular symmetry plane in the planar structures; the T1 equilibrium structure is pyramidal
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at the CASSCF level with cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ basis sets; harmonic frequencies examined at each converged point to confirm it as a true minimum or first-order saddle point. Optimization was terminated when the maximum force and its root-mean-square fell below 0.00045 and 0.0003 hartree/bohr. DFT (B3LYP) and MP2 calculations were carried out alongside.
method: CASSCF for the excited-state surfaces and conical intersections, with B3LYP and MP2 for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals. Six of the active orbitals are the C=O pi and pi*, the oxygen nonbonding orbital and the nitrogen 2pz atomic orbital (a six-electron, four-orbital set for the equilibrium geometries of the low-lying valence states), together with the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-C or C-N bond being cleaved. The seventh active orbital is a valence orbital with antibonding character mainly localized on the C-C, C-O and C-N regions, determined by test calculations.
active_space_protocol: The paper states plainly that choosing the active space is a crucial step that cannot be regarded as completely solved and that most applications still involve trial and error, then documents its own trial explicitly. A four-orbital, six-electron set describes the low-lying valence states at equilibrium, but the dissociation involves C-C or C-N cleavage, so the corresponding sigma and sigma* orbitals must be active; (8,7) is adopted as the compromise giving a balanced description of both equilibrium and transition state structures. The seventh orbital was fixed by a lowest-energy criterion: for the T1 equilibrium geometry three different antibonding candidates localized on the N-H, C-H and C-CO-N regions were each tried as the seventh orbital, giving CAS(8,7)/cc-pVDZ energies of -207.92067, -207.92410 and -207.93051 hartree, so the third was chosen. The one-electron densities on those three orbitals, 0.003, 0.01 and 0.04, track the energy ordering, and the authors note that an antibonding orbital giving relatively low energy generally carries relatively large one-electron density. Similar test calculations were performed for the other stationary structures.
electronic_structure_description: No potential barrier above the endothermicity exists on the S0 dissociation pathway. The C-C and C-N dissociations are endothermic by 86.9 and 88.3 kcal/mol, becoming 80.5 and 82.2 kcal/mol with zero-point correction; the C-N bond dissociation energy is close to the 90 kcal/mol enthalpy change measured for C-N dissociation of N,N-dimethylformamide. A transition state TS1(S0) on the H9 transfer pathway has a barrier of 40.5 and 42.5 kcal/mol at the two levels. The barrier on the second step is 70.9, 69.5 and 71.2 kcal/mol relative to the ground-state reactant and 54.6, 54.2 and 54.9 kcal/mol relative to the intermediate, from three levels of calculation. A value of 24.1 kcal/mol is obtained at MP2/cc-pVDZ and B3LYP/cc-pVDZ against an experimental 12.9 kcal/mol from heats of formation at 0 K. The barrier to decarbonylation to CH3NH2 + CO is 107.2 kcal/mol at B3LYP with both basis sets, 8.2 kcal/mol lower than the MP2 value, and 107.5 kcal/mol by another estimate; a related value of 23.8 kcal/mol is quoted for comparison. The T1 equilibrium structure is pyramidal, with the nitrogen changing toward sp3 hybridization, and the conjugation present in S0 disappears in T1 because of that pyramidal structure. Three conical intersection points S0/S1(1), S0/S1(2) and S0/S1(3) were located, with derivative coupling and gradient difference vectors computed at each.
Other: This paper documents its active-space selection as an experiment rather than asserting it. Having settled on (8,7) as the compromise between describing the low-lying valence states at equilibrium (which needs only the carbonyl pi system, oxygen lone pair and nitrogen 2pz) and describing C-C or C-N cleavage (which needs the relevant sigma/sigma* pair), the identity of the seventh orbital was decided by running three candidates. For the T1 equilibrium geometry, antibonding orbitals localized on N-H, C-H and C-CO-N gave CAS(8,7)/cc-pVDZ energies of -207.92067, -207.92410 and -207.93051 hartree -- a spread of 6.2 kcal/mol from orbital choice alone, at fixed space size and fixed geometry. The C-CO-N orbital was selected on the lowest-energy criterion, and the authors add a second, independent diagnostic that agrees with it: the one-electron densities on the three candidates are 0.003, 0.01 and 0.04, so the orbital that lowers the energy most is also the one actually carrying density. That correlation is offered as a general hint for judging whether a chosen antibonding orbital is reasonable. The same test was repeated at every other stationary structure, meaning the seventh orbital's identity is allowed to vary across the surface -- necessary for a balanced description, but it does mean energies at different stationary points do not all come from an identically composed space. The paper prefaces all of this by stating that active space selection cannot be regarded as completely solved and still involves trial and error.
reference_short: Chen, Fang & Fang, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2003, 125, 9689
notes: The barrier to decarbonylation is high enough that the corresponding pathway is not viable for CH3CONHCH3. A similar S0 to T1 structural change had been predicted in earlier work.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF energies; MP2 and B3LYP results are reported alongside for comparison

point_group: Cs used for labelling the vertical transitions
geometry_source: All geometrical optimizations performed at the CASSCF/6-31G* level, with energies of all critical and nonstationary points, including Franck-Condon points and dissociation fragments at the asymptotic limit, recalculated at CASPT2/CASSCF/ANO-L. method: CASPT2//CASSCF, with multistate MS-CASPT2 single points for vertical transitions including PCM solvent calculations
software: MOLCAS 6.4 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 03 revision B.04 for locating surface crossings, conical intersections and intersystem crossings
basis_set: 6-31G* for all geometry optimizations; ANO-L with the C, N, O [3s2p1d] / H [2s1p] contraction scheme for the energy recalculations
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in ten valence orbitals: 2sO, 2sN, sigma-NN, pi-NO, sigma-NO, np-N, np-O, pi*-NO, sigma*-NN and sigma*-NO. For the tautomerization study a sigma-CH orbital and its corresponding virtual orbital were added, giving 16 electrons in 12 orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is inherited from the authors' previous work on NH2NO and enumerated orbital by orbital. It is enlarged to (16,12) by adding a sigma-CH orbital and its virtual counterpart when tautomerizations are studied, since hydrogen migration cannot be described without them. Fragment spaces are derived from this parent space by reduction rather than being constructed independently, so that dissociation asymptotes connect properly. Geometries use 6-31G* on grounds of molecular size, while energies are recomputed with the more balanced ANO-L to make the vertical transitions and excited-state relative energies quantitative.
electronic_structure_description: The S0 to S1 transition occurs at 3.29 eV with an oscillator strength of 0.003 au and the S0 to S2 transition at 5.30 eV with an oscillator strength of 0.17 au; the second singlet state (2 1A') has np-N to pi*-NO character. Changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, and both sets of values agree well with experiment and with MS-CASPT2 results. Experimentally the first band shows a vibrational progression with an oscillator strength of 0.009 and the second band an oscillator strength of 0.12. Excitation at 363.5 nm corresponds to the S0 to S1 transition and gives the dimethylamino radical with a lifetime above 0.5 s, while excitation at 248 nm implies a different mechanism. Dissociation after excitation at 363.5 nm deviates from planarity, whereas at 250 nm NDMA exhibits planar character. MS-CASPT2 vertical transitions were also computed with PCM in cyclohexane, benzene, methanol and water in increasing order of dielectric constant, and the resulting solvent shifts are small.
Other: Four different spaces are used across one study and their relationships are stated explicitly. The parent (14,10) is inherited from the authors' earlier work on NH2NO and lists its orbitals individually: 2sO, 2sN, sigma-NN, pi-NO, sigma-NO, np-N, np-O, pi*-NO, sigma*-NN and sigma*-NO. Studying the tautomerizations required adding a sigma-CH orbital and its virtual partner, giving (16,12) -- the space grows to accommodate a hydrogen migration that the original set could not represent. The dimethylamine radical fragment gets its own (11,10) built for the two extrusion channels it participates in, and that space is described as obtained by reduction of the parent space, so the fragment and parent descriptions are nested rather than independent. The NO fragment was optimized at yet another level, CASSCF(11,8). Nesting is what makes the dissociation energetics meaningful, since the asymptotic limits and the parent molecule must be described consistently. The basis strategy is split deliberately for the same reason: geometries at 6-31G* justified by the size of the molecule, energies recomputed with the more balanced ANO-L specifically to make the vertical transitions and excited-surface energies quantitative. That split is validated by the observation that changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, so the smaller basis is adequate for the geometry-dependent quantities and the larger one is needed only for energies. Core orbitals were frozen in CASPT2 as optimized at the CASSCF level, and imaginary modes at the Franck-Condon geometries were characterized separately at CASSCF/ANO-L with gradients, rotations and translations projected out.
reference_short: Arenas, Otero, Pelaez & Soto, J. Org. Chem. 2007, 72, 4741
notes: The paper's title identifies excitation to the S2 state as a doorway to dimethylamine radical ground-state chemistry. Potential energy surfaces between relevant points were analysed by interpolation, which also allows tracking the variation of properties such as fragment charge along the path.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 on the CASSCF reference with the 1s core orbitals of C, N and O frozen as optimized at the CASSCF level, with a shift applied to minimize intruder state contamination

compound_name: CH3O(radical) + O2 reaction system, including the methyltrioxy radical CH3OOO and the transition structures for methoxy oxidation
point_group: The methoxy radical ground state is 2E and subject to Jahn-Teller distortion; the reactant system is a doublet of A'' symmetry
geometry_source: All geometries, minima and saddle points, reoptimized with CASSCF wave functions and the 6-311G(d,p) basis using analytical gradient procedures, after the reliability of UHF geometries was questioned. All stationary points characterized as minima or saddle points by harmonic vibrational frequencies obtained by diagonalizing the analytically computed mass-weighted Cartesian force constant matrix at CASSCF/6-311G(d,p). Connections of transition structures to designated minima were confirmed by IRC calculations at the same level using the second-order Gonzalez-Schlegel algorithm with a step size of 0.15 bohr amu^(1/2). Geometries and frequencies of the most relevant stationary points were also computed with CISD and QCISD on a UHF reference with frozen core, using 6-31G(d) and 6-311G(d,p).
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequencies, with single-point frozen-core CCSD(T) energies on a UHF reference for the relative energy ordering; CISD and QCISD used to assess the CASSCF results
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF geometry optimizations and IRC calculations; GAUSSIAN 94 for the analytic frequencies
basis_set: 6-311G(d,p) for the CASSCF; 6-31G(d) and 6-311G(d,p) for CISD and QCISD; 6-311G(d,p), 6-311+G(d,p), 6-311+G(3df,2p) and cc-pVTZ for the coupled-cluster single points
active_space_orbital_description: The complete active spaces were selected following the procedure of Anglada and Bofill, based on the fractional occupation of the natural orbitals generated from the first-order density matrix of an initial multireference single- and double-excitation configuration interaction (MRDCI) wave function correlating all valence electrons. The resulting numbers of active electrons and orbitals are not stated.
active_space_protocol: The space is not chosen by chemical inspection at all. An MRDCI wave function correlating all valence electrons is computed first, its first-order density matrix is formed, and the natural orbitals with fractional occupation are promoted into the active space by the Anglada-Bofill criterion. This makes the selection reproducible and, importantly, geometry-dependent in a controlled way: the same procedure is reapplied at each of the 15 stationary points on the surface, so the space adapts as bonds form and break without any hand-tuning. The motivation is stated explicitly -- the structures involved have substantial correlation effects, which called the reliability of the previously used UHF geometries into question. Dynamic correlation is then added by frozen-core CCSD(T) single points on a UHF reference at the CASSCF geometries, with basis sets extended to cc-pVTZ to establish convergence.
electronic_structure_description: Fifteen stationary points on the ground-state potential energy surface of the CH3O + O2 system were located. The ground state of the reactants is a doublet of A'' symmetry and correlates with the 2A'' ground state of the products. The methoxy radical ground state is 2E and the Jahn-Teller theorem predicts a distorted equilibrium geometry, with an energy lowering of 0.35 to 0.63 kcal/mol on distortion. The methyltrioxy radical 1 exhibits two distinct conformers, with the trans isomer 1.14 and 0.97 kcal/mol higher in energy than the cis isomer by two methods, against a ZPVE-corrected difference of 1.2 kcal/mol. Formation of trans-1 is endoergic by 4.8 kcal/mol with a potential energy barrier of 7.4 kcal/mol, lowered to 5.6 kcal/mol at RCCSD/cc-pVTZ, so that barrier is only 1.8 kcal/mol higher than an alternative; zero-point corrections increase the barrier difference to 4.5 kcal/mol, and one structure lies only 0.2 kcal/mol below trans-1. The gauche-1 to 2 isomerization has a barrier of 46.4 kcal/mol. A structure lies 23.4 kcal/mol above CH3O and is less energetic than gauche-1. The overall reaction is exoergic by -59.0 kcal/mol at CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ with ZPVE. A mechanism proceeding through a transition structure with a 51.4 kcal/mol barrier cannot compete with the direct pathway, which passes through TS1 with a barrier of only 3.7 kcal/mol; the corresponding activation energy is 2.8 kcal/mol, against experimental Arrhenius parameters of Ea = 1.788 +/- 0.596 kcal/mol. A puckered ringlike transition structure lies 50.6 kcal/mol higher. The ringlike transition structure TSB connects a hydrogen-bonded CH2O...HOO complex in the forward direction to a loosely bound CH3O...O2 complex rather than to the expected species. An exoergicity of 30.5 kcal/mol reported by earlier workers is compared against.
Other: The active space here is generated algorithmically rather than chosen: an MRDCI wave function correlating all valence electrons is computed, its first-order density matrix formed, and the fractionally occupied natural orbitals promoted into the space by the Anglada-Bofill criterion. Neither the electron nor the orbital count is reported anywhere, which is the direct cost of an automatic procedure -- the space is reproducible from the recipe but not from the paper. The virtue is that the same recipe is reapplied across fifteen stationary points spanning bond formation, hydrogen transfer and ring closure, so the space tracks the changing correlation structure without hand intervention; the paper's stated motivation is precisely that these structures carry substantial correlation effects, which is why the earlier UHF geometries were distrusted and everything was reoptimized. The CASSCF is used for geometry and frequencies only, with the energetics coming from frozen-core CCSD(T) single points on a UHF reference -- so the multiconfigurational treatment and the correlation treatment are built on different references, and CISD and QCISD on UHF references were run on the most relevant stationary points specifically to assess whether the CASSCF geometries hold up. The energetic payoff is large: the direct hydrogen transfer barrier of 3.7 kcal/mol, giving an activation energy of 2.8 kcal/mol against an experimental 1.788 +/- 0.596, versus 51.4 kcal/mol for the competing mechanism.

notes: The paper presents computational evidence for direct hydrogen atom transfer assisted by an intermolecular noncovalent O...O bonding interaction. Experimental studies of the methoxy radical electronic and vibrational spectra are cited for the 2E ground state assignment.

d_electron_count: 5d10 in the 2A1 state; the gold atom valence space is 5d10 6s1
point_group: C2v; the ground state is X 2B2 and the bent HAuH structure was studied on a bending potential energy surface
geometry_source: Bending potential energy surfaces computed in two and three dimensions for the 2A1 and 2B2 states. Dissociation energies computed by a supermolecular calculation with the Au-H distances set to 10 A, because MRSDCI is not size consistent. Vibrational frequencies computed at the coupled cluster (CCD) and MP2 levels in the same gold basis with aug-cc-pVTZ on hydrogen, and compared with experiment and with DFT.
method: CASSCF followed by multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction (MRSDCI); CCD and MP2 for frequencies; matrix isolation infrared spectroscopy in solid hydrogen for comparison
software: Balasubramanian's programs for all CASSCF and MRSDCI computations
basis_set: Extended (3s3p4d1f) basis for gold with a relativistic effective core potential of Ermler and co-workers replacing 68 electrons and leaving the 5d10 6s1 shells as the valence space; triple-zeta plus polarization for the hydrogens; aug-cc-pVTZ on hydrogen for the frequency calculations
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potential on gold, replacing 68 electrons; relativistic mass-velocity stabilization of the 6s orbital and destabilization of the 5d orbital are noted as essential for gold
active_space_orbital_description: Five a1 orbitals, three b2 orbitals, two b1 orbitals and one a2 orbital, holding all 13 valence electrons of AuH2, distributed in all possible ways among the active orbitals. The space was chosen to include all 5d, 6s and 6p orbitals of gold.
active_space_protocol: The space is dictated by the atomic spectroscopy of gold rather than by the molecular bonding: because the first excited state of the gold atom arises from 5d9 6s2 and the second from 5d10 6p1, all of the 5d, 6s and 6p orbitals must be active if the molecular states correlating with those atomic limits are to be described. Listing the space by symmetry block -- five a1, three b2, two b1 and one a2 -- makes the composition explicit rather than leaving it to a bare count. The MRSDCI built on it correlates the same 13 electrons and takes as references all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients at or above 0.01, which typically gave 65 reference configurations and up to 3.4 million total configurations. Because MRSDCI is not size consistent, dissociation energies were obtained from a supermolecular calculation at 10 A rather than by subtracting fragment energies.
electronic_structure_description: The gold atom 2D state from the 5d9 6s2 configuration lies 1.7 eV above the ground state while the corresponding state from 5d10 6p1 lies 4.9 eV higher, a consequence of relativistic mass-velocity stabilization of the 6s orbital and destabilization of the 5d orbital. The barrier to insert Au(2D) into H2 is 53 kcal/mol, but the 2P state of gold lies considerably above this barrier and is very reactive because it also yields a 2B2 state which undergoes an avoided crossing with the 2B2 state arising from Au(2D); the barrier appears to arise from that avoided crossing. The barrier for formation of the lowest 2A1 state from Au(2S) + H2 is 95 kcal/mol. Once the X 2B2 state is formed through excitation of gold to the 2P state it remains in its potential well, since dissociating back to Au(2D) + H2 requires surmounting a large barrier. The 2B2 and 2A1 surfaces cross at a bond angle of 65 degrees, about 25 kcal/mol above the X 2B2 minimum, and that 25 kcal/mol barrier must be overcome before decomposition to Au(2S) + H2. Spin-orbit coupling between the two states cannot be large because the 2A1 state has predominantly Au(5d10 6s1) character; the 2B2 state has a larger spin-orbit effect but its coupling to 2A1 should be negligible because of the closed 5d10 shell in the latter. X 2B2 is therefore a long-lived ground state, 27 kcal/mol more stable than Au(2D) + H2. A zero-point correction of 6.4 kcal/mol is applied. The computed 2A1 bending surface is close to a previous study but the 2B2 surface differs, especially near the dissociation limit and the minimum. Adding an f function gives unrealistic infrared intensities. The AuH2 anion has also been observed, with a related energy of 68 kcal/mol from DFT.
Other: The composition of the active space is fixed by where the atomic excited states come from, not by which orbitals form bonds: since gold's first excited state is 5d9 6s2 and its second is 5d10 6p1, the 5d, 6s and 6p sets all have to be active for the molecular states correlating with those limits to exist in the wave function at all. That matters directly for the physics being reported, because the barrier to insertion is attributed to an avoided crossing between two 2B2 states arising from the 2D and 2P atomic asymptotes -- a feature that simply cannot appear if the 6p orbitals are outside the space. The paper reports its space by symmetry block (five a1, three b2, two b1, one a2) rather than as a bare pair of numbers, and the MRSDCI inherits it by taking every CASSCF configuration with coefficient at or above 0.01 as a reference, typically 65 references expanding to 3.4 million configurations. One methodological consequence is handled explicitly: MRSDCI is not size consistent, so dissociation energies come from a supermolecular calculation at 10 A separation rather than from fragment subtraction. The comparison with earlier work is instructive -- the 2A1 bending surface reproduces a previous study closely while the 2B2 surface differs near both the minimum and the dissociation limit, which is where the multi-asymptote character of the space would be expected to matter most. Separately, adding an f function to the gold basis produces unrealistic infrared intensities, so the basis was not simply extended for its own sake.

method: CASSCF(6,6) geometry optimization with second-order multireference perturbation theory (MRMP) single points; second-order configuration interaction (SOCI) single points on the CASSCF reference for the Franck-Condon excited singlets; solvation added through an Onsager-type expression
basis_set: 3-21G* for the geometry optimizations; 3-21G* and 6-31G* for the MRMP and CASSCF single-point energies
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals. For the locally excited state the six orbitals are the benzene pi and pi*, the Si-Si bonding and their antibonding counterparts. For the intramolecular charge-transfer state the six orbitals are the benzene pi and pi*, the Si-Si and C-Si bonding orbitals and their antibonding counterparts.
active_space_protocol: One space size, two compositions. For the locally excited state the six active orbitals are the benzene pi and pi* orbitals plus the Si-Si bonding and antibonding orbitals; for the intramolecular charge-transfer state the C-Si bonding and antibonding orbitals join the Si-Si pair. Each state is therefore optimized in a space tailored to the bonds carrying its own electron distribution. Cs symmetry was imposed throughout and the methyl groups of the real compound replaced by hydrogen atoms to make the calculations affordable. Solvation was added afterwards through an Onsager expression using the excited-state dipole moment, the static dielectric constant and an Onsager radius of 4.6 A, assuming the solvent relaxes fully about the solute dipole within the excited-state lifetime.

electronic_structure_description: Optimized geometries were obtained for planar and perpendicular conformers in the S0, locally excited and charge-transfer states. Second-order configuration interaction single points on the CASSCF reference at the ground-state geometry found that all ten lowest excited singlets S1 to S10 correspond to the locally excited state, with none of charge-transfer character. The lowest transition energy from the 0-0 absorption band in cyclohexane is 4.6 eV, and all calculated 0-0 energies at the CASSCF(6,6)/3-21G*, CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G*, MRMP/CASSCF(6,6)/3-21G* and MRMP/CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* levels lie much higher, with the discrepancy significantly improved by the MRMP calculations. The geometry-optimized locally excited state lies below the 0-0 energy while the charge-transfer state lies slightly above it. The charge-transfer states of the planar and perpendicular conformers have large dipole moments of 10.2 and 9.51 D, giving significant solvent-induced stabilization in acetonitrile, where the charge-transfer state falls well below the 0-0 energy at the CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* level; in nonpolar cyclohexane it is only slightly below. Dipole moments of 0.2 and 0.12 D are reported for the planar and perpendicular ground-state conformations, and formal charges of the disilanyl group reach -0.23 and -0.18 for the planar and perpendicular forms. In the locally excited state of the perpendicular conformation all six active orbitals show a particular character, while the charge-transfer state of the planar conformation differs. Experimentally, emission bands from locally excited and charge-transfer states appear at about 3.4e4 and 2.9e4 cm-1 in cyclohexane, and in EPA glass at 77 K three bands are seen, assigned to locally excited fluorescence, charge-transfer fluorescence and phosphorescence.
Other: The active space is held at six electrons in six orbitals for both excited states but its contents are swapped between them: for the locally excited state the six orbitals are the benzene pi and pi* pair together with the Si-Si bonding and antibonding orbitals, while for the intramolecular charge-transfer state the Si-Si pair is joined by the C-Si bonding and antibonding orbitals. That substitution is what allows one space size to describe two states whose defining electron distributions live on different bonds -- the charge-transfer state moves density onto the carbon-silicon linkage, which is simply absent from the locally excited space. The consequence is that the two states are not eigenvalues of a common Hamiltonian matrix but come from separately optimized wave functions, so their relative energies rest on the assumption that the two spaces are of comparable quality. The reference level is demonstrably not adequate on its own: every computed 0-0 energy lies well above the experimental 4.6 eV, and the discrepancy is described as significantly improved by the MRMP perturbative correction. A structural approximation compounds this -- Cs symmetry was imposed throughout because of restricted computing time, and the methyl groups of the real compound were replaced by hydrogens. Separately, second-order configuration interaction single points on the CASSCF reference found that all ten lowest excited singlets at the ground-state geometry correspond to the locally excited state and none to charge transfer, so the charge-transfer state is not reachable vertically and only appears after geometric relaxation -- which is precisely why it needs its own active space rather than a shared one.

notes: Phenyldisilane is the computational stand-in for compound 1 of the experimental study, with methyl groups replaced by hydrogens. geometry_source: Geometries of the lowest 1A1 and 3B1 states optimized at the MCSCF (CASSCF) level; values in parentheses below are from CCSD/6-311++G(d,f) optimizations.
method: Multiconfiguration SCF of the complete active space (CASSCF) type, with the total electronic energy decomposed into frontier-electron and core contributions
basis_set: Huzinaga-based basis sets as defined in the paper text; CCSD/6-311++G(d,f) used for comparison geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in the 1a1, 1b2, 2a1, 1b1, 3a1 and 2b2 orbitals in C2v symmetry, being those that correlate at large internuclear separation into the H 1s and C 2s and 2p atomic orbitals. active_space_protocol: Six electrons distributed in all possible ways among six orbitals selected by their dissociation limits: the orbitals that at large internuclear separation correlate into the H 1s and the heavy-atom ns and np atomic orbitals. In C2v these are the 1a1, 1b2, 2a1, 1b1, 3a1 and 2b2 orbitals for both molecules. The core electrons, 1s2 for carbon and 1s2 2s2 2p6 for silicon, were not correlated. The identical construction for both species is what allows the singlet-triplet gaps to be compared and decomposed term by term.
electronic_structure_description: Optimized CASSCF geometries with CCSD/6-311++G(d,f) values in parentheses: 1A1 has r(C-H) 1.126 (1.115) A and an H-C-H angle of 101.06 (101.42) degrees; 3B1 has r(C-H) 1.090 (1.083) A and an angle of 131.32 (133.06) degrees. CASSCF energies in hartree: 1A1 nuclear 5.94259, electronic -44.89715, total -38.95455; 3B1 nuclear 6.08671, electronic -45.05837, total -38.97166, so the triplet is the ground state. The nuclear repulsion difference favours the singlet by 90.4 kcal/mol, smaller than the corresponding 146.9 kcal/mol for silylene, because the change in M-H bond length between singlet and triplet is smaller in CH2; the M-H bonds are shorter in the triplet states while the wider H-M-H angles reduce hydrogen-hydrogen repulsion, but this effect is much smaller than the increase in M-H repulsion. In the 3B1 state the s-orbital contribution to the in-plane sigma-type singly occupied molecular orbital is 20.8 percent for CH2, compared with 36.2 percent for SiH2. The expectation values of the maximum radial density of the ns and np orbitals are 1.220 and 1.217 A for carbon. A frozen-geometry decomposition gives a singlet-triplet difference of -0.4 kcal/mol for CH2 for one term and -22.6 kcal/mol for another.
Other: The space is defined by an asymptotic criterion rather than by counting bonds: the six correlated electrons are distributed in all possible ways among orbitals that, at large internuclear separation, correlate into the H 1s and the C 2s and 2p or Si 3s and 3p atomic orbitals. Applying one dissociation-based rule to both molecules is what makes the comparison work, because it guarantees that CH2 and SiH2 carry the same orbital set relative to their own atomic limits despite the silicon having an extra filled shell -- the 1s2 2s2 2p6 core of Si and the 1s2 of C are simply uncorrelated. The resulting spaces are the same six orbitals (1a1, 1b2, 2a1, 1b1, 3a1, 2b2) in C2v for both, giving 51 configuration state functions for the 3B1 states and 56 for the 1A1 states. That asymmetry in CSF count between the two multiplicities is a reminder that the singlet needs more configurations than the triplet at equal orbital count, so the two states are not described with identical variational freedom. The whole analysis then rests on partitioning the CASSCF electronic energy into contributions from the two frontier electrons and from everything else, which is only meaningful because the frontier orbitals are inside the active space and optimized there. The paper is careful to say why it chose that partition over the alternative of separating true core from all valence electrons -- it is testing qualitative models that assign the multiplicity change to the two frontier electrons specifically. Geometries at this level track CCSD/6-311++G(d,f) closely, with bond lengths within 0.024 A and angles within 1.7 degrees, so the space is adequate for structure.

The vertical excitation at the Franck-Condon geometry is 164 kcal/mol, corresponding to 174 nm, in agreement with experiment. Experimentally the absorption spectra of unsubstituted imidazole in ethanol and aqueous solution show two broad bands with maxima near 207 nm (139 kcal/mol) and 187-178 nm (153-161 kcal/mol). Two pathways are considered, a conical intersection pathway (path 1) and an internal cyclization-isomerization pathway (path 2), both leading to the observed product. The optimized CI-1 is a conical intersection rather than a true minimum because its energy gradient does not go to zero; its planarity is lost, with an N3-C2-N1-C5 dihedral of 46.60 degrees. Funneling through CI-1 can lead to two different ground-state reaction pathways, and twisting the C5=N1 bond swaps the two neighbouring ring positions. CI-1 lies 109 kcal/mol above the minimum and 56 kcal/mol below FC-A, and after decay at that intersection the observed product forms by a barrierless ground-state relaxation. A structure lying about 110 kcal/mol below FC-A leaves a large excess energy of 110 kcal/mol, sufficient to surmount barriers of about 34 kcal/mol for intermediate 3 to TS-1 and 24 kcal/mol for intermediate 4 to TS-2, so paths 1 and 2 should compete.

compound_name: cis-HNOO, the cis nitroso oxide isomer from NH + O2 recombination
geometry_source: Geometry optimized at the CASSCF(18,13)/6-311+G(d,p) level with vibrational analysis at the same level; energies recomputed with multireference and composite methods.
method: CASSCF for geometries and vibrational analysis, with MC-QDPT2, MR-CISD+Q and MR-AQCC multireference energies and the G3, G3MP2B3, CBS-QB3 and W1U composite procedures; RRKM analysis of the kinetics
active_space_orbital_description: Eighteen electrons in thirteen orbitals, being all valence orbitals with no frozen low-lying molecular orbitals. The decomposition products NH + O2, HNO + O and NO + OH were separately optimized with full valence active spaces chosen so that each pair sums to the same (18,13) total active space.
active_space_protocol: The space is the complete valence set, adopted specifically to replace an earlier treatment that used a (6,6) space with frozen low-lying orbitals. Three changes were made together: expanding the space to all valence orbitals, unfreezing the remaining molecular orbitals, and enlarging the basis to 6-311+G(d,p). Fragment spaces are sized so that the two products of each dissociation channel together carry the same (18,13) total as the parent, keeping the reaction energetics consistent across channels. Results are cross-checked against coupled cluster, MR-AQCC and four composite procedures rather than relied on alone.
electronic_structure_description: The cis conformer is found to be the more stable of the two nitroso oxide isomers, with a superior stability of 12 to 21 kJ/mol, and the relative cis/trans energy difference is well reproduced by all methods applied. Its dipole moment is 1.5 D against 2.6 D for the trans form. The difference between this work's O-O bond distance and the earlier small-active-space value is even more pronounced for the cis isomer than for the trans. Both cis and trans forms are formed initially in the nitrene-dioxygen recombination, but rotational interconversion follows; free energy barriers of 31.1 and 28.8 kJ/mol were computed for the two competing formation channels, an energy difference of about 2 kJ/mol. Factors that equalize the cis and trans formation rate constants cause growth of the cis content. The preferential observation of trans-nitroso oxide under low-temperature conditions therefore cannot be explained on thermochemical grounds and is attributed instead to induced polarization of the xenon matrix. The NH + O2 recombination is highly exothermic.
Other: This paper is an explicit correction of an earlier study built on a small active space, and it quantifies the damage. The previous work used a (6,6) space with frozen low-lying molecular orbitals; here the space is expanded to (18,13), the full valence set, the remaining orbitals are unfrozen, and the basis enlarged to 6-311+G(d,p). The authors state that the small space poorly reproduces the geometrical parameters and seems to allow only a qualitative description of the surface shape. Two concrete consequences follow. For trans-HNOO the O-O distance comes out at 1.281 to 1.299 A across DFT, coupled cluster, CASSCF and MR-AQCC, whereas the small-space calculations underestimate it by 0.03 to 0.05 A, with the discrepancy even larger for the cis isomer. For hydroperoxynitrene the effect is qualitative rather than quantitative: the earlier work gave an O-O bond of 1.472 A, typical of a peroxide (hydrogen peroxide is 1.452 A), and concluded that a covalent peroxide bond dissociates with low activation energy, whereas here CCSD, MP4(SDQ) and MR-AQCC(10,8) give 1.866, 1.971 and 2.030 A and density functionals agree (1.913 A at mPWB95), so the species is a complex of two radicals rather than a covalently bonded molecule. A wrong active space therefore produced not a shifted number but a wrong chemical identity for an intermediate. The dissociation products NH + O2, HNO + O and NO + OH were each optimized with full valence spaces chosen so that every pair sums to the same (18,13) total, which is what makes the reaction energetics size-consistent across channels. Independent confirmation is sought throughout rather than assumed: the H-transfer barrier is 112.5 to 116.1 kJ/mol from composite methods and 118.4 to 120.8 from multireference methods, and the cis/trans energy difference is reproduced by all methods applied.

electronic_structure_description: trans-Acetanilide adopts a planar Cs structure in all three states S0, S1 and D0, with two methyl hydrogens above and below the molecular plane and one facing the amide oxygen. software: Gaussian 98 revision A.6 for the geometry optimizations and paths; MOLCAS 5 for the CASPT2 calculations

At Min S1: S0 34.86, 27.22; S1 79.84, 79.52; S2 128.54, 113.52; S3 134.55, 111.73; S4 150.64, 154.17; T1 75.56, 76.8; T2 80.13, 77.43. The first two excited singlets S1(Bg) and S2(Au) are almost degenerate and are single n-pi* transitions between orbitals 3 to 8 and 4 to 8; the next two are pi-pi* excitations, with S3(Bu) the bright state carrying an oscillator strength of about 0.1 and absorbing at 239 nm, mainly a single excitation between orbitals 7 and 8 located on the central C1-C2 double bond and the adjacent C1-C3 and C2-C4 bonds. The relaxation cascade proceeds from the Franck-Condon region on S3 through the S3/S2 conical intersection, whose departing path does not involve C-C twisting, then onto the lowest S1 (n-pi*) state, with the whole multistate relaxation path preserving planarity, and finally to the twisted S1/S0 deactivation funnel at 90 degrees. A triplet channel via intersystem crossing at Min S1 followed by relaxation on T1 and back intersystem crossing is also considered. The same space is applied to the parent and to both methylated models, which is what makes the substituent trend meaningful: the bright S3 absorption moves 239, 251 and 277 nm across E-1, E-2 and E-3, tracking the experimental 250 and 264 nm maxima of the corresponding threads and attributing the shift to alkyl hyperconjugation rather than to any change in description. notes: Fumaramide E-1 is the unsubstituted parent selected as a model of the fumaramide thread E-4. In vacuo computations reproduce the solution spectroscopic data, from which solvent effects are judged negligible for this system.

compound_name: OCN / NCO reaction system: O(3P) + CN(X2Sigma+) and N(2D) + CO(X1Sigma+) on two coupled surfaces
point_group: Collinear geometries; the 2Pi and 4Sigma- states are the lowest collinear states
geometry_source: Potential energy surfaces built on a grid: 484 energy points per symmetry interpolated by the generalized discrete variable representation (GDVR) method, of which 171 were computed at CASPT2 in the atom-atom separation range 0.83 to 12.97 A. The spin-orbit coupling surface used twice as many points per coordinate, with 684 CASSCF/RASSI points computed for atom-atom distances from 0.83 to 4.67 A in each of RCO and RCN, distributed evenly in the logarithm of the distance to give a more detailed description of the reaction zone. No calculations were made where both coordinates exceed 2.47 A.
method: CASPT2 for the diabatic potential energy surfaces (reported previously) with spin-orbit coupling matrix elements from the RASSI (restricted active space state interaction) method using CASSCF wave functions as the basis; wave packet propagation by the split operator method and trajectory surface hopping for the dynamics
software: MOLCAS 5.2 for the CASPT2 surfaces; MOLCAS 6.0 for the CASSCF/RASSI spin-orbit calculations
basis_set: ANO-L with the 14s9p4d3f primitive set contracted to 4s3p2d1f, used both for the potential energy points and for the spin-orbit calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Not stated in this paper; the CASSCF wave functions serve as the basis for the RASSI spin-orbit calculations and the CASPT2 potential energy surfaces were reported in the authors' earlier work.
active_space_protocol: The multiconfigurational treatment is split across two jobs with different sampling requirements. The CASPT2 surfaces are taken from earlier work and are sampled at 171 computed points per symmetry, expanded to 484 by interpolation. The spin-orbit coupling surface required twice the point density in each coordinate, because it changes more rapidly and has a more complicated shape than the potential surfaces themselves, giving 684 CASSCF/RASSI points; sampling was made uniform in the logarithm of the internuclear distances to concentrate points in the reaction zone. Where the CASSCF/RASSI calculations failed to converge, values were reconstructed by linear interpolation from surrounding geometries.
electronic_structure_description: Both reactions are exothermic, by 0.81 eV on the 2Pi surface and 3.39 eV on the 4Sigma- surface. The 2Pi surface has a potential well 5.85 eV deep, while the 4Sigma- surface has a potential energy barrier of 1.42 eV, so reaction is thermally accessible at room temperature only on the 2Pi surface. The two surfaces cross. A complete picture of the asymptotic fine-structure spin-orbit states would include a 2Sigma- and a 4Pi state in addition to the 4Sigma- and 2Pi states treated. Wave packets were initiated in both the O(3P) + CN(X2Sigma+) and N(2D) + CO(X1Sigma+) channels; for O + CN the kinetic energies studied were well below the 4Sigma- barrier, and only a very small fraction of the reacting wave packet crossed to the 4Sigma- surface through the spin-orbit interaction at the crossing. In this work the wavepacket is initiated on the lower or upper O + CN adiabat rather than on the diabatic 2Pi and 4Sigma- surfaces as in the authors' earlier study.
Other: The interesting active-space-related finding here is about sampling rather than composition: the CASSCF/RASSI spin-orbit coupling surface needed twice the point density in each coordinate as the CASPT2 potential surfaces, because it varies more rapidly and has a more complicated shape, so 684 spin-orbit points were computed against 171 CASPT2 points per symmetry. The coupling that drives the whole two-surface dynamics is therefore the harder quantity to represent, not the energies. The multiconfigurational description also proved fragile in specific places: a ridge appeared where the two surfaces are high in energy and nearly degenerate, and was removed by linear interpolation on the grounds that the wave packet never reaches it, while two deep holes at RCN about 1.0 A with RCO about 2.8 A, and RCN about 1.5 A with RCO about 3.0 A, arose because the CASSCF/RASSI calculations would not converge and had to be filled by interpolating from surrounding geometries. Neither the electron nor the orbital count of the active space is stated anywhere in this paper; both the space and the CASPT2 surfaces are inherited from the authors' earlier study. A stated incompleteness of the state manifold compounds this: a full asymptotic fine-structure treatment would require 2Sigma- and 4Pi states alongside the 2Pi and 4Sigma- ones actually computed.

Both basis sets give nearly identical relative energies and bond lengths, while the two active spaces predict rather different energy and bond length for the second excited state b 1Sigma+; the full valence space reproduces the experimental a-to-b spacing of 0.71 eV much better than the reduced space.

The full valence space is 24 electrons in 16 orbitals; the reduced one drops the Cl 3s-like and N 2s-like orbitals to give 16 electrons in 12. On the NCl monomer the difference is measurable and one-sided: the full valence space reproduces the experimental a-to-b state spacing of 0.71 eV much better, giving b at 2.10 to 2.16 eV against the reduced space's 2.55 to 2.64 eV, while the a state and all three bond lengths barely move between spaces. So the truncation damages one specific state. Far more consequential is where the reduced space fails outright: near a ClN...NCl separation of 2.0 A the electronic structure changes as an N-N double bond begins to form, the N 2s-like orbitals move into the valence region, and several Cl 3p-like orbitals move out as they change from sigma and pi bonding to lone-pair character -- exactly swapping the orbitals that the truncation discarded for ones it kept. notes: Full valence computations are described as prohibitively expensive for two NCl molecules except for occasional energy points, which is why the reduced space is needed for the dimer work.

compound_name: NCl + NCl system, the lowest 18 electronic surfaces and long-range self-quenching of the first excited state
point_group: Linear NCl...ClN, NCl...NCl and ClN...NCl arrangements analysed in C-infinity-v, D-infinity-h, D2h and C2v; cis C2v, trans C2h and C2 structures also considered
geometry_source: Rigid scans of three linear nuclear configurations (NCl...ClN, NCl...NCl and ClN...NCl) over all 18 electronic surfaces. Geometry optimizations used analytical SA-CASSCF gradients. Minima on seams of crossing between states of different spin or spatial symmetry were located with the SEAM program, which projects MOLPRO gradients for two states onto the seam; for states of different symmetry this is a geometry optimization in 3N-7 dimensions. Residual gradients, or their projections onto the seam, were below 1e-4 hartree per bohr or per degree for all reported structures.
method: State-averaged CASSCF (SA-CASSCF) with analytical gradients; minima on seams of crossing located with the SEAM program, and spin-orbit matrix elements at each crossing computed with the full Breit-Pauli spin-orbit Hamiltonian
software: MOLPRO 2000.1 for the SA-CASSCF calculations; the SEAM program for the crossing-seam optimizations
basis_set: 6-31+G(d) and 6-311+G(d), using five spherical harmonic Gaussian functions for the d atomic orbitals rather than six Cartesian ones
active_space_orbital_description: The reduced 16 electron, 12 orbital space, obtained from the 24 electron, 16 orbital full valence space by excluding the Cl 3s-like and N 2s-like orbitals, was used for the dimer optimizations. All occupied orbitals not in the active space were optimized but constrained doubly occupied.
active_space_protocol: Three state-averaging sets were used depending on region: all 18 states, the 13 remaining after excluding five high-lying states from the a+b and b+b manifolds, or only the 6 states of the X+b and a+a manifolds. Two active spaces were available, the full valence 24e/16o and the reduced 16e/12o. Because a single full-valence SA-CASSCF gradient in C2v with the smallest state set required nearly 48 hours on one CPU with about 2 GB of RAM and 18 GB of disk, and seam optimizations need two gradients per cycle, only the reduced space made crossing-seam searches feasible at roughly 6 hours per gradient. The reduced space is explicitly not applicable everywhere: near a ClN...NCl separation of 2.0 A the N 2s-like orbitals move into the valence region while several Cl 3p-like orbitals move out as they change from sigma and pi bonding to lone-pair character, and full valence computations are said to be in order for that region.
nroots_per_mult: Three schemes: all 18 states, 13 states, or 6 states
electronic_structure_description: All 18 electronic surfaces arising from the interaction of two NCl molecules in the X, a and b states were scanned for the high-symmetry linear structures. Only 13 states are distinguishable in the plots because five are doubly degenerate for linear arrangements: 1Delta(g) and 1Delta(u) from the a+b manifold, 1Gamma(g) from the a+a manifold, and 3Delta(g) and 3Delta(u) from the X+a manifold. Minima on seams of crossing between singlet and triplet surfaces were located; although spin-forbidden, transitions between them can occur through spin-orbit interactions, and the spin-orbit matrix element between the two states of each seam was computed at each crossing minimum with the full Breit-Pauli spin-orbit Hamiltonian. Near a ClN...NCl separation of 2.0 A the electronic structure changes dramatically in anticipation of what could be considered formation of an N-N double bond, by analogy with the ground state of dihalodiazenes. State orderings are given for each manifold with energies relative to the asymptotic limit, ordered loosely by the cis energies near R(NN) = 2.5 A.
