Orbitals outside the active space were optimized but constrained doubly occupied.
reference_short: Tschumper, Heaven & Morokuma, J. Phys. Chem. A 2002, 106, 8453
notes: The study addresses long-range self-quenching pathways of the first excited state of NCl. The correlation of states across C-infinity-v, D-infinity-h, D2h, C2v linear, C2v cis, C2h trans and C2 symmetries is tabulated.

compound_name: Two pi-stacked adenines inside a solvated poly(dA).poly(dT) DNA double-strand decamer
geometry_source: A three-layer QM/MM setup on a solvated DNA double-strand decamer: the fourth and fifth pi-stacked adenines, Ade(1) and Ade(2) counting from the 5-position of the poly(dA).poly(dT) decamer, form the high layer described at the SA-CASSCF level, with a hydrogen link-atom approach cutting at the sugar ring carbon directly linked to the base and the adjacent oxygen atom. Adjacent MM groups (sugar-phosphate backbone, stacked and paired bases, hydrogen-bonded waters) form a movable medium layer, and the remaining MM atoms (six base pairs plus backbone and bulk waters) form a low layer optimized after the high plus medium parts converged. QM/MM optimizations at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G*. Minimum energy paths along the La coordinate were computed as optimized scans at fixed increasing values of the C6N1C2N3 and C6'N1'C2'N3' dihedrals. Conical intersection geometries were located with the conical intersection optimizer in the COBRAMM code.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF/Amber QM/MM, with three different state-averaged CASSCF single points on each optimized geometry
software: Gaussian-03 and AMBER-8 for the QM/MM optimizations with the AMBER-8 ff03 force field; MOLCAS-7.7 for the CASPT2 computations, modelling the environment with AMBER point charges; COBRAMM for the interface and conical intersection optimizer
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals for the geometry optimizations: four pi and four pi* orbitals, specifically the HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1 on each of the two stacked adenines. A larger space of twelve electrons in ten orbitals adds the two n orbitals localized on the two adenines.
active_space_protocol: One orbital set is chosen so that several state types can be described at once: taking HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1 from each adenine gives an (8,8) space in which La, Lb, charge-transfer, Ba and Bb states are all simultaneously computable, which is the prerequisite for a mechanism that passes between locally excited and charge-transfer states. Three different state-averaged single points are then run on each optimized geometry rather than one: SA-5-CAS(8,8) for the pi-pi* profiles along the two La decay routes, SA-7-CAS(12,10) adding the two nitrogen lone pairs to resolve where the n-pi* states lie along those paths, and SA-12-CAS(8,8) to resolve the two lowest charge-transfer states, one for electron transfer from Ade1 to Ade2 and one for the reverse. So the number of averaged roots and the orbital set are varied independently according to which states need resolving, on a common set of geometries.
nroots_per_mult: Five, seven or twelve states depending on the single-point scheme: SA-5 with CAS(8,8), SA-7 with CAS(12,10), and SA-12 with CAS(8,8)
electronic_structure_description: Extending the QM region from one adenine to a second stacked adenine reveals a mechanism for populating the charge-transfer state out of the initially excited bright La state: a common relaxation path exists for the two states based on the same leading geometrical deformation, the C2 puckering coordinate, allowing an energetically feasible internal conversion between the charge-transfer and La states. Direct decay from the charge-transfer state to the ground state is energetically too demanding, so deactivation can only proceed through repopulation of the original La state followed by its natural deactivation path. Charge-transfer states therefore act as natural traps and reservoirs of excited dimers, accounting for the longest lifetime component observed in time-resolved experiments. Previous studies identify C2 ring puckering, defined by the C2N1C4C5 dihedral, followed by hydrogen out-of-plane modes defined by the H2N1C4C5 dihedral, as the adenine distortion coordinate leading to the La/S0 conical intersection and the ultrafast decay of the nucleobase monomers along La. A charge-transfer excimer is the absolute excited state minimum for the water-solvated system, and the excited state population corresponds to a dark excimer.
Other: The active space is deliberately built to be state-inclusive rather than state-specific: four frontier orbitals per adenine, chosen as HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1, give an (8,8) space in which La, Lb, the two charge-transfer states and Ba and Bb all exist simultaneously. That is a hard requirement here, since the mechanism being reported is an internal conversion between a locally excited state and a charge-transfer state; a space optimized for either one alone could not describe the crossing. The paper then decouples the two knobs that are usually moved together. The orbital set is enlarged only where it must be -- adding the two adenine n orbitals to give (12,10) purely to locate the n-pi* states along the La paths -- while the number of averaged roots is varied independently from five to twelve on the same (8,8) space to resolve the two directional charge-transfer states. All three single-point schemes sit on one common set of CASSCF(8,8)-optimized geometries, so the state energies are directly comparable even though the references differ. The QM/MM layering is similarly graded, with the two stacked adenines quantum, the immediately adjacent backbone and bases movable classical, and the outer shell relaxed only after the inner parts converge. What the design does not provide is a check on whether the (8,8) geometries themselves would change under the larger space; the enlargement enters only at the single-point level.
reference_short: Conti, Nenov, Hofinger, Altavilla, Rivalta, Dumont, Orlandi & Garavelli, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2015, 17, 7291
notes: The QM region cut includes the sugar ring carbon directly linked to the base and the adjacent oxygen, producing a charge distribution on the nucleobase and its pi system that reflects the covalent link between adenine and the sugar ring. This work extends a previous study in which the second stacked adenine was neglected.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF/AMBER geometries, with the environment modelled by AMBER point charges

compound_name: Malonaldehyde, excited-state intramolecular proton transfer around a three-state conical intersection
point_group: Cs structures; the ground-state proton-transfer barrier is at the C2v configuration
geometry_source: The S0 minimum was optimized with BLYP, giving a structure very similar to MP2 and, unlike CASSCF, correctly reproducing the contraction in hydrogen bond length that is a known consequence of dynamic electron correlation; CASSCF-optimized ground-state structures are therefore described as undesirable starting points for dynamics. All other points were optimized at the CAS level, and Table 3 repeats the survey with the S0 minimum also optimized at CAS. Three minimal energy conical intersections involving S0, S1 and S2 were located with SA-3-CAS(4/4) wave functions using an unconstrained algorithm implemented in MOLPRO. Geometrical parameters of the BLYP and MP2 S0 minima agree well with the experimental structure apart from the H8C2C1 angle, which is known to be inaccurately determined experimentally.
method: State-averaged CASSCF over the lowest three singlets for ab initio multiple spawning dynamics, calibrated against multireference single and double excitation configuration interaction (MRSDCI) and EOM-CCSD
basis_set: 6-31G* for all calculations, with energies at various points compared against larger sets including added polarization and diffuse functions
active_space_orbital_description: Five active spaces were compared. CAS(4/4) comprises the lone pair localized on the oxygen atom participating in the hydrogen bond plus three pi orbitals concentrated along the backbone (n, pi1, pi1* and pi2*), with pi1 and pi1* being the HOMO and LUMO. CAS(6/6) adds a sigma and sigma* orbital localized along the O-H-O moiety. CAS(8/7) contains the entire pi manifold, the lone pair orbital and the sigma* orbital. CAS(10/8) and CAS(14/12) are the medium and extended spaces of an earlier study. Orbitals were generated from CAS(10/8) at the S0 C2v configuration. In the MRSDCI calculations using the (10/8) space, electrons in the five lowest energy molecular orbitals, the heavy-atom 1s orbitals, were not correlated.
active_space_protocol: The paper sets out explicit criteria for the target space rather than choosing one: accuracy in the Franck-Condon region with special attention to the S2/S1 gap, accuracy of the S0 barrier at the transition state, and consistency with large-active-space CASSCF augmented by MRSDCI as benchmark. The stated rationale is that CASSCF addresses static correlation but introduces dynamic correlation in an erratic and unpredictable fashion, and that large spaces bias the covalent states and homogenize bond coordination numbers through an imbalanced description of near-degeneracy and dynamic correlation, so the best space will not necessarily be the most chemically intuitive nor the largest affordable. The calibration is internal, using large-space plus correlation-corrected energy differences as benchmarks with no input from experiment, and is checked by tracing the potential surface at the higher level along the path followed by the dynamics, requiring the two surfaces to be nearly parallel. All doubly occupied orbitals are optimized unless otherwise noted, and orbitals are optimized to minimize the state-averaged energy of the lowest three singlets to eliminate state bias and root flipping.
nroots_per_mult: Three lowest singlet states, state-averaged (SA-3)
electronic_structure_description: Excitation energies and S0 proton-transfer barrier heights in eV, given as S1-S0, S2-S0, S2-S1 and the S0 barrier, with the S0 minimum optimized at BLYP. Experiment: greater than 3.5 (adiabatic), 4.7, less than 1.2, and a benchmark theoretical barrier of 0.19. CAS(4/4) 4.10, 6.32, 2.22, 0.44. CAS(6/6) 4.55, 6.33, 1.78, 1.31. CAS(8/7) 4.50, 6.26, 1.76, 1.89. CAS(10/8) 4.13, 5.67, 1.55, 0.51. CAS(14/12) 4.31, 5.70, 1.39, 1.55. MRSDCI(4/4) 4.16, 5.75, 1.59, 0.35. MRSDCI(6/6) 4.21, 5.64, 1.43, 0.36. MRSDCI(8/7) 4.18, 5.72, 1.54, 0.49. MRSDCI(10/8) 4.24, 5.35, 1.11, 0.35. EOM-CCSD 4.21, 5.26, 1.04. With the S0 minimum optimized at CAS instead of BLYP: CAS(4/4) 4.35, 6.78, 2.43, 0.61; CAS(6/6) 4.64, 6.89, 2.25, 1.49; CAS(8/7) 4.07, 6.99, 2.92, 1.53; CAS(10/8) 4.23, 6.31, 2.08, 0.61; CAS(14/12) 4.53, 6.29, 1.76, 1.85. Geometrical parameters of the S0 minimum at experiment, MP2 and BLYP: C1-C2 1.348, 1.364, 1.367 A; C2-C3 1.454, 1.443, 1.440; C1-O4 1.320, 1.333, 1.322; C3-O5 1.234, 1.250, 1.244; O4-H6 0.969, 1.000, 1.004; O5-H6 1.708, 1.738, 1.692; angle C1C2C3 119.4, 120.0, 119.4 degrees; angle O4C1C2 124.5, 124.9, 124.4. Hydrogen transfer is barrierless on S2. Three minimal energy conical intersections involving S0, S1 and S2 were located. The pi-sigma* state is dismissed as not relevant to the process studied, since reaching it costs more than 0.5 eV and alternative barrierless channels exist.
Other: This is an explicit active-space calibration, and its central result is that enlarging the space makes one target property better and another dramatically worse. The S2/S1 Franck-Condon gap falls monotonically with space size -- 2.22, 1.78, 1.76, 1.55, 1.39 eV across (4/4), (6/6), (8/7), (10/8) and (14/12) -- moving steadily toward the experimental upper bound of 1.2 eV. The S0 proton-transfer barrier does the opposite: 0.44, 1.31, 1.89, 0.51 and 1.55 eV against a benchmark of 0.19, so the smallest space is the most accurate and the chemically intuitive (8/7), which contains the whole pi manifold plus the lone pair and sigma*, is the worst of all. The explanation given is that large spaces produce more open minima and strongly destabilize the transition state, and the authors state directly that this illustrates the danger of naive active space selection based solely on size criteria. They also flag (10/8) as anomalously good and attribute it to a local minimum in an oscillatory convergence of the CAS error rather than to genuine improvement. That the MRSDCI barrier heights are stable at 0.35 to 0.49 eV across every underlying space is taken as evidence that (4/4) already saturates the static correlation needed for the ground state -- so the variation seen in bare CASSCF is erratic dynamic correlation, not missing static correlation. Forced to choose between accurate Franck-Condon gaps and accurate barriers, the authors take the barrier and adopt SA-3-CAS(4/4) for dynamics. Two further practical findings: CASSCF ground-state geometries fail to reproduce the hydrogen-bond contraction that dynamic correlation causes, making BLYP the better starting point for dynamics; and optimizing the S0 minimum at CAS instead grossly worsens the balance between excited states, raising every S2/S1 gap and shifting barriers by 0.1 to 0.35 eV.
reference_short: Coe & Martinez, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 618
notes: The experimental S1 excitation energy is a 0-0 adiabatic line and should be treated as a lower bound to the vertical values it is compared with, making the quoted S2/S1 difference an upper bound. The sigma* orbital was deemed essential to a proper description of the excited-state intramolecular proton transfer by earlier work, which is why it enters at the (6/6) level. The consistency check between dynamics-level and benchmark surfaces is described as requiring the two potential energy surfaces to be nearly parallel along the dynamics path.
correlation_correction: MRSDCI (multireference single and double excitation configuration interaction) on each CASSCF reference, with heavy-atom 1s electrons uncorrelated in the (10/8) case; EOM-CCSD used as an additional benchmark

compound_name: Anionic keto forms of oxyluciferin, OxyLH2(-1): keto-s-cis, keto-s-trans and keto-s-twist
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations of the ground and lowest-lying singlet excited states, run without symmetry constraints with all orbitals optimized and default convergence criteria. Excited-state geometries used state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest singlet excited state and the ground state with equal weights. Ground-state vibrational frequency analysis was performed with the MCKINLEY and MCLR programs.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with multistate CASPT2 (MS-CASPT2) single points using the same state averaging and active spaces; oscillator strengths from the RAS state interaction (RASSI) program
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for all atoms; diffuse functions could not be included because the molecules have C1 symmetry and larger basis sets were beyond the CASSCF software limitations
active_space_orbital_description: Three active spaces were compared: six electrons in six orbitals (three highest occupied and three lowest unoccupied), eight electrons in eight orbitals (four and four), and ten electrons in ten orbitals (five and five).
active_space_protocol: Rather than selecting one space, the study runs (6,6), (8,8) and (10,10) in parallel for every structure and property, each built by taking the corresponding number of highest occupied and lowest unoccupied orbitals. Convergence with respect to space size is then used as the criterion for adequacy. MS-CASPT2 uses the same state averaging and the same active space as the underlying CASSCF, so the comparison across spaces is clean at both levels.
nroots_per_mult: State-averaged over the ground state and lowest singlet excited state with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: Both keto-s-trans(-1) and keto-s-cis(-1) have nearly planar ring structures in their ground states at all three active space sizes, and vibrational frequency analysis confirms the rigorously planar structures as minima with all real frequencies. Keto-s-twist(-1) is a transition state with one imaginary frequency. C2-C2' bond distances between the benzothiazolyl and thiazole fragments are 1.371, 1.377 and 1.385 A for keto-s-cis(-1) and 1.367, 1.369 and 1.371 A for keto-s-trans(-1) at CASSCF(6,6), (8,8) and (10,10). Vertical emission energies for keto-s-cis(-1) are 58.4, 55.6 and 55.1 kcal/mol at CASPT2/CASSCF(6,6), (8,8) and (10,10); for keto-s-trans(-1) they are 58.0, 54.6 and 54.2 kcal/mol. The two isomers give very similar values at any given level, and the energies decrease as the space is enlarged, but the (8,8) and (10,10) results are close enough that (8,8) is judged large enough to describe the spectra of these keto forms. The predicted vertical emission wavelengths of keto-s-cis(-1), 514.2 nm at CASPT2/CASSCF(8,8) and 519.1 nm at CASPT2/CASSCF(10,10), agree well with the experimental 545 nm, so the keto emissions are predicted to be green or green-yellow. Vertical emission energies for keto-s-twist(-1) are 68.4 kcal/mol at CASPT2/CAS(8,8) and 79.4 at CASPT2/CAS(10,10); after checking the excited-state electronic configurations the (8,8) result is judged more reliable. Excited-state geometry optimization for keto-s-twist(-1) failed to converge at CASSCF(6,6). Vertical excitation energies of 70.0, 65.3 and 62.7 kcal/mol with adiabatic emission energies of 61.2, 58.6 and 59.1 kcal/mol are reported for one keto form, and 62.1 kcal/mol vertical with adiabatic emission energies of 62.2, 57.2 and 58.4 kcal/mol for another, across the (6,6), (8,8) and (10,10) spaces. Reported S1 fluorescence emission energies span 55.7 to 63.2 kcal/mol for the anionic enol forms.
Other: Three spaces are run in parallel throughout -- (6,6), (8,8) and (10,10), built simply as the three, four or five highest occupied and lowest unoccupied orbitals -- and convergence is judged by whether the answer stops changing rather than by orbital inspection. For the keto forms the vertical emission energy falls monotonically with space size (58.4, 55.6, 55.1 kcal/mol for keto-s-cis and 58.0, 54.6, 54.2 for keto-s-trans) but the (8,8) and (10,10) values agree closely, which is taken as showing that (8,8) is large enough to describe these spectra. The enol forms are less obliging: enol-s-trans gives 61.4, 61.4 and 55.7 kcal/mol, so the (6,6) and (8,8) results coincide while (10,10) moves by nearly 6 kcal/mol -- exactly the pattern that would produce a false convergence verdict if only the two smaller spaces had been run. The twisted keto form breaks the trend outright, giving 68.4 kcal/mol at (8,8) but 79.4 at (10,10), an 11 kcal/mol jump in the wrong direction, and here the authors reject the larger space on the evidence of the excited-state electronic configurations rather than accepting it on size. That twisted structure also fails to converge at all in the excited state at (6,6). So across one molecule and one property this study exhibits monotone convergence, apparent convergence that is an artefact, a non-monotone jump resolved against the larger space, and outright optimization failure. A separate basis limitation is stated plainly: the molecules have no symmetry, so diffuse functions -- normally recommended for excitation energies -- could not be afforded with the CASSCF software available, and their neglect is justified only on the assumption that all computations would be affected similarly.
reference_short: Yang & Goddard, J. Phys. Chem. A 2007, 111, 4489
notes: The result contradicts earlier AM1 work proposing the twisted keto anion as the light emitter. The keto and enol anions are the two candidate light emitters of firefly bioluminescence, with the resulting colour depending on the keto-enol equilibrium.
correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2 at the CASSCF optimized geometries, using the same active spaces and state averaging

point_group: D-infinity-h; CASSCF state averaging carried out in the D2h subgroup with the final potential energy curves corrected to D-infinity-h
geometry_source: Potential energy curves computed as a function of internuclear distance; the kinetic energy release is evaluated as the energy difference between each curve at the equilibrium distance of neutral nitrogen and the dissociation limit.
method: CASSCF followed by multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) using the CASSCF wave function as the reference; combined with time-of-flight mass spectrometry and kinetic energy release measurements from laser-induced Coulomb explosion
active_space_orbital_description: All valence electrons and orbitals are treated as active, while the 1 sigma-g and 1 sigma-u orbitals are doubly occupied in all calculations. The numerical electron and orbital counts are not stated.
active_space_protocol: A full valence space is used, with only the two core-derived orbitals held doubly occupied, and the same reference then carried into MRCI. State averaging is applied within the D2h subgroup separately for the states of 1Ag and 1Bu symmetry, with the resulting potential energy curves corrected to the true D-infinity-h symmetry afterwards. compound_name: Diels-Alder cycloaddition of cis-butadiene with ethene, spin-coupled valence bond analysis along the CASSCF reaction path

geometry_source: Transition structure and intrinsic reaction coordinate computed at the CASSCF(6,6)/4-31G level using the Gonzalez-Schlegel IRC algorithm, with six points toward products and six toward reactants in steps of 0.1 amu^(1/2) bohr along the path. Hartree-Fock calculations preceded the CASSCF wave function determination at the transition state optimization and the first IRC point to provide initial orbital guesses, and separate Hartree-Fock calculations were run at each of the remaining twelve IRC points.
method: CASSCF for the reaction path, with spin-coupled (SC) modern valence bond wave functions computed at the CASSCF geometries to analyse the electronic mechanism
software: GAUSSIAN94 for all non-spin-coupled computational work
basis_set: 4-31G for the CASSCF(6,6) transition state and IRC calculations; CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* and 3-21G results from the literature are discussed for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, the pi space of the reacting system. The spin-coupled counterpart uses the same six active orbitals, all singly occupied and nonorthogonal, with doubly occupied inactive orbitals holding the core electrons, and an active space spin function that is a general linear combination of all five unique spin-coupling schemes for a six-electron singlet.
active_space_protocol: The same six-orbital, six-electron space serves two different wave function forms: a conventional CASSCF used to locate the transition structure and trace the intrinsic reaction coordinate, and a spin-coupled valence bond function built from the same six orbitals as singly occupied nonorthogonal orbitals with a fully general six-electron singlet spin function. Because both descriptions span the same space, the spin-coupled analysis can be applied directly at geometries taken from the CASSCF path, and the fraction of CASSCF correlation energy that the much more compact spin-coupled function recovers provides the validation. The authors argue explicitly that active space methods introduce correlation just where chemical intuition suggests it is needed and that if the initial choice is wrong it is usually straightforward to modify and enlarge the space until the wave function quality becomes acceptable.

At IRC = 0.6 amu^(1/2) bohr the butadiene and ethene fragments are still well separated, with orbitals 1 and 2 forming one butadiene pi bond and the second formed similarly; the symmetry-related orbitals follow from reflection in the sigma-h plane, with orbital 1 mapping to 4, 2 to 3 and 6 to 5. At each end of the IRC segment the spin function is dominated by just one of its five components, with different components prevailing at the two ends. The whole active space undergoes substantial changes during the cycloaddition, and these occur within a short IRC interval. Literature comparisons: within the CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G* framework the diradical intermediate from the stepwise pathway lies 3.1 kcal/mol below the concerted transition structure, whereas RQCISD(T) at the same geometries places the concerted transition structure 4.3 kcal/mol below the diradical intermediate. The RQCISD(T) activation energy of the concerted transition structure relative to reactants is 25.5 kcal/mol against the CASSCF(6,6) value of 43.8 kcal/mol and an experimental estimate of 25.1 +/- 2 kcal/mol. Experimental evidence indicates the concerted pathway lies 2 to 7 kcal/mol below the stepwise alternative.

The authors' reading is that the 6-in-6 level provides an adequate description of the structural changes in the reacting system while accurate barriers require a higher-quality wave function, because CASSCF captures nondynamic correlation only within its active space whereas RQCISD(T) includes both kinds for all electrons. They cite Borden and Davidson's argument that active-space-only wave functions can be quantitatively and sometimes qualitatively wrong, including a Cope rearrangement case where dynamic correlation changes not just the barrier height but the transition structure geometry, and then defend active space methods on the grounds that they give uniform-quality descriptions across bond-breaking regions and that a wrong initial choice is usually straightforward to enlarge. The quantitative justification for the analysis here is that the compact spin-coupled function built on the same six orbitals recovers 92.9 to 95.8 percent of the CASSCF(6,6) correlation energy along the path, so the interpretive picture does not depend on the part of the wave function that the smaller function discards.

method: CASSCF with CASPT2 and multistate CASPT2, spin-orbit coupling by the complete active space state interaction (CASSI) method solved as first-order quasi-degenerate perturbation theory with the atomic mean-field spin-orbit Hamiltonian as perturbation; MRCI-SD with a posteriori configuration selection and first-order QDPT as an independent route; DFT (PBE and B3LYP) for geometries, solvation and thermochemistry
software: MOLCAS 7.0 for the CASSCF/CASPT2/CASSI calculations; ORCA 2.6.35 for the MRCI calculations; Turbomole 5.8 for the DFT calculations

For MRCI the reference space is enlarged to all five metal d-like orbitals, (6,5) or (5,5), specifically because MRCI does not relax the orbitals and an inappropriate orbital basis would otherwise introduce errors in these nonsymmetric complexes. A level shift of 0.1 au aided CASSCF convergence, an imaginary level shift of 0.1 au removed intruder states in CASPT2 with no orbitals frozen, and CASPT2 energies were placed on the main diagonal of the two-component Hamiltonian matrix to improve accuracy.

nroots_per_mult: Three lowest doublets of the M(3+) complexes, originating in the degenerate 2T2g state of ideal Oh symmetry; state-specific for the M(2+) singlet ground state
electronic_structure_description: Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling produces a systematic shift of approximately -70 mV in the reduction potentials of the studied ruthenium(II/III) complexes, while for osmium(II/III) complexes inclusion of SOC is necessary to avoid systematic errors of about 300 mV. The three lowest doublets of the oxidized complexes originate in the 2T2g state of ideal octahedral symmetry. Electronic energy differences between oxidized and reduced forms and differences in solvation Gibbs free energies are the largest contributions to the oxidation free energy and partially compensate each other, while rotational-vibrational Gibbs free energy differences are much smaller at 0.01 to 0.23 eV. An error of 100 mV corresponds to 9.6 kJ/mol, within the error bars of the quantum-chemical and solvation methods used. Splitting of the quartet states shifts the reduction potentials. This complex belongs to the series of [Ru(bipy)3](2+/3+) derivatives used in the authors' earlier work as the reference for comparing chemically similar compounds with the simplest system as internal calibration. They also note that even for complexes with no symmetry the minimum space forces the three near-degenerate highest occupied orbitals to emerge from the CASSCF optimization as suitable linear combinations of the five metal d atomic orbitals. Basis-set convergence was checked by comparing ANO-RCC contractions, with the DZP contraction already giving reasonably accurate results.

compound_name: Formaldehyde dimer, excitonic coupling of the 1A2 dark excited states in planar and crossed conformations
point_group: Planar (P) and crossed (C) dimer conformations, the latter with 45 degrees between the molecular planes
geometry_source: Six model structures of the formaldehyde dimer at intermonomer separations R of 4.0, 5.0 and 6.0 A in planar and crossed conformations, the crossed one having 45 degrees between the molecular planes.
method: CASSCF and multistate CASPT2 compared against EOM-CCSD, TD-DFT with B3LYP and CAM-B3LYP, the Tamm-Dancoff approximation, CIS and INDO/S, with excitonic couplings estimated by the fragment transition density (FTD) method
software: MOLCAS for the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 09 for the other methods
basis_set: ANO-s for the CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 calculations; 6-31G*, cc-pVTZ and aug-cc-pVTZ for the other methods
active_space_orbital_description: Not stated. The dimer is described as properly treatable within a two-state model that includes the 1A2 state of each monomer.
active_space_protocol: The active space size is not reported. The paper notes an important caveat about how the MS-CASPT2 couplings are obtained: the energies are computed at the perturbative level, but the transition densities that enter the coupling formula do not contain explicit second-order corrections, with only some correlation effects entering through the multistate scheme. The coupling therefore mixes a correlated energy denominator with a largely uncorrelated transition density.
nroots_per_mult: Two-state model including the 1A2 state of each monomer
electronic_structure_description: Singlet excitation energies of the formaldehyde monomer in eV for the 1A2 (n to pi*), 2A1 (pi to pi*) and 1B1 (sigma to pi*) states: EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-pVTZ 3.94, 8.07, 9.24; CIS/aug-cc-pVTZ 4.51, 9.44, 9.64; CIS/6-31G* 4.56, 10.01, 9.69; TD-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ 3.85, 7.33, 8.82; TD-B3LYP/6-31G* 3.99, 9.62, 8.90; TD-CAM-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ 3.84, 7.81, 8.92; TD-CAM-B3LYP/6-31G* 3.96, 9.71, 9.06; INDO/S 3.11, 8.62, 8.82. Excitonic couplings of the 1A2 dark states in meV for planar and crossed dimers at R = 4.0, 5.0 and 6.0 A: EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-pVTZ 37.3 and 6.41, 2.65 and 1.45, 0.478 and 0.424; EOM-CCSD/cc-pVTZ 30.9 and 5.52, 1.75 and 1.10, 0.327 and 0.312; MS-CASPT2/ANO-s 38.0 and 4.18, 2.68 and 0.99, 0.426 and 0.388; CASSCF/ANO-s 22.7 and 4.05, 1.55 and 0.83, 0.253 and 0.305; CIS/aug-cc-pVTZ 24.7 and 6.42, 1.98 and 1.41, 0.430 and 0.411; TD-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ 140 and 4.81, 5.56 and 1.33, 0.593 and 0.419; TDA-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ 145 and 5.70, 5.86 and 1.51, 0.652 and 0.474; TD-CAM-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ 53.0 and 4.91, 3.18 and 1.33, 0.495 and 0.412; TDA-CAM-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ 54.3 and 6.12, 3.38 and 1.53, 0.554 and 0.470. TD-DFT drastically overestimates the coupling, while CASSCF and CIS underestimate it, and INDO/S fails to describe the coupling of dark states. Transition quadrupole moments of 0.982 and 1.240 D A were obtained with the 6-31G* and aug-cc-pVTZ basis sets, close to the CIS values. Since transition multipoles vanish at lower order for these states, the coupling of singlet dark states is governed by quadrupole-quadrupole interaction, which is proportional to a computed quantity that decreases when diffuse functions are removed. Orbital interaction dominates the coupling at R = 4.0 A, producing a large difference between planar and crossed dimers; the difference V(P) minus V(C) amounts to 33.2, 1.20 and 0.054 at the three separations. The coupling decreases considerably on passing from planar to crossed conformations.
Other: The direct CASSCF versus MS-CASPT2 comparison is the finding, and it is a large one: at R = 4.0 A in the planar dimer CASSCF gives 22.7 meV against 38.0 for MS-CASPT2 and 37.3 for the EOM-CCSD reference, so the uncorrelated multiconfigurational treatment underestimates the coupling by about 40 percent while the perturbatively corrected one is essentially exact. The same pattern holds at every separation (1.55 versus 2.68 and 2.65 at 5 A; 0.253 versus 0.426 and 0.478 at 6 A), and the paper concludes explicitly that obtaining accurate values requires taking dynamic electron correlation into account. Where MS-CASPT2 does fall short is traced to the basis rather than the space: in the crossed conformations, where quadrupole-quadrupole interaction dominates, the ANO-s couplings come out low because that basis lacks diffuse functions, and the same effect is demonstrated independently by switching aug-cc-pVTZ for cc-pVTZ in the other methods. A methodological caveat is stated that affects how these numbers should be read: the MS-CASPT2 energies are perturbatively corrected but the transition densities entering the coupling are not, with only partial correlation entering through the multistate scheme, so the reported coupling is a hybrid quantity. The active space size is not reported anywhere. Placed against the other methods, CASSCF errs in the same direction as CIS and by a similar amount, while TD-B3LYP overshoots by nearly a factor of four at short range (140 against 37.3 meV).
reference_short: Voityuk, J. Phys. Chem. B 2015, 119, 7417
notes: Clusters containing two or more formaldehyde molecules are presented as good models for studying electronic interaction of dark states. In the crossed dimer the n orbitals of the monomers are of different symmetry, which affects the short-range term of the excited state coupling.
correlation_correction: Multistate CASPT2, with the caveat that the transition densities used for the couplings do not contain explicit second-order corrections

compound_name: Adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl) cofactor - tyrosine complex in B12-dependent mutases
ligand_set: corrin macrocycle with an axial base, an adenosyl ligand truncated to an ethyl group, and a tyrosine motif in close proximity
geometry_source: Structure taken from previous DFT calculations, with the adenosyl ligand of the AdoCbl-tyrosine complex simplified to a -CH2CH3 group to reduce structural complexity. None of the electronic states were optimized at the multiconfigurational level. Geometrical changes were tested, in particular the energy dependence on the Co-Nax distance, since displacement of the axial base is known to influence the corrin anion radical. QM/MM calculations were also performed on a structural model of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase based on the 4REQ crystal structure.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with second-order multireference perturbation theory in the MC-XQDPT2 formulation for dynamical correlation; DFT and QM/MM used alongside
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Initial orbitals generated from B3LYP/SV(P) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve active electrons in twelve active orbitals. The occupied set comprises two doubly occupied corrin pi orbitals, the sigma(Co-C) orbital, the 3dxz orbital, the p orbital of the tyrosine oxygen, and a tyrosine pi orbital plus an oxygen-centred p orbital. The correlating set comprises three corrin pi* orbitals, sigma*(Co-C), 4dxz, and a tyrosine pi* orbital. The p orbital of the tyrosine oxygen (a lone pair) has no natural correlating counterpart, so a corrin pi* orbital was selected in its place.
active_space_protocol: Different active spaces were tested and analysed starting from initial orbitals generated by B3LYP/SV(P), guided by previously reported CASSCF calculations on cob(I)alamin and on corroles. The space is deliberately built to span both fragments, containing the pi systems of tyrosine as well as of corrin, because the question being asked is whether a diradical state formed between the cofactor and the nearby tyrosine is energetically feasible; a space localized on either fragment alone could not answer it. One orbital pairing is not a genuine bonding-antibonding pair: the tyrosine oxygen lone pair has no correlating partner of its own, so a corrin pi* orbital was substituted, meaning the twelfth orbital correlates a lone pair with an orbital on the other fragment. State averaging was tested over different numbers of states and three were concluded sufficient. CASSCF alone, accounting only for nondynamical correlation, was found insufficient, so MC-XQDPT2 was applied on top.
nroots_per_mult: Three states, state-averaged, after testing different numbers of states
electronic_structure_description: The lowest electronic state of the cofactor-tyrosine complex is the diradical state, with the anionic state 5.3 kcal/mol higher. A third electronic state also has diradical character but arises mainly from excitation from the p orbital of the tyrosyl oxygen to the corrin pi orbital, and lies 19.5 kcal/mol above the anionic state. All three states show monotonic changes with the Co-Nax distance, with energy minima at a Co-Nax distance of about 2.3 A. The CASSCF/MC-XQDPT2 results are fully consistent with conclusions from DFT analysis.
Other: The space is constructed to hold a question rather than a molecule: twelve orbitals split across the corrin macrocycle, the Co-C bond, the cobalt d manifold and the tyrosine pi system, precisely so that a diradical state delocalized over cofactor and tyrosine can compete with a closed-shell anionic state. One consequence is a pairing that is not a real bonding-antibonding partnership -- the tyrosine oxygen lone pair has no correlating counterpart of its own, so a corrin pi* orbital was assigned to it, which means the correlation of that lone pair is described by an orbital on the other fragment entirely. The paper states directly that CASSCF alone, capturing only nondynamical correlation, was not enough to capture the essence of the problem, and that MC-XQDPT2 was required. Three caveats are given explicitly about the resulting 5.3 kcal/mol diradical-anion gap: the geometry came from DFT and none of the electronic states were optimized, the adenosyl ligand was truncated to an ethyl group, and the neutral charges were not shielded by any surrounding environment, so the energy difference is most likely overestimated and has only semiquantitative meaning. The authors present it as proof of concept rather than a converged number, and follow it with QM/MM calculations precisely because gas-phase models might artificially stabilize the diradical state or produce a spurious anionic state through improperly balanced charges. State averaging was itself tested rather than assumed, with three states found sufficient.
reference_short: Kozlowski et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 2010, 114, 5928
notes: The study addresses proton-coupled electron transfer driven enzymatic catalysis in B12-dependent mutases. Gas-phase models are noted as potentially stabilizing the diradical state artificially, which motivated the subsequent QM/MM treatment inside the enzyme.
correlation_correction: MC-XQDPT2 second-order multireference perturbation theory based on the CASSCF wave function

compound_name: 4-Pentenal O-acyloxime (model 1) and the iminyl radical from its photolysis
geometry_source: Reaction coordinate obtained as a minimum energy path at the CASSCF/6-31G* level for 4-pentenal O-acyloxime. Ground-state radical structures, the six-membered alkyl radical formed after cyclization, the connecting transition structure and the intrinsic reaction coordinate joining them were computed at the B3PW91/6-31+G* level.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF: minimum energy paths at CASSCF with the energy profile re-evaluated at CASPT2; ground-state radical chemistry treated by DFT with the B3PW91 functional
software: MOLCAS-6.4 for the CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 03 for the DFT calculations
basis_set: 6-31G* for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; 6-31+G* for the DFT calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in eleven orbitals: the pi and pi* orbitals of the imine, alkene and carbonyl moieties, the nitrogen and oxygen lone pairs, and the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the N-O bond.
active_space_protocol: The space is assembled to cover every chromophore in the molecule plus the bond that breaks: three pi/pi* pairs for the imine, alkene and carbonyl groups, both heteroatom lone pairs so that n-pi* states are available, and the sigma/sigma* pair of the N-O bond undergoing homolysis. Including both the imine pi* and the N-O sigma* in one space is what allows their coupling to be described, and that coupling is the mechanistic conclusion of the paper. The zeroth-order wave function for the CASPT2 single points is a three-root state average over S0, S1 and S2, and the same state-averaged wave function was used elsewhere where necessary to avoid convergence problems.
nroots_per_mult: Three-root state average over S0, S1 and S2
electronic_structure_description: S2 is identified as the spectroscopic state, and its relaxation leads directly to N-O bond breaking through coupling between the imine pi* and the sigma*(N-O) orbitals, generating acetyl and iminyl radicals in the ground state; this facile bond cleavage underlies the use of such systems as photoinitiators for UV-curable coatings. Consistent with the computed minimum energy path, in which relaxation on the S2 surface leads directly to N-O cleavage, no fluorescence was detected experimentally. A CASPT2 calculation on the iminyl radical shows that both its S1 and S2 excited states lie more than 70 kcal/mol above the ground state, establishing that the remainder of the reaction is ground-state chemistry and justifying the switch to DFT. The iminyl radical and the six-membered alkyl radical formed after cyclization are connected through a transition structure confirmed by an intrinsic reaction coordinate calculation; ring closure must surpass a barrier of about 14 kcal/mol, with a gradual uphill segment corresponding to conformational adjustment followed by a progressively steeper incline corresponding to radical addition to the alkene, and the forming N-C distance at the transition structure is 2.095 A. Model 3 shows a preference of more than 3 kcal/mol. Experimentally, an O-acyloxime shows an emissive state at room temperature and 77 K with lifetimes of 10.6 to 10.8 microseconds suggestive of triplet parentage, a quenching rate constant of about 2.2e5 per M per s, and a quantum yield of 0.05 +/- 0.01 for product formation in deoxygenated acetonitrile irradiated at 313 nm. Triplet energies are estimated to be between 56 and 50 kcal/mol, with one energy given as 42 kcal/mol.
Other: The active space is what carries the mechanism: putting the imine pi* and the N-O sigma* in the same eleven-orbital space is precisely what permits the coupling between them that the paper identifies as the reason relaxation on S2 leads straight to bond homolysis. A space built around the chromophores alone, without the N-O sigma/sigma* pair, could not have produced that result, and one built around the breaking bond alone could not have identified S2 as the spectroscopic state. The space is then used to decide where the multiconfigurational treatment can stop: a CASPT2 calculation on the iminyl radical places both S1 and S2 more than 70 kcal/mol above the ground state, which establishes that everything after the homolysis is single-state ground-state chemistry and licenses the switch to B3PW91 DFT for the cyclization, regioselectivity and substituent effects. That is an unusually clean handoff, justified by a computed gap rather than assumed. A three-root state average over S0, S1 and S2 provides the zeroth-order wave function for the CASPT2 single points, and the same averaged wave function had to be used elsewhere purely to avoid convergence problems, so the averaging serves a numerical as well as a physical purpose. The computed picture is corroborated experimentally by the absence of any detected fluorescence, consistent with a surface that leads directly to dissociation.
reference_short: Alonso, Campos, Rodriguez & Sampedro, J. Org. Chem. 2008, 73, 2234
notes: B3PW91 was chosen over pure DFT methods because it has been shown to describe bond cleavage more accurately and had proved satisfactory in previous radical chemistry studies. Calculated transitions for the model compound are compared with the experimental UV spectrum of a related compound.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points re-evaluating the CASSCF minimum energy path energy profile, using a three-root state-averaged CASSCF zeroth-order wave function

point_group: C2v; all optimized geometries came out with all atoms coplanar
geometry_source: Full geometry optimization at the all-pi-electron CASSCF level with the 6-31G* basis, restarting each calculation from the geometry and orbitals of the previous run until a stationary point was found. The GAMESS CASSCF implementation does not allow the configuration state function coefficients to relax during geometry optimization, so large geometry changes altered the coefficients and increased the gradients enough to require reoptimization; at most two restarts were needed. Single-point MCQDPT2 energies were computed at the optimized CASSCF geometries with the 1s orbitals on heavy atoms frozen.
method: All-pi-electron CASSCF with full geometry optimization, followed by single-point MCQDPT2 multireference perturbation theory
basis_set: 6-31G* as implemented in GAMESS and PC GAMESS
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven pi orbitals, the complete pi system of the dimethylene heterocycle. The same space is used for the CASSCF geometry optimizations and for the MCQDPT2 single points, the latter with heavy-atom 1s orbitals frozen.
active_space_protocol: The all-pi-electron space is applied unchanged to every member of the series so that the effect of the heteroatom on the singlet-triplet gap is not confounded with any change in the orbital description. Earlier work on m-xylylene and its analogues had shown that including pi-electron correlation is crucial for reliable singlet-triplet gaps, and the relatively small size and high C2v symmetry of these systems made full geometry optimization at this level feasible. MCQDPT2 single points use the identical space with heavy-atom 1s orbitals frozen.
electronic_structure_description: Singlet and triplet energies and the singlet-triplet gap (delta E(S-T) = -2J, negative meaning a singlet ground state). At the CASSCF level: ES -245.24642 hartree, ET -245.23477 hartree, gap -7.31 kcal/mol. At the MCQDPT2 level: ES -246.04227 hartree, ET -246.04653 hartree, gap 2.67 kcal/mol. This compound has a triplet ground state at the MCQDPT2 level, one of only four in the series (9a, 9b, 9g and 9h) with gaps of 2.67, 4.22, 7.25 and 7.37 kcal/mol respectively. Across the whole series only 9b has a triplet ground state at the CASSCF level, with a singlet(1 1A1)-triplet(1 3B2) gap of 1.6 kcal/mol, while 12 and 9a and 9c through 9m have singlet 1A1 ground states at that level; four structures, 9a, 9b, 9g and 9h, acquire triplet ground-state character at MCQDPT2. The results agree with earlier AM1-CI predictions that 2,5-furandiyl and 2,5-pyrrolediyl systems possess low-spin ground states, but contradict them in finding high-spin states lower for 9a, 9b, 9g and 9h. The singlet-triplet gap correlates with Lowdin charge redistribution on switching state multiplicity, and with the electronegativity of the heteroatom and the resulting electron density there.
Other: A single all-pi (8,7) space is applied to all fourteen dimethylene diradicals, and holding it fixed across the whole heteroatom series is what makes the trend interpretable: the singlet-triplet gap varies from -48.55 to +1.57 kcal/mol at CASSCF purely through the heteroatom, with no change in the orbital description. The perturbative correction then matters decisively and unevenly. At CASSCF only one compound (9b, X = BH2-) has a triplet ground state, at 1.57 kcal/mol; at MCQDPT2 four do -- 9a, 9b, 9g and 9h at 2.67, 4.22, 7.25 and 7.37 kcal/mol -- so dynamical correlation converts three additional singlet ground states into triplets. The shifts are far from uniform in magnitude: 9a moves by 9.98 kcal/mol and 9i by 13.62, while 9f moves by only 3.26, so a rigid offset would not reproduce the reordering. That result also contradicts earlier AM1-CI predictions for two of the systems while agreeing for others. A practical limitation of the implementation is documented: the GAMESS CASSCF does not relax the configuration state function coefficients during geometry optimization, so when an optimization step produced a large geometry change the coefficients also changed, raising the gradients enough to force reoptimization; at most two restarts were needed per structure, with each run restarted from the previous geometry and orbitals. The pi-only space and the resulting coplanarity of all atoms in every optimized structure are consistent, and earlier work on m-xylylene analogues had established that pi-electron correlation is crucial for reliable singlet-triplet gaps in this class.

State-averaged CASSCF(6,6) was used to determine geometries in the intersection space, with conical intersections optimized in the (f-2)-dimensional intersection space by the method of Bearpark et al. Harmonic vibrational frequencies were computed analytically at the CASSCF level to characterize stationary points as minima (all real frequencies) or transition states (one imaginary frequency). Optimization converged when the maximum force and its root-mean-square fell below 0.00045 and 0.00005 hartree/bohr. Localization of minima, transition states and conical intersection minima was performed in Cartesian coordinates, so results are independent of any specific choice of internal variables. Fourteen of the reactions were probed further by intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations using the Gonzalez-Schlegel algorithm.

compound_name: Ozone (O3), ground state equilibrium geometry and harmonic vibrational frequencies
geometry_source: Equilibrium geometries and harmonic vibrational frequencies computed at each level; a ladder of CASSCF active spaces was optimized with the cc-pVDZ basis and the same trends confirmed with cc-pVTZ.
method: Tailored coupled cluster singles and doubles (TCCSD) using Hartree-Fock and CASSCF orbitals, with CASSCF, CAS-CI on Hartree-Fock orbitals, Hartree-Fock, CCSD and CCSD(T) computed for comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in nine spatial orbitals, 5a1 3b2 1b1 4b2 6a1 1a2 2b1 7a1 5b2, in which the 2p orbitals of each oxygen atom are active. Smaller spaces on the ladder are CAS(2,2) with orbitals 1a2 and 2b1; CAS(6,5) with 5a1 6a1 1a2 2b1 5b2; CAS(8,7) with 5a1 4b2 6a1 1a2 2b1 7a1 5b2; and CAS(10,8) with 5a1 1b1 4b2 6a1 1a2 2b1 7a1 5b2.
active_space_protocol: The space is built by a ladder driven by stability analysis of the restricted Hartree-Fock wave function rather than by chemical intuition. The RHF instability with the cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ bases corresponds to the 1a2 to 2b1 excitation, which alone would suggest CAS(2,2); but several other excitations have very small positive eigenvalues and must also be covered for a qualitatively correct SCF wave function. The excitation with the smallest positive eigenvalue is essentially a linear combination of 5a1 to 2b1, 6a1 to 2b1 and 1a2 to 5b2, which recommends CAS(6,5). The space is then extended in the same way, one shell of near-instability at a time, through CAS(8,7) and CAS(10,8) until satisfactory results are reached at CAS(12,9). The acceptance criterion is not energy but whether the correct ordering of the three vibrational frequencies is reproduced.
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF equilibrium geometries and harmonic frequencies with the cc-pVDZ basis, given as O-O bond length in angstroms, bond angle in degrees, and the nu1(a1), nu2(a1) and nu3(b2) frequencies in cm-1, with relative errors from experiment in percent. Hartree-Fock: 1.197 (5.90), 119.0 (1.88), 1533 (35.1), 867 (21.1), 1423 (30.7). CAS(2,2): 1.249 (1.81), 115.3 (1.28), 1160 (2.20), 794 (10.9), 1460 (34.1). CAS(6,5): 1.252 (1.57), 117.3 (0.43), 1170 (3.08), 764 (6.70), 1695 (55.6). CAS(8,7): 1.290 (1.42), 114.8 (1.71), 1039 (8.46), 707 (1.26), 1193 (9.55). CAS(10,8): 1.289 (1.34), 115.3 (1.28), 1049 (7.58), 706 (1.40), 1274 (17.0). CAS(12,9): 1.290 (1.42), 116.4 (0.34), 1059 (6.70), 696 (2.79), 964 (11.5). Experiment: 1.272, 116.8, 1135, 716, 1089. Within a simple picture the electronic ground state of ozone is a two-determinant state built from the (core) 4b2^2 6a1^2 1a2^2 and (core) 4b2^2 6a1^2 2b1^2 configurations, equivalent to a CAS(2,2), but earlier work shows that TCSCF gives qualitatively incorrect results and that adding dynamic correlation with MRCISD or Brillouin-Wigner MRCC is not enough to recover accurate results. With the cc-pVTZ basis, TCCSD/CAS-CI significantly improves the equilibrium geometry and the totally symmetric frequencies nu1 and nu2 relative to CCSD, while the asymmetric stretch nu3 deteriorates, explained by the Hartree-Fock orbitals being optimized for only one of the two dominant configurations. Previous CCSD(T) studies show the frequency varying from 970 to 1081 cm-1 with basis set. Earlier work obtained the most successful results from a ten-reference MRCI with a 4s3p2d atomic natural orbital basis, and CASPT2 results were more or less the same as CASSCF.
Other: The active space ladder here is selected by a criterion that is neither energetic nor chemical: the ordering of the three vibrational frequencies. The naive two-determinant picture of ozone gives CAS(2,2), and Hartree-Fock stability analysis confirms an instability corresponding to the 1a2 to 2b1 excitation; but several further excitations have very small positive eigenvalues, and the space must be grown to cover them, through CAS(6,5), CAS(8,7) and CAS(10,8), before CAS(12,9) finally reproduces the correct frequency order. The intermediate results show why energy or geometry alone would have been a misleading guide: CAS(2,2) already gives a bond length within 1.81 percent and an angle within 1.28 percent of experiment, and CAS(6,5) improves the angle to 0.43 percent, yet its asymmetric stretch is 1695 cm-1 against an experimental 1089, an error of 55.6 percent -- worse than Hartree-Fock's 30.7 percent. The error in nu3 does not fall monotonically either: 34.1, 55.6, 9.55, 17.0 and finally 11.5 percent across the ladder, so any two adjacent spaces could have suggested false convergence. The paper notes that the CAS reference would normally demand very expensive MRCISD or MRCC treatment of dynamic correlation, whereas TCCSD is almost as cheap as standard CCSD and CASSCF with CAS(12,9) is still less expensive than CCSD(T) in both basis sets. A residual limitation is stated: with Hartree-Fock orbitals the totally symmetric frequencies improve while the asymmetric stretch deteriorates, because those orbitals are optimized for only one of the two dominant configurations.

notes: Earlier CASSCF work on ozone used the same CAS(12,9) space. The authors note that the number of configurations could be reduced by careful selection of important ones, but that this procedure could be complicated. Basis set error can vary alongside the error due to the method itself.
correlation_correction: Dynamic correlation introduced through the tailored CCSD ansatz on the CAS reference rather than by MRCISD or MRCC

geometry_source: All geometry optimizations performed in C1 symmetry; the ttt rotamer yielded C2h and the tet and etc rotamers also had symmetry, while the remaining rotamers had lower symmetry. Initial geometry searches used restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock wave functions, followed by CASSCF optimizations in both basis sets. In the STO-3G basis only planar geometries were examined. Bond lengths are converged to +/- 0.0005 A. All C-H bonds lie between 1.07 and 1.10 A.
method: CASSCF geometry optimizations and vertical excitation energies, with restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock for initial searches and vibrational analyses
active_space_orbital_description: All pi electrons distributed among the six lowest pi valence orbitals. In rotamers that are distinctly nonplanar the three highest occupied orbitals are still essentially pi-like, as are the three correlating orbitals obtained in the CASSCF treatment.
active_space_protocol: The space is specified as all pi electrons in the six lowest pi valence orbitals and applied identically to all six rotamers, including the two that deviate significantly from planarity, on the grounds that the relevant orbitals retain pi character even when the molecular framework twists. Excitation energies are computed from CASSCF results for each state involved in the transition, as vertical transitions from the CASSCF equilibrium geometry of the ground state of the given rotamer. The authors state that the limited correlation treatment is not intended to give accurate absolute excitation energies but that the relative ordering across rotamers should still be meaningful.
nroots_per_mult: Two lowest doublet pi excited states
electronic_structure_description: Relative ground-state energies in kcal/mol with respect to the ttt rotamer, for tet, ctt, etc, cct and ccc: STO-3G ROHF 1.85, 2.93, 5.79 (planar only); STO-3G CASSCF 2.14, 2.48, 5.07; 6-31G ROHF 2.27, 3.80, 7.57, 8.53, 14.18; 6-31G CASSCF 2.70, 3.37, 6.90, 8.62, 13.99. Reference ttt energies are -228.76496 hartree (STO-3G ROHF), -228.85212 (STO-3G CASSCF), -231.47014 (6-31G ROHF) and -231.53481 (6-31G CASSCF). The ttt rotamer is the most stable in all cases, and independent of basis set or correlation treatment all six rotamers are stationary points, the ground-state ordering is ttt, tet, ctt, etc, cct, ccc, and two rotamers are clearly nonplanar. Inclusion of correlation decreases the relative energy of the ctt and etc rotamers while raising that of tet. The first two pi excitation energies in eV from CASSCF, given as 6-31G then STO-3G: ccc 2.15 and 3.30; cct 2.14 and 3.34; etc 2.06 and 3.49, with STO-3G 2.22 and 3.54; tet 2.17 and 3.50, with STO-3G 2.28 and 3.57; ctt 2.11 and 3.53, with STO-3G 2.25 and 3.58; ttt 2.16 and 3.59, with STO-3G 2.28 and 3.61. First excitation energies vary by at most 0.1 eV across rotamers in either basis and second excitation energies by about 0.3 eV, with STO-3G results 0.05 to 0.10 eV higher throughout. For the more intense second excitation the 6-31G CASSCF ordering is ccc below cct below etc below tet below ctt below ttt. The ttt rotamer is planar and the most stable of the six in every basis and wave function. Its CASSCF geometry has C-C bond lengths of 1.375, 1.408 and 1.399 A with both central dihedral angles at 180 degrees in the 6-31G basis, and 1.382, 1.429 and 1.417 A in STO-3G. No evidence of symmetry breaking was found at the SCF level for this rotamer, which converged to C2h within numerical convergence limits even when the geometry search began from a C1 configuration, in contrast to the butadiene cation where ROHF in C1 symmetry produced artificially nonsymmetrical geometries.
Other: The active space is defined by a rule that survives loss of symmetry: all pi electrons distributed among the six lowest pi valence orbitals. The paper notes explicitly that in some rotamers the molecule is distinctly nonplanar, yet the three highest occupied orbitals remain essentially pi-like, as do the three correlating orbitals produced by the CASSCF, so the same space is meaningful across planar and twisted conformers alike. That is what makes the six-rotamer comparison legitimate. The space also solves a symmetry-breaking problem carried over from earlier work: in the butadiene cation, ROHF wave functions optimized in C1 symmetry produced artificially nonsymmetrical geometries because the wave function was trying to correlate the three pi electrons, and that artefact disappeared at higher correlation levels. Here no such breaking was found at the SCF level, with the ttt rotamer converging to C2h even when started from C1. What correlating the pi electrons does change is systematic and modest: CASSCF gives somewhat longer bond lengths than ROHF in either basis, and it lowers the relative energies of the ctt and etc rotamers while raising that of tet, though the ground-state ordering ttt, tet, ctt, etc, cct, ccc is unchanged by basis set or correlation treatment. The excitation energies are the more discriminating test and expose a limit of the treatment: the first excitation varies by at most 0.1 eV across all six rotamers and the second by only about 0.3 eV, so the rotamer ordering for the second transition (ccc below cct below etc below tet below ctt below ttt) rests on differences smaller than the 0.2 to 0.3 eV basis-set shift between STO-3G and 6-31G, and the two bases disagree on which pairs are near-degenerate. The authors are explicit that with this limited correlation treatment they do not aim to predict absolute excitation energies, only relative ones.

compound_name: HCN, vibrational band strengths and dipole moment surface
point_group: Calculations performed in the Cs point group on the lowest A' state, corresponding to the X 1Sigma+ state in C-infinity-v symmetry
geometry_source: Energies and dipole moments computed on grids of nuclear geometries: 384 geometries with the smaller active space, a subgroup of 50 nuclear configurations for the contracted CI, and a subgroup of 83 configurations for the full valence active space and its contracted CI. A basis set test used two additional points, one linear with C-N 2.185 and C-H 2.011 bohr and one with a 65 degree bond angle at the same distances, the large angle chosen to probe gross rather than local variations of the dipole moment.
method: CASSCF in the approximate super-CI formulation, followed by contracted CI (CCI) calculations of energies and dipole moments, used to derive vibrational band strengths
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: A smaller basis for the main surface, with a larger 6s5p2d basis for C and N and 4s3p for H used at two geometries to check basis set sensitivity
active_space_orbital_description: The main valence configuration of the ground state is 3sigma2 4sigma2 5sigma2 1pi4, written in Cs symmetry as (3a')2 (4a')2 (5a')2 (6a')2 (1a'')2. In the first stage the 7a' (2pi), 8a' (6sigma) and 2a'' (2pi) orbitals were added as active orbitals to those of the main configuration, giving a (6a', 2a'') space; full distribution of 10 electrons among these orbitals gives 616 configurations. In the second stage the 9a' orbital was included to provide a full valence space description, a (7a', 2a'') space, whose CASSCF expansion contains 2930 configurations.
active_space_protocol: Two active spaces are used in a staged calculation: a smaller (6a', 2a'') space applied to all 384 nuclear geometries, and a full valence (7a', 2a'') space applied to a subgroup of 83 geometries, each followed by contracted CI. The larger space is restricted to fewer geometries purely on cost grounds. An attempted further reduction failed: when the 3sigma orbital was removed from the large active space to make the calculations more tractable, convergence problems were encountered, so that orbital had to be retained. The approximate super-CI formulation of CASSCF was used, converging to six decimal figures in the energy in five to eight iterations.
nroots_per_mult: Lowest A' state
electronic_structure_description: Vibrationally averaged dipole moments in debye include 2.963 for the 000 state. Computed and experimental transition dipole moments include (001 to 010) 0.1 against 0.13 +/- 0.01; (000 to 020) 8.3 against 8.5 +/- 0.2 with another value of 5.6; and (000 to 101) 0.1 against 0.27 +/- 0.03 with another value of 0.32. Following earlier convention the C-N stretch is labelled nu1, the bend nu2 and the C-H stretch nu3. An earlier derivation of the (000 to 010) transition moment from intensity distribution studies of the 14 micron nu2 band gave 0.147 D, but that derivation contains a factor of root two error and the correct value is 0.104 D. Apart from the discrepancy for the nu2 fundamental, agreement between theory and experiment is reasonably good, indicating that the many overtone intensities computed but not tabulated are probably of adequate quality for astrophysical applications. Calculations covered vibrational bands in the interval 3000 to 10000 cm-1.
Other: This paper tests two candidate explanations for a specific failure and rejects both, which is more informative than a successful convergence check. The computed intensity of the nu2 fundamental disagrees substantially with experiment, so the authors first ask whether the dipole moment surface is at fault by repeating two representative geometries with a much larger 6s5p2d/4s3p basis; the differences between the two basis sets are small and do not at all explain the error, and the small basis is said to perform surprisingly well. They then ask whether the CASSCF space is too small, and report that the two active spaces tried -- the (6a', 2a'') space with 616 configurations and the full valence (7a', 2a'') space with 2930 -- showed no large difference in the dipole moment variations either. The conclusion drawn is that perhaps even more diffuse basis functions together with a larger active space may be needed, leaving the discrepancy unresolved rather than papered over. A separate practical finding concerns which orbitals cannot be dropped: removing the 3sigma orbital from the large active space to make the calculations more tractable produced convergence problems, so a deep orbital that contributes little to the chemistry still had to be kept for numerical reasons. The staged design -- small space over 384 geometries, full valence space over only 83 -- means the surface itself is built at the smaller space with the larger one serving as a spot check.
reference_short: Jorgensen, Almlof, Gustafsson, Larsson & Siegbahn, J. Chem. Phys. 1985, 83, 3034
notes: HCN has been observed as a constituent of carbon-rich stellar atmospheres, and accounting for HCN opacity extends the model atmospheres; the calculations target transitions expected to be most important for carbon-star atmosphere structure. Attempts had previously been made to construct the HCN dipole moment function from measured dipole moments.

geometry_source: Initial SCF-level geometry optimizations for a number of BCN structures with the Huzinaga-Dunning DZP basis, a [4s2p1d] contraction of a (9s5p1d) primitive set, followed by single-point CCSD(T) at the optimum geometries; from these only the linear BNC and BCN structures needed further consideration. Geometries, harmonic frequencies and double-harmonic infrared intensities were then obtained at the full-valence CASSCF level using analytical second derivatives. A quartic force field was subsequently computed at CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ on a grid, with pure spherical harmonics and 1s-like core orbitals constrained doubly occupied.
method: Full-valence CASSCF for geometries, harmonic frequencies and infrared intensities, with CCSD(T) quartic force fields for anharmonic spectroscopic constants
software: Calculations run on an IBM RS/6000 Model 365 workstation
basis_set: cc-pVDZ, a [3s2p1d] contraction of an (8s4p1d) primitive set, for the CASSCF work; cc-pVTZ, a [4s3p2d1f] contraction of a (10s5p2d1f) primitive set, for the CCSD(T) quartic force fields; DZP for the initial SCF survey; TZ2P and [5s4p2d1f] used in comparisons
active_space_orbital_description: Full valence active space: all configuration state functions that can be generated by arranging 12 valence electrons in 12 valence orbitals, written as CASSCF[12,12].
active_space_protocol: The full valence space is adopted so that internal correlation is treated exactly within the one-particle basis while no external correlation is included at all. Because higher angular momentum polarization functions are intended mainly to account for external correlation, the smaller cc-pVDZ basis is deemed adequate for the CASSCF calculations, with the larger cc-pVTZ reserved for the CCSD(T) treatment. Since CASSCF and CCSD(T) agree well and these systems are dominated by a single reference configuration, no multireference calculations beyond the full-valence CASSCF were attempted.
electronic_structure_description: Full-valence CASSCF/cc-pVDZ gives harmonic frequencies of 2071, 1177 and 55 cm-1, in excellent agreement with the experimental fundamentals of 2040.0192, 1226.6 and 63.4165(40) cm-1, an agreement described as rather surprising given that no external correlation is included; the computed bond length is predictably considerably too large. At CCSD(T)/TZ2P the bond distance closely approaches the experimental 1.2968(10) A and the stretching frequencies are little changed, but the low bending frequency becomes imaginary, a common problem with the TZ2P basis previously observed for C3 at the CISD level with a Davidson correction. At CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ the frequencies become 2096, 1195 and 79 cm-1, giving no barrier to linearity in agreement with a recent study based on CASSCF/[5s4p2d1f] calculations and analysis of experiment. Including anharmonicity gives fundamentals of 2045, 1214 and 44 cm-1; the first two agree excellently with experiment while the third is distinctly underestimated, unsurprisingly since second-order rovibrational perturbation theory breaks down for such a low frequency and terms higher than quartic in the bending would be needed. The experimental rotational constant Bq is 0.4305723 cm-1, and the extremely low bending frequency is noted as a source of problems.
Other: The full-valence (12,12) space is described in terms of what it does and does not contain: it is an exact treatment of internal correlation within the given one-particle basis but includes no external correlation at all. That framing drives a deliberate basis choice -- since higher angular momentum polarization functions exist mainly to capture external correlation, the modest cc-pVDZ set is judged adequate for the CASSCF work, while the CCSD(T) treatment gets cc-pVTZ. The C3 calibration then shows how far internal correlation alone can carry the answer: full-valence CASSCF/cc-pVDZ gives harmonic frequencies of 2071, 1177 and 55 cm-1 against experimental fundamentals of 2040.0, 1226.6 and 63.4, agreement the authors themselves call rather surprising given that no external correlation is included. The property that internal correlation alone cannot get is the bond length, which is predictably far too long. So the space is excellent for the curvature of the surface and poor for its location, which is exactly the division of labour that motivates using CASSCF for frequencies and CCSD(T) for geometries. A separate and instructive failure appears on the CCSD(T) side rather than the CASSCF side: at CCSD(T)/TZ2P the low bending frequency of C3 becomes imaginary, a known problem with that basis previously seen at CISD with a Davidson correction, and it recovers to 79 cm-1 at CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ. The paper also states plainly that these systems are dominated by a single reference configuration, with CASSCF and CCSD(T) agreeing well, so no attempt was made to perform multireference calculations beyond the full-valence CASSCF itself.

notes: C3 serves as the calibration system for the BCN and BNC predictions, its experimental data being well established.

geometry_source: Stationary points optimized at the CASSCF/6-31G* level, except the concerted transition structures, which could not be fully optimized at this level; for those, constrained optimizations were carried out at the RHF-optimized bond-making and bond-breaking distances and the energies then zero-point corrected using scaled RHF values so that they could be compared with the other computed enthalpies. Zero-point corrections used the recommended scaling of Scott and Radom for BLYP/6-31G* and the values of Curtiss, Raghavachari, Redfern and Pople for RHF/6-31G* and B3LYP/6-31G*.
method: CASSCF with an appropriate active space per system, compared against RHF, BLYP, B3LYP and CASPT2N within a hierarchy of methods
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals: the four pi orbitals plus the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the bond that is broken. This is stated to fully describe the parent Cope rearrangement.
active_space_protocol: The parent system requires only the four pi orbitals plus the sigma/sigma* pair of the breaking bond, and the space is enlarged for the unsaturated analogues by adding the pi orbitals those molecules possess, so that every system gets the same construction rule applied to its own pi system.
electronic_structure_description: Activation enthalpies at 0 K in kcal/mol with activation entropies in eu in parentheses, computed for the concerted reactions across the method hierarchy: 1,5-hexadiene 56.0 (-1.7), 30.8, 29.7 (-9.7), 34.2 (-10.2), 33.5 (-13.8); 1-hexen-5-yne 59.5 (-6.4), 30.7, 27.8 (-7.6), 33.0 (-8.0), 32.7 (-11.6); 1,5-hexadiyne 63.4 (-4.3), 31.6, 26.5 (-5.3), 32.7 (-5.1), 34.4 (-9.4); 1,2-hexadien-5-yne 60.3 (-7.1), 26.7, 28.4 (-6.0), 33.7 (-8.8), 30.8 (-11.7). Relative energies in kcal/mol of optimized structures along stepwise and concerted pathways at CASSCF/6-31G*, given as reactant, diradical, product, reactant-to-diradical transition state, diradical-to-product transition state, concerted transition state, and concerted transition state with zero-point correction: 1,5-hexadiene 0.0, 46.8, 0.0, 48.0, 48.0, 48.7, 46.9; 1-hexen-5-yne 0.0, 47.5, 6.6, 48.2, 49.1, 50.7, 49.5; 1,5-hexadiyne 0.0, 45.9, 8.6, 48.1, 47.3, 51.2, 49.3; 1,2-hexadien-5-yne 0.0, 39.4, 0.0, 39.6, 39.6, 42.6, 41.1. Except for the CASSCF results, each method predicts a concerted pathway through an aromatic transition structure; the CASSCF/6-31G* results predict a stepwise mechanism, though the computed energy difference between the two pathways is less than 2 kcal/mol in each case. Compared with experimental data the CASSCF barriers are overestimated by some 20 to 30 kcal/mol, an overestimate rising from about 22 kcal/mol for the parent system to some 34 kcal/mol for the 1,2-hexadien-5-yne system, since stretching of a pi bond is involved; second-order perturbation methods recover some 15 to 20 kcal/mol. Several methods predict all the activation energies to fall in a narrow 33 to 34 kcal/mol range. For this parent system the reactant and product are degenerate at 0.0 kcal/mol, the diradical lies at 46.8, both transition states at 48.0, and the concerted transition structure at 48.7 falling to 46.9 with zero-point correction. The reactant absolute energy differs by 1 kcal/mol from an earlier computed value, while absolute energies agree to within 0.1 kcal/mol with two other published sets.
Other: The active space is grown system by system according to what unsaturation is present -- (6,6) for the parent Cope rearrangement (four pi orbitals plus the sigma and sigma* of the bond that breaks), (8,8) for the ene-yne by adding a pi pair, and (10,10) for the diyne and allene-yne by adding two further out-of-plane pi orbitals -- so that each molecule receives the same physical description of its own pi system. That uniformity of construction is what makes the four barriers comparable, and it exposes a clean qualitative disagreement: CASSCF/6-31G* predicts a stepwise mechanism through a diradical intermediate for every system, while every other method in the hierarchy predicts a concerted pathway through an aromatic transition structure. The margin is small in each case, under 2 kcal/mol between the two pathways, so the mechanistic verdict rests on differences well inside the error of the reference-only treatment. Two further consequences follow from using CASSCF without dynamic correlation. The absolute barriers are overestimated by roughly 20 to 30 kcal/mol against experiment, and the overestimate is not constant across the series but grows from about 22 kcal/mol for the parent to some 34 kcal/mol for the allene-yne, because stretching a pi bond is involved -- so the error is systematically larger where more pi character is broken, exactly the direction that would distort a trend. Adding perturbative correlation recovers roughly 15 to 20 kcal/mol of that. A practical limitation is also documented: the concerted transition structures could not be fully optimized at the CASSCF level at all, so constrained optimizations were performed at RHF bond-making and bond-breaking distances and then zero-point corrected with scaled RHF values, meaning the concerted energies in the table are not from a stationary point on the CASSCF surface.

geometry_source: CASSCF S1 and S0 energies and gradients computed at the two-root state-averaged level with equal 0.5 weights. Excited state relaxation paths determined by an established methodology; the one-dimensional cross-section of the intersection space was computed with a strategy combining the intrinsic relaxation direction method for finding local steepest-descent directions from a nonstationary point with the conical intersection optimization method for locating conical intersections as stationary points within the intersection space, giving intersection space descent paths. An intrinsic relaxation direction is calculated by locating the energy minimum on a hyperspherical cross-section of the potential energy surface centred on an initial point. active_space_protocol: A minimal six-electron, six-pi-orbital space is used with two-root state averaging at equal 0.5 weights, which is required because the entire study concerns the S1/S0 intersection seam and both states must be described on the same footing everywhere along it. The state averaging also forces a bookkeeping correction: the energies of the first five points along the photoisomerization minimum energy path had to be rescaled by state-averaged single-point calculations so that they would match the remaining points, which were computed at the state-averaged level throughout.
