electronic_structure_description: CASSCF/6-31G* absolute and relative energies, the latter in kcal/mol relative to the lowest-energy conical intersection CI92. Franck-Condon point: single-state S0 -248.26236 and S1 -248.07879 hartree; state-averaged S0 -248.24918 at -59.43 and S1 -248.07206 at 51.72. LP66: S0 -248.1422 at 7.70, S1 -248.13875 at 9.87. CI70: S0 -248.1456 at 5.56, S1 -248.14278 at 7.34. CI92: S0 -248.15455 at -0.05, S1 -248.15447 at 0.00. CI0: S0 -248.04326 at 69.79, S1 -248.04302 at 69.94. CI73': S0 -248.14250 at 7.56, S1 -248.14247 at 7.53. The planar transition structure SP has a single-state S1 energy of -248.08904 hartree. The S1 Z to E photoisomerization path terminates at a 70 degree twisted conical intersection rather than at the lowest-energy conical intersection at 92 degrees. The excited state relaxation path coordinate not only enters the intersection space at CI70 but remains substantially coincident with it up to CI92, and the same intersection space segment extends backward toward the Franck-Condon point, so in that region it runs roughly parallel to the relaxation path. The CI0 point lies 18 kcal/mol above the Franck-Condon point while CI70 lies 7 kcal/mol above CI92. The intersection space cross-section is defined by two branches, CI70 to CI92 and CI0 to CI70. Pyramidalization in the intersection structures is noted as reminiscent of the conical intersection structure found in ethylene.

The state averaging leaves a visible artefact in the reported data: the energies of the first five points along the photoisomerization path had to be rescaled by state-averaged single-point calculations to be commensurable with the remaining points, and the Franck-Condon and planar transition structure energies are quoted as single-state values in parentheses while everything else is state-averaged, so the table mixes two energy conventions. geometry_source: Geometries of the neutral and the hydrogen-dissociated (U-H)- anions optimized at the CASSCF level with the smaller active space, giving planar structures, with zero-point vibrational corrections at the same level in the harmonic approximation. Potential energy curves along the N-H coordinates were explored by linear interpolation of internal coordinates with the final hydrogen separation set at 3.0 A. A constrained optimization with fixed N3-H bond length was performed at the larger active space level, fixing N3-H at its value in the neutral ground-state equilibrium geometry while relaxing all other degrees of freedom. Minimum energy paths were computed as steepest descent paths in mass-weighted coordinates, each step minimizing the energy on a hyperspherical cross-section of predefined radius 0.09 au, with test calculations at 0.05 au.
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 for dynamic correlation, applied to the ground state of neutral uracil and the low-lying doublet states of the anion
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital ANO-L type contracted to C, N, O [4s3p1d] / H [2s1p]
active_space_orbital_description: For the anion minima, the whole valence pi system of the nucleobase, ten electrons in eight pi molecular orbitals, CASSCF(10,8). For the potential energy curves along the N-H reactive coordinates the space was enlarged by four orbitals: the sigma* orbitals of the N1-H and N3-H bonds plus two additional diffuse orbitals required to stabilize the active space along the curves, giving eleven active electrons in twelve active orbitals, CASSCF(11,12). Test minimum energy path calculations used a smaller space of seven electrons in nine orbitals, obtained by excluding two occupied and one virtual pi natural orbitals whose occupation numbers were close to two and zero respectively.
active_space_protocol: Three related spaces are used for three purposes. The anion minima use the complete valence pi system, (10,8). The dissociation curves require the sigma* orbitals of the two N-H bonds, since the pi anion state evolves into a sigma state localized on the bond that breaks, plus two diffuse orbitals included specifically to stabilize the active space along the curves, giving (11,12). Eight states were averaged with equal weights for the anion curves. A reduced (7,9) space, formed by removing two occupied and one virtual pi orbital with occupations near two and zero, was used for test path calculations. The system poses a particular difficulty acknowledged up front: these are temporary anion resonances lying above the neutral in energy and therefore unstable to electron detachment, and conventional quantum chemistry tends to put the extra electron into the most diffuse available orbital to mimic the neutral molecule plus a free electron.
nroots_per_mult: Eight states averaged with equal weights for the anion potential energy curves
electronic_structure_description: Two valence-bound pi- and two sigma- anion states are involved. Along the potential energy curves the pi anion state evolves toward a sigma state localized on the bond that dissociates, and the conical intersections between the pi- and sigma- curves are interpreted as the points that activate hydrogen loss following electron attachment. The anion states lie above the neutral molecule by roughly 0.3 to 0.4 eV. Thresholds for dissociative electron attachment at the N1-H and N3-H bonds are 0.6 to 0.8 and 1.2 to 1.4 eV respectively; energies below 1.2 to 1.4 eV suffice for one process but not the other, and behaviour changes at the calculated 1.4 eV threshold. One conical intersection has an energy of 0.9 eV and a related crossing point appears around 1.1 eV. The electron affinity of the dipole-bound anion in uracil is 0.085 eV, less than 0.1 eV from the neutral ground state. A sharp peak at 1.01 eV is observed in the cross sections and, with one at 0.69 eV, is assigned to vibrational Feshbach resonances of the dipole-bound anion; distinguishing the two peaks is not possible at present. A broad band has its maximum at 1.7 eV, with the vertical electron attachment energy of the second anionic state measured at -1.58 eV. The end of the minimum energy path lies at 1.59 eV, the vertical anion state at 2.24 eV, and the dissociative electron attachment mechanism operates above 1.8 eV. One state lies 0.4 eV below another at the CASPT2 level, and elsewhere a state is only 0.2 eV below the pi2- state. Experimental vibrational Feshbach resonance positions were found 0.1 to 0.2 eV higher than computed.
Other: Two extra diffuse orbitals are added to the active space for an explicitly numerical reason rather than a chemical one -- they are required to stabilize the active space along the dissociation curves -- and the paper states the underlying hazard plainly: these anion states are temporary resonances lying above the neutral in energy and unstable to electron detachment, so conventional calculations tend to dump the extra electron into the most diffuse orbital available, effectively describing the neutral molecule plus a free electron rather than the anion. Including diffuse orbitals inside the active space is a way of controlling where that electron goes. The space also has to change character along the coordinate for a genuine physical reason: the pi anion state evolves into a sigma state localized on the breaking N-H bond, so both N1-H and N3-H sigma* orbitals must be present alongside the full valence pi system, taking the space from (10,8) at the minima to (11,12) along the curves. Eight states are averaged with equal weights, which is what allows the pi-/sigma- crossings that activate hydrogen loss to be located at all. A reduced (7,9) space was used only for test path calculations, formed by discarding two occupied and one virtual pi orbital whose occupations were already near two and zero -- an occupation-number criterion applied to shrink rather than grow the space. Dynamic correlation enters through CASPT2 with an imaginary level shift of 0.2 au against intruder states and an IPEA shift of 0.25 au.

notes: Previous benchmark calculations on vertical and adiabatic electron affinities of DNA and RNA nucleobases were used to select the methodology; those benchmarks characterize the uracil valence anion ground state as a temporary anion resonance, consistent with electron transmission spectroscopy data. The valence-bound anion of uracil is more relevant in condensed phases, with evidence of hydrogen loss reported in superfluid helium and condensed phases.

geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized at HF and DFT (LDA and B3LYP) levels with the 6-311++G(d,p) basis set; the DFT-optimized geometries were used for the ab initio and TD-DFT excited-state calculations. For formic acid monomer the HF bond lengths are slightly underestimated while B3LYP deviates by at most 0.003 A, and HF overestimates bond angles by up to 3 degrees against at most 1.6 degrees for DFT.
method: CASSCF and multireference configuration interaction (MRCI), compared against time-dependent DFT with LDA and B3LYP functionals
software: MOLPRO 2000.1 for the CASSCF and MRCI calculations; GAUSSIAN 98 for the HF and DFT calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Not stated separately for this molecule; the study used a maximum of eight active orbitals with eight active electrons throughout, limited by available resources.
active_space_protocol: A maximum of eight active orbitals holding eight active electrons was used throughout, stated explicitly to be a limit imposed by available resources rather than by the chemistry, even though the paper acknowledges that the choice of active space is critical for CASSCF and MRCI. The dimer spaces of eight orbitals include n, pi, pi* and sigma* orbitals with eight electrons. The nature of each excitation was assigned on the basis of the major orbital contribution.
electronic_structure_description: Wavelengths in nm for the computed vertical excitation energies, given as TDDFT(LDA), TDDFT(B3LYP), CASSCF, MRCI, then experimental absorption maxima and the DFT(B3LYP) oscillator strength. S1, 10a' to 3a'' (n-pi*): 218, 214, 227, 208, experimental 226-260, 210-259.3 and 215, f 0.0010. S2, 10a' to 11a' (n-sigma*): 184, 172, 181, 164, f 0.0347. S3, 2a'' to 3a'' (pi-pi*): 169, 162, 176, 155, experimental 125-185 and 159, f 0.0414. T1, 10a' to 3a'': 240, 239, 243, 220. T2, 2a'' to 3a'': 203, 214, 211, 185. T3, 10a' to 12a': 191, 178, 191, 167. The CASSCF n-pi* value of 227 nm falls within the experimental range.
Other: The active space here is capped by resources rather than by chemistry, and the paper says so twice. It states at the outset that the choice of active space is known to be critical in CASSCF and MRCI calculations, but that only a maximum of eight active orbitals with eight active electrons was used because of the limitation in the available resources. It later concedes directly that a larger active space might improve the CASSCF and MRCI excitation energies for the acetic acid dimer, where both methods overestimate the excitation energy while TD-DFT(B3LYP) lands close to experiment. The size of the resulting error is severe and grows sharply with molecular size, because the same eight-orbital ceiling covers a one-carbon acid and a benzene-bearing one. For formic acid monomer the CASSCF n-pi* transition at 227 nm sits inside the experimental 210 to 260 nm range; for acetic acid monomer CASSCF gives 208 nm against about 207 to 210 nm experimental, still good, while MRCI drops to 167 nm; but for benzoic acid monomer the bright pi-pi* state comes out at 181 nm at CASSCF and 205 nm at MRCI against an experimental 278 to 280 nm, errors of about 100 and 75 nm. The dimers fare worse still: acetic acid dimer gives 117 nm at CASSCF and 134 at MRCI against roughly 203 nm measured. Notably MRCI is not uniformly better than CASSCF -- for the formic acid dimer S2 state MRCI gives 170 nm against CASSCF's 128, closer to experiment, while for both monomers MRCI moves further from experiment than CASSCF does. That non-monotonicity is what one expects when the reference space is too small for the correlated step to build on, and it is the clearest internal evidence that the eight-orbital ceiling rather than the correlation treatment is the binding constraint.
reference_short: Lourderaj, Giri & Sathyamurthy, J. Phys. Chem. A 2006, 110, 2709
notes: The trans form of formic acid monomer was the one optimized. This is the smallest system in the series and the one where the resource-limited active space is least strained.

geometry_source: Conformations first screened by UB3LYP with the 6-31G* basis set for as many conformations as possible, then treated at the CASSCF level with the cc-pVDZ basis set. D0 geometries optimized within C2v and C2h symmetry for the maleic and fumaric anion radicals respectively, with stability confirmed by vibrational analysis. software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for the CASSCF calculations; 6-31G* for the UB3LYP screening; aug-cc-pVDZ for TDDFT

compound_name: C2H4 + H to C2H5 association reaction
geometry_source: Geometries optimized with the 6-311G(d,p) basis (called B2) at four levels: Hartree-Fock, MP2, CASSCF and QCISD(T). Starting from the MP2/6-31G(d,p) saddle point geometry, the minimum energy path and the potential energy along it were computed in an isoinertial mass-weighted coordinate system, with 22 points along the path (reactants, product, saddle point and 19 nonstationary points). Curvilinear coordinates were also explored but did not improve results in the important range, so rectilinear coordinates were used throughout. Single-point energies at the two highest levels were computed all along the MP2 path, not just at stationary points.
method: CASSCF used as one of four levels for geometry optimization and for single points along the minimum energy path, alongside HF, MP2, PMP2 and QCISD(T), within a variational transition state theory treatment with multidimensional tunneling and a variable scaling of external correlation (VSEC) procedure
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Three electrons distributed among three orbitals; the same active space as used by Hase et al. in earlier work on this reaction.
active_space_protocol: The active space is adopted unchanged from earlier work on the same reaction rather than being re-derived, and it is the minimal set for a three-electron association: the ethene pi and pi* orbitals together with the hydrogen 1s. Its role in this study is as one of four levels of electronic structure theory applied to a common set of geometries and to the same 22-point reaction path, so that the differences between methods are attributable to the treatment of correlation rather than to differing geometries or paths.
electronic_structure_description: Energetics in kcal/mol for the C2H4 + H to C2H5 reaction, given as the classical energy of reaction, the classical barrier height, the classical reverse barrier, the zero-point-inclusive energy of reaction, the zero-point-inclusive barrier at the saddle point, and the zero-point-inclusive reverse barrier. MP2/B1: -37.9, 11.0, 48.9, -32.0, 12.7, 44.7. PMP2/B1//MP2/B1: -39.2, 3.1, 42.3, -33.3. CASSCF(3,3)/B2//MP2/B1: -30.7, 8.5, 39.1, -24.8. CASSCF(3,3)/B2: -30.8, 7.9, 38.8, -24.9, 9.4, 34.3. QCISD(T)/B2//MP2/B1: -39.3, 3.9, 43.1, -33.4. QCISD(T)/B2: -39.3, 3.6, 43.0, -33.4, 3.8, 37.2. PMP2/B1//MP2/B1 along the whole path: -39.2, 4.0, 43.2, -33.3, 5.4, 38.7. CASSCF(3,3)/B2//MP2/B1 along the whole path: -30.7, 8.5, 39.1, -24.8, 10.3, 35.1. QCISD(T)/B2//MP2/B1 along the whole path: -39.3, 4.3, 43.6, -33.4, 5.7, 39.1. VSEC//MP2/B1 along the whole path: -43.0, 1.2, 44.2, -37.1, 2.7, 39.8. The energy of the maximum energy structure at the QCISD(T)/B2//MP2/B1 level along the path is very similar to that at the saddle point.

Its barrier heights are reasonable in shape but its reaction energy is badly off: CASSCF(3,3)/B2 gives a classical energy of reaction of -30.8 kcal/mol against -39.3 at QCISD(T)/B2 with the same basis and geometry, an 8.5 kcal/mol shortfall in exothermicity that persists unchanged whether the geometry comes from MP2 or from CASSCF itself (-30.7 versus -30.8), and unchanged again when single points are taken all along the reaction path rather than at stationary points. That invariance is the useful diagnostic: the error is not geometric and not a stationary-point artefact but simply the external correlation energy that a three-orbital reference cannot contain. The classical barrier tells the same story from the other side, 7.9 to 8.5 kcal/mol at CASSCF against 3.6 to 4.3 at QCISD(T). The paper's response is not to enlarge the space but to introduce a variable scaling of external correlation energy, calibrated to give -43.0 and 1.2 kcal/mol, which treats the missing correlation as a scalable quantity along the path rather than something to be recovered variationally. The active space itself is inherited unchanged from earlier work on the same reaction rather than re-derived here.

compound_name: Acetophenone, photochemical generation of the triplet state
point_group: Geometry optimizations performed without symmetry constraints
geometry_source: Stationary points of both singlet and triplet states, and minimum-energy crossing points, were optimized at the XMCQDPT2 level rather than at CASSCF geometries as in previous studies; the paper notes that few studies in the literature are fully obtained at the XMCQDPT2 level because of the computational cost. Reported XMCQDPT2 energies refer to calculations on top of XMCQDPT2 geometries, whereas XMCQDPT2/CASSCF denotes calculations on top of CASSCF geometries. Conical intersection optimizations were performed with Gaussian 09 and spin-orbit couplings at the CASSCF level with GAMESS-US.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with extended multiconfiguration quasi-degenerate second-order perturbation theory (XMCQDPT2) for dynamic correlation, including geometry optimization at the XMCQDPT2 level; spin-orbit couplings computed at the CASSCF level
software: Gaussian 09 for conical intersection optimizations; GAMESS-US for spin-orbit couplings; a further package for the remaining calculations
basis_set: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in nine orbitals: eight p orbitals plus the lone pair of oxygen.
active_space_protocol: The space combines the eight ring and carbonyl p orbitals with the oxygen lone pair, so that both the n-pi* and the pi-pi* manifolds are representable together, which is required because the photochemistry depends on which of them is excited. Wave function optimization uses a state-averaged CASSCF over four singlet roots or two triplet roots, and the XMCQDPT2 step is carried out in a basis of ten interacting states for singlets and six for triplets, both with an intruder state avoidance shift of 0.02 au. The distinguishing methodological choice is that geometries themselves are optimized at the XMCQDPT2 level rather than at CASSCF, so the effect of dynamic correlation on structure can be separated from its effect on energy.
nroots_per_mult: Four singlet roots or two triplet roots in the state-averaged CASSCF; ten interacting singlet states and six triplet states in the XMCQDPT2 step
electronic_structure_description: S1 corresponds to the 1(n-pi*) state, S2 to the 1 1(pi-pi*) state and S3 to the brightest 2 1(pi-pi*) state, in agreement with experiment. Vertical excitations: the dark 1(n-pi*) state has an experimental peak maximum at 3.38 eV, computed at 3.67 eV with XMCQDPT2 geometries and 3.98 eV with CASSCF geometries. The 1 1(pi-pi*) maximum is at about 4.22 eV experimentally, computed at 4.46 eV (XMCQDPT2) and 4.43 eV (XMCQDPT2/CASSCF). The intense, vibrationally well resolved 2 1(pi-pi*) transition has an experimental maximum at 5.17 eV, reproduced very accurately at 5.10 eV (XMCQDPT2) and 5.07 eV (XMCQDPT2/CASSCF). Adiabatic excitations agree better with experiment: 3.44 eV (XMCQDPT2) and 3.45 eV (XMCQDPT2/CASSCF) for the 1(n-pi*) state; 4.32 eV and 4.40 eV for the 1 1(pi-pi*) state, the XMCQDPT2 value being only 0.1 eV from experiment; and 4.73 eV at the XMCQDPT2 level for the 2 1(pi-pi*) state, where a larger difference is observed. Important differences between the two geometry sources are also seen in bond lengths, including in the two triplet states and in the phenyl ring distances, while the remaining bond lengths deviate only slightly. The gradient difference vector at one crossing involves mainly C-O bond elongation, and at another the gradient difference is independent of the C-O bond distance.
Other: This paper isolates the effect of dynamic correlation on geometry rather than on energy, by optimizing every stationary point and minimum-energy crossing point at the XMCQDPT2 level instead of at CASSCF geometries as previous studies did, and then reporting both. The comparison shows the effect is strongly state-dependent. For the dark 1(n-pi*) state the vertical excitation moves from 3.98 eV on CASSCF geometries to 3.67 eV on XMCQDPT2 geometries, against 3.38 eV experimental -- so changing only the geometry recovers 0.31 eV, more than half the error. For both pi-pi* states the geometry source barely matters, 4.46 versus 4.43 eV and 5.10 versus 5.07 eV. The pattern is what one expects when a nine-orbital space containing a single oxygen lone pair describes the pi system well but the carbonyl n orbital poorly: the state whose character depends on that orbital is the one whose CASSCF geometry is wrong. Bond lengths tell the same story, with important differences between the two geometry sources in the triplet states and in the phenyl ring while the rest deviate only slightly. The adiabatic energies, which depend on geometry by construction, agree with experiment far better than the verticals in every case. Intruder states were handled by an avoidance shift of 0.02 au rather than by adjusting the space, and the perturbation is carried out over ten interacting singlet states against only four averaged in the CASSCF reference, so the perturbative and reference state spaces deliberately differ.
reference_short: Huix-Rotllant, Siri & Ferre, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2013, 15, 19293
notes: Acetophenone photochemistry depends strongly on which state is absorbing. The study characterizes state crossings among the 1(n-pi*), 1 1(pi-pi*) and 2 1(pi-pi*) states and the triplet manifold in order to rationalize the pathways leading to triplet acetophenone. A potential source of error against experiment lies in the vertical versus adiabatic interpretation of the measured spectrum.

compound_name: 5-Bromouracil, benign decay versus photolysis on the excited state surface
point_group: Nonsymmetric; the conical intersection optimizer was generalized to nonsymmetric cases
geometry_source: Minimum energy paths optimized at the CASSCF level from the Franck-Condon structure with a step of approximately 1 au. A relaxation path with fixed C5-Br distance was obtained by freezing that internal coordinate; it is not a minimum energy path but maps the surface. To avoid active space orbital rotations along that path it was optimized by state-averaging over three states and optimizing the surface for the second root. Points on the conical intersection seam other than the minimum energy intersection were optimized with the C5-Br or C6-Br bond lengths constrained, using a version of Gaussian03 modified so that the projection of the excited state gradient is carried out with constrained branching space vectors transformed to redundant coordinates; the unconstrained conical intersection gradient is a sum of the projected excited state gradient with branching space components removed plus a penalty term along the gradient difference vector.
method: CASPT2//CASSCF, with three different active spaces for path optimization, seam optimization and energy evaluation
software: MOLCAS 7.0 for the CASPT2 calculations; a modified Gaussian03 for the constrained conical intersection optimizations
active_space_orbital_description: Three spaces are used. For optimization of the minimum energy paths from the Franck-Condon structure, 12 electrons in 10 orbitals comprising 8 orbitals of the pi system and the two orbitals of the C-Br sigma bond. For optimizations on the conical intersection seam the space is reduced to (8,7) by removing from the (12,10) space the pi orbital with occupation closest to 2.0 and the two pi orbitals approximately localized on the C2-O7 group. For the CASPT2 energies a (16,12) space is used throughout, adding to the (12,10) space the in-plane nonbonding orbital of bromine and the pi orbital approximately localized on N1.
active_space_protocol: Each of the three tasks gets the space it requires, and the reasons are stated separately. Path optimization needs the C-Br sigma and sigma* orbitals alongside the pi system because the photolysis breaks that bond, giving (12,10). Seam optimization needs a smaller space for a purely technical reason: the orbital rotation contribution to the gradients of the state-averaged states must be obtained by solving the coupled-perturbed MCSCF equations, which forces the reduction to (8,7), and the orbitals removed are chosen by occupation, the pi orbital closest to 2.0 plus two pi orbitals localized on the carbonyl remote from the reaction. Energy evaluation needs a larger space than either, (16,12), adding the bromine in-plane lone pair and an N1-localized pi orbital so that the energies are consistent across all geometries. The reduced seam space is then validated rather than assumed: the energy degeneracy obtained at the CASSCF level is preserved at the CASPT2 level to within 0.1 eV, which the authors state validates the active space choice. CASPT2 used a state-averaged six-root reference with equal weights, a real level shift of 0.2 au and an IPEA parameter of 0.25 au.
nroots_per_mult: Three states averaged for the constrained relaxation path; six roots with equal weights in the CASPT2 reference
electronic_structure_description: The conical intersection seam is characterized in two segments, optimized by constraining the C5-Br and C6-Br distances respectively. At one intersection the deviation of the bromine from the ideal 90 degree orientation perpendicular to the ring is discussed. Relaxation from the seam leads either back to the reactant or on to dissociation. One route is completed by a barrierless reverse 1,2 shift of the bromine atom, and an unstable species is found with a barrier of less than 0.1 eV. The intersecting states include a dissociative (pi,sigma*)-type state. The seam is energetically accessible for stretched C5-Br distances relative to a vertical excitation of 5.1 eV, and it is there that dissociation can occur. At the CASPT2 level the energy profiles along both paths are similar, but the relatively low quantum yield of the photolysis suggests that the benign path is favoured, and access to the seam region with a stretched C5-Br bond leads to photolysis. The energy of the lowest (n,pi*) state rises along one path and is expected to be higher still along the other, so those states are not involved in the photolysis.
Other: Three different active spaces are used for three different jobs on the same molecule, and the paper gives a distinct reason for each. Path optimization uses (12,10), eight pi orbitals plus the C-Br sigma pair, because the bond that breaks must be in the space. Seam optimization is forced down to (8,7) for a purely technical reason worth recording: the orbital rotation contribution to the gradients of state-averaged states requires solving the coupled-perturbed MCSCF equations, which is only tractable in the smaller space. The three orbitals removed are chosen by an occupation criterion plus a locality argument -- the pi orbital with occupation closest to 2.0, and two pi orbitals localized on the C2-O7 carbonyl remote from the reacting C-Br bond. That reduction is then validated against the property that matters at a seam: the CASSCF degeneracy survives at the CASPT2 level to within 0.1 eV, which the authors state explicitly validates the choice. Energy evaluation uses a larger space than either, (16,12), adding the bromine in-plane lone pair and an N1-localized pi orbital so that all geometries are described consistently. So the space grows and shrinks according to whether the task is a gradient, a degeneracy or an energy, with the largest space reserved for the quantity being reported. A further orbital-stability measure appears along one path, which had to be state-averaged over three states and optimized for the second root purely to prevent active space orbital rotations.
reference_short: Kobylecka, Migani, Asturiol, Rak & Blancafort, J. Phys. Chem. A 2009, 113, 5489
notes: The relatively small quantum yield of the photolysis is a central observation the study seeks to explain. Paths 1 and 2 are understood as limiting cases. To determine the energies of the (n_O, pi*) states arising from excitation of the oxygen lone pairs, separate calculations were carried out at the Franck-Condon geometry and along the first part of the path.

geometry_source: CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations performed at DFT-optimized geometries, the DFT using the PBE exchange-correlation functional.
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 on DFT-optimized geometries, to determine the ground spin states and examine f-orbital participation in bonding
software: Not stated in the extracted text
basis_set: Relativistic all-electron ANO-RCC basis sets of double-zeta quality (ANO-RCC-VDZP) with contractions [7s6p4d2f1g] for Ce, [8s7p5d3f1g] for Pu, Am and Cm, [4s3p1d] for Cl and [3s2p1d] for B and O; ANO-RCC-MB with a [1s] contraction for H
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic effects through the second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian with relativistic all-electron ANO-RCC basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: Final active space of three electrons in three orbitals: the Ce 4f orbital plus a doubly occupied bonding and antibonding pair, the additional orbital corresponding to a Ce 5p. The initial active space had a single electron in the seven 4f orbitals, but expanding it introduced virtual Ce 5d orbitals, so the final space was restricted instead.
active_space_protocol: An initial space of one electron in the seven 4f orbitals was enlarged following the same rule used for the actinides, but the enlargement admitted virtual Ce 5d orbitals rather than the intended bonding pair, so the space was restricted to three electrons in three orbitals: the Ce 4f orbital and one doubly occupied bonding and antibonding pair derived from Ce 5p.
electronic_structure_description: With a Ce 4f1 electronic configuration the ground state is undoubtedly a doublet. The cerium compound is the lanthanide reference against which the trivalent actinide borates are compared, the study aiming to differentiate trivalent lanthanides from actinides through f-orbital participation in bonding. Selected molecular orbitals in the HOMO-LUMO region involving the 4f orbitals were examined at the CASSCF and DFT levels.
Other: The same enlargement rule -- take the f manifold, then add one doubly occupied orbital and its antibonding partner -- pulls a different orbital into the space depending on the metal, and the paper says why. electronic_structure_description: The system exhibits a seam of conical intersections with a first-order sloped topology, in which the reaction path lies approximately parallel to the seam rather than passing through a funnel on the path as it would at a peaked conical intersection. Two decay pathways are therefore possible: an adiabatic reaction followed by decay in the product region, or decay on the reactant side, with the preferred path depending on barrier heights and on the orientation of the reaction path relative to the seam. Both an S0/S1 seam of crossing and an S2/S1 seam of crossing are considered. active_space_orbital_description: The paper does not state the number of active electrons or active orbitals. What it does state is what is kept out: in CASSCF as well as in MRCI the 1s orbitals on Cl and F were frozen, as were the 2s and 2p orbitals on the chlorine atom. The A' electron configurations of the dimer are written as (cc) 1(A')2 (A')2 (py)2 and related occupations, where (cc) denotes the eleven lower-lying doubly occupied orbitals and the highest occupied orbitals returned by RHF are practically pure chlorine 3p-type atomic orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The CASSCF calculation serves to generate the natural orbitals that enter the MRCI computation. All configurations obtained by single and double excitations out of the CASSCF wave function were included in the MRCI treatment with internal contraction, giving a total of about 800000 configuration state functions. The frozen-core choice was revised during the work: initially only the 1s AO on Cl was frozen, and the final protocol also freezes the chlorine 2s and 2p.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: the complex correlates with the 2P ground state of the free chlorine atom, which in Cs splits into two A' surfaces and one A'' surface. The MRCI matrix elements <psi(A'')|Lz|psi2(A')> and <psi(A'')|Lz|psi1(A')> were obtained on the full grid of R, theta and rHF and combined with the BSSE-corrected RCCSD(T) adiabatic potentials V1(A'), V2(A') and V(A'') to give the mixing angle, which then transforms the adiabatic surfaces into four diabatic ones expanded in spherical harmonics. The same expression for the mixing angle had been used earlier for nonadiabatic coupling in H2O and in the Cl-HCl system.
Other: The active-space sensitivity here is entirely about which orbitals are excluded rather than how many are included, and the paper reports it as a diagnosed failure and its fix. Initially only the 1s AO on Cl was frozen. With that choice the chlorine 2pz orbital sometimes appeared among the valence orbitals, and because the orbital that wandered in and out of the correlated space changed with geometry, the computed matrix elements of Lz jumped as a function of geometry. Since the entire purpose of the CASSCF/MRCI step is to supply Lz, and the mixing angle derived from Lz is what converts the three adiabatic RCCSD(T) surfaces into the four diabatic ones, those jumps would have propagated directly into discontinuous diabatic potentials. The fix was to freeze the chlorine 2s and 2p as well as the 1s on both Cl and F, in CASSCF and in MRCI alike, which stabilises the composition of the correlated space across the grid. This is a case where smoothness of a property surface, not total energy, sets the orbital-partitioning choice. A second point worth noting for anyone reusing these numbers: the active space is never given as an electron/orbital count anywhere in the paper, so those fields are left empty here rather than inferred, and the energies on which the surfaces are built are RCCSD(T), not MRCI -- the multireference treatment enters only through the angular momentum matrix elements.

electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives the vertical excitation energies from the CASPT2 method, listing state, CASSCF energy, CASPT2 energy, reference weight, wavelength, oscillator strength and major configurations: the ground state at 0.00 and 0.00 eV with reference weight 0.78 and 91 percent ground configuration; 1 2A1 at 1.81 eV CASSCF and 1.71 eV CASPT2, weight 0.77, 725 nm, oscillator strength 8.8e-2, 90 percent 8a1 to 5b2; 2 2A1 at 3.62 and 3.09 eV, weight 0.75, 401 nm, 1.7e-1, 90 percent 7a1 to 5b2; and 1 2B2 at 3.45 and 3.32 eV, weight 0.75, 373 nm, zero oscillator strength, 77 percent 5b2 to 6b1. Experimentally the radical cation shows a charge resonance band at 600 nm, and the calculated first band is 0.36 eV too low while the second falls where the spectrum has a minimum. Relative energies for the ring opening to the benzene radical cation are tabulated at B3LYP/6-31G*, CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ and CASSCF/6-31G*, with the product roughly 70 kcal/mol below the reactant at CCSD(T) but 92 kcal/mol below at CASSCF; the pi/sigma transition state connecting the 2B2 and 2A1 surfaces lies 7.99 kcal/mol above the reactant at B3LYP, 7.60 at CCSD(T) and only 1.08 at CASSCF, and the conical-intersection-related structure between the 2A1 and 2B1 surfaces lies at 4.42, 4.97 and -7.54 kcal/mol respectively. Two of the transition states are poorly described by single determinants and hence could not be located by DFT.
Other: The paper gives the active space twice and the two statements do not agree, which is worth knowing before reusing these numbers. The Results section says that increasing the active space to (13,12), and thus including a degree of dynamic electron correlation in the CASSCF wave function, moves the two transitions to higher energies, although still not into satisfactory agreement with experiment. The Computational Details section says instead that for some exploratory calculations up to 13 electrons were correlated in 14 orbitals, but this hardly affected the results. The electron count matches, the orbital count does not, and the verdicts point in opposite directions -- one says enlargement changed the transitions, the other says it hardly mattered. Both are reproduced here verbatim rather than reconciled. The substantive active-space lesson is separate and clear. The (5,6) reference space gives a 2B2 ground state that suffers severe symmetry breaking at the CASSCF level for the parent radical cation but not for the hexamethyl or norbornadiene analogues: the CASSCF-optimized geometry localises the SOMO, and hence spin and charge, in one of the two double bonds, which stretches to 1.406 Angstrom while the other stays at 1.348 Angstrom, close to the neutral value, and that broken-symmetry structure lies 7.9 kcal/mol below the C2v-constrained one. The authors argue this symmetry breaking is artifactual, caused by neglect of dynamic correlation, and that because the CASSCF wave function is the zero-order wave function on which the multiconfigurational perturbation treatment builds, CASPT2 may fail to rectify it and thus yield nonsensical results. That is the diagnosis for why a method giving excellent spectra for the two analogues is off by 0.36 eV on the first band of the parent and places the second band where the spectrum has a minimum. Enlarging the space is the direct test of that diagnosis, and it pushed the transitions the right way without closing the gap. A second, non-active-space factor was also identified: the visible band position is exceedingly sensitive to the dihedral angle between the two cyclobutene moieties, and CASPT2 or CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ single points on geometries with the dihedral fixed between 96 and 108 degrees put the minimum near 102 degrees rather than the B3LYP value near 104; at 98 degrees, a distortion costing only 0.5 kcal/mol at CCSD(T), the bands come out at 2.13 and 3.57 eV, in good accord with experiment. So the residual error is attributed to a combination of adverse circumstances rather than to the active space alone.

geometry_source: Three reference paths generated independently at both the CASSCF and the CASPT2 levels: minimum energy paths from the Franck-Condon point of the cis isomer and of the trans isomer, and a conical intersection seam path. All optimizations and MEP calculations used the 6-31G* basis with Cartesian d polarization functions; CASPT2 optimizations and MEPs kept the IPEA parameter at its default value of 0.25.
method: Single-point MRCISD, MRCISD+Q, second-order multireference perturbation theory (CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, QD-NEVPT2, XMCQDPT2 with its diagonal-fit and F(Gamma_ns) variants) and spin-flip equation-of-motion coupled cluster (EOM-SF-CCSD and SF-CCSD(dT)) energies computed along CASSCF and CASPT2 reference paths

active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six pi orbitals, written by the authors as 6-in-6. The same electrons and orbitals form the reference space for the MRCISD and MRCISD+Q calculations. The 1s core orbitals of the carbon and nitrogen atoms were kept frozen in MRCISD and MRCISD+Q; in the CCSD and EOM calculations all electrons were correlated.
active_space_protocol: A single 6-in-6 pi space is held fixed across every method compared, so that differences between the profiles come from the treatment of dynamic correlation rather than from the reference space. An imaginary shift of 0.2 was used in CASPT2 to exclude intruder states, and an intruder state avoidance shift of 0.02 in XMCQDPT2. QD-NEVPT2 was used in its partially contracted variant. MRCISD+Q used the Davidson correction with a relaxed reference. The EOM calculations used the lowest high-spin triplet as reference, computed at ROHF to reduce spin contamination, and only the spin-flip variant was tested.

electronic_structure_description: The S1 potential energy surface is mapped along three paths connecting the cis and trans isomers with structurally and energetically distinct conical intersections belonging to the same intersection space. MRCISD+Q is taken as the most accurate method and as the reference against which nonparallelity errors and energy gaps are judged. Its S1-S0 energy gaps at the equilibrium structures are 101.4 kcal/mol for cis-PSB3 and 104.4 kcal/mol for trans-PSB3, about 9 to 10 kcal/mol smaller than the CASSCF values; dynamic electron correlation consistently reduces the gap at the equilibrium structures. MRCISD without the Davidson correction and the EOM-CC methods give larger gaps than MRCISD+Q, while all the MRPT2 methods underestimate them. Classical XMCQDPT2 gives gaps 7 to 8 kcal/mol smaller than MRCISD+Q, whereas its diagonal-fit and F(Gamma_ns) variants agree very well, the diagonal fit excellently; QD-NEVPT2 also reproduces the MRCISD+Q gaps very well. CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 without the IPEA shift are red-shifted by 9 to 10 kcal/mol, and the IPEA shift significantly improves agreement, with MS-CASPT2 slightly better than CASPT2 both with and without it. SF-CCSD with the perturbative triples correction reproduces the MRCISD+Q gaps very well. At the three conical intersection geometries MRCISD+Q splits the degeneracy that exists at the CASSCF level, by an amount that differs between methods because the intersection is displaced to different geometries along the bond length alternation coordinate.
Other: The active space itself is deliberately held constant at 6-in-6 pi throughout, and the paper's finding is what happens to the surface when only the correlation treatment on top of that fixed space is varied. The conclusion is that dynamic electron correlation has an important effect on the topology of the S1 surface, not merely on its energetics, which is why the reference minimum energy paths and seam had to be regenerated independently at CASSCF and at CASPT2 rather than computing single points on one set of paths. A specific and important caveat concerns what the reference space guarantees about the intersection topology. The crossing points on the computed CASSCF seam display the correct conical intersection dimensionality, the degeneracy being lifted by distortion along two different modes. That is not automatically true for the other theories built on the same space: at MRCISD+Q the degeneracy is lifted only along the bond length alternation mode, because the Davidson correction corrects the energies but not the wave functions of the crossing states, so the intersection is not truly conical even though the authors continue to call these seam points conical intersections. So the same 6-in-6 reference gives a genuine conical intersection at CASSCF and a degeneracy-splitting artefact at the level chosen as the most accurate reference. A further methodological point is that the accuracy ranking depends on the geometry and basis the space is used with: a previous benchmark on the ground state surface found that for cis- and trans-PSB3 with a modest 6-31G* basis and a CASSCF optimized geometry it is more accurate to use CASPT2 without an IPEA shift than with the default value, through a cancellation of errors among the geometry, the IPEA value and the basis, whereas in the present excited-state comparison the IPEA shift significantly improves the gaps. Which choice is right therefore depends on which errors are being cancelled, not on the shift alone.

notes: A methods benchmark: one chemical system, many correlation treatments on one fixed reference space. The three paths are the cis minimum energy path, the trans minimum energy path, and the conical intersection seam.

compound_name: Formic acid, HCOOH, photodissociation and isomerization on the S0, T1 and S1 surfaces
point_group: Cs constraint used for the initial S1 optimizations; the resulting cis and trans structures proved to be second-order saddle points and nonplanar structures were then located by following the imaginary modes; the dissociating radical pair is treated in C1
geometry_source: Stationary structures optimized at CAS(18,13)/cc-pVTZ and reoptimized at CAS(10,8)/cc-pVTZ, with harmonic frequencies examined to confirm each as a minimum or a saddle point; intersection structures characterized at CAS(10,8)/cc-pVTZ
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequency analysis followed by internally contracted MR-CI single-point energies including all single and double excitations relative to the CASSCF reference wave functions; UMP2/aug-cc-pVTZ used for comparison on the T1 barrier
software: Gaussian 98 and Gaussian 03 for the structural optimizations; MOLPRO for the MR-CI single-point energy calculations
basis_set: cc-pVTZ mainly employed; aug-cc-pVTZ for the UMP2 comparison
active_space_orbital_description: Eighteen electrons, which is all the valence electrons of HCOOH, in thirteen orbitals, referred to as CAS(18,13). Besides nine occupied orbitals the active orbitals are the C-O pi*, and the C-H, O-H and C-C sigma*. The authors point out that the three sigma* orbitals in the space are actually delocalized over the whole molecular backbone with remarkable antibonding character in the C-H, O-H and C-C regions. A smaller CAS(10,8) space was also used, and a preliminary CAS(8,7) space of eight electrons in seven orbitals preceded both.
active_space_protocol: The authors state the problem directly: the complete active space formalism contains a certain amount of ambiguity in terms of which particular electrons and orbitals are chosen for inclusion, so selection of the active space becomes a crucial step. Their answer is a three-stage ladder. Preliminary calculations used a small space of eight electrons in seven orbitals. All stationary structures were then optimized at CAS(18,13), the full valence space. Finally, using the CAS(18,13)/cc-pVTZ structures and wave functions as the initial guess, all stationary structures were reoptimized at CAS(10,8), and once convergence was reached harmonic frequencies were examined. The larger space thus serves as the source of the starting guess and of the reported bond parameters for stationary structures, while the smaller one carries the frequency analysis, the zero-point corrections and the intersection structures. The MR-CI single points correlate a total of eighteen valence electrons and all virtual orbitals, with the C and O 1s electrons treated as a frozen core.
multiplicities_studied: singlet and triplet; S0, S1, T1 and T2
electronic_structure_description: Formic acid in S0 is planar and exists as trans and cis isomers with respect to the C-O single bond, the trans form being more stable by 4 to 5 kcal/mol, with a trans-cis isomerization barrier around 13 kcal/mol; partial double bonding across the central O4-C2 bond impedes free internal rotation of the OH group. The S1 structures optimized under a Cs constraint turned out to be second-order saddle points, with imaginary frequencies of 1015.5i and 259.3i per cm corresponding to C-H wagging and O-H torsional motions, and following those modes led to nonplanar S1 structures. Ground-state OH is of 2Pi symmetry and is twofold degenerate while HCO has a 2A' ground state, so the two radicals approaching in C1 symmetry correlate with two singlet states, S0 and S1, and two triplet states, T1 and T2, of HCOOH. No transition state was found on the S0 pathway for dissociation of trans-HCOOH into HCO plus OH; the present MR-CI best estimate for the endothermicity of that dissociation is 103 kcal/mol, against a thermochemical estimate of about 110 kcal/mol and an earlier cited heat of formation of 96.8 kcal/mol. The barrier to S1 dissociation was predicted to be 13.0, 14.7 and 13.5 kcal/mol by CAS(10,8)/cc-pVTZ, CAS(18,13)/cc-pVTZ and MR-CI with CAS(10,8)/cc-pVTZ zero-point corrections respectively, consistent with the experimental range of 7.5 to 20.0 kcal/mol inferred from the S0 to S1 spectrum becoming diffuse near 250 nm and continuous below 225 nm. The T1 dissociation barrier came out at 14.4, 15.4 and 14.9 kcal/mol from CAS(10,8)/cc-pVTZ, CAS(18,13)/cc-pVTZ and UMP2/aug-cc-pVTZ with the CAS(10,8) zero-point correction, and 15.0 kcal/mol from MR-CI single points on the CAS(18,13)/cc-pVTZ structures.
Other: This paper is unusually explicit about active-space selection being a decision rather than a given, and it gives the numbers needed to judge how much the decision mattered. Three spaces appear: a preliminary (8,7), the full valence CAS(18,13), and a reduced CAS(10,8) reached by using the CAS(18,13) structures and wave functions as the initial guess. The reduction is not presented as an approximation of convenience alone; the sequence matters, because converging the small space from the large-space wave function is what keeps the smaller space describing the same physics. The quantitative comparison is the useful part. For the S1 dissociation barrier the three levels give 13.0 kcal/mol at CAS(10,8), 14.7 at CAS(18,13) and 13.5 at MR-CI, a spread of under 2 kcal/mol; for the T1 dissociation barrier they give 14.4, 15.4, 14.9 from UMP2, and 15.0 from MR-CI on CAS(18,13) structures. The authors draw the conclusion explicitly for the triplet: CASSCF, UMP2 and MR-CI agreeing on about 15 kcal/mol gives reason to expect that dynamic electron correlation has little influence on the T1 barrier height, and they note a similar situation for S1. So here enlarging the space from ten electrons in eight orbitals to the full valence eighteen in thirteen, and adding external correlation on top, shifts barrier heights by roughly one kcal/mol rather than changing the mechanism. That is a rare case where the space can be reported as converged for the property of interest. One caution for reuse: the reported geometries are not all from the same space. Bond parameters for the stationary structures in Figure 1 come from CAS(18,13)/cc-pVTZ while those for the intersection structures come from CAS(10,8)/cc-pVTZ, and all zero-point corrections come from CAS(10,8). A further orbital-composition caveat is stated by the authors themselves: the three sigma* orbitals placed in the active space are not localised bond antibonding orbitals but are delocalized over the whole molecular backbone, carrying antibonding character in the C-H, O-H and C-C regions at once, so the space cannot be read as selectively describing one bond breaking.

compound_name: Anisole (compound 1) and its P450 oxidation intermediates
geometry_source: Initial conformation generated with the modeling package ChemX, further conformations built manually, all optimized at RHF/STO-3G and the lowest-energy one selected; geometries then reoptimized with CASSCF in the STO-3G minimal basis starting from UHF-derived natural orbitals. Geometries of intermediates and products were constructed from the optimized geometry of anisole, and the optimized anisole set was used as the starting point for the para-substituted compounds.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization in a minimal basis followed by CASSCF single-point energy and distributed multipole analysis in a split-valence basis
software: GAMESS-UK for the ab initio calculations; ChemX for the initial conformation
basis_set: STO-3G minimal basis for the geometry optimizations; SV 6-31G split-valence basis for the single-point energies and distributed multipole analyses
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in four orbitals for the closed-shell species: HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1. The derived radicals are treated in a five-electron, five-orbital space adding HOMO-2.
active_space_protocol: Two space sizes are used, chosen by spin state rather than by molecule. Closed-shell species, meaning the starting compounds, neutral intermediates and products, are treated in a 4x4 active space comprising HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1. Open-shell species, the radicals, are treated in a 5x5 active space comprising HOMO-2, HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1. Both orbitals and configuration coefficients are optimized in the multiconfiguration wave function, in order to incorporate electron correlation, which the authors note is needed to describe breaking of covalent bonds and formation of radicals. CASSCF optimizations started from UHF-derived natural orbitals. The active space for the SV 6-31G single points was identical to the space used in the corresponding CASSCF/STO-3G geometry optimization.
multiplicities_studied: singlet for the closed-shell species and doublet for the radicals
electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives stabilization energies as CASSCF/SV 6-31G energies of CASSCF/STO-3G optimized geometries, in kJ/mol, for hydrogen abstraction, hydroxyl radical recombination and subsequent reaction, with an overall value. The entries are: 1 to 4, -387.5, then 4 to 9, -216.7, then 9 to 10, -96.4, overall -700.6; 2 to 5, -439.0, then 5 to 11, -178.5, overall -617.5; 5 to 12, -67.0, then 12 to 15, -132.5, overall -638.5; 5 to 13, -109.4, then 13 to 16, -62.5, overall -610.9; 2 to 6, -376.4, then 6 to 14, -263.1, then 14 to 17, -50.1, overall -689.6; 3 to 7, -397.4, then 7 to 18, -225.3, overall -628.2; 3 to 19 via 7, -70.5, then 19 to 22, -160.5, overall -633.9; 7 to 20, -98.7, then 20 to 23, -83.1, overall -584.7; 3 to 8, -385.9, then 8 to 21, -231.1, then 21 to 24, -80.0, overall -702.5. Anisole was found to have a minimum energy conformation in which the methoxy group is coplanar with the aromatic ring. Hydrogen atom abstraction from the methoxy carbon atom is 50.9 kJ/mol more favorable than abstraction from the para position of the aromatic ring, a comparison made at RHF/SV 6-31G with the data not shown. Only radical 4 is predicted to be formed, which is proposed to lead to product 10 and formaldehyde. Spin delocalization is less pronounced in radical 4 than in the benzylic and cyclopropyl radicals derived from the substituted compounds.
Other: The active space in this study is defined not by chemical inspection but by orbital rank around the frontier, and its size is switched by spin state rather than by system. Closed-shell species -- starting compounds, neutral intermediates and products -- get a 4x4 space of HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1. Open-shell species, the radicals, get a 5x5 space of HOMO-2, HOMO-1, HOMO, LUMO and LUMO+1, so the enlargement is one orbital added below the frontier, not one above. That asymmetry is deliberate: the extra electron-rich orbital is what the singly occupied level needs to delocalise into, and spin delocalization is the mechanistic step the whole scheme rests on. The consequence for reusing these numbers is that every reported stabilization energy is a difference between a 5-electron/5-orbital wave function and a 4-electron/4-orbital one, so the space is not held constant across the reaction coordinate whose energy is being reported. A second structural feature of the protocol is that the space is held identical between the two basis-set stages: geometries are optimized with CASSCF in the STO-3G minimal basis, then single-point energies and distributed multipole analyses are computed with CASSCF in the split-valence 6-31G basis using an active space identical to that used in the corresponding STO-3G optimization. So basis-set improvement is decoupled from any change in the reference. The orbital-rank definition also means the space contents are not guaranteed to be the same chemical orbitals across the three substrates: HOMO-1 through LUMO+1 of anisole, p-methylanisole and p-cyclopropylanisole need not correspond to the same bonds or ring orbitals, and the paper's own observation that spin delocalization is much more pronounced in the benzylic and cyclopropyl radicals than in the methoxy-derived ones is exactly the situation where such a rank-based space can shift its character between compounds. Starting orbitals came from UHF-derived natural orbitals, which is the usual way to get a rank-defined space to converge onto the intended correlating orbitals in a minimal basis. Finally, several of the comparisons quoted in the discussion, such as the 50.9, 74.5 and 33.0 kJ/mol preferences for aliphatic over aromatic hydrogen abstraction, are RHF/SV 6-31G numbers, not CASSCF ones, and are labelled data not shown -- so the multiconfigurational treatment does not underlie every energy the paper argues from.
reference_short: de Groot, Donne-Op den Kelder, Commandeur, van Lenthe & Vermeulen, Chem. Res. Toxicol. 1995, 8, 437
notes: Direct aromatic hydroxylation was not taken into account in this study. Anodic acetoxylation of anisole is reported to give mainly ortho- and para-acetylated products, but that is not a radical reaction and so cannot be taken as experimental support for these predictions.
correlation_correction: None beyond CASSCF; no perturbative or CI correction was applied

For [MoW(dpa)4]2+: 33, 17, 14 and 12 percent for the same four. For [W2(dpa)4]2+: 42, 18, 12 and 11 percent. The singlet spin state is the ground state and shows strong multiconfigurational character with several competing configurations, the dominant one being sigma2 pi2 delta2 with a weight of only 24 percent, the smallest of the three. The other relevant configurations are mainly double excitations from the bonding to the antibonding active orbitals. The metal-metal effective bond order is 1.01. For the [M2O(dpa)4]2+ compounds it is ten electrons, six from oxygen and two from each metal centre, in eight orbitals: the bonding and antibonding combinations of the metal-oxygen sigma and pi orbitals, the dz2 orbital of the eight-coordinate metal atom, and the dxy orbital of the metal atom bound to oxygen, denoted CAS(10,8). Holding CAS(6,6) fixed across the Mo2, MoW and W2 series is what makes the central result readable: the weight of the dominant sigma2 pi2 delta2 configuration rises monotonically from 24 to 33 to 42 percent and the effective bond order from 1.01 to 1.33 to 1.59 as molybdenum is replaced by tungsten, so the trend is a property of the metals rather than of a re-tuned reference. The same space also delivers the paper's main qualitative claim, that these are stretched and weak triple bonds: at 24 percent for the ditungsten-free member no single configuration dominates, and the competing configurations are mainly double excitations from the bonding into the antibonding active orbitals, exactly the signature that a single-determinant description would miss. There the dominant metal-oxo sigma2 pi4 configuration accounts for 93 to 94 percent of the wave function and the metal-oxygen effective bond orders are 2.86, 2.86 and 2.85, but the remaining occupied active orbitals, the dz2 on the eight-coordinate metal and the dxy on the oxygen-bound metal, come out localized on their individual metal atoms. The authors draw the explicit inference that because the active-space molecular orbitals are localized on each metal atom, no partial metal-metal interactions can be seen from the CASSCF data. That is a negative result read off orbital localisation within the chosen space, and it depends on the space having been built around the metal-oxygen bond rather than around a metal-metal bond -- a space chosen to describe M-O has no orbital available in which a weak M-M interaction could appear. Two further practical notes. The CASPT2 step deletes the 300 highest-energy secondary orbitals to reduce cost, with an imaginary shift of 0.2 on the external part of the zeroth-order Hamiltonian to prevent weak intruder states and the standard IPEA of 0.25. And the frozen-core choice is compound-specific: orbitals up to and including 3d are frozen on Mo and up to and including 4d on W, so the heterometallic members freeze a different shell on each centre. Other: The most useful thing in this paper for active-space purposes is a stated refusal. The authors set out explicitly why they did not attempt the localized-versus-delocalized question computationally at all, and the argument is about what a reference wave function can support. B3LYP is ruled out because it artifactually overstabilizes delocalized structures, through incomplete cancellation of the self-interaction energy of the unpaired electron by current exchange functionals. Hartree-Fock SCF is ruled out because an accurate account of the subtle balance of forces favouring localization or delocalization requires proper treatment of dynamic electron correlation, and because such methods are prone to artifactual symmetry breaking. Adding correlation perturbatively is ruled out too, and this is the part that bears directly on active-space practice: a localized Hartree-Fock wave function is such a poor zero-order approximation to a correlated delocalized wave function, or the reverse, that perturbation theory is bound to fail in such cases. So the group that is otherwise applying CASSCF/CASPT2 throughout the paper declines to use it on the one question where the reference itself would prejudge the answer, and instead restricts CASPT2 to excited-state energies at fixed geometries where that risk does not arise. The reference quality is nevertheless checked and reported: all excited states are described to more than 70 percent by the CASSCF wave function in the CASPT2 calculation, which is the relevant sanity test given that the whole assignment rests on perturbation theory being applicable. Two further practical points. The 11-electron, 12-orbital space is held identical between the planar D2h and perpendicular D2d geometries, so the two electromers are compared on the same footing and the change in the charge-resonance energy from 0.49 to 0.63 eV reflects the geometry rather than the reference. And the excited-state calculations were performed at the exactly planar geometry for reasons of computational economy, whereas the real product is twisted by about 10 degrees with almost no barrier to planarization; the DFT check quantifies what that costs, moving the charge-resonance excitation from 0.45 to 0.42 eV on twisting by 10.3 degrees, so roughly 0.03 eV.

For the imide compound the default breaks: including only the seven 5f orbitals would not properly describe the covalent bonding between the imide nitrogen and uranium, so the three N 2p orbitals must be added, giving 7 electrons in 10 orbitals. That space still failed, and the failure mode is the diagnostic one worth recording -- CASSCF and CASPT2 predicted different ground states. For the arene-bridged diuranium compound the space is 8 electrons in 14 orbitals, which one can think of as the seven U 5f orbitals on each centre with the corresponding electrons -- but the authors immediately qualify this: the resulting molecular orbitals corresponding to U-arene-U bonding contain contributions from both 5f and 6d orbitals. So the space is specified by a 5f counting rule while its converged contents are not purely 5f, and any interpretation resting on pure f character would be overreading it. The multireference character in that compound is strongly spin-state dependent, which bears directly on how much the space is doing: the quintet is high spin and dominated by a single configuration at 87.1 percent, while the singlet and triplet are much more multireference, the singlet's largest contributions being only about 13 to 14 percent each spread over five configurations. The gas phase was used because solvent effects on the initial part of the photodynamics are small, as shown by the similar subpicosecond dynamics of the compound in methanol and in water and of a related alpha-diazoketone in acetonitrile, and because computed solvent-induced shifts of the vertical excitations in water are less than 0.1 eV for the relevant states.
electronic_structure_description: The red edge of the UV/vis spectrum around 400 nm, where the experiment excites, contains two transitions: a (pi,pi*) state that is bright with an oscillator strength of approximately 0.4, and a (pi,pi*NN) state in which an electron is promoted to the in-plane antibonding pi orbital of the diazo group, with an oscillator strength below 0.001. The initial excitation therefore populates the bright (pi,pi*) state, which is S2 at the Franck-Condon structure. Relaxation of that state from the Franck-Condon structure is barrierless and leads to a conical intersection with the (pi,pi*NN) state, involving ring bond stretching modes, out-of-plane bending of the diazo group, and stretching of the C-N bond from 1.32 to 1.48 Angstrom. From there two paths continue on S1. The main one stays on the (pi,pi*) state along the C-N stretch until it reaches segment 1 of the S1/S0 seam, which lies along the C-N stretch coordinate with the diazo group bent out of the plane; the minimum energy path hits the seam where the C-N distance is 1.65 Angstrom, but the whole segment is energetically accessible. Ground-state decay paths differ along the seam: at 1.65 Angstrom the decay returns to the reactant; at 1.5 Angstrom one path reverts to the reactant and one gives a diazirine side product, expected in low yield because it comes from a high-energy region of the seam and not detected experimentally; at 2.0 Angstrom the decay leads to the carbene intermediate; and at 2.5 Angstrom the ketene can also be formed. On the ground state the carbene is separated from the ketene by a barrier of 0.3 eV and the ketene is more stable by 2.3 eV, which accounts for the estimated carbene lifetime of 10 to 20 ps. A fraction of the wave packet bifurcates at the S2/S1 intersection onto the (pi,pi*NN) state and follows another barrierless path to segment 2 of the seam, where the diazo group is bent in the plane of the ring; apart from that orientation segment 2 resembles segment 1, also lying along the C-N dissociation coordinate.
Other: The active space is split by task rather than held fixed: (10,10) carries every optimized structure and minimum energy path, while the larger (14,13) carries only the CASPT2 energies computed at those structures. That is the reverse of the more common arrangement in which the perturbation step reuses the optimization reference, and it means the seam geometries and the energies quoted along the seam do not come from the same wave function. The choice is defensible here because the topology being mapped is a seam rather than a single point -- segment 1 was traced by constrained conical intersection optimizations with the C-N distance fixed at a series of values and the C3-C2-N12-N13 dihedral fixed at 90 degrees, so what matters from the CASSCF step is that the two states cross consistently along the coordinate, while the energetic accessibility of the whole segment, which is the paper's central claim, is a CASPT2 quantity. The physical demand on the space is unusually explicit: the two states that must both be described are a (pi,pi*) state and a (pi,pi*NN) state in which an electron is promoted into the in-plane antibonding pi orbital of the diazo group. A space chosen only from the ring pi system would carry the bright state and miss the dark one entirely, and since the branching at the S2/S1 intersection between those two states is precisely what determines whether the wave packet reaches segment 1 or segment 2 of the seam, and thence carbene versus ketene, omitting pi*NN would not merely shift energies but remove one of the two product channels. A caveat on the downstream model: the three-dimensional surface used for the wave packet dynamics is fitted to the ab initio data with a root-mean-square error of 0.37 eV, and the authors note the model contains several approximations, so the dynamical conclusions rest on a fit considerably coarser than the underlying CASPT2 energies. The basis set is not stated in the main text, only deferred to the Supporting Information, so it is left blank here rather than guessed.

compound_name: Aniline, ultrafast excited-state dynamics and conical intersections
point_group: None imposed; the ground state is pyramidal at nitrogen with the NH2 plane at about 28 degrees to the ring
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations of the S0, 1 1pipi* and 2 1pipi* minima, and minimum energy crossing point searches for the conical intersections, all at the CASSCF/6-311+G(d) level; orbital rotation derivatives were negated from the solutions of the coupled perturbed multiconfigurational SCF equations when performing conical intersection searches
method: CASSCF with two active spaces, benchmarked against TD-CAM-B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ, EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-pVDZ and SAC-CI; valence bond structures analysed from the spin-exchange density with Boys-localized active space orbitals and the localized one-electron density matrix
basis_set: 6-311+G(d) for the CASSCF calculations; aug-cc-pVTZ for TD-CAM-B3LYP and aug-cc-pVDZ for EOM-CCSD
active_space_orbital_description: CAS1 is eight electrons in seven orbitals: the three ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair n, which is heavily conjugated into the ring pi system, and the three corresponding pi* orbitals. This space gives rise to 490 singlet configuration state functions. CAS2 is ten electrons in nine orbitals, consisting of the CAS1 orbitals plus the corresponding N-H sigma and sigma* orbitals, and generates 5292 singlet configuration state functions.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces are used according to which states must be described. CAS1, the (8,7) pi plus lone pair space, was used for the S0 equilibrium geometry, for the properties of the 1 1pipi* and 2 1pipi* states, and to isolate conical intersections involving the S0, 1 1pipi* and 2 1pipi* surfaces. CAS2, the (10,9) space adding the N-H sigma and sigma*, was constructed specifically to explore conical intersections involving the 1pisigma* and 1 1pipi* states, since without the N-H sigma* orbital the 1pisigma* state does not exist in the space at all. Equally state-averaged orbitals between the upper and lower states involved were used in all conical intersection searches, and equal state averaging with the state immediately lower in energy was also used to compute the vertical and adiabatic excitation energies of the 1pisigma* and 2 1pipi* states.
nroots_per_mult: two-state equal averaging between the upper and lower states involved in each conical intersection, and with the next lower state for the 1pisigma* and 2 1pipi* excitation energies
electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives vertical and adiabatic excitation energies at four levels. Vertical: 1 1pipi* at 4.88 eV (f = 0.036) from TD-CAM-B3LYP, 4.71 eV (f = 0.026) from EOM-CCSD, 4.86 eV from CAS1 and 4.85 eV from CAS2, against an experimental 4.22 eV; 1pisigma* at 4.96 eV (f = 0.007) and 4.90 eV (f = 0.006), not obtained with CAS1 and 5.78 eV state-averaged with CAS2, against an experimental 4.61 eV; 2 1pipi* at 5.53 eV (f = 0.099) and 5.75 eV (f = 0.158), 7.32 eV state-averaged with CAS1 and 8.13 eV state-averaged with CAS2, against about 5.10 eV; 3 1pipi* at 6.61 eV (f = 0.220) and 6.72 eV (f = 0.249), against about 6.05 eV. Adiabatic: 1 1pipi* at 4.66 eV with CAS1 and 4.64 eV with CAS2; 2 1pipi* at 6.81 eV state-averaged with CAS1. The S0 minimum is pyramidal with the NH2 plane at about 28 degrees to the ring; the 1 1pipi* minimum is similar, with all C-C bonds elongated from about 1.40 to about 1.43 Angstrom and only a small reduction of that angle to about 25 degrees, which combined with a small barrier could give the time-averaged quasi-planar structure inferred experimentally. Table 2 gives CASSCF adiabatic energies of the conical intersections relative to the S0 minimum: 1 1pipi*/1pisigma* at 5.57 eV and 1pisigma*/S0 at 4.28 eV, both from CAS2 (10,9); 2 1pipi*/1 1pipi* at 5.87 eV, and three 1 1pipi*/S0 intersections at the ortho, meta and para positions at 5.53, 5.50 and 5.61 eV, all from CAS1 (8,7). The branching space motions at the 1pisigma*/S0 intersection are localized around the amino group and are linear combinations of the umbrella and N-H stretch motions, both previously identified as key mediators of ultrafast N-H fission in ammonia. Unlike phenol, where the 1pisigma* surface is plateau-like near the vertical Franck-Condon region, in aniline it shows a strong quasi-bound profile from stronger Rydberg character through mixing with the 1pi3s manifold, so 1 1pipi* to 1pisigma* coupling drives population into the quasi-bound 3s Rydberg well rather than the dissociative sigma* valence region; inspection of the optimized state-averaged active space orbitals at the 1 1pipi*/1pisigma* intersection shows the N-H sigma* orbital has accumulated notable 3s Rydberg character from the nitrogen atom.
Other: The two spaces here differ by exactly the pair of orbitals that decides whether a whole electronic state exists in the calculation. CAS1, eight electrons in seven orbitals covering the ring pi system and the conjugated nitrogen lone pair, cannot represent the 1pisigma* state at all, and Table 1 records that absence with a dash rather than a number. CAS2 adds the N-H sigma and sigma* and the state appears at 5.78 eV. The cost is steep in configuration count -- 490 singlet configuration state functions for CAS1 against 5292 for CAS2, more than a tenfold increase for two orbitals -- which is why the larger space is confined to the intersections that need it and the pipi* intersections stay on CAS1. The authors then report the control that makes this defensible: vertical and adiabatic energies of the 1 1pipi* state are approximately unaltered between the two spaces, 4.86 versus 4.85 eV vertical and 4.66 versus 4.64 eV adiabatic, so the state common to both is described consistently and the two sets of intersection energies in Table 2 can be read on a common scale. The same comparison also exposes where the space does not save the calculation. The 2 1pipi* vertical energy is 7.32 eV with CAS1 and gets worse, not better, with the larger space, rising to 8.13 eV, against 5.75 eV from EOM-CCSD and an experimental value near 5.10 eV -- an overestimate of about 1.8 eV that enlargement moves the wrong way. The authors diagnose the cause rather than hiding it: 2 1pipi* is an intramolecular charge transfer state, confirmed by their valence bond analysis, and CASSCF is well known to overestimate charge transfer excitations, an error that in principle requires dynamic correlation rather than more active orbitals to fix. Their stated position is that CASSCF fails quantitatively for this state but that the key features of its potential energy landscape should remain qualitatively correct, with the EOM-CCSD and TD-CAM-B3LYP results serving as the benchmark in the vertical Franck-Condon region where those methods are valid. A further point about what the space reveals: the character of the orbital added to make CAS2 is not fixed. At the 1 1pipi*/1pisigma* intersection the optimized state-averaged N-H sigma* orbital has accumulated notable 3s Rydberg character from the nitrogen, which is precisely the finding that distinguishes aniline from phenol -- the quasi-bound Rydberg well that population enters instead of the dissociative valence region. A valence-labelled orbital is doing Rydberg duty, and that would be invisible without inspecting the converged orbitals rather than trusting the label they were selected under.
