compound_name: Adenine, excited-state potential energy surface and deactivation paths
geometry_source: Minimum energy paths and critical points optimized at the CASSCF/6-31G* level with intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations started from the transition structures following the analytical force constants in forward and reverse directions; energies recalculated at CASPT2
method: CASPT2//CASSCF: reaction paths and critical points at CASSCF, energetics recalculated at CASPT2, with analytical frequency calculations to characterize transition structures and a spin-orbit coupling constant computed for the triplet channel
software: Gaussian 03 for the CASSCF optimizations and reaction paths; MOLCAS 5.4 for the CASPT2 energetics
soc_included: yes, a spin-orbit coupling constant was computed at the (n,pi*) minimum
active_space_orbital_description: The full active space is sixteen electrons in twelve orbitals: the ten pi orbitals plus the two in-plane lone pairs of the N1 and N3 atoms. Reduced spaces of seven, eight, nine and ten orbitals were used for individual optimizations, including a ten-pi-orbital space that leaves out the nitrogen lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: A deliberately tiered protocol. All CASPT2 energies of every structure, critical points and points along the paths alike, use the full (16,12) space with a six-state equally weighted CASSCF reference and an imaginary level shift of 0.15, so the final energetics are on a single common footing. The CASSCF optimizations and path calculations instead use reduced spaces, chosen by keeping only orbitals with occupations between 1.99 and 0.01, to reduce effort and avoid convergence problems: the (1La)X and (n,pi*)X conical intersections were optimized with nine orbitals; the (1Lb/n,pi*)TS and (1Lb/1La)TS transition structures with seven and eight orbitals respectively, sizes chosen because analytical frequencies are only feasible up to eight orbitals in the code used; and (n,pi*/1La)TS and (n,pi*)TS with ten orbitals, then reoptimized with seven for their frequencies. Optimizations were state-averaged over two states with equal weights except the ground-state Franck-Condon geometry and the 1Lb minimum, done without state averaging, and (1Lb/n,pi*)TS, averaged over three states using the S1 gradients. Orbital rotation corrections to the gradients were omitted with nine or more orbitals because the coupled perturbed MCSCF equations are not feasible beyond eight active electrons in that code, but were included in all optimizations with seven or eight orbitals. The number of CASPT2 reference states was chosen to always include at least two (pi,pi*) and two (n,pi*) excited states, specifically to avoid orbital rotations that would change the composition of the active space.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, with a triplet state calculation at the (n,pi*) minimum using a five-state equally weighted reference and a spin-orbit coupling constant from a four-state CASSCF(16,12) wave function comprising two singlets and two triplets
nroots_per_mult: six states equally weighted for the CASPT2 reference; two states for most optimizations, three for one transition structure, none for the ground state and 1Lb minimum
electronic_structure_description: Table 2 gives relative CASPT2 energies of the critical points with respect to the ground-state Franck-Condon energy, in eV: the 1Lb minimum at 4.71; the (n,pi*) minimum at 4.35; the (1La)X conical intersection at 3.72 and 4.25 for S1 and S0 at the CASSCF-optimized point, and 3.92 and 4.06 at a point near CASPT2 degeneracy; the (n,pi*)X intersection at 3.84 and 4.56 at the CASSCF point and 4.45 and 4.55 near CASPT2 degeneracy; the (1Lb/n,pi*) transition structure at 4.67, with the highest point along its path at 4.71; the (1Lb/1La) transition structure at 4.46, with the highest point along its path at 4.72; the (n,pi*/1La) transition structure at 4.52; and the (n,pi*) transition structure at 4.95. The results identify a path from the 1Lb minimum to the 1La-type intersection that had not been explicitly considered in previous studies, and a path from the 1Lb minimum to the (n,pi*) minimum with a very small or no barrier, so the two decay channels compete. In contrast, the decay paths from the (n,pi*) minimum to the two conical intersections carry sizable barriers of about 0.1 eV or more, and decay through the (1La)X intersection is energetically more favourable. The short lifetime associated with the 1Lb minimum is attributed not only to its proximity to the (n,pi*) minimum but also to the presence of a virtually barrierless channel.
Other: This paper is an unusually explicit case study in using different active spaces for different jobs and then reconciling them at a single level. Geometry optimizations and reaction paths run on reduced spaces of seven to ten orbitals, selected by an occupation-number criterion -- keeping only orbitals with occupations between 1.99 and 0.01 -- while every reported energy, for critical points and for points along the paths alike, is recomputed at CASPT2 with the full (16,12) space and a six-state reference. So the surface's shape comes from small spaces and its energetics from one large one. The sizes are not chosen for accuracy but by hard code limits, and the paper says so: analytical frequencies are only feasible with up to eight orbitals, which is why two transition structures were optimized with seven and eight orbitals; and orbital rotation corrections to the gradients require solving the coupled perturbed MCSCF equations, not feasible beyond eight active electrons, so those terms were omitted whenever nine or more orbitals were used, with the authors asserting rather than demonstrating that their contribution should be negligible. Two structures were optimized with ten orbitals and then reoptimized with seven purely to obtain frequencies, so their force constants and their geometries come from different references. The most instructive single decision is the path for relaxation of the 1La state, run with a space of ten pi orbitals that leaves out the nitrogen lone pairs. The justification is that those lone pairs are doubly occupied for both (pi,pi*) states at planar and quasiplanar geometries, and the consequence is stated plainly: the (n,pi*) states are effectively neglected during that calculation, though they are restored in the CASSCF reference for the subsequent CASPT2. Exploratory calculations with a larger space showed that including the n orbitals during the path calculation does not change the resulting CASPT2//CASSCF profiles significantly, but makes the computation more tedious because additional crossings between 1La and the (n,pi*) states appear. Deliberately excluding orbitals to remove crossings from a path, then adding them back for the energies, is a real technique with a real risk, and here the risk was tested. The choice of six reference states is also active-space reasoning rather than spectroscopic: the number was picked to always include at least two (pi,pi*) and two (n,pi*) excited states so as to avoid orbital rotations that would change the composition of the space. Finally, a caveat that no space size fixes: at both conical intersections, optimized at CASSCF, there remains an energy gap at CASPT2 of roughly 0.5 and 0.7 eV because of differential correlation between the crossing states. The authors do not attempt to find the CASPT2 minimum energy crossing points; they instead locate nearby points with smaller gaps, stating that the aim is only to confirm the seams exist at the CASPT2 level. Intersection energies in the table are therefore given twice, at the CASSCF-optimized point and at a near-degenerate CASPT2 point, and the two differ by up to 0.6 eV.
reference_short: Blancafort, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2006, 128, 210
notes: An imaginary level shift of 0.15 was used in all CASPT2 calculations. The active spaces used for each structure are summarized in a Supporting Information table not available in the extracted text. For the (n,pi*/1La) and (n,pi*) transition structures, optimized with large spaces, the force constants from the smaller-space analytical frequency calculations were used for the minimum energy paths.

point_group: Cs for the ground state; C2v structures examined for the excited states
geometry_source: Geometries optimized at CASSCF and at MP2; least linear motion paths constructed in internal coordinates; all barriers corrected with zero-point energies from MP2/6-311+G(3df,2p) Hessians
method: Full valence CASSCF, referred to as FORS, with multiconfiguration quasidegenerate perturbation theory (MCQDPT) to recover correlation outside the active orbital set; MP2 and Hartree-Fock used for comparison
software: GAMESS, with MacMolPlt used for viewing and for constructing the least linear motion paths in internal coordinates
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in ten orbitals, the full valence active space.
active_space_protocol: A full valence active space of fourteen electrons in ten orbitals, denoted [14,10]. For the dimethyl compound the analogous space leaves out only the C-H bonds, since they do not participate in the inversion, so both molecules carry the same electron and orbital counts. ROHF orbitals with the Boys localization protocol supplied starting orbitals for the multiconfigurational calculations. Excited singlet wave functions were converged by first computing the triplet CASSCF wave function from ROHF orbitals and using the resulting triplet CASSCF orbitals as the starting orbitals for the excited singlets; the 1A' states converged only with the second-order SCF method, while full Newton-Raphson orbital improvement was used for the singlet A'' states, both triplet A' and A'' states, and all the C2v excited states. The notation MCQDPT/basis denotes a single point energy at that basis on the geometry obtained by CASSCF optimization in the same basis.
multiplicities_studied: singlet and triplet, of both A' and A'' symmetry at the Cs ground-state geometry, together with C2v excited states
electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives ground state inversion barriers, zero-point corrected: 39.1 kcal/mol at MP2/6-311+G(3df,2p), 58.3 at CASSCF/6-311+G(3df,2p) and 31.9 at MCQDPT/6-311+G(3df,2p) as a single point on the CASSCF-optimized geometry. The MP2 value agrees well with an earlier MP2/6-311+G(2d,p) result. Singlet and triplet excited states of A' and A'' symmetry were located at the Cs ground-state geometry. Natural orbital occupation numbers for the two singlet excited states are 1.999, 1.999, 1.998, 1.977, 1.975, 1.990, 1.101, 0.912, 0.028 and 0.022 for the 1A' state, and 1.998, 1.997, 1.975, 1.995, 1.998, 1.962, 1.008, 1.005, 0.043 and 0.020 for the 1A'' state, indicating five nominally doubly occupied and two nominally singly occupied valence orbitals; the singly occupied orbitals do not admit simple descriptions such as n-pi*. Applying the MCQDPT correction considerably lowered the excited state energies relative to the ground state, consistently enough that only corrected relative energies are quoted thereafter. Geometry optimization of some excited states always resulted in dissociation to H2S and O(3P); the optimized 3A'' geometry is qualitatively similar to one of the singlet A'' structures.
Other: The space is full valence and identical in size for both molecules, [14,10], which is what makes the two systems directly comparable: for the hypothetical parent it is simply the full valence space, and for the dimethyl compound the analogous space leaves out only the C-H bonds, on the stated ground that they do not participate in the inversion. Excluding orbitals by whether they participate in the reaction coordinate, rather than by energy ordering, is the right criterion here and it keeps the electron and orbital counts equal between the two molecules so their barriers can be set side by side. The paper then supplies the most useful number in this record: how badly CASSCF alone does on those barriers, and by how much the perturbative correction moves them. For the parent the ground-state inversion barrier is 58.3 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 31.9 at MCQDPT, against 39.1 at MP2; for the dimethyl compound it is 67.6 at CASSCF and 41.5 at MCQDPT, against 50.9 at MP2 in the same basis, with an experimental value of 37.4 kcal/mol for a related aryl sulfoxide. A full valence space therefore overestimates these barriers by 26 kcal/mol in one case and 26 in the other, and the correction overshoots past the MP2 values in both. The authors state the general point directly: electron correlation outside the active orbital set had to be recovered because it is known that MCSCF does not compute excited state energetics accurately, and applying the correction consistently and considerably lowered the excited state energies relative to the ground state, to the extent that they quote relative energies only at the corrected level thereafter. A full valence space is not a substitute for dynamic correlation. The natural orbital occupation numbers are reported and are worth recording because of what they show and what they fail to show. For the two singlet excited states of the parent at the ground-state geometry they run 1.999, 1.999, 1.998, 1.977, 1.975, 1.990, 1.101, 0.912, 0.028, 0.022 and 1.998, 1.997, 1.975, 1.995, 1.998, 1.962, 1.008, 1.005, 0.043, 0.020, described as representative of all the excited state calculations: five nominally doubly occupied and two nominally singly occupied valence orbitals. But the authors add that the singly occupied orbitals did not lend themselves to simple orbital descriptions such as n-pi*, so the space diagnoses the open-shell character without yielding an interpretable assignment. Convergence required a specific orbital-generation ladder, which is the practical lesson for reproducing this kind of calculation: ROHF orbitals with Boys localization gave starting orbitals for the multiconfigurational calculations; the excited singlet wave functions were converged by first computing the triplet CASSCF wave function from ROHF orbitals and then using those triplet CASSCF orbitals as the starting point for the excited singlets; the 1A' states converged only with second-order SCF, while full Newton-Raphson orbital improvement was needed for the singlet A'' states, both triplet states and all the higher-symmetry excited states. Finally, a basis-set note that the authors checked rather than assumed: the inversion barrier for the dimethyl compound differed by less than 0.2 kcal/mol between the two basis sets at fixed geometry and by the same tiny amount for fully optimized MP2 geometries, so the p-polarization functions were dropped, roughly halving the computation time.

notes: Excited states at C2v symmetry are lower in energy than those of Cs symmetry, and the paper presents evidence that the enthalpic barrier from the vertical ground-state geometry to a C2v geometry is low or zero in certain excited states. The excited state at the C2v ground state geometry is acknowledged to have limited physical meaning.

compound_name: Azulene, minimum energy conical intersection optimization
point_group: Optimizations were started near the excited state minimum, releasing any symmetry constraints
geometry_source: Minimum energy conical intersection located by three optimization algorithms starting from a point 1.41 Angstrom away in Cartesian coordinates, near the excited state minimum with symmetry constraints released
method: State-averaged CASSCF, used as the electronic structure method for testing conical intersection optimization algorithms: a conjugate gradient algorithm, the same with composed steps, and a double Newton-Raphson algorithm with composed steps
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Ten active orbitals. The number of active electrons is not stated in the main text; the active spaces of all eleven test cases are detailed in the Supporting Information, which was not available.
active_space_protocol: State-averaged CASSCF/6-31G**. In all optimizations except this one the gradients include the coupled-perturbed multiconfigurational self-consistent field correction, which is only available for active spaces up to eight orbitals. Because this molecule's space has ten active orbitals, approximate gradients without that correction were used here.
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged over the two states involved in the crossing
electronic_structure_description: Table 1 reports the minimum energy conical intersection searches for this molecule, with the starting point 1.41 Angstrom from the converged geometry. The conjugate gradient algorithm converged in 15 cycles with a final ground-to-excited-state energy gap of 0.0001397 au; the composed-step variant took 16 cycles and reached 0.0000465 au; the double Newton-Raphson algorithm with composed steps took 21 cycles, 48 with the pure double Newton-Raphson variant, and reached 0.0000532 au. Across the whole eleven-case test set the averages were 41 cycles and a gap of 0.0000913 au for the conjugate gradient method, 29 cycles and 0.0000142 au for the composed-step version, and 23 cycles and 0.0000099 au for the double Newton-Raphson method.

compound_name: 9H-Adenine, ground and first singlet excited state geometries
geometry_source: Ground and first singlet excited state geometries optimized at CASSCF(4/4)/6-31G, at CIS/6-31G, and with a semiempirical AM1 configuration interaction treatment using the same four-orbital restriction; one excited state geometry reoptimized at CIS/6-31G* as a basis set check
method: CASSCF with a four-electron four-orbital space for excited state geometries, compared against configuration interaction with single excitations and against a semiempirical AM1-CI treatment; INDO/S-CI spectra reported for comparison
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 94 for the CIS calculations; ZINDO for the INDO/S-CI spectra
basis_set: 6-31G for both the CASSCF and CIS calculations, chosen deliberately small so that geometries from different methods could be compared on an equal basis; 6-31G with added d polarization functions on the non-hydrogen atoms used as a check
active_space_orbital_description: Four electrons in four orbitals, denoted (4/4). The space contains only pi orbitals: sigma to sigma* excitations cannot be included, and the n to pi* state is not present in the restricted configuration interaction space.
active_space_protocol: A four-electron, four-orbital space used for the excited state geometry optimizations, matching the restriction used in the semiempirical AM1-CI(4/4) treatment so that the two can be compared directly. The authors note that this necessary restriction excludes sigma to sigma* excitations from the configuration interaction wave function, and that the n to pi* state was not included in the space in either four-orbital calculation.
electronic_structure_description: Both Hartree-Fock and CASSCF predict planar ground state geometries. The mean errors in bond lengths against experiment are 0.013 Angstrom at CASSCF/6-31G, compared with values quoted for AM1 and Hartree-Fock. All three methods predict a rather puckered relaxed first singlet excited state geometry. The four-orbital CASSCF and the AM1-CI(4/4) treatments both give that state pi to pi* character, whereas the single-excitation treatment gives an n to pi* state; the n to pi* state was not in the restricted configuration interaction space of either four-orbital calculation. The single-excitation optimization had serious convergence problems because the character of the first excited state changed during the optimization, and the n to pi* assignment was confirmed by starting from several different geometries. The pi to pi* state, which is the first excited state of the vertical transition spectrum, has only an almost stationary point on the potential energy surface, and it differs from the n to pi* state in the N1-C2-N3 region: the N1-C2 bond is 1.334 Angstrom in the pi to pi* state against 1.388 Angstrom in the n to pi* state, and a marked out-of-plane displacement of the C2-H2 group is found in the n to pi* state while the pi to pi* state is almost planar. In the CASSCF(4/4) geometry the largest out-of-plane displacement is for the hydrogen bonded to C8, whereas in the AM1-CI(4/4) geometry it is for the hydrogen bonded to N9. At the avoided crossing of the two excited state curves the two states are completely mixed with both n to pi* and pi to pi* character, and the vibronic coupling can be extracted as the energy difference between them there.
Other: The active space here is small enough that what it leaves out decides the answer, and the paper documents that twice over. The space is four electrons in four orbitals and contains only pi orbitals: the authors state that the necessary restriction in active space does not allow inclusion of sigma to sigma* type excitations in the configuration interaction wave function, and cite earlier work showing such excitations matter for describing the pi to pi* transitions of benzene, a case where the magnitude of dynamical correlation differs between excited states and where a single-excitation treatment fails seriously on the absorption spectrum. The consequence is visible immediately in the character of the state being optimized. For adenine, the (4,4) space and the semiempirical calculation with the same four-orbital restriction both predict the relaxed first singlet excited state to have pi to pi* character, while the single-excitation configuration interaction treatment gives an n to pi* state instead. The authors are explicit that the n to pi* state was not included in the restricted configuration interaction space in either of the four-orbital calculations -- so the disagreement is not a finding about adenine but a direct consequence of the space excluding the competing state. The single-excitation calculation, which can see both, had serious convergence problems precisely because the character of the first excited state changed during the optimization, and its identification of an n to pi* minimum was confirmed by restarting from several different geometries. The pi to pi* state, which is the first excited state of the vertical spectrum, turns out to have only an almost stationary point on the surface. That is a textbook case of a space chosen around one state producing a clean minimum for it while the real lowest state lies outside the space entirely. For 2-aminopurine the situation is different and the space is on safer ground: all three methods agree that the relaxed first excited state has pi to pi* character, and both the four-orbital and the single-excitation treatments give rather planar geometries, so the exclusion of the n to pi* state costs nothing there. The two isomers differ exactly in whether the omitted state competes, which is the physical reason the paper is about. The authors' own verdict on the method is worth recording: the two ab initio approaches are about equally demanding computationally, and the four-orbital space introduces some electron correlation in both the ground and excited states but cannot admit the sigma excitations, and on the basis of previous experience they choose the single-excitation method for the subsequent photophysics rather than the multiconfigurational one. Basis set effects were checked and found small: a 6-31G geometry reoptimized with added d polarization functions on the non-hydrogen atoms produced only minor geometric and spectroscopic changes, which is why the deliberately modest 6-31G basis was retained so that geometries from the different methods could be compared on equal footing.

notes: This isomer exists in two tautomeric forms in water solution, 9H and 7H, with the 9H tautomer the major component; part of the fluorescence has been attributed to the minor 7H tautomer.
correlation_correction: None beyond CASSCF; the authors note the four-orbital space introduces some electron correlation in both ground and excited states but cannot admit sigma excitations

Loops of radius 0.002 Angstrom probe the surface shape, centred on each method's own crossing point and lying along branching plane vectors computed at the CASSCF level, on the stated assumption that those vectors transfer to the other methods' crossings or project strongly onto them.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, with an ROHF triplet reference used for the spin-flip coupled cluster calculations
electronic_structure_description: Along each loop the wave function of each state is expected to change electronic character twice, alternating between predominantly charge-transfer and predominantly diradical character. The MRCISD calculations reuse the identical six-electron six-orbital reference space, with core orbitals frozen in all the perturbation and configuration interaction calculations, and MRCISD+Q applies the Davidson correction with a relaxed reference. compound_name: Tc2Cl4(PMe3)4, the electron-rich metal-metal triple-bonded ditechnetium chloride phosphine complex
metal_ox_state: +2 at each centre, a Tc2(4+) core
ligand_set: Four chloride and four trimethylphosphine ligands on a Tc2(4+) core
geometry_source: Full geometry optimization at the DFT level with the PBE and PBE0 functionals and def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP basis sets; the CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations were performed at the DFT/PBE0/TZVP optimized geometries. Crystal structures determined experimentally.
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 for the ground state bonding analysis and the electronic excitation energies, with DFT geometry optimization and TDDFT vertical excitations alongside
software: MOLCAS 7.4 for the CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations; TURBOMOLE 6.0 for the DFT and TDDFT work
basis_set: Relativistic all-electron ANO-RCC in two qualities: VTZP contracted 7s6p4d2f1g for Tc, 5s4p2d1f for Cl and P, 6s5p3d1f for Br; and VQZP contracted 8s7p5d3f2g1f for Tc, 6s5p3d2f1g for Cl and P, 7s6p4d2f1g for Br. Double-zeta VDZP for C and H, contracted 3s2p1d and 2s1p. A quasi-relativistic pseudopotential with 28 core electrons on Tc was used in the DFT calculations with def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP.
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic effects through the Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian with all-electron ANO-RCC basis sets in the multiconfigurational calculations; a 28-electron-core quasi-relativistic pseudopotential in the DFT calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve active orbitals, written (14/12): one 4d-sigma, two 4d-pi and one 4d-delta Tc-Tc bonding orbital together with the corresponding antibonding orbitals, plus two Tc-ligand sigma bonding orbitals and their corresponding antibonding orbitals. The two bonding Tc-L orbitals are mainly located on the ligand, while the corresponding antibonding orbitals have a large contribution from the Tc 4d(x2-y2) orbital.
active_space_protocol: A (14/12) space containing the full metal-metal bonding and antibonding manifold together with two metal-ligand sigma bonding and antibonding pairs, so that any ligand influence on the metal-metal bond would be visible in the occupation numbers. In the subsequent CASPT2 calculations orbitals up to and including 3d for Tc, 2p for Cl and P, 3p for Br and 1s for C were kept frozen. Cholesky decomposition combined with local exchange screening was used in all CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations to reduce the two-electron integral cost. The same approach had been applied by the authors to several metal-metal bonded compounds previously.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A1g, whose dominant electronic configuration carries a weight of 85 percent. Table 3 gives effective bond orders, defined as the difference between bonding and antibonding natural orbital occupation numbers divided by their sum, computed at the VTZP level: for Tc2Cl8(2-), Tc-Tc 2.170 Angstrom with sigma 0.88, pi 1.68, delta 0.47 and total 3.03; for Tc2Cl4(PMe3)4, 2.118 Angstrom with 0.90, 1.81, 0.01 and 2.72; for Tc2Br8(2-), 2.173 Angstrom with 0.88, 1.69, 0.50 and 3.07; and for Tc2Br4(PMe3)4, 2.117 Angstrom with 0.90, 1.81, 0.01 and 2.72. The occupancies of the delta and delta* orbitals are nearly identical, giving no contribution to the delta bond, an effective bond order of 0.01, while the similar occupancies of the sigma and the two pi orbitals indicate comparable strength, with 0.90 for sigma and 1.81 for pi and a total of 2.72. Table 4 compares experimental band maxima and absorption coefficients with CASPT2 excitation energies and intensities at the VQZP level: 13477 per cm with epsilon 19, assigned delta* to sigma*, computed 13249 with zero intensity; 16129 with epsilon 19, delta* to pi*, computed 16370 with intensity 0.14e-4; a shoulder at 19200 with epsilon 24, delta to sigma*, computed 20744 with intensity below 1e-8; 22371 with epsilon 54, delta to pi*, computed 24163 with intensity 0.21e-3; and a shoulder at 27777 with epsilon 68, delta to sigma* of Tc-L character, computed 27215 with intensity below 1e-8. The lowest band is the dipole-forbidden delta* to sigma* transition, computed within 228 per cm of experiment. The crystal structure gives Tc(1)-Tc(2) 2.1318 Angstrom, Tc-Cl 2.3852 and 2.3865, and Tc-P 2.4343 and 2.4370 Angstrom, with Tc-Tc-Cl angles of 113.181 and 113.375 degrees and Tc-Tc-P angles of 102.148 and 101.925 degrees.
Other: The space is specified orbital by orbital and is built to answer one question -- what the metal-metal bond order actually is -- while deliberately including enough ligand character to test whether the halide matters. Basis set quality was varied from triple to quadruple zeta and both sets of excitation energies reported, with the effective bond orders taken from the triple-zeta calculations and the tabulated excitations from the quadruple-zeta ones.

notes: Average interatomic distances in the analogous complexes with triethyl, dimethylphenyl and methyldiphenyl phosphines are Tc-Tc 2.133, 2.127 and 2.1384 Angstrom. The delta* to pi* transition, though formally allowed, is very weak as anticipated for an excitation between delta and pi type orbitals.

geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized with a range of density functionals differing in the percentage of exact exchange, and separately with CASSCF; conformers constructed for the 6s-trans, 6s-cis(+) and 6s-cis(-) orientations of the beta-ionone ring. Constrained paths between the minima and along other coordinates were computed with the M06-2X functional, and a room-temperature ab initio molecular dynamics simulation of about 23 ps was run in the cis(-) configuration with a generalized gradient approximation functional.
method: CASPT2 with the IPEA zero-order Hamiltonian and n-electron valence-state second-order perturbation theory (NEVPT2) for ground-state energies and vertical excitations, computed on density functional and on CASSCF geometries; CASSCF used for geometry optimization as the method under test

active_space_orbital_description: The active space is not specified in the main text; the paper refers computational details to the Supporting Information, which was not available.
active_space_protocol: CASPT2 was used with the IPEA zero-order Hamiltonian, which the authors state yields on average more accurate excitations, and its performance is corroborated by agreement with the NEVPT2 excitations computed on the same geometries. electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives vertical excitation energies in nm for the conformers, labelled by the beta-ionone dihedral. On M06-2X geometries: trans at -170.1 degrees gives 561 nm by CASPT2 and 551 nm by NEVPT2; cis(-) at -38.3 degrees gives 537 and 530 nm; cis(+) at 41.8 degrees gives 532 and 523 nm. On the earlier CASSCF geometries: trans at -185.7 degrees gives 544 and 566 nm; cis(-) at -68.2 degrees gives 473 and 477 nm. Both correlated methods agree that the excitations of the three conformers are comparable, differing by only about 30 nm, and cluster at the blue edge of the spectrum. The barriers between isomers are on the order of 2 kcal/mol, so the conformers can coexist at room temperature over the 40 ms trapping times of the action spectroscopy experiments. Along the constrained path between the trans and cis minima the excited-state energy either roughly parallels the ground-state curve or rises further, so rotation of the beta-ionone ring produces blue-shifted excitations at wavelengths shorter than 520 nm. A room-temperature molecular dynamics simulation identifies three active coordinates -- the global bend monitored by the C6-N16 distance, the C10-C11-C12-C13 dihedral, and the C11-C12 bond length, which is inversely correlated with bond length alternation -- with room-temperature fluctuations of 0.2 Angstrom, 10 degrees and 0.025 Angstrom respectively; excitations computed along these coordinates likewise fail to produce the required red shift. Other: The central active-space finding here is a negative one about CASSCF geometries, and it is established by using a correlated method as the referee rather than by argument. Ground-state energies computed with CASPT2 on geometries from a series of density functionals and from CASSCF show that the M06-2X structures give the lowest CASPT2 energies while the CASSCF structures give the highest -- the worst performance of any geometry tested. compound_name: 9-Methyl-2-aminopurine, ground and lowest singlet pipi* and npi* excited states
point_group: Planar Cs assumed for the ground state optimization; the pipi* state optimized in C1, its symmetry broken by manually rotating the methyl protons by 90 degrees about the N9-C9' bond purely to assist CASSCF convergence
geometry_source: Ground state geometry optimized at MP2 under planar Cs symmetry; the lowest singlet pipi* excited state geometry optimized by CASSCF gradient in C1 symmetry with the reduced active space
method: CASSCF for wave functions, geometries and dipole moments, with multiconfiguration quasidegenerate perturbation theory (MCQDPT) applied for more accurate transition energies; solvatochromic shift coefficients derived from the computed dipoles
active_space_orbital_description: Twenty electrons in thirteen orbitals: 5 sigma, 5 pi, 2 pi* and 1 sigma*. A reduced space of fourteen electrons in ten orbitals -- 2 sigma, 5 pi and 3 pi* -- was used for the excited state geometry optimization and for some ground state calculations; the two sigma orbitals in that reduced space have the character of nonbonding orbitals localized on N1 and N3. All occupied pi orbitals were included except one localized to the N9-C9' bond, excluded because excitations from it did not contribute significantly to the electronic configuration at the initial geometry.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces are used. All transition energies come from the twenty-electron thirteen-orbital space, with npi* energies from pure-state wave functions and pipi* energies from equally weighted state-averaged wave functions of the ground and pipi* states; state averaging is described as an effective way of equalizing the contribution of dynamic electron correlation to the ground and excited state energies, and was not used for the npi* state because the ground and npi* states have differing symmetries. The reduced fourteen-electron ten-orbital space was generated by removing three sigma and one sigma* orbital from the larger space, a reduction required to permit excited state geometry optimization with reasonable computational demands. MCQDPT was applied to the state-averaged CASSCF wave functions with the same active space as the corresponding state-averaged CASSCF, and separately to the pure ground and npi* wave functions.
nroots_per_mult: two states, equally weighted, for the state-averaged pipi* calculations; pure states for the ground and npi* calculations
electronic_structure_description: Table 2 gives transition energies and dipoles: the S0 to pipi* excitation at 5.76 eV (215 nm) by CASSCF and 3.97 eV (312 nm) by MCQDPT, against an experimental 4.06 eV (306 nm) in ethyl ether, with a transition dipole orientation of 110 degrees and oscillator strength 0.615; the S0 to npi* excitation at 5.84 eV (212 nm) and 4.91 eV (252 nm), against an estimated experimental 4.46 eV (278 nm) in neutral aqueous buffer, a value the authors call highly uncertain because of the low oscillator strength and extensive solution broadening typical of npi* transitions; and emission from the optimized pipi* geometry at 4.22 eV (294 nm) and 3.67 eV (338 nm), against an experimental 3.60 eV (344 nm) in cyclohexane, with a transition dipole at 113 degrees and oscillator strength 0.113. Table 1 summarizes ten CASSCF calculations with their energies. The npi* state is dominated by a few configuration state functions, the largest coefficient corresponding to a single excitation from a nonbonding A' orbital localized on N1 to an A'' antibonding orbital localized on C6, whose distribution closely resembles the corresponding orbital in the pipi* state. In the optimized excited state the C6-N1 and C5-C6 bond distances increase while the adjacent N1-C2 and C5-N7 bonds shorten, consistent with reduced bond order from occupation of an antibonding orbital localized on C6; C6 buckles 0.13 Angstrom out of the molecular plane with an approximately equal and opposite displacement of H6 of -0.10 Angstrom. Both pipi* absorption and emission are predicted to shift to lower energy with increasing solvent polarity, the shift being slightly larger for emission; the weak solvent dependence of the excitation energy follows from the small change of 0.9 D in dipole moment and 24 degrees in orientation between the two states.
Other: This paper contains an unusually direct demonstration that which orbital types are in the space determines the geometry, not just the energy. The excited state was optimized with a space containing two sigma orbitals alongside the pi manifold, and the resulting structure buckles: C6 moves 0.13 Angstrom out of the molecular plane, with H6 displaced by an approximately equal and opposite 0.10 Angstrom. The authors state that this buckling of the pyrimidine ring is consistent with mixing between the sigma and pi electronic manifolds, as expected when both types of orbital are present in the active space, and then run the control -- a similar optimization with an active space containing no sigma orbitals produced a planar geometry. The conclusion drawn is explicit: coupling the sigma and pi manifolds in the active space is important for geometry optimization. A pi-only space would have returned a planar excited state and missed the out-of-plane distortion entirely. The paper is also careful about which properties survive the reduction from the larger to the smaller space and which may not. The pipi* excitation energy was effectively unchanged by the reduction, and the ground state molecular dipole changes by less than 5 percent in magnitude and less than 10 degrees in direction. But the authors flag the limitation rather than generalising from it: the same consistency may not be evident for the excited states, which will probably depend more sensitively on the composition of the active space, and they nonetheless compare the ground and npi* dipoles computed with twenty electrons in thirteen orbitals directly against the pipi* dipole computed with fourteen electrons in ten. Those dipoles feed the solvatochromic analysis, so that mismatch propagates into the solvent shift coefficients. Two further composition choices are recorded. One occupied pi orbital, localized to the N9-C9' bond, was deliberately excluded because excitations from it did not contribute significantly to the electronic configuration at the initial geometry -- an occupation-based exclusion rather than an energetic one. And the two sigma orbitals retained in the reduced space are specifically the nonbonding orbitals localized on N1 and N3, so the reduction removed bonding sigma character while keeping the lone pairs that the npi* state needs. Finally, state averaging is used asymmetrically by design: equally weighted two-state averaging for the pipi* energies, on the stated grounds that it equalizes the dynamic correlation contribution to ground and excited states, but pure states for the npi*, because the ground and npi* states have differing symmetries. The npi* and pipi* transition energies in the same table therefore come from differently constructed references.

Other: This paper is a clean example of a case where one active space cannot do the job and the authors say so explicitly: it is not possible to include the whole pi system and the lone pairs in the same active space, so two complementary spaces were designed and each excited state is reported from whichever space can represent it. The (16,12) space targets the n to pi* transitions and therefore contains three lone pairs -- two from the nitro group and one from the aldehyde -- together with two pi(CC)/pi*(CC) pairs from the ring, one pi(CO)/pi*(CO) pair, one pi(NO2)/pi*(NO2) pair, and a non-bonding p orbital on the nitro group. The (12,11) space drops the lone pairs entirely to make room for the full aromatic pi system, holding three pi(CC)/pi*(CC) pairs, the pi(CO)/pi*(CO) pair, the pi(NO2)/pi*(NO2) pair and the same non-bonding nitro p orbital, and it exists to describe the high-energy pi to pi* transitions. The consequence is spelled out in the table footnotes and must be carried by anyone reusing these numbers: within a single column of excitation energies, S1 through S3 come from the (16,12) space and S4 through S6 from the (12,11) space. Those are not states of one calculation but of two, spliced by character. State averaging follows the same split -- the (16,12) calculations run one root for the A' ground state and a three-root average over the A'' excited states, while the (12,11) calculations average over four A' roots comprising the ground state and three pi-pi* states, with equal weights throughout. Because the ground state appears in both averages, the two blocks of excitation energies are referenced to slightly different ground states. The trade-off has a visible cost in coverage: several states that the coupled cluster comparison method finds, including additional n to pi* states at intermediate energies, simply have no multiconfigurational counterpart in the tables, marked with a dash, because neither space was built to hold them. A second observation the spaces make possible concerns the two meta conformers. Their S5 energies differ by about 0.4 eV at the perturbation level and 0.2 eV at the coupled cluster level, a gap much larger than for any other transition, and the authors attribute this specifically to the orbitals involved in those transitions not being of the same nature for the two conformers. That is a warning about orbital-composition drift between closely related structures computed in a fixed space: the conformers are nearly degenerate in energy, 0.02 eV apart, yet one particular excited state is carried by different orbitals in each. Dynamical correlation was added by second-order perturbation theory on the state-averaged references with a level shift of 0.3 au to remove intruder states, and oscillator strengths come from the RASSI state interaction method using multistate perturbation energies together with perturbation-modified transition dipole moments -- so intensities and energies are not from the same wave function either. One further inconsistency of provenance: the para and meta calculations were done in Cs symmetry, whereas the ortho isomer's numbers come from an earlier study performed without symmetry.

compound_name: o-Nitrophenol and its aci-nitro isomers, photoisomerization through an intersystem crossing network
point_group: C1; geometries of minima and transition states were fully optimized without imposing any constraint, though all ground-state isomers turn out planar within the aromatic ring while the excited-state nitro forms are nonplanar
geometry_source: Minima and transition states fully optimized at 6SA-CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G(d,p) without symmetry constraints, characterized by harmonic vibrational frequencies at the same level, with intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations to confirm the connected reactant and product. One-dimensional curved surfaces between saddle points were built by linear interpolation in internal coordinates.
method: State-averaged CASSCF for geometries and surfaces, with energies corrected by multireference configuration interaction including the Davidson correction (MRCI+Q); spin-orbit couplings computed by MRCI with the full Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian
basis_set: 6-31G(d,p) for the CASSCF calculations, with 6-31+G(d,p) also tested; cc-pVDZ for the MRCI+Q energy corrections
soc_included: yes, computed at the MRCI level with the full Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals: two pi/pi* pairs in the benzene ring, one pi/pi* pair and a lone pair in the nitro group, with the remaining orbitals being the sigma and sigma* of the N-O bond.
active_space_protocol: The authors state that selection of the active space is the key step in the calculation, and follow Roos's rules to choose it. The composition mixes ring pi, nitro pi and lone pair, and N-O sigma character so that the ring excitations, the nitro-localized excitations and the bond being made and broken are all representable. The nature of the CASSCF orbitals was checked at all relevant local minima and transition states to confirm the space remains appropriate along the reaction. Because the hydrogen transfer involves two low-lying singlets and two low-lying triplets, four-, five- and six-state averaged variants were tested, judged on the natural character of the excited states and on smooth evolution of the molecular orbitals along the reaction coordinate and at the intersystem crossings; basis sets 6-31G(d,p) and 6-31+G(d,p) were compared and larger spaces with more active orbitals and electrons were also tried. The six-state average, comprising three low-lying singlets and three low-lying triplets with equal weights, was confirmed as accurate for the S0, S1, T1 and T2 surfaces and used throughout.

nroots_per_mult: three low-lying singlet and three low-lying triplet states, equally weighted
electronic_structure_description: The ground-state global minimum has a planar geometry with strong intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the hydroxyl and nitro groups, taken as the zero of energy. Three aci-nitro isomers were located on the ground state, all planar within the aromatic ring. The first lies 32.0 kcal/mol above the global minimum and is the only one with an intramolecular hydrogen bond to the ortho oxygen, but it is unstable and returns to the global minimum over a barrier of only 3 kcal/mol; the second lies at 31.8 kcal/mol and the third at 29.7 kcal/mol. Three ground-state transition states were found: a planar hydrogen transfer structure in which the O11-H12 bond is elongated by 0.329 Angstrom and the O15-H12 bond shortened by 0.764 Angstrom, a noncoplanar structure in which the C5-C4-N13-O15 dihedral rotates by -13.9 degrees taking the HONO group out of the aromatic plane, and a migration-of-planarity structure at about 36 kcal/mol that moves the hydrogen between the two nitro oxygens; the second isomer needs 11 kcal/mol to reach the first. Vertical excitation from the ground-state minimum reaches S1 at 100.3 kcal/mol, T2 at 93.9 kcal/mol and T1 at 90.03 kcal/mol. On S1 the lowest minimum is the planar nitro form at 78.8 kcal/mol, followed by isomer1 at 83.2, isomer3 at 61.9 and isomer2 at 53.3 kcal/mol, with the lowest transition state at 103.4 kcal/mol leaving a well about 24.6 kcal/mol deep in which the molecule can be trapped. On T1 the lowest minimum is isomer1 at 47.3 kcal/mol, with the nitro form at 72.0 and isomer3 at 73.1, and the lowest transition state at 91.1 kcal/mol giving a well about 20 kcal/mol deep. On T2 the lowest minimum is isomer3 at 52.4 kcal/mol, followed by isomer2 at 52.9, the nitro form at 56.1 and isomer1 at 89.7, with the lowest transition state as high as 120 kcal/mol, so the molecule cannot adiabatically escape that well once trapped. The excited-state nitro forms are nonplanar, the T1 and T2 forms having C5-C4-N13-O15 dihedrals rotated by 51.0 and -10.9 degrees respectively. The dominant stepwise photoisomerization proceeds through S1 and T1 states first, then T1 and S0, with both intersystem crossing regions showing spin-orbit couplings on the order of 40 per cm.
Other: The active space here is chosen by an explicit rule and then validated in two ways that are worth separating. The composition is stated orbital block by orbital block -- two ring pi/pi* pairs, one nitro pi/pi* pair plus a nitro lone pair, and the N-O sigma and sigma* -- which covers the ring excitations, the nitro-localized excitations and the bond directly involved in the chemistry. The first validation is spatial: the nature of the CASSCF orbitals was checked at all relevant local minima and transition states to make sure the chosen space remains appropriate along the reaction, which is the check that catches a space whose contents drift as the geometry changes. The second is about state averaging, and the criterion used is unusual and instructive. Four-, five- and six-state averages were all tested, and the authors say the main issues were the natural character of the excited states and the smooth evolution of the molecular orbitals along the intrinsic reaction coordinate and at the intersystem crossings. Smoothness of the orbitals along a path, not a variational energy, is what selected the six-state average -- three singlets and three triplets with equal weights. That criterion matters because the entire result is a network of intersystem crossings between four surfaces, and a reference whose orbitals switch character partway along a path would produce spurious crossings. They also report testing two basis sets and even larger spaces with more active orbitals and electrons, settling on the smaller combination as adequate. What that means in practice is that the reference was tuned for the continuity of a multi-surface topology rather than for the accuracy of any single energy, which is consistent with the energies being replaced afterward by MRCI with the Davidson correction in a different basis. A caveat follows from that split: the geometries, frequencies and reaction paths come from a six-state-averaged CASSCF in a 6-31G(d,p) basis while the reported energies come from MRCI+Q in cc-pVDZ, so the stationary points are not stationary at the level of the quoted energies. The spin-orbit couplings, which carry the mechanistic conclusion, come from MRCI with the full Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian rather than from the state-averaged reference, and are on the order of 40 per cm at both crossing regions. The surfaces connecting the saddle points are linear interpolations in internal coordinates rather than relaxed paths, so barrier heights read off them are upper bounds.

compound_name: H2 formation inside the T8 polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane cage, [HSiO1.5]8
geometry_source: Structures optimized at the Hartree-Fock level with the 6-31G(d) basis and characterized by frequency analyses, with single-point MP2 energies on those geometries; transition-state structures for hydrogen insertion into each cage located and used as trajectory starting points
method: Ab initio molecular dynamics at the CASSCF level, with Hartree-Fock geometry optimization and MP2 single-point energies for the reaction energetics
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF dynamics and the Hartree-Fock optimizations; 6-31+G(d,p) used additionally at the MP2 level and to test the CASSCF dissociation curve
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals, being the two electrons and the two orbitals of the colliding hydrogen atoms. The silsesquioxane host is entirely outside the active space.
active_space_protocol: A minimal two-electron two-orbital space confined to the colliding hydrogen atoms, chosen so that the formation and dissociation of the H-H bond is described correctly across the whole trajectory while the cage is treated at the mean-field level. The two-electron two-orbital dissociation curves for the hydrogen molecule were compared between the 6-31G(d) and 6-31+G(d,p) basis sets and found essentially indistinguishable, which justified running all the dynamics in the smaller basis.
electronic_structure_description: Trajectories were started by inserting a second hydrogen atom into the hydrogen-encapsulated cage, and in many cases the gradual formation of a hydrogen molecule was observed after frequent collisions of the two hydrogen atoms within the cage. Two sets of initial conditions were used: inserting the second hydrogen with a small kinetic energy of 0.5 kcal/mol starting from the transition state for the insertion reaction, and inserting it with a kinetic energy larger than the insertion barrier, starting 2.5 Angstrom above a cage face; the latter used 60 kcal/mol of kinetic energy for this cage. The face through which insertion occurs is expanded relative to the other faces, as previously seen for direct H2 insertion. The binding energy of a hydrogen molecule in the gas phase is calculated to be 94.0 kcal/mol at the CASSCF(2,2) level. Of the three reactions considered, insertion of an H atom and insertion of an H2 molecule into the empty cage are endothermic while the stepwise route through the mono-hydrogen adduct is exothermic, and the MP2 stabilization energy of the product relative to the two separated reactants is only slightly smaller than the gas-phase hydrogen binding energy. Both cages expand on including the impurities.
Other: The active space here is as small as a multiconfigurational treatment can be -- two electrons in two orbitals -- and the paper is explicit that those are the orbitals of the two colliding hydrogen atoms and nothing else. The whole silsesquioxane cage, dozens of Si-O and Si-H bonds, is outside the space and described only at the mean-field level. That is a defensible choice for the specific question being asked, because the process under study is the making of a single sigma bond between two hydrogen atoms, which is exactly the textbook case a two-orbital space describes and a single determinant cannot: at large separation the two-electron two-orbital wave function goes correctly to two neutral atoms where a restricted single determinant would not. The cost is that nothing about the cage's own electronic structure can respond multiconfigurationally, so any polarization or charge transfer between the encapsulated hydrogens and the host is only present through the orbital optimization, not through the configuration expansion. Two checks are reported that bear on how much the choice constrains the result. The basis set dependence of the space's central quantity was tested directly: the two-electron two-orbital dissociation curves for the hydrogen molecule in the 6-31G(d) and the larger 6-31+G(d,p) basis sets are described as essentially indistinguishable, which is what justified running the whole dynamics in the smaller basis. Separately, diffuse and polarization functions were found to change inclusion energies by 1.9 to 9.8 kcal/mol and barrier heights by 1.3 to 4.2 kcal/mol at the perturbative level, so the basis matters for the host-guest energetics even though it does not matter for the bond the active space describes. That asymmetry is the practical lesson: the space was validated on the quantity it governs, while the quantities it does not govern were left to a different method. Note also that the energetics quoted for the inclusion reactions come from second-order perturbation theory on Hartree-Fock geometries, not from the multiconfigurational calculation, which supplies only the dynamics and the reference hydrogen binding energy of 94.0 kcal/mol in the gas phase. Anyone reusing these numbers should keep the two levels apart.

notes: Effects of diffuse and polarization functions at the MP2 level change inclusion energies by 1.9 to 9.8 kcal/mol and barrier heights by 1.3 to 4.2 kcal/mol; these energetics come from MP2, not from the multiconfigurational calculation.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF dynamics; MP2 single points on Hartree-Fock geometries supply the reaction energetics separately

compound_name: CO2+ ion, Jahn-Teller and Renner-Teller topological effects among the lowest A'' and three A' states
point_group: Cs is taken as the symmetry for the calculations, so the states are of A' and A'' symmetry; the ground state at the collinear geometry is 2Pi_g
geometry_source: Configuration space sampled on circular contours in a mathematical plane centred on the collinear axis. In the first scheme the O-C bond is fixed at 1.18 Angstrom while a second oxygen revolves around a centre on the collinear axis 0.6 Angstrom from the carbon, with contour radii q varied from 0.2 to 2.4 Angstrom; a second scheme places small circles of radius 0.4 Angstrom around the fixed oxygen.
method: State-averaged CASSCF, used to compute nonadiabatic coupling terms by numerical differentiation, from which adiabatic-to-diabatic transformation angles and topological phases are obtained by contour integration
active_space_orbital_description: Eleven valence electrons distributed among ten active orbitals. Five orbitals were kept closed: the three core orbitals and two valence orbitals. The ion has 21 electrons in total, 15 of them valence and 6 core, with 12 valence orbitals and 3 core orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is defined by closing the three cores plus two valence orbitals and leaving the remaining eleven valence electrons in ten active orbitals. State-averaged three-state calculations with equal weights were used. Nonadiabatic coupling terms were obtained by MOLPRO's numerical differentiation method; because derivatives are needed with respect to only one internal coordinate, the angular variable, a step of one degree was used in most cases.
nroots_per_mult: three states, equally weighted, in the state-averaged calculations; a four-state treatment including the Renner-Teller state was used for one contour
electronic_structure_description: Three types of Jahn-Teller nonadiabatic coupling terms are required, between states 1 and 2, 2 and 3, and 1 and 3. For small contours in the first scheme, radii of 0.2 and 0.3 Angstrom, reasonably quantized topological phases were already obtained with only the two Jahn-Teller states 1A' and 2A', the phase being about pi, which indicates a single (1,2) conical intersection inside the enclosed region; adding the third state made only a minor contribution. Increasing the radius to 1.0, 1.2, 1.4 and 2.1 Angstrom expands the enclosed configuration space from about 0.1 to about 14 square Angstrom and forces the rotating oxygen either to pass between the carbon and the other oxygen or, at 2.1 Angstrom, to surround the CO diatom; the coupling terms then acquire numerous wiggles, the two-state privileged angles become distorted and the phases are far from quantized. Including three Jahn-Teller states restores nicely quantized phases of about pi with deviations of 2 to 3 percent, while the number of (1,2) conical intersections inside the contour remains one. At radii of 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 Angstrom the enclosed area grows to about 18 square Angstrom and the coupling terms become still more wiggled and spikier; three states remain sufficient for quantization, though less accurately, and the quantized phase changes discontinuously from about pi to about 2 pi, revealing a second (1,2) conical intersection. Calculations in the second scheme confirmed the existence of that second intersection near the fixed oxygen, completing the picture of the (1,2) intersection distribution. For the 2.2 Angstrom contour the three-state phase of 6.77 deviated significantly from 2 pi; including the Renner-Teller state in a four-state calculation improved it to 6.34.
Other: The active space is fixed at eleven valence electrons in ten orbitals throughout, and the variable under study is not its size but the number of states averaged over -- which this paper turns into a quantitative diagnostic rather than a convergence chore. The topological phase obtained by integrating nonadiabatic couplings around a closed contour must come out as an integer multiple of pi if the group of states included is complete over the region enclosed, so the quantization defect measures directly whether the state space is sufficient. The results read as a map of that sufficiency. For small contours, two Jahn-Teller states suffice and the third contributes only marginally. As the contour grows and the rotating oxygen is forced to pass between the two heavy atoms, the couplings develop numerous wiggles that reinforce one another, the two-state phases stop being quantized and the derived privileged angles become distorted; adding the third A' state restores quantization to within 2 to 3 percent. Larger still, and the phase jumps discontinuously from about pi to about 2 pi, which is not a failure but the signature of a second conical intersection entering the enclosed region -- confirmed independently by repeating the analysis on small contours around the other oxygen. And where three states left a residual defect, the phase coming out at 6.77 rather than 2 pi, including the Renner-Teller state in a four-state treatment brought it to 6.34. So state-averaging over too few roots produces errors that are visible as a broken quantization condition, and the fix is to add exactly the state whose coupling was being omitted. For anyone reusing this record, the practical points are that the closed-orbital choice removes two valence orbitals as well as the three cores from the correlated treatment, and that the couplings come from numerical differentiation with a one-degree step in a single angular coordinate, so the reported phases inherit whatever numerical error that finite difference carries -- relevant given that the couplings become spiky at the larger radii where the quantization is least accurate.
reference_short: Dhindhwal, Baer & Sathyamurthy, J. Phys. Chem. A 2016, 120, 2999
notes: The work belongs to a series developing procedures for constructing reliable diabatic potential energy surfaces at the ab initio level, for use in analysing chemical reactions, inelastic collisions, unimolecular dissociation, spectroscopic transitions and charge transfer. The theoretical treatment is extended in an appendix to a four-state system formed by three Jahn-Teller states and one Renner-Teller state.

compound_name: O(3P) + CH2OH hydrogen abstraction transition states
geometry_source: Transition states for the two abstraction channels optimized at the CASSCF level with the cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ basis sets; geometry optimizations and frequency calculations performed in Gaussian, single-point energies in Molpro
method: CASSCF geometry optimization for the abstraction transition states, with barrier heights from CASPT2 and from multireference configuration interaction with single and double excitations, some with the Davidson correction; coupled cluster and G3MP2 results for comparison
software: Gaussian for the geometry optimizations and frequencies; Molpro for the single-point energies; Variflex for the kinetics
active_space_orbital_description: Five electrons in five orbitals, denoted CAS(5,5), used for the transition state geometry optimizations. A larger reference of nineteen electrons in thirteen orbitals was used for some of the multireference configuration interaction single points.
active_space_protocol: Multireference SCF methods were adopted because the Hartree-Fock determinant is spin-contaminated at the abstraction transition states, as indicated by the expectation value of S squared. A CAS(5,5) reference was used for the geometry optimizations in both basis sets, and single-point energies were then computed on those geometries at CASPT2 and at MRCISD, the latter both with the small reference and with a larger (19,13) reference, each also with a Davidson correction.
electronic_structure_description: Table 2 gives total energies in hartree with zero-point-corrected barrier heights in kcal/mol in parentheses, for the reactants and the two abstraction transition states. CAS(5,5)/cc-pVDZ: -189.22800, -189.20789 (12.6) and -189.20830 (12.4). CAS(5,5)/cc-pVTZ: -189.28482, -189.26653 (11.5) and -189.26487 (12.5). CASPT2/cc-pVDZ on the double-zeta geometry: -189.60584, -189.63867 (-20.6) and -189.59615 (6.1). CASPT2/cc-pVTZ on the double-zeta geometry: -189.82735, -189.86508 (-23.7) and -189.81914 (5.2). CASPT2/cc-pVTZ on the triple-zeta geometry: -189.82765, -189.87663 (-30.7) and -189.81945 (5.1). MRCISD/cc-pVTZ on the triple-zeta geometry: -189.78861, -189.79326 (-2.9) and -189.77949 (5.7); with the Davidson correction: -189.84678, -189.85780 (-6.9) and -189.84582 (0.6). MRCISD with the larger (19,13) reference: -189.79576 and -189.80175 (-3.8); with the Davidson correction: -189.84558 and -189.85911 (-8.5). G3MP2 on the triple-zeta geometry: -189.92469, -189.92707 (-1.5) and -189.90989 (9.3). For comparison, CISD/cc-pVDZ and cc-pVTZ give barriers of 27.6 and 31.6 kcal/mol for the first transition state and CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ on the CISD geometry gives -0.5 kcal/mol. The conclusion drawn is that the two abstraction paths are essentially barrierless. The reaction has two mechanisms, a chemical activation addition-elimination path in which association of the oxygen atom with the radical proceeds on a barrierless attractive surface, and direct hydrogen abstraction giving either OH plus CH2O or OH plus HCOH.
Other: The instructive feature here is how far the computed barrier moves as the reference and the correlation treatment change, on transition states that turn out to be essentially barrierless. The multireference approach was not a stylistic choice: the Hartree-Fock determinant is spin-contaminated at both abstraction transition states, diagnosed by the expectation value of S squared, so single-reference methods cannot describe these paths correctly. Single-reference configuration interaction confirms this dramatically, giving barriers of 27.6 and 31.6 kcal/mol in the two basis sets for the first channel, against essentially zero from the better treatments. Within the multireference results, however, the spread is still large and instructive. Bare CAS(5,5) puts the first barrier at 12.6 and 11.5 kcal/mol in the two basis sets. Adding second-order perturbation theory on that same five-orbital reference swings it to -20.6, -23.7 and -30.7 kcal/mol depending on basis and geometry -- a change of more than 40 kcal/mol from correlation alone, and one that grows rather than converges as the basis and geometry improve, which is a warning sign that the perturbation is straining. method: A stochastic CASSCF in which full configuration interaction quantum Monte Carlo replaces the deterministic configuration interaction eigensolver inside a Super-CI orbital optimization framework, using the initiator approximation with a threshold of 3.0, the semi-stochastic method with a deterministic subspace of the 10000 most populated determinants, and replica sampling of the reduced density matrices

Metal contractions were Mg (4s3p1d) from 17s12p6d2f2g primitives and Fe (5s4p2d1f) from 21s15p10d6f4g2h primitives, giving 414 and 430 basis functions respectively.

By irreducible representation the active orbitals are 7 of b1u, 6 of b2g, 6 of b3g and 5 of au symmetry, with 20, 17, 17 and 14 inactive orbitals in ag, b3u, b2u and b1g. No sigma orbitals are included.
active_space_protocol: The full pi valence space with no truncation of the configuration space within it and no orbitals frozen or deleted at the multiconfigurational level. Canonical Hartree-Fock orbitals were used as the starting orbitals. The wave function was optimized separately for the 1Ag ground state and for the 1B3u and 1B2u excited states responsible for the Q bands. Walker populations were raised from 200 thousand during the orbital optimization to 5 million and then 10 million for refined solutions.

Table 3 gives excitation energies in eV for the 1Ag to 1B3u and 1Ag to 1B2u transitions: 2.19 and 3.29 with 200 thousand walkers in the double-zeta basis, 2.05 and 3.25 at 5 million, 2.02 and 3.24 at 10 million; 2.08 and 3.27 at 5 million and 2.06 and 3.24 at 10 million in the triple-zeta basis; against 2.55 and 3.38 from a restricted active space calculation, 2.54 and 2.81 with its perturbative correction, and experimental values of 2.02 and 2.39 eV. compound_name: Ce3+ substituted at the Ca1 site of Ca6BaP4O17 with Si codoping
ligand_set: Oxygen coordination shell within the Ca6BaP4O17 host, with a charge-compensating Si4+ substituting for P at a nearby or remote site
geometry_source: Local structures optimized with the DFT-PBE0 method on Ca6BaP4O17 supercells; Ce-centred embedded clusters then constructed from those structures, with the surroundings within a 10 Angstrom sphere represented by 709 to 719 ab initio model potentials and the remainder by 79624 to 80927 point charges at lattice sites generated by Lepetit's method
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2 with spin-orbit coupling, on embedded clusters; DFT-PBE0 used for the host structure, defect formation energies and densities of states
basis_set: A relativistic effective core potential with a [Kr] core and a (14s10p10d8f3g)/[6s5p6d4f1g] Gaussian valence basis for cerium; a [He] core effective core potential with a (5s6p1d)/[2s4p1d] valence basis for oxygen; extra (11s8p)/[1s1p] and (10s7p)/[1s1p] basis sets on the P and Si atoms of the second coordination shell to improve orthogonality of the cluster orbitals with the embedding environment
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potentials on cerium and oxygen
active_space_orbital_description: A [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space, comprising the seven 4f orbitals, the five 5d orbitals and the 6s orbital of Ce3+, holding the single 4f electron.
active_space_protocol: The same [4f, 5d, 6s] space was applied to every dopant centre so that site-to-site differences reflect the environment rather than the reference. Dynamic correlation was introduced afterwards by CASPT2 correlating the Ce3+ 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons together with the O2- 2s and 2p electrons, and spin-orbit coupling was applied on top.
nroots_per_mult: seven 4f levels and five 5d levels per centre
electronic_structure_description: Table 2 gives calculated 4f1 and 5d1 energy levels in per cm for seven centres, with the 4f1 level taken as zero in each. For centres 1 to 5, all with a nearest-neighbour Si at a P1 site, and centres 10 and 11 with a distant compensator, the 4f levels 2 to 7 run 683, 1356, 2240, 2641, 3618, 3821; 588, 1364, 2292, 2655, 3305, 4360; 836, 1256, 2350, 2888, 3507, 4138; 632, 1382, 2297, 2681, 3316, 4398; 562, 1343, 2289, 2635, 3283, 4341; 611, 1414, 2293, 2691, 3365, 4349; and 757, 1417, 2340, 2747, 3499, 4612. The five 5d levels are 25900, 37511, 38624, 45724, 47761 for centre 1; 25193, 34233, 39135, 45158, 51736 for centre 2; 25516, 37669, 38882, 46253, 48076 for centre 3; 25258, 34538, 39387, 45087, 51635 for centre 4; 25271, 34395, 39246, 45596, 51508 for centre 5; 24767, 35302, 40353, 45297, 49877 for centre 10; and 23920, 35521, 40304, 45383, 50117 for centre 11. The tabulated centroid energies range from 39049 to 39279 per cm and the tabulated crystal-field splittings from 21861 to 26543 per cm. Ground term: the 4f1 configuration, split into seven Kramers levels by the crystal field and spin-orbit coupling. For this site the centres with a nearest-neighbour Si at a P1 site, centres 1 and 2, have lowest 5d levels at 25900 and 25193 per cm, against 24767 per cm for the centre with a remote compensator. Without a nearest-neighbour Si4+ the lowest 5d level at this site is higher by 847 per cm than at the other calcium site. The presence of Si4+ at a nearest-neighbour P1 site blueshifts the 4f to 5d transition by an average of 779 per cm for this site type, consistent with experimental observations, the overall blueshift relative to a remote compensator ranging from 426 to 1596 per cm across all centres.
Other: The active space is specified by shell label rather than by counts: a [4f, 5d, 6s] complete active space holding the single cerium valence electron. That is the minimal defensible choice for a lanthanide dopant whose entire optical behaviour is a 4f-to-5d transition, and it embodies a clear division of labour that the paper follows consistently. The space itself carries only the metal-centred manifold; everything that makes the transition energy site-specific enters through other channels. The host is represented by an embedded cluster with the immediate surroundings within a 10 Angstrom sphere modelled by 709 to 719 ab initio model potentials and the remainder by roughly 80000 point charges at lattice sites. Dynamical correlation is added afterwards by second-order perturbation theory correlating the cerium 5s, 5p, 4f and 5d electrons together with the oxygen 2s and 2p electrons -- so the ligand electrons are correlated but never made active, and spin-orbit coupling is applied on top. Including the 6s alongside the 4f and 5d is the notable detail: it is unoccupied in the ground configuration and contributes nothing to the leading configurations, but leaving it out would make the 5d manifold the top of the space with nothing above it to relax into, which matters when the quantity of interest is the crystal-field splitting of that very manifold. The result the space has to support is a set of differences of a few hundred to a few thousand per cm between crystallographically distinct dopant sites, extracted from absolute transition energies near 25000 per cm -- roughly a one percent effect. That the same fixed space is applied identically to every centre is what makes those differences meaningful; the sensitivity being probed is to the environment, not to the reference. Extra basis functions were added on the phosphorus and silicon atoms of the second coordination shell specifically to improve orthogonality of the cluster orbitals with the embedding potentials, which is the standard failure mode of this kind of embedding and worth recording. One internal inconsistency should be flagged rather than reconciled. The crystal-field splitting values tabulated for the seven centres run from 21861 to 26543 per cm, while the running text states that the splitting values are predicted to lie in the range 13204 to 15206 per cm and uses that smaller range to argue that centroid shift and crystal-field splitting contribute comparably to the large redshift. The tabulated numbers are consistent with the difference between the highest and lowest 5d levels in each column; the quoted range is not. Both are reproduced here as printed. A further caveat for reuse: the geometries come from density functional optimization of supercells, not from the multiconfigurational calculation, and the tabulated Ce-Si distances are given in both relaxed and unrelaxed forms.
reference_short: Ning, Huang, Sun, Huang, Chen, Xia & Huang, J. Phys. Chem. C 2016, 120, 3999
notes: Placing the Si4+ at a nearest-neighbour P2 site instead, which is less stable, lowers the computed 5d levels by about 1260 per cm relative to the P1 placement; increasing Ce and Si doping concentrations is argued to hinder lattice relaxation and thereby raise the relative formation probability of those less stable centres, enhancing the low-energy tail seen experimentally.
