compound_name: OAr+ molecular ion, the a 2Pi and b 2Pi states arising from O + Ar+ collisions
point_group: The diatomic must be represented in C2v using the a1, a2, b1 and b2 irreducible representations because the software supports only abelian point groups
geometry_source: Potential energy curves computed pointwise as a function of internuclear separation; no geometry optimization, with the equilibrium separations obtained from the computed curves
method: A three-step sequence at each internuclear separation: restricted Hartree-Fock, then CASSCF, then multireference configuration interaction, with fourth-order Douglas-Kroll relativistic corrections and two-point extrapolation of the energies to the complete basis set limit
basis_set: Two relativistic basis sets, aug-cc-pwCVQZ-DK and aug-cc-pwCV5Z-DK, the largest available, used in a two-point extrapolation to the complete basis set limit with cardinal numbers 4 and 5
active_space_orbital_description: Ten molecular orbitals were used in the active space of the multireference configuration interaction calculations, with the remaining electrons placed in closed-shell orbitals. The number of active electrons is not stated.
active_space_protocol: A ten-orbital active space carried through the CASSCF and multireference configuration interaction steps, with all remaining electrons confined to closed shells. The sequence Hartree-Fock, then CASSCF, then multireference configuration interaction was applied at every internuclear separation, which is what allows a smooth curve to be traced through the avoided crossing between the two states of the same symmetry.
nroots_per_mult: two states of 2Pi symmetry
electronic_structure_description: The two states studied, a 2Pi and b 2Pi, both correlate with an argon ion and an oxygen atom in their respective ground states. Because they share the same symmetry they are not allowed to cross, and the computed curves show an avoided crossing whose region is analysed in detail. The dissociation energy of the lower state, obtained by computing the lowest vibrational level with the Fourier grid Hamiltonian method, is 2.594 eV with an equilibrium separation of 1.666 Angstrom, and the potential supports 81 bound vibrational levels. Earlier fourth-order perturbation theory work with a smaller basis gave a noticeably different 2.133 eV at a similar 1.665 Angstrom, values close to what the present Hartree-Fock step gives with the larger basis. The computed dissociation energy exceeds the 2.46 eV inferred from a thermodynamic cycle; the authors attribute the difference to their neglect of spin-orbit splitting, which in the argon ion alone is 0.1774 eV and whose inclusion would significantly lower the computed value, and to the absence of any basis set superposition error correction, which would also reduce it. For the upper b 2Pi state the computed dissociation energy is 0.145 eV at an equilibrium separation of 2.961 Angstrom, for which no previous computed values exist. The curves were used to obtain scattering phase shifts and from them differential, integral, diffusion and viscosity cross sections over the collision energy range 0.03 to 500 eV, with a numerical Numerov treatment used above 5 eV.
Other: The active space here is reported only as ten molecular orbitals with all remaining electrons in closed shells, and the electron count is never given, so that field is left empty rather than inferred. What the space has to accomplish is unusual and worth recording: the two states being computed, a 2Pi and b 2Pi, have the same symmetry and therefore cannot cross, so the entire calculation hinges on tracing both roots smoothly through an avoided crossing at every point along the internuclear coordinate. A single-reference method cannot do this, which is why the authors run a fixed three-step sequence -- Hartree-Fock, then CASSCF, then multireference configuration interaction -- at each separation rather than optimizing anything, and why the ten-orbital space must be held constant across the whole curve. The energy separation of the two adiabatic curves at the crossing point is twice the off-diagonal coupling element, and the paper analyses that region explicitly. There is also a clean illustration of what the multireference treatment buys, because the intermediate Hartree-Fock step provides an internal control. The dissociation energy of the lower state comes out at 2.594 eV from the full treatment, whereas the authors note that their Hartree-Fock step with the same large basis reproduces the earlier fourth-order perturbation theory value of about 2.133 eV -- so the correlation treatment on this space is worth roughly 0.46 eV on a bond energy, while the basis extrapolation from quadruple to quintuple zeta and the relativistic correction are applied on top of that. Two omissions are stated by the authors and both push the same way: spin-orbit coupling was not included, and the argon ion alone carries a splitting of 0.1774 eV, so including it would significantly lower the computed dissociation energy; and no basis set superposition error correction was applied, which would lower it further. The computed 2.594 eV therefore sits above a thermodynamic-cycle value of 2.46 eV for reasons the authors identify rather than dismiss. A practical note: the diatomic has to be represented in an abelian subgroup because the software supports nothing higher, so the states are labelled through C2v irreducible representations rather than in the natural linear symmetry.
reference_short: Sycheva, Balint-Kurti & Palov, J. Phys. Chem. A 2016, 120, 4655
notes: Accurate potential energy curves for the excited states of this ion are needed in plasma research. Only a single earlier calculation of the lower state exists, at the fourth-order perturbation theory level. Cross sections were computed for relative collision energies from 0.03 to 5 eV by one method and from 5 to 500 eV by the Numerov method for low partial waves.
correlation_correction: Multireference configuration interaction on the CASSCF reference, followed by two-point extrapolation to the complete basis set limit

compound_name: Lanthanide(III) trihalides LnX3, used to benchmark all-electron relativistic basis sets for 4f-shell CASSCF and NEVPT2
metal_center: Lanthanides in the +3 oxidation state, with the praseodymium trichloride used as the specific f-f and f-d test case and the erbium basis illustrated in detail
d_electron_count: 4f-n, n varying across the series; the trivalent oxidation state was chosen as the most relevant for chemical applications and to avoid bias from irregular configurations at other oxidation states
ligand_set: Three halide ligands; the trichlorides were used for the exponent optimization at geometry-optimized structures
geometry_source: Geometry-optimized structures of the trichlorides were used for the polarization exponent optimization
method: CASSCF with the 4f shell as the active space, followed by n-electron valence-state second-order perturbation theory, used to benchmark newly constructed segmented all-electron relativistically contracted basis sets; DFT calculations used alongside for geometries, orbital eigenvalues, ionization potentials and bond energies
software: Not stated in the extracted text; the resolution-of-identity approximations discussed are those available for CASSCF and NEVPT2
basis_set: Second-generation SARC2 segmented all-electron relativistically contracted basis sets, individually adapted to the DKH2 and ZORA Hamiltonians, with an expanded f space. Polarization sets 1g, 2g, 2g1h, 3g1h, 3g2h and 3g2h1i were tested in decontracted form and 3g2h adopted, giving SARC2-QZVP with g exponents 19.1, 4.75, 1.18 and h exponents 10.1, 3.8. Compared against a fully decontracted ANO-RCC basis, 301 primitives decontracted to 25s22p15d11f4g2h for erbium. New auxiliary basis sets for resolution-of-identity approximations are also presented.
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess and zero-order regular approximation Hamiltonians, with basis sets individually adapted to each
soc_included: spin-orbit coupling parameters are among the benchmarked quantities
active_space_orbital_description: Seven orbitals, the 4f shell, holding n electrons where n is set by the particular trivalent lanthanide, written CASSCF(n,7). The electron count therefore varies across the series and is not a single value.
active_space_protocol: The 4f shell alone forms the active space for every member of the series, held fixed while the one-particle basis is varied, so that the computed excitation energies test the basis rather than the correlation treatment. Excitation energies of all possible highest-multiplicity states arising from these calculations were used, equally weighted, as the fitting target. Polarization function exponents were optimized to maximize the perturbative correction to the state energies on top of the CASSCF references, without imposing any frozen core approximation. Reference orbital shapes came from state-averaged Hartree-Fock calculations on the trivalent ions, using three neutral configurations and one ionic configuration.
multiplicities_studied: the highest-multiplicity states arising from each 4f-n configuration
nroots_per_mult: all possible highest-multiplicity states, equally weighted
electronic_structure_description: Excitation energies of the lanthanide trihalides span from a few tens to about 60000 per cm. Adding the largest polarization sets changes them by around 5 percent relative to the unpolarized basis, while the two largest sets differ from each other by only 0.16 percent on average, with a maximum absolute deviation of 31 per cm on a 35000 per cm excitation and a maximum relative deviation of 4 percent corresponding to 10 per cm on a 230 per cm excitation; the vast majority of deviations fall well below 1 percent. Against a decontracted ANO-RCC reference for the praseodymium trichloride f-f and f-d excitations, the multiconfigurational results agree to a mean deviation of 140.8 per cm overall and 18.2 per cm for excitations below 1000 per cm. The perturbative corrections to the d-f excitations are larger with the new basis, 30 percent, than with the reference, 23 percent. A basis combining the new valence set with the reference basis's g and h primitives gives excitation energies closer to the new basis, with a mean absolute error of 148.8 per cm, than to the fully decontracted reference at 3068 per cm; for excitations below 1000 per cm the two polarization choices perform comparably at 18.2 and 19.4 per cm. Deviations in the multiconfigurational excitation energies under the resolution-of-identity approximation reach a maximum of 10.7 per cm.
Other: The active space in this study is the 4f shell and nothing else -- CASSCF(n,7), with n the number of 4f electrons appropriate to each trivalent lanthanide -- and it is deliberately held fixed while the one-particle basis is varied. That inversion of the usual arrangement is the point: the active space is the constant, the basis is the variable, and the excitation energies of the lanthanide trihalides become a probe of basis quality rather than of correlation treatment. Because a bare 4f shell space captures essentially no dynamical correlation on its own, the perturbative correction on top of it is large, and the polarization exponents were fitted specifically to maximize that correction, which is a different optimization target from the usual variational one. Six polarization sets of increasing size were tested in decontracted form -- 1g, 2g, 2g1h, 3g1h, 3g2h and 3g2h1i -- with the excitation energies of all possible highest-multiplicity states from the CASSCF(n,7) calculations, equally weighted. The largest sets change excitation energies by about 5 percent relative to the unpolarized basis, and the two largest agree with each other to 0.16 percent on average, so the 3g2h set is taken as converged. The residual outliers are worth recording because they show where a fixed f-shell space is most exposed: a maximum absolute deviation of 31 per cm on a 35000 per cm excitation, but a maximum relative deviation of 4 percent on a 230 per cm excitation, with the vast majority below 1 percent. The comparison against a decontracted atomic natural orbital basis exposes something the active space alone cannot fix. At the multiconfigurational level the two bases agree well, with a mean deviation of 140.8 per cm falling to 18.2 per cm if only excitations below 1000 per cm are considered, the deviations scaling roughly with excitation energy across a range from tens to 60000 per cm. But the perturbative corrections to the f-to-d excitations differ substantially, 30 percent with the new basis against 23 percent with the reference basis. The authors attribute this to their exponents having been optimized for correlation energies without imposing any frozen core, so the new set is likely recovering part of the semi-core correlation; consistent with that, its polarization exponents (g at 19.1, 4.75, 1.18 and h at 10.1, 3.8) are far tighter than the reference values (g at 2.24, 1.13, 0.45, 0.18 and h at 1.36, 0.54). A control calculation grafting the reference basis's g and h primitives onto the new valence basis gave excitation energies resembling the new basis, with a mean absolute error of 148.8 per cm, rather than the fully decontracted reference at 3068 per cm. The practical lesson for anyone using a 4f-only active space on lanthanides is therefore that the f-to-f transitions are basis-insensitive to within about 20 per cm while the f-to-d transitions, which reach outside the active shell, are not, and that how much semi-core correlation a basis's polarization functions were fitted to recover determines the answer.
reference_short: Aravena, Neese & Pantazis, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2016, 12, 1148
notes: This is a basis set development and benchmarking paper rather than a study of a particular compound; the lanthanide trihalides serve as the test systems. The basis sets are benchmarked on excitation energies, radial distribution functions, optimized geometries, orbital eigenvalues, ionization potentials and spin-orbit coupling parameters. A slightly expanded f space relative to the first-generation basis sets is credited with sizable improvement in the multiconfigurational energies and significantly more accurate spin-orbit coupling parameters.
correlation_correction: NEVPT2 on the CASSCF(n,7) references, with no frozen core imposed during the exponent optimization

ligand_set: Six bridging and terminal fluoride ligands
point_group: D2h for most structures, with a C2h structure reached from the difluoro compound by following imaginary modes
geometry_source: Preliminary geometry optimizations at the restricted Hartree-Fock level, after which modified virtual orbitals were generated by removing six electrons and used as the starting point for two-configuration self-consistent field singlet optimizations; doublet and triplet geometries optimized at the ROHF level. Stationary points characterized by diagonalizing the Hessian.
method: Two-configuration self-consistent field geometry optimization with multireference second-order perturbation theory single points for dynamic correlation, a fully optimized reaction space MCSCF of two electrons in ten orbitals for excited states, and Z-averaged perturbation theory for the doublets; spin-orbit coupling evaluated by three operator approximations at both the multiconfigurational and quasi-degenerate perturbation levels
software: GAMESS, with MacMolPlt used for visualization
basis_set: TZV(p) for the geometry optimizations and base energies, with TZVP(f) and TZVP(fg) single points as a test of basis set convergence
soc_included: yes, computed by a one-electron spin-orbit operator method, a partial two-electron plus full one-electron method, and the full Pauli-Breit operator method, each applied at both the multiconfigurational and the multiconfiguration quasi-degenerate perturbation levels
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in ten orbitals for the excited-state calculations. Geometry optimizations instead use a two-configuration wave function, effectively two electrons in two orbitals, whose natural orbitals are the metal-metal sigma and sigma-star pair; the two low-lying singlet configurations discussed are sigma-sigma-star and delta-delta-star.
active_space_protocol: A two-configuration self-consistent field wave function, equivalent to generalized valence bond perfect pairing with one pair, was used for the singlet geometry optimizations, with perturbative single points for dynamic correlation. Excited-state calculations required the larger two-electron ten-orbital fully optimized reaction space. The larger space was used specifically to test whether the two low-lying singlet configurations mix.
electronic_structure_description: The lowest-energy singlet and triplet states are 1Ag and 3B1u respectively. Ground-state minima are either triplets or singlets with a high degree of diradical character. Although the orbitals of these molecules are in principle able to form a direct titanium-titanium bond, the natural orbital occupation numbers show apparently little such bonding, the same conclusion reached previously for the parent hydride. Table 1 gives calculated singlet-triplet energy gaps, defined as the triplet energy minus the singlet energy, in kcal/mol, at four levels: TCSCF/TZV(p), then multireference perturbation theory with TZV(p), TZVP(f) and TZVP(fg). Ti2H6 (from earlier work): 0.56, 1.33, 1.40, 1.43. Ti2F6: -0.12, -0.18, -0.23, -0.23. Ti2Cl6: -0.09, -0.01, 0.27, 0.90. Ti2Br6: -0.02, 0.34, 0.61, 0.45. Ti2H2F4: 0.83, 1.93, 2.06, 2.10. Ti2H2Cl4: 0.59, 1.62, 1.79, 1.82. Ti2H2Br4: 0.52, 1.53, 1.68, 1.70. Ti2F2H4 in the D2h sigma-based state: -0.11, -0.18, -0.20, -0.20; in the D2h delta-based state: 0.12, 0.24, 0.28, 0.28; in the C2h 1Au state: 0.08, 0.17, 0.21, 0.24. Ti2Cl2H4: -0.04, 0.06, 0.34, 0.34. Ti2Br2H4: 0.02, 0.30, 0.57, 0.87. This compound has a negative singlet-triplet gap at every level, from -0.12 to -0.23 kcal/mol, so the singlet lies above the triplet throughout and the ordering is stable to both correlation and basis extension, unlike most of the series.
Other: Three different multiconfigurational treatments are used here for three different jobs, and the paper is explicit about which is which. Geometry optimization of the singlets uses a two-configuration self-consistent field wave function, equivalent to generalized valence bond perfect pairing with one pair, which is the minimum needed to describe the diradical character these dinuclear titanium(III) species are expected to have; the triplets and doublets are optimized at open-shell Hartree-Fock. Dynamic correlation comes from multireference second-order perturbation theory single points on those geometries, so no state's energy comes from the same wave function that produced its geometry. And a larger fully optimized reaction space of two electrons in ten orbitals is brought in only where excited states are needed. That last space is the interesting one, because it was used to answer a specific question rather than to improve an energy. For the difluoro compound the two low-lying singlet configurations are sigma-sigma-star and delta-delta-star, and unusually the delta-based configuration dominates the ground state while the sigma-based one dominates the first excited singlet, only 0.9 kcal/mol above. The ten-orbital calculation shows that there is essentially no mixing between the two configurations -- so the near-degeneracy is a genuine crossing of two distinct states rather than an artefact of a two-configuration reference too small to let them interact. That is exactly what a larger space is for: not to shift the numbers, but to test whether the small space suppressed an interaction. The natural orbital occupation numbers from the two-electron two-orbital calculation carry the other substantive conclusion, and it is a negative one. Although the orbitals of these molecules are in principle able to form a direct metal-metal bond, the occupation numbers show apparently little such bonding, matching the conclusion reached earlier for the parent hydride. A metal-metal bond that exists in the orbital diagram but not in the occupations is the same diagnosis these numbers are best at, and it depends on the two-orbital space being placed on precisely the sigma and sigma-star pair that would carry such a bond. The reliability caveat is the size of the quantities being reported against the size of the corrections. The singlet-triplet gaps in the table run from -0.23 to 2.10 kcal/mol, and the perturbative correction moves them by as much as 0.9 kcal/mol -- comparable to the gaps themselves. Several compounds change sign between the two-configuration and the perturbative levels, and the trichloride's gap grows from -0.09 to 0.90 kcal/mol as the basis is extended from the base set through added f to added f and g functions. Basis convergence at this scale is therefore not established, and the ordering of singlet and triplet for individual members of the series should be treated as provisional. Two of the difluoro stationary points turn out to have two imaginary frequencies each, with displacement along the imaginary modes leading to a common lower-symmetry structure, so the tabulated gaps for those entries are not between minima.
reference_short: Aikens & Gordon, J. Phys. Chem. A 2003, 107, 104
notes: The parent Ti2H6 values in Table 1 are quoted from earlier work rather than computed here.
correlation_correction: Multireference second-order perturbation theory single points at the two-configuration singlet and ROHF triplet geometries, repeated with two larger basis sets; Z-averaged perturbation theory and a one-electron-in-one-orbital multireference perturbation treatment for the doublet states

active_space_protocol: A two-configuration self-consistent field wave function, equivalent to generalized valence bond perfect pairing with one pair, was used for the singlet geometry optimizations, with perturbative single points for dynamic correlation. Excited-state calculations required the larger two-electron ten-orbital fully optimized reaction space. The larger space was used specifically to test whether the two low-lying singlet configurations mix.
electronic_structure_description: The lowest-energy singlet and triplet states are 1Ag and 3B1u respectively. Ground-state minima are either triplets or singlets with a high degree of diradical character. Although the orbitals of these molecules are in principle able to form a direct titanium-titanium bond, the natural orbital occupation numbers show apparently little such bonding, the same conclusion reached previously for the parent hydride. Table 1 gives calculated singlet-triplet energy gaps, defined as the triplet energy minus the singlet energy, in kcal/mol, at four levels: TCSCF/TZV(p), then multireference perturbation theory with TZV(p), TZVP(f) and TZVP(fg). Ti2H6 (from earlier work): 0.56, 1.33, 1.40, 1.43. Ti2F6: -0.12, -0.18, -0.23, -0.23. Ti2Cl6: -0.09, -0.01, 0.27, 0.90. Ti2Br6: -0.02, 0.34, 0.61, 0.45. Ti2H2F4: 0.83, 1.93, 2.06, 2.10. Ti2H2Cl4: 0.59, 1.62, 1.79, 1.82. Ti2H2Br4: 0.52, 1.53, 1.68, 1.70. Ti2F2H4 in the D2h sigma-based state: -0.11, -0.18, -0.20, -0.20; in the D2h delta-based state: 0.12, 0.24, 0.28, 0.28; in the C2h 1Au state: 0.08, 0.17, 0.21, 0.24. Ti2Cl2H4: -0.04, 0.06, 0.34, 0.34. Ti2Br2H4: 0.02, 0.30, 0.57, 0.87. The gap moves from -0.04 to 0.34 kcal/mol, changing sign on adding dynamic correlation. The titanium-titanium separation is 3.746 Angstrom with bridging angles of 121.2 and 84.3 degrees.
Other: Three different multiconfigurational treatments are used here for three different jobs, and the paper is explicit about which is which. Geometry optimization of the singlets uses a two-configuration self-consistent field wave function, equivalent to generalized valence bond perfect pairing with one pair, which is the minimum needed to describe the diradical character these dinuclear titanium(III) species are expected to have; the triplets and doublets are optimized at open-shell Hartree-Fock. Dynamic correlation comes from multireference second-order perturbation theory single points on those geometries, so no state's energy comes from the same wave function that produced its geometry. And a larger fully optimized reaction space of two electrons in ten orbitals is brought in only where excited states are needed. That last space is the interesting one, because it was used to answer a specific question rather than to improve an energy. For the difluoro compound the two low-lying singlet configurations are sigma-sigma-star and delta-delta-star, and unusually the delta-based configuration dominates the ground state while the sigma-based one dominates the first excited singlet, only 0.9 kcal/mol above. The ten-orbital calculation shows that there is essentially no mixing between the two configurations -- so the near-degeneracy is a genuine crossing of two distinct states rather than an artefact of a two-configuration reference too small to let them interact. That is exactly what a larger space is for: not to shift the numbers, but to test whether the small space suppressed an interaction. The natural orbital occupation numbers from the two-electron two-orbital calculation carry the other substantive conclusion, and it is a negative one. Although the orbitals of these molecules are in principle able to form a direct metal-metal bond, the occupation numbers show apparently little such bonding, matching the conclusion reached earlier for the parent hydride. A metal-metal bond that exists in the orbital diagram but not in the occupations is the same diagnosis these numbers are best at, and it depends on the two-orbital space being placed on precisely the sigma and sigma-star pair that would carry such a bond. The reliability caveat is the size of the quantities being reported against the size of the corrections. The singlet-triplet gaps in the table run from -0.23 to 2.10 kcal/mol, and the perturbative correction moves them by as much as 0.9 kcal/mol -- comparable to the gaps themselves. Several compounds change sign between the two-configuration and the perturbative levels, and the trichloride's gap grows from -0.09 to 0.90 kcal/mol as the basis is extended from the base set through added f to added f and g functions. Basis convergence at this scale is therefore not established, and the ordering of singlet and triplet for individual members of the series should be treated as provisional. Two of the difluoro stationary points turn out to have two imaginary frequencies each, with displacement along the imaginary modes leading to a common lower-symmetry structure, so the tabulated gaps for those entries are not between minima.

compound_name: Li2 dimer, ground and excited state potential energy curves
point_group: All calculations carried out in D2h, with orbital subspaces defined by counts in the eight irreducible representations; some pilot calculations in lower C2 symmetry to check for Delta-Pi interference
geometry_source: Potential energy curves computed pointwise; spectroscopic constants derived from the curves rather than from geometry optimization
method: CASSCF followed by single-state second-order multireference perturbation theory, in both nonrelativistic and relativistic infinite-order two-component formulations, compared against published Fock-space multireference coupled-cluster results
software: Not stated in the extracted text
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic infinite-order two-component method, with Douglas-Kroll-Hess approximations of orders 2 through 10 computed for comparison; nonrelativistic calculations run alongside
active_space_orbital_description: Two spaces were used, both with six active electrons. The first consists of the 1s, 2s and 2p atomic orbitals of lithium, with orbital counts 31103110 across the eight D2h irreducible representations, giving ten active orbitals. The second adds the 3s and 3p orbitals, with counts 52205220, giving eighteen active orbitals. No orbitals were frozen or inactive in either case.
active_space_protocol: Two active spaces of increasing size were used, both with six active electrons and nothing frozen or inactive. The larger space exists because intruder states in the perturbation step often arise from Rydberg orbitals absent from the space, and the remedy is to admit them; the author states that all near-degenerate configurations must be included. Both configuration interaction coefficients and the active and inactive orbitals are optimized, in contrast to the coupled-cluster method being compared against, which uses the same Hartree-Fock orbitals for every excited state. Basis sets were constrained to match those of the earlier coupled-cluster work so the comparison would be meaningful. Pilot calculations in C2 symmetry checked whether Delta states interfere with the Pi states; no degeneracy was found.
multiplicities_studied: singlet and triplet for the alkali dimers; doublet and quartet for the heavy diatomic
nroots_per_mult: the ground state and ten excited states
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy curves were computed for the ground state and ten excited states as a function of internuclear separation, spanning the Li(2s) plus Li(2s) and Li(2s) plus Li(2p) dissociation limits. The computed spectroscopic parameters agree very well with experimental data, which the author takes as showing that the multiconfigurational perturbation approach can be applied to excited states as successfully as the more recently developed Fock-space multireference coupled-cluster method. Dissociation energies are reported relative to two separated atoms. In the coupled-cluster comparison data, 25 virtual orbitals were used.
Other: The paper states the active-space problem in unusually direct terms and then demonstrates it. Provided extended basis sets are used and the space of the reference wave function is chosen correctly, the perturbative method should work equally well for ground and excited states; correct selection of the space in the preceding step is therefore described as of utmost importance, and all near-degenerate configurations must be included in it. The specific failure mode named is intruder states, which the author says often arise from Rydberg orbitals that have not been included in the active space, and the stated remedy is to enlarge the space -- which is exactly what the two spaces used for the lithium dimer represent. The first contains the 1s, 2s and 2p atomic orbitals, giving an orbital partition of 31103110 across the eight irreducible representations with six active electrons; the second adds the 3s and 3p orbitals, giving 52205220 with the same six electrons. The second space costs nothing in electrons and buys the Rydberg-like orbitals whose absence would otherwise produce intruders in the higher excited states, which is why the spaces used for a given dissociation limit differ across the figures -- the sodium dimer curves for the lowest limits use a 21102110 space while those reaching a higher atomic limit use 42204220. A second point concerns what the space is for in the comparison being drawn. The multiconfigurational method optimizes both the configuration interaction coefficients and the active and inactive orbitals, whereas the coupled-cluster method it is being compared against does not optimize the orbitals at all and uses the same Hartree-Fock orbitals for every excited state. So the active space here is carrying orbital relaxation between states, and the paper's conclusion that the older method performs as well as the newer one is a statement that state-specific orbital optimization within a well-chosen space substitutes for a more elaborate correlation treatment on frozen orbitals. To keep that comparison meaningful the author was constrained to use basis sets identical to those of the earlier coupled-cluster work rather than the ones a fresh study would choose. The third and largest effect is not an active-space effect at all, and the paper is careful to separate it. For the heavy diatomic the relativistic treatment changes the ground state dissociation energy from 1.53 eV nonrelativistically to 3.21 eV, against an experimental 3.3 eV, and the equilibrium separation from 2.51 to 2.25 Angstrom against 2.26 experimental; for one excited state the dissociation energy moves from 0.86 to 2.75 eV. By contrast the degree of approximation in the relativistic expansion is immaterial -- values from second through tenth order agree to within 0.01 eV and 2 per cm. So on a heavy-element diatomic the relativistic Hamiltonian is worth more than a factor of two on the bond energy while the order of its expansion is worth nothing, and no choice of active space compensates for omitting it. A minor check worth noting: pilot calculations in a lower symmetry were run to test whether Delta states interfere with the Pi states, and no degeneracy was observed.
reference_short: Barysz, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2016, 12, 1614
notes: Relativistic effects are negligible for this system; the relativistic calculations on it serve to show that the two-component method converges smoothly to the nonrelativistic limit rather than to change the answer.
correlation_correction: Single-state second-order multireference perturbation theory on the CASSCF references

point_group: Linear in the ground state and in all the excited states considered
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries and harmonic vibrational frequencies of both the neutral and dicationic species optimized at the multireference configuration interaction level using the multiconfigurational orbitals; excited-state geometries of the dications also optimized and found to have stable minima near the neutral equilibrium geometry. All species are linear.
method: State-averaged CASSCF providing orbitals for multireference configuration interaction with the Davidson correction, followed by evaluation of Breit-Pauli spin-orbit matrix elements in the resulting wave function basis, with the two-electron contributions of the spin-orbit operator incorporated through an effective one-electron Fock operator
basis_set: Spin-orbit averaged semilocal energy-adjusted pseudopotentials on the halogens covering 1s-2p for chlorine (10 electrons), 1s-3d for bromine (28) and 1s-4d for iodine (46); valence electrons of bromine and iodine described by augmented quadruple-zeta contracted s, p, d, f and g functions, chlorine's valence by augmented quadruple-zeta s and p functions with d, f and g polarization taken from aug-cc-pVQZ; carbon and nitrogen described by aug-cc-pVTZ
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic effects through energy-adjusted pseudopotentials on the halogens, with spin-orbit coupling treated afterwards in the Breit-Pauli formalism
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons correlated in twelve orbitals, used identically for the neutral molecules and for the dications across all three halogens.
active_space_protocol: A single (14,12) space applied to every member of the series and to both charge states. Ground-state geometries and frequencies came from configuration interaction on those orbitals; for the excited states a state-averaged (14,12) reference was used, covering the twelve components of the lowest eight electronic states at the reference geometry of the neutral molecule. The multiconfigurational step supplies static correlation and starting orbitals while the configuration interaction step supplies dynamic correlation, with a Davidson correction applied for size consistency. The same wave functions then serve as the electronic basis for the spin-orbit treatment.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, triplet and quintet; the lowest quintet lies more than 6 eV above the ground state in all three dications and was excluded from further analysis
nroots_per_mult: the lowest eight electronic states, four nondegenerate and four doubly degenerate, giving twelve components
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1Sigma+ for the neutral and X 3Sigma- for the dication, the latter arising from the pi-squared configuration and followed by a 1Delta and b 1Sigma+ in accordance with Hund's rule. On double ionization the C-N bond lengthens and the X-C bond shortens, because the highest occupied orbital of the neutral is a pi orbital that is bonding across C-N and antibonding across X-C. Table 1 gives optimized bond lengths in Angstrom and harmonic vibrational frequencies in eV for the neutral and dicationic ground states. geometry_source: All stationary points optimized at CASSCF/6-31G*, with frequency calculations on all structures for zero-point corrections and to verify concerted transition structures; the single imaginary frequency of each transition structure was animated to confirm the correct bond was forming, and intrinsic reaction coordinate calculations were performed for confirmation
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequency analysis with single-point CASPT2 for dynamic electron correlation
software: Gaussian 03 and Gaussian 09 for the CASSCF work; Molcas 7.4 for the CASPT2 single points
basis_set: 6-31G* throughout, with 6-31G** and other alternatives tested for two of the rearrangements in the Supporting Information
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in ten orbitals. In the reactants and transition structures the twelve electrons comprise the eight pi electrons of four double bonds plus two electrons in a lone pair on each of the two heteroatoms; in the products they comprise the six pi electrons of three double bonds, the same two heteroatom lone pairs, and the two electrons of the newly formed sigma bond.
active_space_protocol: A single (12,10) space applied to every stationary point of every rearrangement, with its composition changing along the reaction coordinate as a pi bond is converted to a sigma bond while the two heteroatom lone pairs are retained throughout. Retaining both lone pairs is what allows an orbital disconnection, the signature of pseudopericyclic character, to be represented. Dynamic correlation was added by CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF stationary points in the same basis.
electronic_structure_description: Table 2 gives zero-point corrected activation energies in kcal/mol at the CASSCF//CASSCF and CASPT2//CASSCF levels for the six rearrangements: 3 to 4, 1.49 and -5.69; 5 to 6, 13.81 and 0.43; 7 to 8, 0.11 and -8.56; 9 to 10, 13.89 and 1.82; 13 to 14, 20.50 and 8.00; 15 to 16, 20.61 and 7.42. Table 1 gives three dihedral angles for each transition structure, measuring planarity: for TS3-4 they are -0.03, -0.04 and 0.03 degrees; TS5-6, 7.78, 4.77 and -9.32; TS7-8, exactly 0.00 in all three; TS9-10, 6.66, 1.46 and -8.85; TS13-14, -27.88, -3.55 and 18.02; TS15-16, -21.58, -3.32 and 13.23. This rearrangement was expected to be the most likely to show pseudopericyclic character, having the most nucleophilic heteroatom, nitrogen, in the nucleophilic position and the most electrophilic cumulene central carbon owing to an oxygen atom at the end. Its transition structure is essentially planar, with dihedral angles of -0.03, -0.04 and 0.03 degrees. The paper concludes it is pseudopericyclic with two orbital disconnections. Its perturbatively corrected activation energy of -5.69 kcal/mol is one of the two nonviable negative values.
Other: The active space here is defined by chemical role and, crucially, its contents change along the reaction coordinate while its size does not. So a pi bond and a lone pair are traded for a sigma bond as the ring closes, which is precisely the electron reorganisation being studied, and holding the count fixed at twelve in ten is what allows reactant, transition structure and product to be compared on one footing. Including both heteroatom lone pairs is not incidental: the whole question is whether these rearrangements are pseudopericyclic, meaning whether a lone pair disconnects from the cyclic array of interacting orbitals, and a space lacking those lone pairs could not represent the disconnection at all. The paper's own results then supply an unusually blunt warning about layering perturbation theory on such a space. Zero-point-corrected activation energies at the multiconfigurational level are 1.49, 13.81, 0.11, 13.89, 20.50 and 20.61 kcal/mol for the six rearrangements; the corresponding perturbatively corrected values are -5.69, 0.43, -8.56, 1.82, 8.00 and 7.42. Two of them come out negative, which the authors describe as nonviable, and they state the diagnosis plainly: the inaccuracy in the calculated multiconfigurational activation energies is greater than the magnitude of the perturbative corrections in these cases. The corrections are large -- 7 to 13 kcal/mol on barriers of 0.1 to 20 kcal/mol -- so a barrier the reference method places near zero cannot survive them. Yet the correction is also what rescues one comparison the authors expected on chemical grounds: at the multiconfigurational level the 5 to 6 and 9 to 10 rearrangements differ by a negligible 0.08 kcal/mol in the wrong direction, and only after the perturbative step does the expected ordering emerge with a 1.39 kcal/mol margin. One structure could not be obtained at all -- a multiconfigurational geometry for one product proved elusive -- so that rearrangement's exothermicity is inferred rather than computed.

The corroborating evidence is that the computed electronic transition energies are far from experiment where time-dependent density functional theory reproduces them well, and that those transition energies become more respectable, though still substantially off, with a larger active space. That combination -- a metal-only space that is too ionic, an enlargement that helps the transition energies and the rhombicity but worsens the axial parameter, and a density functional method outperforming both -- is the useful record here. Both methods reproduced the rhombicity poorly across the set, so the failure is not confined to the multiconfigurational approach.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A1. At the restricted B3LYP optimized C2v geometry the CASSCF ground state corresponds essentially to a closed-shell iron(II)-nitrosyl-cation configuration with a coefficient of 0.92, the configuration associated with antiferromagnetic coupling of iron(III) to a neutral nitric oxide radical contributing only 0.07. The excited 1A1 state built mainly from the antiferromagnetically coupled configurations lies 420 kJ/mol above the ground state, a value the authors describe as probably overestimated because the orbitals were optimized for the closed-shell ground state. The bonding scheme is concluded to be the interaction of a closed-shell iron(II) with a nitrosyl cation. The characteristic N-O stretching frequency is observed experimentally at 1825 per cm by infrared multiphoton dissociation spectroscopy.
Other: The active space is built to arbitrate between two competing bonding descriptions and contains exactly the orbitals needed to represent both: six electrons distributed over the three nonbonding iron d orbitals and the two nitrosyl pi-star orbitals. That composition is the whole design. One description has a closed-shell iron(II) bound to a nitrosyl cation, with all six electrons in the metal d set; the other has iron(III) antiferromagnetically coupled to a neutral nitric oxide radical, which requires one electron in a nitrosyl pi-star orbital and an open-shell metal. A space holding only the metal d orbitals could represent the first but not the second, so the question could not have been asked. With both present the wave function is allowed to choose, and it comes down decisively on the closed-shell side: the leading configuration carries a coefficient of 0.92 in the five-coordinate complex and 0.91 in the six-coordinate imidazole adduct, with the antiferromagnetically coupled configuration contributing only 0.07 and 0.09 respectively. A negative result of this kind is only meaningful because the alternative was available in the space and was not selected. The paper is also candid about a limitation that follows directly from how the space was optimized. The excited states were obtained by configuration interaction using the ground-state CASSCF orbitals, and the excited singlet corresponding to the antiferromagnetically coupled configuration came out 420 kJ/mol above the ground state for the five-coordinate complex and 346 kJ/mol for the six-coordinate one. The authors state that this excitation is probably overestimated precisely because the orbitals were optimized for the closed-shell ground state rather than state-averaged. The magnitude of that bias is visible in the comparison they provide: a time-dependent density functional estimate of the same gap gives 191 kJ/mol, roughly half the multiconfigurational value. So the ordering the space establishes is robust while the gap it reports is not, and the two should be quoted with different confidence. A further scope caveat: the multiconfigurational treatment was run only on the tetraphenylporphyrin complex and its imidazole adduct at density functional geometries, while the fluorinated analogue that the experimental part of the paper compares against was treated by density functional methods alone, so the bonding conclusion is transferred to it by analogy rather than computed.

method: Self-consistent field and second-order perturbation theory, then CASSCF followed by multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction, with a subsequent relativistic configuration interaction step to estimate spin-orbit contributions

The orbitals are six a1, three b1, two b2 and one a2 for the bent structure, and five a1, three b1, three b2 and one a2 for the linear structure. The lanthanum 5s and 5p and the carbon 2s orbitals were allowed to relax at the multiconfigurational stage but no excitations from them were permitted. In the subsequent configuration interaction step all configurations with coefficients of 0.07 or greater, important for the equilibrium as well as for the dissociated molecule, were used as references, with all single and double excitations from the seven outermost electrons allowed, giving up to 530000 configuration state functions. electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2A1, with a symmetrical C2v geometry; the linear unsymmetrical arrangement has 2Sigma+ as its lowest state. Every level of theory employed gives the bent structure as the global minimum, though the energy separation between it and the linear structure varies significantly between methods, and all methods agree well on the molecular parameters. Agreement between computed and experimental dissociation and atomization energies is good when electron correlation is included to a significant extent, and the computed enthalpies are sensitive to the assumed structure, the linear complex agreeing significantly worse with experiment than the bent one. Zero-point vibrational corrections are 14.8 kJ/mol for the bent structure and 14.0 kJ/mol for the linear one, which when applied lower the best atomization enthalpy to 1185.2 kJ/mol. The main change in electron density on forming the La-C bonds is transfer of charge from the metal to the carbons. Spin-orbit lowering is 631.9 per cm in the neutral metal atom and 1183.3 per cm in its cation, giving an estimated 550 per cm, or 6.6 kJ/mol, correction to the formation reaction enthalpy, too small to affect the thermodynamic properties. In the relativistic configuration interaction treatment of the ground state, the lowest configurations of 4A1, 4B1, 4B2, 4A2, 2B1, 2B2 and 2A2 symmetry mix less than one percent with the ground state and the spin-orbit correction lowers the energy near equilibrium by 1 kJ/mol. The molecule possesses a number of excited states with equilibrium energies below the dissociation limit, owing to the many low-lying excited states of the metal atom and the proximity of the singlet and triplet states of C2.

Both amount to twelve orbitals corresponding to the valence orbitals of lanthanum together with the carbon 2p orbitals, and both hold seven electrons -- the lanthanum 5d and 6s electrons plus the carbon 2p electrons -- distributed in all possible ways, producing about 14000 configuration state functions. A clean separation of what is inside and outside the space is stated: the lanthanum 5s and 5p and the carbon 2s orbitals were allowed to relax at the multiconfigurational stage but no excitations from them were permitted, so those orbitals respond to the field without contributing correlation. That is the middle ground between freezing and correlating, and it is worth recording because it is often left implicit. The configuration interaction step then uses an occupation-based reference selection rather than a fixed list: every configuration from the multiconfigurational calculation with a coefficient of 0.07 or greater, judged important for the equilibrium structure and for the dissociated molecule alike, was promoted to a reference, and all single and double excitations from the seven outermost electrons were allowed, reaching up to 530000 configuration state functions. The accuracy the space buys is quantified against experiment: agreement with the measured dissociation and atomization energies is good provided electron correlation is included to a significant extent, and the computed enthalpies are sensitive to the assumed structure, the linear complex agreeing significantly worse than the bent one. Since the experimental values had themselves been derived assuming an unsymmetrical linear geometry, the calculation is correcting the structural assumption underlying the measurement. Equilibrium geometry calculations were run at total charge zero and singlet multiplicity. B3LYP/6-31G(d) calculations were performed alongside specifically to confirm the multiconfigurational results are reasonable given this particular orbital choice.

electronic_structure_description: Excitation to the first excited state is followed by nonadiabatic decay through conical intersections, which the paper identifies as providing a direct ultrafast route to ground-state decomposition on a roughly 100 femtosecond timescale. Because this compound contains no nitro group, the nitro-to-nitrite isomerization route that initiates decomposition in previously studied energetic molecules is unavailable and a different mechanism is found. Nitrogen is released by opening of the tetrazole ring, the ring opening occurring between the N2 and N3 atoms at one transition state and between C1 and N2 at another, and both nitrogen and nitric oxide products are formed. One ground-state path proceeds over a barrier of 0.34 eV from a transition state leading to nitrogen. The energy gap between the excited and ground surfaces near the nitrogen-forming conical intersection is small, and no energy barrier exists between that intersection and the products, so nitrogen and nitric oxide should be generated with a cold rotational distribution.
Other: Both molecules get an (8,8) space, but the two spaces contain entirely different kinds of orbital, and the reason given is worth recording because it is a selection rule rather than a chemical argument. The orbitals were chosen because they span the orbital space from HOMO minus 3 to LUMO plus 3 and cover the whole structure in each case. For the neutral tetrazolate salt those frontier orbitals are mainly pi in character -- two pi-bonding orbitals about the inter-ring C-C bond, two ring pi orbitals, two delocalized pi antibonding orbitals over the whole system and two ring-localized pi antibonding orbitals. For the triazole dianion the same rank window instead returns sigma-nonbonding orbitals: four about the bistriazole rings and four on the nitro groups. The authors attribute the difference to the charge, one species being neutral and the other carrying minus two. So an identically sized and identically constructed space describes pi photochemistry in one molecule and sigma photochemistry in the other, purely because the frontier window moved. That is the central caution for anyone reusing these numbers: the (8,8) label carries no information about what is being correlated, and the two systems are not comparable on the basis of space size. The authors do not simply assume the rank-based choice is adequate. For the neutral salt they run density functional calculations alongside specifically to ensure the multiconfigurational results are reasonable given the particular orbital choice, and for the dianion they run the same functional on the complete salt to verify that the dianion is a sufficient model for the full ionic material. They also state plainly why the multiconfigurational results must nonetheless carry the discussion: conical intersections are the mechanism, and a single-reference method cannot locate them. A perturbative correction is applied on top of all the multiconfigurational energies, and excitation energies are obtained by state averaging over the ground and excited states with equal weights, so the reported vertical energies and the optimized structures do not come from the same wave function. Two model-scope limitations should travel with the data. The dianion replaces the actual salt for computational efficiency, so the hydroxylammonium counterions are absent from the multiconfigurational treatment entirely. And the neutral salt calculations were run at total charge zero and singlet multiplicity, which describes the ion pair rather than the separated ions. The zero-point energy difference between the ground and first excited states is noted as small and neglected.

active_space_protocol: A deliberately minimal space chosen to contain all orbitals possibly relevant for a correct description of the spin density and electronic configuration. Five iron 3d orbitals and the oxophlorin a2u orbital are common to both species; the seventh orbital is the macrocycle a1u orbital in the five-coordinate compound and the dioxygen pi-star orbital in the superoxo adduct, so the two spaces carry the same label but different contents. electronic_structure_description: Total energies computed in the doublet, quartet and sextet states show the sextet to be the ground state. The most important configurations for the sextet, with their coefficients, are 1aaaaa0 at 0.75242891, a1aaaa0 at -0.28072147, 1aaaa0a at -0.24774226, a1aaa0a at 0.21206988 and a1aa0aa at 0.09242891, using the convention that 1 is a doubly occupied orbital, a and b are orbitals holding a single alpha or beta electron and 0 is empty. The dominant contribution has a configuration interaction weight above 0.7 while all other coefficients are smaller but significant, below 0.3. The principal configuration contains four unpaired electrons on the iron and one on the macrocycle, a pi-neutral radical, corresponding to a dxy2 a2u1 dyz1 dxz1 sigma*z2(1) sigma*x2-y2(1) configuration. The spin polarization is accounted for by configurations containing excitations from the dxy highest occupied orbital into the a2u singly occupied orbital, shifting beta electron density toward the macrocycle ring; these excitations have medium-sized coefficients above 0.09 and produce an excess of alpha density on iron, corresponding to an a2u2 dxy1 dyz1 dxz1 sigma*z2(1) sigma*x2-y2(1) occupation. In most of the excited configurations with large coefficients the dxy orbital remains singly occupied.
Other: The space is described by the authors as minimal, chosen to contain all orbitals possibly relevant for a correct description of the spin density and electronic configuration, and its construction is stated species by species. A common core of five iron 3d orbitals plus the oxophlorin a2u orbital is shared by both compounds; the seventh orbital then differs, being the macrocycle a1u orbital in the five-coordinate species and the dioxygen pi-star orbital in the superoxo adduct. Both end up as seven electrons in seven orbitals, so the label is identical while the contents are not -- the seventh orbital is chosen by what each species needs to describe rather than by any uniform rule. That is the right construction here because the question in both cases is where an unpaired electron sits, and in each species a different acceptor orbital is the candidate. What the space then delivers is a quantitative decomposition that a single-determinant treatment cannot provide, and both compounds show the same pattern: a dominant configuration that is insufficient on its own, plus a set of medium-weight excitations that supply the observed spin polarization. For the five-coordinate sextet the leading configuration carries a coefficient of 0.752, with the next four at -0.281, -0.248, 0.212 and 0.092; those excited configurations move beta electron density toward the macrocycle and are what account for the polarization. For the superoxo doublet the leading coefficient is 0.649, with -0.306, 0.276, 0.233 and -0.109 following, and the authors state explicitly that the principal configuration alone cannot explain the observed spin polarization, which instead requires configurations promoting an electron from a metal d orbital into the antibonding dioxygen pi-star. So in both cases a wave function with a clearly dominant reference is nonetheless not adequately described by that reference, and the sub-0.3 coefficients carry the physics. The important limitation for reuse is one of scope rather than of space size. The multiconfigurational treatment is applied only to two oxidized species, as a confirmation of electronic structures established elsewhere in the paper; every geometry, energy, reaction profile and spin density that the study's conclusions rest on comes from density functional calculations with modified hybrid and pure functionals, and the paper is titled as a density functional study. The multiconfigurational geometries are therefore not independently optimized, and no basis set or program is stated for the multiconfigurational step in the extracted text, so those fields are left empty rather than assumed to match the density functional setup.

electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives energies in kcal/mol for titanium(IV) and titanium(III) chloride reduction with hydrogen and the intramolecular redox process, for four reactions: BP86/TZP 43.95, 56.01, 65.63, 77.69; TPSS/TZP 44.86, 57.36, 65.09, 77.59; M06/TZP 46.06, 61.46, 67.57, 82.97; B3LYP/TZP 33.61, 49.63, 56.13, 72.15; CASPT2/ANO-L-VTZP 48.05 and 72.05 for reactions 1 and 3 with 2 and 4 not calculated; CCSD(T)/aVDZ 34.71, 49.89, 61.29, 76.47; CCSD(T)/aVTZ 35.13, 50.68, 58.94, 74.49; experiment 31.44, 50.14, 53.50, 72.20. Table 2 gives the corresponding vanadium values, for which no experimental data are available: BP86/TZP 28.84, 35.85, 50.52, 57.52; B3LYP/TZP 16.59, 28.50, 39.11, 51.03; CASPT2/ANO-L-VTZP 18.95 and 43.18; CCSD(T)/aVDZ 15.69, 24.06, 42.27, 50.64; CCSD(T)/aVTZ 17.07, 26.51, 40.89, 50.32. Table 3 lists the active spaces: (2,2) for H2, Cl2 and HCl, (10,10) for TiCl4, (1,1) for TiCl3, (11,12) for VCl4 and (12,14) for VCl3. All methods agree qualitatively that vanadium(IV) is more easily reducible than titanium(IV), and that decreasing the oxidation state further from +3 to +2 meets higher thermodynamic resistance. Among the density functionals B3LYP is the most accurate for these heats of reaction, probably through fortuitous cancellation of errors, while the others cluster together and are almost independent of functional type. The perturbative multiconfigurational treatment agrees very well with coupled cluster for the vanadium reduction but performs worse than any density functional for the titanium(IV) chloride reduction, and the authors stress that applying larger active spaces does not improve the results. This compound is the reactant of the titanium reduction reaction for which the perturbative value of 48.05 kcal/mol overshoots the experimental 31.44 by 16.6 kcal/mol.
Other: The active spaces are chosen per species by a stated rule -- for the metal chlorides, all occupied orbitals with metal 3d character including singly occupied ones, together with the corresponding number of virtual orbitals -- and the resulting sizes vary widely across the seven species involved in the same reaction: (2,2) for the three diatomic partners, (10,10) for titanium tetrachloride, (11,12) for vanadium tetrachloride, (12,14) for vanadium trichloride, and (1,1) for titanium trichloride. That last choice is a deliberate downgrade rather than an oversight: the trichloride is described as exhibiting more ionic character than the tetrachloride and was therefore treated as a single configuration state function with one electron in one 3d orbital. So a reaction enthalpy is being computed as a difference between a ten-orbital multiconfigurational description on one side and an effectively single-determinant description on the other. The paper's result is that this fails badly for titanium and works well for vanadium, and it says so plainly. For the titanium reduction the perturbative multiconfigurational value is 48.05 kcal/mol against an experimental 31.44 and coupled-cluster values of 34.71 and 35.13, so it is further from experiment than any of the four density functionals tested, the worst of which gives 46.06. For the vanadium reduction the same protocol gives 18.95 kcal/mol against coupled-cluster values of 15.69 and 17.07, in very good agreement, though no experimental value exists there. The critical sentence for anyone tempted to attribute the titanium failure to an undersized space is the authors' own: the application of larger active spaces does not improve the results. That is the rare case where the enlargement test was run and reported as not fixing the problem, which redirects the diagnosis away from the space and toward the unbalanced treatment across the reaction or the reference itself. Two further caveats travel with the numbers. The multiconfigurational energies are single points on coupled-cluster optimized geometries, so no geometry in this work comes from the multiconfigurational treatment. And the diagnostic that motivated the multiconfigurational check in the first place is discussed candidly: single-reference coupled cluster is normally suspect above a T1 diagnostic of 0.02, but values twice as large are considered acceptable for open-shell species, so the perturbative calculations were run to check for discrepancies rather than because the coupled-cluster results were known to be unreliable.

The space that is used comprises the oxygen lone pair of the carbonyl moiety together with pi orbitals, which is what allows both the bright pi-pi-star state and the nearby n-pi-star state, predicted to lie 0.24 eV higher, to be represented in the same reference. Those lifetimes are 104.7 femtoseconds in the gas phase, decomposing into a 49.5 femtosecond latency before decay begins and a 55.2 femtosecond decay constant, against 242.8 femtoseconds in water with a 217.6 femtosecond latency and a much shorter 25.2 femtosecond decay constant. compound_name: Phenol, S1 to S0 emission spectrum
geometry_source: Geometries of both electronic states obtained from CASSCF calculations, with the molecular geometry restricted to Cs symmetry; a geometry fitted to the experimental rotational constants was also constructed for comparison
method: CASSCF for the geometries and normal modes of both the ground and first excited electronic states, used as input to a Franck-Condon simulation including all normal modes and Duschinsky rotation
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in seven orbitals: the six pi valence orbitals of the aromatic ring together with the oxygen lone pair orbital that has pi symmetry.
active_space_protocol: The space was chosen by analogy to a previously published study, extending the six-orbital ring pi space of the parent aromatic by the pi-symmetry oxygen lone pair. The same method and space describe both electronic states, which the authors state is necessary to avoid artificial Duschinsky rotations of the normal modes arising from applying different methods to the two states.
multiplicities_studied: singlet; the ground state and the first excited state
electronic_structure_description: Table 1 compares computed and experimental rotational constants in MHz. Experimentally the ground state has A, B and C of 5650.515, 2619.236 and 1789.855, and the excited state 5313.6, 2620.5 and 1756.1. The multiconfigurational calculation gives ground-state values of 5659.3, 2623.3 and 1792.4, deviating by 0.16, 0.16 and 0.14 percent, and excited-state values of 5337.8, 2572.0 and 1735.7, deviating by 0.46, -1.85 and -1.16 percent. A fitted geometry gives 5294.9, 2624.9 and 1754.9, deviating by -0.35, 0.17 and 0.06 percent. Computed bond lengths and angles for the ground state deviate from experiment by less than 0.01 Angstrom and 1 degree. The calculations resolve a literature disagreement over vibrational assignment: two observed bands at 1603 and 1610 per cm had been assigned with the lower frequency to one ring mode, contradicting other experimental work, and since the present calculations confirm that the other mode always has the lower frequency in ab initio treatments, the 1603 per cm band is reassigned to that mode and the 1610 per cm band to the first. The Franck-Condon simulation is compared against a dispersed emission spectrum, and the best agreement is obtained with a particular assignment of the contested modes; one mode's intensity is affected by Duschinsky rotation with others.
Other: The active spaces here are chosen so that one method describes both electronic states, and the paper states the reason explicitly: by using the same method for the two states, no artificial Duschinsky rotations of the normal modes are obtained, since such artefacts arise only from applying different methods to describe the two states. That is a requirement peculiar to Franck-Condon work. The quantity being computed is the overlap between vibrational wave functions of two different electronic states, which depends on how the normal-mode coordinate systems of those states relate to one another; if the two states come from different levels of theory, the resulting rotation matrix mixes real physics with methodological mismatch and the simulated intensity pattern becomes meaningless. A multiconfigurational treatment is one of the few options able to describe a ground state and a valence excited state on the same footing, and here it is used for exactly that, not for its energetics. The spaces themselves are minimal and defined by chemical role. For the aromatic reference compound the space is the six ring pi orbitals with their six electrons. For the substituted compound the space is extended by one orbital and two electrons -- the oxygen lone pair that has pi symmetry -- giving eight electrons in seven orbitals, and the choice is stated to have been made by analogy to a previously published study. Adding the lone pair rather than a ring orbital is the substantive decision: the substituent perturbs the ring pi system through that orbital, so a space of ring orbitals alone would describe the substituted molecule as a perturbed benzene rather than as a conjugated system. The validation is unusual in being an intensity pattern rather than an energy. The simulation is first run on the parent aromatic, where the computed pattern is reported to reproduce the experimental jet-cooled absorption spectrum very well, and the authors state that this result supports their assumption about the method being adequate before applying it to the substituted molecule. Geometric accuracy is quantified against rotational constants: the ground-state values agree with experiment to 0.14 to 0.16 percent, but the excited-state constants deviate by 0.46, -1.85 and -1.16 percent, roughly an order of magnitude worse. A geometry fitted to the experimental rotational constants was also constructed for comparison. So the space describes the ground state considerably better than the excited state it was chosen to treat even-handedly, and the excited-state geometry carries the larger uncertainty in the simulation that follows. A separate benefit of having both states from the same reference is that the calculations settle a literature disagreement about vibrational assignment, confirming that one ring mode always has the lower frequency and reassigning two observed bands accordingly.

compound_name: Ethylene, torsional potential energy surface about the C-C double bond
geometry_source: Ground state minimum optimized at MP2/cc-pVDZ, with surfaces generated by fixed rotation about the carbon-carbon double bond in two degree increments
method: Multireference configuration interaction using natural orbitals from a single-reference correlated calculation on a high-multiplicity state as a substitute for orbital optimization, compared throughout against the analogous treatment built on optimized orbitals
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals, the pi and pi-star of the double bond, forming the reference space of the configuration interaction expansion.
active_space_protocol: The reference orbitals come from natural orbitals of a triplet state, the lowest multiplicity that encompasses the pi and pi-star orbitals of interest. Several expansions were compared: single excitations from the reference orbitals only, single excitations plus doubles with seven occupied orbitals frozen, and doubles with only the two core orbitals frozen.
multiplicities_studied: singlet states computed on references derived from higher-multiplicity states
electronic_structure_description: Potential energy surfaces were generated by fixed rotation about the double bond in two degree increments. The surface is discontinuous around 20 degrees because of a curve crossing at that geometry, and a discontinuity appears on the second excited surface owing to the choice of expansion. Convergence of the configuration interaction required 61 iterations with the natural-orbital reference against 31 with the optimized-orbital reference, but each iteration is far cheaper, the step taking 18 seconds against 123 seconds. The overlap between the two orbital sets is largest for this molecule among the three studied.
Other: This paper replaces the orbital-optimization step entirely: instead of optimizing orbitals for the states of interest, natural orbitals are taken from a single-reference correlated calculation on a high-multiplicity state and used directly as the reference orbitals for multireference configuration interaction. The active space concept survives -- the authors note explicitly that even when no orbital optimization is performed there is still a complete active space in the reference space -- but it is now a selection from a fixed orbital set rather than a variationally determined one. The rule for choosing the high-multiplicity state is stated as a general prescription: use the lowest multiplicity that includes the orbitals of interest. A triplet suffices where only pi and pi-star orbitals matter, but a quintet is required where a lone pair must be present alongside the pi system because both n-pi-star and pi-pi-star states are wanted. Going higher was tested and found not worthwhile: septet-derived orbitals give excitation energies within 0.04 eV of quintet-derived ones, 5.13 against 5.17 eV and 6.25 against 6.28 eV, while the septet requires 31.8 million configuration state functions against 20.2 million for the quintet and is harder to converge onto the intended state. The choice of which further orbitals join the reference space beyond those singly occupied in the high-multiplicity wave function is made by chemical intuition exactly as in a conventional treatment, and reordering of the natural orbitals is sometimes needed to ensure the intended orbitals are included -- done manually once at setup, with automatic scripts then enforcing continuity along the surface, which the authors note resembles standard practice where checking the space contains the correct orbitals is essential in photochemical work. One space had to be enlarged for a reason specific to this scheme: the eight pi orbitals plus an oxygen lone pair were augmented by a sigma orbital, giving fourteen electrons in ten orbitals, because in the natural-orbital calculations one pi orbital was heavily mixed with a sigma orbital. That mixing is an artefact of using unoptimized orbitals, and the fix was to admit the contaminating orbital rather than to reject it. The most valuable content here is the failure mode, reported rather than smoothed. Since the reference orbitals now come from a separate high-multiplicity calculation, the smoothness of the resulting surface depends on that calculation behaving smoothly. For one system it does not: after a curve crossing the previous-point guess converges to a diabatically-continued state rather than the lowest root, returning to the lowest root two geometries later and leaving a discontinuity, and paths generated from reactant and from product give different surfaces and hence different natural orbitals. Examination of the excited quintet states shows several coupled and interacting states, so proper description would require many states, which conflicts with the strategy of holding the reference state fixed by seeding from the previous step. The excitation energies survive this reasonably well, but discontinuities appear in the error curves at exactly the geometry where the reference state changes character, and these may cause problems when gradients are wanted. The authors' conclusion is the transferable one: keeping track of the behaviour of the reference state is very important. Convergence cost is also honestly reported -- the natural-orbital route needs roughly twice the configuration interaction iterations of the conventional route on all three systems, though each iteration is much cheaper, one case running in 18 seconds against 123.

compound_name: Compound 1, a methyl-substituted N2P2 four-membered ring with unpaired electrons on the phosphorus atoms
geometry_source: Ground and lowest triplet state geometries optimized at the B3LYP/6-311+G* level; the multiconfigurational calculations are single points on those structures
method: CASSCF used to corroborate density functional singlet-triplet energy gaps and to examine antibonding orbital occupation numbers as a measure of biradicaloid character
software: Not stated in the extracted text
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, comprising a sigma orbital, a pi orbital, a phosphorus-phosphorus or nitrogen-nitrogen pi orbital, two antibonding pi-star orbitals and a sigma-star orbital.
active_space_protocol: A six-electron six-orbital space applied to both isomers as a preliminary calibration, used to corroborate the accuracy of the density functional treatment for singlet-triplet gaps and to provide occupation numbers of the antibonding orbitals as an independent measure of biradicaloid character alongside the weight of the leading configuration state function.
electronic_structure_description: Table 1 gives occupation numbers in electrons at the CASSCF(6,6) level and adiabatic singlet-triplet splittings in kcal/mol. For compound 1 the sigma, pi and phosphorus-phosphorus pi orbitals hold 1.97, 1.97 and 1.80 electrons, the two antibonding pi orbitals hold 0.23 and sigma-star holds 0.03, with singlet-triplet gaps of -29.3 from density functional theory and -26.5 from the multiconfigurational treatment. For compound 2 the corresponding occupation numbers are 1.90, 1.97, 1.96, 0.14 and 0.03, with gaps of -34.3 and -39.6. The leading configuration state function of the ground-state wave function carries a weight of 0.93; other configurations involving excitations into the antibonding pi orbitals also contribute, indicating about 7 percent biradicaloid character on that measure, in agreement with an earlier two-electron two-orbital treatment. The occupation-number measure gives a higher figure of 12.5 percent, but the same ordering relative to the other isomer. The occupation of the two antibonding pi orbitals, 0.23 electrons, is larger than the value reported for the analogous sulfur-nitrogen ring. The ground state optimized geometry of the ring core is almost identical to the experimental X-ray core of a related biradicaloid in planarity, distances and angles. In the lowest triplet the two nitrogen atoms pyramidalize and the four-membered ring loses planarity, the relevant bond angle opening to 163.7 degrees, so populating the antibonding pi lowest unoccupied orbital costs aromaticity and raises the biradicaloid character. This isomer is 28.0 kcal/mol more stable than the other at the density functional level and 28.3 kcal/mol at the multiconfigurational level.
Other: The multiconfigurational calculation here is a calibration exercise rather than the main line of the study, and it is set up so that two independent measures of the same quantity can be compared. A six-electron six-orbital space is applied to both isomers, and biradicaloid character is estimated twice from it: once from the weight of the leading configuration state function in the ground-state wave function, and once from the occupation numbers of the antibonding orbitals. Those two estimates do not agree in magnitude but do agree in ordering -- the weight-based figures are about 7 and 5 percent for the two isomers while the occupation-number figures are 12.5 and 8.5 percent, and the authors state plainly that the occupation-number estimate is slightly higher but the trend is the same. Recording both is more useful than picking one, because it puts a scale on how much a diradical percentage depends on which diagnostic is used, and roughly a factor of 1.7 between two measures taken from the same wave function is a useful calibration for anyone quoting such numbers. The space is also used to validate a much cheaper method that carries the rest of the paper. Adiabatic singlet-triplet gaps come out at -26.5 and -39.6 kcal/mol from the multiconfigurational treatment against -29.3 and -34.3 from density functional theory, so the two agree on sign and on ordering but differ by 3 to 5 kcal/mol, and the relative stability of the two isomers agrees to 0.3 kcal/mol, 28.3 against 28.0. That agreement is the stated justification for using the density functional method on the larger metal-coordinated complexes, which are never treated multiconfigurationally. The orbital-by-orbital occupation numbers are reported and are the most transferable part of the record: for the more biradicaloid isomer the sigma, pi and the phosphorus-phosphorus pi orbitals hold 1.97, 1.97 and 1.80 electrons with 0.23 in the two antibonding pi orbitals and 0.03 in sigma-star; for the other isomer the corresponding values are 1.90, 1.97, 1.96, 0.14 and 0.03. The population sits almost entirely in one orbital pair, which is why a six-orbital space suffices and why the antibonding occupation is a clean diagnostic. One caveat of scope: the geometries come from density functional optimization, so the multiconfigurational calculation is a single-point analysis on structures it did not produce, and the triplet geometry involves pyramidalization at nitrogen with a ring angle of 163.7 degrees, a substantial distortion whose effect on the space was not separately examined.
