point_group: C2 constraint imposed except for intersection optimizations
geometry_source: Ground and excited state minima optimized at the CASSCF level; rotary profiles obtained by constrained optimization along the central dihedral angle
method: State-averaged CASSCF over four singlet states for geometry optimization and minimum energy paths, with CASPT2 single points at those geometries using a level shift of 0.3 to avoid intruder states; constrained optimizations along the central dihedral angle were used to trace the rotary profiles, with intersections optimized without the symmetry constraint
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten pi orbitals: the pi and pi* orbitals of the central ethylene bond about which rotation occurs, together with the two degenerate frontier occupied and unoccupied orbitals of each of the two phenyl moieties. The character of individual orbitals changes significantly during rotation while the space as a whole is reported to be well conserved.
active_space_protocol: State averaged over the four lowest singlets -- the closed-shell ground state, the two lowest bright states and the dark state -- described as adequate because excitation populates one of the bright states. A two-fold symmetry constraint was imposed everywhere except in the optimization of conical intersections, to reduce cost, after a density functional survey indicated the relevant structures are essentially symmetric. Triplet states were excluded on the basis of measured singlet-to-triplet isomerization yields.
nroots_per_mult: four singlet states, state-averaged
electronic_structure_description: The unconstrained parent. Reference relative energies in kcal/mol for the four averaged states at each optimized structure: the cis ground state minimum at 4.2 with excited states at 143.3, 144.7 and 166.9; the trans ground minimum at 0.0 with 132.4, 131.4 and 150.1; the perpendicular excited minimum at 52.0 with 119.8, 120.2 and 148.3; the trans excited minimum at 9.2 with 120.7 and 122.5; and the two dark-state minima at 77.0 and 22.8 with the dark state itself at 109.2 and 108.5. The cis structure is markedly twisted, with a secondary dihedral of 43.5 degrees, while the trans structure is planar. The two bright states, conventionally one centred on the central bond and one built from local phenyl excitations, come out mixed in the computed wave functions.
Other: The active space is stated in the useful way, by what each orbital is rather than by rank: the pi and pi* orbitals of the central double bond about which rotation occurs, plus the two degenerate frontier orbitals of each phenyl ring, ten electrons in ten orbitals. Since the whole study is a rotation about that bond, the space is built from the coordinate outward. The validation that matters for a torsional path is then made explicitly and with an important distinction: during the rotary process the nature of individual orbitals changes significantly, but as a whole the active orbitals are well conserved against the geometrical variations. That is the correct thing to check and the correct way to state it -- a space can be stable as a subspace even when no individual orbital in it retains its character, and demanding orbital-by-orbital constancy would reject a perfectly sound space. Only the second, weaker condition is actually needed for a continuous surface. State averaging over four states is likewise justified physically rather than by convergence: the closed-shell ground state, the two lowest bright states, and the dark state, chosen as adequate because excitation is into one of the bright pair and the dark state mediates the decay. The authors note that the two bright states, conventionally described as one centred on the central bond and one built from local phenyl excitations, come out mixed in their wave functions -- so the diabatic labels borrowed from the literature do not survive contact with the calculation, and state character has to be read from the wave functions rather than assumed from the names. Two constraints limit what the space is asked to do, and both are declared. A two-fold symmetry constraint was applied throughout except when optimizing the intersections themselves, adopted purely to reduce cost after a cheaper method indicated the relevant structures are essentially symmetric about that axis. Restricting the symmetry of a rotary path is a substantive restriction for a motor whose unidirectionality is the property under study, since it is precisely asymmetric distortions that break the degeneracy between clockwise and counterclockwise motion; the authors release it exactly where it would matter most, at the intersections. And triplets were excluded on experimental grounds, quoting isomerization yields of 0.52 and 0.35 for the two singlet channels against 0.002 for the triplet, plus the sub-picosecond timescale. Excluding a spin manifold on measured branching ratios rather than on a computed coupling is a defensible shortcut with its evidence stated. The energetics show the reference alone placing excited states 105 to 167 kcal/mol above the ground minima, so the perturbative correction applied at those geometries with a level shift of 0.3 is carrying a large share of the answer, and the paper reports only the reference values for the geometric survey.

method: Full valence pi CASSCF with natural orbital analysis, compared against restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock, against a topological Huckel model, and against unrestricted density functional theory; spin polarization added through restricted active space configuration interaction including all single excitations from the doubly occupied pi orbitals into the singly occupied and empty ones

active_space_protocol: The full valence pi space in every case, so no orbital selection enters. Orbitals were first optimized at the restricted open-shell level for the doublet ground state of the monoradicals and the triplet ground state of the diradicals, then reoptimized in the full pi space. Spin polarization is treated separately by restricted active space single excitations; the program admits at most fifty orbitals in total, which limits the accessible molecular size.

electronic_structure_description: Spin populations on the starred atoms: 0.571, 0.143 and 0.143 from the Huckel model; 0.803, 0.062 and 0.050 from the restricted open-shell single determinant; and 0.591, 0.117 and 0.142 from the almost singly occupied natural orbital of the full pi space. The single-determinant treatment places 40 percent more spin on the exocyclic carbon than either of the other two descriptions and correspondingly starves the ring positions.
Other: This paper is built around a paradox that is entirely about what an active space does, and the result is the reverse of the usual expectation. The space is the full valence pi system in every case, so there is no selection question -- what varies is only the molecule -- and the finding is that the almost-singly-occupied natural orbital of that correlated wave function has a spin distribution close to the topological Huckel prediction, while the restricted open-shell single determinant gives something quite different. For the simplest case the spin population on the exocyclic carbon is 0.571 by Huckel, 0.591 from the full pi space, and 0.803 from the single-determinant reference; the pattern repeats across all six molecules, with the single-reference values running 0.760 to 0.803 while the correlated values track the Huckel numbers to within a few hundredths. The single-reference description concentrates the unpaired electron far too heavily on the methylene groups and correspondingly starves the ring positions -- 0.062 against a Huckel 0.143 and a correlated 0.117 for the first ring carbon of the simplest compound. geometry_source: Configurations generated by classical molecular dynamics with an Amber force field after energy minimization and simulation to 1 nanosecond, then used for the quantum/classical calculations

active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the n, pi and pi* orbitals of one carbonyl group, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of a specific carbon-hydrogen bond, and the n, sigma and sigma* orbitals of the disulfide bridge.
active_space_protocol: Different spaces are used in the two solvents, differing in composition as well as size. The quantum region is 45 atoms inside the beta-turn with two hydrogen link atoms at the cut bonds; all remaining solute atoms and all solvent are classical.
electronic_structure_description: After photocleavage of the disulfide bond, intramolecular hydrogen transfer from one cysteine group to the sulfur of the other is almost barrier-free, under 5 kcal/mol. The hydrogen-transferred state lies 30 kcal/mol below the conical intersection but still 30 kcal/mol above the folded beta-turn state, which the authors use to explain a quantum yield for the fully unfolded structure of only about 5 percent with a sub-nanosecond lifetime. Cleavage is accompanied by conformational change, with a competing reaction occurring within 200 femtoseconds and the sulfur-sulfur separation reaching a maximum of about 15 Angstrom within several hundred picoseconds.
Other: The striking feature here is that a different active space is used for each solvent, and the difference is not merely one orbital in size but a wholesale change of composition. In acetonitrile the space is ten electrons in eight orbitals comprising the n, pi and pi* orbitals of one carbonyl, the sigma and sigma* of a specific C-H bond, and the n, sigma and sigma* of the disulfide bridge. In methanol it is ten electrons in nine orbitals built from the pi and pi* of one carbonyl together with the sigma, sigma* and lone pair of the adjacent C-N bond in that peptide plane, the pi and pi* of a second, different peptide unit, and only the sigma and sigma* of the disulfide. Between the two, a C-H bonding pair is swapped out for a C-N set, a second peptide unit is brought in, and the sulfur lone pair is dropped. Since the paper compares the photochemistry in the two solvents, that comparison is drawn across calculations whose active spaces share only the disulfide sigma pair and one carbonyl pi system. Nothing here is wrong -- each space is chemically sensible for the bonds it must describe, and the methanol space is taken over from earlier work on the same system -- but the solvent effect and the space effect are not separated, and a reader attributing a difference between the two solvents to solvation alone would be over-reading the data. The one common thread is that both spaces contain the sigma and sigma* of the bond being broken, which is the minimum a homolysis requires, and the acetonitrile space adds the sulfur lone pair on top of it. The rest of the design follows the reaction rather than the molecule: carbonyl orbitals enter because the chromophore is there, and the C-H pair enters in one solvent because hydrogen transfer is one of the competing channels. Choosing orbitals by which bonds break and form is the right principle; applying it differently in two cases that will be compared is where it gets awkward. The scope of what the space covers is tightly limited and clearly stated. Only 45 atoms inside the beta-turn are treated quantum mechanically, with two hydrogen link atoms placed at the cut bonds and everything else, including all solvent, handled classically. The correlated treatment supplies only static potential energy profiles for the photochemical steps; all the dynamics -- unfolding, refolding, the competing hydrogen transfer and bicyclization on nanosecond timescales -- is run with a semiempirical Hamiltonian in which the sulfur biradical character is represented by mixing four microstates rather than by any active space. So the multiconfigurational calculation establishes that the hydrogen transfer is nearly barrierless at under 5 kcal/mol and locates the transferred state 30 kcal/mol below the intersection but still 30 above the folded turn, and those three numbers are what the entire dynamical interpretation is anchored to. The authors also note that the competing bicyclization channel could not be given a potential energy profile at all because no optimized reaction path could be defined for it, so one of the two competing processes is characterized energetically and the other is not.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 3H, or X 3H4 once spin-orbit resolved, with an equilibrium bond length of 1.902 Angstrom. All four triplet states are bound while both quintet states are repulsive. Every state is doubly degenerate except the Sigma states, and all bound states run parallel to one another with minima within 0.001 Angstrom of the ground state, because they differ only in which compact 4f orbitals are occupied. Spin-orbit coupling splits the five states into fourteen terms while leaving the bound curves parallel; the first excited multiplet A 3H5 lies 1877 wavenumbers above the ground term. Zero-field splittings are 2658 wavenumbers for the largest state, 1397 for the 5Phi state and 532 for the 3Pi state. The ground state couples only weakly to the excited triplets, the strongest such coupling being with the 3Pi state, and the largest triplet-triplet coupling is 1366 wavenumbers between the lowest 3Sigma-minus and 3Pi states; the two quintets couple to each other at 628 wavenumbers.
Other: The space is pruned by occupation numbers, and the pruning is done properly -- across the whole bond length range rather than at a single geometry. A larger sixteen-orbital space containing the fluorine 2p set together with the lanthanide 4f, 5d and 6s orbitals was run as single points at internuclear distances from 1.4 to 2.6 Angstrom, and the occupations examined at every distance. The fluorine 2p-x and 2p-y orbitals came out at or above 1.97 electrons throughout and the metal 5d and 6s at or below 0.03 throughout, so the first pair was returned to the core and the second set to the virtual space, leaving the seven 4f orbitals plus the fluorine 2p-z that points along the bond. Checking a scan rather than an equilibrium point is what makes this defensible for a dissociation curve, since an orbital that is empty at equilibrium can become occupied as a bond breaks; here the authors demonstrate it does not happen over the range they use. The resulting space is also chemically well motivated rather than merely numerically justified: it keeps the full degenerate 4f set so that the manifold degeneracy is represented, and adds exactly the one ligand orbital with the right symmetry to form the bond. What the space delivers is a striking uniformity that would be easy to mistake for an artifact. All the bound states are parallel to each other, every excited bound state has its minimum within 0.001 Angstrom of the ground state, and after spin-orbit coupling splits five states into fourteen terms the multiplet-resolved curves remain parallel. The authors explain this physically -- the bound states differ only in which 4f orbitals are occupied, and the 4f orbitals are compact and local enough that reshuffling their occupations barely perturbs the bonding. A space built almost entirely from orbitals that do not participate in bonding produces states that differ in energy but not in geometry, which is the f-block analogue of a ligand-field manifold and is exactly what the space was constructed to capture. The spin-orbit analysis then extracts something the space alone could not: coupling constants between individual states, showing that the ground state couples only weakly to the excited triplets and that there is no appreciable coupling at all between the bound triplets and the repulsive quintets -- from which the authors conclude there is no apparent route to homolytic bond cleavage in this system, in contrast to a neighbouring lanthanide fluoride where the ground state does couple moderately to a repulsive high-spin state. That is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from off-diagonal elements rather than from energies, and it depends on having both spin manifolds in the same treatment. Two technical points worth carrying: only the model-potential cores are frozen at the perturbation stage, so everything treated explicitly is correlated; and intruder states are removed by denominator shifts of 0.02 and 0.10 atomic units for the scalar and spin-orbit perturbation calculations respectively, the spin-orbit calculation needing five times the shift.

electronic_structure_description: The lowest excited state is a dark n to pi* transition, promoting an electron from a carbonyl oxygen lone pair into a pi* orbital delocalized over the benzoyl chromophore, with an oscillator strength of 0.00151 and a vertical energy of 93.7 kcal/mol -- about 10 kcal/mol higher than in benzophenone compounds without water, because hydrogen bonding destabilizes the lone pair. On excitation to that state the carbonyl oxygen to water hydrogen bond shortens from 2.071 to 1.841 Angstrom as negative charge concentrates on the carbonyl, with corresponding elongation of the water O-H bonds along the relay. So the active space is being applied to a cluster whose size, not whose orbital selection, sets the accuracy of the solvation-dependent quantities. compound_name: Butadiene, ground and pi to pi* excited state, as a configuration interaction test case
method: CASSCF used as a reference wave function from which a configuration interaction matrix was built, comprising all active space determinants plus all single excitations from them; the matrices were constructed explicitly and diagonalized both by the Davidson algorithm and by a new parallel algorithm being tested
software: MOLCAS 7.4 for the SCF and CASSCF calculations; the CASDI series of programs to build the configuration interaction matrices
active_space_orbital_description: Four active electrons in four active pi orbitals, named individually as 1au, 1bg, 2au and 2bg.
active_space_protocol: The minimal pi space, used to generate a reference wave function for matrix construction rather than to converge a chemical property. A single-determinant reference was used in parallel with the same singles-excitation space on top, so that matrices of identical dimension but different reference character could be compared.
nroots_per_mult: the ground state and the pi to pi* excited state
electronic_structure_description: The ground state and the pi to pi* excited state were computed. The configuration interaction space comprises all determinants of the active space plus all possible single excitations built from them, giving a dimension of 12748 determinants from either reference.
Other: The multiconfigurational calculation here is a benchmark object rather than a chemical result, and reading it that way is what makes it informative: the paper's subject is a parallel matrix diagonalization algorithm, and butadiene supplies a configuration interaction matrix of realistic structure to test it on. The active space is the minimal pi space, four electrons in the four orbitals named individually as 1au, 1bg, 2au and 2bg, and its purpose is to define a reference from which excited determinants are generated rather than to produce a converged excitation energy. What makes the setup instructive is the deliberate pairing: matrices were built from two different reference wave functions, a single-determinant one and this multiconfigurational one, with the same singles-excitation space on top of each. Both give a matrix of 12748 determinants, so the dimension is held fixed while the reference character varies -- the eigenvalue problem changes in its structure and diagonal dominance, not in its size. That is the right way to isolate what a numerical algorithm sees when the underlying wave function becomes multireference, since a multiconfigurational reference distributes weight across many determinants and so produces a matrix whose lowest eigenvector is far less dominated by a single component, which is precisely the regime where iterative diagonalization schemes converge slowly. The configuration space is described exactly: all determinants of the active space plus all possible single excitations built from them, with the resulting matrices constructed explicitly rather than handled in a direct fashion, then diagonalized by both the standard iterative method and the proposed one for comparison. Nothing here tests active space adequacy in the chemical sense -- no space-size series, no correlation treatment beyond the singles, no comparison with experiment -- so the excitation energy this produces should not be reused as a spectroscopic number. Its value to a database of active spaces is as a documented instance of the smallest defensible pi space for this molecule with its orbitals named by symmetry label, and as a record of how large the singles-augmented determinant space becomes on top of a four-orbital reference.

notes: This is a numerical linear algebra paper; the molecule is a test case for a parallel diagonalization algorithm, not the object of study. compound_name: Dinitrogen tetroxide with two water molecules, ground-state proton transfer
geometry_source: Starting structures from classical molecular dynamics with a 1.0 femtosecond timestep and coordinates saved every 100 femtoseconds; minimum energy profiles then built by constrained CASSCF optimization
method: CASSCF geometry optimization within a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics scheme using an Amber force field, with CASPT2 single points on a four-root state-averaged reference; minimum energy profiles built by multistep constrained optimization along the relevant bond coordinate
software: Gaussian for the CASSCF calculations, MOLCAS for the CASPT2 calculations, and the Tinker package for the molecular mechanics
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in nine orbitals: the sigma and sigma* orbitals of each of the two bonds undergoing fission, an O-N bond and an O-H bond, plus eight electrons in five orbitals comprising three pi orbitals and one antibonding pi* orbital of the nitrate moiety together with a non-bonding orbital on oxygen.
active_space_protocol: Built on the stated rule that the sigma and sigma* orbitals of any bond undergoing fission must be included, so four of the nine orbitals are spent on the two breaking bonds. The identical space and the same strategy of orbital choice were used for the gas-phase reoptimization, so the environmental comparison is controlled.
nroots_per_mult: four roots state-averaged in the perturbative step
electronic_structure_description: Ground-state intermolecular proton transfer between the dimer and water, proposed as a route to atmospheric hydroxyl radical. The barrier is 17.1 kcal/mol in the gas phase and 12.6 kcal/mol in the embedded system, 4.5 kcal/mol lower. Asymmetric dimers are about 0.4 kcal/mol more stable than the symmetric form, and the energy level is lowered by 10.8 kcal/mol on hydrogen bonding. A related asymmetric ONONO2 dimer is 8.6 kcal/mol less stable than isolated NO2 monomers, and a comparable barrier from earlier work on that dimer was 31.3 kcal/mol. Crossing the 17.1 kcal/mol barrier the energy curve falls sharply.
Other: The space construction is stated as a rule and then applied twice with different results, which makes the principle easy to extract. The rule is that to describe fission of a bond, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of that bond must be in the space -- so for a process breaking two bonds, both pairs go in, four orbitals spent on bond breaking before any chemistry of the chromophore is considered. The remaining eight electrons in five orbitals are then given as three pi orbitals and one antibonding pi* of the nitrate moiety plus a non-bonding oxygen orbital, giving twelve electrons in nine orbitals in total. For the separate photolysis step a different eight-electron six-orbital space is built by the same recipe: the sigma and sigma* of the single bond being broken, the non-bonding orbitals on the two heavy atoms, and three pi orbitals distinguished explicitly by node count -- zero, one and two nodes. Enumerating pi orbitals by their nodal structure rather than by energy ordering is a small but useful precision, since it fixes which orbitals are meant without reference to a particular calculation's ordering. The important methodological point is that the two reactions get two different spaces, each built for the bonds it breaks, rather than one space stretched across both. That is the right call for reactions studied separately, and the paper does not attempt to place their energies on a common scale, which would be the trap. The same space is, however, used for both the condensed-phase and gas-phase versions of the proton transfer -- the authors say explicitly that the gas-phase profile was reoptimized with the same twelve-electron nine-orbital space and the same strategy of orbital choice -- so the environmental comparison, unlike the reaction comparison, is properly controlled. That gives a clean number: the barrier drops from 17.1 kcal/mol in the gas phase to 12.6 in the embedded system, a 4.5 kcal/mol solvent effect measured with the space held fixed. Two scope limits are worth carrying. The quantum region is only the dimer plus two water molecules, with all remaining water classical, so the active space describes a small cluster embedded in a force field rather than the solvated system; and the perturbative correction uses a four-root state-averaged reference, meaning one orbital set serves four states even though the ground-state proton transfer is a single-state problem. The conclusion the paper draws is negative and rests on comparing barriers across the two differently-spaced calculations -- 17.1 kcal/mol for the proton transfer against alternatives -- so a reader should note that the competing channels were not all computed in one space.

geometry_source: Ground and excited state geometries optimized at the CASSCF level; excited state normal modes computed from those results for the Franck-Condon simulation
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and excited state frequencies, used to simulate a Franck-Condon envelope for comparison with a measured photodissociation action spectrum; time-dependent density functional theory was also employed
active_space_orbital_description: The six valence pi orbitals of the ring, three occupied and three unoccupied, holding six electrons. No sigma orbitals are included.
active_space_protocol: Justified on the grounds that the methyl substituent alters the symmetry but does not significantly perturb the pi system, so a single pi to pi* band is expected near 260 nanometres and a space spanning only the pi system should suffice. Validated against the measured origins of three isotopologues rather than by a space-size series.
nroots_per_mult: the ground state and the first singlet excited state
electronic_structure_description: A single pi to pi* absorption band expected near 260 nanometres. Adiabatic origins for the first singlet excited state are computed at 38605, 38615 and 38776 wavenumbers for the undeuterated ion, the methyl-d3 ion and the ring-d5 ion, against measured values of 38130, 38140 and 38320, giving nearly constant errors of 475, 475 and 456 wavenumbers. Excited state vibrational frequencies were computed for the five most Franck-Condon-active modes of each isotopologue, and the simulated spectrum reproduces an identified vibronic transition; most of the measured room-temperature action spectrum is not sufficiently resolved for detailed comparison. A photoproduct appearing 18 mass units higher, corresponding to water addition, is observed for each isotopologue.
Other: The space is the minimal aromatic pi valence set -- six electrons in the three occupied and three unoccupied pi orbitals of the ring -- and its adequacy is argued from a structural observation rather than from a convergence test: the methyl substituent alters the symmetry but does not significantly perturb the pi system, so a single pi to pi* band is expected and a space spanning only that system should suffice. Choosing the space from what the substituent does not do is an unusual and rather clean argument, and it is then validated against the sharpest possible external check, an isotope series. The calculation reproduces the measured adiabatic origins for three isotopologues at 38605, 38615 and 38776 wavenumbers against measured 38130, 38140 and 38320, so it is high by 475, 475 and 456 wavenumbers respectively. The absolute error is about 1.2 percent, which is unremarkable, but the errors are almost identical across the three species, and the computed isotope shifts are therefore right to within about twenty wavenumbers. That constancy is the meaningful result: a systematic offset of fixed size indicates the space is describing the same physics equally well in all three, whereas an error that varied with isotopic substitution would signal that the excited state geometry or the vibrational structure was being distorted differently in each. Isotopic substitution is a particularly demanding test of an active space precisely because it changes nothing electronic -- any variation in the error must come from the potential surface the space produces, not from the electronic structure of the states. The space is also asked to deliver excited state vibrational frequencies for the five most Franck-Condon-active modes across all three isotopologues, and the resulting simulated spectrum reproduces an identified vibronic transition in the measured action spectrum. Frequencies on an excited state surface are a second-derivative property and so a harder demand on a minimal space than the transition energy itself, and getting the mode displacements right is what allows the Franck-Condon simulation to be compared with experiment at all. Two limits should be recorded. No dynamical correlation treatment is applied on top of the space anywhere in the paper, so the 475 wavenumber offset is uncorrected and would be expected to shrink under a perturbative treatment. And the space contains only pi orbitals, so the sigma framework whose rupture produces the observed photodissociation products lies entirely outside it; the calculation characterizes the bound excited state that absorbs, not the dissociation that follows, which is established experimentally through product characterization instead. The paper is explicit that the photochemistry is interpreted with the aid of the calculations rather than from them.

notes: No dynamical correlation treatment is applied on top of the active space, so the roughly 475 wavenumber offset is uncorrected. compound_name: HO2 with CH2FO2, oxygen-oxygen addition entrance channel

electronic_structure_description: The approach of the two peroxy radicals along the terminal oxygen-oxygen coordinate is repulsive on the triplet surface but attractive on the singlet surface, the qualitative contrast the mechanism depends on. geometry_source: All geometries optimized at the CASSCF level, including the minimum-energy conical intersection and the steepest-descent path connecting it to the Franck-Condon points
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and minimum-energy path following; no perturbative correction was applied, the authors judging dynamic correlation unimportant on the basis of agreement with the measured absorption maximum
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in eleven orbitals: one nitrogen non-bonding 2s orbital, two N-O bonding and two N-O antibonding orbitals, one delocalized O-N-O pi bonding orbital and its pi antibonding partner, one N-N bonding and one N-N antibonding orbital, one pi-type non-bonding oxygen orbital and one sigma-type non-bonding oxygen orbital.

electronic_structure_description: The two lowest excited singlets are both of n to pi* character, with vertical excitation energies of 5.13 and 5.5 eV; the second agrees well with the measured gas-phase absorption maximum of 5.31 eV. A minimum-energy conical intersection between the first excited state and the ground state was located, and the steepest-descent path connecting the Franck-Condon points of both surfaces to that intersection was computed in the same space, accounting for an ultrafast internal conversion that would quench radiative emission.

Both bonds that can rupture are represented together with the full nitro chromophore, so photochemistry and dissociation share one space. The reasoning behind the size is stated in a way worth quoting because it inverts the usual justification: the large space is employed 'not necessarily to include dynamic correlation energy... but for the CI calculations'. That is, the space is sized to describe the configuration mixing at the intersection rather than to recover correlation, which is the right motivation for a conical-intersection study and a useful reminder that space size and correlation recovery are separate goals that happen to be served by the same parameter. The authors skip it because the reference energies agree well with the measured gas-phase absorption maximum -- 5.5 eV computed against 5.31 eV observed -- and take that agreement as indicating dynamic correlation is unimportant for this system. Agreement of a single vertical energy is thin evidence for that conclusion: a bare reference typically overestimates excitation energies, so landing 0.2 eV high is consistent either with correlation being genuinely small or with it being cancelled by the modest split-valence basis, and the two cannot be distinguished without computing the correction. electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2Pi-i. Spin-orbit coupling splits the ground state into 2Pi-3/2 and 2Pi-1/2 components separated by 2023 wavenumbers on density functional geometries and 2062 on perturbation theory geometries, against a photoelectron spectroscopic determination of 2091 plus or minus 40 wavenumbers and an earlier electron resonance estimate of 2330. The spin-orbit corrections computed on the two sets of geometries differ by only 0.2 kJ/mol for this species.
Other: Three different active spaces are used along a single reaction profile, and both dimensions change: eleven valence electrons in fourteen orbitals for the isolated radical, nineteen electrons in fourteen orbitals for the prereactive complex and every transition state, and fifteen electrons in thirteen orbitals for the postreactive complex. The electron count rising by eight from reactant to complex is simply the carbon monoxide valence electrons entering the treatment, so that step is bookkeeping rather than a change of description; the reduction to fifteen electrons and thirteen orbitals for the product complex is a genuine truncation made because that species can afford less. The consequence is the familiar one -- stationary points along one profile are described in spaces of different size, so their relative energies are not strictly on a common footing -- but here it matters less than usual, because the active space is not being used to compute the reaction energetics at all. That job is done by density functional and coupled cluster methods; the multiconfigurational calculation exists to supply spin-orbit corrections through a state-interaction treatment, one species at a time, and a spin-orbit correction is an intensive property of each stationary point rather than a difference between them. Confining a variable-size space to a per-species property, and keeping the differences in a method that can be applied uniformly, is a sensible division of labour that the paper does not spell out but which is what makes the varying spaces defensible. That is a properly closed loop: the residual disagreement is attributed to a named geometric cause and the null cases are checked too. A chemically useful pattern falls out of the per-species corrections: the values for both molecular complexes are close to those of the isolated radical and the isolated iodine atom respectively, indicating that the approaching carbon monoxide barely perturbs the iodine spin-orbit manifold. Doublet and quartet multiplicities were treated in separate calculations throughout.

compound_name: Cyclodec-3-en-1,5-diyne, conformer 1a, and its C2-symmetric cyclization path
point_group: C2, preserved along the entire reaction coordinate
geometry_source: Stationary points and intrinsic reaction coordinates optimized at the CASSCF level after density functional paths proved discontinuous
method: CASSCF geometry optimization of stationary points and intrinsic reaction coordinates, with energies corrected by a modified BLYP functional and by CCSD(T) at those geometries; zero-point energies from CASSCF frequencies scaled by 0.91 to match the functional. Reaction paths were interpolated to the higher levels by an interpolated-single-point-energies scheme, and small-curvature multidimensional tunnelling probabilities computed along the resulting vibrationally adiabatic curve
software: GAMESS for the CASSCF calculations, Gaussian 09 for the density functional and coupled cluster calculations, and POLYRATE with a GAUSSRATE interface modified to read and write GAMESS files for the rate and tunnelling calculations
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF and density functional calculations; cc-pVTZ for the coupled cluster single points
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals; the composition is not itemized.
active_space_protocol: Adopted specifically because every density functional tested -- BLYP, B3LYP, BPW91 and M06-2X -- produced a 0.3 kcal/mol discontinuity in the zero-point energy along the reaction coordinate at the point where the electronic configuration changes from closed shell to open shell. The space supplies geometries, paths and frequencies while the energies are taken from other methods at those geometries.
electronic_structure_description: One of two enediyne minima. Its Bergman cyclization proceeds through a saddle point to a biradical product along a path that preserves two-fold symmetry throughout, so the electronic configuration changes from closed shell to open shell without any symmetry breaking. The measured activation energy for cyclization is 23.8 kcal/mol, determined over a temperature range too narrow to reveal tunnelling; rate constants and carbon kinetic isotope effects were computed from 200 to 343 K instead.
Other: The active space is used here for a purpose it is rarely credited with, and its energies are simultaneously the worst of the three methods applied -- a combination that makes this a clean case study in what a space is actually for. The trigger is a pathology, not a number: along the intrinsic reaction coordinate the zero-point energy changed discontinuously by 0.3 kcal/mol at exactly the point where the electronic configuration switched from closed shell to open shell, and every density functional tested -- four of them, spanning pure, hybrid and meta-hybrid -- showed the same discontinuity. A tunnelling calculation integrates a vibrationally adiabatic curve along that path, so a step in the zero-point energy is fatal in a way it would not be for a barrier height. The stationary points and paths were therefore reoptimized in a ten-electron ten-orbital space, whose whole contribution is to describe both electronic configurations on an equal footing and so produce a continuous path across the closed-to-open-shell transition. Yet on that same path the bare space overestimates the barrier by 14 kcal/mol, against 2 kcal/mol too high for coupled cluster on the same geometries and close agreement for the corrected functional. So a fourteen kcal/mol error in the energy coexists with the space being the only method that gives a usable path -- geometry and topology are one property, energetics are another, and this paper separates them explicitly by taking geometries and frequencies from the space and energies from elsewhere. The zero-point energies are also taken from the space, but scaled by 0.91 to match the functional's values, so even the frequencies are recalibrated rather than used raw. A further detail worth carrying is how the two levels are stitched together: rather than recompute the whole reaction path at the expensive level, the path is computed in the active space and then interpolated to the higher level from single points, an interpolated-single-point-energies scheme. That keeps the continuity the space provides while getting the energetics from a method that can supply them, and it is the general pattern for using a space whose energies you do not trust. The topology the space reveals would also be hard to obtain otherwise: one pathway preserves two-fold symmetry throughout, while the other passes through a valley-ridge inflection on the reactant side of its saddle point, leading to a racemic minimum through a separate saddle point for enantiomeric interconversion. A valley-ridge inflection is a second-derivative feature of the surface, precisely the kind of thing a discontinuous path would either hide or invent. The measured activation energy is 23.8 kcal/mol over a temperature range too narrow to reveal tunnelling, which is why the study computes carbon kinetic isotope effects from 200 to 343 K as the sensitive experimental criterion instead -- and an isotope effect is a ratio of rates over the same surface, so it is far more demanding of path continuity than of absolute barrier accuracy.

geometry_source: Quantum/classical optimized geometries built on crystal structures, with molecular dynamics snapshots used separately to assess the effect of thermal sampling
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 correction using the default shifted zeroth-order Hamiltonian and Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals, within a quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics scheme in which all classical partial charges are retained except those on link atoms; computed alongside time-dependent density functional theory and symmetry-adapted cluster configuration interaction for comparison
software: MOLCAS 7.6 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 09 for the density functional and cluster expansion calculations
basis_set: ANO-S-VDZP for the multiconfigurational calculations; 6-31+G* for the density functional and 6-31G* for the cluster expansion calculations

active_space_protocol: One space held fixed across all four proteins, which share a chemically identical chromophore, so that computed differences reflect the protein environment rather than the treatment. Three nested choices of quantum region were compared separately, and enlarging it was found to change excitation energies by less than 0.005 eV.
electronic_structure_description: The most red-shifted of the four proteins and the reference against which the others are compared. Its excitation energy is 3.336 eV at the reference level with oscillator strength 1.36, and 2.857 eV with strength 1.16 after the perturbative correction, against a measured 2.41 eV. Holding a space constant is usually a compromise; here it is the point of the experiment. The numbers show clearly what the bare reference can and cannot do. Absolute excitation energies at the reference level are 3.336, 3.276, 3.392 and 3.468 eV against measured 2.41, 2.46, 2.54 and 2.74 -- roughly 0.9 eV too high across the board, an error of nearly 40 percent that the perturbative correction reduces to 0.3 to 0.45 eV. So a space that is badly wrong in absolute terms is usable for differences, and the systematic character of its error is what makes that so -- a reminder that the right accuracy question depends on whether the target is an energy or a shift. Reporting a geometry-induced shift of the same order as the method's residual error, and declining to interpret it, is the right handling. compound_name: Phenol with a peroxy radical, hydrogen abstraction saddle point and hydrogen-bonded complex
geometry_source: All structures -- separated reactants, the hydrogen-bonded complex and the saddle point -- optimized at the multireference perturbation theory level using numerical gradients, with Hessians evaluated at the same level at several geometries to locate the saddle point
method: Multireference second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory on CASSCF reference wave functions, used as a benchmark against which a range of density functionals is assessed
basis_set: MG3S, equivalent to 6-311+G(2df,2p) for these systems, for the geometries; aug-cc-pVTZ for the benchmark barrier height at those geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Nine electrons in nine orbitals, constructed by the nominal correlated participating orbitals prescription extended to cover pi bonding, denoted nom-CPO+pi. The recipe is defined in earlier work for an arbitrary reactive system rather than chosen for this molecule.
active_space_protocol: Built from a published systematic prescription rather than by inspection, so it is reproducible and carries a known error statistic: the mean unsigned error of this method and space on a representative barrier-height database is 1.4 kcal/mol. Geometries and Hessians were computed at the correlated level rather than at the reference level because both the bare active space method and density functionals distort the potential energy surface in the saddle-point region.
electronic_structure_description: The abstraction proceeds through a hydrogen-bonded phenol-radical complex preceding the saddle point. At the saddle point the hydroxyl group and the hydrogen bond twist out of the molecular plane, in contrast to the essentially planar equilibrium structures, and the dihedral angle involved is related to the location of an avoided crossing. The spin expectation value of the single-reference wave function is 0.76 at the complex and 1.29 at the saddle point, against 0.75 for a pure doublet; the variation between the two geometries is what indicates the surface would be distorted. The benchmark barrier height with respect to the hydrogen-bonded complex is 12.3 kcal/mol, against 35.0 kcal/mol from unprojected single-reference perturbation theory. Best estimates of 7.4 and 11.5 kcal/mol are given for the barrier and complexation energies. Density functional barrier heights for this reaction have been reported ranging from 4.2 to 9.3 kcal/mol.

Because the recipe is systematic, the space carries a known error statistic rather than an unquantified uncertainty: the mean unsigned error of this method and space combination on a representative barrier-height database is 1.4 kcal/mol, so the benchmark comes with its own error bar. A space that can be reproduced from a rule and whose accuracy has been characterized across a test set is a fundamentally different object from one chosen by inspection for a single molecule, and it is what makes this paper usable as a benchmark for assessing cheaper methods. The sharpest statement concerns what the bare reference cannot do. Geometries and Hessians were all computed at the perturbatively corrected level using numerical gradients, and the reason is given explicitly: lower-level Hessians proved inadequate because both the bare active space method and density functional methods, each for its own reasons, yield distorted potential energy surfaces in the saddle-point region. geometry_source: Full CASSCF geometry optimizations without symmetry constraints, both in vacuum and in solution, with numerical frequencies confirming the nature of each stationary point
method: CASSCF geometry optimization without symmetry constraints, with numerical frequencies to characterize stationary points, linearly interpolated internal reaction coordinate paths linking the critical structures, and conical intersections optimized with state-averaged orbitals omitting the orbital rotation derivative correction; second-order multiconfigurational perturbation theory single points on the same reference at those geometries
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF optimizations; a Dunning correlation-consistent polarized valence double-zeta set contracted [9s4p1d/3s2p1d] for the perturbative single points
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals: the benzene pi and pi* orbitals, the amino nitrogen lone pair, and the four pi and pi* orbitals of the cyano group -- donor, ring and acceptor all represented so that the charge-transfer state can be described.
active_space_protocol: One space serves both molecules of the pair so that the comparison between them is on a common footing. State-averaged orbitals were used for the intersection optimizations. The authors state the condition for the perturbative correction to be trustworthy -- that the reference be valid and the perturbation small -- as a principle rather than demonstrating it with configuration weights.
electronic_structure_description: The unmethylated member of the pair, which does not show dual fluorescence even in polar solvents. The equilibrium lies in favour of the locally excited species: the twisted charge-transfer structure was found at much higher energy and with a low reaction barrier back toward the locally excited state, so the charge-transfer species is not populated appreciably. This is the paper's explanation for the absence of dual fluorescence in this compound.
Other: The space is enumerated by fragment rather than by rank -- the benzene pi and pi* orbitals, the amino nitrogen lone pair, and the four pi and pi* orbitals of the cyano group, twelve electrons in eleven orbitals -- and the composition is precisely what the chemistry demands: a charge-transfer state in these systems moves density from the amino donor to the cyano acceptor through the ring, so all three fragments must be in the space or the transfer cannot be described at all. Including the nitrogen lone pair explicitly, rather than relying on it mixing into a delocalized orbital, is what allows the locally excited and charge-transfer states to be distinguished. One space serves both molecules of the pair, which differ only by methylation of the amino group, so the comparison between them -- the entire point, since one shows dual fluorescence and the other does not -- is drawn on a common footing. The paper also states, unusually explicitly, the condition under which the perturbative correction can be trusted: the results are reliable wherever the reference function is valid, and for the perturbation to succeed it has to be small, so the better the reference the more accurate the correction. That is the correct logical order and it puts the burden on the space rather than on the correction, which is the right place for it -- but it is stated as a principle and not demonstrated here with weights or diagnostics, so a reader cannot check whether the condition holds at the geometries that matter. That gap matters more than usual because the conclusions rest on near-degeneracies. The locally excited and planar charge-transfer minima are described as practically degenerate, and the argument for which species emits turns on small energy differences between minima and on a low barrier between the twisted charge-transfer species and the locally excited one. Distinguishing practically degenerate states is exactly the regime where a reference of marginal quality would fail silently. A structural point worth carrying concerns the intersections. State-averaged orbitals were used for the crossing optimizations and the orbital rotation derivative correction to the gradient was deliberately omitted as usually small, so the located points are the lowest-energy points on the crossing seam rather than fully converged minima of the seam. The authors then make the physically important observation that the remaining coordinates preserve the degeneracy, so the crossing persists over a wide range of geometries and decay can occur away from the minimum energy point depending on the kinetic energy of the system. Treating an intersection as a seam rather than a point is the more honest picture, and it means the located structure is a representative of a manifold rather than the unique funnel. Geometries come from the uncorrected space with a modest split-valence basis, while the energies use a larger correlation-consistent basis at those geometries, so topology and energetics again come from different levels.
reference_short: Gomez, Castro & Reguero, J. Phys. Chem. A 2015, 119, 1983
notes: The negative case of the pair. Its conclusion rests on a barrier being low rather than on a large energy separation, so it depends on the reference describing the region between the two minima accurately.

compound_name: (O2)4 cuboid cluster, the unit cell of the epsilon high-pressure solid phase of oxygen
geometry_source: The B3LYP-optimized periodic unit cell geometry at each pressure, taken in 10 GPa increments; the cluster calculations are single points on those structures
method: CASSCF single points on the cluster cut from the optimized unit cell, used as a diagnostic of multireference character; all structures and enthalpies come from periodic density functional calculations with localized atomic basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals, comprising the two pi-g orbitals of each of the four oxygen molecules in the unit cell.
active_space_protocol: A minimal and unambiguous space repeated unchanged at every pressure in 10 GPa steps, so that the only variable is the geometry. Used purely as a diagnostic of configurational character rather than to compute any energy or structure.
nroots_per_mult: the ground state; the singlet wave function comprises 1252 configuration state functions
electronic_structure_description: The wave function is strongly multiconfigurational at the zero-pressure optimized geometry and becomes progressively better described by a single configuration as the intermolecular distance decreases under pressure. The coefficient of the leading closed-shell configuration rises monotonically from 0.61 at 10 GPa to 0.74 at 95 GPa. Over the same range the root-mean-square error of the B3LYP lattice parameters against experiment falls from 3.2 percent to below 0.38 percent, so the improvement in the density functional structural description tracks the decline in multireference character.
Other: This is an unusually direct demonstration that multireference character is a continuous variable controlled by a physical parameter, and that the accuracy of a single-reference method tracks it. The space is the minimal and obvious one for an oxygen cluster -- eight electrons in eight orbitals, being the two pi-g orbitals from each of the four molecules in the unit cell -- so no selection judgement enters and the space means the same thing at every geometry. What varies is pressure, and with it the intermolecular separation. The diagnostic reported is the coefficient of the leading closed-shell configuration in the CASSCF wave function, and it climbs monotonically from 0.61 at 10 GPa to 0.74 at 95 GPa as the molecules are squeezed together. Over exactly the same range the root-mean-square error of the density functional lattice parameters against experiment falls from 3.2 percent to under 0.38 percent. Plotting the two on one axis against pressure is the whole argument, and it is a better argument than any single number could be: the single-reference method is not simply good or bad for this system, it is bad where the wave function is multiconfigurational and good where it is not, and the crossover is driven by a knob the experiment can turn. A leading coefficient of 0.61 means the closed-shell configuration carries under 40 percent of the wave function, which is about as multireference as a ground state gets, and even at the highest pressure 0.74 is well short of single-determinantal. The active space is used purely as a diagnostic here and not for any energy or geometry -- every structure and every enthalpy in the study comes from periodic density functional calculations, and the cluster calculations are single points on those optimized cells. That is the right division of labour for a solid-state problem where a periodic multiconfigurational treatment is not available, and it is worth recording as a pattern: when the expensive method cannot be applied to the production system, apply it to a representative fragment purely to explain when the cheap method can be trusted. The limitation is the corresponding one: a four-molecule cuboid cut from the cell carries no information about longer-range correlation in the crystal, so the diagnostic describes the local pair interactions rather than the solid. The configuration count is reported as 1252 configuration state functions for the singlet, and the calculation is run in the full point group of the cuboid, so the space is small enough that the analysis could be repeated at 10 GPa intervals across the whole phase range -- which is what makes the correlation visible rather than anecdotal.
reference_short: Ochoa-Calle, Zicovich-Wilson, Hernandez-Lamoneda & Ramirez-Solis, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2015, 11, 1195
notes: The broader study finds that local density and gradient approximation functionals predict too low a transition pressure for the epsilon to zeta phase change, while hybrid functionals whose performance depends on the amount of non-local exchange -- PBE0, M06, B3PW91 and B3LYP -- correctly predict the structural and electronic changes. The four-molecule cluster carries no information about longer-range correlation in the crystal, so the diagnostic describes local pair interactions rather than the solid.
correlation_correction: None; the CASSCF wave function is used directly as a diagnostic of configurational character rather than as a starting point for a correlated energy

compound_name: Phenol, photodissociation along the O-H coordinate
point_group: Cs at the planar equilibrium structure; the diabatization was also tested at significantly distorted ring geometries
geometry_source: Equilibrium geometry optimized with a correlated method; potential surface cuts computed along the O-H stretch and the C-C-O-H torsion with all other geometric parameters frozen at their equilibrium values
method: State-averaged CASSCF over three states with equal weights, used both for adiabatic surfaces and to construct diabatic molecular orbitals by the fourfold way; multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory on those references supplies the diabatic energies and couplings, with an intruder-state denominator shift of 0.02 hartree
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ for the equilibrium geometry optimization; jul-cc-pVDZ for the state-averaged surfaces
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals: three pi and three pi* orbitals of the ring, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the C-O bond, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the O-H bond, and the oxygen lone pair perpendicular to the molecular plane.
active_space_protocol: Composed so that all three states of interest are describable simultaneously -- two of ring pi character and one dissociative sigma* state on the breaking bond -- with equal-weight state averaging over exactly those three. The orbitals are then used to construct a diabatic representation, so their consistency of character along the coordinate matters more than the correlation the space recovers.
nroots_per_mult: three states, equally weighted
electronic_structure_description: Near the equilibrium geometry the three states of interest are of pi-pi, pi-pi* and pi-sigma* character, the last being the only state connecting diabatically to the dissociation products. The planar molecule undergoes two symmetry-allowed crossings along the O-H stretch, and these crossings are portions of conical intersection seams that extend to non-planar geometries. The diabatization was confirmed to remain valid at significantly distorted ring structures by repeating it along a coordinate that breaks the planar symmetry.
Other: The space is enumerated orbital by orbital and every member is there because a specific state or a specific bond requires it: three pi and three pi* orbitals for the ring excitations, the sigma and sigma* pairs of both the C-O and the O-H bonds, and the oxygen lone pair perpendicular to the molecular plane -- twelve electrons in eleven orbitals. The composition is dictated by the three states that must be described simultaneously, two of ring pi character and one of sigma* character on the bond that breaks, and a space missing the O-H sigma* pair simply could not represent the dissociative state at all. State averaging over exactly those three states with equal weights is likewise structural rather than optional, since the whole problem is the crossings between them. What makes this paper distinctive is that the active space orbitals are used to construct a diabatic representation rather than just to compute adiabatic energies. Diabatic molecular orbitals are built from the reference wave functions, and the resulting diabatic states and their couplings are then obtained at the perturbatively corrected level using those orbitals. This means the space is doing something a larger or better space would not automatically do better: the quality of a diabatization depends on whether the orbitals themselves carry consistent character across the coordinate, not on how much correlation the space recovers. The authors confirm the diabatization remains valid even for significantly distorted ring structures by repeating it along a coordinate that breaks the planar symmetry, which is the necessary check -- a diabatic representation that only works near the reference geometry is of no use for dynamics. The symmetry-allowed crossings that occur for planar geometries are noted to be portions of conical intersection seams extending to non-planar geometries, so the whole construction has to survive leaving the plane. Two practical settings are stated. The potential surface cuts are computed along the O-H stretch and the C-C-O-H torsion with all other geometric parameters frozen at their equilibrium values, so these are rigid two-dimensional cuts rather than relaxed paths -- adequate for building a model surface but not for quantitative barrier heights. And an intruder-state denominator shift of 0.02 hartree is applied in the perturbation step. The stated conclusion is the transferable one: diabatization at the perturbatively corrected level using reference diabatic orbitals is a good starting point for multidimensional dynamics, which places the value of the active space in the orbitals it produces rather than in the energies.

correlation_correction: Multiconfigurational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory on the state-averaged reference, with a 0.02 hartree denominator shift against intruder states

ligand_set: Two cyclic alkyl(amino) carbene ligands and two chlorides
method: CASSCF with CASPT2 correction and spin-orbit treatment by restricted active space state interaction, computed alongside SQUID magnetometry, Moessbauer and multi-frequency EPR measurements
soc_included: yes, by restricted active space state interaction
active_space_orbital_description: The metal d orbitals, with separate test calculations adding the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the bonded carbon atoms or of chlorine; counts are not stated.
active_space_protocol: The metal d space was enlarged in separate tests by adding the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the bonded carbon atoms, or of the chlorine, either of which leaves the oxidation-state assignment unchanged; adding all of them simultaneously, described as preferable, was computationally impossible. The authors state that a quantitative account of the spin-orbit effect would require more orbitals than they can afford.
electronic_structure_description: The multiconfigurational calculations show a clear 3d6 character, confirming the iron is in the divalent state as expected. Synthesized by reacting iron dichloride with two equivalents of the carbene, and reduced with potassium graphite to give the monovalent complex.
Other: This paper is unusually candid about a space it knows to be inadequate, and the candour is the useful part. Enlargement was tested, but only one direction at a time: adding the bonding and antibonding orbitals of the bonded carbon atoms, or the chlorine, to the metal d space does not change the oxidation-state assignment -- and the authors state plainly that adding all of them simultaneously, which they say would be preferable, is computationally not possible. That is an honest partial test, and the caveat it implies is worth carrying generally: enlargements that are individually null do not guarantee that a joint enlargement is null, because the orbitals left out in each separate test are exactly the ones that might have mattered in combination. For the robust conclusion here -- that the metal is genuinely in a d7 configuration with three unpaired electrons -- the partial test is adequate, since a qualitative assignment is unlikely to flip on correlation the separate tests each failed to find. For the quantitative magnetic anisotropy it is not, and the authors say so twice. They note that the splitting of the ground term is strongly dependent on the computational model employed and on the electron correlation considered, and later that an accurate quantitative account of the spin-orbit effect requires including more orbitals in the space than they can currently afford, with further work in progress. Declaring a computed number inadequate for the purpose while still publishing the qualitative picture it supports is the right handling of an unconverged space. The physical reason the space is under such strain is instructive. The carbene ligand field produces an unusually small splitting of the ground atomic multiplet, around 5000 wavenumbers for the cationic complex, so the spin-orbit interaction becomes comparatively very important and its effect depends sensitively on exactly how that small orbital splitting comes out. When two effects of similar magnitude compete, the answer is set by their difference, and a space that captures each to ten percent may still get the difference badly wrong. The chloride in the neutral complex acts as a perturbant with combined electrostatic and covalent effect, and departure of the carbon-metal-carbon angle from linearity contributes further splitting, so the ligand field in the cation is weaker still. The comparison the paper draws with a known single-molecule magnet is attributed to the fundamentally different electronic structure of the bonding carbon atoms rather than to any parameter of the calculation, which is a chemical conclusion the space can support even where it cannot support the numbers.

notes: The reference compound of the series, whose straightforward divalent assignment establishes that the method reproduces an uncontroversial case before being applied to the two monovalent complexes.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 on the CASSCF reference, with spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction afterwards

electronic_structure_description: The symmetric low-electronegativity reference compound. With substituents of low electronegativity the selenium-selenium bond becomes activated on electron capture, the captured electron populating its antibonding sigma* orbital, as earlier studies had established.
Other: The most valuable thing here is a diagnosed failure of state-specific optimization, corrected by state averaging, with the mechanism identified rather than guessed. Optimizing the ground state wave function alone produced a substantial overestimation of the selenium-selenium lengthening on electron capture; reoptimizing the lowest root of a six-state average gave better structures, and the authors attribute the difference to the antibonding sigma* orbital of that bond having an unphysically high contribution in the state-specific wave function, which the averaging corrects. This is state averaging changing a geometry rather than an excitation energy, and it is worth carrying because the intuition runs the other way: averaging is usually understood as a compromise that degrades a ground-state description in exchange for balance across states. Here the unaveraged description is the one that is wrong, because a variational optimization of a single root can over-populate exactly the orbital that defines the reaction coordinate. Any study optimizing an anion geometry along a bond-breaking coordinate in a space containing that bond's antibonding orbital is exposed to the same artifact. The space itself is transferred rather than derived: ten electrons in eight orbitals for the neutrals and eleven in nine for the anions, adopted because it gave good results in an analogous study of disulfides. Transferring a space between the sulfur and selenium homologues is reasonable given that the paper's whole argument is that the two behave alike, but it means the space was not independently validated for selenium; the extra electron and extra orbital for the anion is the natural bookkeeping. The multiconfigurational treatment is also deployed selectively and for a stated reason -- because the study involves radicals, the single- or multiconfigurational character of the states had to be checked -- so it functions as an arbiter among the cheaper methods rather than as the production method. Two technical details should be noted. Geometries and energies use different basis sets, the geometries optimized with an atomic natural orbital set contracted for selenium and the energies computed with the smaller basis used for the other methods, so the multireference numbers are not internally consistent in basis. And the electron capture produces multiple stable anion isomers -- two for one derivative and three for another -- distinguished by which bond elongates and by dihedral changes, so the active space must describe a manifold of structures with different bonding patterns rather than a single product.

basis_set: Atomic natural orbital sets contracted to [5s4p3d] on selenium, [3s2p1d] on carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and fluorine and [2s1p] on hydrogen for the geometry optimizations; a smaller basis, the same as used for the other methods, for the perturbative energies
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals for the neutral species; the anions use eleven electrons in nine orbitals. The composition is not itemized beyond the identification of the sigma* orbitals of the Se-Se and Se-X bonds as the ones that accept the captured electron.
active_space_protocol: Ten electrons in eight orbitals for the neutral species and eleven in nine for the anions, transferred from an analogous study of disulfides rather than derived for selenium. State-specific optimization was found to overestimate the selenium-selenium lengthening because the antibonding sigma* orbital of that bond acquired an unphysically high contribution; averaging over the six lowest states corrected this.
multiplicities_studied: singlet for the neutrals and doublet for the radical anions
nroots_per_mult: six lowest states in the state-averaged optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Electron capture yields three distinct stable radical anions, more than any other member of the series. The stretched isomer shows a moderate elongation of about 0.2 Angstrom in both the Se-Se and Se-O bonds together with a substantial opening of the SeSeO angle; the bent anion shows a much larger elongation of about 0.5 Angstrom in the Se-O bond with a decrease in the dihedral angle; and a book isomer, unique to this compound, retains a conformation like the neutral species but with a Se-Se bond about 0.6 Angstrom longer. Its bonding shows characteristics of a charge-shift bond with substantial contribution from ionic resonance forms.
Other: The most valuable thing here is a diagnosed failure of state-specific optimization, corrected by state averaging, with the mechanism identified rather than guessed. Optimizing the ground state wave function alone produced a substantial overestimation of the selenium-selenium lengthening on electron capture; reoptimizing the lowest root of a six-state average gave better structures, and the authors attribute the difference to the antibonding sigma* orbital of that bond having an unphysically high contribution in the state-specific wave function, which the averaging corrects. This is state averaging changing a geometry rather than an excitation energy, and it is worth carrying because the intuition runs the other way: averaging is usually understood as a compromise that degrades a ground-state description in exchange for balance across states. Here the unaveraged description is the one that is wrong, because a variational optimization of a single root can over-populate exactly the orbital that defines the reaction coordinate. Any study optimizing an anion geometry along a bond-breaking coordinate in a space containing that bond's antibonding orbital is exposed to the same artifact. The space itself is transferred rather than derived: ten electrons in eight orbitals for the neutrals and eleven in nine for the anions, adopted because it gave good results in an analogous study of disulfides. Transferring a space between the sulfur and selenium homologues is reasonable given that the paper's whole argument is that the two behave alike, but it means the space was not independently validated for selenium; the extra electron and extra orbital for the anion is the natural bookkeeping. The multiconfigurational treatment is also deployed selectively and for a stated reason -- because the study involves radicals, the single- or multiconfigurational character of the states had to be checked -- so it functions as an arbiter among the cheaper methods rather than as the production method. Two technical details should be noted. Geometries and energies use different basis sets, the geometries optimized with an atomic natural orbital set contracted for selenium and the energies computed with the smaller basis used for the other methods, so the multireference numbers are not internally consistent in basis. And the electron capture produces multiple stable anion isomers -- two for one derivative and three for another -- distinguished by which bond elongates and by dihedral changes, so the active space must describe a manifold of structures with different bonding patterns rather than a single product.
reference_short: Gamez & Yanez, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2010, 6, 3102
notes: The three anion isomers differ in which bond elongates, so one active space has to describe a manifold of structures with quite different bonding patterns rather than a single product.
correlation_correction: Second-order multireference perturbation theory at the CASSCF geometries, using a smaller basis than the optimizations
