compound_name: PSB3, the minimal model of the retinal protonated Schiff base chromophore
geometry_source: Ground-state geometries optimized independently at the CASSCF, second-order and third-order perturbation levels, and compared against coupled cluster, Moller-Plesset and approximate coupled cluster structures; the third-order optimization used neither the frozen core approximation nor the shifted zeroth-order Hamiltonian
method: CASSCF with second-order and third-order complete active space perturbation theory, in single-state and multi-state variants, alongside multireference configuration interaction with Davidson and Pople corrections and a range of single-reference methods; an imaginary shift of 0.1 hartree was used against intruder states
software: MOLCAS 7.6 for the CASSCF and second-order optimizations; MOLPRO 2010.1 and 2012.1 for the third-order and configuration interaction work; Gaussian09 revision D01 for the perturbation and coupled cluster geometries; Turbomole 6.5 for the approximate coupled cluster geometries
basis_set: 6-31G* and ANO-L-VXZP with X = D, T and Q, the quadruple-zeta set used only for CASSCF and second-order perturbation theory; correlation-consistent cc-pVXZ sets for the single-reference methods
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals, the pi valence system of the conjugated chain.
active_space_protocol: One fixed space averaged over three states, held constant while the order of the perturbation treatment is varied, so that differences between second and third order are attributable to the perturbation rather than to the reference. Excitation energies used the single-state second-order protocol with the shifted zeroth-order Hamiltonian unless stated, with the unshifted variant checked separately.
nroots_per_mult: three states in the averaged reference
electronic_structure_description: Of all the methods examined, only third-order perturbation theory reproduces the coupled-cluster-based equilibrium ground-state structure nearly perfectly. Second-order excitation energies deviate from the third-order reference by up to 0.16 eV for the transition to the first excited state but only up to 0.06 eV for the transition to the second. Third-order excitation energies are practically independent of the shift parameter in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian, whereas second-order energies are affected by it dramatically and non-systematically. Ground-state structures optimized with and without that parameter differ in bond lengths by no more than 0.001 Angstrom.
Other: This paper settles, on one fixed space, where the notorious sensitivity to the zeroth-order Hamiltonian shift actually lives -- and the answer is that it is an artifact of second order rather than a property of the reference. The space is the minimal pi system, six electrons in six orbitals averaged over three states, held constant while the perturbation order is varied. Second-order excitation energies are stated to be affected dramatically and non-systematically by the shift parameter, while third-order energies practically do not depend on it at all. Non-systematically is the important word: a systematic offset can be absorbed or calibrated away, whereas a shift that moves different states by different amounts cannot, and it is precisely that behaviour that has made the parameter contentious in retinal spectroscopy. Going one order higher removes the ambiguity without touching the space, which relocates the problem from the reference wave function to the truncation of the perturbation series. Elsewhere in this queue the same parameter was shown to produce a uniform 0.3 to 0.4 eV offset on a different system with a full pi space; here the offset is not uniform, and the difference between those two behaviours is itself worth recording. The residual second-order error is quantified against the higher-order reference and is strongly state-dependent: up to 0.16 eV for the first excitation but only up to 0.06 eV for the second. A method that is two and a half times less accurate for the lower state than the upper one is not simply imprecise, it is unbalanced, and any energy gap between those two states inherits the full 0.16 eV. The geometry result runs the same way. Of every method examined, only the third-order treatment reproduces the coupled-cluster equilibrium structure nearly perfectly, so the same space gives an inadequate geometry at second order and an excellent one at third. Two control experiments are worth carrying because they isolate what does not matter. Structures optimized with and without the shift parameter differ in bond lengths by no more than 0.001 Angstrom, so the parameter that dramatically affects excitation energies has essentially no effect on geometry -- energetics and structure respond to it quite differently. And the third-order optimization was run with neither the frozen core approximation nor the shift, so the benchmark geometry carries none of the approximations under test. An imaginary shift of 0.1 hartree guards against intruder states throughout, and basis sets are pushed to quadruple zeta so that the comparison between perturbation orders is not confounded by basis incompleteness.
reference_short: Grabarek, Walczak & Andruniow, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2016, 12, 2346
notes: The authors state these are the first third-order perturbation theory ground-state geometries reported for this retinal model. The model is a significantly truncated stand-in for the full chromophore, so the conclusions concern the method rather than retinal photochemistry directly.
correlation_correction: Second-order and third-order complete active space perturbation theory on the same reference, with multireference configuration interaction plus Davidson and Pople corrections as a further check; the third-order treatment is the benchmark against which the second-order one is assessed

compound_name: 4,6-Dimethylidenebicyclo[3.1.0]hex-2-ene derivative with X = O and Y = CH2, ring opening to an aromatic reactive intermediate
point_group: C1 imposed for the reaction coordinate calculations; the intermediates are planar with A-prime states
geometry_source: Intrinsic reaction coordinates and stationary points optimized at the CASSCF level under C1 symmetry, with triplet wave functions evaluated at singlet-optimized geometries to locate crossings
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and intrinsic reaction coordinate following under no symmetry constraint, with harmonic frequencies at all stationary points and spin-orbit couplings computed at the same level; singlet-triplet crossing points located by finding where the two states become isoenergetic to within 0.25 kJ/mol, with triplet wave functions evaluated at singlet-optimized geometries. Density functional calculations were used for the wider survey of nine derivatives
basis_set: 6-31G(d), described by the authors as an inexpensive basis chosen to survey the reactions qualitatively
soc_included: yes, computed at the CASSCF level, a treatment reported to carry errors of about 30 percent
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals. At the reactant these are all six pi and pi* orbitals together with the sigma and sigma* pair of the rupturing carbon-carbon bond; on ring opening that sigma pair becomes pi in character, so the intermediate is described by eight pi and pi* orbitals. A ten-electron nine-orbital variant adding the in-plane oxygen lone pair was used to test the symmetry of the triplet state.
active_space_protocol: The space is constructed so that its composition transforms continuously as the bond breaks, the sigma pair of the rupturing bond becoming pi orbitals of the ring-opened intermediate. Separately, it was enlarged by the in-plane oxygen lone pair specifically to make an alternative triplet symmetry representable, so that the state assignment could be tested rather than assumed.
electronic_structure_description: Ring opening proceeds on the singlet surface to a diradical intermediate predicted to have a triplet ground state, so a singlet-triplet crossing must occur. The triplet states of the transition states lie above the singlets, placing the crossing after the transition state. At the crossing point the rupturing carbon-carbon distance is 2.31 Angstrom, well inside the 5 Angstrom range within which spin-orbit coupling is expected to be the primary intersystem crossing mechanism, and the computed coupling is 1.4 wavenumbers. Both the singlet and triplet intermediates are of A-prime symmetry; adding the in-plane oxygen lone pair to the space to allow an A-double-prime triplet confirmed that the A-prime state is lower. The estimated transmission probability between the two states is about 3.6 times ten to the minus five.
Other: Two things here are worth separating. First, the eight-electron eight-orbital space changes composition along the reaction coordinate in a way that is not a choice but a consequence: at the reactant it comprises all six pi and pi* orbitals plus the sigma and sigma* pair of the carbon-carbon bond that ruptures, and ring opening converts that sigma pair into pi character so the intermediate is described by eight pi and pi* orbitals. The count is constant and the orbitals are continuously connected -- the same two orbitals simply change character as the bond breaks. This is the benign version of composition change along a path, in contrast to cases where a space is deliberately rebuilt at different points and the energies stop being comparable. Including the sigma pair of the breaking bond at the reactant is what makes that continuity possible. Second, and more unusual, the space is enlarged for a targeted purpose that has nothing to do with converging an energy. Both the singlet and triplet intermediates come out with A-prime symmetry, and to rule out the possibility that the triplet is really A-double-prime, the in-plane oxygen lone pair was added to give a ten-electron nine-orbital space specifically so that the alternative state could be represented. The A-prime state remained lower. Enlarging a space to make a competing state accessible, rather than to improve a number, is the right use of an enlargement when the question is one of state identity: a space that cannot represent the alternative cannot rule it out, and no amount of energy convergence in the original space would have settled it. The spin-orbit couplings that the mechanism depends on are small and honestly bounded. They come out at 1.4 and 1.1 wavenumbers for the two crossing points, and the authors note the method is reported to carry errors of about 30 percent, put the values in context by citing a threshold of 0.1 wavenumbers above which organic diradical couplings might be considered large and a comparison value of 4.76 from other work, and then compute a transmission probability of about 3.6 times ten to the minus five. Reporting a coupling, its method error, a literature scale and the resulting probability is a complete account, and the conclusion it supports is negative -- the crossing is possible but improbable. The crossing points themselves are located by a numerical criterion rather than optimized, taking the geometry where singlet and triplet are isoenergetic to within 0.25 kJ/mol at this level, with triplet wave functions evaluated at singlet-optimized geometries along the reaction coordinate. Occupation numbers are taken from the diagonal of the final one-electron density matrix, and the whole survey uses a small split-valence polarized basis, described by the authors as qualitative.
reference_short: Stumetz, Nadeau & Cremeens, J. Org. Chem. 2013, 78, 10878
notes: A coupling of 1.4 wavenumbers is well above the 0.1 wavenumber scale at which organic diradical couplings are considered large, and comparable to a value of 4.76 reported for a different ring-opening crossing, yet the transmission probability remains very small -- so the coupling magnitude alone does not decide whether the nonadiabatic channel is viable.
correlation_correction: None applied to the CASSCF results; occupation numbers were taken from the diagonal of the final one-electron density matrix

Other: The active space is used purely to put a number on diradical character, and the interesting content is how that number is cross-checked. A ten-electron ten-orbital space with a mixed basis supplies natural orbital occupation numbers for the lowest unoccupied orbital, which are read directly as the percentage diradical character. electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A1g. Other: The space here is chosen to make two molecules comparable rather than to converge either one, and the authors state that criterion explicitly: to treat benzene and square cyclobutadiene at very much the same qualitatively correct level of theory, both are described by pi-space complete active spaces, six electrons in six orbitals for the aromatic ring and four in four for the antiaromatic one. electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies to the first three excited singlets in eV: 3.64, 3.99 and 5.22 with the mixed basis and 3.48, 3.76 and 5.02 with the full polarized basis at the reference level; 3.07, 3.80 and 4.31 after the multireference perturbative correction; and 3.13, absent, and 4.10 from equation-of-motion coupled cluster with the mixed basis, or 2.95, absent and 3.99 with the full basis. The measured values are 2.74 and 3.44 eV from ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, with alternative determinations of 2.68 and 3.98. The second excited state is doubly excited and cannot be produced by the coupled cluster treatment at all. The photoisomerization proceeds from the third excited state rather than the first.

electronic_structure_description: The single-reference description gives a dominant d8 ground-state configuration with fifty doubly occupied orbitals of one symmetry and forty-five of the other. With an approximately square-planar metal and a d8 count, crystal field arguments leave one d orbital empty. However, the electronic ground state is stated to consist of two dominating configurations, so the reference itself carries multireference character. The measured absorption features span 2.07 to 2.95 eV, with additional features between 2.95 and 3.18 eV, a further band to 3.54 eV and a delta band near 3.76 to 4.13 eV. The lowest energy band is associated with multiple metal-to-ligand charge transfer excitations, and both metal d and corrin pi localized transitions contribute.
Other: The space is built on two explicit design principles and then, unusually, the authors enumerate exactly why it may still be insufficient. Ten electrons in eleven orbitals, of which the metal d manifold is represented twice over -- six orbitals of one symmetry and four of the other carrying d character, included specifically to capture the double shell effect -- plus one extra corrin orbital taken as the lowest unoccupied linear combination of the ring pi orbitals. Pairing each occupied d orbital with a correlating partner is the standard prescription for a transition metal, and adding a single ligand acceptor orbital is what makes metal-to-ligand charge transfer describable at all; a space of only d orbitals could not represent the excitations the spectra are being assigned to. A coordinate-frame subtlety is documented that would otherwise silently break comparison with the literature: the reference frame here is rotated 45 degrees relative to earlier work, which exchanges one unoccupied d orbital label for another, so the same physical space carries different orbital names between studies. Anyone matching orbital labels across papers on this system would be misled without that note. The limitations are stated as a list rather than a hedge, and it is the most useful part of the paper for this database. Their conclusion is correspondingly bounded: the approach is described as reliable for a limited number of low-lying excitations and was used on that basis to validate the cheaper method, not to assign the spectrum outright. Twenty excited states were computed, so the states beyond the lowest few are being reported under a caveat the authors themselves supply. The deeper difficulty is that the ground state itself is not single-configurational: it is stated to consist of two dominating configurations, so the reference against which all excitations are measured carries multireference character before any excitation is considered. That compounds rather than merely accompanies the excited-state problem. Two structural models were built, a 140-atom full structure retaining the corrin side chains and a 45-atom simplification replacing them with hydrogens, and the paper's own framing is that using the full structure rather than a simplified model is what sheds new light -- so model truncation is treated as a variable on the same footing as the electronic structure method.

For the triatomic species that prescription yields seven active orbitals holding seven valence electrons. Defining a space by which atomic shells participate, and stating separately which core shells are relaxed but not correlated, means the same rule can be applied unambiguously to both the nitrogen and phosphorus analogues even though their core structures differ -- one freezes a single shell, the other three. The paper also documents something rarely reported: how the configuration count varies with the symmetry of the state being computed. geometry_source: Stationary points and two minimum-energy conical intersections optimized at the state-averaged CASSCF level; the two lowest-state equilibrium geometries additionally reoptimized at the perturbatively corrected level for comparison
method: Four-state averaged CASSCF for stationary points, conical intersections, energy gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors, with multistate second-order perturbation theory on the same reference for single-point energies and for reoptimizing the two lowest-state equilibrium geometries; ab initio multiple spawning nonadiabatic dynamics run on the CASSCF surface with an intruder-state level shift of 0.2 hartree in the perturbative step and the carbon and oxygen 1s orbitals frozen there
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in nine orbitals: the conjugated pi and pi* orbitals, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the carbon-carbon bonds, and the non-bonding orbital on oxygen.
active_space_protocol: Averaged over four states, because the mechanism proceeds through two distinct conical intersections and the states must be balanced across both. The same space supplies energy gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors for on-the-fly dynamics, not only stationary point energies.

electronic_structure_description: The molecule contains conjugated carbon-carbon and carbon-oxygen double bonds and exhibits aromatic character through their conjugation. Two minimum-energy conical intersections were located. The fitted excited-state lifetime is 125 femtoseconds with a pure exponential decay of the excited-state population. The dominant pathway is sequential: the first carbon-carbon bond breaks on the excited surface and the second breaks on the ground surface after internal conversion through the first intersection region. A minor channel through the second intersection proceeds by asynchronous concerted decarbonylation. The nonadiabatic transition is found to occur within a small energy gap, and high-energy conical intersection regions play an important role.
Other: The space is composed of exactly the orbitals the two competing mechanisms require, and the composition is what makes the mechanistic distinction computable at all: the conjugated pi and pi* orbitals, the sigma and sigma* orbitals of the carbon-carbon bonds, and the non-bonding orbital on oxygen, giving ten electrons in nine orbitals. Since the question is whether decarbonylation is sequential or concerted -- whether the two ring bonds break on different surfaces or together -- both carbon-carbon sigma systems must be in the space simultaneously. A space containing only one of them could not represent the asynchronous concerted pathway, and one containing neither could not represent either. Four-state averaging is likewise dictated by the problem rather than chosen for convergence, since the mechanism runs through two distinct conical intersections and the states must be balanced across both. The demanding part is that this same space is used not merely for stationary points but to supply energy gradients and nonadiabatic coupling vectors for on-the-fly dynamics. That is a far stronger requirement than getting energies right: gradients are first derivatives and coupling vectors are off-diagonal derivative quantities, so the space must describe how the wave function changes with geometry, continuously, over every configuration the trajectories visit rather than at a handful of optimized structures. The resulting simulation yields a fitted excited-state lifetime of 125 femtoseconds, a number that depends on the whole surface rather than on any single point. A specific finding sharpens what the space has to cover: the nonadiabatic transition is found to occur within a small energy gap, and high-energy conical intersection regions are reported to play an important role. Trajectories therefore sample intersection geometries well away from the optimized minimum-energy crossings, so a space validated only at those two located structures would not be sufficient -- the seam matters, not just its lowest points. The correlation treatment is applied consistently rather than only to final energies: multistate perturbation theory on the same reference supplies the single-point energies, and the two lowest-state equilibrium geometries were additionally reoptimized at that corrected level for comparison, so the geometry error of the uncorrected space can be assessed rather than assumed. An intruder-state level shift of 0.2 hartree is applied and the carbon and oxygen 1s orbitals are frozen in the correction. Three basis sets spanning added polarization on heavy atoms and on hydrogen were used, so basis effects are separable from space effects. The limitation to note is that the dynamics runs on the uncorrected surface -- the perturbative treatment enters as single points and reoptimized minima, not as the surface the trajectories move on -- so the 125 femtosecond lifetime carries whatever error the bare space makes in the barrier and gap topography.

active_space_protocol: Contains both bonds that can break at this stage. A reduced six-electron six-orbital space limited to the ring pi system was used instead when locating the singlet-triplet crossing point, because of the memory demands of that search -- so the carbon-chlorine sigma pair is absent from the crossing calculation.
electronic_structure_description: The lowest excited singlet states lie about 100 to 110 kcal/mol above the ground state, with the carbon-chlorine bond length almost unchanged from the ground state, decreasing by only 0.01 Angstrom. The lowest triplet states lie about 66 to 68 kcal/mol above the ground state and are characterized by a distorted carbon skeleton in which one ring carbon sticks out of the molecular plane, with the carbon-chlorine bond stretched to 1.82 Angstrom and negative charge developing on the chlorine. Two triplet conformers are close in energy, one slightly more stable than the other. Stretching the carbon-chlorine bond by about 1 Angstrom on the triplet surface, to about 2.6 Angstrom, costs only about 14 kcal/mol, whereas stretching it by about 0.5 Angstrom on either the ground or excited singlet surface costs about 29 kcal/mol with no dissociation following.

The aryl chloride reactants get ten electrons in ten orbitals -- three pi and three pi* of the ring plus the sigma and sigma* pairs of both the carbon-chlorine and the carbon-silicon bonds. The phenyl cations get eight in nine -- the same ring pi system, the carbon-silicon sigma pair, and the orbital at the dicoordinated carbon, the chlorine orbitals having left with the chloride. The didehydrotoluene products get eight in eight -- the ring pi system plus the orbital at the benzylic position and the one at the dicoordinated carbon. Each space contains the bond being broken or the radical centre being formed at that stage and nothing that has already departed, which is principled: an orbital pair that no longer exists cannot be kept, and one that is about to break must be present. active_space_orbital_description: Sixteen electrons in eleven orbitals covering all valence orbitals: the eight pi electrons together with the lone pair of the amino substituent and both oxygen lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: The larger space is used for geometry optimization and the reduced one for the perturbative energies. The reduction is justified four ways: the excitation from the removed lone pair lies above the states of interest, the correction becomes cheaper, the result becomes comparable with the group's earlier work on the parent nucleobase, and orbital switching during the optimization step is avoided. The basis set changes at the same step, so space and basis differ between geometry and energy simultaneously.

electronic_structure_description: Its lowest energy absorption band is considerably red-shifted, noticeably less intense and broader than that of the parent nucleobase. Its emission shows a much larger Stokes shift than the parent, and its emission band is much narrower than that of the 6-substituted isomer. Two ground state minima were located, one with the amino group almost coplanar with the ring and another with the substituent rotated nearly perpendicular to it. Dynamic correlation has a large effect on the pi-pi* state energetics and almost none on the n-pi* state, making the corrected n-pi* value the more reliable of the two.
Other: The space is reduced between the geometry step and the energy step, and the reduction is justified with three reasons of quite different kinds, which is worth separating. The full space of sixteen electrons in eleven orbitals covers all valence orbitals -- eight pi electrons plus the amino lone pair and both oxygen lone pairs -- and is used for optimizing the ground state and the two lowest excited state minima. One oxygen lone pair is then removed for the perturbative single points, giving fourteen electrons in ten orbitals. The first reason is physical: the excitation out of that lone pair lies higher in energy than the states of interest, as the reference calculations themselves showed, so the orbital is not needed for the states being described. The second is economic, reducing the cost of the correction. The third is neither -- it is comparability with the group's own earlier work on the parent nucleobase, a literature consideration rather than a property of this system. The fourth reason given is the most practical and the least often written down: removing that orbital avoids problems of orbital switching during the optimization step. An orbital that keeps exchanging places with one outside the space makes an optimization unstable regardless of whether it belongs there on physical grounds, and dropping it for that reason alone is a legitimate move that most papers would leave unstated. The paper then reports a state-dependent reliability that follows directly from the space composition. Dynamic correlation is found to have a quite large effect on the energetics of the pi-pi* states but an almost negligible effect on the n-pi* state, from which the authors conclude the corrected value is much more reliable for the n-pi* state than for the other two. That is an unusually candid statement of differential accuracy within a single calculation, and it inverts the usual assumption that a correction improves everything uniformly: here the state that needs the correction least is the one whose corrected value can be trusted most. Two further design points. The oscillator strengths are computed not from the reference wave functions but from perturbatively modified ones supplied by the correction module, so intensities and energies come from the same corrected description rather than intensities from the uncorrected one. And a basis change accompanies the space change -- a split-valence polarized set for the geometries and an atomic natural orbital set for the energies -- so the two steps differ in both space and basis simultaneously. The standard shifted zeroth-order Hamiltonian was used with an imaginary level shift of 0.2, chosen in agreement with the group's earlier uracil work rather than tested here.

electronic_structure_description: The two lowest pi-pi* excited states, conventionally labelled 1La and 1Lb, are close in energy and their order is environment-dependent: the 1Lb state lies lower for indole in the gas phase and in apolar solvents, with an inversion in polar solvents. Twenty density functionals, including double hybrids and the Minnesota family, all failed to describe these two transitions satisfactorily, giving the wrong state order and/or the wrong gap. The perturbatively corrected multiconfigurational treatment and an independent cluster expansion method both give reliable transition energies and the correct ordering.
Other: The case for the active space here is made by exhaustion rather than by assertion: twenty different density functionals were tested, including perturbatively corrected double hybrids and the Minnesota family, and all of them failed to describe the two key transitions satisfactorily. Testing twenty functionals and reporting that every one fails is a far stronger argument than the usual comparison against one or two, because it rules out the possibility that a better-chosen functional would have sufficed. The specific failure is diagnosed rather than left as a magnitude: the cheaper method gives the wrong ORDER of the two lowest pi-pi* states and/or the wrong gap between them. Ordering is the quantity the whole study depends on, since the two states invert between apolar and polar environments and the point of the work is how the protein matrix tunes them. A method that misorders them in the gas phase cannot be trusted to track an environment-driven inversion. The space itself is ten electrons in nine orbitals, held fixed across the chromophore model and used with three different basis sets spanning a split-valence polarized set and relativistic atomic natural orbital sets of double and triple zeta quality, so basis convergence can be assessed separately from the space. Three-state averaging is used for the ground-state geometry optimization, which matters because the two excited states are close enough to invert -- optimizing on either one alone would bias the geometry toward it. The independent check is a genuinely different correlated method rather than a variant of the same one: symmetry-adapted cluster configuration interaction, a single-reference approach, agrees with the perturbatively corrected multiconfigurational result on both the transition energies and the state order. Two methods with unrelated failure modes agreeing on an ordering is much better evidence than either alone, and it is what licenses using the ordering to interpret the protein calculations. The scope limit is the familiar one for a QM/MM study of a protein: the multiconfigurational treatment is applied to a 3-methylindole model of the chromophore in the gas phase, while the protein calculations use a layered quantum-classical scheme, so the space validates the method on the isolated chromophore and the environmental conclusions rest on that validation transferring. An imaginary level shift of 0.2 guards against intruder states in the correction.

point_group: C4v optimized geometry; CASSCF performed under C2v
geometry_source: Optimized with the B3PW91 functional in the BS-I basis, with vibrational frequencies confirming minima and transition states; the CASSCF calculations were single points in BS-II on those geometries
method: CASSCF used as a diagnostic of multireference character on species from a reaction path otherwise computed by density functional theory; geometries and frequencies from the hybrid functional, energies re-evaluated in the larger basis
software: MOLCAS 6.0 for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 03 for the density functional work and NBO 3.1 for population analysis
basis_set: BS-II: cc-pVDZ on carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and hydrogen with a Stuttgart-Dresden-Bonn effective core potential and a (311111/22111/411) valence basis on ruthenium
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen orbitals itemized by symmetry block as five a1, three b1, three a2 and three b2, chosen by three stated rules: all ruthenium 4d orbitals, the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them for the double-shell effect, and the four Gouterman porphyrin pi orbitals (two occupied in a1 and b2, two unoccupied in a2 and b1).
active_space_protocol: The same fourteen orbitals are used for every species in the series, with only the electron count changed to follow the charge, so that comparisons between oxidation states cannot be an artifact of a different orbital choice.
electronic_structure_description: The singlet is the ground state, lying 48.4 kcal/mol below the triplet. The leading configuration of the CASSCF wave function carries 85.66% of the weight and assigns ruthenium the +II oxidation state.
Other: The active space here is specified by three stated rules rather than by a number, and the rules are what make the five species comparable. All ruthenium 4d orbitals and their electrons must be in the space; the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them must also be in, to capture the double-shell effect; and the four porphyrin pi orbitals of the classic Gouterman set -- two occupied, in the totally symmetric and one of the antisymmetric blocks, and two unoccupied -- must be in. That gives fourteen orbitals, itemized by symmetry block as five, three, three and three, and the SAME fourteen orbitals are used for the neutral singlet, the neutral triplet, the cation and the anion, with only the electron count changing to follow the charge: fourteen, fourteen, thirteen and fifteen. Holding the orbital set fixed while the electron count tracks the charge is exactly the design needed to compare oxidation states, since any difference between species then cannot be blamed on a different choice of orbitals. Only for the oxo anion is the set enlarged, by one further orbital added specifically to represent the ruthenium-oxygen antibonding interaction -- an enlargement made because a specific bond is being broken, not to recover more correlation. The space is used as a DIAGNOSTIC rather than as a source of energetics. The reported result is that the leading configuration carries more than 85% of the weight in every one of the five species (85.66, 89.40, 88.80, 88.02 and 85.65 percent), from which the authors conclude static correlation is small and a single-determinant method is adequate; they further check that the natural orbitals from the unrestricted density functional calculation are essentially the same as the multiconfigurational ones. Two independent checks pointing the same way is a stronger licence for the cheaper method than either alone. The second finding is chemical and cuts against the experimental proposal that motivated the calculation: the leading configuration assigns ruthenium the +II oxidation state in ALL five species, including the cation and both anions, so the experimentally proposed +I-to-+III change is not what the wave function shows -- the added or removed electron sits on the porphyrin ring, not on the metal. The scope limit is that these are CASSCF wave functions with no perturbative correction, so the weights speak to static correlation only, and a fourteen-orbital space concentrated on the metal d shell and the Gouterman four cannot report multireference character arising anywhere outside it. The calculations were run in the smaller correlation-consistent basis under C2v symmetry even for the species whose optimized geometry is C4v.

notes: The sentence stating the active spaces lists four electron counts (14, 14, 13, 15) against five species labels; the mapping recorded here follows the charges and the following sentence, which states separately that the oxo anion has fifteen electrons in the fourteen orbitals plus one more.
correlation_correction: None; the CASSCF wave function is used to measure the weight of the leading configuration, not to produce correlated energies

method: GVVPT2, a second-order multistate multireference perturbation theory that admits incomplete active spaces and rigorously avoids intruder states, applied on two different orbital sets in the same space: orbitals from a converged CASSCF, and orbitals from a local-density Kohn-Sham calculation followed by a CASCI and quasi-canonicalization of the average Fock matrix. Compared against published full configuration interaction and, for dinitrogen, against MRCISD in the same space

active_space_protocol: The oxygen 1s-dominated orbital is held doubly occupied when the model space is constructed but is given variable occupancy in the perturbative step, so the reference is frozen-core while the correlation treatment is not.
nroots_per_mult: one, the ground state
electronic_structure_description: A standard test of the balance between static and dynamic correlation, because the two vary in opposite directions along the coordinate: near equilibrium the wave function is heavily dominated by a single determinant while the dynamic correlation is large, and at long bond length the wave function becomes profoundly multiconfigurational while the dynamic correlation falls. Against full configuration interaction the nonparallelity error is 6.0 millihartree with CASSCF orbitals and 3.7 millihartree with density functional orbitals; neither curve shows sharp or irregular features.
Other: This paper isolates a variable that is usually invisible: not the SIZE of the active space but the source of the ORBITALS that span it. The space is held identical between two calculations -- the same valence orbital set, the same symmetry-restricted model space -- and only the orbitals change, coming either from a converged CASSCF or from a plain local-density Kohn-Sham calculation followed by a CASCI and a quasi-canonicalization of the average Fock matrix. Because the space is fixed, any difference in the final energies is attributable to orbital optimization alone, which is a much cleaner experiment than the usual comparison of differently sized spaces. The spaces themselves are defined by SHELL rather than by count: the orbitals kept are those dominated by the atomic valence subshells, so for dinitrogen the nitrogen 2s and 2p subshells generate four totally symmetric orbitals and two of each of the two remaining blocks of the abelian subgroup used. The authors immediately warn that this is not general -- the ordering reverses for dinitrogen in a larger basis -- which is the right way to report a favourable result whose mechanism is not understood. The most demanding test is dicarbon, where ground-state density functional orbitals alone are used to build the model space and the method must still describe two excited states that undergo an avoided crossing and two real crossings within a narrow range of bond length; the nonparallelity errors are 8, 8 and 3 millihartree for the ground and two excited states. Getting excited states from ground-state orbitals is the strongest form of this claim, because it means the orbital set is not tuned to any one state. A deliberate subtlety in the model space construction: the core orbital is held doubly occupied when the model space is built but is allowed variable occupancy in the perturbative step, so the reference is frozen-core while the correlation treatment is not. The stated scope limits are honest and specific: the diffuse functions of the augmented triple-zeta basis did not break the protocol, but the unoccupied density functional orbitals there were still of valence character, and behaviour when those orbitals acquire Rydberg character remains untested. The perturbation theory used here is constructed to tolerate incomplete active spaces and to avoid intruder states rigorously, which is what makes an unoptimized orbital set survivable at all.

compound_name: Small model of the methylcobalamin:homocysteine reactant complex, truncated corrin
ligand_set: corrin macrocycle, a methyl group and a methanethiolate
point_group: Cs, imposed deliberately so that the two sulfur p orbitals could be oriented and treated separately
geometry_source: Optimized with the BP86 functional; the carbon-sulfur distance was varied systematically from 2.6 to 4.6 Angstrom and the geometry fully optimized at each fixed value. Starting coordinates for the full model came from earlier Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics
method: CASSCF followed by multistate CASPT2 with a level shift of 0.3, preceded by a RASSCF calculation at a carbon-sulfur distance of 4.0 Angstrom used to identify which orbitals belong in the space; state-averaged CASSCF over seven states for the ionic wave function and four states for the diradical
basis_set: ANO-L, contracted 6s5p3d1f for cobalt, 5s4p2d for sulfur, 3s2p1d for carbon and nitrogen and 2s for hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in thirteen orbitals: the doubly occupied 3dxz, 3dyz, 3dx2-y2 and the cobalt-carbon sigma orbital, together with a combination of the four nitrogen lone pairs; their correlating partners 4dxz, 4dyz, 4dx2-y2 and the cobalt-carbon sigma antibonding orbital; the unoccupied 3dxy in antibonding combination with the nitrogen lone pairs, which forms a sigma-type donor-acceptor bond between corrin and cobalt; the lowest unoccupied corrin pi antibonding orbital; one sulfur p orbital, doubly occupied for the free thiolate; and the 4dz2 orbital, which is the correlating partner for 3dz2 after cobalt-carbon bond cleavage.
active_space_protocol: Selected by first running a RASSCF calculation at one fixed geometry to identify the important orbitals, then testing several complete-space compositions. The 4d correlating partners for the doubly occupied 3d orbitals, the double-shell effect, were found necessary for a correct description of excited states and molecular properties at the perturbative level. The distribution over symmetry blocks follows the state: eight orbitals in the symmetric block and five in the antisymmetric one for the perpendicular diradical and the ionic wave functions, seven and six for the parallel diradical, because the sulfur p orbital lies perpendicular to the corrin ring in the first two and parallel to it in the third.
nroots_per_mult: seven states for the ionic wave function, four for the diradical
electronic_structure_description: Three wave functions were followed as a function of the carbon-sulfur distance: two diradical states differing in whether the sulfur p orbital is perpendicular or parallel to the corrin ring, and an ionic state. In the diradical states the leading configuration has singly occupied sulfur and corrin pi antibonding orbitals; in the ionic state the sulfur orbitals are doubly occupied. Minor configurations arise mainly from single and double excitations between the cobalt-carbon sigma and sigma antibonding orbitals. Leading configuration weights around 80 percent at 4.2 Angstrom. At the shortest distance studied, 2.6 Angstrom, a weak thiolate-carbon bond forms, particularly in the perpendicular diradical state. At longer distances the diradical is the lowest electronic state, supporting electron-transfer-based reductive cleavage over an SN2 pathway at 4.0 Angstrom.
Other: The active space here was chosen by a stated PROCEDURE rather than by inspection: a restricted active space calculation was run first, at one fixed carbon-sulfur distance, purely to find out which orbitals matter, and only then were complete-space calculations built on that answer and carried along the coordinate. Using a restricted space as a screening tool for a complete one is a genuine method rather than an assertion, and the authors say explicitly that several compositions were tested before settling. Two consequences follow. First, the space is not the same for the two structural models: twelve electrons in thirteen orbitals for the symmetry-constrained truncated model, twelve in eleven for the full corrin model, and the smaller one is not a subset chosen for cost -- the sulfur lone pair of the thiolate has no correlating counterpart available, so an antibonding corrin pi orbital was put in its place. Substituting a chemically unrelated orbital for a missing correlating partner is a compromise worth recording, because it means the two spaces do not measure the same correlation. Second, and more unusual, the space composition CHANGES WITH THE STATE being described rather than being held fixed across states: because the sulfur p orbital is perpendicular to the corrin ring in the perpendicular diradical and ionic wave functions but parallel to it in the parallel diradical wave function, the orbitals fall in different symmetry blocks, giving eight and five orbitals in the two blocks for the first two states and seven and six for the third. This is a symmetry-driven repartition, not a resize, and the plane of symmetry could only be imposed on the truncated model at all -- the authors say the symmetry constraint was the point of building that model, since it lets the two sulfur p orbitals be treated separately rather than as a near-degenerate pair. The double-shell effect is reported as NECESSARY rather than beneficial: 4d correlating partners for each doubly occupied 3d orbital were found required for a correct description of excited states and molecular properties at the perturbative level. The sharpest sensitivity is in the state ORDERING, which the reference and the corrected treatment disagree about: the ionic state sits among the higher excited states at the CASSCF level and moves down under the perturbative correction, and the authors say this disagreement is precisely why a large number of excited states had to be computed -- seven roots for the ionic wave function and four for the diradical. A space that gives the wrong order before correction is only usable if enough roots are carried that the state of interest is still in the calculation when the correction reshuffles them. The two models use different second-order treatments, multistate CASPT2 with a 0.3 level shift for one and extended quasidegenerate perturbation theory for the other, and the agreement of two different corrections on the same qualitative conclusion is the paper's internal check.

The two statements are not reconciled in the text; the ordering is distance-dependent, and the conclusions state only that the diradical is lowest at the longer distances.

active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in eleven orbitals: 3dxz, 3dx2-y2, 3dyz, the cobalt-carbon sigma orbital and the sulfur p orbitals (a lone pair for the free thiolate); the correlating partners are the lowest unoccupied corrin pi antibonding orbital, the cobalt-carbon sigma antibonding orbital, and 4dyz, 4dx2-y2 and 4dxz for the double-shell effect.
active_space_protocol: Chosen using the orbital-selection method established on the truncated model rather than by an independent RASSCF analysis, after testing several possible compositions. One compromise is stated explicitly: the sulfur lone pair of the methanethiolate has no correlating counterpart available, so an unoccupied corrin pi antibonding orbital was selected in its place.
electronic_structure_description: The same three-state picture as in the truncated model. At the longer carbon-sulfur distances the diradical state is the lowest electronic state, and one state is always dominant over the other at any given distance, as shown by the configuration weight percentages; the leading configuration carries 79 percent at 4.2 Angstrom for the parallel diradical. Despite the structural differences between the two models, both give the same conclusion about how the ionic and diradical states are modulated by the carbon-sulfur distance.
Other: The active space here was chosen by a stated PROCEDURE rather than by inspection: a restricted active space calculation was run first, at one fixed carbon-sulfur distance, purely to find out which orbitals matter, and only then were complete-space calculations built on that answer and carried along the coordinate. Using a restricted space as a screening tool for a complete one is a genuine method rather than an assertion, and the authors say explicitly that several compositions were tested before settling. Two consequences follow. First, the space is not the same for the two structural models: twelve electrons in thirteen orbitals for the symmetry-constrained truncated model, twelve in eleven for the full corrin model, and the smaller one is not a subset chosen for cost -- the sulfur lone pair of the thiolate has no correlating counterpart available, so an antibonding corrin pi orbital was put in its place. Substituting a chemically unrelated orbital for a missing correlating partner is a compromise worth recording, because it means the two spaces do not measure the same correlation. Second, and more unusual, the space composition CHANGES WITH THE STATE being described rather than being held fixed across states: because the sulfur p orbital is perpendicular to the corrin ring in the perpendicular diradical and ionic wave functions but parallel to it in the parallel diradical wave function, the orbitals fall in different symmetry blocks, giving eight and five orbitals in the two blocks for the first two states and seven and six for the third. The double-shell effect is reported as NECESSARY rather than beneficial: 4d correlating partners for each doubly occupied 3d orbital were found required for a correct description of excited states and molecular properties at the perturbative level. The sharpest sensitivity is in the state ORDERING, which the reference and the corrected treatment disagree about: the ionic state sits among the higher excited states at the CASSCF level and moves down under the perturbative correction, and the authors say this disagreement is precisely why a large number of excited states had to be computed -- seven roots for the ionic wave function and four for the diradical. A space that gives the wrong order before correction is only usable if enough roots are carried that the state of interest is still in the calculation when the correction reshuffles them. The two models use different second-order treatments, multistate CASPT2 with a 0.3 level shift for one and extended quasidegenerate perturbation theory for the other, and the agreement of two different corrections on the same qualitative conclusion is the paper's internal check.
reference_short: Kumar, Jaworska, Lodowski, Kumar & Kozlowski, J. Phys. Chem. B 2011, 115, 6722
notes: The full corrin model, [Co(corrin)]-Me in contact with methanethiolate, the same model used in earlier density functional work by the group. No symmetry could be imposed on it. The text states in consecutive sentences that the diradical state was the lowest according to both CASSCF and CASPT2, and that the ionic state was found to be the lowest one in the CASPT2 computations while sitting among the higher excited states at CASSCF. The two statements are not reconciled in the text; the ordering is distance-dependent, and the conclusions state only that the diradical is lowest at the longer distances.
correlation_correction: Second-order extended multiconfiguration quasidegenerate perturbation theory on the state-averaged CASSCF reference

compound_name: All-trans retinal protonated Schiff base in bacteriorhodopsin
geometry_source: Structures sampled from ground-state dynamics at 298 K with a layered density functional / force field scheme under electronic embedding, then propagated on the excited state
method: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics on the first excited and ground state surfaces with a layered quantum-mechanics/molecular-mechanics scheme, the quantum region treated by CASSCF and the environment by a classical force field. Ground-state structures were equilibrated and sampled at 298 K by dynamics with a density functional quantum region under electronic embedding; the excited-state dynamics were run in the constant-energy ensemble
software: Not stated in this Letter; the force field is AMBER
active_space_orbital_description: All pi bonds of the retinal protonated Schiff base, giving twelve electrons in twelve orbitals; the quantum region is the chromophore itself.
active_space_protocol: The space is fixed by the rule that the whole pi system is included, so that no double bond is excluded from being able to isomerize. Embedding is switched during the trajectory rather than the space being changed: mechanical embedding while the excited-state gap is large, electronic embedding once it falls below about 35 kcal per mole, because electronic embedding misorders the covalent and ionic excited states in the Franck-Condon region.
electronic_structure_description: Photoisomerization follows a two-state, two-mode mechanism between the ionic Bu-like first excited state and the ground state, with the covalent Ag-like second excited state occasionally mixing in just after excitation in a few trajectories. Decay is exclusively by torsion about one bond, the C13=C14, giving the 13-cis product with a quantum yield of 0.69 to 0.86, in good agreement with the measured 0.6 to 0.7. The mean excited-state lifetime is 114 to 162 femtoseconds, ranging from 75 to 334 femtoseconds, shorter than the experimental value above 200 femtoseconds, which the authors attribute partly to the over-repulsive CASSCF potential. The rotation is always unidirectional. At the crossings the largest twist involves a hydrogen atom, about 81 degrees, and the decay proceeds by an asynchronous crankshaft motion of the C13-C14-C15-N moiety that saves space in the confined protein cavity.
Other: The space is defined by a chemical rule rather than by a count -- ALL pi bonds of the chromophore -- which for this retinal Schiff base gives twelve electrons in twelve orbitals, and the authors state this is the first nonadiabatic dynamics with the complete pi system as the quantum region in this protein. Including all of it matters because the isomerization can in principle happen at several of the double bonds, and a space covering only some of them would prejudge which ones are available. The sensitivity reported here is not about the size of the space but about how the space interacts with the EMBEDDING, which is unusual and worth recording. With electronic embedding, the CASSCF wave function in this space gives the WRONG ORDER of the covalent Ag-like second excited state and the ionic Bu-like first excited state in the Franck-Condon and fluorescent regions -- the environment's electrostatic field differentially stabilizes an ionic state that CASSCF already misplaces, and the two errors compound. The authors say plainly that the proper fix is multistate second-order perturbation theory or multireference configuration interaction and that both are computationally unaffordable for hundreds of trajectories. Their workaround is procedural rather than a change of space: mechanical embedding first, switching to electronic embedding only once the gap to the ground state has fallen below about 35 kcal per mole, i.e. once the trajectory has left the region where the ordering error occurs. Crucially they CHECK the workaround instead of asserting it, reporting that the time to reach the crossing region is similar whether mechanical embedding is used throughout the excited state or the switch is made. The second scope limit is stated equally plainly: CASSCF potentials are over-repulsive, and the computed excited-state lifetime in the protein, 114 to 162 femtoseconds, is accordingly shorter than the experimental value above 200 femtoseconds. What the space does get right is the branching -- the photoisomerization quantum yield of 0.69 to 0.86 in the protein agrees with the measured 0.6 to 0.7, and the much smaller yield in solution is reproduced qualitatively. So this space is fit for topology and product branching but not for timing, which is exactly the distinction a reader needs. A residual state-mixing effect survives the workaround: the covalent second excited state occasionally mixes with the ionic first excited state just after excitation, in a few trajectories, where the gap between them computed at the perturbatively corrected level with mechanical embedding is only about 1 to 8 kcal per mole. Elsewhere that gap oscillates around 20 kcal per mole, so the two-state two-mode picture holds for most of the dynamics but not universally.
reference_short: Li, Chung & Morokuma, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2011, 7, 2694
notes: The chromophore is sandwiched by Trp86, Thr90, Met118, Ile119, Trp182 and Tyr185 except at the C14-C15-N part, which suppresses rotation about the other bonds; a close contact between the C14 hydrogen and Trp86 pretwists the C13=C14 bond in the ground state, fixing the direction of rotation.
correlation_correction: None in the dynamics; the ordering problem it would fix is acknowledged and worked around procedurally, and a perturbatively corrected gap between the two excited states is quoted for the mixing analysis

compound_name: M1, a five-double-bond model of the 11-cis retinal protonated Schiff base, in vacuum
geometry_source: Optimized at state-averaged CASSCF; conical intersections located with a quasi-Newton method using a BFGS-updated approximate Hessian. Perturbative energies were recalculated at these geometries because analytical gradients for the correction are not available in the program used
method: State-averaged CASSCF over the first three roots with equal weights, with dynamic correlation added by second-order perturbation theory as single points on the CASSCF geometries, and multistate perturbation theory at the minimum-energy conical intersection. The solvent is treated by an averaged solvent electrostatic potential taken from molecular dynamics, in an extended form that allows crossing points between free energy surfaces to be located under both equilibrium and frozen-solvent conditions
software: A development version of the ASEP/MD program using data from Gaussian 98 and Moldy; dynamic correlation corrections computed with MOLCAS 6.4
active_space_orbital_description: All electrons of the pi skeleton: ten valence pi electrons in ten orbitals, with all configurations arising from them included.
active_space_protocol: State-averaged over the first three roots with equal weights. The number of states that must be included is set by the environment rather than by the molecule: two states appear sufficient in the gas phase, three are necessary in methanol because the first and second excited states become almost degenerate at the Franck-Condon point.
nroots_per_mult: three, averaged with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: In the gas phase only two states appear to be implicated in the photoisomerization, and the two low-lying excited states are well separated, matching the experimental absorption behaviour of the real chromophore. Several ionic minima differing by less than 1 kcal/mol were located on the first excited state, and several planar minima on the covalent excited surface. Evolution toward the conical intersection is practically barrierless, and de-excitation proceeds mainly nonradiatively through it. The optimized conical intersection has a torsion of about 90 degrees about the central double bond.
Other: The space is the whole pi skeleton -- all ten valence pi electrons in ten orbitals, with every configuration arising from them included -- so its size is fixed by the molecule rather than chosen. What is chosen, and what turns out to matter, is the NUMBER OF STATES averaged over, and the striking finding is that the required number is set by the ENVIRONMENT rather than by the molecule: in the gas phase only two states appear to be implicated in the photoisomerization, while in methanol three are necessary, because the first and second excited states become almost degenerate at the Franck-Condon point in solution. A protocol tuned on the isolated molecule would therefore have been wrong in solution, and not because the space was too small -- the space is already complete over the pi system. The consequence is that a single adiabatic surface carries two different characters: one region of the first excited state is ionic and another is covalent, and the two emit at different frequencies, which is how the paper explains the shape of the fluorescence band as double fluorescence from two minima on one surface. An even sharper sensitivity is reported that has nothing to do with the orbital space at all: at the geometry of the ionic minimum the covalent state lies 15.7 kcal per mole above the ionic one when the solvent is equilibrated to the ionic charge distribution, and the ORDER REVERSES when the same two energies are recomputed at the same geometry with the solvent equilibrated to the covalent charge distribution. The same reversal happens at the covalent minimum. So the state ordering is a function of what the environment is equilibrated to, and solvent fluctuations alone are enough to cross the two states; the authors use this to suggest population can transfer back and forth between them, explaining the several emission times seen experimentally. Two limitations are stated explicitly rather than buried. First, analytical gradients for the perturbative correction are unavailable in the program used, so every geometry is a CASSCF geometry and the correction is applied only as a single point on top -- the conclusions section names this as one reason further work is needed. Second, the perturbative correction was run with NO ionization-potential/electron-affinity shift, a deliberate choice made for consistency with the group's earlier calculations in older versions of the program rather than because zero is thought better; an imaginary shift of 0.1 hartree was added to suppress intruder states. Recording that the shift was set to zero for backward compatibility is exactly the kind of detail that determines whether two studies' excitation energies can be compared. All minima were confirmed by analytical Hessians, with the solvent frozen during the solute vibration for the solution minima.
reference_short: Munoz-Losa, Martin, Fdez. Galvan, Sanchez & Aguilar, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2011, 7, 4050
notes: The model was validated in earlier work as adequate for the photophysics of the real molecule because it reproduces the key experimental feature: two well separated excited states in vacuum that become almost degenerate in methanol.
correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points on the CASSCF geometries, and multistate CASPT2 at the minimum-energy conical intersection, with no ionization-potential/electron-affinity shift (chosen for consistency with the group's earlier work in older program versions) and an imaginary shift of 0.1 hartree to suppress intruder states

ligand_set: two 1,2,3,4-tetraisopropylcyclopentadienyl ligands and two bridging hydrides
point_group: The orbitals and states are labelled in D2h
geometry_source: Not stated in the main text; a crystal structure of the complex is reported and the nickel-nickel distance is 2.28 Angstrom
method: CASSCF followed by CASPT2, alongside density functional theory
software: Not stated in the main text
basis_set: Not stated in the main text
active_space_orbital_description: The size and composition of the space are not stated in the main text. Four frontier orbitals are named and discussed: 1b3u, a nickel-nickel pi bonding orbital; 1b2g and 1b3g, the quasi-degenerate nickel-nickel pi antibonding orbitals that hold the unpaired electrons; and 2b2u, the antibonding orbital of the dinickel dihydride core, which would have nickel-nickel pi bonding character if the hydrides were absent and which the hydride interaction raises about 1000 reciprocal centimetres above 1b3u.
active_space_protocol: Not stated in the main text. The occupation numbers quoted for the four named frontier orbitals sum to 4.14, so those orbitals are a subset of a larger space.
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is a 3B1g triplet, an unexpected intermediate spin state for a dinickel dihydride, arising from half occupation of the two quasi-degenerate nickel-nickel pi antibonding orbitals, which are split by only 57 reciprocal centimetres (82 kelvin). At the CASSCF/CASPT2 level the ground state wave function is 70% the configuration with 1b3u doubly occupied and 1b2g and 1b3g singly occupied, plus 12% of the configuration with 1b3u and 1b2g singly occupied and 1b3g doubly occupied, giving occupation numbers of 1.80, 1.17, 0.91 and 0.26 for 1b3u, 1b2g, 1b3g and 2b2u. The corresponding 1Ag singlet lies only 900 reciprocal centimetres above the ground state and is more strongly multireference: 48%, 16% and 8% for its three largest configurations, with occupation numbers 1.36, 0.71, 1.49 and 0.53. A Mulliken spin density analysis of the triplet puts 0.98 electrons on each nickel, so the spin is shared equally between the two metals. There is a net half pi bonding interaction in one plane counterbalanced by half pi antibonding in the other.
Other: Here the multiconfigurational character is the RESULT rather than an obstacle, and the paper is unusual in that the wave function composition is what explains a magnetic measurement. Four frontier orbitals are named and their occupations reported to two decimal places: a nickel-nickel pi bonding orbital at 1.80, the two quasi-degenerate pi antibonding orbitals that carry the unpaired electrons at 1.17 and 0.91, and the core antibonding orbital at 0.26. None of these is close to an integer, which is the direct evidence of significant static correlation among exactly those four orbitals, and it agrees with the near-degeneracy that the density functional calculation independently shows. The leading configuration of the triplet carries only 70 percent of the weight with a second configuration at 12 percent, so a single-determinant description of this ground state would be qualitatively wrong, not merely imprecise. active_space_protocol: Chosen as an explicit compromise: the authors state that a larger space would usually be more accurate but is unaffordable for on-the-fly nonadiabatic dynamics, and that the nonadiabatic coupling vector cannot be computed in the program used once the space becomes large. compound_name: Fulvene, the parent of the isobenzofulvene series
geometry_source: Optimized with the unrestricted or restricted B3LYP functional in the 6-31G(d) basis; all multiconfigurational calculations are single points on those geometries
method: Full pi-space CASSCF followed by CASPT2, and the analogous full pi-space RASSCF followed by RASPT2, on density functional geometries
software: MOLCAS 7.4 for the multiconfigurational calculations; Gaussian 03 and Gaussian 09 for the density functional work; Molden 4.8 for orbital plots
basis_set: 6-31G(d); the smallest member of the isobenzofulvene series was also checked with cc-pVTZ and with an ANO-L set contracted to 4s3p2d1f for carbon and 3s2p1d for hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: The complete pi system: 6 pi electrons in 6 pi orbitals. In the restricted treatment the same 6 orbitals are partitioned as 2 in the first subspace, the HOMO and LUMO in the second, and 2 in the third.
active_space_protocol: The space is the complete pi system, i electrons in i orbitals, so its size is fixed by the molecule. Where that is unaffordable the same pi space is partitioned into a restricted scheme with the HOMO and LUMO in the fully correlated subspace and (i-2)/2 orbitals in each outer subspace, allowing up to double excitations; this partitioning was calibrated against complete-space results on the smaller members of the series before being extended.
electronic_structure_description: A closed-shell singlet ground state. Relative to it the triplet lies 40.6 kcal/mol at CASPT2 and 32.6 at RASPT2, and the open-shell singlet 61.5 and 52.6 respectively. Natural orbital occupancies of the HOMO and LUMO are 1.890 and 0.151 from the complete space and 1.896 and 0.139 from the restricted one, so biradical character is minimal. A four-point convergence sequence is reported for one molecule (2,2), (4,4) and (10,10) with and without the perturbative correction, and the singlet-triplet gap moves from 13.4 to 17.4 to 15.8 kcal per mole at the corrected level, i.e. it is NOT monotonic in the space size: the two-orbital answer happens to be closer to the full-space answer than the four-orbital one is. That is a warning against reading a small-space number as a lower bound. Beyond fourteen pi electrons the complete space is unaffordable, so the same full pi space is instead partitioned into a restricted scheme with the HOMO and LUMO in the fully correlated middle subspace and (i-2)/2 orbitals in each of the outer subspaces, with up to double excitations. Beyond fourteen pi electrons the complete space is unaffordable, so the same full pi space is instead partitioned into a restricted scheme with the HOMO and LUMO in the fully correlated middle subspace and (i-2)/2 orbitals in each of the outer subspaces, with up to double excitations. It is also validated at the level of the orbitals, not just the energies -- the natural orbitals from the restricted treatment are described as virtually identical to the complete-space ones, though the restricted reference orbitals before correction differ noticeably. Two failures are reported honestly rather than smoothed over. First, for the smallest member of the series the restricted wave functions converged only with great difficulty, orbitals shifted unpredictably between subspaces, converged energies depended on the starting point and convergence parameters, and the corrected energies came out significantly below the complete-space values; the author says plainly that the source of the anomaly is unclear. An alternative partitioning allowing triple excitations from a subspace of zero size in the middle tier behaved better and reproduced the complete-space numbers. Comparing the two partitionings across the series shows a systematic 0.4 to 1.3 kcal per mole offset that GROWS with molecular size, which is exactly the kind of drift that would be invisible from one molecule alone. Second, and important for anyone comparing to older literature, one of the reported gaps differs from a previously published value primarily because of the IPEA shift of 0.25 introduced in newer versions of the program: setting that shift to zero moves 15.8 to 11.4 kcal per mole, a 4.4 kcal per mole swing on a quantity of order fifteen. method: Configuration interaction over 50 septet roots built on a state-averaged CASSCF reference, used to compute the zero-field splitting tensor including both the dipolar spin-spin and the spin-orbit contributions; compared against unrestricted density functional theory
basis_set: SVP (Ahlrichs-VDZ) for the multiconfigurational zero-field splitting calculations; TZVP for the geometry optimization. Preliminary tests found no noticeable influence of basis set size on the accuracy of the zero-field splitting with either method
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in twelve orbitals, shown in a figure. The composition is dictated by a stated requirement: for bromine-substituted nitrenes the space must include the in-plane and out-of-plane lone pair orbitals of the valence p electrons of the bromine atom, which appear among the doubly occupied active orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The space is fixed by the requirement that the bromine valence p lone pairs be active, since they are the source of the spin-orbit contribution being measured. A configuration interaction over 50 septet roots is then run on top of the state-averaged CASSCF wave function.
nroots_per_mult: 50 septet roots
electronic_structure_description: A septet ground state generated in a solid argon matrix at 15 K by brief ultraviolet irradiation of 1,3,5-triazido-2-bromo-4,6-dichlorobenzene. Its electron spin resonance spectrum differs drastically from those of all previously studied septet trinitrenes. The experimental zero-field splitting parameters are a magnitude of 0.1237 reciprocal centimetres and a rhombicity ratio of 0.262, unprecedentedly large and close to the limiting value of one third for high-spin molecules. The multiconfigurational calculation gives a dipolar contribution of -0.099 and a spin-orbit contribution of -0.164 reciprocal centimetres, a total of 0.123 and a ratio of 0.260, in close agreement with experiment; the density functional calculation gives -0.094, +0.131, 0.177 and 0.18. Because the bromine atom makes the spin-orbit term dominant, the easy axis of the total tensor lies in the molecular plane perpendicular to the carbon-bromine bond rather than perpendicular to the plane, and the total parameter is large in magnitude and positive in sign.
Other: The active space here is specified by a chemical REQUIREMENT rather than by a size target: following earlier work, the space for a bromine-substituted nitrene must contain both the in-plane and the out-of-plane lone pair orbitals of the bromine valence p electrons, and that requirement is what fixes the space at twelve electrons in twelve orbitals. This matters because the whole measurement is a heavy-atom effect: the bromine lone pairs are the source of the spin-orbit contribution, so a space that omitted them would not merely be less accurate, it would be missing the physics being measured. Basis set size was tested and found to have no noticeable influence on the accuracy of the zero-field splitting with either method, which localizes the sensitivity squarely in the space rather than in the one-electron basis -- a useful negative result, since it means a modest split-valence set suffices once the right orbitals are active. The decisive comparison is against density functional theory on the same molecule, and the two disagree on a SIGN. The spin-orbit contribution comes out as +0.131 reciprocal centimetres from the functional and -0.164 from the multiconfigurational treatment. Experiment cannot settle this directly, because X-band electron spin resonance gives only the magnitude of the total splitting, so the authors use two independent experimental quantities as references, the magnitude 0.1237 and the rhombicity ratio 0.262. On those the multiconfigurational result is essentially exact -- 0.123 and 0.260 -- while the functional gives 0.177 and 0.18, wrong by 40 percent in the first and by a factor of nearly one and a half in the second. The sign disagreement is not academic: the two tensors being summed have DIFFERENT principal axes, the dipolar one with its easy axis perpendicular to the molecular plane and the spin-orbit one along the carbon-bromine bond, so the total is not a scalar sum and the sign of each component determines which axis ends up dominant. The multiconfigurational calculation puts the largest total component along the in-plane axis perpendicular to the carbon-bromine bond, which is what makes the rhombicity approach its limiting value; the functional puts it along a different axis and reaches the same positive sign for the total by a different and, on this evidence, wrong route. Getting the right answer for the wrong reason is exactly the failure mode that a single scalar comparison would hide, and the paper catches it by comparing tensors rather than numbers. The authors note that earlier density functional and hybrid multiconfigurational studies had already given opposite signs for a related dibromine-substituted trinitrene, which is why they treat the sign as the quantity to be established. A configuration interaction over 50 septet roots is built on the state-averaged reference, and the space is used to compute a property, the anisotropy tensor, rather than an energy difference; a scalar parameter derived from it becomes ambiguous as the rhombicity approaches its limit, which is precisely the regime this molecule sits in.

compound_name: Model spiropyran, the closed form of the photochromic switch
geometry_source: Ground-state stationary points optimized at B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) with frequency calculations confirming their nature; excited-state minima located by minimum energy path optimization at three-root state-averaged CASSCF; conical intersections located at SA3-CASSCF(14,12)/6-31G(d,p)
method: Multistate CASPT2 single points on state-averaged CASSCF geometries: ground-state stationary points from density functional theory, excited-state minimum energy paths from a three-root equal-weight state-averaged CASSCF, and the perturbative energies from a five-root equal-weight reference. Conical intersections and the energy-difference gradient and derivative coupling vectors defining the branching plane were located separately in a split-valence basis
software: MOLCAS 6.4 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; MOLPRO 2009 for the conical intersections and branching-plane vectors; Gaussian 03 for the density functional geometries
basis_set: ANO-S contracted C,O,N[4s3p1d]/H[2s1p] for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; 6-31G(d,p) for the density functional geometries and for the conical intersection and branching-plane work
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen electrons in twelve orbitals; the orbitals are depicted in the supporting information rather than itemized in the main text.
active_space_protocol: Chosen after several trials as a stated compromise between accuracy of the zero-order wave function and computational feasibility. Three-root equal-weight state averaging for geometries and minimum energy paths, five-root equal-weight state averaging for the perturbative reference. The weight of the reference wave function on the final perturbed state was checked in every case against the ground-state value as a balance diagnostic, and an imaginary level shift of 0.2 was applied.
nroots_per_mult: three for geometry optimization, five for the perturbative single points

The bright state responsible for the ultraviolet absorption lies 4.48 eV above the ground state with an oscillator strength of 0.21 and a slightly smaller dipole moment of 1.16 debye; it is a pi-pi* state dominated by the HOMO to LUMO configuration, both orbitals localized on the benzopyran moiety. This state is the third root after correction but the fourth at the uncorrected level. A further state, labelled 1A, is dominated by an excitation from a pyrroline pi orbital to a benzopyran pi antibonding orbital and carries a dipole moment of 13.71 debye, a large charge transfer from one ring to the other which would be stabilized in polar solvents. From the initially excited closed form two ultrafast routes to the ground state are found: one breaking the spiro carbon to oxygen bond and opening the ring, the other lengthening the spiro carbon to nitrogen bond and returning to the closed form with no photoreaction.
