Averaging over more states for the energies than for the geometries is a defensible split -- geometry optimization is cheaper and more stable with fewer roots, while the energetics need every state that could interleave -- but it means the geometries were determined without two of the states that later turn out to matter. That the extra roots matter is demonstrated rather than assumed, because the state ORDER changes under the correction in both forms of the molecule. In the closed form the bright pi-pi* state is the third root after correction but the FOURTH at the uncorrected level; in the open form the ordering of the two lowest excited states inverts, the authors attributing this to the uncorrected method describing n-pi* states better than pi-pi* states. A geometry optimized on the third root of a three-state average is therefore not obviously following the same state that the five-state corrected calculation identifies. The authors do run a diagnostic on the correction rather than trusting it blindly: the weight of the reference wave function on the final perturbed state was computed in every case and compared to the ground-state value, with closeness of the two taken as evidence of a balanced treatment. An imaginary level shift of 0.2 was used against intruder states. A third and rarely reported subtlety is that different bases and different programs were used for different quantities: the energies use a moderately contracted atomic natural orbital set, while the conical intersections and the branching-plane vectors were located in a split-valence polarized basis in another program, so the topology of the intersections and the energies at them do not come from identical calculations. The authors state a limit they could not overcome: optimizing the intersection seam properly would require doing so at the perturbatively corrected level, which several studies indicate is necessary, and which is computationally unreachable for a system of this size -- so the seam is characterized only through interpolated paths on uncorrected geometries. They are equally frank that better methods for determining the ground-state relaxation directions are beyond reach and that they instead estimate them from the branching-plane vectors. Finally, the space is applied to a truncated model: the fused benzene ring of the benzopyran moiety was removed and the methyl groups replaced by hydrogens, retained justification being that the conformational flexibility of the open form survives the truncation. The mechanistic conclusion is stated as depending on a quantity the space may not pin down -- the exact location of a charge-transfer state relative to the bright state is said to play an important role in the accessibility of the ring-opening path and to be able to influence the quantum yield.

compound_name: Bis(eta2-disulfido)iron anion, the D2h isomer of FeS4 minus
ligand_set: two side-on bound disulfide dianion ligands
geometry_source: Geometries of the lowest states optimized at the CASPT2 level; higher-lying states treated as single points on B3LYP geometries. Coupled cluster geometries optimized separately with triple-zeta basis sets
method: State-averaged CASSCF followed by multistate CASPT2, with geometries optimized at the CASPT2 level for the lowest states; compared against B3LYP and against restricted coupled cluster with singles, doubles and perturbative triples, the latter used for relative isomer stabilities because second-order perturbation theory was found unreliable for that quantity on related clusters
software: MOLCAS 7.4 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; MOLPRO 2009 for the coupled cluster calculations
basis_set: ANO-RCC contracted [7s6p4d3f2g] for iron and [6s5p3d2f] for sulfur for the multiconfigurational work; aug-cc-pVTZ-DK for the coupled cluster geometries, with aug-cc-pwCVQZ-DK on iron and aug-cc-pVQZ-DK on sulfur for single points including outer-core correlation
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic effects through the Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian
active_space_orbital_description: The technically maximal possible space: the complete 3d shell of iron together with all 3p orbitals of sulfur, 17 orbitals in total.
active_space_protocol: The space is maximal rather than selected, and is justified by an almost exact degeneracy between the nonbonding iron 3d orbitals and the disulfide pi antibonding orbitals, which makes any smaller partition arbitrary. Because of the resulting dense manifold of low-lying states, state-averaged CASSCF and multistate CASPT2 were mandatory. The IPEA shift was left at its default 0.25 and an imaginary shift of 0.10 was applied against intruder states; iron 3s, 3p and 3d and sulfur 3s and 3p electrons were correlated, with Cholesky decomposition of the two-electron integrals to 1e-6 hartree.
nroots_per_mult: four states averaged per irreducible representation
electronic_structure_description: The predicted ground state of the FeS4 anion: a 4B1g state with two disulfide dianion ligands bound side-on in a D2h arrangement to an iron centre in the +3 oxidation state. Analysis of the CASSCF orbitals shows an almost exact degeneracy between the nonbonding iron 3d orbitals and the disulfide pi antibonding orbitals, producing a dense manifold of low-lying states. At the CASPT2-optimized geometry the iron-sulfur distance is 2.169 and the sulfur-sulfur distance 2.109 Angstrom. A second 4B1g state, differing only in which 3d orbital is doubly occupied, lies 0.28 eV higher at CASPT2 and 0.23 eV at coupled cluster; the 4B2g and 4B3g states lie 0.46 eV higher at CASPT2 and 0.33 and 0.42 eV at coupled cluster. All three computational methods agree that this is the lowest state, which is what licenses assigning the experimental photoelectron spectra to it.
Other: The space here is defined by exhaustion of what the hardware allows rather than by a chemical argument: it is described as the 'technically maximal possible' space, containing the complete iron 3d shell and ALL sulfur 3p orbitals, which comes to 24 or 25 electrons in 17 orbitals depending on the charge. Reporting a space as maximal rather than as chosen is informative in both directions -- there is no arbitrariness left to criticize, but equally there is no headroom, so any residual error cannot be fixed by enlarging it. The orbital-level justification for needing all of it is given explicitly: analysis of the reference orbitals shows an almost exact degeneracy between the nonbonding iron 3d orbitals and the antibonding pi orbitals of the disulfide ligands. When metal and ligand frontier orbitals are that close, splitting them across the active/inactive boundary would be arbitrary, and including all of them is the only defensible option. The consequence of that degeneracy is a dense manifold of low-lying states, so state averaging was mandatory rather than optional -- four states per irreducible representation for one isomer and two for the other -- followed by multistate perturbation theory. geometry_source: Optimized in this work at CASSCF with both active spaces; the geometry actually carried into the spectral simulation was the QCISD/6-31G* one, because the CASSCF bond angles imply a longer bending progression than the observed band shows
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and harmonic frequency calculation with two active spaces, both averaged over two roots, used only for this state because the single-reference QCISD frequency calculation could not be completed for it; ionization energies for all four bands came from RCCSD(T) on QCISD geometries
software: GAUSSIAN 98 for the QCISD and CASSCF calculations; MOLPRO 98 for the RCCSD(T) calculations
basis_set: 6-311+G(2d) for the CASSCF calculations; 6-31G* for the QCISD geometries and aug-cc-pVQZ for the RCCSD(T) energies
active_space_orbital_description: Seven electrons in eight orbitals for the larger space and seven in six for the smaller; the orbital composition is not itemized in the paper.
active_space_protocol: Two spaces were run in parallel, seven electrons in six orbitals and seven in eight, each averaged over two roots, specifically to see how the answer moves with the space. The larger space was then used for force constants while the geometry was taken from the single-reference calculation.

electronic_structure_description: The C state of the cation, a doublet of A2 symmetry, is the fourth and highest of the four photoelectron bands studied. Its geometry is 1.7821 Angstrom and 104.22 degrees from the larger active space, 1.8045 Angstrom and 105.43 degrees from the smaller, against 1.7391 Angstrom and 108.87 degrees from QCISD and an experimentally derived 1.725 Angstrom and 108.9 degrees; the neutral ground state has an angle of 111.3 degrees. Harmonic frequencies for the symmetric stretch, bend and asymmetric stretch are 569.5, 262.1 and 411.6 reciprocal centimetres from the larger space and 565.1, 259.0 and 483.6 from the smaller, against observed values of 613 and 307 for the first two modes. The observed band shows one dominant symmetric-stretch progression with only a weak bending shoulder.
Other: The multiconfigurational treatment appears here for a purely PRACTICAL reason, and the paper is worth recording precisely because of how narrowly it is used. The single-reference method used for every other state failed on this one: the numerical second-derivative calculation ran into excessive iterations in the energy evaluation at some point along the differentiation, so no harmonic frequencies could be obtained that way for the fourth cationic state, and CASSCF was brought in to supply them. The answer is unusually clean and cuts in two directions at once. GEOMETRIES are strongly space-dependent: the two spaces give significantly different minimum-energy structures, with a bond length of 1.8045 Angstrom from the smaller and 1.7821 from the larger, converging toward the 1.7391 of the single-reference reference method as the space grows. FREQUENCIES are nearly space-independent: the bending mode comes out at 259 and 262 reciprocal centimetres from the two spaces, a difference of three, against an observed spacing of 307. So the property that motivated using the method at all is the one least sensitive to the choice of space, while the property that is sensitive is the one the authors did not need. That combination is what licenses their unusual final protocol: they take the force constants from the larger active space but the GEOMETRY from the single-reference calculation as the starting structure for the Franck-Condon fitting, mixing two methods within one spectral simulation on the explicit grounds that each is better at one piece. They also give an independent physical argument for distrusting the multiconfigurational geometry rather than merely preferring the other number: both spaces put the bond angle near 104 to 105 degrees against 108.9 from the single-reference method and 111.3 for the neutral, and such a large computed angle change on ionization would produce a long bending progression in the simulated band, whereas the observed fourth band shows one dominant symmetric-stretch series with only a weak bending shoulder. The experiment therefore adjudicates between the two geometries, and it goes against the active-space result. The residual disagreement is not hidden: agreement for this state is described as merely reasonable rather than good, unlike the other three bands. The active space composition is never itemized, only its electron and orbital counts, so a reader cannot tell which two orbitals the enlargement added.

The spin-orbit coupling is nearly constant over this region, 374, 367 and 352 reciprocal centimetres at the three geometries respectively. From 48 simulations of 150 femtoseconds each, started with a single nuclear basis function on the triplet, an average of 14 basis functions were spawned from triplet to singlet and 7 back per simulation. compound_name: CH3CO-Gly-NH2 peptide analogue, C7 folded conformer, neutral and its radical cation
geometry_source: Optimized at CASSCF/6-31G(d) with the Berny algorithm and default convergence criteria; minima confirmed by analytical frequencies at the same level; reaction paths from relaxed scans in which every parameter except one specified bond distance was optimized
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and potential energy surface exploration, chosen because several configurations contribute to a radical cationic state and near-degeneracy effects from conical intersections between low-lying valence cationic states make single-configuration barriers unreliable; second-order Moller-Plesset theory in a larger basis used for the ionization energy and as a cross-check on relative conformer energies
active_space_orbital_description: For the radical cation, nine electrons in eight orbitals: one oxygen nonbonding orbital on the acetyl group, the sigma bonding and antibonding pair of the acetyl carbonyl, the pi bonding and antibonding pair of the acetyl carbonyl, the delocalized pi bonding and antibonding pair of the amide NCO unit, and one nonbonding pi orbital of that amide unit. The neutral molecule uses ten electrons in eight orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The orbital composition is chosen per conformer rather than transplanted between them: the carbonyl whose pi orbitals enter the space differs between the folded and extended structures, so that the space follows where the hole localizes. Only natural orbitals were considered. A split-valence polarized basis is stated to be sufficient for these ionic pathways provided a proper active space is specified.
multiplicities_studied: doublet for the radical cation; singlet for the neutral
electronic_structure_description: The conformer that folds back on its backbone through a gamma-turn, and the lowest-energy form of the neutral molecule, 0.76 kcal/mol below the extended conformer at CASSCF(10,8)/6-31G(d), with a 4.1 kcal/mol rotational barrier separating them. On the ground doublet surface of the radical cation, direct elimination of the acetyl group carries activation barriers of about 80 and 100 kcal/mol from the vertical ionization point, far more than single-photon ionization at 118.22 nanometres can supply, so that channel is closed. Instead this conformer dissociates by a route that begins with hydrogen transfer, which is accessible and which the fold makes available. The molecular ion is therefore prone to fragmentation.
Other: The most instructive feature here is that the active space has the SAME SIZE for the two conformers but a DIFFERENT ORBITAL COMPOSITION, and the paper itemizes both. Nine electrons in eight orbitals in each case, but for the folded conformer the two pi and pi-antibonding orbitals come from the acetyl carbonyl while the delocalized pair comes from the amide, and for the extended conformer that assignment is exactly reversed -- the pi pair comes from the amide carbonyl and the delocalized pair from the acetyl. The space therefore follows where the hole actually sits rather than being transplanted unchanged between structures. That is the right call chemically, since the whole paper is about the hole localizing differently depending on the fold, but it has a consequence worth flagging: the two conformers' energies are not computed in the same orbital space, so the 0.76 kcal per mole separating them is not a strictly like-for-like difference. The authors are aware the number is delicate -- they say plainly that it is smaller than their best estimate of the numerical error, and argue for the ordering on the separate ground of a 4.1 kcal per mole rotational barrier between them rather than resting on the energy gap alone. The justification for using a multiconfigurational method at all is stated as a specific mechanism rather than a generality: a radical cationic state typically has several contributing configurations, and near-degeneracy effects from conical intersections between the many low-lying valence cationic states become important, so single-configuration methods often over- or underestimate transition-state barriers on a radical cation ground surface. Since the entire conclusion is a comparison of barrier heights -- 80 to 100 kcal per mole for direct elimination against 13.45 for the hydrogen-transfer route -- getting barriers right is exactly what the method must deliver, and a bias of either sign would flip which channel is predicted. The basis choice is defended by a stated conditional: a split-valence polarized set is described as sufficient for these ionic pathways PROVIDED a proper active space is specified, with larger bases raising cost drastically without changing the electronic energy significantly, and this is cross-checked against second-order Moller-Plesset theory in a much larger basis, which gives similar relative conformer energies. Only natural orbitals were considered in constructing the space. A different space, ten electrons in eight orbitals, is used for the neutral molecule -- one more electron in the same number of orbitals, consistent with the neutral being the closed-shell parent of the radical cation -- so the neutral and the ion are also not described in identical spaces. Reaction paths were traced by relaxed scans along a single stretched bond with everything else optimized, and minima were confirmed by analytical frequencies at the same level.

electronic_structure_description: The lowest-lying isomer of this stoichiometry, a rhombus with two hydroxide groups bridging two nickel(I) ions, ground term 1Ag. Its low-lying states organize into Heisenberg spin ladders of four terms each, arising from coupling two nickel(I) ions of 3d8 4s1 configuration each carrying spin three-halves. The ladder built on the ground term continues with terms at 0.012, 0.040 and 0.090 eV; further ladders begin at about 0.07, 0.12 and 0.15 eV. Across the different ladders the singlet-to-septet spread is 0.086 to 0.102 eV. At least 32 terms lie within 0.26 eV. Four terms fall outside the ladder classification. All five symmetry-lowering distortions tested leave the rhombic structure an energy minimum. The reaction of Ni2O2 with dihydrogen to give this isomer is estimated to release about 2 eV.
Other: The space here is chosen by an explicit, reproducible SCREENING PROCEDURE rather than by judgement. A first batch of calculations is run with a deliberately oversized space -- 30 electrons in 18 orbitals, comprising both nickel 4s, all ten nickel 3d and all six oxygen 2p orbitals -- and then every orbital whose occupation number exceeds 1.99 is thrown out. Selecting by occupancy rather than by orbital label means the answer can differ between STATES of the same molecule, and it does: the same isomer is treated with a (6,6) space for one state, (14,10) for another and (18,12) for a third, since which 3d orbitals are genuinely partially occupied depends on the spin coupling. A fixed space would have been either wasteful for the closed-shell-like states or inadequate for the open-shell ones. The procedure also justifies an omission by the same criterion rather than by assertion: the oxygen 2s orbitals are left out of the screening space because even the 2p occupations already come out close to 2. Two further, independent thresholds control the reference space of the correlated step, and the paper is unusually careful to state that they are RELAXED FOR GEOMETRY OPTIMIZATION and tightened for final energies -- configurations with weight above 0.01 for the energies, above 0.05 during structure determination, with correspondingly smaller active spaces during optimization. That is the right trade in principle, but it means the reported geometries and the reported energies do not come from the same wave function, which a reader comparing either quantity to another study should know. A genuine methodological limitation is stated outright rather than glossed: analytical vibrational frequencies are not implemented for this method in the available programs, and numerical differentiation is too expensive, so minima could not be confirmed the usual way. The workaround is manual and specific -- five named distortions are computed by hand for one isomer, three lowering the symmetry one way and two the other, each using the same spaces as the parent structure -- and it produces a real result, since one isomer that was initially assumed planar turned out to lower its energy on out-of-plane bending and had to be reoptimized in lower symmetry, and another was found NOT to be a minimum at all. Reporting a structure as non-stationary, and abandoning its optimization as too slow to converge while saying so, is more informative than quietly dropping it. Basis convergence is addressed by reference to earlier work rather than repeated here: larger sets and extrapolation are said to have changed distances and relative energies only slightly. The one physical effect knowingly left out is spin-orbit coupling, and the authors flag exactly why it matters -- it would destroy the Heisenberg spin-ladder pattern that is the paper's main electronic-structure finding -- so the ladders should be read as a result of the spin-free treatment.

electronic_structure_description: Studied both at the ground-state minimum and at the conical intersection between the ground and first excited singlet states. Despite being the smallest system in the set, it shows the LARGEST deviation between the two orbital choices, 0.48 eV. The authors attribute this to the two-orbital space leaving too little configurational flexibility to compensate for a suboptimal orbital set, the opposite extreme from the full configuration interaction limit where energies become orbital-independent.
Other: Like the best orbital-source studies, this one holds the REFERENCE SPACE FIXED and varies only where the orbitals come from, so any difference is attributable to the orbitals alone. The proposal is to replace state-averaged CASSCF canonical orbitals with natural orbitals taken from a singles-and-doubles configuration interaction on a HIGH-MULTIPLICITY reference state. The motivation is stated plainly: an excited singlet formed by promoting an electron between frontier orbitals has a triplet partner built from the same configuration, and that triplet is the GROUND state of its own spin manifold, so ordinary ground-state machinery applies to it directly. Orbitals optimized for the easy state are then handed to the hard one. Raising the multiplicity from three to five is reported to work much better in most systems here, which matters when several excited states are wanted at once rather than one. Across six molecules the mean absolute deviation from the standard treatment is 0.12 eV uncorrected and 0.15 eV with the size-extensivity correction -- and the correction makes the agreement slightly WORSE, not better, which is worth knowing before applying it. The distribution matters more than the mean: most states agree to within 0.00 to 0.04 eV, with a few stark outliers, so this is not a method with a uniform small bias but one that is usually excellent and occasionally off by half an electronvolt. The failure pattern is counterintuitive and the authors say so: the LARGEST deviation, 0.48 eV, occurs for ethylene, the SIMPLEST molecule in the set, and their explanation is the right one -- in the full configuration interaction limit energies are independent of the orbitals, and a two-electron two-orbital space sits at the opposite extreme, where too little configurational flexibility remains to absorb a poor orbital choice. So the method is least reliable exactly where the active space is smallest, which inverts the usual expectation that small systems are safe. The large-space case behaves as expected instead: uracil, with nine active orbitals, deviates by 0.25 and 0.17 eV for its two lowest states. The second contribution is a virtual-space truncation keyed to occupation, and the numbers are striking: discarding 30 percent of the virtual space costs almost nothing, and one can keep 90 percent of the occupation while truncating 52 percent of the virtuals, or 95 percent of the occupation while truncating 81 percent. The clearest demonstration is that a quadruple-zeta calculation with 97 of 159 virtual orbitals truncated runs in 4 minutes against 2 hours 17 minutes untruncated, a 34-fold speed-up, and gives practically the same answer -- and a better one than an untruncated triple-zeta calculation costing longer. The active spaces themselves are chosen by a consistent chemical rule across the set: all pi and pi antibonding orbitals for conjugated molecules, plus an oxygen lone pair where one contributes to the state of interest. The second oxygen lone pair in uracil is deliberately excluded on the stated evidence that it does not affect the two lowest excitation energies -- an omission justified by prior result rather than by assumption.

electronic_structure_description: Formed by the competing five-membered-ring closure. Also a clean biradical, with the two relevant natural orbitals at 1.00 and 1.00. This step is about 10 kcal/mol endothermic, in line with other computational values, with a barrier of 23.3 kcal/mol, lower than previous computational results. Its transition state has natural orbital occupations of 1.65 and 0.35, again intermediate between biradical and closed-shell singlet. The barrier difference between the two competing cyclizations is about 7 kcal/mol, smaller than other estimates. A related structure with one negative force-constant eigenvalue leads to a bifurcation, with a second transition state connecting to this product along the reaction coordinate.
Other: The space is designed to be valid along the WHOLE reaction path rather than at either end of it, and the paper says so in an unusually direct way: ten orbitals are taken as all the valence pi and pi antibonding orbitals of the REACTANT, and the same ten are noted to correspond to three pi and pi antibonding pairs, a sigma and sigma antibonding pair, and TWO RADICAL ORBITALS of the PRODUCTS. One orbital set has to describe a closed-shell enyne-allene at one end and a biradical at the other, and choosing it by counting the reactant's pi system happens to deliver exactly the orbitals the products need. A space chosen at only one end of such a path would be biased toward that end, and the resulting barrier would be wrong in a direction set by the choice rather than by the chemistry. All configurations in the space were generated, so nothing is truncated within it. They also note that the perturbative correction lowers relative energies by more than 10 kcal per mole from the uncorrected level, describing this as normal for pericyclic reactions -- so the correction is not a refinement here but the dominant contribution to the barrier, and the uncorrected number would be badly wrong. The energy differences the space is asked to resolve are extremely fine: two transition states of different symmetry separated by 0.2 kcal per mole uncorrected and 1.5 corrected, and two reactant conformers separated by 0.04. At that scale the ordering is a genuine test of the method, and the correction changes the margin sevenfold without changing the sign. compound_name: Allylsilane, CH2=CHCH2-SiH3, the unsubstituted parent of the series
geometry_source: Fully optimized at CASSCF(6,6)/6-31G(d) for both electronic states; the perturbative energies are single points on those geometries. Reaction coordinates were followed at the same CASSCF level
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and transition-state location on the ground and lowest triplet surfaces, chosen for its analytic first and second derivatives and hence reliable surface topography, with CASPT2 single points for dynamic correlation
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for geometries and the main results; 6-31+G(d) and 6-31G(d,p) used for additional single points at both levels
active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in six orbitals: the sigma, sigma antibonding, pi and pi antibonding orbitals of the carbon-carbon double bond, together with the sigma and sigma antibonding orbitals of the carbon-silicon bond.
active_space_protocol: The space is specified by naming the bonds it must span rather than by a count, and is held identical across all six derivatives of the series, so that substituent trends cannot be an artifact of a changing description. Both the chromophore and the bond that breaks are inside it.
electronic_structure_description: The parent compound, named explicitly in the text. Its ground-state geometry has a carbon-silicon bond of 1.925 Angstrom and a carbon-carbon double bond of 1.356 Angstrom, with a Mulliken charge of +0.66 on silicon and -0.61 on the carbon bearing it. The singlet-to-triplet transition lengthens the double bond by about 0.15 Angstrom to 1.496 Angstrom and twists it, the HC=CH dihedral falling from 178.93 to 93.09 degrees. The adiabatic triplet-singlet gap is 67.62 kcal/mol uncorrected and 69.69 corrected. The ground-state carbon-silicon bond dissociation energy is 58.84 kcal/mol uncorrected and 69.17 corrected, against an experimental 73 for the trimethylsilyl analogue, a gap the authors close by computing that three methyl groups on silicon strengthen the bond by 3.1 kcal/mol. Dissociation from the triplet is -8.73 kcal/mol uncorrected but only -0.26 corrected, essentially thermoneutral, with a triplet activation energy of 19.59 uncorrected and 24.95 corrected.
Other: The space is defined by naming the BONDS it must cover rather than by counting orbitals, and the choice follows directly from what the reaction does. Because every molecule in the series shares the same carbon-carbon-carbon-silicon backbone, the authors take the sigma and sigma antibonding pair of the carbon-silicon bond that breaks, together with the sigma, sigma antibonding, pi and pi antibonding orbitals of the carbon-carbon double bond that absorbs the excitation, giving six electrons in six orbitals. Both ends of the photochemistry are therefore in the space -- the chromophore and the bond being cleaved -- which is the minimum condition for a homolysis on an excited surface to be described at all, since a space containing only the chromophore would have to break a bond it cannot see. Holding that same six-orbital definition fixed across all six substituted derivatives is what makes the series comparable: substituents are added to the molecule but never to the space, so the reported trends are attributable to substitution rather than to a changing description. The stated justification for the reference is the usual one but is applied here to a specific need -- analytic first and second derivatives, hence reliable surface topography and geometries, which the study depends on because it locates transition states and follows reaction coordinates on the triplet surface. The perturbative correction is applied as single points on those geometries, and its effect is large and systematic rather than a refinement: ground-state bond dissociation energies rise by roughly 10 to 13 kcal per mole across the series, from 58.84 to 69.17 for the parent, and the triplet-state dissociation enthalpies shift by 8 to 12. Most consequentially, the SIGN of the triplet dissociation energy is preserved but its magnitude changes by more than an order of ratio for the parent, from -8.73 to -0.26 kcal per mole, so the uncorrected number would suggest a comfortably exothermic triplet homolysis where the corrected one puts it almost exactly thermoneutral. Any conclusion resting on how exothermic that step is would be qualitatively different at the two levels. What survives the correction unchanged is the TREND -- larger and more numerous alkyl substituents lower the ground-state dissociation energy, make the triplet dissociation more exothermic and lower the triplet activation energy -- and the authors verify that this holds for both levels of theory and for all three basis sets tested, which is the right way to establish that a correlation is not an artifact of one computational choice. The linear correlations the paper is built on are between quantities computed in the same fixed space, so systematic errors in the space largely cancel from the slopes even where they do not cancel from the absolute values. A useful external check is reported: the corrected dissociation energy of 69.17 kcal per mole for the parent compares with an experimental 73 for the trimethylsilyl analogue, and the authors compute that adding three methyl groups to silicon strengthens the bond by 3.1, closing the gap.
reference_short: Varras & Zarkadis, J. Phys. Chem. A 2012, 116, 1425
notes: One of six allylsilanes of general structure CH2=CH-C(R1R2)-SiH3 with R1 and R2 drawn from hydrogen, methyl and ethyl. Across the series, increasing the number and size of the substituents lowers the ground-state bond dissociation energy, makes the triplet-state dissociation more exothermic and lowers the triplet activation energy; the same trend holds at both levels of theory and for all three basis sets. Only two members of the series are identified explicitly in the text, so only those are recorded here. This is compound 1, the only one given as an explicit structural formula.
correlation_correction: CASPT2(6,6) single points on the CASSCF geometries; it raises ground-state dissociation energies by 10 to 13 kcal/mol and changes the triplet dissociation energy of the parent from -8.73 to -0.26 kcal/mol

compound_name: Ethylene plus benzene, ortho [1,2] photocycloaddition channel
geometry_source: Optimized at CASSCF(8,8)/6-31G*, including minimum energy paths and a full second-order analysis of critical points on the conical intersection seam; corrected energies are single points on those geometries
method: CASSCF for all optimizations, minimum energy paths and seam characterization, with CASPT2 single points on selected structures, chiefly the initial excited-state transition states, to gauge the effect of dynamic correlation
software: A development version of Gaussian for the CASSCF work; MOLCAS 7 for the CASPT2 single points
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals, spanning the pi systems of the two reacting partners.
active_space_protocol: One space is used throughout for optimizations, paths and seam analysis. The paper notes that at a point on the seam the bonding patterns of the two diabatic states cancel, so the shape of the seam is controlled by electrons OUTSIDE the active space, through steric and inductive effects, rather than by those inside it.
electronic_structure_description: The 2 pi plus 2 pi addition across adjacent benzene carbons. Its point on the conical intersection seam lies on the low-energy asynchronous branch, and together with the meta channel it is predicted to be a preferred product with similar weight. On the excited surface it is reached through a transition state of mixed asynchronous and synchronous character with a low barrier. Experimentally this mode is favoured by electron-withdrawing substituents.
Other: The most valuable thing this paper records about its active space is a FAILURE, stated openly rather than buried. Recomputing the energy at the perturbatively corrected level on transition states optimized with the eight-electron eight-orbital reference gives NEGATIVE activation energies -- a physically impossible result that can only mean the geometries themselves are wrong at the corrected level and would have to be reoptimized there, which the authors say is not feasible. They go further and offer a mechanism for the failure: an interaction with a zwitterionic state, which carries a large dynamic correlation effect that the reference wave function cannot see. A zwitterionic state is exactly the kind of state whose relative position moves furthest under a correction, so a stationary point located without one can be misplaced along the very coordinate that matters. The authors then do the useful thing, which is to scope their claims rather than abandon them: the DETAILED ENERGETICS on the excited surface are declared uncertain, while the general shape of the surface and the mechanistic information carried by the conical intersection seam are argued to be insensitive to dynamic correlation. That separation -- topology robust, barrier heights not -- is precisely the distinction a reader needs, and it is the same conclusion other careful studies reach for space-dependent quantities. There is a second, subtler point about what the space can and cannot control. The paper's central object is an extended intersection seam, and its shape is analyzed in valence-bond terms: at a point on the seam the bonding pattern of one diabatic state is exactly balanced by that of the other. The authors draw the consequence explicitly -- because the two bonding patterns cancel, the shape of the seam is controlled by factors affecting the electrons OUTSIDE the active space, such as steric and inductive effects, not by the electrons inside it. This is an unusual and important observation: enlarging the active space would not improve the description of the seam's shape, because the active electrons contribute equally to both intersecting states and cancel from their difference. It also explains why the same pair of valence-bond structures recurs along the asynchronous branch of the seam, leaving sterics to determine its profile. The reference is used for everything structural -- optimizations, minimum energy paths, and a full second-order analysis of critical points on the seam itself -- with the correction reserved for selected single points in a different program, so geometries and corrected energies never come from the same calculation.

Other: The active space here is the smallest one that exists for the problem -- two electrons in two orbitals, the bonding and antibonding pair of the bond being broken -- and it is used deliberately as a BASELINE against which a natural orbital functional is measured, not as an attempt at accuracy. The results show very clearly what that minimal space does and does not buy. On its own it is badly wrong: across the six simple hydrides the mean absolute error against experiment is 19.2 kcal per mole in the double-zeta basis and 16.5 in triple-zeta, and across twenty organic molecules it is 11.1, with essentially every bond dissociation energy underestimated. Adding second-order perturbation theory on top of the SAME two-orbital space transforms it, to 8.8 and 3.4 kcal per mole for the hydrides and 5.0 for the organics. The space supplies the correct qualitative picture of a bond breaking homolytically -- which is what a two-configuration reference is for -- while essentially all of the quantitative accuracy comes from the correction. The most instructive detail is the BASIS BEHAVIOUR of the two levels, which differs sharply: the uncorrected error barely moves on going from double to triple zeta, 19.2 to 16.5, whereas the corrected error more than halves, 8.8 to 3.4. That contrast is diagnostic. An uncorrected minimal-space result is limited by missing dynamic correlation rather than by the one-electron basis, so enlarging the basis cannot help it; once the correlation is restored, the basis becomes the binding constraint and basis extension pays. Anyone tempted to converge a small-space CASSCF number with respect to basis should read those two rows. A second, qualitative failure is reported rather than averaged away: the minimal space gets the ORDERING of two dissociation energies backwards -- methane against ammonia, whose experimental values differ by only 2.9 kcal per mole -- and the perturbative correction recovers the correct order. A method that inverts a 3 kcal per mole ordering cannot be used to rank similar bonds, however good its average error looks. The dissociation limit was computed at a fixed 5 Angstrom separation rather than by extrapolation, and zero-point corrections were added to the experimental values rather than removed from the computed ones, so the comparison is on equilibrium dissociation energies throughout. Because the two-orbital space is defined identically for every molecule in the set, the comparison across twenty-six species is strictly like-for-like, which is what makes the mean errors meaningful as a characterization of the method rather than of the individual systems.

compound_name: Water, O-H dissociation to hydroxyl and hydrogen
geometry_source: Single-point energies; the dissociation limit was evaluated at a fixed X-H separation of 5 Angstrom
method: CASSCF with a two-electron two-orbital space and CASPT2 on the same space, computed as a reference standard against which several natural orbital functionals are assessed
software: MOLCAS 8.0 for all wave function based calculations; GAMESS supplied integrals for the natural orbital functional code
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons distributed in two molecular orbitals, the bonding and antibonding pair of the bond undergoing homolysis.
active_space_protocol: The minimal space that can describe homolytic bond cleavage, defined identically for every molecule in the set so that the comparison across species is strictly like-for-like. It is used as a baseline reference rather than as a converged treatment.
multiplicities_studied: singlet for the closed-shell parents; the products are radicals
nroots_per_mult: one
electronic_structure_description: Computed values are 99.4 uncorrected and 114.8 corrected in double-zeta, 102.7 and 122.0 in triple-zeta, against an experimental 126.0. The correction adds more than 19 kcal/mol here, the largest single correction in the hydride set.
Other: The active space here is the smallest one that exists for the problem -- two electrons in two orbitals, the bonding and antibonding pair of the bond being broken -- and it is used deliberately as a BASELINE against which a natural orbital functional is measured, not as an attempt at accuracy. The results show very clearly what that minimal space does and does not buy. On its own it is badly wrong: across the six simple hydrides the mean absolute error against experiment is 19.2 kcal per mole in the double-zeta basis and 16.5 in triple-zeta, and across twenty organic molecules it is 11.1, with essentially every bond dissociation energy underestimated. Anyone tempted to converge a small-space CASSCF number with respect to basis should read those two rows. A second, qualitative failure is reported rather than averaged away: the minimal space gets the ORDERING of two dissociation energies backwards -- methane against ammonia, whose experimental values differ by only 2.9 kcal per mole -- and the perturbative correction recovers the correct order. A method that inverts a 3 kcal per mole ordering cannot be used to rank similar bonds, however good its average error looks. The dissociation limit was computed at a fixed 5 Angstrom separation rather than by extrapolation, and zero-point corrections were added to the experimental values rather than removed from the computed ones, so the comparison is on equilibrium dissociation energies throughout. Because the two-orbital space is defined identically for every molecule in the set, the comparison across twenty-six species is strictly like-for-like, which is what makes the mean errors meaningful as a characterization of the method rather than of the individual systems.

ligand_set: a methylene group and two fluorides
point_group: Approximately Cs at the highest level; C2v optimizations never reached a minimum
geometry_source: Optimized in this work at several levels including density functional theory, Hartree-Fock, CASSCF, coupled cluster with perturbative triples, second-order perturbation theory and multireference configuration interaction, with vibrational frequencies computed to verify minima
method: CASSCF with several active spaces, followed by rotation of the active orbitals to a localized basis and re-expansion of the wave function; configuration interaction coefficients evaluated with excitations restricted to the active space; population analysis plus expectation values of the charge fluctuation and local spin operators. Second-order perturbation theory, multireference configuration interaction and coupled cluster with perturbative triples used alongside
basis_set: Small-core ECP28MWB pseudopotential on cerium with an atomic natural orbital basis using s, p, d, f and g functions, in double, triple and quadruple zeta quality and their augmented variants; segmented def-SV(P) and def2-TZVP sets used for the density functional calculations
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic small-core pseudopotential on cerium
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals in the reduced space: one cerium 4f orbital and the out-of-plane 2p orbital of the ligand atom. The larger space first examined was two electrons in eight orbitals, comprising all seven cerium 4f orbitals plus that same ligand 2p orbital.
active_space_protocol: All seven 4f orbitals were included first, since one cannot know in advance which participates; the space was then reduced to two orbitals after the larger calculation proved to be dominated by two configurations over two orbitals. The reduction was validated against both the energy difference between the two spaces and natural orbital occupation numbers from a configuration interaction correlating 32 electrons. No excitations were allowed from the cerium 4s, 4p and 4d shells or the carbon and oxygen 1s shells in the correlated steps.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, with triplet and open-shell singlet treatments compared
electronic_structure_description: An open-shell singlet ground state. In the basis of the strongly mixed natural CASSCF orbitals the wave function is two-configurational; transformed to nearly pure cerium 4f and carbon 2p orbitals it becomes almost monoconfigurational, dominated by a single configuration with one electron in each, and on that basis the compound is best described as a cerium(III) system. The reduced two-orbital space gives a ground-state energy within 0.044 eV of the eight-orbital space, while either lowers the energy by about 0.8 eV relative to the single-determinant reference. Density functional calculations give a cerium f occupation close to one, in the range 0.9 to 1.3. Optimizations in C2v symmetry retained at least one imaginary frequency at every method even with energy convergence tightened to 1e-14 hartree; only unconstrained optimization located the true minimum.
Other: This paper makes a point that most active-space discussions leave implicit: the multiconfigurational character of a wave function is NOT an invariant property of the molecule, it depends on the orbital basis the wave function is expressed in, and the two compounds here demonstrate that by SWAPPING BEHAVIOUR under the same transformation. Expressed in the delocalized natural orbitals that come out of the calculation, the methylene compound is two-configurational while the oxygen compound is a single closed-shell configuration. Rotate both into orbitals localized on the metal and the ligand atom, and the situation inverts exactly: the methylene compound becomes almost monoconfigurational, dominated by a single cerium-4f-one ligand-2p-one configuration, while the oxygen compound becomes multiconfigurational. The chemical readings follow from the localized picture -- a clean Ce(III) system in one case, a mixed-valent Ce(IV)/Ce(III) system in the other -- so the oxidation state assignment, the thing the title promises, is only extractable AFTER the rotation. Anyone who reports a configuration weight without saying which orbitals it refers to has reported half a number. The space itself was reduced by a justified argument rather than by cost. The larger space, two electrons in eight orbitals covering ALL SEVEN cerium 4f orbitals plus the out-of-plane ligand 2p orbital, was run first; it turned out to be dominated by just two configurations distributing the two electrons over two orbitals, so the space was cut to one 4f orbital and the ligand 2p orbital. The reduction is then VALIDATED energetically rather than assumed: the two spaces differ by 0.044 eV for the methylene compound and 0.2 eV for the oxygen compound, against the roughly 0.8 and 0.6 eV by which either space improves on the single-determinant reference. That framing is the useful one -- the correlation captured is an order of magnitude larger than the error introduced by shrinking the space -- and it is backed independently by natural orbital occupation numbers from a configuration interaction correlating 32 electrons. Including all seven 4f orbitals first, and only then discarding six of them on evidence, is the right order of operations for an f-element where one cannot know in advance which 4f orbital participates. A geometry pathology is reported rather than smoothed over: for the methylene compound, C2v optimizations would not reach a minimum at any method, retaining at least one imaginary frequency even with energy convergence tightened to ten to the minus fourteen hartree, and only unconstrained optimization gave a genuine minimum, which at the highest level turns out to be approximately Cs. The analysis is pushed beyond population numbers to expectation values of the charge fluctuation and local spin operators on the localized orbitals, which is what distinguishes a genuine open-shell singlet from a formally similar closed shell. Core shells of the metal and the light atoms were frozen in all correlated steps.

method: CASSCF with several active spaces, followed by rotation of the active orbitals to a localized basis and re-expansion of the wave function; configuration interaction coefficients evaluated with excitations restricted to the active space; population analysis plus expectation values of the charge fluctuation and local spin operators. Second-order perturbation theory, multireference configuration interaction and coupled cluster with perturbative triples used alongside
basis_set: Small-core ECP28MWB pseudopotential on cerium with an atomic natural orbital basis using s, p, d, f and g functions, in double, triple and quadruple zeta quality and their augmented variants; segmented def-SV(P) and def2-TZVP sets used for the density functional calculations
relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic small-core pseudopotential on cerium
active_space_orbital_description: Two electrons in two orbitals in the reduced space: one cerium 4f orbital and the out-of-plane 2p orbital of the ligand atom. The larger space first examined was two electrons in eight orbitals, comprising all seven cerium 4f orbitals plus that same ligand 2p orbital.
active_space_protocol: All seven 4f orbitals were included first, since one cannot know in advance which participates; the space was then reduced to two orbitals after the larger calculation proved to be dominated by two configurations over two orbitals. The reduction was validated against both the energy difference between the two spaces and natural orbital occupation numbers from a configuration interaction correlating 32 electrons. No excitations were allowed from the cerium 4s, 4p and 4d shells or the carbon and oxygen 1s shells in the correlated steps.
multiplicities_studied: singlet, with triplet and open-shell singlet treatments compared
electronic_structure_description: A singlet ground state which, described with a monoconfigurational wave function built from very strongly mixed cerium 4f and oxygen 2p natural CASSCF orbitals, appears to be closed shell. Transforming to orbitals localized on cerium and oxygen makes the wave function multiconfigurational and reveals the characteristics of a mixed-valent cerium(IV)/cerium(III) compound. The reduced two-orbital space lies 0.2 eV from the eight-orbital space and about 0.6 eV below the single-determinant reference. Density functional calculations give a cerium f occupation close to one, in the range 0.9 to 1.3. The ground-state symmetry is unambiguous here, unlike for the methylene compound.
Other: This paper makes a point that most active-space discussions leave implicit: the multiconfigurational character of a wave function is NOT an invariant property of the molecule, it depends on the orbital basis the wave function is expressed in, and the two compounds here demonstrate that by SWAPPING BEHAVIOUR under the same transformation. Expressed in the delocalized natural orbitals that come out of the calculation, the methylene compound is two-configurational while the oxygen compound is a single closed-shell configuration. Rotate both into orbitals localized on the metal and the ligand atom, and the situation inverts exactly: the methylene compound becomes almost monoconfigurational, dominated by a single cerium-4f-one ligand-2p-one configuration, while the oxygen compound becomes multiconfigurational. The chemical readings follow from the localized picture -- a clean Ce(III) system in one case, a mixed-valent Ce(IV)/Ce(III) system in the other -- so the oxidation state assignment, the thing the title promises, is only extractable AFTER the rotation. Anyone who reports a configuration weight without saying which orbitals it refers to has reported half a number. The space itself was reduced by a justified argument rather than by cost. The larger space, two electrons in eight orbitals covering ALL SEVEN cerium 4f orbitals plus the out-of-plane ligand 2p orbital, was run first; it turned out to be dominated by just two configurations distributing the two electrons over two orbitals, so the space was cut to one 4f orbital and the ligand 2p orbital. The reduction is then VALIDATED energetically rather than assumed: the two spaces differ by 0.044 eV for the methylene compound and 0.2 eV for the oxygen compound, against the roughly 0.8 and 0.6 eV by which either space improves on the single-determinant reference. That framing is the useful one -- the correlation captured is an order of magnitude larger than the error introduced by shrinking the space -- and it is backed independently by natural orbital occupation numbers from a configuration interaction correlating 32 electrons. Including all seven 4f orbitals first, and only then discarding six of them on evidence, is the right order of operations for an f-element where one cannot know in advance which 4f orbital participates. A geometry pathology is reported rather than smoothed over: for the methylene compound, C2v optimizations would not reach a minimum at any method, retaining at least one imaginary frequency even with energy convergence tightened to ten to the minus fourteen hartree, and only unconstrained optimization gave a genuine minimum, which at the highest level turns out to be approximately Cs. The analysis is pushed beyond population numbers to expectation values of the charge fluctuation and local spin operators on the localized orbitals, which is what distinguishes a genuine open-shell singlet from a formally similar closed shell. Core shells of the metal and the light atoms were frozen in all correlated steps.
reference_short: Moossen & Dolg, J. Phys. Chem. A 2016, 120, 3966
notes: The mirror image of the methylene compound: localizing the orbitals INTRODUCES multiconfigurational character where the delocalized picture showed none. Together the two cases show that configuration weights are meaningless without stating the orbital basis.
correlation_correction: Second-order perturbation theory and multireference configuration interaction applied separately; the orbital-rotation analysis is carried out at the CASSCF level, on the stated grounds that small charge-distribution changes from dynamical correlation cannot be rendered in a simple orbital picture anyway

method: Valence bond self-consistent field calculations truncated by seniority number, compared against molecular-orbital-based multiconfigurational calculations truncated by the same criterion from the opposite end, with the complete active space calculation as the benchmark. Two orbital sets were used: strictly localized hybrid atomic orbitals and semilocalized overlap-enhanced orbitals
software: The Xiamen Valence Bond program XMVB, with preliminary restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock calculations in GAMESS to supply integrals and the nuclear repulsion energy
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight orbitals, matching the space used in the reference orbital-based study.
active_space_protocol: The active space is held fixed and truncated internally by seniority number, the count of singly occupied orbitals. The valence-bond expansion begins at maximum seniority and works down; the orbital-based expansion begins at zero seniority and works up, so the two truncate the same Hilbert space from opposite ends. The complete active space result is the benchmark.
nroots_per_mult: one
electronic_structure_description: A model strongly correlated system dissociated symmetrically with all hydrogen-hydrogen distances kept equal along the curve. Used as the first test of whether the seniority-truncated valence-bond expansion converges faster than its orbital-based counterpart, measured by the nonparallelity error against the complete-space benchmark. Natural orbital occupation numbers were tabulated at a stretched distance of 2.5 Angstrom for successive seniority sectors. At the lowest truncation level both formulations involve the same number of determinants, but the orbital-based wave function requires more configuration state functions than the valence-bond one requires structures.
Other: This study holds the active space completely fixed and varies how the space is TRUNCATED FROM THE INSIDE, which is a different question from the usual one of how large to make it. Seniority number -- the count of singly occupied orbitals in a configuration -- is used to slice the same complete Hilbert space into sectors, and the striking result is that the molecular-orbital and valence-bond formulations truncate it from OPPOSITE ENDS. The orbital-based expansion starts at zero seniority, all electrons paired, and adds unpaired-electron sectors; the valence-bond expansion starts at MAXIMUM seniority, every active orbital singly occupied, and works down. Since both converge on the same complete-space answer, the interesting quantity is which reaches it faster, and for bond-breaking the answer is the reverse ordering: for dinitrogen the nonparallelity error along the dissociation curve is 21.6 millihartree for the valence-bond truncation against 53.9 for the orbital-based one at comparable truncation level, with the valence-bond curve lying lower everywhere. This makes chemical sense -- a dissociating bond ends in unpaired electrons, so an expansion that begins there needs fewer terms -- and it means the practical size of a space depends on the coordinate one is describing, not just on the molecule. As both expansions approach completeness the gap narrows to almost nothing, which is the right check: the advantage is in the rate of convergence, not in the limit. A separate compactness comparison is made at fixed content rather than fixed accuracy: at the lowest level both formulations involve the same number of determinants, yet the orbital-based wave function needs more configuration state functions than the valence-bond one needs structures, so the valence-bond side is more compact at equal footing. The ORBITAL choice within the fixed space is treated as a separate variable again, and the trade-off is stated plainly: strictly localized hybrid atomic orbitals make each structure interpretable as a classical Lewis bonding pattern, while semilocalized overlap-enhanced orbitals give a more compact wave function and a lower total energy. Both were run for the hardest case, and crucially the qualitative result survives the choice -- every seniority-truncated valence-bond calculation dissociates correctly to two ground-state atoms regardless of which orbital set is used. A conclusion that holds under both localizations is much safer than one demonstrated with a single choice. The complete-space calculation serves throughout as the benchmark that the truncations are measured against, so the errors quoted are truncation errors within a fixed space rather than errors against experiment.
reference_short: Chen, Zhou & Wu, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2015, 11, 4102
notes: Chosen so that geometries, active space and basis all match an earlier orbital-based seniority study, making the comparison strictly like-for-like.
correlation_correction: None; the study concerns truncation of the reference expansion itself rather than a correction on top of it

geometry_source: Optimized first at the generalized valence bond perfect-pairing level, then at CASSCF; the transition state located with a DIIS-ridge method to a gradient convergence of 1e-3 hartree/bohr
method: Full-valence CASSCF built on natural orbitals inherited from a generalized valence bond perfect-pairing calculation, used to generate forces for ab initio molecular dynamics on the classical Born-Oppenheimer surface; transition state located by a DIIS-ridge method and confirmed by a single imaginary frequency from a finite-difference Hessian
basis_set: 6-31G** plus two diffuse sets, a valence double-zeta basis with one diffuse and one polarization function on each atom, chosen because a triple-zeta basis would make the dynamics prohibitively expensive
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals, the full valence space, built from the natural orbitals of paired treatments of two carbon-hydrogen bonds, one carbon-carbon sigma bond, one carbon-carbon pi bond and one carbon lone pair.
active_space_protocol: The space is the full valence, with its orbitals taken as the natural orbitals of a preceding generalized valence bond perfect-pairing calculation, so every active orbital corresponds to an identifiable bond or lone pair. The carbon 1s orbitals are treated at closed-shell Hartree-Fock level.
nroots_per_mult: one
electronic_structure_description: The high-energy isomer whose rearrangement to acetylene is the subject of the study. Its total energy in this space is -76.898374 hartree and its zero-point energy 14.7 kcal/mol, against 14.87 from coupled cluster and an experimental 14.1; the dideuterated form has 11.5. The rearrangement barrier from this space is 5.6 kcal/mol, or 3.6 with zero-point correction and 4.2 for the dideuterated species, against a coupled-cluster 2.85 and an experimental lower bound of 2.2, so the barrier is likely about 2.8 kcal/mol too high. The molecular expansion consists of 19404 spin eigenfunctions. Dynamics started from vibrationally excited vinylidene show that none of the trajectories equilibrated at 600 K and only 20 percent of those equilibrated at 1440 K isomerize within a picosecond, implying average lifetimes above 1 ps.
Other: The space here is full-valence by construction and, unusually, its ORBITALS ARE INHERITED rather than optimized from scratch: a generalized valence bond calculation with perfect pairing is run first, its natural orbitals are collected, and those ten orbitals become the active space. Building the space from localized bond pairs means every orbital in it has an identifiable chemical owner -- for the neutral species two carbon-hydrogen bonds, a carbon-carbon sigma bond, a carbon-carbon pi bond and a carbon lone pair; for the product two carbon-hydrogen bonds, a sigma bond and two pi bonds. The lone pair is the crucial inclusion, since the whole rearrangement is a migration onto it, and a space chosen by orbital energy ordering might well have missed it. The most quotable thing in the paper is a QUANTIFIED space restriction. For the anion the full space is too slow for dynamics, so the out-of-plane pi bond, which is orthogonal to the reaction coordinate, is demoted from the active space to a paired treatment, dropping ten electrons in ten orbitals to nine in nine and cutting the expansion from 53 136 to 53 004 spin eigenfunctions -- for an energy cost the authors state as one times ten to the minus six hartree. Justifying a restriction by naming the coordinate the removed orbital is orthogonal to, and then measuring the error rather than asserting it is small, is exactly how such a decision should be documented. The BASIS is the compromise, and it is made explicitly and with its cost quoted from prior work: a valence double-zeta set with one diffuse and one polarization function per atom is used because a triple-zeta set would make the dynamics prohibitively expensive, and a plain double-zeta basis is known to raise this barrier by 1.5 to 2.7 kcal per mole and lower the exothermicity by 4. The residual error is then reported honestly against better methods rather than hidden: the space describes the exothermicity well, -47.9 kcal per mole against a coupled-cluster -45.3 and an experimental -49.5, but the barrier is stated to be too high by about 2.8 kcal per mole, 5.6 against 2.85. For a barrier of only a few kcal per mole that is a large relative error, and it matters here because the paper's central claim is about how long molecules survive above that barrier -- a barrier that is too high biases lifetimes upward, which the authors do not conceal. Zero-point energies from this space agree closely with coupled-cluster and experimental values, within a few tenths of a kcal per mole for every species, so the space is evidently good for curvature even where it is imperfect for the barrier top. Cs symmetry was imposed throughout, the carbon 1s orbitals were kept closed-shell, and the transition state was confirmed by a single imaginary frequency from a finite-difference Hessian built on analytic gradients.
reference_short: Hayes, Fattal, Govind & Carter, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2001, 123, 641
notes: The central finding rests on this surface: because the neutral and the anion are structurally similar but both very different from the transition state, the neutral is never formed near the barrier and must wait until enough instantaneous kinetic energy accumulates in the right modes. Every trajectory that did isomerize recrossed the barrier multiple times, violating conventional transition-state theory.
correlation_correction: None; the full-valence CASSCF surface is used directly for the dynamics, with its residual errors against coupled-cluster values stated explicitly

electronic_structure_description: A prototypical system for excitonic coupling: two phenyl rings weakly coupled through the bridging methylene group, so that it behaves as a phenyl dimer. Experiment places the first two excited states at 4.63 to 4.64 eV with a splitting of 123 reciprocal centimetres. The eight-orbital space gives 113 reciprocal centimetres for that splitting, in good agreement, while overestimating the absolute excitation energies by about 1.6 eV; the twelve-orbital space recovers 75 percent of the correlation energy relative to experiment but gives a worse splitting of 159. Perturbative correction on the smaller space improves the excitation energy by 0.2 eV, while its multistate variant and a local coupled-cluster treatment overshoot by 0.45 to 0.50 eV. Splittings reported across levels of theory in the literature range from 265 to 591 reciprocal centimetres and as high as 1429, all generally larger than experiment.
Other: This is an unusually instructive case because enlarging the active space and adding the perturbative correction each IMPROVE ONE QUANTITY WHILE DEGRADING ANOTHER, so no single choice is best and the authors have to say which quantity they care about. The eight-electron eight-orbital space covers the pi systems of both aromatic rings but deliberately excludes the complete set of bonding and antibonding orbitals. With it, the SPLITTING between the two lowest excited states -- the quantity the whole exciton-dynamics study depends on -- comes out at 113 reciprocal centimetres against an experimental 123, excellent agreement. But the ABSOLUTE excitation energies are about 1.6 eV too high, which the authors attribute jointly to the restricted space and to missing dynamic correlation. Enlarging to twelve electrons in twelve orbitals, taking all pi orbitals of both rings, recovers 75 percent of the correlation relative to experiment and so fixes much of the absolute error -- yet the splitting DEGRADES to 159 reciprocal centimetres. The perturbative correction on the smaller space improves the excitation energy by a further 0.2 eV; its multistate variant and a local coupled-cluster method both overshoot by 0.45 to 0.50 eV and are described as not superior to the uncorrected reference. The upshot is that the cheapest, smallest, uncorrected treatment is the best one for the state splitting, and the authors keep it for exactly that reason. A second sensitivity compounds the first and is stated plainly: the splitting is EXTREMELY sensitive to the molecular structure, with slight distortions away from symmetry increasing the gap substantially. Their response is a consistency argument rather than an accuracy one -- the lowest and best gap is obtained by computing energies at the SAME level used for the geometry optimization, so that the structure and the energies are at least mutually consistent. That is the right instinct when a quantity depends more on geometry than on correlation: mixing a high-level energy with a lower-level geometry can be worse than using one level throughout. Context from the literature reinforces the difficulty: reported splittings for this molecule span up to 1429 reciprocal centimetres across levels of theory, and static calculations within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation are known to systematically overestimate the gap for nearly degenerate weakly coupled dimers, which this molecule effectively is -- two aromatic rings weakly coupled through a methylene bridge. A vibronic treatment reduces the splitting. So a value that agrees with experiment here is partly a favourable cancellation, and the authors' choice is defensible on consistency grounds rather than on the claim that the space is converged.

electronic_structure_description: The parent para-phenylene bridged member of the series, whose structure was reported previously.
Other: The active space here is used to build a two-dimensional SURFACE rather than to compute a single number, and that is what makes it testable. Exchange coupling constants were calculated across a grid of donor-bridge and bridge-acceptor torsion angles, producing a colour-coded map onto which the crystallographically determined torsions of six real complexes could be overlaid. Fitting the experimental couplings to that computed surface gives a correlation of R-squared equal to 0.899 for both the exchange and the electronic coupling. A calculation that reproduces one measured number can always be a coincidence; one that reproduces the FUNCTIONAL FORM of a coupling across a two-dimensional conformational landscape, tested against six independently synthesized and crystallographically characterized molecules, is a much stronger claim, and it is the right way to validate a space for a property as sensitive as superexchange. The sharpest quantitative test is at the small-coupling limit, where errors are hardest to hide: for the saturated bicyclooctane bridge the measured coupling is only +1 reciprocal centimetre, and the calculation is described as consistent with it. Predicting a coupling of order one reciprocal centimetre correctly is a demanding check, and it underwrites the paper's central chemical conclusion -- that superexchange through a para-phenylene ring held perpendicular to both radical partners, about 1.7 reciprocal centimetres, is equivalent within experimental resolution to that through a fully saturated bridge. From that equivalence two further negative results follow: there is no measurable difference attributable to the sp2 versus sp3 hybridization of the bridge carbons, and none attributable to the bicyclooctane offering three two-carbon pathways where para-phenylene offers two. Negative results of this kind are only meaningful if the method can resolve the difference it fails to find, which the one-reciprocal-centimetre agreement establishes. The conformational independence of the sigma pathway is then explained on symmetry grounds rather than numerically, from how the three bridgehead-to-methylene bonds transform in the local threefold symmetry of the bridgehead carbon. The significant limitation for a database reader is that this is a Communication: the size and composition of the active space, the basis set and the program are all confined to the supporting information, so none of the parameters that would let the surface be reproduced appear in the paper itself, and the individual coupling constants for five of the six complexes are given only in a figure.

geometry_source: Ground-state conformers optimized with the B3LYP functional; minima, conical intersections and reaction paths optimized at two-root state-averaged CASSCF, with all energies re-evaluated by multistate CASPT2
method: Two-root equal-weight state-averaged CASSCF for minima, conical intersections, minimum-energy profiles and interpolated paths, with multistate CASPT2 in a larger common active space to re-evaluate every energy; ground-state conformers first optimized by density functional theory, and vertical excitations also computed with a range-separated functional for comparison
software: GAUSSIAN 09 for the density functional work and for the CASSCF conical intersection optimizations; MOLCAS 8.0 for the CASPT2 calculations and the CASSCF minima and reaction paths
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals at the CASSCF level, composed differently for each state: five occupied pi and three unoccupied pi antibonding orbitals for the bright pi-pi-antibonding state, with one occupied pi orbital replaced by the carbonyl oxygen lone pair for the dark n-pi-antibonding state. The perturbative step uses twelve electrons in nine orbitals, the union of the two: five occupied pi orbitals, the oxygen lone pair, and three pi antibonding orbitals.
active_space_protocol: State-specific composition at the reference level, so each state gets its best small space, with a larger common space at the correlated level so that energies compared across states share one description. Two-root state averaging with equal weights. An imaginary shift of 0.2 guards against intruder states, Cholesky decomposition is used for the two-electron integrals, and both zero and the default IPEA shift of 0.25 are reported for the vertical excitations.
nroots_per_mult: two, averaged with equal weights
electronic_structure_description: A sunscreen chromophore. Vertical excitation energies at the corrected level with the default shift are 4.72 eV to the bright pi-pi-antibonding state and 5.50 eV to the dark n-pi-antibonding state for the trans isomer, and 4.74 and 5.41 eV for the cis isomer; with the shift set to zero these become 4.12 and 5.23 for trans and 4.13 and 5.13 for cis. For the trans isomer the major deactivation route from the bright state is decay to the dark state through an in-plane crossing point, requiring only a 2.5 kcal/mol barrier, with a minor route to the ground state through a conical intersection reached by out-of-plane photoisomerization. For the cis isomer the two routes are comparable.
Other: Two design decisions here are worth copying. metal_ox_state: formally +4, but the ground state is a mixed-valence superposition of Re(IV) and Re(V) forms

active_space_orbital_description: Six electrons in nine orbitals for the reported calculations: the five rhenium 5d orbitals together with the highest occupied, the lowest unoccupied and two further virtual orbitals of the o-benzoquinone ligand. active_space_protocol: Spaces were varied from four electrons in six orbitals up to eight in ten, and the authors report that similar results were obtained in all cases, which is the relevant check when the question is how much ligand character mixes into metal-based states. The minimal space is the smallest capable of representing the redox ambiguity: the complete metal d shell plus the one ligand orbital that can accept an electron.
nroots_per_mult: 5 quintet, 22 triplet and 25 singlet states in the reported state-averaged calculation
electronic_structure_description: A triplet ground state whose wave function has strongly multireference character: three configurations contribute substantially, and the state is a superposition of a rhenium(IV)-semiquinolate form and a rhenium(V)-catecholate form with comparable weights, the former predominating above 54 percent. The complex is therefore formally a rhenium(IV) semiquinolate but is more accurately a mixed-valence species. This matches the crystallography independently: C-O, C-C and Re-O distances at both 150 and 290 K lie between the semiquinolate and catecholate limits, giving an empirical metrical oxidation state of -1.5 for the dioxolene ligand. In the minimal space the quintet lies 0.38 eV (3060 reciprocal centimetres) above the triplet and the lowest singlet 1.36 eV (10940 reciprocal centimetres) above it. Spin-orbit coupling produces an anomalously large zero-field splitting, 341 reciprocal centimetres with a rhombicity of low value at one level and 481 with a rhombicity of 0.026 at the correlated level, consistent with the measured magnetic susceptibility from 5 to 300 K. The minimal space is defined by a clear rule -- the complete metal d shell plus the one ligand orbital that can accept an electron -- which is the smallest space capable of representing the redox ambiguity at issue. geometry_source: Bond distance scanned to generate the potential energy curve rather than optimized; near equilibrium, 1.65 to 1.75 Angstrom, restricted Hartree-Fock canonical orbitals seeded the optimizations, while every other point was started from the converged natural orbitals and wave function of its neighbouring geometry
method: Generalized active space self-consistent field with second-order perturbation theory on top, compared directly against the complete active space treatment of the same space; the generalized scheme confines each bonding-antibonding pair to its own subspace, permits only two active electrons to be excited within a pair, and forbids excitations between subspaces
